Here is how the prayer of the Gothic Breviary embraces the foregoing exposition with marvelous brevity:

> “Let the mountains receive,” it says, “peace . . . . . they who have been illumined by the primordial ray of faith, so that from the sublimity of the saints the righteousness of the hills may descend” [Col. 0032A].

And if you read through the Isidorian Gothic Office, you will find it filled with authorities from Saint Augustine.

In the Office for the Dead of this Gothic Breviary of ours, prayers are placed under the heading *Abecedaria*. Before them are David’s psalms without numbering, following only the letters of the alphabet, so that beneath each psalm bearing a heading there are found only verses beginning with the same letter, drawn from the whole Psalter of David [Col. 0032B]. For example, the first psalm for the dead begins, “Deliver my soul from the wicked,” and the remaining verses begin with the same letter E; the second psalm begins, “How long will he be exalted?” and all its verses continue with the letter U. The whole arrangement corresponds to the composition of Augustine’s psalm against the Donatists, made according to the letters of the alphabet. For this reason it is called an alphabetical psalm, although in the edition of Cardinal Ximenes and in the present edition, in order to avoid excessive length, some verses are not included under a single letter.

Rabanus Maurus drew a great deal from the two books of Saint Isidore *On the Origin of the Offices*. When the Fathers assembled at the Synod of Aachen undertook to write a rule for canons, they saw that Saint Isidore’s books *On the Offices* were highly useful and well suited to reforming and instructing men, and therefore transcribed almost the whole of them into their rule [Col. 0032C]. We may consequently assert with confidence that Isidore prescribed a norm for the clergy and monks not only in Spain but also in other provinces.

From all this it is clear that the Mozarabic Breviary was rightly entitled by Cardinal Ximenes according to the rule of Blessed Isidore. For although this holy Doctor was not the author of the rite—just as Gregory the Great was not the author of Gregorian chant—their designations were taken from the correctors and organizers. Nor was Dionysius Exiguus the first to calculate the course of the solar and lunar years for the celebration of Easter; nor was Gratian the first compiler of the canons; nor was Baronius the first writer of ecclesiastical annals [Col. 0032D]. They nevertheless rightly claimed such titles for themselves, both because of the greater diligence with which they worked out their studies and because of the superior order and arrangement of their material. In the same way, our Isidore, although not the first institutor of the Gothic liturgy or the author of the canonical hours, was at least the organizer and corrector of both.

Let the most prudent reader, I beg, make allowance for the injuries of time, the changes of circumstances, and the varying rulers of Spain; and let him read with a calm expression the variant readings by which historians are burdened and liturgists entangled, so that they may reach the goal of truth.

The skill we brought to the present edition would have benefited us little if we had not been assisted by the counsel and labor of others [Col. 0033A]. Know, therefore, that we spared neither expense nor effort. At Toledo we assembled a company of learned men, dignitaries, and canons of this holy Church of ours; and at Madrid we consulted other highly approved men [Col. 0034A], one of whom in particular devoted himself to avoiding typographical errors.

If, despite so many and such great vigils, most discerning reader, you should still encounter something objectionable, do not prejudge the matter until you have examined the autographs with your own eyes. Farewell.

[Col. 0033]

# Explanation of the Eugenian or Melodic Chant

Made by Saint Jerome Romero, prebendary of the Holy Church of Toledo, Primate of the Spains, and teacher of melodic chant.

[Col. 0033B] It is universally acknowledged that the great, immutable diatonic system—also called Pythagorean and perfect—celebrated among the ancients, was the North, or Pole, by which all ecclesiastical chant was directed and ordered. It consisted of fifteen strings, which they divided into five tetrachords, by means of which they arranged their compositions, both harmonious and regulated, just as we arrange ours. The final notes of the tones were the same as those observed by modern musicians; the regular *saeculorum* of each tone was correspondingly the same as that which we use at present. Finally, whatever is required for the perfect composition of each tone was found in the aforesaid system, devised either by Pythagoras, Orpheus, or another author, whose investigation is not part of our present purpose. Indeed, we might argue with some that the tones of the psalms descend from King David himself. But it is enough to say that the Church has always carefully guarded the tone. For just as we have keys and signs for recognizing and performing chant, so the ancients also had, in their own way, a key and an infallible sign, by which they sang with as much firmness as we do; furthermore, our signs and keys are universal [Col. 0033C].

For further confirmation, observe that the letter over which the text proceeds is the psalm-tone; every psalm is sung according to the *saeculorum* assigned to it. Moreover, the *saeculorum* assigned to our text is undoubtedly that of the sixth tone; and the sixth tone has its stable seat in the sign F. The strings, or voices, proceeding from it are sung by us today by virtue of the flat, and by the ancients through the third tetrachord. Therefore, since this is diatonic and natural when it governs the choir book, just as when it is governed by the sign G, it cannot be denied—when all the circumstances are considered—that the interpretation assigned to the text is genuine, and not the one that results from the other signs.

You will object, first, that several choir books lack the *saeculorum*, and for that reason cannot be identified. But if you carefully consider the manner in which each tone proceeds within its octave according to its major and minor species, you will very easily find what you seek [Col. 0033D].

You will object, second, that it is exceedingly difficult, almost impossible, to distinguish the various and diverse forms of characters by which the ancients notated their choir books. But consider that, in reality, there is no variation in substance, because the first tone will certainly be perfect if its choir book fills out its entire octave, whatever its manner or whatever characters may have been used to mark or write it. To identify it, therefore, examine whether its final is on D [Col. 0034B]. This will be determined by examining the ascent, descent, principal cadences, and intermediate cadences—a task permitted not to beginners but to those more skilled in ancient and modern chant.

You will object, third: It is known among all singers that the figures or notes of plain or simple chant can neither be increased nor diminished, as is clear from its definition. Since we see them diminished in the text set out above, the text appears to lack art and rule. To resolve this difficulty, observe that plain chant is not always simple, but is very often mixed, as happens in hymns, sequences, and other things sung in the Church. The same occurs in our text, for Gothic singers frequently used mixed chant.

You will object, fourth, that the intonation and the *saeculorum* of our text have been assigned to the sixth tone, but that every notation of the *saeculorum* is made with plain figures, which our text lacks; therefore it is arbitrary. I reply that although the figures of our text do not appear to the eye in print as they are customarily written today, they are nevertheless truly present [Col. 0034C]. Every *saeculorum* is subject to the letter, and according to the length or brevity of the words the letter increases or diminishes it.

So that no doubt may remain for you, I set out these rules.

## First Rule

Mozarabic or Gothic chant is always mixed and is governed with consideration of time, or binary measure, except for hymns, which are in triple measure. For fuller understanding, examine the signs of the text assigned above.

## Rule II

All separate figures, although dotted in different ways, as in numbers 1 and 2, are semibreves, and the value of each is one time, or measure.

## Rule III

Figures joined to two or four others diminish and halve their value, so that two joined figures make one semibreve. This is evident in our text in numbers 3, 4, 6, and 7, and in the letters M and Q, with the sole distinction visible in number 4, where four equal figures are joined, however it may be positioned. Although each of the figures of the letters M and Q joins four other figures, it is to be understood that the first two are minims and the other two semibreves. This will be understood more clearly from the following example. When today, in imperfect time, we see figures joined equally by two semibreves, we assign them twice the value.

## Rule IV

The figure under number 12 is a breve [Col. 0035A], first because the verse is divided there, and second so that a brief rest may be made there before continuing the chant. The final figure, which is under the letter Q, is also a breve because the work ends with it.

I learned what has been said thus far from a celebrated musician. In his *Mappa*, he treats all ancient musical figures, both instrumental and plain, from the second century of our salvation through the fifteenth century inclusive. And if your mind still wavers, read the *History of Musical Chant* prepared by the Reverend Father Giovanni Battista Martini. On page 398, table 5, you will find certain tones written with figures or points similar to ours.

To this I add that from childhood I was instructed in the rules not only of plain and figured chant but also of Eugenian, or melodic, chant, as it is called. This chant has endured into our own time in this venerable Church of Toledo, Primate of the Spains, so that it is mingled alternately with Gregorian chant in marvelous consonance [Col. 0035B].

This chant is called Eugenian after its author, Saint Eugene III [Col. 0036A], archbishop of Toledo in the time of the Gothic kings. This holy Father, highly skilled in the musical art, organized the chant of this Church and himself instructed the children, as the history of the Gothic Fathers and ancient images indicate. In truth, Eugenian chant was founded upon the great system, and we call it Gothic because it persisted not only until the invasion of the Saracens but also during their rule, although corrupted. For this reason the Church of Toledo has rightly claimed the Gothic chant and its interpretation for itself by hereditary right in perpetuity; and by the decree of Saint Pius V appended to the Missal, it was permitted to retain the Toledo chant throughout Spain, moved by the prayers of our Catholic king Philip II.

Eugenian chant, which we now call melodic, has two forms: simple gloss and double gloss. We use the double gloss for all feasts throughout the year, and the simple gloss for ferial days, responsories, and tracts. The matter will become clearer by an example. Here is the double gloss in the Gradual for the Mass of Saints Peter and Paul the Apostles.

[Col. 0035]

On the feast of Saints Peter and Paul the Apostles, at Mass: GRADUAL.

Simple gloss on the same text.

[Col. 0035B] In order that it may be sung with the greatest possible perfection, the following must be observed [Col. 0035C]. First, the *circinum*, or measure, should be brief but not excessively rapid. Second, everything presented to you under both glosses must be performed legato; nevertheless, you must never strike any point, because you would destroy the melody. Third, the triplet, indicated by the letters *tri*, must not last longer than the value of the figure over which it is placed [Col. 0036B], whether that figure continues with a dot or without one. Fourth, you must never depart from the gloss of any point, nor from the smallest detail of the punctuation, because in this consists the harmonic melody of the chant in question [Col. 0036C].

Anyone who is uncertain about the explanation of the text or about the gloss of Eugenian chant should come to this Church of Toledo and will marvel that its memory has been preserved after so many centuries.

[BREVIARY.]

In a leap year, wherever the leap-day occurs, if the feast of Saint Matthias falls on that day, his vigil is fasted on that day, and the feast is celebrated and observed on the following day. [Col. 0043]

# RULE

[Col. 0043A] Here begin the Hours to be sung or recited according to the Rule of the Most Blessed Isidore, Supreme Doctor of Spain, and of the distinguished confessor Ildephonsus, bishop and teacher of Toledo—not exactly as the ancients used that Rule, but in a qualified sense. For in ancient times there were customarily twelve Hours during the day, as is shown in the ancient books, besides certain other Hours that they used at night: namely, at the beginning of the night, before going to bed, at the equinox or middle of the night, and at the rising from bed. These have been discarded and removed by modern usage, but in such a way that moderns continue and perform the Rule as will become clear in what follows.

And because few people know how to preserve and arrange the order of these Hours, owing to the negligence and carelessness of many—since they care only about receiving the revenues of the Church—and because many excellent buildings easily collapse after a long passage of time unless a remedy is applied, therefore a certain unskilled and unworthy cleric, considering this holy and wholly devout work, produced by so great a prelate through divine inspiration and grace, lest it perish but might return to human memory, moved by piety and prompted by devotion, for the glory and praise of the Trinity [Col. 0044A], and of Jesus and Mary his Mother, and for the honor of the aforesaid Supreme Confessor, and for the illumination of present and future clerics, according to the poverty of his knowledge and the weakness of his understanding, having invoked divine assistance and its radiant light, labored to compose this Rule as follows, and translated and reproduced this codex from the Gothic script.

# THE RULE FOLLOWS THUS.

Whether it is a feast day or an ordinary day, the Hours always begin at Vespers, before the day; and the beginning, or commencement, is made by an invocation of Jesus Christ, preceded by the Lord’s Prayer, saying in a subdued voice:

“Lord, have mercy. Christ, have mercy. Lord, have mercy. Our Father.”

And in a loud voice:

“In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, [Col. 0044B] light with peace.”

Response by those present: “Thanks be to God.”

And the priest says:

“The Lord be always with you.”

Response: “And with your spirit.”

And the order of Vespers, whether it is a feast or not, proceeds in this manner. First the Psalm, or Vespertinum—which is the same thing—is said. When it is finished, the priest says:

“The Lord be always with you.”

Response: “And with you.”

Immediately the Sonus is said, if it is a feast, because an ordinary weekday lacks a Sonus—except during the season of the [Col. 0045A] Resurrection, when it is said on account of the solemnity. When it is finished, “The Lord be always,” as above, is said, and immediately one Antiphon is said without Alleluia, with its accompanying Versicle and with “Glory to the Father,” as will be explained below in its proper place. Again: “The Lord be always,” etc. Immediately another Antiphon is said, with Alleluia; this is called the Lauda, with its accompanying Versicle and “Glory to the Father.” When these have been completed, the Hymn follows. When it is finished, the Intercession, or Supplication, follows: “Let us beseech the Redeemer.” Immediately the Capitula follows, with the Lord’s Prayer after it, namely:

“Our Father. And lead us not. But deliver. Deliver us from evil,”

and it is to be said as it is written in the ordering of the Hours. Immediately the Benediction follows, preceded by:

“Bow yourselves for the blessing.”

The Lauda then follows without interruption, with its accompanying Versicle and “Glory.” When this has been completed, one Prayer from Matins must be said, whichever the reciter wishes, except the first, which is joined to the Matutinarium and is never changed from its proper place. Immediately the Commemorations are made, those that are customary or that newly arise.

And know that at Vespers you—or anyone who wishes to perform this Rule or the Office of this Rule—must proceed in the manner stated above. Although there are several Vespertina, Sonus chants, Antiphons, and Laudes in the ordering of the histories, only one Vespertinum or Psalm—which is the same thing—and one Lauda should be said. The Antiphon is what is said without Alleluia; the Lauda is what is said with Alleluia. This is understood of feasts that have no Proper texts, because in those that do have Proper texts, one must say it as it is ordered there; [Col. 0045C] for there are certain feasts that exceed this arrangement in their Antiphons and Prayers.

Matins is likewise to be begun as Vespers is. The Matutinarium follows, and the Psalm “Have mercy on me, O God,” with its attached Prayer; then three Antiphons with their Prayers. Immediately the Response follows at certain feasts, with its Prayer, namely at solemn feasts. Then the Canticle; then the Benediction; then the Sonus; then the Laudes. Immediately the Prophecy follows, and directly after it the Hymn. From there the Supplication follows, namely, “Let us beseech the Redeemer.” Then the Capitula; then the Lauda, which is said at the end of Vespers; and immediately the Benediction is said, the one that was said at Vespers. Immediately the customary Commemorations are made—unless they are solemn feasts. [Col. 0046A]

When Vespers is finished, “In the evening, morning, and at midday” is said, with its Prayer; at Matins, “To announce your mercy in the morning,” with the Prayer that follows; and at Compline, “Guard us, Lord, as the apple of the eye,” with its attached Prayer. Thus the aforementioned Hours are completed, except on Sundays, because at the beginning of Matins there is another arrangement. After the Lord’s Prayer and “In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ,” etc., we begin and say the Hymn “Eternal Maker of all things,” with its following Prayer. Immediately three Psalms follow, namely: “Lord, how they have multiplied who afflict me?”; “Have mercy on me, O God,” the second; and “Have mercy on me,” Psalm 56, with their Antiphons. From there comes the following Prayer, and thereafter everything else as in the other Matins.

And if on principal Sundays, which are treated almost like historical feasts—for example, during Advent or Lent, or on similar Sundays whose observance cannot be changed—a feast should occur, the feast is transferred and celebrated on the following day. And if another, more solemn feast should happen to occur on the following day, that feast is to be observed, and the other is to be celebrated on the nearest ordinary day.

And if the feast being celebrated at present should be more important or of greater solemnity than the feast whose celebration ought to be made, Vespers is to be said for this principal feast, in such a way that the final Lauda, together with the Matins Prayer, belongs to the future feast that is to be celebrated, or to the feast that is to be celebrated on the following day.

And if feasts occur that have an Octave according to the Gregorian Rule—for example, the feasts of Saint Mary, Saint John, and the Apostles Peter and Paul, and similar feasts—then, out of reverence for them, on the intervening ordinary days the Hours must be celebrated for those solemnities, though not with equal solemnity, except on the eighth day. And if another feast should fall on the day of the Octave, the Octave is to be observed on the preceding day.

And if two equal or nearly equal feasts should happen to fall on one day, such as the feast of Philip and James, the feast of Saint Torquatus, or similar feasts, the feast for which a Proper is available should be celebrated, unless it is the Invocation of that feast in that church; for the feast for which there is an Invocation must be solemnized, and the other celebrated on the following day.

And if a feast should coincide with a Sunday, the Sunday is to be omitted, since it will have sufficient opportunity throughout the year, and the feast is to be celebrated on that day. Likewise, concerning fasts, you will see the relevant instructions in their proper places.

[Col. 0047]

## In the Name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen. Here Begins the Breviary for the Proper Performance of the Divine Office According to the Rule of the Most Blessed Isidore, Archbishop of Seville. (C)

### 1. On the First Sunday of the Advent of the Lord

[Col. 0047A]

## At Vespers

Let the priest begin with the sign of the cross.

“In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, light with peace.”

Response: “Thanks be to God.”

Let the priest say:

“The Lord be always with you.”

Response: “And with your spirit.”

All Offices are to be begun in this order, except the Office for the Dead.

### Lauda

“From the rising of the sun to its setting.”

P. “Praised be the name of the Lord.”

V. “May the name of the Lord be blessed, now and forever.”

P. “Praised be the name of the Lord.”

[Col. 0047B]

### Prayer

O God, whose name is blessed from the rising of the sun to its setting, fill our heart with knowledge and appoint our mouth to the duties of your praise, so that, just as you are blessed with due honor throughout all ages, so you may be praised with the harmonious voice of all from the rising of the sun to its setting.

R. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God, who are blessed, and live and rule all things for ages of ages.

R. Amen.

Let the priest say:

“The Lord be always with you.”

Response: “And with your spirit.”

And note that at the end of all Prayers it must always be said in the manner stated above.

### Sonus

“Come, let us exult in the Lord; let us rejoice in God our salvation.

V. Let us go before his face with confession and with psalms.

P. Let us rejoice in God.”

[Col. 0047C]

Let the priest say:

“The Lord be always with you.”

Response: “And with you.”

### Antiphon

Alleluia. Hear, all you peoples, for the Lord, going out from his place, will descend, trampling the ends of the earth.

V. Hear this, all nations; listen with your ears, you who inhabit the world.

P. For the Lord, going out from his place.

V. Glory and honor to the Father, and to the Son, [Col. 0048A] and to the Holy Spirit, for ages of ages. Amen.

P. And he will descend, trampling the ends of the earth.

Let the priest say:

“The Lord be always with you.”

Response: “And with you,” etc.

### Lauda

Alleluia. Send us help from the sanctuary, and from Zion watch over us, Lord.

P. On whatever day we call upon you, alleluia, alleluia.

V. We shall rejoice in your salvation, and in the name of our God we shall glory.

P. And from Zion watch over us, Lord.

V. Glory and honor, etc.

P. On whatever day we call upon you.

### Hymn

Let Christ’s assembly proclaim  
to the Parent of all things the fitting thanks  
that it knows to be due,  
and utter the greatest praises.

He fulfilled long ago  
the oracles of the prophets,  
which had been handed down,  
when the only Son of the Maker of the world  
redeemed us.

The Word, proceeding forth and revealed,  
bore the burden of sins;  
and, taking upon himself our dust,  
destroyed the prince of death.

Born from a mother in time;  
yet everlasting from the Father.

In two substances  
there is one person of the Godhead.

God came, made man,  
so that, reborn in the God who was born,  
the new and true man might shine with a new worship.

Therefore, in joy at his birth,  
the people reborn by grace,  
triumphant in the trophy of the nations,  
offer these yearly feasts.

Let this Advent  
be observed with solemn vows  
by all whom it befits to uphold  
the glory of so great a God.

When the second Advent begins  
and terror presses upon the world,  
may this most humble dignity  
of the Savior come to our aid.

To God the Father be glory,  
and to his only Son,  
together with the Spirit, the Comforter,  
through everlasting ages.

Let the Choir respond:

Amen.

### Supplication

Let us beseech the Redeemer, our Lord Jesus Christ, with every kind of supplication, so that in his mercy he may deign to justify us by the grace of his coming.

R. Grant this, eternal almighty [Col. 0049B] God.

Let the priest say:

“Lord, have mercy.”

R. “Christ, have mercy. Lord, have mercy.”

It must be noted that after the Supplication these Kyrie eleisons must be said, as stated above.

### Capitula

We have heard, O Christ; we confess and believe that, proceeding from the Father’s bosom, you came so that you might be clothed in the garment of our flesh, in order to set free—through the mystery of the incarnation you assumed—that which had perished through the contagion of corrupted nature.

Make us receive the foretold joys of your coming with the most ready devotion of rising, so that, since you, proceeding secretly from your native place in order to save human beings, hastened in human form into public view, we, coming out from the place of sin, may behold the swift advance of your divinity with greater purity.

May you not envelop the final moments of our life in the trampling of any danger; rather, may you summon us by the terror of judgment in such a way that you justify us by your accustomed mercy.

Our Father, who are in heaven.

R. Amen.

Hallowed be your name.

R. Amen.

Your kingdom come.

R. Amen.

Your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.

R. Amen.

Give us this day our daily bread.

R. For you are God.

And forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors.

R. Amen.

And lead us not into temptation.

R. But deliver us from evil.

Let the priest say:

Delivered from evil and always strengthened in what is good, may we deserve to serve you, O God and our Lord. Put an end, Lord, to our sins; give joy to the afflicted; grant redemption to captives; health to the sick; and rest to the dead.

Grant peace and security throughout all our days; break the boldness of our enemies; hear, O God, the prayer of all your servants, all faithful Christians, on this day and at every time.

Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, throughout all ages of ages.

R. Amen.

Let the priest say:

“Bow yourselves for the blessing.”

“The Lord be always with you.”

R. “And with your spirit.”

It must be noted that whenever “Delivered from evil” occurs, it must be said as it is stated here above, up to the point where it says “Benediction.”

Let the priest say:

### Benediction

Christ the Lord, who came for our redemption—not by a change of place, but by the reality of the man he assumed—may raise us, destined to be glorified, into the glory of the kingdom.

R. Amen.

And may the same one, coming to redeem us, preserve us, once redeemed, from every evil.

R. Amen.

And because he himself, humbled, took away our iniquity, may he himself, glorified, grant us the rewards of blessedness.

R. Amen.

Through the mercy of our God, who is blessed, and lives and rules all things throughout ages of ages.

R. Amen.

Let the priest say:

“The Lord be always with you.”

R. “And with you.”

[Col. 0050B]

And note that at the end of all Benedictions it must be said in the manner stated above.

### Lauda

You who sit upon the cherubim, appear.

P. Come and save us, Lord. Alleluia.

V. You who rule Israel, attend; you who lead Joseph like a sheep.

P. Come and save us.

V. Glory and honor to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, for ages of ages. Amen.

P. Come and save us.

### 3. Prayer

O God, Son of God, whose name remains forever, and who, making known that you alone are God and Lord, came as king through the mystery of the incarnation you assumed, in order to redeem the world: grant that we may burn so fervently with devotion to this mystery that through it we may escape the snare of the deceiver.

May we, who with open mouth sing beforehand the joys of your Advent, rejoice when you come as judge, that we have been saved.

R. Amen.

Through his mercy.

“In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, let us complete this in peace.”

R. “Thanks be to God.”

The following Commemoration must be said at the end of every Vespers throughout the year.

### Lauda

“In the evening, and in the morning, and at midday.”

P. “We praise you, Lord.”

### Prayer

Lord, almighty God, who commanded that evening, morning, and midday should be called one day, and ordered the sun to recognize its setting, open, we ask, the darkness of our hearts, so that, when you shine upon us, we may know you as the true God and eternal light.

R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

[Col. 0050D]

Let the priest say:

“In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, let us complete this in peace.”

R. “Thanks be to God.”

It must be noted that at the end of all the Hours “In the name of the Lord” must always be said, as above.

## At Matins

### Hymn

Eternal Maker of all things,  
who governs night and day,  
and grants time its seasons  
to relieve weariness.

Already the herald of day sounds,  
the watchman of the deep night;  
the nocturnal light for travelers,  
separating night from night.

[Col. 0051A]

Awakened by this, the morning star  
releases the heavens from darkness;  
at this, every host of errors  
abandons the path of harm.

At this, the sailor gathers strength,  
and the straits of the sea grow calm;  
at this, the very rock of the Church,  
when it sings, washes away guilt.

Let us therefore rise courageously.  
The cock awakens those lying down  
and rebukes the sleepy;  
the cock condemns those who deny.

When the cock crows, hope returns;  
health is restored to the sick.  
The robber’s sword is sheathed;  
faith returns to those who have fallen.

Look upon those who are slipping, Jesus,  
and correct us by seeing us.  
If you look upon them, the fallen will stand,  
and guilt is loosed by tears.

You are the light: shine upon our senses  
and scatter the sleep of our minds.  
May our voice sound first to you,  
and may we sing psalms to you with our mouths.

Glory to the unbegotten Father,  
glory to the Only-Begotten,  
together with the Holy Spirit,  
through everlasting ages.

R. Amen.

[Col. 0051C]

### Prayer

Every tongue confesses and believes that you are the eternal author, Creator, and Lord of all things. For in the beginning you made all things; you are the very rock of the Church, in which, lamenting our sins, we wash them away.

You, then, look upon those who are slipping in the beginning, and correct us by looking upon us, so that our voice may always resound to you in your courts, and we may deserve to be released for you.

Because of your clemency we ask, ineffable God, that your angelic protection may always watch over us, and that, coming into the light with exultation from your light, we may never depart from it forever, and may deserve to enjoy eternal joys with your elect.

R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

### Antiphon

Lord, how they have multiplied who trouble me? But you, Lord, are my protector.

[Col. 0051D] Psalm 3.

### Antiphon

Wash me, Lord, from my iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin.

Psalm 50.

### Antiphon

Wash me, Lord, from my iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin, Lord.

### Antiphon

In you my soul trusts; deliver me, Lord.

Psalm 56.

### Antiphon

In you my soul trusts; deliver me, Lord.

### Prayer

Lord Jesus Christ, who receive believers by redeeming them and glorify them by exalting them, free your people from the bonds of iniquity and sins. Enrich their hearts with the gift of your truth and wisdom; sanctify their minds, so that, just as glory reigns in heaven with the saints, so your salvation and blessing may remain in us.

R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

The Lord will come as king; there will be one Lord over all the earth.

### Antiphon 2

The Lord will come to the holy place that you desire, and the Angel of the Covenant whom you seek.

P. “Behold, the almighty Lord will come.”

V. “Great is our Lord, and great is his power; and of his wisdom there is no number.”

P. “Behold, he will come.”

[Col. 0052B]

V. “Glory and honor,” etc.

P. “Behold, he will come.”

### Prayer

Christ, Son of God, who, coming to the place of the Virgin’s womb, are recognized as the true Angel of the Covenant, grant us that the faith with which we sing aloud the joys of your incarnation may cleanse us from all debt of our guilt when we see you coming again for judgment.

R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

### Antiphon 3

The one desired by all nations will come.

P. “And every eye will see him.”

V. “God will come manifestly; our God, and he will not be silent.”

P. “And every eye will see him.”

V. “Glory and honor to the Father,” etc.

P. “And every eye will see him.”

### Prayer

O Christ, desired by all nations, coming, save the peoples who confess you, so that you who came first for this purpose, to redeem them, may come again for this purpose: that you may not condemn those who believe in you according to their merits.

R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

R. Come, most merciful Lord; now help us and spare the weary; now, in your mercy, raise up the oppressed. You redeemed the living; rescue the captives. Every creature of yours awaits your coming.

P. While you are here, absolve the guilty; and when you come, defend us, your own.

V. Come, Lord, and do not delay; release the crimes of your people and call back the dispersed to their own land.

P. While you are here.

V. Glory and honor to the Father.

R. Come, most merciful Lord.

### Prayer

Come, most merciful Lord, come; grant freedom in advance to the oppressed. Stir up your power and possess the people you have acquired. Direct the vineyard that you planted through the man of your right hand; and hear, as our advocate, the Son of Man whom you established for yourself.

May the bread of tears have measure amid chastisements, and may the drink of our repentance not weaken but nourish our minds.

R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

## At the Laudes

### For the Canticle

“Let the earth hear the words from my mouth. Let my speech be awaited like rain, and let my words descend like dew.”

### Canticle of Deuteronomy (Chapter 32)

Attend, O heaven, and I will speak;  
* and let the earth hear the words from my mouth.

Let my speech be awaited like rain,  
* and let my words descend like dew,

Like rain upon the grass,  
* and like snow upon the hay.

For I have called upon the name of the Lord:  
* give greatness to the Lord our God.

God—true are his works,  
* and all his ways are judgments.

God is faithful; there is no iniquity in him;  
* the Lord is just and holy.

They sinned against him, though they were not his blameless children;  
* a crooked and perverse nation. Have you repaid this to the Lord,

You foolish and unwise people?  
* Is he not your father, who possessed you, made you, and created you?

[Col. 0053B]

Remember the days of old;  
* understand the years of generation after generation.

Ask your father, and he will tell you;  
* ask your elders, and they will declare it to you.

When the Most High divided the nations,  
* when he scattered the sons of Adam,

He established the boundaries of the nations  
* according to the number of the angels of God.

The Lord’s portion became his people, Jacob;  
* Israel was the cord of his inheritance.

He made him sufficient for himself in a desert land,  
* in the thirst of heat, where there was no water.

He surrounded him and instructed him, like the apple of his eye.  
* As an eagle protects its nest, sitting above its young,

He spread out his wings and took them up,  
* and carried them upon his shoulders.

The Lord alone led them,  
* and there was no foreign god with him.

He placed him upon the heights of the earth,  
* the first growth of the fields.

They offered him honey from the rock,  
* and oil from the hardest rock.

Butter of cattle and milk of sheep, with the fat of lambs and rams, the sons of bulls and goats, with the fat of kidneys,  
* wheat and the blood of the grape.

He drank wine. And Jacob ate,  
* and was filled and grew rebellious.

The beloved one became fat,  
* and grew thick and broad,

[Col. 0053D]

And he abandoned God, who made him,  
* and departed from God his Savior.

They provoked me with foreign gods; with their abominations they stirred me to anger.  
* They sacrificed to demons and not to God,

To gods whom they did not know,  
* new and recent gods whom their kings did not know.

You abandoned the God who begot you,  
* and forgot the God who nourished you.

God saw and was jealous,  
* and was angered by the provocation of his sons and daughters.

And he said: I will turn my face away from them,  
* and I will show what their end will be.

For it is a perverse nation,  
* children in whom there is no faith.

[Col. 0054A]

They stirred me to jealousy  
* by that which is not God;

They provoked me to anger  
* with their idols.

And I will stir them to jealousy with that which is not a nation;  
* I will provoke them with a foolish nation.

For a fire has been kindled in my anger,  
* and it burns down to the depths below;

It will consume the growth of the fields,  
* and set fire to the foundations of the mountains.

I will heap evils upon them,  
* and I will exhaust my arrows against them.

They will waste away with hunger and become food for birds,  
* and incurable tension in their backs;

I will send the teeth of beasts against them,  
* with the fury of creatures that drag themselves upon the earth.

Outside, the sword will kill their children, and within the storehouses,  
* terror—

Young man with virgin,  
* nursing infant with established old man.

I said: I will scatter them;  
* but I will remove their memory from among men.

Were it not for the anger of their enemies,  
* lest they remain long upon the earth, lest their adversaries agree and say: “Our hand is exalted, and the Lord did not make all these things.”

For they are a nation without sound counsel,  
* and there is no understanding in them.

They did not consider in order to understand;  
* they will perceive these things in the future.

How could one pursue a thousand,  
* and two put ten thousand to flight,

Unless the Lord had sold them and the Lord had delivered them up?  
* For our God is not like their gods; but our enemies are senseless.

For their vine is from the vine of Sodom,  
* and their branch from Gomorrah.

Their grape is a grape of gall,  
* and their cluster is bitter to them.

The wine of dragons is their anger,  
* and the incurable fury of asps.

Are these things not gathered up with me,  
* and sealed in my treasuries?

I will repay them on the day of judgment, in due time,  
* when their foot slips.

For the day of their destruction is near,  
* and what is prepared for them will arrive.

For the Lord will judge his people,  
* and he will have compassion on his servants.

For he saw them wearied,  
* exhausted in their oppression and weakened.

And he said: Where are your gods, Israel,  
* in whom you trusted?

Those whose sacrificial fat you ate,  
* and whose libation wine you drank?

Let them rise now and help you,  
* and become your protectors.

See that I am the Lord,  
* and there is no other besides me.

I kill and I make alive;  
* I wound, and I heal, and there is no one who can rescue from my hands.

For I will raise my hand to heaven, swear by my right hand, and say:  
* I live forever.

[Col. 0055A]

For I will sharpen my sword like lightning,  
* and my arrows will be exhausted against them.

And my hand will seize judgment;  
* I will repay judgment to my enemies and render recompense to those who hate me.

I will intoxicate my arrows with blood,  
* and my sword will devour flesh,

With the blood of the wounded,  
* and with captives taken from the head of the enemy princes.

Rejoice, heavens, together with him,  
* and let all his angels adore him.

Rejoice, nations, together with his people,  
* and let all the sons of God strengthen him.

For the blood of his sons will be avenged;  
* he will avenge it, render judgment to his enemies, repay those who hate him, and the Lord will cleanse the land of his people.

[Col. 0055B]

Glory and honor to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.

As it was, etc.

Praise the Lord from the heavens;

Praise him, all his angels;

Praise him, sun and moon;

[Col. 0056A]

Praise him, heavens of heavens,

### Psalm 149

Sing a new song to the Lord;  
* his praise is in the assembly of the saints.

Let Israel rejoice in the one who made him,  
* and let the daughters of Zion exult in their king.

Let them praise his name in the choir;  
* let them sing psalms to him with tambourine and psaltery.

[Col. 0056C]

For the Lord is pleased with his people,  
* and he will exalt the meek in salvation.

The saints will exult in glory;  
* they will rejoice upon their beds.

The exaltations of God are in their throats,  
* and a two-edged sword is in their hands,

To execute vengeance among the nations,  
* rebukes among the peoples,

To bind their kings with fetters,  
* and their nobles with iron chains,

To execute upon them the judgment that has been written.

### Psalm 150

Praise the Lord in his sanctuaries;  
* praise him in the firmament of his power.

Praise him in his mighty deeds;  
* praise him according to the abundance of his greatness.

Praise him with the sound of the trumpet;  
* praise him with psaltery and harp.

Praise him with tambourine and choir;  
* praise him with strings and organ.

Praise him with well-sounding cymbals;  
* praise him with cymbals of jubilation. Let every spirit praise the Lord.

Glory and honor to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.

### 7. Reading from the Book of Ecclesiasticus of Solomon (Chapter 24)

R. Thanks be to God.

My son, whoever hears me will not be put to shame, and those who work through me will not sin; those who make me shine forth will possess eternal life. All these things are the book of life, the covenant of the Most High, and the knowledge of truth.

Moses commanded the Law in ordinances of justice, as an inheritance for the house of Jacob and for Israel’s promises. He appointed David his servant to raise up from him a most powerful king, sitting upon a throne of honor forever.

He fills knowledge like the Pishon, and like the Tigris in the days of new things. He makes understanding full like the Euphrates; he multiplies it like the Jordan in the time of harvest. He sends forth instruction like light, and, standing like the Gihon in the days of the vintage, he was the first to perfect the knowledge of it, and one weaker did not investigate it.

For his thought overflowed from the sea, and his counsel was in the great abyss. I, Wisdom, poured out rivers. I flow like a watercourse in the harvest. I am like the river Dioryx, and like a water conduit I came forth from paradise.

I said: I will water my garden and drench the fruit of my meadow. And behold, my watercourse became abundant, and my river drew near to the sea, because I will illuminate instruction for all like light, and I will proclaim it into the distance.

I will penetrate the lower parts of the earth, inspect all who sleep, and illuminate those who hope in God.

R. Amen.

### Hymn

The almighty King of all,  
coming to save the world,  
assumed the form of a body  
like ours.

He who reigns with the Most High  
enters the Virgin’s womb,  
to be born in the flesh  
and break the bonds of death.

The nations were in darkness.  
They saw the light of radiance  
when the Savior came  
to redeem those whom he had created.

Him whom long ago  
the prophetic oracles foretold,  
now he will come in glory  
to heal our wounds.

Let us now rejoice in the Lord,  
together in the Son of God,  
ready to receive him  
in the glory of his coming.

R. Amen.

Do not despise our prayers, Lord; attend now and graciously hear us, so that we who are cast down, disturbed by the voice of the enemy, may be comforted by the most sacred Advent of your Only-Begotten, and, winged with faith like a dove, may strive toward the things above.

Draw us away, Lord, from the wicked age, and guard us from the snare of the enemy.

Through Christ.

### Our Father

And lead us not.

Delivered from evil and always strengthened in what is good, may we deserve to serve you, O God and our Lord. Put an end, Lord, to our sins; give joy to the afflicted; grant redemption to captives; health to the sick; and rest to the dead.

Grant peace and security throughout all our days; break the boldness of our enemies; hear, O God, the prayer of all your servants, all faithful Christians, on this day and at every time.

Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, throughout all ages of ages.

**Capitula.** O God, whose eternity foreknows and orders the times; who, in the fullness of time, appoints our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, to be born of a Virgin, so that he who proceeds eternally from you, without time, might be born for us as Creator in time; so that he might visit our times and make temporal beings participants in his immortality: may he stand before you on our behalf, so that those whom he wondrously redeemed by his Advent he may enrich most abundantly with his gift.

**The Lord’s Prayer.** Delivered from evil. See fol. 2.

**Blessing.** Christ the Lord, who through the mystery of the flesh he assumed made known to the world the glory of his divinity, by his Advent bring us to life from our sins. **R.** Amen. And he who took upon himself our weakness, may he himself bestow his mercy upon us. **R.** Amen. And he who, coming first in humility, redeemed the world from guilt, coming a second time, may he justify us from all our offenses. **R.** Amen. Through his mercy.

[Col. 0059B] **Lauda.** God will come manifestly, and he will not be silent. Alleluia. **P.** He summoned the heavens above, and the earth, to distinguish his people. Alleluia, alleluia. **V.** The God of gods, the Lord, has spoken, and has summoned the earth. **P.** He summoned. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father. **P.** He summoned.

**Prayer.** O God, Son of God, who, making yourself heard from the ends of the earth, appeared to the world in the flesh: restore yourself as the reward of our faith, so that we who proclaim your wondrous work may be more richly rewarded with that recompense which is before you. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy, our God, etc.

In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, let us complete this in peace. **R.** Thanks be to God.

Let the commemoration be made as in the first Vespers of the Advent of the Lord. Fol. 1.

## MONDAY AFTER THE FIRST SUNDAY OF THE ADVENT OF THE LORD

[Col. 0059C]

### At Matins

**Antiphon.** Lord, how many are those who trouble me! Many rise up against me. **Psalm III.**

**Prayer.** Those who trouble us, Lord, have multiplied; but you are abundant in mercy, and you deliver us. For we fear no impending oppression at all, provided only that we are fortified by your grace, Almighty One. **R.** Amen.

May the Lord be always with you. **R.** And with you.

**Antiphon 1.** Make my name heard, O people, at the ends of the earth, says the Lord; for behold, I am coming, and my glory will illumine all who sit in [Col. 0059D] darkness, so that all the nations may know that I am the Lord. **V.** Hear this, all nations; give ear, you who inhabit the world. **P.** So that all the nations may know. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father. **P.** So that all the nations may know.

**Prayer.** O God, Son of God. See fol. 3.

**Antiphon 2.** Hear, Daniel, the words that I speak to you: close up the utterance and seal the book until Christ the leader. **P.** So that Jerusalem may be built and the Holy of Holies anointed in the place of its sanctification. **V.** I will hear what the Lord God will speak, for he will speak peace to his people. **P.** So that Jerusalem may be built. **V.** Glory and honor. **P.** So that Jerusalem may be built.

**9 Prayer.** O God, who reveal to that holy prophet Daniel, established in the remote places of exile, the mystery of your future mercy, and command him to close the utterance, and ordain that the sealed book remain until Christ the leader: open for us on earth the depths of your mercy, so that whatever in us iniquity has kept closed, the truth of your words may open; that, as we draw near to the manger of our leader, Jesus Christ your Son, we may deserve to be cleansed from every stain of sin. **R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**Antiphon 3.** The work of justice will be peace, and charity forever. **R.** And the people will sit in the beauty of peace. They will see the glory of the Lord and the majesty of our God. **V.** And there will be strength upon the earth; upon the heights of the mountains his fruit will be exalted above Lebanon, [Col. 0060B] and they will flower from the city like the grass of the earth. **R.** And the people will sit. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father, etc. **R.** And the people will sit.

**Prayer.** Behold, we have announced the voice of gladness and joy that we have heard concerning your incarnation, O Christ; we implore your greatness as we await your power, so that we may be made more fruitful in enjoying a sweeter charity, and so that the effect of this voice may prevail everywhere within us, lest we be put to shame by it when your glory is revealed to us. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy, our God, etc.

May the Lord be always with you. **R.** And with your spirit.

**R.** Come, Lord, to deliver your people, for we have been left few from among many, as your eyes see. [Col. 0060C] **P.** And show us the way by which we should walk, and the word that we should do. **V.** O Shepherd of Israel, give heed; you who lead Joseph like a sheep, appear, you who sit above the cherubim. **P.** And show us. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son, etc. Repeat **R.** Come, Lord.

### At Lauds

**At the Canticle. Antiphon.** Behold, the great God, surpassing our knowledge; the number of his years is beyond reckoning.

**Canticle (Job XXXVI).**

Behold, the great God, surpassing our knowledge; * the number of his years is beyond reckoning.

He draws up the drops of rain and pours out showers in the likeness of streams, * which flow from the clouds and spread a covering over all things from above.

If he wishes to extend the clouds like his tent and flash with his light, * from above he also covers the hinges of the sea.

For by these things he judges the peoples, * and gives food to many mortals.

He hides the light in his hands, * and commands it to come forth again.

He looks upon all the heavens beneath, * and his light is over the ends of the earth. * After him the sound roars,

And he thunders with the voice of his majesty; * and when his voice has been heard, it cannot be searched out.

[Col. 0061A] God will thunder wondrously with his voice, * he who does great and unsearchable things.

He commands the snow to descend upon the earth, * and the winter rains and the rain of his strength.

For in the hand of every human being he marks it: * let each one know his own works.

The beast enters its hiding place, * and remains in its cave.

From the inner regions the storm comes forth, * and from Arcturus the cold.

When God blows, ice congeals, * and again the broad waters are poured out.

The cloud desires grain, * and the clouds scatter their light.

They illumine everything around, * wherever the will of the ruler leads them,

To everything that he commands them, * upon the face of the earth.

**P.** Behold, the great God.

Glory and honor to the Father, and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit, etc.

**P.** The number of years.

**Matutinarium. Antiphon.** In your light, O God, we shall see light. **V.** Show your mercy to those who know you, and your justice to those who are upright in heart. **P.** In your light, O God. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father. **P.** In your light, O God.

**Lauda.** Praise the Lord in his sanctuaries. Alleluia, alleluia. Praise him in the firmament of his power. Alleluia. **Psalm CL.** **P.** Praise the Lord. [Col. 0061C] **V.** Glory and honor to the Father, and to the Son, etc. **P.** Praise him in the firmament, etc.

**Prophecy.** My son, he who hears me will not be put to shame. See fol. 7.

In all the following weeks, always seek the Prophecy in the nearest preceding Sunday, and let the course be made through it at Matins, whether it is in the first Sunday, the second, the third, the fourth, or the fifth, or in the sixth week of the Advent of the Lord, up to his Nativity.

**10 Hymn**

The Almighty of all things,

Coming to save the world,

Assumed bodily form

In our likeness.

He who reigns with the Most High

Enters the Virgin’s womb,

About to be born in the flesh,

To break the bonds of death.

Glory to the Unbegotten Father,

Glory to the Only-Begotten,

Together with the Holy Spirit,

For everlasting ages.

Amen.

**Supplication.** Let us pray to the Redeemer. Fol. 2.

**Capitula.** Send forth, almighty Father, from the heights of heaven the light of your brightness, our Lord Jesus Christ, and illumine the hidden places of our hearts. Show your truth, which may rescue us from the false seductions of the enemy; and may he himself restore to you the people whom you had rejected.

**The Lord’s Prayer.** And lead us not into temptation. But deliver us from evil.

Deliver us from evil, and strengthen us in good works in your fear, O Trinity, our God, who are blessed, live, and rule all things forever and ever. **R.** Amen.

May the Lord be always with you. **R.** And with your spirit.

**Lauda.** God will come manifestly, and he will not be silent. See fol. 8.

**Prayer.** Make us, Lord, live justly, soberly, and devoutly in this age, so that, as we await that blessed hope and the Advent of the glory of your majesty, we may run along the paths of justice in such a way that we may rightly approach the eternal inheritance. [Col. 0062B] **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy, our God, who are blessed, live, and rule all things forever and ever. **R.** Amen.

May the Lord be always with you. **R.** And with your spirit.

In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, let us complete this in peace. **R.** Thanks be to God.

**Commemoration**, as on Sunday, fol. 7.

At Vespers let everything be said as at the end of Vespers on the first Sunday of the Advent of the Lord, fol. 8, except the Sono, which is not to be said or sung on weekdays, except during the season of the Resurrection.

**Hymn**

The heavenly Word proceeding,

Once coming forth from the Father,

Who, born for the world’s salvation,

Come by the declining course of time.

Now illumine our hearts,

And set them aflame with your love,

So that, when the herald has been heard,

The slippery things may at last be driven away.

And when, as Judge, you come later

To examine the deeds of our hearts,

Rendering recompense for hidden things,

And the kingdom to the just for their good deeds,

May we not at last be hemmed in by evils

According to the measure of our guilt;

But, made partakers with the blessed,

May we be unmarried forever.

[Col. 0062D] Grant this, most loving Father,

And you, Only-Begotten, equal to the Father,

With the Spirit, the Paraclete,

For everlasting ages.

Amen.

**Supplication.** Let us pray with every supplication to the Redeemer of the world, our Lord Jesus Christ, that he may graciously deign to justify us by the grace of his Advent. **R.** Grant this, eternal almighty God.

**The Presbyter says.** Kyrie eleison. **R.** Christe eleison. Kyrie eleison.

**Capitula.** Arise, O God, who judge the earth, and rule with the arm of your strength those whom you have deigned mercifully to grant your work, and those whom the crimes of their vices weigh down; raise them up by your compassion, so that we may recognize your justice, which the heavens proclaim, and see your glory with all peoples; so that glory may dwell in our land, and redemption may be ours, which we eagerly believe is to come in faith.

**The Lord’s Prayer.** And lead us not into temptation. But deliver us from evil. Amen.

Deliver us from evil and in your fear, as above.

**Blessing.** Christ the Lord, who came for this purpose, to turn impieties away from the house of Jacob, will come again for this purpose, to free those returning to him from the power of death. **R.** Amen. And he who once came and deigned to reconcile the world, coming for judgment, may he free us from every torment of punishment. **R.** Amen. So that we may rejoice with him in glory, whom here we dwell with in a pure conscience of faith. **R.** Amen.

Through the mercy of that God who is our God, who is blessed, lives, and rules all things forever and ever. **R.** Amen.

**Lauda.** God will come manifestly. See fol. 8.

**Prayer.** Make us, Lord, live justly. See fol. 11.

## 11 WEDNESDAY

### At Matins

**Antiphon.** Wash me, Lord, from my injustice. **P.** And cleanse my heart from my sins. **Psalm L**, with the following prayer.

**Prayer.** O God, Son of God, whose name remains forever. See fol. 3.

**Antiphon 1.** On that day the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the Lord, as waters cover the sea; and the root of Jesse will stand as a sign for the peoples. **P.** The nations will entreat him. **V.** He will judge the poor of the people in his justice, and save the children of the poor, and humble the slanderer. **P.** The nations will entreat him. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, etc. **P.** The nations will entreat him.

**Prayer.** The day of the Advent is near, Lord, and that terrible hour of judgment is already at the doors. Therefore let all flesh be silent before your face, and let it wash away the guilt of its fall with tears; and because we cannot do these things by ourselves, we trust that we can accomplish them through you. Therefore we ask that you, who sanctify the elect by calling them to yourself, may raise sinners, destined to be crowned, to eternal blessedness. **R.** Amen.

[Col. 0063D] Through your mercy, etc.

**Antiphon 2.** Be strong in the Lord and in the power of his might, through every prayer and supplication, for the Advent of Jesus Christ our Lord. **V.** In his days justice will arise and an abundance of peace, until the moon is lifted up. **P.** Through every prayer. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father, etc. **P.** Through every prayer.

**Prayer.** Make us, Lord, live justly, soberly, and devoutly in this age, so that, as we await that blessed hope and the Advent of the glory of your majesty, we may run along the paths of justice in such a way that we may rightly approach the eternal inheritance. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy, our God, etc.

**Antiphon 3.** Be comforted, be comforted, my people, says the Lord your God. Speak to the heart of Jerusalem, for she has received double from the hand of the Lord. **P.** Speak to the cities of Judah. **P.** Behold, your God will come in strength. **V.** He summoned the heavens above, and the earth, to distinguish his people. **P.** Speak to the cities. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father. **P.** Behold, your God.

**Prayer.** Christ, Son of God, who once came to be born in the flesh and will come again with the leaders and princes of your people to execute judgment in the glory of majesty: grant us that, when you come, you may not repay us according to our sins, but, for the faith by which we believe in you, may you raise us up to eternal reward. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy, our God, etc.

**R.** The Lord will come and appear among the sons of his people; he will deliver them from the hand of the wicked. **P.** And he will redeem them from death. **V.** The almighty Lord will raise up for us the righteous one, and he himself will save his people from their sins. **P.** And from death. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father, etc. Repeat **R.** The Lord will come.

### At Lauds

**Antiphon.** Your house will be faithful. **P.** And your kingdom forever, says the Lord.

**Canticle (II Kings VII).**

I took you from the pastures, from following the flocks, * to make you leader over my people Israel;

And I was with you everywhere you walked, * and I destroyed all your enemies from before you;

And I made your name great, like the name of the great ones * who are on the earth.

[Col. 0064C] And I will appoint a place for my people Israel, and plant him, and he will dwell beneath it, * and he will no longer be disturbed;

Nor will the sons of iniquity continue to afflict it as before, * from the day when I appointed judges over my people Israel;

And I will give you rest from all your enemies; * and the Lord foretells to you that the Lord will make you a house.

And when your days are fulfilled, * and you sleep with your fathers,

I will raise up your offspring after you, which will go forth from your womb, * and I will establish his kingdom;

He will build a house for my name, * and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever.

[Col. 0064D] I will be a father to him, * and he will be a son to me;

And your house will be faithful, * and your kingdom forever before your face,

And your throne will be most firmly established continually.

**P.** Your house will be faithful.

Glory and honor to the Father, etc.

**P.** And his kingdom.

**Matutinarium. Antiphon.** Send forth your light and your truth, Lord. **V.** They themselves have led me and brought me to your holy mountain and to your tabernacles. **P.** Send forth your light. **V.** Glory [12] and honor to the Father, etc. **P.** Send forth your light.

**Lauda.** Praise the Lord in his sanctuaries: Alleluia, [Col. 0065A] alleluia. Praise him in the firmament of his power. Alleluia. **Psalm CL.**

**Prophecy.** My son, he who hears me will not be put to shame. See fol. 7. **Hymn.** The heavenly Word proceeding. See fol. 10. **Supplication.** Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world, our Lord Jesus Christ. See fol. 2.

**Capitula.** O Lord of hosts, graciously receive the prayers of your servants, and deign to show us what we ought to pray for; strengthen with the food of eternity those whom the bread of tears disturbs; and let rivers of tears flow from our eyes with such miserable weeping that, our sins being struck down, we may be embraced by the abundance of your mercies; and may we who dread the Advent of our Redeemer behold, when he comes, his glorious presence in profound peace.

**The Lord’s Prayer.**

Deliver us from evil. See fol. 10.

**Lauda.** God will come manifestly. See fol. 8.

**Prayer.** Savior Lord, who, ascending Mount Zion, were manifested as Redeemer of the world through the flesh you assumed: free your people Israel from every defilement of wickedness, so that the mercy of him whose name has become known gloriously in the world may not allow the souls of the redeemed to perish. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy, our God, who are blessed, live, and rule all things.

**Commemoration.** Fol. 7.

### At Vespers

[Col. 0065C] **Lauda.** From the rising of the sun to its setting, the name of the Lord is worthy of praise. **V.** May the name of the Lord be blessed, from now and for ever. **P.** Worthy of praise.

**The Presbyter says.** May the Lord be always with you. **R.** And with your spirit.

**Antiphon.** The Lord will come with the elders and princes.

**Lauda.** Your right hand, O God. See fol. 8.

**Hymn**

Behold, a clear voice sounds forth:

It rebukes every dark thing;

Let dreams be driven far away;

Christ shines forth from heaven.

Let the slumbering mind now rise,

Which lies wounded by defilement:

[Col. 0065D] A new star now shines,

To take away every harm.

Behold, the Lamb is sent down from above

To cancel by grace the debt:

Let us all, for pardon,

So that, when he shines forth a second time,

And horror encircles the world,

He may not punish us for guilt,

But may then protect us in mercy.

Grant this, most loving Father,

And you, Only-Begotten, equal to the Father,

With the Spirit, the Paraclete,

For everlasting ages. Amen.

[Col. 0066A] **Supplication.** Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world, our Lord Jesus Christ. See fol. 2.

**Capitula.** O God, upon whose face every faithful person fixes his gaze, and whom he desires to come with the whole longing of his heart: grant us that, when the vision of your humanity appears, the vision of your divinity may rescue us all from torments; so that, beholding the presence of your majesty glorified in the body, we may escape the Tartarean fires of punishment.

**The Lord’s Prayer.**

Deliver us from evil. See fol. 10.

**Blessing.** Our Redeemer and Lord, who, by being born in the flesh, took from us the yoke of the law, may complete in us the benefits of his mercy. **R.** Amen. And he who took from us that which befitted his divinity, may bestow from his own that which may richly endow us as we await him. **R.** Amen. So that all who here receive the first joys of his Advent with glad devotion may exult with all the saints at the time of his second Advent. **R.** Amen. Through the mercy of that God who is our God, who is blessed and rules all things for ever and ever. **R.** Amen.

**The Presbyter says.** May the Lord be always with you. **R.** And with your spirit.

**Lauda.** God will come manifestly and will not be silent, alleluia. See fol. 8.

Through your mercy, our God, who are.

**13 The Presbyter says.** May the Lord be always with you. **R.** And with you.

In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, let us complete this in peace. **R.** Thanks be to God.

## FRIDAY

### At Matins

**Antiphon.** My soul trusts in you, and I shall hope in the shadow of your wings until iniquity passes away. **Psalm LVI.**

**Prayer.** O God, Son of God, whose name remains forever. See fol. 3.

Through your mercy, our God, who are blessed, live, and rule all things. May the Lord be always with you. **R.** And with your spirit.

**Prayer.** We ascend the mountain proclaiming the joys of your Advent, while, founded in your height, O Christ, Son of God, we believe and confess those things which are true concerning you. Let us pray, therefore, that you who are to come to execute judgment may cleanse us from our sins. Amen.

Through mercy, etc.

**Antiphon 3.** Behold, I will send you Elijah the Prophet. [Col. 0067B] **P.** Before the great day of the Lord comes. **V.** Hear this, all nations; give ear, you who inhabit the world. **P.** Before it comes. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father. **P.** Before it comes.

[Col. 0067C] **At the Canticle. Antiphon.** The Lord our God will save us on that day, as the flock of his people.

**Canticle (Zechariah IX).**

Rejoice exceedingly, daughter Zion, * shout for joy, Jerusalem:

Behold, your king will come to you, * righteous and a savior:

Poor himself, riding upon a she-ass, * and upon a colt, the foal of a she-ass.

And I will destroy the chariot of Ephraim * and the horse from Jerusalem,

And the bow of war will be scattered: * and he will speak peace to the nations,

And his power will be from sea to sea, * and from the rivers to the ends of the earth.

You also, in the blood of your covenant, have sent forth [Col. 0067D] your prisoners from the pit * in which there is no water.

Return to the stronghold, prisoners of hope; * today too I announce that I will restore double to you.

For I have bent Judah for myself as a bow and filled Ephraim; * and I will raise up your sons, Zion, against your sons, Greece:

And I will make you like the sword of the mighty. * And the Lord God will be seen over them;

And his dart will go forth like lightning: * and the Lord God will sound the trumpet and go in the whirlwind of the south.

The Lord of hosts will protect them; and they will devour you and subdue you with sling-stones: * and, drinking, they will be drunken as with wine and filled like bowls, and like the horn of the altar.

And the Lord their God will save them on that day, [Col. 0068A] * as the flock of his people. **P.** The Lord will save us.

Glory and honor to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.

As it was, etc.

**P.** The Lord will save us.

**Matutinarium. Antiphon.** You give light wondrously from the eternal mountains; all of us foolish in heart have been troubled. **V.** God is known in Judah; his name is great in Israel. **P.** You give light wondrously. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father. **P.** You give light.

And may we who fear the Advent of our Redeemer, when he himself comes, behold his glorious countenance in deepest peace.

Deliver us from evil. See fol. 10.

## ON THE SECOND SUNDAY OF THE ADVENT OF THE LORD

### At Vespers

**Lauda.** From the rising of the sun onward. **Prayer.** O God, whose name... See fol. 1.

**Sono.** Alleluia. The fields will rejoice, and everything in them. Then all the trees of the forests will exult before the face of the Lord. **P.** For he has come: alleluia. **V.** Sing to the Lord a new song; sing to the Lord, all the earth. Sing psalms to God and bless his name; proclaim his glory among the nations. **P.** For he has come: alleluia.

**The Presbyter says.** May the Lord be always with you. **R.** And with you.

**Antiphon.** Behold, the glory of the Lord will be revealed to the nations. [Col. 0068D] **P.** And all flesh will see what the mouth of the Lord has spoken. **V.** God will come manifestly, and he is our God, and he will not be silent. **P.** And all flesh will see. **P.** Glory and honor to the Father. **V.** And all flesh will see.

**Lauda.** For the Lord will give blessing: alleluia. **P.** And our earth will give its fruit: alleluia, alleluia. **V.** Yet his salvation is near those who fear him, so that glory may dwell in our land. **P.** And our earth. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father. **P.** And our earth.

**Hymn.** The company of Christ. **Supplication.** Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world. See above, fols. 1 and 2. **Capitula.** O God, whom all the earth... See fol. 12. **The Lord’s Prayer.** Delivered from evil. Fol. 2.

**Blessing.** O God, Son of God the Father, who were foretold long ago by the prophecy of the Prophets as destined to be born in the flesh, strengthen within us the virtues that are coming to birth. **R.** Amen. May he not allow those whom he adopted as sons for himself through the mystery of his incarnation to become alienated from him. **R.** Amen. May we increase and multiply the joy that we once receive from faith in him through the exhibition of good works. **R.** Amen. Through mercy.

**Lauda.** The Most High is terrible over all the earth: alleluia. **P.** He subjected peoples to us and nations beneath our feet. **P.** He chose us as an inheritance for himself, which he loved: alleluia, alleluia. **V.** All nations, clap your hands; shout to God with a voice of exultation. **P.** He subjected peoples. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father. **P.** He chose us.

**Prayer.** O God, who will come manifestly. See in the following Matins.

### At Matins

**Hymn.** Eternal creator of all things. Fol. 3.

**Prayer.** The voice of all the faithful sings you as the eternal Lord and creator of all things, who both establish the fixed limits of the times and, by eternal law, appoint the boundaries by which night is separated from day. For the abyss of your wisdom, to relieve the weariness of mortals, assigned one thing to labor and reserved another for rest. Grant, therefore, almighty God, that while the weary mind is roused by the crowing of the cock, it may run eagerly back to the hope of light and always devote the first fruits of the day’s labor to your service. **R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

[Col. 0069C] **Antiphon.** Many say to my soul: There is no salvation for him in his God. **Psalm III.**

**Antiphon.** You will wash me from iniquity. **Psalm L.**

**Antiphon.** Be exalted above the heavens, O God, and your glory above all the earth. **Psalm LVI.**

**Prayer.** Most merciful Lord, who are the perpetual salvation of souls and the strong power of the weak: deliver us from bloodthirsty men, and defend us from the darts of enemies with your shield. Send us invincible help from heaven, and turn those who trample us into an object of disgrace, so that we may rise free for the office of Matins and faithfully offer our vows to your holy name. **R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**Antiphon 1.** God will come manifestly, and he is our God, [Col. 0069D] and he will not be silent. **P.** And around him is a powerful storm. **V.** He summoned the heavens above, and the earth, to distinguish his people. **P.** And around him. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father, etc. **P.** And around him.

**Prayer.** O God, who are believed to be coming manifestly for judgment, show your manifest power of salvation in us, so that you who are endured as terrible may, when you come, be experienced as most gentle. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy, our God, etc.

**Antiphon 2.** Come to deliver us; Lord God of hosts, convert us. **P.** And show your face, and we shall be saved. **V.** O Shepherd of Israel, give heed; you who lead Joseph like a sheep. **P.** And show. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father. **P.** And show your face.

**Prayer.** Come to deliver us, Lord God of hosts; convert us, and show your face, and we shall be saved. By your provision, purified through the gift of worthy repentance, may we deserve to be present at your judgment. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy, etc.

**Antiphon 3.** Come, Lord, and do not delay; release the sins of your people. **P.** And bring back the scattered to their own land. **V.** God of hosts, convert us; show your face, and we shall be saved. **P.** And bring back. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father. **P.** And bring back the scattered.

**Prayer.** Come, Lord, do not delay; now release the sins of your people, so that, while you are awaited, you may turn our dispersion toward eternal joys according to our desire, and come to meet us in judgment for the completion of every kind of help. **R.** Amen.

[Col. 0070B] Through your mercy, etc.

**R.** Thus says the Lord: I will raise up for you a Shepherd from the cities of Judah, and he will reign with you as with your fathers. **P.** And he will have mercy on his land, and you will no longer be in sorrow. **V.** Behold, the Lord will bring vengeance and recompense; God himself will come and save us. **P.** And he will have mercy. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father. Repeat **R.** Thus says the Lord.

**Prayer.** Lord God almighty, who for the redemption of the human race willed to send to us, through the womb of the Virgin Mary, your coeternal and coequal Son, announced by the angel: grant us, at this time of the Advent of your Only-Begotten, the same grace of peace that in past ages you deigned to bestow. And join us to the number of those who meet him in faith, whom we know to have been washed at the beginnings of faith by John in the waters of repentance, and finally baptized by you through the Son in the Holy Spirit and fire. **R.** Amen.

### At Lauds

**At the Canticle. Antiphon.** Let my speech be awaited like rain, and let my words descend like dew, because I have invoked the name of the Lord: give greatness to your God.

**Canticle.** Give ear, O heaven, and I will speak. See fol. 4.

**At the Benedictus, Antiphon.** Bless the Lord, little and great, all of you who await his Advent.

[Col. 0070D] **Canticle.** Blessed are you, Lord, God of our fathers. Fol. 6.

**Sono.** Alleluia. The fields will rejoice. See fol. 14.

**Lauda.** Praise the Lord from the heavens: alleluia. Praise him in the heights: alleluia, alleluia. **Psalm CXLVIII.**

**Reading from the book of Isaiah the Prophet (Chapter XXII).**

**R.** Thanks be to God.

Thus says the Lord: Go, enter in to him who dwells in the tabernacle, to Shebna, the steward of the temple, and say to him: What are you doing here, or who are you here as? For you have cut out a tomb for yourself here; you have carefully cut out a memorial for yourself on high, a tabernacle for yourself in the rock. Behold, the Lord will carry you away, as a rooster is carried away, and he will lift you up like a garment. He will crown you with tribulation; like a ball he will throw you into a broad and spacious land. There you will die, and there will be the chariot of your glory, the disgrace of the house of your Lord God. And I will drive you from your post, and remove you from your office.

And it will be on that day: I will call my servant Eliakim, son of Hilkiah, and I will clothe him in your tunic, and strengthen him with your belt, and place your authority in his hand. He will be like a father to those who dwell in Jerusalem and to the house of Judah. And I will place the key of the house of David upon his shoulder, and he will open, and there will be no one to close; and he will close, and there will be no one to open. And I will fasten him like a peg in a secure place, and he will be on the throne of glory of his father’s house. And I will hang upon him all the glory of his father’s house. **R.** Amen.

[Col. 0071B] **Hymn.** Almighty King of all. See fol. 7. **Supplication.** Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world. See fol. 2.

**Capitula.** Christ, who, destined to be born in the flesh, became the fulfillment of the law: grant us perfection of holiness; and you who once deigned to redeem the world by your Advent, at the time of your judgment preserve the souls of the redeemed from punishment.

**Our Father, who are in heaven.**

Delivered from evil, etc. See fol. 2.

### At the End of Vespers
