[Col. 0071C] **Antiphon.** The Lord will be a crown of glory on that day. **P.** And an ornament of joy for the remnant of his people Israel. **V.** And he will rule from sea to sea, and his branches will extend to the river. **P.** And an ornament of joy. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father. **P.** And an ornament of joy.

**Lauda.** Let all who seek you, Lord, exult and rejoice in you, alleluia. **P.** And let them say: May he always be magnified, alleluia, alleluia. **V.** Lord, they will walk in the light of your face, and in your name they will be exalted. **P.** And let them say. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son. **P.** And let them always say.

### Hymn

Let the host of Christ proclaim aloud.

### Supplication

Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world, our Lord, as above, on the First Sunday of the Lord’s Advent, fols. 1–2.

### Capitulum

Rise up, O God, who judge the earth. See fol. 10.

### Our Father

Delivered from evil, etc. See fol. 2.

### Benediction

May Christ the Lord, who came for this purpose, etc. See fol. 10.

**R.** Amen.

Through his mercy, etc.

### Lauda

In your salvation, alleluia, let us exult exceedingly; we ask for life: grant it, Lord, alleluia, alleluia.

**P.** For length of days, forever and unto ages of ages, alleluia, alleluia.

**V.** Great is his glory in your salvation; you will place glory and great splendor upon him.

**P.** For length of days.

**V.** Glory and honor to the Father.

**P.** For length of days.

### Prayer

Your Advent day, Lord, is near, and already at the doors is that dreadful hour of judgment. Therefore let all flesh be silent before you, and let it wash away the guilt of its fall with tears. And because we are unable to do these things by ourselves, we trust in you to accomplish them. Therefore we ask that you, who sanctify the elect by calling them to yourself, may raise sinners, destined to be crowned, to eternal blessedness.

**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy, etc.

## On the Second Monday of the Second Week

### At Matins

**Antiphon.** Lord, how many are those who afflict me? But you, Lord, are my protector.

**Psalm III**, with its prayer: “They have multiplied,” Lord, fol. 8.

### Antiphon 1

The mountains and hills shall sing before God, and all the trees of the forests shall clap their hands.

**P.** For the Lord, the ruler, shall come as an eternal sign that shall never be taken away.

**V.** The fields shall rejoice, and all the cedars of Lebanon that he planted; there the sparrows shall build their nests.

**P.** For the Lord shall come.

**V.** Glory and honor.

**P.** For he shall come.

### Prayer

O Lord, Ruler, who, coming as the eternal sign of the world’s deliverance, caused the mountains and hills to cry out your praise before you, when you approved all things living in you: grant that you may always make acceptable to yourself the praises that we offer to your glorious and holy name; so that you, who appeared as the sign of salvation when you were about to redeem the world, may, when you come again to judge the world, manifest yourself to our eyes not as avenger but as liberator.

**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

### Antiphon 2

Yet a little while, and indignation shall be brought to an end.

**P.** And on that day the burden shall be taken from our shoulder, and the yoke from our neck.

**V.** Let the poor see and rejoice; seek the Lord, and your soul shall live.

**P.** And on that day.

**V.** Glory and honor.

**P.** And on that day.

### Prayer

Jesus, our Savior and Lord, who lifted the yoke of the law from our neck by the preaching of grace, and took upon your shoulders the burden of our shoulder: grant through the prayers of your Church that she, who, when indignation was brought to an end, shone forth through the commandment of your faith, may by consummate righteousness deserve to be raised up by you when you come to judgment; so that she may live happily here, and afterward, with a happier expectation, behold with joy the face of your divinity.

**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy, O God, etc.

### Antiphon 3

I shall go before you, says the Lord.

**P.** And I shall humble the glorious ones of the earth.

**V.** The God of gods, the Lord, has spoken and summoned the earth.

**P.** And I shall humble the glorious ones.

**V.** Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son.

**P.** And I shall humble the glorious ones of the earth.

### Prayer

Be for us, Lord, a crown of glory on the day when you come to judge the ages by fire, so that here you may mercifully clothe us in the garment of righteousness, and afterward in the freedom of perfected glory.

**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy, etc.

**R.** Behold, your ruler, O Zion, shall come with gladness.

**P.** And all the saints shall rejoice over you with everlasting happiness and joy.

**V.** Come, Lord; do not delay. Release the crimes of your people.

**P.** And all the saints.

**V.** Glory and honor to the Father.

The response is repeated: **Behold, your ruler, O Zion.**

Lord God, creator of all,  
*terrible and mighty, just and merciful,*

the only good king, who alone is excellent,

who delivers Israel from every evil,  
*who chose the fathers and sanctified them:*

*and deliver those who serve nations that despise and abhor them.*

the most excellent Desired One,

God, Son of God, whose being remains forever. See fol. 3.

## At Lauds

### At the Canticle

**Antiphon.** The Lord God shall cause righteousness and praise to spring up before all the nations.

### Canticle (Isaiah LXI)

Rejoicing, I shall rejoice in the Lord;  
*my spirit shall exult in God my Savior;*

for he has clothed me with the garment of salvation  
*and surrounded me with the robe of gladness,*

as a bridegroom adorned with a crown,  
*and as a bride adorned with her jewels.*

For just as the earth brings forth its shoot,  
*and as a garden makes its seed sprout,*

so the Lord God shall cause  
*righteousness and praise to spring up before all the nations.*

For Zion’s sake I shall not be silent,  
*and for Jerusalem’s sake I shall not rest,*

until her righteous one goes forth like brightness  
and her Savior is kindled like a torch.

And the nations shall see your righteous one,  
*and all kings your illustrious one;*

and you shall be called by a new name,  
*which the mouth of the Lord shall name.*

And you shall be a crown of glory in the hand of the Lord,  
*and a royal diadem in the hand of your God.*

You shall no longer be called Forsaken,  
and your land shall no longer be called Desolate;

but you shall be called “My Will Is in Her,”  
*and your land shall be inhabited.*

For a young man shall dwell with a virgin,  
*and your sons shall dwell in you.*

For as a bridegroom rejoices over his bride,  
*so your God shall rejoice over you.*

Upon your walls, Jerusalem, I have appointed guards;  
*all day and all night forever they shall not be silent.*

You who remember the Lord, do not be silent,  
*and do not give him silence until he establishes and until he makes Jerusalem a praise in the earth.*

**P.** The Lord God shall cause righteousness to spring up.

**Glory and honor to the Father, etc.**

**P.** The Lord God shall cause righteousness to spring up.

## Friday in the Advent of the Lord

### At Matins

**Antiphon.** In you my soul trusts, and in the shadow of your wings I shall hope until iniquity passes away.

**Psalm LVI:** Have mercy on me, O God; have mercy on me, for my trust is in you, etc.

### Prayer

God, Son of God, whose name remains forever. See fol. 3.

### Antiphon 1

Behold, the Lord shall sound the trumpet in Zion.

**P.** And he shall come in the whirlwind of the south; the Lord almighty himself shall protect us.

**V.** The Lord is faithful in his words and holy in all his works.

**P.** And he shall come in the whirlwind of the south.

**V.** Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son, etc.

**P.** The Lord himself.

### Prayer

O God, who, holding the trumpet in Zion, came to save sinners in the whirlwind of the south, arousing some to belief through the terror of signs and others through the grace of preaching: protect us from every adversity and temptation, so that the trumpet of your word may always be the salvation of our soul and body.

**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy, our God, etc.

The priest says: The Lord be always with you.

**R.** And with your spirit.

### Antiphon 2

The Lord has gathered the dispersion of his people in mercy.

**P.** And his glory shall be seen in the cloud, as in the days of Moses.

**P.** And he shall be manifested as in the time of King Solomon.

**V.** And he shall rule from sea to sea, and from the river to its branches.

**P.** And his glory shall be seen.

**V.** Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son, etc.

**P.** And he shall be manifested as in the time of King Solomon.

### Prayer

Gather, Lord, in mercy the dispersion of your people, whom long ago, when you were about to redeem the world, you delivered by the power of your arm; and therefore you are invoked with great earnestness by those whom you redeemed. You who deigned to become weak for us as a human being, deign to fortify human beings with the protection of your divinity.

**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy, our God, etc.

### Antiphon 3

The desert and the wasteland shall rejoice, and the solitude shall exult.

**P.** And it shall blossom like a lily; budding, it shall bud.

**V.** The fields shall rejoice, and the cedars of Lebanon that he planted; there the sparrows shall build their nests.

**P.** And it shall blossom like a lily.

**V.** Glory and honor to the Father, etc.

**P.** And it shall blossom like a lily.

### Prayer

The whole Catholic Church proclaims with praise and joy that you, Lord, have come to Zion; therefore we ask that we who now announce your glorious Advent among the peoples may, with you making atonement, be cleansed from our crimes.

**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

The priest says: The Lord be always with you.

**R.** And with your spirit.

**R.** The Lord is awaited, that he may have mercy on us.

**P.** For the Lord is a God of judgment; blessed are all who await him.

**V.** He shall not judge according to the appearance of the eyes, nor reprove according to the hearing of the ears; but he shall judge the poor in righteousness.

**P.** For the Lord is a God of judgment.

**V.** Glory and honor to the Father.

The response is repeated: **The Lord is awaited.**

From the rising of the sun to its setting, with its prayer: “O God, whose name is blessed,” fol. 1.

**V.** Glory and honor to the Father, etc.

Delivered from evil, strengthened, etc. Fol. 2.

**R.** Amen.

**R.** Amen.

### At Matins

### Hymn

Eternal maker of all things. See fol. 3.

### Prayer

After the chorus of the crowing of the roosters and the night’s rest has been driven away, the late night brings forth day for you, Lord; and with wings beating and with the proclamation of their voices, the roosters jubilantly sing the morning hymn. For you, Lord, the birds of heaven utter praises; at your command, when the darkness is dispersed, the sun brings light to the world. These are your miracles, almighty Father. We bring only our vows, offering these morning sacrifices to your holy name, so that, absolved from past sins, we may deserve to be absolved from present tribulation.

**R.** Amen.

Through the mercy of our God, who are blessed and live, etc.

The priest says: The Lord be always with you.

**R.** And with your spirit.

### Antiphon 1

Salvation belongs to the Lord, and your blessing is upon your people.

**Psalm III.**

### Antiphon 2

You have manifested to me the hidden and secret things of your wisdom.

**Psalm L.**

### Antiphon 3

In the shadow of your wings we hope, O God, until iniquity passes away.

**Psalm LVI.**

### Prayer

You, eternal author and creator. See fol. 3.

### Antiphon

Behold, the name of the Lord comes from afar, and his tongue is like a burning fire.

**P.** And his spirit is like an overflowing torrent.

**V.** He summoned the heavens above and the earth to distinguish his people.

**P.** And his spirit is like an overflowing torrent.

**V.** Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son, etc.

**P.** And his spirit is like an overflowing torrent.

### Prayer

The creatures created by you rejoice that your name has come from afar; therefore make us such that we who have received the Advent of your incarnation may be cleansed from the thorns of sins by the spirit of your fiery tongue.

**R.** Amen.

### Antiphon

From Zion the law shall go forth, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.

**P.** He shall judge the nations and reprove many peoples unto the end.

**V.** The Lord is exalted above all nations, and his glory is above the heavens.

**P.** He shall judge the nations.

**V.** Glory and honor to the Father, etc.

**P.** He shall judge.

### Prayer

May your law, O God the Father, the word going forth from Zion, not judge but protect the peoples who confess you; and may it not reprove for sin those whom the mystery of your incarnation has come to free, so that you, who are recognized as glorious among the elect, may always be found merciful and compassionate among sinners.

**R.** Amen.

### Antiphon

Seek the Lord, all you meek of the earth; seek the just one, seek the meek one, and you shall find him.

**V.** Seek the Lord and be strengthened; seek his face always.

**P.** Seek the just one.

**V.** Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son.

**P.** And you shall find him.

### Prayer

Hear mercifully those who seek you, Lord, and defend us from the constricting troubles that bend us down, as we pray; so that they may magnify you through your Church among all nations and exalt your name in the bond of unity; may they learn from you also, so that they may be illumined and attentive; and may they never blush in the face of conscience through their steadfastness in your commandments.

**R.** Amen.

**R.** The Lord shall raise up from Israel a most powerful king, seated upon a throne of honor forever.

**P.** He shall be filled with knowledge like the Pishon, and with understanding like the Euphrates; he himself shall multiply the Jordan in the time of harvest.

**V.** Behold, the day is coming, says the Lord, and I shall raise up for David a righteous branch; and the king shall reign and shall be wise.

**P.** He shall be filled with knowledge like the Pishon.

**V.** Glory and honor to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.

The response is repeated: **The Lord shall raise up from Israel a most powerful king seated upon a throne, etc.**

### Prayer

Almighty God the Father, who have raised up your Son for us as king, at whose manifestation to the world your Church is cleansed in knowledge like the Pishon and made fruitful in understanding of spiritual gifts like the Euphrates: grant us to possess in you the light of knowledge and the fullness of every virtue, so that while we seek the gifts of knowledge, we may return to you, who are the fountain of knowledge.

**R.** Amen.

## At Lauds

### Antiphon

God shall come from Lebanon, and the Holy One from Mount Opauco; his power has covered the heavens, and the earth is full of his praise.

### Canticle (Habakkuk III)

Lord, I have heard your report, and I was afraid.  
*Lord, I considered your works, and I trembled.*

You shall be known in the midst of two living creatures;  
when the years draw near, you shall be made known;  
*when the time comes, you shall be revealed.*

When my soul is troubled in anger,  
*you shall remember your mercy toward me.*

God shall come from Lebanon,  
*and the Holy One from Mount Opauco and the dense forest.*

His power covered the heavens,  
and the earth was full of his praise.  
*His brightness shall be like light.*

Horns are in his hands;  
*there his power of glory has been confirmed, and he established enduring splendor.*

Before his face the word shall go,  
and he went forth into the fields.  
*His feet stood firm, and the earth was shaken.*

He looked, and the nations melted away;  
*the mountains were violently dissolved.*

The everlasting hills flowed down;  
*his age-old paths were made difficult by labors.*

The tents of the Ethiopians saw you,  
*and the tents of the land of Midian trembled.*

Was your anger against the rivers, Lord,  
*or your fury against the sea?*

He who mounted your horses,  
*and your riding was salvation.*

You bent and drew your bow over the scepters, says the Lord;  
*the earth shall be split by rivers.*

The nations shall see and the peoples shall grieve,  
*sprinkling waters of contradiction.*

The abyss gave forth its voice  
*from the height of its imagination. The sun and moon stood in their order.*

In the light of your splendor your arrows shall go forth;  
*in the light of your lightning your armor.*

In your indignation you shall destroy the earth,  
*and in your anger you shall drive the nations.*

You went forth for the salvation of your people,  
*to save your anointed ones.*

You cast death upon the heads of the wicked;  
*you raised up the bonds unto battle.*

You cut off the heads of the mighty in terror;  
*the nations shall be shaken in it and shall open their mouths, the poor man eating in secret.*

You sent your horses into the sea,  
*troubling the many waters.*

He preserved me, and my belly trembled  
*at the sound of the prayer of my lips.*

Fear entered into my bones,  
*and above me my strength was troubled.*

I shall rest on the day of tribulation;  
*I shall ascend to the tents of my migration.*

For the fig tree shall not bear fruit,  
*and there shall be no growth on the vines.*

The work of the olive shall fail,  
*and the fields shall provide no food.*

The sheep shall fail from the fold,  
*and there shall be no cattle at the stalls.*

But I shall glory in the Lord;  
*I shall rejoice in God my Savior.*

The Lord is my strength;  
*he shall establish my feet in completion.*

He shall set me upon the heights;  
*I shall conquer in his splendor.*

**P.** And the earth is full of his praise.

**Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son, etc.**

**P.** And the earth is full of his praise.

### Prophecy

Reading from the Book of the Prophet Ezekiel, chapter XXXIV.

**R.** Thanks be to God.

Thus says the Lord: I shall save my flock, and it shall no longer be for plunder; and I shall judge between sheep and sheep. I shall make a covenant of peace with them, and I shall cause the worst beasts to cease from the land; and those who dwell in the desert shall sleep safely in the forests. I shall place my blessing around my hill, and I shall bring rain in its season; they shall be rains of blessing. The tree of the field shall give its fruit, and the earth shall give its growth, and they shall be in their own land without fear. And they shall know that I am the Lord, when I have broken the chains of their yoke and rescued them from the hand of those who ruled over them. They shall no longer be plunder for the nations, nor shall the beasts of the earth devour them; but they shall dwell securely without any terror. I shall raise up for them a renowned branch, and they shall no longer be diminished by famine in the land, nor shall they bear any longer the reproach of the nations. And they shall know that I am their Lord. I shall be with them, and they shall be my people, the house of Israel, says the Lord. But you, my flocks, are all the flocks of my pasture, and I am the Lord your God.

**R.** Amen.

Those who afflict us have multiplied, Lord; but you are abundant in mercy and deliver us. For we fear no imminent pressure at all, provided that we are fortified by your grace, almighty God.

### Prayer

God the Father, who, directing the way of your only-begotten Son, willed him to share our mortality: make us sharers in his kingdom, so that you who spoke and called him to be present as Redeemer, sparing human beings, may be shown to us rejoicing with him.

**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy, our God, etc.

The priest says: The Lord be always with you.

I shall give salvation in Zion and my glory in Jerusalem.

**V.** The God of gods, the Lord, has spoken and summoned the earth.

**P.** I shall give salvation in Zion.

**V.** Glory and honor to the Father.

**P.** And my glory in Jerusalem.

### Prayer

Behold, Lord our God: how beautiful are the feet of those who evangelize peace and announce good things. Therefore make us such that, with our feet shod in readiness for the gospel of peace, they may rejoice in the course they have completed and in perfected virtue; so that our mouth, which announces your Christ with full faith, may not despise him in the accomplishment of our life and works. Rather, celebrating the annual feasts of his incarnation with devotion, may we offer our vows to him, happy without end.

**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy, our God, etc.

**Prayer.** God the Father, when you were about to send your Son to the earth, you dispatched your messengers—namely, the voices of preachers—to the nations and to the islands, so that, proclaiming his incarnation, they might extend the faith of your word by preaching to those far away who had not heard. Grant us both to repent of our vices as we hear you and, believing in you, to earn the heavenly inheritance, so that, while proclaiming your Christ in words, we may not by our deeds become liable to condemnation before the majesty of your glory. **R.** Amen.

[Col. 0087D]

Delivered from evil and always strengthened in goodness, may we be worthy to serve you, God and our Lord. Put an end, Lord, to our sins; give joy to the afflicted; grant redemption to captives; health to the sick; and rest to the dead. Grant peace and security throughout all our days; break the boldness of our enemies; hear, God, the prayer of all your servants, all the faithful Christians, on this day and at all times; through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, forever and ever. **R.** Amen.

**Blessing.** May the only Son of God, who was begotten from the Father’s womb and came to be incarnate from the Virgin’s womb, wash us from every corruption of the human condition. **R.** Amen.

And may that same one, who came incomprehensible into the truth of a human body, take away from us the uncleanness of human corruption. **R.** Amen.

And may he who came as life to terrify death grant us to feel nothing of death’s condemnation. **R.** Amen.

Through his mercy, etc.

**Prayer.** Lord God, almighty Father, inspirer of prayers and swift hearer of those who call upon you, we pray you to incline the ear of your mercy to our voice and, by your powerful compassion, dissolve the bonds of our sins. And just as you summon us to rise through the crowing of roosters for the grace of morning, and by prophetic prediction announce beforehand the single redemption in the light of the nations, so now, as we journey, assist us with heavenly regard. Thus, we ask, receive the vows of our service, so that, raising us up to the light through abundant mercy, you may lead us there. **R.** Amen.

### Reading from the Book of the Prophet Isaiah (Chapter 42)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

Sing to the Lord a new song, his praise at the ends of the earth, you who have gone down to the sea and its fullness; the islands and their inhabitants. Let the desert and its cities be lifted up; in the houses [Col. 0090B] Cedar will dwell. Praise, inhabitants of Petra; from the summit of the mountains they will cry out. They will give glory to the Lord and proclaim his praise in the islands. The Lord will go forth like a strong man; like a warrior he has stirred up zeal. He will shout and cry out; he will prevail against his enemies.

“I have been silent always; I have kept still; I have been patient. Like a woman in labor, I will speak. I will scatter and swallow at once. I will make mountains and hills desolate, and I will dry up all their grass. I will place rivers in the islands and turn them into pools. I will lead the blind along a way they do not know, and I will make them walk along paths they have not known.”

**R.** Amen.

**Hymn.** “Almighty King of all things.”

**Supplication.** “Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world.” See fol. 2.

**Capitula.** Stir up your power and come to free [Col. 0090C] us, Lord God, so that, because we are oppressed by the storms of temptations, we may be raised up by the help of your strength. May the legions of enemies not prevail against us when we are protected by your majesty; so that you may always bring us assistance and inflict vengeance upon our adversaries.

**Our Father.** And do not lead us … Delivered from evil. Fol. 2.

**Lauda.** “The Lord is around his people.” See fol. 26.

**Blessing.** “The only Son of God.” Fol. 26.

At the conclusion of Vespers:

**Lauda.** “From the rising of the sun.”

**Sono.** “The God of gods.” Fol. 26.

**Antiphon.** The Savior, the Lord, has ascended Mount Zion to free his people Israel.

**P.** And his kingdom will be everlasting.

**V.** All nations, clap your hands; shout to God with a voice of exultation.

**P.** And his kingdom.

**V.** Glory and honor.

**P.** And his kingdom.

**Lauda.** Our eyes are toward the Lord our God, [Col. 0090D] alleluia.

**P.** Until he has mercy on us, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.

**V.** To you we lift our eyes, who dwell in the heavens.

**P.** Until he has mercy.

**V.** Glory and honor.

**P.** Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.

**Hymn.** “Let the company of Christ cry out.”

**Supplication.** “Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world.” Fol. 2.

**Capitula.** God, whose eternity …

**Blessing.** “Christ the Lord.” See fol. 2.

**Lauda.** With you is forgiveness, alleluia, and because of your law I have awaited you, Lord, alleluia.

**P.** For with you is mercy and abundant redemption: alleluia, alleluia.

**V.** May your ears be attentive to the voice of my supplication.

**P.** With you is.

**V.** Glory and honor.

**P.** With you is.

[Col. 0091A]

**Prayer.** Only-Begotten Son of God the Father, whom the islands await, and whose arm of strength the acquired people sustain: we ask and beseech you to make us sinners always blessed, so that, when the glory of your Advent appears, we may not be put to shame when we see your face. Let the choir respond: Amen.

Through your mercy.

# MONDAY OF THE FOURTH WEEK

## At Matins

**Antiphon.** Lord, how they have multiplied.

**Psalm 3.**

**Prayer.** Fol. 8, as on Monday of the first week.

**Antiphon 1.** Behold, the Lord will come from afar.

**P.** Blessed are all who await him.

**V.** All nations, clap your hands; shout to God with a voice of exultation.

**P.** Blessed are all.

**V.** Glory and honor.

**P.** Blessed are all.

[Col. 0091B]

**Prayer.** By awaiting the Advent of your incarnation from afar, Christ, Son of God, the multitude of the blessed is known to have been made blessed. We ask that, through expectation of your second Advent, we may be so blessed that we experience you as merciful in judgment. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon 2.** Put to death now your members that are upon the earth, for, when Christ appears, your life …

**P.** Then you also will appear with him in glory.

**V.** May the name of the Lord be blessed from this time forth and forever.

**P.** Then you also.

**V.** Glory and honor.

**P.** Then you also.

**Prayer.** Put to death, we ask, our members upon the earth from every desire, so that, when you who are our life appear, we too may appear with you, transformed [Col. 0091C] into everlasting glory. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon 3.** I will go before you, says the Lord.

**P.** And I will humble the glorious of the earth.

**V.** The God of gods, the Lord, has spoken and has called the earth.

**P.** And the glorious.

**V.** Glory and honor.

**P.** And the glorious.

**Prayer.** Unbegotten supreme Father, through whom, at the time of the Lord’s birth, the work of righteousness, peace, or security is brought to completion throughout the whole earth: make us perpetually behold, at the second Advent of his glory, the beauty of his indivisible majesty, so that, crowned there forever, we may offer the jubilation of perpetual life, blessed without end. Let the response be made: Amen.

Through his mercy.

[Col. 0091D]

**R.** Believe in your Savior who is coming with glory.

**P.** And be ready to receive the kingdom of God.

**V.** Hear this, inhabitants of the city, you who dwell on the earth: when the sign has been raised upon the mountains and you hear the sound of the trumpet,

**P.** And you be ready.

**V.** Glory and honor.

Repeat **R.** “Believe in your Savior.”

## At Lauds

### At the Canticle

**Antiphon.** Behold, God indeed …

**Canticle.** Lord God, creator of all.

Matutinary, Antiphon, and Lauda: see fol. 16. Prophecy: “Sing to the Lord.” Fol. 28. Hymn: “Behold, the Savior of all.” Supplication: “Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world.” Capitula: “Remember, Lord.” Fol. 17. Lauda: “God will come openly.” See fol. 8. Prayer: “May it come upon us, Lord.” See below, fol. 30.

[Col. 0092A]

At Vespers, let it be said as on Monday of the second week.

## The following Responsories

**R.** Daughters of Zion, extend your branches; bud forth.

**P.** And bring forth the fruit of fertility for my people Israel, for the day of the Lord will come.

**V.** Rejoice, ends of the earth; sound forth, mountains of praise, forests, and all the trees of the region.

**P.** And bring forth the fruit.

**V.** Glory and honor.

**P.** And bring forth the fruit.

### Another Responsory

**R.** Behold, the Lord will come, our Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel.

**P.** Having the crown of the kingdom upon his head.

**V.** Attend to me, my people, and hear me, my tribe, for the day of the Lord is near; my righteous one, and my Savior, has gone forth.

**P.** Having the crown of the kingdom.

**V.** Glory and honor.

[Col. 0092B] Repeat **R.** “Behold, the Lord …”

### Another Responsory

**R.** Hear, hear me, my people, says the Lord; and kings, pay attention and listen with your ears.

**P.** For a law has gone forth from me; my righteousness is approaching swiftly, and my Savior is present, whom the islands await.

**V.** Attend to me, my people, and hear me, my tribe.

**P.** For a law has gone forth from me.

**V.** Glory and honor.

Repeat **R.** “Hear, hear me.”

**R.** You who fear the Lord, await his mercy.

**P.** And do not depart from him, lest you fall, and your reward not be made void.

**V.** You who fear God, believe in him; and in his delight mercy will come to you.

**P.** And do not depart.

**V.** Glory and honor.

Repeat **R.** “You who fear the Lord.”

**R.** Let my people know my name on that day, [Col. 0092C] for behold, I, who speak, will be present to you, says the Lord.

**P.** Like a shoot upon the mountains, proclaiming tidings of peace and announcing good things, so that I may make known to you the Savior of the world.

**V.** God came from Sinai and arose from Seir; he appeared to us from Mount Paran.

**P.** Like a shoot.

**V.** Glory and honor.

Repeat **R.** “Let my people know.”

**R.** Behold, the Lord our God will go forth to us and will have mercy on us.

**P.** Blotting out our iniquities and casting all our sins into the depths of the sea.

**V.** He will raise a sign among nations far away and will whistle from the ends of the earth; and behold, coming swiftly, he will hasten.

**P.** Blotting out.

**V.** Glory and honor.

Repeat **R.** “Behold, the Lord our God.”

**R.** Who is this, beautiful, walking in his robe in the [Col. 0092D] greatness of his strength?

**P.** I, who speak righteousness and am a champion for salvation.

**V.** I, Jesus, send my Angel to testify to human beings, and behold, I am coming soon.

**P.** I, who speak.

**V.** Glory and honor.

Repeat **R.** “Who is this?”

**R.** Why do you delay, God? Come and free your people.

**P.** For all Israel awaits you.

**V.** Come, Lord, and do not delay; release the crimes of your people.

**P.** For all Israel.

**V.** Glory and honor.

Repeat **R.** “Why do you delay?”

**R.** Jerusalem, rejoice at the Advent of the Lord, for he himself will come to you.

**P.** And he will remove from you mourning and anxieties, and will clothe you with beauty at his Advent.

**V.** Jerusalem, the Lord, strong in your midst, [Col. 0093A] will rejoice over you with praise and will exult in jubilation.

**P.** And he will remove from you.

**V.** Glory and honor to the Father.

Repeat **R.** “Jerusalem, rejoice.”

**R.** Behold, salvation will come to us swiftly from the Lord, to break the heavy yoke.

**P.** And to save us from the bonds of our sins, because he is merciful. 30

**V.** Let us cry to the Lord in heaven, because of the face of the one who troubles us, and he will send us a Savior who will free us.

**P.** And to save us.

**V.** Glory and honor to the Father.

Repeat **R.** “Behold, he will come.”

At Vespers, let it be said as on fol. 17.

# TUESDAY OF THE FOURTH WEEK

## At Matins

**Antiphon.** Wash me, Lord, from my iniquity, and cleanse my heart from my sins.

**Psalm 50.**

**Prayer.** God, Son of God, whose name endures forever, [Col. 0093B] and who, making it known that you are one God and Lord, came as king through the mystery of the incarnation you assumed, to redeem the world: grant us to burn so intensely with this mystery of devotion that through it we may escape the snare of the deceiver; so that we who sing beforehand with open mouth the joys of your Advent may rejoice, when you come to judgment as judge, that we have been saved. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon 1.** The daughters of Zion will return and seek the Lord their God, their King David.

**P.** And they will delight in the Lord their God.

**V.** The Lord is faithful in his words and holy in all his works.

**P.** And they will delight.

**V.** Glory and honor to the Father.

**P.** And they will delight in the Lord.

**Prayer.** May the gift of your mercy [Col. 0093C] come upon us, Lord, so that, returning from the sluggishness of our heart and seeking you, the Lord and King in Zion, we may rejoice in that holy contemplation; so that we who await the presence of your face may escape the torments of our merits. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon 2.** Do not judge before the appointed time, until the Lord comes.

**P.** He will also bring to light the hidden things of darkness.

**V.** Hear this, all nations; listen with your ears, you who inhabit the world.

**P.** He will also bring to light.

**V.** Glory and honor to the Father.

**P.** He will also bring to light.

**Prayer.** God, who forbid us to judge before the appointed time and wish us, with great caution, to be content with patience: grant us both the desires of true patience and examples of true [Col. 0093D] endurance, so that, before you come, you who will illuminate the hidden things of hearts, the examples of true patience may so prevail in us that, when you come to judgment, the endurance of charity may free us from torments. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon 3.** From the beginning I have not spoken in secret.

**P.** But from the appointed time, before it happened, I was there.

**V.** He himself called upon me: “You are my Father.” And I will make him firstborn, exalted among the kings of the earth.

**P.** But from the appointed time.

**V.** Glory and honor to the Father.

**P.** But from the appointed time.

**Prayer.** God, who from the beginning spoke to us in secret: make us persist with unwavering love of faith in the beginning of your Word, which is manifest [Col. 0094A] in the flesh, so that he who was with you before the ages, born for us in time, may help us without end. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**R.** Behold, the Lord will come in fire; his chariot is like a whirlwind.

**P.** For the Lord will be judged in fire.

**V.** Fire will burn before him, and around him a mighty storm.

**P.** For the Lord will be judged in fire.

**V.** Glory and honor to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, forever and ever. Amen.

**P.** For …

**Prayer.** Lord God, who declare that you will come in fire: free us from the whirlwind of those who harm us, so that we who proclaim your wondrous work may draw more abundantly that reward which is before you. Let the choir respond: Amen.

[Col. 0094B]

Through your mercy, our God.

## At Lauds

### At the Canticle

**Antiphon.** Your house will be faithful.

**Canticle.** I took you from the pastures, from following the flocks. See on Wednesday of the first week, and likewise everything else through the end of Matins, fols. 10 and 11. At Vespers, fol. 17.

# WEDNESDAY

## At Matins

**Antiphon.** In you my soul trusts. See fol. 13.

**Psalm 56.**

**Prayer.** God, Son of God, whose name endures forever. See fol. 3.

**Antiphon 1.** Wait, wait again, says the Lord. For through the speech of lips …

**P.** And in another tongue I will speak to this people.

**V.** The Lord is faithful in his words [Col. 0094C] and holy in all his works.

**P.** For through the speech …

**V.** Glory and honor to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.

**P.** And in another tongue.

31 **Prayer.** Let us await you, Lord, so that, when you come to judgment, you may not accuse us of sin, but may speak to us mercifully in the spirit of your gentleness. Let the choir respond: Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

**Antiphon 2.** Behold, I will place in the foundations of Zion a precious cornerstone, says the Lord.

**P.** And whoever believes in him will not be put to shame.

**V.** The God of gods, the Lord, has spoken and has called the earth.

**P.** And whoever believes in him.

**V.** Glory and honor to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.

**P.** And whoever.

**Prayer.** Behold, you are already near, Lord; make us [Col. 0094D] always near to you, so that, in no respect anxious because of negligent care, we may await the day of your Advent unharmed. Let the choir respond: Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

**R.** The great day of the Lord will come.

**P.** For on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be salvation, as the Lord said.

**V.** All nations, clap your hands; shout to God with a voice of exultation.

**P.** For on Mount Zion.

**V.** Glory and honor to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.

**P.** For on the mountain.

**Prayer.** Christ, Son of God, who, appearing in the flesh and coming on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem as the great Savior, were called Salvation for those who would believe in you: be for us a Savior according to our desire and a Guide toward the [Col. 0095A] reward, so that you who have become the manifestation of holy salvation may become for sinners, both here and forever, the deliverance they desire. Let the choir respond: Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

Everything else is to be said as on Wednesday of the first week through the end of Matins. At Vespers, see fol. 17.

# THURSDAY

## At Matins

**Antiphon.** Lord, how they have multiplied.

**Prayer.** They have multiplied, Lord, those who trouble us. See fol. 8.

**Psalm 3.**

**Prayer.** God, Son of God, whose name endures forever. See fol. 3.

**Antiphon 1.** The Lord will be known by Egypt [Col. 0095B] when he comes.

**P.** And the Egyptians will know the Lord on that day, and they will indeed worship with sacrifices and gifts.

**V.** God will come openly, our God, and he will not be silent.

**P.** And the Egyptians will know the Lord.

**V.** Glory and honor to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.

**P.** And the Egyptians will know the Lord on that day.

**Prayer.** We know that you will come, Lord, to execute judgment; and therefore we ask that, when you come, you open our mouth and our heart, so that we may praise your holy name, worshiping with acceptable sacrifices in which you reveal the mysteries of your incarnation. Let the choir respond: Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

**Antiphon 2.** You who rule Israel, attend.

**P.** Stir up [Col. 0095C] your power and come to free us.

**V.** You who lead Joseph like a sheep, Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh.

**P.** Stir up your power.

**V.** Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son.

**P.** Stir up your power and come.

**Prayer.** You who rule Israel, attend; you who lead Joseph like a sheep, stir up your power and save those for whom you came, about to be born, into the earth. And you who deigned, through the extended worship of faith, to win a multitude of nations, restore, by a brief act of mercy, the souls of unbelievers rescued from the abyss of faithlessness, so that at last they may believe and become pleasing to you. Let the choir respond: Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

**R.** When the Lord of hosts comes upon Mount [Col. 0095D] Zion and in Jerusalem,

**P.** he will be glorified in the sight of his elders.

**V.** Hear this, all nations; listen with your ears, you who inhabit the world.

**P.** He will be glorified in the sight of his elders.

**V.** Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son.

**P.** He will be glorified in the sight of his elders.

**Prayer.** God, Son of God, who declare that you will be glorified on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem in the sight of the elders: grant us to rejoice in your kingdom with a full knowledge of faith, so that here you may make us flourish in faith, and at your Advent establish us to be crowned with eternal glory. Let the choir respond: Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

The Canticle and everything else that follows through the end of Matins are to be said as on Monday of the second [Col. 0096A] week of the Advent of the Lord. See fol. 16. At Vespers, as above, fol. 17.

# FRIDAY

## At Matins

**Antiphon.** Wash me, Lord, from my iniquity, and cleanse my heart from my sins.

**Psalm 50.**

**Prayer.** God, Son of God, whose name endures 32 forever. See on the weekdays of the first week of the Advent of the Lord, fol. 3.

Antiphon 1. Let us cry out to the Lord in the face of the oppressor. P. And he will send us a Savior and defender who will free us. V. Come, let us worship and fall prostrate before God; let us weep before the Lord who made us, for he is the Lord our God; [Col. 0096B] but we are his people and the sheep of his pasture. P. And he will send us a Savior. V. Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son. P. And he will send us a Savior.

Prayer. Let us cry out to you, Lord, in the face of the oppressor, that you may send us a Savior who will free us from the hand of our enemies; so that we, who await the presence of your face, may escape the torments deserved for our sins. Let the Chorus respond. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God, etc.

Antiphon. The day of the Lord is near; do not be troubled. P. For its joy is our strength. V. Hear, my people, and I will speak to you; and I will testify to you, Israel, if you will listen to me. P. For its joy. [Col. 0096C] V. Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son. P. For its joy is our strength.

Prayer. Your day, Lord, behold, is near, and it is necessary that we hasten with purified consciences. And therefore, because we cannot possess these things from ourselves, we ask you, who are powerful, to grant them to us: we ask that your joy may be our strength in such a way that affliction may not overwhelm us forever. Let the Chorus respond. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

R. Jerusalem, look toward the east. P. And see the joy that will come to you from God. V. Praise the Lord, Jerusalem; praise your God, Zion. P. And see the joy. V. Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son. [Col. 0096D] P. And see the joy.

Prayer. We look, Lord, and now, with the eye of faith purified, we see how ineffable is that joy which, as your city Jerusalem looked toward the east, shone upon it from the Lord in the bestowal of his gift. And therefore we ask that you, who carried it into the joys of your incarnation, preserve us unharmed in its bosom from the contagion of every offense; so that in it the dignity of our works may save us, and the expectation of your Advent may justify us without end. Let the Chorus respond. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

The Canticle and everything else through the end of Matins are to be said as on Wednesday of the second week. See fol. 18. At Vespers, as above, fol. 17.

## ON THE FIFTH SUNDAY OF THE ADVENT OF THE LORD

[Col. 0097A]

### At Vespers

Lauda. From the rising of the sun. Prayer. O God, whose name is blessed. See fol. 1.

Sono. The Savior will appear to us like a bright cloud. P. At midday; alleluia. V. And like drops falling upon the face of thirsty earth. P. At midday; alleluia.

Antiphon. Let all flesh be silent before the face of God, for he is near; the day of the Lord will prepare a sacrifice for us. P. And he will sanctify all his elect. V. God will come openly, our God, and he will not be silent. P. And he will sanctify. V. Glory and honor to the Father. P. And he will sanctify.

Lauda. The Lord will go forth like a strong man and, like a warrior, will stir up zeal; he will shout and cry out: alleluia. P. And he will prevail over his enemies, and they will proclaim his praise in the islands: alleluia, alleluia. V. Praise the name of the Lord; praise him, servants of the Lord. P. And he will prevail. V. Glory and honor. P. And he will prevail over his enemies.

Hymn. Let Christ’s company cry out. Supplication. Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world, our Lord. See fol. 2.

Short Lesson. Christ, Son of God, who, born timelessly from the Father and destined to be born in time through the Virgin, go forth from the Father’s bosom like a strong man; make us ever stronger in your works, so that you, who stirred up the zeal of your power among peoples destined to believe in you, may stir up in us a love of your affection that will never end, by which we may be brought to the promises of your inheritance.

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” See fol. 2.

Blessing. May the Lord, coming from Zion, rescue us from all our iniquities. Let the response be made: Amen. May he who comes to extend his mercies turn our iniquities away from us. Let the response be made: Amen. May he establish us as those to be redeemed in such a way that, when he judges, he does not punish us. Let the response be made: Amen.

Through the mercy of our God.

Lauda. Remember us, Lord, in the favor shown to your people: alleluia. P. Visit us, O God, with your salvation: alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V. That we may confess your holy name and glory in your praise. P. Visit us, O God. V. Glory and honor to the Father. [Col. 0097D] P. Visit us, O God.

Prayer. Strong Lord God, who from the Father’s— as below.

### At Matins

Hymn. Eternal Creator of all things. See fol. 3. Prayer. After the crowing of the cock. See fol. 21.

Over the Psalms. Antiphon. Salvation belongs to the Lord, and your blessing is upon your people. Psalm III.

Antiphon. You have revealed to me the uncertain and hidden things of your wisdom. Psalm L.

Antiphon. In the shadow of your wings I will hope until iniquity passes away.

Prayer. Let us humbly ask the Word uttered ineffably by the Father’s mouth before the ages, and born from the Virgin as man for us at the end of time, that he may mercifully hear our invocation from his holy mountain, and that his blessing may fill the breasts of believers. And just as, by revealing the uncertain things of his secrets, he arouses our hearts to acknowledge him, so may he defend the Catholic people under the protection of his wings; and when he comes as Judge, may he be favorable to them, for whose redemption he appeared humbly in the flesh. Let the Chorus respond. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 1. The Lord will go forth like a strong man; like a warrior he will stir up zeal, to lead the blind along a way they do not know. P. And he will turn their darkness into light. V. All nations, clap your hands; shout to God with a voice of exultation. P. And he will turn their darkness. V. Glory and honor to the Father. P. And he will turn their darkness into light.

[Col. 0098B] Prayer. Strong Lord God, who, going forth from the Father’s secret place and, like a warrior, stirring up the nations destined to believe in you, acquire them for yourself; stir up in us zeal pleasing to you, so that we who already believe that you have come may await your coming again with greater confidence and innocence. Let the Chorus respond. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

Antiphon 2. My justice is near; it will not delay, says the Lord. P. I will bring it as salvation to Zion, and I will place joy upon all who mourn in Israel. V. Hear these things, all nations; perceive them with your ears, you who inhabit the world. P. I will bring it. V. Glory and honor to the Father. P. And I will place joy.

Prayer. Christ God, Wisdom of the supreme Father, Word, who build for yourself the purest house, the womb of the Virgin Mary, in which you yourself, heavenly Justice, appear, and from which you bring forth the fruit of your kindness: while you enter it as God without bodily clothing and come forth from it clothed in flesh; grant us, your suppliants, that you may sanctify us for yourself in the house from which you will appear, coming forth as a bridegroom, surrounded by the dignity of our works. Let the Chorus respond. Amen.

Through the mercy of God.

Antiphon 3. I am the Lord, the first and the last; the islands will see and fear me. P. The ends of the earth will know and will come and draw near to me. V. But I have been established as king by him over Zion, his holy mountain, proclaiming his command. P. The ends of the earth will know. V. Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son. P. The ends of the earth will know.

Prayer. Son of God, who, being first and last, enclose within yourself all things created by you, yet are not yourself enclosed; whom the ends of the earth recognized through the mystery of your incarnation, when they were drawn by you through the call of faith: grant that, through knowledge of this holy faith, we may be so rooted in you by the worship of justice and the dignity of our works that we may thereby deserve to attain eternal rest. Let the Chorus respond. Amen.

Through the mercy of God.

R. Bethlehem, city of the Most High God, from you will come forth the ruler of Israel. P. And his origin is from the beginning, from the days of eternity, and there will be peace in our land when he comes. V. And you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, are you too little among the thousands of Judah? For from you will come forth a king who will rule my people Israel. P. And his origin is from the beginning. V. Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son. Let R. “Bethlehem, city of the Most High God” be repeated.

Prayer. Christ, Son of God the Father Most High, you consecrate the city of your incarnation by declaring that from it you will be born as the true ruler of Israel, and in it you reveal the miracle of your incarnation, unheard of throughout the ages. While within the confines of that same Bethlehemite city you glorify your mother Mary with maternal honor, whose womb you neither open when entering nor violate when departing, we ask that you illumine the inner chambers of our soul with your brightness in such a way that, preserved through the aid of your mother from the serpent’s persuasion, we may obtain unharmed purity of mind. Let the Chorus respond. Amen.

Through the mercy of God.

### At Lauds

At the Canticle. Antiphon. God will come from Lebanon. Canticle. “Lord, I have heard the report.” See fol. 22.

At the Benedictus. Antiphon. Blessed are you, O God. P. Bless the Lord. Canticle of Daniel III. “Blessed are you, Lord God of our fathers.” See fol. 6. Sono. “The Savior will appear to us.” See fol. 32. Lauda. “Praise the Lord from the heavens”: alleluia. See fol. 23. Psalm CXLVIII.

Reading from the Book of the Prophet Micah, chapter IV.

R. Thanks be to God.

[Col. 0099C] It shall come to pass in the last days that the mountain of the house of the Lord will be prepared at the summit of the mountains and raised above the hills, and peoples will flow to it. Many nations will prophesy and say: “Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord and to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us his ways, and we will walk in his paths.” For from Zion the law will go forth, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem. And he will judge among many peoples and rebuke strong nations even at a distance; and they will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation will not take up the sword against nation, and they will no longer learn to wage war. And each man will sit beneath his vine and beneath his fig tree, and there will be no one to frighten him, for the mouth of the Lord of hosts has spoken.

For all peoples will walk, each in the name of the Lord his God; but we will walk in the name of the Lord our God forever and beyond. On that day, says the Lord, I will gather the lame and collect the one whom I had driven away and the one whom I had afflicted. And I will set the lame as a remnant and the one who had been afflicted as a strong nation; and the Lord will reign over them on Mount Zion, now and forever.

And you, tower of the flock, misty daughter of Zion, to you the former dominion will come; the kingdom of the daughter of Jerusalem will come. Now why are you consumed with sorrow? Is there no king for you, or has your counselor perished, because pain has seized you like a woman in labor? Grieve and strive, daughter of Zion, like a woman in labor, because now you will go forth from the city and dwell in the region, and you will come even to Babylon. [Col. 0100A] There you will be delivered; there the Lord will redeem you from the hand of your enemies. Let the Chorus respond. Amen.

Hymn. Almighty King of all things. Supplication. Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world. See on the first Sunday of the Advent of the Lord, fol. 2.

Short Lesson. Lord Jesus Christ, whom we believe to have come humbly in the lowliness of the flesh to redeem the perishing world, and whom we await coming again in the power of your Godhead to judge the sinful age with terror: we, your trembling servants, ask your boundless compassion that, when you come, you may not accuse us of sin but may aid us with ineffable kindness; and that here you may rather accept the confession of our humility, so that there you may forgive all our crimes and establish us to be crowned among those at your right hand.

[Col. 0100B] Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” See fol. 2.

Lauda. Remember us, Lord, in the favor shown to your people: alleluia. P. Visit us, O God, with your salvation: alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V. That we may confess your holy name and glory in your praise. P. Visit us, O God. V. Glory and honor to the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. P. Visit us, O God, in salvation.

Blessing. May the Lord, coming from Zion, rescue us from all our iniquities. Let the Chorus respond: Amen.

Through the mercy of our God. May the Lord be always with us.

In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, let us complete this in peace. R. Thanks be to God.

At the end of Vespers. Lauda. From the rising of the sun to its setting. P. The name of the Lord is worthy of praise. V. May the name of the Lord be blessed, now and forever. P. The name of the Lord is worthy of praise.

Sono. “The Savior will appear to us.” See fol. 32.

Antiphon. The Lord will be like dew; Israel will sprout like a lily. P. And its root will burst forth like Lebanon. V. And there will be firmness on the earth at the summits of the mountains; its fruit will be exalted above Lebanon, and from the city they will bloom like the grass of the earth. P. And its root will burst forth. V. Glory and honor to the Father, [35] and to the Son. P. And its root will burst forth.

Lauda. The God of powers is with us. P. The God of Jacob is our protector. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V. Truth has sprung from the earth, and justice has looked down from heaven. [Col. 0100D] P. The God of Jacob is our protector. V. Glory and honor to the Father. P. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.

Hymn. Let Christ’s company cry out. Supplication. Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world, our Lord. See on the first Sunday of the Advent of the Lord, fol. 2.

Short Lesson. O God, whose eternity foreknows and orders the ages, who, in the fullness of time, appointed our Lord Jesus Christ your Son to be born from the Virgin, so that the Eternal, proceeding from you timelessly, might be born in time for us as Creator, in order both to visit our times and to make those who are temporal partakers of his immortality: may he stand before you on our behalf, so that those whom he wonderfully redeemed by his Advent he may enrich most abundantly by his gift.

[Col. 0101A] Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” See fol. 2.

Blessing. Christ the Lord, who through the humanity he assumed— see fol. 8.

Lauda. There will be firmness on the earth at the summits of the mountains; it will be exalted above Lebanon: alleluia. P. And the name of the Lord will be blessed forever: alleluia, alleluia. V. His name endures before the sun, and his throne before the moon; and all the tribes of the earth will be blessed in him. P. And the name of the Lord will be. V. Glory and honor. P. And the name will be.

Prayer. Strong Lord God, who from the Father’s— Let it be said as at First Vespers of this Sunday, fol. 32.

## MONDAY OF THE FIFTH WEEK IN THE ADVENT OF THE LORD

### At Matins

Antiphon. Lord, why have those who trouble me multiplied? Psalm III, with its prayer, fol. 8.

Antiphon 1. Those to whom he was not announced will see him, and those who did not hear will understand. P. And he will rise up like a young shoot before him. P. And like a root from thirsty earth. V. He will judge the poor of the people in his justice, and he will save the children of the poor, and he will humble the slanderer. P. And he will rise up. V. Glory and honor. P. And like a root.

Prayer. I see a crime exceedingly monstrous committed before your eyes, God the Father, by the reprobate: while they despise your Son, proclaimed in the Law, they have remained in the abyss of their unbelief; while those to whom he had not been announced saw him, and those who had not heard contemplated him with understanding. Therefore, we ask, remove whatever resists you in our works, so that, in a believing heart, the young shoots of your gifts may flourish powerfully in us, and the root of humility may never wither. R. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

Antiphon 2. May the God of peace sanctify you completely, and may your spirit be whole. P. May soul and body be preserved without blame at the Advent of our Lord Jesus Christ. V. Praise the name of the Lord; praise the Lord, servants. P. May soul and body be preserved. V. Glory and honor to the Father. P. May soul and body be preserved.

Prayer. Christ our God, who, coming in the humanity you assumed to judge the world, sanctify us completely, so that on the day of your Advent, when you come to judge the age, our whole spirit, soul, and body may so flourish again in you that we may live with you, destined to reign without end. Let the Chorus respond. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

Antiphon 3. On that day a man will bow down to his Maker. P. And his eyes will look toward the Holy One of Israel. V. The God of gods, the Lord, has spoken and summoned the earth. P. And his eyes will look toward him. V. Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son. P. And his eyes will look toward him.

Prayer. Only-begotten Son of God, whose eyes look toward the Holy One of Israel, incline your mercy toward us, so that we may be able to look upon you as our Maker when you appear in your glory. Let the Chorus respond. Amen.

[Col. 0102A] Through your mercy, our God, etc.

R. Rejoice, daughter of Zion, because your king will come to you with gladness. P. And you, daughter of Jerusalem, rejoice in the Advent of the Lord your God. V. Rejoice greatly and shout for joy, daughter of Zion; behold, your king comes, just and a savior. P. And you, daughter of Jerusalem. V. Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son. Let R. “Rejoice, daughter of Zion” be repeated.

The Canticle and everything else that follows through the end of Matins are to be said as on Monday of the first week of the Advent of the Lord. See fol. 9. Except for the Prophecy: “In the last days the mountain of the house of the Lord will be.” See fol. 34.

At Vespers, let everything be said as above on Monday.

## TUESDAY

### At Matins

Antiphon. “Wash me, Lord.” See fol. 3. Psalm L. Prayer. Son of God, whose [name] endures forever. See fol. 3.

Antiphon 1. The gentle will increase their joy in the Lord. P. And the poor will rejoice when the Holy One of Israel comes. V. Yet his salvation is near those who fear him, so that glory may dwell in our land. P. And the poor. V. Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son. P. And the poor.

Prayer. Once the mystery of your incarnation has been revealed, Christ the Lord, humble poor people rejoice, recognizing you in joy as holy, true, and most gentle. Therefore we ask you: make us sinners blessed, you who make the barren fruitful. Let the Chorus respond. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

Antiphon 2. All will sanctify the Holy One of Jacob and proclaim the God of Israel. P. And those who wander will understand, and those who are unaccustomed will learn the law. V. God will come openly, our God, and will not be silent. P. And those who wander will understand. V. Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son. P. And those who wander.

Prayer. God, toward whom the eyes of all flesh look, grant that we may see your salvation in glory, so that those who wander may understand; that, when the kingdom of your majesty has shone upon all, we may escape the punishment deserved for our merits. Let the Chorus respond. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

[Col. 0102D] R. Be strong at the Advent of the Lord your God, house of Jacob, for you will see the Savior, the light of majesty, sowing the fruit of life. P. And you who are distressed, endure until the Prince of justice comes, removing the weakness of the whole earth. V. Contemplate the way; strengthen your loins and greatly fortify your strength, and hasten at the Advent of the Lord your God. P. And you who are distressed. V. Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son. Let R. “Be strong at the Advent of the Lord” be repeated.

The Canticle and everything else through the end of Matins are to be said as on Wednesday of the first week, fols. 11 and 12. Except for the Prophecy, which is taken from the preceding Sunday, fol. 34. At Vespers, as above, fol. 12.

## WEDNESDAY

[Col. 0103A]

### At Matins

Antiphon. My soul trusts in you. Psalm LVI. Prayer. Son of God, whose [name] endures forever. See fol. 3.

Antiphon. A rod will go forth from the root of Jesse. P. And a flower will rise from his root. P. And he will judge the poor in justice. V. The Lord will send forth the rod of your power from Zion; rule in the midst of your enemies. P. And a flower from the root. V. Glory and honor to the Father. P. And he will judge.

Prayer. Be for us, Lord, a crown of glory on the day when you come to judge the age by fire, so that here you may first clothe us in the garment of justice, and afterward in the perfect freedom of glory. Let the Chorus respond. Amen.

[Col. 0103B] Through your mercy, our God.

Antiphon 1. Those to whom he was not announced will see him. P. And those who did not hear will understand; and he will rise up like a young shoot before him and like a root from thirsty earth. V. He will judge the poor of the people in his justice, and he will save the children of the poor, and he will humble the slanderer. P. And those who did not hear. V. Glory and honor. P. And those who did not hear.

Prayer. Those to whom he was not announced will see him, and those who did not hear will understand, because firm hope always remains in him, in whom is the fullness of perfect glory. Therefore let him fill our mouth with joy, so that our voice may resound with his praises and our soul may be filled with gifts. Let the Chorus respond. Amen.

Through your mercy.

[Col. 0103C] Antiphon 2. Rejoice with joy, Jacob, and enter against the head of the nations. P. Sound forth, sing, and say: P. Save, Lord, your people, the remnant of Israel. V. Take up the psalm and give the tambourine, the joyful psaltery with the lyre. P. Sound forth, sing. V. Glory and honor. P. Save, Lord.

Prayer. Grant, Lord, that we may live justly, soberly, and devoutly in this age, awaiting that blessed hope and the Advent of the glory of your majesty; and so let us run along the paths of justice that we may deservedly be able to approach the eternal inheritance. Let the Chorus respond. Amen.

[37] Through your mercy, our God.

R. Jerusalem, I will be favorable; I will come upon your mountains, and you will rejoice, because the day of the Lord will come to you. Rise, Zion; turn back to your God. Rejoice and be glad, Jacob. P. For your Savior has come forth from the midst of the nations. V. Return, daughter of Zion; return to your cities; return, virgin Israel. P. For he has come forth from the midst. V. Glory and honor to the Father. Let R. “Jerusalem, I will be favorable” be repeated.

Everything else through the end of Matins is to be said as on Friday of the first week, fol. 13. Except for the Prophecy, which is to be taken from the preceding fifth Sunday, fol. 34.

R. Behold, the majesty of God comes by the way that looks toward the east, and his voice is like the voice of many waters. P. And the earth shone with the splendor of the Lord. V. Hear, islands, and pay attention, peoples; be astonished [Col. 0104A] and marvel, for the mountains will be shaken and the foundations of the earth will tremble. P. And the earth shone. V. Glory and honor. Let the Responsory “Behold, the majesty” be repeated.

V. A cry has been made: behold, the bridegroom is coming. P. Go out to meet him. V. Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, the King of Israel. P. Go out. V. Glory and honor to the Father. Let the Responsory “A cry has been made” be repeated.

R. Behold, the Lord will ascend upon a light cloud. P. And he will enter Egypt, and, like a strong king, will rule all nations. V. God will come openly, our God, and will not be silent. P. And he will enter. V. Glory and honor. P. And he will enter.

V. Behold, the Lord will come and will not lie. P. And if he delays, wait for him, because he will surely come and will not delay. V. He sends forth his utterance upon the earth; his word runs swiftly. P. And if he delays. V. Glory and honor to the Father. P. And if he delays.

V. The sun of justice will rise for those who fear God, and healing will be in his wings. V. In his days justice will rise, and abundance of peace, until the moon is exalted. P. And healing. V. Glory and honor to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. P. And healing.

At Vespers, let it be said as on Friday of the first week.

## THURSDAY

### At Matins

Antiphon. Lord, why have those who trouble me multiplied? With its prayer, “They have multiplied, Lord.” See fol. 8.

Antiphon 1. Behold, the Lord will ascend upon a [Col. 0104C] light cloud. P. And he will enter Egypt. P. And, like a strong king, he will rule all nations. V. God will come openly, our God, and will not be silent. P. And he will enter. V. Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son. P. And, like a strong king, he will rule.

Prayer. Behold, the prophecies of the Prophets foretold that you, the Lord, would ascend upon a cloud; and therefore we ask you: you who formerly, destined to be born in the flesh, entered this world as a strong king and obtained dominion over the nations through faith, show yourself merciful toward us when you appear in glory. Let the Chorus respond. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

Antiphon 2. Behold, the Lord will come and will not lie. [Col. 0104D] P. And if he delays, wait for him, because he will surely come and will not delay. V. He who sends his word upon the earth—his word runs swiftly. P. And if he delays. V. Glory and honor to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. P. And if he delays.

Prayer. We await you, Lord, because you will surely come. Yet now, because your kingdom is recognized throughout the bounds of the earth, our weakness complains that you have not lied. And therefore we humbly await you with longing, so that, when you come, you may make us your companions without end. Let the Chorus respond. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

Antiphon 3. The Sun of justice will rise for those who fear God. P. And healing will be in his wings. V. In his days justice will rise, and abundance of peace, until the moon is exalted. P. And healing. V. Glory and honor to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. P. And healing.

Prayer. Rise in our hearts, Sun of justice, and illumine us with the brightness of your Advent, so that we who rejoice at the voice of your promise may in no way be put to shame at the Advent of your glory. Let the Chorus respond. Amen.

Through the mercy of our God.

R. I will come to Zion, says the Lord, and I will dwell in Jerusalem. P. And Jerusalem will be called the holy city. V. Hear, my people, and I will speak; Israel, and I will testify to you, Israel, if you will listen to me. P. And it will be called. V. Glory and honor. P. And it will be called.

Prayer. Come, Lord, as you promised, to Zion, and dwell in Jerusalem, so that you who formerly appeared glorious through faith may there be revealed in the dignity of our works; so that the vision of peace may preserve among us the peaceful honor of your name, and the desire for your Advent may increase for us in it the star of new light. Let the Chorus respond. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

Everything else that follows is to be said as on Monday of the second week, fol. 16. Except for the Prophecy, which is taken from the preceding fifth Sunday, fol. 34.

At Vespers, let it be said as above on Monday, fol. 17.

## FRIDAY

### At Matins

Antiphon. Wash me, Lord, from my iniquity, and cleanse my heart from my sins. Psalm L.

[Col. 0105C] Prayer. Son of God, whose name endures forever, and who, making known that you alone are God and Lord, came as king through the mystery of the incarnation you assumed, in order to redeem the age: grant that we may burn so ardently with this mystery of devotion that through it we may escape the snare of the deceiver; so that we who proclaim the joys of your Advent with open mouth may rejoice that we have been saved when you, as Judge, come to judgment. Let the Chorus respond. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God, who, etc.

Antiphon 1. The Lord sends his Word into Jacob, and it will come into Israel. P. So that all the people may know that he is the one. V. He who sends his word upon the earth—his word runs swiftly. P. So that all the people may know. V. Glory and honor to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy [Col. 0105D] Spirit. P. So that all may know.

Prayer. Send your Word, almighty Father, from your dwelling places, so that he may heal and strengthen all the contrite and raise up the fallen, granting us the joy of his name. Let the Chorus respond. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

Antiphon 2. Behold, a man will come, whose name is “his Rising”; justice will rise beneath him. P. And he himself will be the salvation of the people. V. His justice will rise in the darkness, and there will be firmness on the earth at the summits of the mountains. P. And he himself will be. V. Glory and honor to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. P. And he himself will be.

Prayer. Behold, you are the Lord our God, who formerly came to redeem the world, whose name is “your Rising”; free those who have perished, whom you redeemed at great cost, so that you who deigned to become human and to be weakened for us may deign to fortify human beings with the assistance of your divinity. Let the Chorus respond. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

R. The Lord will free us from the power of our enemies. P. And joy and gladness will come to us swiftly from God our Savior. V. Behold, the days will come, says the Lord: I will raise up over you a good word, and you will call upon me, and you will fear; you will pray, and I will hear you. P. And joy and gladness will come to us. V. Glory and honor to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. P. And joy and gladness will come to us.

Everything else that follows through the end of Matins is to be said as on Wednesday of the second week, fol. [Col. 0106B] 18. Except for the Prophecy, which is taken from the preceding fifth Sunday, fol. 34.

At Vespers, as stated for Wednesday of the second week, fol. 19.

Antiphon. My soul trusts in you. Psalm XLVI.

Prayer. Son of God, whose [name] endures forever, as above.

Antiphon 1. Pay attention to me, my people, and hear me, my tribe. P. For my judgment will appear in the light of the peoples. V. Hear these things, all nations; perceive them with your ears, you who inhabit the world. P. For my judgment. V. Glory and honor to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. P. For my judgment.

Prayer. Behold, your tribe and your people are approaching you, Lord; we ask and implore that your judgment, which appeared in the light of the peoples, may be glorified in the salvation of the redeemed, so that those whom you formerly came to redeem through faith may come again to free from eternal punishment those whom you have redeemed. Let the Chorus respond. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

Antiphon 2. Close the word, says the Lord, and seal the book until the day of the Advent of the Lord. P. For knowledge will be multiplied. V. The God of gods and the Lord has spoken and summoned the earth. P. For knowledge will be multiplied. V. Glory and honor to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. P. For knowledge will be multiplied.

[39] Prayer. O God, who foretold that the knowledge of the messengers would be multiplied as the grace of those preaching increased through the progress of the ages, grant that we may believe and retain the mysteries of the closed word and sealed book in such a way that on the day of your Advent we may deserve to stand before your eyes without confusion. Let the Chorus respond. Amen.

Through your mercy, God.

Antiphon 3. I will raise him up for justice, says the Lord. P. And I will direct all his ways, and I will release the captivity of my people. V. In his days justice will rise, and abundance of peace, until the moon is exalted. P. And all his ways. V. Glory and honor to the Father. P. And all.

Prayer. God the Father, who raised up Jesus Christ your Son for justice by showing him in the flesh, make us always follow his footsteps in work and [Col. 0107A] in word, so that, hearing him without ceasing with the hearing of our heart, we may deserve to share in his glory. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

R. Rejoice with Jerusalem and exult in her, all you who love her, because behold, I will incline over her. P. You will see her like a river of peace, and your heart will rejoice. V. Exult and praise, daughter of Zion, because the Holy One of Israel has come in your midst. P. You will see her like a river of peace. V. Glory and honor to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. Let the Responsory “Rejoice with Jerusalem” be repeated.

Prayer. O God, who foretold by prophetic prophecy that you would appear as perfection in Jerusalem, grant us, through contemplation of your Church, always to remain devoted and to persist unharmed in every respect, so that you may always appear glorious in her, in whom you reveal the mysteries of your incarnation. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

The Canticle and everything else that follows at the end of Matins are to be said as on Friday of the second week, fol. 20. Except for the Prophecy, which is taken from the preceding fifth Sunday, fol. 34.

## ON THE SIXTH SUNDAY OF THE ADVENT OF THE LORD

### At Vespers

Antiphon. There will be great light at evening time. P. For behold, the Lord your God will come. V. And those who are in darkness and sit in the shadow of death will be illumined. P. For behold, he will come.

Sono. Give heed, you who rule Israel. P. And come to free us. Alleluia. V. God of powers, restore us, and show your face. P. And come to free us.

Antiphon. Hosanna; blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord. P. Blessed is the kingdom of our father David that comes: Hosanna in the highest. V. Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, God the Lord, and he has shone upon us. P. Blessed is the kingdom. V. Glory and honor. P. Blessed is the kingdom.

Lauda. The Savior will appear to you like a bright cloud at midday. P. And like drops falling upon the face of thirsty earth. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V. He will judge the poor of the people in his justice, and he will save the children of the poor, and he will humble the slanderer. P. And like drops. V. Glory and honor. P. And like drops.

[Col. 0107D] Hymn. Let Christ’s company cry out. Supplication. Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world. See fol. 2.

Short Lesson. Hosanna to the Son of David; blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord; blessed is the kingdom of our father David that comes; Hosanna in the highest. Therefore we ask and implore that you illumine the hidden places of our hearts with the radiance of the Spirit, the Paraclete, and by the support of your right hand rescue us in the present age from all evils and lead us, rejoicing with your praises, to the kingdom.

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” Fol. 2.

**Benediction.** May God, who has come to set us free, make us such as he makes fit to be set free. **R.** Amen. May he defend the freedom which the Redeemer, redeeming those who were to be redeemed, has bestowed, by preserving redemption. **R.** Amen. May he who came into the world as Redeemer bring us, the redeemed, to heaven. **R.** Amen.

Through his mercy.

**Lauda.** Have mercy, O God, on all; and look upon us. Alleluia. **P.** And show us the light of your mercies. Alleluia, alleluia. **V.** O God, when you turn us, you will give us life, and your people will rejoice in you. **P.** And show us. **V.** Glory and honor. **P.** And show us.

**Prayer.** Console, O Lord, those who await you. See in the Matins of this Sunday.

## At Matins

**Hymn.** Eternal Maker of all things. See fol. 3.  
**Prayer.** After the cockcrow. See fol. 21.

**[Col. 0108B] Over the Psalms.**

**Antiphon.** Salvation belongs to the Lord, and your blessing is upon your people. Psalm III.

**Antiphon.** You have made known to me the hidden and secret things of your wisdom. Psalm L.

**Antiphon.** In the shadow of your wings I will hope until iniquity passes away. Psalm LVI.

**Prayer.** The Word before the ages. Fol. 33.

**First Antiphon.** Strengthen the weary hands; make firm the tottering knees; because you are fainthearted, take courage: there is no reason for you to fear any longer. **P.** Behold, the Savior comes. **V.** Hear this, all nations; listen with your ears, you who inhabit the world. **P.** Behold. **V.** Glory and honor. **P.** Behold.

**Prayer.** Console, O Lord, the hearts of the faithful who await you, so that our weary hands may receive the help of your consolation; and so that our weak knees, while they hasten with tireless steps along the paths of your commandments, may be rewarded by you with the joy of the eternal promise. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.
