**Second Antiphon.** Behold, the Lord will come and save us. **P.** Then the eyes of the blind will be opened, and the ears of the deaf will hear; then the lame man will leap like a stag. **V.** He summoned the heavens above and the earth, to distinguish his people. **P.** Then the eyes of the blind will be opened. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father, etc. **P.** Then the eyes will be opened.

**Prayer.** Come, O Lord, and save us, and do not reject the desire of our heart at the time of your judgment; so that you, who opened the eyes of the blind and restored hearing to the deaf, may continually pour into our hardened hearts that manifest gift of your mercy by which you may lead us to everlasting rewards. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Third Antiphon.** O you who are in the dust, awake. **P.** And praise. **P.** Behold, the Lord will come; do not fear. **V.** All nations, clap your hands; shout joyfully to God with a voice of exultation. **P.** And praise. **V.** Glory. **P.** Behold, the Lord.

**Prayer.** Christ, Son of God the Father, who, coming into this world, commanded those lying in the dust to rise and praise you; now, Lord, you have summoned them not to fear you when you come: grant that we who seek you may advance in the flesh with such purity that we do not fear returning to that dust from which, when you came, you had raised those who lay in it; but shape within us that praise which they were commanded to offer in blessing you, so that you may always be praised unceasingly by us. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**R.** We shall all walk in the name of the Lord forever, for the Lord will reign on Mount Zion. **P.** And you, mist-covered tower of the King, daughter of Zion, to you the Savior will come, and power will come, the first of kings, daughter Jerusalem. **V.** Behold, the inhabitants of the Rock will cry out from the summit of the mountains and say: Come, let us walk in the light of the Lord God. **P.** And you, tower. **V.** Glory and honor. Repeat. **R.** We shall all walk.

**[Col. 0109B] Prayer.** We who all walk in your name, only-begotten Son of God the Father, ask, implore, and earnestly entreat that we who believe you were incarnate in the Virgin’s womb may be rewarded with the prizes of faith; and that you who proclaim yourself destined to reign on Mount Zion may show that you will dwell forever in our hearts. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**At the Canticle. Antiphon.** You who remember the Lord, do not be silent, and do not keep silence for him until he establishes and sets Jerusalem as a praise in the earth.

**Canticle.** Rejoicing, I will rejoice. See fol. 18.

**At the Benedictus. Antiphon.** Bless the Lord, little ones and great, all you who await his coming.

**[Col. 0109C] Canticle of Daniel III.** Blessed are you, Lord God of our fathers. See fol. 6.  
**Sono.** You who rule Israel. See in Vespers, fol. 39.

**Lauda.** Praise the Lord from the heavens. Alleluia; praise him in the heights. Alleluia. Psalm CXLVIII.

**Reading from the Book of the Prophet Isaiah (Chapter VI).**

**R.** Thanks be to God.

The Lord spoke to Ahaz, saying: “Ask a sign for yourself from the Lord your God, either from the depth of hell or from the height above.” And Ahaz said: “I will not ask, and I will not tempt the Lord.” And he said: “Hear, then, house of David: Is it too little for you to be troublesome to men, that you are troublesome even to my God? Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign. Behold, a virgin will conceive and bear a son, and his name will be called Emmanuel. He will eat butter and honey, so that he may know how to reject evil and choose good. For before the child knows how to reject evil and choose good, the land which you detest will be abandoned before the faces of its two kings.

“The Lord will bring upon you, and upon the house of your father, and upon your people, days such as have not come since the days of the separation of Ephraim from Judah, through the king of the Assyrians. On that day the Lord will shave with a hired razor those who are beyond the River, by the king of the Assyrians, the head and the hair of the feet, and he will remove the whole beard. And it will be on that day: A man will nourish a cow and two sheep; and because of the abundance of milk he will eat butter. For everyone who is left in the midst of the land will eat butter and honey.”

And the Lord said to me: “Take for yourself a large book and write in it with a man’s stylus: ‘Quickly take away the spoil; hasten to plunder.’” And I called as witnesses for myself faithful men, Uriah the priest and Zechariah son of Barachiah. And I approached the prophetess, and she conceived and bore a son. And the Lord said to me: “Call his name: ‘Quickly take away the spoil; hasten to plunder.’ For before the child knows how to call his father and his mother, the strength of Damascus and the spoils of Samaria will be taken away before the king of the Assyrians.”

And the Lord continued to speak to me, saying: “Because this people has rejected the waters of Siloam, which flow quietly, and has chosen rather Rezin and the son of Remaliah, therefore, behold, the Lord will bring upon them the strong and abundant waters of the river: the king of the Assyrians and all his glory. He will rise over all its channels and flow over all its banks; he will advance against Judah, flooding it, and, passing through, will reach up to the neck. And the spreading of his wings will fill the height of your land, O Emmanuel.

“Gather together and hear, all you distant lands: take courage, and be overcome; take counsel, and it will be scattered; speak a word, and it will not come to pass, for God is with us.” **R.** Amen.

**Hymn.** Almighty King of all things. Fol. 7.  
**Supplication.** Let us beseech the Redeemer of the world. See fol. 2.

**Capitula.** O Lord, whose kingdom is power, terrible and girded with strength, whom the rivers of the Doctors praise with uplifted voices and the wonders of the sea celebrate together: stir up your power and the terrible strength of your arm, which may break the yoke of our slavery, pressing upon our wretched necks; strengthen our weary hands, make firm our weak knees, and restore courage to the fainthearted. Let there be nothing more for us to fear from the enemy, because we believe that our most merciful Redeemer is coming for our salvation.

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. Fol. 2.

**Lauda.** Have mercy, O God of all.  
**Benediction.** The God who has come. See fol. 39.

In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, let us conclude in peace. **R.** Thanks be to God.

## At the End of Vespers

**Lauda.** There will be great light.  
**Sono.** You who rule Israel. See fol. 39.

**Antiphon.** How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of those who announce peace, proclaiming salvation and saying: **[Col. 0110D] P.** Zion, your God will reign. **V.** All nations, clap your hands; shout joyfully to God with a voice of exultation. **P.** Zion will reign. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son, etc. **P.** Zion will reign.

**Lauda.** Sing to the Lord and bless his name. Alleluia. **P.** Announce well his salvation from day to day. Alleluia, alleluia. **V.** When the Lord restores the captivity of his people, let Jacob rejoice and Israel exult. **P.** Announce. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son, etc. **P.** Announce.

**Hymn.** Let the assembly of Christ proclaim. See fol. 1.  
**Capitula.** God, whose eternity. See fol. 8.  
**Benediction.** Christ the Lord, who through what he assumed. See fol. 8.

**[Col. 0111A] Lauda.** All who await you will not be confounded. Alleluia. **P.** For you are my saving God. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. **V.** Guide me in your truth; teach me, for you are God my Savior. **P.** For you are. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father, etc. **P.** For you are God.

**Prayer.** Console, O Lord, those who await you. See fol. 40.

# Monday of the Sixth Week

## At Matins

**Antiphon.** Lord, why have they multiplied?

**Prayer.** They have multiplied, O Lord. See fol. 8.

**Antiphon.** Behold, I will bring forth my son, the Orient, says the Lord. **P.** For the stone which I placed before Jesus has seven eyes in it. **V.** For my hand will help him, and my arm will strengthen him. **P.** For the stone which I placed. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father. **P.** For the stone which I placed.

**Prayer.** God the Father, who caused your Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, to rise in the flesh at the time of his Incarnation: grant us that, when he comes to judgment, our heart may bloom again at the sight of him, and that we may obtain the gift of consolation from the joys of his vision. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

**Antiphon.** The coming of the Lord has been prepared like the dawn. **P.** And he will come to us like the early rain and the latter rain. **V.** All nations, clap your hands; shout joyfully to God with a voice of exultation. **P.** And he will come to us. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father, etc. **P.** And he will come.

**Prayer.** We know that your rising, Christ the Lord, was prepared at dawn; therefore we ask you: you who rose upon the earth as the early rain and the latter rain, water the soil of our heart with the unfailing rains of your blessing, so that we who devoutly receive the feast of your first coming may be saved by the manifestation of your second coming. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy, our God, etc.

**Third Antiphon.** The Lord has raised up the Just One from the east. **P.** He will give nations into his presence. **P.** And he will possess kings. **V.** Great is our Lord, and great is his power, and of his wisdom there is no number. **P.** He will give into his presence. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father, etc. **P.** And he will possess kings.

**Prayer.** God the Father, who raises up the Just One from the east: grant us that, in the embrace of him whom you sent for our redemption, our souls may revive; and that, by your favor, we may deserve to be participants in the Just One, who is Just without sharing in another’s justice. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**R.** Jerusalem, your salvation will soon come. **P.** Why are you consumed with sorrow? Is there no king for you, or has your counselor perished? **P.** Because sorrow has bent you down like a woman in labor, I will save you and renew you; do not fear. **V.** Behold, I will call my servant and place my words in his mouth, so that he may plant the heavens and establish the earth; and he says to Zion. **P.** Why are you consumed with sorrow? **V.** Glory and honor. **P.** Because sorrow has bent you down.

**Prayer.** Son of God, God, who, making yourself heard from the ends of the earth, appeared in the flesh to the world: restore yourself as the reward of our faith, so that we who proclaim your wondrous work may be enriched with that reward which is before you. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

Everything else that follows until the end of Matins is to be said as on Monday of the first week, fol. 8, except the prophecy, which is said from the preceding Sixth Sunday, fol. 40. At Vespers, as above on Monday.

# On the Vigil of the Nativity of the Lord

## At Matins

**[Col. 0112B] Antiphon.** Wash me, O Lord, from my iniquity, and cleanse my heart from my sins. Psalm L.

**Prayer.** God, Son of God. See fol. 3.

**Antiphon.** A rod will go forth from the root of Jesse. **P.** And a flower will rise from his root, and the Spirit of the Lord will rest upon him, the sevenfold Spirit of wisdom. **V.** The Lord will send forth the rod of your strength from Zion; rule in the midst of your enemies. **V.** And a flower from the root. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father, etc. **P.** And a flower.

**Prayer.** O rod coming forth from the root of Jesse, save the people who believe in you, and pour the sevenfold Spirit into them, so that you who came to be born on earth for salvation may show your glorious name in those who beseech you. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

**[Col. 0112C] Antiphon.** Attend, nations, and hear; listen with your ears. Let the earth hear, and its fullness, and all its offspring. **P.** For the Lord our Savior has come. **V.** All nations, clap your hands; shout joyfully to God with a voice of exultation. **P.** For the Lord our Savior. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son, etc. **P.** For the Lord our Savior.

**Prayer.** Lord Jesus Christ, make us draw near to you; grant us the gift of your mercy, so that we who await the presence of your face may escape the torments due to our merits. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

**Antiphon.** Behold, the Word will proceed from the throne of God; confess the Lord and speak praise to him. **P.** For he comes, and the day of the Lord is great and exceedingly glorious. **V.** He sends forth his word and melts it; his spirit blows, and the waters flow. **P.** For he has come. **V.** Glory and honor. **P.** For he has come.

**Prayer.** O only Word proceeding from the throne of God the Father, save the children of human beings, so that when that great day of your coming arrives, we who confess and praise you may be rescued from eternal punishments through what we now believe concerning you. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**R.** Behold, a Prince will rise for us from the seed of Judah, and the Lord of all nations will appear; the glory of his kingdom will be revealed in the heights to crush the power of his enemies. **P.** And he will give rest to all who fear him. **V.** I have spoken, called him, and brought him. **P.** And he will give rest. **V.** Glory and honor. **P.** And he will give.

**Prayer.** We bless you, O God, our Redeemer, who deigned to be born from the seed of Judah; and we ask that no obstacle may prevent us from your service. May all who confess you, Lord, feel themselves enriched by the gift of your indulgence. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

The Canticle and everything else that follows until the end of Matins are to be said as on Wednesday of the first week of Advent, fols. 11 and 12, except the prophecy, “The Lord spoke to Ahaz,” etc., which is said from the preceding Sixth Sunday, fol. 40.

# On the Nativity of Our Lord Jesus Christ

## [Col. 0113] At Vespers

**Antiphon.** I have prepared a lamp for my Christ; I will clothe his enemies with confusion. **P.** But upon him my holiness will flourish. **V.** The Lord swore to David in truth, and he will not withdraw from him: “From the fruit of your womb I will place upon my throne.” **P.** Upon him. **V.** And I will make him firstborn, highest among the kings of the earth. **P.** Upon him. **V.** And I will be a father to him, and he will be a son to me. **P.** Upon him.

**Prayer.** With the evening praises already offered, Lord, we now prepare a lamp for your Christ, our Lord and God, so that we may be filled with the fruit of righteousness for grace and hold the word of life for glory. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Sono.** In the splendors of the holy ones; from the womb, before the morning star, I begot you. Alleluia. **V.** The Lord has sworn, and he will not repent: You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek. **V.** The Lord at your right hand has shattered kings on the day of his wrath. He will judge among the nations; he will fill the ruins; he will crush many heads in the broad earth. He lives from the torrent on the way; therefore he has lifted up his head.

**Antiphon.** Hear, house of David: the Lord will give you a sign. **P.** Behold, a virgin will conceive and bear a son, and you will call his name Emmanuel. **V.** Hear this, all nations; listen with your ears, you who inhabit the world. **P.** Behold, the Virgin will conceive. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father, etc. **P.** Behold, the Virgin will conceive.

**Prayer.** Lord, who hastening toward salvation appointed that the sign of the house of David should be born of a Virgin for the aid of the human race: grant us that the life brought forth through Mary’s birth may be the eternal redemption of your Church; so that we may conceive in our heart and always bring forth from our mouth the very one whom she carried in her womb and brought forth in childbirth. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon.** Lift up a sign for the peoples. Behold, the Lord has made himself heard to the ends of the earth. Say to the daughter of Zion: **P.** Behold, your Savior comes, and his reward is with him. **V.** All nations, clap your hands; shout joyfully to God with a voice of exultation. **P.** Behold, your Savior comes. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father, etc. **P.** Behold, your Savior comes.

**Prayer.** Lord Jesus Christ, you made known the rising of your Nativity by the sign of a star and taught the ends of the earth to look upon the raised sign of faith: now, raised up from heaven, look upon the cause of your Incarnation, so that because it was necessary for us that you become human, we may have your support, confessing you as both human and God. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy, etc.

**Antiphon.** Drop down dew, you heavens, from above, and let the clouds rain the Just One; let the earth be opened and bring forth the Savior. **P.** And let righteousness arise at the same time; I, the Lord, have created him. **V.** The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament announces the works of his hands. **P.** And let righteousness arise. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father, etc. **P.** And let righteousness arise.

**Lauda.** His power—and there will be no end to his peace. Alleluia. **P.** He will sit upon the throne of David, to set it right. **P.** And he will sit in truth forever. Alleluia, alleluia. **V.** Great is our Lord, and great is his power; and of his wisdom there is no number. **P.** He will sit upon the throne of David. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father, etc. **P.** And he will sit.

**Hymn.**

Come, Redeemer of the nations,  
show forth the Virgin’s childbirth;  
let every age marvel:  
such a birth befits God.

Not from human seed,  
but from mysterious breath,  
the Word of God became flesh,  
and the fruit of the womb flowered.

The Virgin’s womb swells,  
the barriers of modesty remain;  
the banners of virtue shine;  
God moves within the temple.

Proceeding from his chamber,  
the royal hall of modesty,  
a giant of twofold substance,  
he eagerly runs his course.

His coming forth is from the Father;  
his return is to the Father;  
his descent reaches even to the underworld,  
his return to the seat of God.

Equal to the eternal Father,  
gird yourself with the trophy of the flesh;  
strengthen forever  
the weakness of our body with power.

Now your manger shines,  
and the night breathes forth a new light;  
no night can obscure it,  
and it shines with enduring faith.

He endured lying in hay;  
he did not shun the manger;  
and he was fed with a little milk,  
he through whom not even a bird hungers.

The choir of heavenly beings rejoices,  
and the angels sing to God;  
and the Shepherd, Creator of all,  
is openly revealed to shepherds.

Glory to you, O Lord,  
who were born of the Virgin,  
with the Father and the Holy Spirit,  
through everlasting ages.

Amen.

**Supplication.** Let us humbly implore the mercy of God the almighty Father, that he may graciously deign to justify us through the grace of his Christ, our Lord Jesus Christ.

Grant this, eternal and almighty God. Kyrie, eleison. **R.** Christe, eleison. Kyrie, eleison.

**Capitula.** Drop dew from above, O heavens, prophetically announcing Christ, and let the clouds rain the Just One, while all his saints proclaim his coming. Let the earth be opened, so that, when the angel speaks, the Virgin may conceive and bear the Savior. We therefore ask and entreat you, almighty Father, that this dew which comes from you may bring healing to the sick; and grant that this rain of the morning season may water the arid ground of our age, so that, infused with such great grace, it may wash away past wrongdoing and pour the eternal light of righteousness into believers. Moreover, may we, unharmed, behold the presence of this same Son of yours, our Lord, and meet his heavenly company with rejoicing, so that we may joyfully sing beforehand this song of gladness:

“Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord; the Lord God has shone upon us. His coming has redeemed us, and his Nativity has enlightened us. Coming, he sought out the lost and enlightened those placed in darkness.”

Grant, therefore, almighty Father, that we may celebrate the day of his Nativity with such profound devotion that we may experience the day of judgment as most gentle; and that, as we have come to know his kindness in redemption, so we may experience his mercy as tender in judgment.

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. See fol. 2.

**Benediction.** May our Lord Jesus Christ bless you, who long ago appeared gloriously on this day to the shepherds in the manger. **R.** Amen. May he himself protect and defend us in all things, who in mercy assumed human infancy for us. **R.** Amen. May he who is our Lord and Redeemer himself deign graciously to preserve us forever. **R.** Amen.

Through the mercy of our God himself.

**Lauda.** Before he firmly established the mountains beneath the heavens, I was with him, ordering all things; and I rejoiced when the world was completed. **P.** I am he with whom the Father rejoiced daily. Alleluia, alleluia. **V.** Then I said: Behold, I come; at the beginning of the book it is written concerning me, that I should do your will. **P.** I am he with whom the Father. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son, etc. **P.** I am he with whom the Father.

**[Col. 0116A] Prayer.** Bless, O Lord, the crown. See below.

## At Matins

**Antiphon.** Salvation belongs to the Lord, and your blessing, O Lord, is upon your people. Psalm III.

**Prayer.** You are salvation, O Lord, and salvation belongs to you. We rejoice that it has been bestowed upon us, and we ask you to bestow it upon us until the end. Pour out, we ask, your blessing upon your people, so that the curse of punishment may be removed from us, and the fruit of righteousness and joy may grow rich within us. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

**Antiphon.** On the day of our distinguished solemnity. **P.** Bless, O God, the crown of the year of your goodness, so that your fields may be filled with abundance. **V.** A hymn is due to you, O God, in Zion, and a vow will be paid to you in Jerusalem. **P.** Bless, O God. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son, etc. **P.** Bless, O God.

**Prayer.** Bless, O Lord, the crown of the year of your goodness, so that minds may shine with an abundance of teaching and the fields may grow rich with the abundance of your gifts. May substance therefore be granted to us together with your grace, so that the flesh, nourished by crops, and the soul, fed by divine virtues, may rejoice together. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon.** I was watching, and behold, with the clouds of heaven there came one like a son of man. **P.** And dominion, honor, and a kingdom were given to him; every people, tribe, and tongue serves him. **P.** His dominion is an eternal dominion, which will not be taken away, and his kingdom will not be destroyed. **V.** And he will rule from sea to sea and from the river to the ends of the earth. **P.** And dominion was given to him. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son, etc. **P.** His dominion is a dominion.

**Prayer.** Only-begotten Son of God the Father, who are declared the Son of Man when the Prophet sees you in the clouds of heaven, and to whom the Father has granted dominion and a kingdom, having subjected all things to your power: make us your kingdom, granting us perpetual citizenship, so that, always panting with equal desires for the coming kingdom, we may deserve to become co-heirs. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon.** Behold, I announce to you great joy, which will be for all the people: today he has been born for us. **P.** The Savior of the world, who is Christ the Lord; he will reign in the city of David, he will be wise, and there will be no end to his kingdom. **V.** The stone which the builders rejected has become the cornerstone. **P.** The Savior of the world, who is Christ. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son, etc. **P.** The Savior of the world, who is Christ.

**Prayer.** With you favoring us, may the great joy be announced to us through the ministry of the holy angel, a joy that may belong to the Christian people throughout the whole world. For Christ the Lord has been born today as salvation for all, and as the eternal Savior in the city of David, which is the Church. In it he will also reign without end, while he guards and governs it to the end. Grant, therefore, that he may make it entirely his kingdom, while he extends it throughout the world and joins it without end to the eternity of heavenly beings. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**R.** Today, O Jerusalem, the Prince and Savior of all has been born for you; at his command the powers of heaven will be moved. He will reign forever, and his glory will be with the peace of the earth. **P.** In the heights he is proclaimed by the angels. **V.** The Lord has reigned; he has clothed himself with beauty. The Lord has clothed himself with strength and girded himself. **P.** In the heights. **V.** The liftings of the sea are marvelous; the Lord on high is marvelous. **P.** By the angels. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son, etc. **P.** In the heights.

**Prayer.** Make us rejoice, O Lord, in the vision of that blessed Jerusalem and be raised up in perpetual delight in her embrace; so that, in whose womb the multitude of the saints dwells, we too may deserve to share her bosom. May your only-begotten Son, truly the Prince and Savior of all, at whose command the powers of heaven will be moved, reign together with us always in such gentleness that he may adapt our mouths to the praise of his name with the words of his wisdom; so that here he may mercifully help the miserable, and afterward, remaining in his kingdom, may be a consolation to the redeemed. Let the response be made: Amen.

Through your mercy, our God. May the Lord be always with you. **R.** And with you.

**Antiphon.** The voice of the Lord rendering recompense to his enemies: before she was in labor, she gave birth; and before her delivery came, she bore a male child. Who has heard such a thing, or who has seen anything like it? **P.** Shall I, who make others give birth, not give birth myself? says the Lord. Shall I, who grant generation to others, be barren? says the Lord our God. **V.** The voice of the Lord is in power; the voice of the Lord is in majesty. **P.** Shall I, who make others give birth. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son, etc. **P.** Shall I, who make others.

**Prayer.** Almighty God the Father, who by your voice render recompense to the enemies of our soul, and before you uttered the Word from yourself had already begotten that very Word through a new order of birth, and before the time of your delivery arrived had indeed generated a male child: who could ever say that he had heard such a thing, or think that he had seen anything like it, when it was proved that God had begotten God and light had brought forth light? Grant to us, your lowly servants, that you who grant fertility in giving birth to others may yourself bring forth the conception of grace within us; so that the barrenness arising from the defect of our fruitlessness may, with your grace cooperating, overflow within us in greater abundance. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon.** I, the firstborn, came forth before every creature. **P.** I made light arise in the heavens. I dwell in the heights, and my throne will appear upon a pillar of cloud. **V.** The Lord said to me: You are my Son; today I have begotten you. **P.** I made light arise in the heavens.

**Prayer.** True Wisdom of God the Father, who came forth before every creature from the citadel of that invisible Begetter, for we believe that you brought it about in heaven that light might arise, battling with a sword-like flame [*rhompheali* is uncertain]: you who were then present as creator when things were being made, appear merciful as their rewarder in us. And because we understand that you dwelt on high before the world existed, may we be free from our filth, so that, after the likeness of the lawful pillar upon which you declare that your throne appeared, you may likewise make us, your suppliants, like it in all things, so that, made glad by both gifts, you may cause us to remain unharmed with your saints. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon.** Before the hills I was brought forth; the earth had not yet been made. **P.** When he prepared the heavens, I was there; when he enclosed the boundaries with the sea and established a law for the waters, I was there. **V.** Then I said: Behold, I come; at the beginning of the book it is written concerning me, that I should do your will. **P.** When he prepared the heavens. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son, etc. **P.** When he prepared the heavens.

**Prayer.** Teaching of God, Wisdom of the Father, before the hills and the mass of the mountains, before the earth had yet been balanced on an even scale, while the Father was already preparing the peoples: when you were already there, when he enclosed the sea with fixed boundaries and established a law for the waters, you yourself existed in the nature of the one Godhead. Be present to your suppliants, so that the mass of committed sins, by which we are more harshly oppressed, may by the right hand of your mercy be reduced to nothing; and so guide the sails of your protection for us voyaging on the stream of this age that, crossing the sea, you may always lift us to the heights through the wood of your Cross. Let the response be made: Amen.

**[Col. 0118C] R.** On this day the Savior of Israel came forth to free all captives; he illuminated the blind and caused the deaf to hear. The mountains and all the hills will produce shoots. **P.** And those who sit in darkness will cry out and say: Lord, appear over us, the splendor of your glory. **V.** The people who sat in darkness saw a great light; for those dwelling in the region of the shadow of death, light has risen. **P.** And those who. **V.** Glory and honor. **P.** And those who.

**Prayer.** Today the light of the world came forth; today the salvation of the age shone out; today the Savior of Israel descended from the region of heaven to rescue all the captives whom the ancient enemy, the robber, had taken captive through the first man’s sin; and, with grace going before, to restore light to blind minds and hearing to the deaf. Because of the benefits of so great a mystery, the mountains and hills rejoice, and the very elements of the world sing this melody on this day with unspeakable joy. For this reason, let us humbly beseech the clemency of the merciful Redeemer with a groaning prayer, so that we who are wrapped in the darkness of our sins may immediately be cleansed through the heart’s acclamation; and, when he appears within us, may the splendor of his glory shine more joyfully and abundantly in our hearts, and may the joys of salvation grow sweet without end. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy, etc.

**Antiphon.** Before every creature I came forth from the mouth of the Most High; before the morning star arose, I existed; before he spread the fields across the plain and raised the mountains on high, I existed. **P.** With whom he rejoiced daily, while he delighted in the completed world. **V.** For I have known how great the Lord is, and our God above all gods. **P.** With whom he rejoiced. **V.** Glory and honor, etc. **P.** With whom.

**Prayer.** Lord Jesus Christ, who, coming forth from the mouth of the Most High before every creature, established the fabric of the world by wondrous ordering: be present to your Church, which you deigned to gather from the whole world, so that just as you are recognized as the world’s Creator, so you may be known in all things and through all things as the Church’s Savior. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy, our God, etc.

**Antiphon.** The Lord will raise up the King of heaven, who will not be shaken forever. **P.** And his kingdom will not be given to another people; he will strike and crush all kingdoms, and he alone will stand forever. **V.** In his justice he will judge the poor of the people, and he will save the children of the poor; and he will humble the slanderer. **P.** And his kingdom will not be given to another people. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son, etc. **P.** And his kingdom.

**Prayer.** God the Father, who raised up Jesus Christ, your Son, coeternal and coequal with you, as King of heaven by showing him in the flesh: make us always follow his voice in faith and in deed, so that, hearing it without interruption with the hearing of our heart, we may deserve to share in his glory. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy, our God, etc.

**Antiphon.** Send forth the Lamb, O Lord, the Ruler of the earth, from the rock of the desert to the mountain of the daughter of Zion; and his throne will be prepared in mercy. **P.** And he will sit upon it in truth, in the tabernacle of David. **V.** O Lord, save us; O Lord, grant us prosperity. **P.** And he will sit upon it.

**Prayer.** Boundless Wisdom of God the Father, who are proved by the prophecies of the Prophets to be the Son and Lord of David: you who sit upon the Father’s throne and rule from the rock of the desert to the mountain of the daughter of Zion, the house of Jacob—that is, the Church—extend the reins of your protection to all of us who abide in her, so that we may deserve to live with you without end; so that we may live forever upon your throne, whose kingdom we fear has no end; and you who possess one name in the Trinity, with the Father and with the Holy Spirit, through ages of ages. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy, our God, etc.

**R.** Let us receive the kingdom of our holy Most High God and possess it immediately forever and ever, until the Ancient of Days comes, for the time has come for the greatness of the kingdom to be given to every people. **P.** It is above all heaven, and all the kings of the earth will come and obey him. **V.** His power is eternal power, and his kingdom is an everlasting kingdom. **P.** It is above all. **V.** Glory, etc. Repeat: **R.** Let us receive the kingdom of our God.

### Prayer

Lord Jesus Christ, who are ineffable joy to Christians, whose power and peace will have no end, make us receive your kingdom and possess it, so that the dominion of your rule may remain continually over us, and its greatness endure forever. Thus, finding nothing in us that is not yours, remove it, and make us wholly and in every respect yours, so that nothing in us may hinder your authority or resist your peace. May you alone possess us, who, King of kings and Lord of lords, reign now and throughout all ages.  
**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

### Antiphon

A little child is born for us, and a Son is given to us, and authority has been placed upon his shoulders. **P.** And his name shall be called Angel of Great Counsel, Wonderful, Counselor, Mighty God, Ruler, Prince of Peace, Father of the age to come. His dominion shall be multiplied, and there shall be no end of peace. **V.** And there shall be firmness in the earth upon the heights of the mountains, and his fruit shall be exalted above Lebanon; and it shall flower from the city like the grass of the earth. **P.** And his name shall be called. **V.** Glory. **P.** And his name shall be called.

### Prayer

A little child is born for us, and a Son is given to us: you who were the perfect Son from the Father became, for us, a little child from your Mother; there immeasurable, and here small; remaining in the bosom of the Father, carried in the womb of the Mother. While your unchangeable divinity and your singular humanity remain, because in both you subsist as one and the same, in the one creating us and in the other redeeming us.  
**R.** Amen.

Through you, our Lord, who with the Father and the Holy Spirit are one God throughout all ages of ages.  
**R.** Amen.

May the Lord be with you.  
**R.** And with your spirit.

## At Lauds

### At the Canticle

**Antiphon.** The lion’s cub of Judah, from the stock, son: thus you have ascended; resting, you have lain down like a lion, and like a lion’s cub whom no one will dare to rouse.

### Canticle (Genesis, chapter 49)

Jacob called his sons, *and said to them:*

Gather together, that I may announce to you what will come to you *in the last days.*

Gather together and listen, sons of Jacob; *listen to Israel your father.*

Reuben, my firstborn, you are my strength and the beginning of my sorrow: *first in gifts, greater in authority. You have poured yourself out like water; you shall not increase, because you went up upon your father’s bed and defiled his couch.*

Simeon and Levi are his brothers: *weapons of iniquity are their warfare.*

Let my soul not enter their counsel, *nor let my glory be in their assembly,*

For in their anger they killed a man, *and in their will they undermined a wall.*

Cursed be their anger, because it was stubborn, and their indignation, because it was harsh: *I shall divide them in Jacob and scatter them in Israel.*

Judah, your brothers shall praise you; your hands shall be upon the necks of your enemies, and the sons of your father shall bow down to you. *Judah is a lion’s cub; you have gone up to the prey, my son.*

Resting, you have lain down like a lion, *and like a lioness—who will rouse him?*

The scepter shall not be taken from Judah, *nor the ruler from his loins,*

Until he comes who is to be sent, *and he himself shall be the expectation of the nations.*

Binding his colt to the vine, *and his donkey, my son, to the choice vine.*

He shall wash his robe in wine, *and his cloak in the blood of the grape.*

His eyes are more beautiful than wine, *and his teeth whiter than milk.

Zebulun shall dwell on the shore of the sea, *reaching to the station of ships, as far as Sidon.*

Issachar is a strong ass lying down between the boundaries. *He saw that rest was good, and that the land was excellent;*

And he bent his shoulder to bear, *and became a servant under tribute.*

Dan shall judge his people *like another tribe of Israel.*

Let Dan become a serpent on the road, a horned serpent on the path, biting the horse’s hooves, *so that its rider may fall backward. I shall await your salvation, O Lord.*

Gad, girded, shall fight before him, *and he himself shall be girded from behind.*

Asher’s bread shall be rich, *and he shall provide delicacies for kings.*

Naphtali is a doe let loose, *giving words of beauty.*

Joseph is a growing son, a growing son *and handsome in appearance.*

The daughters ran upon the wall. *But they embittered him and quarreled with him, envying him and having arrows.*

His bow remained firm, and the bonds of his arms and hands were loosened by the hand of the Mighty One of Jacob; *from there the shepherd went forth, the shepherd of Israel.*

The God of your father shall be your helper, *and the Almighty shall bless you.*

With blessings from heaven above, with blessings from the abyss lying below, *with blessings of breasts and womb.*

The blessings of your father were strengthened by the blessings of his father, *until the desire of the everlasting hills should come.*

Let them come upon the head of Joseph, *and upon the crown of the Nazarite among his brothers.*

Benjamin is a ravenous wolf: *in the morning he shall eat the prey, and in the evening he shall divide the spoils.*

**P.** And like a lion’s cub.

Glory and honor to the Father, etc. **P.** A lion’s cub.

### Prayer

We have recognized you, Christ the Lord, as having been the lion’s cub in the house of Judah. We ask you with all our heart: you who appeared in the flesh, taking prey from the hand of the mighty, when you come to judgment, grant beforehand the mercy promised to the faithful.  
**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

### At the Canticle

**Antiphon.** My spirit rejoiced in God my Savior, because he regarded the lowliness of his servant; behold, from this time forward all generations shall call me blessed.

### Canticle (Luke, chapter 1)

My soul *magnifies the Lord,*

And my spirit rejoiced *in God my Savior.*

Because he regarded the lowliness of his servant; *behold, from this time forward all generations shall call me blessed.*

Because the Mighty One has done great things for me, *and holy is his name.*

And his mercy is from generation to generation *for those who fear him.*

He has shown strength with his arm; *he has scattered the proud in the thought of their heart.*

He has brought down the mighty from their throne, and exalted the lowly.

He has filled the hungry with good things, *and sent the rich away empty.*

He has received Israel his servant, *remembering his mercy,*

As he spoke to our fathers, *to Abraham and to his seed forever.*

**P.** Because he regarded the lowliness.

Glory and honor to the Father, etc. **P.** My spirit rejoiced.

### Prayer

Lord Jesus Christ, great God from the Father, you deigned to be born a small human being for us, so that through you the world, made through you, might unquestionably be saved. Be favorable and have mercy on us; cleanse us from worldly contaminations, and establish us as pure in this world. You came not to judge but to save, so that, born a little child for us and given to us as a Son, we might deserve in you both the beginning of regeneration and the gift of adoption.  
**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

### At the Benedictus

**Antiphon.** To you alone, God, be honor, glory, strength, and power throughout all ages of ages.

### Canticle

Blessed are you, Lord God of our fathers. See folio 6.

### Song

The Lord said to me: You are my Son; today I have begotten you. Alleluia. **V.** Ask of me, and I will give you the nations as your inheritance, and your possession to the ends of the earth. You shall rule them with an iron rod, and like a potter’s vessel you shall shatter them. And now, kings, understand; be instructed, all you who judge the earth. But I have been appointed king by him over Zion, his holy mountain. **P.** I have begotten you. Alleluia.

### Praise

Praise the Lord from the heavens. Alleluia. 51 [Col. 0122D] Praise him in the heights. Alleluia. Psalm 148.

### Reading from the Prophet Isaiah (chapter 9)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

At the first time the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali were relieved; but in the latter time the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations, was burdened. The people who sat in darkness saw a great light; for those dwelling in the land of the shadow of death, light has risen. You multiplied the nation, but you did not magnify its joy. They shall rejoice before you as people rejoice at harvest, as victors exult when they divide the spoils. For you have broken the yoke of its burden, the rod upon its shoulder, and the scepter of its oppressor, as on the day of Midian. For every violent plundering with tumult, and every garment mixed with blood, shall be burned, and shall become food for the fire. For a little child is born for us, and a Son is given to us, and authority has been placed upon his shoulders. And his name shall be called Wonderful, Counselor, Mighty God, Ruler, Father of the age to come, Prince of Peace. His dominion shall be multiplied, and there shall be no end to his peace. He shall sit upon the throne of David and over his kingdom, to establish and strengthen it in judgment and righteousness, from now and forever. The zeal of the Lord of hosts shall do this.  
**R.** Amen.

### Hymn

Come, Redeemer of the nations. See folio 45.

### Supplication

Let us humbly implore the mercy of God the Almighty Father, that he may graciously deign to justify us by the grace of his Christ, our Lord Jesus Christ.  
**R.** Grant this, eternal almighty God.

Lord, have mercy. Christ, have mercy. Lord, have mercy.

### Chapter

Rest of the angels and of all the saints, Lord Jesus Christ, grant your people rest today on this most sacred recurring feast of your Nativity, so that in you they may rest from sins and the worst burdens. May they bless you together with all creation and receive your blessing in all things and through all things. May you never allow those whom you came to free from the curse to be deprived of the gift of your blessing, but, by blessing you continually, may they remain blessed forever.

Our Father. And lead us not. Delivered from evil. See folio 2.

### Praise

Before he prepared the firm foundations. See folio 46.

### Blessing

May our Lord Jesus Christ bless you. Folio 46.

Let the priest say: May the Lord be always with you.  
**R.** And with your spirit.

In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, let us complete this in peace.  
**R.** Thanks be to God.

## On the Feast of Saint Stephen, Protomartyr

### At Vespers

**Antiphon.** You crowned him, Lord, with glory and honor. **V.** You placed glory and great beauty upon him. **P.** Lord.

### Song

Guard me, Lord, as the apple of the eye, under the shadow of your wings. **P.** Hear, O God, my justice. Alleluia. **V.** Protect me from the face of the wicked who afflict me; my enemies have surrounded my soul. **P.** Hear, O God.

### Antiphon

Earth, do not conceal my blood, nor let my cry find a place of hiding in you. **P.** Behold, my judge is in heaven, and my witness is on high. **V.** Often they have fought against me from my youth, yet they could not prevail against me. **P.** Behold, my judge is in heaven. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father, etc. **P.** Behold, my judge is in heaven.

### Praise

Alleluia. My lips have been touched. **P.** And he opened my mouth, and I said: Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. **V.** I sought my Lord, and he heard me; and from all my tribulations he delivered me. **P.** And he opened my mouth. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father, etc. **P.** And he opened my mouth.

### Hymn

Christ is life, coming into the world,

Suffering at the setting of bitter death;

By the act of death, through the practice of mercy,

He grants life.

He lifted the wound by removing death;

By destroying the author of death, he rises;

Returning to the right hand of the Father, he reigns

Upon the heavenly throne.

Following him, Stephen, the first minister,

Honored by the title of the lot assigned to him,

Which the gracious Spirit of the Lord,

Breathing within him, gave.

He goes bound by the Lord’s example,

Innocent, covered by false witnesses,

The holy man bearing the wicked

Words of judges.

With heavenly speech he refutes the malicious,

And steadfastly proves the false by reason,

Those who are always unworthy to believe

In the Lord of heaven.

Stoned by a shower of stones, he endures;

Paul is present, and the chief of the stone-throwers guards

The garments, so that he may return them free for the blow,

Bloody with slaughter.

He endures the rage of profane death,

Full of every devotion of heart;

For his enemies he seeks pardon,

Moved by a grateful heart.

He first taught blessed human beings,

With upright heart and faithful spirit,

To lay down their limbs, slain by the weapons,

In faith in Christ.

We beseech you with tears, blessed first

Martyr and fellow citizen of the just,

Illustrious heir, mighty in the bright region

Of heaven.

Quickly forgive our offense;

Take away sickness, grant salvation;

Pierce the enemy, lift sorrow,

Death having been subdued.

May the choir sing glory and resound;

May it speak, sing, and proclaim glory;

May the stars cry out to the one name

Of the triune Godhead alone.

**R.** Amen.

### Supplication

Let us humbly implore the mercy of God the almighty Father, that he may graciously deign to justify us by the grace of his Christ, our Lord Jesus Christ, and through the intercession of his holy martyr Stephen.  
**R.** Grant this, eternal almighty God.

Lord, have mercy. Christ, have mercy. Lord, have mercy.

### Chapter

O God, to whom your Church gave Saint Stephen, the first martyr, as the first sheaf of its harvest, and displayed him as the first offering of a new confession, a herald who showed the fruit of ripening faith: grant to the whole assembly, through the intercession of this martyr, that he may aid your Church by his support, which he adorned by his ministry, and cherish by his patronage the Church he built by his example.

Our Father. Delivered from evil. Bow down for the blessing. May the Lord be with you.  
**R.** And with your spirit.

### Blessing

May the Lord Jesus Christ, who made the martyr Stephen the first follower of his passion, grant us, by the example of his passion, to carry victory over the world.  
**R.** Amen.

May he also grant us, through the prayer of his martyr, a similar strength to possess his love and to overcome adversities with equal endurance.  
**R.** Amen.

So that, instructed by the example of the Redeemer and invited by the martyr, we may receive the fullness of our redemption.  
**R.** Amen.

Through his mercy.

### Praise

Blessed is the man who fears the Lord. Alleluia. **P.** He shall greatly desire his commandments. Alleluia, alleluia. **V.** His seed shall be mighty upon the earth; the generation of the upright shall be blessed. **P.** He shall greatly desire his commandments. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father, etc. **P.** He shall greatly desire his commandments.

### Prayer

Lord Jesus Christ. See below on this folio.

## At Matins

**Antiphon.** Lord, you will open my lips. **P.** And my mouth shall proclaim your praise. Psalm: Have mercy on me, O God.

### Prayer

Let our lips rejoice, Lord, in proclaiming the truth, so that they may not turn back to the empty speech of falsehood. Let our tongue speak the judgment of truth, so that it may most readily praise your Christ, the true judge. And let your commandments continually turn over in our heart, so that our steps may not be overthrown by deceitful snares.  
**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

### Antiphon 1

My enemies stoned me. **P.** And the fissures of their stones shall be a testimony against them when I come before the judgment seat to plead for their sins. **V.** I believed, and therefore I spoke; but I was humbled exceedingly. **P.** And the fissures of the stones. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father, etc. **P.** From the fissures of the stones.

### Prayer

Lord Jesus Christ, who so enriched the soul of blessed Stephen with your gift that he not only followed the example of your Passion but also received the lesson of patience: he pleaded for his enemies and did not yield to those raging against him; strong in enduring wounds, strong in not returning insults, strong while being stoned by the wicked, stronger while praying for those who stoned him. Therefore, he who, forgetful of vengeance, prayed for those who stoned him, may, mindful of charity, not be absent from those who plead with you.  
**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

### Antiphon 2

With one accord they rushed upon Stephen. **P.** And false witnesses stoned him as he called upon the Lord and said: Lord Jesus, receive my spirit. **V.** The enemy shall accomplish nothing against him, and the son of iniquity shall do him no harm. **P.** And false witnesses. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father, etc. **P.** And false witnesses stoned him.

### Prayer

The attack made by the crowd of persecutors could not disturb the constancy of your martyr Stephen, Christ the Lord, when, through the credulity given to false witnesses, he laid aside the garments of the flesh, yet did not lose the confession of his mouth by which he believed in you; even when stoned, he prayed to you as God to receive his spirit. Therefore we ask and beseech you to repay us with that merciful grace with which you crowned him after the stones; and you who received his spirit into eternal glory, we ask you, being propitious, to remove punishments from us.  
**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

### Antiphon

They were stoning Stephen, who were in the council, and they gazed upon him. **P.** His face was like the face of an angel of God standing among them. **V.** Preserve me, Lord, because I have hoped in you; save me, my God. **P.** His face was like the face. **V.** Glory and honor, etc. **P.** His face was like the face.

### Prayer

Lord Jesus Christ, who so glorified the face of your most blessed martyr Stephen in the council of those stoning him that, by those who stoned him, his stoned face was seen to be angelic, while you showed that patience was adorned by a teacher surpassing him: grant us to deserve to be raised from this to the reward of eternity.  
**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**R.** Upon the heap of stones my soul is joyful, and for my enemies I have prayed to God; therefore I shall harvest my fruits in peace. **P.** And I shall serve in the presence of the Lord from the good things he has bestowed upon me. **V.** What shall I repay for all the things he has bestowed upon me? I shall receive the cup of salvation. **P.** And I shall serve. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father, etc. **P.** And I shall serve.

### Prayer

Lord Jesus Christ, who adorned the soul of your most blessed martyr Stephen with so great a grace of gifts that he rejoiced upon the heap of stones and pleaded with you for his enemies, asking that you spare them: fill our hearts with the gift of graces and with the unfading gift of virtues, so that, through the intervention of your martyr, we may always serve in your presence from the good things you bestow upon us, so that here we may be enlarged in the work of holiness and afterward harvest our fruits in peace.  
**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

## At Lauds

### At the Canticle

**Antiphon.** I called upon the name of the Lord; give greatness to your God. His works are true, and all his ways are judgments.

Canticle: Hear, O heaven. See folio 4.

### At the Benedictus

**Antiphon.** The Lord’s blessing hastens toward the reward of the just.

Canticle: Blessed are you, Lord God. Folio 6.

### Song

Guard me, Lord. See folio 51.

### Praise

Praise the Lord from the heavens. Alleluia. Praise him in the heights. Alleluia. Psalm 148.

### Prophecy: Reading from the Book of the Wisdom of Solomon (chapter 4)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

If the righteous man is overtaken by death, his soul shall be in refreshment. For venerable old age is not measured by length of time or counted by the number of years; the gray hairs of a person are understanding, and the age of old age is an undefiled life. Pleasing to God, he became beloved, and, living among sinners, he was transferred. He was taken away lest wickedness change his understanding or suffering deceive his soul. For the enchantment of frivolity obscures good things, and the instability of desire perverts an innocent mind. Brought to completion in a short time, he fulfilled many years, for his soul was pleasing to God; therefore he hastened to lead him out from the midst of iniquities. But the peoples saw and did not understand, nor did they lay such things to heart: that there is mercy with God and grace in his holy one, and regard for his chosen one.  
**R.** Amen.

### Hymn

Christ is life. Supplication: Let us pray for the mercy of God the Almighty Father. See folio 52.

### Chapter

Most blessed Stephen, Protomartyr, a new name shall be called for you, which the mouth of the Lord has named, so that, since you took death for him, you might receive through him a crown both in name and in virtue. First in martyrdom, first in reward; first in the court of the world, first in the court of heaven: here stoned for Christ, there crowned by Christ himself, may you rejoice. For him for whom you endured the most cruel punishment here, may you receive there the most precious crown. Therefore, you who were the Church’s first beginning, now be its constant patron, so that Christ may, at your prayer, be favorable to us—the Christ for whom you became a marvelous martyr.

Our Father. Delivered from evil.

### Praise

Blessed is the man who fears the Lord.

### Blessing

The Lord Jesus Christ, who, etc.

In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, let us complete this in peace.  
**R.** Thanks be to God. See folio 52.

## On the Feast of Saint John, Apostle and Evangelist

### At Vespers

### Praise

You have put on confession and beauty. **P.** Clothed in light as with a garment. **V.** Confession and beauty are before him; holiness and magnificence are in his sanctuary. **P.** Clothed in light.

### Song

I will give thanks to you, Lord, with my whole heart; I will recount your wonders. Alleluia. I will be glad and rejoice in you, Lord; I will sing to your name, O Most High. Alleluia.

### Antiphon

“I wish him to remain thus until I come,” said the Lord. **P.** This is the disciple who bears testimony concerning these things. **P.** And we know that his testimony is true. **P.** For my hand shall help him, and my arm shall strengthen him. **P.** This is the disciple. **V.** Glory. **P.** And we know.

### Praise

“I will love him with my whole heart,” says the Lord. **P.** And he shall be as the dew of Israel; he shall sprout like the lily and blossom. Alleluia, alleluia. **V.** And he shall be like a tree transplanted beside streams of water, which gives its fruit in its season. **P.** And he shall be. **V.** Glory, etc. **P.** And he shall be.

### Hymn

This chosen John, most prompt in loving,

An advocate for the everlasting grace of truth,

Receiving the reward of honor, obtains

Whatever he seeks.

By an imperial command he is consigned to be held on the island of Patmos [reading uncertain];

There he beholds mysteries poured forth from heaven,

And, marking profound and difficult things in his mind,

He recounts them.

He receives the Mother of God into his heart,

So that, as minister of truth, he may attend upon the Virgin,

Who, having borne God, alone ever remained

A virgin.

This man, reclining bodily upon the breast

Of the everlasting Godhead, drank in its innermost things,

And by the grace of the Spirit proclaimed

The truth.

When the Redeemer was drawn to the cross, he calls this man

The son of his mother; in turn he commands her to be his mother:

One in flesh, the other in spirit,

That they might remain sons.

Foreknowing his final hour, he then commands his servants

To dig a hollow in the earth, into which, reclining, he falls;

And, in death’s stead, rests, living through every age.

We ask you, we entreat you, holy Apostle of Christ:

Take away pestilence, remove the sore, and cherish the sick;

Drive out disease, strike down the enemy, and remove scandal.

May fire not scorch the earth; may the air not wound it;

May the sad heaven not pour forth storms for vengeance;

May wrath not utterly cast the world down into ruin.

May every sin fall away; may grace follow;

May all guilt be removed; may there be an abundance of salvation;

May every plague be driven away; may charity increase.

Glory be to God the Father; glory be to the Son.

To the abiding Paraclete be ever great glory,

Who is God and lives through all ages of ages.

Amen.

### Supplication

Let us humbly implore the mercy of God the Almighty Father, that he may graciously deign to justify us by the grace of his Christ, our Lord Jesus Christ, and through the intercession of Saint John, Apostle and Evangelist.  
**R.** Grant this, eternal almighty God.

Lord, have mercy. **R.** Christ, have mercy. Lord, have mercy.

### Chapter

Ineffable, Lord, are the streams from your breast, by which that disciple, beloved by you above the rest, reclining upon your bosom, deserved to be satisfied. We therefore beseech you that, our members having been put to death, we may always deserve to cling to your footsteps, so that through the intercession of this Saint John the fire of your love may so burn and consume us as to make us, wholly, a pleasing holocaust to you.

Our Father. Delivered from evil.

Bow down for the blessing.

May the Lord be with you.  
**R.** And with your spirit.

### Blessing

May Christ the Lord, who made the disciple beloved by him recline upon his breast, keep us unharmed in the bosom of mother Church.  
**R.** Amen.

And may he who moistened the soul of the reclining disciple with streams of grace flowing forth from his bosom command us to be comforted by the gift of an everlasting reward.  
**R.** Amen.

So that through him by whom this beloved disciple was made a virgin, sinners may be summoned, in their transformation, into the fellowship of the angels.  
**R.** Amen.

Through his mercy.

### Praise

Your bones shall sprout like willows. Alleluia. **P.** Beside flowing waters. Alleluia, alleluia. **V.** And he shall be like a tree that has been transplanted. **P.** Beside flowing waters. **V.** Glory. **P.** Beside.

### Prayer

Lord Jesus Christ, who [concerning] your most blessed Apostle John. See folio 55.

## At Matins

**Antiphon.** Lord, you will open my lips. **P.** And my mouth shall proclaim your praise. Psalm 50.

### Prayer

May our tongue praise you, Lord, by proclaiming your righteousnesses, and may our lips rejoice in the proclamation of truth, that they may not be dissolved in the empty speech of falsehood; so that, confessing you, with our sins forgiven, we may rejoice in you and, singing in the sacred company of the assembly of the righteous, become heirs of the blessed life.  
**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

### Antiphon 1

My flesh shall rest in hope. **P.** For you will not leave my soul in hell, nor give your holy one to see corruption. **V.** You have made known to me the ways of life; you shall fill me with gladness before your face, and delights at your right hand unto the end. **P.** For you will not leave. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father, etc. **P.** For you will not leave.

### Prayer

Christ, Son of God, who bestowed even in this life upon your virgin disciple the rewards of virginity, so that he might be able to raise the dying limbs from the lot of death—he who did not permit the incitements of deadly lust to rule in his members—be present to us through his prayers, so that, after the falls by which we wantonly lapse in this life, we may come to you with hearts and bodies cleansed.  
**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

### Antiphon 2

Your face shall be made bright as though clear. **P.** Your countenance shall rise like Lucifer; from the noonday portion life shall spring up for you. **V.** By day the sun shall not burn you, nor the moon by night. **P.** Your countenance. **V.** Glory and honor, etc. **P.** Your countenance.

### Prayer

Lord Jesus Christ, who neither forsake your most blessed Apostle John in the bonds of exile nor abandon him in the hollowed-out pit, grant us through his prayers that your mercy may so always cherish us that, under your protection, both here and forever we may everywhere possess the scepter of the everlasting kingdom.  
**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

### Antiphon 2

Guard my body from every defilement. **P.** Your fragrance, Lord, has stirred eternal desires within me. **V.** You have made known to me the ways of life, and you shall fill me with gladness before your face: delights are at your right hand unto the end. **P.** Your fragrance. **V.** Glory and honor, etc. **P.** Your fragrance.

### Prayer

Beloved by you, Lord Jesus Christ, he bore an ineffable testimony to the disciples, when he deserved wonderfully to set forth what we might marvel at, having received it from your breast. Therefore, may the beginning which he both knew by mystical faith and proclaimed in mystical words be in our mouth for the completion of virtue and the effect of pious action, so that we may be joined to you without end, whose power we magnificently confess.  
**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**R.** This man appeared most gentle among his people, burdened with old age and worthy of glory. **P.** This is he who prays for the people and for this city. **V.** This man consecrated the law of God Most High and was found faithful in temptation. **P.** This is he. **V.** Glory and honor, etc. Repeat **R.** This man.

### Prayer

Mindful of your commands, Lord Jesus Christ, by which you commanded us to share in the commemorations of the saints, we celebrate the titles of merit of your most blessed Apostle John, scattered throughout the world; he obtained by the privilege of holiness the crown which he merited by the interpretation of his name. Grant therefore, through his intervention, that we who venerate his praises in the observance of religion may more earnestly obtain his patronage.  
**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

### At the Canticle

**Antiphon.** The throne of glory, his inheritance, grants the desire of one who asks and shall bless the years of the righteous.

### Canticle (1 Kings 2)

My heart is strengthened in the Lord, *and my horn is exalted in God my Savior.*

My mouth is enlarged over my enemies; *I rejoice for myself in your holiness. For there is no other God like our God,*

Nor is there any righteous one besides you, Lord; *and there is no holy one besides you.*

Do not glory on high, and do not speak lofty things in pride; *nor let grand speech go forth from your mouth, for the Lord is a God of knowledge,*

God who prepares his own designs; *the bow of the mighty is weakened, and the weak are girded with strength.*

Those full of bread are diminished, *and the hungry have crossed the land.*

The barren has borne seven, *and she who abounded in children has become weak.*

God kills and gives life; *he leads down to hell and brings back.*

God makes poor and rich; *he humbles and exalts.*

He raises the needy from the earth, *and lifts the poor from the dunghill;*

And makes him sit with the princes of his people, *and shall give him the throne of glory as an inheritance.*

He grants the desire of one who asks and shall bless the years of the righteous, *for a man is not mighty by his own strength.*

For the holy Lord makes every adversary of his weak; *

Let not the wise glory in his wisdom, *nor the rich glory in his riches,*

Nor the strong glory in his strength; but let him glory in this: *he who glories, in knowing and understanding the Lord, in doing judgment and righteousness upon the earth.*

The Lord ascends into the heavens and thunders; *he himself judges the ends of the earth.*

He is mighty and gives strength to kings, *and exalts the horn of his Christ.*

Repeat the Antiphon.

### At the Benedictus

**Antiphon.** The Lord’s blessing hastens toward the reward of the righteous.

Canticle: Blessed are you, Lord God. See folio 6.

### Song

Before the angels I will sing to you, Lord. Alleluia. **V.** I will worship toward your holy temple and give thanks to your name, Lord. **P.** I will sing to you.

### Praise

Praise the Lord from the heavens. Alleluia. Praise him in the heights. Alleluia.

### Another Praise

Alleluia. His confession is above heaven and earth. Alleluia. He shall exalt the horn of his people. Alleluia. **V.** A hymn is for all his saints. Alleluia. Psalm 148.

### Reading from the Book of the Wisdom of Solomon (chapter 10)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

Wisdom led the righteous man by straight paths, showed him the kingdom of God, and gave him knowledge of the holy ones. She honored him in his labors and fulfilled his labors. She was present amid the fraud of those who surrounded him and made him honorable. She guarded him from enemies and protected him from seducers, and gave him a contest with the mighty so that he might conquer and know that wisdom is more powerful than all things. She did not forsake the righteous man when he was bound, but freed him from sinners. She descended with him into the pit and did not leave him in chains, until she brought him the scepter of a kingdom and power against those who oppressed him; she showed to be liars those who had defamed him and gave him eternal brightness.  
**R.** Amen.

### Hymn

This chosen John. See above at Vespers, folio 54. Supplication, as above.

### Chapter

Christ, Son of God, who granted that you, the Beginning which you yourself are, should be confessed in the mouth of the disciple beloved by you, so that his heart might ascend where no other was able: by the grace of your gift make our heart always dwell on high, so that, receiving from there the teaching of all truth, we may attain in future reward that which we have professed here by the mouth. 

Our Father. Delivered from evil. Folio 2.

Praise: Your bones shall sprout. Blessing: Christ the Lord, who is beloved. Folio 54.

In the name of the Lord.

## On the Slaughter of the Infants, or of the Holy Innocents

### At Vespers

### Praise

Light has risen in darkness for the upright in heart: the merciful and compassionate Lord. **V.** He made the way of the righteous straight and prepared the path of the saints. **P.** The merciful.

Let the priest say: May the Lord be always with you.  
**R.** And with your spirit.

### Song

The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and the torment of death shall not touch them. Alleluia. **V.** They seemed, in the eyes of the foolish, to have died; their departure was considered an affliction, but they are in peace. Alleluia.

Let the priest say: May the Lord be always with you.  
**R.** And with your spirit.

### Song

Alleluia. The righteous live forever.

**V.** And their reward is with the Lord. Alleluia, alleluia.

Let the priest say: May the Lord be with you.  
**R.** And with your spirit.

### Antiphon

These are they who follow the Lamb wherever he goes; these were purchased from among humanity as firstfruits for God and for the Lamb. **P.** And no deceit was found in their mouth, for they are without blemish before their God. **V.** But the righteous shall live forever, and their reward is with the Lord. **P.** And no deceit was found. **V.** Glory. **P.** And no deceit was found.

### Praise

These are they who did not defile their garment; they shall walk with me in white, because they are worthy. **P.** And whoever conquers shall be clothed in this way. Alleluia. In a white garment. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. **V.** And the righteous cried to the Lord when they were afflicted; he often delivered them from their necessities. **P.** And whoever conquers. **V.** Glory. **P.** And whoever conquers.

### Hymn

We sing of the God of the saints,

Singing the rewards of Christ,

Who, generous in the Holy Spirit,

Gave triumph to little children.

From the mouth of infants also,

By the perfect praise of the Lord,

The One powerful in all things

Destroyed all the arts of the Devil.

He who, by the goads of visions,

Stirred the mind of the wicked king,

Persuaded him that God,

The King and Lord, could be destroyed.

The Magi follow the sign

Of the star leading the way,

Which, by the rising of its light,

Served the eternal King.

Herod feared the newborn

King owed to Judea,

In which, though foreign by birth,

He feared that another would succeed him.

And, when the heavenly sign had been set forth,

Terrified by the Magi’s arrival on earth,

The blind man, seeking the cause

Of the whole matter of the world, did not understand.

At first, with gentle words,

He pretends that he himself rejoices,

Promising that he will adore

The newborn when they return and reveal him.

But after they had been warned by God;

Through deceit the earth vanished:

He attempts a monstrous crime, unknown to all the ages.

He had heard that Christ was to be born at Bethlehem according to the divine oracle; having heard the name of the city, he was unaware of the parent from whom he was born.

Calculating the time of the birth, the impious man orders boys under two years old, snatched from their mothers’ breasts, to be killed.

Those whom the Lord, destined to suffer at the appointed time, consecrated to himself as witnesses with everlasting praise, amid the mothers’ offered tears, showing that from tears sown certain joys will be reaped for future glory.

Remember, Author of salvation, that once, in being born from an undefiled Virgin, you took on the form of our body.

Glory to you, O Lord, who were born of a Virgin, etc.

**Supplication.** Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world, our Lord Jesus Christ, entreating him with every supplication, that through the grace of his birth and through the intercession of the holy Innocents, the little martyrs, he may graciously deign to grant us salvation of soul and body, forgiveness of sins, and peace.

**R.** Grant this, eternal almighty God.

Kyrie, eleison.  
**R.** Christe, eleison.  
Kyrie, eleison.

**Capitulum.** Christ, inexpressible light of the world, who, while still lying in the very cradle and not yet made a martyr, consecrated hosts of infants with the palm of martyrdom; who made them, though still unable to speak, utter various cries beneath the sword of their savage killers; whose souls you preferred to rescue from the hidden places of hell by dying willingly for us all: inspire them to pray without ceasing for the little ones, so that we, who cannot be cleansed from guilt by our own prayers, may here and eternally be washed by the petitions of those who, wherever you go, will follow you with hymns and songs.

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. See fol. 2.

Humble yourselves for the blessing.

The Lord be always with you.  
**R.** And with your spirit.

**Blessing.** May the only-begotten Son of God, at whose birth on earth the fields of Bethlehem were stained with the blood of the infants killed for him, grant us always to hold an acceptable desire for him and an equal reward of recompense.

**R.** Amen.

And may he who made them victors not by age but by blood make us confessors of our guilt.

**R.** Amen.

So that our confession too may someday be admitted by Christ for reward with those whose blood’s voice cries to God from the earth.

**R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**Laud.** Your Nazarites, O Zion, are brighter than snow.

**P.** They were found more beautiful than sapphires, and they gave glory to God. Alleluia.

**V.** Draw near to God, and be enlightened; and your faces shall not blush.

**P.** They were found more beautiful than sapphires.

**V.** Glory and honor to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.

**P.** They were found more beautiful than sapphires.

**Prayer.** Christ, Son of God, who invite the little ones to yourself through the teaching of heavenly instruction. See below in Matins of this feast.

## At Matins

**Antiphon.** Give us the joy of your salvation, and strengthen us with a governing spirit, O Lord.

**Psalm 50.**

**Prayer.** Restore to us, O Lord, the joy of your salvation, which we lost by acting wickedly and neglected through carelessness. Call us back to it and restore it to us, so that, once sin has been expelled, righteousness may take its place, and once sadness has been driven away, eternal joy may be present. Grant, we ask, this gladness, that we may be worthy to reach eternal salvation.

**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon.** Let the little children come to me.

**P.** And do not hinder them, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these.

**V.** Draw near to God, and be enlightened; and your faces shall not blush.

**P.** And do not hinder them.

**V.** Glory and honor, etc.

**P.** And do not hinder them.

**Prayer.** Christ, Son of God, who invite the little ones to yourself through the teaching of heavenly instruction, make us always little in wickedness and perfect in observing your commandments; and since you declare that the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these, join us without end to those whom you approve as good.

**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon.** The voice of blood crying out to you.

**P.** Hear, O Lord; remember the unconquered deaths of your little Innocents.

**V.** They poured out innocent blood around Jerusalem, and there was no one to bury them.

**P.** Hear, O Lord; remember.

**V.** Glory and honor to the Father, etc.

**P.** Hear, O Lord; remember.

**Prayer.** Remember, O Lord, your unconquered little ones, killed for your name; and grant that you may mercifully hear the voice of their blood crying to you on our behalf, so that you may forgive the sins of us all.

**R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**Antiphon.** Wisdom opened the mouth of the mute.

**P.** And made the tongues of infants eloquent.

**V.** They called upon the Lord, and he heard them; from the pillar of cloud he spoke to them.

**P.** And made the tongues of infants eloquent.

**V.** Glory and honor to the Father, etc.

**P.** And made the tongues of infants eloquent.

**Prayer.** True Wisdom of God the Father, who open the mouth of the mute and make the tongues of infants eloquent, grant perfect observance of your law in our mouth, so that, following you with an undefiled heart, we may always proclaim it with our lips and fulfill it in our deeds; and thus may we praise you without end, who are true wisdom.

**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**R.** These are those who did not stain their garment.

**P.** They walked with the Lord in white garments, for they are worthy; and whoever conquers shall likewise be clothed in a white garment.

**V.** They follow the Lamb wherever he goes, and no falsehood was found in their mouth.

**P.** They walked with the Lord.

**V.** Glory and honor to the Father, etc.

**P.** They walked with the Lord.

**Prayer.** These are they, O Lord, who did not defile their garments, since no enticement to sin could arise for them. Grant, therefore, through the gift of forgiveness, that we may share in those whom you approve as happy before you because of their merits.

**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**At the Canticle. Antiphon.** They are girded with strength though weak. Let the strong man not glory in his strength, but let the one who glories glory in this: that he knows and understands the Lord.

**Canticle.** My heart has been strengthened. See fol. 55.

**At the Benedictus. Antiphon.** Holy and humble in heart, spirits and souls of the righteous, bless the Lord.

**Canticle.** Blessed are you, O Lord, God of our fathers. See fol. 6.

**Sono.** The salvation of the righteous is from the Lord.

**P.** And he will save them. Alleluia. Alleluia.

**V.** For they hoped in the living God.

**P.** And he will save them.

**Laud.** Praise the Lord from the heavens. Alleluia; praise him in the heights. Alleluia.

**Psalm 148.**

**Reading from the Book of the Prophet Jeremiah (Chapter 31).**

**R.** Thanks be to God.

Thus says the Lord:

“A voice was heard in Ramah, lamentation, weeping, and great mourning; Rachel weeping for her children, and she refused to be comforted concerning them, because they are no more.

Thus says the Lord: Let your voice cease from weeping and your eyes from tears, because there is a reward for your work, says the Lord, and they shall return from the land of the enemy. And there is hope for your future, says the Lord, and your children shall return to their borders.

I have surely heard Ephraim mourning: ‘You chastised me, and I was instructed, like an untrained young bull. Convert me, and I shall return, because you are my God.’ For after you converted me, I repented; and after you showed me, I struck my thigh. I was ashamed and confounded, because I bore the disgrace of my youth.
