Is Ephraim a precious son to me, a delicate child? For ever since I spoke of him, I still remember him. Therefore my inward parts are troubled over him; I will surely have compassion on him, says the Lord almighty.”

**Response.** Amen.

**Hymn.**

The company of mothers resounds:

It offers up its crushed pledges,

Whom the tyrant consecrated to Christ

As victims by the thousand.

By miracles he gave grounds for faith

That God was his Father,

Healing infirm bodies

And raising corpses.

The centurion, kneeling,

Prays for the health of his servant;

The immense ardor of his faith

Extinguished the fires of fever.

Peter walks upon the waves,

Raised up by Christ’s right hand;

The path that nature had denied

Faith prepared.

The honor of the mother and the joy,

The immeasurable hope of believers,

Through the dark cups of death

Dissolved our sins.

Remember, Author of salvation,

That once, in being born from an undefiled Virgin,

You took on the form of our body.

Glory to you, O Lord,

Who were born, etc.

**Supplication.** Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world. Fol. 57.

**Capitulum.** May the multitude of the little Innocents, who were drenched in their own blood for the name of their Redeemer, never cease to entreat the Lord for his servants, so that, through your obtaining it for us, although unworthy, after the course of this life we may be joined to the companies of the saints for his name, and may deserve to sing a hymn with them eternally in jubilation.

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. Fol. 2.

**Laud.** Your Nazarites are candidates.

**Blessing.** The only-begotten Son of God. See fol. 57.

In the name of the Lord.

Let everything be said as in the Common of One Martyr and Bishop.

# On the Feast of Saint James the Apostle

## At Vespers

**Laud.** You crowned him with glory and honor.

**P.** O Lord.

**V.** You placed glory and great splendor upon him.

**P.** O Lord.

**Sono.** Alleluia. Blessed is the man who fears the Lord. Alleluia.

**P.** He greatly delights in his commandments. Alleluia, alleluia.

**V.** Glory and riches are in his house, and his righteousness endures forever and ever. Alleluia.

**Antiphon.** The eye of God looked upon the righteous man with favor.

**P.** And he chose him from his humility; he heard him and his voice.

**V.** Blessed is he who understands concerning the needy and the poor; on the evil day the Lord will deliver him.

**P.** And he chose him.

**V.** Glory and honor.

**P.** And he chose him.

**Laud.** The righteous shall be in everlasting remembrance. Alleluia.

**P.** He shall not fear an evil report. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.

**V.** His offspring shall be mighty on earth; the generation of the upright shall be blessed.

**P.** He shall not fear an evil report.

**V.** Glory and honor.

**P.** He shall not fear an evil report.

**Hymn.**

Bright Jerusalem, sole mother of the saints,

Praise together; rejoice exceedingly,

For the desolate woman has many children,

More than she who has a husband.

For this reason James, called your Just One,

As a sacred priest ascends the sacred place;

He alone enters the holy things in the Holy Place,

For he remains a virgin.

Called here the brother of the Lord according to the flesh,

Trusting in grace and in the apostolate,

He instructed the peoples to guard faithfully

The holy teachings of Christ.

Then, set upon a lofty pinnacle by evil men

So that he might deny that Christ had come,

He clearly refutes the impious doctrine

Of the Pharisees.

For this he is hurled to the ground and cast down;

Yet he stands unharmed and repeats what he said before;

Then one of the fullers strikes his sacred

Brain with a club.

We, sorrowful, ask you, holy and kind,

Exalted martyr, joined to the people:

Remove the harsh yoke from the shaken people;

Take away the wars.

May there be salvation for the sick and rest for the dead;

Strength for the weary and pestilence removed;

With vices driven away, may open access to heaven

Be granted to the wretched.

May praise be to God, the Father and the Son;

May abundant honor be to the Three with the Holy Spirit;

May the stars cry out to the Triune Name,

To the Godhead alone.

**R.** Amen.

Let the Supplication be said as on the feast of Saint John the Apostle, changing the name. Fol. 54.

**Capitulum.** Almighty Father, who granted your most blessed Apostle and martyr James the special gift that through you the fragile might become strong, the least great, the soldier a leader, the servant a friend, and the suppliant a wondrous advocate: graciously grant that, through his unceasing intercession, you may now bestow upon the very members from whom he himself was chosen strength for weakness, glory for humility, discipline for military service, freedom for servitude, and advocacy for need.

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. Fol. 2.

Humble yourselves for the blessing.

The Lord be always with you.  
**R.** And with you.

**Blessing.** May the Lord guard us through the intercession of his most blessed Apostle and martyr James.

**R.** Amen.

May he graciously attend to the needs of those who hope in him.

**R.** Amen.

May we, following his footsteps, be able to proceed to the heavenly kingdoms.

**R.** Amen.

Through his mercy.

**Laud.** The righteous shall flourish like a palm tree. Alleluia.

**P.** He shall multiply like a cedar of Lebanon. Alleluia, alleluia.

**V.** His offspring shall be mighty on earth; the generation of the upright shall be blessed.

**P.** He shall multiply like a cedar.

**V.** Glory and honor, etc.

**P.** He shall multiply like a cedar.

**Prayer.** This man has been glorified. See below in Matins.

## At Matins

**Antiphon.** You will open my lips, O Lord.

**P.** And my mouth shall proclaim your praise.

**Psalm 50.**

**Prayer.** May our lips rejoice, O Lord, in proclaiming the truth, so that they may not dissolve into the empty talk of falsehood; and may our tongue speak the judgment of truth, so that with eager devotion it may praise your Christ, the true judge. May your commandments likewise continually occupy our heart, so that our steps may not be tripped up by treacherous snares.

**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon.** This man was greatly honored, and God broke the hearts of his enemies.

**P.** And he hastened into the house of the Lord his God with a perfect heart, and all saw the mighty things God did through him.

**V.** His glory is greatest in your salvation; you will place glory and great splendor upon him.

**P.** And he hastened.

**V.** Glory and honor, etc.

**P.** And he hastened.

**Prayer.** This man is glorified; Christ rejoices. He deserved to be called Just, so that he might proclaim your promised rewards to the peoples. In his honor we bow down and earnestly ask with tearful prayer that you may deign to receive our prayers, gentle and merciful, and make us always cling to your commandments.

**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon.** This saint cried out, and the Lord heard him.

**P.** And he delivered him from all his tribulations.

**V.** Thus shall the man who fears the Lord be blessed.

**P.** And he delivered him from all.

**V.** Glory and honor, etc.

**P.** And he delivered him from all.

**Prayer.** Thus the holy man James, your Apostle, recognized the wickedness of the Jewish people, by whom he was raised to the pinnacle of the Temple and then thrown down from it for confessing your name, and buried beneath stones. As an advocate amid his final sufferings, may he, through the mercy of your goodness, stand as a constant and friendly intercessor for us wretched people, so that we may deserve to be freed from the pressures of evils while beholding your glory.

**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon.** The Lord clothed him in a robe of glory.

**P.** He stored up gladness and rejoicing for him and gave him an eternal inheritance by name.

**V.** His offspring shall be mighty on earth; the generation of the upright shall be blessed.

**P.** He stored up gladness.

**V.** Glory and honor, etc.

**P.** He stored up gladness.

**Prayer.** Your people, rejoicing, O Lord, on this feast of your Apostle James, earnestly beseech you for the same thing: that, just as he was called Just by all, so we may deserve to be called worshipers of righteousness and followers of mercy.

**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**R.** Let the righteous still practice righteousness, and let the holy still be sanctified. Blessed is he who washed his robe.

**P.** So that he may have authority over the tree of life.

**V.** And whoever conquers shall likewise be clothed in a white garment, and I will not erase his name from the book of life.

**P.** So that he may have authority.

**V.** Glory and honor, etc.

Repeat: **R.** Let the righteous still practice righteousness.

## At Lauds

**At the Canticle. Antiphon.** You alone are Lord, for there is no other, neither is there any righteous one besides you, nor any holy one besides you, our God.

**Canticle.** It has been strengthened. See fol. 55.

**At the Benedictus. Antiphon.** The blessing of the Lord hastens as the reward of the righteous.

**Canticle.** Blessed are you, O Lord God of our fathers. See fol. 6.

**Sono.** Alleluia. Blessed is the man who fears the Lord. See fol. 59.

**Laud.** Praise the Lord from the heavens. Alleluia; praise him in the heights. Alleluia, alleluia.

**Psalm 148.**

**Hymn.** Bright Jerusalem, one mother of the saints. See fol. 59.

**Reading from the Book of the Wisdom of Solomon (Chapter 18).**

**R.** Thanks be to God.

The trial of death touched the righteous man, and a disturbance of the multitude arose in the wilderness; but your anger did not last long. For the blameless man hastened to the defence, bringing forth the shield of his service, prayer, and a plea made through incense. He resisted the anger and put an end to the calamity, showing that he was your servant.

He overcame the crowds, not by bodily strength or armor of power, but by the word of God he cast down the destroyer, recalling the oaths made to the ancestors. For when the dead had already fallen in heaps upon one another, he stood between them, cut off the assault, and divided the path that led to the living.

For upon the robe reaching to the feet that he wore was the whole world, and the glories of the ancestors were carved in four rows of stones, while your majesty was inscribed upon the diadem of his head.

**R.** Amen.

**Supplication.** Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world, our Lord Jesus Christ, entreating him with every supplication, that through the grace of his birth and through the intercession of his Apostle Saint James he may graciously deign to grant us salvation of soul and body, forgiveness of sins, and peace.

**R.** Grant this, eternal almighty God.

Kyrie, eleison.  
**R.** Christe, eleison.  
Kyrie, eleison.

**Capitulum.** Righteous Lord, from whom righteousness is rightly granted to the righteous, who grant that those who desire to live justly through you may possess justice: let them show in their deeds the righteousness they retain in their minds. Thus we rightly recognize your holy Apostle James as having been called Just by all. His just words confounded the wickedness of the reprobate, when they, with the deceitfulness of their evil, both called him just and wished to teach injustice.

For this reason they summoned him and set him in a lofty place, so that his preaching might resound far and wide. They refused to accept him speaking the truth, but soon threw him down and, adorning him with suffering, made him glorious. Through his merits, make us hold righteousness in our minds and gladly proclaim it, so that, just as he reached you through the glory of martyrdom, justified by practicing righteousness, so we may, through his intercessions and worthy repentance, deserve to reach the forgiveness we seek.

**Our Father.**

Delivered from evil. Fol. 2.

**Laud.** The righteous shall flourish like a palm tree.

**Blessing.** Of the most blessed James. See fol. 60.

# On the Feast of the Circumcision of Our Lord Jesus Christ

## At Vespers

**Laud.** All your angels have praised you, O Lord, and have sung a hymn while you completed the structure of heaven. The day is yours, and the night is yours.

**P.** You made the sun and the moon.

**V.** You established the sea by your power; you crushed the heads of dragons upon the waters.

**P.** You made the sun and the moon.

**Sono.** Alleluia. Your right hand is full of righteousness. Let Mount Zion rejoice, and let the daughters of Judah exult.

**P.** Because of your judgments. Alleluia, alleluia.

**V.** Alleluia. Great is the Lord and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, on his holy mountain, making the rejoicings of the whole earth abound.

**P.** Because of your judgments.

**Antiphon.** All the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God.

**P.** Sing joyfully to God, all the earth; sing, exult, and chant.

**V.** Sing to our Lord, sing; sing to our King, sing.

**P.** Sing joyfully.

**V.** Glory and honor, etc.

**P.** Sing joyfully to God.

**Prayer.** O Lord, whom human beings saw born from a human being, and whom the ends of the earth, as foretold, saw; who were foretold long before by the voices of the Prophets, seen in time, and glorified in the melodies of the peoples: graciously grant that we may remain your most pure vessels, so that you, the author of light, may continually enlighten us and dwell within us without ceasing.

**R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**Antiphon.** My eyes have seen your salvation, O Lord, which you prepared in the presence of the peoples.

**P.** A light for revelation to the Gentiles and the glory of your people Israel.

**V.** O Lord, our Lord, how wonderful is your name in all the earth.

**P.** A light for revelation.

**V.** Glory and honor, etc.

**P.** A light.

**Laud.** The Lord has made his salvation known; before the sight of the nations he has revealed his righteousness. Alleluia, alleluia.

**V.** He remembered his mercy toward Jacob and his truth toward the house of Israel.

**P.** Before the sight of the nations.

**V.** Glory and honor, etc.

**P.** Before the sight of the nations.

**Hymn.**

The sacred day of the Octave

Shines forth today,

On which Christ, according to the flesh,

Is presented circumcised

To the Father, not by adoption,

But coeternal by nature.

The womb of the undefiled Virgin

Is filled by the Spirit;

She who gave birth remained unmarried,

A virgin whom the Child,

The pure offspring, chose

As an undefiled Mother.

Then aged Simeon,

Rejoicing, receives him in his arms,

And, embracing him, seemed to behold

The salvation of the Lord:

“Now release these fragile limbs

In peace.”

Nor was Anna, advancing in continence,

Unequal to him;

Her husband had made her a widow

In the flower of her youth.

She confesses that the wailing child

Will be the Ruler of the world.

Then, as prescribed by the law,

Venerable offerings are presented:

Pairs of turtledoves and pigeons

For sacrifice,

Teaching the purity

Of body and soul.

In him the ancient circumcision

Of the law was fulfilled,

So that he might show himself

The author of both Testaments,

He who, remaining in the Trinity,

Created all things.

Glory and honor to God,

The Most High everywhere;

To the Father and the Son alike,

And to the illustrious Paraclete,

To whom be praise and power

Through eternal ages.

**R.** Amen.

**Supplication.** Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world, our Lord Jesus Christ, entreating him with every supplication, that he may graciously deign to justify us through the grace of his Circumcision.

**R.** Grant this, eternal almighty God.

Kyrie, eleison.  
**R.** Christe, eleison.  
Kyrie, eleison.

**Capitulum.** Lord Jesus, whose wondrous name the angel foretold, the Mother imposed, Simeon recognized, and Anna praised: save your people throughout the world, whose magnificent name exists in heaven; so that you, who alone are glorious in power, may also be gracious toward the lost through the forgiveness of mercy.

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. Fol. 2.

**Blessing.** May the Lord Jesus Christ, who wished to be the minister of Circumcision in order to confirm the promises made to the Fathers, deign to remove the uncleanness of our hearts.

**R.** Amen.

May the same one, who by the commandment of his law received the sign of cut flesh, cleanse all filth from us through the bond of his love.

**R.** Amen.

And may he who promised to bless the children of Abraham in himself, who is his offspring, enrich us with the bestowal of blessed inheritance.

**R.** Amen.

Through his mercy.

**Laud.** Let the name of the Lord be proclaimed in Zion.

**P.** And his praise in Jerusalem. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.

**V.** And the nations shall fear your name, O Lord, and all the kings of the earth your glory.

**P.** And his praise.

**V.** Glory and honor, etc.

**P.** And his praise.

**Prayer.** Almighty Father and Lord. See below in the following Matins.

## At Matins

**Antiphon.** Salvation belongs to the Lord, and your blessing is upon your people.

**Psalm 3.**

**Prayer.** You are salvation, O Lord. See fol. 46.

**Antiphon.** When his parents brought the child Jesus into the Temple.

**P.** To do for him according to the law of Moses, Simeon took him in his hands and blessed God.

**V.** Great is the Lord and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, on his holy mountain.

**P.** To do for him.

**V.** Glory and honor to the Father, etc.

**P.** To do for him.

**Prayer.** Almighty Father and Lord God, grant peace to your believing people, so that in your Temple we may see your Salvation, whom righteous Simeon received in his arms; so that he who appeared as a light for revelation to the Gentiles may be perceived by believing people as the forgiver of their sins.

**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon.** You are God, and in you is God.

**P.** And besides you there is no other God, the Savior of Israel, whom we did not know.

**V.** Lord God of hosts, who is like you? You are powerful, O Lord, and your truth surrounds you.

**P.** And besides you.

**V.** Glory and honor, etc.

**P.** And besides you.

**Prayer.** You are God, and in you is God, and there is no other besides you. The word that has gone forth from the mouth shall not return; for, although the Son who was born is not believed to be the very one who is the Father, nevertheless we confess that he is himself what the Father is. Grant us, therefore, that we who were reborn in you may now be freed from sins, just as you sent the Word begotten from you to be born in the flesh, so that when you come we may be joined to you alone without end.

**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon 3.** Concerning him the former Prophets spoke: “I am he himself, and now I have come.”

**P.** Blessed are those who announce good things to you; they shall see him whom you now see and hear him whom you now hear.

**V.** Hear, my people, and I will speak; Israel, and I will testify to you. Israel, if you will hear me.

**P.** Blessed are those who announce.

**V.** Glory and honor, etc.

**P.** Blessed are those who announce.

**Prayer.** Approaching your manger, O Lord, with devoted hearts, may we find you of whom the former Prophets spoke. Grant us, therefore, that we who have come to know the knowledge of your name and majesty may arrive at full knowledge of your sweetness, so that in the future you may be our deliverer, you who are believed to be the one Christ, true God and true man.

**R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**R.** Rejoice, heavens, because the Lord has had mercy on his people; cry out, foundations of the earth, and exult, mountains, hills, and all the trees of the forest.

**P.** Because the God of Israel has redeemed us.

**V.** Announce this with a voice of rejoicing, make it heard, carry it to the end of the earth, and say:

**P.** Because he has redeemed us.

**V.** Glory and honor, etc.

**P.** Because he has redeemed us.

**Prayer.** Let the heavens and the earth praise you, O Lord, because you have had mercy on your people, when you caused the mountains and hills to cry out praise before you and approved all living things in yourself. Grant us, therefore, that you yourself may always make acceptable to you the praises we offer to your glorious name, so that you who were revealed as about to redeem the world in the sign of salvation may, when you come again to judge the world, reveal yourself to our eyes not as avenger but as liberator.

**R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**Antiphon.** When they gathered to circumcise the infant.

**P.** They called his name Jesus, which had been given by the angel before he was conceived in the womb.

**V.** The Lord has made his salvation known; in the sight of the nations he has revealed his righteousness.

**P.** They called him.

**V.** Glory.

**P.** They called him.

**Prayer.** Lord Jesus Christ, announced through the recurring figures of the old law, you wished to show that all things were fulfilled in yourself, since in you, true God and man, both circumcision according to the law is expressed and the truth of the name is confirmed. Be present to your people coming to you from circumcision and uncircumcision, and grant an increase of gifts, so that the grace of blessing may be multiplied in an abundance of peace.

**R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**Antiphon.** Simeon raised his voice in the Temple, saying:

**P.** “Now dismiss your servant, O Lord, in peace, for my eyes have seen the salvation of your people.”

**V.** Lord God of hosts, who is like you? You are powerful, O Lord, and your truth surrounds you.

**P.** “Now dismiss.”

**V.** Glory.

**P.** “Now.”

**Prayer.** Cause the blessed voice of your righteous Simeon, O Lord, to resound in us with equal devotion, so that, because we see and believe your salvation, we may be dismissed in peace when you command—not so that the end of life may receive those dismissed by you, but so that, absolved by you from our debt, everlasting peace may possess us at the end.

**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon.** The glory of the Lord, as of the Only-begotten from the Father.

**P.** Full of grace and truth.

**V.** As we have heard, so we have seen in the city of the Lord of hosts, in the city of our God; God founded it forever.

**P.** Full of grace.

**V.** Glory and honor, etc.

**P.** Full.

**Prayer.** We have seen your glory, O Lord, glory as of the Only-begotten from the Father: firstborn in divinity, firstborn in gift; there, the Father’s only one, here, preeminent among brothers; there, one with the Father, here, first among brothers; there, subsisting equally and remaining in the Father’s bosom, here, not abandoning his companions. Grant, therefore, that those toward whom you have been gracious in the world may become sharers in your kingdom, and that for those to whom you first came as Redeemer, you may in the future exist as Rewarder.

**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**R.** He who was born is our Redemption, and is Lord and God.

**P.** He himself will comfort us from our wound and from the labor in the land of our captivity.

**V.** A little one is born for us, a son is given to us, and dominion has been made upon his shoulders.

**P.** He himself will comfort us.

**V.** Glory and honor, etc.

**P.** He himself will comfort us.

**Prayer.** Lord Jesus Christ, who are our Redemption and our salvation, heal the wound of our contrition, you who took on the flesh of human weakness; and, since you deigned to come to lift our burdens, we ask that in your goodness you empty our labors of evil works and strengthen our efforts in what is good.

**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon.** After the eight days were completed for the Lord to be circumcised.

**P.** His name was called Jesus, the name given by the angel before he was conceived in the womb. They took him to Jerusalem, and when they had completed everything according to the law of the Lord, the child grew and became strong, full of wisdom, and the grace of God was in him.

**V.** For behold, the kings of the earth gathered and came together as one.

**P.** His name was called.

**V.** Glory and honor, etc.

**P.** His name was called.

**Prayer.** Christ, Son of God, who were born of a woman and made subject to the law to confirm the promises of the Fathers, you became the minister of circumcision, so that you who had been promised from the law might in time be the fullness of that law. On the eighth day, while consecrating its observance in your glorious flesh, you both received the ancient sign in circumcision and accepted the name announced to you by the angel. Grant to us, unworthy though we are, that when we have received these mysteries of your Incarnation with complete faith, we may love you with a fuller affection of heart; and since in you all the mysteries of our salvation were perfected according to the law of the Lord, may we believe, love, and fulfill the effectiveness of our works accordingly, so that through the perfection of your commandments we may remain unharmed in this pilgrimage and, after our passage, deserve to reach you in blessedness.

**R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

The Lord be with you.  
**R.** And with you.

## At Lauds

**At the Canticle. Antiphon.** All who are upon the earth shall rejoice, for the dew that comes from you is healing for us.

**V.** My spirit keeps vigil toward you by night.

**Canticle (Isaiah 26).**

By night my spirit keeps vigil toward you, O God,  
*for your commandments are light upon the earth.

Learn righteousness, you who dwell upon the earth;  
*for the impious shall cease.

For whoever has not learned righteousness upon the earth  
shall not practice truth;  
*let the impious be taken away, so that he may not see the majesty of the Lord.

O Lord, your arm is exalted, and they did not know it;  
*but when they understand, they shall be confounded.

Zeal has seized the unlearned people,  
*and now fire consumes the adversaries.

O Lord our God, give us peace;  
*for you have given us all things.

O Lord our God, possess us;  
*O Lord, besides you we have known no other; your name we shall invoke.

But the dead shall not see life,  
*nor shall physicians raise them up.

Therefore you brought them upon them,  
*destroyed them, and took away every male among them.

Add evils to them, O Lord;  
*add evils to the glorious people of the earth.

O Lord, in slight tribulation I remembered you;  
*in slight tribulation it came to pass for us.

As a woman near childbirth cries out in her pain,  
*so have we become through our guilt.

Because of your fear, O Lord, we conceived in the womb,  
*and gave birth to the spirit of salvation that you made upon the earth.

Let the dead arise, and let those in the tombs rise again,  
*and let all who are upon the earth rejoice.

For the dew that comes from you is healing for them;  
*but the earth of the impious shall perish.

Go, my people, and enter your chambers;  
hide yourselves for a little while,  
*until the anger of the Lord passes.

**P.** By night my spirit keeps vigil.

Glory and honor to the Father, etc.

**P.** All who are upon the earth shall rejoice.

**Prayer.** O God, who made your salvation known among the peoples in the sight of the Gentiles by revealing your righteousness, manifest to us the abundance of your mercies, so that we who are refreshed by knowledge of your salvation may be comforted by the revelation of your righteousness.

**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**At the Benedictus. Antiphon.** To you alone, God, be honor and glory, power and might, forever and ever.

**Psalm.** Blessed are you, Lord God of our fathers. See fol. 6.

**Sono.** Alleluia. Your right hand is full of righteousness. See fol. 61.

**Laud.** Praise the Lord from the heavens. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. Praise him in the heights. Alleluia. Praise him, all his angels; praise him, all his powers. Alleluia.

**Psalm 148, as above.**

**Reading from the Book of the Prophet Isaiah (Chapter 48).**

**R.** Thanks be to God.

Thus says the Lord:

“Hear me, Jacob, and Israel, whom I call: I am he, I am the first, and I am the last. My hand also founded the earth, and my right hand measured out the heavens; I call them, and they stand together.

Gather together, all of you, and hear: who announced these things to them? The Lord loved him; he will do his will in Babylon and his arm among the Chaldeans.

I spoke, and I called him; I led him, and his way was made straight. Draw near to me and hear this: from the beginning I have not spoken in secret; from the time before it happened, I was there. And now the Lord God has sent me and his Spirit.

Thus says the Lord, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: I am the Lord your God, teaching you what is useful, guiding you on the way that you walk.

If only you had attended to my commandments! Your peace would have become like a river, and your righteousness like the waves of the sea. Your offspring would have been like sand, and the descendants of your womb like its grains; they would not have perished, and his name would not have been rubbed away from my presence.

Go out from Babylon; flee from the Chaldeans. Announce it with a voice of rejoicing; make it heard, carry it to the end of the earth, and say: ‘The Lord has redeemed his servant Jacob.’”

**R.**
Amen.

## Hymn

Holy day of the octave. Supplication. Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world. Folio 61.

## Chapters

The salvation, O Lord of hosts, has become known; it has come to pass, foretold by the proclamation of the Prophets and seen by the gaze of the peoples, when the aged Simeon held in his arms what the earlier Seers had sung. Therefore the prophecy is recognized as both promised and begun, so that he might rest in peace when he had seen Peace; and that Jesus the Lord might come forth as a light for the revelation of the Gentiles and the glory of your people Israel; that the Promised One might emerge and, emerging, appear; and that his light might precede in the world those whom the blindness of darkness had overwhelmed. Grant, therefore, through the prayers of your Church, that those whom you have caused to recognize these wonders may reach you in peace.

**Our Father.** Deliver us from evil. Folio 2.

**Lauda.** Let it be proclaimed in Zion.

**Benediction.** The Lord Jesus Christ. Folio 62. In the name of the Lord.

# On the Sunday before the Epiphany, or Manifestation, of the Lord

## At Vespers

**Lauda.** They praised you, O Lord. Folio 61.

**Sono.** Attend, O Lord.

**P.** Go forth and reign. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.

**V.** My heart has uttered a good word; I speak of my works to the king.

**P.** Go forth.

**Antiphon.** Rejoice, rejoice, Jerusalem, and celebrate the feast, all you who love her.

**P.** Rejoice with great joy, all you who mourned over her.

**V.** Praise the Lord, Jerusalem; praise your God, Zion.

**P.** Rejoice with joy.

**V.** Glory and honor, etc.

**P.** Rejoice.

**Lauda.** Alleluia. The Dawn from on high has visited us.

**P.** To shine upon those who are in darkness, to direct our feet into the way of peace. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.

**V.** As we have heard, so also have we seen, in the city of the Lord of hosts, in the city of our God; God founded it forever.

**P.** To shine upon.

**V.** Glory and honor, etc.

**P.** To shine upon.

## Hymn

Lord, begetter of the Lamb,

Word born of the Virgin,

Conceived without seed,

Leader of light and fountain of life:

Be for us salvation,

Only-begotten Son of God.

Ruler, Jesus Christ,

Look upon our prayer.

You were sent into the world for us

To restore the captives,

To renew sight to the blind,

To loosen the tongues of the mute.

Do not abandon us, O Lord,

Kind Creator of all;

In your mercy, look favorably upon us,

You who desire to lose no one.

And, Lord, Ruler of the world,

Only-begotten Savior,

Protect us from death,

That, captured by your sweet work, we may be [saved].

May Christ the Lord keep watch,

And may our faith put forth shoots;

May the devil’s fortress depart,

And have no power to creep upon us.

Through Jesus Christ the Lord,

Who reigns with God the Father,

And has deemed us worthy to teach us:

Let us believe in the Trinity.

To the Triune God and Lord

Let us all give glory,

For the Father in the beginning

Was always with the Son. Amen.

**Supplication.** Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world, our Lord Jesus Christ; with every supplication let us ask that he increase the faith of his holy catholic Church, grant peace, and provide protection.

**R.** Grant this, eternal almighty God.

## Chapters

God without beginning and without end, from whom the beginning of the whole creation of the world comes: grant us to pass through the end and middle of this year with prosperity pleasing to you, as we offer its beginning for dedication to you, so that we may abound in possessions and shine in works of holiness.

**Our Father.** Deliver us from evil. Folio 2.

**Benediction.** May our Lord Jesus Christ, who is the crown of the whole Church formed by him, grant us to pass through this year in peace.

**R.** Amen.

May he console us with fruits and deem us worthy to reward us with virtues.

**R.** Amen.

May we deserve to pass unharmed through all the days of the year in joyful prosperity pleasing to him.

**R.** Amen.

Through his mercy.

**Lauda.** Alleluia. The desert and the trackless land shall rejoice.

**P.** The wilderness shall exult and shall blossom like a lily. Alleluia, alleluia.

**V.** Let all the earth rejoice in God; serve the Lord with gladness.

**P.** The wilderness shall exult.

**V.** Glory and honor, etc.

**P.** The wilderness shall exult.

**Prayer.** Shake off from us, Only-begotten One. Seek below at Matins.

**Hymn.** Eternal Creator of things. Seek on folio 3.

**Prayer.** Almighty, eternal, and merciful God, who appoint the times of the times and give grace to each season for its proper service: lest the mind should grow overheated through the length of darkness, you console us by the crowing of the cock, so that, when the herald of day sounds, meditation on the work of the day may revive. Look, therefore, continually upon us, and stir us up, lest, persuaded by the error of deep night, we forget the unending day; but raise us when we slip in darkness and correct us by making us see, so that, with Peter, we may repent of our errors and mourn our committed sins with equal tears.

**R.** Amen. Through your mercy.

**Antiphon 1.** Your salvation, O Lord, is upon your people, and blessing. **Psalm 3.**

**Antiphon 2.** Blot out, O Lord, our iniquities, and cleanse our heart from our sins. **Psalm 50.**

**Antiphon 3.** I shall cry to God Most High, to God the Creator of all things, who has done good to me. **Psalm 56.**

**Prayer.** Shake off from us, Only-begotten One of the unbegotten Father, the sleep of the body; and, mercifully appeased, spare our offenses, so that the abundance of the redeemed may be frequented by holy vigils in you and may be held worthy of your sacred sight. May what the lowly frailty of the flesh now sows arise, by the gift of your divinity, in glory. Therefore, Lord, bestow abundant help upon all who trust in you, and draw us toward the heavenly homeland beneath the shadow of your wings.

**R.** Amen. Through your mercy.

**Antiphon.** The Lord possessed me before he made the earth.

**P.** Before the mountains were established; before all the hills, he begot me.

**V.** My heart has uttered a good word; I speak of my works to the king.

**P.** Before.

**V.** Glory and honor, etc.

**P.** Before.

**Prayer.** Wisdom of God the Father, coeternal with him, who testify that you were with the Father before he made the earth or established the heights of the mountains, when he begot you before the creation of all the hills: we ask and beseech you that we who celebrate with rejoicing the joys of your incorruptible birth may reach you through believing, in order to receive our reward. You who are born from the Father before the foundation of the mountains, and who, born from the Virgin’s womb in the fullness of time, sanctify those who believe in you, reward the sanctified with the glory of eternity.

**R.** Amen. Through your mercy.

**Antiphon.** The people who sat in darkness.

**P.** Saw a great light; for those dwelling in the land of the shadow of death, a bright light has risen.

**V.** Clap your hands, all you nations; rejoice to God with a voice of exultation.

**P.** Saw a great light.

**V.** Glory and honor, etc.

**P.** Saw the light.

**Prayer.** Only-begotten Son of God, who caused those dwelling in the land of the shadow of death to see the light, who shone forth as light through the mystery of the Incarnation you assumed: grant that, with you illuminating us, we may be firmly established, so that we who have welcomed the day of your birth with rejoicing may be consoled by the gifts of your divinity.

**R.** Amen. Through your mercy.

**Antiphon.** The almighty Lord has visited his people, the house of Judah.

**P.** And he will establish him like a beautiful horse in battle.

**V.** As we have heard, so also have we seen, in the city of the Lord of hosts, in the city of our God; God founded it forever.

**P.** And he will establish him.

**V.** Glory and honor, etc.

**P.** And he will establish him.

**Prayer.** Almighty Lord, who have visited your people, the house of Judah: visit us as we awaken from our crimes, so that, while we flee the darkness of sins through your radiance, you may empty the power of death by your strength. Thus may we be enlightened when you now appear, so that, with you opposing it, we may be freed from the dominion of death.

**R.** Amen. Through your mercy.

**R.** This righteous one is my Savior.

**P.** He himself has freed his city and will forgive the sins of his people—not for a price or in exchange for money.

**V.** Lift your eyes to heaven and see who created these things: the Lord God, who created the ends of the earth.

**P.** He himself has freed.

**V.** Glory and honor, etc.

**P.** He himself has freed.

**Prayer.** This is our righteous one, in whom we hoped by faith, with the Prophet singing beforehand, and to whom we have come as he appeared through grace. Therefore let us ask his mercy, that he may free us and forgive the sins of his people, for whom he has deigned to expend himself entirely.

**R.** Amen. Through your mercy.

## At Lauds

**For the Canticle. Antiphon.** A growing son, beautiful in appearance: he is the one who gives words of beauty.

**Canticle.** Jacob called his sons. Folio 50.

**For the Benedictus. Antiphon.** Blessed are you, O Lord, and blessed is the name of your glory.

**P.** Bless the Lord, all his elect; may his holy name be blessed throughout all ages of ages.

**Canticle.** Blessed are you, O Lord. Folio 6.

**Sono.** Attend, O Lord; go forth. Folio 65.

**Lauda.** Praise the Lord from the heavens; praise him in the heights. **Psalm 148.**

## Reading from the Book of the Proverbs of Solomon  
### Chapter 8

**R.** Thanks be to God.

The Lord possessed me at the beginning of his ways, before he made anything, from the beginning. I was anointed from eternity, before he made the earth. When there were not yet abysses, I had already been conceived; the fountains of waters had not yet burst forth; the mountains had not yet stood firm in their massive weight; before the hills, I was brought forth. He had not yet made the earth, the rivers, or the foundations of the world. When he prepared the heavens, I was there; when, by a fixed law and a circle, he enclosed the abysses; when he strengthened the sky above and balanced the fountains of waters; when he surrounded the sea with boundaries and appointed a law for the waters, lest they pass beyond their limits; when he hung the foundations of the earth—I was with him, arranging all things. I rejoiced day by day, playing before him throughout the world; and my delights were with the children of men.

Now, therefore, sons, hear me: blessed are those who keep my ways. Hear instruction and become wise, and do not cast it away.

**R.** Amen.

## Hymn

Radiance of the Father’s glory,

Bringing forth light from light,

Light of light and fountain of brightness,

Day illuminating day:

True sun, descend upon us,

Shining with everlasting splendor,

And pour the radiance of the Holy Spirit

Into our senses.

Let us call upon the Father with our prayers,

The Father of everlasting glory:

May the Father of powerful grace

Drive away slippery guilt.

May he shape our vigorous deeds,

Blunt the tooth of envy,

Give success in harsh circumstances,

And grant the grace to carry them out.

May he guide and rule the mind

In a chaste and faithful body;

May faith burn with warmth

And know nothing of the poisons of deceit.

May Christ be food for us,

And faith our drink;

Joyfully let us drink

The sober intoxication of the Spirit.

May this joyful day pass by;

May modesty be like the dawn,

Faith like midday;

May the mind know no twilight.

The dawn advances on its course;

May the whole dawn shine brightly:

The Son wholly in the Father,

And the Father wholly in the Word.

Glory to the unbegotten Father,

Glory to the Only-begotten,

Together with the Holy Spirit,

Throughout everlasting ages.

Amen.

**Chapters.** God without beginning.

**And Lauda.** Alleluia. The desert shall rejoice.

**And Benediction.** Our Lord Jesus Christ. Folio 66.

In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.

# The Office of the Fasts Begins on the Kalends of January

It is observed for three days before the feast of the Epiphany, as follows.

## On the First Day

### At Matins

**Antiphon.** But you, O Lord, are my protector, my glory, and the one who lifts up my head. **Psalm 3.**

**Prayer.** Although a very great multitude of the wicked denies that our salvation is in you, Lord our God, our strength of hope is nevertheless greatly increased by this: that you have deigned to be our protector. Therefore let the mouth of those who speak iniquity be stopped, while constant mercy surrounds those who hope in you.

**R.** Amen. Through your mercy.

**Antiphon 1.** Who is God besides the Lord? Or who is God besides our God? **Psalm 17.**

**Prayer.** You are our strength. Grant us to possess love for your name forever. Deign to be our power against those who oppose us, our support against those who attack us, and our deliverer from those who take us captive. Surrounded entirely by your defenses, may our mind fear the adversities of the world without seeking its flatteries; may it rejoice, always content with the gifts of your grace.

**R.** Amen. Through your mercy.

**Antiphon 2.** You alone understand transgressions; cleanse us from our sins, O Lord. **Psalm 18.**

**Prayer.** Cleanse us from our hidden faults, O Lord, purifying the conscience that is stained by inward and personal blemishes. Also spare your servants from the faults of others, so that you may forgive what we either learn from the examples of the wicked or commit after being enticed by corrupt persuasions. May we who acknowledge you as our true Lord no longer experience the domination of sins.

**R.** Amen. Through your mercy.

**Antiphon 3.** Hear us on the day when we call upon you, O Lord our God. **Psalm 19.**

**Prayer.** Draw the tribulations of our heart—which repentance for our crimes reveals through fear of judgment—through your mercy, O Lord, toward the joy of forgiveness. Send us help from the sanctuary, and make the sorrow of our hearts a rich holocaust for you. Inspire in our minds the counsel that pleases you and suggest the work by which you are pleased. Complete our petitions in such a way that you erase our sins, and mercifully admit us into that region where life is without end.

**R.** Amen. Through your mercy.

**R.** When the Lord came, he took away all the darkness of night; where there was no light, brightness was made.

**P.** And day appeared.

**V.** The people who sat in darkness saw a great light; for those dwelling in the land of the shadow of death, light has risen.

**P.** And day appeared.

**V.** Glory and honor, etc.

**P.** And day appeared.

## At Lauds

**Antiphon.** Turn your face from our sins, and blot out all our iniquities. **Psalm 50.**

**Prayer.** Turn your face from our sins, O Lord, and blot out all our iniquities. Remove from before your eyes the crime of our evil pleasures, and mercifully lend your ear to our confession. Have mercy, we ask, on us who beseech you—you who mercifully look upon those in adversity and grant a repentant heart to the despairing. Give support to our confessions for the sake of your glory.

Since the tax collector, standing far off and striking his breast, was cleansed by confession alone, hear us sinners in the same way, so that, just as you granted him the worthy fruit of his petition, you may also deign to bestow forgiveness of sins upon us, your unworthy servants who implore you.

**R.** Amen. Through your mercy.

**For the Canticle. Antiphon.** Arise, O Lord God, and deliver your people, lest our adversaries ever say: “Our hand is exalted, and God did not do all these things.”

**Canticle.** Give ear, O heaven, and I shall speak. Folio 4.

**The Antiphon is repeated.** Arise, O Lord.

**Prayer.** Let the mountains sing to us and let the earth hear, as they heard Moses your servant in the proclamation of your wonders and commandments. Let the grace of the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, descend upon us like dew upon the earth, like rain upon the grass, and like snow upon the hay. May it cleanse us imperceptibly from the craft of impiety, there where the multitude of our sins cannot be weighed by any satisfaction.

But you, O Lord, who are the light of the blind, the way of the wandering, and the resurrection of the dead: by the regard of your mercy illuminate the darkness of our conscience; call sinners back to repentance, and lavish forgiveness upon the repentant through the ready compassion that is always found in you.

**R.** Amen. Through your mercy.

**Matutinarian. Antiphon.** Light has risen in the darkness for the upright of heart.

**P.** The Lord is merciful, compassionate, and just.

**V.** They cried to the Lord when they were afflicted, and he delivered them from their necessities.

**P.** The Lord is merciful.

**V.** Glory and honor, etc.

**P.** The Lord is merciful.

**Lauda.** Praise him in his holy places; praise him in the heights. **Psalm 148.**

## Reading from the Book of the Wisdom of Solomon  
### Chapters 14–15

**R.** Thanks be to God.

Son, blessed is the wood through which justice comes to be. But by human hands an idol is made; both it and the one who made it are accursed. For the maker indeed has worked, but the fragile object has been called a god. Likewise, the ungodly and his ungodliness are hateful to God. For what has been made will suffer torment together with the one who made it.

Therefore there will be no regard for the idols of the nations, because the creatures of God have been made into abominations, into a temptation for human souls, and into snares for the feet of the foolish. The beginning of fornication is the seeking out of idols, and their invention is the corruption of life. For the worship of unspeakable idols is the cause, beginning, and end of every evil.

For either, while they rejoice, they go mad; or they prophesy falsely; or they live unjustly; or they quickly swear false oaths. While they trust in lifeless idols, those who swear wickedly do not expect to be harmed. Therefore both things will justly come upon them, because they thought wrongly about God, attending to idols, and swore unjustly, despising justice in an idol.

For it is not the strength of those who swear oaths, but the punishment of sinners, that always walks over the transgression of the unjust.

But you, Lord our God, are good and true, patient, and you order all things in mercy. For even if we sin, we are yours, knowing your greatness; and if we do not sin, we know that we are counted among yours. To know you is perfect justice, and to know your justice and truth is the root of immortality.

**R.** Amen.

## Hymn

God, fountain of kindness,

Who, possessing goodness without end,

Are ever merciful and ever good

Toward the evil deeds of the wicked:

We beat our sufficiently sorrowful hearts,

And strike our grieving breasts;

We pour out the waters of our eyes,

And bring sadness upon our cheeks.

We are deeply sorry for what we have done,

Horrible, foul, and utterly wicked;

We confess every harmful deed

To be most shameful and filthy.

An uplifted voice asks for you:

“Spare,” it says, “O Creator.”

Already it cries, pleading:

“Forgive what we have committed.”

May anger not consume the sorrowful;

May punishment not crush the weary.

Quickly comfort the contrite,

And give us joy.

Grant this, most holy Father,

Only-begotten One equal to the Father,

With the Spirit, the Paraclete,

Reigning throughout every age.

Amen.

**Supplication.** Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world, our Lord Jesus Christ; with every supplication let us ask that, by his grace and through the intercession of holy Mary, his Virgin Mother, he may mercifully deign to grant us forgiveness of sins and peace during this holy fast.

**R.** Grant this, eternal almighty God.

Lord, have mercy.

**R.** Christ, have mercy.

Lord, have mercy.

## Chapters

Most beloved brothers, since with the Psalmist you believe that all the idols of the nations are demons, I ask that we reject their rites and monstrous practices in every way. And if you see any of the sons of the Church either practicing such things or taking pleasure in them, reprove them by your admonition and call them back from error to the way of salvation, so that you may freely proclaim with me and with them the words of the Lord’s Prayer, which you learned when the Lord himself taught them, saying on earth:

**Our Father.** Deliver us from evil. Folio 10.

**Lauda.** Alleluia. The desert and the trackless land shall rejoice, and the wilderness shall exult.

**P.** And it shall blossom like a lily. Alleluia, alleluia.

**V.** Let all the earth rejoice in the Lord; serve the Lord with gladness.

**P.** And it shall.

**V.** Glory and honor, etc.

**P.** And it shall.

**Benediction.** Christ the Lord, who with the Father and the Holy Spirit exists as the one Creator both of years and of times, may he deign to accept your fast at the beginning of this year.

**R.** Amen.

May he who was the Redeemer of the whole world always be your guide.

**R.** Amen.

May you celebrate with joy the feast of his Manifestation, just as you have now diligently completed the solemn rites of his birth.

**R.** Amen. Through. In the name.

## At Terce

The Prophecy and everything else follow in order.

## From the Proverbs of Solomon  
### Chapter 3

**R.** Thanks be to God.

My son, do not forget my law, and let your heart keep my commandments. For they will add length of days, years of life, and peace to you. Let mercy and truth not abandon you; bind them around your throat and write them on the tablets of your heart. Then you will find grace and good discipline before God and human beings.

Trust in the Lord with all your heart, and do not lean on your own understanding. In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will direct your steps. Do not be wise in your own eyes; fear the Lord and turn away from evil.

**R.** Amen.

## Reading from the Book of Exodus  
### Chapter 32

**R.** Thanks be to God.

In those days, when the people saw that Moses was delaying in coming down from the mountain, they gathered against Aaron and said: “Rise, make gods for us who shall go before us. As for this Moses, the man who brought us out of the land of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him.”

Aaron said to them: “Take the golden earrings from the ears of your wives, your sons, and your daughters, and bring them to me.” The people did what he had commanded and brought the earrings to Aaron. When he had received them, he shaped them by casting and made from them a molten calf. They said: “These are your gods, Israel, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.”

When Aaron saw this, he built an altar before it, and he proclaimed aloud: “Tomorrow is a solemnity of the Lord.” Rising early, they offered holocausts and peace offerings; the people sat down to eat and drink, and then rose to play.

The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: “Go, descend. Your people, whom you brought out of the land of Egypt, have sinned. They have departed from the way that you showed them. They have made for themselves a molten calf, sacrificed to it, and, sacrificing offerings to it, said: ‘These are your gods, Israel, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.’”

Again the Lord said to Moses: “I see that this people is stiff-necked. Leave me, so that my anger may burn against them, that I may destroy them, and make you into a great nation.”

But Moses prayed to the Lord his God, saying: “Why, O Lord, does your anger burn against your people, whom you brought out of the land of Egypt with great strength and a mighty hand? I beg you, do not let the Egyptians say: ‘He brought them out deceitfully, in order to kill them in the mountains and wipe them from the earth.’ Let your anger cease, and be appeased concerning the wickedness of your people. Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, your servants, to whom you swore by yourself, saying: ‘I will multiply your offspring like the stars of heaven, and I will give all this land of which I have spoken to your offspring, and you shall possess it forever.’”

The Lord was appeased and did not do the evil that he had spoken of doing against his people.

Moses returned from the mountain, carrying in his hand the two tablets of the testimony, written on both sides and made by the work of God; the writing of God was also engraved on the tablets.

When Joshua heard the tumult of the shouting people, he said to Moses: “The sound of battle is heard in the camp.” He replied: “It is not the cry of those encouraging battle, nor the shout of those compelling flight; I hear the voice of singers.”

When he had drawn near to the camp, he saw the calf and the dances. Enraged, he threw the tablets from his hand and broke them at the foot of the mountain. Seizing the calf that they had made, he burned it and ground it to powder, scattered it in water, and gave it to the children of Israel to drink.

He said to Aaron: “What did this people do to you, that you brought such a great sin upon it?”

He answered: “Let not my lord be indignant. You know this people, that it is inclined toward evil. They said to me: ‘Make gods for us who shall go before us. As for this Moses, the man who brought us out of the land of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him.’

Then I said to them: ‘Which of you has gold?’ They took it and gave it to me, and I threw it into the fire; and this calf came out.”

When Moses saw that the people had been stripped—for Aaron had stripped them for the disgrace of their filth and had set them naked among their enemies—he stood at the gate of the camp and said: “If anyone belongs to the Lord, let him join me.” All the sons of Levi gathered to him.

He said to them: “Thus says the Lord God of Israel: Let each man put his sword upon his thigh. Go and return from gate to gate through the middle of the camp, and let each man kill his brother, his friend, and his neighbor.”

The sons of Levi did according to Moses’ word, and about twenty-three thousand men fell on that day.

Moses said: “You have consecrated your hands today, each man against his son and his brother, so that a blessing may be given to you.”

**R.** Amen.

## Reading from the Book of the Prophet Isaiah  
### Chapter 33

**R.** Thanks be to God.

Thus says the Lord: “Hear, you who are far away, what I have done, and you who are near, acknowledge my strength. The sinners in Zion are terrified; fear has seized the hypocrites. Who among you can dwell with devouring fire? Who among you can dwell with everlasting burnings?

The one who walks in justice and speaks truth, who rejects greed and slander, who shakes his hands free from every bribe, who stops his ears so as not to hear of bloodshed and closes his eyes so as not to see evil—this one shall dwell on high. The heights of the rocky fortresses shall be his refuge; his bread shall be given him, and his waters shall be sure.

His eyes shall see the king in his beauty; they shall behold a distant land. His heart shall meditate on fear: ‘Where is the learned one? Where is the one who weighs the words of the law? Where is the teacher of little ones?’

You shall not see the uncomprehending people, the people of profound speech, whose language you cannot understand, in whom there is no wisdom.”

**R.** Amen.

## Continuation of the Epistle of the Apostle Paul to the Corinthians  
### First Epistle, Chapter 10

**R.** Thanks be to God.

Brothers, we do not want you to be unaware that our fathers were all under the cloud, all passed through the sea, and all were baptized into Moses, in the cloud and in the sea. They all ate the same spiritual food, and all drank the same spiritual drink—for they drank from the spiritual rock that followed them, and the rock was Christ.

Yet God was not well pleased with most of them, for they were struck down in the wilderness. These things happened as figures for us, so that we might not be desirous of evil things, as they desired them. Nor must you become idolaters, as some of them did, as it is written: “The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.”

Nor let us commit fornication, as some of them committed fornication, and twenty-three thousand fell in one day. Nor let us test Christ, as some of them tested him and perished by serpents. Nor let us murmur, as some of them murmured and perished by the destroyer.

All these things happened to them figuratively; they were written for our correction, upon whom the ends of the ages have come. Therefore, whoever thinks that he stands must take care lest he fall.

Let no temptation seize you except what is human. But God is faithful, and he will not allow you to be tempted beyond what you can bear; with the temptation he will also provide a way out, so that you may be able to endure it.

Therefore, my beloved, flee from the worship of idols. I speak as to prudent people; judge for yourselves what I say. Is not the cup of blessing that we bless a participation in the blood of Christ? And is not the bread that we break a participation in the body of the Lord?

Because there is one bread, we, though many, are one body, for we all share in the one bread and the one cup. Consider Israel according to the flesh: are not those who eat the sacrifices participants in the altar?

What then? Am I saying that something sacrificed to idols is anything, or that an idol is anything? No; but what the Gentiles sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons and not to God. I do not want you to become partners with demons. You cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons. You cannot share in the table of the Lord and the table of demons.

Are we provoking the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than he?

“All things are lawful for me,” but not all things build up. Let no one seek his own advantage, but that of the other.

Whatever is sold in the marketplace, eat without asking questions for the sake of conscience. “The earth is the Lord’s and its fullness.”

If an unbeliever invites you and you wish to go, eat whatever is set before you, asking no questions for the sake of conscience. But if someone says, “This has been sacrificed to idols,” do not eat it, for the sake of the one who informed you and for the sake of conscience.

I mean not your own conscience, but that of the other. For why should my freedom be judged by another conscience? If I partake with thanksgiving, why am I blasphemed for that for which I give thanks?

Therefore, whether you eat or drink or do anything else, do everything for the glory of God. Be without offense to Jews, Gentiles, and the Church of God, just as I in all things please everyone, not seeking my own advantage but that of many, so that they may be saved.

**R.** Amen.

## Antiphon 1

The idols of the nations are works of human hands. May those who make them and all who trust in them become like them. But those who fear the Lord should hope in the Lord; he is their helper and protector. **Psalm 113.**

**Prayer.** Lord, who dwell above in the heavens and hold and govern earthly powers: give glory to your name; give forgiveness to sinners. May what we presume upon from your mercy be received in truth, and may we draw from it what we seek, so that your mercy may exclude idols from the assembly of the Church and truth may turn doubtful hearts toward recognition of your worship.

We ask, Lord, add your blessing upon your people and upon their children. Grant the crown of everlasting life that you have promised to those who fear you and for whom you have become salvation. May we not, dead through sins, be cast away from your blessing; but, made participants in life, may we praise your name throughout the ages.

**R.** Amen. Through your mercy, etc.

## Antiphon 2

Rejoice in God our helper; rejoice aloud to the God of Jacob. **Psalm 80.**

**Prayer.** To you, Lord our helper, we pray, applauding with the rejoicing of faith and hope, that our petition, poured out in tribulation, may draw near to your ears and make known the causes of our necessities. May your goodness always attend the prayers of each person, so that you may deliver us. Having been rescued, grant us the ardor of desire to reach you and to proclaim devoutly and harmoniously the unity of the triune majesty.

May we, always devoted to your praises and having attained the path of your justifications, acquire in you, we ask, the ornaments of rejoicing, the remedies of hope, and the crown of faith.

**R.** Amen. Through the mercy of our God, etc.

May the Lord be always with you.

**R.** And with your spirit.

## Antiphon 3

Let the nations know that your name is Lord; you alone are Most High over all the earth. **Psalm 82.**

**R.** Have mercy, O Lord, on our sins for the sake of your name.

**P.** Lest they ever say among the nations: “Where is their God?”

**V.** Help us, God our Savior, and be merciful to our sins.

**P.** Lest they ever say, etc.

**V.** Glory and honor to the Father, etc.

Repeat: Have mercy, O Lord.

To you we cry, O Lord.

**P.** Have mercy and spare your people.

**V.** Priests, pray; bending your knees, say:

**P.** Have mercy.

**V.** Forgive the evils we have done and be merciful toward us.

**P.** Have mercy.

**V.** Look now upon the parched earth and grant the rain of grace.

**P.** Have mercy and spare your people.

## Chapters

May the nations know, Christ, that your name is Lord, for whose sake you were hung upon the cross. May knowledge restore to the Creator those whom ignorance and sloth had surrendered, so that conscience may be converted through faith and they may rejoice in glory through hope.

**Our Father.**

**V.** Deliver us from evil. Folio 10.

Through your mercy, our God, who are blessed and live and rule all things forever and ever.

**R.** Amen.

May the Lord be always with you.

**R.** And with your spirit.

**V.** In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, let us complete this in peace.

**R.** Thanks be to God.

In this order the Hours are completed—namely, Terce, Sext, and None—on the days of the fasts: that is, on the Kalends of January, three days before the Epiphany of the Lord, on Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, and Saturday, which is the Vigil of holy Pentecost; three days before the feast of Saint Cyprian; on the Kalends of November, three days before the feast of Saint Martin; and on the ferial days that occur during the year, except those that have a blessing.

## At Sext

## Reading from the Book of the Prophet Isaiah  
### Chapter 31

**R.** Thanks be to God.

Thus says the Lord: As when a lion roars, and a young lion over its prey, though a multitude of shepherds should gather against it, it will not be frightened by their voice nor terrified by their number, so the Lord of hosts will descend to fight upon Mount Zion and upon its hill. As birds flying, so the Lord of hosts will protect Jerusalem, protecting and delivering, passing over and saving. Return, as you had withdrawn into the depths, children of Israel. On that day each man will cast away the idols of his silver and the idols of his gold, which your hands made for you as a sin. And Assyria will fall by a sword not wielded by a man, and a sword not human will devour it; it will flee, but not from the face of a sword; and its young men will become tributary. And its strength will pass away through terror, and its princes, fleeing, will be afraid: says the Lord, whose fire is in Zion and whose furnace is in Jerusalem.

Behold, a king will reign in righteousness, and princes will rule in judgment. 73 And a man will be as one hiding from the wind and sheltering himself from the storm; as streams of water in thirst, and the shade of a lasting rock in a parched land. The eyes of those who see will not be dimmed, and the ears of those who hear will listen attentively. And the heart of fools will understand knowledge, and the tongue of stammerers will speak quickly and clearly. No longer will the one who is foolish be called a prince, nor will the fraudulent be called noble, says the Lord Almighty.

R. Amen.

Antiphon 1. Our eyes are toward the Lord our God, until he has mercy on us. Psalm 122.

Prayer. To you, Lord, we raise our eyes, whom we confess to sustain the heavens and the structure of the earth by your power. Have mercy, therefore, on us, Lord, have mercy; and pardon our sins, for which we fear you, so that in your merciful kindness you may look upon our contempt and rescue us from the reproach of our offenses by the right hand of your power.

R. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

May the Lord be always with you.

R. And with you, etc.

Antiphon 2. Do good, Lord, to those who are good and upright in heart. Psalm 124.

Prayer. Do good, Lord, and bestow the governance of salvation upon those who are good and upright in heart; watch continually over the protection of your people, and restrain by your right hand the fury of the wicked.

R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

R. Have mercy, for you are God.

V. To you we raise our eyes, who dwell in the heavens.

P. Merciful one.

R. Have mercy.

Prayers. To you we cry out, Lord.

P. We beseech you to hear us.

V. Hear the voice of those who plead, and grant the remedy of life.

P. We beseech you.

V. Remove the causes of sin, and make room for forgiveness.

V. Grant us help, you who remove danger.

P. We beseech you.

Chapters. Exalt our horn, Lord, through the merit of the Catholic faith; let the mind not be stained by the disease of pride, and grant that our steps may walk across the breadth of this world. Let us not proceed, guilty, in fetters, but, thinking humbly, grant us to hasten toward the fullness of hope.

## At None

Proverbs of Solomon (Chapter 3).

R. Thanks be to God.

My son, do not hinder one who is able to do good; if you are able, do good yourself. Do not say to your friend, “Go, return, and tomorrow I shall give,” when you can give at once. For you do not know what the coming day will bring forth. Do not devise evil against your friend when he has confidence in you. Do not contend with a man without cause when he has done you no harm. Do not envy an unjust man or imitate his ways, for every mocker is an abomination to the Lord, and his discourse is with the simple. Want is from the Lord upon the house of the wicked, but the dwellings of the righteous will be blessed. He will mock mockers, and gives grace to the meek.

R. Amen.

Reading from the Book of Exodus (Chapters 32–33).

R. Thanks be to God.

In those days Moses spoke to the children of Israel, saying: “You have committed a very great sin. I will go up to the Lord, to see whether somehow I may be able to plead with him for your crime.” And when he had returned to the Lord, he said: “I beg you, Lord: this people has committed a very great sin, and they have made gods of gold for themselves. Either forgive them this offense, or, if you do not, erase me from your book, which you have written.” The Lord answered him: “Whoever has sinned against me, I will erase him from my book. But now go, and lead this people where I have told you. My angel will go before you. Yet on the day of vengeance I will visit this sin of theirs also.” So the Lord struck the people because of their guilt concerning the calf that Aaron had made.

And the Lord spoke to Moses: “Go, ascend from this place—you and your people whom you led out of the land of Egypt—into the land that I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying: ‘I will give it to your offspring.’ And I will send an angel before you, so that I may drive out the Canaanite, Hittite, Amorite, Cethite, Perizzite, Hivite, and Jebusite, and that they may enter a land flowing with milk and honey. For I will not go up with you, because you are a stiff-necked people, lest I perhaps destroy you on the way.”

When the people heard this very evil word, they mourned, and no one, as was customary, put on his adornment. And the Lord said to Moses: “Say to the children of Israel: ‘You are a stiff-necked people. If I go up among you even once, I will destroy you. Now remove your adornment from yourself, so that I may know what I shall do with you.’” Therefore the children of Israel removed their adornment from Mount Horeb. Moses also took the tabernacle and pitched it outside the camp, far away, and called it the Tabernacle of the Covenant.

R. Amen.

Reading from the Book of the Prophet Isaiah (Chapter 46).

R. Thanks be to God.

Thus says the Lord: “Hear me, house of Jacob and all the remnant of the house of Israel, who have been carried from my womb, who have been borne from my belly. Until old age I am the same, and until gray hairs I will carry you. I made you, and I will bear you; I will carry you and save you. To whom have you compared me, equated me, likened me, and made me similar? You who bring gold from a purse and weigh silver on a balance, hiring a craftsman to make a god, and falling down, worshiping it. They carry it on their shoulders and set it in its place; it will stand, and will not move from its place. Even when they cry out to it, it will not hear, nor will it save them from tribulation.

“Remember this and be ashamed; return to your heart, transgressors. Remember the former age, for I am God, and there is no God beyond me, nor is there one like me, announcing the end from the beginning, and from the outset things that have not yet been done, saying: ‘My counsel shall stand, and all my will shall be accomplished’; calling from the east a bird, and from a distant land the man of my will. I have spoken, and I will bring him; I have created him, and I will make him.”

R. Amen.

Continuation of the Second Epistle of the Apostle Paul to the Corinthians (Chapters 6–7).

R. Thanks be to God.

Brothers, our mouth is open to you, O Corinthians; our heart is enlarged. You are not restricted by us, but you are restricted in your own inward parts. Since you have the same recompense, I speak as to children: be enlarged yourselves also. And do not be yoked with unbelievers. For what partnership is there between righteousness and iniquity? Or what fellowship between light and darkness? What agreement is there between Christ and Belial? Or what share does a believer have with an unbeliever? What agreement is there between the temple of God and idols? For you are the temple of the living God, as the Lord says:

“For I will dwell in them, and walk among them; I will be their God, and they will be my people.”

Therefore, “Come out from their midst and be separate,” says the Almighty Lord, “and do not touch what is unclean; and I will receive you. And I will be a father to you, and you will be sons and daughters to me,” says the Lord.

Therefore, having these promises, beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from every defilement of flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.

R. Amen.

Antiphon 1. Great is the Lord and exceedingly worthy of praise. Psalm 47.

Prayer. Great Lord, exceedingly worthy of praise, extend throughout all peoples the faith of your Church, so that, in whose steps you are recognized as God, in that same Church you may also be praised with the full devotion of the faithful. Graciously receive its prayers, and guard as a solicitous governor those troubled amid the storms of the world, so that, entering by your mercy the city which you founded forever, we may be received within it, proclaiming your wonders in its towers.

R. Amen.

Through your mercy, etc.

Antiphon 2. Remember your congregation, Lord, which you created from the beginning. Psalm 73.

Prayer. Remember, Lord, your congregation, which you created from the beginning and which you redeemed wondrously and mercifully at the price of your blood; you chose this very congregation from among the nations as your possession. Therefore deliver the rod of your inheritance from the attacks of the usurper; and rule it by justifying it in the present age, so that it may inherit it in the age to come. May it, which by divine tradition begs for the coming of your kingdom, reach that same kingdom by hereditary succession, its offense having been forgiven.

R. Amen.

Through your mercy, etc.

Antiphon 3. Let our cry reach you, and do not turn your face from me. Psalm 101.

Prayer. Lord, hear our prayer, and let our cry reach you once every obstacle has been removed. On whatever day we call upon you, may our prayer quickly be opened before you. Do not turn your face from our groans, nor restrain your governance from our conduct, so that we may rejoice in obtaining what we ask, when our desires have reached you.

R. Amen.

Through your mercy, etc.

### At the Canticle

Antiphon. God is not like man, that he should lie, nor like a son of man, that he should be changed.

Canticle of Numbers (Chapter 23).

“Balak, king of the Moabites, brought me from Aram, from the mountains of the east. ‘Come,’ he said, ‘curse Jacob; hurry and denounce Israel.’ How shall I curse one whom God has not cursed?

By what means shall I denounce one whom God does not denounce?

From the summits of the crags I shall see him, and from the hills I shall behold him.

The people shall dwell alone, and shall not be reckoned among the nations.

Who can count the dust of Jacob, or know the number of the offspring of Israel?

May my soul die the death of the righteous, and may my end become like theirs.” 76

“Stand, Balak, and listen; hear, son of Sepnor:

God is not like man, that he should lie, nor like a son of man, that he should be changed.

Has he said something, and will he not do it? Has he spoken, and will he not fulfill it?

I was brought to bless; I cannot prevent the blessing.

There is no idol in Jacob, nor is an image seen in Israel.

The Lord their God is with them, and the trumpet-blast of a king’s victory is among them.

God brought him out of Egypt; his strength is like that of a rhinoceros.

There is no augury in Jacob, nor divination in Israel.

In its times it will be said of Jacob and Israel: What has God done?

Behold, the people rise like a lioness, and lift themselves up like a lion:

It will not lie down until it has devoured its prey and drunk the blood of the slain.”

Prayer. You are, Lord, the star of truth rising from Jacob, and the man arising from Israel. By a new star you are shown to be God, and, placed in a manger, you are believed to be one Christ, God and man. Therefore, because of your great mercy, extend to us the grace of the vision of these things [horum; reading uncertain], so that the radiant sign of your light may appear upon us and drive away all the darkness of vices; and may we who pant with desire for the vision of you be consoled by the reward of your vision.

R. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

Reading from the Book of the Prophet Isaiah (Chapter 2).

R. Thanks be to God.

Thus says the Lord: “Enter into the rock; hide in a pit in the ground from the face of the fear of the Lord and from the glory of his majesty. The haughty eyes of men will be humbled, and the loftiness of men will be bowed down; and the Lord alone will be exalted on that day. For the day of the Lord of hosts is against every proud and lofty person, and against every arrogant one, and he will be humbled; against all the lofty and upright cedars of Lebanon, and against all the oaks of Bashan; against all the high mountains and all the elevated hills; against every lofty tower and every fortified wall; against all the ships of Tarshish and every beautiful object to behold. And every human loftiness will be bowed down, and the height of men will be humbled, and the Lord alone will be exalted on that day. And idols will be utterly crushed.

“And they will enter into the caves of the rocks and the hollows of the earth, from the face of the fear of the Lord and from the glory of his majesty, when he rises to strike the earth. On that day a man will cast away the idols of his silver and the images of his gold, which they made for themselves to worship moles and bats. And he will enter into the fissures of the rocks and the caverns of the stones, from the face of the dread of the Lord and from the glory of his majesty, when he rises to strike the earth. Therefore cease from man, whose breath is in his nostrils, for he is considered exalted.”

R. Amen.

Chapters. Most beloved brothers.

Praise. Alleluia. It shall rejoice.
