## At Terce

Wisdom of Solomon in Proverbs (Chapter 21).

R. Thanks be to God.

My son, whoever closes his ear to the cry of the poor will himself cry out and not be heard. A gift secretly given extinguishes anger, and a present placed in the bosom extinguishes the greatest indignation. It is joy for the just person to practice judgment, and terror for those who work iniquity. The man who strays from the way of instruction will dwell among the assembly of giants. Whoever loves banquets will be in poverty, and whoever loves wine and rich foods will not become wealthy. In place of the just, the wicked is given; in place of the upright, the iniquitous. It is better to dwell in a deserted land than with a quarrelsome and angry woman. A desirable treasure and oil are in the dwelling of the just, but the imprudent man scatters them. Whoever pursues righteousness and mercy will find righteousness, life, and glory.

R. Amen.

Reading from the Book of Deuteronomy (Chapters 5–6).

R. Thanks be to God.

In those days Moses called all Israel and said to them: “Hear, Israel, the ceremonies and judgments that I speak in your ears. Learn them today and fulfill them in deed. The Lord our God made a covenant with us at Horeb. He did not make the covenant with our fathers, but with us, who are present here today; he spoke to us face to face on the mountain from the midst of the fire. I was mediator and stood between the Lord and you at that time, to announce his words to you, for you feared the fire and did not go up the mountain.

“And [the Lord] said: ‘[I am] the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, from the house of slavery. You shall not have foreign gods in my sight. You shall not make for yourself a carved image, nor the likeness of people who are in heaven above, or on earth below, or who move in the waters under the earth. You shall not worship or serve them. For I am the Lord your God, a jealous God, repaying the iniquity of the fathers upon the children to the third and fourth generation of those who hate me, and showing mercy to many thousands who love me and keep my commandments.

“‘You shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain, for whoever has used his name for vanity will not go unpunished. Honor your father and your mother, as the Lord your God commanded you, so that you may live long and it may go well with you in the land that the Lord your God will give you. You shall not kill. Nor shall you commit adultery. You shall not steal. Nor shall you speak false testimony against your neighbor. You shall not covet your neighbor’s wife, nor his house, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his donkey, nor anything that belongs to him.’

“These are the commandments, ceremonies, and judgments that the Lord your God commanded me to teach you, so that you may do them in the land into which you are crossing to possess it; so that you may fear the Lord your God and keep all his commandments and precepts that I command you, you, your children, and your grandchildren, all the days of your life, so that your days may be prolonged. Hear, Israel, and observe that you may do them, and that it may go well with you and you may multiply still more, as the Lord, the God of your fathers, promised to give you a land flowing with milk and honey.”

R. Amen.

Reading from the Book of the Prophet Ezekiel (Chapter 18).

R. Thanks be to God.

The word of the Lord came to me, saying: “What does it mean that you turn this proverb into a saying among yourselves, saying: ‘The fathers ate a sour grape, and the teeth of the children were set on edge’? As I live, says the Lord God, this proverb shall no longer be a saying for you in Israel. Behold, all souls are mine; as the soul of the father is mine, so also the soul of the son is mine. The soul that sins, it shall die.

“And if a man is righteous and practices judgment and righteousness, does not eat upon the mountains, does not lift his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel, does not violate his neighbor’s wife, and does not approach a menstruating woman; if he does not grieve anyone, returns a pledge to the debtor, takes nothing by force, gives his bread to the hungry, and covers the naked with clothing; if he does not lend at interest and does not take more, turns his soul away from iniquity, makes true judgment between one man and another, walks in my precepts, and keeps my judgments so as to practice truth: he is righteous; he shall surely live and shall not die, says the Lord Almighty.”

R. Amen.

Continuation of the First Epistle of the Apostle Paul to the Corinthians (Chapter 8).

Brothers, I think that I have the Spirit of God. Concerning things sacrificed to idols, we know that we all possess knowledge. Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up. If anyone thinks that he knows something, he has not yet known how he ought to know. If anyone loves God, he is known by him.

Concerning foods sacrificed to idols, we know that an idol is nothing in the world, and that there is no God but one. For although there are those who are called gods, whether in heaven or on earth—for indeed there are many gods and many lords—yet for us there is one God, the Father, from whom are all things, and one Lord, Jesus Christ, who enlightens us, through whom are all things and we through him.

But knowledge is not possessed by everyone. Some, even now, with knowledge of the idol, eat the food sacrificed to idols, and their conscience, being weak, is defiled. Food, however, does not commend us to God. For neither will we be lacking if we do not eat, nor will we abound if we eat.

But see to it that this liberty of yours does not somehow become a stumbling block to the weak. For if someone sees one who possesses knowledge reclining in an idol’s temple, will not his conscience, being weak, be emboldened to eat food sacrificed to idols? And will the weak person perish through your knowledge—the brother for whom Christ died? Thus, by sinning against the brothers and striking their weak conscience, you sin against Christ. Therefore, if food causes my brother to stumble, I will never eat meat, lest I cause my brother to stumble.

Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Have I not seen Jesus Christ our Lord? Are you not my work in the Lord? If I am not an apostle to others, yet surely I am to you; for you are the seal of my apostleship in the Lord.

R. Amen.

The spirit of Egypt will be torn apart within it, and I will overthrow its counsel; and they will consult their idols and their diviners, their mediums and their soothsayers. And I will deliver Egypt into the hand of cruel masters, and a strong king will rule over them, says the Lord Almighty.

May the torrent of your delight overflow within us, so that our soul may rejoice that it has crossed the torrent of vices without danger. May we not be torn by the teeth of enemies, but may we rejoice that we have been snatched from the snares of hunters. And you, our helper, may you establish us as heirs in eternal possession—you who, with your Word and Holy Spirit cooperating, made heaven and earth.

God, who through the prophetic voice declares those who fear you blessed, grant within us the pleasing service of your fear, so that from this you may cause us to walk in your ways. ## At None

Proverbs of Solomon (Chapter 21).

R. Thanks be to God.

My son, whoever guards his mouth and his tongue guards his soul from distress. The proud and arrogant person is called unlearned, who acts with arrogance in anger. Sloth kills the lazy person, for his hands refused to do anything. All day he covets and desires, but the righteous person gives and does not cease. The sacrifices of the wicked are abominable, because they are offered from crime. A lying witness will perish; an obedient man speaks victory. The wicked man boldly hardens his face, but the upright corrects his way. There is no wisdom, nor prudence, nor counsel against the Lord. The horse is prepared for the day of battle, but the Lord grants salvation.

Reading from the Book of Deuteronomy (Chapter 6).

R. Thanks be to God.

In those days Moses spoke to the whole assembly of the children of Israel and said to them: “Hear, Israel: the Lord your God is one God. You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your strength. And these words that I command you today shall be in your heart. You shall recount them to your children, and meditate on them sitting in your house, walking on the road, sleeping, and rising. You shall bind them as a sign upon your hand; they shall be and move before your eyes. You shall write them on the threshold and doors of your house.

“And when the Lord your God has brought you into the land concerning which he swore to your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and has given you great and excellent cities that you did not build, houses full of every possession that you did not construct, cisterns that you did not dig, vineyards and olive groves that you did not plant, and when you have eaten and are satisfied, take great care lest you forget the Lord who brought you out of the land of Egypt and from the house of slavery. You shall fear the Lord your God and serve him, and swear by his name. You shall not follow foreign gods, any of the nations that surround you, because the Lord your God, who is in your midst, is a jealous God, lest the anger of the Lord your God be kindled against you and remove you from the face of the earth. You shall not tempt the Lord your God, as you tempted him in the place of temptation. Keep the commandments of the Lord your God, his testimonies and ceremonies, which he commanded you, and do what is pleasing and good in the sight of the Lord, so that it may go well with you and you may enter and possess the land that the Lord your God will give you.”

R. Amen.

Reading from the Book of the Prophet Isaiah (Chapter 49).

Thus says the Lord: “Lift up your eyes around you and see: all these have gathered; they have come to you. As I live, says the Lord, you will clothe yourself with all these as with an ornament.

They will bring your sons in their arms, and carry your daughters upon their shoulders. Kings will be your guardians, and queens your nurses. With face lowered to the earth they will worship you, and they will lick the dust of your feet. And you will know that I am the Lord; those who wait for him will not be put to shame.

“Can spoil be taken from the strong, or can what has been captured by the mighty be saved? For thus says the Lord: Indeed, the captive will be taken from the strong, and what has been taken from the mighty will be saved. I myself will judge those who judged you, and I myself will save your children. I will feed your enemies their own flesh, and they will become drunk with their own blood as with new wine. And all flesh will know that I am the Lord, your Savior and your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel.”

R. Amen.

Continuation of the Epistle of the Apostle Paul to the Ephesians (Chapter 4).

R. Thanks be to God.

Brothers, I say this and testify in the Lord: you must no longer walk as the nations walked in the vanity of their mind, having their understanding darkened, alienated from the life of God through the ignorance that is in them because of the blindness of their hearts. 80 They, despairing, have handed themselves over to immorality, to the practice of every impurity, in greed.

But you did not learn Christ in this way, if indeed you heard him and were taught in him, as truth is in Jesus: that you should put off, according to your former way of life, the old man, who is corrupted according to the desires of error; that you should be renewed in the spirit of your mind and put on the new man, who has been created according to God in righteousness and holiness of truth.

R. Amen.

Antiphon 1. But our God is in heaven, and high in heaven, and on earth; he has done all that he willed. Psalm 134.

Prayer. We praise you, Lord, because you are kind and great. Your greatness and goodness are attested both by wonders and by works. Great, therefore, are you, Lord, in creating such astonishing and manifold things from nothing; kind, in restoring the perishing world through the blood of your Christ; great, in raising corpses from the dead; kind, in granting unending life to those raised. Grant, Almighty God, to us your suppliants both the power to understand such greatness and the peace to receive your kindness.

R. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God, etc.

May the Lord be always with you.

R. And with your spirit.

Prayer. God, who is like you in goodness as well as in power? You who instruct your saints in goodness and defend them in power; you who restrain the raging mouths of enemies and acknowledge the supplications of your own: grant to us, who trust in your goodness, a share in good works that may make us safe from the enemy’s counsel and show us, cleansed from guilt, to be pleasing to you. And may you lead us to eternal glory, you who alone are Most High over all the earth.

R. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God, etc.

**Chapters.** Rise up, O God, who judge the earth, and rule by the arm of your strength those whom you have deigned to acquire through the trophy of the Cross; and from those for whom the pouring out of sacred blood stands as redemption, let a dutiful confession be offered to you. When the herald has proclaimed it at the sound of the trumpet, may we hasten joyfully to your advent. ### On the Fast of the Epiphany

Let us all fast in order to entreat our Lord Jesus Christ for our sins and to obtain peace; or let us frequently attend the Lord’s church to hear the sacred readings.

## ON THE THIRD DAY, WHICH IS THE VIGIL OF THE EPIPHANY OF THE LORD

### At Matins

**Antiphon.** But you, O Lord, are my protector, my glory, and the one who lifts up my head. Psalm III.

**Prayer.** Although, Lord. See fol. 68.

**Antiphon 1.** Announce his salvation from day to day. Psalm XCXV.

[Col. 0170B] **Prayer.** May the multitude of the redeemed sing a new song to you. You have performed new wonders: a new light has arisen from the Virgin, which nevertheless was not new to the Godhead; but new is the miracle displayed in an extraordinary manner, a new mystery of regeneration, in which you renew the whole world. New kinds of power appear in the healing of the sick; a new manner of humility and patience in the face of the pride of persecutors; a new and wondrous kind of power in the glory of the one rising again. The power of your majesty is displayed anew to human eyes when you carry the true human being to the heights of heaven. Grant that those for whom you, glorious maker, have brought about such new wonders may be followers of your footsteps and heirs of your glory; and that you may mingle the melody of song, as well as our resounding voices, among the tumult of the saints. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon 2.** The Lord is great in Zion and exalted above all peoples. Psalm XCVIII.

**Prayer.** Our Redeemer and Lord, who are exalted above every height and acknowledged as great in Zion: increase and perfect the faith of your Church in you, and cause the peoples to grow together in its sincerity, so that, confessing your name, which is great, and offering you the honor of royal glory through the service of faith, you may look upon us in mercy from on high and transfer us from this lowliness of earth to the dwellings of heaven. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God, etc.

[Col. 0170D] **Antiphon 3.** The Lord remembered us and blessed us. Psalm CXIII.

**Prayer.** Lord, who are above. See fol. 72.

R\. Jerusalem, the holy city, no longer needs the sun, because the glory of God illuminates it.  
P. Its splendor is the Lamb.  
V\. The towers of Jerusalem shall be built of gold, and its battlements of pure gold.  
P. Its splendor.  
V\. Glory and honor to the Father, etc.  
P. Its splendor.

### At Lauds

**Antiphon.** Do not cast us away, O Lord, from your presence, and do not take your Holy Spirit from us. Psalm L.

**Prayer.** Do not cast us away, O Lord, from your presence, and do not take your mercy from us; so that those whom the guilt of their crimes holds liable may be absolved by the clemency of your compassion. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God, etc.

**For the Canticle. Antiphon.** The splendor of light illuminates it, and its lamp is the Lamb.

### Canticle of Tobit (Chapter XIII)

You shall shine with bright light throughout all the boundaries of the earth; * many nations shall come to you from afar, and the inhabitants of the remotest parts of the earth shall come to the name of the Lord God,

bringing their gifts in their hands, to offer them with joy to the King of heaven. * And the name of the Lord shall be great throughout all ages of ages.

Cursed are all who despise you, * and all who blaspheme you;

cursed are all who hate you, * and all who have spoken a harsh word against you;

cursed are all who cast you down, and all who destroy your walls, * and all who overthrow your towers, and all who set your dwellings on fire;

and blessed shall be all who build you, * forever.

Then rejoice and be glad with the children of the righteous, * because they shall all be gathered together and shall bless the Lord forever.

Blessed are those who love you; * blessed are those who rejoice in your peace.

And blessed are all people who shall be saddened by all your scourges, * for they shall rejoice and behold all your joy throughout the ages.

My soul shall bless the Lord, the great King, * because he has delivered Jerusalem,

and his house shall be built again, * and throughout all ages of ages it shall confess the name of the King of heaven.

The gates of Jerusalem shall be fashioned of emerald and sapphire, * and all your walls of precious stones;

the towers of Jerusalem shall be built of gold, * and its battlements of pure gold.

The streets of Jerusalem sing a song of joy, * and every lane of it says, Alleluia.

Blessed is the Lord, who exalts you, and blessed is he throughout all ages of ages, * because in you every holy person shall be blessed forever.

[Col. 0171D] **Matutinal Responsory. Antiphon.** Send forth your light and your truth, O Lord.  
V\. They themselves have led me and brought me to your holy mountain.  
Glory and honor to the Father, etc.

**Lauda.** Let every spirit praise the Lord. Psalm CXLVIII.

### Reading from the Book of the Prophet Isaiah (Chapter XLVIII)

R\. Thanks be to God.

Thus says the Lord: Hear these things from me, O house of Jacob, you who are called by the name of Israel and have come forth from the waters of Judah; you who swear by the name of the Lord and make mention of the God of Israel, but not in truth or in righteousness. For they are called from the holy city and established upon the God of Israel; the Lord of hosts is his name.

[Col. 0172A] I announced the former things from that time; they went forth from my mouth, and I made them known. Suddenly I acted, and they came to pass. For I knew that you are hard, that your neck is an iron sinew, and your forehead bronze. I foretold them to you from that time, and before they came I declared them to you, lest you should say, “My idols have done these things, and my carved images and cast images have commanded them.” You have heard; see it all. But you did not announce it. From that time I made new things known to you, hidden things that you did not know. Now they have been created, and not from that time; even before the day, and you did not see them, lest you should say, “Behold, I knew them.”

You have neither heard nor known, nor has your ear been open from that time; for I know that you will act treacherously, treacherously, and from the womb I called you a transgressor. For the sake of my name I shall put off my anger, and I shall bridle you with my praise, lest you perish. Behold, I have refined you, but not as silver; I have chosen you in the furnace of poverty. For my own sake I shall act, so that I may not be blasphemed, and I shall give my glory to no other. R\. Amen.

**Hymn.** Fountain of kindness.  
**Supplication.** Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world.  
**Chapters.** Most beloved brothers, who [have everything].  
**Lauda.** Alleluia. The deserted places shall rejoice.  
**Blessing.** Christ the Lord, who is with the Father. See fol. 69 and 70.

### At Terce

### From the Proverbs of Solomon (Chapter XV)

R\. Thanks be to God.

My son, the lips of the wise scatter knowledge, but the heart of fools is unlike them. The sacrifices of the wicked are abominable to the Lord, but the vows of the righteous are acceptable. The way of the wicked is an abomination to the Lord; whoever follows righteousness is loved by him. Severe correction is for one who abandons the way of life; whoever hates reproof shall die. Hell and destruction are before the Lord; how much more the hearts of the children of men? A scoffer does not love one who corrects him, nor does he go to the wise. The heart of the wise makes the face cheerful, but in sorrow of spirit the spirit is cast down. The heart of the wise seeks instruction, but the mouth of fools feeds on ignorance. All the days of the poor are evil; a secure mind is like a continual banquet. Better is a little with the fear of the Lord than great treasures and insatiability. Better is an invitation to vegetables with love than to a fattened calf with hatred. An angry man provokes quarrels, but one who is patient calms those that have been stirred up. The way of the wicked is like a hedge of thorns; the way of the righteous is without stumbling. R\. Amen.

### Reading from the Book of Deuteronomy (Chapters VII–VIII)

R\. Thanks be to God.

In those days Moses spoke to the children of Israel, saying: Hear, O Israel: the Lord your God is in your midst, a great and fearsome God. He himself shall destroy these nations before you, little by little and in stages. You will not be able to destroy them all at once, lest the beasts of the earth multiply against you. And the Lord your God shall deliver them into your sight, and he shall kill them until you have utterly destroyed them. He shall deliver their kings into your hands, and you shall destroy their name from under heaven; no one shall be able to resist you until you crush them. You shall burn their carved images with fire. You shall not covet the silver and gold from which they are made, nor take anything from them for yourself, lest you offend, because it is an abomination to the Lord your God. You shall not bring anything from an idol into your house, lest you become accursed, as it too is. You shall detest it as filth and regard it as pollution and the dirt of abomination, because it is accursed.

[Col. 0173A] Carefully observe every commandment that I command you today, so that you may do it, live, and multiply; and, having entered, may possess the land for which the Lord swore to your fathers. And you shall remember the whole journey by which the Lord your God led you for forty years through the wilderness, to afflict you and test you, and to make known what was in your heart, whether you would keep his commandments or not. He afflicted you with want; he gave you food, manna, which neither you nor your fathers knew, to show you that man does not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds from the mouth of God. R\. Amen.

### Reading from the Book of the Prophet Isaiah (Chapter XXX)

R\. Thanks be to God.

The Lord waits to have mercy on you, and therefore he shall be exalted in sparing you, because the Lord is a God of judgment. Blessed are all who wait for him. For the people of Zion shall dwell in Jerusalem; you shall weep no more. When he has mercy, he shall have mercy on you; at the sound of your cry, as soon as he hears it, he shall answer you. And the Lord shall give you scant bread and little water, and he shall no longer cause your teacher to fly away from you; your eyes shall see your instructor. And your ears shall hear a word behind you warning, “This is the way; walk in it,” whether you turn to the right or to the left.

[Col. 0173C] And you shall defile the plates of your silver carvings and the covering of your golden cast image, and you shall scatter them like the uncleanness of a menstruating woman. “Go out,” you shall say to it. And rain shall be given to your seed wherever you sow on the earth; and the bread of the produce of the land shall be most abundant and rich. On that day your lamb shall feed in a spacious pasture, and your oxen and the young asses that work the land shall eat mingled fodder, as on a threshing floor when it has been winnowed. And on every lofty mountain and every raised hill there shall be streams of flowing waters, on the day of the slaughter of many, when the tower falls. And the light of the moon shall be like the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, like the light of seven days, on the day when the Lord binds up the wound of his people and heals the stroke of its wound. R\. Amen.

### The Sequel of the Epistle of Paul the Apostle to the Ephesians (Chapter V)

R\. Thanks be to God.

Brothers, be imitators of God, as beloved children, and walk in love, just as Christ loved us and gave himself for us as an offering and sacrifice to God, for a fragrant odor. But let fornication, and every uncleanness or greed, not even be named among you, as is fitting for saints; nor obscenity, foolish talk, or coarse joking, which has no proper place, but rather thanksgiving. For know this and understand: no fornicator, or impure person, or unclean person, or greedy person—which is service of idols—has an inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and God. Let no one deceive you with empty words, for because of these things the anger of God comes upon the sons of disobedience. Therefore do not become their partners.

[Col. 0174A] For once you were darkness, but now you are light in the Lord. Walk as children of light—for the fruit of light is in all goodness, righteousness, and truth—testing what is pleasing to the Lord. And do not participate in the unfruitful works of darkness; rather, expose them. For the things they do in secret are shameful even to mention. But everything that is exposed is made manifest by the light, and everything that is made manifest is light. Therefore he says: “Rise, you who sleep; arise from the dead, and Christ will enlighten you.” R\. Amen.

**Antiphon 1.** Great is our Lord and fearsome above all gods. For all the gods of the nations are demons, but the Lord made the heavens. Psalm XCXV.

**Prayer.** Lord, who are exalted above all nations and dwell gloriously in the heavens, look down favorably from on high upon our lowliness. Just as your Church, which had been hindered by the defect of barrenness, is now, believing in you, full of the merits of virtues and rich in children, so may our mind, barren and unfruitful in works, by your gift receive the seed of the word and abound in plentiful fruits. And may it strive with the unity of the heart to love your name, renowned from the rising of the sun to its setting, and praise it with the assent of faith. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon 2.** Serve the Lord your God, and do not worship foreign gods, for the Lord is holy. Rejoice in God our helper; shout for joy to the God of Jacob. Psalm LXXX.

**Prayer.** To you, our Lord and helper, with the rejoicing of faith. See fol. 72.

**Antiphon 3.** Turn to God with all your heart, remove foreign gods from your midst, serve the Lord alone, and he will deliver you from the hand of your enemies. Hear this, all nations; perceive it with your ears, you who inhabit the world. Psalm XLVIII.

R\. The glory of God appeared in the cloud.  
P. As in the days of Moses.  
And he shall be revealed just as Solomon prayed in supplication.  
V\. The Lord has been revealed, for he dwelt on high; he filled Zion with judgment and righteousness, and there shall be faith in his times.  
P. As in the days of Moses.  
V\. Glory and honor, etc.  
P. As in the days of Moses.

**Intercessions.** We cry to you, God; hear us.  
P. And deliver us from the scourge of your anger.  
V\. Cherish the contrite and protect the humbled; raise up those who have been cast down; have mercy on those who entreat you.  
P. And deliver us from the scourge.  
V\. Exalted God, attend to our cry, forgive our sins, and quickly grant rain.  
P. And deliver us from the scourge.  
V\. Hear those who weep and comfort those who mourn; give joy to captives and restore their homeland to exiles.  
P. And deliver us from the scourge.

**Supplication.** Let us pray to our Lord Jesus Christ, the Author of light; let us entreat him with every supplication to deign graciously to illuminate us with his brightness.  
R\. Grant this, eternal almighty God.

**Chapters.** Open, we beseech you, Lord, our mouth with wisdom, so that we may meditate with our heart and speak prudence with our tongue; and, lest we be compared with senseless beasts, let us be instructed in the teachings of divine law. Thus may our understanding seek only you, and, praising you in eternal joy with all the saints, receive everlasting rewards.

**Our Father, etc.**

At Sext, let everything be said as at Sext, which is said throughout the year. At None, let them be said as on the second preceding day of the fasts.

# 85. ON THE FEAST OF THE APPARITION OF THE LORD

[Col. 0175]

### At Vespers

[Col. 0175A]

**Lauda.** He who made the sun.  
P. For the brightness of day; the moon and stars for the light of night.  
V\. He who troubles the sea and makes its waves resound—the Lord almighty is his name.  
P. For the brightness of day.

**Prayer.** Lord, with whom is the fountain of life and in whose light we see light, nourish within us the splendor of your knowledge, so that you may give us who thirst the drink of life and restore the understanding of our darkened souls with heavenly light. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Sono.** His name remains before the sun, and his throne before the moon; and all the tribes of the earth shall be blessed in him. Alleluia.  
V\. In his days righteousness shall arise, and abundance of peace, until the moon is lifted up. And he shall rule from sea to sea and from the rivers to the ends of the earth. Before him the Ethiopians shall fall. Alleluia.  
The Lord be always with you.  
R\. And with you.

[Col. 0175C] **Antiphon.** The great King has appeared in Israel, and the kings of the earth have come.  
P. To adore him; and they offered him gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh.  
V\. For behold, the kings of the earth have gathered and come together as one.  
P. To adore him; and they offered him gifts.  
V\. Glory and honor to the Father, etc.  
P. To adore him; and they offered him gifts.

**Prayer.** Lord Jesus Christ, whose gifts the Magi offered in mystery declare you to be God, king, and human being: so that in these gifts you might accept the first fruits of the nations, perfecting the fullness of the nations in salvation, be present to us through those things which we truly believe to remain distinct yet without confusion in you—while for us you suffer as an innocent human being, conquer as a powerful king, and remain incorruptible as almighty God. To your Passion, indeed, myrrh is owed; to your kingship, gold; and to your Godhead, incense. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon.** The fields of the wilderness have put forth a shoot, the flowering shoot of Israel.  
P. Because the Lord the King has come with joy in the light of his majesty, so that they may adore him.  
V\. Let the heavens rejoice, let the earth exult; let the sea and its fullness be moved.  
P. Because the King has come.  
V\. Glory and honor, etc.  
P. Because the King has come.  
The Lord be always with you.  
R\. And with you.

**Lauda.** Let all his angels adore him, alleluia.  
P. It heard, and Zion rejoiced. Alleluia, alleluia.  
V\. The Lord has reigned; let the earth exult; let the many islands rejoice.  
P. It heard, and Zion rejoiced.  
V\. Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son, etc.  
P. It heard, and Zion rejoiced.

### Hymn

Illuminating the loftiest  
sphere of shining stars,  
peace, life, light, and truth,  
Jesus, favor those who pray.

But by the mystical baptism  
the waters of the Jordan,  
which once were turned backward,  
consecrated the present day.

Or whether a star shining in heaven  
marked the Virgin’s childbirth,  
and, adored on this day,  
led the Magi to the manger;

or whether he infused  
the taste of wine into jars full of water,  
the knowing servant drew out  
what he himself had not filled.

Seeing the waters changed in color,  
the rivers become drunk,  
the elements, transformed, marvel  
at passing into other usages.

Thus, while five loaves  
are divided among five thousand men,  
food grew beneath the teeth  
of those eating in their mouths;  
it multiplied even more  
at the expense of the bread.

He who saw these things marveled  
at the continuous courses of the springs.  
Among the hands of those breaking it,  
the flowing bread is poured forth;  
the things left untouched, which the men had not broken,  
slip beneath the fragments.

Remember, Author of salvation, etc.

Glory to you, O Lord, etc.

**Supplication.** Let us pray to our Lord Jesus Christ, the Author of light; let us entreat him with every supplication to deign graciously to illuminate and enlighten us with the light of his brightness.  
R\. Grant this, eternal almighty God.

Kyrie, have mercy.  
R\. Christ, have mercy.  
Kyrie, have mercy.

**Chapters.** Alpha and Omega, beginning and end, God and human being, infinite and finite; in whom the Godhead is perceived as the beginning and the Humanity as the final point; surpassing all things, giving life to everything, and containing the universe: have mercy on us, because you deigned to be born for us while remaining in yourself and appearing to us; while subsisting in yourself and helping us; while never being absent in power from the Father and being mercifully present to save the wretched; while filling the heavenly realms and not abandoning earthly things. Perfect in us, we beseech you, the benefits of the most compassionate Redeemer, while preserving the glory of the immeasurable Creator, so that through the devotion with which you stood forth as Redeemer, you may also be recognized as the forgiver of sins.

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. Fol. 2.

Humble yourselves for the blessing.

The Lord be always with you.  
R\. And with you.

**Blessing.** May the Only-Begotten Son of almighty God the Father, called Alpha and Omega, bless you.  
R\. Amen.  
He who is the beginning and the end: may he raise us up to live with him through infinite ages.  
R\. Amen.  
And, having rescued you from evils, may he so illumine you with the light of his brightness that he may enrich you both with the rewards of glory and with the gifts of eternity.  
R\. Amen.  
Through his mercy.

**Lauda.** He sent me to heal the brokenhearted, alleluia.  
P. To proclaim redemption to captives and restore light to the blind. Alleluia, alleluia.  
V\. The Lord sent redemption to his people; he commanded his covenant forever.  
P. To proclaim redemption to captives.  
V\. Glory and honor to the Father, etc.  
P. To proclaim redemption to captives.

**Prayer.** Lord God, who willed that John the child should precede the coming of your Only-Begotten Son, so that, sent by you, he might prepare the way for Christ in the hearts of unbelievers by healing the brokenhearted and restoring the brightness of light to the blind: by his intercession enlighten also the blindness of our hearts and change the tribulations of our hearts into eternal joy, so that we who are lifted up with Christian joy by the birth of your Only-Begotten Son may not be saddened at his judgment by any bonds of punishment. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Let the priest say: The Lord be always with you.  
R\. And with you.  
In the name of the Lord.

### At Matins

**Antiphon.** Salvation belongs to the Lord, and your blessing is upon your people. Psalm III.

**Prayer.** You are, Lord, salvation. See fol. 46.

**Antiphon 1.** In you, Jerusalem, the Lord shall appear.  
P. And his honor shall be seen upon you. And kings shall walk in your light, and nations shall walk in your brightness.  
V\. And it shall remain with the sun and before the moon, from generation to generation and forever and ever.  
P. And his honor.  
V\. Glory and honor, etc.  
P. And his honor.

**Prayer.** Make us rejoice, Lord, in the vision of that blessed Jerusalem and be raised up in perpetual joy within her bosom, in which you promise to shine as eternal light and whose honor you promise to be. Grant us, therefore, to be stripped of worldly trifles through desire for her and clothed in abundant virtues, so that we may always embrace her as our mother, for whom, by appearing, you became unfailing light. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon 2.** Glorious is his appearance, and his form among the children of men.  
P. Before him kings shall shut their mouths. Those to whom he was not announced shall adore him.  
V\. Before him the Ethiopians shall fall, and his enemies shall lick the earth.  
P. Before him they shall shut their mouths.  
V\. Glory and honor to the Father, etc.  
P. Before him they shall shut their mouths.

**Prayer.** God, Son of God, whose form and appearance among human beings are glorious, take us up to yourself to be glorified and establish us in the placement of those crowned at your right hand, so that we who open our mouths in your praises may not be weighed down by the senses of the flesh; and that we who seek the consolation of your glorious appearance may fully enjoy the consolation of your vision. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon 3.** In the days of King Herod, behold, Magi came from the East to Jerusalem.  
P. Saying: Where is he who has been born King of the Jews? For we saw his star in the East and have come to adore him.  
V\. For behold, the kings of the earth have gathered and come together as one.  
P. Saying: Where is he?  
V\. Glory and honor to the Father, etc.  
P. Saying: Where is he?

**Prayer.** King of all ages, most high Christ God, who, born of the Virgin in the days of King Herod, were revealed to the Magi, who were seeking you, by a new star: may the protection of your power appear in us to drive away every danger of darkness, so that the star of your majesty may shine in us in such a way that no obstacle of error may stand in our way when we seek you; that we may run eagerly to see you and, having seen you, rejoice without delay. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

R\. Jerusalem, behold, the King of kings has appeared in you, and the islands shall be shaken from their places. All the princes of the nations shall descend from their thrones and bring the diadem from their heads.  
P. And they shall offer him gold, frankincense, and myrrh from their precious stones.  
V\. Behold, the kings of the earth have gathered and come together as one.  
P. And they shall offer him.  
V\. The kings of Tarshish and the islands shall offer gifts; the kings of Arabia and Sheba shall bring gifts to God.  
P. Gold.  
V\. Glory and honor to the Father, etc.  
P. Jerusalem.

**Prayer.** God, Son of God, ineffable power of the Father, who by a new star have shown yourself great among the nations as King of kings and appear glorious in that blessed city; whom the islands tremble before, whom princes and the nations of the Gentiles obey, while all kingdoms yield to you and the diadems of kings are laid beneath you: deign now in grace to show yourself compassionate to our senses and manifest in our conduct, so that, possessing the first fruits of the spirit, we may always dedicate to you through gifts those things by which, with hearts pleasing to you, we may deserve to enter that blessed Jerusalem; and, bringing you the purest gold of our works, may deserve to be participants in your kingdom. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon.** The kings of Tarshish and the islands offer gifts; the kings of Arabia and Sheba shall bring presents.  
P. And all the kings of the earth shall adore in his presence; all nations serve him, because he delivered the needy from the powerful and the poor who had no helper.  
V\. He delivered their souls from usury and iniquity, and their name is honored before him.  
P. And they shall adore.  
R\. Glory, etc.  
P. And they shall adore.

**Prayer.** Lord Jesus Christ, to whom kings and islands offer gifts, who came with unconquered power to free the poor from the powerful and, through heavenly compassion, to rescue the fragile human race from the power of the ancient enemy: when we had been kept far from you, made needy of your mercies, subjected to his iniquity, and consigned to the bonds of sins, may your goodness now rescue us from his cruelty and commend us, restored to you, to remain with you. Thus may we who confess that we have been redeemed through your mercy rejoice afterward, through your gift, in glorifying you as our rewarder. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon.** Those who nourish you, O Lord, shall be kings, and your queens shall be your nurses.  
P. With face inclined to the earth they shall adore you, and they shall lick the dust of your feet; and you shall be acknowledged as the Lord, in whom all who await you shall not be put to shame.  
V\. Nation and offspring shall praise your works together and proclaim your power.  
P. With face inclined to the earth.  
V\. Glory and honor to the Father, etc.  
P. With face inclined to the earth.

**Prayer.** Lord, whom peoples adore with face bowed to the ground while all things are subjected to your rule, grant Christian peoples unfailing joy and extend the joys of your Apparition today, to be dedicated among the nations. May you also always be favorable to us, so that you may be found compassionate in judgment, and so that from your face there may arise such unceasing consolation for our life that none of ours may perish who awaits you as the one true God. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon.** Herod questioned the Magi: What sign did you see above the newborn king?  
P. We saw a shining star and have come to adore God.  
V\. Clap your hands, all nations; shout to God with a voice of exultation.  
P. We saw a star.  
V\. Glory and honor to the Father, etc.  
P. We saw a star.

**Prayer.** Lord Jesus Christ, who so illumine the mouths of the Magi with the proclamation of your truth in answer to Herod’s question that through them you reveal yourself as King of kings, when they say that they saw the sign of a shining star that illuminates the whole world: we ask and beseech you to grant your Church the desired light of your vision. May you also appear in it as a star precious to all, so that, deterred by no questioning of the adversary, we may proclaim your great works with open mouth and be everywhere illumined by the protection of eternal light. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

R\. A man appeared in his majesty, surrounded by radiance; and from the brightness of the Lord’s coming the earth shall be illumined, and there shall be joy and gladness for all the people.  
P. Thus indeed kings and princes shall come and adore him.  
V\. His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and it reaches to the Ancient of Days; and all power has been given to him.  
P. Thus indeed kings and princes shall come.

V\. Glory and honor to the Father, etc.  
P. Thus indeed kings and princes shall come.

## 88. Prayer

God, who willed to clothe the very small star with the brightness of sudden grace, show, we beseech you, your face to Christian peoples, so that, just as you finally showed the wandering Magi the path of the true road, so you may grant us sinners a harbor of eternal salvation. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon.** Lofty men shall pass over to you and shall be yours; they shall adore you and entreat you. Only in you is God, and there is none besides you.  
P. Truly you are a hidden God, the God of Israel, the Savior.  
V\. Lord God of hosts, who is like you? You are powerful, Lord, and your truth is all around you.  
P. Truly you are God.  
V\. Glory and honor, etc.  
P. Truly.

**Prayer.** All the lofty and exalted men of the earth shall adore you, Lord Jesus Christ, because you deigned to be born humbly on earth in order to save human beings. For in you God truly is present, because you, the Word hidden in flesh but not changed, possess one name with the Father. Therefore let all who oppose you be put to shame: either let them be ashamed in such a way that they return to you, or let them be confounded in you if they do not turn to you at all. Therefore appear as our Savior for us who are to be saved, while you grant us to believe in you, pass over to you, and love you with our whole heart. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy. And you are God, blessed and glorious throughout the ages of ages.  
R\. Amen.

**Antiphon.** The light of the moon shall be like the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, like the light of seven days.  
P. On the day when the Lord binds up the wound of his people and heals the stroke of its wound: for behold, the Lord comes with joy.  
V\. And the nations shall fear your name, O Lord, and all the kings of the earth your glory.  
P. On the day when he binds up the wound.  
V\. Glory and honor, etc.  
P. On the day when he binds up the wound.

**Prayer.** God, who are to come to bind up the wound of your people and heal the stroke of our wound, be present, so that you may illuminate whatever is faulty or slippery in us with the light of your divinity. Thus may neither the moon burn us through the night of this age, nor the sun of truth in the day of the coming judgment grieve us by burning us. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon.** Behold the star that the Magi had seen in the East went before them until it came above the place where the child was.  
P. When the Magi saw the star, they rejoiced with exceedingly great joy.  
V\. Seeing it in this way, they were amazed and troubled, and all their inward parts were moved.  
P. When the Magi saw the star.  
V\. Glory and honor, etc.  
P. When the Magi saw the star.

**Prayer.** That star, Lord, which announced to the astonished Magi that you, born on earth, were king, did not follow the celestial paths of the stars when a new star appeared with the Virgin’s new childbirth; rather, to show you to human beings as Christ, it went ahead as far as the very place of your birth. Therefore we implore you with poured-out prayers: you who, through its indication, directed the journeys of the Magi without error, sanctify our hearts when you appear, so that, walking before you in equity and righteousness, we may deserve to reach the joys you have promised. R\. Amen.

May the grace of your right hand lead us, Lord Jesus Christ, who live with the Father and the Holy Spirit and rule all things throughout the ages of ages.

The Lord be always with you.  
R\. And with you.

R\. You shall shine with bright light throughout all the boundaries of the earth. Many nations shall come to you from afar, and the inhabitants of the remotest parts of the earth shall come bearing gifts.  
P. They offer them with joy to the King of heaven, and the name of the Lord shall be great throughout all ages.  
V\. All shall come from Sheba, bringing gold and frankincense and announcing praise to the Lord.  
P. To the King of heaven.  
V\. Glory and honor, etc.  
P. To the King of heaven.

**Prayer.** May the light of your brightness abound, we beseech you, Lord, throughout our days and to the ends of the earth, so that those whom you illumine with the light of your Apparition you may lift up everywhere with an abundance of peace. And while we fulfill the vow of service assigned to us, may we receive the luminous effect of heavenly light. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon.** A great sign appeared in heaven: a woman clothed with the sun, and the moon beneath her feet, and upon her head a crown of twelve stars. And she was hastening to give birth, and she gave birth to a son.  
P. He is to rule all nations with an iron rod.  
V\. He placed his tent in the sun and himself, like a bridegroom coming forth from his bridal chamber.  
P. He is to rule all nations.  
V\. Glory and honor, etc.  
P. He is to rule all nations.

## Prayer

O God, sanctifier of this present day, who bestowed the name of this holy feast from its wonders: grant to your Church that, just as it is called Epiphany—that is, today’s solemnity, [Col. 0181C] 89 and manifestation and appearance—so the splendor of your Majesty may shine among your people, and the light of holiness may appear; so that this people, consecrated in your name, may continually possess in its manner of life that which this feast is called by name. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

## Antiphon

Behold, the fragrance of my son is like the fragrance of a full field, which the Lord has blessed. May God give you the dew of heaven and the richness of the earth. P. So that nations may serve you and tribes may worship you.

V. Ask of me, and I will give you the nations as your inheritance, and the ends of the earth as your possession. P. So that nations may serve you and worship you.

V. Glory and honor, etc. P. So that they may serve.

## Prayer

Glorious God, Father and Lord, who granted that nations should serve and tribes worship your only-begotten [Col. 0181D] and coeternal Son: we ask that we may ourselves be his possession; that we may not depart from the commands of this Son of yours, and that you may bind us indivisibly to him, whom you gloriously proclaim to have been begotten from you. R. Amen.

For with you, supreme Father, and with the Holy Spirit, he is one God forever and ever.

The Lord be with you. R. And with you.

## Antiphon

The hearer of the words of the Lord, who saw the vision of the Almighty, said: I shall see him, but not now; I shall behold him, but not near. A star shall arise from Jacob, and a man shall rise from Israel.

V. Great is our Lord, and great is his power; and there is no number to his wisdom. P. I shall see him.

V. Glory and honor, etc. P. I shall see.

## Prayer

You are, Lord, the star of truth arising from Jacob, [Col. 0182A] and the man rising from Israel; and in the new star you showed yourself as God, and, placed in the manger as God and man, you were believed to be one Christ. Because of your great mercy, prolong for us the grace of seeing you; let the radiant sign of your light appear in us, so that it may drive away all the darkness of vices; so that we who pant with desire to see you may be comforted by the reward of seeing you. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

## Response

Heaven shines, and earth gleams with the brightness of God, because he has come forth from his holy dwelling to heal the brokenhearted and restore light to the blind. P. Rejoice today, all nations, because the Savior has appeared in your midst; fear no longer.

V. For the grace of God our Savior has appeared to all people. [Col. 0182B] P. Rejoice today.

V. Glory and honor, etc. P. Rejoice today.

## Prayer

The bright-red heaven shines, Lord, with the serenity of the stars, and the earth itself is made serene with resplendent light, because you have deigned to appear to the world from your holy dwelling. Therefore heal the sadness of our hearts, because you came for this purpose: to redeem all things. Grant to our eyes that light by which, purified, we may always be worthy to behold you; so that we who joyfully proclaim the gladness of your Appearance among the nations may rejoice with you in unending joy. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

## Antiphon

I am Alpha and Omega, the first and the last, the beginning and the end. P. I am the root and offspring of David, the bright and morning star. The bridegroom and the bride [Col. 0182C] say: Come. And let the one who thirsts come, and let him receive the water of life freely.

V. The Lord, God of gods, has spoken and summoned the earth. P. I am.

V. Glory, etc. P. I am Alpha and Omega.

## Prayer

Alpha and Omega, beginning and end, root and offspring, son and lord of David, Christ, God and man, through whom indeed exists the one from whom you deigned to be: be favorable to us, while you rule us as David’s Lord and redeem us as the humble and merciful one; so that, subjecting our devotion to your scepter, you alone may possess us forever, you who alone became victor over the realms below. R. Amen.

And you remain blessed God forever and ever. R. Amen.

[Col. 0182D] The Lord be with you. R. And with you.

## At Lauds

### At the Canticle

**Antiphon.** Blessed are you, Lord God of Israel, because you have visited us and have wrought the redemption of your people.

### Canticle of Zechariah (Chapter I)

And he raised up a horn of salvation for us, * in the house of David his servant.

As he spoke through the mouth of his holy prophets, * who have been from of old:

Salvation from our enemies, * and from the hand of all who hate us:

To show mercy to our fathers, * and to remember his holy covenant.

The oath that he swore to Abraham our father, * that he would grant us:

That, delivered from the hand of our enemies * and without fear, we might serve him;

In holiness and righteousness before him, * all our days.

And you, child, shall be called the prophet of the Most High; * 90 for you will go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways:

To give knowledge of salvation to his people, * for the forgiveness of their sins:

Through the merciful compassion of our God, * by which the dawn from on high has visited us,

To illuminate those who sit in darkness and the shadow of death, * to guide our feet into the way of peace.

**Antiphon.** Blessed are you, Lord God of Israel. Glory [Col. 0183B] and honor, etc. P. Because he has visited us.

## Prayer

Almighty God, whose children we continually become when we are cleansed by the washing of saving water: make us receive the gift of your blessing in such a way that we may rightly be called children of the heavenly city, Jerusalem; so that you, who were manifested to the nations in the star, may appear for salvation to those who believe; and you, who renewed us by the water of blessing through the washing, may renew us in the future through the promise of the grace granted. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

### At Another Canticle

**Antiphon.** Your light is present, Jerusalem, and the majesty of the Lord will be seen upon you.

### Canticle of Isaiah (Chapter LX)

Arise, shine, Jerusalem, * for your light has come, and the glory of the Lord has risen upon you.

For behold, darkness shall cover the earth, * and gloom the peoples.

But the Lord shall rise upon you, * and his glory shall be seen upon you.

And nations shall walk by your light, * and kings by the splendor of your rising.

Lift up your eyes round about and see: * all these have gathered and have come to you.

Your sons shall come from afar, * and your daughters shall rise at your side.

Then you shall see and overflow, * and your heart shall marvel and be enlarged,

When the multitude of the sea has turned toward you, * and the strength of the nations has come to you.

Your light is present, Jerusalem, * and the majesty of the Lord shall be seen upon you.

**The antiphon is repeated.** Your light is present.

## Prayer

Christ, Son of God, who, by the advance of the radiant star, wished to show yourself placed in the manger to the Magi who sought you: as your grace goes before us or follows after us, may the eternal star shine upon us, by which we may find you daily to be our food, you who became the food of the redeemed. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

### At the Benedictus

**Antiphon.** To you alone, God, be honor, glory, strength, and power forever and ever.

**Canticle.** Blessed are you, Lord. Fol. 6.

**Sono.** I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end, says the Lord God. Alleluia.

V. Alleluia. I am the first and the last; I am the root and origin of David; I am the bright and morning star. Alleluia.

**Lauda.** Praise the Lord from the heavens. Alleluia. Praise him in the heights. Alleluia, alleluia. Praise him, all his angels; praise him, all his powers. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. Psalm 148.

## Reading from the Book of the Prophet Isaiah (Chapter XLV)

R. Thanks be to God.

Thus says the Lord: The labor of Egypt and the commerce of Ethiopia, and the Sabeans, men of stature, shall pass over to you and shall be yours. They shall walk behind you; bound in fetters, they shall proceed. They shall worship you and entreat you: Only in you is God, and there is no God besides you.

Truly you are a hidden God, God of Israel, Savior. They have all been confounded and ashamed; together they have gone into confusion, the makers of errors. Israel has been saved by the Lord with eternal salvation; you shall not be confounded, and you shall not be ashamed forever and ever.

For thus says the Lord, who created the heavens, he himself the Lord who formed the earth and made it; he himself its molder. He did not create it in vain; he formed it to be inhabited. I am the Lord, and there is no other.

I have not spoken in secret, in a dark place of the earth; I did not say to the offspring of Jacob, “Seek me in vain.” I am the Lord, speaking righteousness, declaring upright things.

Gather yourselves and come; draw near together, you who have been saved from the nations. They had no knowledge, those who carried their carved images together and prayed to a god who cannot save.

Declare and come; take counsel together. Who made this heard from the beginning and foretold it from that time? Was it not I, the Lord, and is there no other God besides me? There is no just God and Savior except me.

Turn to me and you shall be saved, all the ends of the earth. R. Amen.

## Hymn

Wicked Herod, enemy,  
Why do you fear Christ’s coming?  
He does not seize mortal kingdoms  
Who grants the heavenly realms.

The Magi went, following  
The star they had seen going before:  
91 They seek the Light by means of light;  
By their gift they confess God.

The heavenly Lamb touched  
The baths of the pure stream;  
The sins that he had not incurred, he took away by washing us.

A new kind of power:  
The jars of water blush,  
And the water, commanded to pour forth wine,  
Changed its nature.

On the fourth day, Lazarus, already stinking,  
Received life again;  
Freed from the bonds of death,  
He became a survivor for himself.

A garment, once touched, staunched  
The streams of dreadful blood;  
As the suppliant wept and watered it,  
The flow of blood dried up.

Ordered suddenly to rise,  
With his whole body released,  
The sick man in turn carried  
His bed with his own steps.

Then that Judas, the executioner,  
Dared to betray his Master;  
He brought peace with a kiss,  
Which he did not carry in his heart.

The truthful one is delivered to deceivers;  
The impious one scourges the pious;  
The innocent one, fixed to the cross,  
Is joined to criminals.

After the Sabbath, certain women  
Were carrying spices to the body.  
The angels address them:  
The Living One is not enclosed in the tomb.

Come with sweet hymns;  
Let us all sing of Tartarus, subjected  
To Christ’s triumph—Christ,  
Who redeemed us when sold.

He trampled the envy  
Of the jealous Dragon  
And the mouth of the worst Lion,  
The Only-Begotten of God,  
And returned himself to the heavens.

Glory to you, Lord,  
Who appeared today,  
With the Father and the Holy Spirit,  
Throughout the everlasting ages.

Amen.

## Supplication

Let us pray to the author of light. Fol. 83.

Lord, have mercy. R. Christ, have mercy. Lord, have mercy.

## Capitula

Glorious, holy, almighty God, who have always taken pity on the various errors of the human race: without doubt for this reason you also supplied the Magi, established in dark superstition or gloom, with the light of the guiding star as far as your holy cradle, so that you might kindle in all who live in error a desire for knowledge of you.

Kindle us also, we pray, with the saving ardor of your love, so that we who have already come to know you through the gift of your illumination, aflame also with the ardor of your love, may be worthy to cling to you forever.

**Our Father.** Deliver us from evil. Fol. 2.

**Lauda.** He sent me to heal.

**Blessing.** May Alpha and Omega bless you. Fol. 86.

[Col. 0185D] In the name of the Lord.

## The Octave of Epiphany

Everything is to be said as on the day itself. Fol. 85.

# On the First Sunday after the Octave of the Lord’s Epiphany

## At Vespers

**Lauda.** The lifting of my hands. P. As an evening sacrifice.

V. Let my prayer, Lord, be directed in your sight like incense. P. As an evening sacrifice.

## Prayer

O God, whose name is praiseworthy from the rising of the sun to its setting: may our prayer be directed in your sight like incense, and may the lifting of our hands, our evening sacrifice, fulfill the solemnity for you. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Sono.** In the evening weeping will remain, and in the morning, joy. Alleluia.

V. Alleluia. You have turned my mourning into joy for me, Lord; you have torn my sackcloth and girded me with gladness. Alleluia.

The Lord be always with you. R. And with you.

## Antiphon

Who is this, whose stars shone in their watches and rejoiced when he called them? They shone with joy for him who made them.

V. He made the moon for appointed times; the sun knew its setting. P. And they rejoiced.

V. Glory and honor, etc. P. And they rejoiced.

The Lord be always with you. R. And with you.

**Lauda.** Alleluia. I shall confess to you, Lord, with the direction of my heart. Alleluia. P. In that I have learned the judgments of your righteousness. Alleluia.

V. I shall meditate on your justifications; I shall not forget your words. [Col. 0186B] P. In that I have learned.

V. Glory and honor to the Father, etc. P. In that I have learned.

## Hymn

Good guide and maker of the glowing light,  
Who divide the seasons at their appointed turns,  
When the sun has sunk, dreadful chaos presses in:  
Christ, restore the light to your faithful.

92 The heights shine with clear light,  
And the courts with moving flames;  
Rival light drives away the absent day,  
Illuminating night with its guiding radiance.

Through holy joys we draw the night  
Into festive gatherings;  
With equal song and sweet-sounding melodies  
We release our mouths in hymns.

O worthy thing, God, which your flock  
Will offer to you at the beginning  
Of the remaining night:  
Nothing is more precious than the light you grant,  
The light by which we see the remaining rewards.

You are true light to the eyes,  
And light within to the senses;  
You are mirror and fountain. Receive  
The light your people taste,  
Dyed with the oil of peaceful chrism.

Through Christ, your Son, begotten, supreme Father,  
In whom visible glory stands for you;  
He who is our Lord, your Only-Begotten,  
Breathes forth the Paraclete from the Father’s heart.

Through him are splendor, honor, praise, wisdom,  
Majesty, goodness, and devotion.  
You contain the kingdom under the threefold Name,  
Weaving age upon age forever.

Amen.

## Supplication

Let us pray to the Redeemer. Fol. 66.

## Capitula

May our prayer be directed, Lord, like incense in your sight, so that you may not allow evening weeping to remain in us; but may tranquil joy be granted in the morning sacrifices. May our prayers be received through your angel, just as you deigned to hear the desires of Tobiah and Sarah. Care for us in our infirmities and heal all our diseases, so that, just as we believe this day has been offered, the darkness of the approaching night may find the day of the life of recompense already accomplished, through him who taught us to pray.

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. Seek fol. 2.

[Col. 0187A] **Blessing.** May the gracious Lord pour upon you the flame of the blessing of heaven, and may the inseparable Trinity never depart from you. R. Amen.

May he crush the battles of your adversaries, and may heavenly fire consume their battle lines. R. Amen.

May indivisible charity rule in you, and may eternal majesty preserve you. R. Amen.

Through his mercy.

**Lauda.** Teach me goodness, discipline, and knowledge, O God. Alleluia. P. Because I have believed in your commandments. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.

V. I considered my ways and turned my feet toward your testimonies. P. Because I have believed in your commandments.

V. Glory and honor, etc. P. Because I have believed.

## Prayer

Lord Jesus Christ, who [believers in you]. [Col. 0187B] Seek in the Matins of this Sunday. Fol. 3.

At the beginning of Matins on Sundays we say, namely:

**Hymn.** Eternal Maker of all things.

**Prayer.** Eternal author. Seek fol. 3.

## Antiphons

**Antiphon.** Lord, how many are those who trouble me? But you, Lord, are my protector. Psalm 3.

**Antiphon.** Wash me from my iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin, Lord. Psalm 50.

**Antiphon 3.** In you my soul trusts; deliver me, Lord. Psalm 56.

**Antiphon.** Lord, how many are those who trouble me? But you, Lord, are my protector.

V. Glory and honor to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.

**Antiphon.** Wash me from my iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin, Lord.

V. As it was in the beginning, is now, and always will be.

**Antiphon.** In you my soul trusts; deliver me, Lord. P. And forever and ever. Amen.

## Prayer

Lord Jesus Christ, who [believers]. Seek fol. 3.

**Antiphon 1.** Serve the Lord in fear, and rejoice in him with trembling. Embrace discipline. P. Lest the Lord become angry and you perish from the righteous way.

V. Why did the nations rage, and the peoples meditate on vain things? P. Lest he become angry.

V. Glory and honor, etc. P. Lest he become angry.

## Prayer

As we serve you, Lord, in fear, may your discipline instruct and possess us; and as we rejoice with trembling, may modest gladness lift us up. Let us not become lost by withdrawing from the righteous way; but, trusting in you, may we be worthy to be blessed. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon 2.** In our tribulation, God, you enlarged us. P. Have mercy on us and hear our prayer.

V. When I called, you heard me, God of my righteousness; in my tribulation you enlarged me. Have mercy on me and hear my prayer. P. Have mercy on us and hear.

V. Glory and honor, etc. P. Have mercy on us.

## Prayer

Lord, who are always present to those who call upon you, and who delight in bringing 93 help to those established in tribulation: grant that, hating the vanity of the world and rejecting falsehood, we may rejoice that your Christ—whom we acknowledge to have been magnified by you—is our supreme and eternal reward. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon 3.** Turn, Lord; rescue our souls. Save us for the sake of your mercy. P. For in death there is no one who remembers you.

V. Lord, do not rebuke me in your anger, nor correct me in your fury. P. For in death there is no one.

V. Glory and honor, etc. P. For in death there is no one.

## Prayer

Lord, do not rebuke us in your anger, nor correct us in your fury; but anoint us, instead of the severity of punishment, with the mercy of gentleness, so that your discipline may bring us not destruction through punishment, but instruction. R. Amen.

[Col. 0188B] Through your mercy.

**Response.** Our iniquities have multiplied beyond the number of the sand of the sea. P. And now we are justly restrained, so that we may raise our head: we have sinned, Lord, we have sinned.

V. We sinned with our fathers; we acted unjustly; we committed iniquities. P. And now we are justly restrained.

V. Glory and honor, etc. P. And now.

## At Lauds

### At the Canticle

**Antiphon.** For I will bless you and multiply you like the stars of heaven, says the Lord.

### Canticle of Genesis (Chapters XII, XIII, XVII)

Go out from your land, and from your kindred, and from your father’s house, * and come into the land that I shall show you.

And I will make you into a great nation, and I will bless you, * and I will magnify your name, and you shall be blessed.

I will bless those who bless you, and curse those who curse you, * and in you all the kindreds of the earth shall be blessed.

Lift up your eyes and look from the place * where you now are, toward the north and the south, the east and the west.

All the land that you see, * I will give to you and to your offspring forever.

For I will bless you, * and multiply you like the stars of heaven and like the sand on the seashore.

Your offspring shall possess the gates of your enemies, * and all the nations of the earth shall be blessed in your offspring.

I am the Lord, who brought you out from Ur of the Chaldeans; I am God Almighty: * walk before me and be perfect.

And I will establish my covenant between me and you, * and I will multiply you exceedingly. I am, and my covenant is with you.

And you shall be the father of many nations. * And I will establish you among the nations, and kings shall come forth from you.

And I will establish my covenant between me and you, and between your offspring after you throughout their generations, by an everlasting covenant: * that I may be your God and the God of your offspring after you.

And I will give to you and to your offspring the land of your sojourning, * as an everlasting possession, and I will be their God.

## Matutinarium

**Antiphon.** My king and my God: to you I shall pray, Lord.

V. Give ear to my words, Lord; understand my cry. P. My king and my God.

V. Glory and honor, etc. P. My king.

**Lauda.** Praise the Lord in his holy places. Alleluia, alleluia. Praise him in the firmament of his strength. Alleluia, alleluia. Psalm 150.

P. Praise the Lord in his holy places. Alleluia, alleluia.

V. Glory and honor to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. P. Praise him in the firmament of his strength.

V. As it was in the beginning, is now and always, and forever and ever. Amen. P. Alleluia, alleluia.

## Reading from the Book of Proverbs of Solomon (Chapter III)

[Col. 0192D] R. Thanks be to God.

My son, place your trust in the Lord with all your heart, and do not rely on your own prudence. Consider him in all your ways, and he himself will direct your steps. Do not be wise in your 96 own eyes; fear the Lord and turn away from evil. R. Amen.

## Hymn

Author of the shining heavens,  
Who established the moon’s light for the nights  
And the sun for the courses of the days  
By a fixed path.

Dark night is now driven away,  
The brightness of the world is reborn,  
And a new vigor of mind  
Has already lifted sweet things on high.

The returning day now admonishes us  
To sound praises;  
And with a gentler face  
Of heaven, let it make our hearts serene.

Let us avoid every slippery thing;  
Let the spirit turn away from evil;  
Let life not be stained by wrongdoing;  
Let guilt not entangle the tongue.

But while the sun completes the day,  
Let deep faith burn;  
Let hope call us toward the promises;  
Let charity unite us to Christ.

Glory be to God the Father.

## Supplication

Let us pray with every supplication to the Redeemer of the world, our Lord Jesus Christ, asking that through his grace, and through the intercession of holy Mary, his Virgin Mother, and of all his saints, he may graciously grant us salvation of soul and body, forgiveness of sins, and peace. R. Grant this, eternal almighty God.

Lord, have mercy. R. Christ, have mercy. Lord, have mercy.

## Capitula

Our King and our God, drive from our hearts the night of error and ignorance, so that, renewing us into the new human being, and hearing our voices at dawn, you may make us stand before you at first light in good works; and grant us the sacrament of your Appearance, so that we may contemplate you.

**Our Father.** Deliver us from evil. See fol. 10.

**Lauda.** Cleanse us from our sins, Lord. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.

V. And spare your servant from hidden sins. P. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.

V. Glory and honor, etc. P. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.

**Antiphon 2.** Guard us, Lord, from every evil. P. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.

V. Protect us beneath the shadow of your wings. P. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.

V. Glory and honor. P. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.

**Blessing.** May the almighty Lord bless. Seek fol. 94.

And thus Matins end in the Blessings. Immediately make commemorations of the Church’s Vocation and of any others you wish, in which you have devotion. Afterwards say the Our Father silently; when it is finished, let the commemoration be made.

[Col. 0193D] **Lauda.** To announce in the morning.

**Prayer.** In the morning, Lord, prayer. Seek fol. 7.

**Lauda from the fountain.** With you, Lord, is the fountain of life. Alleluia.

V. And in your light we shall see light. P. Alleluia.

V. Glory and honor, etc. P. Alleluia.

# At Terce

## Reading from the Book of Proverbs of Solomon (Chapter 7)

R. Thanks be to God.

My son, keep my words and store up my commandments for yourself. Keep my precepts, and you shall live. R. Amen.

**Antiphon 1.** Understand my cry, Lord; attend to the voice of my prayer. Psalm 5.

## Prayer

Lead us, Lord, in good things, and direct our way in your sight, so that our faith, by the call of your salvation, may follow you, who are our King and our God, with an unharmed step, and may reach its course with speed. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon 2.** Do not rebuke me in your anger, Lord. Psalm 6.

## Prayer

Lord, do not rebuke us in your anger, nor correct us in your fury; but anoint the severity of punishment with the mercy of gentleness, so that your discipline may bring us not destruction through punishment, but instruction. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon 3.** My just help is from the Lord, [Col. 0194B] who saves the upright in heart. Psalm 7. The antiphon is repeated: My just help. The Lord be always with you. R. And with you.
