V. Glory and honor, etc. The response is repeated.

**Lauda.** Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. My lips shall rejoice when I sing praise to you, God. P. Alleluia, alleluia.

V. And I shall praise you, God, with instruments of psalmody; 97 I shall sing to you. P. Alleluia.

V. Glory and honor, etc. P. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.

**Prayers:** There is no other one to whom supplication may be made, O gracious Lord:

**V.** Lift the yoke; incline the necks of those who are burdened.  
**P.** O gracious one, restrain wars; grant peace.  
**V.** Rescue captives; raise up the submerged.  
**P.** O gracious one, restrain wars.  
**V.** Grant pardon; bestow grace, O gracious Lord.

Let the first **V.**, namely, “There is no other one,” be repeated.

**Capitulum.** Glorious, powerful, and merciful God, rescue us from the ambushes of the enemy; and, lest our soul be snatched away by the swift seizure of the roaring lion, appoint the protection of your right hand for our keeping—so that, when there is no one to redeem, the savage one may not destroy it, or, if there is no one to save, he may not overthrow it. But you, Lion of the tribe of Judah, arise in your anger; and in the severity of judgment destroy the troops of the treacherous enemy. Grant that we may believe in and remain faithful to the commandment that you have given.

**Our Father.** Deliver us from evil. Folio 10.

**At Sext**, let everything be said as at Sext, which is said throughout the year. **At None**, as above.

## At Vespers

**Laud.** You are the one who illumines my lamp, O Lord.  
**The Lord be always.** **R.** And with you.

**Antiphon.** How wonderful is your name, O Lord, throughout all the earth. Psalm VIII.

**Laud.** In the law of the Lord he will meditate, alleluia, by day and by night. Alleluia.  
**P.** And he will yield his fruit in its season. Alleluia, alleluia.  
**V.** And he will be like a tree planted beside the courses of waters, which will yield its fruit in its season.  
**R.** And he will yield his fruit.  
**V.** Glory and honor, etc.  
**P.** And he will yield his fruit.

### Hymn

Christ, Savior of all,  
Most high God of heaven,  
We ask your glory  
While the day bends downward.

Now the sun, as evening presses on,  
Advances toward its setting,  
Enclosing the world in darkness,  
Observing its appointed order.

So may the quiet night,  
O exalted Lord,  
Receive us, your servants,  
Wearied by the labor of the day,  
As we pray.

So that, with our minds not darkened,  
The day of light may depart;  
But, protected by your grace,  
May we behold the favorable light.

Glory be to God the Father.

**Supplication.** Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world. See folio 96. Kyrie, eleison. **R.** Christe, eleison. Kyrie, eleison.

**Capitulum.** O Lord our illumination and salvation, remove from us the night of sorrow and ignorance; grant the light of truth and knowledge, so that our hope may remain fixed in you; and let the whole assembly of the wicked, which strives to attack us, waste away. Let our exaltation be upon the rock, so that, strengthened through Christ, we may be made lofty in love within him, in whom we are built up as believers through faith.

**Our Father.** Deliver us from evil. Folio 10.

**Blessing.** Deign, O Lord, to look upon this family of yours with a peaceful countenance, which you see celebrating your solemn rites with joy. **R.** Amen. May they possess holy devotion within themselves and hold a worthy fervor in your faith. **R.** Amen. Defend them from every adversity by your right hand, and grant that they may persevere continually undefiled in your Church. **R.** Amen.

Through his mercy.

**Laud.** Upon Zion, his holy mountain—alleluia, alleluia.  
**P.** Proclaiming the commandment of the Lord. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.  
**V.** Yet I have been appointed king by him upon Zion, his holy mountain.  
**P.** Proclaiming the commandment of the Lord.  
**V.** Glory and honor, etc.  
**P.** Proclaiming the commandment.

**Prayer.** Turn away our enemies, O Lord. See below.

# TUESDAY

## At Matins

**Antiphon.** According to your great mercy, blot out my iniquities, O Lord. Psalm L.

**Prayer.** According to the multitude of your mercies, blot out our iniquities, O Lord: so that, because these weigh us down, those may raise us up. Do not despise in us a contrite and humbled heart; but, through the ineffable power of the Trinity, let the Holy Spirit dwell within us; let the upright spirit renew us; let the princely spirit strengthen us; and let there be one power of testimony, so that, strengthened by the Father, renewed through the Son, and guarded by the Holy Spirit, we may rejoice that we are preserved. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon 1.** I will rejoice and exult in you, and I will sing to your name, O Most High. Psalm IX.

**Prayer.** With our whole heart we shall confess your name, O Lord, because you have made our enemy turn backward, binding him powerfully with a fiery chain; and you have freed us from the gates of death through the victory of your Passion. Be now, we ask, the guardian of the redeemed, you who became the price of sinners; be the refuge of the poor, the defense of widows, and the protection of orphans. As you come to the needs of each person with individual favor, may you be ceaselessly praised by all with singular faith. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

## At Lauds

**Antiphon 2.** To you the poor man is abandoned; you will be the helper of the orphan. Psalm IX. Division.

**Prayer.** Turn our enemies backward, O Lord, so that, while you look upon them, they may grow weak. And since you yourself are the helper in times of opportunity and in tribulation, grant us the grace of opportunity and lighten the burden of tribulations, so that neither prosperity may recall us to negligence nor distress drag us into ruin; but may your mercy lead us to pardon. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon 3.** The Lord hears the desire of the poor. Psalm IX. Division.

**Prayer.** Graciously attend in this way to the desire of your poor, O Lord, that you may grant us an abundance of heavenly gifts and turn away from us the love of passing things. May your ear also understand our prayer in such a way that, when you have rendered judgment for the orphan and the humble, you may soothe us with paternal indulgence and repay the humiliation of present things with the joys of eternal things. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**R.** You are my helper, O Lord; do not abandon me.  
**P.** And do not despise me, O God my Savior.  
**V.** Establish a law for me, O Lord, on your way, and direct me on the straight path.  
**P.** And do not despise me.  
**V.** Glory and honor, etc. Let **R.** be repeated.

## At the Canticle

**Antiphon.** Almighty God is his name; may he bless us and make us increase into companies of peoples.

### Canticle from Genesis (chapters XXVII–XXVIII)

Behold, the scent of my son is like the scent of a field full [of fragrance], * which the Lord has blessed.

May the Lord give you dew from heaven and from the richness of the earth an abundance of grain, wine, and oil, * and may tribes worship you.

Be lord of your brothers, * and may the sons of your mother bow before you.

May almighty God bless you * and make you increase and multiply, so that you may become companies of peoples.

And may he give you the blessings of Abraham, and to your offspring after you, * so that you may possess the land of your sojourning.

**Antiphon.** Almighty God is his name; may he bless us and make us increase into companies of peoples.

**Matins responsory.**  
**R.** In the morning you will hear my voice, O Lord.  
**P.** In the morning I will stand before you and worship you.  
**V.** Give ear to my words, O Lord; understand my cry.  
**P.** In the morning I will stand before you.  
**V.** Glory and honor, etc. Let **R.** “In the morning you will hear” be repeated.

**Laud.** Praise the Lord in his holy places. Alleluia, alleluia; praise the Lord in the firmament of his power. Alleluia, alleluia. Psalm CL.

**Prophecy.** My son, have confidence in the Lord. See folio 95.

### Hymn

God of eternal light,  
Inexpressible radiance,  
Judge of the coming day,  
You who see the hidden things of the mind.

You hold the kingdom of heaven,  
And you are wholly in the Word;  
Through the Son you rule all things;  
For the Holy Spirit you are the fountain.

You behold the threefold Name on high;  
You are one and can do all things;  
And, wondrous through the sign of the Cross,  
You are the ruler of immense light.

You are the founder of the world;  
You sit upon an everlasting throne,  
Judge, humble from on high:  
You came to suffer for us.

You are almighty Sabaoth [Lord of Hosts],  
You are Hosanna [Save, we pray] of the highest height;  
To you belongs wondrous praise;  
You are the first Anastasis [Resurrection].

You are the hearer of faith,  
And you look upon the humble;  
You behold the lofty throne;  
To you belongs divine honor.

To Christ, eternal God,  
And to the Father, with the Holy Spirit,  
Let us offer gifts in you  
From age to age.

Amen.

**Supplication.** Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world. See folio 96.

**Capitulum.** With your ears, almighty God, hear the words of our mouth; and, as a gracious examiner, understand at dawn the cry of your servants. Grant that we may be so fortified by the shield of your will that a vicious suggestion may not creep into our minds. Let our devotion in prayer to you also be constant and faithful, so that your contemplation may be granted to us in the morning.

**Our Father.** Deliver us from evil. See folio 10.

**Laud.** May the hands of the Lord be strengthened in his holy ones. Alleluia.  
**P.** And their bones will sprout like grass. Alleluia, alleluia.  
**V.** Planted in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God.  
**P.** And their bones will sprout.  
**R.** Glory and honor, etc.  
**P.** And their bones will sprout.  
**The Lord be always.** **R.** And with you.

**V.** O God, hear our prayer.  
**P.** May our cry reach you.  
**V.** Glory and honor, etc.  
**P.** Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.

**Blessing.** Deign, O Lord, to look upon this [family of yours]. See folio 97. And immediately make the commemorations that you are accustomed to make, namely: “To announce your mercy in the morning,” etc.

Through mercy.

**P.** Alleluia, alleluia.

**The Lord be always with you.** **R.** And with you.

**The Lord be always with you.** **V.** And with you.

### Hymn

Christ, perpetual light,  
Splendor of stars and constellations,  
Illumine our night,  
Preserve pure hearts.

Let no one proceed into snares,  
Let no one be burdened by enemies;  
Nor let bodies be stained  
By lust during sleep.

Guard the hearts of all,  
And, by your greatest protection,  
Guard the faithful  
With your own power, O Christ.

So that the soul may rejoice  
At having seen the favorable light,  
At having fulfilled its proper vows,  
Which must be rendered to you, O Trinity.

Glory be to God the Father,  
And to his only Son,  
With the Spirit, the Paraclete,  
For everlasting ages.

Amen.

**Supplication.** Let us pray to the Redeemer. Folio 96.

**Capitulum.** Almighty God, unworthy as we are, we ask your glory and entreat you to admit our prayers to the seat of your mercy; grant aid to those who seek it; cleanse away the stain of all our sins; remove the scourge; apply healing to the sick; break the assault of enemies; grant peace, security, and quiet times; and deign, in your customary mercy, to restore for the better whatever the enemy had overcome by his enticement.

**Our Father.** Deliver us from evil. See folio 10.

**Blessing.** May the Lord enrich us with his blessing and make us co-heirs of the heavenly kingdoms. **R.** Amen. May he grant us the span of the present life and, in his mercy, bestow fellowship with the elect. **R.** Amen. And may he always rescue us from evil in such a way that he mercifully guards and preserves us in what is good. **R.** Amen. Through mercy.

**P.** And they will rejoice forever. Alleluia.  
**P.** And you will dwell in them. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.  
**V.** And let all who hope in you rejoice in you.  
**P.** Forever.  
**V.** Glory and honor to the Father, etc.  
**P.** And you will dwell in them.

**Prayer.** Make known to us, O Lord, the ways of life, and fill us with delight at your right hand; and establish upon us the yoke that is gentle through the moderation of your own hand. **R.** Amen. Through your mercy.

In the name of the Lord.

**Commemoration**, as was said on Monday.

# WEDNESDAY

## At Matins

**Antiphon.** Blot out my iniquities, O Lord, and cleanse me from my sins. Psalm L.

**Prayer.** Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy; so that, as we acknowledge our misery, your mercy may go before us. Let the voice of confession therefore be ready and pardon near; let the hearing that comes from your propitiation be swift, so that you may blot out all our sins and grant the strength by which we may fulfill your commandments. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon 1.** Fill us with joy in your countenance; delights are at your right hand forever. Psalm XV.

**Prayer.** Make known to us, O Lord. See above.

**Antiphon 2.** I cried out because you heard me, O God; incline your ear to me and hear me. Psalm XVI, up to “From those who resist your right hand.”

**Prayer.** Hear us, O God, as we cry to you, O Lord; perfect our steps in your paths, so that, while we walk the narrow way of your law, we may deserve to enter through the breadth of love into the gate of justice. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon 3.** Guard me, O Lord, as the apple of the eye. Guard me, O Lord, under the shadow of your wings. Psalm XVI.

**Prayer.** Guard us, O Lord, as the apple of the eye, lest the storm of carnal desire corrupt the lights of our innocence. Protect us under the shadow of your wings, lest we be caught by the allurements of those who lay snares for pleasures. Thus may we, who endure with the help of abiding grace, deserve to be satisfied when your glory appears. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**R.** You are our helper and deliverer.  
**P.** You, O Lord.  
**R.** O God, attend to our assistance; hasten to help us.  
**P.** You, O Lord.  
**V.** Glory and honor, etc. Let **R.** “You are our helper” be repeated.

### Canticle from Genesis (chapter XXXII)

God of our father Abraham and God of our father Isaac, * O Lord, who said to me: Return to your land and to the place of your birth, and I will do good to you.

I remember all the mercies * and the truth that you have fulfilled for your servant.

With my staff I crossed this Jordan, * and now I am returning with two companies.

Rescue me from the hand of my brother Esau, because I fear him greatly, * lest perhaps he come and strike the mother together with the children.

For you spoke that you would do good to me * and enlarge my offspring like the sand, which cannot be counted because of its multitude.

Glory and honor to the Father, etc.

**P.** Giving light to the eyes.

### Hymn

God the unbegotten Father  
And only-begotten Son,  
Whom the unity of the Trinity  
Joins to the Holy Spirit.

No one invokes you in vain,  
Nor does the lover of your light  
Ever raise his face to heaven  
With empty words.

And you, O God, always graciously look upon  
The one who sighs,  
The vows of those who pray,  
And the hearts of those who confess.

The rising of the light admonishes us  
To offer due thanks  
And to speak praises to you,  
Because the dark night has passed.

We pray for a good day,  
So that you, Savior,  
In kindly goodness, may guide our actions  
With continual sincerity.

Glory be to God the Father, etc.

May we be taught by your discipline, directed by your instruction, and enlarged through spiritual growth. Let us offer you, O Lord, the service of faith, so that we may deserve to receive from you the crown of glory as our reward. **R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

Through your mercy.

**Capitulum.** O Lord, our strength, grant us to possess continually the love of your name. Deign to be our strength against those who oppose us; our support against those who attack us; and our deliverer against those who take us captive. Thus, surrounded on every side by your defenses, may our mind neither fear the adversities of the world nor seek its blandishments; and, content always with your grace, may it rejoice in your gifts.

Be present to our prayers;  
Be present now in mercy,

May we not meditate on iniquity in our senses, nor may our minds be weakened by deception; but, bound with the belt of chastity, may we deserve to serve at the morning hour with pure heart and body.

**Our Father.** Deliver us from evil. See folio 10.

**Blessing.** May the Lord grant us the reward of the most sincere charity, so that we may always live in peace with everyone. **R.** Amen. May we overcome the ambushes of all enemies and pass through the present life without crime. **R.** Amen. # THURSDAY

## At Matins

**Antiphon.** In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, light with peace. **R.** Thanks be to God.  
**The Lord be always with you.** **R.** And with you.

**Antiphon.** You blot out my iniquities, my God. Psalm L.

**Prayer.** As we acknowledge our iniquities and disclose to you, O Lord, our own offenses, we pray as suppliants, wailing with tears and beating our breasts: turn your face away from our crimes and blot out all the sins we have committed. Create, therefore, O God, in our heart what you love; and in your customary propitiation forgive what you hate. And if our evil vices repeatedly provoke you to anger, let your abundant indulgence make you reconciled to us. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy, our God, etc.

**Antiphon 1.** You alone understand offenses; cleanse us from our sins, O Lord. Psalm XVIII.

**Prayer.** Cleanse us from our hidden sins, O Lord, purifying the conscience that is defiled by inward and personal stains. Also spare your servants from the sins of others, so that you may forgive those things that we either learn through the examples of evil people or commit after being enticed by wicked persuasions. Since we acknowledge you as our own Lord, may we never again feel the domination of sins. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon 2.** Hear us on the day when we call upon you, O Lord our God. Psalm XIX.

**Prayer.** Fulfill all our petitions, O Lord, and send us help from the holy place. Remember all our sacrifice, which we offer to you not only through oblation but also through prayer and affliction, so that you may always make us humble before you and regard us as contrite. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon 3.** We shall sing and chant your powers, O Lord. Psalm XX.

**Prayer.** O Lord, who have deigned to go before us with the grace of redemption, go before us also with the blessing of sweetness. You who grant temporal life to all mortals, bestow upon us all life that is truly eternal. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**R.** Our help.

### Canticle from Deuteronomy (chapter IX)

O Lord, Lord, king of the gods of heaven, * do not destroy your people,

and your inheritance, which you redeemed from the land of Egypt, * by your great power and your outstretched arm.

Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, your servants, * to whom you swore by yourself.

Do not look upon the hardness of this people, * nor their impiety and sins,

lest the inhabitants of the land from which you led us out say in their hearts:

“Because God was not able to bring them into the land * that he had promised them, and because he hated them, he brought them out to kill them in the wilderness.”

And this people is your people and your handiwork, * whom you brought out from the land of Egypt by your great power and your outstretched arm.

Glory and honor to the Father, etc.

We rise in the morning,  
Rendering due praises  
To God and to the Lord Jesus,  
In the unity of glory.

We sing with the choir of the holy ones,  
We bend our necks,  
And we prostrate our knees.

We disclose our sins;  
Let us pray to God continually,  
Let us conquer evil with good  
With the fruit of repentance,  
And render an everlasting vow.

Let us ask Christ and the Father,  
And the Spirit of Christ and the Father,  
To grant us help  
And repel the envious enemy.

And because you are the fountain of life flowing forth, may we draw from you what we thirst for in faith; may we shine in the light of knowledge within your light; and may we reap the fruit of justice in everlasting exaltation.

**Antiphon 1.** O God, our God, look upon us; do not abandon us who hope in you. Psalm XXI, up to “But you, O Lord, do not withdraw.”

**Prayer.** Christ, who from the gallows cried out to the Father, “Why have you abandoned me?”; who by your Cross redeemed the human being lost through sin; and who handed over the author of sin to burn in eternal fires: we ask your holy mercy that you never abandon us who believe in you and do not reject our confidence from your Godhead. Rather, receive our cry by day, and at night grant us to serve you in service pleasing to you. Kindle our hearts, ever burning with love for you, by spiritual fire; and restore, through our conversion, your grace, which we lost by sinning. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

For we shall truly be saved if you turn the gaze of your countenance upon us and join yourself cheerfully to our souls. Since our fathers hoped in you and were saved, make us enter into the inheritance of their hope, and grant us to rejoice with them in equal and eternal exultation. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

### Hymn

Christ, heavenly medicine of the Father,  
True physician of human salvation,  
Powerfully open your favor  
To the prayers of your provident people.

Behold, we beseech you on behalf of the sick,  
Whom the harmful disease of illness weakens;  
As the gracious one, relieve the sickness  
Of those who lie afflicted.

You who showed your power  
When you swiftly saved  
Peter’s mother-in-law lying in fever,  
The official’s son, and the centurion’s boy.

Bring strength to the suffering people;  
Pour abundant salvation upon the peoples;  
Restore the sick, as is your custom,  
To their former strength.

Heal the diseases of bodies and souls;  
Apply a remedy to the causes of wounds,  
Lest suffering burn our bodies  
Without fruit.

Let every assault wholly withdraw;  
Let every painful attack dissolve;  
Let the freshness of the desired salvation  
Foster the afflicted limbs.

Now, O God, have mercy on our tears,  
For those whom we now ask you to heal,  
So that every sick person lying here  
May feel your healing.

So that, while the evils inflicted are worn away,  
They may enter, beautiful among the number of the instructed,  
Having received their reward, accompanied by its fruit,
The realms of the heavens.

Let the choir sing glory and resound with it;

let it speak, sing, and repeat glory;

let the stars proclaim it to the Triune Name,

to the one Godhead.

Amen.

**Supplication.** Let us beseech the Redeemer of the world, our Lord Jesus Christ, with every supplication, that he may graciously deign to heal the wounds of all his servants, the faithful who are ill.

Lord, have mercy.

**R.** Christ, have mercy.

Lord, have mercy.

**Capitulum.** We beseech you, Lord, that in your anger you do not rebuke us and do not allow your fury to rage against us; but, as a gentle corrector, remove the practice of sinning, lest by rebuking us too harshly you drive us to nothingness. Therefore have mercy on our weakness, and grant your healing to all your servants, the faithful who are ill; and those whom you see troubled by their own sin, count as peaceful, mercifully forgiving them.

**[Col. 0208B] The Lord’s Prayer.** Deliver us from evil. [See] fol. 10.

**R.** Amen.

And may he who took our weakness upon himself grant to us and to them the reward of endurance without end.

**R.** Amen.

May his piety cherish us all together in such a way that neither our corrupted health rages against us nor the infirmity inflicted upon us succumbs to despair.

**R.** Amen.

Through the mercy [of God].

## Saturday of Saint Mary

It should be known that on every Saturday throughout the year—unless a feast of nine lessons occurs—we always perform the office of the Blessed Virgin Mary in the following manner. It begins as follows.

### At Vespers

**[Col. 0211B] Lauda.** Virgin of Israel, adorn yourself with your tambourines.

**P.** And go forth in the choir of those who sing psalms.

**V.** Blessed are you, queen, who look forth like light.

**P.** And go forth in the choir.

**Prayer.** Virgin of Israel, who are understood to be the mother of the Seer: adorn your tambourines, that is, the members of your Church; so that we may have you as our patron in this age, whom we believe will remain a blessed queen in the future. As we look upon you as undoubtedly the light of our faith, may we, through your intercession, deserve to obtain the favor of the firmest blessedness.

**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Sono.** May the Lord, God of heaven, bless you; he will place the honor of the kingdom in your hand.

**P.** And the sons of many nations will worship before you. Alleluia.

**V.** Hear, daughter, for you have been exalted, and your face shines in the temple of God; the sun of righteousness will rise at your entrance.

**P.** Alleluia.

The Lord be always with you.

**R.** And with you.

**Antiphon.** Blessed are you by God Most High, above all women.

**P.** Therefore your praise shall not depart from the mouths of human beings forever.

**V.** All generations will call me blessed, for God has looked upon the humility of his handmaid.

**P.** Therefore.

**V.** Glory and honor, etc.

**P.** Therefore.

The Lord be always [with you].

**R.** And with you.

**Lauda.** Alleluia. Rejoice, daughter of Zion; be glad and exult with all your heart, daughter of Jerusalem.

**P.** For the king of Israel, the Lord, has taken away your enemies. Alleluia.

**V.** Praise the Lord, Jerusalem, and praise your God together, Zion.

**[Col. 0211D P.** For he has taken away.

**V.** Glory and honor, etc.

**P.** For he has taken away.

### Hymn

O sacred glory of virgins,

the Only-Begotten, whom the Virgin bears,

whom the holy, life-giving virginal ladies follow.

You have now made the virginal dwelling

like a chariot,

in which the preeminent head is renowned

with companies of virgins.

The heavenly Godhead fashioned this earthly temple,

from whom the redeemed world exists,

and all Tartarus.

**[Col. 0212A] He who thus received the Virgin,

queen of heaven and earth,

made her share in the company of angels

in the highest citadel.

There, most holy Virgin,

bring forward our prayers,

where you have crossed over in glory,

illustrious in commemoration.

Through your Only-Begotten,

whom you bore as Lord,

let us seek heaven’s embrace

for all ages without end.

Amen.

**Supplication.** Let us beseech the Redeemer of the world, our Lord Jesus Christ, with every supplication, that by his grace and through the intercession of his holy mother, the Virgin Mary, he may graciously deign to grant us salvation of soul and body.

**[Col. 0212B R.** Grant this, eternal almighty God.

Lord, have mercy.

**R.** Christ, have mercy.

Lord, have mercy.

**Capitulum.** Virgin, mother of Christ and restorer of the human race, present the prayers of those who implore you to the divine ears, so that we, worthy to rejoice in your gift, may through your intercession obtain forgiveness of sins from God, whose Savior you bore for all, your sex remaining undefiled.

**The Lord’s Prayer.** Delivered from evil. See fol. 2.

**Blessing.** May the Lord Jesus Christ, who once deigned to be born from a Virgin, sanctify us through the intercession of his mother.

**R.** Amen.

And may he who preserved his mother from the contagion of corruption cleanse the breast of our heart from sin.

**R.** Amen.

And may he who caused her to remain a virgin after childbirth grant us possession of heaven after our passing.

**R.** Amen.

Through the mercy of that same God of ours, etc.

**Lauda.** My branches are branches of honor and grace. Alleluia.

**P.** I flourished like a vine in the sweetness of fragrance. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.

**V.** But I, like a fruitful olive tree in the house of the Lord, will hope in the mercy of my God forever and ever.

**P.** I flourished like a vine.

**V.** Glory and honor to the Father, etc.

**P.** I flourished like a vine.

**Prayer.** Truly wondrous, Lord, is the root of your Church, which advances and grows until the perfect day; its branches are the martyrs, its hanging shoots have become the confessors, among whom is the most blessed Virgin Mary, your mother. Like a true vine bearing fruit, while she offers the fragrance of grace to the faithful in this age, she deserves to be consoled by an eternal reward. Therefore we ask that, through her intercession, we may drive away the odors of sin by the fragrance of virtues.

**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

In the name of the Lord.

### At Matins

**Antiphon.** Lord, open my lips, and my mouth will proclaim your praise. Psalm 50.

**Prayer.** May our lips rejoice in you, Lord, by proclaiming the truth, to celebrate together the true commemoration of the undefiled mother Mary; and since she deserved by divine power to be raised from earth to heavenly dwellings, may we, through her favor, deserve to be mercifully rescued here from every sin and there to be led among the shining choirs of the blessed.

**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

**Antiphon 1.** Hail, Mary, full of grace; the Lord is with you.

**P.** Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb.

**R.** Grace has been poured upon your lips; therefore God has blessed you forever.

**P.** Blessed are you among women.

**V.** Glory and honor to the Father, etc.

**P.** Blessed are you among women.

**Prayer.** We believe that you are full of grace, O Virgin, mother of Christ and glorious restorer of the human race, Mary. By giving birth you brought us such great joys that the fruit of your womb, Christ the Son of God, rescued us from the dominion of the enemy raging against us and made us his companions in the eternal kingdom. Therefore we ask and beseech you to be our patron, so that through your merit your Son may make us exiles from sin and afterward lead us, destined to dwell eternally, into his kingdom.

**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy, etc.

The Lord be always with you.

**R.** And with your spirit.

**Antiphon 2.** We have now seen a great miracle in the Virgin’s conception: she neither lost her virginity nor experienced the burdens of motherhood.

**V.** She alone deserved to bear God after heaven; she alone, a virgin, deserved to come forth after childbirth.

**V.** The earth is the Lord’s and its fullness, the inhabited world and all who dwell in it.

**P.** She alone deserved to bear God.

**V.** Glory and honor to the Father, etc.

**[Col. 0213C P.** She alone deserved.

**Prayer.** We have seen a very great miracle in the Virgin’s conception: she neither lacked the beauty of modesty nor endured the burdens of mothers. For it was not fitting that she should have sighs who gave birth to the joy of all, or that the source of gladness should know the force of pain. Thus alone the virgin deserved to come forth after childbirth, because in her the Word became flesh. For this reason we beseech you, good Jesus: just as you bestowed this reward upon your mother, so be present to us in our misery by granting us remedy.

**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

**Antiphon 3.** My soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit has rejoiced in God my Savior.

**P.** For he has looked upon the humility of his handmaid.

**V.** My heart has poured forth a good word; I speak of my works to the king.

**P.** For he has looked upon.

**V.** Glory and honor to the Father, etc.

**P.** For he has looked upon.

**Prayer.** How many and how great gifts divine piety has distributed to you, most holy Virgin and Mother of God! Though you were an earthly virgin, you became the Mother and handmaid of the Most High, so that he whose holy name you proclaimed in every generation and lineage might come to the aid of us who are weak, once the evil suggestion of bitterness has been wiped away. And may he who comes to dwell abundantly in you deign to preside over us as the gentlest rewarder, so that through the one God, perfect in the Trinity, both the merits of faith may flourish and the joys of his gifts may increase. Though unworthy, we ask this of you, queen and mother of the Creator of all ages: through you may we enjoy the flowery delight of paradise, you who remained an undefiled, godlike Virgin.

**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**R.** Chastity and immaculate virginity pleased God.

**P.** Therefore holy piety entered her womb from the Word and revealed an extraordinary birth: a virgin gave birth to God and man.

**V.** The heavens proclaimed the righteousness of God, and all peoples saw his glory.

**P.** Therefore.

**V.** Glory and honor to the Father, etc.

Repeat: “Chastity pleased God.”

### Hymn

Christ, light of the world, salvation and power,

who fill the day with the sun’s rays,

and make the night tawny,

painting it with a flashing star.

So that you may regulate the whole world

with fixed customs through returning cycles,

and release everyone’s labors

by the allotment of rest.

Behold, the hour rolls the declining sun

toward the sunset of returning evening;

then the whole choir of stars

rises from high Olympus.

We, singing beforehand to you

with devout worship, modulate

sacred hymns with our voices;

with all our senses together

we are roused to proclaim your praises.

We pour incense to you, great ruler,

and offer sacred light to the Lord,

a warm, dripping nectar,

moist from its highest summit.

May it fulfill our vow;

may it bring healing;

may it grant pardon for our sins;

may it strengthen our minds

and soothe our limbs

with peaceful rest.

And although the depths of night approach,

covered by the world’s dreadful darkness,

may our mind nevertheless shine

with the rising of heavenly faith.

May sins cease; may our spirit,

slipping into wakefulness in turn,

keep watch; and may no band

of wandering spirits entangle

our more serious senses.

May our heart keep watch in sleep,

dream of Christ, and always let

the Lord resound in psalms;

may it meditate in hymns

by night and by day.

May glory celebrate the highest Father;

glory to Christ, and likewise to the Holy Spirit;

may every age proclaim

the Triune Name with devout voice.

Amen.

**Supplication.** Let us beseech the Redeemer. See fol. 108.

May health and chastity immediately blaze forth with the returning rising of light; and may the golden twilights again illuminate us, so that, stripped of the veil of night, the alternating day may reclaim us.

At your command all things obey that subsist by your authorship; and this is their honor, that they were created by you and are subject to you. Therefore grant that we may advance in such a way that, while we open our lips in your blessings, we may obtain the blessing of heavenly grace.

**Reading from the book of Ecclesiastes of Solomon, chapter 3**

**R.** Thanks be to God.

My son, God gave the good person, in his own sight, wisdom, understanding, and joy; but to the sinner he gave affliction and excessive care, so that he might add, gather, and hand it over to one who pleased God. But this too is vanity and empty concern of mind.

Everything has its time, and all things pass beneath the sun in their appointed intervals: a time to be born and a time to die; a time to plant and a time to uproot what has been planted; a time to kill and a time to heal; a time to destroy and a time to build; a time to weep and a time to laugh; a time to mourn and a time to dance; a time to scatter stones and a time to gather them; a time to embrace and a time to be far from embraces; a time to acquire and a time to lose; a time to keep and a time to cast away; a time to tear and a time to sew; a time to be silent and a time to speak; a time for love and a time for hatred; a time for war and a time for peace.

What more does a human being have from his labor? I saw the affliction that God gave the children of humanity, so that they might be occupied with it. He made everything good in its time [Col. 0219A] and handed the world over to their disputation, so that no one may discover the work that God has done from beginning to end. And I learned that there was nothing better than to rejoice and to do good during one’s life.

**R.** Amen.

**Hymn.** Splendor of the Father’s glory. See fol. 67.

**Supplication.** Let us beseech the Redeemer of the world. See fol. 66.

**Capitulum.** May your Church, Lord, sing a new song to you faithfully in the choir and confidently sing to you again and again in meditation upon the tambourines. Therefore, merciful one, grant that you may be pleased with your peoples just as you joyfully rejoice among the angels; and just as the diversity of the redeemed celebrates you together at Matins, so may it present to you, in the light, the service pleasing to you that belongs to its office. Grant, therefore, almighty God, that your people may please you abundantly and proclaim your praise in complete holiness.

Make us pass through the moments of this day in such a way that the adversary may not impede with a fetter the steps of those hastening toward you; so that those whom you purchased with blood, saved through the cross, and lifted up through faith, you may raise up in power and lead to heaven in indescribable majesty.

And may those who now look toward you from the earth with sorrowful eyes and follow you from the depths with grieving hearts be drawn upward by your right hand; and, clothed in robes of glory, may they glorify you in a new hymn with the saints in everlasting joy.

Prayer. The whole Church, firmly founded upon the rock, everywhere spread abroad, confesses you as the almighty Lord and Ruler of all things, the Redeemer of the human race. In it you hear those who pray to you, wash away the sins of those who weep, and turn the mourning of the sorrowful into joy. Thus, when the cock crows, you grant hope to all; thus you make those afflicted by the sickness of sins recover with confidence. Therefore we ask that, in consideration of your compassion, you mercifully correct those who stray from the faith, and grant forgiveness of sins to all your suppliants; and that our voice may resound in the morning offices, proclaiming and praising you, the true God, first and always exalted, and may keep watch.

## At Lauds

[Col. 0222D] For the Canticle. Antiphon. The faithful God, in whom there is no iniquity: the Lord God is just and holy.

Prayer. Faithful God, in whom there is no iniquity: you are just and holy, and the Lord. Although you are rightly angered by our deeds, you do not exact vengeance as we have sinned, nor chastise transgressors with a punishment proportionate to their deserts. You admonish with terror and address us with compassion, so that you may uphold justice and not abandon mercy. Therefore carry us on your wings as orphans, and protect us as your children, so that you may lead us into the strength of the earth and nourish us with an abundance of virtues and fruits.  
R\. Amen.

Reading from the Book of Ecclesiastes of Solomon (Chapter IX).

R\. Thanks be to God.

Child, there are just and wise men, and their works are in the [Col. 0223B] hand of God; yet no one knows whether he is worthy of love or hatred, but all things are reserved for the future in uncertainty, since the same things happen alike to the just and the wicked, to the good and the bad, to the clean and the unclean, to one who offers sacrifices and one who despises them. As the good man is, so is the sinner; as the perjurer, so is the one who spoke the truth. This is the worst among all the things that happen under the sun, that the same things happen to everyone. Hence the hearts of the children of men are filled with wickedness and contempt during their life, and afterward they are led to the underworld. No one lives forever or has confidence in this matter: a living dog is better than a dead lion. For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing more, nor do they have any further reward, because the memory of them has been consigned to oblivion. [Col. 0223C] Love, hatred, and envy have likewise perished together; they have no share in this age or in the work that is done under the sun. Go, then, eat your bread with joy and drink your wine with gladness, for God approves your works.  
R\. Amen.

Hymn. Splendor of the Father. fol. 67.

Supplication. Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world. See fol. 66.

Chapters. How great a praise does your creation offer you, Lord? Do human praises profit you at all, or do you lack anything so that you delight in the praises of earthly beings? You, who are so praiseworthy, are worthily praised among the holy and acclaimed with such great proclamations of the Law. But you are pleased to receive a portion of praise for this reason: you know how to bestow full praise even upon those who praise you. Therefore, Lord, grant us something worthy by which you may worthily be praised by us. May you be ceaselessly praised by the heavenly army of your power; may the greatness of confession celebrate your greatness; may the proclamations of the Prophets exult in you with trumpets, and may the sweetness of the songs of the psalms resound upon the harp. May the perfection of holiness sound forth for you on timbrels; may the sacred vessels of virgins surround you upon thrones; may all hearts caress you through frequent meditation and resound sweetly upon their particular instruments. Thus may all your creation, ringing with the cymbals of lips in faith, cry out in perpetual movement; may every spirit leap forth in due praise of you; and may every redeemed creature rejoice in you with perfect blessedness.

R\. Amen. Through your mercy.

[Col. 0224C] Sonus. You are my refuge; my God, I shall hope in him. For he himself P. Has delivered me from the snare of the hunters and from the harsh word. Alleluia. V\. Whoever dwells in the help of the Most High will abide under the protection of the God of heaven. He says to God: You are my protector, my God. P. Has delivered me.

The Lord be [with you]. R\. And with you.

Antiphon. Behold, the watchman cries: Come in the morning and at night. P. If you seek, seek. Turn back, come. V\. Come, let us exult in the Lord; let us rejoice in God our salvation. P. If you seek. V\. Glory, etc. P. If you seek.

The Lord be [with you]. R\. And with you.

Lauda. My soul clings to the pavement, Lord. P. Give me life according to your word. Alleluia, [Col. 0224D] alleluia, alleluia. V\. I have declared my ways, and you answered me; teach me your judgments. P. Give me life. V\. Glory, etc. P. Give me life.

Hymn. Inventor of the radiant lights, leader of goodness. fol. 91. Supplication. Let us pray to the Redeemer. See fol. 66.

Chapters. God, author of light, creator of brightness, who have removed all the works of darkness so that the fullness of your light might reign in us: look, we beseech you, upon this light that has been kindled, and, entreated by us all, pour forth this grace of blessing, so that, just as this flame, established for the service of your altar, conquers and drives away darkness, so your illumination may overcome every source of vices in our senses.

Our Father. Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

[Col. 0225A] Bow for the blessing.

The Lord be [with you]. R\. And with you.

Blessing. May Christ the Lord mercifully guard us and, appeased, bless us.  
R\. Amen. May he protect us by his clemency and defend us continually from all evils.  
R\. Amen. May you rejoice as those worthy of the gift of him who kindly grants forgiveness of sins.  
R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Lauda. You have commanded your commandments. Alleluia. P. To keep them exceedingly. Alleluia, alleluia. V\. My soul has desired to long for your judgments at all times. P. To keep them exceedingly. V\. Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son, etc. P. To keep.

Prayer. O God, strength and refuge. See in the following Matins.

## At Matins

Hymn. Eternal Creator of things. See fol. 3.

[Col. 0225B] Prayer. God, who by your provident majesty provide governance for the whole of creation and oppose nocturnal rest to the cares of day, lest the mind grow overheated through the length of darkness, you console us with the crowing of the cock, so that, while the herald of day sounds, meditation upon the work of day may revive. Look upon us continually with a merciful gaze, and stir us up lest, persuaded by the dew of profound night, we forget the everlasting day; but raise us when we fall in darkness and correct us by allowing us to see, so that with Peter we may repent of our errors and bewail our committed sins with matching tears.  
R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

[Col. 0225C] The Lord be [with you]. R\. And with you.

Antiphon. My glory and the one who exalts my head. Psalm III.

Antiphon. Against you alone I have sinned; have mercy on me, O God. Psalm L.

Antiphon. Send from heaven and deliver me, Lord; put to shame those who trample me. Psalm LVI.

Prayer. Almighty Lord, to whom the highest glory is rightly offered by the Angels in heaven: grant that our glorying may be in you, and that the humble confession of the peoples may reach you; and concerning the things by which we have offended you through sinning, grant that, with you propitious, we may return to the fruit of forgiveness, so that you may pardon our errors in mercy and assist us with illustrious virtue to merit you.  
R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

[Col. 0225D] Antiphon 1. God is our refuge and strength. P. A helper in tribulations that have found us exceedingly. V\. Therefore we shall not fear when the earth is shaken and the mountains are moved into the heart of the sea. P. A helper. V\. Glory and honor. P. A helper.

Prayer. God, our strength and refuge, be our helper in tribulations, so that our conscience may fear nothing when the earth is shaken by your judgment. The surge of your river, as though dwelling among your saints, gladdens the city; and there may it receive help from your countenance when, by your gift, it has received the grace of the Holy Spirit.  
R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Antiphon 2. Convert us, God our Savior, [Col. 0226A] and turn your anger away from us. P. Do not be angry with us forever. V\. You, God, will turn and give us life, and your people will rejoice in you. P. Do not be angry forever. V\. Glory and honor. P. Do not be angry forever.

Prayer. Convert us, God our salvation, and turn your anger away from us; grant peace to your people, which you proclaim, so that your people may rejoice in you. Understanding your salvation as the guardian of salvation, may it recognize your mercy in the prosperity of the times or receive your kindness in the abundance of fruits.  
R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Antiphon 3. God, our God, look upon us. P. We who hope in you; do not abandon us. V\. They cried to you and were saved; they hoped in you and were not confounded. P. We who hope. V\. Glory and honor. P. We who hope.

Prayer. Look upon us, Lord our God; do not abandon us in any way by turning your face away from us. For we shall truly be saved if you turn the gaze of your countenance upon us and joyfully join yourself to our souls. Since our fathers hoped in you and were saved, make us succeed to their hereditary hope, and, equal to them, let us rejoice with them in eternal exultation.  
R\. Amen.

Through your mercy, etc.

[Col. 0226C] R\. Lord, every one of our consciences is guilty before you. P. But you, God, are powerful to cleanse us from our sins, because our offenses are not hidden from you. V\. We have sinned with our fathers; we have acted unjustly and committed iniquities. P. But you, God. V\. Glory and honor. Let R\. be repeated.

## At Lauds

[Col. 0226D] For the Canticle. Antiphon. The Lord is the God of knowledge; he puts to death and gives life, leads down to the underworld and brings back.

Canticle. My heart is steadfast. See fol. 55.

P. The Lord is the God of knowledge; he puts to death and gives life, leads down to the underworld and brings back.

Prayer. Lord God of knowledge and immeasurable wisdom, you prepare your designs in order to weaken the bows of the mighty and gird the weak with strength; while you cast down those who trust in themselves and raise up those who hope in you; while you diminish those who are full of bread and fill the hungry with sufficiency. You exclude those swollen with knowledge, and command those who are humbly wise neither to trust in grandiloquence nor to boast proudly of your gifts, but to be so devoted to learning that we give you glory while reserving obedience for ourselves.  
R\. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

For the Benedictus. Antiphon. Nights and days, light and darkness, bless the Lord our God.

Canticle. Blessed are you, Lord God of our fathers. fol. 6. Prayer. Lord God, who above, see fol. 111.

Sonus. Alleluia. In the morning I shall meditate upon you, Lord, for you have become my helper. Alleluia, alleluia. V\. My God, my God, I rise to you at dawn; my soul thirsts for you.

[Col. 0227A] Lauda. Praise the Lord from the heavens; alleluia; praise him in the heights. Alleluia, alleluia. Psalm CXLVIII.

Reading from the Book of the Wisdom of Solomon (Chapter VI).

R\. Thanks be to God.

Kings of the peoples, love righteousness, so that you may reign forever. But what wisdom is, and how it came to be, I shall report, and I shall not hide from you the mystery of God; from the beginning of its birth I shall investigate it, place its knowledge in the light, and not pass over the truth. Nor shall I keep company with wasting envy, for such a person will not share in wisdom. The multitude of the wise is the health of the world, and a wise king is the people’s stability. Therefore receive instruction through my words, [Col. 0227B] and it will benefit you.

(Chapter VII.) I too am a mortal man, like everyone else, and descended from the earthly one who was made first; in my mother’s womb I was fashioned as flesh, coagulated over nine months in blood, from the seed of a man and the pleasure appropriate to a human being. I too, once born, received the common air and fell upon the earth, made in the same way; I uttered my first voice, like everyone, crying. I was nourished in swaddling clothes and wailing in the cradle. No king has had any other beginning of birth. Therefore, there is one entrance into life for all and a similar departure. For this reason I prayed, and understanding was given to me; I called, and the spirit of wisdom came into me.  
R\. Amen.

Hymn. Splendor of the Father’s glory. fol. 67.

[Col. 0227C] Supplication. Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world. See fol. 66.

Chapters. Send forth, Lord, your light and your truth in the return of days and into the hearts of believers; in the order of the seasons and in the devotion of the peoples; in the gift of grace and in the ministry of creation. Let your light open our sight and your truth our understanding; let your light illumine and your truth shape; let your light scatter darkness and your truth error. Through the effectiveness of both, let neither our inner person totter on the slippery waves of uncertainty nor our outer person be stained by the contagion of sin; but let the works within us be works of light and works of truth. Let your light provide in due season, and let truth confirm in its gift.

Our Father. Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

[Col. 0227D] Lauda. Sing a new song to the Lord. Alleluia, alleluia. R\. His praise is in the assembly of the saints. Alleluia.

Prayer. To you, Lord, we sing in the Church of the Saints, and to you we proclaim our thanksgiving. Grant us to utter your praises, in whom we believe that we shall obtain an everlasting reward.  
R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

In the name of the Lord, etc.

The commemorations are to be said as on fol. 94. Likewise, at the conclusion of Vespers, everything is to be said as at the conclusion of Vespers on the First Sunday after the Octave of Epiphany, fol. 94, except that the following Chapters and Blessing are to be said.

[Col. 0228A] Kyrie, eleison. R\. Christ, have mercy. Kyrie, eleison.

Chapters. In our evening prayers we beseech you, eternal Lord, to pass over our evil deeds, spare our sins, and kindly extinguish the flame of evil desire; kindle within us that fire of your Holy Spirit by which we may be able to keep your commandments. Drive away death, grant life, instill virtue, and mercifully cut away vices. Receive our prayers and grant compassion, so that we may overcome the darkness of this night and, reaching the day, walk in the light, lest we stray from the way of truth. We beseech you, most loving Father, that we may rise in you, be animated by your Holy Spirit, and shine with eternal splendors in Christ your Son.

[Col. 0228B] Our Father. And lead us not. Delivered from evil, etc. fol. 2.

Bow for the blessing.

The Lord be [with you]. R\. And with your spirit.

Blessing. May the petition poured forth in your prayers ascend to the Lord.  
R\. Amen. May the Most Merciful Shepherd grant whatever you ask of him.  
R\. Amen. May he govern your minds with saving counsel and not permit your souls to be led into temptation.  
R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

The Lauda is to be said as at the conclusion of the First Sunday after the Octave of Epiphany; likewise the Prayer on fol. 94.

## On the Fifth Sunday after the Octave of Epiphany

[Col. 0228C]

### Saturday at Vespers

Lauda. In the evening weeping will remain; P. And in the morning, joy. V\. You turned my mourning into joy; you tore off my sackcloth and girded me with gladness. P. And in the morning, joy.

Prayer. Heal us, Lord, while we cry out to you; and so that you may turn our evening tears into joy, may morning gladness, with your help, come to us more swiftly.  
R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Sonus. Enter the gates of the Lord with confession, his courts with hymns of confession. Alleluia. V\. Praise his name, for it is sweet; his mercy is forever and ever, and his truth endures from age to age. Alleluia.

The Lord be always with you. R\. And with you.

Antiphon. I will bless you, Lord my God. P. And I will praise your name, because you are the one who performs wonders. V\. I will exalt you, Lord my God and my King, and bless your name forever and ever. P. And I will praise. V\. Glory and honor. P. And I will praise.

The Lord be always with you. R\. And with you.

Lauda. Alleluia. Teach me goodness, discipline, and knowledge, O God. Alleluia. P. For I have believed in your commandments. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V\. You have dealt well with your servant, Lord, according to [Col. 0229A] your word. P. For I have believed in your commandments. V\. Glory and honor, etc. P. For I have believed.

Hymn. Christ, light of the world. See fol. 110. Supplication. Let us pray. See fol. 66.

Chapters. Almighty God, who grant us, without exception of any hour or time, the hope of calling upon you: now that we have assembled for the evening solemnities and are performing the duty of the divine Office, graciously deign to hear us, and grant that, when this day is ended, we may be held guilty of no sin and liable for no offense; and if our weakness has committed any error, may it be wiped away by the clemency of your mercy.

Our Father. And lead us not. Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

Bow for the blessing.

The Lord be [with you]. R\. And with you, etc.

[Col. 0229B] Blessing. May the Lord fill you with spiritual gifts and make you sharers in the kingdom of heaven.  
R\. Amen. May he mortify your flesh by putting an end to vices and give life to your souls through the beginning of virtues.  
R\. Amen. And may he enrich you so fully with the abundance of his grace that he may always delight in dwelling in your hearts.  
R\. Amen.

Through [your mercy].

Lauda. It is good for me. Alleluia. P. The law of your mouth. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V\. Teach me goodness, discipline, and knowledge, for I have believed in your commandments. P. The law of your mouth. V\. Glory and honor, etc. P. The law of your mouth.

Prayer. Let your mercy, Lord, be upon us. In the same folio. The commemorations as above, fol. 94.

## At Matins

[Col. 0229C]

Hymn. Eternal Creator of things. See fol. 3.

Prayer. God, whom the created greatness of the whole work celebrates in praise as the Maker of all things, whose power rational creation marvels at: we humbly bring honor to you and invoke you with the voices of our hearts. You awaken us to the Office of Matins when the cock proclaims the coming day; make the vows of our service pleasing to you, so that, supported by your protection, you may wash away what we have stained by sinning, and continually grant us the grace of your justification through prayer.  
R\. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God, etc.

Antiphon. Your salvation, Lord, is upon your people, and your blessing. Psalm III.

Antiphon. Blot out my iniquities, Lord. Psalm [Col. 0229D] L.

Antiphon. I shall cry out to God Most High, to God the creator of all, who has done good to me. Psalm LVI.

119 Prayer. Lord God, for whom we rise to perform the duty of our service, pour an abundance of blessing and salvation upon your people. In your mercy blot out the guilt we have incurred, and make us free from the burden of our offenses. Hear the groans of the penitent and bestow the fruit of forgiveness; and, moved by the cries of the faithful who knock, grant each one the remedy requested.  
R\. Amen.

Through your mercy, God, etc.

Antiphon 1. You have turned your face away from us, Lord, [Col. 0230A] and we have been troubled. We cry out to you, Lord, and beseech you, our God. P. That you may hear us and have mercy on us. V\. To you we lift our eyes, who dwell in the heavens. P. That you may hear us. V\. Glory and honor to the Father. P. That you may hear us.

Prayer. We exalt you, Lord, magnifying your name, so that you may not turn your face away from us and may not trouble us in your anger, because we cry out to you, our God, and beseech you to hear us and have mercy on us. Turn our heart to you in goodness, so that we may praise your name and persistently recount your wonders.  
R\. Amen.

Through your mercy, etc.

Antiphon. Behold, the eyes of the Lord are upon those who fear him and upon those who hope in his mercy. P. To deliver their souls from death. V\. Our soul waits for the Lord, for he is our helper and protector. P. To deliver. V\. Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son. P. To deliver from death.

Prayer. Let your mercy, Lord, be upon us, so that you who fashion the hearts of human beings one by one may sanctify them in a special way. Since your eyes are upon those who fear you, grant us the fullness of your fear, so that you may bestow upon us the abundance of knowledge of you.  
R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Antiphon 3. The Lord is near to those who are troubled in heart, and he will save the humble. P. He will not abandon all who hope in him. V\. Many are the tribulations of the just, and from all of them the Lord will deliver them. P. He will not abandon. V\. Glory. P. He will not abandon.

[Col. 0230C] Prayer. Hear graciously, Lord, those who seek you, and, as one who mercifully grants favors, grant that our soul may rejoice in you. You who are near to those troubled in heart, open your ear to the contrition of our spirit and turn our bodies and hearts toward your peace, which surpasses all understanding.  
R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

R\. Lord, our whole conscience is guilty before you. P. But you, powerful God, can cleanse us from our sins, because our offenses are not hidden from you. V\. We have sinned with our fathers; we have acted unjustly and committed iniquities. P. But you, God. V\. Glory and honor. Let R\. be repeated.

## At Lauds

[Col. 0230D] For the Canticle. Antiphon. The Lord makes humble and exalts. He raises the needy from the earth and lifts the poor from the dungheap, making him sit with the powerful of the people.

Canticle. My heart is steadfast. See fol. 55. Prayer. Lord God of knowledge. See fol. 117.

For the Benedictus. Antiphon. Seas and rivers, bless the Lord; bless the Lord, springs.

Canticle. Blessed are you, Lord God of our fathers. See fol. 6. On the First Sunday of Advent. Prayer. Lord God of the fathers. See fol. 93.

Sonus. At morning and evening you will rejoice, O God. Alleluia, alleluia. V\. You visited the earth; you multiplied its abundance, O God. Alleluia, alleluia.

[Col. 0231A] Lauda. Praise the Lord from the heavens. Alleluia. Praise him in the heights. Alleluia. Psalm CXLVIII.

Reading from the Book of Ecclesiasticus of Solomon (Chapter I).

R\. Thanks be to God.

Child, all wisdom is from the Lord God, and it has always been with him and exists before the age. Who can count the sand of the sea, the drops of rain, and the days of the age? Who has measured the height of heaven, the breadth of the earth, and the depth of the abyss? Who has investigated the wisdom of God, which precedes all things? Wisdom was created before all other things, and the understanding of prudence from eternity. The source of wisdom is the word of God in the highest, and its ways are eternal commandments. To whom has the root of wisdom been revealed and manifested? And who has understood the multiplication of its ways? There is one Most High, the almighty Creator, [Col. 0231B] a powerful and exceedingly fearsome King, seated upon the throne, the Lord God. He created him by the Holy Spirit.  
R\. Amen.

120 Hymn. Splendor of the Father, etc. See fol. 67. Supplication. Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world. fol. 66.

Chapters. This Sunday, dearest brothers, is to be honored by us with pious devotion. The day of Resurrection and peace has dawned, the day of true light and life, on which Christ, the life of believers, rose from the dead. Let us render abundant thanks and praises to God, so that, as we solemnly celebrate the day of the Lord’s Resurrection, he may deign to offer us tranquil peace and a special joy; so that, from the morning vigil until night, protected by the favor of his mercy, we may rejoice in the gift of our Redeemer.

[Col. 0231C] Our Father. And lead us not. Deliver us from evil, etc. See fol. 10.

Lauda. Sing a new song to the Lord. Alleluia, alleluia. V\. His praise is in the assembly of the Saints. Alleluia.

Prayer. To you, Lord, in the Church. See fol. 117. The commemorations as above, fol. 94.

Likewise, at the conclusion of Vespers everything is to be said as on the First Sunday, as above, fol. 94, except that the following Chapters and Blessing are to be said.

Kyrie, eleison. R\. Christ, have mercy. Kyrie, eleison.

Chapters. Now that we have drawn near to the darkness of night, there is nothing truer or better to choose than to ask you, almighty God, for forgiveness of our sins, since we acknowledge you, [Col. 0231D] Lord, as our Maker. Be present, Lord, in the prayers of your people, and generously forgive the sins of all. Do not remember that at the beginning man sinned, when in your divinity you see our Redeemer made like us. You know how much the enemy lies in wait for us. We ask that he find none of us whom he may win, since your glorious Trinity is continually proclaimed as worthy of worship in the Catholic Church.

Our Father. And lead us not. Delivered from evil, etc. fol. 2.

Blessing. May almighty Lord, in whom there is an immeasurable abundance of compassion, fill you with every blessing and mercifully defend you from evil.  
R\. Amen. May the Lord mercifully forgive all your sins and make you pleasing to him forever.  
R\. Amen. May you be secure under the protection of him by whose gracious favor you have been redeemed.  
R\. Amen.

Through your mercy, etc.

## On the Sixth Sunday after the Octave of Epiphany

### Saturday at Vespers

[Col. 0232A] In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, light with peace. R\. Thanks be to God.

Lauda. With you, Lord, is the fountain of life, and in your light P. We shall see light. V\. The children of men will hope in the protection of your wings. They will be filled with the abundance of your house, and you will give them drink from the torrent of your delight. P. We shall see light.

Prayer. Lord, with whom is the fountain of life and in whose light we see light, nourish within us the [Col. 0232B] splendor of your knowledge, so that, as we thirst, you may grant us life-giving drink, and restore the understanding of our darkened souls to the light from above.  
R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

The Lord be [with you]. R\. And with you.

Sonus. Darkness will not be dark to you. P. And night will be illuminated like day. Alleluia. V\. Your eyes saw my unfinished substance, and in your book they will all be written; the days will be formed. Alleluia. P. And night will be like.

The Lord be always with you. R\. And with you.

Antiphon. Bless the Lord in all his works. Give glory to his name. P. And confess him with a voice of praise and in the songs of your lips. V\. Praise the Lord, children; praise the name of the Lord. [Col. 0232C] P. And confess him. V\. Glory and honor. P. And confess him.

The Lord be always [with you]. R\. And with your spirit.

Lauda. Let your mercies come to me, and I shall live. Alleluia. P. For your law is my meditation. Alleluia, alleluia. V\. Let your mercy now come to me, that it may console me, according to your word to your servant. P. For your law. V\. Glory and honor. P. For your law.

Hymn. O blessed light of the Trinity. See fol. 113. Supplication. Let us pray to the Redeemer. See fol. 66.

Chapters. Our defense and abundant illumination, Lord, illumine the dark places of our heart, which sinful filth and thick Chaos cloud. Illumine the secret places of our breast, so that we may contemplate the Redeemer’s compassion. Receive the vows of the faithful and grant the remedy of the gifts of repentance. Receive the evening sacrifice with the duty of praise, and restore [Col. 0232D] the morning benefit with the gift of eternity. Grant that we who here believe you to be almighty may, at the Resurrection of all, drink more abundantly of your good things.

Our Father. And lead us not. Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

Blessing. May almighty Lord bless you, who has deigned to form you from nothing.  
R\. Amen. May he himself heal your weaknesses, who alone is Lord and Redeemer of all.  
R\. Amen. And may our Lord himself always care for you, in whom is the fullness of your salvation.  
R\. Amen. Through your mercy.

Lauda. According to your mercy, Lord, give me life. P. That I may keep the testimonies of your mouth. Alleluia, [Col. 0233A] alleluia. V\. Forever, Lord, your word remains in heaven. P. That I may keep. V\. Glory. P. That I may.

Prayer. Show us your mercy, Lord. See below. The commemorations as above, fol. 94.

## At Matins
Hymn. “Eternal Creator of all things.” See fol. 3.

Prayer. O God, who illumine the whole world, enveloped in darkness, with a ray of your splendor, and awaken the present day for our uses by the miracle of your Epiphany: grant, eternal God, that, rising from our falls, and having shaken off the sleep of unbelief, we may be roused with vigilant care and our whole affection to your praises; so that, stripped of the works of darkness, we may follow you, the true prince of light. As the brightness [Col. 0233B] of day, poured forth, scatters the density of nocturnal gloom, so pour forth the work of healing upon the sick, grant consolation to the anxious, show the way of salvation to those who wander, bestow the gift of pardon upon penitents, and appear in gentle, radiant light to those who seek you; so that, while the splendor of your glory shines back in us, your whole Church may gleam with hope, faith, and charity. R. Amen. Through your mercy, our God, etc.

Antiphon. “But you, O Lord, are my protector, my glory, and the one who lifts up my head.” Psalm III.

Antiphon. “According to your great mercy, O Lord, blot out my iniquities.” Psalm L.

Antiphon. “Send from heaven and deliver me, O Lord; give over to reproach those who trample me.” Psalm LVI.

[Col. 0233C] Prayer. O Lord, our protector, lift up our head in glory and enrich us with your mercy; wash the innermost parts of our heart from injustice and cleanse them from the defilements of sin. Send from heaven and rescue us from the reproach of those who trample us, so that, rejoicing, we may hasten back to this altar of yours and offer you the morning sacrifice in the temple. R. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God, who are blessed, etc.

The Lord be always with you. R. And with your spirit.

Antiphon 1. “In you our fathers hoped, O Lord.” P. “They hoped, and you delivered them.” V. “To you they cried out and were saved; in you they hoped and were not confounded.” P. “They hoped.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “They hoped.”

[Col. 0233D] Prayer. Look upon us, O Lord our God; do not abandon us in any way by turning your face away from us. For we shall truly be saved if you turn the gaze of your countenance toward us and join yourself gladly to our souls, so that, because our fathers hoped in you and were saved, you may cause us to succeed to their inherited hope and, following their likeness, rejoice with them in eternal exultation. R. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God, etc.

Antiphon 2. “May your mercy, O Lord, follow us.” P. “All the days of our life.” V. “Show us, O Lord, your mercy, and grant us your salvation.” P. “All the days of our life.” V. “Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son.” P. “All the days of our life.”

[Col. 0234A] Prayer. Show us your mercy, O Lord, and fill with joy the people awaiting you, so that you may both forgive the iniquity of your people and, appeased, cover our sins. R. Amen.

Through your mercy, O God, etc.

Antiphon 3. “Let the wicked man turn back from his evil way, and let the unjust cease to sin.” P. “And I shall come to you in joyfulness, says the Lord.” V. “Do not hope in iniquity, and do not desire plunder; if riches increase, do not set your heart upon them.” P. “And I shall come to you.” V. “Glory and honor to the Father.” P. “And I shall come to you.”

Prayer. As we pour out our hearts before you in prayer, hear and have mercy, O Lord, who are the hope of all; make us subject to serve you, and in your propitious kindness meet those subjected to sin. Make us free from the plunder of iniquity, and let us seek the ornaments of your riches; and may we deserve to desire you, to know you, and to have you as God throughout all the time of our life. P. Amen.

Through mercy.

P. O Lord, we have acted wickedly; every age bears a guilty conscience; we have sinned against you, O Lord. P. Turn toward mercy. V. We have sinned; we have acted impiously, withdrawn, and strayed from your commandments. P. Turn toward mercy. V. Glory and honor. Let P. be repeated.

At Lauds.

For the Canticle. Antiphon. “The underworld will not confess to you, O God, nor will death praise you. The living, the living will confess to you; and he will make your mercy known.”

Canticle of Hezekiah (Isaiah XXXVIII).

I said: In the midst of my days * I shall go to the gates of the underworld.

I sought the remnant of my years; * I said: I shall not see the Lord God in the land of the living.

I shall look upon man no more, * nor any inhabitant of repose.

My generation has been taken away from me, rolled up, * like a shepherd’s tent.

My life has been cut off like a weaver’s web; while I was still beginning it, he severed me; * from morning until evening you will finish me.

I hoped until morning, * like a lion he crushed all my bones:

[Col. 0234D] From morning until evening you will finish me; * like a swallow’s fledgling, so I cried out; I moaned like a dove.

My eyes have grown weak, * looking upward.

O Lord, I am oppressed; answer on my behalf. * What shall I say, or what will he answer me, since I myself have done it?

I shall recall all my years * in the bitterness of my soul.

O Lord, if life is lived in this way, and if the life of my spirit is such, * you will correct me and restore me to life.

Behold, my bitterness is most bitter in peace; * but you have rescued my soul so that I should not perish, and have cast all my sins behind your back.

For the underworld will not confess to you, nor will death praise you; * those who descend into the pit will not await your truth.

[Col. 0235A] The living, the living will confess to you, as I do today; * the father will make your truth known to his children.

O Lord, save us, * and we shall sing our psalms all the days of our life in the house of the Lord.

V. Glory and honor.

P. “The underworld will not confess to you, nor will death”—P. “praise you. The living, the living will confess to you; and he will make your mercy known.”

Prayer. Rescue our souls, O Lord, so that we may not perish in destruction; cast all the deeds of our sins behind your back, so that we may not be cast down, lost, into hell. Rather, having been given life by you, may we confess you here, and, awaiting your truth, continually sing our psalms in your house. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

[Col. 0235B] For the Benedictus. Antiphon. “Children of men, bless the Lord of Israel; and all priests, servants of God, bless the Lord.”

Canticle. “Blessed are you, O Lord God.” Fol. 6.

Chant. “May God have mercy on us.” P. “May he bless us.” Alleluia. V. “May the Lord illuminate his face upon us.” P. “And may he bless us.”

Praise. “Praise the Lord from the heavens.” Alleluia, alleluia. Psalm CXLVIII.

Reading from the Book of Ecclesiasticus of Solomon (chapters VI–VII).

R. Thanks be to God.

My son, keep the thought of God’s commandments, and be especially constant in his precepts; and he himself will give you a heart, and the desire for wisdom will be given to you. Do not do evil, [Col. 0235C] and it will not seize you. Depart from the unjust, and evils will withdraw from you. Do not sow evil in the furrows of justice, and you will not reap it sevenfold. Do not seek leadership from a man, nor a seat of honor from a king. Do not justify yourself before God, for he himself is the knower of the heart; and do not wish to appear wise before the king. Do not seek to become a judge unless you are able by your strength to break through injustices, lest perhaps you fear the face of the powerful and place a stumbling block in your own integrity. Do not sin amid the multitude of the city, nor thrust yourself among the people, nor love double sins; for you will not be innocent in one. Do not be fainthearted in your soul; do not neglect to entreat and to give alms. Do not say: “God will look upon me because of the multitude of my gifts, and when I offer, the Most High will accept my gifts.” [Col. 0235D] Do not mock a man in the bitterness of his soul, for there is one who humbles and exalts: God is the observer. R. Amen.

Hymn. “Splendor of the Father.” Fol. 67. 123 Supplication. “Let us pray to the Redeemer.” See fol. 66.

Lord, have mercy. R. Christ, have mercy. Lord, have mercy.

Capitulum. Now the rising sun shines forth, now the day hastens on; the darkness driven away, dawn glows with the purest light. The heaven and the shining sun send forth their rays upon the world. All things hasten, all things hurry, desiring to have the Lord propitious, whom they always acknowledge as their creator and likewise their defender.

Our Father. “And lead us not.” Delivered from evil, etc.

Praise. “Sing a new song to the Lord.” Alleluia, [Col. 0236A] alleluia. V. “His praise is in the assembly of the saints.” Alleluia.

Prayer. To you, O Lord, we sing in the assembly of the saints, and to you we proclaim our gratitude. Grant us to utter your praises, in which we believe that we shall obtain an eternal reward. R. Amen.

Through.

In the name…

The commemorations are said as on fol. 94.

Likewise, at the conclusion of Vespers, everything is to be said as at the conclusion of Vespers on the first Sunday, fol. 94, except the Capitulum and Blessing, which are to be said as follows.

Lord, have mercy. R. Christ, have mercy. Lord, have mercy.

Capitulum. “At Vespers, O Lord.”

Blessing. “May the Lord grant to us.” Fol. 102.

IN THE SEVENTH SUNDAY AFTER THE OCTAVE OF EPIPHANY.

[Col. 0236B]

Saturday at Vespers.

Praise. “The Lord commanded by day.” Prayer. “O God, who your...” See fol. 110.

Chant. “Alleluia. In the evening there will be weeping, and in the morning, joy. Alleluia.” V. “Alleluia. You have turned my mourning into joy for me, O Lord; you have torn my sackcloth and girded me with gladness.” Alleluia.

The Lord be always with you. R. And with your spirit.

Antiphon. “Yours is the kingdom, O Lord; you are over all rulers.” P. “In your hand are strength and power; in your hand are might and dominion.” V. “O Lord, God of hosts, convert us and show us your face, and we shall be saved.” P. “In your hand.” V. “Glory and honor to the Father.” P. “In your hand is strength.”

The Lord be with you. R. And with you.

Praise. “You founded the earth, and it endures.” Alleluia. P. “By your ordinance the day persists.” Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V. “Forever, O Lord, your word remains in heaven.” P. “By your ordinance.” V. “Glory.” P. “By your ordinance.”

Hymn. “Inventor of the ruddy light.” Fol. 91. Supplication. “Let us pray to the Redeemer.” Fol. 66.

Capitulum. If we were to receive as much punishment for our sins as we deserve from the guilt of our origin, the human race would long ago have been brought headlong to the earth, unless he had restored us to you, O Lord, released from such a bond by the price of his blood. But now, O Lord, what can your people proclaim in praises to you for such great benefits? What gifts can it arrange to present to you, gifts that have in no way been bestowed by them? But now, O Lord, we ask you that this evening light, which has been kindled for you, may be acceptable to your eyes and pleasing; may it be like that unquenchable fire which went before your people in the wilderness at night in a pillar of fire; may it be like that fire which carried Elijah away from this world and conveyed him heavenward in a fiery chariot, which Elisha saw with his own eyes as he watched, and, unwilling to leave his father, cried out in a living voice, “The chariot of Israel and its charioteer”; the fire which Moses was deemed worthy to see, and which he announced to the people when he declared that he had spoken with the Lord.

[Col. 0237A] Our Father. Delivered from evil. See fol. 2.

Blessing. May the Lord graciously regard your devotion and restore to you suitable remedies. R. Amen. May he grant you a tranquil life and make you abound in every good thing. R. Amen. May he guide you in the world with such support of his loving-kindness that he may raise you to heaven by the merit of blessedness. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Praise. “How I have loved your law, O Lord!” [Translator’s note: The source prints *regem tuam*, an irregular phrase combining “king” with a feminine possessive; “law” follows the probable intended *legem tuam*.] Alleluia. P. “It is my meditation all the day.” Alleluia, alleluia. V. “How sweet are your words to my throat, sweeter than honey to my mouth!” P. “It is my meditation all the day.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “It is my meditation all the day.”
