Prayer. “Crying out to you, O Lord.” See fol. 124.

The commemorations are as in Vespers on the first Sunday of Advent of the Lord.

At Matins.

Hymn. “Eternal Creator of all things.” See fol. 3.

Prayer. “Lord God, almighty Father, inspirer...” See fol. 26.

Antiphon. “My glory, O my God, and the one who lifts up my head.” Psalm III.

Antiphon. “Against you alone have I sinned; have mercy on me, O God.” Psalm L.

124 Antiphon. “Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me, for my soul trusts in you.” Psalm LVI.

Prayer. To you, O Lord, we send forth the cry of our voice, and we beseech you to hear us from your holy mountain. Since you know the weak strength of our submission, strengthen us by your right hand; blot out harmful evils, and stir up our hearts to follow you. Since human frailty does not trust in being able to save itself, may your mercy, sent from heaven, rescue our souls. R. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God, etc.

Antiphon 1. “Bless, O Lord, your inheritance.” P. “And govern it, and raise it up forever.” V. “For you, O Lord, are gentle and mild, and very merciful to those who call upon you.” P. “And govern it.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “And govern it.”

Prayer. Crying out to you, O Lord, we pray that you not be silent in our consolation, nor, abandoning us according to the desires of our heart, hand us over together with sinners. Save your people, whom you yourself created, and bless your inheritance, which you redeemed with your precious blood. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Antiphon 2. “Give strength, O Lord, to your people.” P. “And bless your people in peace.” V. “And govern it, and raise it up forever.” P. “And bless it.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “And bless it.”

Prayer. Give strength, O Lord, to your people against all the evils of adversity, and enrich your people with the gift of peace, so that, because of their abundant tranquility, all may sing glory to you in your temple, and, likewise forgetting the evils of this life, always offer praise and honor to your majesty. R. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

[Col. 0238A] Antiphon 3. “Be for us, O Lord, a protecting God.” P. “And a fortified place, so that you may save us.” V. “How great is the abundance of your sweetness, O Lord, which you have stored up for those who fear you, and perfected for those who hope in you, in the sight of the children of men.” P. “And a fortified place.” V. “Glory and honor to the Father.” P. “And a fortified place.”

Prayer. Be for us, O Lord, a protecting God, lest, while inhabitants besiege us, the integrity of our minds be struck down. In place of a fortified place, may we deserve to have your help; for when you overshadow us, no force will be able to break in, nor will temptation penetrate our hidden recesses, if you are present within and without and give us your right hand as our strength and refuge. R. Amen.

[Col. 0238B] Through your mercy.

R. O Lord of hosts, you judge sinners with tranquility and correct the erring with reverence. P. You give the sinner a place for repentance; you grant time and delay by which we may be cleansed from wickedness. V. And you, O Lord God of hosts, are gentle and mild, patient, and in mercy you dispose of us. P. You give the sinner a place. V. Glory and honor, etc. Let R. be repeated.

At Lauds.

For the Canticle. Antiphon. “By night my spirit watches for you, O God, for your commandments are light upon the earth.” P. “Learn justice.”

Canticle. “By night my spirit watches.” See fol. 64.

Prayer. O God, illumine with the light of your beautiful commandments our spirit that watches for you by night; be watchful over those who seek you in the storm, and be present as noonday light. Let no darkness hinder us as we follow you, nor the love of injustice draw our footsteps back from you. Rather, let us be able to learn justice; with eager desire we ask you, the author of justice, to make us advance. And while we long to embrace you with enduring sight, may we also cling forever to the embraces of your wisdom. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

For the Benedictus.

Antiphon. “Priests, servants of the Most High God, bless our Lord.”

Canticle. “Blessed are you, O Lord, God of our fathers.” [Col. 0238D] See on the first Sunday of Advent of the Lord, fol. 6. Prayer. “Lord God of the fathers.” Fol. 93.

Chant. “You are wondrous in giving light.” Alleluia. P. “From the everlasting mountains.” Alleluia. V. “The thought of man will confess you, O God, and the remnants of thought will keep festival for you.” P. “From the everlasting mountains.”

Praise. “Praise the Lord from the heavens.” Alleluia. “Praise him in the heights.” Alleluia, alleluia. Psalm CXLVIII.

Reading from the Book of Wisdom, Ecclesiasticus, of Solomon (chapters XXXII–XXXIII).

R. Thanks be to God.

My son, do nothing without counsel, and after the deed you will not repent. Do not go on the road of ruin, and you will not stumble over a stone; do not expose yourself to a laborious way, [Col. 0239A] nor place a stumbling block before your soul. Be cautious about your ways, and pay attention to those of your household. In every work believe with the faith of your soul, for this is the keeping of the commandments. Whoever believes in God and attends to his commandments, and those who trust in him, will not be diminished. Evils do not meet the one who fears the Lord, but in temptation God preserves him and delivers him from evil. R. Amen.

Hymn. “Splendor of the Father.” Fol. 67. Supplication. “Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world.” Fol. 66.

Capitulum. How magnificent are your works, O Lord! You have made all things in wisdom. Behold, already the gloom of the dark night is sprinkled with the splendor of the stars, and the golden beauty of the dawning day’s light enters. Behold, already, with the night’s course completed, light shines forth from the bright height of heaven [Col. 0239B] and flashes throughout the whole world with the splendor and brilliance of your radiance. Behold, already, after the chorus of the roosters, the chattering voices of sparrows resound in varied melodies, and the different kinds of birds, rowing with their wings, seek the heights toward the stars. [Translator’s note: The supplied *aures*, “ears,” is unclear in this clause; the rendering follows the evident upward flight described.] Therefore, almighty Father, we tirelessly ask the abundant clemency of your loving-kindness, that you allow us to pass this day without sin; so that, just as you distribute the radiance of your omnipotence to all, you may also send into our hearts the gleam of a small spark of your divinity.

Our Father. “And lead us not.” Delivered from evil, etc. See fol. 2.

The Lord be always with you. R. And with your spirit.

Praise. “Sing a new song to the Lord.” Alleluia, [Col. 0239C] alleluia. V. “His praise is in the assembly of the saints.” Alleluia.

Prayer. “To you, O Lord, in the assembly of the saints.” Fol. 117. The commemorations as on fol. 94.

Likewise, at the conclusion of Vespers, everything is to be said as at the conclusion of Vespers on the first Sunday after Epiphany, fol. 94, except the Capitulum and Blessing, which follow.

Capitulum. O God, who first illumined the darkness and founded visible substance from unstable creation, look upon us with a most gentle face, and accept our prayers as an evening sacrifice, so that we may not be seized by any evil terrors in this night. Rather, grant us a pure heart and a mind alienated from every crime, so that the enemy may find no place in us for doing harm.

[Col. 0239D] Our Father. Delivered from evil. Fol. 2.

Blessing. Show, O Lord, your mercy upon these servants of yours, and, while your holy Angel keeps watch, guard them. R. Amen. May continual joy and everlasting gladness come upon them, O Lord. R. Amen. May the heavenly seal which you have deigned to bestow upon them through the Holy Spirit remain in them. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Praise. “They were songs to me.” See fol. 94. Prayer. “Crying out to you, O Lord.” See fol. 124.

IN THE EIGHTH SUNDAY AFTER THE OCTAVE OF EPIPHANY.

Saturday at Vespers.

Praise. “Illumine my eyes.” Prayer. “Illumine our eyes, O Lord.” See fol. 113.

Chant. “To you a hymn is due, O God, in Zion, and to you a vow shall be paid.” P. “In Jerusalem.” Alleluia. V. “Hear our prayer, O God; to you all flesh shall come.” P. “In.”

The Lord be with you. R. And with you.

Antiphon. “The Lord founded the earth by wisdom; he established the heavens by prudence.” P. “By his wisdom the abysses burst forth, and the clouds grow dense with dew.” V. “He made the moon for its appointed times; the sun knows its setting.” P. “By his wisdom.” V. “Glory and honor to the Father.” P. “By his wisdom.”

The Lord be always with you. R. And with your spirit.

Praise. “Keep my feet from every evil way, O Lord.” [Col. 0240B] P. “That I may keep your commandments.” Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V. “From your precepts I have understood; therefore I have hated every way of iniquity.” P. “That I may keep your commandments.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “That I may keep your commandments.”

Hymn. “Christ, light of the world.” See fol. 110. Supplication. “Let us pray to the Redeemer.” See fol. 66.

Capitulum. Illumine us, O Lord, as we rest in this night, so that with our hands we may present the cross in prayer before you, and not fear the tempter who walks in darkness, having with us the revelation of the nations and the glory of your people Israel. For then the enemy withdraws if you deign to be propitious; then he will turn away from the sword of his fury if your mercy turns back toward us. Do not abandon us, O Lord, to the jaws of wolves, nor condemn us to the teeth of lions; rather, in the assembly of your saints, may we deserve to enter your gates in confession of spiritual joys.

Our Father. Delivered from evil.

Humble yourselves for the blessing.

The Lord be always with you. R. And with your spirit.

Blessing. May the most merciful Lord, in whose hand is every prosperity, always grant you increase of blessing and peace. R. Amen. May you always be united and share in good works, so that you never deviate from the commandments of the Lord. R. Amen. May the Lord mercifully forgive all your sins and, in his favor, lead you to everlasting glory. R. Amen. Through his mercy, etc.

[Col. 0240D] Praise. “Approve the free offering of my mouth, O Lord.” Alleluia. P. “Teach me your...” Alleluia. V. “Your word is a lamp to my feet, O Lord, and a light to my paths.” P. “And your judgments.” V. “Glory and honor to the Father, etc.” P. “And your judgments.”

Prayer. “To you, O Lord, our eyes…” See at the following Matins.

At Matins.

Hymn. “Eternal Creator of all things.” See fol. 3.

Prayer. After the song of the crowing roosters and the exclusion of the night’s rest, mature night gives birth to the day for you, O Lord, and the roosters, with beating wings, proclaim the morning hymn with their heralding voices. The birds of heaven send forth praises to you. At your command, the darkness being scattered, the sun sends forth its rays upon the world. These are your miracles, almighty Father. We bring only our vows, offering these morning sacrifices to your holy name, so that, absolved from past sins, we may deserve to be absolved from present tribulation. R. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God, etc.

Antiphon 1. “Salvation belongs to the Lord, and your blessing is upon your people.” Psalm III.

Antiphon. “You have made known to me the uncertain and hidden things of your wisdom.” Psalm L.

Antiphon. “In the shadow of your wings we hope, O God, while iniquity passes by.” Psalm LVI.

Prayer. “The Word ineffably before the ages.” See fol. 33.

Antiphon 1. “Hear from heaven, O Lord.” P. “And forgive the sins of your servants and your people.” V. “For you, O Lord, are gentle and mild, and very merciful to those who call upon you.” P. “And forgive the sins.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “And forgive the sins of your servants.”

Prayer. To you, O Lord, we raise our eyes; we confess that you dwell in the heavens and sustain the structure of the earth by your power. Therefore have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy; spare our sins, for which we fear you. Look upon our contempt with merciful kindness, and rescue us by the right hand of your power from the reproach of sin. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 2. “Come, O God, to deliver us.” P. “Hasten to help us.” V. “Give ear, you who rule Israel, you who lead Joseph like a sheep. Appear, you who sit upon the Cherubim.” P. “To help us.” V. “Glory and...” P. “To help us.”

Prayer. You who rule Israel, give ear through your mercy, O Lord; you who lead Joseph like a sheep, provide the remedies of a shepherd’s governance and a protector’s care. Convert us and show your face, and we shall be saved, while you, the Most High, look upon the lowly and, appeased, hear the prayers of those who pray. R. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God, etc.

Antiphon 3. “O Lord our God.” P. “Hear us; be propitious and save us.” V. “Let your mercy, O Lord, quickly go before us, for we have become exceedingly poor.” P. “Hear us.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “Hear us.”

[Col. 0241D] Prayer. Be propitious toward our sins, O Lord, and, for the honor of your name, restore us with perfect freedom, lest, while we are worn down by the indictment of our sins, we be reduced to the reproach of the nations. Therefore, so that you may not punish us with the severity of a sentence, wash away from us the cause of our crimes; and let the groaning of the bound enter into your presence, so that from your hidden place your granted grace may go before us into our manifest condition. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

R. O God, who give a place for repentance, grant pardon to our sins. For who will say to you, “What have you done?” Or who will stand against your judgment? For there is no other God besides you. P. “For you care for all.” V. “Have mercy, O God, on all, for you can do all things, and you overlook the sins of men for the sake of repentance.” P. “For you care for all.” V. “Glory and honor.” R. is repeated.

Another Responsory. The almighty Lord heard the voice of the Publican and of the sinner. P. The true and merciful God grants forgiveness to the faithful who confesses. V. The Publican stood at a distance and did not dare to raise his eyes toward heaven, but he struck his breast, saying: “Be propitious to me, a sinner.” P. The true God. V. “Glory and honor,” etc. The Responsory is repeated.

At Lauds.

For the Canticle. Antiphon. “Your commandments are light upon the earth, O Lord. Learn justice, inhabitants of the earth.”

Canticle. “By night my spirit watches.” See fol. 64.

Prayer. “The spirit that watches by night.” See fol. 124.

[Col. 0242B] For the Benedictus. Antiphon. “Blessed are you, O God, and blessed is the name of your glory. Bless the Lord, all his elect; may his holy name be blessed throughout all ages of ages.”

Canticle. “Blessed are you, O Lord, God of our fathers.” See fol. 6. Prayer. “Lord God, who are above the Cherubim.” See fol. 111.

Chant. “Make your power known to me in the morning, O Lord, for I trust in you.” P. “Show me...” Alleluia. V. “Alleluia. I remembered your ancient days, O Lord, and I shall meditate on the work of your hands.” P. “Show me...”

Praise. “Praise the Lord from the heavens.” Alleluia, alleluia. “Praise him in the heights.” Alleluia, alleluia. Psalm CXLVIII.

[Col. 0242C] Reading from the Book of Ecclesiasticus of Solomon (chapter XXXIV).

R. Thanks be to God.

My son, whoever fears the Lord will fear nothing, for he himself is his hope. Blessed is the soul that fears the Lord. Upon whom will it look, and what is its strength? The eyes of the Lord are upon those who fear him: he is the protector of power, the support of strength, the shelter from heat, the shade at noonday, the prayer against stumbling, and the help in falling; he exalts the soul, enlightens the eyes, and gives health, life, and blessing. The offering of one who sacrifices from injustice is defiled, and the mockeries of the unjust are not pleasing. You alone, O Lord, are with those who endure on the way of truth and justice. [Translator’s note: The supplied *Dominus solus ... es* mixes nominative “Lord” and second-person “you are”; the address follows the latter.] The Most High does not approve the gifts of the unjust, nor the offerings of the wicked; nor is he appeased for sins by the multitude of sacrifices. Whoever offers a sacrifice from the substance of the poor is like one who slaughters a son in the presence of his father. Whoever takes away bread earned by sweat is like one who kills his neighbor. Whoever sheds blood and whoever defrauds laborers are brothers. One builds while another destroys: what do they gain except labor? One prays and another curses: whose voice will God hear? Whoever is washed after touching a dead person and then touches him again, what benefit is his washing? So it is with one who fasts in his sins and then does the same things again: what benefit is there in humbling himself? Who will hear his prayer? (Chapter XXXV.) Whoever keeps the law multiplies prayer. A saving sacrifice is to attend to the commandments and depart from every iniquity. And an entreaty for sins is to depart from injustice. You will not appear empty before the presence of the Lord. For these things are required because of the commandment of the Lord. The offering of the just makes the altar rich, and it is an odor of sweetness in the presence of the Most High. R. Amen.

Hymn. “Splendor of the Father.” Fol. 67.

Supplication. “Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world.” See fol. 57.

Capitulum. Invoked at the morning hours, be present, true Light-bringer; and you who sprinkle your heavens with splendor, gladden our breasts and hearts, so that, animated by the illumination of faith, we may always adore you as our guide and the prince of light.

Our Father. Delivered from evil. Fol. 2.

Praise. “Sing a new song to the Lord.” Alleluia, [Col. 0243B] alleluia. V. “His praise is in the assembly of the saints.” Alleluia.

Prayer. “To you, O Lord.” Fol. 117. The commemorations as above, fol. 94.

Likewise, at the conclusion of Vespers, everything is to be said as in the first conclusion of Vespers on the first Sunday after the Octave of Epiphany, fol. 94, except the Epistle and Blessing, which follow.

Lord, have mercy. R. Christ, have mercy. Lord, have mercy.

Capitulum. O God, whose radiance is never extinguished and whose brightness never comes to an end, we ask you: while the daily day is brought to an end by the succession of night, may your light always rise upon our senses, and may our inner person be strengthened by the splendor of your visitation, so that we may not be overwhelmed by any darkness of sins.

[Col. 0243C] Our Father. Delivered from evil. Fol. 2.

Blessing. May the Lord, to whom you make supplication, hear your prayers and, in his customary compassion, forgive all your offenses. R. Amen. May the Lord send upon you the gifts of his blessing, and may the giver of mercies graciously pour down showers of compassion. R. Amen. May you prepare a place for him in your hearts in this life through good works, so that, justified, you may reign with Christ forever. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

IN THE SUNDAY BEFORE ASH WEDNESDAY.

Saturday at Vespers.

Praise. “In the nights lift up your hands toward the holy place.” P. “And bless the Lord.” V. “You who stand in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God.” P. “And bless the Lord.”

The Lord be with you. R. And with you.

Chant. “Enter the gates of the Lord with confession, his courts.” P. “With hymns of confession.” Alleluia. V. “Praise his name, for he is sweet; his mercy endures forever, and his truth throughout all ages of ages.” Alleluia. P. “With hymns.”

The Lord be with you. And with you.

Antiphon. “Behold, the watchman cries: Morning has come.” P. “And night.” “You inquire; inquire; turn back; come.” V. “Praise the Lord, children; praise the name of the Lord.” P. “And night.” V. “Glory.” P. “And night.”

The Lord be with you. R. And with your spirit.

Praise. “Do not remember our former iniquities, O God.” [Col. 0244A] Alleluia, alleluia. “May your mercy, O Lord, quickly go before us.” P. “Our iniquities.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “Our iniquities.”

Hymn. “Inventor of the ruddy light.” See fol. 92. Supplication. “Let us pray to the Redeemer.” Fol. 66. Capitulum. “Our defense,” and Blessing. “May the Lord bless you.” Praise. “According to your mercy.” Fol. 121.

At Matins.

Hymn. “Eternal Creator of all things.” Prayer. “Eternal you...” Fol. 3.

Antiphon. “Your salvation, O Lord, and your blessing is upon your people.” Psalm III.

Antiphon. “Blot out my iniquities, O Lord, and have mercy on me.” Psalm L.

Antiphon. “I cry to God Most High, to the Lord [Col. 0244B] who has done good to me.” Psalm LVI.

Antiphon 1. “Convert us, O God our Savior, and turn your anger away from us.” P. “Will you be angry with us forever?” V. “O God, you will turn and give us life, and your people will rejoice in you.” P. “Will you be angry forever?” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “Will you be angry...”

Prayer. Convert us, O God our Savior, and turn your anger away from us. Grant peace to your people, which you proclaim, so that your people may rejoice in you; and, recognizing your salvation as the preservation of salvation, may they know your mercy through prosperity, or receive your kindness through the fruitfulness of abundance. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Antiphon 2. “The Lord is compassionate and merciful, [Col. 0244C] patient and very merciful.” P. “He will not be angry forever, nor will he be indignant forever.” V. “Do not deal with us according to our sins, nor repay us according to our iniquities.” P. “He will not be angry forever.” V. “Glory and honor to the Father.” P. “He will not be angry forever.”

Prayer. O compassionate and merciful Lord, do not be angry with us forever. But as far as the East is from the West, put every iniquity far from us, and, according to the height of heaven above the earth, extend your mercy over us. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 3. “Have mercy, O God, on all, for you can do all things.” P. “And you overlook the sins of men for the sake of repentance.” V. “To you we lift our eyes, who dwell in the heavens.” P. “And you overlook.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “And you overlook.”

Prayer. O God, Lord of mercies, for whose power to will is to accomplish, show your abundant goodness toward us, and remove our footsteps from the height of the most evil way. Grant that, with sound limbs, we may come to you along the paths. R. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

R. All souls trust in you, saying: “Soon God will have mercy on us, because the Lord has spoken, saying: I shall rejoice over one penitent.” P. “More than over ninety-nine righteous people who do not need repentance.” V. “There will be joy in heaven before the angels of God over one sinner doing penance.” P. [Col. 0245A] “More than over ninety-nine.” V. “Glory and honor.” The Responsory is repeated.

At Lauds.

For the Canticle. Antiphon. “You, O Lord, have been called merciful because of sinners; for if you have had mercy on us, you will be called merciful.”

Canticle of Ezra (Book IV, chapter VIII).

O Lord, who dwell forever, * whose eyes are raised and above the air;

Whose throne is beyond estimation, * and whose glory incomprehensible;

Before whom the whole army of angels stands in trembling, * whose watchfulness will be turned into wind and fire.

[Col. 0245B] Whose word is firm, and whose sayings enduring; * 129 whose ordinance is strong, and whose command terrible;

Whose gaze dries up the abysses, * whose indignation makes the mountains waste away, and whose truth bears witness:

Hear, O Lord, the prayer of your servant; * receive with your ears the petition of your creature.

Attend to my words, for while I live I shall speak; * and while I have understanding, I shall answer:

Do not regard, O Lord, the sins of your people; * those who serve you in truth.

Nor heed the pursuits of those who act wickedly, * but heed those who have kept your covenants amid sorrows.

Nor think to destroy those who have behaved falsely in your sight, * but remember those who, of their own will, have come to know your name with fear.

[Col. 0245C] Nor desire to destroy those who have had the habits of beasts; * but look upon those who have taught the law splendidly.

Nor be indignant with those who have been judged worse than beasts; * but love those who have always trusted in your glory.

For we and our fathers have lived by such ways; * but because of us sinners you are called merciful.

For if you desire to have mercy upon us, * then you will be called merciful:

For we do not possess works of righteousness. But the just, for whom many works have been stored up, * will receive their reward from their own works with you, O Lord.

[Col. 0245D] What is a human being, that you should be indignant with him, * or a corruptible race, that you should be so embittered against it?

For in truth, among those born there is no one who has not acted wickedly; * nor among those who confess, anyone who has not sinned against you.

For by this your goodness and your justice, O Lord, will be proclaimed, * when you have had mercy on those who do not possess the substance of good works.

At the Benedictus. Antiphon. Sons of men, bless the Lord of Israel; and all priests, servants of God, bless the Lord.

Canticle. Blessed are you, Lord, God of our fathers. See fol. 6.

Sound. May God have mercy on us and bless us: [Col. 0246A] Alleluia. V. May the Lord illuminate his face upon us. P. And bless us. Alleluia.

Praise. Praise the Lord from the heavens: Alleluia, alleluia. Praise him in the heights. Alleluia, alleluia. Psalm 148.

Reading from the Book of Ecclesiasticus, the Wisdom of Solomon (chapter 2).

R. Thanks be to God.

Those who fear the Lord endure his mercy; and do not turn away from him, lest you fall. You who fear the Lord, believe in him, and your reward will not be emptied. You who fear the Lord, hope in him, and mercy will come to you for your delight. You who fear the Lord, love him, and your hearts will be enlightened. Look upon the generations of the children of men, and know: who has hoped in the Lord and been put to shame? Who has remained in his commandments and been forsaken? And who has called upon him and been despised by him? For God is gracious and merciful, and in the time of tribulation he forgives sins to all who seek him in truth. Woe to the double-hearted, and to deceitful lips, and to the sinner who walks the earth by two ways. Woe to the fainthearted, who will not believe God; therefore they are not protected by him. Woe to those who have lost endurance, who have abandoned straight paths and turned aside into crooked ways. And what will you do when the Lord begins to look upon you? Those who fear the Lord will not be unbelieving toward his word, and those who love him will preserve his way. Those who fear the Lord will seek what pleases him, and those who love him will be filled with his law. Those who fear the Lord will prepare their hearts, and in his sight they will sanctify their souls. R. Amen.

Hymn. *The splendour of the Father’s...* Fol. 67. Supplication. *Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world*. Fol. 66. Short Chapter. *God, author of light*. See fol. 115.

Praise. Be angry, and do not sin: Alleluia. Speak in your hearts. P. And be pricked in your beds. Alleluia, alleluia. V. Offer the sacrifice of righteousness, and hope in the Lord. Many say: Who will show us good things? P. And in your beds. V. Glory. P. And in.

Prayer. To you, O Lord, in. See fol. 117. Commemorations, as above, fol. 94.

## Wednesday. At the Beginning of the Fast.

### At Matins

Antiphon. But you, O Lord, are my protector, my glory, and the one who lifts up my head. Psalm 3.

Prayer. Although a very great multitude of the wicked denies, O Lord, that our salvation is in you, the Lord our God, our strength of hope is nevertheless greatly increased for this reason: you have deigned to be our protector. Therefore let the mouth of those speaking wicked things be stopped, while constant mercy surrounds those who hope in you. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 1. Come, let us adore and fall prostrate before God; and let us weep before the Lord, who made us. V. Let us go before the face of God with confession, and let us rejoice to him with psalms. Psalm 94.

Prayer. Going before your face, O Lord, with confession, and rejoicing to you with fitting melody in the psalms, we adore and fall prostrate before you, entreating you with inward weeping and a sigh: because you made us and you are our God, may you, the gracious Lord, protect us, your people, and as a watchful shepherd tend the sheep of your pasture; and grant grace to those for whom you laid down your life. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Antiphon 2. The Lord is merciful, compassionate, and just. V. A man is gracious who has compassion. Psalm 102.

Prayer. Merciful and just Lord, make us always merciful and wholly ready with every ease to serve one another’s welfare. Do not terrify us with an evil report when you judge us, but set us at your right hand to be glorified. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Antiphon 3. Seek the Lord and be strengthened; seek his face always. Psalm 104.

Prayer. Grant strength, O Lord, to those who seek you, and pour into them a holy love of seeking you continually, so that those who desire to behold your face may not desire the destructive pleasure of the world; nor let the allurements of the age hold them altogether captive, so that the light of your face may make those already blessed shine. R. Amen.

Through your mercy, etc.

R. Have mercy, O Lord, upon your people, because they have sinned against you; and do not remember all their iniquities, but show them mercy. P. And hear those for whom they have called upon you, O Lord. V. Turn, O Lord, for a little while, and take pleasure in your servants. P. And hear them. V. Glory and honor. Let R. be repeated.

### At Lauds

Antiphon. Turn your face away from my sins, and blot out all my iniquities. Psalm 50.

Prayer. Turn your face away from our sins, O Lord, and blot out all our iniquities. Remove from your eyes the crime of our evil pleasures, and mercifully incline your ear to our confession. Have mercy, we ask, upon us who plead with you, who look favorably upon us in adversity and grant a repentant heart to the despairing for confession of your glory. But since the Publican, standing far off and striking his breast, was cleansed by confession alone, hear us sinners likewise, so that just as you granted him the worthy fruits of his petition, so you may deign to grant forgiveness of sins to us, your unworthy servants who implore you. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

At the Canticle. Antiphon. Do not destroy your people, O Lord, and your inheritance, which you have redeemed.

Canticle. Lord, Lord, king of the gods of heaven. See fol. 103.

Matutinarium (morning chant). Antiphon. May God have mercy on us and bless us. P. May he illuminate his face upon us. V. That we may know your way on earth, among all nations, your salvation. P. May he illuminate. V. Glory and honor, etc. P. May he illuminate.

Praise. Praise the Lord in his holy ones. Alleluia, alleluia. Praise the Lord in the firmament of his strength. Alleluia, alleluia. Psalm 150.

Reading from the Book of the Wisdom of Solomon (chapter 12).

R. Thanks be to God.

O God, who grant a place for repentance, grant forgiveness for our sins. For who will say to you, “What have you done?” Or who will stand against your judgment? Or who will come before you as an avenger of unjust men? Or who will charge you if nations perish whom you made? For there is no other God besides you, whose care is for all, so that you may show that you have not judged unjustly. Neither king nor tyrant will inquire in your presence about those whom you have destroyed. Since you are just, you order all things justly; you also condemn the one who deserves to be punished, and regard him as alien to your power. For your power is the beginning of justice; and because you are our Lord, you make yourself merciful to all. You show your power when you are not believed to be perfect in power, but you convict the boldness of those who know it. But you, O ruler and Lord of power, judge sinners with tranquility and govern us with great reverence; for the ability to do so is subject to you whenever you wish. For through such works you taught your people that the righteous person must be humane, and you made your children hopeful, because you grant a place for repentance in sins. For if you punished the enemies of your servants, who deserved death, with such care, and freed them by granting time and a means by which they could be cleansed from wickedness, with what diligence did you judge your children, whose parents you had given oaths and the covenant of your promises? Therefore, when you give us discipline, you scourge our enemies in many ways, so that, judging, we may consider your goodness; and when judgment is passed upon us, we may hope for mercy. R. Amen.

Hymn. *God, fountain of kindness*, etc. Supplication. *Let us pray to the Redeemer*. See fol. 69.

Short Chapter. We are ashamed, O Lord, to call you Father in our words, since we have lost the dignity of sons. But because you save us with paternal affection when you judge us for our own sins, although we are unworthy sons, nevertheless we pour out a prayer to your fatherly compassion, asking that in this time of our affliction you command our sin to be forgiven, so that, even if we cannot invoke you as Father by our merits, at least by the affection of our hearts we may call upon you as Father and say:

Our Father. And lead us not. Deliver us from evil, etc. See fol. 10.

Humble yourselves for the blessing.

May the Lord be always with you. R. And with.

Praise. Be angry, and do not sin: Alleluia. Speak in your hearts, Alleluia. P. And be pricked in your beds. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V. Offer the sacrifice of righteousness; hope in the Lord. Many say: Who will show us good things? P. And in.

Blessing. May almighty God, because through this appointed fast we disclose our crimes, make us free from every offense. R. Amen. May he who receives the prayer of your abstinence never allow you to be separated from his body. R. Amen. Just as his admonition went before you, by which you escaped the sentence of divine judgment, so may mercy follow, by which you may be led to the crown. R. Amen.

Through.

Let the commemorations be said as in fol. 94.

### At Terce

Prophecy. *My son, keep the words*. Fol. 96.

Reading from the Book of Exodus (chapters 19–20).

R. Thanks be to God.

In those days: The Lord called Moses from the mountain and said: “Thus you shall say to the house of Jacob and announce to the children of Israel: You yourselves have seen what I did to the Egyptians, how I carried you on eagles’ wings and took you to myself. Therefore, if you will hear my voice and keep my covenant, you shall be my treasured possession among all peoples, for the whole earth is mine. And you shall be to me a priestly kingdom and a holy nation. These are the words that you shall speak to the children of Israel.”

Moses came and called the elders of the people, and set before them all these words that the Lord had commanded. And all the people answered together: “Everything that the Lord has spoken, we will do.” When Moses had reported the words of the people to the Lord, the Lord said to him: “Now I shall come to you in the darkness of a cloud, so that the people may hear me speaking and believe you forever.” Thus Moses reported the words of the people to the Lord.

And he said to him: “Go to the people and sanctify them today and tomorrow; let them wash their garments and be ready for the third day. On the third day the Lord will descend before all the people upon Mount Sinai. You shall establish a boundary around the people, saying: ‘Beware of going up the mountain or touching its limits. Whoever touches the mountain shall be put to death. No hand shall touch him, but he shall be stoned or pierced with arrows, whether beast or man; he shall not live.’ When the trumpet begins to sound, then let them go up the mountain.”

Moses descended from the mountain to the people and sanctified them. When they had washed their garments, he said to them: “Be ready for the third day, and do not approach your wives.”

Now the third day had come, and morning had dawned. Thunder began to be heard, lightning flashed, and an extremely dense cloud covered the mountain; the sound of the trumpet resounded with increasing force, and the people who were in the camp were afraid. When Moses had led them out from the camp to meet God, they stood at the foot of the mountain. The whole of Mount Sinai was smoking, because the Lord had descended upon it in fire; its smoke rose like smoke from a furnace, and the mountain was terrifying. The sound of the trumpet gradually grew louder and extended further. Moses spoke, and God answered him.

The Lord descended upon Mount Sinai, upon the very summit of the mountain, and called Moses to its peak. When he had ascended, he said to him: “Go down and warn the people, lest perhaps they wish to cross the boundaries to see the Lord, and a very great multitude of them perish. The priests also who approach the Lord must be sanctified, lest he strike them.”

Moses said to the Lord: “The common people cannot ascend Mount Sinai, for you yourself testified and solemnly commanded, saying: ‘Set boundaries around the mountain and sanctify it.’” The Lord said to him: “Go, descend; then you shall ascend, and Aaron with you. But the priests and the people must not cross the boundaries or ascend to the Lord, lest perhaps he kill them.” Moses descended to the people and told them everything.

And the Lord spoke all these words: “I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, from the house of slavery. You shall have no foreign god before me. You shall not make for yourself a carved image, nor any likeness of what is in heaven above, or on the earth below, or in the waters beneath the earth. You shall not adore them or worship them. I am the Lord your God, mighty and jealous, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children to the third and fourth generation of those who hate me, and showing mercy to thousands of those who love me and keep my commandments.

“You shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain, for the Lord will not hold innocent the one who takes the name of the Lord his God in vain. Honor your father and your mother, so that you may live long upon the land that the Lord your God will give you. You shall not kill. You shall not commit adultery. You shall not steal. You shall not speak false witness against your neighbor. You shall not covet your neighbor’s house; nor desire his wife, his servant, his maidservant, his ox, his donkey, or anything that belongs to him.”

All the people heard the voices and the sound of the trumpet, and saw the flashes and the smoking mountain. Terrified and shaken with fear, they stood far away, saying to Moses: “Speak to us yourself, and we will hear; let not the Lord speak to us, lest perhaps we die.” Moses said to the people: “Do not be afraid. God has come to test you, and so that his terror may be among you, so that you may not sin.” R. Amen.

Reading from the Book of the Prophet Isaiah (chapter 58).

R. Thanks be to God.

Thus says the Lord: Cry out; do not cease. Raise your voice like a trumpet, and announce to my people their crimes and to the house of Judah their sins. For day after day they seek me and desire to know my ways, like a nation that has done justice and has not abandoned the judgment of its God. They ask me for judgments of justice; they desire to draw near to God. “Why have we fasted, and you did not look upon us? We humbled our souls, and you did not know?”

Behold, on the day of your fast your pleasure is found, and you demand all your debtors. Behold, you fast for disputes and quarrels, and you strike wickedly with your fist. Do not fast as you have done until this day, so that your cry may be heard on high. Is this the fast that I have chosen: for a person to afflict his soul for a day? Is it to bend his head like a reed and spread sackcloth and ashes? Will you call this a fast and a day acceptable to the Lord?

Is this not rather the fast that I have chosen? Loosen the bonds of wickedness; undo the bundles that oppress; set free those who are crushed, and break every burden. Break your bread for the hungry, and bring the poor and homeless into your house. When you see the naked, cover him, and do not despise your own flesh.

Then your light will break forth like the morning, and your healing will quickly arise; your justice will go before your face, and the glory of the Lord will gather you. Then you will call, and the Lord will hear; you will cry out, and he will say: “Here I am.” If you remove the chain from your midst, and cease extending the finger and speaking what does not profit; if you pour out your soul for the hungry and satisfy the afflicted soul, your light will rise in darkness, and your darkness will be like midday.

The Lord will always give you rest, fill your soul with splendor, and deliver your bones; and you will be like a watered garden and like a spring of waters whose waters do not fail. R. Amen.

The continuation of the Epistle of the Apostle Paul to the Colossians (chapter 2).

R. Thanks be to God.

Brothers: As you received Christ Jesus, walk in him, rooted and built up in him, and strengthened in faith, as you were taught, abounding in thanksgiving. See that no one deceive you through philosophy and empty deceit, according to human tradition, according to the elements of the world, and not according to Christ; for in him the whole fullness of divinity dwells bodily. And you have been filled in him, who is the head of every principality and power. In him you were also circumcised with a circumcision not made by hand, in the stripping away of the body of flesh, in the circumcision of Christ; and you were buried with him in baptism, in which you also rose through faith in the working of God, who raised him from the dead. And when you were dead in offenses and in the uncircumcision of your flesh, he made you alive together with him, forgiving you all offenses. R. Amen.

Antiphon 1. Serve the Lord in fear, and exalt him with trembling. Embrace discipline, lest the Lord become angry and you perish from the right way. V. Why did the nations rage, and the peoples meditate on vain things? Psalm 2.

Prayer. May your discipline, O Lord, join us to you and to holy fear, and may it draw us by fear toward your exultation. Keep us from departing from the right way, and grant that we may be able to trust in you and be blessed. R. Amen. Through your mercy, O God, etc.

Antiphon 2. In our tribulation you have enlarged us, O God. Have mercy on us and hear our prayer. V. When I called upon you, you heard me, O God of my righteousness; in my tribulation you enlarged me. Have mercy on me and hear my prayer. Psalm 4.

Prayer. Since our offenses make you opposed to us, almighty God, may our invocation, inspired by you, we ask, make you favorable, and our confession make you appeased. By your mercy, may worldly tribulation neither cast down our mind, nor harmful persuasion possess it, nor dark unbelief imprison it; but may we shine beneath the marked light of your face, and always walk in that same splendor with the stability of true faith. R. Amen.

Through your mercy, O God, etc.

Antiphon 3. Turn, O Lord, and rescue our souls; save us for the sake of your mercy. For there is no one in death who remembers you. V. O Lord, do not rebuke me in your anger, nor correct me in your wrath. Psalm 6.

R. Rise up, O Lord, have mercy on us, for the time of having mercy has come. The nations will fear your name, and all the kings of the earth your glory. P. Look upon the prayers of the poor, and do not despise their petitions. V. You have set our iniquities before you; all our days have failed, and in your anger we have wasted away. O Lord, be our refuge from evil days. P. Look upon the prayers of the poor. V. Glory and honor to the Father, etc. P. Look upon the prayers of the poor.

Prayers. We ask forgiveness, Christ; hear us. P. Be appeased and have mercy. V. Only-begotten Jesus, Son of God the Father, who are the Lord of immeasurable goodness. P. Be appeased and have mercy. V. We all ask as we plead with sighs; together we all beseech you. P. Be appeased and have mercy. V. May your clemency now overcome our evils; look upon us now with your serene face. P. Be appeased and have mercy. V. We ask forgiveness of all sins; mercifully pardon the evils we have committed. P. Be appeased and have mercy.

Short Chapter. Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy; let the weakness of our sins not bring us death. Heal us, O Lord, so that the soul troubled by guilt may be tranquil through grace. Pour medicine into the sick by granting forgiveness for their offenses. R. Amen.

Our Father. And lead us not.

### At Sext

Reading from the Book of the Prophet Ezekiel (chapter 18).

R. Thanks be to God.

Thus says the Lord: Turn back and repent of all your iniquities, and iniquity will not be your ruin. Cast away from you all your transgressions by which you have transgressed, and make for yourselves a new heart and a right spirit. And why will you die, house of Israel? For I do not desire the death of the one who dies, says the Lord. Return and live.

(Chapter 20.) And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: “Son of man, speak to the elders of Israel, and say to them: Thus says the Lord: Have you come to inquire of me? As I live, says the Lord, I will not answer you. If you judge them—if you judge them, son of man—show them the abominations of their fathers. Walk in my justice, keep my judgments, and perform them, so that there may be a sign between me and you, and it may be known that I am the Lord your God.” R. Amen.

Antiphon 1. The Lord has heard the desire of the poor; your ear will hear the preparation of their heart. To judge the orphan and the humble, P. so that a human being may no longer presume to exalt himself upon the earth. V. Rise up, O Lord my God, and let your hand be exalted; do not forget the poor forever. P. So that a human being may no longer presume. V. Glory and honor. P. So that he may no longer presume. Psalm 9.

[Col. 0253A; p. 134] Prayer. Attend favorably, O Lord, to the desire of your poor, so that you may grant us an abundance of heavenly gifts and turn away from us the love of passing things. May your ear attend to our prayer in such a way that, when you judge the orphan and the humble, you may caress us with paternal indulgence, and in place of present humiliation repay us with eternal joys. R. Amen. Through your mercy, O God, etc.

Antiphon 2. Because of the distress of the needy and the groaning of the poor. P. Now I shall arise, says the Lord. V. The words of the Lord are pure words, silver tested by fire, purified seven times [the printed form *septuptum* is uncertain]. P. Now I shall arise. V. Glory and honor to the Father, etc. P. Now I shall arise. Psalm 11.

Prayer. O God, who resist the proud and destroy the boastful tongue and deceitful lips, grant that we may receive your pure words, tested like silver proved by fire, so that, casting down every swelling of arrogance and exposing the contagion of our condition, we may receive in our condition the splendor of dignity, marked by holiness, and retain it in every way, renewed through you. R. Amen.

Through your mercy, O God, etc.

Antiphon 3. How long, O Lord, will you forget us forever? How long will you turn your face away from us? P. Look upon us and hear us, O Lord our God. V. How long shall I set counsels in my soul, sorrow in my heart by day? How long will my enemy be exalted over me? P. Look upon us and hear us. V. Glory and honor, etc. P. Look upon us. Psalm 12.

R. Hear, O God the Lord, the groaning of your people, and see the distress that we suffer. P. And quickly have mercy. V. You, O Lord, are our Father, our Redeemer; your name is from eternity. Why have you made us wander from your ways? Why have you hardened our heart so that we would not fear you? Turn, O Lord, toward your servants, the tribes of your inheritance. P. And quickly. V. Glory and honor to the Father, etc. Let R. be repeated.

Prayers. Hear us, O Lord, hear us. P. And, having had mercy, grant us forgiveness. V. Most High, maker of heaven and earth, forgive our sin. P. And, having had mercy. V. See, O Lord, the lamentations of your people; pour out abundant rain. P. And, having had mercy. V. Forgive what we confess with groaning, and grant what we ask. P. And, having had mercy. V. Come to the aid of those who now repent, O Christ, and cleanse the prayers of all. P. And, having had mercy.

Short Chapter. *Look upon us and hear us*. Fol. 99.

Prophecy. *My son, have confidence in the Lord*. Fol. 95.

Reading from the Book of Exodus (chapter 23).

R. Thanks be to God.

In those days: The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: “Behold, I shall send my angel, who will go before you, guard you on the way, and bring you to the place that I have prepared for you. Observe him and hear his voice, and do not think him contemptible, for he will not forgive when you sin, and my name is in him. But if you hear his voice and do everything that I speak, I shall be an enemy to your enemies and afflict those who afflict you.

“My angel will go before you and bring you to the Amorite, Hittite, Perizzite, Canaanite, and Jebusite, whom I shall crush. You shall not adore their gods or worship them; you shall not do their works, but you shall destroy them and shatter their statues. You shall serve the Lord your God, and he will bless your bread and your waters, and I shall remove sickness from your midst. Your land shall not be barren or sterile; I shall fulfill the number of your days.

“I shall send my terror ahead of you and kill every people into whose land you enter; I shall make all your enemies turn their backs before you enter. I shall not drive them out from your sight in one year, lest the land become a wilderness and the beasts increase against you. Little by little I shall drive them out from your sight, until you increase and possess the land that the Lord your God will give you.” R. Amen.

Reading from the Book of the Prophet Jeremiah (chapter 4).

R. Thanks be to God.

Thus says the Lord: The whole land shall be desolate, but I will not make a complete end. The earth shall mourn, and the heavens above shall grieve, because I have spoken; I have determined, and I have not repented, nor turned away from it. At the sound of the horseman and the one who shoots the arrow, every city flees. They have entered the difficult places and climbed the rocks; all the cities have been abandoned, and no one lives in them.

But you, devastated one, what will you do? When you clothe yourself in scarlet, when you adorn yourself with a golden ring and paint your eyes with eye-shadow, you adorn yourself in vain. Your lovers have despised you; they seek your life. For I heard a sound like that of a woman in labor, anguish like that of a woman giving birth: the voice of the daughter of Zion, dying and stretching out her hands. “Woe is me, for my soul has failed because of the slain.”

(Chapter 5.) Go around the streets of Jerusalem, look, consider, and seek in its squares whether you can find a man who practices justice and seeks faithfulness, and I will be merciful to him. R. Amen.

[Col. 0254D] The continuation of the Epistle of the blessed Apostle Paul to the Colossians (chapter 3).

R. Thanks be to God.

Brothers: When Christ, your life, appears, then you also will appear with him in glory. Therefore put to death your members that are upon the earth: fornication, impurity, lust, evil desire, and greed, which is the worship of idols. Because of these things the wrath of God comes upon the children of unbelief; among them you also once walked, when you lived in them.

But now put away all these things: anger, indignation, malice, blasphemy, and obscene speech; do not let them issue from your mouth. Do not lie to one another. Strip off the old person with his deeds, and put on the new, the one who is being renewed in knowledge according to the image of the one who created him, where there is no Gentile and Jew, male and female, circumcision and uncircumcision, Barbarian and Scythian, slave and free. R. Amen.

Antiphon 1. You alone understand our sins, O Lord; cleanse us from our sins. P. And spare your servants, O Lord, from those of others. V. The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament proclaims the works of his hands. P. And spare us from those of others. V. Glory and honor to the Father, etc. P. And spare us from those of others. Psalm 18.

Prayer. Cleanse us from our hidden sins. See fol. LXVIII.

Antiphon 2. Send us help from the sanctuary. P. And from Zion protect us, O Lord. V. May the Lord hear you in the day of tribulation; may the name of the God of Jacob protect you. P. And from Zion. V. Glory and honor. P. And from Zion. Psalm 19.

Prayer. Fulfill our petitions, O Lord, and send us help from the sanctuary. Remember all our sacrifice, which we offer to you not only through oblation but also through affliction, so that you may always regard us as humble and contrite before you. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 3. Grant us the desire of our soul, O Lord. P. Go before us with the blessing of sweetness. V. The king will rejoice in your strength, O Lord, and will exult greatly in your salvation. P. Go before us. V. Glory and honor to the Father, etc. P. Go before us. Psalm 20.

Prayers. Have mercy and spare your people, most merciful Lord. P. Because we have sinned against you. V. Prostrate, we pour forth tears, disclosing to you the hidden things we have committed; from you, O God, we ask them. P. Because we have sinned. V. Receive the prayers of the priests, and lavishly grant forgiveness to those who ask it; and have mercy on your people, O Lord. P. Because we have sinned against you. V. You have brought your fury upon us; our dreadful sins have troubled us, and we have failed without any hope. P. Because we have sinned against you. V. Grant remission of sins, and give us an abundance of rain; we call upon you, be present. P. Because we have sinned against you.

Lord, have mercy. R. Christ, have mercy. Lord, have mercy.

Short Chapter. May our soul and our flesh be subjected to you, O Lord of immeasurable power; may our life serve you with complete sincerity. Fulfill the desire of our soul, by which it may reach you; receive the supplication of our lips, lest that adversary secretly steal it away through any devices. Overcome the hidden enemy by your power, go before us with blessing, and lead us through the way of life to everlasting joys.

Our Father. And lead us not. Deliver us from evil, etc. Fol. 10.

Humble yourselves for the blessing.

May the Lord be always with you. R. And with your spirit.

Sermon of our most blessed Father Isidore, Bishop, for putting away meat.

Dearly beloved brothers, I beg and admonish you that on this lawful and most sacred day—apart from Sundays—no one should presume to eat a meal, unless perhaps illness prevents him from fasting. For on other days to fast is either a remedy or a reward; during Lent, not to fast is a sin. At another time, whoever fasts receives indulgence; during Lent, whoever can fast but does not will feel the penalty.

Even he, however, who is unable to fast should have what he is to receive prepared for himself alone, or together with another sick person in his own house. Do not invite those who are able to fast to a meal; for if you do this, both God and human beings may understand that they are not unable to fast because of illness, but that greed prevents them from fasting. Let it be enough for him that he himself is unable to fast. Rather, with groaning, sighing, and anguish of heart, let him grieve over the fact that, while others are fasting, he cannot abstain.

Let whatever is necessary be prepared privately for each sick person, either for him alone or with another similarly sick person. It is not fitting to invite a healthy person to dine with him, lest he increase his own sin through another’s greed. Since he cannot fast, he ought nevertheless to give more generously to the poor, so that the sins he cannot cure by fasting he may redeem by giving alms.

It is good to fast, brothers, but it is better to give alms. If someone can do both, there are two good things; but if he cannot, almsgiving is better. If there is no possibility of fasting, almsgiving is sufficient without fasting; fasting without almsgiving is wholly insufficient. Therefore, if someone cannot fast, let him give alms. Almsgiving without fasting is good. If, then, he is able to fast together with almsgiving, that is a double good; but fasting without almsgiving is no good at all, unless perhaps someone is so poor that he has absolutely nothing to give.

For those who have nothing from which to give, good will is sufficient, according to what is written: “Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace to people of good will.” But who could excuse himself, when the Lord has promised a reward even for a cup of cold water? And why did he say “cold”? Perhaps so that some poor person could not excuse himself on account of a lack of firewood, or say that he had no vessel in which to warm the water.

Finally, through the blessed Prophet, dearly beloved brothers, the Lord so exhorts and admonishes us to give alms that scarcely any poor person can excuse himself. For he says:

“This is the fast that I have chosen, says the Lord: Break your bread for the hungry.”

He does not say that one should give the whole loaf, lest the poor person perhaps have no other; but he says, “Break it”—that is: even if your poverty is so great that you have only one loaf, break off a portion of it and give it to the poor. “And bring the needy and the homeless into your house.”

If someone is so poor that he has no food, let him prepare a little bed for a stranger in one corner of his house; what shall we say, brothers? What excuse can we have, who possess large and spacious houses yet scarcely ever deign to receive a stranger? We do not know—or rather, we do not believe—that Christ is received in every stranger, even though he himself said: “I was a stranger and you did not receive me,” and, “As long as you did not do it for one of the least of these, you did not do it for me.”

It is burdensome and distasteful to us to receive Christ in the poor [Col. 0257A] into our homeland. I fear that he may say to us: “Depart,” and may not receive us into his blessedness. We despise him in this world; I fear that he may despise us in heaven, according to what he himself said: “I was hungry and you did not give me food,” and, “As long as you did not do it for one of the least of these, you did not do it for me,” together with what follows.

Brothers, may God turn this away from us; for afterward he adds these words: “Depart from me, accursed ones; go into the eternal fire.”

I judge no one according to this sentence. Let each person attend to his own sentence. Nor do I accuse or reproach anyone, since perhaps through negligence it has sometimes happened that garments which ought to have gone to the poor have been spoiled by moths. I fear that those very garments may be brought forward as witnesses on the day of judgment, according to what James says: “Come now, you rich; weep and howl over the miseries that are coming upon you. Your riches have rotted.”

And all this, dearly beloved brothers, is as Christ threatens through his Apostle. Although it should not terrify us excessively, we must nevertheless not despair of God’s mercy. If I and my people have been negligent, let us, with God’s help, resolve to amend ourselves while we are able. Let us distribute more generously the alms we have hitherto given sparingly, and let us give with sorrow, groaning, and hope of rest what the Lord’s mercy teaches us to give for past sins.

Therefore, as we have already suggested, dearly beloved brothers, let the richness of almsgiving commend our fasts. For fasting without almsgiving is like a lamp without oil. If a lamp lit without oil can smoke, it cannot give light; so fasting without almsgiving indeed torments the flesh, but does not illumine the soul with the light of charity.

For the present, brothers, let us fast in such a way that we distribute our meals to the poor, so that what we were going to eat may be stored not in our purses but in the bowels of the poor. For the hand of the poor is Christ’s treasury: whatever it receives, lest it perish, it stores in heaven. Although what the poor person receives is consumed, the reward of the good work is nevertheless stored up in heaven.

For if we take pains to spend our meals, with elaborate flavors and multiplied courses, at dinner—so that our bodily delights are not merely undiminished but doubled—then, just as nothing is diminished from the body, nothing is added to the soul.

I admonish you in this, brothers, fearing this rather than believing anything evil about you. For I know that, by God’s favor, many among you continually receive strangers and frequently give to the poor. May what I suggest therefore serve this purpose. Whoever does not do this, or has perhaps done it too slowly, should make this holy and wholly pleasing work his habitual practice.

Although I believe that, through God’s inspiration, whenever the feasts approach, Your Charity observes chastity and charity for many days beforehand, even with your own wives, nevertheless—even though this reminder is superfluous, since I believe you already do it—I urge you to cultivate charity in contemplation, so that throughout Lent and until the end of Easter, with God’s help, you may preserve chastity and charity. Thus, at that most sacred paschal solemnity, you may be clothed in the lamp of charity, whitened by almsgiving, and adorned with prayers, vigils, fasts, and other heavenly and spiritual pearls, not only with friends but also with enemies.

Then, as peacemakers, approaching the Lord’s altar with a free and secure conscience, you may receive his body and blood not for judgment but for healing.

But when we speak of almsgiving, let narrow poverty not be troubled. No one can accomplish everything; when someone has done what he could, the perfect will to do is reckoned as the deed itself. Yet this is fulfilled by the one who chooses to regard a poor person as though he were himself, and gives to the poor what he would wish to be done for himself if he were in such need. Whoever does this has fulfilled the precepts of the Old and New Testaments, fulfilling the Gospel saying: “Whatever you wish people to do to you, do likewise to them.”

For thus the Law and the Prophets are fulfilled, to the glory to which the merciful Lord, by his protection, may lead you through the law of true and perfect charity. Amen.

Through our Lord Jesus Christ, to whom belong honor and dominion without end, forever and ever. Response: Amen.

In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, light with peace. Response: Thanks be to God.

May the Lord be always with you. Response: And with you, etc.

# On the First Sunday of Lent

## At Vespers

Praise. “He alone made the great lights.”  
P. “For his mercy endures forever.”  
V. “The sun to rule the day, the moon and stars to rule the night.”  
P. “For his mercy endures.”

May the Lord be always with you. Response: And with you.

Song. “Turn your face, O Lord, from my sins, and blot out all my iniquities. Alleluia.”  
V. “Have mercy on me, O God, according to your great mercy; and according to the multitude of your mercies, blot out my iniquities. Wash me thoroughly from my injustice, and cleanse me from my sin. Alleluia.”  
V. “I myself know my iniquity, O Lord, and my sin is always before me. Against you alone have I sinned, and I have done evil before you. Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me. Alleluia.”

May the Lord be with you. Response: And with you.

Antiphon. “If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. But if we confess our sins:”  
P. “He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and cleanse us from all iniquity.”  
V. “Come, let us adore and fall down before God; let us weep before the Lord who made us.”  
P. “He is faithful.”  
V. “Glory and honor…”

May the Lord be with you. Response: And with you.

Praise. “I will direct your ways. Alleluia.”  
P. “You shall go forth in joy and depart with gladness. The mountains and hills shall rejoice, awaiting you with glory. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.”  
V. “No evil shall approach you, and no scourge shall draw near your dwelling.”  
P. “You shall go forth in joy.”  
V. “Glory and honor to the Father, etc.”

### Hymn

Utter Alleluia with devout praises;

Heavenly citizens, sing together

The everlasting Alleluia.

You dwellers in perpetual light,

Resound with hymn-bearing choirs

The everlasting Alleluia.

That splendid City of God will receive you,

Resounding with joyful songs, and raising up

The everlasting Alleluia.

Take up joys in a happy return,

Giving the Lord a glorious melody,

The everlasting Alleluia.

Receive now the nourishing glory

Of the starry homeland, victorious,

So that you may sing

The everlasting Alleluia.

There the King’s honor resounds

In illustrious voices, with joyful song,

The everlasting Alleluia.

This is rest for the weary,

This is food, this is drink,

Delighting those who return, overflowing in draughts:

The everlasting Alleluia.

You, Creator, we sing abundantly

With songs of the universe

And with praise:

The everlasting Alleluia.

Almighty glory celebrates you, Christ,

With our voices,

And to you we say:

The everlasting Alleluia.

The everlasting Alleluia.

Amen.

Supplication. Let us beseech with every supplication the Redeemer of the world, our Lord Jesus Christ, that by his grace and through the intercession of holy Mary, his Virgin Mother, he may deign to grant us forgiveness of sins and peace during the holy season of Lent.

Capitula. Alleluia is in heaven and on earth: in heaven it is perpetuated, and on earth it is sung. There it sounds continually; here, faithfully. There, eternally; here, sweetly. There, happily; here, harmoniously. There, ineffably; here, earnestly. There, without syllables; here, with melodies. There, by the Angels; here, by the peoples.

When Christ the Lord was born, the inhabitants of heaven sang his praise and confession not only in heaven [Col. 0259D] but also on earth, announcing, “Glory to God in the highest, and peace on earth to people of good will.” Therefore we ask, Lord, that by praising you we may strive to imitate their ministries and, by our manner of life, deserve their fellowship in blessed life.

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” fol. 2.

Blessing. May the Alleluia, which is sung ineffably in heaven, be declared more effectively in your praises. Response: Amen. And may that which is sung there without interruption by the Angels be here composed at every moment with greater affection by all peoples. Response: Amen. May this same praise, which is called God’s praise and by which he now causes peoples to be initiated into praise, enroll you as companions in the eternal dwelling. Response: Amen.

Praise. “You shall go, Alleluia. You shall have a prosperous journey, Alleluia.”  
P. “And return again to us with joy.” Alleluia.  
V. “For they shall carry you in their hands, lest you ever strike your foot against a stone.”  
P. “And return again.”  
V. “Glory and honor, Psalm 90.”

Kyrie, eleison. Response: Christe, eleison. Kyrie, eleison.

Our Father.

Prayers. Lord of mercies, forget our sins.  
“In the beginning you created heaven and earth.”  
P. “Forget our sins.”  
V. “You made humanity in your image and likeness.”  
P. “Forget them.”  
V. “Among all nations you multiplied peoples from Abraham.”  
P. “Forget them.”

Prayer. Hear our prayer, O Lord, and receive our groans with your ears. For we acknowledge our iniquities and disclose our sins before you. O God, we have sinned against you, and in confessing to you we ask for forgiveness. Because we have departed from your commandments and have scarcely obeyed your law, turn, O Lord, toward your servants whom you redeemed with your blood. Forgive us, we ask, and grant pardon for our sins; deign to bestow upon us the mercy of your goodness. Response: Amen.

## At Matins

Hymn. “Eternal Maker of the universe.” fol. 2.

Prayer. Almighty, eternal, and merciful God, who gives times their times and grants each age the grace by which it is administered: when you come, you burn away the length of darkness and console us through the crowing of the cock. When the herald of day sounds, may meditation on the work of the day revive. Therefore continually look upon us and stir us up, lest, persuaded by the error of deep night, we forget the eternal [reality; the source is elliptical]; but raise us when we fall in darkness and correct us through living rightly, so that with Peter we may repent of our errors and mourn our committed crimes with matching tears. Response: Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon. “Your salvation, O Lord, is upon your people, and your blessing.” Psalm 3.

Another Antiphon. “Blot out my iniquities, O Lord.” Psalm 50.

Antiphon. “I will cry to the Lord, the Most High God, who has done good to me.” Psalm 56.

Prayer. Only-begotten Son of the unbegotten Father, drive bodily sleep away from us; and, merciful and gracious, spare our sins. May the multitude of the redeemed now fill the sacred vigils with devotion and be deemed worthy of your holy sight; and may what the lowly frailty of the flesh now sows rise, by the gift of your divinity, in glory. Therefore, O Lord, bestow abundant help upon all who trust in you, and draw us beneath the shadow of your wings toward our heavenly homeland. Response: Amen.

Through your mercy.

Antiphon 1. “Sons of men: rich and poor together as one.”  
P. “Let us incline our hearts to God, so that we may not fear on the evil day.”  
V. “Hear this, all nations; listen, all you who inhabit the world.”  
P. “Let us incline.”  
V. “Glory and honor to the Father.”  
P. “Let us incline.”

Prayer. May all nations hear you, O Lord, and may rich and poor alike incline the ear of their heart to you. May we neither fear on the evil day nor, having abandoned the honor of faith, be compared with foolish beasts. May our understanding, attaining you alone, seek you, and may it receive eternal rewards while praising you with all the saints in everlasting joy. Response: Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 2. “Hope in God, all the counsel of the peoples.”  
P. “Pour out your hearts before him, for he is our helper.”  
V. “Do not hope in iniquity, and do not desire plunder. If riches increase, do not set your hearts upon them.”  
P. “Pour out before him.”  
V. “Glory and honor to the Father.”  
P. “Pour out before him.”

Prayer. As we pour out our hearts before you in prayer, hear and have mercy, O Lord, who are the hope of all. Bring us into your service, and in your propitious kindness meet those subjected to sin. Make us free from the plunder of iniquity and cause us to seek the ornaments of your riches. Grant that we may know and desire you, and that we may deserve to have God with us throughout all the days and seasons of our life. Response: Amen.

Through your mercy.

Antiphon 3. “Turn us, O God our Savior.”  
P. “And turn your anger away from us, and grant peace to your people. Do not be angry with us forever.”  
V. “O God, when you turn us, you will give us life, and your people will rejoice in you.”  
P. “And turn your anger away.”  
V. “Glory and honor.”  
P. “And turn your anger away.”

Prayer. Turn us, O God our Savior, and turn your anger away from us. Grant peace to your people, which you promise, so that your people may rejoice in you. May they understand your salvation as the guardian of salvation, recognize your mercy in times of prosperity, and receive the fruitfulness of abundance through your kindness. Response: Amen.

Through mercy.

Response: Behold, the days of the great Lord of almsgiving and fasting will come. Be ready to do good to the oppressed, widows, and orphans.  
P. “So that you may receive your reward in the last times,” says the Lord.  
V. “Cease to act perversely; learn to do good. Seek justice; help the oppressed.”  
P. “So that you may receive your reward.”  
V. “Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son.”  
P. “So that you may receive your reward.”

Prayer. O God, who command us to give alms, so that what the torrent of human fallenness soils with the filth of [feet?—uncertain reading] may be covered as though by something extended over it: make us first distribute fitting alms to ourselves, and thus show compassion to those in need, so that we may first spare our own lives and provide ourselves with the pious substance of good works while correcting our ways from evil deeds. Thus, made more worthy through a good conscience, may we enlighten the hearts of our neighbors with instruction and doctrine, and refresh their poverty with the support of grace. Response: Amen.

Through mercy.

## At Lauds

At the Canticle. Antiphon. “Keep in mind the days of the ages; understand the years of generation after generation. Ask your father, and he will tell you; your elders, and they will announce it to you.”

Canticle. “Attend, O Heaven.” fol. 4.

Prayer. Mountains, sing for us, and let the earth hear, as in the wondrous confession of Moses your servant concerning your marvels and commandments. Let the grace of the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, descend upon us like dew upon the earth, like rain upon the grass, and like snow upon the hay. May it cleanse us of impiety there by its imperceptible power, where the multitude of our sins cannot be weighed by any satisfaction.

But you, O Lord, who are the light of the blind, the way of the wandering, and the resurrection of the dead, illumine the darkness of our conscience by the regard of your clemency. Call sinners back to repentance; grant the repentant forgiveness and ever-ready mercy in you. Response: Amen.

Through mercy.

At the Benedictus. Antiphon. “Sons of men, bless the Lord of Israel; and all priests, servants of God, bless the Lord.”

Canticle. “Blessed are you, O Lord, God of our fathers.” fol. 6.

Song. “Do not forget, O God, the voice of those who beseech you. Alleluia.”  
V. “Remember your congregation, which you established from the beginning, the tribe of your inheritance.”

Praise. “Alleluia. Praise the Lord from the heavens. Alleluia. Praise him in the heights. Alleluia.” Psalm 148.

### Reading from the Book of Proverbs of Solomon (Chapter I)

Response: Thanks be to God.

“Sons of men, turn to my correction, and I will pour out my Spirit upon you and show you my words. For I called, and you refused; I stretched out my hand, and there was no one who looked. You despised all my counsel and neglected my rebukes. I also will laugh at your destruction and mock you when what you feared comes upon you. When sudden calamity rushes upon you and destruction comes like a storm; when tribulation and distress come upon you, then they will call upon me, and I will not answer. They will rise early and will not find me, because they hated discipline and did not receive the fear of the Lord; they did not heed my counsel and have despised all my correction. Therefore they shall eat the fruit of their way and be filled with their own counsels.

The turning away of the simple will kill them, and the prosperity of fools will destroy them. But whoever listens to me will rest without fear and enjoy abundance, freed from the dread of evils.”

(Chapter II.) “My son, if you receive my words and store my commandments within you, so that your ear may hear wisdom, incline your heart to understand prudence. For if you call upon wisdom and incline your heart to prudence; if you seek her as money and search her out like treasures, then you will understand the fear of the Lord and find the knowledge of God. For the Lord gives wisdom, and from his mouth proceed knowledge and prudence. He will guard the salvation of the upright and protect those who walk simply, preserving the paths of justice and guarding the way of the holy. Then you will understand justice, judgment, equity, and every good path.” Response: Amen.

Hymn. “Alleluia, with devout praises.” See fol. 137.

Capitula. Alleluia, a name which in its interpretation resounds the praise of God, be the completion of the morning office. Grant also, O God, that while we live we may sing this to you with open mouth, and after our departure, when the end of the world has been accomplished, may sing it to you. Thus, having here been made sweet in its renewal, may we embrace you more abundantly in its harmony after our death.

Our Father. “And do not…”

Praise. “You shall go, Alleluia, on a prosperous journey.” See fol. 138. Blessing. “Alleluia, which is sung ineffably…” fol. 138.

## At the End of Vespers

“In the nights lift up your hands in the holy place, and bless the Lord.”  
V. “You who stand in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God.”

Prayer. In the nights we lift our hands to you, O Lord, so that you may establish us firmly in your Church and, while we are pressed by worldly burdens, grant us to praise you by our deeds. Response: Amen.

Through your mercy.

Song. Antiphon. “In the nights lift up your hands in the holy place, and bless the Lord.”  
P. “May the Lord bless you, he who made heaven and earth.”  
V. “Behold now, bless the Lord, all servants of the Lord.”  
P. “May the Lord bless you.”  
V. “Glory and honor.”  
P. “May he bless.”

Praise. “Remain with us today, and tomorrow you shall depart, Alleluia.”  
P. “And when day has risen, you shall walk on your way.” Alleluia, alleluia.  
V. “May the Lord guard you from every evil; may the Lord guard your soul.”  
P. “And when day has risen.”  
V. “Glory and honor.”  
P. “And when day has risen.”

Hymn. “Alleluia, with devout praises.” See fol. 137.

Capitula. Behold your praise, O God, which is Alleluia: it fills heaven and earth. It is expressed in the ineffable harmony of those above and declared in the offices of those on earth. Therefore we ask, O God, that when our eyes see you in glory on that day, our heart may rejoice over the Alleluia; so that through the devout offering of this praise we may here deserve forgiveness of sins and afterward be led into eternal glory when your face has been revealed to us.

Our Father.

Blessing. May the Alleluia, a holy and joyful name, be spread to the praise of God on the lips of all peoples. Response: Amen. May it be bright among the ranks of believers, glorious as it is displayed in the choirs of Angels. Response: Amen. And may that which shines among the eternal citizens without the clamor of sound bear richer fruit in your hearts through devotion. Response: Amen.

Through mercy.

Praise. “May the good Angel of the Lord accompany you, Alleluia, and prepare every good thing for your journey.”  
P. “And return again to us with joy, Alleluia.”  
V. “May he send you help from the sanctuary and protect you from Zion.”  
P. “And return again.”  
V. “Glory and honor.”  
P. “And return again.” Here the Alleluia is concluded.
