Psalm. “Have mercy on me, O God,” entire, with the Gloria. Then Kyrie, eleison; Christe, eleison; Kyrie, eleison. Our Father, silently.

Prayers. “Turn your anger away from us, O Lord.”  
“Let your power be present with us.”  
P. “Turn your anger away, O Lord.”  
V. “Bless your inheritance, O Lord.”  
P. “Turn your anger away, O Lord.”  
V. “Grant peace to your Church.”  
P. “Turn your anger away from us, O Lord.”

Prayer. “Hear our prayer, O Lord.” fol. 138.

# Monday

## At Matins

Antiphon. “But you, O Lord, are my protector.” Psalm 3.

Prayer. Although a great multitude of evildoers denies, O Lord, that our salvation is in you, the strength of our hope nevertheless increases greatly, because you have deigned to be our protector. Therefore the mouth of those who speak evil is closed when continual mercy surrounds those who hope in you. Response: Amen.

Through…

Antiphon 1. “Our desire is in the law of the Lord, and in his law we meditate day and night.” Psalm 1.

Prayer. O Lord, with whom is the full salvation of justice and the perfection of incorruptible blessedness: grant that we may pass our time meditating on your law day and night, and that we may turn away from the counsel of the ungodly, from the way of sinners, and from the seat of pestilence. Thus, like a fruitful tree nourished by flowing waters, may we be filled with fruits and adorned with grace. Response: Amen.

Through…

Antiphon 2. “Now, kings, understand; be instructed, all you who judge the earth. Serve the Lord in fear.” Psalm 2.

Prayer. May your discipline, O Lord, unite us to you and to holy fear, and may it draw us through fear toward your exultation. Keep us from turning away from the right path, so that we may be blessed. Grant that we may be able to trust in you. Response: Amen.

Through…

Antiphon 3. “Sacrifice the sacrifice of justice, and hope in the Lord.” Psalm 4.

Prayer. Establish us uniquely in your hope, so that we who walk here by faith and not by sight may be brought by hope itself to the reality of the promise. May it sustain our desire through patient expectation and bring it to perfection through charity. Response: Amen.

Through…

Response: Open your eyes, O Lord, and see our misery; incline your ear and hear us, your servants, lest your vineyard perish.  
P. “Which you have deigned to plant.”  
V. “O Lord God of hosts, turn again; now look down from heaven, see, and visit your vineyard.”  
P. “Which you…”  
V. “Glory.” Let it be repeated. Response.

## At Lauds

Antiphon. “Have mercy on me, O God, according to your great mercy.” Psalm 50.

Prayer. Have mercy, O Lord, on the wretched; and because we acknowledge our misery, let us anticipate your mercy. Let the voice of confession therefore be ready and forgiveness near; let the hearing come from your propitiation, so that you may blot out all our sins and grant the strength by which we may perform your commandments. Response: Amen.

Through…

Antiphon. “I will bless you and multiply you like the stars of heaven,” says the Lord God.

Canticle. “Go forth from your land.” fol. 95.

Antiphon. “I will bless you.” Glory and honor to the Father.

Prayer. At your inspiration and call, O Lord, may we abandon and cast off earthly conduct, so that, rejecting carnal vices and renouncing worldly desires and pleasures, we may hasten toward the heavenly promises and receive from you the promised inheritance of the heavenly homeland. Response: Amen.

Through…

At the Benedictus. Antiphon. “In the morning you will hear my voice, O Lord. In the morning I will stand before you and adore you.”  
V. “Give heed to my words, O Lord; understand my cry. Attend to the voice of my prayer, my King and my God. For to you I will pray, O Lord.”

Canticle. “Blessed are you, Lord.” fol. 6.

Praise. “According to the multitude of his greatness, praise the Lord in his holy places. Praise the Lord from the heavens.” Psalm 150.

Reading from the Book of the Wisdom of Solomon. Response: Thanks be to God. “My son, have confidence in the Lord,” etc. See fol. 95.

### Reading from the Book of Genesis (Chapter II)

Response: Thanks be to God.

“In those days the heavens and the earth were completed, and all their adornment. And God completed on the seventh day his work that he had made, and on the seventh day he rested from all the work that he had done. And he blessed the seventh day and sanctified it, because on it he had ceased from all his work that God created in order to make.

“These are the generations of heaven and earth when they were created, on the day when the Lord God made heaven and earth, and every shrub of the field before it arose on the earth, and every plant of the region before it sprouted. For the Lord God had not yet rained upon the earth, and there was no human being to work the ground. But a spring rose from the earth, watering the whole surface of the earth.

“Then the Lord God formed the human being from the clay of the earth, breathed into his face the breath of life, and the human being became a living soul. And the Lord God had planted a paradise of delight from the beginning, in which he placed the human being whom he had formed.

“And the Lord God brought forth from the ground every tree beautiful to see and pleasant to eat, and also the tree of life in the midst of the paradise, and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. And a river went out from the place of delight to water the paradise, and from there it was divided into four heads.

“The name of the first is Pishon; it is the one that circles the whole land of Havilah, where gold is born. The gold of that land is excellent; there too are found bdellium and the onyx stone. The name of the second river is Gihon; it is the one that circles the whole land of Ethiopia. The name of the third river is Tigris; it flows opposite Assyria. The fourth river is the Euphrates.

“So the Lord God took the human being and placed him in the paradise of delight, to work it and guard it. And he commanded him, saying: ‘From every tree of paradise you may eat; but from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil you shall not eat. For on whatever day you eat from it, you shall die the death.’

“And the Lord God said: ‘It is not good for the human being to be alone. Let us make him a helper like himself.’

“Then, after the Lord God had formed from the soil every animal of the earth and every bird of the heavens, he brought them to Adam to see what he would call them. For whatever Adam called a living soul, that was its name. And Adam gave names to all the animals, to all the birds of the heavens, and to all the beasts of the earth. But for Adam no helper like himself was found.

“So the Lord God cast a deep sleep upon Adam. When he had fallen asleep, he took one of his ribs and filled its place with flesh. And the Lord God built the rib that he had taken from Adam into a woman and brought her to Adam.

“And Adam said: ‘This now is bone from my bones and flesh from my flesh. She shall be called woman, because she was taken from man.’

“Therefore a man shall leave his father and mother and cling to his wife, and the two shall be one flesh. Now both were naked, Adam and his wife, and they were not ashamed.

### Chapter III

“Now the serpent was more cunning than all the animals of the earth that the Lord God had made. He said to the woman: ‘Why did God command you not to eat from every tree of paradise?’

“The woman answered him: ‘We eat of the fruit of the trees that are in paradise. But concerning the fruit of the tree that is in the middle of paradise, God commanded us not to eat from it and not to touch it, lest perhaps we die.’

“The serpent said to the woman: ‘You shall certainly not die. For God knows that on whatever day you eat from it, your eyes will be opened, and you will be like gods, knowing good and evil.’

“Therefore the woman saw that the tree was good for eating, beautiful to the eyes, and delightful to behold. She took its fruit and ate; and she gave some to her husband, who ate.

“And the eyes of both were opened. When they realized that they were naked, they sewed fig leaves together and made themselves loincloths. And when they heard the voice of the Lord God walking in the paradise at the afternoon breeze, Adam and his wife hid themselves from the face of the Lord God among the trees of the paradise.

“And the Lord God called Adam and said to him: ‘Adam, where are you?’ He said: ‘I heard your voice, Lord, in the paradise, and I was afraid because I was naked, and I hid myself.’

“He said to him: ‘Who told you that you were naked, unless you have eaten from the tree from which I commanded you not to eat?’

“Adam said: ‘The woman whom you gave as my companion gave me fruit from the tree, and I ate.’

“And the Lord God said to the woman: ‘Why have you done this?’ She answered: ‘The serpent deceived me, and I ate.’

“And the Lord God said to the serpent: ‘Because you have done this, you are accursed among all the animals and beasts of the earth. You shall walk upon your breast, and you shall eat earth all the days of your life. I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed. She shall crush your head, and you shall lie in wait for her heel.’

“To the woman he said: ‘I will multiply your labors and your conceptions. In pain you shall bear children. You shall be under the power of your husband, and he shall rule over you.’

“But to Adam he said: ‘Because you listened to the voice of your wife and ate from the tree concerning which I commanded you not to eat, cursed is the earth in your work. In labor you shall eat from it all the days of your life. It shall produce thorns and thistles for you, and you shall eat the plants of the earth. In the sweat of your face you shall eat bread until you return to the earth from which you were taken; for you are dust, and to dust you shall return.’

“And Adam called his wife’s name Eve, because she was the mother of all the living. The Lord God also made tunics of skins for Adam and his wife and clothed them.

“And he said: ‘Behold, Adam has become like one of us, knowing good and evil. Now, therefore, lest he perhaps stretch out his hand and take also from the tree of life, eat, and live forever…’

“The Lord sent him out from the paradise of delight, to work the earth from which he had been taken. And he expelled Adam and placed before the paradise of delight cherubim and a flaming, turning sword to guard the way to the tree of life.”

Response: Amen.

Hymn. “Author of the shining heavens,” etc. See fol. 96.

Prayers. Let us pray that, in the season of Lent, [the most holy fast may …] us. See the First Vespers of the First Sunday of Lent.

Capitula. Our King and our God, drive from our hearts the night of error and ignorance, so that, renewing us into a new person, you may hear our voices in the morning; make us rise early to serve you in good works; and grant us the mystery of your resurrection, so that we may contemplate you.

Our Father. And…

Lauds. The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom. P. Good understanding belongs to those who practice it. V. His praise endures forever and ever. P. Good understanding. V. Glory and honor to the Father, etc. P. Good understanding.

[Col. 0267D] Prayer. Merciful Lord, you are the beginning of fear and wisdom; instruct us, therefore, in the former and establish us in the latter. Begin us with fear and bring us to completion in the perfection of wisdom. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Another Lauds. Would that, Lord, our ways might be directed to keep your ordinances. V. Then I shall not be put to shame when I regard all your commandments. P. Our ways. V. Glory and honor. P. Our ways.

Prayer. May our ways be directed, Lord, to keep your ordinances; and may we, who strive to search out the secrets of your law, likewise be led to your rewards. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

At Terce.

[Col. 0268A]

Prophecy. My son, do not forget my law. See fol. 40.

Reading from the Book of Genesis (Chapter IV).

R. Thanks be to God.

In those days: Adam knew Eve, his wife. She conceived and gave birth to Cain, saying, “I have acquired a man through the Lord.” Then she gave birth to his brother Abel. Abel was a shepherd, and Cain a farmer. After many days Cain brought an offering to the Lord from the fruits of the earth. Abel also brought from the firstborn of his flock and from their fat portions. And the Lord looked upon Abel and his offerings, but upon Cain and his offerings he did not look. Cain became very angry, and his face fell.

[Col. 0268B] The Lord said to him: “Why are you angry, and why has your face fallen? If you act well, will you not receive acceptance? But if you act badly, sin will immediately be at the door. Its desire will be toward you, but you will rule over it.”

Cain said to his brother Abel, “Let us go outside.” And when they were in the field, Cain rose up against his brother Abel and killed him. The Lord said to Cain, “Where is your brother Abel?” He answered, “I do not know. Am I my brother’s keeper?” He said to him, “What have you done? The voice of your brother’s blood cries out to me from the earth. Therefore you shall be cursed upon the earth, which has opened its mouth and received your brother’s blood from your hand. When you work it, it shall not give you its fruits. You shall be a wanderer and a fugitive upon the earth all the days of your life.”

[Col. 0268C] Cain said to the Lord, “My iniquity is greater than that I should deserve forgiveness. Behold, today you drive me from the face of the earth, and I shall be hidden from your face; I shall be a wanderer and a fugitive on the earth, and everyone who finds me will kill me.”

God said to him, “By no means shall this happen; rather, whoever kills Cain shall be punished sevenfold.” And the Lord placed a mark on Cain, so that no one who found him would kill him. Cain went out from the presence of the Lord and lived as a fugitive in the land east of Eden.

Cain knew his wife, and she conceived and gave birth to Enoch. He built a city and called its name after his son Enoch. Enoch fathered Irad, and Irad fathered Maviael, [Col. 0268D] and Maviael fathered Mathusael, and Mathusael fathered Lamech. He took two wives: the name of one was Ada, and the name of the other Sella. Ada gave birth to Jabel, who was the father of those who dwell in tents and keep livestock. His brother’s name was Jubal; he was the father of those who play the cithara and the organ. Sella also gave birth to Tubalcain, who was a hammerer and craftsman in every work of bronze and iron. Tubalcain’s sister was Noema.

And Lamech said to his wives, Ada and Sella: “Hear my voice, wives of Lamech; listen to my speech. For I have killed a man for my wound, and a young man for my bruise. Sevenfold vengeance shall be taken for Cain, but for Lamech seventy-sevenfold.”

Adam again knew his wife, and she gave birth to a son and called his name [Col. 0269A] Seth, saying: “God has appointed for me another offspring in place of Abel, whom Cain killed.” Seth also had a son, whom he called Enos; he began to call upon the name of the Lord. R. Amen.

Antiphon 1. The Lord hears the desire of the poor. Psalm IX.

Prayer. Raise us, Lord, from the gates of death, so that we may proclaim your praises at the gates of the daughter of Zion. Draw us there, and remove us from here, so that the uplifted movement of our mind may extend itself toward the heavenly will, and the purpose of our conversion may abandon the works of darkness. R. Amen.

Through your mercy, etc.

Antiphon 2. The Lord is just and has loved justice; his face beholds equity. Psalm X.

[Col. 0269B] Prayer. You are just, Lord, and you love justice, and you behold equity. Grant that we may accomplish before your eyes what has pleased you and what will please you, and always complete works worthy of your justice and equity. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Antiphon 3. You, Lord, will preserve us and guard us from this generation and from generation to generation. Psalm XI.

R. Let us turn back to the Lord our God. P. For he is gracious and gentle in forgiving. V. Come, let us rejoice in the Lord; let us acclaim God our salvation. P. For he is gracious. V. Glory and honor to the Father. The R. is repeated.

Prayers. To you we cry out, Lord. P. Have mercy and spare your people. V. Priests, pray; and, kneeling, say: P. Have mercy and spare. V. We have sinned against you alone, and we have done evil before you. P. Have mercy.

V. Acknowledge the evils we have committed; be favorable toward us. P. Have mercy. V. Look now upon the parched earth and grant the rain of grace. P. Have mercy and spare your people.

Hymn to be said on all days of Lent at Terce, Sext, or None during the week.

MONDAY.

Hymn.

O Nazarene, light of Bethlehem, Word of the Father,

whom the Virgin’s womb brought forth in childbirth,

be present with those observing chaste abstinence, O Christ,

and look serenely upon our feast,

while we offer the sacrifice of fasting.

Nothing is surely purer than this mystery,

by which the living heart’s inward fiber is cleansed,

by which uncontrolled entrails are subdued,

lest fat sweating forth its rotten drunkenness

oppress the understanding of the strangled mind.

By this luxury is subdued, and shameful gluttony,

the debased dullness of wine and sleep,

sordid lust, shameless pleasure,

and the various plagues of languid senses

feel the discipline of frugality brought under control.

For if the limbs, properly fasting,

do not restrain themselves from flowing freely into drink and food,

then, through frequent, enervating indulgence,

the noble spark of the mind grows lukewarm,

and the spirit snores dully within the breast.

Amen. Honor, power, etc.

TUESDAY.

At Terce.

Hymn.

Therefore let the desires of the body be curbed,

and let prudence shine forth, cleansed within.

Thus, with keen perception awakened,

the spirit, free and breathing more expansively,

will pray more rightly to the Parent of all things.

Elijah grew in such observance,

the ancient priest, guest of the arid countryside.

They tell how, removed and separated from every tumult,

he despised the frequentation of sins,

enjoying the chaste silence of the Syrtes.

Honor, power.

WEDNESDAY.

At Terce.

Hymn.

But soon, borne into the air on fiery steeds

and carried away in swift flight,

so that the dire world might not breathe upon

the quiet man, renowned of old

for proven fasts, through contagion from nearby filth,

he departed.

Before Moses, the faithful interpreter

of the sevenfold heaven’s majestic throne,

could see its Prince,

the sun, passing through the stars after

four cycles of ten recurring journeys,

had to behold him wholly lacking in substance.

The only food of the one who prayed was tears:

for, weeping through the night,

he watered the dust and pressed his bowed face

against the moist ground,

until, struck by the voice of the speaking God,

he feared the fire unbearable to the eyes.

Honor, power.

THURSDAY.

At Terce.

Hymn.

John, no less powerful in this discipline,

went before the everlasting Son of God.

He straightened the winding paths of the roads,

correcting their crooked deviations,

and gave a straight line to be followed.

This preparation the messenger was making,

constructing a road for God who would soon arrive,

so that the steep places might be changed into level ground,

the broken places into smooth paths,

and Truth, descending upon the earth,

might find nothing crooked.

Honor, power, etc.

FRIDAY.

At Terce.

Hymn.

Born here not according to customary births,

the late-born infant stretched toward his mother’s breasts,

whose withered breast had already forgotten milk.

Nor was he poured forth from the aged womb

until he had proclaimed the Virgin full of God.

Afterward he withdrew into the open solitudes,

clothed in the rough hides of beasts,

or covered with bristles and shaggy fleece,

horrified at being stained and polluted

by the contaminated customs of the towns.

There, devoted to frugal abstinence,

the man of severe discipline rejected

drink and food until late evening,

accustomed to give his body little nourishment

from locusts and the liquor of wild honeycombs.

Honor, power, etc.

SATURDAY.

At Terce.

Hymn.

He was the first exhorter and teacher of the new salvation;

for, in the consecrated river,

the devotion of former times washed away

the marks of ancient errors.

But after the limbs had been cleansed by baptism,

the Spirit flowed in, shining from heaven.

After this washing, with the stain of sins removed,

the reborn went forth as though

a vein of raw gold, smelted again, were shining beautifully;

or as though the light of silver metal

were gleaming brightly after polished cleansing.

Honor, power.

At Sext.

Hymn.

I wish now to recount the lineage of the ancient fast,

handed down in a faithful book,

how, for the inhabitants of the city destined to be destroyed,

the thunderbolt of the merciful Father,

with his fires piously restrained,

spared them.

A people powerful in insolent boasting

once flourished; corrupt wantonness had wickedly dissolved it,

flowing among the common people.

Then, stubborn in brutish contempt,

it neglected the worship of the heavenly God.

At last, offended by the censure

of long-standing indulgence,

he is stirred to just movements;

he arms his right hand with the fire of the sword;

brandishing crashing clouds and violent whirlwinds,

he shakes the thunder-bearing cloud with flames.

But while a brief day for repentance was granted,

in case they might wish to tame and break

their wicked lust and ancient follies,

merciful fear suspended the blow,

and the pronounced sentence paused for a little while.

Honor, power, etc.

TUESDAY.

At Sext.

Hymn.

The gentle Avenger rouses the prophet Jonah

to go as herald of the impending punishment.

But knowing that the threatening judge

preferred to spare rather than strike and chastise,

he secretly turned his flight toward Tarsus.

He climbs aboard a high ship prepared with bridges;

the vessel, fastened by a wet rope, is released.

They travel across the deep; the sea becomes stormy.

Then the cause of so great a danger is sought.

The lot, cast for the fugitive prophet,

falls upon him.

Ordered to perish alone among all,

the guilty man whose crime the rolling lot had revealed,

he is whirled headlong and plunged into the deep.

Then received into a beast’s jaws,

he is swallowed alive in the cavern of its capacious belly.

Honor, power.

146 WEDNESDAY.

At Sext.

Hymn.

The prey, swiftly passed through the empty spaces between the teeth,

evades their blows, flying harmlessly across the bloodless tongue,

lest, held fast by the bite,

the living molars should cut the morsel apart.

It passes through the whole mouth and goes beyond the palate.

For three days and nights

he remained devoured in the beast’s throat.

There he wandered through the hidden recesses of its organs;

breathless, with his inward parts seething,

he traversed the winding chambers of its belly.

Then, untouched, at the turn of the third night,

he is driven out by the hiccups of the vomiting monster,

where the waves break at the murmuring shore

and the gleaming foam beats the salty rocks.

Cast forth, he emerges and marvels that he has been saved.

Honor, power.

THURSDAY.

At Sext.

Hymn.

Compelled, he turns back with hurried step

to the Ninevites.

When he had rebuked them,

laying shameful reproaches upon them as censor,

he declared: “The wrath of the supreme Avenger is coming!

Soon fire will consume the city—believe it!”

Then he seeks the summit of a lofty mountain,

to see from there the gathered smoke

of the ruin and the dreadful heap of destruction.

Covered by the lashes of a many-branched plant,

he suddenly enjoys its sheltering shade.

But when the sorrowful city

had increased the wound of its new grief—

alas, the deepest grief!—it throbs.

Through the broad streets the people and Senate

run together in crowds, every age of citizens:

the young grow pale, and the women wail.

Honor, power.

FRIDAY.

At Sext.

Hymn.

They resolve to appease the wrathful Christ by public fasts; the practice of eating is rejected.

The matron, having removed her necklaces, puts on blue-gray garments; and, instead of jewels and silk, ash sprinkles her flowing hair.

The dark-clad Fathers, their garments ungirded, are dishevelled; the mourning crowd puts on woven haircloth; the maiden, dishevelled in the shaggy hair of beasts, covers her face with a dark veil; and the boy lies upon the sands.

[Col. 0273A] The king himself, Choos,

was stripping off the purple cloak

whose clasp he had torn away,

along with its green gems and sewn stones;

he removed the band that marked his forehead,

and soiled his hair, tangled in filthy dust.

Honor.

SATURDAY.

At Sext.

Hymn.

No one remembered drinking; no one remembered eating;

all the fasting youth had left the tables.

Indeed, the cradles of the wailing little ones were wet with their tears, and the sparing nurse withheld the milk of the breast.

The careful concern of men also shut up the very herds,

lest the wandering animals should touch

the dewy grass with their mouths,

or drink from the murmuring spring;

the empty stalls resounded with lament.

Moved by these and similar things,

God restrains his brief anger,

tempering the oracle and quickly turning it aside.

For ready mercy easily releases

the guilt of supplicant mortals,

and becomes the helper of those who weep.

Honor, power.

MONDAY.

At None.

Hymn.

But why do I speak of the example of an ancient people?

Long ago, when Jesus was weighed down

with frail limbs, he fasted with consecrated heart—

he who had been foretold by the prophetic voice.

Is he Emmanuel, that is, “God with us”?

He who made this naturally soft body,

enslaved beneath the loose yoke of pleasures,

free by the strict law of virtue,

the emancipator of the enslaved creature,

already victorious over the desire that once ruled?

For, secluded in an inhospitable place,

through forty passing days,

he claimed no favor of food,

strengthening by salutary fasting

the vessel weak against desired pleasures.

Honor, power.

TUESDAY.

At None.

Hymn.

The enemy marvels that frail, wasting flesh

can endure and suffer so much labor.

The inquisitor tests by cunning craft

whether God has been received in earthly limbs;

but, rebuked for his fraud, he falls behind.

Let us each follow this according to our strength,

which you, O Christ, consecrated Teacher of doctrine,

gave to your followers:

so that, when the desire to devour has been conquered,

the spirit, the emperor, may triumph widely.

This is what the black envy of the enemy begrudges;

what the governor of the world and the heavens approves;

what makes the altar of the altar acceptable;

what awakens faith in the sleeping heart;

what files down the body’s diseased desire.

Honor, power, etc.

THURSDAY.

At None.

Hymn.

No more surely is flame extinguished by a flood,

nor do snowflakes melt so completely beneath the hot sun,

than the rough harvest of turbid sins

vanishes in the belly, crushed beneath fasting,

if generous giving is always joined to it.

For this too is a great kind of virtue:

to clothe the naked; to feed the needy;

to bring generous aid to those who supplicate;

to establish one and equal share

of the human condition between the powerful and the poor.

Everyone is sufficiently blessed who stretches out his right hand,

greedy for praise but generous with money,

whose left hand does not know the good deed.

Everlasting riches immediately fill him,

and the fruit, yielding interest, enriches him a hundredfold.

Honor, power, fullness of grace

to the everlasting God, the simple Trinity,

whose blessed glory, eternal,

fills the globe and the whole fabric of things,

and holds the kingdom forever through the ages.

Amen.

Supplication. Let us pray that, through the holy fast of Lent, we… fol. 143.

[Col. 0274C] Capitula. Guard us, Lord, from generation to generation; do not let us be swept along with the present age, since we have already clung to your foundation. But arise as the consoler of our miseries, and wipe away our sorrows with an increase of joy.

Our Father. Deliver us from evil. fol. 10. Blessing. See the blessing at None, which is said throughout the year on weekdays.

At Sext.

Reading from the Book of the Prophet Isaiah (Chapter I).

R. Thanks be to God.

Thus says the Lord: “Hear, hear the word of the Lord, princes of Sodom; listen with your ears to the law of your God, people of Gomorrah. What use to me is the multitude of your sacrifices?” says the Lord. “I am full: I do not desire the holocausts of rams, the fat of fattened animals, the blood of calves, lambs, and goats. When you come before my sight, who has required these things from your hands, that you should walk in my courts? Do not offer sacrifice uselessly any longer; incense is an abomination to me. New moons and Sabbaths and other festivals I will not endure; your assemblies are wicked. My soul has hated your new moons; they have become burdensome to me; I am weary of enduring them. When you stretch out your hands, I shall turn my eyes away from you; and when you multiply your prayers, I shall not hear. Your hands are full of blood. Wash yourselves; be clean. Remove the evil of your thoughts from my eyes. Cease to act perversely; learn to do good. Seek judgment; assist the oppressed; judge for the orphan; defend the widow.

[Col. 0275A] “Come, and argue with me,” says the Lord. “Though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be made white as snow; and though they are red like crimson, they shall be white like wool. If you are willing and listen to me, you shall eat the good things of the land,” says the Lord Almighty. R. Amen.

Antiphon 1. When the Lord turns back the captivity of his people, let Jacob rejoice and Israel exult. Psalm XIII.

Prayer. Make us always believe in and invoke your name, Lord, so that we may not feel with the hearts of the foolish, who cry out with faithless voice, “There is no God.” Turn the corruption of their minds toward the truth of the faithful, so that the perversity of unbelievers may not overthrow the faithful; rather, may the faithful win them through the teaching of devotion. May unbelievers reject their abominable sect and, together with the faithful, confess and believe with undivided heart in the essence of the Trinity, so that they may be counted among righteous generations and obtain, with his holy ones, the glory of blessedness. R. Amen.

Antiphon 2. Fill us with joy through your face, Lord. Psalm XV.

148 Prayer. Lord God, the portion of our inheritance rests in your eternity. Therefore we beseech you, Lord: preserve your inheritance according to your customary compassion, and always grant it for healing the cup of suffering which you drank for it. Thus, just as the gifts of redemption are glorious, so may the acquisition of the redeemed be abundant. And may we, who have been redeemed by your cross, be forever your inheritance. Do not leave our soul in hell, but raise it up to live with you forever in incorruption. R. Amen.

Antiphon 3. My strength. Psalm XVII.

R. Have confidence before the Lord, and let your hearts be strengthened. P. In holiness. V. Be perfect; encourage one another; be of one mind; live in peace, and the God of peace will be with you. P. In holiness. V. Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son. The R. is repeated.

Prayers. To you we cry out, Lord. P. We beseech you to hear us. V. Hear the voice of those who supplicate, and grant the remedy of life. P. We beseech you to hear us. V. Remove the causes of sin and make room for forgiveness. P. We beseech you to hear us. V. Give us help that surpasses danger. P. We beseech you to hear us. V. Hear, O God, the tears of widows and orphans. P. We beseech you to hear us.

Hymn. O Nazarene, light of Bethlehem, etc. See fol. 144. Supplication. Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world. fol. 138.

Capitula. Let us always place our refuge, Lord, in your judgment, so that we may neither be dashed against rocks nor overwhelmed by the storms of swelling worldly waves. Rather, in every adversity may we deserve to be protected by the strength of your right hand; may we be taught by your discipline, guided by your teaching, and enlarged through spiritual growth. May we render you, Lord, the service of faith, so that we may deserve to receive from you the crown of glory as our reward.

Our Father. And lead us not…

At None.

From Ecclesiasticus of Solomon (Chapter XVII).

R. Thanks be to God.

My son, God created man from the earth and made him according to his own image. He again returned him to it and clothed him with strength according to himself. He gave him the number of his days and a time, and authority over the things that are upon the earth. He placed his fear over all flesh, and he ruled over winged creatures. From him he created a helper like himself; he gave them counsel, tongue, eyes, ears, and a heart for thinking.

[Col. 0276B] He filled them with discipline and understanding. He created for them knowledge of the spirit; he filled their heart with perception and showed them good and evil. He placed his eye upon their hearts, to show them the greatness of his works, so that they might praise the name of his holiness, glory in his wonders, and recount the greatness of his works. He added discipline to them and handed down to them the law of life. He established an eternal covenant with them and showed them his judgments. R. Amen.

At None.

Reading from the Book of Genesis (Chapter V).

R. Thanks be to God.

This is the book of the generation of Adam. On the day when God created man, he made him in the likeness of God. He created them male and female, and blessed them; and he called their name Adam, on the day when they were created.

Adam lived one hundred and thirty years, and begot a son according to his image and likeness, and called his name Seth. After he begot Seth, the days of Adam were eight hundred years, and he begot sons and daughters. All the time that Adam lived was nine hundred and thirty years, and he died.

Seth also lived one hundred and five years, and begot Enos. After he begot Enos, Seth lived eight hundred and seven years, and begot sons and daughters. All the days of Seth were nine hundred and twelve years, and he died.

Enos lived ninety years, and begot Cainan. After his birth he lived eight hundred and fifteen years, and begot [Col. 0276D] sons and daughters. All the days of Enos were nine hundred and five years, and he died.

Cainan also lived seventy years, and begot Malaleel. After he begot Malaleel, Cainan lived eight hundred and forty years, and begot sons and daughters. All the days of Cainan were nine hundred and ten years, and he died.

Malaleel lived sixty-five years, and begot Jared. After he begot Jared, Malaleel lived eight hundred and thirty years, and begot sons and daughters. All the days of Malaleel were eight hundred and ninety-five years, and he died.

Jared also lived one hundred and sixty-two years, and begot Enoch. After he begot [Col. 0277A] Enoch, Jared lived eight hundred years, and begot sons and daughters. All the days of Jared were nine hundred and sixty-two years, and he died.

Enoch lived sixty-five years, and begot Methuselah. Enoch walked with God. After he begot Methuselah, Enoch lived three hundred years, and begot sons and daughters. All the days of Enoch were three hundred and sixty-five years. He walked with God and then was no longer seen, because God took him.

Methuselah lived one hundred and eighty-seven years, and begot Lamech. After he begot Lamech, Methuselah lived seven hundred and eighty-two years, and begot sons and daughters. All the days of Methuselah were nine hundred and seventy-nine years, and he died.

Lamech lived one hundred and eighty-two years, and begot [Col. 0277B] a son. He called his name Noah, saying: “This one will console us from our works and from the labors of our hands, in the land which the Lord has cursed.” R. Amen.

Antiphon 1. Look upon our defense, our God. Psalm XXI.

Prayer. Graciously look upon our defense, Lord our God; rescue our souls from the sword. Do not let us be nourished by deadly teaching; govern us with your protection. At the same time, deliver us from the mouth of the lion that seeks to snatch us away, and protect us with vigilant attention and watchful care from the faithlessness of the barking dog. R. Amen.

Through.

Antiphon 2. You alone understand transgressions; cleanse us from our sins, Lord. Psalm XVIII.

[Col. 0277C] Prayer. Cleanse us from our hidden faults, Lord, purifying the conscience that is stained by inward and personal blemishes. Also spare your servants from the faults of others, so that you may forgive what we either learn from the examples of the wicked or commit after being enticed by corrupt persuasions. May we, who acknowledge you as our own Lord, no longer experience the dominion of sins. R. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God, etc.

Antiphon 3. Hear us on the day when we call upon you, Lord our God. Psalm XIX.

Hymn. O Nazarene. fol. 144.

Capitula. Fulfill, Lord, all our petitions, and send us help from the holy place. Remember all our sacrifice, which we offer to you not only through offering but also through prayer and affliction, so that you may always make us humble before you and regard us when we are contrite.

Our Father. And lead us not…

May the Lord be always with you. R. And with your spirit.

At Vespers.

Lauds. You enlighten my lamp, Lord.

Antiphon. Save your people, Lord, and bless your inheritance. Psalm XXVII.

Lauds. May our ways be directed, Lord. P. To keep your ordinances. V. Blessed are the undefiled in the way, who walk in the law of the Lord. Glory and honor to the Father. P. To keep your ordinances.

Hymn. Christ, Savior of all the heavens, etc. See fol. 97. Supplication. Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world. See fol. 138.

[Col. 0278A] Capitula. May our fast be a festival before you, Lord, who blot out iniquities and forgive sins. See the sighs of those who confess to you and willingly hear the prayers of all, so that those who serve you in truth may be troubled by no adversity. Remove every evil from our hearts, so that, clinging to your commandments, you may gladden us with your peace.

Our Father.

Blessing. May Jesus the Savior and our God cleanse you, through the purity of abstinence, from every stain of sin. R. Amen. And may he who is the redemption of your souls be the rewarder of your fasts. R. Amen. May eternal glory be granted to you by him through whom you desire to be sanctified by abstinence. R. Amen.

[Col. 0278B] Through.

Lauds. The fear of the Lord is the beginning. fol. 143.

TUESDAY.

At Matins.

With my voice I cried to the Lord, and he heard me from his holy mountain. Psalm III.

Prayer. To you, Lord, we direct the cry of our own voice; we do not strike you with words of loud sound, but with the whole affection of our heart we beg you to be merciful. Hear us, we beseech you, from your holy mountain, Jesus Christ our Lord, whose height raises us, whose strength enlarges us, and whose breadth confirms us. R. Amen.

Through.

Antiphon 1. The Lord will give strength to his people and will bless his people with peace. [Col. 0278C] Psalm XXVIII.

150 Prayer. Give strength, Lord, to your people against all the evils of adversity, and enrich your people with the gift of peace, so that, amid abundant tranquility, all may sing glory to you in your temple and, forgetting the evils of this life, may likewise offer praise and honor continually to your majesty. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Antiphon 2. Mercy will surround those who hope in the Lord. Psalm XXXI.

Prayer. Forgive, Lord, the impiety of our heart, for which every holy person pleads with you at the proper time. Grant us understanding through the support of prayer, which we ask; and instruct us in the way of this life along which we walk. R. Amen.

Through your mercy, etc.

Antiphon 3. Give thanks to the Lord on the cithara; sing psalms to him on the ten-stringed psaltery. Psalm CXXXII.

Prayer. Pour into the inward parts of your servants, Lord, the joy of the righteous that is found in you, so that your praise, which befits the upright, may cleanse every perversity from our senses. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Responsory. Let us turn back to the Lord our God. P. For he is gracious and gentle in forgiving; in the time of tribulation he forgives our sins. V. Come, let us adore and fall down before God, and let us weep before the Lord, who made us. P. [Col. 0279A] For he is gracious. V. Glory, etc. The Responsory is repeated.

At Lauds.

Antiphon. According to your great mercy, blot out my iniquities, Lord. Psalm L.

Prayer. According to the multitude of your mercies, Lord, blot out our iniquities, so that, since these weigh us down, those may raise us up. Do not reject in us a contrite and humbled heart; rather, through the ineffable power of the Trinity, may the Holy Spirit dwell in us, may the right spirit renew us, and may the princely spirit strengthen us. May there be one power of testimony, so that, strengthened by the Father, we may rejoice that we have been brought forth through the Holy Spirit. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

[Col. 0279B] At the Canticle. Antiphon. Let us raise our hearts with tears to the Lord in heaven.

Canticle from Lamentations III.

Why has the living man murmured, * the man for his sins?

Let us examine our ways and seek, * and let us return to the Lord.

Let us raise our hearts with our hands * to the Lord in heaven.

We have acted wickedly and provoked you to anger; * therefore you are inexorable.

You have covered yourself in anger and struck us; * you have killed and shown no mercy.

You have set a cloud before you, * so that prayer may not pass through.

Glory and honor to the Father.

[Col. 0279C] At Benedictus. Antiphon. In your light, O God, we shall see light. V. Show your mercy to those who know you, and your justice to those who are upright in heart.

Canticle. Benedictus. fol. 6.

Lauds. Praise the Lord in his holy places; praise the Lord in the firmament of his strength. Psalm CL.

Reading from the Book of Genesis (Chapter XI).

R. Thanks be to God.

In those days: The earth had one language and the same words. As they journeyed from the east, they found a plain in the land of Shinar and settled there. And one said to his neighbor: “Come, let us make bricks and bake them.” They used [Col. 0279D] bricks for stone and bitumen for mortar, and they said: “Come, let us build ourselves a city and a tower whose summit may reach to heaven; and let us make our name famous before we are divided throughout all the lands.”

But the Lord came down to see the city that the sons of Adam were building, and he said: “Behold, they are one people, and they all have one language. They have begun to do this, and they will not desist from their plans until they complete them in deed. Come, therefore, let us go down and confuse their languages there, so that each one may not understand the voice of his neighbor.”

And so the Lord divided them from that place throughout all the lands, and they ceased building the city. Therefore its name was called Babel, because there the language of the whole earth was confused—and from there the Lord scattered them [Col. 0280A] over the face of all the regions.

These are the generations of Shem: Shem was one hundred years old when he fathered Arphaxad, two years after the flood. Shem lived five hundred years after he fathered Arphaxad, and he fathered sons and daughters.

Arphaxad [151] lived thirty-five years and fathered Shelah. Arphaxad lived three hundred and three years after he fathered Shelah, and he fathered sons and daughters.

Shelah also lived thirty years and fathered Eber. Shelah lived four hundred and three years after he fathered Eber.

Eber lived thirty-four years and fathered Peleg. Eber lived four hundred and thirty years after he fathered Peleg, and he fathered sons and daughters.

Peleg lived thirty years and fathered Reu. Peleg lived two hundred and nine years after he fathered Reu, [Col. 0280B] and he fathered sons and daughters.

Reu lived thirty-five years and fathered Serug. Reu lived two hundred and seven years after he fathered Serug, and he fathered sons and daughters.

Serug lived thirty years and fathered Nahor. Serug lived two hundred years after he fathered Nahor, and he fathered sons and daughters.

Nahor lived twenty-nine years and fathered Terah. Nahor lived one hundred and nineteen years after he fathered Terah, and he fathered sons and daughters.

Terah lived seventy years and fathered Abram, Nahor, and Haran. Haran fathered Lot. Haran died before Terah his father in the land of his birth, in Ur of the Chaldeans.

Abram and Nahor took wives: the name [Col. 0280C] of Abram’s wife was Sarai, and the name of Nahor’s wife was Milcah, daughter of Haran, the father of Milcah and the father of Iscah. Sarai was barren and had no children.

Terah therefore took Abram his son, and Lot, the son of Haran and his grandson, and Sarai his daughter-in-law, the wife of his son Abram, and led them out of Ur of the Chaldeans to go to the land of Canaan. They came as far as Harran and settled there. All the days of Terah were two hundred and five years, and he died in Harran.

*(Chapter XII.)* The Lord said to Abram: “Go forth from your land, from your kindred, and from your father’s house, and come into the land that I shall show you. I will make you into a great nation, and I will bless you and magnify your name, and you shall be blessed. I will bless those who bless you, and I will curse those who curse you; and in you [Col. 0280D] all the families of the earth shall be blessed.”

So Abram departed as the Lord had commanded him, and Lot went with him. Abram was seventy-five years old when he departed from Harran. Abram took Sarai his wife, and Lot his brother’s son, and all the possessions they had acquired, and the persons they had gathered in Harran; and they set out to go to the land of Canaan.

When they had entered it, Abram passed through the land as far as the place of Shechem, to the notable valley. At that time the Canaanite was in the land. God appeared to Abram and said to him: “To your offspring I will give this land.” And he built there an altar to the Lord, who had appeared to him.

Moving on from there to the mountain that lay to the east of Bethel, he pitched his [Col. 0281A] tent there, with Bethel to the west and Ai to the east. He also built an altar to the Lord and invoked his name.

**R.** Amen.

**Hymn.** “God of eternal light, ineffable radiance.” See fol. 98.

**Prayers.** Let us pray that, during the sacred fast of Lent, we may… as above.

**Capitulum.** Lord, with whom is the fountain of life, and in whose light we behold light, nourish within us the splendor of your knowledge, so that, as we thirst, you may grant us life-giving drink; and restore the understanding of heavenly light to our souls when they are in darkness.

**Our Father.**

**Lauda.** “Let us glory, Lord.” **P.** “In your praise.” **V.** “That we may confess your holy name and glory in [Col. 0281B] your praise.” **P.** “In your praise.” **V.** “Glory and honor.” **P.** “In your praise.”

**Prayer.** Save us, Lord our God, and visit us with your salvation. Let not the punishment of our iniquity, but the discipline of your fear, humble us, so that we may glory in your praise and confess in your name. May your goodness also rouse us to see the joy of your chosen ones, and may the inheritance of your kingdom admit us to praise it.

**R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

## At Terce

**Proverbs of Solomon (Chapter V).**

**R.** Thanks be to God.

My son, drink water from your own cistern and streams from your own well. Let your springs flow outward, and distribute your waters in the streets. Keep them for yourself alone, and let no strangers share [Col. 0281C] them with you.

Let your fountain be blessed, and rejoice with the wife of your youth: a most beloved hind and a most gracious fawn. Let her breasts intoxicate you at all times, and delight continually in her love.

Why, my son, are you seduced by a stranger and embraced in the bosom of another? The Lord watches the ways of a man and considers all his steps. His iniquities capture the wicked, and he is bound by the cords [152] of his sins. He himself will die because he did not accept discipline, and he is deceived by the abundance of his folly.

My son, if you have pledged yourself for your friend, you have given your hand to a stranger; you have been entangled by the words of your mouth and trapped by your own speech. Do therefore what I tell you, my son, and free yourself.

**R.** Amen.

**Reading from the Book of Genesis (Chapter XII).**

**R.** Thanks be to God.

[Col. 0281D] In those days: A famine occurred in the land, and Abram went down to Egypt to sojourn there, for the famine had grown severe in the land. When he was near entering Egypt, he said to Sarai his wife: “I know that you are a beautiful woman. When the Egyptians see you, they will say, ‘She is his wife,’ and they will kill me but preserve you. Say, therefore, I beg you, that you are my sister, so that it may go well with me because of you, and my life may be spared on your account.”

When Abram had entered Egypt, the Egyptians saw that the woman was exceedingly beautiful. The princes informed Pharaoh and praised her before him, and the woman was taken into Pharaoh’s house. They treated Abram [Col. 0282A] well because of her, and he acquired sheep, cattle, donkeys, male and female servants, she-donkeys, and camels.

But the Lord struck Pharaoh and his household with very great plagues because of Sarai, Abram’s wife. Pharaoh summoned Abram and said to him: “What have you done to me? Why did you not tell me that she was your wife? Why did you say that she was your sister, so that I took her for my wife? Now, therefore, here is your wife; take her and go.”

Pharaoh gave orders concerning Abram to his men, and they escorted him away, together with his wife and all that he possessed.

*(Chapter XIII.)* Abram therefore went up from Egypt, he and his wife and all that he possessed, and Lot with him, toward the south. He was very rich in silver and gold.

He returned by the way he had come, [Col. 0282B] from the south to Bethel, as far as the place where he had previously pitched his tent, between Bethel and Ai, at the site of the altar he had formerly made. There he invoked the name of the Lord.

Lot also, who was with Abram, had flocks of sheep, herds, and tents. The land could not contain them so that they might dwell together, for their possessions were many, and they could not live together. Hence strife arose between the herdsmen of Abram’s flocks and those of Lot. At that time the Canaanite and the Perizzite were dwelling in the land.

Abram therefore said to Lot: “Please, let there be no quarrel between me and you, nor between my herdsmen and yours, for we are brothers. Behold, the whole land is before you; withdraw from me, I beg you. If you go to the left, I will hold to the right; if you choose the right, [Col. 0282C] I will go to the left.”

Lot, raising his eyes, saw the whole region around the Jordan, which was entirely watered—before the Lord destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah—like the paradise of the Lord and like Egypt as one approaches Zoar. Lot chose for himself the region around the Jordan and departed toward the east. And they separated from one another.

Abram dwelt in the land of Canaan, while Lot stayed in the towns around the Jordan and dwelt in Sodom. The people of Sodom were exceedingly wicked and sinful before the Lord.

The Lord said to Abram, after Lot had separated from him: “Raise your eyes directly and look from the place where you now are, toward the north and the south, the east and the west. All the land that you see [Col. 0282D] I will give to you and to your offspring forever. I will make your offspring like the dust of the earth. If anyone can count the dust of the earth, he will also be able to count your offspring. Rise, walk through the land in its length and breadth, for I will give it to you.”

Abram therefore moved his tent and came to dwell beside the valley of Mamre, which is at Hebron. There he built an altar to the Lord.

**R.** Amen.

**Antiphon 1.** “Our soul waits for the Lord, for he is our helper and protector.” Psalm XXXII.

**Prayer.** To you, Lord, our soul patiently waits; [Col. 0283A] from you it desires to receive both the strength of endurance and its reward. Therefore may your mercy toward us be as we have hoped, and may your accustomed grace go before us.

**R.** Amen.

Through mercy, etc.

**Antiphon 2.** “Magnify the Lord with me, and let us exalt his name together.” Psalm XXXIII.

**Prayer.** Graciously hear those who seek you, Lord; and, so that our soul may praise you, mercifully grant your favor. You are near to those whose hearts are troubled; open your ear [153] to the contrition of our spirit, and turn our bodies and hearts toward your peace, which surpasses all understanding.

**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

[Col. 0283B] **Antiphon 3.** “The children of men hope in the protection of your wings, Lord.” Psalm XXXV.

**R.** May God do good to us and deliver us from every evil. **P.** And grant peace in our days. **V.** May he illumine his face upon us. **P.** And grant it. **V.** Glory. Repeat **R.**

**Prayers.**

Turn away, Lord, the anger of your wrath. **P.** And, taking pity, spare your people.

**V.** Grant a merciful hearing to the prayers of all, and quickly grant in holiness what we ask.

**V.** Christ, look upon our tearful sighs; loose the bonds of death and grant life. **P.** And, taking pity.

**V.** Now see our tears; understand those who mourn; at last, in your mercy, forgive our offenses. **P.** And, taking pity.

**V.** There is none among us whom you willingly hear; for your own sake, Christ, come to our aid. **P.** And, taking pity.

[Col. 0283C] **Hymn.** “To render again what is ancient.” Fol. 145.

**Capitulum.** Lord, do not expose the children of men who hope in the protection of your wings; but, like young birds, nourish us by your fostering care, so that, as chicks, we may be prepared for heavenly flights. Do not allow us to be snatched away and torn apart by the violence of those who lie in wait; nor permit us to fly away from the nest of your Church. Rather, while you shelter us beneath your paternal royal covering, may we come, aided by your help, to the abundance of your house.

**Our Father.**

## At Sext

**Reading from the Book of the Prophet Isaiah (Chapter V).**

**R.** Thanks be to God.

Thus says the Lord: Woe to you who join house to house and add field to field, even to the boundary [Col. 0283D] of the place. Will you alone dwell in the midst of the land?

In my ears are these words, says the Lord of hosts: Unless many houses, great and beautiful, become deserted and without inhabitants. For ten *iugera* (acres) of vineyard will produce one small jar, and thirty measures of seed will produce three measures.

Woe to you who rise early to pursue drunkenness and continue drinking until evening, so that you may burn with wine. Harp, lyre, tambourine, flute, and wine are in your banquets, but you do not regard the work of the Lord, nor consider the works of his hands.

Therefore my people have been led captive because they lacked knowledge; their nobles have perished from hunger, and their multitude has been parched with thirst. Therefore Sheol has enlarged its [Col. 0284A] soul and opened its mouth without limit; and its mighty ones, its people, and its exalted and glorious ones will descend to it.

Man will be bowed down, and the human being humbled, and the eyes of the exalted brought low. But the Lord of hosts will be exalted in judgment, and the holy God will be sanctified in justice.

**R.** Amen.

**Antiphon 1.** “Rise up, Lord; help us and deliver us for the sake of your name.” Psalm XLIII.

**Prayer.** Rise up, Lord, and help us against all the malice of those who persecute us; and deliver us for the sake of your name from the contact of unclean spirits, so that you who humbled us in a place of affliction may again exalt us in the recompense of virtue.

**R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**Antiphon 2.** “We remember your name, God, throughout every [Col. 0284B] generation and progeny.” Psalm XLIV.

**Prayer.** Make us, Lord, love justice and hate iniquity; and as we seek your beauty through its appearance, may your right hand lead us wondrously. When the incentive to fornication has been put to death within us, gird our loins with the sword of chastity.

**R.** Amen. Through your mercy.

**Antiphon 3.** “God is our refuge and strength, a helper in the tribulations that have found us exceedingly.” Psalm XLV.

**R.** Turn your anger away from us, Lord.  
**R.** Do not be angry with us forever.  
**V.** Lessen all your anger, Lord, and turn away from the wrath of your indignation.  
**P.** Not forever.  
**V.** Glory.  
**P.** Not forever.

**Prayers.**

[Col. 0284C] To you we cry, Lord. **P.** We beg you to hear us.

**V.** Christ, Redeemer of all, hear the prayers of your suppliants. **P.** We beg you.

**V.** Grant us the gift of grace and the fruit of repentance. **P.** We beg you.

**V.** Remove from us the sword, famine, and pestilence. **P.** We beg you.

**V.** Release us from the danger of sin and grant forgiveness. **P.** We beg you.

**Hymn.** “O Nazarene, light.” Fol. 144.

**Prayer.** Be our refuge, our God, in adversity, and in the struggles of this world grant us the consolation of your strength. While, at your coming, the earth is troubled and mournful, may those who weep over the deeds they have committed in this age because of fear of judgment [154] be joined to you in joy. Thus may you, Lord of virtues, be with us—the judge whom we fear and the redeemer whom we acknowledge.

**Our Father.**

## At None

[Col. 0284D]

**Reading from the Book of Ecclesiasticus of Solomon (Chapter II).**

**R.** Thanks be to God.

My son, when you approach the service of the Lord, stand in justice and fear, and prepare your soul for temptation. Humble your heart and endure; incline your ear and receive words of understanding; do not hasten into a time of distress. Endure the sustaining acts of God, cling to God, and endure so that your life may increase at the end.

**R.** Amen.

**Reading from the Book of Genesis (Chapter XV).**

**R.** Thanks be to God.

In those days: The word of the Lord came to Abram in a vision, saying: “Do not fear, Abram; I am your protector, [Col. 0285A] and your reward is exceedingly great.”

Abram said: “Lord God, what will you give me? I shall go without children, and the son of the steward of my house is this Eliezer of Damascus.” Abram added: “You have not given me offspring, and behold, my household servant will be my heir.”

Immediately the word of the Lord came to him, saying: “He will not be your heir; but the one who will come forth from your body, he shall be your heir.” He led him outside and said to him: “Look up at heaven and count the stars, if you can.” And he said to him: “So shall your offspring be.”

Abram believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness. And he said to him: “I am the Lord who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldeans, to give you this land and that you might possess it.”

But he said: “Lord God, how can I know [Col. 0285B] that I shall possess it?”

The Lord answered: “Take for me a three-year-old heifer, a three-year-old she-goat, and a three-year-old ram, together with a turtledove and a pigeon.” He took all these, divided them down the middle, and placed the two halves opposite one another; but he did not divide the birds.

Birds descended upon the carcasses, and Abram drove them away. When the sun was setting, a deep sleep fell upon Abram, and a great and dark terror seized him. And it was said to him: “Know beforehand that your offspring will be strangers in a land not their own; they will subject them to slavery and oppress them for four hundred years. Nevertheless, I will judge the nation whom they will serve, and afterward they will depart with great possessions.

“But you will go to your fathers in peace [Col. 0285C] and be buried in a good old age. In the fourth generation they will return here, for the iniquities of the Amorites are not yet complete up to the present time.”

When the sun had set, a dark gloom arose, and behold, a smoking furnace and a flaming torch passed between those divided pieces. On that day the Lord made a covenant with Abram, saying: “To your offspring I will give this land, from the river of Egypt to the great river Euphrates: the Kenites, the Kenizzites, the Kadmonites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Rephaim, the Amorites, the Hivites, the Canaanites, the Girgashites, and the Jebusites.”

*(Chapter XVI.)* Now Sarai, Abram’s wife, had not borne children. [Col. 0285D] But she had an Egyptian maidservant named Hagar, and she said to her husband: “Behold, the Lord has closed me off from bearing children. Go in to my maidservant; perhaps at least through her I may have children.”

When he consented to her request, Sarai took her Egyptian maidservant Hagar, ten years after they had begun to dwell in the land of Canaan, and gave her to her husband as a wife. He went in to her. But when she saw that she had conceived, she despised her mistress.

Sarai said to Abram: “You act unjustly toward me. I gave my maidservant into your bosom, and when she saw that she had conceived, she holds me in contempt. May the Lord judge between me and you.”

Abram answered her: “Behold, your maidservant is in your hand; use her as you wish.” When Sarai afflicted her, she fled.

When the Angel of the Lord found her beside a spring of water in the wilderness, on the road to Shur in the desert, he said to her: “Hagar, maidservant of Sarai, where have you come from, and where are you going?”

She replied: “[Col. 0286A] I am fleeing from the face of Sarai, my mistress.”

The Angel of the Lord said to her: “Return to your mistress and humble yourself under her hand.” And again he said: “I will multiply your offspring exceedingly, and they shall not be counted because of their multitude.”

Then he said: “Behold, you have conceived, and you will bear a son; you shall call his name Ishmael, because the Lord has heard your affliction. He will be a wild man; his hand will be against everyone, and everyone’s hand against him. He will pitch his tents opposite all his brothers.”

Hagar called the name of the Lord who spoke to her. For she said: “Surely here I have seen the back of the one who sees me.” Therefore she called that well “The Well of the Living One Who Sees Me.” It is between Kadesh and Bered.

Hagar bore Abram a son, and Abram called his name Ishmael. Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Ishmael to him. [Col. 0286B]

*(Chapter XVII.)* When he had begun to be ninety-nine years old, God appeared to him and said: “I am God Almighty; walk before me and be perfect. I will establish my covenant between me and you, and I will multiply you exceedingly.”

Abram fell facedown. God said to him: “I am he, and I will establish my covenant with you, and you shall be the father of many nations. No longer shall your name be called Abram, but Abraham, because I have appointed you father of many nations. I will make you increase exceedingly, and I will establish you among nations; kings shall come forth from you.

“I will establish my covenant between me and you and between your offspring after you throughout their [Col. 0286C] generations, by an everlasting covenant, so that I may be your God and the God of your offspring after you. I will give to you and to your offspring after you the land of your sojournings, all the land of Canaan, as an everlasting possession, and I will be their God.”

Again God said to Abraham: “And you, therefore, shall keep my covenant, you and your offspring after you throughout their generations. This is my covenant that you shall observe between me and you, and your offspring after you: Every male among you shall be circumcised. You shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin, and it shall be a sign of the covenant between me and you.

“An infant eight days old shall be circumcised among you; every male throughout your generations, whether born in the household or bought, and even those who are not of your stock, shall be circumcised. My covenant shall be in your flesh as an everlasting covenant.

[Col. 0286D] “Any male whose foreskin has not been circumcised shall be cut off from his people, because he has broken my covenant.”

God also said to Abraham: “You shall not call your wife Sarai ‘Sarai,’ but ‘Sarah.’ I will bless her, and from her I will give you a son. I will bless him, and he shall become nations; kings of peoples shall arise from him.”

Abraham fell on his face and laughed in his heart, saying: “Can a son be born to a hundred-year-old man? And will Sarah, ninety years old, bear?”

And he said to the Lord: “If only Ishmael might live before you!”

The Lord said to Abraham: “Sarah your wife shall bear you a son, and you shall call his name Isaac. I will establish my covenant with him as an everlasting covenant, and with his offspring after him.

“I have also heard you concerning Ishmael. Behold, I will bless him, increase him, and multiply him [Col. 0287A] exceedingly. He shall father twelve princes, and I will make him into a great nation. But I will establish my covenant with Isaac, whom Sarah will bear to you at this time in the following year.”

**R.** Amen.

**Antiphon 1.** “Rich and poor together: hear this, all you who inhabit the world.” Psalm XLVIII.

**Prayer.** May all nations hear you together, Lord; may rich and poor alike incline the ear of their hearts to you. May the hearing of all be prepared there for faith, where the fullness of grace is promised to those who are to be saved.

Through your mercy, God, etc.

**Prayer.** Hear us, God our Savior, and gird us with your strength. While we desire firmness of [Col. 0287B] faith, may we obtain rest in hope and arrive at repose through charity.

# Wednesday

## At Matins

**Antiphon.** “My glory, exalting my [Col. 0288B] head. With my voice I cried to the Lord, and he heard me from his holy mountain.” Psalm III.

**Prayer.** God our glory, grant us to glory in you without end. You have made us exalted through the raising up of our head; we ask that you make us secure through the perfected salvation of the whole body. Let your great majesty lift up our lowliness, so that we who are raised from earthly things by your humility may also deserve to be carried to heavenly things by your exaltation.

**R.** Amen.

Through.

**Antiphon 1.** “Preserve us, Lord, for we hope in you. For you, Lord, are the portion of our inheritance.” Psalm XV.

**Prayer.** Preserve us, Lord, in the fear by which you are loved, and separate us from the contagion of sin, so that, since you have no need of our goods, you may associate us with your [Col. 0288C] gifts.

**R.** Amen.

Through.

**Antiphon 2.** “Seek the Lord, and your soul shall live.” Psalm LXVIII.

**Prayer.** To those who seek you, Lord, grant yourself as the life of our soul. Hear your poor, who are filled not by their own righteousness but by your gift; let them be nourished by your substance and protected by your grace. Do not despise the bound, whose desires sigh for you; whose souls will be present to you; and whose devotion continually pursues what is yours.

**R.** Amen.

Through.

**Antiphon 3.** “Attend to our help, Lord; hasten to help me.” Psalm LXIX.

[Col. 0288D] **Prayer.** Attend to our help, Lord, and hasten to come to our aid. Grant strength to accomplish what we know, and reckon as perfected what we desire, so that, while you complete your commandments in us through your work, you may reckon praise to yourself. May we be exalted in reward through the outcome of your work; may the uprightness of our work magnify you; may your recompense raise us up.

**R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**R.** Wash yourselves, be clean; remove the evil of your thoughts from my eyes. Cease to act perversely; learn to do good; seek judgment; assist the oppressed; judge the orphan; defend the widow.

**P.** “If you are willing and listen, you shall eat the good things of the land,” says the Lord.

**V.** If your sins are like scarlet, they shall be made white as snow; and if they are red [Col. 0289A] like the worm, they shall become like wool. **P.** If you are willing.

**V.** Glory. Repeat **R.** “Wash yourselves.”

## At Lauds

**Antiphon.** “Have mercy on me, God, according to your great mercy, and according to the multitude of your mercies, Lord, blot out my iniquities.” Psalm L.

**Prayer.** “Have mercy, Lord.” Fol. 141.

**Canticle of Esther XIII**

[Col. 0289B] Lord God, almighty King, * all things are placed under your dominion,

and there is none who can resist your will, * if you have decreed to save Israel.

You made heaven and earth, * and whatever is contained within heaven’s circuit.

For you are Lord of all, * and there is none who can resist your majesty.

And now, Lord God of Abraham, have mercy on your people, * and do not despise your portion, [157] which you redeemed from Egypt.

Hear my supplication, and be gracious to your lot and your measuring-line, * and turn our mourning into joy,
