**For the Benedictus. Antiphon.** “May God have mercy on us and bless us; may the Lord illumine his face [Col. 0289C] upon us.” **V.** “That we may know your way on earth, your salvation among all nations.”

**Canticle.** “Blessed are you.”

**Lauda.** “Mountains and all hills, fruit-bearing trees and all cedars, praise the Lord.” Psalm CXLVIII.

**Reading from the Book of Genesis (Chapter XVIII).**

**R.** Thanks be to God.

In those days: God appeared to Abraham in the valley of Mamre, as he sat at the entrance of his tent in the heat of the day. When he had raised his eyes, three men appeared to him standing near him. When he saw them, he ran to meet them from the entrance of his tent and bowed to the ground.

And he said: “Lord, if I have found favor in your eyes, do not pass by your servant. But let a little water [Col. 0289D] be brought, and wash your feet, and rest beneath the tree. I will set out a morsel of bread, and strengthen your hearts; afterward you may pass on, since you have turned aside to your servant.”

They said: “Do as you have spoken.”

Abraham hastened into the tent to Sarah and said to her: “Quickly, mix three measures of fine flour and make cakes.” He himself ran to the herd and took a tender and excellent calf, gave it to the servant, who hastened to cook it. He also took butter and milk and the calf he had prepared and set them before them, while he himself stood beside them under the tree.

When they had eaten, they said to him: “Where is Sarah your wife?”

He answered: “Behold, she is in the tent.”

And he said: “I will return to you at this time, life accompanying me, and [Col. 0290A] Sarah your wife shall have a son.”

When she heard this, Sarah laughed behind the door of the tent. They were both old and advanced in age, and Sarah had ceased to experience the condition of women. She laughed secretly, saying: “After I have grown old, and my lord is an old man, shall I give myself to pleasure?”

The Lord said to Abraham: “Why did Sarah your wife laugh, saying: ‘Shall I really bear a child, an old woman that I am?’ Is anything difficult for God? At the appointed time I will return to you, at this same time, life accompanying me, and Sarah shall have a son.”

Sarah denied it, saying: “I did not laugh,” because she was terrified. But the Lord said: “It is not so; you did laugh.”

When the men had risen from there, they directed their eyes toward Sodom, and Abraham went with them, escorting them. The Lord said: “Can I hide from Abraham what I am about to do, since he is to become a great and very powerful nation, and all the nations of the earth are [Col. 0290B] to be blessed in him?

“For I know that he will command his sons and his household after him to keep the way of the Lord and to practice judgment and justice, so that the Lord may bring upon Abraham all that he has spoken to him.”

The Lord therefore said: “The outcry of Sodom and Gomorrah has multiplied, and their sin has become exceedingly grave. I will go down and see whether they have completed in deed the outcry that has come to me, or whether it is not so, that I may know.”

They turned from there and went toward Sodom, but Abraham still stood before the Lord. Approaching, he said: “Will you destroy the just with the wicked? If there are fifty just people in the [Col. 0290C] city, will they perish together? Will you not spare that place for the sake of the fifty just, if they are in it?

“Far be it from you to do such a thing, to kill the just with the wicked, so that the just should be treated like the wicked. This is not fitting for you. Will the judge of all the earth not execute judgment?”

The Lord said to him: “If I find fifty just people in Sodom, in the midst of the city, I will spare the whole place for their sake.”

Abraham answered: “Since I have once begun, I will speak to my Lord, although I am dust and ashes. What if there are five fewer than fifty just? Will you destroy the whole city because of forty-five?”

He said: “I will not destroy it if I find forty-five there.”

Again he spoke to him: “But if forty are found there, what will you do?”

He said: “I will not strike it for the sake of forty.”

“Please,” he said, “do not be angry, Lord, if I speak. What if thirty are found there?”

He answered: “I will not do it if I find thirty there.”

“Since I have once begun,” he said, “I will speak to my Lord. What if twenty are found there?”

He said: “I will not destroy it for the sake of twenty.”

“Please,” he said, “do not be angry, Lord, if I speak once more. What if ten are found [158] [Col. 0290D] there?”

He said: “I will not destroy it for the sake of ten.”

The Lord departed after he had ceased speaking to Abraham, and he returned to his place.

**R.** Amen.

**Hymn.** “Unbegotten God the Father.” See fol. 101.

**Supplication.** Let us pray that, during the sacred fast of Lent, we may…

**Capitulum.** “Illumine your face, Lord.” Fol. 26.

**Our Father.** “Deliver us from evil,” etc. Fol. 10.

**Lauda.** “From our sins.” **P.** “Cleanse us, Lord.”

**V.** “And spare your servants [Col. 0291A] from those of others.” **P.** “Cleanse us.”

**V.** “Glory and honor,” etc. **P.** “Cleanse us.”

**Prayer.** Cleanse us from our hidden sins, Lord, purifying the conscience that is stained by inward and personal blemishes. Also spare your servants from the sins of others, so that you may forgive the things we either learn from the examples of the wicked or commit after being enticed by perverse persuasions. May we who acknowledge you as our own Lord no longer experience the domination of sins.

**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

## At Terce

**Proverbs of Solomon (Chapter X).**

**R.** Thanks be to God.

The wise son gladdens his father; but the foolish son is the sorrow of his mother. Treasures of wickedness will profit nothing, but righteousness will deliver from death. The Lord will not afflict the soul of the righteous with hunger, and he will overthrow the plots of the wicked. Slackness of hand produces poverty, but the hand of the strong prepares riches. Whoever relies on lies feeds the winds; that same person pursues flying birds. Whoever gathers during the harvest is a wise son; but whoever sleeps through the summer is a son of disgrace. The Lord’s blessing is upon the head of the righteous, but the mouth of the wicked conceals iniquity. The memory of the righteous is accompanied by praise, but the name of the wicked will rot. The wise in heart will receive commandments, but the fool is struck down by his lips. Whoever walks straightforwardly walks confidently, but whoever perverts his ways will be exposed. Whoever winks with the eye causes pain, and the fool will be beaten by his lips. The mouth of the righteous is a vein of life, but the mouth of the wicked conceals iniquity. Hatred stirs up quarrels, but charity covers all offenses. **R.** Amen.

### Reading from the Book of Genesis (Chapter 19)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

In those days, two Angels came to Sodom in the evening, while Lot was sitting at the city gate. When he saw them, he rose and went to meet them; and he bowed with his face to the ground and said: “I beg you, my lords, turn aside into the house of your servant and stay there; wash your feet, and in the morning you shall go on your way.” They said: “Not at all; we shall stay in the street.” He pressed them very strongly to turn aside to him. When they had entered his house, he prepared a feast for them and baked unleavened bread, and they ate.

But before they went to bed, the men of the city besieged the house, from boy to old man—all the people together. They called Lot and said to him: “Where are the men who came in to you during the night? Bring them out to us, so that we may know them.” Lot went out to them, closing the door behind him, and said: “Do not, I beg you, my brothers; do not commit this evil. I have two daughters who have not yet known a man. I shall bring them out to you, and you may abuse them as you please, provided that you do nothing evil to these men, because they have entered under the shadow of my roof.”

But they said: “Go away from there.” And again they said: “You came in as a stranger; are you now going to act as a judge? We shall therefore afflict you more than them.” And they pressed violently against Lot, and were already close to breaking down the doors. And behold, the men reached out their hands, drew Lot inside to them, and shut the door. They struck those who were outside with blindness, from the least to the greatest, so that they could not find the door.

Then they said to Lot: “Do you have anyone of your own here—a son-in-law, or sons, or daughters? Bring out all who belong to you from this city, for we are about to destroy this place, because their outcry has grown great before the Lord, who sent us to destroy them.” So Lot went out and spoke to his sons-in-law, who were to receive his daughters, and said: “Rise, leave this place, because the Lord is about to destroy this city.” But he appeared to them to be speaking in jest.

When morning came, the Angels urged him, saying: “Rise, take your wife and your two daughters whom you have, lest you too perish in the wickedness of the city.” Since he delayed, they took him by the hand, and his wife and his two daughters by the hand, because the Lord spared him. They led him out and placed him beyond the city. There they spoke to him, saying: “Save your life. Do not look back, and do not remain anywhere in the surrounding region; but save yourself on the mountain, lest you too perish.”

Lot said to them: “I beg you, my lord, because your servant has found favor before you, and you have magnified your glory and the mercy you have shown me by saving my life. I cannot be saved on the mountain, lest evil overtake me and I die. There is a city nearby to which I can flee; it is small, and I shall be saved there. Is it not small, and shall my life not live?” He said to him: “Behold, I have also granted your request in this matter, so that I will not overthrow the city about which you have spoken. Hurry and save yourself there, because I cannot do anything until you enter it.” Therefore that city was called Segor.

The sun had risen over the land, and Lot entered Segor. Then the Lord rained upon Sodom and Gomorrah sulfur and fire from the Lord out of heaven; and he overthrew those cities and the whole surrounding region, all the inhabitants of the cities, and everything green that grew from the earth. His wife looked behind her and was turned into a statue of salt.

Abraham, rising early, went to the place where he had previously stood with the Lord. He looked toward Sodom and Gomorrah and the whole land of that region, and saw smoke rising from the earth like the smoke of a furnace. When God overthrew the cities of that region, he remembered Abraham and rescued Lot from the destruction of the cities in which he had lived. **R.** Amen.

## At Sext

### Reading from the Book of the Prophet Isaiah (Chapter 5)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

Thus says the Lord: Woe to those who drag iniquity with cords of vanity and sin as though with a cart rope. Those who say: “Let him hurry and quickly bring about his work, so that we may see; let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel draw near and come, so that we may know it.” Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, who put darkness for light and light for darkness, who put bitter for sweet and sweet for bitter.

Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes and prudent in their own sight. Woe to those who are mighty at drinking wine and strong men at mixing drunkenness. They justify the wicked for gifts and take away the justice of the righteous from him.

Therefore, just as a tongue of fire devours straw and the heat of the flame consumes it, so their root will be like embers, and their shoot will rise like dust. For they have rejected the law of the Lord of hosts and blasphemed the word of the Holy One of Israel.

Therefore the anger of the Lord has burned against his peoples; he has stretched out his hand over them and struck them. The mountains were shaken, and their corpses became like dung in the middle of the streets. In all this the anger of the Lord has not turned away, but his hand is still extended.

He will raise a signal among distant nations and whistle to it from the ends of the earth; and behold, it will come swiftly and speedily. There is no one failing or growing weary among them; he will not slumber or sleep. The belt of his loins will not come loose, and the strap of his sandals will not break. **R.** Amen.

### Antiphon 1

Have mercy, therefore, on us, Lord—have mercy—and spare our sins, for which we fear you. Look upon our contempt with kindly compassion, and by the right hand of your power rescue us from the disgrace of sin. **R.** Amen.

And lest the burden of sin press down our back, place upon our shoulders the gentle burdens of the evangelical commandments, through which you may destroy the structure of sin and build us up, by the sacred joints, in the merits of virtues. **R.** Amen.

### Antiphon 2

### Antiphon

Turn your face away from our sins, and blot out all our iniquities. **Psalm 50.**

### Prayer

Turn your face away from our sins, Lord, and blot out all our iniquities. Remove from your eyes the crime of our evil pleasures, and mercifully apply your hearing to our confession. Have mercy, we ask, on us who plead with you—you who look favorably upon those in adversity, who grant a repentant heart to the despairing, and your grace to our confessions.

But because the tax collector, standing far away and beating his breast, was cleansed by confession alone, hear us sinners in the same way, so that, just as you granted him the fruit of his petition according to his merit, you may likewise deign to grant forgiveness of sins to us, your unworthy servants, as we entreat you. **R.** Amen.

May God give you dew from heaven and the fatness of the earth, abundance of grain, wine, and oil; and may peoples serve you and tribes worship you.

### Reading from the Book of Genesis (Chapter 20)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

In those days, Abraham departed for the southern land and dwelt between Cades and Sur; he sojourned in Gerara. He said of Sarah his wife: “She is my sister.” Therefore Abimelech, king of Gerara, sent for her and took her.

But God came to Abimelech in a dream at night and said to him: “Behold, you shall die because of the woman whom you have taken, for she has a husband.” Abimelech, however, had not touched her, and he said: “Lord, will you destroy an ignorant and righteous nation? Did he himself not say, ‘She is my sister’? In the simplicity of my heart and the cleanness of my hands I have done this.”

God said to him: “I know that you acted with a simple heart, and therefore I guarded you so that you would not sin against me, and I did not permit you to touch her. Now therefore return the wife to her husband, because he is a prophet; he will pray for you, and you will live. But if you are unwilling to return her, know that you shall die, you and all that is yours.”

Immediately Abimelech rose during the night and called all his servants. He spoke all these words in their hearing, and all the men were greatly afraid. Abimelech also called Abraham and said to him: “What have you done to us? In what have we sinned against you, that you have brought such great sin upon me and upon my kingdom? You have done to us what you ought not to have done.” And again, reproaching him, he said: “What did you see, that you did this?”

Abraham answered: “I thought to myself, saying: ‘Perhaps there is no fear of God in this place, and they will kill me because of my wife.’ Besides, she is truly my sister, the daughter of my father but not the daughter of my mother, and I took her as my wife. After God led me out of my father’s house, I said to her: ‘You shall show me this kindness: in every place into which we enter, say that I am your brother.’”

Then Abimelech took sheep and oxen, male and female slaves, and gave them to Abraham. He restored Sarah his wife to him and said: “The land is before you; dwell wherever it pleases you.”

To Sarah he said: “Behold, I have given a thousand pieces of silver to your brother; this shall be a covering for your eyes and for all who are with you, and wherever you go, remember that you were exposed.”

When Abraham prayed, God healed Abimelech, his wife, and his female slaves, and they bore children, for God had closed every womb of Abimelech’s household because of Sarah, Abraham’s wife.

### Chapter 21

The Lord visited Sarah as he had promised, and fulfilled what he had spoken. She conceived and bore a son in her old age, at the time that God had foretold. Abraham called the name of his son, whom Sarah bore to him, Isaac, and he circumcised him on the eighth day, as God had commanded him, when he was one hundred years old. For Isaac was born at this age of his father.

Sarah said: “God has made laughter for me; whoever hears of it will laugh with me.” And again she said: “Who would have believed Abraham that Sarah would nurse a son, whom she bore to him in his old age?”

The child grew and was weaned. Abraham held a great feast on the day of his weaning. When Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian playing with her son Isaac, she said to Abraham: “Cast out this slave woman and her son, for the son of the slave woman shall not be heir with my son Isaac.” Abraham took this very hard because of his son.

God said to him: “Do not let this seem harsh to you concerning the boy and concerning your slave woman. Listen to everything Sarah says to you, because in Isaac your offspring shall be called. But I shall also make the son of the slave woman into a great nation, because he is your offspring.”

So Abraham rose early, took bread and a skin of water, placed them on her shoulder, handed over the child, and sent her away. When she had departed, she wandered in the wilderness of Bersabee. When the water in the skin had been used up, she cast the child under one of the trees that was there. She went away and sat opposite him as far as a bowshot, for she said: “I shall not see the child die.” And sitting opposite him, she raised her voice and wept.

God heard the voice of the child. The Angel of the Lord called Hagar from heaven, saying: “What are you doing, Hagar? Do not be afraid, for God has heard the voice of the child from the place where he is. Rise, take the child, and hold him by the hand, because I shall make him into a great nation.”

God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water. She went and filled the skin and gave the child a drink. God was with him; he grew and dwelt in the wilderness, becoming a young archer. He lived in the desert of Pharan, and his mother took a wife for him from the land of Egypt.

At that same time Abimelech and Phicol, the commander of his army, said to Abraham: “God is with you in everything you do. Swear therefore by the Lord that you will not harm me, my descendants, or my offspring; but according to the mercy that I have shown you, you shall deal with me and with the land in which you have lived as a foreigner.”

Abraham said: “I shall swear.” And he reproached Abimelech concerning the well of water which his servants had seized by force. Abimelech answered: “I did not know who had done this thing; you did not tell me, and I did not hear of it until today.”

Then Abraham took sheep and oxen and gave them to Abimelech, and the two of them made a covenant. Abraham set apart seven ewe lambs of the flock. Abimelech said to him: “What do these seven ewe lambs mean, which you have set apart?” He answered: “You shall receive seven ewe lambs from my hand, so that they may be a testimony for me that I dug this well.”

Therefore that place was called Bersabee, because there the two of them swore an oath. And they made a covenant over the well of the oath. Then Abimelech and Phicol, the commander of his army, rose and returned to the land of the Philistines.

But Abraham planted a grove at Bersabee and there called upon the name of the eternal God. **R.** Amen.

## Order for Terce

### From the Proverbs of Solomon (Chapter 19)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

My son, a false witness will not go unpunished, and whoever speaks lies will perish; he will not escape. Many court the favor of the powerful and are friends of the one who gives gifts. The brothers of a poor man hate him; indeed, his friends have withdrawn far from him.

Whoever pursues only words will have nothing; but whoever possesses understanding loves his own soul, and whoever guards prudence will find good things. A false witness will not go unpunished, and whoever speaks a lie will perish. Pleasures do not suit a fool, nor does it suit a slave to rule over princes.

A man’s understanding is known through patience, and it is his glory to pass over wrongdoing. As the roaring of a lion is the king’s anger, so his cheerfulness is like dew upon grass. A foolish son is the father’s grief, and a quarrelsome woman is like a roof continually dripping.

House and riches are inherited from fathers, but a prudent wife is from the Lord. Laziness brings sleep, and a careless soul will hunger. Whoever keeps the commandment keeps his soul, but whoever neglects his ways will die.

Whoever has mercy on the poor lends to the Lord, and he will repay him for his deed. Discipline your son; do not despair, and do not set your soul on his destruction. Whoever is impatient will suffer loss, and when he has seized something, he will add another thing to it.

Listen to counsel and accept discipline, so that you may be wise in your latter days. There are many thoughts in a man’s heart, but the will of the Lord will remain. **R.** Amen.

### Reading from the Book of Genesis (Chapter 24)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

In those days Abraham was old and advanced in years, and the Lord had blessed him in all things. He said to the older servant of his household, who was in charge of everything he possessed: “Place your hand under my thigh, so that I may bind you by an oath to the Lord, the God of heaven and earth, that you will not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I dwell; but that you will go to my land and my kindred and take a wife from there for my son Isaac.”

The servant answered: “If the woman is unwilling to come with me into this land, must I take your son back to the place from which you came?” Abraham said: “Beware that you never take my son back there. The Lord God of heaven, who took me from my father’s house and from the land of my birth, who spoke to me and swore, saying, ‘To your offspring I shall give this land’—he himself will send his Angel before you, and you will take a wife for my son from there. But if the woman is unwilling to follow you, you will not be bound by the oath; only do not take my son back there.”

Therefore the servant placed his hand under the thigh of Abraham his master and swore to him concerning this matter. Then he took ten camels from his master’s herd and departed, carrying with him goods of every kind belonging to his master. He went to Mesopotamia, to the city of Nahor.

When he had made the camels kneel outside the town near the well of water, in the evening, at the time when women customarily go out to draw water, he prayed to the Lord, saying: “Lord God of my master Abraham, meet me, I beg you, today, and show mercy to my master Abraham. Behold, I stand near the spring of water, and the daughters of the inhabitants of this city will come out to draw water. Let the girl to whom I say, ‘Incline your jar so that I may drink,’ and who answers, ‘Drink, and I shall also give your camels water,’ be the one whom you have prepared for your servant Isaac; and by this I shall know that you have shown mercy to my master Abraham.”

Before he had finished speaking within himself, behold, Rebecca came out, the daughter of Bathuel, son of Melcha, wife of Nahor, Abraham’s brother. She had a jar on her shoulder; she was exceedingly beautiful, a virgin and unknown to a man. She had gone down to the spring, filled her jar, and was returning.

The servant ran to meet her and said: “Give me a little water to drink from your jar.” She answered: “Drink, my lord,” and quickly lowered the jar onto her arm and gave him a drink. When he had drunk, she added: “Indeed, I shall draw water for your camels also, until they have all drunk.”

Pouring out the jar into the troughs, she ran back to the well to draw water and gave what she had drawn to all the camels. The man watched her silently, wanting to know whether God had made his journey prosperous or not.

The man brought out golden earrings weighing two shekels and two bracelets weighing ten shekels. He said to her: “Whose daughter are you? Tell me. Is there room in your father’s house for us to stay?” She answered: “I am the daughter of Bathuel, son of Nahor, whom Melcha bore to him.” And she added: “We have a great deal of straw and hay, and ample room for staying.”

The man bowed and worshiped the Lord, saying: “Blessed be the Lord, the God of my master Abraham, who has not withdrawn his mercy and truth from my master and has led me by a straight road to the house of my master’s brother.”

The girl ran and announced in her mother’s house everything she had heard. Rebecca had a brother named Laban, who hurried out to the man at the spring. When he saw the earrings and bracelets on his sister’s hands and heard all the words she reported—“This is what the man said to me”—he came to the man, who was standing beside the camels and near the spring of water.

He said to him: “Come in, blessed of the Lord. Why are you standing outside? I have prepared the house and a place for your camels.” He brought the man into the lodging, unloaded the camels, and gave them straw and hay, as well as water for washing the feet of the camels and of the men who had come with him. Bread was set before him.

He said: “I will not eat until I have spoken my words.” Laban answered him: “Speak.”

He said: “I am Abraham’s servant, and the Lord has greatly blessed my master, and he has become great. He has given him sheep and oxen, silver and gold, male and female slaves, camels and donkeys. Sarah, my master’s wife, bore a son to my master in his old age, and he gave him everything he possessed.

“My master bound me by an oath, saying: ‘You shall not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, in whose land I dwell. Instead, you shall go to my father’s house and take a wife for my son from my kindred.’ I said to my master: ‘What if the woman is unwilling to come with me?’ He said: ‘The Lord, before whom I walk, will send his Angel with you and direct your way, and you shall take a wife for my son from my kindred and from my father’s house. You shall be innocent of my curse when you come to my relatives and they do not give her to you.’

“So today I came to the spring of water and said: ‘Lord God of my master Abraham, if you have directed the way in which I now walk, behold, I stand beside the spring of water. Let the virgin who comes out to draw water hear me say, “Give me a little water to drink from your jar,” and let her say to me, “You also drink, and I shall draw water for your camels.” Let her be the woman whom the Lord has prepared for my master’s son.’

“While I was silently turning these things over within myself, Rebecca appeared, coming with a jar which she carried on her shoulder. She went down to the spring and drew water. I said to her: ‘Give me a little to drink.’ She quickly lowered the jar from her shoulder and said to me: ‘You also drink, and I shall give your camels water.’ I drank, and she watered the camels.

“I questioned her and said: ‘Whose daughter are you?’ She answered: ‘I am the daughter of Bathuel, son of Nahor, whom Melcha bore to him.’ So I hung the earrings on her to adorn her face, and placed the bracelets on her hands. I bowed down and worshiped the Lord, blessing the Lord, the God of my master Abraham, who had led me by a straight road so that I might take the daughter of my master’s brother for his son.

“Therefore, if you are going to show mercy and truth toward my master, tell me; but if you prefer otherwise, tell me that too, so that I may go either to the right or to the left.”

Laban and Bathuel answered: “The word has come forth from the Lord; we cannot say anything else to you beyond his pleasure. Behold, Rebecca is before you. Take her and depart, and let her be the wife of the son of your master, as the Lord has spoken.”

When Abraham’s servant heard this, he fell to the ground and worshiped the Lord. Bringing out silver and gold vessels and clothing, he gave them to Rebecca as a gift; he also offered gifts to her brothers and her mother. They held a feast, and they ate and drank together and stayed there.

When he rose in the morning, the servant said: “Send me away, so that I may go to my master.” Her brother and mother answered: “Let the girl remain with us at least ten days, and afterward she will depart.”

“Do not,” he said, “hold me back, because the Lord has directed my way. Send me away, so that I may go to my master.”

They said: “Let us call the girl and ask her wishes.” When she had been called, they asked her: “Do you wish to go with this man?” She said: “I will go.”

So they sent her away, along with her nurse, Abraham’s servant, and his companions, invoking prosperity upon their sister and saying: “You are our sister; may you grow into thousands upon thousands, and may your offspring possess the gates of their enemies.”

Then Rebecca and her maidens mounted camels and followed the man, who was returning quickly to his master. At that time Isaac was walking along the road that leads to the Well of the Living One Who Sees; for he lived in the southern land. He had gone out to meditate in the field as day was declining. When he lifted his eyes, he saw camels coming from a distance.

Rebecca also saw Isaac, dismounted from the camel, and said to the servant: “Who is that man coming through the field to meet us?” He said to her: “That is my master.” Then she quickly took her cloak and covered herself.

The servant reported to his master Isaac everything he had done. Isaac brought her into the tent of Sarah his mother, took her as his wife, and loved her so deeply that he was comforted for the grief caused by his mother’s death. **R.** Amen.

### Reading from the Book of the Prophet Jeremiah (Chapter 31)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

“Behold, the days are coming,” says the Lord, “when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah—not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers on the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt. They broke that covenant, although I had threatened them,” says the Lord.

Thus, devoted always to your praises and having attained the path of your commandments, may we acquire in you, we ask, the adornments of rejoicing, the remedies of hope, and the crown of faith.

### Reading from the Book of Proverbs (Chapter 22)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

“My son, the man who is inclined to mercy will be blessed, for he has given from his bread to the poor. He who gives gifts will acquire victory and honor, but he takes away the soul of those who receive. Drive out the scoffer, and strife will depart with him; causes and insults will cease. He who loves purity of heart will have the king as his friend because of the grace of his lips. The eyes of the Lord guard knowledge, but the words of the wicked are overthrown.

“The lazy man says, ‘There is a lion outside; I will be killed in the middle of the streets.’ The mouth of a foreign woman is a deep pit; the one with whom the Lord is angry will fall into it. Folly is bound up in the heart of a child, but the rod of discipline will drive it out. He who slanders the poor in order to increase his riches will himself give to one richer and will be in need.

“My son, incline your ear and hear the words of wisdom; apply your heart to my teaching. It will be beautiful for you when you preserve it within, and it will overflow upon your lips, so that your trust may be in the Lord.”

**R.** Amen.

### Reading from the Book of Genesis (Chapter 25)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

These are the descendants of Isaac, son of Abraham. Abraham begot Isaac. When Isaac was forty years old, he took Rebecca, daughter of Bethuel the Syrian of Mesopotamia, sister of Laban, as his wife. Isaac entreated the Lord for his wife, because she was barren; and he heard him and granted conception to Rebecca.

But the children struggled in her womb, and she said: “If this was to happen to me, why was it necessary for me to conceive?” She went to consult the Lord. He answered her: “Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples will be divided from your belly. One people will overcome the other, and the elder will serve the younger.”

The time of giving birth had arrived, and behold, twins were found in her womb. The first who came forth was red and entirely hairy like a hide; his name was called Esau. Immediately the other came forth, holding his brother’s heel in his hand; therefore he called him Jacob. Isaac was sixty years old when the children were born.

When they had grown up, Esau became a man skilled in hunting, a farmer; but Jacob was a simple man and lived in tents. Isaac loved Esau because he ate of his hunting, while Rebecca loved Jacob.

Jacob cooked a stew. When Esau came from the field, tired, he said to him: “Give me some of this red stew, for I am extremely tired.” For this reason his name was called Edom. Jacob said to him: “Sell me your birthright.” He answered: “Behold, I am dying; what good will the birthright do me?” Jacob said: “Swear it to me.” Esau swore to him and sold his birthright. Thus, after receiving bread and the lentil dish, he ate and drank and went away, thinking little of having sold his birthright.

### Chapter 26

A famine arose in the land, after the barrenness that had occurred in the days of Abraham. Isaac went to Abimelech, king of the Philistines, at Gerar. The Lord appeared to him and said:

“Do not go down into Egypt, but remain in the land that I shall tell you. Dwell as a stranger in it, and I will be with you and bless you. For I will give all these regions to you and to your offspring, fulfilling the oath that I swore to your father Abraham. I will multiply your offspring like the stars of heaven, and I will give all these regions to your descendants. In your offspring all the nations of the earth will be blessed, because Abraham obeyed my voice and kept my precepts and commandments, observing my ceremonies and laws.”

Isaac therefore remained at Gerar. When the men of that place asked him about his wife, he answered: “She is my sister,” for he was afraid to confess that she was joined to him in marriage, thinking that they might kill him because of her beauty.

After many days had passed and he was staying there, Abimelech, king of the Philistines, looked through a window and saw him playing with Rebecca, his wife. He summoned him and said: “It is clear that she is your wife. Why did you say that she was your sister?” He answered: “I was afraid that I would die because of her.”

Abimelech said: “Why have you deceived us? Someone from the people might have lain with your wife, and you would have brought great sin upon us.” He commanded all the people, saying: “Whoever touches this man’s wife shall surely be put to death.”

Isaac sowed in that land and found a hundredfold in that same year; and God blessed him. The man became wealthy and continued advancing and growing, until he became exceedingly great. He possessed flocks of sheep and herds of cattle and a very large household.

Because of this, the Philistines envied him and, at that time, stopped up all the wells that the servants of his father Abraham had dug, filling them with earth. So much so that Abimelech himself said to Isaac: “Depart from us, for you have become much stronger than we.”

He departed from there and came to the torrent of Gerar, where he settled. He dug again the wells that the servants of his father Abraham had dug and that the Philistines had stopped up long ago after Abraham’s death; and he called them by the same names by which his father had formerly called them.

They dug in the torrent and found living water. But there too the shepherds of Gerar quarreled with Isaac’s shepherds, saying: “The water is ours.” Therefore, because of what had happened, he called the name of the well Quarrel. They dug another well, and they quarreled over that one also; so he called it Enmity.

Moving on from there, he dug another well, over which they did not contend. Therefore he called its name Broad Place, saying: “Now the Lord has given us room and caused us to increase upon the land.”

Isaac went up from that place to Beersheba. The Lord appeared to him that same night and said:

“I am the God of your father Abraham. Do not be afraid, for I am with you. I will bless you and multiply your offspring for the sake of my servant Abraham.”

Thus he built an altar there to the Lord and called upon the name of the Lord.

**R.** Amen.

### Reading from the Book of Genesis (Chapter 27)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

In those days, when Isaac had grown old and his eyes had grown dim so that he could not see, he called Esau, his elder son, and said to him: “My son?” He answered: “Here I am.” His father said to him:

“You see that I have grown old and do not know the day of my death. Take your weapons, your quiver, and your bow, and go outside. When you have caught something by hunting, prepare for me a dish, as you know I like, and bring it to me to eat, so that my soul may bless you before I die.”

When Rebecca heard this, and Esau had gone into the field to fulfill his father’s command, she said to her son Jacob:

“I heard your father speaking with your brother Esau and saying to him: ‘Bring me some of your hunting and prepare food for me to eat, and I will bless you before the Lord before I die.’ Now therefore, my son, follow my advice. Go to the flock and bring me two of the best young goats, so that I may prepare from them food for your father, which he will eat. When you bring it to him and he has eaten, he will bless you before he dies.”

He answered her:

“You know that my brother Esau is a hairy man, whereas I am smooth. If my father touches me and recognizes me, I fear that he will think I wanted to mock him and will bring a curse upon me instead of a blessing.”

His mother said to him:

“Let that curse fall upon me, my son. Only listen to my voice, go, and bring what I have said.”

He went and brought them and gave them to his mother. She prepared food just as she knew his father liked. She clothed him in the very fine garments of Esau that she had at home, and she wrapped the skins of the young goats around his hands and covered the nakedness of his neck. She gave him the dish and handed him the bread that she had baked.

When he had brought them in, he said: “My father?” He answered: “I hear you. Who are you, my son?” Jacob said to him:

“I am Esau, your firstborn. I have done as you commanded me. Rise, sit, and eat from my hunting, so that your soul may bless me.”

Again Isaac said to his son: “How were you able to find it so quickly, my son?” He answered: “It was God’s will that what I wanted should quickly come to me.”

Isaac said: “Come here, so that I may touch you, my son, and test whether you are my son Esau or not.” He came near to his father, and when he had felt him, Isaac said:

“The voice is indeed Jacob’s voice, but the hands are Esau’s hands.”

He did not recognize him, because his hairy hands resembled those of his elder brother. As he blessed him, he said: “Are you my son Esau?” He answered: “I am.”

He said: “Bring me food from your hunting, my son, so that my soul may bless you.” When he had brought it and Isaac had eaten it, he also offered him wine. After drinking it, he said to him:

“Come near me and give me a kiss, my son.”

He came near and kissed him. As soon as Isaac perceived the fragrance of his garments, he blessed him and said:

“Behold, the fragrance of my son is like the fragrance of a full field that the Lord has blessed. May God give you of the dew of heaven and of the richness of the earth, abundance of grain and wine and oil. May peoples serve you and tribes bow down to you. Be lord of your brothers, and may the sons of your mother bow before you. Let him who curses you be cursed, and let him who blesses you be filled with blessings.”

Isaac had scarcely finished speaking when Jacob went outside. Esau came in, brought food prepared from his hunting to his father, and said:

“Rise, my father, and eat from the hunting of your son, so that your soul may bless me.”

Isaac said: “Who are you?” He answered: “I am your firstborn son, Esau.”

Isaac was struck with exceedingly great astonishment and, wondering beyond what can be believed, said:

“Who, then, is the one who brought me his catch a little while ago? I ate from everything before you came, and I blessed him; and he will be blessed.”

When Esau heard his father’s words, he roared with a great cry and, shaken, fell upon the ground, saying:

“Bless me too, my father.”

He said: “Your brother came deceitfully and took your blessing.”

He added: “His name was rightly called Jacob, for he has supplanted me twice: he took away my birthright before, and now for the second time he has stolen my blessing.”

Again he said to his father: “Have you not reserved a blessing for me also?”

Isaac answered: “I have made him your lord and subjected all his brothers to his service, and established him with grain and wine; what more can I do for you now, my son?”

Esau said: “Do you have only one blessing, father? I ask you also to bless me.” As he wept with a great lamentation, Isaac was moved and said to him:

“Your blessing will be in the richness of the earth and in the dew of heaven from above. You will live by the sword and serve your brother. But the time will come when you will shake off and loose his yoke from your neck.”

Esau therefore always hated Jacob because of the blessing with which his father had blessed him. He said in his heart: “Let the days of mourning for my father come, so that I may kill my brother Jacob.”

These things were reported to Rebecca. She sent for Jacob, her son, and said to him:

“Behold, your brother Esau threatens to kill you. Now therefore, my son, listen to my voice. Arise and flee to my brother Laban in Haran. You shall dwell with him for a few days, until your brother’s fury subsides and his anger ceases; until he forgets what you have done to him. Afterwards I will send for you and bring you back here. Why should I be deprived of both sons on one day?”

Rebecca also said to Isaac:

“I am weary of my life because of the daughters of Heth. If Jacob takes a wife from the daughters of this land, I do not want to live.”

### Chapter 28

Isaac called Jacob and blessed him. He commanded him, saying:

“Do not take a wife from the race of Canaan. But go and travel to Mesopotamia of Syria, to the house of Bethuel, your mother’s father, and take a wife for yourself there from the daughters of Laban, your maternal uncle. May almighty God bless you, make you grow, and multiply you, so that you may become companies of peoples. May he give you the blessings of Abraham, and to your offspring after you, so that you may possess the land of your sojourning, which he promised to your grandfather.”

**R.** Amen.

Now let the pale night yield

Now, joyful, we rise from our beds,

May anger not provoke quarrels,

may hunger not pervert our work,  
nor shameful excess seize us.

But, steadfast in sobriety,

with wholly faithful spirit,  
may we pass through this day, O Christ.

To God the Father be glory,  
and to his only Son,  
with the Spirit, the Paraclete,  
through everlasting ages.

### From the Proverbs of Solomon (Chapter 11)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

“My son, the justice of the innocent will direct his way, but the wicked will fall by his own impiety. The justice of the upright will deliver them, but the unjust will be caught in their own snares. When the wicked man dies, there will be no further hope, and the expectation of the anxious will perish.

“The just man is freed from distress, and the wicked is handed over in his place. The deceiver with his mouth tricks his friend, but the just will be delivered by knowledge. In the prosperity of the just the city will rejoice, and in the destruction of the wicked there will be praise. By the blessing of the just the city will be exalted, but by the mouth of the wicked it will be overthrown.

“He who deceives his friend is thirsty in his heart, but the prudent man will keep silent. He who walks deceitfully reveals secrets, but the faithful in spirit conceals what has been entrusted. Where there is no governor, the people will fall; but there is safety where there is much counsel.

“He will be afflicted by evil who gives surety for a stranger, but he who avoids snares will be secure. A gracious woman will find glory, and the strong will possess riches. The merciful man does good to his own soul, but the cruel man rejects his relatives. The wicked man makes his rewards unstable, but for the one who sows justice there is a faithful work.”

**R.** Amen.

### Reading from the Book of Genesis (Chapter 29)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

In those days, Jacob set out and came to the eastern land. He saw a well in the field and three flocks of sheep lying beside it, for the animals were watered from it; and its mouth was closed with a large stone. It was customary that, when all the sheep had gathered, they would roll away the stone and, after the flocks had been watered, place it again over the mouth of the well.

He said to the shepherds: “Brothers, where are you from?” They answered: “From Haran.” He asked them: “Do you know Laban, son of Nahor?” They said: “We know him.” He asked: “Is he well?” They answered: “He is well. Behold, Rachel his daughter is coming with her flock.”

Jacob said: “There is still much of the day remaining, and it is not yet time to bring the flocks back to their folds. Give the sheep water first, and then lead them back to pasture.”

They answered: “We cannot, until all the animals have been gathered and we have removed the stone from the mouth of the well, so that we may water the flocks.”

They were still speaking when Rachel came with her father’s sheep, for she herself was tending the flock. When Jacob saw her and recognized that she was his cousin and that the sheep belonged to Laban, his maternal uncle, he removed the stone that covered the well. After watering the flock, he kissed her, raised his voice, and wept. He told her that he was her father’s brother and the son of Rebecca. She hurried to announce this to her father.

When he heard that Jacob, the son of his sister, had come, he ran to meet him. He embraced him, showered him with kisses, and led him into his house. After hearing the reason for his journey, he answered:

“You are my bone and my flesh.”

After a month had passed, he said to him: “Because you are my brother, will you serve me for nothing? Tell me what wages you will receive.”

Laban had two daughters. The name of the elder was Leah, and the younger was called Rachel. Leah’s eyes were weak, but Rachel was beautiful in face and pleasing in appearance. Jacob loved her and said:

“I will serve you seven years for Rachel, your younger daughter.”

Laban answered: “It is better that I give her to you than to another man. Remain with me.”

Jacob therefore served seven years for Rachel, and they seemed to him only a few days because of the greatness of his love. He said to Laban:

“Give me my wife, for the time is fulfilled, so that I may go in to her.”

Laban gathered a great crowd of friends for a feast and held a wedding. In the evening he brought his daughter Leah to Jacob, giving her Zilpah as a maidservant. When Jacob had gone in to her according to custom, morning came and he saw that it was Leah. He said to his father-in-law:

“What is this that you have done to me? Did I not serve you for Rachel? Why have you deceived me?”

Laban answered:

“It is not customary in our place to give the younger daughter in marriage first. Complete the week of this union, and I will also give her to you for the work by which you will serve me for another seven years.”

Jacob agreed to the arrangement. After the week had passed, he took Rachel as his wife.

### Reading from the Book of the Prophet Isaiah (Chapter 33)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

O Lord, have mercy on us; for we have waited for you. Be our arm in the morning and our salvation in the time of tribulation. At the voice of the Angel the peoples fled, and at your expectation the nations were scattered. Your spoils will be gathered as the locust is gathered, as when ditches are filled with it.

The Lord has been exalted, for he has dwelt on high; he has filled Zion with judgment and righteousness. Faithfulness will be established in his times; the riches of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge. The fear of the Lord itself is his treasure.

Behold, those who see will cry out outside, and the Angels of peace will weep bitterly. The roads have been deserted; the traveler has ceased from the path. The covenant has been annulled; he has rejected the cities and regarded men as nothing.

The earth mourned and languished. Lebanon was confounded and withered, and Sharon became like a desert; Bashan and Carmel were shaken.

“Now I will arise,” says the Lord; “now I will be exalted; now I will lift myself up.”

**R.** Amen.

### Reading from the Book of Genesis (chapter XXXII)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

In those days, Jacob sent messengers ahead of him to Esau his brother, in the land of Seir, in the region of Edom. He commanded them, saying: “Speak thus to my lord Esau: ‘This is what your brother Jacob says: I have lived as a stranger with Laban and have remained there until the present day. I have oxen, donkeys, sheep, male servants, and female servants; and now I am sending a delegation to my lord, so that I may find favor in your sight.’”

The messengers returned to Jacob, saying: “We came to Esau your brother, and behold, he is hastening to meet you with four hundred men.” Jacob was greatly afraid and, terrified, divided the people who were with him, as well as the flocks, sheep, oxen, and camels, into two companies, saying: “If Esau comes upon one company and strikes it, the other company that remains will be saved.”

And Jacob said: “God of my father Abraham, and God of my father Isaac, O Lord, who said to me, ‘Return to your land and to the place of your birth, and I will do good to you’: I am less than all your mercies and than the faithfulness that you have shown your servant. With only my staff I crossed this Jordan, and now I return with two companies. Deliver me from the hand of my brother Esau, for I fear him greatly, lest perhaps he come and strike the mother together with her children. You said that you would do good to me and multiply my offspring like the sand of the sea, which cannot be numbered because of its multitude.”

After he had slept there that night, he set aside from what he possessed gifts for Esau his brother: two hundred she-goats and twenty he-goats, two hundred sheep and twenty rams, thirty camels with their young, forty cows and twenty bulls, twenty she-donkeys and ten of their young. He sent each flock separately by the hands of his servants and said to his servants: “Go ahead of me, and let there be space between one flock and the next.”

He commanded the first, saying: “If you meet my brother Esau and he asks you, ‘Whose are you?’ or, ‘Where are you going?’ or, ‘Whose are these things that follow you?’ you shall answer: ‘They belong to your servant Jacob; he has sent them as gifts to his lord Esau, and he himself is coming after us.’”

In the same way he gave instructions to the second, the third, and all who followed the flocks, saying: “Speak these same words to Esau when you find him. And you shall add: ‘Your servant Jacob himself is following our journey,’ for he said, ‘I will appease him with the gifts that go before me, and afterward I shall see him; perhaps he will be gracious to me.’”

The gifts therefore went ahead of him, while he himself remained that night in the camp.

When he had risen early, he took his two wives and their two maidservants, together with his eleven sons, and crossed the ford of the Jabbok. After he had brought across everything that belonged to him, he remained alone; and behold, a man wrestled with him until morning. When he saw that he could not overcome him, he touched the sinew of his thigh, and immediately it withered.

He said to him: “Release me, for dawn has already risen.” He answered: “I will not release you unless you bless me.” Then he said: “What is your name?” He answered: “Jacob.” But he said: “Your name shall no longer be called Jacob, but Israel, because if you have been strong against God, how much more will you prevail against human beings?”

Jacob asked him: “Tell me, by what name are you called?” He answered: “Why do you ask my name, which is wondrous?” And he blessed him there.

Jacob called the name of that place Phanuel, saying: “I have seen God face to face, and my life has been saved.” Immediately the sun rose for him after he had crossed Phanuel, but he himself was limping on one foot.

For this reason the children of Israel do not eat the sinew that withered in Jacob’s thigh to the present day, because he touched the sinew of his thigh and it became numb.

**(Chapter XXXIII.)** Jacob lifted up his eyes and saw Esau coming, with four hundred men. He divided the children of Leah and Rachel and of both maidservants, placing the two maidservants and their children first, Leah and her children second, and Rachel and Joseph last.

He himself went forward and bowed to the ground seven times, until his brother drew near. Esau ran to meet his brother, embraced him, clasped his neck, and kissed him; and he wept.

When Esau lifted up his eyes, he saw the women and their little ones and said: “Who are these people belonging to you?” He answered: “They are the little ones whom God has given to your servant.” The maidservants and their children drew near and bowed. Leah also approached with her children, and when they had likewise bowed, Joseph and Rachel, who were last, bowed.

Esau said: “What are these companies that I met?” He answered: “That I might find favor before my lord.” But Esau said to him: “I have very much, my brother; let what is yours remain yours.”

Jacob said: “Do not do so, I beseech you; but if I have found favor in your sight, accept this little gift from my hands. For I have seen your face as though I had seen the face of God. Be gracious to me and accept the blessing that I have brought you, and which God, who gives me everything, has bestowed upon me.”

Although his brother urged him, he scarcely accepted it, and said: “Let us travel together, and I shall be your companion on the journey.”

Jacob said: “You know, my lord, that I have tender children with me, as well as sheep and cows with young; if I make them labor too much in walking, all the flocks will die in a single day. Let my lord go ahead of his servant, and I shall follow slowly in his footsteps, as I see that my children are able, until I come to my lord in Seir.”

Esau answered: “I ask you to leave with you at least some of the people who are with me as companions for your journey.” He replied: “There is no need, my lord. I need only this: to find favor in your sight.”

That day Esau returned by the way he had come toward Seir. Jacob came to Succoth, where he built a house and fixed up tents; therefore he called the name of that place Succoth, that is, “tents.”

He crossed over to Salem, a city of the Shechemites, which is in the land of Canaan, after returning from Mesopotamia of Syria, and he dwelt near the town. He bought from the sons of Hamor, the father of Shechem, for a hundred lambs, the portion of the field where he had pitched his tents. There he erected an altar and invoked upon it the most powerful God of Israel.  
**R.** Amen.

### From Proverbs (chapter XV)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

My son, the heart of the wise seeks instruction, but the mouth of fools feeds on ignorance. All the days of the poor are evil; a tranquil mind is like an unending banquet. Better is a little with fear of the Lord than great treasures that cannot satisfy. Better to be invited to vegetables with love than to a fattened calf with hatred. An angry man provokes quarrels, but the patient man calms those that have been aroused. The way of the lazy is like a hedge of thorns; the path of the righteous is without stumbling. A wise son gladdens his father, but a foolish man despises his mother. Folly is joy to the fool, but the prudent man directs his steps. Plans are scattered where there is no counsel, but where there are many counselors they are confirmed. A man rejoices in the answer of his mouth, and an apt word is best. The path of life is above the instructed, so that he may turn away from the lowest hell. The Lord will demolish the house of the proud and make firm the boundaries of the widow. The thoughts of the wicked are an abomination to the Lord, but the purest speech will be established by him. He who pursues greed troubles his own house, but he who hates gifts will live. Through mercy and faith sins are cleansed, but through fear of the Lord everyone turns away from evil. The mind of the righteous meditates obedience. The Lord is far from the wicked, but he will hear the prayers of the righteous.  
**R.** Amen.

### Reading from the Book of Genesis (chapter 37)

Thanks be to God.

[Col. 0319C]

In those days, when Joseph was sixteen years old, he was tending the flock with his brothers, still a boy. He was with the sons of Bilhah and Zilpah, his father’s wives, and he accused his brothers before his father of a very serious offense.

Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his sons, because he had begotten him in his old age; and he made him a coat of many colors. When his brothers saw that he was loved by his father more than all his sons, they hated him and could not speak peaceably to him.

It happened also that he reported a dream to his brothers, which became the cause and seed of greater hatred. He said to them: “Hear the dream that I saw. I thought that we were binding sheaves in the field, and that my sheaf, as though rising up, stood, while your sheaves surrounded it and bowed down to my sheaf.”

His brothers answered him: “Will you perhaps be our king? Or shall we be subjected to your authority?” This, therefore, supplied fuel for envy and hatred because of his dreams and words.

He saw another dream as well, and when he told it to his brothers he said: “I saw in a dream, as though the sun, the moon, and eleven stars were bowing down to me.”

When he had told it to his father and brothers, his father rebuked him and said: “What does this dream that you have seen mean? Shall I and your mother and your brothers bow down to you upon the earth?”

His brothers therefore envied him, but his father silently considered the matter.

When his brothers were staying at Shechem while tending their father’s flocks, Israel said to him: “Your brothers are pasturing the sheep at Shechem. Come; I will send you to them.” When he answered, “I am ready,” he said: “Go and see whether all is well with your brothers and the flocks, and report to me what is happening.”

Sent from the Valley of Hebron, he came to Shechem. A man found him wandering in the field and asked what he was seeking. He answered: “I am looking for my brothers. Tell me where they are pasturing their flocks.”

The man said to him: “They have departed from this place. But I heard them saying, ‘Let us go to Dothan.’”

Joseph therefore went after his brothers and found them at Dothan. When they saw him from a distance, before he came near them, they considered killing him and said to one another: “Behold, the dreamer is coming. Come, let us kill him and throw him into an old cistern; we shall say, ‘A most savage beast has devoured him,’ and then it will appear what his dreams will profit him.”

When Reuben heard this, he tried to rescue him from their hands and said: “Let us not kill him, nor shed his blood. Instead, throw him into this old cistern, which is in the wilderness, and keep your hands innocent.” He said this because he wished to rescue him from their hands and restore him to his father.

As soon as he came to his brothers, they stripped him of his long, many-colored tunic and threw him into an old cistern that had no water.

While they sat down to eat bread, they saw traveling Ishmaelites coming from Gilead, with their camels carrying spices, resin, and *sacten* [an uncertainly read substance] to Egypt.

Then Judah said to his brothers: “What will it profit us if we kill our brother and conceal his blood? It is better for him to be sold to the Ishmaelites, and for our hands not to be defiled; for he is our brother and our flesh.” His brothers agreed to his words.

When the Midianite merchants passed by, they drew him out of the cistern and sold him to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of silver. They brought him to Egypt.

When Reuben returned to the cistern and did not find the boy, he tore his garments and went to his brothers, saying: “The boy is gone. Where shall I go?”

They took his tunic and dipped it in the blood of a kid that they had killed. They sent someone to carry it to their father and say: “We found this. See whether it is your son’s tunic or not.”

When the father recognized it, he said: “It is my son’s tunic. A most savage beast has eaten him; a wild animal has devoured Joseph.”

Tearing his garments, he put on sackcloth and mourned his son for a long time. When all his children gathered to ease their father’s grief, he refused to accept consolation and said: “I shall go down mourning to my son in the underworld.”

While he continued in weeping, the Midianites sold Joseph in Egypt to Potiphar, Pharaoh’s eunuch and commander of the army.  
**R.** Amen.

### Reading from the Book of the Prophet Isaiah (chapter LXV)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

Thus says the Lord:

The people who provoke me to anger are always before my face; they sacrifice in gardens and offer sacrifice upon bricks; they dwell in tombs and sleep in the shrines of idols; they eat swine’s flesh, and profane broth is in their vessels.

They say: “Withdraw from me; do not come near me, for you are unclean.” These shall be smoke in my anger, a fire burning all day.

Behold, it is written before me: I shall not be silent, but I shall repay and requite your iniquities in their bosom, says the Lord, together with the iniquities of your fathers, who sacrificed upon the mountains and reproached me upon the hills; and I shall measure out their former work in their bosom.

Thus says the Lord: As when a seed is found in a cluster and it is said, “Do not destroy it, for it is a blessing,” so I shall act for the sake of my servants, so that I may not destroy everything. I shall bring forth offspring from Jacob and one who will possess my mountains from Judah; my chosen ones shall inherit it, and my servants shall dwell there.

### Hymn

Author of light, Son of the Virgin,  
Father of the Mother, Son of the Father,  
You gave light to the blind man  
Sitting and begging.

The blind man sat oppressed by darkness;  
He whom God had willed to be born blind,  
So that his power might be displayed  
To all who believe.

The blind man rejoices, having received light;  
The exalted Physician visited him,  
Beloved by the Father,  
That the world’s sin might be washed away.

The Hebrew people likewise said:  
“Let his parents come,  
Through whom they may inquire  
How he who was born blind was enlightened.”

But the Hebrew parents confessed:  
“He was born blind from his mother’s womb.  
He is of age; ask him.  
Let him speak the truth.”

The blind man who had been healed confessed:  
“A great Prophet came to me;  
By his power, in eye and heart,  
I have been enlightened.”

He made clay from holy spittle,  
Smeared my eyes with the clay,  
And commanded me to wash in Siloam;  
The pool made me radiant.

Everlasting glory to the Father,  
Glory to Christ and to the Holy Spirit;  
May every age proclaim  
The Triune Name with devout voice.

Amen.

**Supplication.** Let us pray to the Redeemer.

**Capitula.** Christ God, everlasting source of light, who willed the seventh course of the day to be a time of sanctification rather than of labor for those who confess you: behold, we seek your face, but the customary darkness of our conscience hinders us. We try to rise, but we fall back into sorrow. Do not therefore reject us who seek you, you who deigned to appear even to those who were not seeking you.

Behold, by recurring observances we offer the tenths of our days to your holy name; now we have completed the seventh day among those tenths. Grant us, therefore, help along the road of this laborious journey, so that our services may be dedicated to you undefiled; that you may lighten our labors through desire for your love and awaken the sluggishness of our understanding through the fervent abundance of your love; so that our life may not suffer a fall in you, but faith may find its reward.

**Prayer.** Merciful and compassionate Lord, do not be angry with us forever; but, as far as the east is from the west, put every iniquity far from us, and, as high as heaven is above the earth, enlarge your mercy within us.

**R.** Thus says the Lord: “I have afflicted my people exceedingly; they have not turned back from their ways; their widows have multiplied for me more than the sand of the sea.”  
**P.** “Therefore, if they repent of their evil, they shall dwell in the land without fear forever.”  
**V.** “They refused to understand all my ways, so that they might cause the cry of the needy to reach me and make me hear the voice of the poor.”  
**P.** “Therefore.”

**Prayer.** O Lord, our protector, turn us back from our crooked ways and make us dwell without fear in the land of our inheritance. Thus, once freed, hold us within the guidance of faith, so that we may neither be lifted up by the prosperity of the age nor troubled by the adversity of the envious enemy, nor be overshadowed by the cloud of crimes. Rather, while hoping in you, we beseech you to free us in your justice and not justly repay us what our deeds deserve. Enlighten your face, therefore, upon your inheritance, and save us for the sake of your mercy.

Through mercy.

**Antiphon.** “In our tribulation let us remember you, O God; in slight tribulation your instruction has been given to us.”

**Canticle.** “He keeps watch by night.” fol. 64. Repeat the antiphon: “In tribulation.”

**Prayer.** O God, adorn our spirit, which keeps watch for you by night, with the light of your commandments, and keep watch in the tempest over those who seek you, so that you may be present like the midday light. May no darkness hinder us as we follow you; may love of injustice not draw our steps back from you. Rather, may we be able to speak of justice and ask you, the author of justice, with advancing eagerness; and while we desire to embrace you continually, may we also cling to the embraces of your wisdom.

**Psalm CXLVIII.**

### Reading from the Book of Genesis (chapter XXXIX)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

In those days Joseph was brought down into Egypt, and Potiphar, Pharaoh’s eunuch and commander of his army, an Egyptian man, bought him from the hand of the Ishmaelites, by whom he had been brought there. The Lord was with him, [Col. 0326C] and he was a man prospering in all things. He lived in the house of his master, who knew very well that the Lord was with him and that the Lord directed everything he did. Joseph found favor in the sight of his master and ministered to him. His master appointed him over everything, and he governed the household entrusted to him and all that had been placed in his charge. The Lord blessed the Egyptian’s house for Joseph’s sake and multiplied all his possessions, both in the house and in the fields. He knew nothing else except the bread that he ate.

Joseph was handsome in face and attractive in appearance. After many days, his mistress cast her eyes upon Joseph and said, “Sleep with me.” But he refused entirely to consent to the wicked deed and said to her: [Col. 0326D] “Behold, my master, having entrusted everything to me, does not know what he has in his house. There is nothing that is not in my power, or that he has not entrusted to me, except you, who are his wife. How, then, can I do this evil and sin against my Lord?”

She spoke to him in this manner day after day, and the woman harassed the young man, while he refused the adultery. One day Joseph entered the house to perform some task without witnesses. She seized the edge of his garment and said, “Sleep with me.” But he left his cloak in her hand, fled, and went outside.

When the woman saw the garment in her hands and realized that she had been despised, she called the men of her household and said to them: “See, he has brought in a Hebrew man to mock us. He came to me to lie with me, but when I cried out and he heard my voice, he left the cloak that I was holding and fled outside.” As evidence of her story, she showed the retained cloak to her husband when he returned home and said: “The Hebrew servant whom you brought here to mock me came in to me. When he heard me cry out, he left the cloak that I was holding and fled outside.” [181]

When the master heard this, and was excessively credulous toward his wife’s words, he became very angry. He handed Joseph over to the prison where the king’s prisoners were kept, and there he was confined. But the Lord was with Joseph, had mercy on him, and granted him favor in the sight of the prison governor. He entrusted to Joseph’s care all the prisoners who were held in custody, and everything that was done there was under his authority. He knew nothing of anything, since everything had been entrusted to him; for the Lord was with him and directed all his works. [Col. 0327B]

### Chapter XL

After these things, it happened that two eunuchs offended their master, the king of Egypt: the king’s cupbearer and his baker. Pharaoh became angry with them—for one was in charge of the cupbearers and the other of the bakers—and sent them to the prison of the commander of the army, where Joseph was also confined. The prison keeper assigned them to Joseph, and he ministered to them.

Some time passed, and they remained in custody. Both of them dreamed a dream on the same night, each dream having an appropriate interpretation. When Joseph came to them in the morning and saw that they were sad, he questioned them, saying: “Why is your face sadder than usual today?” They replied: “We have had a dream, and there is no one to interpret it for us.” Joseph said to them: [Col. 0327C] “Does not interpretation belong to God? Tell me what you have seen.”

The chief cupbearer first related his dream: “I saw before me a vine on which were three branches. It gradually grew into buds, and afterward its blossoms ripened into grapes. Pharaoh’s cup was in my hand. I took the grapes, pressed them into the cup that I was holding, and gave the cup to Pharaoh.”

Joseph answered: “This is the interpretation of the dream: the three branches are three more days. After them Pharaoh will remember your service and restore you to your former position. You will give him the cup according to your office, as you used to do before. Only remember me when it goes well with you, and show me kindness by mentioning me to Pharaoh, so that he may bring me out of this prison; for I was secretly carried away from the land of the Hebrews, and here I was thrown into the pit though innocent.”

When the chief baker saw that he had interpreted the dream intelligently, he said: “I too had a dream: I seemed to have three baskets of flour on my head. In the highest basket I thought I was carrying all the foods made by the baker’s craft, while birds were eating from it.”

Joseph answered: “This is the interpretation of the dream: the three baskets are three more days. After them Pharaoh will take your head from you and hang you on a cross, and the birds will tear your flesh.”

From then on, the third day—the king’s birthday—arrived. Pharaoh held a great feast for his servants and, amid the banquet, remembered the chief cupbearer and the chief baker. He restored one to his position, so that he might present the cup to the king; the other he hanged on the gallows, so that the truth of the interpreter might be demonstrated. [Col. 0328A]

**Response:** Amen.

Grant that your trumpet may be the clear confession of our faith; that our lips may be your cymbals, and that the services of our inner and outer selves may sound in harmony; that our souls may be your lyres and may charm the praise of your mercy with generous melody. **R.** Amen.

**Hymn.**

O God, who by fixed laws  
Distinguish night and day,  
That sleep may loosen  
And restore weary bodies,

During the time of dreadful night  
We ask you that sleep,  
While it holds the tired mind,  
May illumine it with the light of faith.

May the deceitful enemy not stir  
Care through wanton pleasures,  
Calling forth, in the secrecy of night,  
The gentle heats of the body.

May no terror of anxious fear  
Steal upon the senses;  
May no deceptive image  
Mock the mind’s sight.

But when deep sleep has carried us away,  
Unmindful of cares,  
May faith in no way sleep,  
And may the vigilant sense dream.

To God the Father be glory,  
And to his only Son,  
Together with the holy Paraclete,  
Throughout everlasting ages.

Amen.

Grant us, therefore, that just as that blind man obtained, through a confession of true faith, the gift of granted salvation, so we may attain in these words the effect of our devout petition when we have proclaimed from the earth what you taught us:
