**Psalm CXLIX.**

**Reading from the Book of Genesis (Chapter XLI).**

**R.** Thanks be to God.

In those days Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before King Pharaoh, and he went throughout all the regions of Egypt. Seven years of fertility came, and the harvests were gathered into sheaves and stored in the granaries of Egypt. All the abundance of grain was also stored in each city; and such was the abundance of wheat that it equaled the sand of the sea, and its supply exceeded measure. Two sons were born to Joseph before the famine came; Aseneth, daughter of Potiphera, priest of Heliopolis, bore them to him. He called the name of the firstborn Manasseh, saying: “God has made me forget all my labors and my father’s house.” He also called the second Ephraim, saying: “God has made me grow in the land of my poverty.”

When the seven years of abundance that had been in Egypt had passed, the seven years of scarcity that Joseph had foretold began to come. Famine prevailed throughout the whole world; there was famine throughout all the land of Egypt as well. When it was hungry, the people cried out to Pharaoh, asking for food. He answered them: “Go to Joseph, and whatever he tells you, do.”

The famine increased daily throughout the whole land. Joseph opened all the granaries and sold grain to the Egyptians, for the famine had also oppressed them. All the provinces came to Egypt to buy food and lessen the evil of scarcity. [Col. 0332B]

### Chapter XLII

When Jacob heard that food was being sold in Egypt, he said to his sons: “Why have you neglected this? I have heard that grain is sold in Egypt. Go down and buy what we need, so that we may live and not be consumed by scarcity.”

Joseph’s ten brothers therefore went down to buy grain in Egypt, while Benjamin was kept at home by Jacob, who had said to his brothers: “Perhaps he may suffer some misfortune on the journey.” They entered the land of Egypt with others who were going to buy. There was famine in the land of Canaan.

Joseph was ruler in the land of Egypt, and at his command grain was sold to the people. When his brothers had bowed down to him and he recognized them, he spoke harshly to them as though they were strangers, asking: “Where have you come from?”

They answered: “From the land of Canaan, to buy provisions for food.” Yet, although Joseph recognized his brothers, they did not recognize him.

Remembering the dreams that he had once seen, he said to them: “You are spies. You have come to see the weaker parts of the land.”

They said: “It is not so, my lord. Your servants have come to buy food. We are all the sons of one man. We have come peacefully, and your servants are plotting no evil.”

He answered them: “It is otherwise. You have come to inspect the unfortified parts of this land.”

They said: “We, your servants, are twelve brothers, sons of one man in the land of Canaan. The youngest is with our father; the other is no more.”

He said: “This is what I said: You are spies. Now I shall test you. By the life of Pharaoh, you will not leave this place until your youngest brother comes. Send one of you to bring him; you, however, will remain in chains until it is proved whether what you have said is true or false. Otherwise, by the life of Pharaoh, you are spies.”

He handed them over to custody for three days. On the third day, after bringing them out of prison, he said: “Do what I have said, and you will live, for I fear God. If you are peaceful men, let one of your brothers be bound in prison, while you go and carry the grain you bought to your houses. Then bring your youngest brother to me, so that I may test your words and you may not die.”

They did as he had said and said to one another: “We rightly suffer these things, because we sinned against our brother. We saw the distress of his soul when he pleaded with us, and we did not listen; therefore this tribulation has come upon us.”

One of them, Reuben, answered: “Did I not tell you, ‘Do not sin against the boy’? And you did not listen to me. Behold, his blood is being demanded.”

They did not know that Joseph understood, because he spoke to them through an interpreter. He turned away from them for a moment and wept; then he returned and spoke to them.

He took Simeon and bound him in their presence. He ordered the servants to fill their sacks with wheat and to put each man’s money back in his sack, adding provisions for the journey. They did so.

They carried the grain on their donkeys and departed. When one of them opened his sack at the lodging place to give fodder to his animal, he saw the money at the mouth of the sack and said to his brothers: “My money has been returned; behold, it is in the sack.”

They were astonished and troubled and said to one another: “What is this that God has done to us?”

They came to their father Jacob in the land of Canaan and told him everything that had happened to them. They said: “The lord of the land spoke harshly to us and thought that we were spies of the province. We answered him: ‘We are peaceful men and are plotting no ambushes. We are twelve brothers, born of one father; one is no more, and the youngest is with our father in the land of Canaan.’

“He said to us: ‘This is how I shall test whether you are peaceful: leave one of your brothers with me, take the provisions necessary for your households, and go. Bring your youngest brother to me, so that I may know that you are not spies and that I may return this one who is held in chains to you; afterward you may have permission to buy whatever you wish.’”

When they poured out the grain, each of them found his money tied at the mouth of his sack. They were all terrified. Their father Jacob said: “You have made me childless. Joseph is no more; Simeon is held in chains; and you will take Benjamin. All these evils have fallen upon me.”

Reuben answered him: “Put my two sons to death if I do not bring him back to you. Put him into my hand, and I will restore him to you.”

But he said: “My son will not go down with you. His brother is dead, and he alone remains. If some adversity befalls him in the land to which you are going, you will bring my gray hairs down to the underworld in sorrow.” [Col. 0333D]

### Chapter XLIII

Meanwhile the famine pressed heavily upon the whole land. When they had consumed the food that they had brought from Egypt, Jacob said to his sons: “Return and buy us a little food.”

Judah answered: “That man solemnly warned us under oath, saying: ‘You shall not see my face unless you bring your youngest brother with you.’ Therefore, if you are willing to send him with us, we shall go together and buy what you need. But if you are unwilling, we shall not go, for the man, as we have often said, warned us: ‘You shall not see my face without your youngest brother.’”

Israel said to them: “Why did you bring this misery upon me by telling him that you had another brother?”

They answered: “The man questioned us carefully about our family: whether our father was alive and whether we had a brother. We answered him accordingly, in response to what he had asked. Could we have known that he would say, ‘Bring your brother with you’?”

Judah also said to his father: “Send the boy with me, so that we may depart and live, and so that we may not die, both we and our little ones. I will take responsibility for the boy. Require him from my hand. If I do not bring him back and restore him to you, I shall be guilty of sin against you forever. If delay had not intervened, we would already have returned a second time.”

Then Israel, their father, said to them: “If it must be so, do what you wish. Take some of the best fruits of the land in your vessels, and carry gifts to the man: a little resin, honey, storax, stacte, terebinth, and almonds. Carry double money with you, and take back the money that you found in your sacks, in case it happened through a mistake. But take your brother and go to the man. May almighty God make him favorable to you.” **R.** Amen.

We confess that you were born for us, and, sheltered beneath the covering of your wings and your cross, we praise you. Grant, therefore, that we who proclaim your gifts in the sacred mystery may enjoy you as the supreme gift.

**Prayer.** Confirm your mercy toward us, Lord, so that together with all nations we may praise you while present in this world; and, saved by your truth, may always remain with you in the eternal kingdom. **R.** Amen.

### At Terce

**From the Proverbs of Solomon (Chapter XXIII).**

**R.** Thanks be to God.

“My son, listen and be wise, and direct your heart along the right way. Do not be among drinkers at banquets, nor among those who bring meat together for feasting; for those who devote themselves to drinking and contribute their shares will be consumed, and drowsiness will be clothed in rags. Listen to your father who begot you, and do not despise your mother when she grows old. Buy truth, and do not sell wisdom, instruction, or understanding. The father of a righteous child rejoices greatly; he who has begotten a wise one will rejoice in him. Let your father and mother rejoice, and let her who bore you exult.” **R.** Amen.

**Reading from the Book of Genesis (Chapter XLIII).**

**R.** Thanks be to God.

In those days the sons of Israel went down to Egypt and stood before Joseph. When he saw them, and Benjamin with them, he commanded the steward of his house, saying: “Bring the men into the house, slaughter victims, and prepare a feast, because they will eat with me at midday.”

He did as he had been commanded and brought the men into the house. There, terrified, they said to one another: “We have been brought in because of the money that we previously returned in our sacks, so that he may bring an accusation against us and violently subject both us and our donkeys to slavery.” [Col. 0335A]

Therefore, approaching the steward at the very entrance, they spoke to him: “We beg you, sir, listen to us. We came down earlier to buy food. When we had bought it and arrived at the lodging place, we opened our sacks and found the money at the mouths of our sacks. We have now brought it back in the same weight. We have also brought other silver with us, so that we may buy what we need. We do not know who put the money in our bags.”

He replied: “Peace be with you; do not be afraid. Your God and the God of your father has given you treasures in your sacks. As for the money you gave me, I have it as tested and accounted for.” [Col. 0335B]

He brought Simeon out to them. After leading them into the house, he brought water, and they washed their feet; he also gave fodder to their donkeys. They prepared their gifts until Joseph should enter at midday, for they had heard that they would eat bread there.

Then Joseph entered his house, and they offered him the gifts they were holding in their hands, bowing down to the ground. He greeted them kindly and asked them: “Is your aged father well, about whom you told me? Is he still alive?”

They replied: “Your servant our father is well; he is still alive.” And they bowed down and worshiped him.

Joseph raised his eyes and saw Benjamin, his brother by the same mother, and said: “Is this your younger brother, about whom you told me?” And again he said: “May God have mercy on you, my son.”

He hurried into the house, because his compassion had been stirred toward his brother and tears were bursting forth. Entering his chamber, he wept. After washing his face, he came out again, restrained himself, and said: “Set out the bread.”

When it had been served, Joseph sat separately, his brothers separately, and the Egyptians who were eating with them separately—for it is unlawful for Egyptians to eat with Hebrews, and they regard such a meal as profane. They sat before him, the firstborn according to his birthright and the youngest according to his age. They were greatly amazed, receiving portions from him; but Benjamin’s portion was greater, so that it exceeded the others fivefold. They drank and became drunk with him. [Col. 0335D]

### Chapter XLIV

Joseph commanded the steward of his house, saying: “Fill their sacks with grain, as much as they can hold, and put each man’s money at the top of his sack. Put my silver cup, together with the price of the grain, in the mouth of the youngest one’s sack.” It was done accordingly.

When morning came, they were sent away with their donkeys. They had already gone out of the city and proceeded a short distance when Joseph summoned the steward of his house and said: “Rise and pursue the men. When you have caught them, say to them: ‘Why have you repaid good with evil? The cup that you stole is the one from which my master drinks and by which he practices divination. You have done a very wicked thing.’”

He did as he had been ordered. When he had caught up with them, he spoke to them in turn. They replied: “Why does our master speak in this way, as though his servants had committed so great a crime? The money that we found at the top of our sacks we brought back to you from the land of Canaan. How, then, could it be plausible that we had stolen gold or silver from your master’s house? With whichever of your servants the thing you seek is found, let him die, and we shall be slaves to our master.”

He said to them: “Let it be according to your sentence: the one with whom it is found shall be my slave, but you shall be innocent.”

So they quickly lowered their sacks to the ground and opened each one. He searched them, beginning with the oldest and ending with the youngest, and found the cup in Benjamin’s sack. They tore their garments, loaded their donkeys again, and returned to the town.

Judah entered first with his brothers to Joseph—for he had not yet departed from the place—and they all fell together before him on the ground. He said to them: “Why did you wish to act in this way? Did you not know that there is no one like me in the knowledge of divination?”

Judah replied: “What shall we answer my lord? What shall we say, or what just claim can we make? God has discovered the iniquity of your servants. Behold, we are all my lord’s slaves, both we and the one with whom the cup was found.”

Joseph answered: “Far be it from me to act in this way. The one who stole the cup shall be my slave; but you may go up in freedom to your father.”

Judah came closer and said boldly: “I beg you, my lord, listen to me. Let your servant speak a word in your ears, and do not be angry with your servant; for you are my lord, second only to Pharaoh. You questioned your servants earlier: ‘Do you have a father or a brother?’ And we answered you, my lord: ‘We have an aged father and a young boy, born to him in his old age; his brother by the same mother is dead, and he alone remains to his mother, while his father loves him tenderly.’

“You said to your servants: ‘Bring him to me, and I will set my eyes upon him.’ We suggested to you, my lord: ‘The boy cannot leave his father; for if he leaves him, his father will die.’ But you said to your servants: ‘Unless your youngest brother comes with you, you shall not see my face again.’

“When we had gone up to your servant our father, we told him everything that my lord had said. Our father replied: ‘Return and buy us a little grain.’ We said to him: ‘We cannot go. If our youngest brother goes down with us, we shall go together; otherwise, if he is absent, we dare not see the man’s face.’

“He replied: ‘You know that my wife bore me two sons. One went out, and you said, “A beast devoured him”; and he has not appeared to this day. If you take this one also, and some misfortune happens to him on the journey, you will bring my gray hairs down to the underworld in sorrow.’

“Therefore, if I go to your servant our father and the boy is absent—since his life depends upon the boy’s life—and he sees that he is not with us, he will die; and your servants will bring his gray hairs down to the underworld in sorrow. I am personally your servant, for I accepted responsibility for this boy and pledged myself, saying: ‘If I do not bring him back, I shall be guilty of sin against my father forever.’ Therefore I shall remain your servant instead of the boy, in my lord’s service, while the boy may go up with his brothers. [Col. 0337A] For I cannot return to my father without the boy, lest I stand as a witness to the calamity that will overwhelm my father.”

### Chapter XLV

Joseph could no longer restrain himself before all those standing nearby. He therefore ordered everyone to go outside, so that no stranger would be present at the recognition between them. He raised his voice with weeping, and the Egyptians heard him, as did the entire household of Pharaoh.

He said to his brothers: “I am Joseph. Is my father still alive?” His brothers could not answer him, for they were terrified beyond measure. He said to them kindly: “Come closer to me.” When they had come near, he said: “I am Joseph, your brother, whom you sold into Egypt. Do not be afraid, and do not let it seem harsh to you that you sold me into these regions; for God sent me ahead of you into Egypt for your preservation. For it is now two years since the famine began in the land, and five years still remain in which there will be neither plowing nor harvest. God sent me ahead so that you might be preserved on the earth and have food to sustain life.

“It was not by your plan but by God’s will that I was sent here. He has made me like a father to Pharaoh, lord of all his household, and ruler throughout the whole land of Egypt. Hurry, go up to my father, and say to him: ‘Your son Joseph sends this message: God has made me lord of the whole land of Egypt. Come down to me; do not delay. You shall dwell in the land of Goshen, and you shall be near me—you, your sons, your grandsons, your sheep, your cattle, and everything that you possess. There I shall feed you, for five years of famine still remain, lest you, your household, and everything you possess perish.’

“Behold, your eyes and the eyes of my brother Benjamin see that my mouth is speaking to you. Tell my father of all my glory and everything that you have seen in Egypt. Hurry and bring him to me.”

Then he fell upon the neck of his brother Benjamin while embracing him, and wept; Benjamin likewise wept upon his neck. Joseph kissed all his brothers and wept over each of them. Afterward his brothers dared to speak with him.

The news was heard and widely reported throughout the king’s court: “Joseph’s brothers have arrived.” Pharaoh and all his household rejoiced. [Col. 0337D]

**R.** Amen.

**Antiphon 1.** “Now the desire of the poor shall be heard,” says the Lord.

May your ear attend to our prayer in such a way that, when you have judged the orphan and the humble, you may console us with fatherly indulgence and repay the humiliation of the present with the joys of eternal things. **R.** Amen.

**Antiphon 2.** The Lord is righteous and has loved righteousness; his countenance has looked upon equity.

**Psalm X.**

## At Sext

**Reading from the Book of the Prophet Isaiah (Chapter LXV).**

**R\.** Thanks be to God.

Thus says the Lord: Those who previously did not inquire have sought me; those who did not seek me have found me. I said: Here I am, here I am, to a nation that did not know me and that did not invoke my name. I stretched out my hands all day to an unbelieving people, who walk in a way that is not good, following their own thoughts. A people who continually provoke me to anger before my face; who sacrifice in gardens and offer sacrifice upon bricks; who dwell in tombs and sleep in the shrines [Col. 0338C] of idols; who eat swine’s flesh, and unclean broth is in their vessels. Those who say, “Withdraw from me; do not come near me, for you are unclean”—these shall be smoke in my wrath, a fire burning all day. Behold, it is written before me: I will not be silent, but I will repay and recompense your iniquities into their bosom, and the iniquities of your fathers together, says the Lord, who sacrificed upon the mountains and reproached me upon the hills; and I will measure out their former work into their bosom.

Thus says the Lord: As when a grain is found in a cluster and it is said, “Do not destroy it, for there is a blessing in it,” so I will act for the sake of my servants, so that I may not destroy everything. And I will bring forth offspring from Jacob, and from Judah one who possesses my mountains [Col. 0338D]—and my chosen ones shall inherit it, and my servants shall dwell there. **R\. Amen.**

Therefore have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy; and forgive our sins, for which we fear you, so that in your merciful kindness you may look upon our contempt, and by the right hand of your power rescue us from the reproach of sin. **R\. Amen.**

Through your mercy.

Through your mercy.

## At None

**From the Proverbs of Solomon (Chapter XXIII).**

**R\.** Thanks be to God.

My son, let your heart enter into instruction, and let your ears attend to words of knowledge. Do not withhold discipline from a child; [Col. 0339C] for if you strike him with a rod, he will not die. You shall strike him with the rod, and you will deliver his soul from hell. My son, if your mind is wise, my heart too will rejoice with you; and my inmost being will exult when your lips speak what is right. Let your heart not envy sinners, but be in the fear of the Lord all day; for you will have hope at the end, and your expectation will not be taken away. **R\. Amen.**

**189 Reading from the Book of Genesis (Chapter XLV).**

**R\.** Thanks be to God.

In those days: It was heard, and the news was widely proclaimed in the king’s court: “Joseph’s brothers have come”; and Pharaoh and all his household rejoiced. He said to Joseph that he should command his brothers, saying: “Load your beasts, go to the land of Canaan, [Col. 0339D] and take from there your father and your families, and come to me; and I will give you all the good things of Egypt, so that you may eat the richness of the land. Command also that they take wagons from the land of Egypt for transporting their little ones and wives; and say: ‘Take your father and come as quickly as possible.’ Do not leave anything of your possessions behind, for all the wealth of Egypt shall be yours.”

The sons of Israel did as they had been commanded. Joseph gave them wagons, according to Pharaoh’s order, and provisions for the journey. He ordered two garments to be brought out for each of them; but to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver and five finest garments, sending his father an equal amount of money and clothing, and adding ten male donkeys [Col. 0340A] to carry away all the riches of Egypt, and as many female donkeys carrying grain and bread for the journey. Thus he dismissed his brothers and said to them as they departed: “Do not quarrel on the way.”

They went up from Egypt and came into the land of Canaan to their father Jacob. They announced to him, saying: “Your son Joseph is alive, and he rules over the whole land of Egypt.” When he heard this, he awoke as though from a deep sleep, yet he did not believe them. But they, in turn, related to him the entire sequence of events. When he saw the wagons and everything that Joseph had sent, his spirit revived, and he said: “It is enough for me if my son Joseph is still alive; I will go and see him before I die.”

**(Chapter XLVI.)** Israel set out with all that he had and came to the Well of the Oath. After sacrificing victims there to the God of his father Isaac, [Col. 0340B] he heard him calling him in a vision by night and saying to him: “Jacob,” to which he replied, “Here I am.” God said to him: “I am the mighty God of your father; do not fear; go down into Egypt, for there I will make you into a great nation. I will go down there with you, and I will bring you back from there when you return; Joseph also shall place his hand upon your eyes.”

Jacob rose from the Well of the Oath. His sons carried him, together with the little ones and their wives, in the wagons that Pharaoh had sent to transport the old man, and all that he possessed in the land of Canaan. He came into Egypt with all his offspring: his sons and grandsons, his daughters, and his entire progeny together. **R\. Amen.**

**Antiphon 1.** O God, our God, look upon us; do not abandon those who hope in you. **Psalm XXI.**

[Col. 0340C] **Prayer.** Look upon us, O Lord our God; do not abandon us in any way by turning your face away from us. For we shall truly be saved if you turn the gaze of your countenance toward us and joyfully unite yourself with our souls, so that, since our fathers hoped in you and were saved, you may make us enter into their hereditary hope and rejoice with them in eternal exultation in an equal fellowship. **R\. Amen.**

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon 2.** Look upon our defense, O our God. **Psalm XXI.**

**Prayer.** For our defense. See fol. 149.

**Antiphon 3.** Save your people, O Lord, and bless your inheritance; rule them and lift them up forever. **Psalm XXVII.**

[Col. 0340D] **Hymn.** O Nazarene, light. Fol. 144.

**Prayer.** Our helper and Redeemer, O Lord, help us; and may our flesh blossom either with the green vigor of chastity or with the newness of holiness. Since you are the strength of your people, save your people and exalt your inheritance with the abundance of your blessing.

**Reading from the Book of Genesis (Chapter XLVI).**

[Col. 0342C] **R\.** Thanks be to God.

In those days: Jacob sent Judah ahead of him to Joseph in Egypt, to announce his arrival and to have him meet him in Goshen. When he arrived there, Joseph yoked his chariot and went up to meet his father at the same place. When he saw him, he rushed upon his neck and wept amid their embraces. The father said to Joseph: “Now I shall die joyful, because I have seen your face and leave you alive.”

Joseph spoke to his brothers and to all his father’s household: “I will go up and announce it to Pharaoh, and I will say to him: ‘My brothers and my father’s household, who were in the land of Canaan, have come to me. They are shepherds, men who care for the feeding of flocks; they have brought with them their sheep, cattle, and everything they have been able [Col. 0342D] [191] to possess.’ When he calls you and says, ‘What is your occupation?’ you shall answer: ‘We, your servants, are shepherds from our infancy until now, both we and our fathers.’ You shall say this so that you may dwell in the land of Goshen, because all shepherds of sheep are detestable to the Egyptians.”

**(Chapter XLVII.)** Joseph entered and announced to Pharaoh, saying: “My father and my brothers, their sheep and cattle, and all that they possess, have come from the land of Canaan; and behold, they are staying in the land of Goshen.” He also placed five men, the last of his brothers, before the king, and the king asked them: “What is your occupation?” They replied: “We, your servants, are shepherds of sheep, both we and our fathers. We have come to dwell as strangers in your land, because there is no [Col. 0343A] pasture for the flocks of your servants, since the famine has grown severe in the land of Canaan. We ask that you order us to be your servants in the land of Goshen.”

The king said to Joseph: “Your father and your brothers have come to you. The land of Egypt is before you; settle them in the best place, and give them the land of Goshen. If you know that there are capable men among them, appoint them overseers of my livestock.”

After this Joseph brought his father before the king and presented him to him. He blessed him, and when the king asked him, “How many are the days of the years of your life?” he answered: “The days of the years of my pilgrimage are one hundred and thirty years, few and evil; they have not reached the days of my fathers, in which they journeyed as strangers.” And after blessing the king, he went out.

[Col. 0343B] Joseph gave his father and brothers a possession in Egypt, in the best part of the land, Ramesses, as Pharaoh had commanded. He nourished them and provided provisions for his entire father’s household, giving food to each. **R\. Amen.**

**Hymn.** God of eternal light. Fol. 98. **Capitulum.** O Lord, with whom... Fol. 151.

**Praise.** Do not take the word of truth from my mouth, O Lord. **P.** For I have hoped in your judgments. **V\.** Let your mercy come upon me, O Lord, your salvation and your word. **P.** For I have hoped in your judgments. **V\.** Glory and honor to the Father, etc. **P.** For I have hoped in...

**Prayer.** May your mercy come upon us, O Lord, as we pray to you; may your salvation instruct our heart, and the teaching of your word nourish our mind, so that we who hope in your sayings may be [Col. 0343C] comforted in every way by your powers. And while our hope is directed toward you, may the request of that hope be granted to us by you. **R\. Amen.**

Through your mercy.

**From the Proverbs of Solomon (Chapter XI).**

**R\.** Thanks be to God.

My son, every desire of the righteous is good; the expectation of the wicked is fury. Some distribute their own possessions and become richer; others seize what is not theirs and are always in want. The soul that blesses shall be made rich, and whoever gives drink shall himself also be given drink. Whoever hides grain shall be cursed among the people, but blessing shall be upon the head of those who sell it. He who seeks good rises early and prospers; but whoever investigates evil [Col. 0343D] shall be crushed by it. Whoever trusts in his riches shall fall, but the righteous shall sprout like a flourishing leaf. Whoever troubles his household possesses the winds, and the fool shall serve the wise. The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life, and whoever wins a soul is wise. If the righteous person is repaid on earth, how much more the wicked and the sinner?

**(Chapter XII.)** Whoever loves discipline loves knowledge, but whoever hates reproof is foolish. Whoever is good will draw grace to himself from the Lord, but whoever trusts in his own thoughts acts impiously. A man shall not be strengthened by wickedness, and the root of the righteous shall not be moved. **R\. Amen.**

**Reading from the Book of Genesis (Chapter XLVII).**

**R\.** Thanks be to God.

[Col. 0344A] In those days: All Egypt came to Joseph, saying: “Give us bread; why should we die before you, since our money has failed?” He answered them: “Bring your livestock, and I will give you food in exchange for them, if you have no money.” When they had brought them, he gave them provisions in exchange for horses, sheep, oxen, and donkeys; and he sustained them that year in exchange for their livestock.

They came again in the second year and said to him: “We will not conceal from our lord that, since our money has failed, our livestock too has failed; nor is it hidden from you that, apart from our livestock and land, we have nothing. Why then should we die while you look on? Both we and our land shall be yours; buy us into royal servitude and provide seed, lest, when the cultivator perishes, the land be reduced to a wilderness.”

Joseph therefore bought all the land of Egypt, [Col. 0344B] as each person sold his possessions because of the great severity of the famine. He subjected it to Pharaoh, together with all its peoples, from the farthest boundaries of Egypt to its extreme borders, except the land of the priests. Their appointed rations were supplied from the public storehouses, which had been granted to them by the king; [192] therefore they were not compelled to sell their possessions.

Joseph said to the people: “Behold, as you see, both you and your land belong to Pharaoh. Take seed and sow your fields, so that you may have crops. You shall give a fifth part to the king; I leave you the other four parts for seed and for food for your servants and children.” They replied: “Our life is in your hand; let our lord [Col. 0344C] look favorably upon us, and we shall gladly serve the king.”

From that time to the present day, throughout the whole land of Egypt, a fifth part is paid to the kings, and it became established as law, except for the land of the priests, which was free from this condition. **R\. Amen.**

## At Sext

**Reading from the Book of the Prophet Isaiah (Chapter LXIII).**

**R\.** Thanks be to God.

Look down, O Lord, from heaven, and see from the dwelling-place of your holiness and your glory. Where are your zeal and your strength, the abundance of your compassion and your mercies? They have restrained themselves from me. For you are our father, though Abraham did not know us and Israel did not acknowledge us. You, O Lord, are our father and [Col. 0345C] our redeemer; your name is from eternity. Why have you caused us to stray, O Lord, from your ways? Why have you hardened our heart so that we would not fear you? Turn back for the sake of your servants, the tribes of your inheritance. They possessed your holy people as though it were nothing; our enemies have trampled your sanctuary. We have become as at the beginning, when you did not rule over us and your name was not invoked over us.

**(Chapter LXIV.)** Would that you would rend the heavens and descend; the mountains would melt before your face. As at the burning of fire they would melt, and waters would burn with fire, so that your name might be made known to your enemies; before your face the nations would be troubled. When you perform wonders, we shall not endure them; you descended, and before your face the mountains melted. From eternity they have not heard, nor perceived with their ears; no eye has seen, O God, apart from you, what you have prepared for those who await you.

You met the one who rejoices and practices justice; in your ways they will remember you. Behold, you were angry, and we sinned; we have always remained in our sins, and we shall be saved. We have all become like unclean things, and like the menstrual cloth of the whole earth; we have all fallen like a leaf, and our iniquities have carried us away like the wind. There is no one who invokes your name, who rises and takes hold of you [the printed reading “neat” is uncertain]; you have hidden your face from us and have crushed us in the hand of our iniquity.

[Col. 0345D] [193] And now, O Lord, you are our father; we are clay, and you are our maker, and we are all the work of your hands. Do not be exceedingly angry, O Lord, and do not remember our iniquity forever. **R\. Amen.**

[Col. 0346A] **Antiphon 1.** Judge rightly, sons of men. **Psalm LVII.**

**Prayer.** O God, whose utterances are pure and judgments right, grant us to bring forth your words with a chaste mouth and to preserve the commands of your judgments with a most pure heart. Therefore extend your bow for our defense, and direct spiritual arrows to weaken the counsels of our enemies; crush the millstones of the lions that strive to demolish your scepter, so that the multitude of the redeemed may rejoice in you, who are the crown of the righteous, and so that we may sing to you a psalm of joy, by whose gift one reaches the fruit of justice. **R\. Amen.**

Through your mercy, etc.

**Antiphon 2.** Restore our captivity, O Lord, like a torrent in the south. **Psalm CXXV.**

[Col. 0346B] **Prayer.** Restore our captivity, O Lord, by redeeming us from the seductive allurements of the enemy; fill with the consolation of forgiveness those whom you see desolated because of the admission of wickedness. Grant us, we ask, to seek the humility of a contrite heart and to wash away with streams of tears the stains that defile us. Thus may we sow the remedies of confession in tears, so that we may reap the fruit of forgiveness in joys. **R\. Amen.**

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon 3.** Our help is in the name of the Lord, who made heaven and earth. **Psalm CXXIII.**

**R\.** You who sit upon the throne and judge equity, **P.** be a refuge for the poor in tribulation, because you alone regard labor and sorrow. **V\.** [Col. 0346C] You who rule Israel, attend; you who lead Joseph like a sheep, you who sit upon the cherubim, **P.** be a refuge for the poor in tribulation, because you alone regard labor and sorrow. **V\.** Glory, etc. Repeat the response.

**Intercessions.** Let us all say: Be reconciled to your people, O Christ. **P.** And have mercy. **V\.** At last attend to our prayers; attend now in mercy. **P.** And have mercy. **V\.** We have sinned; we have acted wickedly. **P.** And have mercy. **V\.** Turn away your anger and grant forgiveness. **P.** And have mercy. **V\.** Purify us, O Lord, from our sins and offenses. **P.** And have mercy.

**Hymn.** O Nazarene, light. Fol. 144.

**Capitulum.** Our help is in your name, O Lord. Grant us to hate the allurements of the world and to avoid the trap of those who hunt for pleasures, so that you yourself may destroy [Col. 0346D] the one lying in wait, and yourself strengthen and defend the one who trusts in you.

**The Lord’s Prayer.**

## At None

**From the Proverbs of Solomon (Chapter XXIII).**

**R\.** Thanks be to God.

My son, hear your father who begot you, and do not despise your mother when she grows old. Buy truth, and do not sell wisdom, instruction, or understanding. Let the father of the righteous rejoice greatly; let him who begot the wise man rejoice in him. Let your father and your mother rejoice, and let he who begot you exult. **R\. Amen.**

**Reading from the Book of Genesis (Chapter XLVII).**

**R\.** Thanks be to God.

[Col. 0347A] In those days: Israel dwelt in Egypt, that is, in the land of Goshen, and possessed it. He increased and multiplied greatly. He lived there for seventeen years, and all the days of his life were one hundred and forty-seven years. When he saw that the day of his death was approaching, he called his son Joseph and said to him: “If I have found favor in your sight, place your hand beneath my thigh and show me mercy and truth: do not bury me in Egypt, but let me sleep with my fathers; carry me away from this land and bury me in the tomb of my ancestors.” He replied: “I will do what you have commanded.” And he said: “Swear to me.” When he had sworn, Israel worshiped the Lord, turning toward the head of the bed.

**(Chapter XLVIII.)** After these things Joseph was told that [Col. 0347B] his father was ill. He took his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim, and went to him. It was reported to the old man: “Behold, your son Joseph is coming to you.” He strengthened himself and sat up in bed. When Joseph had entered, he said: “Almighty God appeared to me at Luz, in the land of Canaan, and blessed me. He said: ‘I will increase you and multiply you, and I will make you into throngs of peoples. I will give this land to you and to your offspring after you as an everlasting possession.’

“Therefore your two sons who were born to you in the land of Egypt before I came here to you shall be mine: Ephraim and Manasseh shall be reckoned to me as Reuben and Simeon. The others whom you beget after them shall be yours, and they shall be called by the name of their brothers in their possessions. For when I was coming from Mesopotamia, [Col. 0347C] Rachel died for me in the land of Canaan along the way; it was springtime, and I was entering Ephrathah. I buried her beside the road to Ephrathah, which is also called Bethlehem.”

When he saw Joseph’s sons, he said to him: “Who are these?” He replied: “They are my sons, whom God gave me in this place.” He said: “Bring them to me, so that I may bless them.” Israel’s eyes had grown dim from extreme old age, and he could not see clearly. When Joseph brought them near him, he kissed and embraced them, and said to his son: “I had not expected to see your face, and behold, God has shown me your offspring.”

When Joseph had taken them from his father’s lap, he bowed with his face to the ground. He placed Ephraim at his right hand—that is, at Israel’s left—and Manasseh at his left, namely, at his [Col. 0347D] father’s right, and brought both near him. Stretching out his right hand, he placed it upon the head of Ephraim, the younger brother; and his left upon the head of Manasseh, who was the elder, crossing his hands.

Jacob blessed Joseph’s sons and said: “The God before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac walked, the God who has fed me from my youth until this day; the angel who has rescued me from all evils—may he bless these boys. May my name and the names of my fathers Abraham and Isaac be invoked over them, and may they grow into a multitude upon the earth.”

When Joseph saw that his father had placed his right hand upon Ephraim’s head, he was displeased. He took hold of his father’s hand and [Col. 0348A] tried to lift it from Ephraim’s head and transfer it to Manasseh’s head. He said to his father: “Not so, my father, for this one is the firstborn; place your right hand upon his head.” But he refused and said: “I know, my son, I know. He too shall become a people and shall be multiplied; but his younger brother shall be greater than he, and his offspring shall grow into nations.”

He blessed them at that time, saying: “In you Israel shall be blessed, and it shall be said: ‘May God make you like Ephraim and like Manasseh.’” And he placed Ephraim before Manasseh. He said to his son Joseph: “Behold, I am dying, and God will be with you and will bring you back to the land of your fathers. I give you one portion beyond your brothers, which I took from the hand of the Amorite with my sword and bow.” **R\. Amen.**

[Col. 0348B] **Antiphon 1.** Give us help, O God, in tribulation. **Psalm LIX.**

**Prayer.** Give us help, O Lord, in tribulation, because salvation from man is vain. In you we shall act valiantly, for you strengthen your servants and reduce enemies to nothing. **R\. Amen.**

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon 2.** Let every land adore you, O Lord, and sing to you with a share in incorruptible life, so that, just as all things were formed by your workmanship, so likewise all things may be subjected to your rule. **R\. Amen.**

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon 3.** Attend to our help, O Lord; hasten to assist us. **Psalm LXIX.**

**Hymn.** O Nazarene. Fol. 144.

[Col. 0348C] **Capitulum.** Attend to our help, O Lord, and hasten to assist us; for our efforts in good works make no progress unless you sustain us, from whom every step is directed. For you are the one through whom our weakness is strengthened.

**The Lord’s Prayer.**

The Lord is my light and my salvation.

The Lord be always with you. **R\.** And with you.

# WEDNESDAY

## At Matins

**Antiphon.** My glory... Fol. 156. **Psalm III.** **Prayer.** Our glory, O our God... Fol. 156.

**Antiphon 1.** Let us sing to the Lord from the songs of Zion, so that he may remember us and deliver us. **Psalm CXXXVI.**

**Prayer.** Remember your pilgrim Church, O Lord; and while we sit weeping beside the rivers of Babylon, do not let us be carried away by the force of the passing age. Rather, freed from the contagion of the present life, may our intention be raised toward the Jerusalem above. **R\. Amen.**

[Col. 0349A] Through your mercy.

**195 Antiphon 2.** It is good for us to cling to God, to place our hope in the Lord. **Psalm LXXII.**

**Prayer.** It is good for us to cling to God; it is good for us to cling to you, O Lord. But so increase in us the desire for good that the hope which joins us to you may not waver through any faltering of faith, but may endure with the steadfastness of charity. **R\. Amen.**

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon 3.** Remember. **Prayer.** Remember us, O Lord. Fol. 177. **Psalm CV.**

**R\.** We have become, O Lord, like strangers to you. Woe to us, for we have sinned; your enemies have defiled your holy things. **P.** Would that you would rend the heavens and descend, [Col. 0349B] and make your name known, and that before your anger the nations would be troubled. **V\.** We have become as at the beginning, when you did not rule over us and your name was not invoked over us. **P.** Would that you would. **V\.** Glory and honor to the Father, etc. **P.** Would that you would.

## At Lauds

**Antiphon.** According to the multitude of your compassions, wash me from my iniquity; forgive my evils and wipe away all my iniquities. **Psalm L.**

**Prayer.** Merciful Lord, according to your great mercy have mercy on us in your kindness, so that those whose hidden things are not concealed from you may receive manifest mercy because they trust in you. And since we groan inwardly over our offenses and sigh for the forgiveness of our sins, do not cast us away from your face; but, with the piety owed to you alone, lead us to the harbor of forgiveness. **R\. Amen.**

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon.** Like overflowing waters, so is our groaning before you, O Lord our God.

[Col. 0349C] **Canticle of Job (Chapter III).**

May the day perish on which I was born, * and the night in which it was said: “A man has been conceived.”

May that day be turned into darkness; * may God not seek it from above, and may it not be illumined by light.

May darkness and the shadow of death obscure it; * may gloom seize it, and may it be enveloped in bitterness.

May a dark whirlwind possess that night; * may it not be counted among the days of the year or numbered among the months.

[Col. 0349D] May that night be solitary and unworthy of praise; * may those who curse the day curse it, those who are ready to awaken Leviathan.

Let the stars be darkened by its gloom; * let it look for light and not see it, nor the rising of the dawn’s emergence;

because it did not close the doors of the womb that carried me, nor remove trouble from my eyes.

Why did I not die in the womb? Why, when I came forth from the uterus, did I not perish immediately?

Why was I received upon knees? * Why was I suckled at the breasts?

For now I would be lying silent, * and in my sleep I would be at rest,

with the kings and consuls of the earth who build themselves desolate places,

[Col. 0350A] or with princes who possess gold * and fill their houses with silver;

or, like a hidden miscarriage, I would not exist, * like those conceived who did not see the light.

There the wicked cease from turmoil, * and there the weary in strength find rest.

There, too, prisoners rest together without distress; * they do not hear the voice of the taskmaster.

Small and great are there, * and the servant is free from his master.

Why is light given to the miserable, * and life to those who are bitter in soul?

To those who await death, and it does not come, as though they were digging for treasures; * they rejoice exceedingly when they find the grave—

[Col. 0350B] to the man whose way is hidden, * and whom God has surrounded with darkness?

Before I eat, I sigh; * and, like overflowing waters, so is my groaning.

For the fear that I feared has come upon me, and what I dreaded has happened.

Have I not dissembled? Have I not kept silent? Have I not rested? * Yet indignation has come upon me.

The antiphon is repeated: “Like overflowing waters.”

Prayer. As long as, Lord, we remain in the exile of this life, may neither the wickedness of evil prevail, nor the strength of our virtue grow weak, nor the turbulent agitation of precipitate anger obscure the tranquillity of our mind, nor the muddy delight of carnal pleasures stain the brightness of purity; but may the expectation of the future judgment [Col. 0350C] cleanse us from every defilement and impurity. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

At the Matins Office.

At the Benedictus. Antiphon. Enlighten your countenance, O Lord, upon us, and have mercy on us, that we may know your way upon the earth. V\. May God have mercy on us and bless us; may the Lord enlighten his countenance upon us.

Canticle. Blessed are you, Lord God.

Lauda. Praise the name of the Lord, mountains and all hills, fruitful trees and all cedars. Psalm CXLVIII.

Reading from the Book of Genesis (Chapter XLIX).

[Col. 0350D] R\. Thanks be to God.

In those days: Jacob blessed his sons with their proper blessings. And he commanded them, saying: “I am gathered to my people; bury me with my fathers in the double cave that is in the field of Ephron the Hittite, opposite Mamre in the land of Canaan, which Abraham bought with the field from Ephron the Hittite as a possession for a burial place. There they buried him and Sarah his wife; there Isaac was buried with Rebecca his wife; and there Leah also lies buried.”

When he had finished the commands with which he instructed his sons, he drew up his feet upon the bed, and departed; and he was gathered to his people. (Chapter L.) When Joseph saw this, he fell upon his father’s face, weeping and kissing him. And he commanded his servants, the physicians, to embalm [Col. 0351A] his father with spices. When they had fulfilled his orders, forty days passed—for this was the customary period for embalmed corpses—and Egypt mourned for him seventy days.

When the period of mourning was completed, Joseph spoke to the household of Pharaoh, saying: “If I have found favor in your sight, speak in the ears of Pharaoh, because my father adjured me, saying: ‘Behold, I am dying. In my tomb, which I dug for myself in the land of Canaan, you shall bury me.’ Therefore let me go up and bury my father, and I will return.”

And Pharaoh said to him: “Go up and bury your father, as you were adjured.”

When he went up, all the elders of Pharaoh’s household went with him, and all the elders of the land of Egypt; the household of Joseph with his brothers, except for the little ones and the flocks and herds, which they left in the [Col. 0351B] land of Goshen. He also had chariots and horsemen in his company, and a very great multitude was formed.

And they came to the threshing floor of Atad, which is beyond the Jordan. There, while they performed the funeral rites with great and vehement mourning, they completed seven days. When the inhabitants of the land of Canaan saw this, they said: “This is a great mourning for the Egyptians.” And for this reason they called the name of that place “The Mourning of Egypt.”

Thus the sons of Jacob did as he had commanded them. Carrying him into the land of Canaan, they buried him in the double cave that Abraham had bought with the field as a burial possession from Ephron the Hittite, opposite Mamre.

Joseph returned to Egypt with his brothers and all the company after his father had been buried. When he died, his brothers were afraid and spoke together, saying: “[Col. 0351C] Perhaps he will remember the injury he suffered and repay us for all the evil that we did.” So they sent word to him, saying: “Your father commanded us before he died to say these words to you: ‘I ask you to forget the crimes of your brothers, and the sin and malice that they practiced against you.’ We also ask that you forgive this iniquity to the servants of the God of your father.”

When Joseph heard this, he wept. And his brothers came to him and, prostrate upon the ground, said: “We are your servants.”

He answered them: “Do not be afraid. Can we resist God’s will? You intended evil against me, but God turned it to good, so that he might exalt me, as you now see, and save many peoples. Do not be afraid; I will feed you and your little ones.”

And he comforted them, and spoke to them gently and kindly. [Col. 0351D] He lived in Egypt with all his father’s household, and he lived one hundred and ten years. He saw the sons of Ephraim to the third generation. The sons also of Machir, the son of Manasseh, were born upon Joseph’s knees.

After these things he spoke to his brothers: “After my death God will visit you, and will bring you up from this land to the land that he swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.” And when he had adjured them, saying, “God will visit you; carry my bones with you from this place,” he died, having completed one hundred and ten years of his life. And after being embalmed with spices, he was placed in a coffin in Egypt. R\. Amen.

[Col. 0352A] Hymn. “Unbegotten God the Father.” See folio 101. Capitula. “Enlighten, O Lord.” See folio 26.

Lauda. Receive your servant for good. P. So that the proud may not slander me. V\. My eyes have failed in expectation of your salvation and in the word of your righteousness. P. So that they may not. V\. Glory. P. So that they may not.

Prayer. Teach us to do judgment and righteousness, O Lord, so that we may be able to trample down the slanders of the proud. Receive your servants for good, those who hope in your salvation; and make those whose inner eyes await the kingdom of your Christ share in the fellowship of the elect. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

197 At Terce.

From the Ecclesiasticus of Solomon (Chapter X).

[Col. 0352B] R\. Thanks be to God.

My son, according to the judge of the people, so are his ministers; and what the ruler of a city is, such also are its inhabitants. A foolish king will destroy his people, but cities will be inhabited through the prudence of the wise. In God’s hand is the power of the earth, and he will raise up a useful ruler over it in due time. In God’s hand is the power of man, and upon the face of the scribe he will place his honor.

Do not remember any injury done by your neighbor, and do nothing in acts of injury. Every pride is hateful before God, and every iniquity of the nations is accursed. A kingdom will be transferred from one nation to another because of injustice, injuries, insults, and various deceits.

Nothing is more wicked than a miser. Why are you proud, earth and ashes? [Col. 0352C] Nothing is more iniquitous than loving money; for such a man even sells his own soul, because in his lifetime he has cast away his inmost self.

The fear of the Lord is this: not to despise a just poor man, and not to honor a rich sinful man. Humble wisdom will exalt his head and make him sit among the great upon the earth. R\. Amen.

Beginning of the Book of Exodus (Chapter I).

R\. Thanks be to God.

These are the names of the sons of Israel who entered Egypt with Jacob; each entered with his household: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun and Benjamin, Dan and Naphtali, Gad and Asher.

Therefore all the persons who came into Egypt from Jacob’s thigh were seventy. Joseph [Col. 0352D] was already in Egypt. After he had died, and all his brothers and that entire generation, the sons of Israel increased and multiplied like spreading shoots; they became exceedingly strong and filled the land.

Meanwhile a new king arose over Egypt who did not know Joseph. And he said to his people: “Behold, the people of the children of Israel are numerous and stronger than we. Come, let us oppress them wisely, lest they multiply; and if war should break out against us, they may join our enemies, defeat us, and depart from the land.”

Therefore he set over them overseers of the works to afflict them with burdens. They built for Pharaoh store-cities, Pithom and Rameses. But the more they oppressed them, the more they [Col. 0353A] multiplied and increased. The Egyptians hated the sons of Israel, and afflicted them, mocking and envying them; and they made their lives bitter with hard labor in clay and brick, and with every kind of service by which they were oppressed in the works of the land.

The king of Egypt spoke to the Hebrew midwives—one of whom was named Shiphrah and the other Puah—and commanded them: “When you act as midwives for the Hebrew women, and the time of delivery has come, if it is a male child, kill him; if it is a female, preserve her.”

But the midwives feared God and did not act according to the command of the king of Egypt; instead, they preserved the males. When they were summoned before him, the king said: “Why have you wanted to do this, preserving the boys?”

They answered: “The Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women. For they themselves possess the knowledge of midwifery, and before [Col. 0353B] we come to them, they give birth.”

Therefore God dealt well with the midwives, and the people grew and became exceedingly strong. And because the midwives feared God, he built houses for them.

Then Pharaoh commanded all his people, saying: “Whatever male child is born, throw him into the river; whatever is female, preserve.”

(Chapter II.) After these things a man from the house of Levi went out, and took a wife from his own lineage. She conceived and bore a son; and when she saw that he was beautiful, she hid him for three months. When she could no longer conceal him, she took a basket of reeds, coated it with bitumen and pitch, placed the infant inside it, and set it among the reeds on the bank of the river. His sister stood at a distance, watching to see what would happen.

Behold, Pharaoh’s daughter [Col. 0353C] came down to bathe in the river, while her attendants walked along the bank of the channel. When she saw the basket among the papyrus, she sent one of her maidservants. When the basket had been brought and opened, and she saw in it a little child crying, she had pity on him and said: “This is one of the infants of the Hebrews.”

The child’s sister said to her: “Do you wish me to go and call a Hebrew woman who can nurse the infant for you?”

She replied: “Go.”

The girl went and called the child’s mother. Pharaoh’s daughter said to her: “Take this child and nurse him for me; I will give you your wages.”

The woman took him and nursed the child. When he had grown, she brought him to Pharaoh’s daughter. She adopted him as a son, and called his name Moses, saying: “Because I drew him out of the water.” R\. Amen.

Antiphon 1. Those who trust in the Lord are like Mount [Col. 0353D] Zion; they shall not be moved forever. Psalm CXXIV.

198 Prayer. Deal well, O Lord, with those who are good and upright in heart. Grant them salutary guidance; watch continually over the protection of your people; and bridle with your right hand the fury of the malicious. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 2. Arise, O God, judge the earth, for you rule over all nations. Psalm LXXXI.

Prayer. Arise, O Lord, who judge the earth; and since in your goodness you dwell as the possessor of the faith of all nations, do not allow us to remain in darkness, but make us behold the light of your truth, so that we may build the foundations of our faith not upon sand, which the storm might cast down, [Col. 0354A] but be established upon the rock whose firmness you are. R\. Amen.

Through.

Antiphon 3. O God, who is like you? Do not be silent, nor be restrained, O God. Psalm LXXXII.

R\. Attend, and you shall listen, says the Lord: no one speaks what is good. P. There is no one who repents of his sin. V\. Why is this people in Jerusalem turned against me with contentious rebellion? They seized falsehood and were unwilling to return. P. There is no one. V\. Glory and honor. Repeat R\.

Supplications. You, merciful Lord, rescue us from the scourge of your anger; be favorable to us. P. And have mercy on us. V\. Defend the Church that you chose above all; willingly receive the vows of the [Col. 0354B] priests; hear our prayer. P. And have mercy. V\. Almighty, eternal ruler of the heavens, Most High God, behold our groaning and weeping; give ear. P. And have mercy. V\. Elders, young people, and infants are struck down by dreadful death in their anguish: Redeemer, spare us. P. And have mercy. V\. We have sinned; we have committed our iniquities. You, Redeemer, wash away every offense; release us from guilt. P. And have mercy.

Hymn. “O Nazarene, light.” See folio 144.

Capitula. Arise; do not be silent or be restrained, O God. Since those who hate you have raised their head, fill their faces with disgrace, so that they may seek your name after recognizing their confusion; and save your people, so that they may understand the testimony of your power. Be favorable to your inheritance, you who alone are most high over [Col. 0354C] all the earth.

The Lord’s Prayer.

At Sext.

Reading from the Book of the Prophet Ezekiel (Chapter XVIII).

R\. Thanks be to God.

The word of the Lord came to me, saying: “What is this proverb that you turn into a byword among yourselves in the land of Israel, saying: ‘The fathers have eaten a sour grape, and the teeth of the children are set on edge’?

As I live, says the Lord God, this proverb shall no longer be a byword for you in Israel. Behold, all souls are mine: as the soul of the father is mine, so also is the soul of the son mine; the soul that sins, it shall die.

If a man is righteous and practices judgment and righteousness, does not eat upon the mountains, does not lift his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel, does not violate his neighbor’s wife, and does not approach a menstruating woman; if he does not grieve anyone, returns a debtor’s pledge, takes nothing by force, gives his bread to the hungry, covers the naked with clothing, lends nothing at interest and takes nothing more, turns his hand away from iniquity, gives true judgment between one man and another, walks in my commandments and keeps my judgments so as to practice truth—he is righteous; he shall surely live and shall not die, says the Lord Almighty.” R\. Amen.

Antiphon 1. Take up the psalm and give the timbrel; [Col. 0355A] the joyful psaltery with the lyre. Psalm LXXX.

Prayer. Let us rejoice in you, O Lord, whom we acknowledge and confess as our helper. Therefore we raise a joyful song to you in our desires; in instruction we offer a psalm; in mortification we offer the timbrel. For in praising you we celebrate the feast, and we rejoice in the remembrance of your wondrous deeds. Grant us, therefore, O Lord, that because we recall your benefits, we may also receive your rewards. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Antiphon 2. With the Lord there is mercy, and with him is abundant redemption. Psalm CXXIX.

Prayer. May your ears be open. See folio 160.

Antiphon 3. Let Israel hope in the Lord, from this time [Col. 0355B] forth and forever. Psalm CXXX.

R\. Our evils have surrounded us, and there is no number to them; our iniquities have seized us, and our sins oppose us. P. Spare us, O Lord, for our sorrow is exceedingly bitter. V\. Our sins have overflowed upon our head, and our iniquities have reached to the heavens. P. Spare us, O Lord. The Gloria is not to be said. Repeat R\.

Supplications. Let us all say. P. Have mercy, O Lord. V\. There are many iniquities. Have mercy. Charity grows cold. P. Have mercy, O Lord. V\. Against you alone have we sinned. P. Have mercy, O Lord. V\. We ask pardon. P. Have mercy. V\. Christ, Redeemer of the world. P. Have mercy, O Lord.

[Col. 0355C] Hymn. “O Nazarene.” See folio 144. Capitula. “Exalt our horn.” See folio 172.

At Vespers.

Lauda. In the evening, and in the morning, and at midday, we praise you, O Lord.

Antiphon. Break, O God, the bonds of sinners, so that we may sacrifice to you an offering of praise. Psalm CXV.

Lauda. Your hands made me and fashioned me. P. Give me understanding, O Lord. V\. Those who fear you will see me and rejoice, because I have hoped in your word. P. Give. V\. Glory. P. Give me.
