THURSDAY.

At Matins.

Antiphon. “But you, O Lord.” Psalm III. Prayer. “Although, O Lord.” See folio 141.

Antiphon 1. It is good to confess to the Lord and sing psalms to your name, O Most High. Psalm XCI.

Prayer. It is good for us to confess to you, O Lord, and sing psalms to your most high name, so that confession may rescue us from dangers, and the diligence of singing psalms may make us more pleasing before you. R\. Amen.

Through.

Antiphon 2. The Lord will not reject his people, and he will not abandon his inheritance. Psalm XCXIII.

[Col. 0356A] Prayer. “He will not reject.” See folio 168. Antiphon 3. Let us go before him. Psalm XCXIV.

Prayer. “Going before him.” See folio 168.

R\. Have mercy, O Lord, on the contrite in heart, and restore the captives to their land. P. Provide the propitiatory Lamb and the day of redemption, and comfort all who mourn. V\. Turn, O Lord, for a little while, and take delight in your servants. P. Provide.

At Lauds.

Antiphon. Turn your face away from our sins; cleanse us, O Lord. Psalm L.

Prayer. Turn your face away from our sins, O Lord, and, blotting out all our iniquities, remove from your eyes the crime of our evil pleasures. Mercifully incline your ear to our confession. Have mercy, we ask, on us who entreat you, since you look favorably upon those in adversity; and may your grace never turn away from our confessions, since you grant a penitent heart to those who despair.

But because the Publican, standing far off and striking his breast, was cleansed by confession alone, hear us sinners in the same way, so that just as you granted him the fruit of his petition according to his merit, you may likewise deign to bestow forgiveness of sins upon us, your unworthy servants, as we plead.

Therefore, because you are appeased by the sacrifice of a contrite heart, grant that we may offer you what you command and merit the indulgence that you promise. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

At the Matins Office. God is not like man, that he should lie, nor like a son of man, that he should change.

[Col. 0356C] Canticle. “Balak brought me from Aram.” See folio 53. Prayer. “You are, O Lord, the star of truth.” See folio 89.

Matins Office.

At the Benedictus. Antiphon. I will sing and understand in the morning, when you come to me. V\. I will sing of mercy and judgment to you, O Lord.

Canticle. Blessed are you, Lord God.

Lauda. Praise the Lord with timbrel and choir; praise him with strings and organ.

Reading from the Book of Exodus (Chapter III).

R\. Thanks be to God.

In those days: The Lord said to Moses: “Go, gather the elders of Israel, and say to them: ‘The Lord God of your fathers has appeared to me, the God of Abraham, [Col. 0356D] the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, saying: “Visiting, I have visited you, and I have seen all that has happened to you in Egypt. And I have said that I will bring you out of the affliction of Egypt into the land of the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Amorite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite, into a land flowing with milk and honey.”’

“And they will hear your voice. You shall enter, you and the elders of Israel, to the king of Egypt, and you shall say to him: ‘The Lord God of the Hebrews has called us, and we will go a three days’ journey into the wilderness, so that we may sacrifice to the Lord our God.’

“But I know that the king of Egypt will not let you go unless by a mighty hand. I will stretch out my hand and strike Egypt with all the wonders that I shall perform in its midst; after this he will let you go. And I will give this people favor in the sight of the Egyptians. [Col. 0357A] When you depart, you shall not go empty-handed; but every woman shall ask from her neighbor and from her houseguest vessels of gold and silver, and clothing. You shall place these upon your sons and daughters, and you shall despoil Egypt.”

(Chapter IV.) Moses answered and said: “They will not believe me, nor hear my voice; but they will say: ‘The Lord has not appeared to you.’”

Therefore he said to him: “What is that which you hold in your hand?”

He answered: “A staff.”

And the Lord said: “Throw it upon the ground.”

He threw it down, and it became a serpent, so that Moses fled from it. And God said: “Stretch out your hand and seize its tail.” He stretched out his hand and held it, and it became a staff again.

“This is so that they may believe,” he said, “that the Lord God of their fathers has appeared to you, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.”

[Col. 0357B] And the Lord said again: “Put your hand into your bosom.” When he had put it into his bosom, he brought it out leprous like snow. “Put your hand back into your bosom,” he said. He put it back and brought it out again, and it was like the rest of his flesh.

“If they do not believe you,” he said, “nor hear the word of the first sign, they will believe the word of the second sign. But if they do not believe even these two signs, nor hear your voice, take water from the river and pour it upon the dry ground; and whatever you draw from the river will be changed into blood.”

Moses said: “I beg you, Lord, I am not eloquent—not from yesterday or the day before yesterday. Since you spoke to your servant, I have become slower and more impeded in speech.”

The Lord said to him: “Who made man’s mouth? Or who fashioned the mute and the deaf, the seeing and the blind? Is it not I? [Col. 0357C] Go, therefore, and I will be in your mouth, and I will teach you what you should say.”

But he said: “I beg you, Lord, send whom you will send.”

The Lord became angry with Moses and said: “Aaron your brother, the Levite—I know that he is eloquent. Behold, he will come out to meet you, and when he sees you he will rejoice in his heart. Speak to him and put my words in his mouth. I will be in your mouth and in his mouth, and I will show you what you must do. He will speak for you to the people and will be your mouth; but you will be concerned with the things that pertain to God.

“Take this staff also in your hand, with which you will perform the signs.”

Moses went away and returned to Jethro, his kinsman, and said to him: “I will go and return to my brothers in Egypt, to see whether they are still alive.”

Jethro said to him: [Col. 0357D] “Go in peace.”

Then the Lord said to Moses in Midian: “Go and return to Egypt, for all those who sought your life have died.”

Therefore Moses took his wife and his sons, placed them upon a donkey, and returned to Egypt, carrying the staff of God in his hand.

And the Lord said to Moses as he was returning to Egypt: “See that you perform before Pharaoh all the wonders that I have placed in your hand. I will harden his heart, and he will not let the people go. And you shall say to him: ‘Thus says the Lord: Israel is my firstborn son. I said to you: “Let my son go, so that he may serve me”; but you were unwilling to let him go. Behold, I will kill your firstborn son.’”

The Lord also said to Aaron: “Go to meet Moses in the wilderness.”

He went to meet him at the mountain of God and kissed him. [Col. 0358A] Moses told Aaron all the words of the Lord for which he had sent him, and the signs that he had commanded him to perform. They went together and gathered all the elders of the sons of Israel. Aaron spoke all the words that the Lord had spoken to Moses, and he performed the signs before the people; and the people believed. They heard that the Lord had visited the sons of Israel and had looked upon their affliction, and they bowed down and worshiped.

(Chapter V.) After this Moses and Aaron entered and said to Pharaoh: “Thus says the Lord God of Israel: ‘Let my people go, so that they may sacrifice to me in the wilderness.’”

But he answered: “Who is the Lord, that I should hear his voice and let Israel go? I do not know the Lord, and I will not let Israel go.”

They said: “The God of the Hebrews has called us, so that we may go a three days’ journey into the wilderness [Col. 0358B] and sacrifice to the Lord our God, lest pestilence or the sword overtake us.”

The king of Egypt said to them: “Why do Moses and Aaron distract the people from their works? Go to your burdens.”

And Pharaoh said: “The people of the land are numerous. You see that the multitude has increased; how much more so if you give them rest from their works?”

Therefore on that day Pharaoh commanded the overseers of the works and the taskmasters of the people, saying: “You shall no longer give straw to the people for making bricks, as before; let them go and gather straw for themselves. And you shall impose upon them the same quota of bricks that they made before, and you shall diminish nothing from it, [201] for they are idle, and therefore they cry out, saying: ‘Let us go and sacrifice to our God.’ Let them be oppressed with works and complete them, so that they may not listen to lying words.”

[Col. 0358C] Then the overseers of the works and the taskmasters went out and said to the people: “Thus says Pharaoh: ‘I do not give you straw. Go and gather it wherever you can find it, and nothing shall be diminished from your works.’”

The people were scattered throughout the whole land of Egypt to gather straw. The overseers of the works also pressed them, saying: “Complete your daily work as you used to do when straw was given to you.”

Those who were in charge of the works of the sons of Israel were flogged by Pharaoh’s taskmasters, who said: “Why have you not completed the quota of bricks as before, neither yesterday nor today?”

The overseers of the sons of Israel came and cried out to Pharaoh, saying: “Why do you act this way against your servants? Straw is not given to us, yet bricks are required of us just the same. Behold, your servants are beaten with whips, and your people are treated unjustly.”

[Col. 0358D] He said: “You are idle, and therefore you say: ‘Let us go and sacrifice to the Lord.’ Go, therefore, and work. Straw will not be given to you, and you shall deliver the customary number of bricks.”

The overseers of the sons of Israel saw themselves in distress because it was said to them: “Nothing shall be diminished from the bricks for each day.”

Moses and Aaron encountered them as they came out from Pharaoh, and they said to them: “May the Lord see and judge, because you have made our odor offensive before Pharaoh and his servants, and you have put a sword into their hands to kill us.”

Moses returned to the Lord and said: “Lord, why have you afflicted your people? Why have you sent me? For from the time I entered Pharaoh’s presence to speak [Col. 0359A] in your name, he has afflicted your people, and you have not delivered them.”

(Chapter VI.) And the Lord said to Moses: “Now you shall see what I will do to Pharaoh. For by a strong hand he will let them go, and by a mighty hand he will drive them out of his land.” R\. Amen.

Hymn. “We rise in the morning.” See folio 103.

Capitula. Singing mercy and judgment to you, O Lord, we pray and sing psalms, so that we may walk intelligently in the blameless way; that we may pursue what is right through the prompting of mercy, and correct our errors through fear of judgment.

The Lord’s Prayer. And.

Lauda. Turn my eyes away, so that they may not see vanity. P. And revive me in your way, O Lord. V\. Establish for me, O Lord, the way of your justifications, [Col. 0359B] and I will seek it always. P. And in your way. R\. Glory and honor to the Father. P. And in your way.

Prayer. Turn our eyes away, O Lord, so that they may not see vanity, and revive us in your way. Make us hate the world and love Christ. R\. Amen.

Through.

At Terce.

The Wisdom of Solomon (Chapter X).

R\. Thanks be to God.

My son, those who passed by wisdom fell not only into this error, that they failed to recognize good things, but also left to humanity a memorial of their folly, so that they could not even remain hidden in the things in which they had sinned.

But wisdom delivered from sufferings those who observed her. She delivered the righteous people and the blameless offspring from the nations that oppressed them. She entered the soul of the servant of God and stood against terrible kings with portents and signs. She repaid the righteous for the wages of their labors and led them by a wondrous way. She was a covering for them by day and a light of stars by night. She brought them across the Red Sea and conveyed them through abundant water. But she drowned their enemies in the sea and brought them up from the depths of the underworld.

Therefore the righteous took the spoils of the wicked, and sang out, “Lord,” your holy name, and together praised your victorious hand. R\. Amen.

Reading from the Book of Exodus (Chapter VI).

R\. Thanks be to God.

In those days: The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: “I am the Lord. Speak to Pharaoh, king of Egypt, everything that I speak to you.” And Moses said before the Lord: “Behold, I am uncircumcised of lips; how will Pharaoh listen to me?” (Chapter VII.) And the Lord said to him: “Behold, I have appointed you as God to Pharaoh, and your brother Aaron shall be your prophet. You shall speak everything that I command you, and he shall speak to Pharaoh, so that he may send the children of Israel away from his land. But I shall harden his heart, and multiply my signs and wonders in the land of Egypt, and he shall not listen to you. I shall stretch out my hand over Egypt and bring out my army and my people, the children of Israel, from the land of Egypt by great judgments. And the Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord when I stretch out my hand over Egypt, 202 and bring out the children of Israel from their midst.”

So Moses and Aaron did just as the Lord had commanded; thus they acted. Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron eighty-three, when they spoke to Pharaoh. And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron: “When Pharaoh says to you, ‘Show signs,’ you shall say to Aaron: ‘Take your staff and throw it before Pharaoh, and let it be turned into a serpent.’” Moses and Aaron therefore went in to Pharaoh and did as the Lord had commanded. Aaron took his staff before Pharaoh and his servants, and it was turned into a serpent. Pharaoh, however, called the wise men and the sorcerers; and they too, by their Egyptian enchantments and certain secret arts, did likewise. Each threw down his staff, and they were turned into dragons; but Aaron’s staff swallowed their staffs. [Col. 0360B] Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he did not listen to them, as the Lord had commanded.

And the Lord said to Moses: “Pharaoh’s heart is heavy, and he does not wish to send my people away. Go to him in the morning; behold, he will go out to the waters. Stand to meet him on the bank of the river, and take in your hand the staff that was turned into a dragon. And you shall say to him: ‘The Lord, the God of the Hebrews, sent me to you, saying: Send my people away, so that they may sacrifice to me in the wilderness; and until now you have not been willing to listen. Thus says the Lord: By this you shall know that I am the Lord. Behold, I shall strike the water of the river with the staff that is in my hand, and it shall be turned into blood. The fish also that are in the river shall die, the waters shall become foul, and the Egyptians shall be afflicted when they drink the water of the river.’”

The Lord also said to Moses: “Say to Aaron: ‘Take your staff and stretch out your hand over the waters of Egypt, over their rivers, their channels and marshes, and over all their pools of water, and let them be turned into blood; let there be blood throughout the whole land of Egypt, both in wooden vessels and in stone ones.’”

Moses and Aaron did as the Lord had commanded. Moses lifted up the staff and struck the water of the river before Pharaoh and his servants, and it was turned into blood. The fish that were in the river died; the river became foul, and the Egyptians could not drink the water of the river. There was blood throughout the whole land of Egypt. The Egyptian sorcerers did likewise by their enchantments, and Pharaoh’s heart was hardened; he did not listen to them, as the Lord had commanded. He turned away and entered his house, and he did not set his heart on this matter either. The Egyptians dug around the river for wells in order to drink water, for they could not drink from the water of the river. Seven days were completed after the Lord struck the river.

(Chapter VIII.) And the Lord said to Moses: “Go in to Pharaoh and say to him: ‘Thus says the Lord: Send my people away, so that they may sacrifice to me. But if you refuse to send them away, behold, I shall strike all your borders with frogs. The river shall boil with frogs; they shall go up and enter your house, your bedchamber and your bed, the houses of your servants and your people, your ovens and the remains of your food; frogs shall enter both you, your people, and all your servants.’”

And the Lord said to Moses: “Say to Aaron: ‘Stretch out your hand over the river and its channels and marshes, and bring frogs up over the land of Egypt.’” Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt, and the frogs came up and covered the land of Egypt. The sorcerers also did likewise by their enchantments and brought frogs up over the land of Egypt.

Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron and said to them: “Pray to the Lord to take the frogs away from me and from my people, and I shall send the people away to sacrifice to the Lord.” Moses said to Pharaoh: “Set for me the time when I should pray for you, for your servants, and for your people, so that the frogs may be driven away from you, from your house, from your servants, and from your people, and remain only in the river.” He replied: “Tomorrow.” And Moses said: “According to your word, I shall do this, so that you may know that there is none like the Lord our God. The frogs shall withdraw from you, from your house, from your servants, and from your people; they shall remain only in the river.”

Moses and Aaron went out from Pharaoh, and Moses cried to the Lord concerning the promise about the frogs that he had made to Pharaoh. The Lord acted according to Moses’ word, and the frogs died in the houses, the villages, and the fields. They gathered them into immense heaps, and the land became foul. When Pharaoh saw that relief had been granted, he hardened his heart and did not listen to them, as the Lord had commanded.

And the Lord said to Moses: “Say to Aaron: ‘Stretch out your staff and strike the dust of the earth, and let there be gnats throughout the whole land of Egypt.’” They did so. Aaron stretched out his hand, holding the staff, and struck the dust of the earth; gnats came upon human beings and animals. All the dust of the earth throughout the whole land of Egypt became gnats. The sorcerers likewise acted by their enchantments in order to bring out gnats, but they could not. The gnats were upon human beings and animals. And the sorcerers said to Pharaoh: “This is the finger of God.” But Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he did not listen, as the Lord had commanded.

And the Lord said to Moses: “Rise early and stand before Pharaoh, for he will go out to the waters. Say to him: ‘Thus says the Lord: Send my people away, so that they may sacrifice to me. But if you do not send him away, behold, I shall send upon you, your servants, your people, and your houses every kind of fly. The houses of the Egyptians shall be filled with flies of various kinds, and also the whole land in which they shall be. On that day I shall make the land of Goshen, where my people is, remarkable, so that there will be no flies there; and you shall know that I am the Lord in the midst of the land. I shall establish a division between my people and your people; tomorrow this sign shall occur.’”

And the Lord did so. A very grievous swarm of flies came into Pharaoh’s house and the houses of his servants, and throughout the whole land of Egypt; the land was corrupted by such flies. Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron and said to them: “Go, sacrifice to your God in the land.” And Moses said: “It cannot be done in this way, for we shall sacrifice to the Lord our God the abominations of the Egyptians. If we sacrifice before their eyes what the Egyptians worship, they will stone us. We shall go a three-days’ journey into the wilderness and sacrifice to the Lord our God, as he has commanded us.”

Pharaoh said: “I shall send you away to sacrifice to the Lord your God in the wilderness; nevertheless, do not go farther away. Pray for me.” And Moses said: “When I have gone out from you, I shall pray to the Lord, and tomorrow the fly shall depart from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people. But do not deceive us any longer by refusing to send the people away to sacrifice to the Lord.” Moses went out from Pharaoh and prayed to the Lord, who acted according to his words. R. Amen.

**Antiphon 1.** Let our cry reach you, O Lord, and do not turn your face away from us. **Psalm CI.**

[Col. 0362B] **Prayer.** Hear our prayer, O God, and, with every impediment removed, let our cry reach you. On whatever day we call upon you, may our prayer quickly become known to you. Do not turn your face away from our groans, nor withhold your governance from our conduct, so that we may rejoice in obtaining what we ask, while our desires have reached you. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon 2.** The nations shall fear your name, O Lord, and all the kings of the earth your glory. **Psalm CI.** And they shall fear.

**Prayer.** Arise, O God, and have mercy on Zion, because the time for showing us mercy has come. Look upon the prayer of our poverty and embrace the plea of your humble servants. R. Amen.

[Col. 0362C] Through the mercy of our God.

**Antiphon 3.** As a father has mercy on his children, so God has had mercy on those who fear him. **Psalm CII.**

R. Let us all cry out to the Lord with our whole heart, and let each person turn away from his sins.  
P. And the God of heaven will turn back from the anger of his fury, because he is merciful.  
V. Turn back and withdraw from all your iniquities, and turn your faces away from all your defilements.  
P. And the God of heaven will turn back.  
V. Glory and honor to the Father, etc. Let R. be repeated.

**Prayers.** Show us mercy, O Lord; grant forgiveness; bestow pardon.  
P. And, appeased, have mercy.  
V. Almighty, Unbegotten One, most holy Father of the Only-Begotten, receive our prayer.  
P. And have mercy.  
V. Spare all, we ask; spare those who ask; assist those who mourn; pardon those who repent.  
P. And have mercy.  
V. Rescue the souls of those at rest from hell, holy Lord; restore them to paradise.  
P. And have mercy.  
V. Christ, who possesses the heavens, redeeming the world, most merciful God, cleanse our sins.  
P. And have mercy.

**Hymn.** O Nazarene, Light. Folio 144.

**Capitulum.** May our soul bless you, O Lord, and may all its inward parts cry out in your praises, so that, having heard our prayer, you may hasten to heal our infirmities, redeem our life from destruction, satisfy our desire with good things, and crown our vow with perfection.

**Our Father.**

## At Sext

[Col. 0363A]

**Reading from the Book of the Prophet Jeremiah (Chapter III).**

R. Thanks be to God.

Thus says the Lord: “Turn back, returning children, and I shall heal your apostasies.” Behold, we come to you, for you are the Lord our God. Truly the hills were deceitful, the multitude of the mountains; truly in the Lord our God is the salvation of Israel. Shame has consumed the labor of our fathers from our youth: their flocks and their herds, the sons of Israel and their daughters. We shall sleep in our shame, and our disgrace shall cover us, because we have sinned against the Lord our God, we and our fathers, from our youth to this day, and we have not listened to the voice of our God.

(Chapter IV.) “If you return to me, Israel,” says the Lord, “return to me. If you remove your offenses from my sight, you shall not be moved. And you shall swear: ‘The Lord lives in truth, in judgment, and in righteousness’; and the nations shall bless him and praise him.” R. Amen.

**Antiphon 1.** The Lord remembered us and blessed us. **Psalm CXIII.**

**Prayer.** Remember us, O Lord, and bless us. Lest we turn away from you with a forgetful mind, bring us back into your remembrance; and just as you freed Israel from Egypt through signs, so may you deem us worthy to separate us from worldly defilement. R. Amen.

Through your mercy, etc.

**Antiphon 2.** Fill our mouth, O God, with joy, and our tongue with exultation. **Psalm CXXV.**

[Col. 0363C] **Prayer.** Fill our mouth, O Lord, with joy, and enrich our tongue with exultation, so that we who sow the word of life in tears may reap the fruit of righteousness with joy. R. Amen.

Through.

**Antiphon 3.** Blessed are all who fear the Lord and walk in his ways. **Psalm CXXVIII.**

R. Stretch out your hand over your servants, O Lord, and free us  
P. from tribulation.  
V. Save us in your name, O God, and deliver us by your power.  
P. From tribulation.  
V. Glory and honor to the Father. Let R. be repeated.

**Prayers.** Hear our prayers, O Lord.  
P. And have mercy on us.  
V. Attend, O Lord, from your sanctuary.  
P. And have mercy on us.  
V. Grant forgiveness to those who confess the evils they have committed.  
P. And have mercy on us.  
V. Always renew the Catholic Church in goodness.  
P. And have mercy on us.  
V. Pardon those who have fallen, and spare our sins.  
P. And have mercy on us.

**Hymn.** O Nazarene, Light. See folio 144.

**Prayer.** O God, who through the prophetic voice declares blessed those who fear you, grant within us the pleasing service of your fear, so that from this you may cause us to walk in your ways. Under your guidance, may our labor be pleasing in your eyes, and may its fruit become most sweet at the time of reward. Thus may our labor itself strive through charity, so that its fruits may be stored up with you in blessedness.

**Our Father.**

## At None

[Col. 0364A]

**The Wisdom of Solomon (Chapter XI).**

R. Thanks be to God.

Child, when the children of Israel were flourishing, they rejoiced; through the very things by which they were deprived, it went well with them. For instead of the fountain of an everlasting river, you gave the unjust human blood. When they were diminished through the destruction of the infants who had been killed, you gave them abundant water unexpectedly, showing through the thirst that then afflicted them how you would exalt your own and destroy their adversaries. For when they were tested—and indeed received discipline with mercy—they learned how the impious, judged in anger, suffer torments. You tested these as a father admonishing them; but those you condemned as a stern king questioning them. For absent and present alike were tortured. A twofold weariness had seized them, and groaning together with the memory of former things. But when they heard that things had gone well with the others through their own torments, they remembered the Lord, marveling at the outcome in the end. For the one whom they had derided when cast out in disgrace, at the end of the event they wondered at. You did not act similarly toward the righteous, because as the moment of the balance is before you, so is the whole world. For you have mercy on all, and you can do all things, and you overlook the sins of human beings for the sake of repentance. R. Amen.

**Reading from the Book of Exodus (Chapter IX).**

R. Thanks be to God.

In those days: The Lord said to Moses: “Go in to Pharaoh and speak to him: ‘Thus says the Lord, the God of the Hebrews: Send my people away, so that they may sacrifice to me. But if you still refuse and retain them, behold, my hand shall be upon your fields, your horses, camels, sheep, and oxen: a very severe pestilence. The Lord shall make a distinction between the possessions of Israel and the possessions of the Egyptians, so that nothing at all shall perish of what belongs to the children of Israel.’”

And the Lord set a time, saying: “Tomorrow the Lord shall do this thing in the land of Egypt.” The next day the Lord did this thing: all the livestock of the Egyptians died, but none at all of the animals of the children of Israel perished. Pharaoh sent to see, and nothing was dead of what Israel possessed. But Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he did not send the people away.

And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron: “Take handfuls of ashes from the furnace, and let Moses scatter them toward heaven before Pharaoh. Let the dust be over the whole land of Egypt; for there shall be sores and swelling blisters upon human beings and animals throughout the whole land of Egypt.” They took ashes from the furnace and stood before Pharaoh, and Moses scattered them toward heaven. There arose swelling blister-sores upon human beings and animals. The sorcerers could not stand before Moses because of the sores that were upon them and throughout the whole land of Egypt. The Lord hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he did not listen to them, as the Lord had commanded them.

[Col. 0365A] And the Lord said to Moses: “Rise early, stand before Pharaoh, and say to him: ‘Thus says the Lord, the God of the Hebrews: Send my people away, so that they may sacrifice to me. For this time I shall send all my plagues upon your heart, upon your servants, and upon your people, so that you may know that there is none like me in all the earth. For now, stretching out my hand, I shall strike you and your people with pestilence, and you shall perish from the land. For this reason I have appointed you, to show my strength in you, and so that my name may be proclaimed throughout all the earth. Do you still retain my people and refuse to send them away? Behold, tomorrow at this very hour I shall rain down very heavy hail, such as has never been in Egypt from the day it was founded until the present time. Therefore send now and gather your livestock and everything you have in the field. For the human beings, animals, and all that are found outside and not gathered in from the fields—hail shall fall upon them, and they shall die.’”

Whoever feared the word of the Lord among Pharaoh’s servants made his servants and animals flee into the houses; but whoever disregarded the Lord’s word left his servants and animals in the fields.

And the Lord said to Moses: “Stretch out your hand toward heaven, so that hail may fall throughout the land of Egypt, upon human beings, animals, and every plant of the field in the land of Egypt.” Moses stretched out his staff toward heaven, and the Lord gave thunder and hail, with lightning flashing across the land of Egypt. Hail and fire mingled together and fell; it was of such great magnitude that nothing like it had ever appeared throughout the whole land of Egypt since that nation was founded. The hail struck everything that was in the fields throughout the whole land of Egypt, from human being to animal; it struck every plant of the field and shattered every tree of the region. Only in the land of Goshen, where the children of Israel were, did the hail not fall.

Pharaoh sent for Moses and Aaron and said to them: “I have sinned even now. The Lord is righteous; I and my people are impious. Pray to the Lord, and let God’s thunder and the hail cease; then I shall send you away, and you shall no longer remain here.” Moses said: “When I have gone out of the city, I shall stretch out my palms to the Lord, and the thunder shall cease, and there shall be no more hail, so that you may know that the earth belongs to the Lord. But I know that neither you nor your servants yet fear the Lord God.”

The flax and the barley were damaged, because the barley was green and the flax had already produced pods; but the wheat and spelt were not damaged, because they were late crops. Moses went out from Pharaoh, from the city, and stretched out his hands to the Lord; the thunder and hail ceased. R. Amen.

**Canticle of Jeremiah (Chapter V of the Lamentations).**

Remember, O Lord, what has happened to us; * look and see our disgrace.

Our inheritance has been turned over to strangers, * our houses to foreigners.

We have become orphans, as though we had no father; * our mothers are like widows.

We bought our water with money, * and purchased our wood at a price.

We were driven on at the neck; * when exhausted, we were given no rest.

We gave our hand to Egypt * and to the Assyrians, so that we might be satisfied with bread.

Our fathers sinned and are no more; * but we have borne their iniquities.

Servants have ruled over us, * and there is no one to redeem us from their hands.

With our own hands we acquired our bread, * in the face of the sword and the wilderness.

Our skin, like an oven, has become livid * because of blows and hunger.

Women were humbled in Zion, * and virgins in the cities of Judah.

Princes were hanged by their hands, * and they did not honor the faces of elders.

The chosen ones were turning millstones, * and young men were fastened to the wood.

The elders failed at the gate, * and the chosen ceased from their songs.

The joy of our heart has been dissolved; * our chorus has been turned into mourning.

The crown has fallen from our head; * woe to us now, because we have sinned.

[Col. 0367D] Because of this our heart has become sorrowful, and our eyes have grown dim, * so that they do not see Mount Zion, because it has been destroyed; foxes have passed through it.

But you, O Lord, remain forever, * and your throne is for age upon age.

207 Why do you forget us in the struggle? * Do you forsake us for the length of our days?

Turn us back to yourself, O God, and we shall turn back; * renew our days as before.

For rejecting, you have utterly rejected us; * you have been exceedingly angry with us.

**Matutinarium.**

**At Benedictus. Antiphon.** They kept watch before dawn and came to him; * and they remembered that the Lord is their helper.

**Reading from the Book of Exodus (Chapter IX).**

R. Thanks be to God.

In those days: When Pharaoh saw that the rain, hail, and thunder had ceased, he increased his sin; the heart of Pharaoh and his servants was hardened and became exceedingly obstinate, and he did not send the children of Israel away, as the Lord had commanded through Moses.

(Chapter X.) And the Lord said to Moses: “Go in to Pharaoh, for I have hardened his heart and the hearts of his servants, so that I may perform these signs of mine among them, and so that you may tell your sons and your grandsons how often I crushed the Egyptians, and the signs that I performed among them; and you shall know that I am the Lord.”

Moses and Aaron went in to Pharaoh and said to him: “Send my people away, so that they may sacrifice to me. But if you do not wish to send him away, behold, tomorrow I shall bring locusts into your borders. They shall cover the face of the earth, so that none of it shall be visible, but what remains after the hail shall be eaten; for they shall gnaw every tree that sprouts in the fields. They shall fill your houses, the houses of your servants, and the houses of all the Egyptians, such as your fathers have not seen from the day they arose upon the earth until the present day.”

He turned away and went out from Pharaoh. Pharaoh’s servants said to him: “How long shall we endure this scandal? Send the people away, so that they may sacrifice to the Lord their God. Do you not see that Egypt has perished?” They called Moses and Aaron back to Pharaoh, and he said to them: “Go, sacrifice to the Lord your God. Who are the ones who will go?” Moses said: “We shall go with our little ones and our elders, with our sons and daughters, with our sheep and herds, for it is the solemn feast of the Lord our God.”

Pharaoh replied: “May the Lord be with you in the same way that I shall send you and your little ones away! Who can doubt that you are planning something evil? It shall not be so; go only, you men, and sacrifice to the Lord, for this is what you yourselves requested.” And they were immediately driven out from Pharaoh’s presence.

The Lord said to Moses: “Stretch out your hand over the land of Egypt for the locust, so that it may rise upon it and devour every plant that the hail has left.” Moses stretched out his staff over the land of Egypt, and the Lord brought an arid wind all that day and night. When morning came, the wind lifted the locusts, which rose over the whole land of Egypt and settled throughout all the borders of Egypt in countless numbers, such as had never been before and would never be afterward. They covered everything over the face of the earth, devastating it all. Every plant of the land and all the fruit on the trees that the hail had left were devoured; nothing green at all remained on the trees or in the plants of the earth throughout all Egypt.

Therefore Pharaoh hastened to call Moses and Aaron and said to them: “I have sinned against the Lord your God and against you. But now forgive me my sin this time also, and pray to the Lord your God, so that he may take this death away from me.” Moses went out from Pharaoh’s presence and prayed to the Lord. He caused a very strong west wind to blow, seized the locusts, and cast them into the Red Sea. R. Amen.

## At Terce

**The Wisdom of Solomon (Chapter III).**

R. Thanks be to God.

Child, unhappy is the one who rejects wisdom and discipline; their hope is empty, their labors fruitless, and their works useless. Their women are senseless, and their children exceedingly wicked. Their offspring is accursed, for blessed is the barren woman who is undefiled, who has not known a marriage-bed in sin; she shall have fruit when holy souls are examined. And the eunuch who has not done evil with his hands nor conceived wickedness against the Lord shall receive the chosen gift of faith and a most acceptable portion in the temple of the Lord. For glorious is the fruit of good labors, and the root of wisdom does not fail. But the children of adulterers shall be brought to an end, and offspring from an unlawful bed shall be exterminated. Even if they live long, they shall be counted as nothing, and their final old age shall be without honor. And if they die sooner, they shall have no hope, nor an answer on the day of greatness.

(Chapter IV.) For a generation with honor is better, since its memory is immortal; it is known both to God and to human beings, and, crowned forever, it triumphs. R. Amen.

**Reading from the Book of Exodus (Chapter X).**

R. Thanks be to God.

In those days: The Lord said to Moses: “Stretch out your hand toward heaven, and let there be darkness over the land of Egypt, so thick that it may be felt.” Moses stretched out his hand toward heaven, and terrible darkness arose throughout the whole land of Egypt for three days. No brother saw his brother, nor did anyone move from the place where he was; but wherever the children of Israel dwelt, there was light.

Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron and said: “Go, sacrifice to the Lord; only let your sheep and herds remain, while your little ones go with you.” Moses said: “You must also give us sacrifices and burnt offerings to offer to the Lord our God. All our flocks shall go with us; not a hoof shall remain behind. For we need them for the worship of the Lord our God, especially since we do not know what must be offered until we reach the place itself.”

The Lord hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he was unwilling to send them away. Pharaoh said to him: “Withdraw from me. Beware of seeing my face again; on whatever day you appear before me, you shall die.” Moses replied: “It shall be as you have spoken; I shall not see your face again.”

(Chapter XI.) And the Lord said to Moses: “I shall strike Pharaoh and Egypt with one more plague only, and after this he shall send you away and compel you to depart. Therefore tell all the people that each man should ask his friend, and each woman her neighbor, for silver and gold vessels. The Lord shall grant the people favor in the sight of the Egyptians.” Moses was a very great man in the land of Egypt, in the sight of Pharaoh’s servants and of all the people.

And Moses said: “Thus says the Lord: At midnight I shall enter Egypt, and every firstborn in the land of the Egyptians shall die, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sits upon his throne to the firstborn of the maidservant who is at the mill, and all the firstborn of the animals. There shall be a great cry throughout the whole land of Egypt, such as there has never been before and shall never be again. But among all the children of Israel not even a dog shall bark, from human being to animal, so that you may know by what a wonder he distinguishes between the Egyptians and Israel. And all these servants of yours shall come down to me and bow before me, saying: ‘Go out, you and all the people who are subject to you’; after this we shall depart.”

And he went out from Pharaoh exceedingly angry. But the Lord said to Moses: “Pharaoh will not listen to you, so that many signs may be performed in the land of Egypt.” Moses and Aaron did all the wonders that are written before Pharaoh. And the Lord hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he did not send the children of Israel away from his land.

(Chapter XII.) It happened at midnight that the Lord struck every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sat upon his throne to the firstborn of the animals. Pharaoh rose at night, together with all his servants and all Egypt, and a great cry arose in Egypt, for there was no house in which someone did not lie dead.

He called Moses and Aaron and said: “Rise, go out from among my people, you and your sons; go, sacrifice to the Lord as you have said. Take your sheep and your herds, as you requested, and depart; bless me also.”

The Egyptians pressed the people to leave the land quickly, saying: “We shall all die.” Therefore the people took the dough they had mixed before it was leavened; binding it in cloaks, they placed it upon their shoulders. 209 The children of Israel did as the Lord had commanded Moses, and they asked the Egyptians for silver and gold vessels and a great deal of clothing. The Lord granted the people favor in the sight of the Egyptians, so that they lent these things to them; and they despoiled the Egyptians.

[Col. 0371A] The children of Israel departed from Rameses for Succoth, about six hundred thousand men on foot, apart from the little ones. An innumerable mixed multitude also went up with them, together with sheep, herds, and very many animals of various kinds. They baked the dough that they had recently brought mixed from Egypt, and made unleavened cakes baked under the ashes, for they could not be leavened, since the Egyptians were pressing them to leave and would not allow them any delay; nor had they prepared any cooked food. The dwelling of the children of Israel in which they remained in Egypt lasted four hundred and thirty years. When these years were completed, on that same day the entire army of the Lord went out from the land of Egypt. R. Amen.

Antiphon. Yours, O Lord, are magnificence, power, [Col. 0373D] and glory; and to you belongs praise.

Canticle (1 Chronicles 29).

Blessed are you, O Lord, God of Israel our father, * from age to age.

Yours, indeed, O Lord, are magnificence, power, glory, and victory, * and to you belongs praise.

For all things in heaven and on earth are yours; * yours is the kingdom, O Lord, and you are above all rulers.

Riches are yours, and glory is yours; * in your hand are strength and power; in your hand are greatness and dominion over men.

Now, therefore, we confess to you, * and we praise your glorious name.

[Col. 0374A] But who am I, * and who is my people, that we should be able to promise you all these things?

All things are yours, * and what we have received from your hand, we have given to you.

For we are strangers before you, * and sojourners, like all our fathers.

Our days are like a shadow upon the earth, * and there is no delay.

O Lord my God, all this abundance that I have gathered to build a house for your holy name * is from your hand.

I know, my God, that you test hearts, * and that you love integrity.

Therefore, in the integrity of my heart, I have gladly offered all these things; * and I have seen your people, who are found here, offer gifts to you with great joy.

O Lord, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, our fathers, * preserve forever this purpose of their hearts, and may this mind always remain in your reverence.

Prayer. We beseech you, Lord of the most abundant generosity, that we may receive from your hand an abundance of heavenly gifts, which we may prepare for you in order to establish your house in our hearts; that with simple vows we may offer you what is yours, and praise your glorious name with manifold confession. R\. Amen.

At the Benedictus. Antiphon. May the splendor of the Lord [Col. 0374C] our God be upon us. P. Direct the works of our hands for us. V\. Look upon your servants and upon your works, and direct their children. P. And the works of our hands.

Reading from the Book of Exodus (chapter 17).

R\. Thanks be to God.

In those days: The whole multitude of the children of Israel departed from the wilderness of Sin by their stages, according to the word of the Lord, and encamped at Rephidim, where there was no water for the people to drink. They quarreled with Moses and said: “Give us water, that we may drink.” Moses answered them: “Why do you quarrel with me? Why do you test the Lord?” Thus the people thirsted there because of the lack of water and murmured against Moses: “Why did you bring us out of Egypt—to kill us, our children, and our livestock with thirst?” Moses cried out to the Lord, saying: “What shall I do with this people? A little more, and they will stone me.”

The Lord said to Moses: “Go before the people, and take with you some of the elders of Israel. Take in your hand the staff with which you struck the river, and go. Behold, I shall stand before you there upon the rock at Horeb. You shall strike the rock, and water will come out of it, so that the people may drink.” Moses did so before the elders of Israel. He called the name of that place “Temptation,” because of the quarrel of the children of Israel and because they tested God, saying: “Is God among us or not?”

Then Amalek came and fought [Col. 0375A] against the children of Israel at Rephidim. Moses said to Joshua: “Choose men, and go out to fight against Amalek tomorrow. I shall stand on the top of the hill, holding the staff of God in my hand.” Joshua did as Moses had said and fought against Amalek. But Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill. When Moses raised his hands, Israel prevailed; but when he lowered them a little, Amalek overcame them. Moses’ hands grew heavy. So they took a stone and placed it beneath him, and he sat upon it; while Aaron and Hur supported his hands on either side. And his hands did not grow weary until sunset. Joshua put Amalek and his people to flight with the edge of the sword.

The Lord said to Moses: “Write this as a memorial in a book and give it to Joshua’s ears, for I shall blot out the memory of Amalek from under heaven.” Moses built an altar to the Lord and called its name “The Lord is my exaltation.”

Hymn. God, creator of all. Fol. 175.
