R\. Thanks be to God.

My son, like a bird migrating from its place is a man who abandons his place. The heart is delighted by perfume and various fragrances, and the soul is sweetened by the good counsel of a friend. Do not forsake your friend or your father’s friend on the day of your affliction, and do not enter your brother’s house on the day of your affliction. A neighbor nearby is better than a brother far away.

Strive after wisdom, my son, and gladden my heart, so that you may be able to answer him who reproaches you with a word. The prudent person sees evil and hides himself; the simple pass by and suffer loss. Take away his garment who guarantees for a stranger, and seize a pledge from him on behalf of foreigners. Whoever blesses his neighbor with a loud voice, rising at night, will be like one who curses him. Iron is sharpened by iron, and a man sharpens the face of his friend.

Sheol and destruction are never filled; likewise the eyes of men are never satisfied. An evil heart seeks evil, but an upright heart seeks knowledge. R\. Amen.

Reading from the Book of Exodus (chapter 18).

R\. Thanks be to God.

In those days: When Jethro, the priest of Midian and Moses’ kinsman, heard all that God had done for Moses and for his people Israel, how the Lord had brought Israel out of Egypt, he took Zipporah, Moses’ wife whom he had sent away, and her two sons. One was called Gershom, his father saying: “I was a stranger in a foreign land.” The other was Eliezer: “For,” he said, “the God of my father is my helper, and he rescued me from the hand of Pharaoh.”

So Jethro, Moses’ kinsman, came, together with Moses’ wife and his sons, to Moses in the wilderness, where he was encamped beside the mountain of God. He sent word to Moses, saying: “I, your kinsman Jethro, am coming to you, together with your wife and your two sons with her.”

Moses went out to meet his kinsman, bowed down, and kissed him; and they greeted one another with words of peace. When they had entered the tent, Moses told his kinsman everything that the Lord had done to Pharaoh [Col. 0376B] and the Egyptians for Israel’s sake, and all the hardship that had befallen them on the journey by which the Lord had delivered them.

Jethro rejoiced over all that God had done for Israel, because he had rescued him from the hand of the Egyptians, and he said: “Blessed is the Lord, who delivered us from the hand of the Egyptians and from the hand of Pharaoh, who rescued his people from the hand of Egypt. Now I know that the Lord is greater than all gods, because they acted arrogantly against them.”

Then Jethro, Moses’ kinsman, offered burnt offerings and sacrifices to God. Aaron and all the elders of Israel came and ate bread with him before the Lord.

The next day Moses sat to judge the people, and they stood around Moses from morning until evening. When Moses’ kinsman saw everything he was doing among the people, he said: “What is this that you are doing among the people? Why do you sit alone while the whole people wait from morning until evening?”

Moses answered him: “The people come to me seeking God’s decision. Whenever any dispute arises among them, they come to me to judge between them, and I make known the precepts of God and his law.”

He replied: “You are not doing a good thing. You will wear yourself out with foolish labor, both you and this people who are with you. The task is beyond your strength; you cannot bear it alone. But hear my words and counsel, and God will be with you.

“Be the people’s representative in matters pertaining to God, so that you may bring their words to him. Show the people the ceremonies and the rite of worship, the way in which they must walk, and the work they must do.

“Provide from the whole people capable men who fear God, in whom there is truth, who hate avarice; appoint them over the people as tribunes, centurions, commanders of fifty, and commanders of ten. Let them judge the people at all times. Whatever is more serious, let them refer to you, while they themselves judge only the lesser matters. Thus the burden will be lighter for you, when the responsibility is divided among others.

“If you do this, you will fulfill God’s command, and you will be able to sustain his precepts; and all this people will return in peace to their homes.”

When Moses heard this, he did all that Jethro had suggested. Choosing capable men from all Israel, he appointed them leaders over Israel—tribunes, centurions, commanders of fifty, and commanders of ten. They judged the people at all times; whatever was more serious, they referred to him, judging only the easier matters. Then he dismissed his kinsman, who returned and went to his own home. R\. Amen.

Antiphon 1. The Lord is merciful, compassionate, and just. Kind is the man who has mercy. Psalm 111.

Prayer. Merciful and just Lord, make us always merciful and wholly ready to assist one another with every kindness. Do not frighten us with an evil hearing when you judge us, but set us at your right hand, to be glorified. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Antiphon 2. I have known how great the Lord is, and our God is above all gods. Psalm 134.

[Col. 0377B] Prayer. Lord, who brings forth clouds from the end of the earth and has filled the whole world with holy teachers, mercifully turn lightning into rain, so that you may refresh with blessing those whom you terrify with your commands in order to correct them, and bless more abundantly those filled with your grace. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

Antiphon 3. Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy endures forever. Psalm 136.

R\. We have sinned against you, O God; show mercy. P. And before we perish, may your hand deliver us. V\. Why will you forget us forever and abandon us for the length of days? P. And before we perish.

Prayers. We ask forgiveness, O Christ; hear us. P. Be appeased and have mercy. V\. Jesus, only-begotten Son of God the Father, Lord of immense goodness. P. Be appeased. V\. We all beseech you with groans; and together we all entreat you. P. Be appeased. V\. May your clemency now overcome our evils; look upon us now with your serene face. P. Be appeased. V\. We ask remission of all sins; merciful one, we beseech you, forgive the evils we have committed. P. Be appeased and have mercy.

Hymn. O Nazarene, light. See fol. 144.

Capitulum. To you, O Lord, we confess, who made the heavens by understanding and exalt the learned by wisdom; who founded the earth upon the waters and raised your Church above the passing age. Grant that the fluid delights of the world may not overwhelm us, but that the virtues we have received may lift us to heavenly things.

[Col. 0377D] Our Father. And lead us not.

At Sext.

Reading from the Book of the Prophet Ezekiel (chapter 33).

R\. Thanks be to God.

The word of the Lord came to me, saying: “Son of man, speak to the house of Israel: Thus you have spoken, saying: ‘Our iniquities and our sins are upon us, and in them we waste away. How, then, can we live?’ Say to them: ‘As I live,’ says the Lord God, ‘I do not desire the death of the wicked, but that the wicked turn from his way and live. Turn back from your evil ways. Why will you die, O house of Israel?’

“You, therefore, son of man, say to the children of your people: ‘The righteousness of the righteous man will not deliver him on whatever day he sins, and the wickedness of the wicked man will not harm him on whatever day he turns from his iniquity; nor will the righteous man be able to live by his righteousness on whatever day he sins.

“‘Even if I say to the righteous man that he shall surely live, and, trusting in his righteousness, he commits iniquity, all his righteousness shall be consigned to oblivion, and in the iniquity he has committed, in that he shall die.

“‘But if I say to the wicked man, “You shall surely die,” and he repents of his sin, does what is just and right, restores the pledge, returns what he has stolen, walks in the commandments of life, and does nothing unjust, he shall surely live and shall not die.’ Thus says the Lord God almighty.” R\. Amen.

Antiphon 1. The Lord raises up those who are bowed down; the Lord sets free those who are bound. The Lord gives light to the blind; the Lord loves the righteous. Psalm 145.

Prayer. O Lord, who raise up those who are bowed down, set free those who are bound, and give light to the blind: raise us also when our falls bend us down; free us when sins bind us round; and enlighten us when the darkness of ignorance surrounds us. May our soul always praise you, and may our life be humble in faithful devotion. Since what we are is your gift, may everything we live serve you. R\. Amen.

Through.

Antiphon 2. He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds. Great is the Lord, and great is his power. Psalm 146.

Prayer. O God, who heal the brokenhearted, grant healing to our wounds; and you who number the multitude of the stars, join us to those predestined for life, so that we may be pleasing to you and that you may command us to be exalted in eternal salvation. R\. Amen.

Through.

Antiphon 3. Our eyes are toward the Lord our God until he has mercy on us. Psalm 122.

R\. Have mercy, for you are God. P. Merciful one, have mercy, for we have sinned against you. V\. To you we lift our eyes, who dwell in the heavens. P. Merciful one, have mercy.

Prayers. May your mercy come to our aid, O Lord. P. Quickly. V\. Glorious God, understand our cry with patience. P. Quickly. V\. Attend to our prayers and grant us what we ask. P. Quickly. V\. Father, free us from every evil by your right hand. P. Quickly. V\. O Lord, hear the prayers of the humble with kindly ears. P. Quickly. V\. Wipe away from our senses the zeal of sin and hatred. P. Quickly. V\. Remove every danger and, appeased, justify us. P. Quickly. V\. Kindly attend and receive the supplications of all who groan. P. Quickly. V\. When you come as judge of all, be the support of the redeemed. P. Quickly.

Hymn. O Nazarene, light. Fol. 144.

Capitulum. As the eyes of servants are upon the hands of their masters, so are ours upon you, O Lord, until you remit the offense of sinners, lessen the wounds of those who are beaten, give food to the needy, and grant healing to the wounded.

Our Father.

## ON THE THIRD SUNDAY OF LENT

[Col. 0379A]

At Vespers.

Laud. Offer the evening sacrifice. P. And hope in the Lord, children of men. V\. Give thanks to the Lord and call upon his name. P. And hope.

May the Lord be with you. R\. And with you.

Antiphon. Let us examine the ways of the Lord and question our hearts, whether they are not double-minded. P. And so let us stand before the face of God with a pure heart and not with a divided tongue. V\. For the Lord will not reject his people, nor abandon his inheritance. P. And so let us stand.

May the Lord be with you. R\. And with you.

Laud. It is good for me that you humbled me, O God, so that I may learn your ordinances. P. Better for me is the law of your mouth than thousands of gold and silver. V\. You have dealt well with your servant, O Lord, according to your word. P. Better for me.

Hymn.

Christ, immense, holy Ruler,

Guard the people whom you redeemed

With your sacred, precious blood;

You yourself saved them.

Glory shines forth, and the Lord acted;

He came to Bethany, to Lazarus,

Whom he raised, and manifested

His glory.

But Mary, kept at home,

Awaited him; with immense devotion

Her sister Martha came to meet him

And announced it to her.

“The Teacher is here.” The sisters come,

And, weeping and confessing Christ,

They were found worthy to see

Their brother rising again.

At the tomb Jesus cried out:

“Lazarus, come; the Lord is with you.”

He rose, and the whole crowd

Was converted there.

In Samaria, as a man, he thirsted,

And forgave the woman her sins;

The man born blind, indeed, saw

The great light at Siloam.

In Samaria he made them confess;

In Bethany, he raised Lazarus;

He made the deaf hear and the mute speak—

Those whom he visited.

Glory to the Father, the eternal Trinity;

Glory to Christ and to the Holy Spirit.

With devout voice let every age

Proclaim the name of the Trinity.

R\. Amen.

Supplication. Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world, etc.

Capitulum. Now, with the course of the fourteenth day of the tithes of our days already completed, we lift our eyes to you, O Lord, who dwell in the heavens. Bestow mercy upon the wretched and extend healing to the wounded. Make the path we have undertaken peaceful for us. Direct our hearts along the paths of your commandments. Through you may we find the way of light; through you may we grasp the luminous fires of your love. Grant rest to those who labor, and a dwelling to those who are weary, so that, pleasing you through the observance of these days, we may deserve to share in your glory.

Our Father.

Humble yourselves for the blessing.

May the Lord be with you. R\. And with your spirit.

Blessing. May Christ, the Son of God, look favorably upon your labors and dispel the darkness of your hearts by enlightening them. R\. Amen. May your paths also be so happily directed according to his commandments that you may always deserve to obtain the fruit of his ordinances. R\. Amen. May he favorably assist the course of your labor and, in his mercy, illumine the darkness of your blindness. R\. Amen.

Through.

May the Lord be with you. R\. And with your spirit.

Laud. My soul has languished for your salvation. P. And I have hoped in your word, O Lord. V\. My eyes have failed while awaiting your promise, saying: “When will you comfort me?” P. And in your word. V\. Glory and honor to the Father, etc. P. And in your word.

Prayer. Our soul has languished for your salvation, O Lord; may it advance through tireless desire by the gift of overflowing grace, destined to receive consolation as its reward. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Laud 2. You have dealt well with your servant, O Lord. P. According to your word, justify me. V\. You have dealt well with your servant, O Lord, because I have believed your commandments. P. According to your word. V\. Glory. P. According to your word.

Prayer. Teach us goodness, discipline, and knowledge, O Lord, so that neither wickedness may make us harsh, nor sloth make us negligent, nor foolishness make us lazy. R\. Amen.

Psalm. Have mercy on me, O God. Entire, with Gloria. And Kyrie, eleison. Christ, have mercy. Kyrie, eleison.

Our Father. And lead us not.

Prayers. Lord of mercies. P. Forget our sins. V\. You who gave life to the dead, light to the blind, and hearing to the deaf. P. Forget them. V\. You who gave speech to the mute, walking to the lame, and health to lepers. P. Forget them. V\. You who endured injuries to our flesh in your own body. P. Forget them.

[Col. 0380D] Prayer. Hear our prayer. Fol. 138.

At Matins.

Hymn. Eternal maker of all things. Fol. 3.

Prayer. The voice of all the faithful sings you as the eternal Lord and creator of all things, who establish fixed boundaries and set the limits by which night is separated from day, appointing them by eternal law. For the abyss of your wisdom, so as to relieve the weariness of mortals, has assigned one thing to labor and preserved another for rest. Grant, therefore, almighty God, that while the weary mind is admonished by the crowing of the rooster, it may run eagerly back to the hope of light and always devote the first fruits of the day’s labor to your service. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Antiphon 1. O Lord, why are those who trouble me so many? But you, O Lord, are my protector. Psalm 3.

Antiphon 2. Blot out my iniquities, O Lord. Psalm 50.

Antiphon 3. My soul trusts in you. Psalm 56.

Prayer. O Lord God, with whom those who confess find the healing of salvation: erase the wounds of sin from human hearts; show us the radiant face of your clemency; incline your holy ear to the cries of those who supplicate. Pour the gift of your grace into our minds and grant those who ask the remedy they seek. Since we rise to undertake the duty of our service, pour upon your people an abundance of blessing and salvation. Mercifully erase the crime contracted and make us free from the guilt of wrongdoing. Hear the groans of those who ask; bestow the fruit of forgiveness; and grant to each faithful petitioner who knocks the aid requested. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Antiphon 1. Turn us, O God our Savior. P. And turn your anger away from us. Do not be angry with us forever. V\. You, O God, will turn and revive us, and your people will rejoice in you. P. And turn your anger away. V\. Glory and honor.

Prayer. Turn us to yourself, O God our Savior, so that you may turn your anger away from us; for there will be respite if you suspend your fury. Let clemency be near, so that anger may be far away. Turn us, so that in your mercy you may heal our wounds; do not, having justly turned away because of sin, multiply our wounds instead. Therefore we ask that compassion anticipate justice and forgiveness forestall punishment. Turn us also to yourself, so that you may grant salvation and withdraw vengeance. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Antiphon 2. Judge the orphan and the needy. P. Justify the humble and the poor. Rescue the poor and needy; deliver him from the hand of the sinner. P. The poor and needy. V\. Glory and honor.

Prayer. Rise up, O Lord, who judge the earth, and who, as their gracious possessor, dwell in the faith of all nations. Do not allow us to remain in darkness, but make us behold the light of your truth, so that we may not build the foundations of our faith upon sand, which a whirlwind could cast down, but place them upon the rock, whose firmness you are. [Col. 0381D] R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Antiphon 3. You are our refuge, O Lord, from the oppression that surrounds us. P. For the scourges of our sins are many. V\. For this every holy person will pray to you at an opportune time. P. Many. V\. Glory and honor.

Prayer. Grant us remission of sins, O Lord, who bestow blessedness upon the purified. Be our refuge from the oppression of condemnation, you who grant freedom. Since we feel the many scourges of sins upon us when the wound strikes, grant that, trusting in you, we may feel ourselves surrounded by your mercy. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

[Col. 0382A] R\. Who will comfort you, virgin daughter of Zion, for your crushing is great as the sea? Pour out your heart like water. P. In the sight of the Lord, lift up your hands to him for the healing of your sins. V\. Let your tears flow like a torrent by day and by night, and let the pupils of your eyes not be silent. P. In the sight of the Lord. V\. Glory and honor.

Prayer. Comfort us, O Lord, in our tribulation. We are daily saddened by our sins; pierce our hearts so that we may pour out tears like water in your sight. Thus, lifting our hands to you, may we never be cast down in human praises, but, mindful of you, in whom all glory resides, may we rejoice. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

[Col. 0382B] At Lauds.

At the Canticle. Antiphon. As a woman near childbirth is close to giving birth and cries out in her labor, so we have become for the beloved. Because of your fear, O Lord, we conceived in the womb and gave birth to the spirit of salvation, which you made upon the earth.

Canticle. He keeps vigil through the night. Fol. 64.

At the Benedictus. Antiphon. In the morning I shall stand before you and see you, for you are God who does not will iniquity. V\. Hear my words, O Lord; understand my cry. Attend to the voice of my prayer, my king and my God. For to you I shall pray, O Lord.

Canticle. Blessed are you, O Lord. See fol. 6.

Laud. Praise the Lord from the heavens, all stars and light; heavens of heavens, and waters that are above [Col. 0382C] the heavens. P. Let them praise the name of the Lord. V\. Kings of the earth and all peoples, princes and all judges of the earth. P. Let them praise.

Reading from the Book of Numbers (chapter 13).

R\. Thanks be to God.

In those days, the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

“Send men to inspect the land of Canaan, which I am about to give to the children of Israel—one from each tribe, from among its princes.”

Moses did as the Lord had commanded, sending principal men from the desert of Pharan. These are their names:

From the tribe of Reuben, Shammua son of Zaccur; from the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat son of Hori; from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh; from the tribe of Issachar, Igal son of Joseph; from the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea son of Nun; from the tribe of Benjamin, [Col. 0382D] Palti son of Raphu; from the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel son of Sodi; from Joseph, from the tribe of Manasseh, Gaddi son of Susi; from the tribe of Dan, Ammiel son of Gemalli; from the tribe of Asher, Sethur son of Michael; from the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi son of Vophsi; from the tribe of Gad, Guel son of Machi.

These are the names of the men whom Moses sent to inspect the land. And he called Joshua son of Nun. Thus he sent them to inspect the land of Canaan and said to them:

“Go up through the southern region. When you have reached the mountains, inspect the land to see what it is like, and the people who dwell in it, whether they are strong or weak, few in number or many; whether the land itself is good or bad; what sort of cities they have, whether fortified or without walls; whether the soil is fertile or barren, wooded or without trees. Take courage and bring us some of the fruits of that land.”

It was the season when the first-ripe grapes could already be eaten.

So they went up and explored the land from the desert of Sin as far as Rehob, at the entrance to Hamath. They went up through the south and came to Hebron, where were Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, descendants of Anak. Hebron had been founded seven years before Tanis, a city of Egypt.

Proceeding as far as the Torrent of the Cluster, they cut off a branch with its cluster of grapes, which two men carried on a pole. They also took pomegranates and figs from that place. That place was called Neheleschol, that is, “Torrent of the Cluster,” because the children of Israel had carried a cluster from there.

After forty days, the explorers returned from the land, having traversed the whole region, and came to Moses and Aaron and the entire assembly of the children of Israel in the desert of Pharan, which is at Kadesh. They spoke to them and displayed the fruits of the land before the whole multitude, saying:

“We came to the land to which you sent us. It truly flows with milk and honey, as can be recognized from these fruits. But its inhabitants are very strong, and its cities are large and fortified. We saw the descendants of Anak there. Amalek dwells in the south; the Hittite, the Jebusite, and the Amorite in the hill country; while the Canaanite dwells by the sea and along the banks of the Jordan.”

Meanwhile Caleb, quieting the murmuring of the people that had arisen against Moses, said:

“Let us go up and possess the land, for we shall be able to obtain it.”

But the others who had gone up with him said:

“We cannot go up against this people, because they are stronger than we are.”

And they disparaged the land which they had inspected before the children of Israel, saying:

“The land through which we passed in exploration devours its inhabitants. All the people whom we saw there are of great stature. There we saw certain monstrous descendants of Anak, of the race of giants; compared with them, we seemed like grasshoppers.”

(Cap. XIV.) Then the whole multitude raised a cry and wept that night, and all the children of Israel murmured against Moses, saying:

“If only we had died—and not in this vast wilderness! If only we might perish—and not have the Lord bring us into this land, lest we fall by the sword and our wives and children be led away captive! Is it not better for us to return to Egypt?”

And they said to one another:

“Let us appoint a leader for ourselves and return to Egypt.”

When Moses and Aaron heard this, they fell prostrate before the multitude of the children of Israel. But Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, who had also explored the land, tore their garments and spoke to the entire multitude of the children of Israel:

“The land through which we passed is exceedingly good. If the Lord is favorable to us, he will bring us into it and give us a land flowing with milk and honey. Do not rebel against the Lord, and do not fear the people of this land, for we shall be able to devour them as bread. Their protection has departed from them; the Lord is with us. Do not fear.”

When the entire multitude cried out and wanted to overwhelm them with stones, the glory of the Lord appeared over the roof of the tent of meeting to all the children of Israel. [Col. 0384A]

And the Lord said to Moses:

“How long will this people disparage me? How long will they refuse to believe me, despite all the signs that I have performed before them? Therefore I will strike them with pestilence and consume them; but you I will make ruler over a great nation, stronger than this one.”

Moses said to the Lord:

“The Egyptians will hear this, from whose midst you brought out this people, as will the inhabitants of this land, who have heard that you, Lord, are among this people, and that you are seen face to face; that your cloud protects them, and that you go before them in a pillar of cloud by day and in a pillar of fire by night; and that you have killed such a great multitude as though it were one man.

“And they will say: ‘He was unable to bring this people into the land for which he had sworn; therefore he killed them in the wilderness.’ [Col. 0384B]

“Let the strength of the Lord, then, be magnified, just as you swore, saying:

“‘The Lord is patient and of great mercy, taking away iniquities and crimes, yet leaving no one innocent; visiting the sins of the fathers upon the children to the third and fourth generation.’

“Forgive, I beg you, the sin of this people according to the greatness of your mercy, just as you were favorable to them from their departure out of Egypt until this place.”

And the Lord said:

“I have forgiven them according to your word. As I live, says the Lord, the whole earth shall be filled with the glory of the Lord. Nevertheless, all the men who have seen my majesty and the signs that I performed in Egypt and in the wilderness, and who have tested me these ten times already and have not obeyed my voice, shall not see the land that I swore to their fathers. Nor shall any of those who have disparaged me see it. [Col. 0384C]

“But my servant Caleb, who, filled with another spirit, followed me, I will bring into this land which he explored, and his descendants shall possess it.”

R. Amen.

Hymn. “Immense Christ, holy ruler.” Fol. 214.

Capitula. Understanding the prayer of our cry, O clarify by the presence of eternal light the vows of those standing before you in the morning; and so command the brightness of the everlasting day to shine forth within us that the thickness of the gloomy night and the darkness friendly to error may flee away. May the true Sun also guard us by cleansing us with his ray.

Our Father.

Lauda. “His praise.” And Prayer. “Your praise.” See fol. 181.

[Col. 0384D]

At Second Vespers.

Lauda. “In the nights lift up your hands toward the holy place, and bless the Lord.”

V. “You who stand in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God.”

Prayer. In the nights we lift our hands to you, Lord, that you may establish us fixed within your Church; and, while we are weighed down by worldly burdens, grant that our action may praise you. R. Amen.

Antiphon. “Have mercy on us, O great and terrible God, who keep covenant and mercy with those who call upon you.” P. “And with those who keep your commandments.”

V. “Behold, thus shall the man who fears the Lord be blessed.” P. “And with those who keep them.” 218

V. “Glory and honor.” P. “And with those who keep them.”

[Col. 0385A]

“May the Lord be always.” R. “And with.”

Lauda. “Open my eyes, and I shall contemplate the wonders of your law. I am a sojourner on the earth.”

P. “Do not hide your commandments from me.”

V. “Reward your servant; I shall live, and I shall keep your words.”

P. “Do not hide [your commandments from me].”

V. “Glory and honor.”

Hymn.

On the fourth day, Lazarus, already stinking,  
received life again;  
freed from the bonds of death,  
he became a survivor for himself.

The garment touched by the streams  
of steaming blood restrains them;  
the streams of blood grow dry  
when watered by the weeping of the suppliant.

He suddenly commanded the man,  
released from every torpor, to rise;  
the sick man in turn carried  
his little bed with his own steps.

To God the Father be glory,  
and to his only Son,  
with the Spirit, the Paraclete,  
now and throughout every age. Amen.

Supplication. “Let us beseech the Redeemer.”

Capitula. O good, lovable, and wondrous Jesus, author, receive the sacrifice of your servants. You granted Lazarus, when he heard your voice, to rise from the tomb; grant us, as we receive you through inner hearing, to rise again by grace from the depth of our own sin. Thus, just as we have now confidently offered before you the voice of the devout prayer by which you taught us on earth to beseech you, may we also rejoice that we have received from you the fulfillment of its petition.

Our Father.

Humble yourselves for the blessing.

May the Lord be always [with you]. R. And with your spirit.

Blessing. Jesus Christ, Son of God, who restored dead Lazarus to his former life: may he himself illumine us with the sanctification of new life. R. Amen.

And he who commanded Lazarus to depart, once the bonds of his hands and feet had been loosed: may he himself, releasing the fetters of your bonds, always make you walk on straight paths. R. Amen.

And he who through the miracle of so great a deed manifested his glory to the peoples: may he himself lead you into everlasting joys. R. Amen.

Through his mercy.

May the Lord be always with you. R. And with your spirit.

Lauda. “Your testimonies are wondrous, O Lord.”

P. “Therefore my soul has searched them out.”

V. “The explanation of your words gives light and grants understanding to the simple.”

P. “Therefore my soul has searched them out.”

V. “Glory and honor.”

Prayer. As we search out, Lord, the wonders of your testimonies, reveal the understanding of your illumination. We who, with open mouth, have drawn in the breath of life and, sated with the richness of the holy Sacrifice, belch it forth: may we always grow in fear of your words; and may we behold the glory of your presence through the peaceful manifestation of your appearance. R. Amen.

Another Lauda 2. “Keep my feet from every evil way.”

P. “Restrain my feet, O Lord.”

V. “How I have loved your law, O Lord! It is my meditation all day long.”

P. “Restrain [my feet].”

Prayer. Restrain our feet, Lord, from every evil way; and grant that we may keep your Word with complete attention. Make us turn away from evil and continually be pleasing to you. R. Amen.

Lauda 3. “You founded the earth, and it endures. By your ordinance the days persevere.”

P. “For all things serve you.”

V. “Forever, O Lord, your word remains in heaven.”

P. “For all things [serve you].”

Prayer. Lord, may your Word, which remains forever in heaven, always dwell in the temple of your Church, so that the presence of its inhabitant may be an unfailing brightness to its dwelling places. R. Amen.

Lauda 4. “How I have loved your law, O Lord?”

P. “It is my meditation all day long.”

V. “By your commandment you have made me wiser than my enemies, for it is mine forever.”

P. “It is my meditation all day.”

Prayer. Grant us, Lord, to love your law in such a way that we continually meditate upon it in our hearts and, having received your approval, may be perfected in action. R. Amen.

Another Lauda 5. “Your hands made me and fashioned me.”

P. “Give me understanding, O Lord.”

V. “Those who fear you will see me and rejoice, because I have hoped in your word.”

P. “Give me [understanding].”

Prayer. To you, Lord, we lift our eyes, because we are the workmanship of your hands. Give us understanding to learn your commandments, and fill those who fear you with joy. May your mercy come for our consolation, rescuing us from every evil and teaching us to make the dignity of our works pleasing to you. R. Amen.

Lauda 6. “Those who fear you will see me and rejoice.”

P. “For I have hoped in your word, O Lord.”

V. “I know, O Lord, that your judgments are righteous; and in your truth you have humbled me.”

P. “For I have hoped in your word.”

Prayer. Grant us, Lord, understanding to learn your commandments. Instruct us through constant meditation, so that laziness may not draw us back from any duty; rather, may your mercy become our consolation. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

[Col. 0386D]

Prayers. “Turn your anger away from us, O Lord.”

And Prayer. “Turn your face away, O Lord.” See fol. 130.

MONDAY.

At Matins.

Antiphon. “But you, O Lord.” Psalm III. And Prayer. “Although, O Lord.” Fol. 141.

Antiphon. “You alone understand sins: cleanse us from our sins, O Lord.” Psalm XVIII.

Prayer. Cleanse us, Lord, from our hidden faults, purifying the conscience that is stained by inward and personal blemishes. Also spare your servants from the faults of others, so that you may forgive those things which we either learn through the examples of the wicked or commit after being enticed by perverse persuasions. Since we acknowledge you as our own Lord, may we in no way continue to feel the dominion of sins. V. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 2. “Hear us on the day when we call upon you, O Lord our God.” Psalm XIX.

Prayer. Fulfill, Lord, all our petitions; send us help from the holy place. Remember all our sacrifice, which we offer to you not only through offering but also through prayer and affliction, so that you may always make us humble before you and attend to the contrite. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 3. “Look upon our defense, O God.” Psalm XXI.

Prayer. Graciously look upon our defense, Lord our God; rescue our souls from the sword. Do not let us be fed with deadly instruction, but rule us by your protection. At the same time, free us from the mouth of the lion that desires to seize us; and because of the treachery of the barking dog, protect us with vigilant attention and solicitous care. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

R. “If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. But if we confess our sins, he is faithful and just.”

P. “That he may forgive us our sins and cleanse us from all iniquity.”

V. “I write these things to you so that you may not sin. But if anyone does sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ.”

P. “That he may forgive us.”

[Col. 0387C]

At Lauds.

Antiphon. “Have mercy on me, O God, according to your great mercy.” Psalm L.

Prayer. Have mercy on us, Lord, according to your great mercy. What we are ashamed of, may you forgive; and what we regret having done, may you mercifully pardon. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

At the Canticle. Antiphon. “I shall now sing to my beloved a song of my beloved vineyard. A vineyard was made for the beloved in a fertile place.”

Canticle of Isaiah (Cap. V).

I shall now sing to my beloved  
a song of my beloved vineyard.

A vineyard was made for the beloved on a horn,  
in a fertile place. [Col. 0387D]  
And I surrounded it with a hedge,  
dug around it, and planted a choice vine.

I built a tower in its midst  
and dug a winepress in it.  
I hoped that it would produce grapes,  
but it produced thorns.

And now, man of Judah  
and you who dwell in Jerusalem,  
judge between me and my vineyard.

What more was there to do for my vineyard  
that I had not done for it?  
I hoped that it would produce grapes,  
but it produced thorns.

And now, behold, I announce to you  
what I am about to do for my vineyard:  
I shall remove its hedge,  
and it will be for plunder;  
I shall destroy its walls,  
and it will be for trampling.

[Col. 0388A]

I shall abandon my vineyard;  
it will not be pruned or dug.  
Thorns will rise up in it  
as in untilled ground;  
and I shall command the clouds  
not to rain rain upon it.

For the vineyard of the Lord of Hosts  
is the house of Israel;  
and the man of Judah  
is his beloved young plant.

I hoped that he would produce judgment,  
but he produced iniquity;  
not righteousness, but a cry. R. Amen.

Prayer. Lord, who rejected the Israelite vineyard because it yielded thorns instead of fruit, enlarge your Church through the infusion of virtues. May you encompass us with the commandments that served as the hedge from which they were exposed; and grant us the tower of the kingdom and the winepress of the altar that you diminished for them. Thus, when the rain of the clouds is broken into showers, may we not produce the fitting thorns of flames; rather, may you, in your kindness, nourish heavenly fruits in us and receive them from us. R. Amen.

At the Benedictus. Antiphon. “Send forth your light and your truth, O Lord.”

V. “They themselves have led me and brought me to your holy mountain and to your tabernacle.”

Canticle. “Blessed are you, O Lord.” Fol. 6.

Lauda. “With well-sounding cymbals, with cymbals of jubilation; let every spirit praise the Lord.” Psalm CL.

Reading from the Book of Deuteronomy (Cap. XXXIV).

R. Thanks be to God.

In those days: Moses went up from the plains of Moab onto Mount Nebo, to the summit of Phasga opposite Jericho. The Lord showed him the whole land of Gilead as far as Dan, all Naphtali, and the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, and the whole land as far as the western sea, the southern region, and the breadth of the plain of Jericho, the city of palms, as far as Zoar. The Lord said to him:

“This is the land for which I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying: ‘I will give it to your offspring.’ You have seen it with your eyes, but you shall not cross over into it.”

And Moses, the servant of the Lord, died in the land of Moab at the Lord’s command. He buried him in the valley of the land of Moab opposite Phogor; and no one has known his tomb to the present day. Moses was one hundred and twenty years old when he died. His eye had not grown dim, nor had his teeth become loose. The children of Israel wept for him in the plains of Moab for twenty days, and the days of mourning for those grieving for Moses were completed.

Now Joshua son of Nun was filled with the spirit of wisdom, because Moses had laid his hands upon him. The children of Israel obeyed him and did as the Lord had commanded Moses. No prophet arose thereafter in Israel like Moses, whom the Lord knew face to face, in all the signs and portents which he sent him to perform in Egypt against Pharaoh, all his servants, and his entire land, and in all the strong hand and great wonders that Moses performed before all Israel. R. Amen.

Hymn. “Author of the shining one.” Fol. 96.

Capitula. Send forth your light and your truth, Lord our God, so that the splendor of your divinity may dispel the darkness of our mind, and the true assumption of humanity may be manifest as the redemption of the human race. While you are shown to be true God and true human in us and for us, may your omnipotence rescue your work, the captives, from the enemy, and may your mercy nourish those already redeemed.

Our Father.

Lauda. “Your testimonies are wondrous, O Lord.”

P. “Therefore my soul has searched them out.”

V. “The explanation of your words gives light and grants understanding to the simple.”

P. “Therefore.”

V. “Glory and honor, etc.”

P. “Therefore.”

Prayer. As we search out, Lord, the wonders of your testimonies, reveal the understanding of your illumination. We who, with open mouth, have drawn in the breath of life and, sated with the richness of the holy Sacrifice, belch it forth: may we always grow in fear of your words, and may we behold the glory of your presence through the peaceful manifestation of your appearance. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

At Terce.

From the Wisdom of Ecclesiasticus of Solomon (Cap. IX).

R. Thanks be to God.

Son, according to your ability, beware of your neighbor, and associate with the wise and prudent. Let just men be your companions at table; let your glory be in the fear of the Lord; let the thought of God be in your understanding, and let all your speech concern the commandments of the Most High. In the hand of craftsmen, a work will be praised; and the ruler of the people in the wisdom of his speech, but among the elders the word is praised for its understanding. A talkative man is terrifying in his city, and one reckless with his tongue is hateful.

(Cap. X.) A wise judge will vindicate his people, and the rule of a sensible man will be stable. A foolish king will destroy his people, but cities will be inhabited through the understanding of the prudent. The power of the earth is in the hand of God, and he will raise up a useful ruler over it in due time. R. Amen.

Reading from the Book of Joshua (Cap. I).

R. Thanks be to God.

In those days: After the death of Moses, the servant of the Lord, the Lord spoke to Joshua son of Nun, the minister of Moses, and said to him:

“Moses, my servant, is dead. Rise and cross this Jordan, you and all the people with you, into the land that I will give to the children of Israel. Every place that the sole of your foot treads upon, I will give you, just as I spoke to Moses. From the desert and Lebanon as far as the great river Euphrates, the entire land of the Hittites as far as the Great Sea toward the setting of the sun shall be your boundary. No one will be able to withstand you all the days of your life. As I was with Moses, so I will also be with you. I will not abandon you or forsake you.

“Take courage and be very strong, so that you may keep and do the whole law that Moses my servant commanded you. Do not turn away from it to the right or to the left, so that you may understand all that you do. Let not the book of this law depart from your mouth, but meditate upon it day and night, so that you may keep and do everything written in it. Then you shall direct your way and understand it. Behold, I command you: take courage and be strong. Do not fear, for the Lord your God is with you wherever you go.”

Joshua commanded the leaders of the people, saying:

“Pass through the middle of the camp and command the people, saying: ‘Prepare provisions for yourselves, because after three days you shall cross the Jordan and enter to possess the land that the Lord your God will give you.’

“And he said to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh: ‘Remember the word that Moses, the servant of the Lord, spoke to you, saying: “The Lord your God has given you rest and this whole land.” Your wives, children, and livestock shall remain in the land that Moses gave us beyond the Jordan. But you shall cross over armed before your brothers, all you warriors, and fight for them until the Lord gives your brothers rest, as he has given you, and they too possess the land of their inheritance. Then you shall dwell in the land that Moses, the servant of the Lord, gave you beyond the Jordan toward the rising of the sun.’”

They answered Joshua and said:

“Everything that you have commanded us we shall do, and wherever you send us we shall go. Just as we obeyed Moses in everything, so we shall obey you; only may the Lord your God be with you, as he was with Moses. Whoever contradicts you and does not obey all the words that you command him shall be put to death. Only take courage and act manfully.”

(Cap. II.) Then Joshua son of Nun sent two men secretly from Shittim as spies and said to them:

“Go and inspect the land and the city of Jericho.”

They went and entered the house of a prostitute named Rahab, and rested there. It was reported to the king of Jericho and said:

“Behold, men from the children of Israel have entered here by night to explore the land.”

The king of Jericho sent to Rahab, saying:

“Bring out the men who came to you and entered your house, for they are spies and have come to explore the entire land.”

But the woman took the men and hid them, and said:

“I admit that they came to me, but I did not know where they were from. When the gate was closed in the darkness, they went out together; I do not know where they went. Pursue them quickly and overtake them.”

She had made the men climb onto the roof of her house and covered them with stalks of flax that were there. [Col. 0390D] The men who had been sent pursued them along the road leading to the ford of the Jordan. As soon as they had gone out, the gate was closed.

The men who were hiding had not yet fallen asleep when, behold, the woman came up to them and said:

“I know that the Lord has given you the land, that your terror has fallen upon us, and that all the inhabitants of the land have grown faint. We have heard how the Lord dried up the waters of the Red Sea before you when you came out of Egypt, and what you did to the two Amorite kings beyond the Jordan, Sihon and Og, whom you killed. When we heard these things, we were terrified, and our heart fainted; no spirit of life remained in us at your coming. For the Lord your God is himself Lord in heaven above and on earth below.

“Now therefore swear to me by the Lord that, just as I showed you mercy, so you will show mercy to my father’s household. Give me a sign, save my father and mother, my brothers and sisters, and all who belong to me, and rescue our lives from death.”

They answered her:

“Let our life be given for yours unto death, provided that you do not betray us. When the Lord gives us the land, we shall show you mercy and faithfulness.”

So she let them down by a rope through the window, for her house was attached to the wall. She said to them:

“Climb up into the mountains, lest those who have been pursuing you encounter you on your return. Hide there for three days, until they return; afterward you shall go on your way.”

They said to her:

“We shall be free of this oath with which you have bound us, if, when we enter the land, this scarlet cord is the sign, and you tie it in the window through which you let us down; and if you gather your father, mother, brothers, and all your kindred into your house.

“Whoever goes out through the door of your house, his blood shall be upon his own head, and we shall be innocent. But the blood of all who are with you in the house shall fall upon our heads if anyone lays a hand on them. If you wish to betray us and bring this matter into the open, we shall be free of this oath with which you bound us.”

She answered:

“As you have spoken, so let it be.”

And she sent them away, and hung the scarlet cord in the window. They went on and reached the mountains, where they remained for three days, until those who had pursued them returned. They had searched along the entire road but did not find them.

When the pursuers had entered the city, the spies returned and came down from the mountain. They crossed the Jordan and came to Joshua son of Nun. They reported everything that had happened to them and said:

“The Lord has delivered all this land into our hands, and all its inhabitants have been struck down with terror.”

(Cap. III.) Then Joshua rose during the night and moved the camp. They went out from Shittim and came to the Jordan, he and all the children of Israel, and remained there for three days. When these had passed, heralds went through the middle of the camp and began to cry out:

“When you see the ark of the covenant of the Lord your God, and the priests of Levitical descent carrying it, you too shall rise and follow those going before you. Let there be between you and the ark a distance of two thousand cubits, so that you may see it from afar and know by which way you are to enter, because you have not traveled that way before. Take care not to approach the ark.”

Joshua said to the people:

“Sanctify yourselves, for tomorrow the Lord will perform wonders among you.”

Let the choir respond. Amen.

Antiphon 1. “God, our God, look upon us; do not abandon us who hope in you.” Psalm XXI.

Prayer. Look upon us, Lord our God. Do not abandon us in any way by turning your face away from us. We shall truly be saved if you turn the gaze of your countenance toward us and joyfully join yourself to our souls. Since our fathers hoped in you and were saved, make us succeed to their hereditary hope, and grant us to rejoice with them in eternal exultation, equal to theirs. Let the choir respond. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God, etc.

Antiphon 2. “Mercy will surround those who hope in the Lord.” Psalm XXXI.

Prayer. Forgive, Lord, the impiety of our heart, for which every holy person entreats you at the appropriate time. Grant us understanding through the help of the deed for which we pray, and instruct us in the way of this life, by which we may walk. R. Amen.

At Sext.

Reading from the Prophet Jeremiah (Cap. XXXIII).

R. Thanks be to God.

Thus says the Lord:

“Call upon me, and I will answer you, and I will announce to you great and firm things that you do not know. For thus says the Lord of Hosts, the God of Israel, concerning the houses of this city and the houses of the king of Judah, which have been destroyed, and concerning the fortifications and the sword of those coming to fight against the Chaldeans and to fill them with the corpses of men whom I struck in my fury and indignation, hiding my face from this city because of all their wickedness. Behold, I will bring them a scar and healing, and I will cure them; I will reveal to them a supplication for peace and truth.

“I will turn the captivity of Judah and the captivity of Jerusalem, and I will build them as at the beginning. I will cleanse them from all their iniquity by which they sinned against me, and I will be favorable toward all their iniquities by which they abandoned and despised me. They shall become for me a name, a joy, a praise, and an exultation among all the nations of the earth that hear of all the good things I am about to do for them. They shall fear and tremble because of all the good things and all the peace that I shall make for them.

“Thus says the Lord: In this place, which you say is deserted because there is neither human being nor beast—in the cities of Judah and outside Jerusalem, which are desolate, without human being, without inhabitant, and without livestock—there shall again be heard the voice of joy and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, the voice of those saying: ‘Give thanks to the Lord of Hosts, for the Lord is good, for his mercy is forever.’”

R. Amen.

Antiphon 1. “Give thanks to the Lord on the lyre; sing psalms to him on the ten-stringed psaltery.” Psalm XXXII.

Prayer. May our soul be pleasing to you, Lord, from whom it desires to receive both the virtue of endurance and its reward. Therefore may your mercy be upon us, as we have hoped; and may your customary grace come before us. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 2. “Magnify the Lord with me, and let us exalt his name together.” Psalm XXXIII.

Prayer. Graciously hear us as we seek you, Lord; and, as one who mercifully forgives, grant that our soul may rejoice in you. Since you are near to those whose heart is troubled, open your ear to the contrition of our spirit, and turn our bodies and hearts toward your peace, which surpasses all understanding. R. Amen.

V. “Blessed is the Lord, who is great forever, for his kingdom is throughout the ages; for he chastises and again has mercy.”

P. “Grant us forgiveness.”

P. “Grant us.”

Hymn. “O Nazarene, light.” Fol. 144.

[Col. 0393D]

Prayer. Do not uncover, Lord, the children of men who hope in the protection of your wings. Rather, like orphans whom you are preparing for flights on high, nourish us by cherishing us. Do not permit us to be torn away by the violence of those lying in wait, nor allow us to fly away from the nest of your Church. Instead, while you cover us with the shelter of a fatherly king, may we come, aided by your help, to the abundance of your house.

Our Father.

At None.

From Ecclesiasticus of Solomon (Cap. XXVIII).

R. Thanks be to God.

Son, the whisperer and the double-tongued person is accursed, for he has disturbed many who were living in peace. The third tongue has stirred up many and scattered them from nation to nation; it destroys fortified cities and tears down the houses of the great. It overthrows the strength of peoples and dissolves strong nations. The third tongue has driven out married women and deprived them of their labors. Whoever looks to it has no rest, nor will he have a friend in whom he may rest.

The blow of a scourge causes a bruise, but the blow of the tongue crushes bones. Many have fallen by the edge of the sword, but not as many as those who have fallen by their own tongue. Hedge your ears with thorns; do not listen to an evil tongue, and make nets and bolts for your mouth.

Blessed is the one who is sheltered from his evil tongue, who has not passed into its anger, who has not dragged its yoke, and who has not been bound in its chains. R. Amen.

Reading from the Book of Joshua (Cap. V).

[Col. 0394B]

R. Thanks be to God.

In those days: When Joshua was in the field near the city of Jericho, he lifted his eyes and saw a man standing before him, holding a drawn sword. He went toward him and said, “Are you one of ours or one of our adversaries?” He replied, “Not at all; rather, I am the commander of the army of the Lord, and now I have come.” Joshua fell face-down upon the ground and, worshiping, said, “What does my lord say to his servant?” “Take off,” he said, “[p. 224] your sandal from your feet, for the place on which you stand is holy ground.” Joshua did as he had been commanded.

*(Chapter VI.)* Now Jericho was shut and fortified because of the Israelites, and no one dared either to go out or to enter. And the Lord said to Joshua: “Behold, I have delivered Jericho into your hands, together with its king and all its mighty men. All the warriors shall march around the city once each day; thus you shall do for six days. On the seventh day, let the priests take seven trumpets, the kind used at the jubilee, and go before the ark of the covenant. You shall march around the city seven times, and the priests shall blow the trumpets. And when the sound becomes prolonged and sharper, and resounds in your ears, let the whole people shout with a very great cry; then the walls of the city will fall completely, and each person shall enter by the place opposite which he is standing.”

Therefore Joshua son of Nun summoned the priests and said to them: “Take up the ark of the covenant; and let seven other priests take seven jubilee trumpets and march before the ark of the Lord.” He also said to the people: “Go and march around the city, armed, going before the ark of the Lord.”

When Joshua had finished speaking, and the seven priests were blowing the seven trumpets before the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and all Israel was going before as an armed army, the rest of the populace followed the ark, and everything resounded with the trumpets. Joshua had commanded the people: “You shall not shout, and your voice shall not be heard, nor shall any word come from your mouth, until the day comes when I say to you, ‘Shout and cry aloud.’”

So the ark of the Lord marched around the city once each day, and, returning to the camp, remained there. Then, when Joshua rose during the night, the priests took up the ark of the Lord, and seven of them took the seven trumpets used at the jubilees. They went before the ark of the Lord, walking and blowing; the armed people went before them, while the rest of the populace followed the ark, and the trumpets resounded.

They marched around the city once on the second day and returned to the camp. Thus they did for six days. On the seventh day, rising at dawn, they marched around the city as ordered, seven times. And when, on the seventh circuit, the priests were blowing the trumpets, Joshua said to all Israel: “Shout aloud, for the Lord has delivered the city to you. Let this city be accursed, and everything in it belong to the Lord. Only Rahab the prostitute shall live, together with all who are with her in the house, because she hid the messengers whom we sent. But you must beware of touching anything that has been commanded; otherwise you will incur guilt by transgression, and the whole camp of Israel will be in sin and be thrown into confusion. Whatever there is of gold and silver, and of bronze and iron vessels, shall be consecrated to the Lord and deposited in his treasury.”

So, when all the people were shouting and the trumpets were sounding, after the voice and noise had resounded in the ears of the multitude, the walls immediately collapsed. Each person went up by the place opposite him; and they captured the city and killed everything in it, from man to woman, from child to old man. They also killed the cattle, sheep, and donkeys with the sword.

But Joshua said to the two men who had been sent as spies: “Enter the house of the prostitute and bring her out, together with everything belonging to her, just as you swore to her.” The young men entered and brought out Rahab, her parents, her brothers, all her possessions, and her whole family, and they made them remain outside the camp of Israel.

They burned the city and everything in it, except the silver and gold and the bronze and iron vessels, which they consecrated to the treasury of the Lord. But Joshua preserved Rahab the prostitute, her father’s household, and everything she possessed; and they lived in the midst of Israel to the present day, because she had hidden the messengers whom he had sent to spy out Jericho.

At that time Joshua pronounced this curse, saying: “Cursed before the Lord be the man who rises up and rebuilds Jericho. At the cost of his firstborn let him lay its foundations, and at the cost of his youngest let him set up its gates.” Thus the Lord was with Joshua, and his name became renowned throughout the whole land.

**Antiphon 1.** Give thanks to the Lord on the lyre; sing psalms to him on the ten-stringed psaltery. **Psalm 32.**

**Prayer.** O Lord, who make the joy of the righteous your commandment; whose praise both obeys you by loving and loves you by praising; who sing a new song to you on the lyre of the Law and leap forth with holy resounding through devout voices on the psaltery: grant, O Lord, that we may cling to their footsteps and, with them, loudly proclaim your praise. And since your word is upright and your works are faithful, grant that we may believe you with a faithful heart and deserve more earnestly to obtain your mercy. [p. 225] **Response:** Amen.

Through mercy.

**Antiphon 2.** Our soul waits patiently for the Lord, for he is our helper and our protector. **Psalm 32.**

**Prayer.** To you, O Lord. See folio 223.

**Antiphon 3.** The Lord will redeem the souls of his servants, and he will not abandon all who hope in him. **Psalm 33.**

**Prayer.** May our soul bless you, O Lord, at all times, because your mercy is always present in our afflictions: while you correct us through discipline and comfort us through indulgence; while you heal by striking and strengthen by healing. Grant us, therefore, that we who have tasted your sweetness in faith may receive the fullest sweetness in recompense.

Our Father, who are.

# Tuesday

## At Matins

**Antiphon.** My voice. **Psalm 3.**

## Reading from the Book of Joshua (Chapter VII)

**Response:** Thanks be to God.

In those days: The Lord was with Joshua, and his name became renowned throughout the whole land. But the Israelites transgressed the commandment and appropriated something from what had been placed under the ban. For Achan son of Charmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took something from the ban; and the Lord was angry with the Israelites.

When Joshua sent men from Jericho against Ai, which is near Beth-aven, east of Bethel, he said to them: “Go up and inspect the land.” They carried out the command and reconnoitered Ai. Returning, [p. 226] they said to him: “Let not the whole people go up; let two or three thousand men go and destroy the city. Why should the whole people be troubled needlessly against very few enemies?”

So three thousand warriors went up. But they immediately turned their backs and were struck down by the men of Ai; thirty-six of them fell. The enemy pursued them from the gate as far as Shebarim, and they fell while fleeing down the slopes. The heart of the people was overcome with fear and melted like water.

Joshua son of Nun tore his garments and fell face-down upon the ground before the ark of the Lord until evening, he and all Israel. They put dust upon their heads, and Joshua said: “Alas, Lord God, why did you wish to bring this people across the Jordan, in order to hand us over to the Amorites and destroy us? If only we had been content to remain across the Jordan, as we began! Ah, Lord God, what shall I say, seeing Israel turn its back before its enemies? The Canaanites and all the inhabitants of the land will hear, and, gathering together, will surround us and wipe out our name from the earth. And what will you do for your great name?”

The Lord said to Joshua: “Rise; why are you lying face-down upon the ground? Israel has sinned and transgressed my covenant. They have taken from what was under the ban; they have stolen, lied, and hidden it among their possessions. Israel cannot stand before its enemies, but will flee from them, because it is polluted by the ban. I will not be with you until you destroy the one who is guilty of this crime.

“Sanctify the people for tomorrow, for thus says the Lord God of Israel: ‘The ban is in your midst, O Israel; you cannot stand before your enemies until the one contaminated by this crime is removed from among you.’ You shall therefore approach individually in the morning according to your tribes. Whichever tribe the lot selects shall approach by its clans, the clan by its households, and the household by its men. Whoever is discovered to have committed this offense shall be burned with fire, together with all his property, because he has transgressed the covenant of the Lord and committed an outrage in Israel.”

So Joshua rose early and presented Israel by its tribes, and the tribe of Judah was identified. When it was presented by its families, the family of Zerah was identified. Presenting that family by its men, he found Zabdi. Dividing his household among its individual men, he found Achan son of Charmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah.

And he said to Achan: “My son, give glory to the Lord God of Israel and confess; tell me what you have done and do not conceal it.”

He replied: “Truly I have sinned against the Lord God of Israel, and this is what I did: I saw among the spoil a very fine scarlet cloak, two hundred shekels of silver, and a gold bar weighing fifty shekels. I coveted them, took them, and hid them in the ground opposite the middle of my tent; the silver I covered with earth in a pit.”

Joshua therefore sent messengers. They ran to his tent and found everything hidden in the same place. Taking the objects from the tent, they brought them to Joshua and all the Israelites, and laid them before the Lord.

Then Joshua took Achan son of Zerah, the silver, the cloak, and the gold bar, together with his sons and daughters, his oxen and donkeys, his sheep, the tent itself, and all his possessions—and all Israel with him—and led them to the Valley of Achor. There Joshua said: “Because you have troubled us, may the Lord trouble you this day.”

All Israel stoned him, and everything that belonged to him was burned with fire. They heaped over him a great pile of stones, which remains to the present day. **Response:** Amen.

## At Terce

### Proverbs of Solomon (Chapter XVII)

**Response:** Thanks be to God.

My son, the crown of dignity is old age, and it will be found in the ways of justice. The patient man is better than the strong man, and whoever rules his spirit is better than one who captures cities. Lots are cast as a sign, but they are directed by the Lord. Better is a dry morsel with joy than a house full of sacrifices with strife. A wise servant will rule over foolish sons and will divide the inheritance among brothers. As silver is tested in the fire and gold in the furnace, so the Lord tests hearts. An evil person obeys an unrighteous tongue, and a deceitful person gives heed to lying lips. Whoever despises the poor insults his Maker, and whoever rejoices in another’s ruin will not go unpunished. The crown of old men is their children’s children, and the glory of children is their fathers. Fine words do not suit a fool, nor lying lips a prince. A most precious jewel is the expectation of one who waits; wherever he turns, he understands wisely. **Response:** Amen.

## Reading from the Book of Joshua (Chapter VIII)

**Response:** Thanks be to God.

In those days: The Lord said to Joshua: “Take with you the entire multitude of warriors, and rise and go up against the town of Ai. Behold, I have delivered its king, its people, its city, and its land into your hand. You shall do to Ai and its king as you did to Jericho and its king. But you shall take its spoil and all its animals for yourselves. Set an ambush behind the city.”

Joshua rose, and the whole army of warriors with him, to go up against Ai. He selected thirty thousand strong men and sent them by night, commanding them: “Set an ambush behind the city; do not go far away, and be ready. I and the rest of the people with me will approach the city from the front. When they come out against us, as before, we shall flee and turn our backs until, pursuing us, they are drawn far away from the city; for they will think that we are fleeing from them as before. When we flee and they pursue, you shall rise from the ambush and lay waste to the city. The Lord your God will deliver it into your hands. When you have captured it, burn it. Thus shall you do as you have been commanded.”

He dismissed them, and they went to the place of the ambush and sat between Bethel and Ai, west of the town of Ai. Joshua spent that night among the people. Rising at dawn, he reviewed his companions and went up with the elders at the head of the army, surrounded by the aid of the warriors.

When everyone had come and advanced opposite the city, they stood on the northern side of Ai, with a valley between it and them. He had selected five thousand men and placed them in ambush between Beth-aven and Ai, on the western side of the same city. The rest of the army drew up its line to the north, so that the rear of the multitude reached the western side of the city.

Joshua went that night and stood in the middle of the valley. When the king of Ai saw this, he hurried out in the morning with the whole army of the city and drew up his line toward the wilderness, unaware that an ambush lay behind him.

Joshua and all Israel withdrew to a position, pretending fear, and fled by the way of the wilderness. But the enemy shouted and encouraged one another and pursued them. When they had withdrawn from the city, and not one man remained in Ai or Bethel who was not pursuing Israel—as they had burst out, leaving the towns open—the Lord said to Joshua: “Raise the shield that is in your hand toward Ai, for I will deliver it to you.”

When he raised the shield toward the city, the ambush that had been concealed rose immediately. They went to the city, captured it, and burned it. The men of the city who were pursuing Joshua looked back and saw the smoke of the city rising to heaven, but they could no longer flee here and there, especially since those who had pretended to flee and were heading toward the wilderness had turned and resisted their pursuers with the greatest force.

When Joshua and all Israel saw that the city had been captured and its smoke was rising, Joshua turned back and struck the men of Ai. Indeed, those who had captured and burned the city came out against their own people and began to strike the enemy in the middle. When the adversaries were being killed on both sides, so that no one of so great a multitude survived, they also seized the king of Ai alive and brought him to Joshua.

After all those who had pursued Israel while it fled toward the wilderness had been killed and had fallen by the sword in that same place, the Israelites returned and struck the city. The number of those who fell that day, men and women, was twelve thousand—all the inhabitants of Ai.

Joshua did not withdraw the hand that he had stretched upward, holding the shield, until he had killed all the inhabitants of Ai. The Israelites divided the animals and spoil of the city among themselves, as the Lord had commanded Joshua. He burned the city and made it an everlasting mound. He also hanged its king on a gallows until evening and until after sunset.

Joshua then commanded, and they took his corpse down from the cross. They threw it at the very entrance of the city and piled a great heap of stones over it, which remains to the present day. Then Joshua built an altar to the Lord, the God of Israel. **Response:** Amen.

## At None

### Proverbs of Solomon (Chapter XXI)

**Response:** Thanks be to God.

My son, the soul of the wicked desires evil and will not show mercy to his neighbor. When the pestilent man is punished, the simple will become wiser; and if he follows the wise, he will gain knowledge. The righteous considers the house of the wicked, to bring the wicked away from evil. Whoever hardens his ear against the cry of the poor will himself cry out and not be heard. A gift given secretly extinguishes anger, and a present placed in the bosom quiets the greatest indignation. It is joy to the righteous to practice judgment, but terror to those who work iniquity. The man who strays from the way of instruction will dwell among the assembly of giants. Whoever loves feasting will be in poverty, and whoever loves wine and rich foods will not grow wealthy. The wicked will be given in place of the righteous, and the unrighteous in place of the upright. It is better to live in the wilderness than with a quarrelsome and angry woman. A desirable treasure and oil are in the dwelling of the righteous; a foolish man will squander them. Whoever follows justice and mercy will find life, justice, and glory. **Response:** Amen.

## Reading from the Book of Joshua (Chapter IX)

**Response:** Thanks be to God.

In those days: When those who lived in Gibeon had heard all that Joshua had done to Jericho and Ai, they acted craftily. They took provisions for themselves, placed old sacks on their donkeys, and took torn and mended wine-skins. They wore very old sandals, patched with pieces as evidence of their age, and dressed in old garments. The bread they carried for their journey was hard and crumbled into pieces.

They went to Joshua, who was then staying in the camp at Gilgal, and said to him and to all Israel together: “We have come from a very distant land, wishing to make peace with you.”

The Israelites answered them: “Perhaps you live in the land allotted to us, and we cannot make a covenant with you.”

But they said to Joshua: “We are your servants.”

Joshua said to them: “Who are you, and from where have you come?”

They replied: “Your servants have come from a very distant land in the name of the Lord your God. For we have heard of his power and of all that he did in Egypt, and to the two Amorite kings beyond the Jordan, Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan, who was in Ashtaroth.

“Our elders and all the inhabitants of our land said to us: ‘Take provisions in your hands for a very long journey, go to meet them, and say: “We are your servants; make a covenant with us.”’

“Behold, when we left our homes to come to you, we took this bread hot; now it has become dry and crumbled from excessive age. We filled these wine-skins new; now they are torn. Our garments have come apart, and the sandals with which we are clothed and which are on our feet have become worn and nearly consumed because of the length of the journey.”

So they accepted some of their provisions and did not inquire of the word of the Lord. Joshua made a covenant with them and, having entered into the treaty, promised that they would not be killed. The leaders of the multitude also swore to them.

But three days after they had entered into the covenant, they heard that the people lived nearby and would be among them. The Israelites broke camp and came to their cities on the third day. Their names were Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath-jearim.

They did not strike them, because the leaders of the multitude had sworn to them by the name of the Lord God of Israel. So the whole populace murmured against the leaders. They replied: “We swore to them by the name of the Lord God of Israel; therefore we cannot touch them. But this is what we shall do: Let them be preserved alive, lest the Lord’s anger be stirred against us if we break our oath. Yet let them live in such a way that they cut wood and carry water for the use of the entire multitude.”

While they were speaking thus, Joshua summoned the Gibeonites and said to them: “Why did you wish to deceive us by saying, ‘We live very far from you,’ when you are living in our midst? Therefore you shall be under a curse, and none of your stock shall cease from cutting wood and carrying water into the house of the Lord my God.”

They replied: “It was reported to us, your servants, that the Lord your God had promised Moses his servant that he would give you the whole land and destroy all its inhabitants. We were therefore very much afraid and, compelled by fear of you, took thought for our lives and devised this plan. Now we are in your hand; do with us what seems good and right to you.”

Joshua did as he had said and rescued them from the hands of the Israelites, so that they would not be killed. On that day he appointed them for the service of all the people and of the Lord’s altar, cutting wood and carrying water, to the present time. **Response:** Amen.

## Reading from the Book of Joshua (Chapter X)

**Response:** Thanks be to God.

In those days: When Adonizedek, king of Jerusalem, heard that Joshua had captured Ai and had overthrown it (as he had done to Jericho and its king, so he did to Ai and its king), and that the Gibeonites had defected to Israel and had entered into alliance with them, he was greatly afraid. For Gibeon was a large city, one of the royal cities, and larger than Ai; and all its warriors were very strong. Therefore Adonizedek, king of Jerusalem, sent to Hoham, king of Hebron, to Piram, king of Jarmuth, to Japhia, king of Lachish, and to Debir, king of Eglon, saying: “Come up to me and bring aid, so that we may attack Gibeon, because it has defected to Joshua and the Israelites.”

So the five kings of the Amorites assembled and went up—the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon—with their armies; and they encamped around Gibeon to besiege it. But the inhabitants of Gibeon, the besieged city, sent to Joshua, who was then staying in the camp at Gilgal, and said to him: “Do not withdraw your hands from the aid of your servants; come up quickly and rescue us, and bring us assistance. For all the kings of the Amorites who dwell in the hill country have gathered against us.”

Joshua therefore went up from Gilgal, and with him all the army of warriors, exceedingly strong. And the Lord said to Joshua: “Do not fear them, for I have delivered them into your hands; none of them will be able to withstand you.” So Joshua fell upon them suddenly, having gone up all night from Gilgal. And the Lord threw them into confusion before Israel; and he crushed them with a great slaughter at Gibeon, pursuing them along the ascent of Beth-horon, and striking them as far as Azekah and Makkedah.

And while they were fleeing from the Israelites, and were on the ascent of Beth-horon, the Lord cast great stones upon them from heaven as far as Azekah; and far more died from the hailstones than those whom the Israelites struck with the sword. Then Joshua spoke to the Lord on the day when he delivered the Amorite into the sight of the Israelites, and he said before them: “Sun, do not move against Gibeon, and Moon, against the valley of Aijalon.” And the Sun and Moon stood still until the nation had taken vengeance on its enemies. Is this not written in the Book of the Just? So the Sun stood in the middle of the sky and did not hasten to set for the space of one day. There had been no day like it before or afterward, when the Lord obeyed the voice of a man fighting on behalf of Israel.

And Joshua returned with all Israel to the camp at Gilgal. For the five kings had fled and hidden themselves in a cave at the city of Makkedah. And it was reported to Joshua that five kings had been found hiding in the cave at Makkedah. He then ordered his companions and said: “Roll enormous stones to the mouth of the cave, and station diligent men to guard those shut inside. But you must not remain here; pursue the enemies and cut down the rear ranks of all the fugitives. Do not allow them to enter the strongholds of their cities, for God has delivered them into your hands.”

After the adversaries had been struck down in a great slaughter and had been almost completely destroyed, those who had been able to escape from Israel entered the fortified cities. And the whole army returned to Joshua at Makkedah, where the camp then was, safe and at full strength; and no one dared mutter against the Israelites.

Joshua then ordered, saying: “Open the mouth of the cave and bring out to me the five kings who are hiding in it.” The servants did as they had been commanded and brought out to him the five kings from the cave: the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon. When they had been brought out to him, he summoned all the men of Israel and said to the commanders of the army who were with him: “Go and place your feet upon the necks of these kings.” When they had gone and had trodden upon the necks of those beneath their feet, he said to them again: “Do not fear or be terrified; take courage and be strong. For thus will the Lord deal with all your enemies against whom you fight.”

Then Joshua struck them and killed them, and hanged them on five stakes; and they remained hanging until evening. When the Sun was setting, he ordered his companions to take them down from the gallows. After taking them down, they threw them into the cave in which they had hidden, and placed great stones over them, which remain to the present day.

**R.** Amen.

**Hymn.** *Unbegotten God the Father.* See fol. 101.

**Capitulum.** May your unblemished law convert our souls, and may your faithful testimony grant wisdom to the simple; may justice also gladden our hearts, not grieve them; and may your command enlighten the eyes of our minds.

Our Father.

**P.** For all things serve you.

**P.** For all things serve you.

**V.** Glory and honor to the Father.

**Prayer.** O Lord, may your Word, which endures forever in heaven, always dwell in the temple of your Church, so that the presence of its inhabitant may be unfailing splendor to the dwelling-place.
