[Col. 0442B] Lauda. Praise the Lord from the heavens on high.

V. The sun and moon, all the stars and the light.

Psalm CXLVIII.

Reading from the Book of Ruth (Chapter I).

R. Thanks be to God.

In the days of one of the judges, when the judges ruled, there was a famine in the land. A man went out from Bethlehem of Judah to dwell as a stranger in the land of Moab, with his wife and two sons. He was called Elimelech, and his wife Noemi; and his two sons were called Mahlon and Chelion, Ephrathites from Bethlehem of Judah. They entered the region of Moab and lived there.

Elimelech, Noemi’s husband, died, and she remained with her sons. They took Moabite wives, one of whom was called Orpah and the other Ruth. They remained there for ten years, and both sons—Mahlon and Chelion—also died. The woman was left bereft of her two sons and her husband.

She rose to go to her homeland with both daughters-in-law from the region of Moab, for she had heard that the Lord had looked upon his people and given them food. So she departed from the place of her sojourn with both daughters-in-law. As she was already on the road to return to the land of Judah, she said to them: “Go into your father’s house. May the Lord show mercy to you, as you have done with the dead and with me. May he grant you to find rest in the houses of the husbands whom you are to receive.” And she kissed them. They raised their voices and began to weep, saying: “We will go with you to your people.”

But she answered them: “Return, my daughters. Why are you coming with me? Do I still have sons in my womb, so that you could hope for husbands from me? Return, my daughters, and go; for I am already worn out in old age and unfit for marriage. Even if I could conceive this night and bear sons, if you were willing to wait for them until they grew and reached the age of puberty, you would be old women before you married. Do not do this, I beg you, my daughters, for your distress has weighed upon me even more, and the hand of the Lord has gone out against me.”

They again raised their voices and began to weep. Orpah kissed her mother-in-law and returned, but Ruth clung to her mother-in-law. Noemi said to her: “Behold, your sister-in-law has returned to her people and to her gods; go with her.”

But she answered: “Do not oppose me by asking me to leave you and depart. Wherever you go, I will go; and wherever you dwell, I too will dwell. Your people shall be my people, and your God my God. In the land that receives you when you die, I shall die, and there shall I receive a place of burial. May God do these things to me, and add more, if anything but death separates me and you.”

When Noemi saw that Ruth was firmly resolved to go with her, she did not wish to oppose her or persuade her further to return to her people. So they went together and came to Bethlehem. When they entered the city, the news quickly spread among everyone, and the women said: “This is that Noemi.”

She said to them: “Do not call me Noemi”—that is, “beautiful”—“but call me Mara”—that is, “bitter”—“because the Almighty has filled me with great bitterness. I went out full, and the Lord has brought me back empty. Why, then, do you call me Noemi, whom the Lord has humbled and the Almighty has afflicted?”

So Noemi returned with Ruth the Moabite, her daughter-in-law, from the land of her sojourn, and she came back to Bethlehem when the barley harvest was beginning.

(Chapter II.) Now Elimelech had a kinsman, a powerful and wealthy man, named Booz. Ruth the Moabite said to her mother-in-law: “If you command me, I will go into the field and gather the ears that have escaped the hands of the harvesters, wherever I find favor with a kind master.”

She answered her: “Go, my daughter.” So she went and gathered behind the harvesters.

It happened that the field belonged to a man named Booz, who was of the family of Elimelech. And behold, he came from Bethlehem and said to the harvesters: “The Lord be with you.” They answered him: “May the Lord bless you.”

Booz said to the young man who was in charge of the harvesters: “Whose girl is this?” He answered: “She is a Moabite who came with Noemi from the region of Moab, and she asked to gather the ears that remained, following the footsteps of the harvesters. From morning until now she has stood in the field and has not returned home even for a moment.”

Booz said to Ruth: “Listen, my daughter. Do not go to gather in another field, and do not leave this place; but join my girls, and follow wherever they harvest. For I have commanded my young men that no one molest you. If you are thirsty, go to the vessels and drink the water from which my young men also drink.”

She fell on her face, bowed down, and said: “How have I found such favor before your eyes, that you should acknowledge me, a foreign woman?”

He answered her: “Everything that you did for your mother-in-law after your husband’s death has been reported to me, and also that you left your parents and the land in which you were born and came to a people whom previously you did not know. May the Lord repay you for your work, and may you receive a full reward from the Lord, the God of Israel, to whom you have come and under whose wings you have taken refuge.”

She said: “I have found favor before your eyes, my lord, for you have consoled me and spoken to the heart of your servant, though I am not like one of your girls.”

Booz said to her: “When it is time to eat, come here, eat bread, and dip your morsel in vinegar.” So she sat beside the harvesters, gathered roasted grain for herself, ate, was satisfied, and kept what remained.

Then she rose to gather ears as usual. Booz commanded his young men, saying: “Even if she wishes to harvest with you, do not hinder her; and deliberately throw some of your sheaves for her, leaving them so that she may gather without shame, and do not rebuke her as she gathers.”

So she gathered in the field until evening. When she beat out and threshed what she had gathered, she found about an ephah of barley—that is, three measures. Carrying it, she returned to the city and showed it to her mother-in-law; moreover, she brought out and gave her the leftovers of the food with which she had been satisfied.

Her mother-in-law said to her: “Where did you gather today, and where did you work? Blessed be the one who showed you mercy.” She told her with whom she had worked and said that the man’s name was Booz.

Noemi answered her: “Blessed is he by the Lord, because he has preserved for the living and the dead the same kindness that he had shown.” And again she said: “The man is our kinsman.”

“And he also commanded me,” Ruth said, “to remain with his harvesters until all the crops were harvested.”

Her mother-in-law said to her: “It is better, my daughter, for you to go out to harvest with his girls, lest someone resist you in another field.”

So she joined Booz’s girls and harvested with them until the barley and wheat were stored in the granaries.

(Chapter III.) After she had returned to her mother-in-law, the latter said to her: “My daughter, I shall seek rest for you and arrange that it may go well with you. This Booz, whose girls you joined in the field, is our kinsman, and tonight he is winnowing barley on the threshing floor. Wash, therefore, anoint yourself, put on your finer garments, and go down to the threshing floor. Do not let the man see you until he has finished eating and drinking. When he goes to sleep, note the place where he lies; then come, uncover the cloak with which he is covered at his feet, throw yourself down, and lie there. He will tell you what you must do.”

She answered: “Whatever you command me, I will do.”

She went down to the threshing floor and did everything her mother-in-law had commanded. When Booz had eaten and drunk and had become more cheerful, and had gone to sleep beside the heap of sheaves, she came secretly; and, after uncovering the cloak at his feet, she lay down.

And behold, at midnight the man was startled and troubled. He saw a woman lying at his feet and said to her: “Who are you?”

She answered: “I am Ruth, your servant. Spread your cloak over your maidservant, because you are a kinsman.”

He said: “You are blessed by the Lord, my daughter, and you have surpassed your former kindness by this latter one, because you have not followed young men, whether poor or rich. Therefore do not be afraid, but whatever you have said to me I will do for you. All the people who dwell within the gates of my city know that you are a woman of virtue. I do not deny that I am your kinsman, but there is another kinsman closer than I. Remain tonight. In the morning, if he wishes to retain you by right of kinship, well and good; but if he does not wish to do so, I will receive you without hesitation, as the Lord lives. Sleep until morning.”

So she slept at his feet until the night had passed. She rose before people could recognize one another and Booz said: “Take care that no one knows that you came here.”

And again he said: “Spread out the cloak with which you are covered and hold it with both hands.” When she had spread it and held it, he measured six measures of barley and placed them upon her.

Carrying them, she entered the city and came to her mother-in-law. The latter said to her: “What happened, my daughter?” She told her everything the man had done for her and said: “Behold, he gave me six measures of barley and said, ‘I do not want you to return empty to your home.’”

Noemi said: “Wait, my daughter, until we see what the outcome will be. For the man will not rest until he has completed what he said.”

(Chapter IV.) Booz went up to the gate and sat there. When he saw the kinsman pass by, the one previously mentioned, he said to him: “Turn aside for a while and sit here,” calling him by his name. He turned aside and sat.

Booz took ten men from the elders of the city and said to them: “Sit here.” When they had sat down, he spoke to the kinsman: “Noemi, who has returned from the region of Moab, is selling the portion of the field belonging to our brother Elimelech. I wanted you to know this and to tell you in the presence of all those sitting here and the elders of my people. If you wish to possess it by right of kinship, buy it and possess it. But if it displeases you, tell me, so that I may know what I ought to do; for there is no kinsman apart from you who is first, and me, who am second.”

He answered: “I will buy the field.”

Booz said to him: “When you buy the field from the hand of the woman, you must also take Ruth the Moabite, who was the wife of the deceased, in order to raise up the name of your kinsman.”

He answered: “I yield my right of kinship, for I ought not to destroy the posterity of my family. Use my privilege, which I freely declare myself willing to surrender.”

Now this was the ancient custom in Israel among kinsmen: whenever one yielded his right to another, to make the transfer binding, the man removed his sandal and gave it to his kinsman. This was the testimony of the transfer in Israel.

So Booz said to his kinsman: “Take off your sandal.” And he immediately removed it from his foot.

Booz said to the elders and to all the people: “You are witnesses today that I have acquired everything that belonged to Elimelech, Chelion, and Mahlon, from the hand of Noemi; and that I have taken Ruth the Moabite, Mahlon’s wife, in marriage, in order to raise up the name of the deceased in his inheritance, so that his name may not be erased from his family, his brothers, or his people. You are witnesses of this.”

All the people who were at the gate and the elders answered: “We are witnesses. May the Lord make this woman who is entering your house like Rachel and Leah, who built up the house of Israel, so that she may be an example of virtue in Ephratha and have a celebrated name in Bethlehem. May your house be like the house of Phares, whom Tamar bore to Judah, from the offspring that the Lord will give you by this girl.”

So Booz took Ruth and received her as his wife. He went in to her, and the Lord granted her conception, and she bore a son.

The women said to Noemi: “Blessed is the Lord, who has not allowed a successor to your family to fail, and whose name may be called in Israel. May you have one who comforts your soul and nourishes your old age; for your daughter-in-law has borne him, and he will love you. He is much better for you than if you had seven sons.”

Noemi took the child and placed him in her lap, and she served as his nurse and bearer. The neighboring women congratulated her, saying: “A son has been born to Noemi.” They called his name Obed. He is the father of Jesse, the father of David.

These are the generations of Phares: Phares begot Esron; Esron begot Aram; Aram begot Aminadab; Aminadab begot Nahasson; Nahasson begot Salmon; Salmon begot Booz; Booz begot Obed; Obed begot Jesse; Jesse begot David the king.

[Col. 0446B] R. Amen.

Hymn.

The time of night is now passing;

Already the cock is crowing;

At the cock’s crow, hope is restored to the living;

Salvation is poured back upon the sick.

Rise, weighed down by sleep;

Confess the guilt of your heart,

And sing praise to Jesus,

Who redeemed us with his blood.

Not like the deceitful disciple,

Who, bringing peace with a kiss

While holding deceit in his heart,

Betrayed the Master to the crowds.

Jesus was seized by the impious;

The disciples were scattered;

He spoke as Lord,

Bringing scandal in the night.

Jesus, while proclaiming his cross

To his disciples,

Warned that he would be denied;

Peter denied that he would do so.

Peter, fervent in spirit,

Followed into the praetorium;

But, recognized as a disciple,

He denied Christ the Lord.

Peter swore to everyone

That he did not know the man.

For the voice of the cock resounds,

And Peter remembers his guilt.

[Col. 0446D] When Jesus looked upon Peter,

When he received Peter’s faith,

Peter, weeping, recovered

What shortly before he had lost.

And we pray you, O Lord,

To receive Peter’s faith,

And the apostolic faith,

As we weep for our crime.

When the cock crows, we come;

We render praises to God,

Giving him true faith

In our own confession.

Depart, prince of demons,

With your harmful phantoms.

[Col. 0447A] Now truth has cleansed us;

Now charity has wiped away our reproaches.

Therefore, O God, we ask you

To destroy the wandering demons

By the sign of salvation,

And free us from fear.

At this hour of night, foreknowing

The glory that was to come,

David multiplies prayers to God,

Keeping watch at Matins.

We ought to rise at this hour

With that vigor of body

And that resolve of spirit

By which we may be cleansed of filth.

Rise up, O God, with us,

[Col. 0447B] Receive the praises of your servants,

Cleansing slippery hearts

By the grace of the new light.

To God the Father be glory,

And to his only Son,

258 With the Paraclete Spirit,

Reigning throughout every age.

Amen.

Supplication. Let us pray. fol. 138.

Chapters. O God, Son of God, who willingly endured the snare of hunters and likewise are believed to have been crucified willingly: grant us both to rejoice uniquely in the acceptance of your passion and faithfully to be raised up by the joy of your resurrection. Thus may we, who devotedly begin to sing the solemnities of your passion in songs, be more abundantly enlightened by the sight of your light.

Our Father.

Lauda. His praise is in the choir.

Prayer. Your praise, O Lord.

Another Lauda. Let them praise the name of God in the choir.

Prayer. God, who by ineffable … fol. 181.

Lauda. How greatly your works have been magnified, O Lord, until evening!

The Lord be with you.

R. And with you.

Antiphon. Do not hand me over, O Lord, to the desire of the sinner; they have plotted against me.

P. Do not abandon me, lest they ever be exalted.

V. Rescue me, O Lord, from the evil man; deliver me from the unjust and deceitful man.

P. Do not abandon me.

The Lord be with you.

R. And with you.

[Col. 0447D] Lauda. Rescue me, O Lord, from the slanders of men, because I have kept your commandments. Make your face shine upon your servant.

P. And teach me your ordinances, O Lord.

V. Wonderful are your testimonies, O Lord; therefore my soul has searched them out.

P. And teach me.

V. Glory, etc.

P. And teach me.

Hymn. The Word of the Father. fol. 252.

Chapters. We know, O Lord, that, after enduring the injury of your betrayer, you did not abandon patience even unto death. And when that insatiable murderer handed you, the Master, over to be killed, you nevertheless did not wish even him to die. Grant us, therefore, we ask, steadfastness in enduring the wicked and the resolve to hold fast to examples of patience. Let the abyss of anger not cast us down, nor let the evil tempter, like a thief, defile us at any hour during the night of this world, so that the marks of your passion may be for us a protection in unwearied vigilance.

Our Father.

Humble yourselves for the blessing.

The Lord be with you.

R. And with you.

Blessing. Christ, Son of God, who once, at this time in the course of the feast of this day, endured the tongues of those who reviled him, make the speech of all of us eloquent.

R. Amen.

And may he who suffered innocently for the ungodly make you his companions without end.

R. Amen.

May you, saddened as you now receive his passion, approach the joy of his resurrection with rejoicing hearts.

R. Amen.

Through mercy.

[Col. 0448B] Lauda. Your word is a lamp for my feet, O Lord.

P. And a light for my paths, my God.

V. I swore and resolved to keep the judgments of your justice.

Prayer. Show us your light, O Lord, through knowledge of your law, so that, with your help, we may be raised up from slippery falls and hasten eagerly in your light toward the joys of your eternity appointed for us. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Lauda. Sinners have laid traps for me.

P. But I have not declined from your commandments, O Lord.

V. I have acquired your testimonies as an inheritance forever, because they are the joy of my heart.

Prayer. Grant us, O Lord, help to turn aside from the hatred of the wicked and to overcome the deceit of transgressors. Be the protector of those who hope in your word, and receive the humble according to your utterance, so that we may keep your commandments, fear your judgments, and obtain forgiveness for our offenses. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Lauda. I have hated and abhorred the wicked.

P. But I have loved your law, my God.

V. You are my helper and my protector, and I have hoped in your word.

Prayer. Help us, O Lord, and we shall be saved; for when you withdraw, there is destruction, and when you preserve us, there is the fullness of life. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Intercessions. Turn your anger away from us, O Lord. With its prayer, fol. 183.

SECOND FERIA AFTER THE MID-FEAST DAY.

At Matins.

Rise up, O Lord; save me, my God. Psalm III.

Prayer. Rise up, O Lord our God, to aid the humble and to destroy those who persecute us. Crush our adversaries, who strive to turn us away from your commandments by deceitful promises and open threats. Their snares will accomplish nothing if we are always protected by the help of your grace. R. Amen.

Through.

Antiphon 1. The kings of the earth stood forth, and the rulers gathered together against the Lord and against his Christ.

P. He who dwells in the heavens will laugh at them, and the Lord will mock them; in his anger he will trouble them.

V. Why did the nations rage, and the peoples meditate on vain things?

P. He who dwells.

V. Glory.

P. He who dwells.

Prayer. God, Father of the only-begotten Son, who dwell in the heavens and show that all the kings of the earth and rulers who gather against your Christ are to be laughed at and mocked: grant us this special gift of your grace, that we may in no way yield to adversity. Thus let unbelief be troubled in your anger, so that through your help our faith may be crowned. R. Amen.

Through.

Antiphon 2. You have hated, O Lord, all who work iniquity.

P. You will destroy those who speak lies.

V. Judge them, O God. Let them fall because of their own thoughts.

Prayer. God, who hate all who work iniquity, fill us with the protection of charity, so that those who speak lies against you may, when they are eventually converted to you, feel the full measure of their sorrow. R. Amen.

Through.

Antiphon 3. For there is no truth in the mouth of the enemies; their heart is vain. Their throat is an open tomb.

P. They acted deceitfully with their tongues; judge them, O God.

V. For you have struck all those who oppose me without cause; you have crushed the teeth of sinners.

[Col. 0449C] Prayer. There is no truth in the mouth of your enemies, O Lord, because, when they turn away from you in their inmost being, their heart is destroyed by vanity. Grant us, therefore, that our tongue, together with purity of conscience, may offer you an acceptable hymn, so that it may not become an open tomb of wickedness. R. Amen.

Through.

R. I am afflicted with miseries and troubled; all day long I went about in sadness, for my soul is filled with mockeries.

P. And there is no soundness in my flesh.

V. For your arrows are fixed in me, and you have strengthened your hand upon me.

P. And there is no soundness.

Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ, who, before your death, knowingly foretold that the one who would betray you would hand you over to death; and who, when you were dying, descended to the underworld, to that place where the dwelling of every living person is established: grant that, when the time of our calling arrives, we may not go there only to remain in punishment. You, our liberator, entered there through forgiveness when you died; but, extending your hand from the depths of hell, reveal your power and free us—you who alone deigned to lay down your soul for the ungodly. R. Amen.

Through.

At Lauds.

Antiphon. For I myself acknowledge my iniquity, O Lord; cleanse me from it. I plead with you: have mercy on me, have mercy.

Psalm L.

Prayer. Acknowledging our iniquities and laying our offenses before you, Lord, we pray as suppliants, wailing with tears and striking our breasts: turn your face away from our crimes and wipe away all the sins we have committed. Create, therefore, in our hearts, O God, what you love; and by your customary mercy forgive what you hate. If our vices repeatedly provoke you to anger, may your forgiveness make you favorable toward us. R. Amen.

Through.

At the Canticle. Antiphon. Let all who persecute me be confounded, and let me not be confounded; let them fear, and let me not fear.

Canticle of Jeremiah (Chapter XVII).

Heal me, O Lord, and I shall be healed; * save me, and I shall be saved, for you are my praise and my strength.

[Col. 0450B] Behold, they themselves say to me: “Where is the word of the Lord? * Let it come.” But I am not troubled, following you as shepherd.

And I did not desire the day of man; you know it. * What came forth from my lips was right in your sight.

Do not become a terror to me; * you are my hope in the day of my affliction.

Let all who persecute me be confounded, and let me not be confounded; * let them fear, and let me not fear.

Bring upon them a day of affliction, * and crush them with double destruction.

Prayer. Let all those who persecute your holy name in us, O Lord, be confounded, and let us not be confounded—we who venerate and believe in the affront of your passion and the power of your resurrection. May the power of your glory prevail, both to deter those who persecute you from wickedness and to join those who believe in you to everlasting rejoicing. R. Amen.

Through, etc.

260 At the Benedictus. Antiphon. I have cried to you, O Lord, and in the morning my prayer will come before you.

V. O Lord, God of my salvation, by day I cried out, and by night before you.

Lauda. Praise the Lord in his holy ones; praise him with psaltery and harp. Psalm CL.

Reading from the Book of Samuel (First Book of Kings, Chapter I).

R. Thanks be to God.

In those days Hannah conceived and bore a son, and she called his name Samuel, because she had asked him from the Lord. Elkanah and all his household went up to offer the Lord the solemn sacrifice and fulfill his vow, but Hannah did not go up, for she said to her husband: “I will not go until the child is weaned; then I will bring him, and he will appear in the presence of God and remain there continually.”

Her husband Elkanah said to her: “Do what seems good to you, and remain until you have weaned him.” So the woman stayed and nursed her son until she had weaned him. After she had weaned him, she took him with her, along with three calves, three measures of flour, and a jar of wine, and brought him to the house of the Lord at Shiloh.

The child was still very young. They sacrificed a calf and presented the child to Heli. Hannah said: “I beg you, my lord, as your soul lives, I am that woman who stood here before you praying to the Lord. I prayed for this child, and the Lord granted me my petition, which I asked of him. Therefore I have lent him to the Lord for all the days that he is lent to the Lord.” And she worshiped the Lord there.

Hannah prayed and said: “My heart has exulted in the Lord, and my horn has been exalted in my God my Savior.”

(Chapter II.) Elkanah returned to Ramatha, his city. The boy Samuel was ministering in the presence of the Lord before Heli the priest.

Now the sons of Heli were sons of Belial, not knowing the Lord or the duty of priests toward the people. Whenever anyone sacrificed a victim, the priest’s servant would come while the meat was being boiled. He had a three-pronged fork in his hand, and he would thrust it into the cauldron, kettle, pot, or pan; and whatever the fork lifted, the priest took for himself. This is what he did for all the Israelites who came to Shiloh.

Even before they burned the fat, the priest’s servant would come and say to the one sacrificing: “Give me meat, so that I may cook it for the priest; for I will not accept cooked meat from you, but raw.”

The one sacrificing would say: “Let the fat first be burned according to the custom, and then take as much as your soul desires.”

But he would answer: “No indeed; otherwise you will give it, or I will take it by force.”

The sin of the young men was very great before the Lord, because they turned people away from the Lord’s sacrifice.

Samuel ministered in the presence of the Lord, the boy girded with a linen ephod. His mother made him a little tunic, which she brought to him on the appointed days, going up with her husband to offer the solemn sacrifice.

Heli blessed Elkanah and his wife Hannah and said: “May the Lord give you offspring from this woman in return for the loan that you lent to the Lord.” And they went to their place.

The Lord visited Hannah, and she conceived and bore three sons and two daughters. The boy Samuel grew in greatness before God.

Heli was very old, and he heard all that his sons did to all Israel, and how they slept with the women who kept watch at the door of the tabernacle. He said to them: “Why do you do such things, things that I hear from all the people? Do not do this, my sons, for the report I hear is not good: you are making the Lord’s people transgress. If a man sins against another man, God may be appeased on his behalf; but if he sins against the Lord, who will pray for him?”

They did not listen to the voice of their father, because the Lord wished to kill them. But the boy Samuel advanced and grew, and he was pleasing both to God and to men. R. Amen.

Hymn. The time of night is now passing. fol. 257.

Chapters. Deliver us, O Lord, from iniquitous lips and from a boastful tongue—you who were hung upon the balance of the Cross. Grant that neither an opportunity to accuse may be opened to the accuser, nor your people yield to his snares, nor deceitful suggestion stir up your anger. But you, O Lord, cut down with the divine sword that clever ambusher of the human race, and arise in glorious goodness for the distress of the poor.

[Col. 0452A] Our Father. Deliver us from evil, etc.

Lauda. Your word is a lamp for my feet, O Lord.

V. And a light for my paths, my God.

P. I swore and resolved to keep the judgments of your justice.

Prayer. Show us your light, O Lord, through knowledge of your law, so that, with your help, we may be raised up from slippery falls; so that we may hasten eagerly in your light toward the joys of your eternity appointed for us. R. Amen.

Through.

At Terce.

From the Proverbs of Solomon (Chapter XXVIII).

R. Thanks be to God.

My son, whoever gives to the poor will not be in need; whoever despises the one who begs will suffer want. When the wicked rise up, people will hide themselves; when they perish, the righteous will multiply.

(Chapter XXIX.) A man who, stiff-necked, despises the one who reproves him will suddenly be destroyed, and healing will not follow him. When the righteous multiply, the people will rejoice; when the wicked take power, the people groan. A man who loves wisdom makes his father glad; but whoever nourishes a prostitute will lose his substance. A just king raises up the land; a greedy man destroys it. A flattering man who speaks smooth words to his friend spreads a net for his steps. A snare entangles a sinful, wicked man, but the righteous will praise and rejoice. R. Amen.

Reading from the Book of Samuel (First Book of Kings, Chapter II).

R. Thanks be to God.

In those days: A man of God came to Eli and said to him: “Thus says the Lord: Did I not openly reveal myself to the house of your father when they were in Egypt, in the house of Pharaoh? And I chose him from all the tribes of Israel for myself as priest, to ascend my altar, burn incense for me, and carry the ephod before me; and I gave to the house of your father all the offerings of the sons of Israel. Why have you spurned my sacrifice with your heel, and my gifts which I commanded to be offered in the temple? And why have you honored your sons more than me, so that you might eat the first portions of every sacrifice of my people? Therefore says the Lord God of Israel: Speaking, I spoke that your house and the house of your father should minister in my sight forever. But now, says the Lord, far be this from me; rather, whoever honors me, I will glorify, but those who despise me shall be held in low esteem.

“Behold, the days are coming, and I will cut off your arm and the arm of your father’s house, so that there will be no old man in your house. And you will see your rival in the temple, amid all the prosperity of Israel; and there will be no old man in your house for all days. Nevertheless, I will not altogether remove a man from my altar, but only so that your eyes may fail and your soul may waste away; and the greater part of your house shall die when they reach manhood. This shall be the sign for you of what is to come: your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, shall both die on one day.

“And I will raise up for myself a faithful priest, who will act according to my heart and my soul; and I will build him a faithful house, and he shall walk before my Anointed One all his days. It shall happen that whoever remains in your house will come to be prayed for, and to offer a silver coin and a round loaf of bread, saying: ‘Assign me, I beg you, to one priestly office, so that I may eat a morsel of bread.’”

(Chapter III.) Now the boy Samuel ministered before Eli, and the word of the Lord was precious; in those days there was no clear vision. It happened one day that Eli was lying in his place, and his eyes had grown dim, so that he could not see the lamp of God before it was extinguished. Samuel, however, was sleeping in the temple of the Lord, where the ark of God was.

And the Lord called Samuel. He answered: “Here I am.” And he ran to Eli and said: “Here I am, for you called me.” He said: “I did not call you, my son; go back and sleep.” He went away and slept.

And the Lord called again: “Samuel.” Samuel arose and went to Eli and said: “Here I am, for you called me.” He answered: “I did not call you, my son; go back and sleep.” Now Samuel did not yet know the Lord, and the word of the Lord had not yet been revealed to him.

And the Lord called Samuel again, a third time. He arose and went to Eli and said: “Here I am, for you called me.” Eli therefore understood that the Lord was calling the boy, and he said to Samuel: “Go, sleep; and if he calls you again, say: ‘Speak, Lord, for your servant is listening.’” Samuel went away and slept in his place.

And the Lord came and stood there, and called as he had called the second and third time: “Samuel.” And Samuel said: “Speak, Lord, for your servant is listening.” And the Lord said to Samuel: “Behold, I am doing a deed in Israel, which whoever hears will have both ears ringing. On that day I will raise up against Eli everything that I have spoken concerning his house; I will begin and I will complete it. For I foretold to him that I would judge his house forever, because of the iniquity of his sons, since he knew that his sons were acting disgracefully and did not correct them. Therefore I swore to the house of Eli that the iniquity of his house would not be expiated by sacrifices or offerings forever.”

Samuel slept until morning, and opened the doors of the house of the Lord. Samuel was afraid to tell Eli the vision. So Eli called Samuel and said: “My son Samuel?” He answered: “Here I am.” And he questioned him: “What is the word of the Lord that he spoke to you? Do not hide it from me. May God do these things to you, and add these things, if you hide from me any word of all that was spoken to you.” Samuel therefore told him every word and concealed nothing from him. And he answered: “It is the Lord. Let him do what is good in his sight.”

Samuel grew, and the Lord was with him.

R. Amen.

Antiphon 1. Heal me, Lord; my bones are troubled, and my soul is greatly troubled. You, Lord, turn back and deliver my soul. V. Lord, do not rebuke me in your anger, nor correct me in your fury.

Prayer. Christ, Son of God, whose bones and soul were troubled in the Passion, heal the wound of our heart, so that, once the bones of our virtues have been strengthened, we may sing the praises of your Passion in such a way that we may afterward rejoice all the more in the glory of the Resurrection to come. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 2. My eye has grown dim because of bitterness; I have grown old among all my enemies. Depart from me, all you who work iniquity, for the Lord has heard the voice of my weeping. V. I have labored in my groaning; every night I will wash my bed; I will water my couch with tears.

Prayer. Only-begotten Son of God the Father, Jesus Christ, whose divine eyes are not troubled by the injury of the Passion, yet who, having assumed Passion in humanity alone, receive us your servants: in whose path of bitterness both the eye has grown dim and life, set among enemies, grows old—so exclude every access of wickedness from us that we may be made possessors of eternal happiness. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 3. Lord God, save me according to my justice; and let the wickedness of the sinner be brought to an end, and direct the just one, O God who searches hearts and kidneys. V. Lord my God, in you I have hoped; save me from all those who persecute me, and deliver me.

R. Let those who await you not be put to shame because of me, Lord, Lord of hosts. Let those who seek you not be confounded because of me, God of Israel. P. For because of you I have endured reproach. V. Do not turn your face away from your servant, for I am troubled; hear me quickly. P. For because of you.

Prayers. To you we cry, Lord. P. Have mercy and spare your people. V. Be our advocate, you who commend your mother from the cross. P. Have mercy. V. You who receive Peter’s tears, gently raise us up after our fall. P. Have mercy. V. So that we who now believe that you suffered may live without end with you. P. Have mercy.

Psalm L.

Hymn. O Nazarene, light of Bethlehem. folio 144.

Prayer. Lord God, save your people according to the justice-giving gift accepted by you, in which you have granted us the mystery of holy faith, so that, when the title of the Cross has been set forth, the wickedness of the sinner may be brought to an end, and the just may be directed along the paths of equity.

Our Father.

At Sext.

Reading from the Book of the Prophet Ezekiel (Chapter XXXIV).

R. Thanks be to God.

The word of the Lord came to me, saying: “Son of man, prophesy concerning the shepherds of Israel; prophesy and say to the shepherds: Thus says the Lord: Woe to the shepherds of Israel who fed themselves. Are not flocks fed by shepherds? You ate the milk, clothed yourselves with the wool, and slaughtered what was fat; but you did not feed my flock. You did not strengthen the weak, heal the sick, bind up the broken, bring back the cast-away, or seek the lost; but you ruled them with harshness and power.

“And my sheep were scattered because there was no shepherd, and they became food for all the beasts of the field and were scattered. My flocks wandered over every mountain and every high hill; and my flocks were scattered over the whole face of the earth, with no one to seek them.

“Therefore, shepherds, hear the word of the Lord: As I live, says the Lord, because my flocks became a prey and my sheep became food for all the beasts of the field, because there was no shepherd—for the shepherds did not seek my flock, but fed themselves and not my flocks—therefore, shepherds, hear the word of the Lord.

“Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I myself will seek my flock from their hand, and I will make them cease from feeding my flock any longer; and my flock shall no longer be food for them, says the Lord Almighty.”

R. Amen.

Antiphon 1. When I called upon you, you heard me, God of my justice. V. In tribulation you enlarged me. Have mercy on me and hear my prayer.

Prayer. When we call upon you, hear us, Christ, who are our justice, so that you who suffered the injury of tribulations for the ungodly may grant indulgence to us who entreat you. R. Amen.

Through.

Antiphon 2. I have labored in my groaning; every night I will wash my bed; I will water my couch with my tears. V. My eye is troubled because of anger; I have grown old among all my enemies.

Prayer. We believe that you, Jesus, labored in groaning for the ungodly through the Passion. Therefore we ask that the singular example of your patience may benefit our soul, so that night after night we may water our bed and couch with tears in such a way that we may continually receive the aids of holiness. R. Amen.

Through.

Antiphon 3. The Lord has heard the voice of my weeping; the Lord has heard my supplication. V. Depart from me, all you who work iniquity, for the Lord has heard the voice of my weeping.

R. All day long I walked in sorrow. P. For my soul is filled with illusions, and there is no health in my flesh. V. I am bent and greatly humbled; I roared continually because of the groaning of my heart. P. For my soul is filled with illusions, and there is no health in my flesh.

Prayers. Word of the Most High Father. P. Redeemer, have mercy on sinners. V. Destroy our crime, you who were handed over for us. P. Redeemer, have mercy on sinners. V. Purify us from vices, you who were struck with blows. P. Redeemer, have mercy on sinners. V. You were given gall to drink for us; fill us with sweetness. P. Redeemer, have mercy on sinners. V. Kindle us with the fire of your cross, whom you redeemed with blood. P. Redeemer, have mercy on sinners.

Hymn. O Nazarene, light. folio 144.

Prayer. Save us, Lord, because of your mercy, for you know that we are weakened by our own iniquity; and since our soul is troubled by fear of your righteous judgments, let it rest because of the most joyful gift of your indulgence, and let the one who confesses the wounds of his sins receive it as the reward of healing, so that, cleansed by grace, he may receive forgiveness and reach you without shame.

Our Father.

At None.

Reading from the Book of Ecclesiasticus of Solomon (Chapter III).

R. Thanks be to God.

Son, how great is the power of God alone, and he is honored by all. Do not investigate what is higher than you, and do not seek what is stronger than you; but always consider what God has commanded you, and do not be curious about many of his works. For you have no need of the things hidden from your eyes. Do not investigate excessively matters that are superfluous, and do not be curious about many of his works. For many things beyond human understanding have been shown to you. For suspicion of them has overthrown many and held their senses in vanity. A hard heart will fare badly at the end, and whoever loves danger will perish in it. A heart that enters upon two paths will have no success, and a perverse heart will be scandalized in them. A wicked heart will be weighed down with sorrows, and the sinner will add to sinning. A wise heart is understood through wisdom, and a good ear will hear wisdom’s desire. Water extinguishes a burning fire, and almsgiving extinguishes sin. A wise and understanding heart will abstain from sin and will have success in works of justice.

R. Amen.

Reading from the Book of Samuel (First Book of Kings, chapter IV).

R. Thanks be to God.

In those days: Israel went out to meet the Philistines and encamped beside the Stone of Help. The Philistines came to Aphek and drew up their battle line against Israel. When the battle had begun, Israel turned its back before the Philistines; and on that day about four thousand men were struck down here and there through the fields. The people returned to the camp, and the elders of Israel said: “Why has the Lord struck us today before the Philistines? Let us bring the ark of the covenant of the Lord from Shiloh to us, so that it may come into our midst and save us from the hand of our enemies.”

So the people sent to Shiloh, and they brought from there the ark of the covenant of the Lord of hosts, who sits upon the cherubim. Eli’s two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, were with the ark of the covenant of the Lord. When the ark of the covenant of the Lord came into the camp, all the people shouted with a great cry, and the earth resounded. The Philistines heard the sound of the shouting and said: “What is this sound of such a great cry in the camp of the Hebrews?” And they learned that the ark of the Lord had come into the camp.

The Philistines were afraid, saying: “God has come into the camp.” And they groaned, saying: “Woe to us! For there was no such rejoicing yesterday or the day before. Woe to us! Who will save us from the hand of these exalted gods? These are the gods who struck Egypt with every plague in the wilderness. Take courage and be men, Philistines, lest you serve the Hebrews as they served us. Take courage and fight.”

The Philistines fought, and Israel was struck down; each man fled to his tent, and the slaughter was very great. Thirty thousand foot soldiers of Israel fell. The ark of God was captured and carried away, and Eli’s two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, died.

A man of Benjamin, running from the battle line, came to Shiloh that day with his garment torn and dust upon his head. When he arrived, Eli was sitting on a chair beside the road, watching, for his heart was anxious about the ark of the Lord. When the man entered, he announced it to the city, and the whole city wailed.

Eli heard the sound of the outcry and said: “What is the sound of this tumult?” The man hurried, came, and announced it to Eli. Eli was ninety-eight years old, and his eyes had grown dim, so that he could not see. He said to Eli: “I am the one who has come from the battle; I fled from the battle line today.”

He said to him: “What has happened, my son?” The messenger answered: “Israel fled before the Philistines, and there has been a great slaughter among the people. Moreover, your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, have died, and the ark of God has been captured.”

When he mentioned the ark of God, Eli fell backward from his chair; his neck broke, and he died. For he was an old and elderly man, and he had judged Israel for forty years.

R. Amen.

Antiphon 1. My soul trusts in the Lord, for his eyes look upon the poor. V. For behold, sinners have bent the bow; they have prepared their arrows in the quiver, to shoot in darkness at the upright in heart.

Prayer. God, whose eyes look upon the poor, grant help to our soul that trusts in you, so that we who implore healing from the wounds of your Passion may, with you as our helper, be delivered from our own sufferings. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 2. The feet of the wicked are swift to shed blood. They did not call upon God for themselves; they were afraid with fear where there was no fear. V. The fool said in his heart: “There is no God.” They were corrupt and became abominable in their pleasures; there is none who does good, not even one. The Gloria and honor are not to be said.

Prayer. Your enemies, Lord, assembled against you, not to be pierced by saving repentance, but—as was their custom—to approach you in cruel mockery in order to put you to the test. Therefore, since you, innocent, endured from enemies both mockeries and wounds, wash away our sins in these, having been appeased. R. Amen.

Antiphon 3. Lord, save me from the contradictions of the people; you will set me as head of the nations, and the God of my salvation will be exalted. V. I will love you, Lord, my strength; God is my foundation, my refuge, and my deliverer.

Hymn. O Nazarene. folio 144.

Prayer. Christ our God, who were despised by the contradictions of a stubborn people and for this reason were made head of the nations, do not allow us, whom through your Passion and Resurrection you willed to be made head, ever to be cut off from you, so that, with you as our guide, we may triumph over hostile powers—we who believe that you were exalted for us upon the gallows of the Cross.

Our Father.

At Vespers.

Lauda. You illumine my lamp, Lord.

May the Lord be always with you. R. And with you.

Antiphon. My help is from the Lord, who made heaven and earth. Psalm CXX.

Lauda. From all those who persecute me. P. Deliver me, Lord. V. Lord God, in you I have hoped; save me from all those who persecute me, and deliver me. P. Deliver.

Hymn. Word of the Father. folio 252.

Capitulum. Glorious, powerful, and merciful God, rescue us from the snares of the enemy; and, lest our soul be seized by the swift snatching of the roaring lion, let the protection of your right hand be appointed for our keeping, lest, while there is no one to redeem us, that savage one kill us, or, if there is no one to save us, he overthrow us. But you, Lion from the tribe of Judah, arise in your anger and, with the severity of judgment, destroy the ranks of the treacherous enemy; and grant that we may believe in and persevere in the commandment that you have given.

Our Father.

Humble yourselves for the blessing.

May the Lord be always with you. R. And with you.

Blessing. Christ the Lord, who by his death conquered the four-day death of our humanity, make you victors over your crime. R. Amen. And may he who allowed himself to be handed over by the wicked rescue you from the punishments of eternal torments. R. Amen. So may you live without end with him who became victor over death. R. Amen.

Through his mercy, etc.

Lauda. Your word is a lamp to my feet. folio 260.

TUESDAY.

At Matins.

Antiphon. Arise, Lord; save me. Psalm III. Prayer. Arise, Lord our God, to help the humble. folio 258.

Antiphon 1. Save me, Lord, for the holy one has failed; for truths have diminished among the children of men. Each person spoke vainly to his neighbor: “May the Lord destroy all deceitful lips and the tongue that speaks great things.”

Prayer. Save your people, Lord, for we rejoice in the glorious receiving of your Passion, so that we may not have deceitful lips in our heart, but, with a simple mouth, may put an end to vain speakers and be able to kindle charity in those who believe in you. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 2. Make known to me the paths of life, Lord; you will fill me with joy in your presence; delights are at your right hand forever. V. Preserve me, Lord, for I have hoped in you. I said to the Lord: “You are my God, for you have no need of my goods.”

Prayer. We ask you, Lord, almighty Father and God: just as you have deigned to grant us understanding, so show us the paths of eternal life. Thus, filled with joy in your presence, may we rejoice at your right hand in your kingdom. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 3. How long, Lord, will my enemy be exalted over me? Look upon me and hear me, Lord my God, lest my enemy ever say: “I have prevailed against him.” But I have hoped in your mercy. My heart exulted in your salvation.

Prayer. How long, Lord, will the enemy of our soul be exalted—the one who corrodes us with the daily rust of vices? Look upon us now and hear us, and lest our enemy boast that he has prevailed against us, raise us always to heavenly things by the victory of your Cross, and plunge beneath our feet the one who attempts to seize us, that he may be crushed. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

R. Do not harden your ear to my prayer; you have come to my aid, Lord. On the day when I called upon you, you said: P. Do not be afraid. V. Draw out the sword and close ranks against those who persecute me, and say to my soul: P. Do not be afraid.

Prayer. Do not harden your ear, Lord, to the prayer of your Church; come to her aid, so that your Divinity may not disdain her when she calls upon you—you who endured for her the harsh punishments of suffering—but, as she is conformed to your sufferings, may she also be comforted by your gifts. R. Amen.

Through.

At Lauds.

Antiphon. According to your great mercy, have mercy on me, my God. For my heart is contrite, I beg you: have mercy on me. Psalm L.

Prayer. Have mercy on us, Lord, according to your great mercy, and open the door of your clemency to those who turn back from error. Therefore, by the greatness of your mercies, we are not permitted to be overwhelmed by the weight of our evils; for we acknowledge our iniquities, and we are punished in our own eyes by the burdens of the crimes we have committed. For this reason, Lord: where we are ashamed, forgive; and what we regret having done, mercifully erase. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

At the Canticle. Antiphon. “Who will grant that my request may come, and that God may give me what I await?”

Canticle of Job (Chapter VI).

My words are full of pain, * because the arrows of the Lord are in me.

Their indignation drinks up my spirit, * and the terrors of the Lord wage war against me.

Does the wild ass bray when it has grass, * or does the ox bellow when it stands before a full manger?

Can what is tasteless and unsalted be eaten? * Or can anyone taste what, once tasted, brings death?

The things my soul formerly refused to touch * are now, in my anguish, my food.

Who will grant that my request may come, * and that God may give me what I await?

May he who began also crush me; * may he loose his hand and cut me off?

And may this be my consolation: that, while afflicting me with sorrow, he does not spare me, * and that I do not contradict holy words.

For what is my strength, that I should endure evils? * Or what is my end, that I should act patiently?

My strength is not the strength of stones, * nor is my flesh bronze.

Behold, there is no help for me in myself, * and even my necessary companions have departed from me.

R. Amen.

Prayer. Who will grant that the request of your Church may come, Christ, except you, who are the best deliverer? Grant that you, who became needy and poor for her, may in the future enrich her with heavenly gifts. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

At the Benedictus. Antiphon. In the morning I will meditate on you, for you have been my helper, Lord. V. God, my God, to you I keep watch from the light of dawn.

Canticle of Daniel III. Blessed are you, Lord God. folio 6.

Lauda. According to the multitude of his greatness: praise the Lord in his holy places. Psalm CL.

Reading from the Book of Samuel (First Book of Kings, chapter VII).

R. Thanks be to God.

In those days: The men of Kiriath-jearim came and brought back the ark of the Lord, and carried it into the house of Abinadab at Gibeah. They consecrated Eleazar, his son, to guard the ark of the Lord at Kiriath-jearim.

And from the day on which the ark of the Lord remained at Kiriath-jearim, the days multiplied—for it was already the twentieth year—and the whole house of Israel rested after the Lord.

Samuel said to the whole house of Israel: “If you turn to the Lord with all your heart, remove the foreign gods from your midst, the Baals and the Astartes; prepare your hearts for the Lord, serve him alone, and he will rescue you from the hand of the Philistines.”

So the children of Israel removed the Baals and the Astartes and served the Lord alone. Samuel said: “Gather all Israel at Mizpah, so that I may pray to the Lord for you.” They gathered at Mizpah, drew water, and poured it out before the Lord; they fasted that day and said: “We have sinned against you, Lord.” And Samuel judged the children of Israel at Mizpah.

The Philistines heard that the children of Israel had gathered at Mizpah, and the rulers of the Philistines came up against Israel. When the children of Israel heard this, they were afraid before the Philistines. The children of Israel said to Samuel: “Do not cease crying out to the Lord our God for us, so that he may save us from the hand of the Philistines.”

Samuel took one suckling lamb and offered it as a whole burnt offering to the Lord. Samuel cried out to the Lord for Israel, and the Lord heard him. And while Samuel was offering the burnt offering, the Philistines began battle against Israel. The Lord thundered with a great roar against the Philistines that day, terrified them, and they were struck down by the children of Israel.

The children of Israel went out from Mizpah, pursued the Philistines, and struck them as far as Beth-car. Samuel took one stone and placed it between Mizpah and Shen, and he called its name the Stone of Help. He said: “Thus far the Lord has helped us.”

The Philistines were humbled, and they did not come again into the borders of Israel. The hand of the Lord was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel. The cities that the Philistines had taken from Israel were restored to Israel, from Ekron to Gath, together with their territory. Israel delivered them from the hand of the Philistines, and there was peace between Israel and the Amorite.

Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life. He went every year around Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah, and judged Israel in those places. Then he returned to Ramah, where his house was, and there he judged Israel. And he built an altar there to the Lord.

Hymn. The time of night. folio 257.

Capitulum. Deliver us, Lord. folio 260.

Lauda. Sinners have set traps for me, but I have not turned aside from your commandments, Lord. V. I have acquired your testimonies as an inheritance forever, for they are the exultation of my heart.

Prayer. Grant us help, Lord; avert the hatreds of the wicked and enable us to overcome the deceit of transgressors. Be the protector of those who hope in your word, and receive the humble according to your saying, so that we may be able to keep your commandments, fear your judgments, and merit forgiveness for our offenses. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

At Terce.

Ecclesiastes of Solomon (Chapter VIII).

R. Thanks be to God.

Son, it is not in human power to restrain the spirit, nor does anyone have authority over the day of death; one is not permitted to rest when war breaks out, nor will ungodliness save the ungodly. I considered all these things and gave my heart to the many works that are done under the sun.

At times a person rules over another to his own harm. I saw the wicked buried—those who, while they were still alive, had been in the holy place and were praised in the city as though they had performed just works—but this too is vanity.

Because sentence against evil deeds is not quickly carried out, the hearts of the children of men are fully set on doing evil. Yet, although a sinner has done evil a hundred times and is sustained by patience, I know that it will be well with those who fear God, who revere his face. It will not be well with the wicked, nor will his days be prolonged; but, like a shadow, those who do not fear the face of God will pass away.

Love and hatred alike perish, and they have no part in the age or in the work that is done under the sun. Go, then, eat your bread with joy and drink your wine with gladness, for God approves your works.

R. Amen.

Reading from the Book of Samuel (First Book of Kings, chapter VIII).

R. Thanks be to God.

In those days: When Samuel had grown old, he appointed his sons as judges over Israel. The name of his firstborn son was Joel, and the name of the second was Abijah; they were judges at Beersheba. His sons did not walk in his ways, but turned after greed, accepted gifts, and perverted judgment.

Therefore all the elders of Israel gathered and came to Samuel at Ramah. They said to him: “Behold, you have grown old, and your sons do not walk in your ways. Appoint a king for us, to judge us, as all the nations have.”

The word displeased Samuel, because they had said: “Give us a king to judge us.” Samuel prayed to the Lord. The Lord said to Samuel: “Hear the voice of the people in everything they say to you; for they have not rejected you, but me, so that I should not reign over them. According to all their works, which they have done from the day when I brought them out of Egypt until this day—just as they abandoned me and served foreign gods, so they will do to you also.

“Now therefore hear their voice; nevertheless, testify against them and proclaim to them the right of the king who will reign over them.”

Samuel therefore spoke all the words of the Lord to the people who had asked him for a king, and said: “This will be the right of the king who will rule over you: he will take your sons and place them in his chariots, and make them his horsemen and runners before his chariots. He will appoint for himself tribunes and centurions, plowers of his fields, reapers of his crops, and craftsmen of his weapons and chariots.

“He will also take your daughters as perfumers, cooks, and bakers. He will take your fields, vineyards, and best olive groves and give them to his servants. He will tithe your crops and the produce of your vineyards in order to give them to his eunuchs and servants. He will also take your male servants, female servants, your finest young men, and your donkeys, and put them to his work. He will tithe your flocks, and you will be his servants.

“You will cry out on that day because of the face of your king whom you have chosen for yourselves, and the Lord will not hear you on that day, because you asked for a king.”

The people refused to hear Samuel’s voice and said: “No! There shall be a king over us, and we too shall be like all the nations; our king shall judge us and go out before us and fight our battles for us.”

Samuel heard all the words of the people and spoke them in the ears of the Lord. The Lord said to Samuel: “Hear their voice and appoint a king over them.”

R. Amen.

Antiphon 1. Each person spoke vainly to his neighbor; with deceitful lips and a heart, they spoke evil. P. May the Lord destroy all deceitful lips. V. Save me, Lord, for the holy one has failed; for truths have diminished among the children of men. P. May he destroy them.

Prayer. Those who disdain to confess you as the Son of God speak very vainly about you, Lord, with wicked voices. Therefore destroy deceitful lips from the assembly of your Church, so that, once the vanity of pride has been destroyed, the radiance of humble discipline may shine brightly within us. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 2. They seized me like a lion prepared for prey. Arise, Lord; confront them and overthrow them; deliver my soul from the hands of my enemies. V. Hear, God, my justice; attend to my supplication. Give ear to my prayer, and not to deceitful lips.

Prayer. Help, Lord, and assist your Church, which our adversary attempts to seize for devouring like a lion prepared for prey. Arise now, Lord, and confront our enemies, overthrowing them both by the glory of your Passion and by the power of your Resurrection, so that, once they have been converted, your Passion may prepare for us together the title of victory, and your Resurrection confer the eternal reward. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 3. You will destroy the fruit of the enemies, Lord, from the earth, and their offspring from the children of men. P. For they turned evil things against you; they devised plans that they could not establish. V. The Lord will trouble them in his anger, and fire will devour them. P. For they—

R. How many are the days of your servant? P. Lord, when will you execute judgment upon those who persecute me? V. Sinners have set traps for me, but I have not strayed from your commandments. P. Lord.

Prayers. Let us all say: Have mercy on us, God. P. Have mercy on us. V. You, Redeemer Jesus Christ, save the world by your death. P. Have mercy on us. V. You who were struck for us and unjustly judged. P. Have mercy on us. V. You who, bound, carry the cross and call upon the Father on the cross. P. Have mercy. V. You whose side is pierced and whose humility is mocked. P. Have mercy on us.

Hymn. O Nazarene, light. folio 144.

Capitulum. Destroy, Lord, the fruit of the enemies from the earth and their offspring from the children of men, who refuse to confess you as the one Christ, Son of God and Son of man. May your Cross, which is a stumbling block to the Jews but foolishness to the Gentiles, direct both peoples to the rule of faith and join them forever to you, to be united and crowned.

Our Father.

At Sext.

Reading from the Book of the Prophet Ezekiel (Chapter XXVIII).

R. Thanks be to God.

The word of the Lord came to me, saying: “Son of man, set your face against Sidon; prophesy concerning it, and say: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am against you, Sidon, and I shall be glorified in your midst; and they shall know that I am the Lord when I execute judgments in her and am sanctified in her.

“I will send pestilence and blood upon her streets, and the slain shall fall in her midst by the sword on every side; and they shall know that I am the Lord.

“And the house of Israel shall no longer have a stumbling block of bitterness or a thorn causing pain from all around among those who oppose them; and they shall know that I am the Lord God.

“When I gather the house of Israel from the peoples among whom they have been scattered, I shall be sanctified in them before the nations; and they shall dwell in their own land, which I gave to my servant Jacob.

“They shall dwell in it securely; they shall build houses and plant vineyards, and dwell confidently when I have executed judgments upon all those who oppose them on every side; and they shall know that I am the Lord their God.”

R. Amen.

Antiphon 1. Depart from me, evil ones. P. For the Lord has heard the voice of my weeping, and has received my prayer. V. I have labored in my groaning; every night I will wash my bed; I will water my couch with tears. P. For the Lord has heard.

## Prayer

“Let all the wicked depart from you, O Lord”—those whom the abyss of their unbelief has caused to depart from you; not so that they may withdraw from you and perish under punitive vengeance, but so that, when the insolence of their unbelief has departed, they may submit their necks, with utmost gentleness, to your light yoke.

**R.** Amen.

**Through mercy.**

## Antiphon 2

O Lord my God, in you I have hoped.

**P.** Save me; deliver me from all who persecute me.

**V.** Lest he seize my soul like a lion, [Col. 0464B] while there is no one to redeem or save.

**P.** Save me.

## Prayer

O Lord God, save your Church that hopes in you; since you suffered for her, deliver her from all who persecute her, and grant that she may rejoice forever with all who love you.

**R.** Amen.

**Through mercy.**

## Antiphon 3

My God, my deliverer from wrathful nations.

**P.** And deliver me, O Lord, from those who rise up against me.

**V.** I will love you, O Lord, my strength; the Lord is my firmament and my deliverer.

**P.** And from those who rise up against me.

**R.** I am humbled and bowed down exceedingly.

**P.** All day long I walked in mourning.

**V.** For my soul is filled with illusions, and there is no health [Col. 0464C] in my flesh.

**P.** All day long.

Your servants, O Lord, lie prostrate.

**P.** Mercy.

**V.** Grant pardon for sins, you who were mocked by the impious. [269]

**P.** Mercy.

**R.** Those whom you redeemed by the cross, do not allow to come into death.

**P.** Mercy.

**V.** May the outpouring of your blood avail for the deliverance of the redeemed.

**P.** Mercy.

## Hymn

“O Nazarene, light.” See fol. 144.

## Prayer

Our deliverer and Lord, grant us love with which to love you, so that, praising you, we may call upon you; and send your arrows, disperse our enemies, and rescue us from those who hate us. Thus may they be confounded as they are crushed, while we rejoice and are saved under your protection.

## The Lord’s Prayer

## At None

[Col. 0464D]

## Ecclesiastes (chapter 10)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

Son, the words of the mouth of the wise bring grace, but the lips of the fool swallow him up. The beginning of his words is folly, and the end of his mouth is the worst kind of error. The fool multiplies words. A person does not know what has been before or what will be afterward; who can tell him? The labor of fools will afflict them, those who do not know how to go into the city.

Woe to you, land whose king is a boy and whose princes eat in the morning. Blessed is the land whose king is noble and whose princes eat at the proper time, for refreshment and not for luxury. Through idleness the framework sags, and through the weakness of the hands the house leaks. [Col. 0465A] They make bread for laughter and wine so that the living may feast; and everything obeys money.

In your thoughts do not revile the king, and in the secret of your bedroom do not curse the rich, because the birds of heaven will carry your voice, and the winged creature will announce your judgment.

Cast your bread upon the passing waters, because after many days you will find it.

**R.** Amen.

## Reading from the Book of Samuel (First Book of Kings, chapter 9)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

In those days, there was a man from Benjamin named Kish, son of Abiel, son of Seor, son of Bechorath, son of Aphiah, son of a man of Jemini, a man mighty in strength. He had a son named Saul, chosen and good; there was no better man among the sons of Israel than he. From his shoulder upward he stood taller than all the people. [Col. 0465B]

Now the asses of Kish, Saul’s father, had wandered away. Kish said to Saul his son, “Take one of the servants with you, rise, go, and look for the asses.” When they had passed through Mount Ephraim and the land of Salisa without finding them, they also passed through the land of Salim, but they were not there; they went through the land of Jemini as well, but found nothing.

When they had come to the land of Suph and had not found them, Saul said to his servant who was with him, “Come, let us return, lest my father cease to care about the asses and become anxious about us.”

He replied, “Behold, there is a man of God in this city, a noble man; everything he says certainly comes to pass. Now, then, let us go; perhaps he will tell us about the matter for which we have come.”

Saul said to his servant, “Behold, we will go. What [Col. 0465C] shall we bring to the man? The bread in our bags is gone, and we have no gift to give the man of God, nor anything else.”

Again the servant answered Saul and said, “Behold, a quarter of a silver shekel has been found in my hand. Let us give it to the man of God, so that he may tell us our way.”

*(Formerly in Israel, when someone went to consult the Lord, he would speak in this way: “Come, let us go to the Seer.” For the one who is now called a Prophet was formerly called a Seer.)*

And Saul said to his servant, “Your word is excellent. Come, let us go.” And they went into the city where the man of God was.

As they were ascending the slope of the city, they found girls coming out to draw water, and they said to them, “Is the Seer here?” They answered them, “He is. Behold, he is before you; hurry now. [Col. 0465D] For he came into the city today, because there is a sacrifice for the people on the high place.”

As soon as you enter the city, you will find him before he goes up to the high place to eat. The people will not eat until he comes, because he will bless the sacrifice, and afterward those who have been invited will eat. Now, then, go up, for today you will find him.

And they went up into the city. As they were walking in the middle of the city, Samuel appeared, coming out to meet them as he was going up to the high place.

The Lord had revealed Samuel’s ear one day before Saul came, saying: “At this very hour tomorrow I will send to you a man from the land of Benjamin, and you shall anoint him as leader over my people. He will save my people from the hand [Col. 0466A] of the Philistines, because I have looked upon my people, and their cry has come before me.”

When Samuel had looked upon Saul, the Lord said to him, “Behold the man of whom I told you; he shall rule my people.”

Saul approached Samuel in the middle of the gate and said, “Tell me, please, where is the house of the Seer?”

Samuel answered, saying, “[270] I am the Seer. Go up before me to the high place, so that you may eat with me today; tomorrow morning I will let you go, and I will tell you everything that is in your heart. As for the asses that you lost three days ago, do not be concerned, because they have been found. And to whom will belong all the best things in Israel? Will they not belong to you and to all your father’s house?”

Saul answered and said, “Am I not a son of Jemini, from the smallest tribe of Israel, and is not my clan the least among all the clans of the [Col. 0466B] tribe of Benjamin? Why, then, have you spoken this word to me?”

Samuel took Saul and his servant and brought them into the dining room, giving them a place at the head among those who had been invited; there were about thirty men.

Samuel said to the cook, “Bring the portion that I gave you and ordered you to set aside with you.”

The cook lifted the shoulder and placed it before Saul. Samuel said to him, “Behold what remains; set it before you and eat, because it was deliberately kept for you when I invited the people.”

And Saul ate with Samuel that day. Then they came down from the high place into the town.

**R.** Amen.

## Antiphon 1

Let the impious be ashamed and be led down to hell; let the lying lips that speak [Col. 0466C] iniquity against the just be made mute.

**V.** In you, O Lord, I have hoped; I shall not be confounded forever. In your justice deliver me and rescue me.

**Psalm 30**

## Prayer

Let the impious be ashamed, O Lord, and be led down to hell—those who denied you, Christ, the Son of God—so that the mouths of those who speak of you, strengthened by the lofty summit of preaching, may prevail, when you have destroyed the lips of those speaking iniquity against the just.

**R.** Amen.

**Through mercy.**

Judge, O Lord, those who injure me, and fight against those who attack me. Take up weapons and shield, and rise to my help.

**V.** Bring out the sword and close ranks against those who persecute me; say to my soul: “I am your salvation.”

**Psalm 34**

[Col. 0466D]

## Prayer

Judge, O Lord, those who injure us, and yourself fight against those who attack us, so that you who were first attacked in our body may now make us unconquerable, as we remain in your body.

**R.** Amen.

## Antiphon 3

They gnashed their teeth against me. O Lord, when you look upon me, will you restore my soul?

**V.** Let those who unjustly oppose me not insult me—those who hate me without cause and nodded with their eyes.

**Psalm 34**

## Hymn

“O Nazarene, light.” See fol. 144.

## Prayer

Christ, Son of God, you who were not shaken by the teeth of snarling enemies, but in singular patience offer both a dart to their unbridled snarls and medicine to human weaknesses: restore our souls to yourself through true repentance, so that, looked upon by you, we may not be carried headlong [Col. 0467A] into anger and condemnation, but, following the example of your passion, may be made gentle in all things.

## The Lord’s Prayer

## At Vespers

## Praise

The Lord is my light and my salvation.

May the Lord be [with you].

**R.** And with [your spirit].

## Antiphon

Attend to my soul, O Lord, and deliver it.

**Psalm 68**

## Praise

With my whole heart I have sought you, O God.

**P.** Do not reject me from your commandments.

## Reading from the Book of Samuel (First Book of Kings, chapter 9)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

In those days, Samuel called Saul onto the roof of the house, saying, “Rise, and I will let you go.” Saul rose, and both of them went out, namely Saul and Samuel.

As they were descending at the edge of the city, Samuel said to Saul, “Tell the servant to go on ahead of us and pass by; but you remain here for a little while, so that I may tell you the word of the Lord.” [272]

## Chapter 10

Samuel took a small flask of oil, poured it on his [Col. 0469B] head, kissed him, and said: “Behold, the Lord has anointed you as leader over his inheritance. When you depart from me today, you will find two men near Rachel’s tomb, in the territory of Benjamin, at midday. They will say to you: ‘The asses that you went to seek have been found; and your father, having ceased to care about the asses, is anxious about you and says, “What shall I do about my son?”’

“When you depart from there and go farther, you will meet three men at the oak of Tabor, going up to God at Bethel. One will be carrying three young goats, another three loaves of bread, and another carrying a skin of wine. When they greet you, they will give you two loaves, and you shall receive them from their hands.

“After this you will come to the hill of the Lord, where there is a garrison of the Philistines. When you enter the city, you will meet a band [Col. 0469C] of prophets coming down from the high place, with a psaltery, a tambourine, a flute, and a lyre before them, and they themselves prophesying.

“The Spirit of the Lord will rush upon you, and you will prophesy with them and be changed into another man. When these signs come upon you, do whatever your hand finds, because the Lord is with you.

“You shall go down before me to Gilgal, and I will indeed come down to you, to offer peace offerings. You shall wait seven days until I come to you and show you what you are to do.”

And when he had turned his shoulder to depart from Samuel, God changed his heart into another heart, and all these signs came to pass on that day.

They came to the aforesaid hill, and behold, a band of prophets met him. The Spirit of the Lord rushed upon him, and he prophesied in their midst.

When those [Col. 0469D] who had known him yesterday and the day before saw that he was with the prophets and prophesying, they said to one another, “What has happened to the son of Kish? Is Saul also among the prophets?”

And one answered the other, saying, “And who is their father?” Therefore it became a proverb: “Is Saul also among the prophets?”

When he had ceased prophesying, he came to the high place.

Saul’s father said to him and to his servant, “Where did you go?”

They answered, “To seek the asses. When we did not find them, we came to Samuel.”

His father said to him, “Tell me what Samuel said to you.”

Saul said to his father, “He told us that the asses had been found.” But he did not tell him about the matter of the kingdom that Samuel had spoken to him.

Samuel summoned the people to the Lord at Mizpah and said to the children of Israel: “Thus says the Lord God of Israel: I brought Israel up from Egypt, and rescued you from the hand of the Egyptians and from the hand of all the kings, [Col. 0470A] who afflicted you. But today you rejected the Lord your God, who alone saved you from all your evils and tribulations, and you said, ‘No, but appoint a king over us.’ Now, therefore, stand before the Lord by your tribes and by your families.”

Samuel brought forward all the tribes of Israel, and the lot fell upon the tribe of Benjamin. He brought forward the tribe of Benjamin and its clans, and the lot fell upon a man’s clan; finally it reached Saul son of Kish.

So they sought him, but he was not found. After this they consulted the Lord whether he would come there. The Lord answered, “Behold, he is hidden [Col. 0470B] at home.”

They sent and brought him from there. He stood in the midst of the people, and he was taller than all the people by a shoulder and upward.

Samuel said to all the people, “Surely you see whom the Lord has chosen, for there is none like him among all the people.”

All the people shouted and said, “Long live the king!”

Samuel spoke the law of the kingdom to the people, wrote it in a book, and placed it before the Lord.

**R.** Amen.

Do not delay or tarry: attend now, turn now, look now, so that the sighs of our prayer [Col. 0470C]—which now, through compunction over its secrets, turns into our own bosom—may be directed before your sight from a cleansed heart.
