# At Terce

## Proverbs of Solomon (chapter 14)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

Son, whoever despises his neighbor sins, but whoever has mercy on the poor will be blessed. Those who do evil go astray; mercy and truth prepare good things. There will be abundance in every work, but where there are very many words, there is often poverty. The crown of the wise is their wealth; the folly of fools is impiety. A faithful witness delivers souls, but a deceitful person brings forth lies.

In the fear of the Lord there is confidence of strength, and for his children there will be hope. The fear of the Lord is a fountain of life, so that one may turn away from the ruin of death. In the multitude of the people lies the dignity of the king; in the smallness of the people, the disgrace of the ruler.

Whoever is patient is governed by great prudence, but whoever is impatient exalts his own folly. The life of the flesh is the health of the heart; the rotting of the bones is envy. Whoever slanders the needy reproaches his Maker, but whoever has mercy on the poor honors [Col. 0471A] him.

**R.** Amen.

## Reading from the Book of Samuel (First Book of Kings, chapter 11)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

In those days, Saul went to his house in Gibeah, and with him went a part of the army whose hearts God had touched.

But the sons of Belial said, “Can this man save us?” They despised him and brought him no gifts, but he pretended not to hear.

Then Nahash the Ammonite went up and began to fight against Jabesh-gilead. All the men of Jabesh said to Nahash, “Make a covenant with us, and we will serve you.”

Nahash the Ammonite answered them, “On this condition I will make a covenant with you: that I may gouge out the right eyes of all of you and make you a reproach [Col. 0471B] throughout all Israel.”

The elders of Jabesh said to him, “Grant us seven days, so that we may send messengers throughout all the territories of Israel; and if there is no one to defend us, we will come out to you.”

The messengers came to Gibeah to Saul and spoke these words in the hearing of the people. All the people raised their voice and wept.

And behold, Saul was coming behind the oxen from the field, and he heard that the people were weeping. They told him the words of the men of Jabesh.

The Spirit of the Lord rushed upon Saul when he heard these words, and his anger burned exceedingly.

He took both oxen, cut them into pieces, and sent them throughout all the territories of Israel by the hand of messengers, saying: “Whoever does not go out and follow Saul and Samuel—so shall it be done to his oxen.”

The fear of the Lord therefore fell upon the people, and they went out [Col. 0471C] as one man to Bezek. The sons of Israel numbered three hundred thousand, and the men of Judah thirty thousand.

They said to the messengers who had come, “Thus shall you say to the men who are in Jabesh-gilead: ‘Tomorrow there will be salvation for us, when the sun grows hot.’”

The messengers came and announced this to the men of Jabesh, who rejoiced and said, “Tomorrow we shall go out to you, and you may do to us whatever seems good to you.”

The next day Saul divided the people into three companies. He entered the middle of the camp at the morning watch and struck the Ammonites until the day grew light. The survivors were scattered, so that no two of them remained together.

The people said to Samuel, “Who is the man who said, ‘Shall Saul reign [Col. 0471D] over us?’ Bring the men, and we will kill them.”

Saul said, “No one shall be killed on this day, because today the Lord has brought salvation to Israel.”

Samuel said to the people, “Come, let us go to Gilgal and renew the kingdom there.”

All the people went to Gilgal, and there they made Saul king before the Lord at Gilgal, and offered peace offerings there before the Lord. Saul and all the men of Israel rejoiced there.

**R.** Amen.

## Reading from the Book of the Prophet Ezekiel (chapter 29)

The word of the Lord came to me, saying: “Son of man, set your face against Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and prophesy against him and against all Egypt. Speak, and say: Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I am against you, Pharaoh, king of Egypt, great dragon, who lie in the midst of your rivers and have said, ‘The river is mine, and I made myself.’

“I will put a bridle in your jaws and fasten the fish of your rivers to you. I will cast you into the desert, and all the fish of your rivers with you. Upon [Col. 0473A] the face of the earth you shall fall; you shall not be gathered up or collected. I have given you to the beasts of the earth and the birds of heaven to be devoured.

“All the inhabitants of Egypt shall know that I am the Lord, because you were a staff of reed to the house of Israel. When they grasped you with the hand, you broke, and you tore their whole shoulder; and when they leaned upon you, you were shattered and dissolved all their loins.

“Therefore thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will bring a sword upon you and kill man and beast among you. The land of Egypt shall become a desert and a wilderness, and they shall know that I am the Lord.”

Therefore gladden our hearts by obedience to your fear, strengthen the uncertainty of our mind with the sweetness of consolation, and, because you are gracious and gentle, let us draw sweetness from your indulgence and experience you as gracious and gentle in your recompense.

[276] ## Prayer

You, O Lord, deigned to be turned into a lyre and song amid the enemies, while you endured the tongues of those who disparaged you. Indeed, the unbelievers [Col. 0475C] slandered you in a story; they departed from you and abhorred you, and did not spare you even their spitting in the face. Therefore, you are our salvation and Savior: enter into us to save us, so that you who were tormented by the sufferings of your persecutors may be pleased by the confessions and deeds of those who believe in you.

## At Lauds

## Antiphon

**Psalm 50**
## Prayer

To you alone we have sinned, Lord; and we have done evil before you: yet our hidden things are not concealed from you, things held within the chambers of the heart; and still we are ashamed to reveal what we do not fear to perpetrate. But you, Lord, who do not despise the penitent, receive the prayers of the humble and grant forgiveness of sins. Through the power of the Trinity, may the Holy Spirit teach us the uprightness by which we may walk, [Col. 0475D] and may the upright Spirit draw us toward the glory of holiness, while the chief Spirit leads us toward justification: so that the immense power of the one divine virtue may govern those whom the Father created, guard those whom the Son redeemed, and fill those whom the Holy Spirit created. R. Amen.

## At the Canticle

**Antiphon.** Lord, may those who persecute me fall and become weak.

**Canticle of Jeremiah (Chapter XX).**

You seduced me, Lord, and I was seduced;  
you were stronger than I, and you prevailed.

I have become a laughingstock all day long;  
everyone mocks me.

For a long time now I speak, crying out, “Injustice!”;  
I cry, “Devastation!”

[Col. 0476A] And the word of the Lord has become for me a reproach  
and a mockery all day long.

And I said: “I will not remember him,  
nor will I speak any longer in his name.”

And it became in my heart like a raging fire,  
shut up in my bones;  
and I grew weak, unable to endure it.

For I heard the insults of many  
and terrors all around:

“Pursue him, and let us pursue him,”  
from all the men who had been at peace with me  
and who guarded my side,

to see whether he might somehow be deceived,  
so that we might prevail against him  
and take vengeance upon him.

But the Lord is with me like a mighty warrior;  
[Col. 0476B] therefore those who persecute me will fall  
and become weak.

They will be utterly confounded,  
because they have not understood an everlasting reproach  
that will never be erased.

And you, Lord of hosts, examiner of the just,  
who test hearts and kidneys,

let me, I beg you, see vengeance upon them;  
for to you I have revealed my cause.

## Prayer

O God, whose soul the ravenousness of lions was unable to devour, because the justice found in him seemed to ward off their fury, send your Angel to close the mouth of that lion which runs roaring through the world, seeking whom he may devour; and rescue our souls from his persuasion and domination. R. Amen.

[Col. 0476C]

## Reading from the Book of Samuel  
*(First Book of Kings, chapters XIV–XV)*

**R.** Thanks be to God.

In those days, Saul fought against Moab, the Ammonites, Edom, the kings of Zobah, and the Philistines; and wherever he turned, he was victorious. After gathering an army, he struck Amalek and rescued Israel from the hand of its devastators.

The sons of Saul were Jonathan, Jessui, and Melchishua. The names of his two daughters were Merob, the name of the firstborn, and [Col. 0476D] Michol, the name of the younger. The name of Saul’s wife was Achinoam, daughter of Achimaas; and the name of the commander of his army was Abner, son of Ner, Saul’s cousin. Kish was Saul’s father, and Ner, Abner’s father, was the son of Abiel.

There was a powerful war against the Philistines throughout 277 all the days of Saul. For whenever Saul saw any strong man fit for battle, he joined him to himself.

And Samuel said to Saul: “The Lord sent me to anoint you king over his people Israel. Now therefore listen to the voice of the Lord. Thus says the Lord of hosts: I have considered all that Amalek did to Israel, how he opposed him on the way when they came up from Egypt. Now therefore go, strike Amalek, and destroy all that belongs to him. Do not spare him, but kill man and woman, child and infant, ox and [Col. 0477A] sheep, camel and donkey.” 

So Saul commanded the people and counted them like lambs: two hundred thousand foot soldiers and ten thousand men of Judah. When Saul came as far as the city of Amalek, he laid an ambush in the valley. 

And Saul said to the Kenite: “Go away, withdraw, and depart from Amalek, lest I involve you with him. For you showed kindness to all the children of Israel when they came up from Egypt.” And the Kenite withdrew from the midst of Amalek.

Saul struck Amalek from Havilah until he came to Shur, which is in the region of Egypt. He captured Agag, king of Amalek, alive; but he killed all the common people with the edge of the sword.

Saul and all the people spared Agag, as well as the best sheep and herds, the garments, the rams, and everything that was beautiful; they did not wish to destroy these. But whatever was worthless and rejected, that they destroyed. [Col. 0477B]

The word of the Lord came to Samuel, saying: “I regret that I made Saul king, because he has abandoned me and has not fulfilled my words in deed.” Samuel was grieved and cried out to the Lord throughout that entire night.

When Samuel rose during the night to go to Saul in the morning, it was reported to Samuel that Saul had come to Carmel, had erected a triumphal arch for himself, and, after passing through, had gone down to Gilgal.

Samuel therefore came to Saul, and Samuel said: “What is this sound of flocks that reaches my ears, and of herds that I hear?”

Saul replied: “They brought them from Amalek. The people spared the best sheep and herds in order to sacrifice them to the Lord your God; the rest we killed.” [Col. 0477C]

Samuel said to Saul: “Let me tell you what the Lord spoke to me during the night.”

He said to him: “Speak.”

And Samuel said: “Were you not small in your own eyes when you became head of the tribes of Israel? The Lord anointed you king over Israel, and the Lord sent you on your way and said: ‘Go and kill the sinners, the Amalekites, and fight against them until they are utterly destroyed.’ Why, then, did you not listen to the voice of the Lord? Instead, you turned to the spoil and did what was evil in the eyes of the Lord.”

Saul said to Samuel: “On the contrary, I listened to the voice of the Lord and walked in the way on which the Lord sent me. I brought back Agag, king of Amalek, and I killed Amalek. But the people took sheep and oxen from the spoil, the firstfruits of what had been slaughtered, to sacrifice to the Lord their God at Gilgal.” [Col. 0477D] R. Amen.

**The Time of Night.** fol. 257.

## Capitulum

Deliver our soul, Lord, from tribulation—you who endured spitting and scourging for us—so that, once delivered from the prison of this world, after our death we may proclaim the triumphs of your Cross with due praise.

Our Father.

## Lauda

I have clung to your testimonies.  
**P.** Lord, do not put me to shame.  
**V.** My soul has clung to the pavement; revive me according to your word.  
**P.** I have clung.

## Prayer

Remove our steps, Lord, from the way of iniquity, and establish our course on the path of your commandments. Raise up, then, with saving remedy, the soul clinging to the pavement; and, instructed in your justifications, revive it by the power of your word. [Col. 0478A] R. Amen.

Through mercy.

## At Terce

**From the Proverbs of Solomon (Chapter XIII).**

**R.** Thanks be to God.

My son, the good man will be filled from the fruit of his mouth, but the soul of the transgressors is wicked. Whoever guards his mouth guards his soul; but whoever is careless in speaking will experience evils. The lazy man both desires and does not desire; but the soul of those who work will be enriched. The just man detests lying speech; the impious man is confounded. Justice guards innocence, but wickedness undermines the sinner.

There is one who is like a rich man though he possesses nothing, and one who is like a poor man though he has many riches. [Col. 0478B] A man’s wealth is the redemption of his soul; but the poor man does not endure reproach. The light of the just brings joy, but the lamp of the wicked is extinguished. 

Among the proud there are always quarrels; but those who do everything 278 with counsel are governed by wisdom. Whoever betrays a matter binds himself for the future; but whoever fears the commandment will live in peace. R. Amen.

## Reading from the Book of Samuel  
*(First Book of Kings, chapter XVII)*

**R.** Thanks be to God.

In those days, the Philistines gathered their forces for battle and assembled at Socoh of Judah. They encamped between Socoh and Azekah, on the borders of Domim.

Saul and the men of Israel gathered and came to the Valley of the Terebinth, and they drew up their lines for battle against the Philistines. The Philistines stood on [Col. 0478C] the mountain on one side, and Israel stood on the mountain on the other; and the valley lay between them. 

A bastard came out from the camp of the Philistines, named Goliath, from Gath, whose height was six cubits and a span. He had a bronze helmet on his head and wore an armored breastplate. The weight of his breastplate was five thousand bronze shekels. He had bronze greaves on his legs, and a bronze shield covered his shoulders. The shaft of his spear was like a weaver’s beam, and the iron of his spear weighed six hundred iron shekels. His armor-bearer went before him.

Standing, he shouted against the battle lines of Israel and said to them: “Why have you come prepared for battle? Am I not a Philistine, and are you not servants of Saul? [Col. 0478D] Choose one of your men and let him come down to single combat. If he can fight with me and strike me, we will be your servants; but if I prevail and strike him, you will be our servants and serve us.” 

And the Philistine said: “Today I defy the ranks of Israel. Give me a man, and let him engage me in single combat.”

When Saul and all the Israelite men heard these words of the Philistine, they were terrified and greatly afraid.

David was the son of an Ephrathite man, as stated above, from Bethlehem of Judah, whose name was Jesse. He had eight sons, and in the days of Saul he was an old and advanced man among men.

Three of his older sons had followed Saul into battle. The names of his three sons who went to war were Eliab the firstborn, [Col. 0479A] Abinadab the second, and Shammah the third. David was the youngest. 

After the three older sons had followed Saul, David departed from Saul and returned to Bethlehem to pasture his father’s flock. Jesse said to his son David: “Take an ephah of meal for your brothers, these ten loaves, and run to the camp to your brothers. You shall also carry these ten portions of cheese to the tribune. Visit your brothers to see whether they are doing well, and learn with whom they have been stationed.”

Saul and all the sons of Israel were fighting against the Philistines in the Valley of the Terebinth. David rose early, entrusted the flock to a keeper, and departed laden, as Jesse had commanded him.

He came to the place of Magala and to the army, which had gone out shouting for battle. Israel had drawn up its line, and [Col. 0479B] the Philistines likewise stood ready opposite. 

David therefore left the supplies he had brought under the hand of the keeper of the baggage, ran to the place of battle, and asked whether everything was going well for his brothers.

While he was still speaking with them, that bastard, the Philistine named Goliath, from Gath, came up from the camp of the Philistines. As he spoke the same words, David heard him.

When all the Israelites saw the man, they fled from his presence, greatly fearing him. Someone from Israel said: “Have you seen this man who has come up? The man who strikes him will be enriched by the king with great wealth; he will also give him his daughter and make his father’s house tax-exempt in Israel.”

David said to the men who stood with him: “What will be given to the man who strikes this Philistine and removes [Col. 0479C] the reproach? For who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the ranks of the living God?” 

The people repeated the same statement to him: “This will be given to the man who strikes him.”

When Eliab, his older brother, heard him speaking with the others, he became angry with David and said: “Why have you come, and why have you abandoned those few sheep in the wilderness? I know your arrogance and the wickedness of your heart, because you came down to see the battle.”

David said: “What have I done? Is it not merely a word?” And he turned slightly away from him toward another and repeated the same statement. The people answered him as before.

The words spoken by David were heard, and they were reported in Saul’s presence. When David had been brought to him, [Col. 0479D] he said to Saul: “Let no one’s heart fail because of him. I, your servant, will go and fight against this Philistine.” 

Saul said to David: “You cannot resist this Philistine or fight against him, because you are a boy, while he has been a warrior from his youth.” 279

David said to Saul: “Your servant was keeping his father’s flock, and a lion or a bear would come and carry away a ram from the midst of the flock. I would pursue them, strike them, and rescue it from their mouth. When they rose against me, I would seize them by the jaw, strangle them, and kill them.

“For I, your servant, have killed both a lion and a bear. This uncircumcised Philistine, then, will be like one of them, because he dared to curse the army of the living God.”

[Col. 0480A] And he said: “The Lord, who rescued me from the hand of the lion and from the hand of the bear, will rescue me from the hand of this Philistine.”  R. Amen.

## Antiphon 1

My soul is filled with mockeries.  
**P.** And there is no health in my flesh. Do not abandon me, Lord.  
**V.** I am bent down and humbled; I roared continually because of the groaning of my heart.  
**P.** And there is no health in my flesh.

## Prayer

Christ our God, who allowed yourself to be mocked and scourged in your body, cleanse our soul, filled with mockeries, from every stain of pollution, so that, with true health dwelling in our flesh, we may be found worthy to reach the crown appointed for us. R. Amen.

## Antiphon 2

My enemies have multiplied beyond the hairs of my head. It pleased the Lord to rescue me.  
[Col. 0480B] **P.** Lord, look upon me to help me.  
**V.** But you, Lord, do not keep your help far from me; look toward my defense.  
**P.** Lord, look upon me to help me.

## Prayer

Christ, Son of God, who at the time of your Passion, while those who hated you without cause multiplied beyond the hairs of your head, paid what you were proved not to have stolen, free us from the multitude of our sins. May an abundance of virtues grow beyond the number of the hairs of our heads, and may the punishment we deserve escape through the outpouring of your mercy. R. Amen.

## Antiphon 3

Judah, why do you glory in wickedness, you who are powerful in iniquity?  
**P.** All day long your tongue devised injustice; you made deceit like a sharp razor.  
**V.** [Col. 0480C] You loved wickedness more than kindness, and iniquity more than speaking righteousness.  
**P.** All day long your tongue devised injustice.  
The Gloria is not said.

## Response

Alas for me, because my exile has been prolonged; I have lived with the inhabitants of Kedar. My soul has been a long-time exile. With those who hated peace I was peaceful; when I spoke to them, they waged war against me.  
**P.** Without cause.

**V.** Unjust witnesses rose up and questioned me about things I did not know; they repaid me evil for good.  
**P.** Without cause.  
The Gloria is not said.

## Prayers

We ask for pardon, Christ; hear us.  
**P.** Be appeased and have mercy.

**V.** Redeemer, price of the redeemed, sanctify us; on your Cross erase our crimes.  
**P.** Be appeased and have mercy.

**V.** You who endure human judgments, though innocent, raise us up in the glory of your judgment.  
**P.** Be appeased.

**V.** You who look from the Cross upon [Col. 0480D] your Mother and your Disciple, now look graciously upon us from heaven.  
**P.** Be appeased.

## Hymn

**O Nazarene, light.** See folio 144.

## Prayer

Only-begotten Word of the unbegotten Father, you endure the proud people who glory against you in wickedness; save the flock of the faithful who confess you. While the whole crowd of evil people devises injustices all day long with its tongue, may the people trusting in your name bring you songs, pleasing to you without end.

Our Father.

## At Sext

## Reading from the Book of the Prophet Jeremiah  
*(Chapter II)*

**R.** Thanks be to God.

Thus says the Lord: “The children of [Col. 0481A] Israel have turned their backs to me and not their faces; and in the time of their affliction they will say: ‘Arise and save us.’ 

“Where are your gods, which you made for yourself? Let them arise and save you in the time of your affliction. For, Judah, your gods were as numerous as your cities.

“Why do you wish to contend with me in judgment? You have all abandoned me, says the Lord. In vain I struck your children; they did not accept discipline. Your sword devoured your prophets, like a destroying lion your generation.

“See the word of the Lord: Have I become a wilderness to Israel, or a late-producing land? Why then did my people say: ‘We have withdrawn; we will no longer come to you’?

“Does a woman forget her ornament, or a bride the band around her breast? Yet my people have forgotten me for countless days.

“Why do you strive to display [Col. 0481B] your good way in seeking love, when you have even taught your ways your wickedness, and the blood of the souls of the poor and innocent has been found on your wings? I did not find them in pits, but in all the places I have mentioned above. 

“And you said: ‘I am without sin and innocent; therefore let your anger turn away from me.’ But I will contend with you in judgment because you said: ‘I have not sinned.’

“How utterly vile you have become, repeating your ways! You will be put to shame by Egypt, just as you were put to shame by Assyria. For you will also depart from that place, and your hands will be upon your head, because the Lord has shattered your confidence, and you will have no prosperity. 280

“It is commonly said: ‘If a man divorces his wife, and she leaves him and marries another man, will he return to her again? [Col. 0481C] Will that woman not be polluted and defiled?’ But you have prostituted yourself with many lovers; nevertheless, return to me, says the Lord.”  R. Amen.

## Antiphon 1

The sinner watches the just man and seeks to destroy him.  
**P.** But the Lord did not abandon him.

**P.** But the Lord did not abandon him.

## Prayer

The sinner watches, Lord, the just man, lying in wait to destroy your most faithful flock, which lives by faith and trusts in your mercy. Do not therefore abandon us to perish in his hands—you who for our sake were fastened to the wood of the Cross. R. Amen.

[Col. 0481D]

**P.** All day long your tongue devised injustice.

O God, who endure a disciple glorying against you in wickedness, grant that we may glory greatly in your sufferings. As the wickedness of the outstretched bow released an arrow of pain, so may faith fix the dart of the wound in him through his willing confession. R. Amen.

**V.** You who are led like a sheep and crucified.  
**P.** Lord.

Restrain the mighty who rush upon me, Christ the Lord, by the power of your strength. [Col. 0482B]

## At None

## From the Proverbs of Solomon  
*(Chapter XII)*

**R.** Thanks be to God.

My son, the fruit of the just is a tree of life, and whoever wins souls is wise. If the just man is repaid on earth, how much more the sinner and the impious? Whoever loves discipline loves knowledge, but whoever hates correction is foolish.

Whoever is good receives grace from the Lord, but whoever trusts in his own thoughts acts impiously. A man will not be strengthened by wickedness, and the root of the just will not be moved.

A diligent woman is a crown for her husband, [Col. 0482C] but she who acts shamefully is rottenness in his bones. The thoughts of the just are judgments, but the counsels of the wicked are deceitful. The words of the wicked lie in wait for blood, but the mouth of the just will deliver them. 

Overturn the wicked, and they will be no more; but the house of the just will remain. R. Amen.

## Reading from the Book of Samuel  
*(First Book of Kings, chapter XVII)*

**R.** Thanks be to God.

In those days, David said: “The Lord, who rescued me from the hand of the lion and from the hand of the bear, will himself rescue me from the hand of this Philistine.”

Saul said to David: “Go, and may the Lord be with you.”

Saul clothed David in his garments, placed a bronze helmet on his head, and dressed him in a breastplate. David, girded with Saul’s sword over his garment, began to test whether he could walk while armed; for he was not accustomed to it. [Col. 0482D]

David said to Saul: “I cannot walk in this way, because I am not accustomed to it.” And he removed them. He took the staff he always carried in his hands, chose for himself five very smooth stones from the stream, put them into the shepherd’s bag he carried with him, and took a sling in his hand. Then he went out against the Philistine.

The Philistine proceeded, walking and drawing near against David, with his armor-bearer before him. 281 When the Philistine looked and saw David, he despised him, for he was a young man, ruddy and handsome in appearance.

The Philistine said to David: “Am I a dog, that you come against me with a staff?” And the Philistine cursed David by his gods. He said to David: “Come to me, and I will give your flesh to the birds of the air and the beasts of the earth.” [Col. 0483A]

David said to the Philistine: “You come against me with sword, spear, and shield; but I come against you in the name of the Lord of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, which you have defied today. The Lord will deliver you into my hand, and I will strike you and take your head from you. Today I will give the corpses of the camp of the Philistines to the birds of the air and the beasts of the earth, so that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel.

“And this whole assembly shall know that the Lord does not save by sword or spear, for the battle is the Lord’s, and he will deliver you into our hands.”

When the Philistine rose, came, and drew near against David, David hurried and ran toward the battle to meet the Philistine. He put his hand into the bag, took out one stone, [Col. 0483B] hurled it with the sling, and struck the Philistine on the forehead. The stone sank into his forehead, and he fell on his face to the ground. 

David prevailed over the Philistine and killed him. Since David had no sword in his hand, he ran, stood over the Philistine, took his sword, drew it from its sheath, killed him, and cut off his head.

When the Philistines saw that their strongest man was dead, they fled. The men of Israel and Judah rose up, shouted, and pursued the Philistines until they came to the valley and the gates of Ekron. The wounded Philistines fell along the road to Shaaraim, as far as Gath and Ekron.

The children of Israel returned after pursuing the Philistines and plundered their camp. [Col. 0483C] David took the head of the Philistine and brought it to Jerusalem; but he placed his weapons in his own tent.  R. Amen.

## Antiphon 1

I humbled my soul with fasting, and it became a reproach to me.  
**P.** Those who sat at the gate were hostile to me.  
**V.** But I offer my prayer to you, Lord, at the favorable time of God.  
**P.** Those who sat at the gate were hostile to me.

## Prayer

Christ, Son of God, look upon our humility in fasting. You who, though innocent, were handed over to the punishment of the Cross through the deceit of the treacherous disciple, and for whose capture the rewards were received, grant that we may neither deceive our neighbors by swearing nor strive to destroy ourselves through harmful behavior. Rather, following the teaching of your patience, may we prevail over our inward and [Col. 0483D] outward enemies. R. Amen.

## Antiphon 2

My God, rescue me from the hand of the sinner, from the hand of the lawless and wicked man.  
**P.** For you are my patience.  
**V.** I have hoped in you, O God; Lord, let me never be put to shame.  
**P.** For you are my patience.

## Prayer

Our God, rescue us from the hand of the sinner—you who for us deigned to endure the punishment of the Cross—so that you alone may be our patience, you who for us endured burial. R. Amen.

## Antiphon 3

Sinners built upon my back; they prolonged their iniquity.  
**P.** The just Lord will cut down the necks of sinners.  
**V.** They often attacked me from my youth; let Israel now say:  
**P.** The just Lord will cut down the necks of sinners. 

[Col. 0484A]

## Hymn

**O Nazarene.** fol. 144.

## Prayer

Behold, Lord, upon the back of your Church the burdensome iniquity of proud sinners has been built, when those who are incorrigible in their conduct cruelly oppress your members.

Grant, therefore, we ask, that we may be so supported by the virtue of endurance that those whom we carry upon the back of our soul to be healed may be brought safely with us to the heavenly stable. Thus, having received with them the one and singular denarius, may we be found worthy to receive profit from our preaching, while they receive with us an everlasting reward for their obedience. 

Our Father.

# Friday

## At Matins

[Col. 0484C] **Antiphon.** Lord, why have those who afflict me multiplied? Many rise up against me. Psalm III. 

## Prayer

Those who afflict us have multiplied, Lord; but you are abundant in mercy, by which you rescue us. We will fear no imminent oppression at all, provided only that we are fortified by your grace, Almighty One. R. Amen.

## Antiphon 1

You are my refuge from the oppression that surrounds me, Lord.  
**P.** My joy, redeem me from those who surround me.  
**V.** I will give you understanding and instruct you in the way you shall go; I will fix my eyes upon you, Lord.  
**P.** My joy, redeem me.

## Prayer

You are our refuge, Lord, from the oppression that surrounds us. Therefore, since by suffering [Col. 0484D] for us you became our exaltation, redeem us from the snare of the enemies who surround us. R. Amen. 

## Antiphon 2

When they troubled me,  
**P.** I put on sackcloth and humbled my soul with fasting.  
**V.** Judge, Lord, those who harm me, and fight against those who fight me.  
**P.** I put on sackcloth.

## Prayer

Grant us, Lord, to carry your mortification in our body—you who gave us life in your body—so that, when enemies trouble us, we may not go against them to return vengeance. Rather, clothed in sackcloth and humbling our soul with fasting, may we offer you, the Lord, an acceptable prayer poured out within our breast. R. Amen.

## Antiphon 3

Arise, Lord, and attend to [Col. 0485A] my judgment; my God and my Lord, attend to my cause.  
**P.** Let not my enemies rejoice over me, nor say in their heart: “We will devour him.”  
**V.** Let all who seek my soul be confounded and put to shame together.  
**P.** Let not my enemies rejoice over me.

## Prayer

Our God and Lord Jesus Christ, be ever present in the cause of your Church, by which you patiently distinguish her from the others; you alone endured the wounds of the Passion for her. R. Amen.

## Response

I have suffered insults and reproach from them; and my neighbors, who guarded my side, said: “Let us deceive him and prevail against him.” But you, Lord, are with me like a mighty warrior; let them fall into everlasting disgrace.  
**P.** And let me see vengeance upon them, because I have revealed my cause to you.

[Col. 0485B] **V.** Give their children over to famine, and deliver them into the hand of the sword. Let their wives be childless and widowed, and let their husbands be killed by death.  
**P.** And let me see vengeance upon them.  
The Gloria is not said.

## Prayer

What can a creature formed by you restore to you, Lord, for whom, enduring the reproaches of those who reviled you, you alone sat overwhelmed with threats? For those on whose behalf you bore so many wounds of suffering, we ask that you not permit them to be cast down by the sufferings of the flesh or submerged in the abyss of Hell. R. Amen.

## At Lauds

**Antiphon.** In iniquities I was conceived, and in sins my mother bore me. To you alone I have sinned, Lord, and done evil before you; have mercy on me. [Col. 0485C] Psalm L.

## Prayer

Acknowledging our iniquities and laying bare before you, Lord, our personal offenses, we pray as suppliants, wailing with tears and beating our breast: turn your face away from our crimes and erase all the sins we have committed.

Create, therefore, O God, in our heart what you love; and in your accustomed favor forgive what you hate. And if our wicked vices repeatedly provoke you to anger, may your abundant indulgence render you favorable to us. R. Amen.

**Antiphon.** Behold, my judge is in heaven, and the one who knows me is on high.

## Canticle of Job  
*(Chapter XVI)*

Now behold, my pain has oppressed me,  
and all my limbs have been [Col. 0485D] reduced to nothing. 

Those who roar bear witness against me,  
and a liar is raised up against my face, contradicting me.

He gathered his fury against me,  
and, threatening me, roared against me with his teeth.  
The enemy looked upon me with exceedingly terrifying eyes.

They opened their mouths against me;  
reproaching me, they struck my cheek.  
They were satisfied with my sufferings.

God has shut me up with the wicked  
and delivered me into the hands of the impious.

I, who was once wealthy,  
have been crushed. 283

He seized my neck and broke me,  
and set me as a yoke for himself.

He surrounded me with spears and pierced me through;  
he did not spare [Col. 0486A] my loins  
and poured out my entrails upon the ground. 

He made wounds in me  
and rushed upon wound like a giant.  
I sewed my sackcloth over my skin  
and covered my flesh with ashes.

My face swelled from weeping,  
and my eyelids grew dim.

I have suffered these things without iniquity in my hands,  
when I offered pure prayers to God.

May the earth not cover my blood,  
nor may my cry find a place to hide in you.

For behold, my witness is in heaven,  
and the one who knows me is on high.

## Prayer

[Col. 0486B] Lord Jesus, you understand with compassionate governance the pain of your Church, whose bones have been reduced to nothing, while the filth of temptations destroys others outside her. Grant us that, since you alone were tempted and suffered for us, you alone may rescue us from our temptations and sufferings, so that our testimony within your Church may be so beneficial that we may be found worthy to please you without end.  R. Amen.

## At Matins

**Antiphon.** God, my God, to you I keep vigil from the light of dawn. My soul thirsted for you; how greatly my flesh also thirsted for you!  
**V.** Thus I appeared to you in the holy place, O God, that I might see your power and your glory.

**Lauda.** Let the young together with the elders praise the name of the Lord. Psalm CXLVIII.

## Reading from the Book of Samuel  
*(First Book of Kings, chapter XVII)*

**R.** Thanks be to God.

At that time, when Saul saw David going out [Col. 0486C] against the Philistine, he said to Abner, commander of the army: “From what family does this young man descend?” And Abner said: “As your life lives, O king, I do not know.” And the king said: “Ask whose son this boy is.” When David returned, having struck down the Philistine, Abner took him and brought him before King Saul, carrying the Philistine’s head in his hand. And Saul said to David: “From what lineage are you, young man?” And David said: “I am the son of your servant Jesse the Bethlehemite.”

(Cap. XVIII.) And when he had finished speaking to Saul, Jonathan’s soul was bound to David’s soul, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul. For Jonathan stripped off the tunic with which he was clothed and gave it to David, together with [Col. 0486D] his other garments, even his sword, bow, and belt. David went out to everything Saul sent him to do and acted wisely. Saul appointed him over the men of war, and he was well received in the eyes of all the people, and especially in the sight of Saul’s servants.

When David returned after striking down the Philistine, women came out from all the cities, singing and leading dances to meet King Saul, with tambourines of joy and sistra. The women sang responsively, praising and saying:

“Saul has struck down his thousands,  
and David his ten thousands.”

Saul was exceedingly angry, and this saying displeased him. He said: “They have given David ten thousand, and to me they have given one thousand. What more can he have except the kingdom?” From that day onward [Col. 0487A] Saul looked upon David with hostile eyes.

The next day an evil spirit from the Lord rushed upon Saul, and he was prophesying in the midst of his house. David, meanwhile, was playing the lyre with his hand, as he did day after day. Saul was holding a spear and hurled it, thinking that he could pin David to the wall; but David moved aside from his presence twice. Saul was afraid of David, because the Lord was with him and had departed from Saul. Therefore Saul removed him from his presence and made him commander over a thousand men. He went out and came in before the people. In all his ways David acted wisely, and the Lord was with him.

When Saul saw that David was very wise, he began to beware of him. All Israel and Judah loved David, for he went out and came in before them.

[Col. 0487B] Saul said to David: “Here is my elder daughter Merab; I will give her to you as a wife. Only be a brave man and fight the Lord’s battles.” Saul was thinking: “Let my hand not be upon him, but let the hand of the Philistines be upon him.”

David said to Saul: “Who am I, or what is my life, or what is my father’s kinship in Israel, that I should become the king’s son-in-law?”

But when the time came for Saul’s daughter Merab to be given to David, she was given as wife to Adriel the Molathite. Now Saul’s other daughter Michal loved David, and this was reported to Saul, and it pleased him. Saul said: “I will give her to him, so that she may become a snare for him and the hand of the Philistines may be against him.”

284 Then Saul said to David: “Today you shall be my son-in-law in two ways.” [Col. 0487C] And Saul commanded his servants: “Speak secretly to David, saying: ‘Behold, you please the king, and all his servants love you. Now therefore become the king’s son-in-law.’”

Saul’s servants spoke all these words in David’s hearing. And David said: “Does it seem a small thing to you to become the king’s son-in-law? I am a poor and insignificant man.” The servants reported to Saul, saying: “David has spoken words of this kind.”

Saul said: “Speak to David in this way: ‘The king has no need of a bride-price, except for one hundred foreskins of Philistines, so that vengeance may be taken on the king’s enemies.’” Saul was planning to deliver David into the hands of the Philistines.

When his servants reported to David the words Saul had spoken, the proposal pleased David, so that he might become the king’s son-in-law. After a few days David rose [Col. 0487D] and went with the men who were under him. He struck down two hundred Philistines, brought their foreskins, and counted them before the king, so that he might become the king’s son-in-law. Saul therefore gave him his daughter Michal as wife.

Saul saw and understood that the Lord was with David. Michal, Saul’s daughter, loved him. Saul began to fear David even more, and Saul became David’s enemy all his days. The princes of the Philistines went out, and from the beginning of their going out David acted more wisely than all Saul’s men. His name became exceedingly renowned.

R\. Amen.

### Hymn

“Nighttime.” See fol. 257.

### Capitulum

On the day of our tribulation, O Lord, receive the prayer that we pour out; and, with hands extended through the night, understand what we desire. Come [Col. 0488A] to our souls as the best Consoler, and show yourself our Redeemer through gracious favor. You who acquired us by voluntary suffering, rescue us from the snare of the hunter by unconquerable power.

Our Father.

### Praise

“Remember your word to your servant, in which you gave me hope. This has consoled me in my humiliation.”

V\. “The arrogant acted wickedly against me everywhere, but I did not turn aside from your law.”

### Prayer

May the hope that you gave us, O Lord, itself be our consolation in our humiliation; may it become for us the fullness of glory in exaltation.

R\. Amen.

## At Terce

### From the Proverbs of Solomon

(Cap. XXV.)

R\. Thanks be to God.

[Col. 0488B] Son, a cloud, mist, wind, and rain that do not follow: such is a glorious man who does not fulfill his promises.

Patience will soften a ruler, and a gentle tongue breaks hardness.

You have found honey; eat what is sufficient for you, lest, being filled, you vomit it up.

Withdraw your foot from your neighbor’s house, lest, when he has had enough of you, he hate you.

A dart, a sword, and a sharp arrow is a man who speaks false testimony against his neighbor.

A rotten tooth and a slipping foot is one who trusts in the faithless on the day of distress and loses his cloak on the day of cold.

Vinegar on soda, and one who sings songs to a most wicked heart.

As the moth harms a garment and the worm harms wood, so sorrow harms a man’s heart.

If your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him water to drink. For you will heap burning coals upon his head, [Col. 0488C] and the Lord will repay you.

The north wind scatters the rains, and a sad face the slandering tongue.

It is better to sit in the corner of a housetop than with a quarrelsome woman, even in a common house.

Cold water for a thirsty soul, and good news from a distant land.

A spring muddied by the foot and a corrupted stream is a righteous man falling before the wicked.

As it is not good for one who eats much honey, so one who examines majesty will be crushed by glory.

As an open city without a surrounding wall is a man who cannot restrain his spirit in speaking.

Eat honey, my son, because it is good, and the honeycomb is sweetest to your throat.

So also is the teaching of your soul: when you have found it, you will have hope in the end, and your hope will not perish.

[Col. 0488D] R\. Amen.

### Reading from the Book of Samuel

(First Book of Kings, chap. XIX.)

R\. Thanks be to God.

In those days Saul spoke to Jonathan his son and to all his servants, ordering them to kill David. But Jonathan, Saul’s son, loved David greatly, and Jonathan disclosed this to David, saying: “My father Saul is seeking to kill you. Therefore, please be on your guard in the morning; remain hidden and conceal yourself. I will go out and stand beside my father in the field, wherever he may be, and I will speak good things about you to my father. Whatever I see, I will report to you.”

Jonathan spoke good things about David to his father and said to him: “Let not the king sin against his servant David, for he has not sinned against you, [Col. 0489A] and his deeds are very good toward you. He placed his life in his hand, struck down the Philistine, and the Lord brought about a great salvation for all Israel. You saw it and rejoiced. Why then do you sin against innocent blood by killing David, who is without guilt?”

When Saul heard this, he was appeased by Jonathan’s voice and swore: “As the Lord lives, he shall not be killed.”

Jonathan therefore called David and reported all these words to him. Jonathan brought David to Saul, and he was before him as he had been yesterday and the day before.

War broke out again, and David went out and fought against the Philistines. He struck them with a great blow, and they fled before him. The evil spirit of the Lord came upon Saul. He was sitting in his house and holding a spear, while David was playing the lyre [Col. 0489B] with his hand. Saul tried to pin David to the wall with the spear, but David moved aside from Saul’s presence. The spear passed harmlessly into the wall, and David fled and was saved that night.

Saul sent his attendants by night to David’s house, to guard him so that he might be killed in the morning. When David’s wife Michal announced this to him, saying: “Unless you save yourself this night, tomorrow you will die,” she lowered him through the window. He went away, fled, and was saved.

Michal took a statue, placed it on the bed, put a hairy goatskin at its head, and covered it with clothing. Saul sent officers to seize David, and it was reported to them that he was ill. Saul sent messengers again to see David, saying: “Bring [Col. 0489C] him to me in the bed, so that he may be killed.”

When the messengers came, a statue was found on the bed, with a goatskin at its head. Saul said to Michal: “Why have you deceived me in this way and sent my enemy away so that he could escape?”

Michal answered Saul: “Because he himself said to me: ‘Let me go, or I will kill you.’”

David fled and was saved. He came to Samuel at Ramah and reported to him all that Saul had done to him. He and Samuel went away and remained at Naioth.

It was reported to Saul: “Behold, David is at Naioth in Ramah.” Saul therefore sent guards to seize David. When they saw the company of prophets prophesying, with Samuel standing over them, the Spirit [Col. 0489D] of God came upon them also, and they too began to prophesy.

When this was reported to Saul, he sent other messengers, and they also prophesied. Saul sent messengers a third time, and they too prophesied.

Saul became furious and went himself to Ramah. He came as far as the great cistern that is in Socho and asked: “Where are Samuel and David?” He was told: “Behold, they are at Naioth in Ramah.”

He went to Naioth in Ramah, and the Spirit of the Lord came upon him also. He walked along, entering and prophesying, until he came to Naioth in Ramah. He stripped off his garments as well and prophesied with the others before Samuel. He sang naked all day and all night. Hence the proverb arose:

“Is Saul also among the prophets?”

(Cap. XX.) David fled from Naioth, which was in Ramah, and came and spoke before Jonathan: “What have I done? What is my iniquity, and what is my sin against your father, that he seeks my life?”

He said to him: “Far be it from you; you shall not die. For my father will do nothing, great or small, without first revealing it to me. Has my father hidden this matter from me alone? It shall certainly not be so.” And he swore again to David.

David said: “Your father surely knows that I have found favor in your eyes, and he says: ‘Let Jonathan not know this, lest he be grieved.’ Indeed, as the Lord lives and as your soul lives, there is only one step, so to speak, between me and death.”

Jonathan said to David: “Whatever your soul tells me, I will do for you.”

David said to Jonathan: “Behold, tomorrow is the new moon, and I customarily sit beside the king to eat. Therefore let me go and hide in the field until the evening of the third day. If your father looks for me, you will answer him: ‘David earnestly asked me to go quickly to his city, Bethlehem, because there is a solemn sacrifice there for all his fellow clansmen.’

“If he says, ‘Good,’ there will be peace for your servant. But if he becomes angry, know that his wickedness is complete. Therefore show mercy to your servant, because you made me, your servant, enter into the Lord’s covenant with you.”

R\. Amen.

### Antiphon 1

“I have announced my life to you, O God; you have placed my tears in your sight, O Lord. As in your promise, O God, my God, let [Col. 0490C] my enemies turn back.”

V\. “Have mercy on me, O Lord, for man has trampled me; all day long he has afflicted me in battle.”

### Prayer

We announce our life to you, O God, because by dying you conquered the underworld. You are the firm one who knows what is ours; you alone are the examiner of the heart. We ask you to place our tears in your sight, so that they may receive the gift of the promise, while through it we prepare the holy fruit of forgiveness.

R\. Amen.

### Antiphon 2

“Let those who wait for you, O Lord, God of hosts, not be put to shame because of me. For on your account I have borne reproach; shame has covered my face. Come now, O Lord, to my soul and redeem [Col. 0490D] it; because of my enemies, deliver me.”

V\. “For zeal for your house has consumed me, and the reproaches of those reproaching you have fallen upon me.”

### Prayer

Let those who await you, O Lord, God of hosts, not be put to shame in us, since you will judge human deeds. May the power of your Cross present us to you as willing workers of salvation and not allow the court of the heavenly army to be saddened by our deeds.

R\. Amen.

### Antiphon 3

“My tongue will meditate on your justice, O Lord; all day long I will praise you, when all who seek evil against me have been confounded and put to shame.”

V\. “I have hoped in you, O Lord; let the one who dwells in Jerusalem not be put to shame forever.”

R\. “My enemies placed me in distress, and [Col. 0491A] he whom I loved delivered me to bitterness.”

P. “Without cause he wounded me; you, O Lord, deliver me.”

V\. “For the man of my peace, in whom I trusted, who ate my bread—”

P. “Without cause.”

### Prayers

We beseech you, holy King and God of the ages.

P. “Now have mercy.”

V\. Jesus the Redeemer, who alone became a sacrifice most pleasing to the Father for the world, mercifully deliver us.

P. “Now.”

V\. When he was dying, the earth trembled, giving birth from the tombs to those buried, for the faith of believers.

P. “Now.”

V\. You who, placed in the tomb, rest there, refresh the dead by your rest, striking the underworld.

P. “Now.”

V\. You who are closed in by the stone of the tomb and rise again unknown to the guards, cleanse us from vices.

P. “Now.”

### Hymn

“O Nazarene, light.” Fol. 144.

[Col. 0491B] ### Prayer

May our tongue, O Lord, meditate on your acts of justice, so that your praise may proceed all day from our mouth, inasmuch as the glory of your Passion has been proclaimed by us; so that in that justice by which we live from faith, both now and forever without end, we may praise you.

Our Father.

### Reading from the Book of the Prophet Ezekiel

(Cap. XXXV.)

R\. Thanks be to God.

The word of the Lord came to me, saying: “Son of man, set your face against Mount Seir. I will stretch out my hand over you and make you desolate and deserted. I will demolish your cities, and you will be deserted; and you will know that I am the Lord.

“Because you have been an everlasting enemy and have confined the children of Israel in the hand of the sword at the time of extreme iniquity, [Col. 0491C] therefore, as I live, says the Lord God, I will deliver you over to blood, and blood will pursue you. I will make Mount Seir desolate and deserted, and I will remove from it one who goes out and one who returns.

“I will fill its mountains with those slain by it; on its hills, in its valleys, and in its ravines, those killed by the sword will fall. I will deliver you over to everlasting desolation, and your cities will not be inhabited; and you will know that I am the Lord.”

R\. Amen.

### Antiphon

“Behold, God helps me, and the Lord is the sustainer of my soul, repaying evil to my enemies.”

V\. “Save me, O God, by your name, and deliver me by your power.”

### Prayer

Help us, O God our Savior, who are the sustainer of our souls, so that we may rejoice in your [Col. 0491D] holy name. May we who are called by the name of Christ deserve to enjoy participation in him. Thus may we attain eternal joys and overcome present adversities, so that in all things we may praise you and rejoice that you are in us.

R\. Amen.

### Antiphon 2

“Behold, I fled far away and remained in solitude.”

P. “I awaited God, who would save me from faintheartedness and tempest.”

V\. “Hurl them down, O Lord, and divide their tongues, for I have seen iniquity and contradiction in the city. Day and night it will surround her upon her walls.”

### Prayer

Behold, O Lord, placed amid the world’s disturbances and choosing the quiet of solitude, we desire to flee far away from earthly affairs, so that we may be saved from faintheartedness [Col. 0492A] and tempest. Therefore, as we now await the rest prepared for us in these places, grant us that, once human clamor has been removed, we may rejoice in the contemplation of your sweetness alone.

R\. Amen.

287 ### Antiphon 3

V\. “Rescue me, O Lord, from the evil man; deliver me from the unjust and deceitful man.”

P. “You who are powerful in mercy.”

P. “You who—”

V\. By your dying, may we live.

P. “You who—”

“O Nazarene.” Fol. 144.

### Prayer

Protect us, O Lord, from the assembly of wicked enemies, you who endured the reproach of the Cross. Those who sharpened their tongues against you like a sword, you won over through the most health-giving gift of your grace; may they be devoured by the bite of the Church.

Our Father.

# SATURDAY

## At Matins

### Antiphon

“But you, O Lord.”

Psalm III.

### Prayer

“Although, O Lord.” Fol. 141.

### Antiphon 1

“O God, crush the teeth of the enemies; break the jaws of lions, so that they may come to nothing like flowing water, and so that the righteous may rejoice when he sees vengeance upon the wicked.”

V\. “Indeed, you speak justice; judge rightly, children of men.”

[Col. 0492D] ### Prayer

O God, who by the marvelous challenge of your answer crushes the teeth of enemies and breaks the jaws of lions, while preparing an unconquerable weapon against their questions and, mocking their cries, showing yourself alive after being crucified through wounds: now, we ask, break the boldness of the enemies who follow against you, so that those who desire to scatter the teachings of their wickedness within your Church may come to nothing like flowing water.

R\. Amen.

### Antiphon 2

“My enemies have seized my soul, O Lord; the strong have rushed upon me. Behold, they speak against me, and there is a sword on their lips. Scatter them by your power and destroy them, my protector.”

V\. “Deliver me from my enemies, my God, and free me from those who rise up against me.”

[Col. 0493A] ### Prayer

The strong seized your soul, Christ the Lord, and rushed fiercely upon you, when at the time of your Passion a company of the proud attacked you. Therefore, we ask, now look upon the prayer of your Church and remove the bloody sword from the hand of the enemy, so that he may feel himself cut down by his own blade when, through those whom he had held, he recognizes that the doctrine of your faith is being proclaimed.

R\. Amen.

### Antiphon 3

“O God, attend to my help; O Lord, hasten to help me. Let those who seek my soul be confounded and put to shame.”

V\. “Let those who devise evil against me be turned back and confounded.”

### Prayer

O God, attend to our help, so that we who long with most sincere vows to share in your sufferings [Col. 0493B] may feel you as our helper in our own efforts.

R\. Amen.

R\. “Along the way by which I walked, they hid a snare for me. I looked to the right and saw, but there was no one who knew me. Escape has failed me, and there is no one who seeks my soul.”

V\. “Why, O Lord, do you turn your face away from me in my prayer?”

### Prayer

As we pour out our prayer before you, O Lord, stand beside us as a merciful helper. Be our protection, you who are our redemption. Direct our understanding beneath your kindness, and regard our paths with tranquil guidance, so that amid the hidden snares on this road of yours along which we walk, we may hasten in desire for you in such a way that, by the footprint of faith, we may come to the portion pleasing to you.

R\. Amen.

[Col. 0493C] ### Antiphon

“To you alone I have sinned, O Lord; I have done evil before you. Have mercy on me.”

Psalm L.
