## At Matins

### Antiphon

“O God, my God, to you I keep vigil from the light.”

V\. “My soul has thirsted for you; how greatly also my flesh has thirsted for you, in a deserted, pathless, and waterless land.”

### Praise

“Let every spirit praise the name of the Lord.”

Psalm CL.

### Reading from the Book of Samuel

(First Book of Kings, chap. XXI.)

R\. Thanks be to God.

In those days David came to Nob, to Ahimelech [Col. 0493D] the priest. Ahimelech was astonished that David had come, and he said to him: “Why are you alone, and no one is with you?”

David said to Ahimelech the priest: “The king commanded me concerning a matter and said: ‘Let no one know the business for which I have sent you or what orders I have given you. I have also instructed the young men to meet me at such and such a place.’ Now therefore, if you have anything at hand—even five loaves—give them to me, or whatever you may find.”

The priest answered David and said to him: “I do not have ordinary bread at hand, but only holy bread—provided that the young men are clean, especially from women.”

David answered the priest and said to him: “Indeed, if women are in question, we have kept ourselves from them since yesterday and the day before, when we were setting out, and the vessels [Col. 0494A] of the young men were holy. Moreover, this way is polluted, but today it will be sanctified in the vessels.”

Therefore the priest gave him consecrated bread, for there was no bread there except the bread of the Presence, which had been removed from before the Lord so that hot bread might be placed there.

There was a man there that day, inside the tabernacle of the Lord, one of Saul’s servants. His name was Doeg the Idumean, the most powerful of Saul’s shepherds; he was tending Saul’s mules.

David said to Ahimelech: “If you have a sword or a spear here at hand, give it to me, because I did not bring my sword or my weapons with me. The king’s command was urgent.”

The priest said: “Behold, here is the sword of Goliath the Philistine, whom you struck down in the Valley of the Terebinth. It is wrapped in a cloak behind the ephod. If you wish to take it, take it, for there is no other [Col. 0494B] here besides it.”

David said: “There is no other like it; give it to me.”

David rose and fled that day from Saul’s presence. He came to Achish, king of Gath. When they saw David, Achish’s servants said: “Is this not David, the king of the land? Did they not sing of him in dances, saying: ‘Saul has struck down his thousands, and David his ten thousands’?”

David stored these words in his heart and was greatly afraid before Achish, king of Gath. He changed his expression before Achish, acted madly in their hands, beat against the doors of the gate, and let his saliva run down into his beard.

Achish said to his servants: “You see that the man is insane. Why have you brought him to me? Are we lacking madmen, that you have brought this fellow to rave in my presence? Let him go; he shall not enter my [Col. 0494C] house.”

(Cap. XXII.) David departed from there and fled to the cave of Adullam. When his brothers heard of it, they went down to him there. Everyone who was in distress, oppressed by a foreign king, and bitter in spirit gathered to him. He became their leader, and about four hundred men were with him.

David departed from there and went to Mizpah in Moab. He said to the king of Moab: “Please let my father and my mother remain with you until I know what God will do for me.” He left them before the king of Moab, and they remained with him all the days that David was in the stronghold.

The prophet Gad said to David: “Do not remain in the stronghold. Depart and go into the land of Judah.” David departed and came to the forest of Hareth.

[Col. 0494D] Saul heard that David had appeared, together with the men who were with him. Saul was staying in Gibeah, in the forest that is in Ramah, holding a spear in his hand, while all his servants stood around him. He said to the servants who attended him: “Listen, sons of Benjamin. Will the son of Jesse give all of you fields and vineyards, and make all of you commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds? For you have all conspired against me, and there is no one who reports to me, especially since my son has also made a covenant with the son of Jesse.

“There is no one among you who grieves over my situation or reports to me, because my son has stirred up my servant against me, lying in wait for me to this day.”

[Col. 0495A] Doeg the Idumean, who attended him and was chief among Saul’s servants, answered: “I saw the son of Jesse at Nob, with Ahimelech son of Ahitub, the priest. He consulted the Lord for him, gave him provisions, and also gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine.”

The king therefore sent to summon Ahimelech son of Ahitub, the priest, and all his father’s household, the priests who were in Nob. They all came to the king.

Saul said: “Listen, son of Ahitub.”

He answered: “I am here, my lord.”

Saul said to him: “Why have you conspired against me, you and the son of Jesse? You gave him bread and a sword, and you consulted the Lord for him, so that he might rise up against me and remain in ambush against me to this day.”

Ahimelech answered the king and said: “Who among all your servants is like David, faithful, the king’s son-in-law, obedient to your command, and honored in your [Col. 0495B] house? Is today the first day I have consulted the Lord for him? Far be this from me. Let not the king suspect his servant of such a matter in all my father’s house, for your servant knew nothing of this affair, either small or great.”

The king said: “You shall surely die, Ahimelech—you and your father’s entire household.”

The king said to the messengers who stood around him: “Turn and kill the priests of the Lord, for their hand is with David. They knew that he had fled and did not report it to me.”

But the king’s servants would not stretch out their hands against the priests of the Lord.

The king said to Doeg the Idumean: “You turn and rush upon the priests of the Lord.”

Doeg the Idumean turned and rushed upon the priests of the Lord, and on that day he slaughtered eighty-five men wearing the linen ephod.

[Col. 0495C] He struck Nob, the city of the priests, with the edge of the sword: men and women, children and infants, ox and donkey and sheep—all with the edge of the sword.

One son of Ahimelech son of Ahitub, whose name was Abiathar, escaped and fled to David. He reported to him that Saul had killed the priests of the Lord.

David said to Abiathar: “I knew on that day, since Doeg the Idumean was there, that he would surely report it to Saul. I am responsible for every life belonging to your father’s household. Remain with me; if anyone seeks my life, he will also seek your life, and with me you will be safe.”

(Cap. XXIII.) David was told: “Behold, the Philistines are attacking Keilah and plundering the threshing floors.”

David therefore consulted the Lord, saying: “Shall I go and strike these Philistines?”

The Lord said to David: “Go, [Col. 0495D] and you will strike the Philistines and save Keilah.”

The men who were with David said to him: “Behold, while we remain here in Judah, we are afraid; how much more if we go to Keilah against the armies of the Philistines?”

David again consulted the Lord. He answered and said: “Arise and go to Keilah, for I will deliver the Philistines into your hand.”

David and his men went to Keilah, fought against the Philistines, drove away their livestock, and struck them with a great blow. Thus David saved the inhabitants of Keilah.

At that time, when Abiathar son of Ahimelech fled to David at Keilah, he had brought the ephod down with him.

Saul was informed that David had come to Keilah, and Saul said: “God has delivered him into my hands, [Col. 0496A] for he has entered a city with gates and bars and is shut in.”

Saul commanded all the people to go down to Keilah for battle and besiege David and his men.

When David learned that Saul was secretly preparing a hand against him, he said to Abiathar the priest: “Bring the ephod here.”

David said: “Lord God of Israel, your servant has certainly heard that Saul is planning to come to Keilah to destroy the city because of me. Will the men of Keilah deliver me into his hand? Will Saul come down, as your servant has heard? Lord God of Israel, reveal this to your servant.”

The Lord said: “He will come down.”

David said: “Will the men of Keilah deliver me and the men who are with me into the hands of Saul?”

The Lord said: “They will deliver you.”

David and his men, about six hundred, rose and went out from Keilah. They wandered here and there, [Col. 0496B] uncertain where to go. Saul was told that David had fled from Keilah, and therefore he refrained from going out.

David remained in the wilderness, in the strongest places, and stayed on the mountain in the wilderness of Ziph. Saul sought him continually, but God did not deliver him into his hands.

David saw that Saul had gone out to seek his life. David was in the wilderness of Ziph, in the forest.

Jonathan, Saul’s son, rose and went to the forest and strengthened David’s hands in the Lord. He said to him: “Do not be afraid, for the hand of my father Saul will not find you. You will reign over Israel, and I will be second to you. Even my father Saul knows this.”

Thus the two of them made a covenant before the Lord. David remained in the forest, while Jonathan returned to his house.

[Col. 0496C] R\. Amen.

### Hymn

“Nighttime.” Fol. 257.

### Capitulum

We believe and confess that you, good Christ, were pierced for us with many wounds, and that, apart from the punishments of the flesh, you endure the pains of your Passion both speaking and remaining silent. For when you spoke, they cried out that you had blasphemed—those who ought to have been converted; and when you were silent, those who did not fear the gentleness of your humility burned with an abundance of fury.

Grant us, therefore, that we who sing together the pains of your Passion may be freed from our own pains, so that, endowed with a great measure of discernment, when we speak about you and proclaim what is true, our silence may be useful and our speech may advance us toward an eternal reward.

Our Father.

[Col. 0496D] ### Praise

“I remembered your judgments from of old, O Lord, and I was consoled.”

V\. “Faintness held me because of sinners who forsake your law.”

### Prayer

As we remember you in the night, O Lord, grant us to keep your law. May those who do not remain silent about you even in tribulations never stumble away from your words, but endure with firm stability.

R\. Amen.

## At Terce

### Reading from the Book of Proverbs

(Cap. XXII.)

R\. Thanks be to God.

Son, a good name is better than great riches, and good favor is better than gold and silver.

Rich and poor have met one another; the Lord is the maker of both.

The prudent sees evil and hides himself; [Col. 0497A] the innocent passes through and suffers harm.

The end of modesty is the fear of the Lord; riches, glory, and life follow it.

Weapons and swords are on the way of the perverse; one who guards his soul keeps far away from them.

There is a proverb: “A young man, even when he grows old, will not depart from his way.”

The rich rule over the poor, and the borrower is the servant of the lender.

Whoever sows iniquity will reap evils and will complete the rod of his anger.

Whoever is inclined to mercy will be blessed, for he has given the poor from his bread.

R\. Amen.

### Reading from the Book of Samuel

(First Book of Kings, chap. XXIII.)

R\. Thanks be to God.

In those days the Ziphites went up to Saul at Gibeah, saying: “Is not David hiding among us in the safest places of the forest, on the hill of Hachilah, which is to the right of the wilderness? Now therefore, just as your heart has resolved that you should go down, go down; and it will be our task to hand him over into the king’s power.”

And Saul said: “Blessed are you by the Lord, who have pitied my cause. Go, I beg you, and hasten more diligently; act with the greatest care, and determine the place where his foot is, or who has seen him there. For he is considering that I am craftily lying in wait for him. Examine and observe all his hiding places in which he is concealed; then return to me with certainty, and I shall go with you. But if he has even withdrawn into the land, I shall search him out among the many thousands of Judah.”

They therefore arose and went to Ziph before Saul. But David and his men were in the wilderness of Maon, in the plain, to the right of Jeshimon. [Col. 0497C] Saul and his companions went out to seek him, and David was informed. Immediately he went down toward the rock and remained in the wilderness of Maon. When Saul heard this, he pursued David in the wilderness of Maon.

Saul went along one side of the mountain, while David and his men were on the other side. David, however, was despairing of being able to escape from Saul’s presence. Thus Saul and his men surrounded David and his men in the manner of a ring, in order to capture them.

A messenger then came to Saul, saying: “Hurry and come, for the Philistines have poured themselves over the land.” Saul therefore returned, ceasing to pursue David, and went to meet the Philistines. For this reason they called that place “the Dividing Rock.”

David then went up from there and departed to the safest places of Engedi. When Saul had returned with three thousand chosen men from all Israel, he went to search for David and his men, even over the steepest rocks, which are passable only for wild goats.

He came to sheepfolds beside the road, and there was a cave into which Saul entered to relieve himself. David and his men, however, were hiding in the innermost part of the cave.

David’s men said to him: “Behold, this is the day of which the Lord spoke to you: ‘I shall deliver your enemy into your hand, so that you may do to him whatever seems good in your eyes.’”

David therefore rose and silently cut off the edge of Saul’s cloak. Afterward his heart struck him because he had cut off the edge of Saul’s cloak. He said to his men: “May the Lord be gracious to me, and may I not do this thing to my lord, the Lord’s anointed, by extending my hand against him, because he is the Lord’s anointed.”

And David restrained his men by these words, and did not permit them to rise against Saul. Saul, meanwhile, rose from the cave and continued on the journey he had begun.

David also rose afterward and, going out of the cave, called after Saul’s back, saying: “My lord the king!” Saul looked behind him, [Col. 0498A] and David, bowing forward with his face to the ground, worshiped and said to Saul:

“Why do you listen to the words of men who say, ‘David is seeking evil against you’? Behold, today your eyes have seen that the Lord delivered you into my hand in the cave. I considered killing you, but my eye spared you; for I said: ‘I will not extend my hand against my lord, because he is the Lord’s anointed.’

“Indeed, my father, see and recognize the edge of your cloak in my hand: how, when I cut off the top of your cloak, I did not wish to extend my hand against you. Consider and see that there is no evil or injustice in my hand, and that I have not sinned against you. Yet you lie in wait for my life, to take it.

“May the Lord judge between me and you, and may the Lord avenge me upon you; but may my hand not be against you. As it is also said in the ancient proverb: ‘From the wicked comes wickedness’; therefore may my hand not be against you.

“Whom are you pursuing? You are pursuing a dead dog and a single flea. May the Lord be judge, and may he judge between me and you; may he see and judge my case, and deliver me from your hand.”

When David had finished speaking these words to Saul, Saul said: “Is this your voice, my son David?” Saul raised his voice and wept, and said to David:

“You are more righteous than I, for you have repaid me with good, while I have repaid you with evil. And today you have shown the good you have done to me—how the Lord delivered me into your hand, and you did not kill me.

“For who, when he has found his enemy, would send him away on a good path? But may the Lord repay you for this exchange, because today you have acted toward me.

“And now, because I know with absolute certainty that you shall reign, and that the kingdom of Israel shall be in your hand, swear to me by the Lord that you will not destroy my descendants after me, nor remove my name from my father’s house.”

David swore this to Saul. Saul then went to his house, while David and his men went up to safer places in the wilderness. [Col. 0498D] R. Amen.

Antiphon 1. Attend to my defense, O Lord. Deliver my soul from the sword, and my only one from the hand of the dog. Save me, my king and my God.

V. Do not depart from me, for distress is near, and there is no one to help.

Prayer. Look upon the defense of the Church, shepherd of souls, Lord Jesus Christ, mercifully delivering our souls from the lion’s mouth—he whose soul was delivered from the sword and the hand of the dog. R. Amen.

Antiphon 2. You are my strength and my refuge, my God. Deliver me from the hand of the one acting against the law, and from [in qui…].

V. For you are my patience, O Lord; my hope from my youth.

[Col. 0499A] Prayer. Our strength and refuge, we beseech you, O crucified Lord: deliver us from the hand of the sinner and establish us, crowned, in a fortified place. R. Amen.

Antiphon 3. Why, O Lord, do you cast away my soul? Why do you turn your face from me? I am poor and afflicted from my youth. You have put far from me friend and companion; you have taken away my acquaintance.

V. Your terrors have passed over me, and your fears have troubled me.

R. My God, save me from the hand of the ungodly; from the hand of the unjust and the harmful one, for you are my expectation, O God. O Lord, you are my hope from my youth.

V. Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man; free me from the unjust man.

[Col. 0499B] Prayers. Have mercy, O Lord, on those who entreat you.

P. And grant us forgiveness.

V. We believe that you, Christ the Lord, suffered for us.

P. You.

V. We confess that you were scourged with slaps and punishments.

P. And.

V. The earth trembled when you were dead; when you rose, it rejoiced.

P. You.

V. Now, freed by your death, may we receive the kingdom of heaven.

P. And grant it.

Hymn. “O Nazarene.” Fol. 144.

Capitulum. Consider our need and poverty, good Christ; so that, when you turn your face from us, you may not cast away our soul. Thus may we, who have been poor and afflicted from our youth, be sometime refreshed by heavenly delights and rejoice, clothed in eternal immortality.

[Col. 0499C] Our Father.

At Sext.

Reading from the Book of the Prophet Jeremiah (chapter V).

R. Thanks be to God.

Thus says the Lord: “Hear, people who have no heart, who have eyes but do not see. Will you not fear me, says the Lord, and will you not grieve before my face? I set the sand as a boundary for the sea, an everlasting command that it cannot pass; its waves are stirred, but they cannot prevail; its waves swell, but they do not cross over it.

“But this people has acquired an unbelieving and rebellious heart; they have turned aside and gone away. They did not say in their heart: ‘Let us fear the Lord our God, who gives us the early and late rain in its season, preserving for us the fullness of the annual harvest.’

“Your iniquities have turned you away from him, and your sins have withheld good from us. Wicked men have been found among my people, lying in wait like bird-catchers, setting snares and traps for capturing men. Like a cage full of birds, so their houses are full of deceit, because they have grown great and wealthy. They have become fat and sleek, and they have passed beyond my words most wickedly.

“They have not judged the case of the widow, nor administered the case of the orphan, nor judged the judgment of the poor. Shall I not visit these things, says the Lord? Or shall my soul not avenge itself upon such a nation?

“Dreadful and astonishing things have occurred in the land: the prophets prophesied lies, and the priests applauded [Col. 0500A] with their hands; and my people loved such things. What, then, will happen at its end?

“Strengthen yourselves, sons of Benjamin, in the midst of Jerusalem.” R. Amen.

Antiphon 1. Do not hand me over together with sinners, and do not destroy me, O Lord, together with those who work iniquity.

V. Give them, O Lord, according to their works and according to the wickedness of their schemes.

Prayer. Christ our God, who were handed over to the punishment of the cross among sinners, namely with thieves, and endured it: we ask that you not hand us over together with sinners, nor punish us together with those who work iniquity; so that those whom you deigned to free by your Passion from the power of the devil, you may separate both here and forever from the infernal lot of sinners. R. Amen.

Antiphon 2. O Lord, hear my prayer, and let my cry come to you. On whatever day I am troubled, incline your ear to me.

V. On whatever day I call upon you, hear me quickly.

Prayer. O Lord, hear my prayer, and let our cry reach your kindly ear with the peace of your benevolence. Do not recall us in the middle of our days; but, as we move toward a secure station, make us complete the course of virtue and, through the pursuit of sanctification, obtain the eternal kingdom of glory amid the brief span of these present days. R. Amen.

Antiphon 3. Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man and from the unjust man and from the deceitful tongue.

V. Guard me, O Lord, from the hand of the sinner, and free me from unjust men who have devised ways to trip my steps.

[Col. 0500C] R. Deliver me from my enemies, O Lord.

P. For you are my God.

V. Deliver me from those who work iniquity, and free me from men of blood.

P. For you are.

Prayers. To you we all cry, O Lord.

P. Have mercy.

V. Hear, O God, your people, and defend us from the enemy.

P. Have mercy.

V. Hear, O God, the Pontiff and his priest.

P. Have mercy.

V. Hear, O God, the miserable, and recall the captives.

P. Have mercy.

V. Hear, O God, the widows and the tears of orphans.

P. Have mercy.

V. Hear, O God, the blind, and restore to them light forever; may we live with you without end.

P. Have mercy.

Hymn. “O Nazarene, Light.” Fol. 144.

Prayer. Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man—you who were handed over for another’s crime—so that your Passion may deliver us from future torments, the Passion which was made a mockery by the ungodly.

Our Father.

## On the Fifth Sunday of Lent

At Vespers.

Praise-song. “Sacrifice a sacrifice.” Fol. 214.

Prayer. God of our righteousness, appear merciful to us when we call upon you, so that we may offer the evening sacrifice and, with your help, reach the heavenly rewards. R. Amen.

Antiphon. Moses said to the people: “On the fourteenth day of the month of Nisan you shall celebrate the Passover.”

V. “Sound the trumpet at the beginning of the month, amid the signs of our solemnity.”

[Col. 0501A] Praise-song. Weariness has seized me because of those who abandon your law. Your ordinances were songs for me in the place of my pilgrimage.

V. Remember your word to your servant, by which you gave me hope.

Hymn. “The Father’s Word.” See fol. 252.

Capitulum. Christ our God, who for all of us took upon yourself the insult of the Passion; who are found peaceful among those who hate peace, and are crucified innocent by the guilty; and thus, by your death, transform the death of the human race: grant us that the multiplied iniquity of the proud may not prevail against us, and that meditation on your law may not depart from the devotion of our hearts.

Or, since you alone for all of us endured both death and the tomb, grant believers in you both the light of eternal life and the reward.

[Col. 0501B] Our Father.

Blessing. May Christ the Lord, who by his death conquered the death of our humanity, make you victorious over your crime.

R. Amen.

And may he who permitted himself to be handed over by the ungodly deliver you from the punishments of eternal torments.

R. Amen.

And may you live without end with him who became victor over death.

R. Amen.

Praise-song. Many are those who persecute and trouble me, O Lord; yet I have not turned aside from your law, my God.

V. See my humility and deliver me, for I have not forgotten your law.

Prayer. May your many mercies, O Lord, erase all our iniquities and lead us, cleansed, to your forgiveness. R. Amen.

Praise-song 2. With my whole heart I have cried out; hear me, O Lord.

V. I have cried to you; save me, so that I may keep your testimonies.

[Col. 0501C] Prayer. We cry out to you, O Lord, so that you may hear us and admit us, with eyes inclined from the earth, to you; so that, as your serenity illumines us, we may always remain in the light. R. Amen.

Praise-song 3. See my humility and deliver me, O Lord, for I have not forgotten your law.

V. Judge my cause and redeem me; because of your word, give me life.

Prayer. See our humility, O Lord, and deliver us. When you look upon us, even if we are cast down, we are lifted up; when you sustain us, we are received lest we fall. R. Amen.

[Col. 0501D] Prayers. Lord of mercies.

P. Forget our sins.

V. You who, rising from the dead, sit at the right hand of God the Father.

P. Forget them.

V. You who promise rewards to the just and threaten punishments to the unjust.

P. Forget them.

V. You who do not judge the sinner, but call him to repentance and await him.

P. Forget them.

V. You who call the righteous to endurance and, after testing, summon them to the crown.

P. Forget them.

Prayer. “Hear the prayer.” Fol. 138.

At Matins.

Hymn. “Eternal Creator of all things.” See fol. 3.

Prayer. God, whom created greatness celebrates together in praise as the maker of the whole work, and whose power rational creation marvels at: we suppliantly offer you honor and call upon you with the voices of our hearts. [Col. 0502A] You awaken us to the office of Matins when the cock announces the dawn; make the vows of our peaceful service pleasing to you, and by your gentle protection wash away what we have sullied by sinning. We continually beseech you to grant us the grace of your righteousness. R. Amen.

Antiphon. God is my glory and the one who lifts up my head. Psalm III.

Antiphon. Against you alone I have sinned; have mercy on me, O God. Psalm L.

Prayer. O Lord, our protector, lift up our head in glory and enrich us with your mercy. Wash the inmost part of our heart from the injustice within our heart, and cleanse it from the stains of sin. Send from heaven and rescue us from the reproach of those who trample us, [Col. 0502B] so that, joyful, we may return to this altar of yours and offer you the morning sacrifice in the temple. R. Amen.

Antiphon. I shall sing to your name, O Most High. When my enemy turns backward, they shall be weakened and perish from your presence.

V. For you have carried out my judgment and my cause; you have sat upon the throne, judging righteousness.

Prayer. May your Church always sing to your name, O Most High God, who through the triumph of your Passion turned backward the enemy of our soul. We therefore ask that, when he and his attendants have likewise been weakened and destroyed, your glorious Passion may always abundantly protect us. R. Amen.

Antiphon 2. Sinners have drawn the bow; they have prepared arrows in the quiver, to shoot in darkness at the upright in heart. What you established, they destroyed; but the righteous one—what has he done?

V. The Lord is in his holy temple; the Lord’s throne is in heaven.

Prayer. Against you, Christ the Lord, sinners displaying their malignity have stretched the bow, but they have nevertheless been pierced by the arrows of their own deceit. Since they were unable, as they attempted, to pierce you in the darkness of wickedness with the darts of their tongue, we ask that you draw us out from their teeth by the protection of your Passion, so that those who wickedly persecuted you, upright in heart, may perceive you as our protector in all things. R. Amen.

Antiphon 3. May the Lord destroy all deceitful lips and the boastful tongue—those who say: “Our lips are with us; who is our God?” I shall place my trust in his salvation; I shall act confidently in him.

V. Save me, O Lord, for the holy man has failed; truths have diminished among the children of men.

Prayer. Destroy, O Lord, all deceitful lips and the boastful tongue, so that those who refuse to act confidently in your salvation may be confounded by the wickedness of their lips. And, once they have been called in Christ our Lord through repentance and made one with us in the language of faith, may deceitful lips altogether disappear from among us. R. Amen.

R. Wicked men said: “Let us oppress the righteous man unjustly and swallow him like a living underworld; let us remove his memory from the earth.”

P. And let us cast lots among ourselves for his spoils; but those murderers have stored up evil for themselves. They were foolish and wicked: they hated wisdom, and became guilty in their thoughts.

V. They said: “Come, let us strike him with the tongue and pay no attention to all his words.”

P. And for his spoils.

Prayer. Christ, Son of God, whose life wicked men determined to oppress and swallow, striving, as the underworld decreed, to remove your memory from the earth—you who created heaven and earth—we ask and beseech you: since you graciously endured the casting of lots for the garment of your clothing, patiently endure the falls of our frailty; and, having cleansed us from the accusation of every crime, preserve us, so that, when you have freed us from the bonds of evil habit, you may associate us in the future with the choirs of the saints, to be crowned. R. Amen.

At Lauds.

For the Canticle. Antiphon. The portion of the Lord became the people of Jacob, Israel the cord of his inheritance. He gave them sufficiency in a deserted land, in the heat of thirst where there was no water.

Canticle. “Give ear, O heaven.” Fol. 4.

Prayer. Make us, O Lord our God, to be a portion of the cord of your inheritance, so that we may deserve to be refreshed by you, who are our hope and satisfaction, with the sufficiency of the heat of your fire in the thirsting land of your body. R. Amen.

For the Benedictus. Antiphon. Send forth your light, O Lord, for you are my God and my strength.

[Col. 0503C] V. O God, my God, to you I keep watch from the dawn.

Canticle. “Blessed are you, O Lord.” See fol. 6.

Praise-song. Praise the Lord from the earth: mountains and all hills, fruitful trees and all cedars, for his name alone has been exalted.

P. And he exalted the horn of his people.

V. His praise is in all his saints.

P. And he exalted.

Reading from the Book of Samuel (First Book of Kings, chapter XXV).

R. Thanks be to God.

In those days, there was a certain man in the wilderness of Maon, whose property was in Carmel. The man was very wealthy; he had three thousand sheep and a thousand goats. It happened that his flock was being sheared in Carmel.

The man’s name was Nabal, and his wife’s name was Abigail. That woman was exceedingly prudent and beautiful; but her husband was harsh, very wicked, and malicious. He was of the family of Caleb.

When David heard in the wilderness that Nabal was shearing his flock, he sent ten young men and said to them: “Go up to Carmel, and you shall come to Nabal and greet him peacefully in my name. And say this:

“‘Peace to my brothers, and peace to you, peace to your house, and peace to all that you possess. Since for many years I have kept what is yours and all that is yours safe, I have heard that your shepherds were shearing your flocks, which were with us in the wilderness. We were never troublesome to them, nor did anything from the whole flock ever go missing during all the time they were with us in Carmel.

“‘Ask your servants, and they will tell you. Now therefore, may my young men find favor in your eyes, for we have come to you on a good day. Whatever your hand finds, give to your servants and to your son David.’”

When David’s young men arrived, they spoke all these words to Nabal in David’s name, and then were silent.

But Nabal answered David’s young men and said: “Who is David? Or who is the son of Jesse? Today servants are increasing who flee from their masters. Shall I take my bread, my water, and the meat of the sheep that I slaughtered for my shearers, and give them to men whom I do not know where they come from?”

David’s young men therefore returned by their way. They came back and reported to him all the words Nabal had spoken. Then David said to his men: “Let each man gird on his sword.”

Each one girded on his sword, and David also girded on his own sword. About four hundred men followed David, while two hundred remained with the baggage.

One of the young men reported to Abigail, Nabal’s wife, saying: “Behold, David sent messengers from the wilderness to bless our lord, but he opposed them. These men were very good to us and were not troublesome; nor did anything ever go missing during all the time we lived with them in the wilderness. They were a wall for us both by night and by day, throughout all the days when we pastured the flocks near them.

“Therefore consider and think what you should do, for evil has been completed against your husband and against your house; and he is a son of Belial, so that no one can speak to him.”

Abigail therefore hurried and took two hundred loaves, two skins of wine, five cooked sheep, five measures of meal, one hundred clusters of raisins, and two hundred cakes of figs, and placed them on donkeys.

She said to her young men: “Go ahead of me, and behold, I shall follow you behind.” But she did not tell her husband Nabal.

When she had mounted the donkey and was descending toward the base of the mountain, David and his men were coming down to meet her, and she met them. David said:

“Truly, I guarded all that belonged to this man in the wilderness for nothing, and nothing was lost of everything that belonged to him; yet he has repaid me evil for good. May God do this to David’s enemies, and may he add to it, if I leave by morning a single one of all that belong to him who urinates against the wall.”

When Abigail saw David, she hurried and dismounted from the donkey. She fell before David on her face, bowed to the ground, fell at his feet, and said:

“Upon me, my lord, be this iniquity. Let your maidservant speak, I beg you, in your ears, and hear the words of your servant. Please, let my lord the king not set his heart against this wicked man Nabal; for according to his name he is a fool, and folly is with him. But I, your maidservant, my lord the king, did not see the young men whom you sent.

“Now therefore, my lord, as the Lord lives and as your soul lives, it is the Lord who prevented you from coming to bloodshed and saved your hand for you. Now therefore, may the enemies of my lord and those who seek evil against my lord be like Nabal.

“Therefore accept this blessing which your maidservant has brought to you, my lord, and give it to the young men who follow you, my lord.

“Take away the iniquity of your maidservant. For the Lord will certainly make a faithful house for my lord, because you fight the battles of the Lord, my lord; therefore let no evil be found in you throughout all the days of your life.

“For if a man should ever rise up to pursue you or seek your life, the soul of my lord shall be kept as though in the bundle of the living with the Lord your God; but the souls of your enemies shall be whirled about as by the force and circle of a sling.

“When the Lord has done for my lord all the good things he has spoken concerning you, and has appointed you leader over Israel, this will not be for you a cause of grief or a stumbling block of heart, my lord, that you have shed innocent blood or avenged yourself.

“And when the Lord has dealt well with my lord, remember your maidservant, and you will deal well with her.”

David said to Abigail: “Blessed is the Lord, the God of Israel, who sent you today to meet me; and blessed is your speech, and blessed are you, who prevented me today from going to bloodshed and avenging myself with my own hand.

“Otherwise, as the Lord God of Israel lives, who prevented me from doing evil to you, unless you had quickly come to meet me, Nabal would not have remained until the morning light—not even one who urinates against the wall.”

David therefore received from her hand everything she had brought him, and said to her: “Go in peace to your house. Behold, I have heard your voice and honored your face.”

Abigail came to Nabal, and behold, he had a feast in his house, like the feast of a king, and Nabal’s heart was cheerful, for he was exceedingly drunk. She did not tell him a small thing or a great thing until morning.

At dawn, when Nabal’s wine had dissipated, his wife told him these words. His heart died within him, and he became like a stone.

When ten days had passed, the Lord struck Nabal, and he died.

When David heard that Nabal was dead, he said: “Blessed is the Lord, who judged the cause of my reproach from Nabal’s hand and kept his servant from evil.” R. Amen.

Hymn. “The Time of Night.” Fol. 257.

Capitulum. Only-begotten Son of God, who, taking upon yourself the sufferings of our mortality, willed us to be participants in your Passion: make us both followers of light and workers of truth, so that, escaping the shipwrecks of our death, and being more abundantly illumined by the fourfold stream of your Gospels, we may deserve to be made worthy by the example of your Passion.

Our Father.

## At Second Vespers

Praise-song. “How greatly your works are magnified until evening, O Lord!”

Antiphon. Let us humble our souls in fasting, for the Lord’s Passover is near, and the Lord will deliver us from the house of bondage.

V. May God have mercy on us and bless us; may the Lord illumine his face upon us and have mercy on us.

Praise-song. Sinners have waited for me in order to destroy me, but they have not understood your testimonies. [lacuna]. Forever, O Lord, your word remains in heaven.

[Col. 0506A] Hymn. “The Father’s Word.” Fol. 252.

Capitulum. As we humble our souls in fasting, O Lord God, lead them out from the underworld and rescue us from those descending into the pit. You, who in unspeakable power, descending from above to redeem the world, shattered the recesses of the underworld: mercifully guard us, lest we be led there under the rule of sin. Grant that, together with those enrolled for eternal life, we may sing psalms to you in the measure of devotion and, in your loves, deserve the fellowship of blessedness.

Our Father.

Blessing. May the only-begotten Son of God, who suffered that the assumed human being should be hung upon the wood, deign to save us through the mystery of his cross.

Amen.

R. May he who was wounded by the tongues of his persecutors remove our mouth from every fall of temptation.

R. Amen.

And may he who by his singular death conquered the four-day bite of our death deliver us from the torment of eternal punishment.

R. Amen.

Praise-song. Princes have persecuted me without cause, but my heart feared your words. I rejoice over your sayings, like one who finds abundant spoils.

V. I have hated iniquity and abhorred it, but I have loved your law.

Prayer. May there be peace in your love, O God, for those who love you. Since you rejoice in the goodness of peace, refresh us with the gift of your peace, and through the reward of charity remove scandal from us, so that by your peace we may overcome hatred and through charity may cover the multitude of our sins. Thus may we keep your commandments and be led to the glory of your presence by the sweetness of charity. R. Amen.

Antiphon 2. See my humility and deliver me, O Lord.

R. Judge my cause and redeem me; because of your word, give me life.

Prayer. See our humility, O Lord, and deliver us. When you look upon us, even if we are cast down, we are lifted up; when you sustain us, we are received lest we fall. R. Amen.

Praise-song 3. With my whole heart I have cried out; hear me, O Lord.

R. I have cried to you; save me, so that I may keep your testimonies.

Prayer. We cry out to you, O Lord, so that you may hear us and admit us, with eyes inclined from the earth, to you; so that, as your serenity illumines us, we may always remain in the light. R. Amen.

Praise-song 4. I have done judgment and justice, O Lord; do not hand me over to those who persecute me.

R. Receive your servant for good, so that the proud may not slander me.

Prayer. Teach us to do judgment and justice, O Lord, so that we may be able to trample down the slanders of the proud. Receive your servants for good, those who hope in your salvation; and make those whose inner eyes await the kingdom of your Christ share in the company of the Elect. R. Amen.

Prayers and Prayer. “Turn away your anger, O Lord.” Fol. 183.

## Monday

[Col. 0507A]

At Matins.

“After the Sheepfold.”

Antiphon. “My glory, the one who exalts.” Fol. 156.

Psalm III. Prayer. “God our glory.” Fol. 156.

Antiphon. Have mercy on me, O Lord, and see my humility before my enemies. You who raise me up from the gates of death.

V. So that I may announce all your praises in the gates of the daughter of Zion; and I shall rejoice in your salvation.

Prayer. Have mercy on us, O Lord, and see our humility before our enemies. Since you could be held by no bonds of infernal suffering, deign powerfully to raise us from the gates of death. R. Amen.

Antiphon 2. The fool has said in his heart: “There is no God.” They are corrupt and have become detestable in their desires; there is no one who does good, not even one.

V. The Lord looked down from heaven upon the sons of men, to see whether there was anyone intelligent or seeking God.

Prayer. Jesus, ineffable Word of God the Father, whose hearts fools therefore refuse to believe are truly God, because in their own hearts they have become corrupt and detestable: we ask and beseech you that they too may come to know you, just as we have come to know you, so that these people may joyfully be joined to the faithful through true knowledge of faith and may rejoice fully that they have been added to the number of the redeemed. R. Amen.

Antiphon 3. My enemies have surrounded my soul; they have enclosed it in their fat. Their mouth has spoken pride. Deliver my soul from the ungodly, O Lord.

V. Hear, O God, my justice; attend to my prayer. Give ear to my prayer, and not to deceitful lips.

Prayer. Christ, Son of God, whose soul insatiable enemies surrounded, blinded by the fat of their malice, while they spoke pride: deliver our soul from the ungodly. May your Passion extinguish our passions, so that we may never set our eyes on turning toward the earth. R. Amen.

R. They have multiplied beyond the hairs of my head.

P. Those who hate me without cause.

My enemies, who persecuted me unjustly, have grown strong; what I did not seize, then I restored. You, O God, know my ignorance, and my offenses are not hidden from you.

V. Pour out your anger upon my enemies, O Lord, and may the indignation of your wrath seize those who hate me.

Prayer. Lord God, before whom our offenses are not hidden, whose eyes see not only outward things but also penetrate the depths of the heart with an imperceptible gaze: grant us a garment as a remedy of repentance in place of sackcloth; grant us the proclamation of confession in exchange for forgiveness; grant that our eyes may pour out rivers of tears for what we have done; grant our voice to seek the support of prayers through groans.

And you, O Lord, hear our prayer, for your mercy is gracious. May the multitude of your mercies look upon us, lest the depth of the underworld absorb us or muddy crimes overthrow us. R. Amen.

Antiphon. You shall sprinkle me, O Lord, with hyssop, and I shall be cleansed; you shall wash me, and I shall become whiter than snow. Psalm L.

Prayer. God, who uncover our crimes hidden beneath pretence, who in your customary mercy disclose uncertain matters to the doubtful and hidden matters to those who know: when our harmfulness has been revealed, sprinkle us with the dew of your mercy, so that we may be made white like snow by the correction of life. Turn your face away from our sins, we ask; and, blotting out all our iniquities, renew within our inward parts the infusion of your Holy Spirit, so that, rejoicing in such an inhabitant, we may continually open our lips to announce your praise. R. Amen.

Canticle. “Heal me, O Lord.” Fol. 259.

Prayer. Heal us, O Lord, and we shall be healed. Let all who persecute us in your holy name be confounded, but let us not be confounded, who venerate and believe in the power of your Passion. Therefore may the power of your glory prevail, so that it may join those who believe in you to eternal and joyful fellowship. R. Amen.

Matins responsory. I have cried to you, O Lord, and in the morning is my prayer.

V. O Lord, God of my salvation, by day I have cried out and by night before you.

Praise-song. Let us sing a hymn on psaltery and harp. In the choir let praise resound to the Lord, on strings and organ. Psalm CL.

Reading from the Book of Samuel (First Book of Kings, chapter XXVIII).

R. Thanks be to God.

In those days: Samuel died, and all Israel mourned for him, and they buried him in Ramah, his own city. Saul had removed the magicians and diviners from the land and had killed those who had python-spirits [*pythones*] in [Col. 0508C] their bodies. The Philistines gathered together, came, and encamped at Shunem; Saul also gathered all Israel and came to Gilboa. When Saul saw the camp of the Philistines, he was afraid, and his heart was greatly terrified. He consulted the Lord, but the Lord did not answer him, neither through dreams, nor through priests, nor through prophets.

Then Saul said to his servants, “Seek out for me a woman who has a python-spirit, so that I may go to her and inquire through her.” His servants said to him, “There is a woman with a python-spirit at Endor.” So Saul changed his appearance, put on different clothing, and went, he and two men with him. [298] They came to the woman by night, and he said to her, “Divine for me by means of the python-spirit, and raise up for me the one whom I shall name to you.”

The woman said to him, “You know how much Saul has done, and how he has [Col. 0508D] eradicated the magicians and diviners from the land. Why, then, are you laying a snare for my life, so that I may be killed?” Saul swore to her by the Lord, saying, “As the Lord lives, no evil shall befall you on account of this matter.” The woman said, “Whom shall I raise up for you?” He replied, “Raise up Samuel for me.”

When the woman saw Samuel, she cried out with a loud voice and said to Saul, “Why have you deceived me? You are Saul!” The king said to her, “Do not be afraid. What did you see?” The woman said to Saul, “I saw divine beings [*deos*] ascending from the earth.” He said to her, “What is his appearance?” She replied, “An old man is ascending, and he is wrapped in a cloak.”

Saul understood that it was Samuel. He bowed with his face to the ground and worshiped. Samuel said to Saul, “Why have [Col. 0509A] you disturbed me by raising me up?” Saul answered, “I am in great distress. The Philistines are fighting against me, God has departed from me, and he has refused to answer me, either through the prophets or through dreams. Therefore I summoned you, so that you might show me what I should do.”

Samuel said, “Why do you ask me, when the Lord has departed from you and has passed over to your rival? The Lord will do to you as he spoke through me: he will tear the kingdom from your hand and give it to your neighbor David, because you did not obey the voice of the Lord and did not carry out his fierce anger against Amalek. This is why the Lord has done to you today what you are suffering. The Lord will also give Israel, together with you, into the hand of the Philistines. Tomorrow you and your sons shall be with me; and the Lord will also give the camp of Israel into the hand of the Philistines.”

Immediately Saul fell [Col. 0509B] stretched out upon the ground, for he was terrified by Samuel’s words, and there was no strength in him, because he had eaten no food throughout that day. The woman came to Saul—and he was greatly shaken—and said to him, “Behold, your servant has obeyed your voice. I have placed my life in your hand and have listened to the words you spoke to me. Now, then, you also listen to the voice of your servant, and let me set before you a morsel of bread, so that you may eat, regain your strength, and be able to make the journey.”

He refused and said, “I will not eat.” But his servants and the woman compelled him, and at last, after hearing their words, he rose from the ground and sat upon the bed. The woman had a calf from the pasture in the house. She hurried and slaughtered it; then she took flour, kneaded it, baked unleavened bread, and set it before Saul and [Col. 0509C] his servants. When they had eaten, they rose and walked throughout that entire night.

**Response:** Amen.

**Hymn.** “The time of night.” Folio 257.

**Capitula.** “Deliver us, Lord.” Folio 260.

**Lauda.** “With my whole heart I cried out; hear me, Lord.”  
**Verse.** “I cried to you; save me, so that I may keep your testimonies.”

**Prayer.** We cry out to you, Lord, that you may hear us, and that you may admit our eyes, inclined from the earth, toward you, so that, with your serenity shining upon us, we may always remain in the light. Amen.

## At Terce

**Reading from the Book of Proverbs of Solomon (Chapter XIX).**

**Response:** Thanks be to God.

Son, when the poor man speaks with entreaties, the rich man [Col. 0509D] answers harshly. A sociable man will be more a friend than a brother. Better is the poor man who walks in his simplicity than the fool who twists his lips. Where there is no knowledge in the mind, there is no good; and whoever is hasty with his feet will stumble. The folly of a man overturns his steps, and in his heart he rages against God. Riches add many friends, but from the poor even those whom he had withdraw. A false witness will not go unpunished, and whoever speaks lies will not escape. Many honor the person of the powerful, and everyone is a friend to one who gives gifts. The brothers of a poor man hate him; moreover, even his friends have withdrawn far from him. Whoever pursues only words will possess nothing; but whoever possesses a sound mind loves his own life, and the guardian of prudence will find good things.

**Response:** Amen.

[Col. 0510A] **Reading from the Book of Samuel (First Book of Kings, chapter XXIX).**

**Response:** Thanks be to God.

In those days: All the armies of the Philistines were gathered at Aphek, while Israel was encamped by the spring that was in Jezreel. The satraps of the Philistines advanced in companies of hundreds and thousands; David and his men were in the rear with Achish.

The princes of the Philistines said to Achish, “What do these Hebrews want?” Achish replied to the princes of the Philistines, “Do you not know David, who was the servant of Saul, king of Israel, and who has been with me for many days and years? I have found nothing wrong in him from the day he deserted to me [299] until this day.”

But the princes of the Philistines were angry with him and said to him, “Send the man back, and let him remain in the place [Col. 0510B] where you appointed him; let him not go down with us into battle, lest he become our adversary when we begin to fight. For how else could he appease his lord except with our heads? Is this not David, of whom they sang in the dances, saying, ‘Saul struck down his thousands, and David his ten thousands’?”

So Achish summoned David and said to him, “As the Lord lives, you are upright, and you are good in my sight. Your going out and your coming in with me in the camp have been good, and I have found nothing wrong in you from the day you came to me until this day. But you do not please the satraps. Therefore return and go in peace, and do not offend the eyes of the satraps of the Philistines.”

David said to Achish, “But what [Col. 0510C] have I done? Or what have you found in your servant from the day I came before you until this day, that I should not come and fight against the enemies of my lord the king?”

Achish answered and said to David, “I know that you are good in my eyes, like an angel of the Lord. But the princes of the Philistines have said, ‘He shall not go up with us into battle.’ Therefore rise early, you and the servants of your lord who came with you; and when you rise before dawn, as soon as it becomes light, depart.”

So David rose by night, he and his men, to depart in the morning and return to the land of the Philistines; but the Philistines went up to Jezreel.

**(Chapter XXX.)** When David and his men came to Ziklag on the third day, the Amalekites made a raid from the south against Ziklag. They struck [Col. 0510D] Ziklag and burned it with fire. They took captive the women in it, from the smallest to the greatest, but they killed no one; they carried them away and went on their way.

When David and his men came to the city and found it burned with fire, and their wives, sons, and daughters taken captive, David and the people who were with him raised their voices and wept until they had no more tears. David’s two wives had also been taken captive: Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail, the wife of Nabal of Carmel.

David was greatly distressed, for the people intended to stone him, because the soul of each man was embittered over his sons and daughters. But David strengthened himself in the Lord his God. He said to Abiathar the priest, [Col. 0511A] son of Ahimelech, “Bring me the ephod.” Abiathar brought the ephod to David, and David consulted the Lord, saying, “Shall I pursue this band of raiders, and shall I overtake them, or not?”

The Lord said to him, “Pursue, for you shall surely overtake them and recover the spoil.”

So David went, he and the six hundred men who were with him, and they came as far as the torrent of Besor. Some of them, being exhausted, remained behind. David himself pursued, with four hundred men; for two hundred had remained behind, since they were too exhausted to cross the torrent of Besor.

They found an Egyptian man in the field and brought him to David. They gave him bread to eat and water to drink, as well as a piece of a cake of figs and two clusters of raisins. When he had eaten, [Col. 0511B] his spirit returned to him, and he revived; for he had eaten no bread and drunk no water for three days and three nights.

David said to him, “To whom do you belong? Where are you from, and where are you going?” He replied, “I am an Egyptian boy, the servant of an Amalekite man. My master abandoned me because I began to fall ill three days ago. We made a raid against the southern region of the Cherethites, against Judah, the south of Caleb, and Ziklag, and we burned it with fire.”

David said to him, “Can you lead me to this band?” He replied, “Swear to me by God that you will not kill me and will not hand me over to my master, and I will lead you to this band.” David swore to him.

When he had led him there, behold, they were spread out over the whole land, eating and drinking and celebrating [Col. 0511C] a day as though it were a festival, because of all the spoil and plunder they had taken from the land of the Philistines and from the land of Judah.

David struck them from evening until the evening of the next day. None of them escaped except four hundred young men who mounted camels and fled. David recovered everything that the Amalekites had taken, and he rescued his two wives. Nothing was missing, from the smallest to the greatest, whether sons or daughters, spoil or anything else that they had carried away: David brought everything back. He took all the flocks and herds and drove them before him. They said, “This is David’s spoil.”

When David came to the two hundred men who had been too exhausted to follow him, and whom he had ordered to remain by the torrent [Col. 0511D] of Besor, [300] they came out to meet David and the people who were with him. David approached the people and greeted them peacefully.

But one wicked and worthless man among those who had been with David said, “Because they did not come with us, we shall give them nothing from the spoil that we recovered. Let each man have only his wife and his children; once they have received them, let them depart.”

David said, “You shall not do this, my brothers, with what the Lord has given us. He guarded us and delivered into our hands the band that had raided us. No one shall listen to you in this matter. The share of the one who went down into battle shall be equal to the share of the one who remained with the baggage; they shall divide alike.”

And from that day forward this was established and ordained, as though it were a law in Israel, even to this day.

[Col. 0512A] **Antiphon 1.** “Let your hand be found, Lord, against all your enemies; let your right hand find all who hate you. You shall set them like a furnace of fire at the time of your appearing.”  
**Verse.** “The king shall rejoice in your strength, Lord, and shall exult exceedingly in your salvation.”

**Prayer.** May your hand, Lord, be found against all your enemies for vengeance—those who refuse to bow their necks beneath your Cross. May your right hand also be found among those who hate you, showing mercy when you have made them participants in your right hand, so that, at the time of your appearing, when your face has been revealed to us, they may not be placed like a furnace of fire, but may be transferred with us to be crowned in the heavenly kingdoms.

**Response:** Amen.

[Col. 0512B] **Antiphon 2.** “Deliver my soul, O God, from the sword, and my only one from the hand of the dog. Save me from the mouth of the lion, and my lowliness from the horns of the unicorns.”  
**Verse.** “I shall declare your name to my brothers; in the midst of the Church I shall praise you.”

**Prayer.** Deliver our soul from the sword of the most powerful enemy, Christ, Son of God, so that you may be our deliverer from the mouth of the lion, you who powerfully brought your soul out from the underworld.

**Response:** Amen.

**Antiphon 3.** “Incline your ear to me, Lord; hasten to deliver me.”  
**Verse.** “Be for me a protecting God and a fortified place, so that you may save me.”

**Response:** “They have seized me like a lion prepared for prey [Col. 0512C] and like a lion’s cub dwelling in hiding places.”  
**Petition:** “Rise up, Lord; go before them and overthrow them. Deliver my soul from them.”  
**Verse:** “Guard me, Lord, as the apple of the eye. Protect me beneath the shadow of your wings, for all my enemies have surrounded me.”  
**Petition:** “Rise up, Lord.”

**Prayers.** We pray to you, Christ, with eyes inclined toward you: spare us.  
**Petition:** And have mercy.

**Verse:** You who appeared in the form of a servant and came to save the world, restore what had perished by the power of your Cross.  
**Petition:** And have mercy.

**Verse:** You who conquer death by dying and are scourged though innocent, deliver us from the eternal pain of punishments.  
**Petition:** And have mercy.

**Verse:** You who grant the repentant Thief the rest of paradise, grant us forgiveness through the glory of your Cross.  
**Petition:** And have mercy.

**Verse:** You, Lord, receive for us the voice of this Thief [Col. 0512D]: “Remember us, Lord, and spare us when you come to judge.”  
**Petition:** And have mercy.

**Hymn.** “O Nazarene, light.” Folio 144.

**Capitula.** We ask, Lord, that by the power of your victorious authority you may always blunt the swords of those who wage war, and correct by the discipline of your truth those who plot madness against your lot. May those who proclaim blasphemies against your Christ turn their hearts to the preaching of the true faith, so that by your mercy you may break the bonds of sins by which they are held captive, and, with the pen of your finger, write in the book of life all those whom you have justified.

**Our Father.**

## At Sext

[Col. 0513A] **Reading from the Book of the Prophet Amos (Chapter IX).**

Thanks be to God.

I saw the Lord standing above the altar, and he said: “Strike the lintel, and let the thresholds be shaken; for greed is upon the heads of men, and I shall kill the last of them with the sword. There shall be no escape for them. Even if one of them flees, he shall not be saved. If they descend even to the underworld, from there my hand shall bring them out; and if they ascend to the heavens, from there I shall drag them down. If they hide themselves on the summit of Carmel, from there I shall search them out and take them away; and if they conceal themselves from my eyes in the depth of the sea, there I shall command the serpent, and it shall bite them. If they go into captivity before their enemies, there I shall command the sword, and it shall kill them. I shall set my eyes upon them for evil and not for good.

“The Lord, who touches the earth and it melts, is he whose inhabitants all shall mourn; it shall rise like a river [Col. 0513B] and flow down like the stream of Egypt. He builds his ascent in heaven and establishes his bundle [301] upon the earth; he calls the waters of the sea and pours them out upon the face of the earth—the Lord is his name.”

**Response:** Amen.

**Antiphon 1.** “May the foot of pride not come against me, Lord, and may the hand of the wicked not move me.”  
**Response:** “The unjust man said within himself that he should sin; there is no fear of God before his eyes.”

**Prayer.** May the foot of pride not come against us, nor the hand of the sinner move us, so that you, whom we reverently receive in your [Col. 0513C] Passion, may cause our soul to arrive not at punishment but at everlasting life.

**Response:** Amen.

**Antiphon 2.** “The just man shall rejoice when he sees the vengeance of the wicked; he shall wash his hands in the blood of sinners.”  
**Verse:** “If indeed you speak justice, judge rightly, sons of men.”

**Prayer.** As we hope in you, Lord, may we not be saddened, so that you neither disturb our soul nor separate us from your flock; but, hoping in you, may we confess you and sing psalms to you with a pure heart.

**Antiphon 3.** “My God, my helper; I shall hope in him. My protector, the horn of my salvation, and my redeemer.”  
**Verse:** “My deliverer from my angry enemies; from those rising up against me you will exalt [Col. 0513D] me; from the unjust man you will rescue me.”

**Response:** “Lord, judge those who harm me and fight against those who fight against me. Take up weapons and shield, and rise up, my God, to help me.”  
**Response:** “Rise up, Lord, and attend to my judgment; my God and my Lord, help me and look upon me.”  
**Petition:** In your help.

**Prayers.** May your mercy, Lord, come to our aid.  
**Petition:** Quickly.

**Verse:** May the sacrifice of your blood free us from crimes.  
**Petition:** Quickly.

**Verse:** Having endured the Cross, Lord, free us from torment.  
**Petition:** Quickly.

**Verse:** By the protection of your Cross, free us from punishment.  
**Petition:** Quickly.

**Verse:** When you come as judge of all the redeemed, be our refuge.  
**Petition:** Quickly.

**Hymn.** “O Nazarene, light.” Folio 144.

[Col. 0514A] **Prayer.** Glorious, powerful, and merciful God, rescue us from the snares of the enemy. Let the protection of your right hand be appointed for the guarding of us, lest our soul be swiftly snatched away by the attack [Col. 0514A] of the roaring lion; lest, when there is no one to redeem us, that savage one should kill us, or, when there is no one to save us, he should overthrow us. But you, Lion of the tribe of Judah, rise up in your anger, and in the severity of judgment destroy the troops of the treacherous enemy. Grant that we may believe in and remain faithful to the commandment that you have given.

**Our Father.**

## At None

**From Ecclesiasticus of Solomon (Chapter XXII).**

**Response:** Thanks be to God.

Son, weep over the dead, for his light has failed; [Col. 0514B] and weep over the fool, for his understanding has failed. Weep little over the dead, for he has found rest. For the life of the wickedest fool is worse than death. The mourning for the dead lasts seven days, but for the fool and the impious, all the days of their life. Do not speak at length with a fool, and do not go along with the senseless. Keep yourself from him, so that you do not suffer annoyance and are not stained by his sin. Turn away from him, and you will find rest, and you will not be wearied by his folly.

What can be heavier than lead? And what other name does he have but “fool”? Sand, salt, and a mass of iron are easier to carry than an imprudent, foolish, and impious man. Just as a wooden beam fastened into the foundation of a building is not loosened, so too a heart [Col. 0514C] established in the thought of counsel.

Lord, Father and God of my life, do not abandon me to the thoughts of the wicked. Do not give me haughty eyes, and take every perverse desire away from me. Lord, give a guard to my mouth and a sure seal upon my lips.

**Response:** Amen.

**Reading from the First Book of Samuel (First Book of Kings, chapter XXXI).**

**Response:** Thanks be to God.

In those days: The Philistines were fighting against Israel, and the men of Israel fled before the Philistines and fell slain on Mount Gilboa. The Philistines pressed hard upon Saul and his sons; they struck Jonathan, Abinadab, and Melchishua, Saul’s sons. The whole burden of the battle fell upon Saul, and the archers overtook him; he was severely [Col. 0514D] wounded by the archers.

Saul said to his armor-bearer, “Draw your sword and strike me, lest these uncircumcised men come and kill me, mocking me.” But his armor-bearer refused, for he was terrified by great fear. Therefore Saul seized his sword and fell upon it. When his armor-bearer saw this—that Saul was dead—he too fell upon his sword and died with him.

So Saul died, and his three sons, his armor-bearer, and all his men [302] died together on that day. When the men of Israel who were across the valley and across the Jordan saw that the Israelites had fled and that Saul and his sons were dead, they abandoned their cities and fled. The Philistines came and settled there.

On the following day [Col. 0515A] the Philistines came to strip the slain, and they found Saul and his sons lying on Mount Gilboa. They cut off Saul’s head, stripped off his armor, and sent it throughout the land of the Philistines, to be proclaimed in the temples of their idols and among the people. They placed his armor in the temple of Astarte, but they hung his body on the walls of Beth-shean.

When the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul, all the bravest men rose, marched throughout the whole night, and took the corpse of Saul and the corpses of his sons from the wall of Beth-shean. The men of Jabesh-gilead came and burned them with fire. They took their bones and buried them in the grove at Jabesh, and fasted for seven days.

**(Chapter I.)** After [Col. 0515B] Saul had died, David returned from the slaughter of the Amalekites and remained two days at Ziklag. On the third day, a man appeared, coming from Saul’s camp, with his clothing torn and dust upon his head. When he came to David, he fell upon his face and worshiped.

David said to him, “Where do you come from?” He replied, “I have fled from the camp of Israel.” David said to him, “What has happened? Tell me.” He replied, “The people fled from the battle, and many of the people fell and died; Saul and his son Jonathan also died.”

David said to the young man who reported this to him, “How do you know that Saul and his son Jonathan are dead?” The young man who told him replied, “By chance I came upon Mount Gilboa, and Saul was leaning upon his spear. The chariots and [Col. 0515C] horsemen were approaching him. He turned behind him, saw me, and called me. When I answered, ‘Here I am,’ he said to me, ‘Who are you?’ I replied, ‘I am an Amalekite.’

“He said to me, ‘Stand over me and kill me, for anguish has seized me, and my whole life is still in me.’ So I stood over him and killed him, for I knew that he could not live after his fall. I took the diadem that was upon his head and the bracelet from his arm, and I brought them here to you, my lord.”

David seized his garments and tore them, and all the men who were with him did likewise. They mourned, wept, and fasted until evening for Saul, for Jonathan his son, for the people of the Lord, and for the house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword.

David said [Col. 0515D] to the young man who had reported this to him, “Where are you from?” He answered, “I am the son of an immigrant, an Amalekite.” David said to him, “Why were you not afraid to stretch out your hand to kill the Lord’s anointed?”

Then David called one of his young men and said, “Come forward and strike him.” He struck him, and he died. David said to him, “Your blood be upon your head, for your own mouth testified against you when you said, ‘I killed the Lord’s anointed.’”

David mourned this lament over Saul and over Jonathan his son, and he commanded that they teach the sons of Judah the bow, as it is written in the Book of Jashar. He said:

“Consider, Israel, for those who have died,  
wounded upon your heights.  
Your glorious ones, Israel, have been slain upon your [Col. 0516A] mountains.  
How the mighty have fallen!

“Do not announce it in Gath,  
and do not proclaim it in the sight of Ashkelon,  
lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice,  
lest the daughters of the uncircumcised exult.

“Mountains of Gilboa,  
may neither dew nor rain come upon you,  
nor fields of firstfruits.  
For there the shield of the mighty was cast away,  
the shield of Saul, as though he had not been anointed with oil.

“From the blood of the slain,  
from the fat of the mighty,  
the arrow of Jonathan never turned back,  
and the sword of Saul did not return empty.

“Saul and Jonathan, beloved and beautiful in life,  
were not divided in death.  
They were swifter than eagles,  
stronger than lions.

“Daughters of Israel, weep over Saul,  
who clothed you in scarlet amid delights,  
who supplied golden ornaments for our adornment.

“How the mighty have fallen in [Col. 0516B] battle!  
Jonathan, you have been slain upon your heights.

“I grieve for you, my brother Jonathan,  
exceedingly beautiful and beloved,  
more beloved than the love of women.  
As a mother loves her only son,  
so I loved you.

“How the strong have fallen,  
and the weapons of war have perished!”

**(Chapter II.)** After this David consulted the Lord, saying, “Shall I go up to one of the cities of Judah?” The Lord said to him, “Go up.” David said, “Where shall I go up?” He answered him, “To Hebron.”

So David went up, together with his two wives, Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail, the wife of Nabal of Carmel. He also brought up [303] the men who were with him, each with his household. They remained in the towns of Hebron.

The men of Judah came and anointed David there to reign over the house of Judah. It was reported to David that the men of Jabesh-gilead had buried Saul. Therefore David sent messengers to the men of Jabesh-gilead and said to them:

“Blessed are you by the Lord, because you showed this mercy to your lord Saul and buried him. And now may the Lord repay you with mercy and truth; and I also shall repay you with kindness, because you have done this deed. Let your hands be strengthened, and be sons of valor. Although your lord Saul is dead, the house [Col. 0516C] of Judah has nevertheless anointed me as its king.”

**Response:** Amen.

**Antiphon 1.** “Say to my soul, Lord: I am your salvation. Let all who seek my soul to take it be confounded and put to shame.”  
**Verse:** “Judge, Lord, those who harm me, and fight against those who fight against me.”

**Prayer.** Say to our soul, Lord: “I am your salvation.” May your enemies also, who have gathered against you, be ashamed; and may those who plot against your faith be corrected through repentance. You who, though innocent, endured the mockery and wounds of your enemies, cleanse our sins in these things, having been reconciled to us.

**Response:** Amen.

[Col. 0516D] **Antiphon 2.** “Look upon my defense. Deliver my soul, O God, from the sword, and my only one from the hand of the dog. Save me, Lord, from the mouth of the lion.”  
**Verse:** “I shall declare your name to my brothers; in the midst of the Church I shall praise you.”

**Prayer.** Attend, Lord, to the defense of your household, and now deliver its soul from the sword of the persecutor and from the hand of the dog—you who alone deigned to lay down your soul for all of us.

[Col. 0517A] **Antiphon 3.** “You have made me a reproach to fools. I was silent and did not open my mouth, because you did it; remove your scourges from me.”  
**Verse:** [Col. 0517B] “I said, ‘I shall guard my ways, and I shall not sin with my tongue.’ I set a guard upon my mouth while the sinner stood against me.”

**Hymn.** “O Nazarene.” Folio 144.

**Prayer.** Christ, Son of God, who became a reproach to fools, remove your scourges from us and offer medicine for our sicknesses, so that, regarded by you, we may not be carried away into condemnation by precipitate anger, but may be made gentle in all things by the example of your Passion.

**Our Father.**
