All the men of Israel therefore came running to the king and said to him, “Why have our brothers, the men of Judah, stolen you away and brought the king and his household across the Jordan, and all David’s men with him?” Every man of Judah answered the men of Israel, “Because the king is closer to me. Why are you angry about this? Have we eaten anything belonging to the king, or have gifts been given to us?” The men of Israel answered the men of Judah and said, “I am ten times greater with the king, and David belongs more to me than to you. Why have you insulted me, and why was I not told first, so that I might bring back my king?” But the men of Judah answered the men of Israel more harshly.

(Chapter XX.) It happened that there was there a man of Belial named Sheba, son of Bichri, a man of Jemini. He sounded the trumpet and said, “We have no share in David, nor inheritance in the son of Jesse. Every man to his tents, O Israel.” So all Israel separated from David and followed Sheba son of Bichri. But the men of Judah remained attached to their king, from the Jordan to Jerusalem.

When the king came to his house in Jerusalem, he took the ten concubines whom he had left to guard the house and placed them in custody, providing them with food. He did not go in to them; they remained confined until the day of their death, living in widowhood.

The king said to Amasa, “Summon all the men of Judah to me by the third day, and be present yourself.” Amasa went to summon Judah, but he delayed beyond the time appointed for him by the king. David said to Abishai, “Now Sheba son of Bichri will afflict us more than Absalom did. Take the servants of your lord and pursue him, lest he find fortified cities and escape us.” [Col. 0550C]

So Joab’s men went out with him, as did the Cherethites and Pelethites; and all the strong men went out from Jerusalem to pursue Sheba son of Bichri. When they were near the great stone that is in Gibeon, Amasa came and met them. Joab was wearing a close-fitting tunic suited to his stature, and over it he was girded with a sword hanging down to his thighs in its sheath, which could be drawn and strike with a slight movement.

Joab said to Amasa, “Greetings, my brother.” And he took Amasa by the chin with his right hand, as though to kiss him. Amasa did not notice the sword that Joab had, and Joab struck him in the side and spilled his entrails onto the ground, and he died; nor did he inflict a second wound.

Joab and his brother Abishai pursued Sheba son of Bichri. Meanwhile some men from Joab’s companions, standing beside Amasa’s corpse, said, “Look, the one who wished to be David’s companion for Joab.” Amasa, covered with blood, lay in the middle of the road. A man saw that all the people were stopping to look at him, so he moved Amasa from the road into a field and covered him with a garment, lest passersby stop because of him. Once he had been removed from the road, every man passed on after Joab to pursue Sheba son of Bichri.

Sheba had passed through all the tribes of Israel as far as Abel and Beth-maacah, and all the chosen men had gathered to him. They came and attacked him at Abel and Beth-maacah; they surrounded the city with siegeworks, and the city was besieged. All the crowd that was with Joab labored to destroy the walls.

A wise woman cried out from the city, “Listen, listen! Tell Joab, ‘Come here, and I will speak with you.’” When he had approached her, she said to him, “Are you Joab?” He answered, “I am.” She said to him, “Hear the words of your handmaid.” He replied, “I hear.” Again she said, “A saying was commonly spoken in the old proverb: ‘Let them ask in Abel,’ and so they would finish. Am I not the one who answers truthfully in Israel? Yet you seek to overthrow the city and destroy a mother in Israel. Why do you throw down the inheritance of the Lord?”

Joab answered, “Far be it, far be it from me! I do not throw down or destroy it. The matter is not so. A man from the hill country of Ephraim, Sheba son of Bichri by name, has raised his hand against King David. Give up only him, and we will withdraw from the city.” The woman said to Joab, “Behold, his head will be thrown to you over the wall.”

Then she went to all the people and spoke wisely to them. They cut off the head of Sheba son of Bichri and threw it to Joab. He sounded the trumpet, and they withdrew from the city, each to his tent; Joab returned to Jerusalem to the king.

Joab was over all the army of Israel; Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and Pelethites; Adoram was over the tribute; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was the recorder; Siva was the scribe; Zadok and Abiathar were priests. Hiram the Hiraite was David’s priest.

(Chapter XXI.) There was again a famine in the days of David for three continuous years, and David consulted the oracle of the Lord. The Lord said, “It is because of Saul and his bloodstained house, because he killed the Gibeonites.”

When the Gibeonites had been summoned, the king said to them—for the Gibeonites were not among the children of Israel, but remnants of the Amorites; the children of Israel had sworn an oath to them, and Saul had sought to strike them in his zeal, as though on behalf of the children of Israel and Judah—David said to the Gibeonites, “What shall I do for you, and what shall be the expiation by which you may bless the inheritance of the Lord?”

The Gibeonites said to him, “We have no dispute concerning silver or gold, but against Saul and his house; nor do we wish that any man of Israel be killed.” The king said to them, “What then do you want me to do for you?” They said to the king, “We must destroy the man who crushed and unjustly oppressed us, so that not one of his descendants may remain within all the borders of Israel. Let seven men of his sons be given to us, that we may crucify them to the Lord at Gibeah of Saul, once the Lord’s chosen one.” The king said, “I will give them.”

The king spared Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, because of the oath that had been between David and Jonathan, the son of Saul. The king took the two sons of Rizpah, daughter of Aiah, whom she had borne to Saul—Armoni and Mephibosheth—and the five sons of Michal, daughter of Saul, whom she had borne to Hadriel son of Barzillai, who was from Meholah; and he gave them into the hands of the Gibeonites. They crucified them before the Lord on the mountain, and these seven fell together, killed during the days of the first harvest, at the beginning of the barley harvest. [Col. 0552A]

Rizpah, daughter of Aiah, took sackcloth and spread it beneath them upon the rock, from the beginning of the harvest until water dripped upon them from heaven. She did not allow the birds to tear them by day or the beasts by night. It was reported to David what Rizpah, daughter of Aiah, Saul’s concubine, had done.

David went and took the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son from the men of Jabesh-gilead, who had stolen them from the street of Beth-shan, where the Philistines had hung them after killing Saul at Gilboa. He brought away from there the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son. They gathered the bones of those who had been impaled and buried them with the bones of Saul and Jonathan his son in the land of Benjamin, beside the tomb of Kish his father. They did everything the king had commanded, and afterward God was reconciled to the land. [Col. 0552B]

There was again a battle between the Philistines and Israel. David and his servants went down and fought against the Philistines. David grew weary, and Ishbi-benob, who was of the race of Rapha, whose iron spearhead weighed three hundred ounces and who was girded with a new sword, attempted to strike David. Abishai son of Zeruiah came to his aid, struck the Philistine, and killed him.

Then David’s men swore, saying, “You shall no longer go out with us to war, lest you extinguish the lamp of Israel.” There was also a second battle at Gob against the Philistines; then Sibbecai of Hushah struck Saph, who was of the race of Rapha, of the family of giants. There was also a third battle at Gob against the Philistines, in which Adeodatus son of the Forest, a Bethlehemite weaver [or: embroiderer], struck Goliath of Gath, whose spear shaft was like a weaver’s beam. There was a fourth battle at Gath, in which there was a tall man who had six fingers on his hands and six toes on his feet—that is, twenty-four—and he was of the lineage of Rapha. He blasphemed Israel, but Jonathan son of Shimeah, David’s brother, struck him. These four were born to Rapha in Gath, and they fell by the hand of David and his servants. R. Amen.

Hymn. “The Time of Night.” fol. 257.

Capitulum. “In the day of tribulation.” fol. 284.

Praise. I have practiced judgment and justice, O Lord; do not hand me over to those who harm me. V. Receive your servant for good, so that the proud may not slander me.

Prayer. Teach us to practice judgment and justice, O Lord, so that we may be able to trample upon the slanders of the proud. Receive your servants for good, who hope in your salvation; and make those whose inward eyes await the kingdom of Christ share in the fellowship of the Elect. [Col. 0552D] R. Amen.

At Terce.

Ecclesiasticus of Solomon (Chapter XI).

R. Thanks be to God.

Son, they marveled at the works of the Most High alone—his glorious, hidden, and unseen works. Many tyrants sat upon a throne, and men unsuspected [or: unexpected] will bear the diadem. Many who were greater withdrew far away, and the glorious were handed over into another’s power. (Chapter XXIV.)

Moses commanded the Law in ordinances of righteousness, and an inheritance to the house of Jacob, and promises to Israel. He appointed David his servant to raise up from his own line a most powerful king, sitting upon a throne of honor (Chapter XXXIX). He will investigate the hidden matters of proverbs and occupy himself with concealed parables. He will sit among the great and judge in the sight of all. He will pass into the land of foreign nations, for he will test what is good and evil among men. He will give his heart to keeping watch at dawn for the Lord who made him, and in the sight of the Most High he will entreat. And the Lord will fill him with the spirit of understanding; and he himself will pour forth sayings of wisdom like showers, and in prayer he will confess to the Lord. And he himself directs his counsel and discipline, and in his hidden matters he will deliberate. He will make the discipline of his teaching public, and he will glory in the Law of the Lord’s covenant.  
**R.** Amen.

## Beginning of the Book of Kings (III Kings, Chapter I)

In those days, King David had grown old and had lived through many days. When he was covered with clothing, he was not warmed. Therefore his servants said to him: “Let us seek for our lord the king a young virgin, and let her stand before the king, warm him, sleep in his bosom, and warm our lord the king.” So they sought a beautiful young woman throughout all the borders of Israel. They found Abishag the Shunammite and brought her to the king. The girl was exceedingly beautiful; she slept with the king and ministered to him, but the king did not know her.

Now Adonijah, the son of Haggith, exalted himself, saying: “I shall reign.” He made for himself chariots and horsemen, and fifty men to run before him. His father had never rebuked him, saying, “Why have you done this?” 327 He was also very handsome, and was second in birth after Absalom. His dealings were with Joab the son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest, who supported Adonijah’s cause. But Zadok the priest, Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, the Cherethites and the Pelethites, and all the strength of David’s army were not with Adonijah.

When Adonijah had sacrificed rams, calves, and all the fatlings beside the stone of Zoheleth, which was near the spring of Rogel, he summoned all his brothers, the king’s sons, and all the men of Judah, the king’s servants. But he did not summon Nathan the prophet, Benaiah, the mighty men, or his brother Solomon.

Then Nathan said to Bathsheba, Solomon’s mother: “Have you not heard that Adonijah, the son of Haggith, has become king, and that our lord David knows nothing of it? Now therefore come, accept my counsel, and save your life and the life of your son Solomon. Go and enter King David’s presence, and say to him: ‘Did you not, my lord the king, swear to your servant, saying: “Your son Solomon shall reign after me, and he himself shall sit upon my throne”? Why then does Adonijah reign?’ And while you are still speaking there with the king, I shall come after you and confirm your words.”

So Bathsheba entered the king’s chamber. The king had grown very old, and Abishag the Shunammite ministered to him. Bathsheba bowed and worshiped the king. The king said to her: “What do you want?” She answered: “My lord the king, you swore by the Lord your God to your servant: ‘Your son Solomon shall reign after me, and he himself shall sit upon my throne.’ And now Adonijah reigns, while you, my lord the king, know nothing of it. He has slaughtered oxen and all kinds of fatlings and many rams, and he has summoned all the king’s sons, Abiathar the priest, and Joab the commander of the army; but he has not summoned Solomon your servant. Nevertheless, my lord the king, the eyes of all Israel look to you, so that you may declare to them who ought to sit upon your throne, my lord the king, after you. And when my lord the king sleeps with his fathers, I and my son will be counted as sinners.”

While she was still speaking with the king, Nathan the prophet came. They announced to the king: “Nathan the prophet is here.” When he had entered the king’s presence and bowed before him with his face to the ground, Nathan said: “My lord the king, did you say, ‘Let Adonijah reign after me, and let him sit upon my throne’? For he went down today and sacrificed oxen, fatlings, and many rams, and summoned all the king’s sons and the commanders, as well as Abiathar the priest. While they eat and drink before him and say, ‘Long live King Adonijah,’ he has not summoned me your servant, Zadok the priest, Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, or your servant Solomon. Has this word gone forth from my lord the king, without your informing me your servant who should sit upon the throne of my lord the king after him?”

King David answered: “Call Bathsheba to me.” She entered before the king and stood before him. The king swore and said: “As the Lord lives, who has rescued my life from every distress, just as I swore to you by the Lord God of Israel, saying, ‘Your son Solomon shall reign after me, and he himself shall sit upon my throne in my place,’ so I shall do today.”

Bathsheba bowed with her face to the ground and worshiped the king, saying: “May my lord King David live forever.” King David also said: “Call Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada to me.” When they had entered before the king, he said to them: “Take with you the servants of your lord, set my son Solomon upon my mule, and lead him down to Gihon. There Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet shall anoint him king over Israel. Blow the trumpet and say: ‘Long live King Solomon!’ Then go up after him, and come to Jerusalem. He shall sit upon my throne, and he shall reign in my place. I shall command him to be leader over Israel and over Judah.”

Benaiah the son of Jehoiada answered the king: “Amen. Thus may the Lord God of my lord the king speak. As the Lord was with my lord the king, so may he be with Solomon, and may he make his throne greater than the throne of my lord King David.”

So Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, the Cherethites, and the Pelethites went down. They set Solomon upon King David’s mule and brought him to Gihon. Zadok the priest took the horn of oil from the tabernacle and anointed Solomon. They blew the trumpet, and all the people said: “Long live King Solomon!” All the multitude went up after him, together with the people playing pipes and rejoicing with great joy, and the earth resounded with their shouting.

Adonijah and all those who had been invited by him heard it, although the banquet had already ended. But Joab, hearing the sound of the trumpet, said: “What does this shouting from the tumultuous city mean?” While he was still speaking, Jonathan the son of Abiathar the priest arrived. Adonijah said to him: “Enter, for you are a brave man and bring good news.”

Jonathan answered Adonijah: “Not at all. Our lord King David has made Solomon king. He sent with him Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites and Pelethites, and they set him upon the king’s mule. Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anointed him king at Gihon. They went up from there rejoicing, and the city resounded. This is the voice that you heard. Moreover, Solomon sits upon the throne of the kingdom.”

The king’s servants entered and blessed our lord King David, saying: “May God make Solomon’s name greater than your name, and magnify his throne above yours.” The king worshiped upon his bed and also said: “Blessed is the Lord, the God of Israel, who has today granted that one should sit upon my throne while my eyes behold it.”  
**R.** Amen.

## Antiphon 1

Pour out, O Lord, your wrath upon my enemies, and let the indignation of your anger seize them. Let their dwelling become desolate, and let them not enter into your righteousness.  
**V.** Let them be blotted from the book of the living, and let them not be written among the righteous.

**Prayer.** Pour out, O Lord, your wrath upon my enemies, so that, when their dwelling has at last remained desolate, they may eventually recognize the place of their fury and injustice, and that a way may be opened in the Church for their conversion to you, since they have lost the supports of the earthly city of Jerusalem.  
**R.** Amen.

## Antiphon 2

When all gathered together against me to take my life, they plotted. But I hoped in you, O Lord.  
**V.** Shine your face upon your servant, and save me in your mercy.

**Prayer.** O Lord, you shone forth with ineffable patience when the whole crowd of unbelievers gathered together against you to take your life and endeavored by their schemes to seize you in your words, since they did not know that you were the Word of God. Therefore, because you conquered so mightily in your own things, deign to glorify yourself in our confessions.  
**R.** Amen.

## Antiphon 3

Repay, O Lord, on my behalf; O Lord, your mercy is forever. Do not despise the works of your hands.  
**V.** Let all the kings of the earth confess to you, for they have heard all the words of your mouth.

**R.** Behold, I have no help, and my beloved have withdrawn from me; a lying accuser has been raised up against me.  
**P.** Contradicting me, he gnashed his teeth at me.  
**V.** My inheritance has become for me like a lion in the forest; the adversary raised his voice against me.  
**P.** Contradicting me.

## Prayers

Have mercy and spare your people, most merciful Lord.  
**P.** For we have sinned against you.

**V.** Look upon us, wretched and fettered by the bonds of our sufferings, from the throne of the Cross; release us, Redeemer, from our punishments.  
**P.** For we have sinned against you.

**V.** Having suffered scourging and the outrage of the Cross, enduring the insults of your persecutors, grant repentance for our offenses.  
**P.** For we have sinned against you.

**V.** You, the just judge who were unjustly judged and innocently accepted the punishments of the Cross, save us from our punishments by redeeming us.  
**P.** For we have sinned against you.

**V.** May your voice plead with the Father for us—the voice that once was silent before the judge—so that, with you reigning, we may enjoy the Lord.  
**P.** For we have sinned against you.

**Hymn.** O Nazarene. Folio 144.

**Capitula.** Rise up, O God, and judge the earth, so that you, who rule over all nations, may now be believed to have risen by those by whom you were crucified; so that the two peoples may agree with one another in love, while you bind circumcision and uncircumcision together by the bond of Christian faith.

**Our Father.**

## At Sext

### Reading from the Book of the Prophet Jeremiah (Chapter III)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying:

“Have you seen what faithless Israel has done? She went up for herself upon every high mountain and beneath every leafy tree, and there she prostituted herself. And I said, after she had done all these things: ‘Return to me’; but she did not return. And her treacherous sister Judah saw that, because faithless Israel had committed adultery, I had dismissed her and given her a bill of divorce; yet treacherous Judah, her sister, did not fear, but went away and prostituted herself also. By the ease of her prostitution she polluted the land and committed adultery with stone and wood. And amid all these things her treacherous sister Judah did not return to me with all her heart, but in deceit, says the Lord.

“And the Lord said to me: ‘Faithless Israel has justified her soul in comparison with treacherous Judah. Go and proclaim these words toward the north, and say: “Return, faithless Israel,” says the Lord, “and I will not turn my face away from you, for I am holy,” says the Lord, “and I will not be angry forever. Nevertheless, know your iniquity, for you have transgressed against the Lord your God. You have scattered your ways among strangers beneath every leafy tree, and you have not listened to my voice,” says the Lord. “Return, returning children,” says the Lord.’”  
**R.** Amen.

## Antiphon 1

To the Lord, when I was in distress, I cried, and he heard me. O Lord, deliver my soul from lying lips and from a deceitful tongue.

**Prayer.** To you, Lord, we cry when we are in distress, so that you may deliver us from lying lips and guard us from a deceitful tongue. Do not humble us through those who flatter iniquity, nor bend our assent toward those who persuade us to withdraw from the truth.  
**R.** Amen.

## Antiphon 2

Judge my cause, O Lord, against an unholy nation; deliver me from a wicked and deceitful man.  
**V.** Why are you sad, my soul, and why do you trouble me? Hope in God, for I shall yet confess him: the salvation of my face and my God.

**Prayer.** Only-begotten Son of God the Father, who by your Passion distinguish the cause of your people from the flock of the insatiable enemy, distinguish our cause from an unholy nation through the power of your Passion, so that you alone may be recognized as defender in the cause of your Church—you who willed to become the price of our redemption.  
**R.** Amen.

## Antiphon 3

In God I shall praise the word; in the Lord I shall praise the saying. In the Lord I shall hope; I shall not fear what man can do to me.  
**V.** The Lord is my helper, and I shall look down upon my enemies.

**R.** My enemies surrounded me like bees around wax, and they burned against me like fire in thorns.  
**P.** I was driven like a heap of sand so that I might fall, but the Lord received me.  
**V.** Like a wall broken through and a gate opened, they rushed upon me, and they rolled themselves upon my miseries.  
**P.** Like a heap.

## Prayers

Hear, O Lord, our prayers.  
**P.** And have mercy on us.

**V.** Crucified and condemned to death,  
**P.** And have mercy on us.

**V.** You who, dying, redeemed the world,  
**P.** And have mercy on us.

**V.** So that, saved through the Cross, we may be able to pass through,  
**P.** And have mercy on us.

**V.** May your death confer eternal life upon us.  
**P.** And have mercy.

**Hymn.** O Nazarene. Folio 144.

**Prayer.** Look upon your people, O Lord, and exalt yourself magnificently over those who hate you. Turn those who hasten to turn aside against your faithful into precipitous ruin, so that, confounded and troubled, they may recognize you alone, the Most High Lord throughout all the earth.

**Our Father.**

## At Vespers

**Lauda.** The sun knew its setting. He made darkness, and night came.

**Antiphon.** Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man; free me from the unjust man. Psalm 139.

**Lauda.** They saw me and shook their heads. Help me, O Lord my God.  
**V.** O Lord, God of my salvation, by day I cried out, and by night before you.

**Hymn.** The Word of the Father. Folio 252.

**Capitula.** Our iniquities are many, O Lord; but you, Lord, who are the most just repayer, mercifully blot out our offenses. See the tears of those who wail. Come to the captives as an excellent restorer. And let those who in these days ask you for pardon from their transgressions not find you a most severe judge, but rejoice that they have found a gentle father and lord.

**Our Father.**

**Blessing.** May God, with whom abundant mercy dwells, make us for himself vessels most clean through groaning.  
**R.** Amen.

And may he who is the unfailing nature of divinity refresh our weakness with spiritual delights.  
**R.** Amen.

May our hearts always hunger and thirst for him, to whom the vows of our abstinence cry out.  
**R.** Amen.

**Lauda.** I have done judgment and righteousness. Folio 296.

# Saturday

## At Matins

**Antiphon.** But you, O Lord. Psalm 3.  
**Prayer.** Although. Folio 141.

## Antiphon 1

My soul has wandered very far. With those who hated peace I was peaceful; while I spoke to them, they attacked me without cause.  
**V.** To the Lord, when I was in distress, I cried, and he heard me.

**Prayer.** O Christ, true light of righteousness, strip away the darkness of our sins from our soul, which has wandered very far in the tents of Kedar, and pour over it the light of your holy brightness, so that in this world we may be peaceful with those who hate peace and in the age to come may deserve to be blessed with the children of Jerusalem, in holy concord joined together.  
**R.** Amen.

## Antiphon 2

Judge me, O God, and distinguish my cause from an unholy nation; deliver me from a wicked and deceitful man.  
**V.** For you are my God and my strength. Why have you rejected me, and why do I go about sadly while the enemy afflicts me?

**Prayer.** Christ, Son of God, distinguish our cause from an unholy nation through your Passion, so that you alone may be our defender in our cause—you who for us endured burial.  
**R.** Amen.

## Antiphon 3

You are my helper and my protector, O God; do not depart from me. Attend to my help, O Lord; hasten to help me.  
**V.** Let my enemies who seek my life be confounded and put to shame.

**Prayer.** O Lord, our helper and protector, attend to our help, so that as we ardently desire your sufferings with most sincere vows, we may feel you as our helper in our very efforts.  
**R.** Amen.

**R.** For your sake, O God of Israel, I endured reproach; I covered my face with reverence. I became a stranger to my brothers and a guest to the sons of my mother.  
**P.** For zeal for your house consumed me.  
**V.** In the multitude of your mercy, hear me, in the truth of your salvation.  
**P.** For zeal.

**Prayer.** Christ, Son of God, whom zeal for the house of God—that is, for the Church of your Father—consumed, when you boldly drove out those doing evil with a cord, release us from every cord of iniquities, and grant that we may dwell worthily in the midst of your house, so that, having ourselves become a spiritual house for you, we may deserve to be crowned by you from heaven.  
**R.** Amen.

## At Lauds

**Antiphon.** Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within my inward parts. Psalm 50.

**Prayer.** Of our heart. Folio 210.

**Canticle.** Heal me, O Lord. Folio 259.

**Matutinarium.** Make me hear your mercy in the morning, for I have hoped in you, O Lord.  
**V.** Show me the way in which I should walk, for to you, O Lord, I have lifted up my soul.

**Lauda.** In his saints.

## Reading from the Book of Kings (III Kings, Chapter II)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

In those days, Solomon sat upon the throne of David his father, and his kingdom was firmly established. Adonijah, the son of Haggith, entered Bathsheba, Solomon’s mother. She said to him: “Is your entrance peaceful?” He answered: “Peaceful.” And he added: “I have a word for you.” She said to him: “Speak.” He said: “You know that the kingdom was mine, and all Israel had set me forward as king; but the kingdom was transferred and became my brother’s, for it was appointed to him by the Lord. Now therefore I ask one request of you; do not put me to shame.” She said to him: “Speak.” He said: “I beg you to say to King Solomon—for he will not refuse you anything—that he give me Abishag the Shunammite as wife.”

Bathsheba said: “Good; I shall speak to the king on your behalf.” Bathsheba therefore came to King Solomon to speak to him on behalf of Adonijah. The king rose to meet her, bowed to her, and sat upon his throne. A throne was placed for the king’s mother, and she sat at his right hand. She said to him: “I ask one small request of you; do not put me to shame.” The king said to her: “Ask, my mother, for it is not right that I turn my face away from you.” She said: “Let Abishag the Shunammite be given as wife to your brother Adonijah.”

King Solomon answered and said to his mother: “Why do you ask for Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? Ask for the kingdom for him also, for he is my elder brother, and he has Abiathar the priest and Joab the son of Zeruiah.”

Then King Solomon swore by the Lord, saying: “May God do these things to me and add these things, because Adonijah has spoken this word against his own life. And now, as the Lord lives, who established me and placed me upon the throne of David my father, and who made me a house as he spoke, Adonijah shall be put to death today.”

The king sent Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, who struck him, and he died. The king also said to Abiathar the priest: “Go to Anathoth, to your field, for indeed you are a man deserving of death; but today I shall not put you to death, because you carried the ark of the Lord God before David my father and endured toil in everything in which my father labored.”

So Solomon expelled Abiathar, so that he would not be priest of the Lord, in order to fulfill the word of the Lord that he had spoken concerning the house of Eli at Shiloh. A messenger came to Solomon saying that Joab had turned after Adonijah but had not turned after Solomon. Therefore Joab fled to the tabernacle of the Lord and seized the horns of the altar.

It was reported to King Solomon that Joab had fled to the tabernacle of the Lord and was beside the altar. Solomon sent Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, saying: “Go and kill him.” Benaiah came to the tabernacle of the Lord and said to him: “The king says: Come out.” He answered: “I shall not come out; here I shall die.”

Benaiah reported the words to the king, saying: “Thus spoke Joab, and thus he spoke to me.” The king said to him: “Do as he has spoken, kill him, bury him, and remove from me and from my father’s house the innocent blood that Joab shed. The Lord will return his blood upon his head, because he killed two righteous men better than himself with the sword, without my father David’s knowledge: Abner the son of Ner, commander of Israel’s army, and Amasa the son of Jether, commander of the army of Judah. Their blood will return upon the head of Joab and upon the head of his offspring forever. But may there be peace for David and for his offspring, his house, and his throne forever from the Lord.”

Benaiah the son of Jehoiada went up, attacked him, and killed him; and he was buried in his own house in the wilderness. The king appointed Benaiah the son of Jehoiada in his place over the army, and he appointed Zadok priest in place of Abiathar.

The king sent for Shimei and summoned him. He said to him: “Build yourself a house in Jerusalem and live there, and do not go out from there here or there. On whatever day you go out and cross the torrent of Kidron, know that you shall certainly be put to death; your blood shall be upon your own head.”

Shimei said to the king: “The word is good. As my lord the king has spoken, so your servant shall do.” So Shimei lived in Jerusalem for many days.

But after three years it happened that Shimei’s servants fled to Achish the son of Maacah, king of Gath. It was reported to Shimei that his servants had gone to Gath. Shimei arose, saddled his donkey, went to Achish at Gath to seek his servants, and brought them back from Gath.

It was reported to King Solomon that Shimei had gone from Jerusalem to Gath and had returned. He sent for him and said to him: “Did I not testify to you by the Lord and warn you: ‘On whatever day you go out here or there, know that you shall die’? And you answered me: ‘The word I have heard is good.’ Why then did you not keep the oath of the Lord and the commandment that I commanded you?”

The king said to Shimei: “You know all the evil of which your heart is conscious, which you did to David my father. The Lord has returned your wickedness upon your head. And King Solomon is blessed, and the throne of David shall be established before the Lord forever.”

Then the king commanded Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, who attacked him, struck him, and he died.

(III Kings, Chapter III.) Thus the kingdom was confirmed in the hand of Solomon. He became related by marriage to Pharaoh, king of Egypt, for he took his daughter and brought her into the city of David until he had finished building his own house, the house of the Lord, and the wall around Jerusalem. Nevertheless, the people sacrificed upon the high places, for the temple had not yet been built for the name of the Lord until that day. Solomon loved the Lord, walking in the commandments of David his father.  
**R.** Amen.

**Hymn.** The time of night. Folio 257.

**Capitula.** Let the nations know, O Christ, that your name is Lord—you who were hung upon the gibbet of the Cross for them. Let knowledge restore to the Creator those whom the sluggishness of ignorance had given over, so that they may be converted through steadfastness of faith and rejoice in glory.

**Our Father.**

**Lauda.** I have done judgment and righteousness. Folio 296.

## At Terce

### Ecclesiasticus of Solomon (Chapter I)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

Son, the fear of the Lord is glory, boasting, joy, and a crown of exultation. The fear of the Lord will delight the heart and give joy and gladness for length of days. It will be well with the one who fears the Lord at the end, and on the day of his death he will be blessed. The love of God is honorable wisdom. Those to whom she appears in vision love her in beholding her and in recognizing her great works. The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord; she was created together with the faithful in the womb and walks with chosen women. Desire wisdom, and God will provide her to you, for wisdom and discipline are the fear of the Lord; and what is pleasing to him—faith and gentleness—will fill his treasures.

Listen, son, and receive words of understanding, and do not reject my counsel. Put your foot in her fetters and your neck in her collar. Whoever hears her judges peoples, and whoever gazes upon her will remain secure.  
**R.** Amen.

### Reading from the Book of Kings (III Kings, Chapter III)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

In those days, the Lord appeared to Solomon in a dream by night, saying: “Ask what you wish me to give you.”

Solomon said: “You showed great mercy to your servant David my father, just as he walked before you in truth, righteousness, and an upright heart with you. You preserved for him your great mercy and gave him a son sitting upon the throne, as it is today. And now, Lord God, you have made your servant king in place of David my father, but I am a little child, not knowing my going out or my coming in. Your servant is in the midst of the people whom you have chosen, an innumerable people, who cannot be counted or numbered because of their multitude. Therefore give your servant an understanding heart, so that he may judge your people and discern between good and evil. For who can judge this great people of yours?”

The word pleased the Lord, because Solomon had asked for such a thing. And the Lord said to Solomon: “Because you asked for this word and did not ask for yourself long life, nor riches, nor the lives of your enemies, but asked for yourself wisdom to discern judgment, behold, I have done according to your words and have given you a wise and understanding heart, so that no one like you has existed before you, nor shall arise after you. Moreover, if you walk in my ways and keep my precepts and commandments, as your father walked, I shall lengthen your days.”

Then Solomon awoke, and he understood that it had been a dream. When he came to Jerusalem, he stood before the ark of the covenant of the Lord, offered holocausts, made peace offerings, and held a great feast for all his servants.

Then two prostitute women came to the king and stood before him. One of them said: “I beg you, my lord: I and this woman lived in one house, and I gave birth beside her in the room. On the third day after I gave birth, she also gave birth, and we were together; no one else was in the house except the two of us. This woman’s son died during the night, for while she slept she had lain upon him. Rising in the silence of the dead of night, she took my son from beside me, your maidservant, while I slept, and placed him in her bosom. But her son, who was dead, she placed in my bosom. When I rose in the morning to nurse my son, he appeared to be dead. Examining him more carefully in the clear light, I discovered that he was not my son whom I had borne.”

The other woman answered: “It is not as you say; your son is dead, but mine is alive.” The first replied: “You are lying; my son is alive, and your son is dead.” And in this way they argued before the king.

Then the king said: “This woman says, ‘My son is alive, and your son is dead’; and that one replies, ‘No, your son is dead, but mine is alive.’” The king therefore said: “Bring me a sword.” When they had brought a sword before the king, he said: “Divide the living child into two parts, and give half to one and half to the other.”

But the woman whose son was alive said to the king—for her inward parts were moved with compassion for her son: “I beg you, my lord, give the living child to her, and do not kill him.” The other replied: “Let it be neither mine nor yours, but let it be divided.”

The king answered and said: “Give the living child to this woman, and do not kill him; she is his mother.”

All Israel heard of the judgment that the king had rendered, and they feared the king, seeing that the wisdom of God was in him to administer justice.  
**R.** Amen.

## Antiphon 1

My God, do not draw far away from me; my God, attend to my help.  
**V.** In you I have hoped, O Lord; I shall not be confounded forever.

**Prayer.** Our God, you who became far from your persecutors, do not draw far away, so that you alone may look upon us for help—you who triumph over the powers of this world upon your Cross.  
**R.** Amen.

They sharpened their tongues like serpents; the poison of asps is beneath their lips.  
**V.** They devised evils in their heart; all day long they prepared battles.

**Prayer.** Deliver, O Lord, the flock of your people from the snares of the wicked man, so that, strengthened by the protection of your Passion, Christian simplicity may neither encounter an enemy in man nor fear the darts of a deceitful tongue in matters of faith.  
**R.** Amen.

Deliver me, O Lord, from the lion’s mouth and from the horns of unicorns my humility.  
**V.** I shall proclaim your name to my brothers; in the midst of the church I shall praise you.

**P.** And there is no one to comfort me except you, O God.  
**V.** My enemies surrounded me like bees around wax, and they burned like fire in thorns.  
**P.** And there is no one.

## Prayers

True Son of God, Christ,  
**P.** Hear us; have mercy on the supplicating people.

**V.** You alone saved the world through the triumph of your Cross; free us from the punishment of your blood.  
**P.** And hear us.

**V.** You who, dying, condemn death and, rising, grant life, enduring for us an undeserved punishment,  
**P.** And hear us.

**V.** May we celebrate the days of your Passion unharmed, so that through this your sweetness may cherish us.  
**P.** And hear us.

## At Sext

### Reading from the Prophet Ezekiel (Chapter XXXVI)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

Thus says the Lord:

“I shall take you from among the nations, gather you from all the lands, and bring you into your own land. I shall pour clean water over you, and you shall be cleansed from all your iniquities; I shall cleanse you from all your idols. I shall make you walk in my precepts and keep my judgments, so that it may be a sign between me and you, and you may know that I am the Lord your God.”  
**R.** Amen.

## Antiphon 1

“I shall take you from among the nations and gather you from all the lands. And I shall pour clean water over you.”  
**V.** Hear, my people, and I shall speak; Israel, and I shall testify to you: I am God, your God.

**Prayer.** Pour out, O Lord, upon us the clean water by which you have raised up your Church for all ages, so that those whom you gather into it from the nations—that is, from all the lands—you may grant your kingdom everywhere.

“I shall make you walk in my precepts and keep my judgments, so that you may no longer suffer the reproach of famine among the nations.”  
**V.** Hear this, all nations; listen with your ears, you who inhabit the world.

**Prayer.** Make us walk in your precepts, O Lord, and keep your judgments, so that we who are often struck by the hungry mouth of evils may be freed through the strength of the protection of your right hand.

The Law of the Lord is immaculate, converting souls; the testimony of the Lord is faithful, granting wisdom to the little ones.

**Prayer.** May your blameless Law convert our souls, and may your faithful testimony grant wisdom to the little ones. May our hearts rejoice in your righteousness and not be saddened; may your command illuminate the eyes of our minds.

334 As Vespers begins on Palm Sunday.
