Prayer. Illuminate, O Lord, your face over us, so that the declaration of your words may illuminate our hearts, and understanding nourish the breasts of the little ones; so that, while we desire your commandments, we may receive with an opened heart the spirit of wisdom and understanding. R. Amen.

Antiphon. Blessed of my Father, come: P. Receive the kingdom that was prepared for you from the beginning of the world. V. Magnify the Lord with me, and let us exalt his name together.

Lauda. You are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people belonging to God. V. Come, children, listen to me: I will teach you the fear of the Lord.

Hymn.

[Col. 0564C] You are called to life, O sacred race of God,

The Creator adopting you, loves what he has made;

The Redeemer draws you with gracious spirit;

“Come,” he says, “I alone am your God.”

The heavy yoke of condemnation pressed upon you;

You gave your neck to the burden of wickedness;

The mouth soothed the throat, and destruction;

Stand firm: whatever flows forth, all collapses.

Having utterly abandoned the light of brightness,

A vast chaos had most wickedly enclosed you;

The place of blessedness no longer existed;

The bloodstained earth—whence death had entered.

Behold, I, God, have come, gentle, creating and recreating.

Mighty, sharing in your weakness,

I will carry you powerfully; come together,

[Col. 0564D] So that the sheepfold of joy may now receive you.

Let the forehead be marked beforehand with the sign of the cross;

Let the anointing, poured over the ears and mouth, mark them;

Give your heart’s ear to the words; with living voice

Sing aloud the song of confession.

All rejoice in the new name;

The inheritance of the new lot cherishes all;

No one will remain a servant subjected to the enemy;

You will be the enduring kingdom of the one God.

Honor and glory be to the eternal God,

To the one Father and to his only Son,

With the Spirit; this Trinity eternally

Lives in power for ages upon ages.

Amen.

[Col. 0565A] Capitula. O God, who will come to judgment with all the saints, and yet now cause peoples to dwell together in faith within the bosom of Mother Church, receive the prayer of your household and bless your inheritance. Grant that, for all of us who have now been reborn through water and the Holy Spirit, there may be forgiveness of sins; and that for those who are initiated into the sacraments of faith, the mystery of perfect belief may be impressed upon them. Thus may the sacraments of true faith bear fruit both in us and in them, so that you alone, the author of those sacraments, may now and forever rejoice in us alone.

Our Father.

Blessing. May God, who enriches his Church with the manifold fruitfulness of believers, grant his grace to those who have been reborn, and grant those who are to be reborn that they may attain the consummation of the mysteries of holy faith. R. Amen. May there be full salvation for both groups, since he is the true redemption of Christians. R. Amen. May you have life in him, you who believe, and possess heavenly joys with those who will believe. R. Amen.

Lauda. Father, glorify me with the glory that I had with you before the world existed. V. The declaration of your words gives light and grants understanding to the simple.

Prayer. May the declaration of your words, O Lord, illuminating hearts and understanding, nourish the breasts of the little ones, so that, while we desire your commandments, we may receive with an opened heart the spirit of wisdom and understanding. R. Amen.

[Col. 0565C] Lauda. This is the generation of those who seek the Lord, of those who seek the face of the God of Jacob. V. The earth is the Lord’s and its fullness, the world and all who dwell in it.

Prayer. Build upon the water of refreshment, O Lord, the people whom you formed through the water of baptism, so that, made drunk with legal teachings, it may seize our desire there where you promise to give the eternal reward of the blessed. R. Amen.

Lauda. Those who seek the Lord will lack no good thing. Come, children, listen to me: I will teach you the fear of the Lord. V. Magnify the Lord with me, and let us exalt his name together.

Prayer. Graciously hear those who seek you, O Lord, and mercifully grant that our soul may be praised in you; and because you are near to those who are contrite in heart, open your ear to the contrition of our spirit, and turn our bodies and hearts toward the peace that surpasses all understanding. R. Amen.

PALM SUNDAY.

At Matins.

Hymn. Eternal of all things. fol. 3.

Prayer. O Lord God, almighty Father, inspirer of prayers and swift hearer of those who invoke you, we ask you to bend the ear of your mercy to our voice, and by your powerful compassion dissolve the bonds of our sins. Just as you summon us to rise at the crowing of the cocks for the grace of morning, and by prophetic prediction announce in advance the one redemption as the light of the nations, so [Col. 0566A] now, as we journey, stand beside us with heavenly regard. Thus, we pray, receive the vows of our service, so that, raising us up by abundant mercy, you may lead us to the light of light. R. Amen.

Antiphon. Upon your people, O God, be your salvation and blessing. Psalm III.

Antiphon. Create in us a clean heart, O God, and renew a steadfast spirit within me. Psalm L.

Antiphon. In the shadow of your wings we hope, O God, until iniquity passes away from us. Psalm LVI.

Prayer. O Lord God, with whom those who confess find the remedy of salvation, erase the wounds of guilt from human hearts and show over us the most radiant face of your mercy. Bend your holy hearing to the cries of those who plead; [Col. 0566B] pour the gift of your grace into our minds and grant those who ask the remedy they seek. As we rise to render the service we owe, pour an abundance of blessing and salvation upon your people. Mercifully erase the crime contracted and make us free from the guilt of our offenses. Hear the groans of the penitent; bestow the fruit of forgiveness; and grant each of the faithful who knock with their cries the aid they request. R. Amen.

Antiphon 1. A generation to come will be proclaimed to the Lord. P. And they will proclaim his justice to the people who will be born, whom the Lord has made. V. I will tell your name to my brothers; in the midst of the Church I will praise you.

[Col. 0566C] Prayer. Behold, O Lord, the coming generation whom the Prophet once foretold, which has indeed journeyed by faith in order to come to you. Receive it, therefore, so that, washed in the perfection of the saving bath, it may possess with us the unending joys of the eternal Jerusalem. R. Amen.

Antiphon 2. All the ends of the earth will remember and turn to the Lord, and all the nations’ families will worship in his presence. V. The poor will eat and be satisfied, and those who seek him will praise the Lord; their hearts live forever and ever.

Prayer. O Christ, who, because of the unbelief of the synagogue, left that people and enlarged for yourself an innumerable people of the Church from every nation, fulfill what you foretold through prophetic prediction: that all the ends of the earth may remember and turn to you, God, and that all the nations’ families may worship you, who alone have truly saved the world. Raise up for yourself, therefore, sons of belief coming from the Circumcision and the Uncircumcision, so that all who come may be brought into the kingdom of faith, and all who have come or will come may not be deprived of your inheritance by any stain of their merits. R. Amen.

Antiphon 3. Enter the Lord’s gates with confession. P. His courts with hymns of confession. V. Sing joyfully to the Lord, all the earth; sing a psalm to his name.

Prayer. Serving you in fear, O Lord, let us enter your gates with confession and your courts with hymns of confession. Let us praise your name, for you are sweet; and, so that our mouth may be opened wide in your praises, stir our heart. Your boundless truth will go before us forever. R. Amen.

R. You are my cattle and the sheep of my flock;

P. And I am your Lord, says the Lord.

V. I will place my law within you and write it upon your hearts, and you will be my people. P. And I am.

Prayer. O Christ, Son of God the Father, who testify that you were sent to the sheep of the house of Israel that had perished, watch over your sheep as the true shepherd and extend pastoral governance over them. Thus, fortified by the protection of your care, both believers and those who will believe may escape the bite of the insatiable enemy. R. Amen.

At the Canticle. Antiphon. Give ear, O heaven, and I will speak, and let the earth hear the words from my mouth; let my discourse be awaited [Col. 0567B] like rain. For I have called upon the name of the Lord.

Canticle. Give ear, O heaven. fol. 4.

Matutinarium. O Jerusalem, the splendor of life that will come upon you from God: behold, your sons gathered from east and west, rejoicing in the kingdom of God. V. Praise the Lord, Jerusalem; praise your God, Zion.

Lauda. Elders together with the young, praise the Lord. P. And exalt his name alone. V. Confess to the Lord in heaven and on earth. P. And exalt it. V. Sing a hymn to God, all his servants. P. And exalt it.

Reading from the Book of Samuel (I Kings, chapter XVI).

R. Thanks be to God.

[Col. 0567C] In those days the Lord said to Samuel: “How long will you mourn Saul, since I have rejected him from reigning over Israel? Fill your horn with oil and come, so that I may send you to Jesse the Bethlehemite; for I have provided myself a king among his sons.” And Samuel said: “How shall I go? Saul will hear of it and kill me.” And the Lord said: “You shall take a calf from the herd in your hand and say: ‘I have come to sacrifice to the Lord.’ And you shall call Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will show you what you are to do; you shall anoint the one whom I point out to you.”

Samuel therefore did as the Lord had spoken to him. He came to Bethlehem, and the elders of the city were astonished, coming to meet him. And they said: “Is your entrance peaceful?” And he said: “Peaceful. I have come to sacrifice to the Lord. Be sanctified and come with me, so that I may sacrifice.” [Col. 0567D] Samuel therefore sanctified Jesse and his sons and called them to the sacrifice. And when they had entered, he saw Eliab and said: “Is the Lord’s anointed before him?” The Lord said to Samuel: “Do not look upon his face or the height of his stature, for I have rejected him. I do not judge according to a man’s appearance: a man sees those things that appear, but the Lord looks upon the heart.”

And Jesse called Aminadab and brought him before Samuel. He said: “The Lord has not chosen this one either.” Jesse brought Samma, concerning whom he said: “The Lord has not chosen this one either.” Thus Jesse brought seven of his sons before Samuel, and Samuel said to Jesse: “The Lord has not chosen any of these.” And Samuel said to Jesse: “Are these all your sons?” He answered: “There remains the youngest, and he is tending the sheep.” And Samuel said to Jesse: “Send and bring him, for we will not sit down before he comes here.”

He sent, therefore, and brought him. He was ruddy, handsome in appearance, and fair of face. And the Lord said: “Rise and anoint him, for this is he.” Samuel therefore took the horn of oil and anointed him in the midst of his brothers; and the Spirit of the Lord was directed toward David from that day onward. R. Amen.

Hymn. You are called to life. fol. 334.

Little Chapter. Do not forget, O Lord, the voice of those who seek you, nor the pride of those who hate you, rising forever. Grant that those who have been received into the bosom of Mother Church through the inscription of their office may deserve to approach the grace of holy Baptism, so that the mystery of the bath received among us may not be denied to those who desire such things, and that they themselves may possess with us the unending joy.

Lauda. Father, glorify me. fol. 334.

As Vespers comes to an end.

Lauda. In the nights, exalt. fol. 140.

Antiphon. Holy Father, those whom you have given me, I desire that where I am, they also may be with me. V. I will tell your name to my brothers; in the midst of the Church I will praise you.

Lauda. I have given them your word, and the world has hated them. Sanctify them, so that they too may be holy in truth. V. The declaration of your words gives light and grants understanding to the simple.

Hymn. You are called to life. fol. 334.

Little Chapter. This is, O Lord, the illustrious faith of the new generation, which seeks you in order to see you and desires you in order to live happily in you. Open for them, we ask, the sacrament of holy faith, so that in the perfection in which we recognize that we have ascended, we may also rejoice to see them become illustrious in it. Thus may they reach the joys of redemption, and may we preserve undefiled within us the mysteries of the redemption we have received.

Our Father.

Blessing. May Christ the Lord, who gives salvation to the human race through the sign of his salvation, grant us to arrive at the eternal inheritance with those who now come to his faith. R. Amen. May he also grant you to receive undefiled the fruit of our redemption, and grant them happily to reach the mystery of the saving bath. R. Amen. May the grace of divine protection favor those reborn and those to be reborn in such a way that it excludes none of them from the eternal possession. R. Amen.

Lauda. I have made your name known to them, O Lord, and I will make it known, so that the love with which you loved me may be in them, and I in them. V. The law of the Lord is immaculate, restoring souls.

Prayer. Make your justice known to us, O Lord, and kindle our heart with the fire of charity, so that we may seek it. Give understanding to our mind, by which we may be able to search out the hidden things of your law. Give perfection of faith, so that we may be able to keep the order of your commandments; so that through these things we may both be free from sin and become heirs of blessed life. R. Amen.

Lauda. Establish for them, O Lord, the law as the way of justice, and let them always seek it. R. Give me understanding, and I will search out your law, and keep it with my whole heart, O Lord.

Prayer. Incline our heart toward your testimonies, O Lord; turn it away from the sight of vanity, so that you may separate us from earthly love and join us to heavenly love. R. Amen.

Lauda. Give them understanding, O Lord, so that they may learn your commandments. R. Those who fear you will see me and rejoice, because I have hoped in your word.

Prayer. Grant us, O Lord, to grasp the equity of your testimonies with more eager understanding, so that the wisdom appointed by you may give life to what folly kills in us. R. Amen.

MONDAY AFTER PALM SUNDAY.

At Matins.

[Col. 0569B]

Antiphon. Arise, O Lord; save me, my God, for you have struck all those who oppose me without cause. Psalm III.

Prayer. Arise, O Lord—not from sleep, nor from a place, nor from a time, but immeasurably and eternally watchful—because many persecute and many tear apart your little flock. Be present as its merciful helper and defender, its hope amid the storm and its shelter from the heat. Despise, we ask, the ferocity of those rising against us and their wicked counsels; crush the teeth and feet of those raging against us; and scatter the gathered thousands surrounding us. R. Amen.

Antiphon 1. Do not hand me over, O Lord, into the hands of those who persecute me, for false witnesses have risen against me and have lied against themselves. You are my helper, O Lord; do not abandon me. V. The Lord is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? The Lord is the defender of my life; from whom shall I tremble?

Prayer. Do not hand your Church, O Lord, over to the bloody hand of those who persecute her, so that the false witnesses rising against her may recoil when the banners of the Cross have been raised within her. R. Amen.

Antiphon 2. Do not destroy me, O Lord, with those who work iniquity, with those who speak peace with their neighbor but evil is in their hearts. R. Repay them according to the work of their hands; repay them with their own retribution.

Prayer. Do not destroy us, O Lord, with those who work iniquity. Since, at the time of your Passion, you deigned with singular patience to endure those who spoke peace outwardly but meditated evil in their hearts, free us, your servants, from every fault of hostility, and make us here and forever strangers to the company of such people. R. Amen.

Antiphon 3. My enemies surrounded me like bees around wax, and they burned like fire among thorns; and in the name of the Lord I overcame them. V. I was pushed like a heap of sand so that I might fall, and the Lord received me.

Little Chapter. The enemies surrounding your soul, O Christ the Lord, rushed eagerly upon you like bees upon wax; at the time of your Passion, the mass of them burned against you like fire among thorns. Therefore, we ask, now look upon the prayer of your Church and take the bloodstained sword of the raging enemy from his hand, so that he may feel his own point cut off when, through those whom he has held captive, he learns that the doctrine of your faith is being preached. R. Amen.

R. All the princes of Judah gathered against the righteous man and seized him, saying: “Let this man die.” And he spoke to them, saying: P. “Behold, I am in your hands; do to me as you have decided in your hearts. Nevertheless, if you condemn me to death, know that you are bringing innocent blood upon yourselves.” V. They all lay in ambush for the righteous man’s blood; they hunted him to death, but he spoke peaceful words to them. P. “Behold.” No Gloria.

[Col. 0570B] Prayer. Jesus, our Savior and Lord, against whom all the princes of the Jews gathered, perpetrating a monstrous crime and shedding innocent blood, by which both the world is cleansed from the indictment of its ancient crime and all things on earth are recognized as joined in the unity of peace: cleanse us from every stain of sin through the reception of that same blood of yours, and adorn us with the good of innocence. Thus, bound together by the bond of mutual peace, may we at the time of your judgment be presented to you as true children of peace, and never be put to shame by the sight of your vision. R. Amen.

At Lauds.

Antiphon. Turn your face away from my sins, and blot out all my iniquities. Psalm L.

Prayer. Turn your face away. fol. 161.

[Col. 0570C] At the Canticle. Antiphon. I have become an object of ridicule all day long, and everyone mocked me.

Canticle. You have seduced me, O Lord. fol. 276.

Matutinarium. In the morning I will meditate upon you, for you have become my protector, O Lord. V. O God, my God, to you I keep watch from dawn.

Lauda. Praise the Lord from the heavens; praise him in the heights. His angels, praise him.

Reading from the Book of Malachim. (III Kings, chapter XI).

R. Thanks be to God.

In those days, when Solomon had grown old, his heart was perverted by women, so that he followed foreign gods; and his heart was not perfect with the Lord his God, as was the heart of David his father. Solomon worshiped Astherthen, the goddess of the Sidonians, and Chamos, the god of the Moabites, and Moloch, the idol of the Ammonites. Solomon did what was displeasing before the Lord and did not fulfill his duty to follow the Lord as David his father had done.

Then Solomon built a shrine for Chamos, the idol of Moab, on the mountain opposite Jerusalem, and for Moloch, the idol of the sons of Ammon. He did likewise for all his foreign wives, who burned incense and sacrificed to their gods. Therefore the Lord was angry with Solomon, because his mind had been turned away from the Lord God of Israel, who had appeared to him twice and had commanded him concerning this matter not to follow foreign gods; and he did not keep what the Lord had commanded him.

The Lord therefore said to Solomon: “Because you have had this within yourself and have not kept my covenant and my commandments that I gave you, breaking them, I will tear your kingdom apart and give it to your servant. Nevertheless, I will not do this in your days, for the sake of David your father; I will tear it from the hand of your son. Yet I will not take away the whole kingdom; I will give one tribe to your son, for the sake of David my servant and Jerusalem, which I have chosen.”

The Lord also raised up an adversary against Solomon, Hadad the Edomite, of royal descent, who was in Edom. For when David was in Idumea and Joab, the commander of the army, had gone up to bury those who had been killed, he killed every male in Idumea—for Joab and all Israel had remained there six months, until he had killed every male in Idumea. Hadad himself and the Edomite men who were servants of his father fled with him to enter Egypt. [Col. 0571B] Hadad was then a very young child.

When they had risen from Midian, they came to Pharan, took men from Pharan with them, and entered Egypt to Pharaoh, king of Egypt. He gave him a house, appointed provisions for him, and assigned him land. Hadad found very great favor with Pharaoh, so that he gave him as a wife the sister of his own wife, the full sister of Taphnes the queen. Taphnes’ sister bore him Genebath, and Taphnes raised him in Pharaoh’s house. Genebath lived with Pharaoh among his sons.

When Hadad heard in Egypt that David had slept with his fathers and that Joab, the commander of the army, was dead, he said to Pharaoh: “Send me away, so that I may go to my own land.” Pharaoh said to him: “What do you lack with me, that you seek to go to your own land?” He answered: “Nothing; but I beg you to send me away.”

God also raised up against him an adversary, Razon son of Eliada, who had fled from Hadadezer, king of Zobah, his lord. He gathered men against him and became the leader of brigands when David killed them. They went to Damascus, lived there, and appointed him king in Damascus. He was an adversary of Israel throughout all the days of Solomon. This was the evil of Hadad, and his hatred against Israel: he reigned in Syria.

Jeroboam, son of Nebat, an Ephrathean from Zereda, a servant of Solomon, whose mother was named Zeruah, a widow, also raised his hand against the king. This was the cause of his rebellion against him: Solomon had built Millo and leveled the ravine of the city of David his father. Jeroboam was a strong and capable man. When Solomon saw that the young man was well-born and industrious, he appointed him overseer of the tribute of the whole house of Joseph.

It happened at that time that Jeroboam went out from Jerusalem, and the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite met him on the road, covered with a new cloak. They were alone in the countryside. Ahijah seized his new cloak with which he was covered, tore it into twelve pieces, and said to Jeroboam: “Take ten pieces for yourself, for thus says the Lord God of Israel: ‘I will tear the kingdom from the hand of Solomon and give you ten tribes. One tribe will remain to him for the sake of my servant David and Jerusalem, the city that I have chosen from all the tribes of Israel, because he abandoned me and worshiped Astherthen, the goddess of the Sidonians, and Chamos, the god of Moab, and Moloch, the god of the sons of Ammon; and he did not walk in my ways, doing what is right before me, nor keep my commandments and judgments as David his father did.

“‘I will not take the whole kingdom from his hand, but I will make him ruler all the days of his life, for the sake of David my servant, whom I chose, who kept my commandments and precepts. But I will take the kingdom from the hand of his son and give you ten tribes. To his son I will give one tribe, so that a lamp may remain for David my servant all his days before me in Jerusalem, the city that I have chosen so that my name may be there.

“‘But I will take you, and you shall reign over everything that your soul desires, and you shall be king over Israel. If, therefore, you listen to all that I command you, walk in my ways, and do what is right before me, keeping my commandments and precepts as David my servant did, I will be with you. I will build you a faithful house, as I built a house for David, and I will give Israel to you. I will afflict the offspring of David because of this, but not forever.’”

Solomon therefore sought to kill Jeroboam. He arose and fled to Egypt, to Shishak, king of Egypt, and remained in Egypt until Solomon’s death. The rest of the words of Solomon, all that he did, and his wisdom—behold, everything is written in the Book of the Words of Solomon. The days that Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel were forty years. Solomon slept with his fathers and was buried in the city of David his father; and his son Rehoboam reigned in his place.

(Chapter XII.) Rehoboam came to Shechem, for all Israel had gathered there to make him king. But Jeroboam son of Nebat, who was still a fugitive in Egypt from the face of King Solomon, when he heard of Solomon’s death, returned from Egypt. They sent and called him, and Jeroboam came, with the whole assembly of Israel, and spoke to Rehoboam, saying: “Your father placed an exceedingly harsh yoke upon us. Therefore now lighten somewhat the severe rule of your father and the very heavy yoke that he placed upon us, and we will serve you.”

He said to them: “Go away until the third day, and return to me.” When the people had departed, King Rehoboam took counsel with the elders who had stood before his father Solomon while he was still alive, and said: “What counsel do you give me, so that I may answer this people?” They said to him: “If today you obey this people, serve them, and yield to their petition, speaking gentle words to them, they will be your servants all their days.”

But he abandoned the counsel of the elders, which they had given him, and consulted the young men who had grown up with him and stood before him. He said to them: “What counsel do you give me, so that I may answer this people who said to me: ‘Lighten the yoke that your father placed upon us’?” The young men who had grown up with him said to him: “Speak thus to this people who spoke to you, saying: ‘Your father made our yoke heavy; you lighten it for us.’ Speak to them in this way: ‘My little finger is thicker than my father’s back. And now my father placed a heavy yoke upon you; I will add to your yoke. My father scourged you with whips; I will scourge you with scorpions.’”

The king did not listen to the people, because the Lord had opposed him, in order to establish his word, which he had spoken through Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam son of Nebat. When all Israel saw that the king was unwilling to listen to them, they answered him, saying: “What share have we in David? What inheritance have we in the son of Jesse? To your tents, Israel! Now look after your own house, David.” And Israel went to its tents.

Over the Israelites who lived in the cities of Judah, Rehoboam reigned. King Rehoboam therefore sent Adoram, who was over the tribute, and all Israel stoned him, and he died. King Rehoboam quickly mounted his chariot and fled to Jerusalem. Thus Israel withdrew from the house of David to the present day.

When all Israel heard that Jeroboam had returned, they sent and called him, and, after assembling together, made him king over all Israel. No one followed the house of David except the tribe of Judah alone. Rehoboam came to Jerusalem and gathered the whole house of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin—one hundred and eighty thousand chosen men and warriors—to fight against the house of Israel and restore the kingdom to Rehoboam, son of Solomon.

[Col. 0573C] The word of the Lord came to Shemaiah, the man of God, saying: “Speak to Rehoboam son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all the house of Judah and Benjamin and the remainder of the people, saying: Thus says the Lord: You shall not go up and you shall not fight against your brothers, the sons of Israel. Let each man return to his house, for this word has come from me.” They heard the word of the Lord and returned from their journey, as the Lord had commanded them. R. Amen.

Hymn. The time of night is now passing. fol. 257.

Little Chapter. Hear, O Lord, the lamentable groaning of your Church, for whom you bore the injury of sufferings. May she, who knows that she has been saved by your sufferings, be free from disgrace, so that, by the judgment of your eternity, you may both relieve her from the tribulations of her pressures and join her to yourself, to be crowned without end.

Our Father.

Lauda. Those who seek the Lord will lack no good thing. Come, children, listen to me: I will teach you the fear of the Lord. V. The Lord redeems the souls of his servants, and he will not abandon all who hope in him.

Prayer. Graciously hear those who seek you, O Lord, and mercifully grant that our soul may be praised in you; and because you are near to those who are contrite in heart, open your ear to the contrition of our spirit, and turn our bodies and hearts toward the peace that surpasses all understanding. R. Amen.

At Terce.

[Col. 0574A]

From Ecclesiasticus of Solomon (chapter XXXVII).

R. Thanks be to God.

Son, every friend will say: “I too have formed a friendship,” but there is a friend who is a friend in name only. Is there not sorrow even unto death? A companion and a friend will turn into enemies. O most wicked presumption, whence were you created to cover arid ground with wickedness and its deceit? A companion grieves with his friend for the sake of his belly, and against the enemy he will take up a shield.

Do not forget your friend in your heart, and do not be unmindful of him in your works. Every counselor reveals counsel, but there is a counselor who is counselor only to himself. Guard your soul from a counselor; first learn what his need is and what he is considering in his heart, lest perhaps he cast a stake into the ground and say to you: “Your way is good,” while he stands opposite to see what happens to you. Deal with a religious man concerning holiness, and with a righteous man concerning justice. R. Amen.

Antiphon 1. The kings of the earth stood forth, and the princes gathered together against the Lord and against his Anointed. V. Let us break their bonds and cast their yoke away from us.

Prayer. O Christ God, before whom the kings of the earth stood meditating on empty things and the princes gathered together, grant us this special gift of grace: that we may in no way yield to adversity. Thus may unbelief be disturbed in your wrath, so that through your help our faith may be crowned. R. Amen.

[Col. 0574C] Antiphon 2. My knees have grown weak from fasting, and my flesh has been changed because of oil. And I became a reproach to them. V. Do not be silent, O God of my praise, for the mouth of the sinner and the mouth of the deceitful have been opened against me.

Prayer. Only-begotten Son of God, whose knees grew weak in fasting, and whose flesh was changed because of oil, make us run effectively after you in the fragrance of ointments, so that you who became a reproach to our enemies may become saving power. R. Amen.

Antiphon 3. I, when they troubled me, clothed myself in sackcloth. I humbled my soul with fasting, and my prayer returned into my bosom. V. As for a neighbor and as for our brother, so I was pleased; as one mourning and sorrowful, so I humbled myself. Gloria is not to be said.

R. I have handed over my beloved soul into the hands of my enemies. And my inheritance became for me like a lion in the forest. The adversary raised his voice against me, saying: “Gather together and hurry to devour him.” They placed me in a desert of solitude. P. And the whole earth mourned over me, because no one was found who knew me or would do good. V. They placed me in the lowest pit, in darkness and in the shadow of death. P. And it mourned. Let R. be repeated.

Prayers. Attend, O Lord, to the prayer of your people. P. And pardon our sins, for you are merciful. V. Creator of the world, Lord, who judge with equity, deliver us from evil by your right hand. P. And pardon. V. You who acquire for yourself a people of the nations through your cross, merciful Christ, erase the sins of all. P. And. V. You who invoke your Father and ask him to forgive: forgive us our debts, loosen our bonds. P. And. V. You who first grant the penitent thief rest in paradise, help the penitent who are bound. P. And.

Hymn. O Nazarene. fol. 144.

Little Chapter. Son of God, who in the flesh of true humanity that you assumed deigned to endure the injury of sufferings for us, free us from everlasting death through the mystery of your Passion, so that those whom, dying and rising again, you freed from darkness, you may rescue from torments when you judge and reign.

Our Father, etc.

At Sext.

[Col. 0575B]

Reading from the Book of the Prophet Ezekiel (chapter XXV).

R. Thanks be to God.

The word of the Lord came to me, saying: “Son of man, set your face against the sons of Ammon, and you shall prophesy concerning them. And you shall say to the sons of Ammon: Hear the word of the Lord God. Thus says the Lord God: Because you said, ‘Aha, aha!’ over my sanctuary, because it has been profaned, and over the house of Judah, because they have been led into captivity, therefore behold, I will hand you over to the sons of the East as an inheritance. They will place their sheepfolds in you and set up their tents in you; they will eat your crops and drink your milk.

“I will make Rabbah a dwelling place for camels and the sons of Ammon a resting place for flocks, and you shall know that I am the Lord. For thus says the Lord God: Because you clapped your hands and stamped your feet and rejoiced with all your heart over the land of Israel, therefore behold, I will stretch out my hand over you and hand you over to the plunder of the nations. I will destroy you from among the peoples, wipe you out from the lands, and crush you; and you shall know that I am the Lord your God.” R. Amen.

Antiphon 1. Guard me, O Lord, from the hand of the sinner; deliver me, O Lord, from wicked men. V. Rescue me, O Lord, from the evil man; deliver me from the unjust and deceitful man.

Prayer. Guard us, O Lord, from the hand of the sinner, and deliver us from wicked men, so that, because you are our protection, we may receive you as our protector unto everlasting glory. R. Amen.

[Col. 0575D] Antiphon 2. They gave me gall for food, and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink. Let their table become a snare before them. V. Let their eyes be darkened, so that they may not see, and continually bend their backs.

Prayer. O Christ, Son of God, who at the final consummation of your Passion were given gall and vinegar to drink by the Jews: grant us that, through this bitterness which was offered to you, you may make us drunk with the draught of your bitter sufferings; so that the bitterness of your death may increase the flame of your love toward us, and the power of your resurrection may perfectly reveal to us the promised glory of your countenance. R. Amen.

Antiphon 3. I am counted among those who descend into the pit; I have become like a man without help, free among the dead. V. O Lord, God of my salvation, by day I cried out, and by night before you.

R. Let each man guard himself from his neighbor, and let him not trust his brother; for every brother supplants, and every friend walks deceitfully, P. and does not speak the truth. V. With his lips the enemy speaks gently, to overthrow his friend in a pit; for by much talk he has plotted against him, and mocks him. P. And he does not speak.

Prayers. Show us mercy, O Lord: grant pardon; bestow forgiveness; P. and, appeased, have mercy. V. You who came to save the world and were judged: when you come as judge, do not hand us over with the ungodly; P. and have mercy. V. You who were hung upon the wood of the cross, bearing on your shoulders the death of our sin: P. have mercy. V. You who, though you never die, suffered once for the ungodly: put us to death with respect to our vices, and heal us by the wound of the cross; P. and have mercy. V. May your face not be presented against us in judgment for punishment, but grant us pardon; P. and have mercy.

Hymn. “O Nazarene.” fol. 144.

Capitulum. O God, Son of God, who suffered innocently for the ungodly: illumine us with the dignity of innocence pleasing to you, and save us through the disgraces of your Passion, so that through the undeserved punishments of your death we may escape the deserved torments of our iniquity. R. Amen.

Our Father. And lead us not.

## At None

Reading from the Book of Ecclesiasticus of Solomon (Chapter XXVII).

R. Thanks be to God.

My son, love your neighbor and join yourself to him in faith. But if you have revealed his secrets, do not pursue him afterward. For just as one who destroys his friend is, so also is one who destroys his neighbor’s friendship. And just as one who lets a bird escape from his hand, so are you when you have abandoned your neighbor: you cannot seize him again; do not pursue him, for he is far away. To reveal a friend’s secrets is the despair of an unhappy soul. Winking with his eye, he contrives wickedness, and no one will cast him away; before your eyes he tramples his mouth, and he will marvel at your words; but at last he will pervert his mouth and give offense through your words. Whoever throws a stone upward will have it fall upon his own head; and a treacherous blow will divide the wounds of the treacherous. Whoever digs a pit will fall into it; and whoever places a stone in his neighbor’s path will stumble over it; and whoever sets a snare for another will perish in it. The wicked counsel one devises will roll back upon himself, and he will not know from where it will come upon him. Mockery and reproach will lie in wait for the proud like a lion. Those who delight in the downfall of the righteous will perish in a snare; sorrow will consume them before they die. (Chapter XXVIII.) Forgive your neighbor who has harmed you; then, when you pray, your sins will be forgiven you. R. Amen.

Reading from the Book of Malachim (III Kings, Chapter XII).

R. Thanks be to God.

In those days Jeroboam held a solemn feast for the children of Israel and went up to the altar to burn incense. (Chapter XIII.) And behold, a man of God came from Judah by the word of the Lord to Bethel, while Jeroboam stood beside the altar and was throwing incense upon it. He cried out against the altar by the word of the Lord and said: “Altar, altar, thus says the Lord: Behold, a son shall be born to the house of David, Josiah by name, and he shall sacrifice upon you the priests of the high places who now burn incense upon you, and he shall burn human bones upon you.” And on that day he gave a sign, saying: “This shall be the sign that the Lord has spoken: Behold, the altar shall be split, and the ashes that are upon it shall be poured out.”

When the king heard the word of the man of God, who had cried out against the altar at Bethel, he stretched out his hand from the altar, saying: “Seize him.” And his hand, which he had stretched out against him, withered, and he could not draw it back to himself. The altar also was split, and the ashes were poured out from the altar, according to the sign that the man of God had foretold by the word of the Lord.

And the king said to the man of God: “Entreat the face of the Lord your God, and pray for me, that my hand may be restored to me.” The man of God entreated the face of the Lord, and the king’s hand was restored to him and became as it had been before.

Then the king said to the man of God: “Come home with me to eat, and I will give you gifts.” The man of God answered the king: “Even if you were to give me half your house, I would not go with you, nor eat bread nor drink water in this place; for thus I was commanded by the word of the Lord: ‘You shall not eat bread, nor drink water, nor return by the way by which you came.’” So he departed by another way and did not return by the road by which he had come to Bethel.

Now a certain old prophet lived at Bethel. His sons came and told him all the works that the man of God had done that day at Bethel, and they told their father the words that he had spoken to the king. He said to them: “By what way did he go?” His sons showed him the way by which the man of God who had come from Judah had departed. And he said to his sons: “Saddle my donkey.” When they had saddled it, he mounted and went after the man of God, and found him sitting beneath a terebinth. He said to him: “Are you the man of God who came from Judah?” He answered: “I am.” And he said to him: “Come home with me and eat bread.”

He replied: “I cannot return, nor come with you, nor eat bread nor drink water in this place, because the Lord spoke to me by the word of the Lord, saying: ‘You shall not eat bread, nor drink water there, nor return by the way by which you went.’” He said to him: “I too am a prophet like you, and an angel spoke by the word of the Lord, saying: ‘Bring him back with you into your house, so that he may eat bread and drink water.’” But he deceived him and brought him back with him. So he ate bread in his house and drank water.

While they were sitting at table, the word of the Lord came to the prophet who had brought him back. And he cried out to the man of God who had come from Judah, saying: “Thus says the Lord: Because you were disobedient to the mouth of the Lord and did not keep the command that the Lord your God gave you, but returned and ate bread and drank water in the place where he commanded you not to eat bread or drink water, your corpse shall not be brought into the tomb of your fathers.”

When he had eaten and drunk, the prophet whom he had brought back saddled his donkey for him. When he had departed, a lion found him on the road and killed him, and his corpse lay thrown upon the road; the donkey stood beside him, and the lion stood beside the corpse. And behold, men passing by saw the corpse thrown upon the road and the lion standing beside the corpse. They came and reported it in the city where that old prophet lived.

When the prophet who had brought him back from the road heard this, he said: “He is the man of God who was disobedient to the mouth of the Lord; therefore the Lord delivered him to the lion, which tore him apart and killed him according to the word of the Lord that he had spoken to him.” And he said to his sons: “Saddle my donkey.” When they had saddled it and he had departed, he found his corpse thrown upon the road, and the donkey and the lion standing beside the corpse. The lion had not eaten the corpse and had not harmed the donkey.

The prophet took the corpse of the man of God, placed it upon the donkey, and returned with it to the city of the old prophet, to mourn him; and he placed his corpse in his own tomb, and they mourned him, saying: “Alas, alas, my brother.” When they had mourned him, he said to his sons: “When I die, bury me in the tomb in which the man of God is buried; place my bones beside his bones.” R. Amen.

Antiphon 1. I am poor and in troubles from my youth; your terrors have passed over me; they have surrounded me like water, all day long; they have encircled me together. You have put far from me my friend and my acquaintances because of misery. V. O Lord, God of my salvation, by day I cried out, and by night before you. The Gloria is not to be said.

Prayer. Come quickly as comforter to your Church, which is needy and remains in troubles, O Christ; so that you, who for her became needy and poor, may hereafter reward her with heavenly gifts. R. Amen.

Antiphon 2. O God, the unjust rise up against me, and the assembly of the wicked seeks my soul, and they do not set you before themselves. V. But you, O Lord God, are compassionate, merciful, and true. The Gloria is not to be said.

Prayer. O Savior and Lord, whom the wickedness of those rising unjustly against you struck, and whom the assembly of the wicked, raging with their tongues, crucified: grant us always to follow you in the profound mystery of piety, so that, since you suffered both the cross and the tomb for us, we may pass victoriously through the conquered world to heaven. R. Amen.

Antiphon 3. I am troubled by the voice of the enemy and by the distress of the sinner, for iniquities have inclined against me, and in wrath they were troublesome to me. V. My heart is troubled within me, and the fear of death has fallen upon me.

Hymn. “O Nazarene.” fol. 144.

Prayer. Behold, O Lord, we are saddened by the voice of the enemy, while deadly arrows of hatred fall upon us; but you, who endured bitter insults for us, put far from us, your servants, the distress of the sinner, and by the power of your strength scatter the iniquities that incline against us.

Our Father.

## At Vespers

[Col. 0579A]

Praise. “You illumine my lamp, O Lord.”

Antiphon. “Arise, O Lord, and attend to my judgment, my God and my Lord, to my cause.” Psalm XXXIV.

Praise. “You have commanded us to keep your commandments exceedingly.” V. “Blessed are the undefiled in the way, who walk in the law of the Lord.”

Hymn. “You are called to life.” fol. 334.

Capitulum. O God, author of light and creator of splendor, who have removed all the works of darkness so that the fullness of your light might reign in us: look upon us, we beseech you; and through this light that has been kindled, entreated by us all, pour forth the grace of your blessing, so that, just as this flame, appointed for the service of your altar, overcomes and drives away darkness, so your illumination may overcome every fuel of vice in our senses.

Our Father.

Blessing. May Christ the Lord graciously guard you and, appeased, bless you. R. Amen. May his mercy protect you and continually defend you from every evil. R. Amen. May you rejoice as worthy of the gift of him who in his kindness grants forgiveness of sins. R. Amen.

Praise. “Those who seek the Lord.” Seek. fol. 340.

## Tuesday

### At Matins

Antiphon. “Arise, O Lord; save me, my God, for you have struck all those who oppose me without cause.” Psalm III.

Prayer. “Arise, O Lord our God, to our aid.” fol. 258.

Antiphon 1. “Deliver my soul from the sword, O Lord, and my only one from the hand of the dog. Save me from the lion’s mouth and my humility from the horns of the unicorns.” V. “I will proclaim your name to my brothers; in the midst of the Church I will praise you.” The Gloria is not to be said.

Prayer. O Christ, Son of God, deliver our soul from the sword of the most powerful enemy, so that you may always be our deliverer from the lion’s mouth—you who powerfully brought your soul out from the underworld. R. Amen.

[Col. 0579D]

Antiphon 2. “They spoke against me with a deceitful tongue, and surrounded me with words of hatred; they fought against me without cause. Instead of loving me, they slandered me; but I prayed.” V. “They repaid me evil for good, and hatred for my love.”

Prayer. Your enemies, O Lord, spoke evil against you—especially when, by deceitful flattery, they praised you as the good Teacher. Since you permitted yourself to be attacked and surrounded by their hateful words, receive, we beseech you, the prayers of our confession, offered in supplication. R. Amen.

Antiphon 3. “Often they have fought against me from my youth,” let Israel now say; “often from my youth”—but they could not prevail against me. Sinners fashioned upon my back; they prolonged their iniquity. V. “Let all who hate Zion be confounded and turned backward.”

Prayer. Behold, O Lord, upon the back of your Church the burdensome iniquity of proud sinners has been fashioned, while those incorrigible in conduct savagely attack your members. Grant us, therefore, we beseech you, to be so supported by the virtue of endurance that we may bring safely with us to the heavenly fold those whom we carry upon the back of our soul for healing; so that, having received with them the one and singular denarius, we too may deserve to receive profit from our preaching, and they may obtain with us an eternal reward for their obedience. R. Amen.

R. My enemies placed me like a target for the spear and seized me with their arm. They fed me bitterness and made my only one drunk with gall. They struck my teeth according to their number; P. and they brought my soul to an end in peace. V. My enemies captured me without cause like a bird in a hunt. My life fell into a pit, and they placed a stone over me; O. and they brought it to an end.

Prayer. Save your people, O Lord, by your right hand; and you who gave those who fear you the sign of the cross, grant the dignity of fullest faith, so that those whom you had repelled when they sinned, you may receive when they turn back; and give the necessary help in tribulation, you who became the price for sinners; and yourself reduce the enemy who afflicts us to nothing; yourself bring the redeemed into the city of their surrounding refuge. R. Amen.

### At Lauds

Antiphon. “Deliver me from bloodshed, O God, God of my salvation, and my tongue shall exult in your justice.” Psalm L.

Prayer. O Christ God of our salvation, who by your sufferings extinguish the sufferings caused by our crimes: deliver us from men of blood and from all our corruptions, so that, turning away from the works of flesh and blood, we may deserve to be numbered not among those destroyed by the precipice of men of blood, but among those who please you. R. Amen.

At the Canticle. Antiphon. “O Lord, I am oppressed; answer for me. What shall I say, or what shall I answer you, since I myself have done it?”

[Col. 0580D]

Canticle. “I said: In the middle of my days,” etc. fol. 122.

Prayer. Remember, Lord Jesus Christ, that you suffered in the sight of your enemies, when they found you innocent amid their fabrications; but because we are harassed by our enemies, grant that our answer may be found true before you. R. Amen.

Matutinary. “My king and my God, to you I shall pray; O Lord, in the morning you will hear my voice.” V. “Attend to my words with your ears, O Lord; understand my cry. Attend to the voice of my prayer, my king and my God. For to you I shall pray, O Lord.”

Praise. “Praise the Lord from the heavens; praise him in the heights. Praise him, all his angels; praise.”

[Col. 0581A]

Reading from the Book of Malachim (III Kings, Chapter XVII).

R. Thanks be to God.

In those days the Lord spoke to Elijah the Tishbite, saying: “Depart from here, and go toward the east, and hide in the torrent Carith, which is opposite the Jordan; and there you shall drink from the torrent. I have commanded the ravens to feed you there.”

So he departed and acted according to the word of the Lord. When he had gone, he sat by the torrent Carith, which is opposite the Jordan. The ravens brought him bread and meat in the morning, and likewise bread and meat in the evening, and he drank from the torrent.

After some days the torrent dried up, for it had not rained upon the earth. Then the word of the Lord came to him, saying: “Arise and go to Sarepta of the Sidonians, and remain there; for I have commanded a widow woman there to feed you.”

He arose and went to Sarepta of the Sidonians. When he had come to the gate of the city, a widow woman appeared to him gathering sticks. He called her and said: “Give me a little water in a vessel, that I may drink.” As she was going to fetch it, he called after her, saying: “Bring me also, I beg you, a morsel of bread in your hand.”

She answered: “As the Lord your God lives, I have no bread, except as much flour as a handful can contain in a jar, and a little oil in a flask. Behold, I am gathering two sticks, so that I may go in and prepare it for myself and my son, that we may eat and die.”

Elijah said to her: “Do not fear, but go and do as you have said; nevertheless, first make for me from that little flour a small cake baked under the ashes, and bring it to me; afterward you shall make some for yourself and your son. For thus says the Lord God of Israel: The jar of flour shall not fail, nor shall the flask of oil diminish until the day on which the Lord gives rain upon the face of the earth.”

She went and acted according to the word of Elijah. He, and she, and her household ate; and from that day the jar of flour did not fail, and the flask of oil was not diminished, according to the word of the Lord that he had spoken through Elijah.

After these events the son of the woman, the mistress of the house, became ill; and his illness was exceedingly severe, so that no breath remained in him. She said to Elijah: “What have I to do with you, man of God? You came to me so that my iniquities might be remembered and my son might be killed?”

Elijah said to her: “Give me your son.” He took him from her bosom and carried him up to the upper room where he lived, and placed him upon his bed. He cried out to the Lord and said: “O Lord my God, have you also afflicted the widow with whom I am in some way sustained, so as to kill her son?”

And he stretched himself and measured himself over the child three times, and cried out to the Lord and said: “O Lord my God, I beseech you, let the soul of this child return into his body.”

The Lord heard the voice of Elijah, and the soul of the child returned within him, and he revived. Elijah took the child and brought him down from the upper room into the lower house, gave him to his mother, and said to her: “Behold, your son lives.”

The woman said to Elijah: “Now by this I know that you are a man of God, and that the word of the Lord in your mouth is true.” R. Amen.

[Col. 0582A]

Hymn. “Now the time of night.” fol. 257.

Capitulum. O Christ, Son of God, who, while loving, are hated, and while sparing, are assailed to be killed; while you show yourself kind among your persecutors and are found merciful: grant us that through the wounds of your Passion our offenses may be expiated, so that you who in humility suffered death for us may, in glory, grant us eternal splendor.

Our Father.

Praise. “This is the generation of those who seek the Lord, who seek the face of the God of Jacob.” V. “The earth is the Lord’s and its fullness, the world and all who dwell in it.”

Prayer. Lead to the waters of refreshment, O Lord, the people whom you formed through the water of baptism, so that, made drunk with lawful teachings, it may carry our desire there where you promise to give the eternal reward of the blessed. R. Amen.

## At Terce

From Ecclesiasticus of Solomon (Chapter XV).

R. Thanks be to God.

My son, the wisdom of God is great and strong in power, seeing all without ceasing. The eyes of the Lord are upon those who fear him, and he recognizes every work of man. Beware of the unrighteous man, and guard yourself from your neighbor. (Chapter XVII.) Their ways are always before him; they are not hidden from his eyes. He appointed a ruler over every nation, and Israel became the portion of God made manifest. All their works are like the sun in the sight of God, and his eyes continually inspect their ways. Their covenants are not hidden because of their iniquity, and all their iniquities are before God. The almsgiving of a man is like a seal with him, and he will preserve a man’s grace like the pupil of his eye; afterward he will arise and repay them with repayment, placing it upon each one’s head, and he will turn toward the lower parts of the earth. But to those who repent he gave the way of justice; he strengthened the failing to endure, and appointed the lot of truth. Turn back to the Lord and abandon your sins; stand in the portion of the oversight and prayer of God Most High. R. Amen.

Reading from the Prophet Jeremiah, Lamentations (Chapter III).

R. Thanks be to God.

I am the man who sees my poverty and the rod of his indignation. He threatened me and led me into darkness, not into light. Against me alone he turned his hand all day long. He made my skin old and crushed my flesh and bones. He built around me and surrounded me with gall and toil. He placed me in darkness like those who have been dead forever. He built around me so that I could not go out; he made my fetter heavy. Even when I cried out and prayed, he shut out my prayer. He enclosed my ways with squared stones; he overturned my paths. He became a bear lying in wait for me, a lion in hiding. He overturned my paths and broke me; he made me desolate. He bent his bow and set me like a target for an arrow; he sent the daughters of his quiver into my kidneys. I became a mockery to all my people, their song all day long. He filled me with bitterness and made me drunk with wormwood. He struck my teeth according to their number; he fed me ashes. My enemies captured me without cause like a bird in a hunt. My life fell into a pit, and they placed a stone over me. The waters flowed over my head, and I said: “I am lost.” I invoked your name, O Lord, from the deepest pit. You heard my voice; do not turn your ear away from my most grievous sighing and cries. You drew near on the day when I invoked you; you said: “Do not fear.” You judged, O Lord, the cause of my soul, redeemer of my life. You saw, O Lord, their iniquities against me; judge my judgment. You heard their reproaches, O Lord, all their thoughts against me, the lips of those rising against me, and their meditations against me all day long. See their sitting and their rising; I am their song. Repay them, O Lord, according to the works of their hands. You shall give them the labor of your shield upon their heart. (Chapter IV.) Our persecutors were swifter than the eagles of heaven; they pursued us over the mountains and lay in wait for us in the wilderness. The breath of our mouth, Christ the Lord, was captured in our sins; to him we said: “In your shadow we shall live among the nations.” R. Amen.

Antiphon 1. “Deliver me, O Lord, from the lion’s mouth, and rescue my soul, my only one, from the hand of the dog, that I may proclaim your name to my brothers; in the midst of the Church I will praise you, O Lord my God.” V. “Deliver my soul from the sword, and my only one from the hand of the dog.”

[Col. 0583C]

Prayer. Deliver us, O Lord, from the lion’s mouth—you who suffered injury upon the cross—so that, praising you in the midst of the Church, we may proclaim your name to our brothers; for you alone became the victor over death. R. Amen.

Antiphon 2. Unjust witnesses rose up; they questioned me about things I did not know. They repaid me evil for good. But I clothed myself in sackcloth and humbled my soul with fasting. V. As for a neighbor and as for our brother, so I took pleasure in him; like one mourning and sorrowful, so I humbled myself.

Prayer. O God, Son of God, against whom the wicked rose up, when, questioning you about what they did not know, they slaughtered themselves through the blindness of ignorance, repaying you evil for good: grant us to rejoice so in your sufferings that we may deserve to be admitted for crowning in the court of heavenly glory. R. Amen.

Antiphon 3. My soul expected reproach and misery. I waited for one who would grieve with me, but there was none; I found no one to comfort me. V. They gave me gall for food, and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.

R. The enemy enclosed my ways; he became an ambusher for me, like a lion in hiding. He overturned my path and broke me. He bent his bow and set me like a target for an arrow. He filled me and made me drunk with bitterness. My enemies seized me without cause like a bird in a snare. They led my life down into the pit of death and placed a stone against me. See, O Lord, their iniquities and judge the cause of my soul, P. defender of my life. V. See their sitting and their rising; I am their song. Repay them, O Lord, P. defender.

Prayers. Spare us, Jesus the Redeemer; help the redeemed, wiping away our sins. P. By the price of blood. V. May those sacred hands, which were fastened to the cross, cleanse us from guilt. P. By the price. V. May the voice that prayed the Father to spare his enemies commend us to you, wiping away our sins. P. By the price. V. Fill us with every good and make us free from evil, so that we may all be satisfied. P. By the price. V. Today put an end to our sins, O Christ, so that tomorrow we may be refreshed. P. By the price.

Hymn. “O Nazarene, light.” fol. 144.

Capitulum. O Christ, Son of God, whom the savage crowd of persecutors pursues with blind fury, and in pursuing is itself blinded; while it punishes in you the Man through sufferings and does not recognize in you the substance of the Godhead: grant us, confessing that you are true God and Man, one Christ, to deserve to be counted banished from eternal punishments.

Our Father.

## At Sext

Reading from the Book of the Prophet Micah (Chapter VII).

R. Thanks be to God.

Thus says the Lord: The holy man has perished from the earth, and there is no upright man among human beings; all lie in wait for blood, each man hunts his brother to death. They call the evil of their hands good. The prince demands, and the judge is ready to repay; the great man has spoken the desire of his soul, and they have disturbed it. The best among them is like a thornbush, and the upright like a thorn from a hedge. The day of your visitation, your inspection, has come; now their destruction will be. Do not believe a friend, and do not trust a leader; guard the doors of your mouth from her who sleeps upon your breast. For the son dishonors his father, the daughter rises against her mother, the daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law, and a man’s enemies are those of his own household.

But I will look toward the Lord; I will await God my Savior; my God will hear me. Do not rejoice over me, my enemy, because I have fallen; I shall rise when I sit in darkness; the Lord is my light. I shall bear the wrath of the Lord, because I have sinned against him, until he judges my cause and executes my judgment; he will lead me into the light, and I shall see his justice. My enemy will look and be covered with shame, she who says to me: “Where is the Lord your God?” My eyes shall see her; now she will be trampled like the mud of the streets.

The day will come when your walls are to be built; on that day the law will be far removed. On that day Assyria will come even to you, and to the fortified cities; and from the fortified cities to the river, and from sea to sea, and from mountain to mountain. And the land shall become desolate because of its inhabitants and because of the fruit of their thoughts. Feed your people with your rod, the flock of your inheritance. R. Amen.

Antiphon 1. My enemies hunted me like a bird without cause. They delivered my soul to death. V. And you, O Lord, will mock them; you will hold all nations as nothing.

Prayer. O Christ, Son of God, who without any guilt were delivered to death and entangled in the snares of those who hunted you: cause the death owed by us to be overcome through your undeserved death, so that you who were delivered up innocently for us may one day bring us, happy, to yourself through the goodness of innocence. R. Amen.

Antiphon 2. All day long my enemies reproached me, and those who praised me swore against me; but you, O Lord, have mercy on me. V. For I ate ashes like bread, and mingled my drink with weeping.

Prayer. All day long your enemies unjustly reproached you, when they not only did not acknowledge you as Lord of the world, but men of peace also swore against you. Grant us, therefore, that we who rightly believe your Passion may live with you forever without end in the eternal resurrection. R. Amen.

Antiphon 3. The Lord is my helper; I will not fear what man can do to me. The Lord is my helper, and I shall look upon my enemies. V. I was thrust like a heap of sand so that I might fall, but the Lord received me.

R. The envious devil suddenly wounded me, and my bones were reduced to nothing. My brothers bear witness against me. P. Deliver me, O Lord. V. Guard me, O Lord, from the hand of the sinner and from wicked men. P. Deliver me, O Lord.

Prayers. Spare us, Jesus the Redeemer, and help the redeemed, wiping away our sins. P. By the price of your blood. V. Save our body, which you wished to be fastened to the cross, when you are the judge. P. By the price. V. Do not judge in anger those for whom you were judged and struck with blows, wiping away our sins. P. By the price. V. Guard those whose sins you bore upon your shoulders, lest they fall. P. By the price. V. Today let them feel in us the cleansing of foulness, and tomorrow fill us, wiping away our sins. P. By the price.

Hymn. “O Nazarene, light.” fol. 144.

348 Prayer. O Christ God, who endured the injury of death and the cross for us: grant us to become conquerors of our guilt through you, so that, just as you rise after death into glory, we may rise through grace from the death of our vices, never to fall again.

[Col. 0585D]

Our Father.

## At None

From the Wisdom of Solomon (Chapter XVI).

R. Thanks be to God.

My son, God heals all things by his word. For he has power over life and death; he leads down to the gates of death and brings back. But man kills his own soul through wickedness; and when the spirit goes out, it does not return, nor does he recall the soul that has been received. But it is impossible to escape your hand, O Lord.

For the ungodly, denying that they know you, were scourged by the strength of your arm; they suffered persecution through strange waters and hail and were consumed by fire. For what was remarkable in the water, which extinguishes everything, the fire was more powerful; for the world is the avenger of the righteous. But this was so that they themselves, seeing it, might know that they suffer persecution by God’s judgment. And at one time the fire burned above the power of water, so that it might destroy the unjust land of their birth.

Instead of these things, you fed your people with the food of angels and gave them prepared bread from heaven without labor, containing every delight in itself and the sweetness of every flavor. Thus your children whom you loved, O Lord, might know that it is not the fruits of birth that feed human beings, but that your word preserves those who believe in you. For what could not be destroyed by fire, immediately melted when warmed by a slight ray of the sun, so that it might be known to all that one ought to anticipate the sun for blessing and worship you, the Lord, at the rising of the light. R. Amen.

Reading from the Book of Malachim (III Kings, Chapter XVIII).

[Col. 0586B]

R. Thanks be to God.

In those days the word of the Lord came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying: “Go, and show yourself to Ahab, that I may give rain upon the face of the earth.” So Elijah went to show himself to Ahab. Now there was a severe famine in Samaria. Ahab called Obadiah, the steward of his household; but Obadiah feared the Lord God greatly. For when Jezebel was killing the prophets of the Lord, he took a hundred prophets and hid them by fifties in caves, and fed them with bread and water.

Ahab therefore said to Obadiah: “Go through the land, to all the springs of water and all the valleys, if perhaps we can find grass and save the horses and mules, so that the beasts may not perish altogether.” And they divided the regions between them to go through them. [Col. 0586C] Ahab went by one road, and Obadiah went separately by another.

When Obadiah was on the road, Elijah met him. Recognizing him, he fell on his face and said: “Are you my lord Elijah?” He answered him: “I am.” And he said: “Go and tell your lord: ‘Elijah is here.’”

But he said: “What have I done wrong, that you are handing your servant over to Ahab, so that he may kill me? As the Lord your God lives, there is no nation or kingdom where my lord has not sent men seeking you; and when all replied, ‘He is not here,’ he adjured each kingdom and nation, because you could not be found. And now you say to me: ‘Go and tell your lord: “Elijah is here.”’ When I leave you, the spirit of the Lord will carry you to a place that I do not know. I will enter and report to [Col. 0586D] Ahab, and, if he does not find you, he will kill me. Yet your servant has feared the Lord from his childhood.

“Has it not been reported to my lord what I did when Jezebel was killing the prophets of the Lord—how I hid a hundred of the Lord’s prophets, by fifties in caves, and fed them with bread and water? And now you say: ‘Go and tell your lord: “Elijah is here,”’ so that he may kill me?”

And Elijah said: “As the Lord of hosts lives, before whose face I stand, today I shall appear to him.”

So Obadiah went to meet Ahab and told him. And Ahab came to meet Elijah. When he saw him, he said: “Are you the one who troubles Israel?” He answered: “It is not I who have troubled Israel, but you and your father’s house, because you have abandoned the commandments of the Lord and followed the Baals. [Col. 0587A] Nevertheless, now send and gather all Israel to me on Mount Carmel, together with the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal and the four hundred prophets of the groves, who eat at Jezebel’s table.”

Ahab sent to all the children of Israel and gathered the prophets on Mount Carmel. Elijah approached all the people of Israel and said: “How long will you limp between two sides? If the Lord is God, follow him; but if Baal is God, follow him.” And the people did not answer him a word. 349

Elijah said again to the people: “I alone have remained a prophet of the Lord; but the prophets of Baal are four hundred and fifty men, and the prophets of the groves are four hundred. Let two oxen be given to us. Let them choose one ox for themselves, [Col. 0587B] cut it into pieces, and place it upon the wood, but let them not put fire beneath it. I shall prepare the other ox and place it upon the wood, but I shall not put fire beneath it. Call upon the names of your gods, and I shall call upon the name of my God; and the God who answers by fire—he shall be God.”

All the people answered: “This is an excellent proposal, which Elijah has spoken.”

Then Elijah said to the prophets of Baal: “Choose one ox for yourselves and prepare it first, because you are more numerous; and call upon the names of your gods, but do not put fire beneath it.”

So they took the ox that had been given to them and prepared it. And they called upon the name of Baal from morning until midday, saying: “Baal, hear us!” But there was neither voice nor anyone who answered. And they leapt around the altar that they had made. [Col. 0587C]

When it was already midday, Elijah mocked them, saying: “Cry out with a louder voice! For he is a god, and perhaps he is speaking, or is staying in an inn, or is on a journey, or at least he is asleep and must be awakened.”

So they cried out with a loud voice and cut themselves with knives and lances according to their rite, until they were covered with blood. After midday had passed, and while they were prophesying, the time had come when the sacrifice is usually offered; but there was neither voice nor answer, and no one attended to those praying.

Elijah said to all the people: “Come to me.” When the people approached him, he repaired the altar of the Lord that had been destroyed. He took twelve stones, according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Jacob, to whom the word of the Lord had come, saying: “Israel shall be your name.” And he built an altar from the stones in the name of the [Col. 0587D] Lord. He made a channel, as if for two little ploughings, around the altar, and arranged the wood. He divided the ox into pieces and placed it upon the wood.

Then he said: “Fill four jars with water and pour it over the burnt offering and over the wood.” Again he said: “Do this a second time.” When they had done it a second time, he said: “Do the same thing a third time.” They did it a third time, and the water ran around the altar, and the channel was filled with water.

When it was already the time for the burnt offering to be presented, the prophet Elijah approached and said: “Lord God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, show today that you are God in Israel, and that I am your servant, and that I have done all these things according to your command. Hear me, Lord, hear me, so that this [Col. 0588A] people may learn that you are the Lord God, and that you have turned their heart back again.”

Then the fire of the Lord fell and consumed the burnt offering, the wood, and the stones and dust; it also licked up the water that was in the channel. When all the people saw this, they fell upon their faces and said: “The Lord himself is God! The Lord himself is God!”

Elijah said to them: “Seize the prophets of Baal, and let not one of them escape.” When they had seized them, Elijah led them to the brook Kishon and killed them there.

R. Amen.

**Antiphon 1.** If I walk in the midst of tribulation, you will revive me; and against the anger of my enemies you have stretched out your hand, and your right hand has saved me.

V. The Lord will repay for me; Lord, your mercy is forever. Do not despise the works of your hands. [Col. 0588B]

**Prayer.** If we walk in the midst of our tribulation, Lord, revive us; and against the anger of our enemies send forth your hand, and deliver us by your right hand—you who conquered the world through the unconquerable sign of your Cross—so that, remarkably delivered through you from the airy powers of this world, we may seek the innermost places of heaven in triumph and rejoicing.

R. Amen.

**Antiphon 2.** Place my tears in your sight, O Lord; may my enemies turn back, and I shall know that you are my God.

V. On whatever day I call upon you, hear me swiftly. You have multiplied my soul in strength; behold, I have known that you are my God.

**Prayer.** Place before your sight, O Lord, against those [Col. 0588C] who hate us, the barriers of our tears, so that at last our enemies, who persecute us with insane hatred, may turn back. And so, we ask, may the abundance of tears extinguish the fires of our guilt, so that the celebration of your Passion may draw us, walking along the narrow way, toward endless joys.

R. Amen.

**Antiphon 3.** Deliver me, O Lord, from the snare of an evil tongue and from lips that work deceit. Deliver me from those who roar, prepared for prey, and from the hand of those seeking my life.

V. To the Lord I cried when I was in tribulation, and he heard me. 350

**Hymn.** O Nazarene. Folio 144.

**Prayer.** Christ, the undivided offspring of God the Father, who, having assumed humanity, endured the snares of an evil tongue: [Col. 0588D] deliver your Church from the enticements of every affliction; preserve her unharmed from the harmfulness of slanderous lips, so that, freed from those who roar—that is, from the servants of diabolical power—she may cling gloriously to you in the heavenly court.

Our Father.

**Laud.** The Lord is my illumination and my salvation.

**Antiphon.** Call upon me in the day of tribulation; I will deliver you, and you will glorify me.

**Psalm XLIX.**

**Laud.** May your mercy, O Lord, come upon us, together with your salvation and your word.

V. And I shall answer those who reproach me with a word, because I have hoped in your words.

[Col. 0589A]

**Hymn.** You are called to life. Folio 334.

**Capitulum.** God, author of light. Folio 343.
