## Wednesday

### At Matins

**Antiphon.** Save me, my God, for you have struck down all those who oppose me without cause; you have shattered the teeth of sinners.

**Psalm III.**

**Prayer.** After our rest, Lord, make our confession worthy of your sight, so that, just as our resurrection has taken its beginning from you, so our life may receive its reward from you, and our frailty may be fortified by your help. May the thousands of enemies surrounding us with savage roaring be scattered by your judgment, crushed by your regard, and wounded by your arrows. [Col. 0589B] And may the people created by you, redeemed by you, and received from you, always hasten toward you through the merit of faith and holy service; may it often rise in your courts to praise you.

R. Amen.

**Antiphon 1.** I have set my face like the hardest rock, and I know that I shall not be put to shame, for he who justifies me is near.

V. Deliver me from my enemies, my God, and free me from those who rise up against me.

**Prayer.** Christ God, who, coming to free the world in the flesh, set your face like the hardest rock: raise us up by the example of your Passion and surround us with the protection of the Cross, so that unbelief, confounded through you, may perish, and faithfulness, crowned by you, may come again to its reward.

R. Amen.

**Antiphon 2.** Gather my enemies, O Lord, [Col. 0589C] like a flock for sacrifice; sanctify them on the day of slaughter, for they have said: “He will not see our end.”

V. Lord, hear my prayer, and let my cry come to you. Do not turn your face from me.

**Prayer.** Gather your enemies, O Lord, like a flock for sacrifice, so that either, coming to their senses, they may return to forgiveness, or, persisting in evil, may waste away under the judgment of eternity. Thus may you alone, who were offered to the Father as a pure victim for us, make us victorious over our guilt.

R. Amen.

**Antiphon 3.** Do not turn your ear from my sobbing and cries, Lord my God. Draw near in the day of tribulation and say to my soul: “Do not fear.” See, O Lord, their iniquities against [Col. 0589D] me; judge my judgment.

**Prayer.** Do not turn your ear from our sobbing, O Lord, nor remove your gaze from a contrite heart; but draw near to help your Church, so that the one who is conformed to your sufferings may also be consoled by your gifts.

R. Amen.

**R.** All my adversaries have persecuted me and have not been satisfied. Behold, my words shall be written with a stylus and placed in a book, to stand as testimony: I know that it is eternal.

P. He who abandoned me upon the earth. My flesh, which suffers these things, shall rise again.

V. The Lord God opened my ear, but I did not resist. Behold, God is my helper.

P. He who.

[Col. 0590A]

**Prayer.** Almighty Son of God, Christ, whose words are recognized as written with an iron stylus—that is, with the strong judgment of the Fathers—soften upon the hardest rock, namely, the hearts of the nations, all the hearts of the members of your Church; write their names with your holy stylus upon the page of the book of life, so that they may be free from natural swelling and shine with the grace of true humility.

R. Amen.

### At Lauds

**Antiphon.** For your sake, O God, turn your face away from my sins, and blot out all my iniquities. For I was conceived in iniquities, and my mother bore me in sins.

**Psalm L.**

351 **Prayer.** Acknowledging in ourselves. Folio 259.

**Antiphon.** The Lord is with me like a strong warrior; therefore those who persecute me shall fall and become weak. They shall be utterly confounded, because they have not understood everlasting disgrace.

**Canticle.** You have seduced me, O Lord. Folio 276.

**Prayer.** Lord God, strong warrior and Redeemer of the human race, who, enduring the winepress of the Passion, are recognized as having trampled even the winepress in which you are the treader, while you also rise from death and show those who persecuted you falling and becoming weak: grant us, amid your sufferings, both to embrace bitterness with joy and to rejoice more abundantly, so that while unbelief torments the faithless, conversion may free the faithful from iniquity.

R. Amen.

**Matutinal responsory.** In the morning I shall meditate upon you, for you have been my helper, O Lord.

V. My God, my God, [Col. 0590C] to you I keep watch from the light of dawn.

**Laud.** Praise the Lord in his holy places.

**Reading from the Book of Malachim (Third Book of Kings, chapter XVIII).**

R. Thanks be to God.

In those days Elijah said to Ahab: “Go up, eat and drink, for there is the sound of abundant rain.” Ahab went up to eat and drink, but Elijah went up to the summit of Carmel. Bending down to the earth, he placed his face between his knees and said to his servant: “Go up and look toward the sea.” When he had gone up and looked, he said: “There is nothing.” Again he said to him: “Return seven times.”

On the seventh occasion, behold, a small cloud, like a man’s footprint, was rising from the sea. Elijah said: “Go up and tell Ahab: ‘Harness your chariot and go down, [Col. 0590D] lest the rain overtake you.’”

While he turned this way and that, behold, the heavens grew dark with clouds and wind, and there was a great rain. Ahab mounted and went to Jezreel. The hand of the Lord was upon Elijah, and, girding his loins, he ran before Ahab until he came to Jezreel.

**Chapter XIX.** Ahab reported to Jezebel all that Elijah had done and how he had killed all the prophets of Baal with the sword. Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah, saying: “May the gods do these things to me and add even more, unless by this time tomorrow I make your life like the life of one of them.”

So Elijah was afraid, and, rising, went wherever his will led him. He came to Beersheba of Judah, left his servant there, and went on into the wilderness, a day’s journey. [Col. 0591A] When he had arrived and sat beneath a juniper tree, he asked that his soul might die and said: “It is enough, Lord; take my life, for I am no better than my fathers.”

He threw himself down and fell asleep in the shade of the juniper tree. And behold, an angel of the Lord touched him and said: “Rise and eat.” He looked, and behold, at his head was a hearth-cake and a vessel of water. He ate and drank, and again fell asleep.

The angel of the Lord returned a second time, touched him, and said: “Rise and eat, for a great journey remains for you.” When he had risen, he ate and drank, and he walked in the strength of that food for forty days and forty nights, as far as Mount Horeb, the mountain of God.

When he had come there, he stayed in a cave. And behold, the word [Col. 0591B] of the Lord came to him and said: “What are you doing here, Elijah?” He answered: “I have been very zealous for the Lord God of hosts, because the children of Israel have abandoned your covenant; they have destroyed your altars, killed your prophets with the sword, and I alone have been left, and they seek my life to take it away.”

And he said to him: “Go out and stand on the mountain before the Lord.” And behold, the Lord passed by, and a great and strong wind overturned mountains and shattered rocks before the Lord. The Lord was not in the wind. After the wind came an earthquake; the Lord was not in the earthquake. After the earthquake came a fire; the Lord was not in the fire. After the fire came the sound of a gentle breeze.

When Elijah heard this, he covered his face with his cloak and went out and stood at the entrance of the cave. And behold, a voice came to him, saying: “What are you doing [Col. 0591C] here, Elijah?” He answered: “I have been very zealous for the Lord God of hosts, because the children of Israel have abandoned your covenant; they have destroyed your altars and killed your prophets with the sword, and I alone have been left, and they seek my life to take it away.”

And the Lord said to him: “Go and return by your way through the wilderness to Damascus. When you have arrived there, you shall anoint Hazael as king over Syria; and Jehu son of Nimshi you shall anoint as king over Israel; and Elisha son of Shaphat, who is from Abel-meholah, you shall anoint as prophet in your place. And whoever escapes the sword of Hazael, Jehu shall kill; and whoever escapes the sword of Jehu, Elisha shall kill. [Col. 0591D] And I shall leave seven thousand men for myself in Israel, whose knees have not bowed before Baal and whose mouth has not kissed him by kissing his hand.”

So Elijah departed from there and found Elisha son of Shaphat plowing with twelve yoke of oxen; and he himself was one of the twelve pairs of oxen plowing. When Elijah came to him, he cast his cloak over him. Immediately leaving the oxen, he ran after Elijah and said: “Let me kiss, I beg you, my father and my mother, and then I will follow you.”

He said to him: “Go and return; for what was mine, I have done for you.” Returning from him, Elisha took a yoke of oxen, slaughtered it, boiled the flesh with the wood of the oxen’s plow, and gave it to the people, and they ate. Then he rose, went away, followed Elijah, and ministered to him.

R. Amen.

**Hymn.** The time of night. Folio 257.

[Col. 0592A]

**Capitulum.** You are just, O Lord, who, though innocent, were unjustly judged for us; and therefore we ask that you, who were punished without your own guilt, absolve us from our crime.

Our Father.

**Laud.** Establish for them, O Lord, the law—the way of your justice—and may they always seek it.

V. Give me understanding, and I shall examine your law and keep it with my whole heart.

**Prayer.** Incline our heart to your testimonies, O Lord, and turn it away from the perverse gaze of vanity, so that you may separate us from earthly love and unite us to heavenly love.

### At Terce

**From the Proverbs of Solomon (chapter XVII).**

[Col. 0592B]

R. Thanks be to God.

My son, whoever despises the poor reproaches his Maker; and whoever rejoices in another’s ruin shall not go unpunished. Whoever repays evil for good shall not see evil depart from his house. Whoever justifies the wicked and whoever condemns the just are both detestable before God.

What benefit is it for a fool to possess riches when he cannot acquire wisdom? Whoever is a friend loves at all times, and a brother is proved in adversity. A foolish man claps his hands when he has given surety for his friend. Whoever devises disputes loves quarrels, and whoever exalts his heart seeks ruin. Whoever is crooked of heart will find no good, and whoever twists his tongue will fall into evil. The wicked man receives gifts from the bosom, to pervert the paths of the just.

It is not good [Col. 0592C] to harm the just, nor to strike a ruler who judges rightly. Whoever wishes to withdraw from a friend seeks pretexts; he will be reproachable at all times. The words of the just are deep water, and an overflowing torrent is a fountain of wisdom.

R. Amen.

**Reading from the Prophet Isaiah (chapter LXIII).**

R. Thanks be to God.

Thus says the Lord: “Who is this who comes from Edom, with garments dyed from Bozrah? This one is beautiful in his robe, proceeding in the greatness of his strength.”

“I am the one who speak justice, and I am a defender for saving. Why, then, is your garment red, and your clothing like that of those who tread in the winepress?”

“I have trodden the winepress alone, and of the nations there was no man with me. I trod them [Col. 0592D] in my fury and trampled them in my anger. Their blood was sprinkled upon my garments, and I stained all my clothing. For the day of vengeance was in my heart; the year of my redemption has come.

“I looked around, and there was no helper. I sought, and there was no one to assist. My own arm saved me, and my indignation itself came to my aid. I trampled peoples in my fury, intoxicated them with my indignation, and brought their strength down to the earth.

“I shall remember the mercies of the Lord, the praise of the Lord for all that the Lord has repaid us, and for the abundance of good things granted to the house of Israel according to his clemency and the multitude of his mercies.”

And he said: “Yet [Col. 0593A] they are my people, children who do not deny.” And he became their savior. In all their tribulation he was not afflicted, and the angel of his presence saved them. In his love and clemency he himself redeemed them, carried them, and lifted them up all the days of eternity.

R. Amen.

**Antiphon 1.** The enemy has closed my way, and my soul is troubled with sorrow; help me, my God.

V. Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man; from the unjust man and the deceitful tongue free me.

**Prayer.** Christ, power of God and wisdom of God, while the ancient enemy strives to close your ways by persecution, he is wonderfully trampled by you, who are the Way. Therefore, we ask, surround us with your grace, so that we may neither be confined in the way of sinners by the obstacle of the ancient enemy, nor, [Col. 0593B] with your help, run again with an expanded heart along the paths of your will.

R. Amen.

**Antiphon 2.** I shall always see vengeance upon my enemies. They have placed a burden upon my neck; see, O Lord, and judge; do not abandon me.

V. Judge, O Lord, those who harm me, and fight against those who fight against me. 353

**Prayer.** Rise, O God, and judge the earth mercifully—you who were judged for us on earth; who, condemned, absolve the guilty; who, dying, give life to the dead; who, rising again, strengthen the doubtful and confound the wicked. May the nations be called into your inheritance through faith, confessing that you rose again for the salvation of the faithful.

R. Amen.

**Antiphon 3.** They devised evil against my soul [Col. 0593C] and concealed their sins. Remember that I stood before your face and spoke good things on their behalf.

V. Suddenly the envious enemy wounded me, and my bones were reduced to nothing.

P. But you, O Lord.

Let there be no Gloria.

[Col. 0593D]

**Prayers.** You, good shepherd, who laid down your life for the sheep, remember us.

P. Be appeased and have mercy.

V. Everlasting power, wisdom of the Most High God, Word of the Father, remember us.

P. Be appeased.

V. Creator of all things, life of all, ruler of angels, remember us.

P. Be appeased.

P. Be appeased.

P. Be appeased.

**Hymn.** O Nazarene. Folio 144.

**Capitulum.** You patiently endure the evils devised against your soul, O Christ, so that, as shepherd, you might offer your own good example to your flocks; you endure the arrows of your persecutors and plead with the Father for your persecutors. [Col. 0594A] Grant us, therefore, to be cleansed from our own sufferings through the sacrament of your Passion, so that you, who endured those who blasphemed you with the greatest patience, may rescue those who believe in you from the eternal condemnation of judgment.

### At Sext

**Reading from the Book of the Prophet Jeremiah (chapter X).**

R. Thanks be to God.

Thus says the Lord: “Behold, this time I shall cast the inhabitants of the land far away, and I shall afflict them so that they will not be found.

“Woe is me because of my destruction, my grievous wound. But I said: ‘Truly, this is my weakness, and I shall bear it.’ My tabernacle has been laid waste; all my cords have been torn apart. [Col. 0594B] My children have gone out from me, and they do not remain. There is no one who will extend my tent further and raise up my skins.

“For the shepherds have acted foolishly and have not sought the Lord. Therefore they have not understood, and their entire flock has been scattered. Behold, the sound of a report comes, and a great disturbance from the land of the north, to make the cities of Judah a desolation and a dwelling-place of dragons.

**Chapter XI.** Hear the words of this covenant, and speak them to the men of Judah and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem. And you shall say to them: Thus says the Lord God of Israel: Cursed is the man who does not hear the words of this covenant, which I commanded your fathers on the day when I brought them out of the land of Egypt, from the iron furnace, saying: Hear my voice and do all that I have commanded you, and you shall be my people, [Col. 0594C] and I shall be your God.”

R. Amen.

**Antiphon 1.** May the Lord increase his people and multiply them among many thousands of peoples.

V. Let them confess to the Lord his mercies and his wonders to the children of men.

**Prayer.** Increase your people greatly, O Lord, and exalt them either in merits or in possessions, so that, though we are bitten by the teeth of the envious, we may always stand more happily through your favor.

R. Amen.

**Antiphon 2.** Let them rejoice, O Lord, over your words, like one who finds abundant spoils.

V. And let them sacrifice the sacrifice of praise and declare his works with rejoicing.

**Prayer.** Let them rejoice, O Lord, over your words, which [Col. 0594D] are sweeter than honey and the honeycomb; may they not bring us merely temporal love, but may they always lead us joyfully toward heavenly delight.

R. Amen.

**Antiphon 3.** Your testimony, O Lord, which is faithful, gives wisdom to the little ones.

V. The judgments of the Lord are right, making hearts rejoice.

**Prayer.** May we become heirs of your testimonies, O Lord, which have been made credible to us. May they be constant in our meditation, just as they are sincere in the truth of faith; and may they be completed in our works just as they are spoken by our mouths. May they govern mourners with consolation and make those who hear them more ready for you.

R. Amen.

**R.** Direct their steps, O God, along your paths.

P. So that their footsteps may not be moved.

V. The declaration of your words gives light and gives understanding to the little ones.

P. So that.

[Col. 0595A]

**Prayers.**

Lord, hear, save, and deliver me.

P. Lord.

V. May my prayer rise to you, O God, and deliver me.

P. Lord.

V. Do not turn your face from me, but deliver me.

P. Lord.

V. They have devised things against me; do not abandon me, but deliver me.

P. Lord.

V. For you are my God and my helper; you help me.

P. Lord.

V. May your exalted hand rescue me and protect me.

P. Lord.

V. Stand by me always for help and deliver me.

P. Lord.

V. Behold, now my sorrow has overwhelmed me; deliver me now.

P. Lord.

V. My spirit has grown faint within me; revive me.

P. Lord.

V. My limbs have been reduced to nothing; restore me now.

P. Lord.

[Col. 0595B]

V. My enemies have filled up their fury; rescue me.

P. Lord.

V. They have gnashed their teeth against me; deliver me.

P. Lord.

V. They have opened their mouths against me; guard me.

P. Lord.

V. May my prayer stand before you, O God, and hear me.

P. Lord.

V. May my cry come to you, and hear me.

P. Lord.

V. May your power rescue the afflicted and protect me.

**Hymn.** O Nazarene, light. Folio 144.

[Col. 0595D]

**Capitulum.** Strengthen our steps, O Lord, along your paths, so that as we walk in your way, your mercies may help us and protect us in temptations; so that when your justice appears, we may appear before you without shame and be filled with your glory without shame.

Our Father.

### At Vespers

[Col. 0595C]

**Laud.** In the evening, morning, and at midday we praise you, O Lord.

**Antiphon.** Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man, and free me from the unjust man.

**Psalm CXXXIX.**

**Laud.** Do not be silent, O God, my praise, for the mouth of the wicked has surrounded me and they have fought against me without cause.

**Hymn.**

Now the shadow of the law is closed,  
and the new Passover has appeared;  
when the true light, rising over the evening,  
shines forth upon the world.

From here, O Christ the King, after two days,  
you will celebrate the banquet of the Supper,  
by which the former mystical Passover  
is transformed into our Passover.

Hear the prayers of the faithful,  
you who endured the betrayer;  
illumine us on this night,  
wash the flesh and prepare the heart.

May the ardor of your sweetness  
set our inward parts ablaze;  
may faith renew those who are prepared,  
and may our work call us to the kingdom.

So that, invited from here  
by the sweetness of grace,  
we may tomorrow be intoxicated  
with cups of your consecrated blood.

[Col. 0596A]

To God the Father be glory,  
and to his only Son,  
with the Spirit, the Paraclete,  
who reigns throughout every age.

Amen.

**Capitulum.** As your devoted people receive the solemn rites of your approaching Passion, O Christ God, they desire to be prepared as a living offering for you. Therefore we ask that, since tomorrow we are to approach your banquet, you grant that in receiving this venerable night we may be free from the darkness of guilt and set aflame with the fire of your love.

Our Father.

**Blessing.** May the Passion preserve us by everlasting right.

R. Amen.

May it wash us from crime today and enrich us tomorrow with its gift. [Col. 0596B]

R. Amen.

So that, with vices driven away, you may celebrate Easter with him.

R. Amen.

**Laud.** Establish for them the law, O Lord. Folio 352.

## Thursday

### At Matins

**Antiphon.** God, you have struck down all those who oppose me without cause; you have shattered the teeth of sinners.

**Psalm III.**

**Prayer.** Lord, our glory and our head, raise us up so that we may not be drowned in the whirlpool of vices; and lift us up so that manifold tribulation may not bend us. With you helping us, neither the multitude of those who afflict us shall harm us, nor shall the pride of those rising against us remain unbroken. Pour your blessing, therefore, upon the peoples, you who are the author and defender of our salvation.

R. Amen.

[Col. 0596C]

**Antiphon 1.** You showed me, O Lord, and I understood. Like a gentle lamb I was led to the sacrifice, and now I have understood that they devised plans against me.

V. And you, O Lord, will laugh at them and hold all the nations as nothing. Let there be no Gloria.

**Prayer.** Like a gentle lamb handed over for us, O Lord, you were led to the sacrifice, certainly without sin or fault. Grant us, therefore, to attain the innocence of the lamb, so that we may live with you forever without end.

R. Amen.

**Antiphon 2.** My inheritance has become for me like a lion in the forest; it has raised its voice against me.

V. For those whom you established have destroyed; but the just one—what has he done? Let there be no Gloria.

[Col. 0596D]

**Prayer.** Christ, Son of God, whose inheritance became for you like a lion in the forest, crying out against you in a cruel manner so that you might be crucified: fill us with the infusion of the Holy Spirit, so that, fervent with the fire of charity, we may direct the cry of an innocent voice to the hearing of your omnipotence and strive with all our strength to lay down our souls for our brothers.

R. Amen.

**Antiphon 3.** I did not sit in their council while they played, but I feared their presence. I sat alone, because I was filled with bitterness.

V. I hated the assemblies of the wicked, and I shall not sit with the impious. Let there be no Gloria.

**Prayer.** Only-begotten Son of God, who, appearing in the flesh to die, did not sit in the council of those who played, but sat [Col. 0597A] alone, filled with bitterness for us: grant us, in no way ashamed of your sufferings, to deserve to share in your glory without end.

R. Amen.

**R.** “The one who has put his hand with me in the dish—he is the one who will betray me today.”

P. Woe to the man through whom the Son of Man will be betrayed. It would have been good for that man if he had not been born.

V. The Lord Jesus Christ spoke to his disciples, saying: “Rise, let us go. Behold, the one who will betray me is drawing near.”

P. Woe to the man.

Let there be no Gloria.

**Prayer.** Christ, Son of God, who, about to pass from this world to the Father, foretold your betrayer by a special sign, so that he would not merely remain hidden among the [Col. 0597B] others but rather be distinguished from them: we ask and entreat you that we, who have been redeemed by your precious blood, may not be cut off from the member of the Church; and that no one established in your Church may fall into torpor. Instead, may we be summoned to glory by the glorious examples of your patience, imitating in nothing the aims of your betrayer, but receiving both the teaching and the rewards of the good disciples.

R. Amen.

**Antiphon.** Do not despise a contrite and humbled heart, O God; but graciously act, I beg you, and have mercy on me, God, have mercy.

**Psalm L.**

**Prayer.** The secrets of our heart. Folio 210.

**At the Canticle. Antiphon.** Just judge, O Lord, who tests hearts and reins, let me, I beg, see vengeance upon my enemies, for I have revealed my cause to you.

[Col. 0597C]

**Canticle.** You have seduced me, O Lord. Folio 276.

**Prayer.** Just judge, O God, who recognize that the cause of your Son, revealed to you—the injury of his Passion—is to be punished in the unbelieving, let us, we ask, see vengeance upon his enemies, so that either, turning back from unbelief, they may punish themselves through repentance, or, persisting in faithlessness, may be punished by the justice of him whose manifest mercy they now despise.

R. Amen.

**Matutinal responsory.** But I shall sing of your power, O Lord, and I shall exalt your mercy in the morning, for you have become my protector, O Lord.

V. Deliver me from my enemies, my God, and free me from those who rise up against me.

**Laud.** The mountains and all the hills praise you; the rulers and all the judges of the earth praise you; all the angels [Col. 0597D] praise you together. Praise.

**Reading from the Book of Malachim (Fourth Book of Kings, chapter VI).**

R. Thanks be to God.

In those days: Ben-hadad, king of Syria, gathered his entire army, went up, and besieged Samaria. And a great famine arose in Samaria, and it was besieged so long that a donkey’s head was sold for eighty pieces of silver, and a quarter-cab of dove’s dung for five pieces of silver. As the king of Israel was passing along the wall, a certain woman cried out to him, saying, “Save me, my lord the king.” He replied, “If the Lord does not save you, from where can I save you? From the threshing floor, or from the winepress?” And the king said to her, [Col. 0598A] “What is the matter with you?” She answered: “This woman said to me, ‘Give your son, so that we may eat him today, and we will eat my son tomorrow.’ So we cooked my son and ate him; and I said to her the next day, ‘Give your son, so that we may eat him.’ But she hid her son.” When the king heard this, he tore his garments and was passing along the wall. And all the people saw the haircloth with which he was clothed underneath, next to his flesh. And the king said, “May God do this to me, and may he add this also, if the head of Elisha son of Shaphat remains on him today.”

Now Elisha was sitting in his house, and the elders were sitting with him. So he sent a man ahead; and before that messenger arrived, he said to the elders: “Do you know that this son of a murderer has sent someone here to cut off my head? Therefore watch: when the messenger comes, [Col. 0598B] shut the door and do not let him enter; for, behold, the sound of his master’s feet is behind him.” While he was still speaking with them, the messenger appeared, coming toward him. And he said: “Behold, this great evil is from the Lord; what more shall I expect from the Lord?”

(Cap. VII.) But Elisha said: “Hear the word of the Lord: thus says the Lord: At this time tomorrow, a measure of fine flour will be sold for one shekel, and two measures of barley for one shekel, at the gate of Samaria.” One of the officers, on whose hand the king leaned, answered the man of God and said: “Even if the Lord were to make floodgates in heaven, could what you say possibly happen?” He said: “You shall see it with your eyes, but you shall not eat of it.”

Now there were four leprous men near the entrance of the gate, and they said to one another: “Why should we remain here until we die? If we wish to enter [Col. 0598C] the city, we shall die of famine; if we remain here, we must die. Come, then, let us desert to the camp of Syria. If they spare us, we shall live; but if they wish to kill us, we shall die nevertheless.” So they rose at evening to go to the camp of Syria. When they had come to the beginning of the Syrian camp, they found no one there. For the Lord had caused the sound of chariots and horses and a very great army to be heard; and they said to one another: “Behold, the king of Israel has hired against us the kings of the Hittites and the Egyptians, and they have come against us.” So they rose and fled in the darkness, abandoning their tents, horses, donkeys, and mules in the camp; and they fled, wishing only to save their lives.

When those lepers had reached the beginning [Col. 0598D] of the camp, they entered one tent, ate and drank, and took silver, gold, and clothing from it; then they went away and hid them. They returned again to another tent, and, taking things from it in the same way, hid them. Then they said to one another: “We are not doing right. This day is a day of good news. If we remain silent and do not announce it until morning, we shall be charged with wrongdoing. Come, let us go and report it in the king’s court.”

When they came to the gate of the city, they told them, saying: “We went to the camp of Syria, and found no one there except horses and donkeys tied up, and the tents standing.” So the gatekeepers went and reported it inside the king’s palace. He rose by night and said to his servants, [Col. 0599A] “I will tell you what the Syrians have done to us. They know that we are suffering from famine, and therefore they have gone out from the camp and are hiding in the fields, saying, ‘When they have gone out from the city, we shall seize them alive, and then we shall be able to enter the city.’”

But one of his servants answered: “Let us take five horses that have remained in the city—for they alone are left among the entire multitude of Israel, since the others have been consumed—and, sending them out, we shall be able to reconnoiter.” So they brought out two horses, and the king sent them into the Syrian camp, saying: “Go and see.” They went after them as far as the Jordan; and behold, the whole way was full of clothing and vessels that the Syrians had thrown away in their panic. The messengers returned and reported this to the king. And the people went out and plundered the camp of Syria; and a measure of fine flour was sold for one shekel, and two measures of barley for [Col. 0599B] one shekel, according to the word of the Lord.

Moreover, the king appointed that officer, on whose hand he had leaned, at the gate; but the crowd trampled him at the entrance of the gate, and he died, according to what the man of God had spoken.

R. Amen.

Hymn. “The Time of Night.” fol. 257.

Capitulum. Christ, Son of God, whom God the Father delivered up for us all, when he himself accepted you as the true sacrifice for us: receive the desire of your people; save those whom you redeemed; give life to those whom you liberated; do not allow those whom you came to redeem, lest they perish forever, to go away into perpetual mourning. Pierce our heart with the nails of your fear—you who for us all endured both the cross and the tomb—so that through you there may be for us here forgiveness of sins and, in the future, everlasting joy; [Col. 0599C] for we believe you to have been crucified for all.

Our Father.

Lauda. “Give them understanding, O Lord, that they may learn your commandments.” V. “Lead me in the law of your commandments, for I have desired it.”

Prayer. Grant us, O Lord, to grasp the equity of your testimonies with a more eager understanding, so that what folly mortifies in us may be brought to life by the wisdom appointed by you.

R. Amen.

At Terce.

From the Proverbs of Solomon (Cap. I).

R. Thanks be to God.

My son, hear the discipline of your father, and do not forsake the law of your mother, so that grace may be added to your head and a necklace to your [Col. 0599D] neck. My son, if sinners entice you, do not consent to them. If they say, “Come with us; let us lie in wait for blood; let us hide snares for the innocent without cause; let us swallow him alive like the underworld, and whole, as one descending into a pit. We shall find every precious substance; we shall fill our houses with spoils. Cast in your lot with us; let there be one purse for all of us.” My son, do not walk with them; restrain your foot from their paths. For their feet run toward evil and hasten to shed blood. But a net is cast in vain before the eyes of birds. They themselves also lie in wait for their own blood and devise frauds against their own lives.

(Cap. II.) My son, if wisdom enters your heart and knowledge pleases your soul, [Col. 0600A] counsel will guard you and prudence will preserve you, so that you may be delivered from the evil way and from the man who speaks perversely; from those who abandon the straight path and walk along dark roads; who rejoice when they have done evil and exult in the worst deeds; whose ways are crooked and whose steps are infamous.

(Cap. VII.) Keep, my son, my commandments, and you shall live; and keep my law as the apple of your eye.

R. Amen.

Reading from the Book of the Prophet Isaiah (Cap. L).

R. Thanks be to God.

“What is this bill of divorce of your mother, by which I dismissed her? Or who is my creditor, to whom I sold you? Behold, you were sold because of your iniquities, and because of your crimes I dismissed your mother. For I came, and there was no man; I called, and there was no one who would hear. Has my hand become shortened and [Col. 0600B] reduced, so that I could not redeem? Or is there no strength in me to deliver? Behold, at my rebuke I shall make the sea desolate; I shall turn rivers into dry land. The fish shall putrefy for lack of water and die of thirst. I shall clothe the heavens with darkness and make sackcloth their covering.

“The Lord God has given me a learned tongue, so that I may know how to sustain with a word one who has fallen.” Morning by morning he awakens; morning by morning he awakens my ear, so that I may hear like a teacher. The Lord God has opened my ear, and I do not resist; I have not turned back. I gave my body to those who struck me, and my cheeks to those who pulled them out. I did not turn my face away from those who rebuked me and spat upon me. The Lord God is my helper; therefore I have not been confounded. Therefore I set my face [Col. 0600C] like the hardest stone, and I know that I shall not be ashamed. He is near who justifies me; who will contradict me? Let us stand together; who is my adversary? Let him approach me. Behold, the Lord God is my helper; who is he who will condemn me? Behold, they shall all be worn away like a garment; the moth shall consume them.

“Who among you fears the Lord and hears the voice of his servant?”

(Cap. XLI.) Thus says the Lord: “Behold, all who fight against you shall be confounded and put to shame; they shall be as though they did not exist, and the men who oppose you shall perish. You shall seek them, and you shall not find your rebellious men; they shall be as though they did not exist, and the men warring against you shall be like complete destruction. For I am the Lord your God, holding your hand and saying to you: ‘Do not fear; I have helped you,’ says the Lord [Col. 0600D] Almighty.”

R. Amen.

Antiphon 3. “They said within themselves, thinking evil: ‘This man declares blessed the end of the righteous and boasts that he has God as his father. Let us see whether his words are true, and let us test what will happen to him. For if he is truly the Son of God, he will receive him and deliver him from the hands of his adversaries.’” V. “And they entered in, to see that their heart had spoken vanity; they gathered iniquity for themselves. And they went out and spoke.” Let “Glory” not be said.

Prayer. Christ, Son of God, who patiently endured against yourself the evil thoughts and bloody counsels of the wicked: grant us, following your example, to have a patient heart and to overcome adversaries with equal endurance, so that [Col. 0601A] we who acknowledge you to have God as Father may be saved by faith in this knowledge, and that we who recall the days of your passion may be cleansed from the filth of our own sufferings.

R. Amen.

Antiphon 2. “The Lord Jesus Christ spoke to his disciples, saying: ‘Rise, let us go; behold, the one who will betray me is approaching.’” V. “For even the man of my peace, in whom I trusted, who ate my bread, has magnified his treachery against me.”

Prayer. Christ, Son of God, who, specifically commanding your disciples before you were betrayed, ordered them to rise: grant us, we ask, steadfastness in enduring wicked people and that we may hold fast to the examples of patience, so that, learning from you how meek and humble you are in heart, we may share in the example of your sufferings [Col. 0601B] and obtain the assistance of eternal blessedness.

R. Amen.

Antiphon 3. “Behold, the hour is coming when you will be scattered and will leave me alone; but I am not alone, because the Father is with me. Take courage: I have conquered the world.” V. “For if my enemy had cursed me, I would surely have endured it; and if the one who hated me had spoken great things against me, I would surely have hidden myself from him.”

R. “The one who ate my bread with me has lifted his heel against me. But you, O Lord, have mercy on me and raise me up.” V. “Behold, he has betrayed me, the one whom I loved, and has struck me with a cruel wound. Now, O God, bring healing to my wound.” P. “And raise me up.” Let “Glory” not be said.

Prayers. “We cry out to you, O God; hear us.” P. “And [Col. 0601C] deliver us from the scourge of your wrath.” V. “O Holy Redeemer, who were handed over to death, give life to the flock that you redeemed with your blood.” P. “And from the scourge.” V. “You who are scourged by the impious and wicked, who are given vinegar to drink, deliver us from future evils.” P. “And from the scourge.” V. “You who bear a crown of thorns upon your head, so that you may cleanse us, your members, from the thorns of our sins.” P. “And from the scourge.” V. “May your voice now intercede with the Father for us—the voice that cried out on the Cross so that it might assist those who were ignorant.” P. “And from the scourge.” V. “Save us, O Christ, by the price of your blood, and join us to yourself through the favor of the blessed cross.” P. “And from the scourge.” V. “May your punishment absolve our guilt, and may your death extinguish death after it has been conquered.” P. “And from the scourge.”

Hymn. “O Nazarene.” fol. 144.

Prayer. Christ, who from the gibbet cried out to the Father, “Why [Col. 0601D] have you forsaken me?”; who by your cross redeemed the man lost through sin and delivered the author of sin himself to burn in everlasting fires: we ask your holy mercy that you may never forsake us who believe in you, nor drive our confidence away from your Godhead; but, being favorable, receive our cry and grant us to serve you with service pleasing to you.

Our Father.

ON THE LORD’S SUPPER.

At None.

Antiphon 1. “They have plotted against me.” Do not forsake me, O Lord. P. “Lest they be exalted.” V. “Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man; free me from the unjust man. They have plotted injustices in their heart; all day long they prepared [Col. 0602A] wars.” P. “Do not forsake me, O Lord, lest they be exalted.” V. “They have sharpened their tongues like serpents; the venom of asps is under their lips.” P. “Do not forsake me, O Lord.”

Capitulum. Let us love and follow everlasting righteousness, dearest brothers, desiring to eat the Lord’s Supper; for when the master of the household comes, the rejected guest is cast into the outer darkness, and the one found without a wedding garment is condemned. Let no one come stained by evil thoughts; let no one receive the heavenly sacraments as a pretender. Rather, let us imitate the patience of the Savior, from whom we see the betrayer’s treachery tolerated in such a way that the Lord Jesus Christ, who knew all things beforehand, allowed the one who was thinking evil to dine with him, lest he deprive him of the sanctified bread. [Col. 0602B] Let us imitate his humility, for he humbly washed the disciples’ feet; let us imitate his goodness, for he granted fruitful tears to Peter when he denied him. Let us beware of physically avoiding restless brothers, and let us gladly display simplicity, charity, and humility toward everyone. Let us discharge the sacrifice of repentance by fasting and praying, so that we may always hasten securely to the heavenly banquet.

R. Amen.

Antiphon 2. “The Lord Jesus entered a house and reclined. And behold, a woman having an alabaster jar of precious ointment stood behind him at his feet; she kissed his feet, watered them with her tears, and wiped them with her hair.” P. “And she anointed him with ointment.” V. “When those who were with him saw this, they said within themselves: ‘If this man were a prophet, he would know who and what sort of woman this is who touches him: [Col. 0602C] for she is a sinner.’ Knowing their thoughts, the Lord said to them: ‘Why do you trouble the woman? For she has performed a good work upon me. Therefore I say to you: Her many sins are forgiven, because she loved much.’” P. “And she anointed him with ointment.”

Prayer. As we are about to approach the Lord’s Supper, dearest brothers, let us today anticipate the face of the Lord Jesus and our Redeemer in confession, with complete confidence, asking him with tears to strip us of all our crimes and make us approach the chalice of his most holy passion.

R. Amen.

Antiphon 3. “The Lord Jesus sent his disciples and said to them: ‘Go and prepare the Passover for us, so that we may eat.’” P. “For I have earnestly desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer.” V. “While [Col. 0602D] they were dining, Jesus took bread, blessed it, gave it to his disciples, and said: ‘Take and eat.’” P. “For I have earnestly desired it.” V. “He also took the chalice after he had supped and gave it to his disciples, saying: ‘Drink from this, all of you. For this is my blood of the new covenant, which will be poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins. From now on I shall not drink until I drink it new with you in the kingdom of my Father.’” P. “For I have earnestly desired it.”

Prayer. Considering and seeing our sins, we do not offer you bloody victims, O Lord, but with simple vows we offer you the body of the eternal Priest. Remember, therefore, O Lord, what he endured for us, who bore our sins. Clothe us, then, [Col. 0603A] with the robe of righteousness, so that no one may recline at your supper without a wedding garment; may the banquet of the new covenant flourish with heavenly joys; let deceit, by which that evil disciple was deceived, be far removed; let true faith, certain hope, and pure charity be present in all, so that the conscience may not be condemned by spiritual sacraments, but, cleansed from every vice through the sweetness of your peace and charity, we may cry out to you from the earth:

Our Father.

At Vespers after the altar has been stripped.

Antiphon. “Why have you come to seize me as a robber, with swords and clubs? I was with you, teaching, and you did not seize me. One of you will betray me.” The disciples answered, saying, “Surely it is I, Lord?” He said, “The one who puts his hand [Col. 0603B] with me into the dish is the one who will betray me today.” Psalm 108.

Prayer. What tears for the cross, O Lord Jesus Christ, what sighs or lamentations for the shedding of blood, shall we answer to you? What devout vows shall we repay? Behold, now you appear for us, about to be tormented by undeserved punishments: behold, you are seized; about to be spat upon, you are spat upon; about to be scourged, you are scourged; about to be crucified, you are crucified; about to be mocked, you are mocked; about to be given vinegar to drink, you are given it; about to be brought to completion, you are brought to completion. You who will rise wondrously, spare us, Christ the Lord; we ask you to spare us through the marvelous power of your holy passion and resurrection. And just as you made the robber a citizen of paradise, so through the victory of your cross free the whole world from evil [Col. 0603C] and redeem the entire human race, so that the darkness of our consciences, which has cast us down into mourning, may be lifted by the brightness of your resurrection into joy.

R. Amen.

Another Prayer. Cleanse, we ask, O Lord, all the guilt of our crimes, so that, having laid aside the garment of the old man through the example of your most magnificent passion, renewed by the joy of your divine resurrection, we may feel ourselves illumined by heavenly works.

R. Amen.

Through your mercy, etc.

The Lord be with you. R. And with you.

For the washing of the feet.

Antiphon. “Good Teacher, wash me from my iniquity and cleanse me from my sin. For if I, Teacher and Lord, have washed [Col. 0603D] your feet, you also ought to wash one another’s feet. For I have left you an example, so that, just as I have done, you also may do likewise.” V. “Blessed are the undefiled in the way, who walk in the law of the Lord.”

Prayer. Only-begotten Son of God the Father, who for the salvation of the world deigned to assume the flesh of our humility; who mercifully restored to the path of paradise the man whom you had formed but who had been deceived by the persuasion of the devil, through the grace of your humility; who did not disdain to wash the feet of your disciples, so that by imitating your saving example you might make us reign with you: we ask your clemency, almighty God, that you may wipe away the crimes of our sins, [Col. 0604A] so that, washed from our offenses, we may deserve to become participants with the saints in the heavenly kingdom.

R. Amen.

Another Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, who were announced in time and begotten from the Father before all times; who also, after many ages, deigned to be born from a virgin mother; who, taking the form of a servant in the likeness of man, never departed from the bosom of the unbegotten Father; who did not disdain to wash the feet of your disciples; who are also Lord of the angels: we ask your omnipotence, most merciful God, that we may deserve to become participants in the kingdom of the one whose example we strive to imitate, so that, washed from all the vices of our sins, we may serve your holy name. Wash our conduct with the water of your word and purify it from the contagion of filth [Col. 0604B] with saving grace. And may we, who annually recall the humility of your Only-begotten in this action while we wash our brothers’ feet with water, diligently pursue humility; and what we visibly bestow upon the feet, may you invisibly grant to our souls.

R. Amen.

GOOD FRIDAY.

At Matins.

Antiphon. “I acknowledge my iniquity, and my sin is always before me. Against you alone I have sinned. Have mercy on me, O God.” Psalm 50.

Prayers. Let us beseech the Lord that he may graciously deign to grant us forgiveness of sins and peace. Let us all say: P. “Lord, hear and have mercy.” V. “With all our heart and with all our mind we humbly beseech you.” P. “Lord, hear.” V. “Do not repay us according to our sins.” P. “Lord.” V. “But according [Col. 0604C] to your mercy, forgive us.” P. “Lord.” V. “Let us all say.” P. “Lord, hear.” Let the capitulum be repeated. And the Deacon says, “Rise.” And the Priest says:

Prayer. Acknowledging our iniquities and our crimes, Christ our God and our salvation, who by your sufferings extinguish all our sufferings: grant us, your servants, Lord Jesus Christ, pardon for our crimes and forgiveness of sins, and may we deserve to attain eternal life from you, O Lord.

R. Amen.

Antiphon. “You have put my acquaintances far from me; they have made me an abomination to themselves. I was handed over, and [Col. 0604D] I did not go out.” V. “Lord God of my salvation, by day I cried out, and by night before you.”

Prayers. Let us beseech the Lord, as above.

Prayers. Let us all say: P. “Lord, hear and have mercy.” V. “O God, may our habitual sins not overcome the mercy of your compassion.” P. “Lord.” V. “O God, who have mercy with greater kindness than we sin with ease.” P. “Lord.” V. “Attend, we ask, to us who confess, and console those who mourn.” P. “Lord, hear.” Let us all say. Let the capitulum be repeated. And the Deacon says, “Rise.” And the Priest says:

Prayer. Christ, Son of God the Father, who, when your disciples stood far away from you in your passion, set before them the vision of the cross: do not permit us, we ask, to be far from you, but make known to us the paths of your sweetness. [Col. 0605A] And you who, though handed over, do not go out—namely, because, hidden within your own depths, you do not allow yourself to be shown as God to human beings—satisfy us with true knowledge of your Godhead, so that after our passage we may possess you in that substance; you who remain one with God the Father and the Holy Spirit in the Trinity and in everlasting glory.

Antiphon. “He shall sit alone and be silent, because he has taken the heavy yoke upon himself. He gave his cheek to the one who struck him; he shall be filled with reproaches. He shall put his mouth in the dust, as hope for the sufferer.” V. “I have been counted among those descending into the pit; I have become like a man without help, free among the dead.”

Prayers. Let us beseech the Lord, as above.

Prayers. Let us all say: P. “Lord, hear and have mercy.” V. “Our iniquities have increased before you, and our sins have answered us.” P. “Lord.” V. “Our life has failed because of bitterness; our heart has been consumed in sorrow.” P. “Lord.” V. “You have covered yourself with a cloud, so that our prayer could not reach you.” P. “Lord.” Let us all say. Let the capitulum be repeated, etc.

Prayer. Jesus, our God, who offered your cheek to those who struck you, yourself filled with reproaches for us: grant us, your wretched servants, that, instructed by the example of your [Col. 0605B] passion, we may always be fit to bear your easy yoke, so that, learning from you how meek and humble you are in heart, we may share in the example of your passion and obtain the assistance of eternal blessedness.

R. Amen.

Antiphon. “I was handed over until morning. My eyes [Col. 0605C] failed while I looked up toward heaven to the Lord, who had mercy on me.” V. “Will you work wonders for the dead? Or will physicians raise them up, and will they confess to you?”

Prayers. Let us beseech the Lord.

Prayers. Let us all say: P. “Lord, hear and have mercy.” V. “Receive now the groaning of penitents, and turn toward them the face of your grace.” P. “Lord.” V. “Be present to the wretched when entreated; be present always when called upon.” P. “Lord.” V. “Let the stubbornness of sinners not turn away the compassion of your mercy.” P. “Lord.” Let us all say. Let the capitulum be repeated, etc.

Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ, who for us were handed over to death, hung upon the cross, and given gall [Col. 0605D] mixed with vinegar to drink: receive the groaning of your servants, grant your help to their miseries, and may your holy name always be invoked over us.

R. Amen.

Antiphon. “When I sit in darkness, the Lord is my light. I shall endure the Lord’s anger. Do not rejoice, enemy death; for though I have fallen, I shall rise again.” V. “Deliver me from my enemies, O my God, and free me from those who rise up against me.”

Prayers. Let us beseech the Lord, as above.

Prayers. Let us all say: P. “Lord, hear and have mercy.” V. “May the grace of your Christ, who accepted passion for us, come to our aid.” P. “Lord.” V. “May he who by his own death freed the world tear up the record of our sins.” P. “Lord.” V. “May he whose blood redeemed us save sinners [Col. 0606A].” P. “Lord.” Let us say. Let the capitulum be repeated, etc.

Prayer. Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, who fell into the hands of the enemy and handed over your beloved soul to death for us, your servants; afterward you rose from the tomb in the glory of God the Father and redeemed the world: we ask your holy clemency that your grace may come upon us, and grant that we may stand without blemish on the day of your resurrection.

R. Amen.

Antiphon. “I have become their song; I have become a proverb among them. They abhor me and flee far from me.” V. “Incline your ear, O Lord, and hear me, for I am needy and poor.”

Prayers. Let us beseech the Lord, as above.

Prayers. Let us all say: P. “Lord, hear and have mercy.” V. “Grant peace and tranquility of the times to your Church.” P. “Lord.” V. “Provide help for this city [Col. 0606B] and be favorable to us.” P. “Lord.” V. “Take away the yoke of captivity, the stain of pestilence, and poverty.” P. “Lord.” Let us all say. Let the capitulum be repeated.

Prayer. Christ God, who came to free the world and were turned into the song of unbelievers because they did not recognize you as God, and therefore attacked you with insults as though you were a man to be provoked: raise us up through the example of your passion and surround us with the protection of the cross, so that unbelief, confounded by you, may perish, and faith, to be crowned by you, may come again.

R. Amen.

Antiphon. “They pursued the poor and needy man, and handed the brokenhearted over to death.” [Col. 0606C] V. “O God, do not be silent about my praise, for the mouth of the sinner and the mouth of the deceitful man have been opened against me.”

Prayers. Let us beseech the Lord, as above.

Prayers. Let us all say: P. “Lord, hear and have mercy.” V. “Grant healing to the sick; give substance to the needy.” P. “Lord.” V. “Deliver all the oppressed and release those in chains.” P. “Lord.” V. “Prosper travelers; restore captives to their homeland.” P. “Lord.” V. “Grant forgiveness of sins and wipe away the guilt of crimes.” P. “Lord, hear.” Let us all say. Let the capitulum be repeated, etc.

Prayer. A numerous crowd of iniquity surrounds us, O Lord; and therefore, unless you, the Redeemer, help us, our soul will almost fall into the pit of death. Deliver us, then, both from works that send us into the punishments of the underworld [Col. 0606D] and from the penal torments of Tartarus. You who, having conquered and shattered the gates of the underworld, carried the rescued spoil into the heavenly kingdoms: pour out the work of healing upon the sick; show the wandering the way of salvation; restore homeland to travelers and captives; and grant forgiveness for our sins.

R. Amen.

Song. “Who ascended the cross for the ungodly? Or who took captivity on high?” P. “The one innocent in hands and pure in heart.”

II. “The earth is the Lord’s and its fullness, the world and all who dwell in it. He founded it upon the seas and prepared it upon the rivers.” P. “The one innocent.”

III. “Who shall ascend the mountain of the Lord? Or who shall stand in his holy place? The one who has not received his soul in vain, nor sworn [Col. 0607A] deceitfully against his neighbor. He shall receive blessing from the Lord and mercy from God his Savior.” P.

IV. “This is the generation of those who seek the Lord, who seek the face of the God of Jacob. Lift up your gates, O princes, and be lifted up, eternal gates, and the King of glory shall enter: the Lord, strong and mighty, the Lord mighty in battle.” P. “The one innocent.” V. “Glory and honor to the Father.” P. “The one innocent.”

When this is completed, they repeat: “Who shall ascend the mountain of the Lord?”

Lauda. “Wait for me,” says the Lord, “until the day of my resurrection in the future; for my judgment is to gather the nations and assemble the kingdoms.” Psalm 138.

Capitula. Lord Jesus Christ, who today were handed over like a gentle lamb for sacrifice, turn [Col. 0607B] our captivity. Today, placing your back before the scourges and your cheeks before slaps; today, good Jesus, not turning your face away from the shame of spitting for us; today, Jesus the Redeemer, you were mocked for us, struck on the cheek by the blows of unbelievers, and crowned by them with thorns. Today, good Shepherd, you laid down your life for the sheep upon the cross; you were fastened among robbers, and your sacred hands were fastened to the cross with nails. Today, you were placed in the tomb under guards, and the tombs of the saints were opened. Today, good Jesus, put an end to our sins, so that on the day of your resurrection we may receive your holy body with joy and be refreshed by your sacred blood.

Therefore we ask and implore your holy clemency, Christ, who undertook and [Col. 0607C] suffered such great things for us in your holy body: redeem us, your servants, from the darkness of the underworld and from the snares of our enemies, so that, filled with the Holy Spirit on the day of your resurrection and cleansed from every sin, we may obtain the assistance of eternal blessedness.

Our Father.

At Terce.

From the Proverbs of Solomon (Cap. III).

R. Thanks be to God.

My son, if you sleep, you shall be safe; you shall rest, and your sleep shall be sweet. Do not fear sudden terror or the powers of the wicked rushing upon you. The Lord will be at your side and will guard your foot, lest you be caught by evil.

R. Amen.

Antiphon. “They were not afraid to spit in my face; [Col. 0607D] immediately they rose up and overwhelmed me. They lay in wait, and there was no one to bring help.” V. “My heart expected reproach and misery; I looked for someone who would grieve with me and someone who would console me, but there was none.”

Prayer. Christ, Son of God, whose face was exposed to the spitting of unbelievers for us: grant that what unbelief rejected in you may become for us a protection of our faith; and in the very thing by which it was offended—so that it crucified you, the Lord of glory—may we be established for you, always awaiting you as our liberator and judge.

R. Amen.

Antiphon 2. “I gave my back to the scourges and my cheeks to slaps; I did not turn my face [Col. 0608A] away from the shame of spitting, and the Lord became my protector.” V. “Guard me from the hand of the sinner and free me, O Lord, from unjust men who have plotted to trip my steps.”

Prayer. It is most wondrous, O Lord, that for the guilty you, innocent, and for the impious, you, pious, laid down your life, placing your back before the scourges and your cheeks before slaps, and not turning your face away from the shame of spitting. Since you suffered such great things in the body assumed for us, make us rejoice eternally in the vision of your Godhead.

R. Amen.

Antiphon 3. “My enemies pursued me and showed me no mercy; they struck me with a spear in the kidneys, but I cried out to the [Col. 0608B] Lord.” V. “Pour out your wrath upon my enemies, and may the indignation of your anger seize them.”

Prayer. Lord Jesus, who in your compassion understand the suffering of your Church, whose bones have been reduced to nothing, while the abyss of unbelief casts some outside her and the foulness of temptations destroys others within her: grant that, since you alone were tempted and suffered for us, you alone may rescue us from both our temptations and our sufferings, so that our testimony within your Church may be so beneficial that we may deserve to please you without end.

R. “Like a heavy burden, they have weighed heavily upon me; my wounds have become putrid.” P. “For I am ready for scourges, and my sorrow is always [Col. 0608C] before me.” V. “My heart has dried up, and my kidneys have been weakened; I have been reduced to nothing.” P. “For I am ready.” Let us bend our knees.

Prayers. Let us beseech the Lord that he may graciously deign to deliver us from the scourge of his wrath.

Prayers. “Lord, have mercy on me and deliver me.” P. “Lord, hear and have mercy.” V. “Lord, I am suffering violence; answer for me and deliver me.” P. “Lord.” V. “The sons of my mother have fought against me; you deliver me.” P. “Lord, hear.” V. “They surrounded me on every side, and there is no one to rescue me; you deliver me.” P. “Lord, hear and have mercy.” V. “Like a gentle lamb I have been led to sacrifice; now deliver me.” P. “Lord.” V. “I gave my back to those who struck me and my cheeks to those who [Col. 0608D] pulled them out; you deliver me.” P. “Lord.” V. “I did not turn my face away from those who rebuked and spat upon me; you deliver me.” P. “Lord.” V. “I have been filled with bitterness; I have been intoxicated with gall; you protect me and deliver me.” P. “Lord.” V. “I was handed over to death; I was counted among criminals; you raise me up and deliver me.” P. “Lord.” V. “Judge the cause of my soul, defender of my life, and deliver me.” P. “Lord.” V. “Let us all say.” The Deacon says, “Rise.” And the Bishop says:

Prayer. Only-begotten Christ of the unbegotten Father, who today were killed innocently by the impious for us: remember the price of your blood and wipe away the sin of the whole people. You who for us also deigned to endure spitting, insults, bonds, blows, slaps, and scourges, [Col. 0609A] the cross, nails, bitterness, death, the spear, and finally burial: grant us wretched people, for whom you suffered these things, the endless blessedness of the heavenly kingdom, so that we who bow prostrate in veneration of your passion may be raised up to heavenly things by the joys of your resurrection.

Our Father. “And lead us not…”

AT THE SALUTATION OF THE LORD’S WOOD.

Hymn.

Sing, tongue, of the glorious battle,

And proclaim the noble triumph

Of the trophy of the Cross:

How the Redeemer of the world,

Offered in sacrifice,

Conquered.

[Col. 0609B] Grieving over the deception

Of the first-created parent,

When, by the bite of the deadly fruit,

He fell into death:

He himself then marked the wood,

To make good the wood’s losses.

This work of our salvation

The order of things demanded,

That the many-shaped craft of the traitor

Might outwit his craft,

And bring healing from the place

Where the enemy had wounded us.

When, therefore, the fullness

Of the sacred time had come,

He was sent from the Father’s citadel,

The Maker of the world, born;

And, having become flesh

In a Virgin’s womb, he came forth.

The infant wails, enclosed

Within the narrow manger;

The Virgin Mother binds

His limbs in swaddling clothes,

And wraps his hands, feet, and legs

With a tight band.

When six periods of years

Had now been completed,

Fulfilling the appointed time of his bodily life,

He, of his own will, born for this,

Gave himself over to suffering,

And the Lamb was lifted upon

The wood of the Cross, to be sacrificed.

[Col. 0609D] Here are vinegar, gall, reed,

Spittle, nails, and lance;

His gentle body is pierced;

Blood flows forth like a stream.

Earth, sea, stars, and the world—

By what a flood they are washed!

Faithful Cross, among all

The one noble tree:

No forest produces another such

In leaf, flower, or shoot.

Sweet wood, sweet nails,

Bearing a sweet burden.

Bend your branches, lofty tree;

Loosen your stretched fibers;

[Col. 0610A] Let that stiffness grow supple

Which nature gave you,

So that you may extend upon a gentle trunk

The limbs of the heavenly King.

You alone were worthy

To bear the price of the world,

And, as a sailor, to prepare a harbor

For the shipwrecked world,

Which the sacred blood anointed

With the Lamb’s poured-out blood.

Praise to you throughout all time,

Undivided Trinity;

Praise, honor, and highest power,

Unique glory,

Which may resound to you, God of the ages,

[Col. 0610B] Through the ages.

Amen.

Prayer. O holy Cross, on which our salvation hung: through you may we enter to the Father; through you may we merit pardon; through you may we have indulgence and forgiveness with Christ. R. Amen.

Antiphon of the Lord’s Wood. Bearing a sign in remembrance of the commandment of your law, we entrust our souls to a small piece of wood, that, crossing the sea, we may be delivered through you, Lord the Savior. V. The Lord has reigned upon the wood. For he has set the world firm, which shall not be moved.

Antiphon 2. We make our journey by the wood that bears us; invoke the Father, so that, crossing the sea, we may be delivered through the wood. V. My help is from the Lord, who made [Col. 0610C] heaven and earth.

Antiphon 3. Blessed is the wood through which justice is accomplished. By this, Lord, you have shown our enemies that you are the one who delivers from every evil. V. Let the heavens rejoice, and let the earth exult; let the sea and its fullness be moved.

At None, for indulgence.

Tone. My people, what have I done to you? In what have I grieved you? Answer me.

P. Because I led you out of the land of Egypt, you prepared a cross for me.

II. Hear what the Lord says: Rise, and bring a judgment against the mountains, and let the hills hear your voice.

P. Because I led you out?

III. Hear, mountains, the judgment of the Lord, and you enduring foundations of the earth; for the Lord has a judgment with his people, and he will dispute with Israel, saying:

P. Because I [Col. 0610D] led you out.

IV. My people, what have I done to you? Or in what have I grieved you? Or in what have I troubled you? Answer me: because I led you out of the land of Egypt? And I freed you from the house of slavery? And I sent Moses, Aaron, and Miriam before you?

P. Because I led you out.

V. If a human being should afflict God—because you crucified me, and said, “In what did we crucify you?”—your words prevailed against me; and you crucified me, the whole people.

P. Because I led you out.

VI. What worthy offering shall I make to the Lord? I shall bend my knees before the exalted God. Shall I offer him burnt offerings, or a year-old calf? Can the Lord be appeased by thousands of rams, or by many thousands of fat goats?

P. You prepared a cross.

VII. Shall I give my firstborn for my crime, the fruit of my womb for the sin of my soul?

P. You prepared a cross.

VIII. I will show you, human being, what is good, and what the Lord requires of you: surely, to do justice, to love mercy, and to walk attentively with your God.

P. You prepared a cross.

Prologue. For the end, for the morning reception, a psalm of David himself. The twenty-first. Far from my salvation are the words of my transgressions.

III. My God, I shall cry out by day, and you will not hear; and by night, yet not for my folly.

Keep silence.

I. But I am a worm and not a human being, the reproach of humankind and the outcast of the people.

II. All who saw me mocked me; they spoke with their lips and shook their heads.

III. He hoped in the Lord; let him rescue him. Let him save him, because he desires him.

Keep silence.

I. For you are the one who brought me out of the womb; my hope from my mother’s breasts.

II. Upon you I was cast from the womb; from my mother’s womb you are my God. Do not depart from me.

III. For affliction is near, and there is no one to help.

Keep silence.

I. Many calves surrounded me; fat bulls besieged me.

II. They opened their mouths against me, like a lion seizing and roaring.

III. I was poured out like water, and all my bones were scattered.

Keep silence.

I. My heart became like melting wax in the midst of my belly.

II. My strength dried up like a potsherd, and my tongue clung to my jaws; and you brought me down into the dust of death.

III. For many dogs surrounded me; the assembly of the wicked besieged me.

Keep silence.

I. They dug through my hands and my feet; they counted all my bones.

II. But they themselves looked and gazed at me; they divided my garments among themselves, and over my clothing they cast lots.

III. But you, Lord, do not draw your help far from me; look to my defense, my God.

Keep silence.

I. Rescue my soul from the sword, and my only one from the hand of the dog.

II. Deliver me, Lord, from the lion’s mouth, and my humility from the horns of the unicorns.

III. I will proclaim your name to my brothers; in the midst of the Church I will praise you, Lord.

[Col. 0611D] Keep silence. Prayers. Penitents, pray; bend your knees before God.

Let us beseech the Lord our God to deign to grant us pardon for our crimes and forgiveness of sins.

Rise; pray; bend your knees before God.

Let us beseech the Lord our God to stretch out his hand to those who have fallen, and mercifully grant the protection that is sought from him.

Rise; pray; bend your knees before God.

Let us beseech the Lord our God that, remembering the evils we have committed, we may henceforth avoid the snares of the enemy; and that those whom the devil had withdrawn from the altar of God by his persuasion may be recalled by the protective outpouring of tears.

Rise; our prayer has been completed. With one voice, let us all ask the Lord for indulgence.

[Col. 0612A] We prostrate ourselves for prayers. Indulgence three hundred times. O. O. O. O. O. O. O. O. O. O. This three hundred times.

R. You, good Shepherd, laid down your life for the sheep. You, good Shepherd. Let it be repeated three times.

Prayers. We prostrate our prayers before your face: hear us; be appeased; forgive, Lord, and have mercy on us.

After this the Deacon says this prayer: Let us beseech the Lord that he may mercifully deign to grant us forgiveness of sins and peace.

Then the Archdeacon says these prayers:

We beseech you, Lord.

P. Indulgence.

V. May it proceed from the Most High.

P. Indulgence.

V. May it come to our misery.

P. Indulgence.

V. May it cleanse all offenses.

P. Indulgence.

V. May it be granted to penitents.

P. Indulgence.

V. May it be a protector to those who mourn.

[Col. 0612B] P. Indulgence.

V. May it correct the wandering through faith.

P. Indulgence.

V. May it raise up those fallen into sins.

P. Indulgence.

V. We beseech you, Lord.

P. Indulgence.

After this the Deacon says, etc.

Prayer. Only-begotten Son of God the Father, whose precious flesh is condemned by the Jews, mocked by the ungrateful, and compared with the bodies of criminals to be crucified, from whose side blood and water flowed—and I do not marvel at the blood from the flesh, but as for the water, from what I understand, I shall not marvel! For it is surely that water which once gave life to us, dead through Adam, when we were regenerated, proceeding from one who was dead. Therefore we ask your mercy: just as, for love of the human race, you did not disdain to take on our death, so also, rising from the dead, cause us to obtain victory over the conquered enemy. R. Amen.

[Col. 0612C] Through the mercy of our God, who lives with God the Father and reigns with the Holy Spirit forever and ever. Amen.

When this has been completed, the Deacon cries out: Indulgence two hundred times. C. C. Indulgences. O. O. O. O. O. O. O. O. O. O. This two hundred times.

R. You, good Shepherd, laid down your life for the sheep. You, good Shepherd. Let it be repeated twice.

Prayers. We have sinned against you, God, by departing from you: shame belongs to us, but mercy and propitiation to you.

Prayers. Let us beseech the Lord that he may mercifully deign to grant us forgiveness of sins and peace.

Prayers. We beseech you, Lord.

P. Indulgence.

V. May it reconcile us to the Father.

P. Indulgence.

V. May the grace of Christ [Col. 0612D] confirm us.

P. Indulgence.

V. May it conform us to the Holy Spirit.

P. Indulgence.

V. May it wash away pestilence and famine.

P. Indulgence.

V. May it confer healing upon the sick.

P. Indulgence.

V. May it restore captives to their homeland.

P. Indulgence.

V. May it temper the changes of the weather.

P. Indulgence.

V. We beseech you, Lord.

P. Indulgence.

Prayer. Only-begotten Son of God the Father, who, about to bestow so great a grace, deigned to be born on earth in order to raise us to heaven; who therefore extended your own hands upon the wood of the Cross so that, in your mercy, you might recall us to the tree of life, from which Adam was not worthy to taste after he incurred the crime of transgression. Therefore your Cross, God, is the tree of life: may it give eternal life to whoever tastes from it. We therefore ask your mercy, that our past evils may be removed from your eyes; that future good things may be born; that the deceptive light of this world may be disregarded; and that the eternity of your eternity may be sought by us. R. Amen.

Through the mercy, etc.

After this the following psalm, “Have mercy on me, God,” etc., is sung with its Antiphon, imposed by the Bishop.

Antiphon. Spare us, God, because—

Psalm 50.

After the psalm has been said, together with the Gloria Patri, the Deacon says “Indulgence” three times, no more than one hundred times. And the Bishop says this response: “You, good Shepherd.” And the Deacon says aloud, at each verse of the psalm “Have mercy on me, God,” the following: “Who grant indulgence after sins.”

Antiphon. Spare us, God, because we have despised your commandments, who grant indulgence after sins.

Psalm 50. Have mercy on me, God, according to your great mercy. And according to the multitude of your mercy, etc.

After each verse let “Who grant indulgence after sins” be repeated.

After the psalm has been said, together with the Gloria Patri, the Deacon says “Indulgence” three times, no more than one hundred times. O. O. O. O. O. O. O. O. O. O. This one hundred times.

Responsory. You, good Shepherd.

Then the Deacon says aloud: Have mercy on us, God, because you can do all things. For you overlook human sins because of repentance.

Then the Deacon says this prayer: Let us beseech the Lord that he may deign to grant us forgiveness of sins and peace.

Prayers. We beseech you, Lord.

P. Indulgence.

V. May it restore us to Paradise.

P. Indulgence.

V. May it open the gates of heaven.

P. Indulgence.

V. May it remove punishment.

P. Indulgence.

V. May it extinguish the fire of Gehenna.

P. Indulgence.

V. May it grant rest to the dead.

P. Indulgence.

V. May it confer a place of repose.

P. Indulgence.

V. May it make us companions of the saints.

P. Indulgence.

V. We beseech you, Lord.

V. Indulgence.

Prayer. Only-begotten Son of God the Father, of whom the Prophet sang this verse so many years ago: “You will be known in the midst of two living creatures”; you were clearly known not only hanging upon the wood between two criminals, or in the midst of the two Testaments, but also in the flight of the sun, the setting of the day, and the shaking of the earth. You, Christ, descended to the underworld, [Col. 0613D] and the holy tombs were opened. Therefore we ask your mercy, so that we may understand how much you will grant us, rising in the kingdom, who, when you died, raised us with glory from the underworld.

Our Father, who are in heaven.

R. Amen. Hallowed be your name, etc.

Let the Presbyter say: Delivered from evil and established always in good, may we be worthy to cling to you, God and our Lord Jesus Christ. Grant forgiveness for our sins, and rest to all your faithful servants who have died. Break and strike all the snares of our enemy; defend us from all evil works, and strengthen us in every good. Receive our fast or vow, and hear our prayer in these days and at all times. Grant us peace and security, devotion and sincere charity, and grace through the mark of your passion, our God, Son of God, who live with God the Father and reign with the Holy Spirit, one God in the Trinity, forever and ever.

R. Amen.

May the Lord be present.

Forever.

Forever and ever.

[Col. 0614B] Prayer. Our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who alone, governing all things by the word of his power and bearing all the marks of the Cross, crushed the iron bars and broke through the bolts of the bronze gates; who descended into the depths of Tartarus; who shone with the brightness of an unknown light upon those sitting in the shadow of death; may the sun of righteousness, proceeding from the tomb after the body had been raised, wonderfully illuminate our darkness with his rays.

R. Amen.

Chapters. Celebrating the solemnity of this night, the most excellent of your Resurrection, Christ, in which you yourself, rising as a new day from the tomb, transformed the ancient darkness of the former night into heavenly brightness, we implore you with whatever tearful cries we can muster; [Col. 0615A] so that you, who redeemed us by the price of your blood, may accept the ordinances you established as our prayer. Let there be pardon for crimes; let the highest glory of heavenly virtues also be granted. Remember, Lord, that we are earth, and receive the contrition of our spirit, so that we who are cast down to earth by the weakness of the flesh may be lifted to heaven by spiritual discipline and fasts. And because the falling is from us, may the rising be from you. At your command, we say:

Our Father. And lead us not. Delivered from evil. See fol. 2.

Humble yourselves for the blessing.

May the Lord be always present.

And may he grant you to be renewed in the wisdom of his sweetness, who allowed himself to be offered the bitter cup of gall.

R. Amen.

So that the whole Church, celebrating his praises with rejoicing, may be worthy to be preserved by the great standard of the Cross.

R. Amen.

Through your mercy, etc.

In the name of the Lord.

## At the joy of the day of Easter Resurrection

Antiphon. I slept, and I rose again, because the Lord raised me up.

Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ, who for us took on the sleep of death so that we would no longer fall asleep into death, grant that we who are reborn as you die may also rise from the bed of sins as you give life; and that we may no longer be overwhelmed by the punishment of sin, we who rejoice that we have been redeemed by the price of your sacred blood.

R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Antiphon 1. The Lord rose from the tomb.

P. And he broke the gates of hell.

Prayer. Christ, true redemption of the world, who, when the angel rolled the stone away from the entrance of the tomb, triumphed by the wondrous power of your Resurrection, when the weaker sex of women, who sought you with ardent desire, was the first of all to deserve to hear from the angel that you had risen; grant us that, with the sluggishness of our frailty removed, we may enjoy the unceasing comfort of your service; so that, loving you more ardently, and with no immovable stone of hardness obstructing the entrance of our mouths when we confess you, we may deserve eternal consolation from your gift.

R. Amen. Through—

Antiphon 2. Go, Mary, announce to my brothers.

R. Amen.

[Col. 0616C] Through the mercy.
