### At Lauds

For the Canticle. Antiphon. This is my God, and I will honor him; the God of my father, and I will exalt him.

Canticle from Exodus, chapter 15.

Let us sing to the Lord, for he has been gloriously honored; * he cast horse and rider into the sea.

The Lord was my helper and protector * for salvation.

This is my God, and I will honor him; * the God of my father, and I will exalt him.

The Lord, who crushes wars, * the Lord is his name.

Pharaoh’s chariots and his army * he cast into the sea.

370 His chosen horsemen he struck down; * he drowned the warriors in the Red Sea.

The deep covered them; * they sank into the depths like a stone.

Your right hand, Lord, has been glorified in power; your right hand has shattered the enemies. * And by the greatness of your majesty you crushed your adversaries.

You sent forth your wrath, and it consumed them like stubble. * And by the breath of your anger the water was divided.

[Col. 0617B] They congealed like a wall of water; * the waves congealed in the midst of the sea.

The enemy said: “Pursuing, I shall overtake them; I shall divide the spoils; I shall fill my soul.

I shall kill them with my sword; * my hand shall rule.”

You sent forth your spirit, and the sea covered them; * they sank into the depths like lead in mighty waters.

Who is like you among the gods, Lord? Who is like you, honored among the holy, wondrous in majesty, performing great deeds? * You stretched out your right hand, and the earth swallowed them.

You guided this people of yours whom you delivered by your justice; * you consoled them by your strength, in the sanctuary of your resting place.

The nations heard and grew angry; * anguish seized the inhabitants of Philistia.

Then the princes of Edom hastened, and the chiefs of Moab; * trembling seized them, and all the inhabitants of Canaan melted away.

Let fear and trembling fall upon them, * by the greatness of your arm.

Let them become like stone until your people pass over, Lord, * until this people of yours passes over, whom you delivered.

Bring them in and plant them on the mountain of your inheritance, * in the dwelling-place you prepared, which you prepared for yourself, [Col. 0617D] Lord; your sanctuary, which your hands prepared.

Lord, who reign forever and ever and beyond. * For Pharaoh’s cavalry entered the sea with chariots and horsemen,

And the Lord brought the waters of the sea over them; * but the children of Israel walked on dry land through the midst of the sea.

Let the Antiphon “This is my God” be repeated.

For the Benedictus. Antiphon. To you alone, God, belong glory, power, and authority forever and ever. Amen.

Canticle. Blessed are you, Lord God of our fathers. See fol. 6.

Tone. I slept and rested, and I rose again, because the Lord raised me up.

P. My glory. Alleluia.

V. I will not fear thousands of people surrounding me; arise, Lord, save me, my God.

P. My glory. Alleluia.

Praise. Alleluia. Praise the Lord from the heavens. Alleluia, alleluia.

Psalm 148.

Beginning of the Apocalypse of the Apostle John, chapter 1.

R. Thanks be to God.

The Apocalypse of Jesus Christ, which God gave him to make known to his servants what must soon take place; and he signified it by sending it through his angel to his servant John, who bore witness to the word of God and to the testimony of Jesus Christ, to all that he saw. Blessed is the one who reads and those who hear the words of the prophecy and keep what is written in it, for the time is near.

John to the seven churches that are in Asia. Grace to you and peace from him who is, and who was, and who is to come, and from the seven spirits who are before his throne, and from Jesus Christ, who is the faithful witness, the firstborn from the dead, and the ruler of the kings of the earth; who loved us and washed us from our sins in his blood, and made us a kingdom and priests for his God and Father—to him be glory forever.

Behold, he comes with the clouds, and every eye saw him, including those who pierced him. And all the tribes of the earth will mourn over him.

I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end, says the Lord God, who is, and who was, and who is to come, the Almighty.

R. Amen.

Hymn.

This is the true day of God,

Serene with holy light,

On which the sacred blood washed away

The shameful crimes of the world;

Restoring faith to the lost,

Illuminating the blind with sight,

On which the acquittal of the thief

Freed us from grievous fear.

He who exchanged the Cross for a reward

Swiftly acquired faith in Jesus,

And by a path shorter than that of the just

Reached the kingdom of God.

The angels marvel at this work,

Seeing the punishment of the body;

That the criminal clinging to Christ

Should receive blessed life.

A wondrous mystery!

[Col. 0618D] That flesh might wash away

The pollution of the world,

And flesh, cleansing the faults of all,

Might remove the sins of the flesh.

371 What can be more exalted than this,

That grace should seek out guilt?

That love should dissolve fear,

And death restore new life?

That death should devour its own hook,

And bind itself in its own knots?

That the Life of humankind should die,

And the Life of all should rise again?

That while death passes through all,

All the dead should rise?

That death, consumed by its own blow,

Should mourn that it alone has perished?

[Col. 0619A] We ask you, author of all things,

In this Paschal joy,

Defend your people

From every assault of death.

Glory to you, Lord,

Who rose from the dead,

With the Father and the Holy Spirit,

Through everlasting ages.

Amen.

Supplication. Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world, our Lord Jesus Christ; with every supplication let us ask that he may mercifully deign to justify us by the glory of his Resurrection.

R. Grant this, eternal and almighty God.

Kyrie, eleison. V. Christe, eleison. Kyrie, [Col. 0619B] eleison.

Chapters. Christ, Son of God, who consecrated the course of this venerable day both by the mysteries of the light first created by you and by the mysteries of your true Resurrection, when, as victor, you once triumphed on this day over hell after conquering the devil by a singular trophy; grant that we may come forth from the tomb of vices to you, the true light, who are the beginning of our resurrection. Since death can no longer in any way rule over you, may our sins likewise no longer rule over us, through the true power of your Resurrection, which we most truly confess. And since you yourself were offered for us as the morning sacrifice, command that in this morning season of your Resurrection we be purified from every offense.

Our Father. Delivered from evil. Fol. 2.

[Col. 0619C] The Lord.

V. Glory and honor to the Father.

P. Through the glory.

Chapters. God, who have made this one day distinct from all others, in which you willed it to be both the indicator of the present light among created things and the witness of eternal light, so that on it the illumination of the ages might rise again and the illumination of souls might rise again; and who, as the first day of the Lord’s work and the fitting day of the Resurrection, turning in the cycle and returning in the reckoning, caused the mystery of the Paschal solemnity to begin and completed its sacrament; look in this acceptable time and on this day of salvation upon your servants, Lord, whom you redeemed from spiritual captivity by the trophy of the Lord’s passion; whom, marked with the blood of your Lamb lest the destroyer should harm them, you delivered.

Be our guide in the wilderness of this life, so that in the day you may shade us, protecting us like a cloud, from the heat of our temptation, and at night illuminate us from the darkness of sins like a pillar of fire; so that, while you are present for salvation, you may lead us to rest.

Our Father. Delivered from evil, etc. Fol. 2.

Blessing. Christ the Lord, who consecrated this day by the mystery of his Resurrection, may grant you the power to rise from sin.

R. Amen.

And he who once rose from the dead on this day, granting you the gift of complete mortification, may make you rise through the gift of heavenly virtues.

R. Amen.

So that you may always have life in him, into whose death you rejoice that you have been buried together with him.

R. Amen.

R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

May the Lord be always present.

In the name of the Lord.

“Write to the angel of the church at Ephesus: ‘Thus says he who holds the seven stars in his right hand, who walks in the midst of the seven golden lampstands: I know your works, your labor, and your endurance, and that you cannot tolerate the wicked; and you tested those who call themselves apostles and are not, and you found them liars. You have endurance, and you have borne up for my name and have not grown weary. But I have this against you: that you have abandoned your first love. Therefore remember from where you have fallen, and repent, and do the first works; but if not, I am coming to you and will move your lampstand from its place, unless you repent. But you have this: you hate the deeds of the Nicolaitans, which I also hate. Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches. To the one who conquers I will give to eat from the tree of life, which is in the paradise of my God.’” R\. Amen.

Through your mercy, etc.

Prayer. We believe, Lord, that you were condemned to an undeserved death for us and raised up by your own power; and therefore, with an overflowing flood of tears, we earnestly ask that we who now believe that you rose for our justification may find you merciful and gentle in the judgment. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

R\. You are God, who alone performs wonders. P. And you reign forever, Lord. V\. You have made your power known among the peoples; with your arm you have delivered your people. P. And you. V\. Glory and honor. P. And you.

Prayer. Almighty and wondrous Lord, you are he who alone performs wonders, and you reign forever. Do not forget us, nor let us be cast down by human praises; but, mindful of you—in whom supreme glory consists—may we rejoice. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy, etc.

[Col. 0624D] At Lauds.

At the Canticle. Antiphon. The Lord has become my helper and protector for salvation.

Canticle. Let us sing to the Lord: gloriously. See fol. 369.

Prayer. Lord, our helper and protector, we ask you to apply your power to save us. For you are our God, who is honored as a duty and exalted as a merit; and while crushing wars, you reveal the name that belongs to you alone through mighty deeds, or make yourself known through wonders. Cast Pharaoh’s chariots and his army into the sea, so that those who pursue us from behind may be drowned by the very assault with which they persecute us; nor let us be submerged with them in the deep or in the opened sea. R\. Amen.

Through.

375 At the Benedictus. Antiphon. In the temple of your glory you are blessed, O Lord.

Canticle. Blessed are you, Lord. fol. 6.

Sono. I slept and rested, and I rose again, because the Lord raised me up.

Lauda. Praise the Lord from the heavens. Alleluia. Psalm 148.

The Apocalypse of John the Apostle (chapter 2).

R\. Thanks be to God.

“I, John, servant of Jesus Christ, heard a voice from heaven saying to me: ‘Write to the angel of the church at Smyrna: Thus says the First and the Last, who was dead and lives: I know your tribulation and your poverty, but you are rich; and you are blasphemed by those who call themselves Jews and are not, but lie; they are a synagogue of Satan. Fear none of the things you are about to suffer. Behold, the devil is about to cast some of you into prison, so that you may be tested, and you will have tribulation for ten days. Be faithful unto death, and I will give you the crown of life. Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches. The one who conquers will not be harmed by the second death.’” R\. Amen.

Hymn. This is the day. Supplication. Let us pray to the Redeemer. fol. 371.

Capitulum. Recognizing the bright image of the third day, in which, through the firmament that was created, waters were divided from waters—that is, the faithful were separated from the unfaithful—we ask and beseech you, Lord, to instruct us in true faith and separate us from unbelief; so that we who believe that you were raised from the dead on the third day may be fortified by the protection of eternal light.

Our Father. Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

Lauda. Christ has risen from the dead, alleluia. P. Through the glory of the Father. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V\. Sing to the Lord a new song, for he has done marvelous things. P. Through the glory. V\. Glory and honor. P. Through the glory.

Blessing. Christ, Son of God, who in the body of our mortality… fol. 374.

In the name of the Lord our…

On the same day at Vespers.

[Col. 0625D] Lauda. They praised you, Lord. Prayer. They praise you, Lord. fol. 371.

The Lord be with you always. R\. And with your spirit.

Antiphon. For we were buried with Christ through baptism into death, so that just as Christ rose from the dead through the glory of the Father, P. so we too may walk in newness of life. V\. He made us, and not we ourselves; but we are his people and the sheep of his pasture. P. So we too.

The Lord be with you always. R\. And with your spirit.

[Col. 0626A] Lauda. The Lord redeemed us, P. and delivered us. Alleluia, alleluia. V\. Praise the Lord, servants; praise the name of the Lord. P. And delivered us. V\. Glory and honor. P. And delivered us.

Hymn. This is the true day. Supplication. Let us pray to the Redeemer. fol. 371.

Capitulum. Almighty God the Father, who on the third day deigned to separate from the hearts of the unbelieving, as dry land from the lower salty waters, dry land—that is, a people thirsting for the fountain of faith—grant us, separated from the snares of unbelievers, to proclaim without doubt the resurrection of your Son; so that he who was raised from the underworld on the third day may raise us up by the threefold bond of the virtues, so that, strengthened by faith, hope, and charity, we may deserve to be comforted by the eternal gift of resurrection.

[Col. 0626B] Our Father. Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

Blessing. God, the Son of God, who spread the glory of his resurrection throughout the world, may he justify you through the sacrament of this belief. R\. Amen. And he who, rising again, dies no more, may he rescue you from the dominion of infinite death. R\. Amen. May there be perpetual joy for us in him in whom the example of true resurrection has gone before us. R\. Amen.

Through his mercy, etc. The Lord be with you. R\. And with your spirit.

Lauda. Remain with us, Lord, P. because the day is already declining toward evening. Alleluia, alleluia. V\. Draw near to God and be enlightened, and your faces shall not be ashamed. P. Because the day is already. V\. Glory and honor. P. Because the day is already.

[Col. 0626C] Prayer. Grant us, Lord, that we who celebrate the triumphs of your resurrection with full faith may not perform the works of death; so that, mocking everlasting death through a good life, we may receive the protection of the new inheritance. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

In the name of our Lord.

376 WEDNESDAY.

At Matins.

Antiphon. I slept. Psalm 3. Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ. fol. 369.

Antiphon 1. I shall deliver them from the hand of death; I shall redeem them from death. P. I shall be your death, O death; I shall be your bite, O underworld. V\. Because of the misery of the needy and the groaning of the poor, now I will arise, says the Lord. I will place him in my salvation; I will act with confidence in him. P. I shall be death. V\. Glory and honor. P. I shall be death.

Prayer. Grant us, Lord. Above.

Antiphon 2. Death has been swallowed up by prevailing power; and the Lord has taken away the curse of the people from every mouth and wiped away the tears from every face. P. This is our God; let us rejoice and be glad in his salvation. V\. Let us go before his face with confession, and let us shout to him in psalms. P. This is. V\. Glory and honor. P. This is.

Prayer. God, Son of God, whose death swallowed up death and removed the curse of the world: make us always rejoice together in the victory of your resurrection, so that, while we proclaim the glory of the Cross, we may continually enjoy the reward of truth. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Antiphon 3. Where is your victory, O death? P. Where is your sting, O death? I have risen, says the Lord. V\. Because of the misery of the needy and the groaning of the poor, now I will arise, says the Lord. I will place him in my salvation; I will act with confidence in him. P. Where is. V\. Glory and honor. P. Where is.

Prayer. Christ God, by whom death has been swallowed up in victory, who destroyed both death’s victory and its sting and bestowed upon the world the great protection of redemption: grant us that, mocking the death of vices through the progress of virtues, we may at last be led, made happier, to eternal joys. R\. Amen.

[Col. 0627B] Through your mercy.

R\. Great and wondrous are your works, Lord; your ways are just and true. P. King of all nations. V\. Who would not fear you, Lord, and glorify your name? For you alone are just. P. King of all. V\. Glory and honor. P. King of all.

Prayer. Great and wondrous are your works, Lord, because your judgments are true and just. Place us beneath your footsteps, so that the faith of your Church may surround your feet and may deserve to embrace grace in those things in which the Gospel woman deserved forgiveness by kissing them. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

At Lauds.

At the Canticle. Antiphon. This is my God, and I will honor him; the God of my father, and I will exalt him.

Canticle. Let us sing to the Lord: gloriously. fol. 369.

Prayer. Drive away from us, Lord, the deadly destruction of wicked Pharaoh, so that, once the yoke of Egyptian slavery has been broken, we may serve you in the joy of eternal freedom. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

At the Benedictus. Antiphon. In the temple of your glory you are blessed, O Lord.

Canticle. Blessed are you, Lord. fol. 6. Sono. I slept. fol. 370.

Lauda. Praise the Lord from the heavens. Alleluia, alleluia. Psalm 148.

The Apocalypse of John the Apostle (chapter 2).

R\. Thanks be to God.

[Col. 0627D] “Write to the angel of the church at Pergamum: ‘Thus says he who has the sword sharp on both sides: I know where you dwell, where Satan’s throne is; and you hold fast to my name and have not denied my faith. In those days Antipas, my faithful witness, was killed among you, where Satan dwells. But I have a few things against you: that you have there those who hold the teaching of Balaam, who taught Balak to put a stumbling block before the children of Israel, to eat and to commit fornication; so you also have those who hold the teaching of the Nicolaitans. Likewise repent; otherwise I will come to you soon and fight against them with the sword of my mouth. Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches. To the one who conquers I will give some of the hidden manna, and I will give him a white stone, and on the stone a new name written, which no one knows except the one who receives it.’” R\. Amen.

Hymn. This is the day. Supplication. Let us pray. fol. 371.

Capitulum. The luminous morning light of the fourth day shines forth, on which you, Almighty God, establishing the great lights in the firmament of heaven, watered the whole world through the fourfold stream of the Gospels when you redeemed it with your precious blood. Grant us, therefore, to shine in the firmament of the Church, so that we may deserve to reach eternal rest; so that you who are believed to be the Firstborn from the dead may also be found in judgment to be the forgiver of sins.

Pater noster. Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

Lauda. Christ has risen from the dead, alleluia. P. [Col. 0628B] Through the glory of the Father. Alleluia, alleluia. V\. Sing to the Lord a new song, for he has done marvelous things. P. Through the glory. V\. Glory and honor. P. Through the glory.

In the name of the Lord.

The Lord be with you. R\. And with your spirit.

Antiphon. He handed his soul over to death and was counted among the wicked. P. And he himself bore the sins of many and carried our iniquities in himself. V\. Sing to the Lord a new song, for he has done marvelous things. P. And he himself. V\. Glory and honor. P. And he himself.

The Lord be with you. R\. And with your spirit.

Lauda. Behold, the Lord has remembered his people, alleluia, and has had mercy on his inheritance. Alleluia. P. These days shall be observed with the greatest devotion and great joy. Alleluia, alleluia. V\. O Lord, save us; O Lord, grant success. P. These days shall. V\. Glory and honor. P. These days shall.

The Lord be with you. R\. And with your spirit.

Lauda. Bless the Lord, all of you, and praise his majesty together. P. Keep this day as a day of joy. [Col. 0628D] Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V\. The voice of joy and salvation is in the tents of the righteous. P. Keep this day. V\. Glory and honor. P. Keep this day.

The Lord be with you. R\. And with your spirit.

Lauda. I saw water flowing out from the temple on the right side, alleluia. P. And all to whom this water came were saved, and they shall say: Alleluia, alleluia. V\. The right hand of the Lord has shown its power; the right hand of the Lord has exalted me. P. And all. V\. Glory and honor. P. And all.

Hymn. This is the day. Supplication. Let us pray. fol. 371.

Capitulum. Behold, Lord, we are passing through the evening of this fourth day with its dutiful lights, on which, establishing the lights in the firmament of heaven and fixing them, as it were, in the solid foundation of the law, you deigned to illumine the hearts of the four Evangelists singing of you with one voice; so that with united voices they might announce to the four quarters of the world that you tasted death for us and rose from the dead. We therefore ask and beseech you: in the darkness of this life, may the grace of your resurrection shine so brightly in us that, destined to rise again, we may deserve to reach the crown.

Our Father. Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

Blessing. The true Lamb of God, who was sacrificed for us on the Cross, may he cleanse us from every stain of defilement. R\. Amen. And he who was killed in weakness and rose again powerfully, may he powerfully conquer all the desires of your flesh. R\. Amen. And he who, having conquered death, conquered the author of death, may he, with your sins conquered, make you live forever in himself. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Lauda. Christ suffered for us, leaving us an example, P. so that we might follow his footsteps. Alleluia, alleluia. V\. Sing to the Lord a new song, for the Lord has done marvelous things. P. So that we might follow. V\. Glory and honor. P. So that we might follow.

Prayer. Christ, Son of God, at whose death the desired life and salvation were given to the world: grant us abundant joy in this festival of your resurrection; so that we who believe that we died with you may also live with you forever; and since we believe that death will no longer rule over you, may we be freed from the dominion of everlasting death. R\. Amen. Through your mercy.

In the name of the Lord.

THURSDAY.

At Matins.

Antiphon. I slept. Psalm 3. Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ. fol. 369.

Antiphon 1. If we have died with Christ, we believe that we shall also live with him. P. Knowing that Christ, rising from the dead, dies no more, death shall no longer rule over him. V\. Great is our Lord, and great is his power; and of his wisdom there is no number. P. Knowing. V\. Glory and honor. P. Knowing.

Prayer. Christ, Son of God. See above in the preceding Vespers.

Antiphon 2. If you have risen with Christ, seek the things that are above, where Christ is seated at the right hand of God. P. For you have died, and your life is hidden with Christ. V\. Sing psalms to our God on the lyre, on the lyre and with the voice of a psalm. P. For you have died. V\. Glory and honor. P. For you have died.

Prayer. With overflowing gladness we rejoice that we have now risen with you, Christ, through faith; therefore make us always seek the things that are above, so that, rising from the wickedness of our sins, we may someday deserve to arrive happily where you sit at the right hand of the Father. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

[Col. 0630A] The Lord be with you. R\. And with your spirit.

Antiphon 3. Christ, rising from the dead, dies no more. P. Death shall no longer rule over him. V\. Hear this, all nations; give ear, all who dwell in the world. P. Death. V\. Glory and honor. P. Death.

Prayer. Christ, who, rising from the dead, die no more: grant that no death of sin may thereafter prevail in us, so that we who venerate the mystery of your resurrection with the most eager faith may be freed from the harmful dominion of death. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

R\. You are God, who alone performs wonders. P. And you have made your power known among the peoples. V\. With your arm you have delivered your people, the children of Israel and Joseph. P. And you have made known. V\. Glory and honor. P. And you have made known.

Prayer. You are God, who alone performs wonders. Come to our souls as the best consoler, and show yourself as Redeemer in merciful favor. You who acquired us through voluntary suffering, rescue us by unconquerable power from the snare of the hunter. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

At Lauds.

At the Canticle. Antiphon. Let us sing to the Lord, for he has been gloriously honored: he cast horse and rider into the sea.

Canticle. Let us sing to the Lord. fol. 369.

Antiphon. In the temple of your glory you are blessed, O Lord.

[Col. 0630C] Canticle. Blessed are you, Lord. fol. 6. Sono. I slept. fol. 370.

Lauda. Alleluia. Praise the Lord from the heavens. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. Psalm 148.

The Apocalypse of John the Apostle (chapter 2).

R\. Thanks be to God.

“Write to the angel of the church at Thyatira: ‘Thus says the Son of God, who has eyes like a flame of fire, and whose feet are like brass: I know your works, your love, your faith, your ministry, and your endurance; and your later works are more numerous than the first. But I have this against you: that you permit the woman Jezebel, who calls herself a prophetess, to teach and lead my servants astray—to commit fornication and eat things sacrificed to idols. And I gave her time to repent, but she does not wish to repent of her fornication. Behold, I am casting her onto a bed, and those who commit adultery with her into great tribulation, unless they repent of their works; and I will strike her children with death. And all the churches shall know that I am he who searches the kidneys and hearts, and I will give to each according to his works.

“But I say to you and to the rest who are in Thyatira: whoever does not hold this teaching and has not known the depths of Satan, as they say, I will not lay another burden upon you. Nevertheless, hold fast what you have until I come. And to the one who conquers and who keeps my works to the end, I will give authority over the nations; and he shall rule them with an iron rod, and they shall be broken like a potter’s vessel, just as I also received from my Father. [Col. 0631A] And I will give him the morning star. Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.’” R\. Amen.

Hymn. This is the day. Supplication. Let us pray. fol. 371.

Capitulum. Gazing upon the beginning of the luminous rising of the fifth day, on which you, our God, deigned to form the creeping creatures of living souls and the birds, we beseech and ask you: draw us whom you have made alive and renewed through the water of Baptism upward by raising us from vices; and as we rejoice that you rose from the dead very early, may we always rejoice, through the gift of your resurrection, that we have flown toward heavenly things.

Our Father. Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

Lauda. Christ has risen from the dead, alleluia. P. [Col. 0631B] Through the glory of the Father. Alleluia, alleluia. V\. Sing to the Lord a new song, for he has done marvelous things. P. Through the glory. V\. Glory and honor. P. Through the glory.

Blessing. The true Lamb of God. fol. 377.

In the name of the Lord.

Lauda. They praised you, Lord. And Prayer. They praise you, Lord. fol. 371.

Sono. Clap your hands, all nations; shout to God, 379 P. with a voice of exultation. Alleluia. V\. Sing psalms to our God, sing psalms; sing psalms to our King, sing psalms. For God is King of all the earth; sing psalms. P. With a voice.

The Lord be with you. R\. And with your spirit.

[Col. 0631C] Antiphon. From the hand of death I will deliver them; from death I will redeem them. P. I shall be your death, O death; I shall be your bite, O underworld. V\. Because of the misery of the needy and the groaning of the poor, now I will arise, says the Lord. I will place him in my salvation; I will act with confidence in him. P. I shall be your death. V\. Glory and honor. P. I shall be death.

The Lord be with you. R\. And with your spirit.

Lauda. Keep in mind this day, on which you came out of Egypt. P. This is the month of new things; celebrate the Passover for the Lord. Alleluia. V\. Take up the psalm and give the tambourine, the pleasing lyre with the harp. P. This is the month of new things. V\. Glory and honor. P. This is the month of new things.

The Lord be with you. R\. And with your spirit.

Lauda. I saw a great multitude of many angels in heaven [Col. 0631D] saying with a loud voice: “Worthy is the Lamb who was slain to receive power, glory, and honor.” And I heard them all saying to the one seated on the throne and to the Lamb: P. “Blessing, honor, glory, and power,” alleluia, alleluia. V\. Great is the Lord and greatly to be praised; and of his greatness there is no end. P. Blessing. V\. Glory and honor. P. Blessing.

Hymn. This is the day. Supplication. Let us pray. fol. 371.

Capitulum. God, who in the work of the fifth day created the creeping creatures of living souls—that is, human beings renewed through the sacrament of Baptism—and formed the birds of heaven, namely, the souls of the saints flying upward through the manifest light of virtues: grant our souls unconquerable consolation from your resurrection, so that, renewed through you, we may rise to glory through him by whom we have been reborn to life.

Our Father. Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

Blessing. May the grace by which you rejoice that you have been buried with Christ through faith put you to death to every contagion of iniquity. R\. Amen. And he who spread the joys of his resurrection throughout the world may grant complete sanctification to your heart. R\. Amen. May he who raised him from the dead also raise you to the glory of eternal recompense. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Lauda. Thanks be to God, who gave us the victory. P. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Alleluia, alleluia. V\. Sing to the Lord a new song, for he has done marvelous things. P. Through the Lord. V\. Glory and honor. P. Through.

Prayer. God the Father, make us bear fruit for you in such a way that we may belong only to him whom you raised from the dead, namely Christ your Son; so that, finally raising us from vices to virtue, you may bring us to the eternal inheritance. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

In the name of the Lord.

FRIDAY.

At Matins.

Antiphon. I slept. Psalm 3. And Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ. fol. 369.

Antiphon 1. For we were buried with Christ through baptism into death, so that just as Christ rose from the dead through the glory of the Father, P. so we too may walk in newness of life. V\. He made us, and not we ourselves; but we are his people and the sheep of his pasture. P. So. V\. Glory and honor. P. So.

Prayer. Christ, with whom we were buried into death so that we might rise to you through faith in your resurrection: wash us from our sins in your blood, so that those whom you once cleansed by the water of Baptism you may continually purify through the forgiveness of your mercy. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Antiphon 2. Let us bear fruit for God, so that we may belong to him, P. who rose from the dead. V\. The Lord reigns; he has clothed himself with beauty. The Lord has clothed himself with strength and girded himself. For he established the world, which shall not be moved. L. Who. V\. Glory and honor. P. Who.

Prayer. Make us bear fruit. See above in the preceding Vespers.

Antiphon 3. Christ Jesus died at the appointed time for the ungodly, the just for the unjust. Therefore he commends his love toward us, P. so that, justified in his blood, we may be saved from wrath through him. V\. The sayings of the Lord are pure sayings, silver tested by fire, purified sevenfold. P. So that, justified. V\. Glory and honor. P. So that.

Prayer. Christ our God and Lord, who strengthened us by the mystery of the Cross and sealed us with the mystery of the power of your resurrection, 380 giving the pledge of the Spirit in our hearts: grant, we ask, that we may keep the dignity of our redemption blamelessly; so that, once the impulse of fleshly desire has been broken, we may follow with the first fruits of the Spirit; so that the glorious power of your resurrection, which first went before in our Head, may also be fulfilled in the members, now through the effectiveness of good works and afterward through the raising of the glorified body. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

R\. Who is a great God like our God? P. You are God, who alone performs great wonders. V\. Lord, your way is in the sea, and your paths in many waters. You led your people like sheep. P. You are God.

Prayer. We believe, Lord, that you were condemned to an undeserved death for us and raised by your own power; and therefore, with an overflowing flood of tears, we earnestly ask you that we who now believe that you rose for our justification may find you merciful and gentle in the judgment. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

At Lauds.

At the Canticle. Antiphon. The Lord has become my helper and protector for salvation.

Canticle. Let us sing to the Lord. fol. 369.

Prayer. Behold, Lord, faithful Jerusalem rejoices in the victory of the Cross and the power of the Savior. Grant, therefore, that those who love her may remain in her peace, and that those who depart from her may at last reach her embrace; so that, once mourning has been removed, and refreshed by the joys of eternal resurrection, we may deserve to be established forever in her peace. R\. Amen.

[Col. 0633C] Through your mercy.

At the Benedictus. Antiphon. In the temple of your glory you are blessed, O Lord.

Canticle. Blessed are you. fol. 6. Sono. I slept. fol. 370.

Lauda. Praise the Lord from the heavens. Alleluia. Praise the Lord in the highest. Alleluia, alleluia. Psalm 148.

The Apocalypse of John the Apostle (chapter 3).

R\. Thanks be to God.

“Write to the angel of the church at Sardis: ‘Thus says he who has the seven Spirits of God and the seven stars: I know your works, that you have a name that you are alive, but you are dead. Be watchful, and strengthen the rest that were about to die, for I have not found your works complete before my God. Remember, therefore, how you received and heard; keep it and repent. If, therefore, you do not keep watch, I will come like a thief, and you will not know at what hour I will come to you. But you have a few names in Sardis who have not defiled their garments; they will walk with me in white, because they are worthy. The one who conquers will thus be clothed in white garments, and I will not erase his name from the Book of Life; and I will confess his name before my Father and before his angels. Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.’” R\. Amen.

Hymn. This is the day. And Supplication. Let us pray. fol. 371.

Capitulum. The radiant course of the sixth day is present, containing the mystery of the sixth age: in the former, the human being was formed from nothing; in the latter, restored from something. In this age, you, Son of God, by accepting an undeserved death for us, conquered the author of death. Grant, therefore, that those whom you redeemed from the hand of so great an enemy with your blood you may not allow to be tormented by eternal sufferings; so that you who command us, through the triumph of your resurrection, to seek the things that are above may, through the moderation of your mercy, put our hearts to death with respect to sins.

Our Father, delivered from evil. fol. 2.

The Lord be with you. R\. And with your spirit.

Lauda. The Lord Jesus Christ, who is the faithful witness, the firstborn from the dead, and the ruler of the kings of the earth: P. He loved us and washed us from our sins in his blood. Alleluia. V\. The stone which the builders rejected has become the cornerstone. P. He. V\. Glory and honor. P. He.

Blessing. The grace by which you… fol. 379.

In the name of our Lord.

At Vespers.

Lauda. They praised you, Lord. And Prayer. They praise you, Lord. fol. 371.

Sono. Rejoice in the Lord, all the earth. P. Sing to God; exult and sing psalms. Alleluia, alleluia. R\. Sing psalms to our God with the lyre and with the voice of a psalm; with forged trumpets and the voice of the horn. Rejoice before the presence of the King, the Lord. L. Sing to God.

The Lord be with you. R\. And with your spirit.

Antiphon. The Lord, the God of our fathers, raised up his Son Jesus, whom you killed, V. crying out before Pilate’s tribunal: “Crucify him, crucify him.” [Col. 0634C] R. The Lord has made known his salvation; before the nations he has revealed his righteousness. P. Crying out. 381 V. Glory and honor. P. Crying out.

The Lord be with you. R. And with you.

Praise. Say among the nations: “The Lord has reigned from the wood.” P. For he established the world, and it shall not be moved. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V. Let the heavens rejoice and the earth exult; let the sea and its fullness be stirred. P. For he established it.

The Lord be with you. R. And with you.

Praise. Rejoice, O heaven, and exult, O earth, alleluia. Let the mountains break forth in joy, alleluia. P. For the Lord has had mercy on his people, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V. Let the rivers of Judah pour forth waters; the mountains distilled sweetness, and the hills flowed with milk, because a fountain went forth from the house of the Lord, alleluia, alleluia. P. For. R. Glory and honor. P. For.

Hymn. This is the day. And supplication. Let us pray. fol. 371.

Chapters. O God, Son of God, who on the sixth day formed the human being from nothing and in the sixth age of the world redeemed him by your blood; and he who, well created then, fell badly, has now been restored for the better and has risen: grant us so truly to weigh the mystery of our redemption that we may eternally glory in your death and resurrection; so that you, who at the time of salvation, coming to meet the world, conquered our death by dying, may free us from the eternal condemnation of judgment.

[Col. 0635A] Our Father. Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

Blessing. Christ, Son of God, who was fastened to the gibbet of the Cross for the ungodly, may save you by the glory of his saving Passion. R. Amen. And may he who by dying conquered death himself turn away from you all the torments of hell. R. Amen. May he bring you to rise to glory in him whose resurrection you now receive with joy. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Praise. Thanks be to God, who gave us the victory. P. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. R. Sing to the Lord a new song, for he has done wondrous things. P. Through our Lord. V. Glory and honor. P. Through our Lord.

Prayer. We give you thanks, God the Father, because you rescued us from the power of darkness, transferring us into the kingdom of your Son; grant us, therefore, we ask, that those whom through death he recalled to life he may through his compassion raise to everlasting joys. R. Amen.

Through mercy. In the name of the Lord.

SATURDAY.

At Matins.

Antiphon. I slept. Psalm 369. And prayer: Lord Jesus Christ. fol. 369.

Antiphon 1. Thanks be to God, who gave us the victory. P. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. V. Say among the nations: “The Lord has reigned from the wood.” For he established the world, and it shall not be moved; he will judge the peoples with equity. P. Through. V. Glory. P. Through the Lord.

[Col. 0635C] Prayer. What thanks shall we be able to offer you, Lord, for this: that you granted us victory through the shedding of your Son’s blood? And therefore, because you regard our deficiency, extend the supplement of your compassion, so that whatever the mind suggests should be proclaimed in praise of you, the mouth may bring forth in faithful utterance for the gain of eternity. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 2. The grace of God has been given to us through the illumination of our Savior Jesus Christ. P. Who destroyed death and illuminated life. V. Great is our Lord, and great is his power; and of his wisdom there is no number. P. Who. V. Glory and honor. P. Who.

[Col. 0635D] Prayer. We give thanks. Seek it in the preceding Vespers.

Antiphon 3. We give you thanks, Lord our God, who are, and who were, and who are to come, the Almighty. V. For your mercy has been magnified to the heavens, and your truth to the clouds. P. Who are. V. Glory and honor. P. Who are.

Prayer. Lord our God, who are, and who were, and who are to come, every creature formed by you will render you thanks, because the kingdom of this world has become that of our Lord Jesus Christ; therefore we ask that those whom you wished to be his kingdom you may console with an eternal gift. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

R. How greatly magnified are your works, O Lord. P. Your works, O Lord. [Col. 0636A] V. You made all things in wisdom; the earth is filled. P. Your works.

Prayer. Greatly magnified are your works, O Lord, and far beyond human understanding. Their visible beauty urges us to praise the Creator, the most beautiful of all. But fill us with the spirit of discernment, so that while we marvel at your works, our understanding may praise and magnify you in your works. 382 R. Amen.

Through mercy.

At Lauds.

For the Canticle. Antiphon. This is my God.

Canticle. Let us sing to the Lord. fol. 369.

For the Benedictus. Antiphon. Blessed are you, Lord, in the temple of your glory.

[Col. 0636B] Canticle. Blessed are you, Lord. fol. 6. Sounding. I slept. fol. 370.

Praise. Praise the Lord from the heavens: alleluia, alleluia. Praise him in the heights: alleluia, alleluia. Psalm 148.

Apocalypse of the Apostle John (chapter 3).

R. Thanks be to God.

“Write to the angel of the church of Laodicea: Thus says the faithful and true Witness, who is the beginning of God’s creation. I know your works: you are neither cold nor hot. Would that you were cold or hot! But because you are lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I am about to vomit you out of my mouth. For you say, ‘I am rich, I have become wealthy, and I need nothing,’ and you do not know that you are wretched, pitiable, poor, blind, and naked. I advise you to buy from me gold refined by fire, so that you may be saved, and white garments, so that you may be clothed and the shame of your nakedness may not appear, and anoint your eyes with salve, so that you may see. I reprove and discipline those whom I love. Be zealous, therefore, and repent. Behold, I stand at the door and knock: if anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will enter in to him and dine with him, and he with me. To the one who conquers I will grant to sit with me on my throne, just as I conquered and sit with my Father on his throne. Let the one who has an ear hear what the Spirit says to the churches.” R. Amen.

Hymn. This is the day. And supplication: Let us pray. fol. 371.

[Col. 0636D] Kyrie, eleison. R. Christe, eleison. Kyrie, eleison.

Chapters. Christ, Son of God, who consecrated the dawn of the seventh day in your rest, when, placed in the tomb, you completed the sabbath’s repose: grant our heart a rest pleasing to you, so that we may truly rest in you from our works and not, during the sabbath’s repose, be weighed down by the burdens of our sins; so that we who faithfully believe that you rose from the quiet of the tomb may likewise experience you, Most Merciful One, coming from heaven for judgment with utmost gentleness.

Our Father. Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

Praise. Thanks be to God, who gave us the victory. P. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Alleluia, alleluia. V. Sing to the Lord a new song, for he has done wondrous things. P. Through our Lord. R. Glory and honor. P. Through our Lord.

Blessing. Christ, Son of God, who in the body of our mortality bore the reproach of the Cross, may rescue you from every harmful torment of suffering. R. Amen.

Through mercy, etc.

The Lord be with you. R. And with you.

In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, let us complete it in peace. R. Thanks be to God.

SATURDAY WITHIN THE OCTAVE OF EASTER.

At Vespers.

Praise. They praised you, Lord. And prayer. They praise you, Lord. fol. 371.

Sounding. Alleluia. After the Lord Jesus [Col. 0637B] Christ had risen from the dead, standing in the midst of his disciples, he spoke, saying: P. Peace be with you; I am he who rose from the dead. Alleluia. V. Then he opened their understanding, so that they might understand the Scriptures, and he said to them: “For thus it is written: Was it not necessary for Christ to suffer and to rise from the dead?” Alleluia. P. Peace.

The Lord be with you. R. And with you.

Antiphon. If you have risen with Christ, seek the things that are above, where Christ is, seated at the right hand of God. P. For you have died, and your life is hidden with Christ. R. Lord, save us; O Lord, grant good success. Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord. We bless you from the house of the Lord. God is the Lord, and he has shone upon us. P. For you have died. V. Glory and honor. P. For you have died.

[Col. 0637C] The Lord be with you. R. And with you.

Praise. The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone. P. This was done by the Lord; it is wonderful in our eyes. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V. Sing praises to our God, sing praises; sing praises to our King, sing praises. P. This was done by the Lord. V. Glory. P. This was done by the Lord.

Hymn.

A hundred thousand angels of the legions

Applaud you with song and jubilate melodiously,

Christ Jesus, Alpha and Omega, almighty,

Once buried, and living through the ages,

Faithful Witness and true Beginning.

You cast down the prince of this world,

Redeeming the world with your gracious Blood;

Holy and true, Begotten of the Unbegotten,

Opening what was closed and closing what was open,

Making us a royal priesthood for God.

You are the true and only spotless Lamb,

Seated at the Father’s right hand upon the throne,

The only one who came forth from the Lord’s citadel,

Like jasper and sardius,

An iris around it, an emerald encircling it.

You are God’s pledge and the Son of humankind;

You were found worthy to open the book

Sealed with seven seals and to break its seals:

The Lamb slain, mighty with seven horns,

Shining with seven fiery lights.

From the throne proceed flashes of lightning and thunder,

[Col. 0638A] Seven burning lamps before the throne,

The seven Spirits of God sent everywhere,

Seven stars gleam at the Lamb’s right hand,

And seven golden lampstands stand beside him.

The twenty-four elders sit around,

All clothed in white robes,

And crowned with golden diadems;

They carry golden bowls of spices,

And play upon golden instruments and lyres.

Before the throne stands the shining glassy sea;

Four mighty beings, likewise living creatures:

The human by nature, the lion roaring in voice,

The young bull proclaiming priesthood with its mouth,

The eagle seeking the stars in the manner of flight.

Each of the four forms has six wings,

[Col. 0638B] Before and behind, all full of eyes,

Ever watchful, unable to sleep,

Continually crying in turn, “Holy” three times,

To him who was, who is, and who is to come.

Glory to the Father, praise and wisdom

To the Lamb seated upon the throne in heaven;

He reigns with the Father and with the Holy Spirit,

One Godhead joined together in three,

Through infinite ages of ages.

Amen.

Supplication. Let us pray. fol. 371.

Chapters. Christ, Son of God, rest of our souls, who, resting in the tomb, completed the sabbath’s repose, so that in the place where you had once rested from every work, you might also rest in the sepulcher, [Col. 0638C] truly sanctifying for us this day, whose evening dawns for us on the first sabbath, which is also the eighth day: so that you, who had said that light should shine forth from darkness, might visibly appear in the flesh, rising from the dead; direct the course of our life into the way of complete sanctification, so that during these seven days in which this world is carried out, and in which the Lamb is slain for us daily and Easter is celebrated daily, we may conduct ourselves along a healthier course of life; so that without the leaven of malice we may deserve to celebrate the true Passover daily; and so that on this day we may rest from all our works in a sanctification pleasing to you, that we may be consoled by the glory of the resurrection of that eternal eighth day, because at your command we pray:

[Col. 0638D] Our Father. Delivered from evil. Seek folio 2.

Blessing. Christ, Son of God, who on this day, dying, rested in the tomb, grant the desired rest to your hearts. R. Amen. And may he who, placed in the sepulcher, bore the reproach of the Cross grant you to cease from every work of sin. R. Amen. May he make the desired joy of his resurrection bring you devotion here and raise you up to the gift of eternity in the future. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Praise. Jesus appeared to his disciples behind closed doors; one of them, Thomas, did not believe that he was the Lord. P. Put your hand into the marks of my nails, and now be faithful: “My Lord and my God.” Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V. May the name of the Lord be blessed, now and forever. P. Put your hand. V. Glory and honor. P. Put your hand. Prayer: Almighty God. Seek below.

Through mercy.

In the name of the Lord.

SUNDAY WITHIN THE OCTAVE OF EASTER.

At Matins.

Antiphon. I slept. Psalm 3. Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ. fol. 369.

Antiphon 1. By his bruise we were healed. We all went astray like sheep, and the Lord laid upon him the iniquities of us all; he was handed over, P. because he himself willed it, and he did not open his mouth. V. All nations, clap your hands; shout joyfully to God with a voice of exultation. P. Because. V. Glory and honor. P. Because.

Prayer. Almighty God the Father, who redeemed us with the precious blood of your Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, do not allow those who believe in you to be plunged into the abyss of eternal punishment, so that through confession of our crimes we may deserve to be admitted to you through him upon whom you laid the iniquities of us all; so that we may be protected by the unceasing guardianship of him by whose bruise we were healed. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 2. The Just One, judging, bore our sins in his body upon the wood. P. So that, separated from evil, we might live with righteousness. V. Shout joyfully to the Lord, all the earth; serve the Lord with gladness. P. So that, separated from evil. [Col. 0639C] V. Glory and honor to the Father. P. So that, separated from evil.

Prayer. Indeed, O Lord, the Just One, judging, you bore our sins in your body upon the wood, when you conquered the devil not by power but by justice, so that we who had been subjected to his servitude through our deserved death might return to the grace of liberty through your undeserved death. Make us, therefore, so that we may always be free in you, so that we may live with you, both here and forever without end. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 3. He was wounded for our iniquities and crushed for our crimes. P. The discipline of our peace was upon him; by his bruise we were healed. V. Come and see the works of the Lord, the wonders he has placed upon the earth. P. The discipline. V. Glory [Col. 0639D] and honor. P. The discipline.

Prayer. Christ, Son of God, who willingly subjected your flesh to death for us and became the discipline of our peace, make us subject to your disciplines, so that we who were healed by your bruise may always obey the judgment of your will. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

R. The lion of the tribe of Judah, the root of David, has conquered, to open the book and break its seals; and with him the army of Angels crying out and saying: P. Praise, honor, and power to our God. V. I saw in heaven a great crowd that no one could count, and they cried out with a loud voice, saying: P. Praise and honor.

Prayer. Lion of the tribe of Judah, root of David, open in us the light of your knowledge, so that we who now reverently celebrate the Paschal feasts may sing to your glorious name in your kingdom with your elect and with the armies of Angels. Amen.

Through mercy.

At Lauds.

For the Canticle. Antiphon. Let us sing to the Lord, for he has been gloriously honored.

Canticle. Let us sing to the Lord. fol. 369.

For the Benedictus. Antiphon. To you alone, God, belong honor and glory.

Canticle. Blessed are you, Lord. fol. 6. Sounding. I slept. fol. 370.

Praise. Praise the Lord from the heavens: alleluia, alleluia. Praise him in the heights: alleluia. Psalm [Col. 0640B] 148.

Apocalypse of the Apostle John (chapter 5).

R. Thanks be to God.

I, John, was in the Spirit, and I saw in the right hand of the one seated upon the throne a book written within and without, sealed with seven seals. And I saw a mighty Angel proclaiming in a loud voice: “Who is worthy to open the book and break its seals?” And no one in heaven, or on earth, or under the earth, was able to open the book or look at it. I wept greatly because no one was found worthy to open the book or see it. And one of the elders said to me: “Do not weep. Behold, the lion of the tribe of Judah, the root of David, has conquered so as to open the book and its seven seals.” And I saw, and behold, in the midst of the throne and of the four living creatures, and in the midst of the elders, a Lamb standing as though slain, having seven horns and seven eyes, which are the seven Spirits of God sent throughout the whole earth. And he came and took the book from the right hand of the one seated on the throne. And when he had opened the book, the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders fell before the Lamb, each holding a harp, golden bowls, and golden vessels full of spices, which are the prayers of the saints. And they sang a new song, saying: “You are worthy to receive the book and to open its seals, because you were slain and redeemed us for God by your blood, from every tribe and language and people and nation, and you made us a kingdom and priests for our God, and they shall reign upon the earth.” And I saw and heard the voice of many Angels around the throne and the living creatures and the elders; and their number was thousands of thousands, saying with a loud voice: “Worthy is the Lamb who was slain to receive power and divinity and wisdom and strength and honor and glory and blessing.” And every creature that is in heaven and upon the earth and under the earth, and those that are in the sea and in it, all of them I heard saying: “To the one seated upon the throne and to the Lamb be blessing and honor and glory and power, to our God through the ages of ages.” 385 R. Amen.

Hymn. This is the day. Supplication. Let us pray. fol. 371.

Chapters. When, Christ the Lord, the service of the Paschal solemnity has run its course and the joy of your resurrection has been completed—the true light by which you shone forth from darkness upon the world, by which you flashed upon blind minds—we adore and, behold, prostrate ourselves before you, God, who, excluding the malice of the old leaven by the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth, do not leave any corruption of adulterous mixture within the purity and simplicity of faith, but have consecrated for us the day of unleavened bread, ourselves unleavened, without the leaven of human seed. We ask that you, the arbiter of devotion, look upon the public vows of faith, and that, as a merciful propitiator, you regard the completed worship of your Passion and resurrection. And since grace and truth have come through you, instruct with your truth toward understanding those whom grace has led to worship.

Our Father. Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

Praise. He appeared behind closed doors. Blessing: Christ, Son [Col. 0641B] of God. fol. 383.

In the name of the Lord.

At the end of Vespers.

Praise. They praised you. fol. 371.

Prayer. May all the Angels and powers praise you in the heights, O Lord; may everything that takes its origin from you, its author, offer you praise from the earth; and may you, who are praised by the services of those above, always delight in the obedience of those below. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Sounding. Alleluia. After you had risen. fol. 382.

Antiphon. This is the day that the Lord has made. P. Let us rejoice and be glad in it. V. O Lord, save us; O Lord, grant good success. P. Let us rejoice. [Col. 0641C] V. Glory and honor. P. Let us rejoice.

The Lord be with you. R. And with you.

Praise. You shall celebrate this appointed day for the Lord, alleluia. P. And your children forever. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V. Rejoice in God our helper; shout joyfully to the God of Jacob. P. And your children. V. Glory and honor. P. And your children.

Hymn.

Let the height of heaven sing praise,

Let all the Angels sing praise,

Let whatever power exists anywhere

Sing praise to God:

Let no voice of any tongue be silent,

But let every voice resound together.

Give me a plectrum, boy,

[Col. 0641D] That I may sing for the faithful

A sweet and melodious song,

The glorious deeds of Christ;

Let our Muse sing of him alone,

Let the lyre praise him.

He is the Christ whom the king-priest,

Crowned with the mitre,

Sang as coming immediately,

With voice, string, and drum,

Drawing in through his marrow

The Spirit flowing from heaven.

We sing deeds and miracles

Already accomplished and proven.

The world is witness; nor does the earth itself

Deny what it has seen;

It reveals God, brought near

To mortal beings for their instruction.

Born from the Father’s heart

Before the beginning of the world,

Called Alpha and Omega;

He himself is the fountain and the end

Of all things that are, that were,

And that shall be hereafter.

He commanded, and they were created;

He spoke, and they came to be:

Earth, heaven, the sea’s deep,

The threefold structure of things,

And whatever lives in them beneath

The high sphere of sun and moon.

He put on the form of frail flesh,

[Col. 0642B] Limbs subject to death,

So that the race might not perish

From the seed of the first [plusti; reading uncertain],

Whom the deadly law had plunged

Into the deep of Tartarus.

O blessed was that birth,

When the Virgin, in childbirth,

Brought forth our salvation,

Pregnant with the Holy Spirit;

And the child, the world’s Redeemer,

Opened his sacred mouth.

Glory and honor to God,

The Most High everywhere,

One with the Father and the Son,

And with the illustrious Paraclete;

[Col. 0642C] To him be praise and power

Through eternal ages.

Amen.

Supplication. Let us pray. fol. 371.

Chapters and Blessing, to be said on all Sundays until the Lord’s Ascension.

At the end of Vespers.

Chapters. God, whose one [ …]. Blessing. Christ the Lord, who [the day …]. fol. 372. Praise. He appeared behind closed doors. fol. 383.

Prayer. The lion of the tribe of Judah. fol. 384.

ON THE THIRD SUNDAY AFTER EASTER.

At Vespers.

Praise. They praised you, Lord. Prayer. They praise [Col. 0642D] you, Lord. fol. 371.

Sounding. The Lord Jesus Christ rose from the dead on the third day. P. And he lives by the power of God. Alleluia. V. Our Savior, rising from the dead, troubled death and illuminated us with the eternity of life. P. And he lives.

The Lord be with you. R. And with you.

Antiphon. God, who is rich in mercy, because of his exceedingly great love with which he loved us, P. even when we were dead in sin, made us alive together with Christ, by whose grace we have been saved. V. For who among the clouds shall be equal to the Lord? Or who shall be like the Lord among the sons of God? P. Even when we were dead in sin, Christ made us alive together, by whose grace we have been saved. V. Glory and honor. P. Even when we were dead in sin, Christ made us alive together, by whose grace we have been saved.

The Lord be with you. R. And with you.

[Col. 0643A] Praise. Your streets, Jerusalem, shall be paved with pure gold: alleluia. P. And a song of joy shall be sung in you, alleluia; and throughout all your lanes everyone shall say: alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V. Praise the Lord, Jerusalem; praise your God, Zion. P. And a song shall be sung. V. Glory and honor. P. And a song shall be sung.

Hymn. A hundred thousand angels of the legions. fol. 382. Supplication. Let us pray. fol. 371.

Chapters. Christ, Son of God.

Blessing. Christ, Son of God. fol. 383.

Praise. The wisdom of God is above precious stones, alleluia; its dwelling is in golden vessels, alleluia. P. Its prudence proceeds from an invisible treasure, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V. Stretching out the heavens like a skin, he covers its upper regions with waters. P. Its prudence. V. Glory and honor. P. Its prudence.

Prayer. Great and awesome King, Lord, may true faith rejoice in you among all the nations; and grant that we may sing praise to you not only with our voice but also with our mind, for you are our King, so that we may live with you without end. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

In the name of the Lord.

At Matins.

Antiphon. I slept. Psalm 3.

Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ. fol. 369.

Antiphon 1. Sing to the Lord a new song; sing praise to him well with jubilation. P. For the word of the Lord is upright, and all his works are in faithfulness. V. Give thanks to the Lord upon the harp; sing praise to him on the ten-stringed psaltery. P. For. V. Glory and honor. P. For.

Prayer. Let us sing to you, Lord, a new song, because your word is upright and your works are faithful, so that you who make us ascend to the kingdoms of heaven amid the prophet’s jubilation and the blast of the evangelical trumpet may draw us there, where you yourself go before us. R. Amen.

Through.

Antiphon 2. The King of the whole earth, God, chose us as his inheritance. P. Sing praises to our God, sing praises; sing praises to our King, sing praises. V. All nations, clap your hands; shout joyfully to God with a voice of exultation. P. Sing praises. V. Glory and honor. P. Sing praises.

Prayer. Great and awesome King. Seek it earlier in the preceding Vespers.

[Col. 0643D] Antiphon 3. Shout joyfully to God, all the earth. P. Sing, exult, and sing praise. V. Sing to the Lord a new song, for he has done wondrous things. P. Sing. V. Glory and honor. P. Sing.

Prayer. May the whole earth rejoice in you, Lord; may it sing a psalm, exult, and sing praise to your name, whose name is wondrous and renowned. Grant, therefore, to your Church through its prayers that those whom you call in faith you may not abandon in temptation; and may those who sound forth a jubilation of praise to you forever deserve the reward of eternal blessedness in the future. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

R. The Lord has reigned over all the earth, and the whole earth shall be inhabited. P. You will encircle all the earth like paradise. V. The Lord has reigned; let the earth rejoice; let the many islands be glad. P. You will encircle it like paradise.

387 Prayer. Your testimonies are wondrous, Lord God; by them your only-begotten Son reigns over the whole earth. Grant us, therefore, that we who behold his glory with unveiled face may be placed at his right hand in judgment. R. Amen.

Through.

At Lauds.

For the Canticle. Antiphon. The Lord was my helper and protector for salvation; this is my God, and I will honor him; the God of my Father, and I will exalt him.

Canticle. Let us sing to the Lord. fol. 369.

For the Benedictus. Antiphon. To you alone, God, belong honor, glory, strength, and power through the ages of ages.

[Col. 0644B] Canticle. Blessed are you, Lord. fol. 6.

Sounding. I slept. fol. 370.

Praise. Praise the Lord from the heavens: alleluia, alleluia. Praise him in the heights: alleluia, alleluia. Psalm 148.

Apocalypse of the Apostle John (chapter 3).

R. Thanks be to God.

“Write to the angel of the church of Philadelphia: Thus says the Holy and True One, who has the key of David, who opens and no one shuts, and shuts, and no one has opened. I know your works, and I have set before you an open door that no one can shut, because you have little strength, and you have kept my word and have not denied my name. Behold, I will make those of the synagogue of Satan—who say that they are Jews and are not, but lie—behold, I will make them come and worship before your feet, and they shall know that I have loved you. Because you kept my word of patience, I also will keep you from the hour of temptation that is coming upon the whole world to test those who dwell on the earth. I am coming soon. Hold fast what you have, so that no one may take your crown. The one who conquers I will make a pillar in the temple of my God, and he shall never go out again. And I will write upon him the name of my God, and the name of the city of my God, the new Jerusalem, which descends from heaven from my God, and my new name. Let the one who has an ear hear what the Spirit says to the churches.” R. Amen.

Hymn. This is the day. Supplication. Let us pray. Chapters. Christ, Son of God, who is venerable. fol. 371. Praise. The wisdom of God above the stone. fol. 385. Blessing. [Col. 0644D] Christ the Lord, who ascended the gibbet. fol. 386.

In the name of the Lord.

At the end of Vespers.

Praise. They praised you, Lord. Prayer. They praise you, Lord. fol. 371. Sounding. The Lord Jesus Christ. fol. 373.

Antiphon. The Lord made the heavens by his power. P. For he established the world, and it shall not be moved. V. Let the heavens rejoice and the earth exult; let the sea and its fullness be stirred. P. For he established it. V. Glory and honor. P. For he established it.

The Lord be with you. R. And with you.

Praise. I saw holy Jerusalem, the new one, descending [Col. 0645A] from heaven. P. And I heard the voice of those saying: Alleluia, alleluia. V. Praise the Lord, Jerusalem; praise your God, Zion. P. And I heard. V. Glory and honor. P. And I heard.

Hymn. Let the height of heaven sing praise. fol. 385. Supplication. Let us pray. Chapters. God, whose one [this …]. Blessing. Christ the Lord, who [this day of the Resurrection …]. fol. 371. Praise. The wisdom of God. Prayer. Great King. fol. 386.

ON THE FOURTH SUNDAY OF EASTER.

At Vespers.

Praise. They praised you. Prayer. They praise you. fol. 371.

Sounding. Come and see how the Angel rolled away the stone. P. The soldiers guarding the Holy One. Alleluia, alleluia. V. The women weeping, seeking the Savior. The Angel said to the Marys: “He is not here; for the Lord has risen.” P. The soldiers.

The Lord be with you. R. And with you.

Antiphon. The Lord our God Almighty has reigned; let us rejoice and exult. P. For the vows of the Lamb have come, which are the justifications of the saints. V. All nations, clap your hands; shout joyfully to God with a voice of exultation. P. For. V. Glory and honor. P. For.

The Lord be with you. R. And with you.

Praise. Sing to God, alleluia; to our God P. Sing a new song: alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V. Praise the Lord, servants; praise the name of the Lord. P. Sing a new song. 388 V. Glory and honor. P. Sing a new song.

[Col. 0645C] Hymn. A hundred thousand angels of the legions. Supplication. Let us pray. fol. 371. Chapters. Christ, Son of God, our [rest]. Blessing. Christ, Son of God, who on this day. fol. 383.

Praise. The people of Israel rejoiced, alleluia, and the whole multitude of Jacob worshiped the Lord according to the law. P. And David, with the singers, struck the harp in the house of the Lord and gave praise to the Lord: alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V. He did not permit anyone to harm them, but he reproved kings for their sake. P. And David. V. Glory and honor to the Father. P. And David.

Prayer. Wondrous Lord, your name is worthy of praise in all the ends of the earth. Grant us, therefore, to avoid the empty exaltation of the world, so that your praise may be perfected from our mouth and the fullness of knowledge may grow within us through the nourishment of true faith. R. Amen.

[Col. 0645D] Through mercy.

In the name of the Lord.

At Matins.

Antiphon. I slept. Psalm 3. Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ. fol. 369.

Antiphon 1. Lord our God, how wondrous is your name. P. Throughout all the earth! V. For your magnificence has been exalted above the heavens. P. Throughout all the earth. V. Glory and. P. Throughout all the earth.

Prayer. Wondrous Lord, your name. In the preceding Vespers.

Antiphon 2. Sing to the Lord a new song; sing to the Lord, all the earth. P. Sing to the Lord and bless his name. V. Announce his salvation from day to day. P. Sing. V. Glory and honor. P. Sing.

Prayer. May the whole earth sing to you, Lord, a new song, because through the blood of your Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, you redeemed the whole world, so that we who have been buried with him in his death may exult with infinite joy together with him. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 3. How greatly magnified are your works, O Lord! P. You made all things in wisdom; the earth is filled with your creation. V. This is the great and spacious sea; there are creeping things without number, small and great animals. P. You made all things in wisdom. V. Glory and honor. P. You made all things.

[Col. 0646B] Prayer. How greatly magnified are your works, O Lord! You made all things in wisdom. Fill us, nevertheless, with the spirit of direction, so that while we marvel at your works, our understanding may praise you in your works. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

R. I am God, and I do not change. Turn back to me, my people, for I testify to you that there is no other God besides me. I made the earth and the human being upon it; I established the heavens. P. And I commanded all the stars to shine. V. I, the firstborn, went forth before every creature; I made light arise in the heavens. P. And I commanded all the stars to shine.

Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ, true God and true human being, who do not change but are holy in all your works, turn unbelief away from us and the doubt of the mind, [Col. 0646C] and fill our heart with the gifts of your grace, so that you may be believed and known as true God, you who are approved as the Savior of all by miracles and powers. R. Amen.

Through.

At Lauds.

For the Canticle. Antiphon. The Lord, who crushes wars—the Lord is his name—cast Pharaoh’s chariots and his army into the sea.

Canticle. Let us sing to the Lord.

For the Benedictus. Antiphon. To you alone, God. Sounding. I slept. fol. 370.

Apocalypse of the Apostle John (chapter 14).

R. Thanks be to God.

I, John, was in the Spirit, and I saw, and behold, the Lamb stood upon Mount Zion, and with him were one hundred and forty-four thousand who had his name and the name of his Father written upon their foreheads. And I heard a voice from heaven, like the voice of many waters and like the voice of great thunder; and the voice that I heard was like that of harpists playing their harps. And they sang as though a new song before the throne and before the four living creatures and the elders; and no one could sing the song except the one hundred and forty-four thousand who had been purchased from the earth. These are they who were not defiled with women, for they are virgins. These follow the Lamb wherever he goes. These were purchased from among humankind as first fruits for God and for the Lamb, and no lie was found in their mouth, for they are without blemish. And I saw another Angel flying through the midst of heaven, having an eternal Gospel, to proclaim it to those seated upon the earth and to every nation and tribe and people and language, saying with a loud voice: “Fear the Lord and give him honor, because the hour of his judgment has come; and worship him who made heaven and earth, the sea and the fountains of waters.” R. Amen.

Hymn. This is the day. Supplication. Let us pray. Chapters. Christ, Son of God, who is venerable on this day. fol. 371. Praise. The people of Israel rejoiced. Seek folio 388. Blessing. Christ the Lord, who made this day. fol. 372.

In the name of the Lord, etc.

[Col. 0647B] At the end of Vespers.

Praise. They praised you. Prayer. They praise you, Lord. fol. 371. Sounding. Come and see. Seek fol. 375.

Antiphon. You are the King of kings, to whom the God of heaven has given a kingdom strong, P. powerful, and honored. V. Lord God of hosts, convert us, and show us your face, and we shall be saved. P. Powerful. V. Glory and honor, etc. P. Powerful.

May the Lord be always with you. R. And with you.

Lauda. Sing to the Lord a new song, Alleluia, because the Lord has done marvelous things. His right hand and his holy arm have delivered us. Alleluia. V. The Lord has made his salvation known; before the sight of the nations he has revealed his righteousness. P. He has delivered us. V. Glory and honor. P. He has delivered us.

[Col. 0647C] Hymn. “Let the height of heaven sing praise.” See folio 385. Supplication. “Let us pray to the Redeemer.” Folio 385. Prayers, as above. Capitulum. “O God, through whom we have distinguished this day from all others.” Benediction. “Christ the Lord, who [has made] this day of the Resurrection.” See folio 372.

Lauda. Every perfect gift will come from heaven, Alleluia, P. descending from the Father of lights. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V. Sing praise to our God on the harp, on the harp and with the voice of a psalm. P. Descending. V. Glory and honor. P. Descending.

Prayer. O wondrous Lord, your name. Folio 388.

## On the Fifth Sunday of Easter

### At Vespers

Lauda. “They praised you, Lord.” Prayer. “They praise you, Lord.” [Col. 0647D] Folio 371.

Sono. Who is a great God like our God? P. You are the God who alone works wonders. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.—Glorious among the holy ones, wondrous in majesty, performing marvels. R. You are.

May the Lord be always with you. R. And with you.

Antiphon. Alleluia. God waters the mountains from above; the earth shall be satisfied from the fruit of your works. P. Bringing forth grass for cattle and plants for the service of human beings. V. How magnified are your works, O Lord! You have made all things in wisdom; the earth is filled with your creation. P. Bringing forth. V. Glory. P. Bringing forth.

May the Lord be with you. R. And with you.

[Col. 0648A] Lauda. I saw and heard the voices of many angels around the throne, standing in the presence of the Lamb, the voices of the four living creatures and the elders. P. They resounded with a great roar: Alleluia. R. Great is our Lord, and great is his power, and there is no number to his wisdom. P. With a great roar. V. Glory. P. With a great roar.

Hymn. “You hundred thousand times ten thousand.” Folio 382. Supplication. “Let us pray to the Redeemer.” Capitulum. “Christ, Son of God, rest of our [souls].” Benediction. “Christ, Son of God, who on this day.” Folio 383.

Lauda. Wisdom is from the Lord God, Alleluia, P. and it was always with him and exists before the ages. Alleluia, alleluia. V. The Lord has made his salvation known; before the sight of the nations he has revealed his righteousness. [Col. 0648B] P. And it was with him. 390 V. Glory and honor to the Father, etc. P. And with him.

Prayer. Christ, Son of God, who, having been slain as the Lamb, rise in glory, and, possessing human power, have deigned to illumine the earth, so that, watered by the rains of your passion and resurrection, it might follow you alone to life—the earth that once had shattered itself in a fall into death; favoring our prayers, we ask you: grant us both the opportunity to rise again in good works and the power to die to works of wickedness. Through your mercy.

In the name of the Lord.

### At Matins

Antiphon. “I slept.” Psalm III. Prayer. “Lord Jesus Christ.” See folio 369.

[Col. 0648C] Antiphon 1. I saw a Lamb, as though slain, in the midst of the elders; and they sang a new song, saying: P. You are worthy to receive the book and to break its seals, because you redeemed the world. R. You made him a little lower than the angels; you crowned him with glory and honor. P. You are worthy. V. Glory and honor. P. You are worthy.

Prayer. Christ, Son of God, who was slain. See during the Vespers of this Sunday.

Antiphon 2. The Lord alone made great lights: the sun to rule the day; P. but the moon and the stars to rule the night. V. Praise the name of the Lord; praise, servants of the Lord. P. But the moon. V. Glory and honor to the Father. P. The moon.

Prayer. Lord, who alone made the great lights, [Col. 0648D] and in wisdom placed the moon and stars under the rule of night, lead us out from the yoke of spiritual wickedness with a strong hand and an outstretched arm; and cut away whatever obstacles oppose us along our course, because you are Lord of lords and remain the guardian of our souls. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Antiphon 3. Great are the works of the Lord, sought out P. according to all his desires. V. He has made a memorial of his wonders; the Lord is merciful and compassionate. P. According to all. V. Glory, etc. P. According to all.

Prayer. Great are your works, Lord, sought out according to all your desires. Grant us, your servants, that, while we marvel at the greatness of your works, we may praise the magnificence of the Creator with due confession; and that we may seek your faithful commandments with reverent wisdom, and make the perfect beauty of understanding into obedience through fear. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

R. I am the Lord your God, and there is no other Savior besides me. The islands have heard and the ends of the earth have feared. P. Hear, Israel, my servant, my chosen Jacob, offspring of Abraham, my friend. V. I am the first, and I am the last. My hand also founded the earth, and my right hand is a table for the heavens [reading *mensa est*; uncertain]. P. Hear, Israel.

Prayer. You are the Lord God, and there is no other besides you; yet you are not confined, whom the ends of the earth have recognized, while they were drawn forth by the calling of faith from you [the reading is uncertain]. Grant us, therefore, to be so rooted in you that, through the worship of righteousness and the dignity of our works, we may deserve to attain eternal rest. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

### At Lauds

For the Canticle. Antiphon. You guided your people, Lord, in your righteousness—this people whom you redeemed.

Canticle. Let us sing to the Lord gloriously. See folio 369.

Prayer. May your right hand be glorified, Lord, which crushes the enemies of our soul and life; and through the greatness of your majesty may it still crush them. And may it three times engulf us, who are the contrivers of evil thoughts, words, and deeds. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.
