[Col. 0649C] For the Benedictus. Antiphon. To you alone, O God, be honor. Canticle. Blessed is the Lord, God of our fathers. Folio 6. Sono: “I slept and rested.” See folio 370.

391 Lauda. Praise the Lord from the heavens, Alleluia, alleluia; praise him in the highest. Alleluia. Psalm CXLVIII.

### Apocalypse of the Apostle John (Chapter XIX)

R. Thanks be to God.

I, John, was in the Spirit, and I saw heaven opened, and behold, a white horse; and he who sat upon it is called Faithful and True, and in righteousness he judges and fights. His eyes are like a flame of fire, and upon his head are many diadems; he has a name written that no one knows except himself. He was clothed [Col. 0649D] in a garment sprinkled with blood, and his name is called THE WORD OF GOD. And the armies that are in heaven followed him on white horses, clothed in clean white linen. And from his mouth proceeds a sharp sword, so that with it he may strike the nations. And he will rule them with an iron rod; and he himself treads the winepress of the wine of the fury of the wrath of Almighty God. And upon his garment and upon his thigh he has a name written: King of kings and Lord of lords. R. Amen.

Hymn. “This is the true day of God.” Capitulum. “Christ, Son of God, who [the venerable course] of this day.” See folio 371. Lauda. “Wisdom is from the Lord God.” See folio 389. Benediction. “Christ the Lord, who [made] the day of the Resurrection.” Folio 372.

[Col. 0650A] At the end of Vespers.

Lauda. “They praised you, Lord.” Prayer. “They praise you, Lord.” See folio 371. Sono. “Who is a great God.” Folio 389.

Antiphon. May the glory of the Lord be forever and ever; P. the Lord will rejoice in his works. V. He looks upon the earth and makes it tremble; he touches the mountains, and they smoke. P. The Lord will rejoice. V. Glory and honor to the Father. P. The Lord will rejoice.

May the Lord be always with you. R. And with you.

Lauda. Go up to Jerusalem, daughters of Zion, P. and praise your God. Alleluia, alleluia. V. From the rising of the sun to its setting, praise the name of the Lord. P. And praise. V. Glory and honor to the Father. P. And praise.

Hymn. “Let the height of heaven sing praise.” See folio 385. [Col. 0650B] Supplication. “Let us pray.” Capitulum. “O God, through whom we have distinguished this day from all others.” Benediction. “Christ the Lord, who.” See folio 372. Lauda. “Wisdom is from the Lord God.” Prayer. “Christ, Son of God.” See folio 390.

## On the Sixth Sunday of Easter

### At Vespers

Lauda. “They praised you, Lord.” Prayer. “They praise you, Lord.” Folio 371.

Sono. All nations, clap your hands; shout joyfully to God. P. With a voice of rejoicing, Alleluia. V. Sing psalms to our God, sing psalms; sing psalms to our King, sing psalms. For God is King of all the earth; sing psalms. P. With a voice.

May the Lord be always with you. R. And with you.

Antiphon. I heard a loud voice in heaven, saying: The Lamb who was slain P. is worthy to receive power, divinity, wisdom, and blessing forever and ever. V. Sing to the Lord a new song, because he has done marvelous things. P. Is worthy. V. Glory and honor to the Father. P. Is worthy.

May the Lord be always with you. R. And with you.

Lauda. The Lord has heard the poor and has not abandoned his fettered ones. P. Let heaven and earth praise him. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V. Let the poor see and rejoice; seek the Lord, and your soul shall live. P. Let them praise. V. Glory. P. Let them praise.

Hymn. “You hundred thousand legions.” Supplication. “Let us pray.” Capitulum. “Christ, Son of God.” Benediction. “Christ, Son of God, who in this.” See folio 382.

Lauda. Alleluia. Sing to the Lord on the harp, Alleluia, on the harp and with the voice of a psalm. Alleluia, alleluia. P. Shout joyfully to God, all the earth; sing a psalm to his name. V. On the harp. V. Glory. P. On the harp.

Prayer. Wondrous and immeasurable Lord, mercifully make us humble and attentive, so that, since your name is wondrous in all the earth, you may more firmly heap upon us the discipline of truth. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

### At Matins

Antiphon. “I slept.” Psalm III. Prayer. “Lord Jesus Christ.” See folio 369.

Antiphon 1. Your testimonies, Lord, have become exceedingly trustworthy. P. Throughout the length of days. 392 V. The upheavals of the sea are wondrous; the Lord is wondrous in the heights. [Col. 0651A] P. Throughout the length. V. Glory, etc. P. Throughout the length.

Prayer. May your testimonies, Lord, which have become trustworthy for us, be constant in our meditation, just as they are sincere in the truth of faith; and may they thus be completed in our works as they are uttered by our mouths; may they govern those who mourn through consolation and make them more ready. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Antiphon 2. The birds of heaven and the fish that travel the paths of the sea. P. For your name, Lord, is wondrous in all the earth. V. And you appointed him over the works of your hands. You subjected all things beneath his feet. P. Wondrous. V. Glory and honor. P. Wondrous.

[Col. 0651B] Prayer. Wondrous Lord. See above at the end of Vespers of this Sunday.

Antiphon 3. Sing psalms to our God, sing psalms; sing psalms to our King, sing psalms. P. For God is King of all the earth; sing psalms wisely. V. All nations, clap your hands; shout joyfully to God with a voice of rejoicing. P. For God is King. V. Glory and honor. P. For God is King.

Prayer. Grant us, Lord, to sing psalms to you wisely, not only with our voice but also with our mind, so that, in accordance with the greatness of your name, you may magnify your praise through our voices. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

R. Remember our fathers, how they were saved in the Red Sea while their enemies pursued them, and let us cry out to heaven; and the Lord will have mercy on us, according to the covenant of our fathers. P. So that all nations may know that there is one who redeems and frees Israel. V. Your right hand, Lord, has been glorified in strength; your right hand has crushed the enemies. And through the greatness of your majesty you have shattered your adversaries. P. So that they may know.

Prayer. Remember, Lord, how you freed our fathers while their enemies pursued them; you exalted your right hand against their adversaries. For you are our God, who are honored according to what is owed and exalted according to merit. Grant us, therefore, that we who travel through the sea of this age may not be broken by any blows from the waves of the world. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

[Col. 0651D] At Lauds.

For the Canticle. Antiphon. The waves of the sea froze like a wall; the flowing wave stood in the midst of the sea.

Canticle. Let us sing to the Lord gloriously.

For the Benedictus. Antiphon. To you alone, O God. Sono. “I slept and rested.” See folio 370.

[Col. 0652A] Apocalypse of the Apostle John (Chapter XXII)

R. Thanks be to God.

I, John, was in the Spirit, and the Lord showed me a river of the water of life, bright as crystal, proceeding from the throne of God and of the Lamb. In the midst of its street, and on either side of the river, was the tree of life, bearing twelve fruits and yielding its fruit each month; and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations. And there shall no longer be any curse; but the throne of God and of the Lamb shall be in it, and his servants shall serve him. And they shall see his face, and his name shall be on their foreheads. And night shall be no more; and they shall need neither the light of a lamp nor the light of the sun, because the Lord God will illumine them, and they shall reign forever and ever. R. Amen.

[Col. 0652B] Hymn. “This is the true day of God.” Capitulum. “Christ, Son of God, who [the venerable course] of this day.” See folio 371. Lauda. “Alleluia, sing to the Lord on the harp.” Folio 391. Benediction. “Christ, Son of God.” Folio 383.

At the end of Vespers.

Lauda. “They praised you, Lord.” Prayer. “They praise you, Lord.” See 317. Sono. “All nations, clap your hands.” Folio 391. Antiphon. I saw a Lamb, as though slain, in the midst of the elders; for he had upon his garment P. and upon his head written: King of kings and Lord of lords. V. Great is the Lord and exceedingly worthy of praise, and there is no end to his greatness. P. And upon his head. V. Glory and honor to the Father. P. And upon his head.

May the Lord be always with you. R. And with you.

Lauda. All say praise to our God. P. You who fear him, small and great. Alleluia, alleluia. R. Behold, now bless the Lord, all servants of the Lord. P. You who fear him. 393 V. Glory and honor to the Father. P. You who fear him.

May the Lord be with you. R. And with you.

Another Lauda. Alleluia. With joy we shall enter the sanctuary of the Lord, and with exultation P. we shall return, singing: Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V. Let all the earth adore you, O God, and sing psalms to you; let it sing a psalm to your name. P. We shall return. V. Glory and honor. P. We shall return.

May the Lord be with you. R. And with you.

Another Lauda. A fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, P. which flow forcefully from Lebanon. Alleluia, [Col. 0652D] alleluia. V. Watering the mountains from above; the earth shall be satisfied from the fruit of your works. P. Which flow. V. Glory. P. Which.

Hymn. “Let the height sing praise.” Supplication, Capitulum, and Benediction, as on folio 386. Lauda. “Alleluia, sing to the Lord on the harp.”

Prayer. Wondrous Lord. Folio 391.

## On the Ascension of the Lord

[Col. 0651]

### At Vespers

[Col. 0651D]

395 Lauda. “They praised you, Lord.” Prayer. “They praise you, Lord.” Folio 371.

Sono. The earth is the Lord’s, and its fullness; the world, P. and all who dwell in it. Alleluia. [Col. 0652D] V. Lift up your gates, O princes, and be lifted up, eternal gates, and the King of glory shall enter. P. And all who dwell in it.

May the Lord be with you. R. And with you.

Antiphon. The Father of glory raised Jesus Christ [Col. 0653A] from the dead and seated him at his right hand above the heavens, above every Principality, Power, Virtue, and Dominion, P. and above every name that is named. V. God has ascended amid rejoicing; the Lord amid the sound of the trumpet. P. And above. V. Glory. P. And above.

Prayer. Almighty God, Father of glory, who raised our Lord Jesus Christ from the dead, seating him at your right hand above every Principality and Power, raise up in us the pursuits of complete holiness, so that the first fruits of our spirit may be bound to him alone who, rising from the dead, conquered the prince of death by his own power. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Antiphon 2. Ascender of heaven, our helper, P. the clouds proclaim his magnificence; his dwelling is above. V. The chariot of God is ten thousandfold, thousands of rejoicing ones; the Lord is among them, at Sinai, in the sanctuary. P. His magnificence. V. Glory and honor. P. His magnificence.

May the Lord be with you. R. And with you.

Lauda. I heard the voice of a great multitude saying: Alleluia; honor and glory to our God. P. Because his judgments are just and true. And again they said: Alleluia. P. And they worshiped him who sat upon the throne, saying: Amen and Alleluia. V. The Lord is exalted above all nations; his glory is above the heavens. P. Because his judgments are just. V. Glory. P. And they worshiped.

Hymn.

Eternal King most high,  
Redeemer and of the faithful,  
by whom death, being loosed, perishes,  
the triumph of grace is given;  
whom the subdued law of Tartarus,  
fading in Avernus, drove out;  
deprived of its deadly sword,  
it sent him back to the Father’s throne.

Ascending the tribunal  
at the Father’s right hand,  
all power was bestowed upon Jesus from heaven,  
which he did not possess according to his humanity.

So that the threefold structure of creation—  
of heavenly, earthly,  
and infernal things—  
now subjected may bend the knee.

And in no way may salvation  
be outside your name;  
by whom all things were created,  
and all things were recreated and made holy.

This great grace of Christ  
removed the bond of sins;  
he took a body of his own  
and possesses the whole expanse of heaven.

The angels tremble, seeing  
the condition of mortals reversed:  
the flesh is culpable, and the flesh cleanses;  
God’s flesh reigns as God.

It surpasses the highest virtues,  
far above the heavenly ones:  
God in flesh and spirit,  
fully God and true Man.

The angels say from the stars  
that he will finally return in this manner;  
we believe that he will return,  
and we know that he will reign completely.

You, Christ, our joy,  
remaining endowed with Olympus,  
rule the fabric of the world,  
overcoming worldly joys.

Therefore, praying, we ask you:  
forgive all our sins;  
lift our hearts upward  
to you by heavenly grace.

So that when you begin to shine  
in the red cloud of the Judge,  
you may repel the punishments we deserve  
and restore the crowns we have lost.

Grant us to strive there  
with diligent devotion,  
where we believe you sit with the Father  
in the citadel of the kingdom.

Glory to you, Lord,  
who ascend above the stars,  
with the Father and the Holy Spirit,  
through everlasting ages.

Amen.

396 Supplication. Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world, our Lord Jesus Christ; let us beseech him with every supplication, that he may graciously deign to justify us through the glory of his Ascension. R. Grant this, eternal and almighty God.

Lord, have mercy. R. Christ, have mercy. Lord, have mercy.

Capitulum. Be graciously present and favor those celebrating the feast of your Ascension, O Lord; and you who have carried the frailty of our flesh with you to be glorified in heaven, remove the corruption of former sins and restore to us the dignity of our former life, so that by believing that you have ascended there we may deserve to ascend, [reading: “q o,” evidently quo, “where”] where we now truly believe that you have gone up.

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” Folio 2.

Benediction. May Christ the Lord, who by ascending brought the assumed human being to the Father’s throne, lead you to the freedom of eternal glory. R. Amen. And may he who, when he was lifted up from the earth, promised to draw all things to himself, allow none of you to be separated from his body. R. Amen. May he establish you to be crowned without end by himself, who alone, ascending in your body, entered the hidden places of heaven. R. Amen.

Through.

Lauda. I shall ascend to my Father and your Father, Alleluia. P. To my God and your God. Alleluia, alleluia. V. The Lord is exalted above all nations, and his glory is above the heavens. P. To my God. V. Glory and honor. P. To my God.

Prayer. Immeasurable King of kings, to whom the God of heaven has given a kingdom strong, powerful, and honored, while he subjected all things to your power; to whom thousands upon thousands of angels minister: grant your people rest from all the burdens under which we remain weighed down, [Col. 0655A] so that you who ascended gloriously into heaven may be gentle when your glory has been revealed. R. Amen.

Through your mercy, etc.

In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, let us complete this in peace. R. Thanks be to God.

## On the Ascension of the Lord

### At Matins

Antiphon. “I slept and rose again.” Psalm III. Prayer. “Lord Jesus Christ, who for us took sleep,” etc. See folio 369.

Antiphon 1. Thrones were set in place, and the Ancient of Days sat down; his garment was splendid, and his throne was a flame of fire. P. Thousands upon thousands served him, and ten thousand times a hundred thousand stood before him. V. All nations [Col. 0655B] clap their hands; shout joyfully to God with a voice of rejoicing. P. Thousands upon thousands. V. Glory and honor to the Father. P. Thousands upon thousands.

Prayer. Immeasurable King of kings, etc. See during the Vespers of this feast.

Antiphon 2. In the likeness of a man I saw a man seated upon a throne, possessing great splendor; P. and all the armies of the heavenly host of angels cried out together, saying: Behold, his dominion, kingdom, and glory remain without end forever. V. Your footsteps were seen, O God, the footsteps of my God, of the king who is in the sanctuary. P. And all the armies. V. Glory and honor. P. And all the armies.

Prayer. Only-begotten Son of God, who, having conquered death and making the passage from earthly things to heavenly things, appeared as the Son [Col. 0655C] of man, possessing great splendor upon the throne, whom the entire heavenly army of angels praises: grant us not to be bound in our hearts by any chains of wickedness in this age, as we sing with glorious devotion of faith that you have ascended to the Father, so that the gaze of our hearts may be directed continually to that place to which you ascended gloriously after your wounds. R. Amen.

Through your mercy, etc.

Antiphon 3. Men of Galilee, why do you stand looking into heaven? P. This Jesus, who has been taken up from you, will come in the same way as you saw him going into heaven. V. From your temple, which is in Jerusalem, kings will offer gifts to you. P. This Jesus. V. Glory [Col. 0655D] and honor. P. This Jesus.

Prayer. Our Savior and Lord, who, as you ascended into heaven, deigned to appear glorified to the eyes of those who watched, while you promise that you will come to judgment just as you ascended: make us receive the feast of your Ascension today with pure devotion of heart, so that our life may always advance for the better by ascending in you, and may so behold you, when you come to judgment, with an unashamed gaze of vision. R. Amen.

Through.

R. The heavens bowed down when the Creator of the stars trod upon the heads of the clouds, and when the Ruler of all ascended into heaven; the multitude of angels was shaken with trembling as they cried out 397 and said: P. How great is this one, whom Thrones and Dominions meet? V. I saw in heaven a multitude of many angels, which no one could number; and they cried out with a loud voice, saying: P. How great.

Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ, Creator of the stars, who bowed the heads of the clouds when you humbled yourself in the life of mortals, so that in that body in which you endured the insults of the ungodly for us, in that same body you might ascend above all the heavens of heavens and receive the praises of the angels: hear us graciously, and in your mercy grant us this, that, freed from our crimes, we may now follow you as our guide in our hearts to that place to which you ascended glorified in human form, so that even then we may behold you as the eternal Creator and Lord in majesty, whom we now await as true God and judge. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

[Col. 0656B] At Lauds.

For the Canticle. Antiphon. The Lord ascended into the heavens and thunders; he himself judges the ends of the earth. He is powerful and gives strength to our kings, and he has exalted the horn of his people.

Canticle. My heart has been established in the Lord. Folio 55. Let the antiphon be repeated: “The Lord ascended into the heavens and thunders,” etc.

Prayer. Christ, Son of God, who, ascending into heaven as conqueror, thunder: grant us always to see you in truth and to enjoy the grace of your vision. And you who, having conquered death, return by ascending to the paternal throne, give strength to our kings and exalt the majesty of your glory. V. Amen.

[Col. 0656C] Through your mercy.

For the Benedictus. Antiphon. We bless you, Lord, who sit above the cherubim, King of Israel.

Canticle. Blessed are you, Lord God of our fathers. See folio 6.

Sono. Alleluia. Kingdoms of the earth, sing to God; Alleluia, alleluia, sing psalms to the Lord; sing psalms to our God, Alleluia, who ascended above the heavens of heavens toward the east. Behold, he will give his voice, the voice of his power. Alleluia.

Lauda. Praise the Lord from the heavens, Alleluia. V. Praise him in the highest, Alleluia, alleluia. Praise him, all his angels, Alleluia, alleluia. Psalm CXLVIII.

### Reading from the Book of the Prophet Daniel (Chapter VII)

[Col. 0656D] V. Thanks be to God.

In those days: I, Daniel, was watching until thrones were set in place and the Ancient of Days sat down. His clothing was white as snow, and the hair of his head was like clean wool; his throne was a flame of fire, and its wheels were burning fire. A stream of fire, rapid and flowing, came forth from before him; thousands upon thousands served him, and ten thousand times a hundred thousand stood before him. The court sat, and the books were opened.

I continued watching in the vision of the night, and behold, with the clouds of heaven there came one like a son of man, and he came even to the Ancient of Days; and they presented him before him. And he gave him power, honor, and a kingdom; and every people, tribe, and language serves him. His power is an eternal power that shall not be taken away, and his kingdom shall not be destroyed. R. Amen.

Hymn. “Eternal King most high, Redeemer and of the faithful.” Supplication. “Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world,” etc. See folio 396.

Capitulum. Lord, King of glory, who, when the oracles of the prophets had been revealed and fulfilled, return as though lifting up the eternal gates to the Father’s throne: because, while your divinity returns to the place from which it never departed, access to heaven is opened to the human race; grant that our intention may be extended there, where our true redemption has gone before us; and let us not cling in captive delight to earthly things, since the head of our body already reigns with you in heaven.

Our Father. “Delivered from evil,” etc. Folio 2.

[Col. 0657B] Lauda. “I shall ascend to my Father.” Benediction. “Christ the Lord, who assumed the human being.” See folio 396.

At the end of Vespers on the Ascension of the Lord.

Lauda. By day the Lord commanded his mercy; P. and by night he declared it. V. With me is prayer to the God of my life; I shall say to my God: You are my protector. P. And by night he declared it.

Prayer. O God, who by day commands your mercy and by night declares it, we ask that by day you protect us for salvation and by night defend us for rest. R. Amen.

Through your mercy, etc.

Sono. “The earth is the Lord’s.” Folio 395.

Antiphon. God has ascended amid rejoicing, P. the Lord amid the sound of the trumpet. V. All nations, clap your hands; shout joyfully to God with a voice of [Col. 0657C] rejoicing. P. The Lord amid the sound.

May the Lord be always with you. R. And with you.

Lauda. The Lord ascended into the heavens and thundered, Alleluia. P. He himself judges the ends of the earth. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V. The Lord is exalted above all nations; his glory is above the heavens. P. He himself judges. V. Glory and honor. P. He himself judges.

May the Lord be with you. R. And with you.

Lauda. Sing psalms to God, Alleluia. P. To him who ascended above the heavens of heavens toward the east. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V. Exalt God, our helper; shout joyfully to the God of Jacob. P. To him who ascended. V. Glory and [Col. 0657D] honor. P. To him who ascended.

Hymn. “Eternal King most high.” Folio 395.

Supplication. “Let us pray.” See folio 396.

Capitulum. Christ, power of God and wisdom of God, who for us and for our salvation descended from heaven and deigned to be clothed in the flesh of the human race, so that by a most worthy fellowship you might clothe us with your divinity, and so that what you had assumed as mortal in descending you might grant to immortality in ascending: grant us, through the intervention of today’s solemnity, by which we both desire and rejoice to follow you as you ascend into heaven, that, recognizing the gifts of this most gracious dispensation, we may render to your goodness the only thing we can—the vows of praise—while awaiting the consolations of eternal joys at your second coming, at whose command we say:

[Col. 0658A] Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” Folio 2.

Benediction. May Jesus Christ the Lord preserve in you whole and undefiled the peace that, returning to heaven, he gave to his disciples. V. Amen. May he also assign to you as a defense the holy angels whom, as he was about to ascend into heaven, he chose for his service. R. Amen. May he, as author, raise you there by faith, where you hope to be taken up by him into rest. R. Amen.

Through his mercy, etc.

Lauda. “I shall ascend to my Father.”

Prayer. King of kings, to whom the God of heaven [has given …]. See above at the first Vespers.

## On the Sunday after the Ascension of the Lord

### At Vespers

[Col. 0658B] Lauda. “They praised you, Lord,” with its prayer. See folio 371.

Sono. Alleluia. Kingdoms of the earth, sing to God; Alleluia, alleluia. V. Sing psalms to the Lord; sing psalms to our God, Alleluia, who ascended above the heavens of heavens toward the east. Behold, he will give his voice, the voice of his power. Alleluia.

May the Lord be with you. R. And with you.

Antiphon. He who ascended above the heavens of heavens, P. toward the east: the Lord is his name. V. Kingdoms of the earth, sing to God; sing psalms to the Lord; sing psalms to God. P. Toward the east. V. Glory and honor. P. Toward the east.

May the Lord be with you. R. And with you.

Lauda. The Savior, performing signs and wonders in heaven and on earth, P. has himself freed us, who ascended into the heavens. Alleluia. V. Great is our Lord, and great is his power, and there is no number to his wisdom. P. He himself. V. Glory and honor. P. He himself.

Hymn.

The hallowed seasons of Christ,  
foretold by prophetic oracles,  
the truth of faith fulfilled, strengthening hearts with power:  
that the Lord of the world had come  
in the temple of his holy body,  
so that he himself might save  
the human being whom he had made  
and who had been lost.

While he suffers as one able to suffer,  
the assumed human being dies.  
The impassible God,  
Creator of all, rises again.

Having been raised in the body,  
on the days long before foretold,  
he brought forth the riches of salvation  
in the number forty.

When all these forty days  
had been completed,  
ascending on high, he led captive  
captivity  
and gave gifts to human beings.

Before his disciples,  
who had been warned of his coming,  
so that they might behold him returning  
when the appointed time had arrived.

That time was known only to the Father,  
unknown even to the Son,  
as the anxious disciples learned;  
it was not permitted to us to know it.

Yet they, accustomed to standing,  
were commanded by the highest Messengers  
to remain until they received  
the power of the Spirit  
sent from on high.

That power, provided for our salvation,  
we celebrate with joy;  
as a companion of the praises of the saints,  
the hymn resounds for all.

399 Grant us to strive there  
with diligent devotion,  
where we believe you sit with the Father  
in the citadel of the kingdom.

[Col. 0659B] Glory to you, Lord,  
who ascend above the stars,  
with the Father and the Holy Spirit,  
through everlasting ages.

Amen.

Supplication. Let us pray. See folio 396.

Capitulum. Lord Jesus Christ, who ascended above the heavens of heavens toward the east, conquering the west: those whom you received to redeem, perfect in yourself so that they may be raised to the heights; so that where you, the glorified Head, have gone before, you may draw the whole body there to be honored; and do not leave in the setting world those whom, as the conqueror, you raise toward the perpetual east.

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” Folio 2.

Benediction. May Christ, Son of God, who ascended to the Father amid triumphal rejoicing, glorify you by the heavenly ascent of your hearts. R. Amen. And may he who was exalted from the earth in the form of your body draw you, through the gifts of his divinity, to things above. R. Amen. May he draw all of you there, to the faith that is to be rewarded, where he himself, glorified in human form, ascended. R. Amen.

Through.

Lauda. The Lord has prepared his throne in heaven, Alleluia, and his kingdom shall rule over all. Alleluia. P. Bless the Lord, all his angels. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V. Praise him, all nations; praise him, all peoples. P. Bless. V. Glory. P. Bless.

[Col. 0659D] Prayer. Lord, who dwell in the heights and look upon the humble in heaven and on earth, graciously bend us before you; and you who promise the blessedness of angels in all things, deign to form us according to angelic obedience. R. Amen.

Through.

In the name.

## On the Sunday after the Ascension of the Lord

### At Matins

Antiphon. “I slept.” Psalm III. Prayer. “Lord Jesus Christ.” See folio 369.

Antiphon 1. Your throne is prepared from of old, O God. P. And you are from eternity. V. The rivers have lifted up, Lord; the rivers have lifted up their voices. P. And you are from eternity. V. Glory and honor to the Father, etc. P. And from eternity.

[Col. 0660A] Prayer. Lord, who are clothed with strength and girded with power, make us ready before the throne of your majesty, so that from of old and from eternity we may magnify your name, and may you deign to be gracious on earth, you who are wondrous in the heights. R. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God, etc.

Antiphon 2. Who is like the Lord our God, P. who dwells in the heights and looks upon the humble in heaven and on earth? V. The Lord is exalted above all nations; his glory is above the heavens. P. Who dwells in the heights. V. Glory and honor. P. Who.

Prayer. Lord, who dwell in the heights. See above during the preceding Vespers.

Antiphon 3. The Lord is exalted and looks upon the humble, P. and he recognizes the lofty from afar. V. Praise the Lord, children, [Col. 0660B] praise the name of the Lord. P. And the lofty. V. Glory. P. And the lofty.

Prayer. Exalted Lord, who regardest the humble, grant us the humility by which thou art pleased; nor let pride remain in us, which thou knowest from afar and destroyest when near: so that, by thy mercy, the arrogance that casts down may depart from our mind, and the contrition that glorifies thee may remain in our heart. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

R. With trumpets beaten out, and with the voice of the horn, sing for joy before the King, the Lord: let the sea and its fullness be moved; the inhabited world and all who dwell in it. Rivers. P. Let them clap their hands together. V. The mountains and hills shall sing praise before God, and all the trees of the region. P. Let them clap their hands [Col. 0660C].

Prayer. The whole earth rejoices in thee, Lord, and all who dwell in it; the rivers clap their hands to thee; the mouths of teachers obey thee not only in the service of speech, but also in the ministry of good works: Grant therefore, our God, that by thy authorship both forms of praise may prevail in us—continual and unwearied meditation, and the sincere, undefiled practice of holy conduct. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

## At Lauds

For the Canticle. Antiphon. Thy right hand, Lord, has been glorified in power; thy right hand, Lord, has shattered the enemies. And by the greatness of thy majesty thou hast crushed the adversaries.

Canticle. Let us sing to the Lord. Folio 369.

For the Benedictus. Antiphon. Above the throne of thy kingdom, in the firmament of heaven, blessed art thou, Lord.

Canticle. Blessed art thou, Lord. Folio 6. Tone. Alleluia, kingdoms of the earth. Folio 397.

Laud. Praise the Lord from the heavens, alleluia, alleluia; praise him in the highest. Psalm 148.

## Revelation of John the Apostle (Chapter VII)

R. Thanks be to God.

I, John, was in the Spirit, and I saw a great multitude which no one could number, from every nation, tribe, people, and language, standing before the throne and in the sight of the Lamb, clothed in white robes, with palms in their hands. And they cried out with a loud voice, saying: Salvation belongs to our God, who sits upon the throne, and to the Lamb. And all the angels stood around the throne, and around the elders and the four living creatures; and they fell on their faces before the throne and worshiped God, saying: Amen. Blessing and glory and wisdom and thanksgiving and honor and power and strength be to our God for ever and ever. R. Amen.

Hymn. The sacred times of Christ. Folio 398. Supplication. Let us pray. Folio 396.

Chapters. Lord, who hast ascended on high, leading captivity captive, rescue us from the captivity of the Devil by the triumphs of thy victory; so that, while thou bestowest thy gifts upon human beings, thou mayest make those human beings wholly participate in thy gifts.

[Col. 0661B] Our Father. Deliver us from evil. Folio 2.

Laud. The Lord is in heaven. Folio 399.

Blessing. Christ, the Son of God, who in triumphal procession—Folio 399.

In the name of the Lord.

## At the End of Vespers

Laud. They praised with their prayer. Folio 371. Tone. Alleluia, kingdoms of the earth. Folio 397.

Antiphon. The Lord is exalted in the heavens. P. His glory. V. Who is like the Lord our God, who dwells on high and regards the humble in heaven and on earth? P. His glory. V. Glory and—P. His glory.

The Lord. R. And.

Laud. God has ascended amid jubilation, alleluia; the Lord with the sound of the trumpet, alleluia. P. Sing praises to our God, alleluia; sing praises. Alleluia. V. All nations, clap your hands; shout joyfully to God with a voice of exultation. P. Sing praises. V. Glory and—P. Sing praises.

The Lord. R. And with.

Laud 2. I saw a radiant man seated upon the throne of his glory, alleluia. P. And around the elders voices cried out through the instrument, saying: Alleluia, alleluia. V. For I have known that the Lord is great, and our God above all gods. P. And around. V. Glory and—P. And around.

Hymn. The sacred times of Christ. Seek at folio 398. Supplication. Let us pray, as above.

Chapters. Lord Jesus Christ, who hast exalted thy throne more highly in Jerusalem, thy city, which is indeed the Church, while thou dost gloriously acquire it and triumphantly ascendest from it to the Father; while in the human nature assumed thou makest manifest the glory of thy Assumption: therefore may our vows be pleasing to thee and our works acceptable, so that thereby we may possess the kingdom with thee in everlasting glory.

Our Father. Deliver us from evil. Folio 2.

Blessing. May the Lord Christ be your helper, who, taken up into the heavens, now sits at the right hand of the Father. R. Amen. May your body likewise suffer no enslavement to any torpid passions, he who took him up glorified into heaven. R. Amen. So that you who have seen the glory of his ascension may not be punished by the sentence of the Judge. R. Amen.

Through.

[Col. 0662A] Laud. The Lord has prepared in heaven. Prayer. Lord, who dwellest on high. Folio 399.

In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ begins the Office of the fasts, observed on Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, and Saturday before holy Pentecost, to entreat our Lord Jesus Christ for our sins and to obtain peace, or to hear the sacred readings; and, so that the Spirit Paraclete may come and find our dwelling places clean, let us frequent the Church of the Lord.

Prayer. Although, Lord. Folio 68.

Let thy mercy, Lord, be upon us, since thou who fashionest human hearts individually mayest sanctify them distinctly; and because thy eyes are upon those who fear thee, grant us the fullness of thy fear, so that thou mayest also bestow upon us an abundance of the knowledge of thee. R. Amen.

## Reading from the Book of the Proverbs of Solomon (Chapter III)

R. Thanks be to God.

My son, put your trust in the Lord with all your heart, and do not rely on your own prudence. In all your ways acknowledge him, and he himself will direct your steps. Do not be wise in your own eyes; fear the Lord and depart from evil. For it will be health to your body and refreshment to your bones. Honor the Lord from your substance and from the firstfruits of all your produce; and your barns will be filled with abundance, and your winepresses will overflow with wine. My son, do not reject the discipline of the Lord, nor grow weary when you are rebuked by him; for the Lord rebukes the one whom he loves, and, like a father with his son, he takes pleasure in him. R. Amen.

Hymn. Of kindness. Supplication. Let us pray. Folio 69.

Chapters. May the Holy Spirit descend to us, Lord, through whom thou mayest possess our cleansed hearts and receive the prayer instituted by thee; so that thou mayest accept our petitions not through us but through him, just as through him thou dost wipe away our crimes. With him, who reigns equally with thee and with the Father, interceding for us, through him we cry out to thee from the earth.

Our Father, who art in heaven. Deliver us from evil. Folio 10.

Laud. The Lord has prepared his throne in heaven, alleluia, and his kingdom shall rule over all, alleluia. P. Bless the Lord, all his angels, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V. Praise the Lord, all nations, and praise him together, all peoples. P. Bless the Lord. V. Glory and honor. P. Bless the Lord.

Blessing. May the Spirit make those who await him spotless from defilement. R. Amen. May he fill with his gift those whom he sees enduring for him. R. Amen. So that when he comes we may be filled with the holiness of the one whose coming we lovingly await. R. Amen. By the service and help of him who, with the Father and the Son, lives and reigns, one God, for ever and ever. R. Amen.

May the Lord be always with you. R. And with you.

In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, etc.

The following are to be said at Terce, Sext, and None.

## At Terce

Prophecy. My son, keep my words. Seek at folio 96.

## Reading from the Book of Exodus (Chapter XVI)

R. Thanks be to God.

In those days, the whole congregation of the children of Israel came into the desert of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month after they had gone out from the land of Egypt. And the whole congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and against Aaron. Therefore the children of Israel said: Would that we had died by the hand of the Lord in the land of Egypt, when we sat by pots of meat and ate bread to satiety! Why have you brought us into this desert, to kill the whole multitude with hunger?

But the Lord said to Moses: Behold, I shall rain bread for you from heaven. Let the people go out and gather what is sufficient for each day, so that I may test them, whether they will walk in my ways or not. But on the sixth day let them prepare what they bring in, and let it be twice what they were accustomed to gather each day.

And Moses and Aaron said to all the children of Israel: In the evening you shall know that the Lord brought you out from the land of Egypt; and in the morning you shall see his glory. For I have heard your murmuring against the Lord. But what are we, that you murmur against us? And Moses said: The Lord will give you meat to eat in the evening, and bread to satiety in the morning, because he has heard the murmuring with which you have murmured against him. For what are we? Your murmuring is not against us but against God.

And Moses said to Aaron: Say to the whole congregation of the children of Israel: Draw near before the Lord, for he has heard your murmuring. And while Aaron was speaking to the whole assembly of the children of Israel, they looked toward the wilderness, and behold, the glory of the Lord appeared in the cloud.

The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: I have heard the murmuring of the children of Israel. Speak to them: In the evening you shall eat meat, and in the morning you shall be filled with bread; and you shall know that I am the Lord your God.

And it came to pass in the evening that quail rose up and covered the camp; and in the morning dew also lay all around the camp. And when it had covered the surface of the earth, there appeared in the wilderness something minute, as if shaved with a razor, resembling frost upon the ground. When the children of Israel saw it, they said to one another: “Manhu?”—which means, “What is this?” For they did not know what it was.

Moses said to them: This is the bread which the Lord has given you to eat. This is the word which the Lord has commanded: and the house of Israel called its name “Man.” It was like white coriander seed, and its taste was like flour with honey.

Moses said: This is the word which the Lord has commanded: Fill a gomor from it, and let it be kept for future generations, so that they may know the bread with which I fed you in the wilderness when you were brought out from the land of Egypt.

And Moses said to Aaron: Take one vessel and put there as much Man as a gomor can hold, and place it before the Lord to be preserved throughout your generations, as the Lord commanded Moses. And Aaron placed it in the tabernacle to be kept.

The children of Israel ate Man for forty years, until they came to an inhabited land. R. Amen.

## Reading from the Book of the Prophet Haggai (Chapters I–II)

R. Thanks be to God.

Thus says the Lord: Set your hearts upon your ways. Go up to the mountain, bring wood, build the house; and it shall be acceptable to me, and I shall be glorified, says the Lord.

And the Lord stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and the spirit of Jesus son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and the spirit of all the remnant of the people. And they entered and worked on the house of the Lord of hosts, their God.

The word of the Lord came through the hand of Haggai the prophet, saying: My spirit shall be in your midst; do not fear. For thus says the Lord of hosts: Yet a little while, and I shall shake heaven and earth, the sea and the dry land. And I shall shake all nations, and the Desired One shall come to all nations; and I shall fill this house with glory, says the Lord of hosts.

Great shall be the glory of this last house, more than that of the first, says the Lord of hosts; and in this place I shall give peace, says the Lord of hosts. R. Amen.

## Reading from the Acts of the Apostles (Chapter X)

R. Thanks be to God.

In those days, there was a certain man in Caesarea named Cornelius, a centurion of the cohort called the Italian, devout and fearing God with all his household, giving many alms to the people and always beseeching God. He saw clearly in a vision, about the ninth hour of the day, an angel of God entering to him and saying to him: “Cornelius.” He, looking at him and seized with fear, said: “Who are you, Lord?” And he said to him: “Your prayers and your alms have ascended as a memorial in the sight of God. And now send men to Joppa and summon a certain Simon who is called Peter. He is lodging with a certain Simon, a tanner, whose house is beside the sea; he will tell you what you ought to do.”

And when the angel who spoke to him had departed, he called two of his household servants and a soldier who feared the Lord, from among those who obeyed him. When he had related everything to them, he sent them to Joppa.

On the following day, while they were traveling and drawing near to the city, Peter went up to the upper room to pray, about the sixth hour. And when he was hungry, he wished to taste something. While they were preparing it, an ecstasy came upon him, and he saw heaven opened and a certain vessel descending, like a great linen cloth lowered by its four corners from heaven to earth. In it were all kinds of four-footed animals and reptiles of the earth and birds of heaven.

And a voice came to him: “Rise, Peter; kill and eat.” But Peter said: “By no means, Lord, for I have never eaten anything common or unclean.” And again the voice came to him: “What God has cleansed, do not call common.”

This happened three times, and immediately the vessel was taken back up into heaven. While Peter was pondering within himself what the vision he had seen might mean, behold, the men who had been sent by Cornelius, seeking Simon’s house, stood at the door. And when they called, they asked whether Simon who was called Peter was lodging there.

As Peter was thinking about the vision, the Spirit said to him: “Behold, three men are seeking you. Rise, therefore, go down, and go with them without hesitation, because I sent them.”

And Peter, going down to the men, said: “Behold, I am the one whom you seek. What is the reason for which you have come?” They said: “Cornelius the centurion, a just man who fears God and has a good testimony from the whole nation of the Jews, received an answer from a holy angel to summon you to his house and hear words from you.”

Therefore, bringing them in, he received them as guests. On the following day he rose and departed with them, and some of the brothers from Joppa accompanied him. On the next day he entered Caesarea. Cornelius was waiting for them, having summoned his relatives and close friends.

And when Peter entered, Cornelius came to meet him and, falling at his feet, worshiped him. But Peter raised him up, saying: “Rise; I myself am also a human being.”

And speaking with him, he entered and found many who had gathered. He said to them: “You know how abominable it is for a Jewish man to join himself to or approach a foreigner; but God has shown me that I should call no human being common or unclean. Therefore, without hesitation, I came when summoned. So I ask for what reason you summoned me.”

And Cornelius said: “Four days ago, at this very hour, I was praying in my house, and behold, a man stood before me in a white garment and said: ‘Cornelius, your prayer has been heard, and your alms have been remembered in the sight of the Lord. Send therefore to Joppa and summon Simon who is called Peter; he is lodging in the house of Simon the tanner beside the sea.’

“Therefore I immediately sent for you, and you have done well by coming. Now therefore we are all present in your sight, to hear everything that has been commanded you by the Lord.” R. Amen.

Antiphon 1. May your right hand save us, and hear us. Psalm 59.

Prayer. Save thy people, Lord, by thy right hand; and to those to whom thou hast given the sign of the Cross, grant the fullest dignity of faith, so that those whom thou hadst driven away when they were sinning thou mayest receive when they turn back. And grant the necessary help in tribulation, thou who becamest the price for sinners; and do thou reduce the tribulating enemy to nothing; do thou bring the redeemed into the city of the surrounding company. R. Amen.

Through.

Antiphon 2. Give thanks to the Lord with the harp; sing praises to him with the ten-stringed psaltery. Psalm 32.

Prayer. Lord, who makest the joy of the righteous to be thy command, whose praise both obeys thee by loving and loves thee by praising; who sing a new song to thee through the harp of the Law and leap forth with pious voices through the psaltery’s sacred resounding: grant, Lord, that we may cling to their footsteps and, with them, cry out thy praise. And because thy word is upright and thy works faithful, grant that we may believe thee with a faithful heart and may deserve more earnestly to attain thy mercy. R. Amen.

## Reading from the Book of the Prophet Isaiah (Chapter XXXII)

R. Thanks be to God.

Thus says the Lord: Rise up, wealthy women, and hear my voice; daughters who are confident, receive my word with your ears. After days and years, you too shall be troubled, confident ones; for the vintage is finished, the gathering will not come again. Be astonished, wealthy women; be troubled, confident ones; strip yourselves and be ashamed; gird your loins. Beat your breasts over the desirable land, over the fruitful vine. Upon the soil of my people thorns and briers shall rise; how much more upon all the houses of joy of the exultant city? For the house has been abandoned; the multitude of the city has been deserted; darkness and groping shall be over the cave forever. The pasture of wild asses shall be the feeding place of flocks, until the spirit is poured out upon us from on high; and the wilderness shall become Carmel, and Carmel shall be reckoned as a forest. And judgment shall dwell in the wilderness, and justice shall sit in Carmel. And the work of justice shall be peace, and the guardianship of justice shall be silence, and security shall last forever. R. Amen.

## Reading from the Book of Numbers (Chapters XVII–XVIII)

R. Thanks be to God.

In those days, the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the children of Israel and take from them one staff for each family, from all the leaders of the tribes: twelve staffs; and write each man’s name upon his staff. The name of Aaron shall be in the tribe of Levi, and one staff shall represent all their families. And you shall place them in the tabernacle of the covenant before the testimony, where I speak to you. The one whom I choose, his staff shall blossom; and I shall restrain from myself the complaints of the children of Israel with which they murmur against you.

And Moses spoke to the children of Israel, and all their leaders gave him staffs, one for each tribe. There were twelve staffs, apart from Aaron’s staff. When Moses had placed them before the Lord in the tabernacle of the testimony, on the following day he went in and found that Aaron’s staff had blossomed in the house of Levi. Its buds had swelled, and flowers had burst forth, which, when their leaves had spread, had taken the form of almonds.

Therefore Moses brought out all the staffs from the presence of the Lord to all the children of Israel. They saw them, and each took back his own staff.

The Lord said to Moses: Let Aaron’s staff return to the tabernacle of the testimony, to be kept as a sign for the rebellious children, so that their complaints against me may cease and they may not die. And Moses did as the Lord had commanded.

But the children of Israel said to Moses: Behold, we are consumed; we have all perished. Whoever approaches the tabernacle of the Lord dies. Are we all to be destroyed to the point of extermination?

And the Lord said to Aaron: You, your sons, and your father’s house with you shall bear the iniquity of the sanctuary; and you and your sons together shall bear the sins of your priesthood. But also take with you your brothers from the tribe of Levi and the tribe of your father, so that they may stand ready and minister to you. You and your sons, however, shall minister in the tabernacle of the testimony. R. Amen.

Prophecy. Hear, leaders of Jacob. Folio 245.

## Reading from the Acts of the Apostles (Chapter X)

R. Thanks be to God.

In those days, Peter opened his mouth and said: In truth I have learned that God is not a respecter of persons, but in every nation whoever fears him and works justice is acceptable to him. He sent his word to the children of Israel, announcing peace through Jesus Christ—for he is Lord of all.

You know what happened throughout all Judea, beginning from Galilee, after the baptism which John preached: Jesus of Nazareth—how God anointed him with the Holy Spirit and with power. He went about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the Devil, because God was with him.

And we are witnesses of all these things that he did in the region of the Jews and in Jerusalem. They also killed him by hanging him on a tree. God raised him up on the third day and granted that he be made manifest, not to all the people, but to witnesses preordained by God—to us, who ate and drank with him after he rose from the dead, for forty days.

And he commanded us to preach to the people and testify that he is the one appointed by God as judge of the living and the dead. To him all the prophets bear witness that through his name all who believe in him receive forgiveness of sins.

While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit fell upon all who heard the word. And the faithful of the circumcision who had come with Peter were astonished, because the grace of the Holy Spirit had also been poured out upon the nations. For they heard them speaking in languages and magnifying the Lord.

Then Peter answered: Can anyone forbid water, so that these who have received the Holy Spirit as we have should not be baptized? And he commanded them to be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. Then they asked him to remain with them for several days.

The apostles and the brothers who were in Judea heard that the Gentiles too had received the word of God and were glorifying God.

R. Amen.

[Col. 0669B] Antiphon 1. But mercy shall surround those who hope in the Lord. Psalm 31.

Prayer. God, from whom the hidden things of hearts are not concealed and to whom the secrets of conscience are not hidden, we beseech thee, forgive our iniquities and blot out all our sins, so that, by forgiving our offenses, thou mayest gain our souls and, by covering our transgressions, possess them. And because thou art our exultation, redeem us by having mercy and, by redeeming us, free us from the scourges of sins. R. Amen.

## Reading from the Book of the Proverbs of Solomon (Chapter III)

R. Thanks be to God.

Blessed is the man who has found wisdom and who abounds in prudence. Its acquisition is better than trade in silver, and its first fruits are better than gold; it is more precious than all riches, and all desirable things cannot be compared with it. Length of days are in its right hand, and in its left are riches and glory. Its ways are beautiful ways, and its paths are peaceful. It is a tree of life to those who grasp it, and blessed is the one who holds it.

The Lord founded the earth by wisdom and established the heavens by prudence. By his wisdom the abysses burst forth, and the clouds grow thick with dew.

My son, let these things not flow away from your eyes. Keep my law and my counsel, and it shall be life for your soul and grace for your throat. Then you shall walk confidently in your way, and your foot shall not stumble. If you sleep, you shall not fear; you shall rest, and your sleep shall be sweet. Do not fear sudden terror or the powers of the wicked rushing upon you. For the Lord will be at your side and will guard your foot, so that you are not caught by evil. R. Amen.

[Col. 0672A] Hymn. Of kindness. Folio 69. Chapters. May the Holy Spirit descend, Lord. Laud. The Lord is in heaven. Folio 399.

## Reading from the Book of Ecclesiasticus (Chapter VI)

R. Thanks be to God.

My son, receive instruction from your youth, and you will find wisdom even unto gray hairs. Approach it like one who plows and sows, and you will await its fruits; for you will labor only a little in its work, and soon you will eat of its produce. R. Amen.

## Reading from the Book of Numbers (Chapter XVI)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

In those days: Korah son of Izhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, and Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab, and On son of Peleth, descendants of Reuben, rose up against Moses, together with two hundred and fifty other leaders of the Israelite assembly, men summoned by name at the time of the council.

When they stood against Moses and Aaron, they said: “You have gone far enough, for the whole multitude is holy, and the Lord is among them. Why do you exalt yourselves above the Lord’s people?”

When Moses heard this, he fell facedown. He spoke to Korah and the entire multitude, saying: “Tomorrow the Lord will make known who belong to him, and he will bring the holy ones near to himself; those whom he chooses will approach him. Do this, then: let each man take his censer—you, Korah, and your entire assembly—and, having taken fire tomorrow, put incense upon it before the Lord. The one whom he chooses will be holy. You have gone too far, sons of Levi.”

And he said again to Korah: “Hear, sons of Levi. Is it too little for you that the Lord God of Israel has set you apart from the whole people and joined you to himself, so that you might serve him in the worship of the tabernacle, stand before the assembly of the people, and minister to him? He has brought you and all your Levitical brothers near to himself, and yet you also claim the priesthood for yourselves, so that your entire company may stand before the Lord. What, after all, is Aaron, that you should murmur against him?”

Then Moses sent for Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab. They replied: “We will not go. Is it not enough for you that you brought us out of a land flowing with milk and honey, to kill us in the wilderness, unless you also make yourself our ruler? In truth, you have brought us into a land flowing with streams of milk and honey, and you have given us possession of fields and vineyards. Do you intend to put out our eyes? We will not go.”

Moses became very angry and said to the Lord: “Do not look upon their sacrifices. You know that I have never taken even a donkey from them, nor harmed any one of them.”

And he said to Korah: “You and your whole congregation, stand apart before the Lord, and Aaron separately tomorrow. Let each of you take his censer and put incense upon it, and let them offer to the Lord two hundred and fifty censers. Aaron also shall hold his censer.”

When they had done this, while Moses and Aaron were standing there and they had gathered the whole multitude against them at the entrance of the tabernacle, the glory of the Lord appeared to everyone. The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying: “Separate yourselves from the midst of this congregation, so that I may suddenly destroy them.”

They fell facedown upon the ground and said: “Most mighty God of the spirits of all flesh, will your anger rage against everyone because one man has sinned?”

And the Lord said to Moses: “Command the whole people to separate themselves from the tabernacle of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.”

Moses rose and went to Dathan and Abiram. The elders of Israel followed him. He said to the crowd: “Withdraw from the tents of these wicked men, and do not touch anything that belongs to them, lest you become involved in their sins.”

When they had withdrawn on every side from their tents, Dathan and Abiram came out and stood at the entrance of their tents, with their wives and children and the whole company. Moses said: “By this you shall know that the Lord has sent me to do all these things that you see, and that I have not spoken them from my own heart: if these men die the ordinary death of all human beings, and if they are visited by the affliction with which others are ordinarily visited, then the Lord has not sent me. But if the Lord does something new—if the earth opens its mouth and swallows them and everything belonging to them, and they go down alive into the underworld—then you shall know that they have blasphemed the Lord.”

As soon as Moses finished speaking, the earth split beneath their feet. It opened its mouth and swallowed them, together with their tents and all their possessions. They went down alive into the underworld, covered by the earth, and perished from the midst of the assembly.

But all Israel who were standing around fled at the cry of those who were perishing, saying: “Perhaps the earth will swallow us also.”

Fire likewise came forth from the Lord and consumed the two hundred and fifty men who were offering incense.

The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: “Command Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, to remove the censers lying amid the burning and scatter the fire here and there, for they have been sanctified by the deaths of sinners. Let him beat them into plates and fasten them to the altar, because incense was offered in them to the Lord and they have been sanctified, so that the Israelites may see them as a sign and memorial.”

So Eleazar the priest took the bronze censers in which the men whom the fire had consumed had offered incense, and he beat them into plates and fastened them to the altar, so that afterward the Israelites might have a reminder and no outsider—anyone not descended from Aaron—might approach and suffer as Korah and his whole congregation had suffered, as the Lord had spoken to Moses.

The entire multitude of the Israelites murmured against Moses and Aaron on the following day, saying: “You have killed the Lord’s people.”

When sedition arose and the tumult increased, Moses and Aaron fled to the tabernacle of the covenant. After they entered it, the cloud covered it, and the glory of the Lord appeared. The Lord said to Moses: “Withdraw from the midst of this multitude; even now I will destroy them.”

While they were lying facedown on the ground, Moses said to Aaron: “Take the censer, draw fire from the altar, and put incense upon it. Go quickly to the people and intercede for them, for wrath has already gone forth from the Lord, and the plague is raging.”

When Aaron had done this and had run into the midst of the multitude, which the fire was already devastating, he offered the incense. Standing between the dead and the living, he prayed for the people, and the Lord’s wrath was halted in Israel.

**R.** Amen.

## Reading from the Book of the Prophet Ezekiel (Chapter XXXIX)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

Thus says the Lord: “I will set my glory among the nations, and all the nations shall see my judgment that I have executed, and my hand that I have stretched out over them. And the house of Israel shall know that I am the Lord their God, from that day and thereafter.

“And the nations shall know that the house of Israel was taken captive in its iniquity, because they abandoned me; and I hid my face from them and delivered them into the hands of their enemies, and they all fell by the sword. According to their uncleanness and their wickedness I dealt with them, and I hid my face from them.

“Therefore thus says the Lord God: Now I shall restore the captivity of Jacob and have mercy on all Israel, and I shall be zealous for my holy name. They shall bear their disgrace and all their transgression with which they transgressed against me, when they dwell securely in their own land, fearing no one. When I bring them back from the peoples and gather them from the lands of their enemies, I shall be sanctified in them before the eyes of many nations.

“And they shall know that I am the Lord their God, because I transported them among the nations and gathered them into their own land, and I did not leave any of them there. I shall no longer hide my face from them, because I have poured out my Spirit upon the whole house of Israel,” says the Lord God.

**R.** Amen.

## Reading from the Acts of the Apostles (Chapter XV)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

In those days: Some men belonging to the sect of the Pharisees who had believed rose up, saying: “It is necessary to circumcise them and command them also to keep the law of Moses.” The Apostles and the elders gathered to consider this matter.

When much discussion had taken place, Peter rose and said to them: “Men, brothers, you know that from ancient days God chose among us that through my mouth the Gentiles should hear the word of the Gospel and believe. And God, who knows hearts, bore witness to them, giving them the Holy Spirit just as he gave it to us, and made no distinction between us and them, cleansing their hearts by faith.

“Now, therefore, why do you test God by placing upon the necks of the disciples a yoke that neither our fathers nor we have been able to bear? But through the grace of the Lord Jesus we believe that we are saved, in the same way as they.”

The whole multitude fell silent, and they listened to Barnabas and Paul recounting how many signs and wonders God had performed among the Gentiles through them.

After they had fallen silent, James answered, saying: “Men, brothers, hear me. Simon has related how God first visited the Gentiles to take from them a people for his name. And the words of the Prophets agree with this, as it is written:

“‘After this I shall return, and rebuild the tabernacle of David, which has fallen; I shall rebuild its ruins and raise it up, so that the rest of humanity may seek the Lord, and all the nations upon whom my name has been invoked.’”

**R.** Amen.

## Antiphon 1

Those who trust in the Lord are like Mount Zion; it shall not be moved forever. Psalm 124.

**Prayer.** Grant us, Lord, to trust firmly in you in such a way that the storm of the enemy cannot move us. Establish our faith upon Mount Zion, and deign continually to be present amid your people, lest the multitude of the redeemed desire to stretch out its hands toward iniquity. Thus may they reject the pleasures of the world, break harmful bonds by your power, and receive your goodness through sacred generosity.

**R.** Amen.

**Through—**

## Antiphon 2

The Lord will give strength to his people and will bless his people with peace. Psalm 28.

**Prayer.** O God, whose children—that is, the Angels—offer glory, and to whom all the Saints proclaim honor and praise: subject to you, we adore you; humbly, we beseech you. Receive, Lord, the faithful vows of our hearts, and restrain the pride of the flesh. Accept the prayers of your servants and grant them fellowship with the Angels, so that, as your voice thundered in power and shone forth in magnificence, you may remove the darkness of ignorance from the depths of their hearts and mercifully kindle the light of knowledge by which we may be worthy to contemplate you.

**R.** Amen.

### Reading from the Book of the Prophet Ezekiel (Chapter XXXIV)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

Thus says the Lord: “I shall save my flock, and it shall no longer be for plunder; and I shall judge between sheep and sheep. I shall make a covenant of peace with them and cause the most savage beasts to cease from the land. Those who dwell in the wilderness shall sleep securely in the forests.

“I shall make them and the region around my hill a blessing, and I shall bring rain in its season; they shall be rains of blessing. The tree of the field shall yield its fruit, and the earth shall yield its growth, and they shall be in their own land without fear. They shall know that I am the Lord, when I have broken the chains of their yoke and rescued them from the hand of those who ruled over them.

“They shall no longer be plunder for the nations, nor shall the beasts of the earth devour them. They shall dwell securely, without any terror. I shall raise up for them a renowned shoot, and they shall no longer be diminished by famine in the land, nor shall they bear the reproach of the nations any longer.

“They shall know that I am the Lord their God, that I am with them, and that they are my people, the house of Israel,” says the Lord God.

“But you, my flocks, are the sheep of my pasture; you are human beings, and I am the Lord your God.”

**R.** Amen.

## Reading from the Book of Deuteronomy (Chapter X)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

In those days: The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: “Speak to the whole assembly of the children of Israel, and say to them: Hear, Israel: what does the Lord your God require of you except that you fear the Lord, walk in his ways, love him, serve the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul, and keep the commandments and ordinances of the Lord that I command you today, so that it may be well with you?

“Behold, the heaven and the heaven of heavens, the earth and everything that is in them, belong to the Lord your God. Yet the Lord was attached to your fathers and loved them, and chose their offspring after them—that is, you—from among all the nations, as is evident today.

“Therefore circumcise the foreskin of your heart, and no longer stiffen your neck. For the Lord your God is himself God of gods and Lord of lords, the great and mighty and awesome God, who shows no partiality and accepts no gifts. He executes judgment for the orphan and the widow; he loves the stranger and gives him food and clothing.

“You too, therefore, must love the strangers, because you yourselves were strangers in the land of Egypt. You shall fear the Lord your God and serve him alone; you shall cling to him and swear by his name. He is your praise and your God, who did for you great and awesome things that your eyes have seen.

“Your fathers went down into the land of Egypt with seventy persons, and now behold, the Lord your God has multiplied you like the stars of heaven.

“Love, therefore, the Lord your God, and observe his precepts, ordinances, judgments, and commandments at all times.” (Chapter XI.)

**R.** Amen.

## Reading from the Book of the Prophet Ezekiel (Chapter XI)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

The word of the Lord came to me, saying: “Son of man, your brothers, your kinsmen, and the whole house of Israel, all of them, to whom the inhabitants of Jerusalem said: ‘Go far away from the Lord; this land has been given to us as a possession.’

“Therefore thus says the Lord God: Because I have driven them far away among the nations and scattered them through the lands, I shall be a small sanctuary for them in the lands to which they have gone.

“Therefore speak: Thus says the Lord God: I shall gather you from the peoples and assemble you from the lands in which you have been scattered, and I shall give you the land of Israel. They shall enter there, and I shall remove from it all offenses and all its abominations.

“I shall give them a new heart and place a right spirit within them. I shall remove the stony heart from their flesh and give them a heart of flesh, so that they may walk in my commandments, keep my judgments, and perform them. They shall be my people, and I shall be their God.”

**R.** Amen.

## Reading from the Acts of the Apostles (Chapter VIII)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

In those days: When the Apostles who were in Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent Peter and John to them. When they arrived, they prayed for them that they might receive the Holy Spirit, for he had not yet come upon any of them, but they had only been baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.

Then they laid their hands upon them, and they received the Holy Spirit. When Simon saw that the Holy Spirit was given through the laying on of the Apostles’ hands, he offered them money, saying: “Give me this power also, so that whoever upon whom I lay hands may receive the Holy Spirit.””

But Peter said to him: “May your money be with you for destruction, because you thought that the gift of God could be acquired with money. You have no part or share in this matter, for your heart is not right before God.

“Repent, therefore, of this wickedness of yours, and pray to the Lord that perhaps this thought of your heart may be forgiven you. For I see that you are in the gall of bitterness and in the bondage of iniquity.”

Simon answered and said: “Pray for me to the Lord, so that none of these things you have said may come upon me.”

After they had testified and spoken the word of God, they returned to Jerusalem and evangelized the Lord Jesus Christ in many Samaritan villages.

**R.** Amen.

Those whom worldly allurements cause to withdraw from you through the contagion of various things, may sincere confession cause to cling to you; and, crying out in your praise with humble devotion and unanimity of heart, may they fulfill their vows.

## Reading from the Book of Proverbs (Chapter IV)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

Son, possess wisdom as the beginning of wisdom, and acquire wisdom with all your possessions. Seize it, and it will exalt you; it will glorify you when you embrace it. It will give increase of graces to your head, and the renowned crown of the Lord will protect you.

Hear, my son, and receive my words, so that the years of your life may be multiplied. I shall show you the way of wisdom; I shall lead you along the paths of justice. When you have entered them, your steps will not be cramped, and when you run, you will not stumble.

Hold fast to discipline; do not abandon it. Guard it, because it is your life. Do not take delight in the paths of the wicked, and do not let the way of evil please you. Flee from it; do not pass along it. Turn aside and leave it, for they do not sleep unless they have done evil, nor does sleep come upon them unless they have tripped someone up.

They eat the bread of wickedness and drink the wine of iniquity. But the path of the just is like a shining light; it proceeds and grows until the perfect day.

**R.** Amen.

## Reading from the Book of Numbers (Chapter XXVII)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

In those days: The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: “Go up this mountain of Abarim and look from there upon the land that I shall give to the children of Israel. When you have seen it, you too shall go to your people, as your brother Aaron also went, because you offended me in the wilderness of Zin in the dispute of the multitude and did not wish to sanctify me before them over the waters. These are the waters of dispute at Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin.”

Moses answered him: “May the Lord, the God of the spirits of all flesh, provide a man who may stand over this multitude and go out and come in before them, lead them out and bring them in, so that the people of the Lord may not be without a shepherd.”

And the Lord said to him: “Take Joshua son of Nun, a man in whom is the spirit, and lay your hand upon him. He shall stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole multitude, and you shall give him commands in the sight of all and a portion of your glory, so that the whole assembly of the children of Israel may hear him.

“If anything must be done, Eleazar the priest shall consult the Lord on his behalf. At his word he shall go in and go out, he and all the children of Israel with him, and the rest of the multitude.”

Moses did as the Lord had commanded. When he had brought Joshua forward, he set him before Eleazar the priest and the whole assembly of the people. Having laid his hands upon his head, he repeated everything that the Lord had commanded.

**R.** Amen.

## Reading from the Book of the Prophet Ezekiel (Chapter IX)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

Thus says the Lord: “The iniquity of the house of Israel and Judah is exceedingly great, and the land is filled with blood, and the city is filled with apostasy. For they said: ‘The Lord has abandoned the land, and the Lord does not see.’

“Therefore my eye also shall not spare, nor shall I have mercy; I shall repay their way upon their head.”

And behold, the man clothed in linen, who had an ink-horn at his back, answered the word, saying: “I have done as you commanded me.” (Chapter X.)

And I saw, and behold, upon the firmament that was over the heads of the cherubim there appeared something like a sapphire stone, and above it appeared something resembling the likeness of a throne. And he said to the man clothed in linen: “Take fire from the midst of the wheels that are between the cherubim.”

And he entered in while I watched, and behold, there were four wheels beside the cherubim: one wheel beside one cherub and another wheel beside another cherub. The appearance of the wheels was like the sight of a chrysolite stone. When they stood, they stood; and when they were lifted, they were lifted with them, for the spirit of life was in them.

And the glory of the Lord went out from the threshold of the temple and stood over the cherubim. And the spirit lifted me and brought me to the eastern gate of the Lord, which looks toward the rising of the sun. And the glory of the Lord went up from the midst of the city and stood over the mountain that is east of the city, and the glory of the God of Israel was over it.

**R.** Amen.

## Reading from the Acts of the Apostles (Chapter XIII)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

In those days: There were in the Church at Antioch prophets and teachers, among whom were Barnabas, Simon who is called Niger, Lucius of Cyrene, Manaen, the foster-brother of Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.

As they were ministering to the Lord and fasting, the Spirit said: “Set apart Barnabas and Paul for the work to which I have called them.” Then, after fasting and praying, they laid their hands upon them and dismissed them.

And they, sent by the Holy Spirit, went down to Seleucia; from there they sailed to Cyprus. When they arrived at Salamis, they preached the word of the Lord in the synagogues of the Jews. They also had John in their ministry.

When they had traveled through the whole island as far as Paphos, they found a certain magician, a false prophet, a Jew named Bar-Jesus, who was with the proconsul Sergius Paulus, an intelligent man. This man summoned Barnabas and Paul and desired to hear the word of God.

But Elymas the magician—for this is how his name is interpreted—resisted them, seeking to turn the proconsul away from the faith. Saul, who is also Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, looked intently at him and said: “O man full of every deceit and every fraud, son of the devil, enemy of all justice, will you never cease to pervert the straight ways of the Lord?

“And now behold, the hand of the Lord is upon you, and you shall be blind, not seeing the sun for a time.”

Immediately mist and darkness fell upon him, and he went around seeking someone to give him his hand. Then the proconsul, when he saw what had happened, believed, astonished at the teaching of the Lord.

**R.** Amen.

## Antiphon 1

**Prayer.** Be favorable to our sins, Lord, and for the honor of your name restore us through complete freedom, so that, while we are crushed by the reproach of our sins, we may not be reduced to the disgrace of the nations. Therefore, so that you may not punish us with the penalty of truth, cleanse from us the cause of our crimes; let the groaning of the fettered enter your sight, and let bestowed grace proceed from your hidden place into our manifest condition.

## Reading from the Book of the Prophet Isaiah (Chapter XXIX)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

“Be stunned and amazed; stagger and totter; be drunk, but not with wine; be shaken, but not by drunkenness. For the Lord has mixed for you a spirit of lethargy and will close your eyes. The prophets and your rulers, who see visions, shall perish.

“And the vision of all this shall be for you like the words of a sealed book. When it is given to one who knows letters, and he is told, ‘Read this,’ he will answer, ‘I cannot, for it is sealed.’ And the book shall be given to one who does not know letters, and he shall be told, ‘Read,’ and he will answer, ‘I do not know letters.’

“And the Lord said: Because this people draws near with its mouth and honors me with its lips, but its heart is far from me, and they have feared me according to the commandment and teachings of men, therefore behold, I shall add to this people a cause for astonishment. I shall make it a great and wondrous marvel. The wisdom of its wise men shall perish, and the understanding of its prudent men shall be hidden.

“Woe to you who are deep of heart, to hide counsel from the Lord, whose works are in darkness, and who say: ‘Who sees us?’ Shall not Lebanon, in a little while and in a short time, be turned into a fruitful field, and the fruitful field be counted as a forest?

“And on that day the deaf shall hear the words of the book, and from darkness and gloom the eyes of the blind shall see. The meek shall increase their joy in the Lord, and the poor among men shall exult in the Holy One of Israel.”

**R.** Amen.
