## Reading from the Book of Leviticus (Chapter XXIII)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

In those days: The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the children of Israel, and say to them: When you have entered the land that I shall give you, and have reaped its grain, you shall bring to the priest sheaves of ears of grain, the firstfruits of your harvest. He shall raise the sheaf before the Lord, so that it may be acceptable for you, on the day after the Sabbath. And on the same day on which the sheaf is consecrated, an unblemished [Col. 0683D] year-old lamb shall be sacrificed as a holocaust to the Lord. And libations shall be offered with it: twelve cakes of fine flour mixed with oil, as an offering to the Lord, with a most pleasing aroma; also a libation of wine, a fourth of a hin. You shall not eat bread, parched grain, or porridge from the harvest until the day on which you offer it to the Lord your God. For this is an everlasting precept throughout your generations and in all your dwellings. You shall count from the day after the Sabbath, on which you offered the sheaf of the firstfruits, seven full weeks, until the day after the completion of the seventh week—that is, fifty days—and then you shall offer a new sacrifice to the Lord from all your dwellings: two loaves of the firstfruits, made from two-tenths of fermented fine flour, which you shall bake and offer as firstfruits [Col. 0684A] for a sweet-smelling fragrance. R\. Amen.

Reading from the Book of the Prophet Ezekiel (Chapter 35).

R\. Thanks be to God.

The word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, set your face against Mount Seir, and prophesy against it, saying to it: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am against you, Mount Seir, and I shall stretch out my hand over you, and make you desolate and deserted. I shall demolish your cities, and you shall be desolate; 415 and you shall know that I am the Lord. Because you have been an everlasting enemy, and have delivered the children of Israel into the hands of the sword in the time of their affliction, in the time of their final iniquity. Therefore, as I live, says the Lord God: I shall hand you over to bloodshed, and bloodshed shall pursue you; and since you have hated bloodshed, bloodshed shall pursue [Col. 0684B] you. And I shall make Mount Seir desolate and deserted, and remove from it the one going out and the one returning. And I shall fill their mountains with their slain: on their hills, in their valleys, and in their ravines, those killed by the sword shall fall. I shall deliver you over to everlasting desolations, and your cities shall not be inhabited; and you shall know that I am the Lord God. R\. Amen.

Reading from the Book of the Acts of the Apostles (Chapter 15).

R\. Thanks be to God.

In those days: It pleased the Apostles and the elders, together with the whole Church, to choose men and send them to Antioch with Paul, Barnabas, and Silas, leading men among the brothers, writing by their hands:

“The Apostles and the elder brothers to the brothers who are of the Gentiles in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia: greetings. Since we have heard that certain men who went out from us have disturbed you with words, subverting your souls, though we gave them no such command, it has pleased us, assembled together, to choose men and send them to you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul, men who have handed over their lives to God. Therefore we have sent Judas and Silas, who themselves will also report to you the same things in words. For it has seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us to impose no further burden upon you than these necessary things: that you abstain from sacrifices offered to idols, from blood, from what has been strangled, and from fornication. If you keep yourselves from these, you will do well. Farewell.”

So, having been dismissed, they came to Antioch; and, after gathering the multitude, they delivered the letter. When they had read it, they rejoiced over the consolation. Judas and Silas, being prophets themselves, also consoled the brothers with many words and strengthened them. After they had spent some time there, they were dismissed in peace by the brothers to those who had sent them. But it seemed good to Silas to remain there; Judas alone departed. Paul and Barnabas remained in Antioch, teaching and proclaiming the word of God with many others. R\. Amen.

Antiphon 1. Who is a great God like our God? You are the God who alone works wonders. Psalm 76.

Prayer. We beseech you, Lord, do not reject us from your mercy; but grant still time for obtaining mercy, so that the right hand which was an avenger in punishing crimes may itself be an everlasting remedy for us who are contrite. R\. Amen.

[Col. 0685A] Through mercy.

Antiphon 2. For you, Lord, are gracious and gentle, and abundantly merciful to those who call upon you. Psalm 85.

Prayer. Have mercy, Lord, on those who cry out to you all day and who call upon you in tribulation; be favorable to us, so that you may worthily receive those among whom we praise you by adoring your majesty, and mercifully forgive those for whom we fear you. Therefore gladden our hearts by obedience to your fear, and strengthen the uncertainty of our mind with the sweetness of consolation. But since you are gracious and gentle, let us draw sweetness from your indulgence and experience you as gracious and gentle in your recompense. R\. Amen.

Through.

Christ, look upon our mournful sighs; release the bonds of death and bestow life. P. And, in your mercy. V\. Now see our tears; understand those who mourn; at last, in your mercy, pardon our offenses. P. And, in your mercy. V\. Place the Angel of salvation before our ears as a sign; do not permit him to harm us any longer. P. And, in your mercy.

Prayer. Let us go before your face, Lord, in confession, and, exulting in the psalms with due melody offered to you, we worship and fall prostrate before you, entreating you with inward weeping and sighing: since you made us and you are our God, may you, the merciful Lord, protect us, your people, and, as the watchful shepherd, attend to the sheep of your pasture; and grant grace to those for whom you laid down your life.

Our Father. Deliver us from evil. fol. 10.

Let the blessing be said as at None, which is said throughout the year.

At Vespers.

Lauda. The sun knows its setting. You appoint darkness, and it becomes night.

The Lord be with you. R\. And with your spirit.

Antiphon. Fill our mouth, O God, with joy, and our tongue with exultation. Psalm 125.

Lauda. With my whole heart I have sought you. P. 416 [Col. 0685D] Do not reject me from your commandments. V\. I have hidden your sayings in my heart, so that I may not sin against you. P. Do not reject me. V\. Glory and honor. P. Do not reject me.

Hymn. Fountain of kindness. folio 69. The Chapters, Blessing, and Lauda: fol. 406.

Prayer. May your right hand deliver us, Lord, and bend the hearts of the arrogant by your command, so that the nations may rejoice at the coming of truth and receive the salvation revealed with humility of heart. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

SATURDAY.

At Matins.

Antiphon. You are the Lord. Psalm 3. Prayer. Although, Lord, very many. fol. 68.

Antiphon 1. The Lord will not reject his people, [Col. 0686A] and he will not forsake his inheritance. Psalm 93.

Prayer. Do not reject, Lord, the people whom you purchased; do not forsake the inheritance for which you were hung upon the Cross. But until justice, now hidden, shines forth openly in judgment, guide us with your extended mercy; and according to the multitude of our sorrows, gladden us by your consolation, so that you who now shape suffering for us in accordance with your command may grant us rest in the age to come. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 2. Announce his salvation from day to day. Psalm 95.

Prayer. May a new song be sung to you. fol. 80.

Antiphon 3. May your right hand and your holy arm deliver us, Lord. Psalm 97.

[Col. 0686B] Prayer. May your right hand deliver us, Lord. Seek above.

R\. May our sins have an end, Lord; may iniquity be blotted out, and may we be clothed in your holy righteousness. P. So that Jerusalem may rejoice again. V\. You will arise and have mercy on Zion, because the time for showing mercy has come. P. So that it may rejoice.

At Lauds.

Antiphon. Turn your face away from my sins, and blot out all my iniquities. Psalm 50.

Prayer. Turn your face away. fol. 68.

For the Canticle. Antiphon. Do not destroy.

Canticle. Lord, Lord, King. fol. 103.

Matutinarium. Antiphon. May God have mercy on us and bless us. P. May the Lord make his face shine upon us. V\. So that we may know your way on earth, your salvation among all nations. P. May the Lord make his face shine upon us.

Lauda. Mountains and all hills, fruitful trees and all cedars. Psalm 148.

Reading from the Book of the Proverbs of Solomon (Chapter 16).

R\. Thanks be to God.

Son: The Lord has made everything for his own purpose, and the wicked for the evil day. Everyone who is arrogant is an abomination to the Lord; even if hand joins hand, he will not be innocent. Iniquity is redeemed by mercy and truth, and evil is avoided through fear of the Lord. When the ways of a man please the Lord, he will turn even his enemies to peace. Better is a little with justice than abundant revenues with iniquity. The heart of a man plans his way, [Col. 0686D] but it belongs to the Lord to direct his steps. Divination is on the lips of a king; his mouth will not err in judgment. The balance and scales are the Lord’s judgments, and all the weights of the bag are his work. Those who act wickedly are abominable to a king, for the throne is made firm by justice. The lips of kings favor what is right; whoever speaks rightly will be guided. R\. Amen.

Hymn. Fountain of kindness. fol. 69. Chapters. May the Lord descend upon us. Lauda. The Lord has prepared in heaven. Blessing. While they await one another. fol. 401.

At Terce.

Prophecy. Son, keep the sayings. fol. 96.

Reading from the Book of Deuteronomy, Chapter 28.

R\. Thanks be to God.

In those days: The Lord spoke to Moses, [Col. 0687A] saying: Speak to the entire assembly of the children of Israel, and say to them: I am the Lord your God. If you listen to the voice of the Lord your God, so as to do and keep all his commandments that I command you today, the Lord your God will make you higher than all the nations that dwell upon the earth. And all these blessings shall come upon you and overtake you, if you listen to his commandments. Blessed are you in the city, and blessed in the field. Blessed is the fruit of your womb, the fruit of your land, and the fruit of your animals, the herds of your cattle and the flocks of your sheep. Blessed are your barns, and blessed your stores. Blessed shall you be when you go out and when you return. The Lord will cause your enemies who rise against you to fall before your face; they will come against you by one road and flee before you by seven. And the Lord will send a blessing upon your storehouses and upon all the works of your hands; and he will bless you in the land that you will receive. The Lord will raise you up 417 for himself as a holy people, if you keep the commandments of the Lord your God and walk in his ways. All the peoples of the earth shall see that the name of the Lord has been invoked over you, and they shall fear you. The Lord will make you abound in all good things, in the fruits of your land, which the Lord swore to your fathers that he would give you. The Lord will open his rich treasury, heaven, and give rain to your land in its season; and he will bless all the works of your hands. You will lend to many nations, and you yourself will receive interest from none. The Lord will set you [Col. 0687C] as the head and not the tail; you shall be above and not beneath, if you listen to the commandments of the Lord your God that I command you, so that it may be well with you, and you may possess the land that the Lord your God will give you. R\. Amen.

Prophecy. Turn back and act. fol. 133.

Reading from the Acts of the Apostles (Chapter 20).

R\. Thanks be to God.

In those days: Paul had decided to sail past Ephesus, so that he might not be delayed in Asia. For he was hastening, if it were possible for him, to celebrate the day of Pentecost at Jerusalem. But from Miletus he sent to Ephesus and summoned the elders of the Church. When they had come to him and were assembled together, he said to them: You know, from the first day on which I entered Asia, how I lived among you throughout the whole time, serving [Col. 0687D] God with humility and tears and trials that befell me through the plots of the Jews; how I held back nothing that was useful, but announced it to you and taught you publicly and from house to house, testifying both to Jews and to Gentiles repentance toward God and faith in our Lord Jesus Christ. And now, behold, bound in spirit, I am going to Jerusalem, not knowing what will happen to me there, except that the Holy Spirit testifies to me in every city, saying that bonds and tribulations await me in Jerusalem. But I fear none of these things, nor do I count my life more precious than myself, provided that I complete my course and the ministry that I received from the Lord Jesus, to testify to the gospel of the grace of God. And now, behold, I know that all of you among whom I passed preaching the kingdom of God will see my face no more. Therefore I testify to you this day that I am clean from the blood of all. For I have not shrunk from announcing to you the whole counsel of God. Pay attention to yourselves and to the whole flock, in which the Holy Spirit has placed you as bishops, to govern the Church of God, which he acquired with his own blood. R\. Amen.

Antiphon 1. Prepare yourselves as a living, holy sacrifice pleasing to God, your spiritual worship. And do not grieve the Holy Spirit. P. Hear this, all nations; perceive it with your ears, all you who dwell in the world. Psalm 48.

Prayer. May they hear you together. fol. 409.

Antiphon 2. The Spirit of the Lord is the Spirit of life, and blessed is the glory of the Lord from his place. V\. By the word of the Lord the heavens were established, and by the Spirit of his mouth all their host. Psalm 32.

Prayer. Lord, who [of the righteous]. fol. 403.

Antiphon 3. I shall send among you the Spirit of truth, who proceeds from the Father; he will convict the world concerning sin, judgment, and righteousness. Psalm 49.

R\. Most powerful God, Spirit of all flesh, will you perhaps destroy everyone in your anger? You are merciful and of great compassion. P. Lord, forgive the sins of your people. V\. Ruler and Lord, merciful and gracious God. P. Lord.

[Col. 0688C] Intercessions. Let us all say: Merciful Lord.

P. Have mercy. V\. You who are one in power and of the same substance with your Begetter. P. Have mercy. V\. You who are chief of priests, ruler of kings, Lord of peoples. P. Have mercy. V\. You who restore their homeland to captives, help to the weak, and consolation to those who mourn. P. Have mercy. V\. We ask for pardon; grant it. Give salvation to the penitent. P. Have mercy.

Supplication. Let us pray; let us humbly implore the mercy of God the almighty Father, so that the grace of his Christ, our Lord, and the power of his Holy Spirit may graciously deign to enlighten us.

Chapters. Lord Jesus Christ, whom we believe to have come humble in the abasement of flesh to redeem the perishing world, and whom we await as coming again in the power of your Godhead to judge the sinful age with terror: we, your servants, trembling before your immeasurable mercy, beseech you that, when you come, you may not convict us of sin, but in your ineffable goodness come to our aid; and that here you may rather accept the confession of our humility, so that there also you may forgive all our crimes and appoint us to be crowned among those at your right hand.

Our Father. Deliver us from evil. fol. 10.

Let the blessing be said as at Terce, which is said throughout the year. At Sext and None, let it be said as on the preceding Friday, fol. 411.

FOR HOLY PENTECOST.

[Col. 0689]

419 At Vespers.

[Col. 0689A]

Lauda. For with you is the fountain of life, and in your light we shall see light. Show your mercy. P. To those who know you. V\. Lord, your mercy is in heaven, and your truth; you have multiplied your mercies. P. To those who know you.

The Lord be always with you. R\. And with your spirit.

Prayer. God, with whom is the fountain of life, and in whose light we behold light: nourish within us, we beseech you, the splendor of your knowledge, by which we may be able to approach the abundance of your fountain. Gather for us also the places of diverse teachings, filled with your streams, to be offered to us as drink, so that, while we thirst, you may grant us life-giving drink, and restore heavenly light to our darkened souls. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

[Col. 0689B] Sono. If you love me, keep my commandments. And I shall ask my Father, and he will give you another Paraclete, so that he may remain with you. P. Forever. Alleluia. V\. When the Paraclete comes, whom I shall send to you from the Father, the Spirit of truth, he will bear witness about me; and you also will bear witness, because you have been with me from the beginning. P. Forever. V\. Father, the hour has come: glorify your Son, and your Son will glorify you, because those whom you gave me, I desire that where I am, they also may be with me, so that they may see my glory, which you gave me, because you loved me before the foundation of the world. P. Forever.

The Lord be with you. R\. And with your spirit.

Antiphon. The Paraclete Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, will teach you everything that I shall say to you. P. I give you my peace; I commend my peace to you. V\. Praise the Lord, servants; praise the name of the Lord. P. My peace. V\. Glory and honor. P. My peace.

Prayer. Console, Jesus, the minds of the faithful, deprived of good studies, through the gift of the Holy Spirit, so that that Paraclete Spirit, rich in overflowing gifts, whom you testified that the Father would send in your name, may rescue us—the Spirit who reigns with you and with the Father, of undivided substance and power—so that, taught by him, we may be made fit to follow your peace in all things and, instructed, never abandon your love. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 2. When the Paraclete comes, he will bear witness about me, [Col. 0689D] and you also will bear witness. P. Because you have been with me from the beginning. V\. The Lord, God of gods, has spoken and summoned the earth; from the rising of the sun to its setting, from Zion, the perfection of his beauty. P. Because. V\. Glory and honor. P. Because.

The Lord be with you. R\. And with you.

Lauda. God is Spirit, and those who worship him must worship in spirit and truth. P. It is necessary to worship. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V\. Great is our Lord, and great is his power, and there is no measure of his wisdom. P. It is necessary to worship. V\. Glory and honor. P. It is necessary to worship.

Hymn.

[Col. 0690A]

Come, Holy Spirit,

Paraclete from the Father’s mouth,

promised long ago,

proclaimed by the prophet Joel:

“In the last times,

the inner parts shall be filled,”

he says; “prophesy

the peaceful signs pleasing to the God of all.”

Our God poured him out upon the Disciples

on this day,

ascending, as he had promised,

to his throne, death left behind.

When blind and envious Judea

saw them, the people thus confessed:

[Col. 0690B] “They are full of new wine,” they cried,

while they did not believe the mighty deeds.

Peter, steadfast, rebuked them:

“They are not filled with wine,

as you suppose,

but with the Spirit

of whom the Prophet speaks.”

After this, very many,

receiving the word

and searching their hearts,

and having received increased fullness,

were joined to Christ’s company.

The hidden mystery,

which was once hidden from Israel,

is now sung as revealed,

displayed in the Apostles.

This is the fiftieth day,

which is handed down as a jubilee:

a solemn joy for us,

proper to remission.

Let us sing a hymn to the Father,

let us sing a hymn to the Son,

420 together with the Holy Spirit,

with attentive voice and heart.

Amen.

Supplication. Let us humbly implore the mercy of God the almighty Father, so that the grace of his Christ, our Lord, and the power of the Holy Spirit may graciously deign to justify us. R\. Grant this, eternal almighty God.

Kyrie eleison. R\. Christe eleison. Kyrie eleison.

[Col. 0690D] Chapters. Let your mercy, Lord, be upon us, and let the radiance of your Spirit shine into our inner parts, so that he himself may kindle those who are cold and enlighten those who are dark, he who always remains glorious and splendid with you.

Our Father. Delivered from evil. fol. 10.

Blessing. May the Paraclete Spirit, who formerly was openly manifested to the Disciples as fire in the gift, cleanse you from all sins by the heat of his fire. R\. Amen. And may he who, as the merciful Consoler, came to their sorrowful hearts instruct you with the great grace of his sacrament. R\. Amen. And may he who then taught the Apostles the truth nourish you now also with faith and lead you afterward to eternal rest. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

Lauda. I shall pour out my Spirit upon all flesh, alleluia. P. And your sons shall prophesy. Alleluia, alleluia. V\. Send forth your Spirit, and they shall be created, and you shall renew the face of the earth. P. And they shall prophesy. V\. Glory and honor. P. And.

Prayer. O Holy Spirit, who proceed from the Father and the Son, teach us to practice truth, so that you who received your procession from the Father and the Son may join us in invisible love to those from whom you proceed so ineffably. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

In the name of the Lord.

At Matins.

[Col. 0691B]

Hymn. Eternal Creator of all things. See fol. 3.

Prayer. The voice of all the faithful sings you, Lord, as eternal and the Creator of all things: you who establish fixed limits of time and, by eternal law, appoint the boundaries by which night is separated from day. For the abyss of your wisdom, in order to relieve the weariness of mortals, assigned one part to labor and reserved another for rest. Grant therefore, almighty God, that while the sick mind, disturbed by sleep, is admonished by the crowing of the cock, it may run eagerly back to the hope of light and always devote the first fruits of divine labor to your service. R\. Amen. Through mercy.

Over the psalm, Antiphon. I slept and rose again, because the Lord raised me up. Psalm 3.

Antiphon. Restore to me the joy of your salvation, and strengthen me, Lord, with a princely spirit. Psalm 50.

Antiphon. He sent from heaven and delivered me; he gave those who trampled me over to reproach. Psalm 56.

Prayer. Holy Spirit, who proceed from the Father and the Son, enrich us with the gift of your blessing, so that, strengthened by a princely spirit, we may deserve to be delivered daily by heavenly sending forth. Therefore may your blessing be upon us, and may it always strengthen us through the ineffable power of the Trinity, so that the Holy Spirit may dwell in us, the right Spirit renew us, and the princely Spirit strengthen us, and so that there may be one testimony of power: that, strengthened by the Father, renewed by the Son, and guarded by the Holy Spirit, we may rejoice that we are kept safe. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 1. The Lord said to his disciples: Receive the Holy Spirit. P. In my name cast out demons, lay your hands upon the sick, and they shall be well. V\. The Lord, God of gods, has spoken and summoned the earth; from the rising of the sun to its setting, from Zion, the perfection of his beauty. P. In my name. V\. Glory. P. In my name.

Prayer. God, who taught that in the power of the Holy Spirit demons are cast out and the sick can be healed in your name: grant us to be so filled with the gift of this Holy Spirit that we may deserve to be freed from every temptation of demons, so that, relieved by him from our infirmities, we may through him be well, when we have received an everlasting good as the reward for our works. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 2. The Creator and Lord of all things taught wisdom. P. The Holy Spirit: one, simple, manifold, subtle, undefiled, gracious, and loving. V\. Great is our Lord, and great is his power, and there is no measure of his wisdom. P. The Holy Spirit. 421 V\. Glory and honor. P. The Holy Spirit.

Prayer. The Creator and Lord of all things taught wisdom, in which is the Holy Spirit, one, simple, manifold, subtle, so that the one Father, one Son, and one Holy Spirit may not be displayed through a plurality of divinity, [Col. 0692B] but joined in unity of power; and so that they may lack union of person while remaining in unity of nature. Let nothing there be diverse where one thing resounds in each. Therefore, believing you, Holy Trinity, with this knowledge of faith, we ask and entreat that, through the manifestation of your Spirit, you may shine into our heart in such a way that we may avoid the works of the flesh and pursue the perfection of complete holiness. R\. Amen.

Through.

Antiphon 3. The Lord said to his disciples: Receive the Holy Spirit. Whose sins you forgive, they are forgiven; whose you retain, they are retained. P. I give you my peace; I commend my peace to you. V\. He sends forth his word to the earth; his message runs swiftly. P. My peace. V\. Glory. [Col. 0692C] P. My peace.

Prayer. Christ, Son of God, who promised that through the Holy Spirit sins would be forgiven within the Church to those who confess them to you, when, good Master, you granted your disciples the power of binding and loosing: grant us to abound more richly in this gift, so that by its fire our concentrated crimes may be burned away within us and the manifest blessings of your peace may be bestowed. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

R\. Behold, the Spirit of truth will come, who will teach you all truth; for he will not speak from himself, but whatever he hears, he will speak. P. And he will announce to you the things that are to come. V\. The Spirit of truth, whom the Father will send from heaven, will teach you every way of righteousness. P. And the things that are to come. V\. Glory and P. And the things that are to come.

Prayer. O Holy Spirit. fol. 420.

At Lauds.

For the Canticle. Antiphon. Because of your fear, Lord, we conceived in the womb and gave birth to the Spirit of salvation, whom you made upon the earth.

Canticle. My spirit watches through the night. folio 64.

Prayer. Place your Spirit in us, Lord, so that we may give birth to the Spirit of salvation, whom you made upon the earth, so that, while he remains with us forever, we may not be tormented by any punishments in the future judgment. R\. Amen.

Through.

For the Benedictus. Antiphon. To you alone, God, belong honor and glory, power and authority, for ever and ever.

[Col. 0693A] Canticle. Blessed are you, Lord God of our fathers. fol. 6.

Sono. I shall pour out, says the Lord, my Spirit. P. Upon all flesh. Alleluia. V\. Your sons and daughters shall prophesy, and everyone who calls upon the Lord shall be saved. P. Upon all flesh.

The Lord be with you. R\. And with your spirit.

Lauda. Alleluia. Praise the Lord from the heavens; praise him in the heights. Alleluia, alleluia. V\. Praise him, all his angels; praise him, all his powers. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. Psalm 148.

Reading from the Book of the Prophet Joel (Chapter 2).

R\. Thanks be to God.

Thus says the Lord: Do not fear, earth; exult and rejoice, for the Lord has acted magnificently. Do not fear, animals of the region, for the beautiful places of the wilderness have sprouted, because the tree has yielded its fruit, and the fig tree and the vine have given their strength. And you, daughters of Zion, exult and rejoice in the Lord your God, because he has given you a teacher of righteousness, and he will cause the early and late rain to descend upon you, as at the beginning. Your threshing floors shall be filled with grain, and the winepresses shall overflow with wine and oil. You shall eat, eating your fill, and you shall be satisfied; and you shall praise the name of our God, who has done wonders with you, and my people shall not be put to shame forever. And you shall know that I alone am in the midst of Israel. Do not fear, but exult and rejoice, because the Lord has acted magnificently; and I am the Lord your God, and there is no other; and my people shall not be put to shame forever. And it shall be after this: I shall pour out my Spirit upon the earth; your sons and your daughters shall prophesy; your old men shall dream dreams, and your young men shall see visions. Moreover, upon my servants and my handmaids in those days I shall pour out my Spirit. And I shall give wonders in heaven above and signs on the earth below, blood and fire and vapor of smoke. The sun shall be turned into darkness and the moon into blood, before the great and terrible day of the Lord comes. And everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord shall be saved. R\. Amen.

422 Hymn.

The blessed joys

of the year’s course have returned,

when the Paraclete Spirit

shone upon the Disciples.

Fire, with trembling light,

bore the form of tongues,

so that they might overflow with words

and burn with love.

They speak in the languages of all;

the Gentile crowds are afraid;

they suppose those whom the Spirit had filled

to be drunk with new wine.

These things were accomplished mystically,

after the time of Passover had been completed,

according to the sacred number of days

by which remission is made according to the law.

[Col. 0694A] To you now, most merciful God,

we pray, bowing with downcast face:

grant us the gifts of the Spirit

that have fallen upon us from heaven.

Long ago you filled

consecrated hearts with your grace;

now forgive our sins

and grant us peaceful times.

When the months of the year have passed,

such great joys return;

and the desired day,

long awaited in faithful vows, arrives,

on which the Spirit of the Lord

filled the earth with joys.

The lights of his heavenly coming

run their course through the world.

This was proved by witnesses,

by the voices of the Apostles,

when, with diverse mouths,

they spoke to the foolish nations.

Redeemed by so great a gift,

let us render perpetual thanks

to the Spirit of the Father and the Son,

to God everlasting throughout the ages.

Glory to you, Trinity,

one equal Godhead,

before all ages,

now, and forever.

Amen.

Supplication. Let us pray to God the Father. See folio 417.

[Col. 0694C] Chapters. Lord Jesus Christ, pour into us the Holy Spirit promised by the Father, who gives life and teaches us the fullness of truth in the mystery of the blessed and undivided Trinity, so that in his gift may lie the perfection of our salvation, in whom the whole sum of power consists.

Our Father. Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

Lauda. I shall pour out my Spirit. Blessing. The Paraclete Spirit. fol. 420.

In the name of the Lord.

At the end of Vespers, for the holy day of Pentecost.

Lauda. For with you is the fountain of life. Sono. If you love me, keep my commandments. fol. 419.

Antiphon. The Spirit of truth, whom the Father will send from heaven. P. He will teach you every way of righteousness. V\. [Col. 0694D] By the word of the Lord the heavens were established, and by the Spirit of his mouth all their host. P. He will. V\. Glory. P. He will.

The Lord be with you. R\. And with your spirit.

Lauda 1. When the days of Pentecost were completed, all the Apostles were together in one place. P. And suddenly there came from heaven a sound like that of a mighty Spirit arriving. Alleluia. V\. May the glory of the Lord endure for ever and ever; the Lord shall rejoice in his works. P. And suddenly there came. V\. Glory. P. And suddenly there came.

The Lord be with you. R\. And with your spirit.

Lauda 2. Alleluia. They were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in various languages, as the Spirit granted them to utter. Alleluia. V\. Blessed is the nation whose God is the Lord, the people whom the Lord chose for himself as an inheritance. P. And began. V\. Glory. P. And.

The Lord. R\. And with your spirit.

Lauda 3. You gave them your Spirit, Lord, to teach them, and you did not deprive their mouth of manna. P. And you gave them water in their thirst. Alleluia. V\. Lord of hosts, turn us back; show your face, and we shall be saved. P. And you gave them water. V\. Glory. P. And you gave them water.

Hymn. The blessed joys. As above.

Chapters. May the Holy Spirit, Lord, lead us on the right path, so that wickedness may not prevail in us and divinity may abound in all things.

Our Father. Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

Blessing. May the good Spirit of God lead you on the right path and separate your journeys from the fall of sins. R\. Amen. May he also be the guide of your journey, who once appeared openly to the Disciples. R\. Amen. So that, filled by the same Spirit, you may cross the sea of this age unharmed and deserve to be consoled by the eternal gift. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

Lauda. I shall pour out my Spirit. Prayer. O Holy Spirit. fol. 402.

423 ON THE FIRST SUNDAY AFTER HOLY PENTECOST, ON THE DAY OF THE MOST HOLY TRINITY.

At Vespers.

Lauda. With you, Lord. P. Is the fountain of life, and in your light we shall see light. V\. The children of men shall hope in the protection of your wings; they shall be inebriated by the abundance of your house, and you shall give them drink from the torrent of your delight, Lord. P. The fountain of life.

Prayer. Lord, with whom is the fountain of life, and in whose light we behold light: nourish within us the splendor of your knowledge, so that, while we thirst, you may grant us life-giving drink, and restore understanding by heavenly light to our darkened souls. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Sono. You stretch out the heavens like a skin; you cover its upper parts with waters. P. You make your angels spirits and your ministers a burning fire. Alleluia. V\. You founded the earth upon its stability; it shall not be moved for ever and ever. P. You make.

The Lord be with you. R\. And with your spirit.

[Col. 0695D] Antiphon. Alleluia. Sons of Zion, exult and rejoice in your God. P. For he has given you a teacher of righteousness and poured out his Spirit upon all flesh. V\. Exult in God our helper; sing joyfully to the God of Jacob. P. For he has given. V\. Glory. P. For he has given. The Lord be with you. R\. And with your spirit.

Lauda. Alleluia. The Lord has cleansed us from all evils and given us a new heart and a right spirit. P. And he will take away the heart of stone from our flesh, so that we may walk in his ways. Alleluia. V\. Great is our Lord, and great is his power, and there is no measure of his wisdom. P. And he will take away. R\. Glory and. P. And he will take away.

Hymn. O blessed light of the Trinity. fol. 113.

[Col. 0696A] Supplication. Let us pray to the immense and ineffable Trinity of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, so that it may direct our life in good works and, after our passage from this age, grant us eternal rest with the righteous. R\. Grant this, eternal almighty God.

Kyrie eleison. R\. Christe eleison, Kyrie eleison.

Chapters. God the Holy Spirit, from whom all things were created and the whole universe restored, who in the beginning—that is, in your Son, our Lord Jesus Christ—made heaven and earth: grant us that your Spirit, who is good in all things, may be poured into our hearts. You who wonderfully distribute gifts of grace among individuals, show yourself uniquely present in forgiving our iniquities.

[Col. 0696B] **The Lord’s Prayer.** “Delivered from evil.” fol. 2.

**Blessing.** May the Holy Spirit, who appeared to the disciples from heaven with a sudden sound, in fiery tongues, work in you the fullness of his sanctification. R. Amen. And as, when he taught them, the disciples proclaimed great things, so, with him inspiring you, confess your sins in order to obtain his mercy. R. Amen. Through him by whom they were taught to speak in every tongue, may the remission of all sins be granted to you. R. Amen.

**Through.**

**Praise.** “By the word of the Lord the heavens were established,” Alleluia. P. “And by the breath of his mouth all their host.” Alleluia. “Let all the earth fear the Lord.” Alleluia. R. “For he spoke, and they were made; he commanded, and they were created.” [Col. 0696C] P. “By the breath.” V. “Glory.” P. “By the breath.”

**Prayer.** Almighty God the Father, who in the beginning—that is, in your Son Jesus Christ our Lord—made heaven and earth: grant us that your Spirit, who moves upon the waters—that is, upon our dark and fluid heart—may produce in us fruits pleasing to you, so that, sanctifying us in our body through an abundant outpouring of virtues, he may kindle us with the unceasing fire of your love. R. Amen.

**Through.**

## At Matins

**Hymn.** *Eternal Maker of all things.* **Prayer.** *Eternal Author.* fol. 3.

**Antiphon.** “Lord, how many are those who trouble me? But you, Lord, are my protector.” [Col. 0696D] **Psalm III.**

**Antiphon.** “Wash me from my iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin, O Lord.” **Psalm L.**

**Antiphon.** “In you my soul trusts; deliver me, O Lord.” **Psalm LVI.**

**Prayer.** “Lord Jesus Christ, who [—] those who believe in you.” fol. 3.

**Antiphon 1.** “By the word of the Lord the heavens were established.” P. “And by the breath of his mouth all their adornment.” V. “He loves mercy and judgment; the earth is full of the mercy of the Lord.” 424 P. “And by the breath.” R. “Glory,” and P. “And by the breath.”

**Prayer.** By your Word, O Lord, the heavens were made, and by the Spirit they were adorned; for in the blessed Trinity nothing is divided in the work, nothing is found separated in the gift. Whatever the Father does, the Son also does, and the Holy Spirit likewise performs indivisibly. Therefore the heavenly structure is joined together by the Father’s Word, and its adornment is completed by the Spirit of his mouth. Grant us, then, to recognize your works in faith, while we believe you, Lord of the Trinity, to be one in essence and equal. R. Amen.

**Through.**

**Antiphon 2.** “My Spirit shall be in your midst.” P. “For I will shake heaven and earth, and I will fill this house with glory, says the Lord.” V. “All nations, clap your hands; shout to God with a voice of rejoicing.” P. “For I will.” V. “Glory.” P. “For I will.”

**Prayer.** Lord God, stir up in us your Holy Spirit, by whom your Church may be made fruitful, so that the same Spirit, placed in our midst, may teach us his gifts, filling your house with unspeakable glory, so that in this place both the abundance of peace may overflow and the richness of graces may abound. R. Amen.

**Through mercy.**

**Antiphon 3.** “The Spirit of the Lord has filled the world.” P. “And he who contains all things has knowledge of understanding. For he created all things to exist.” V. “The Lord is exalted above all nations, and his glory is above the heavens.” P. “And he who.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “And he who.”

**Prayer.** Place your Spirit, O Lord, in our midst. Let him wash us with the pure waters of repentance and prepare us always to be a living offering to you, so that neither desire may defile the temple of our heart, nor the flame of eternal fire punishably afflict the earth of our body. V. Amen.

**Through mercy.**

R. “The hand of the Lord came upon me; and I saw, and behold, a shining Spirit was coming from the east, and great clouds were in it.” P. “And fire was in its midst.” V. “Wherever the Spirit went, the wheels were also lifted up, following it; for the spirit of life was in the wheels.” P. “And fire.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “And fire.”

**Prayer.** “Almighty God the Father.” See above in the preceding Vespers.

## At Lauds

[Col. 0697D] **At the Canticle. Antiphon.** “My spirit keeps vigil through the night.”

**Canticle.** “My spirit keeps vigil through the night.” fol. 64.

**Prayer.** “Keeping vigil through the night.” fol. 124.

**At the Benedictus. Antiphon.** “To you alone, God, belong honor, glory, virtue, and power, for ever and ever.”

**Canticle.** “Blessed are you, O Lord.” fol. 6. **Tone.** “Who stretches out the heavens like a skin.” fol. 423.

**Praise.** “Praise the Lord from the heavens,” Alleluia; “praise him in the heights,” Alleluia, alleluia. **Psalm CXLVIII.**

**Reading from the Book of the Wisdom of Solomon (Chapter I).**

R. Thanks be to God.

Love righteousness, you who judge the earth. Think of the Lord in goodness, and seek him in simplicity of heart, for he is found by those who do not tempt him, and he appears to those who have faith in him. For perverse thoughts separate from God, but tested virtue rebukes the foolish, because wisdom will not enter a malicious soul, nor dwell in a body subject to sins. For the holy Spirit of discipline will flee deceit, and withdraw from thoughts without understanding, and will be rebuked when iniquity comes upon him. For the Spirit of wisdom is kindly, and will not acquit one who curses with his lips, because God is witness to his innermost being, and the true examiner of his heart, and the helper of his tongue. For the Spirit of the Lord has filled the world. R. Amen.

[Col. 0698B] **Hymn.** “Radiance of the Father’s glory.” fol. 67. **Supplication.** “Let us pray the immense One.” **Capitulum.** “Holy Spirit of God.” **Praise.** “By the word of the Lord the heavens.” **Blessing.** “The Holy Spirit, who appeared with a sudden sound.” See fol. 423.

In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.

## At the conclusion of Vespers

**Praise.** “With you is, O Lord,” and **Prayer.** “Lord, with whom.” See fol. 423. **Tone.** “Who stretches out the heavens like a skin,” as above.

**Antiphon.** “By the word of the Lord the heavens were established; by the breath of his mouth is all their host.” V. “Bless the Lord, my soul, at all times; his praise is always in my mouth.”

**May the Lord be with you.** R. And with you.

**Praise 1. Alleluia.** “May your good Spirit, O God, lead us in the right way.” Alleluia. V. “For the Lord is great and exceedingly worthy of praise; he is terrible above all gods.” P. “May he lead us.” V. “Glory and honor to the Father.” P. “May he lead us.”

**May the Lord be always with you.** R. And with you.

**Praise 2.** “Bless the Lord, my soul.” Alleluia. “Who makes the cloud his ascent.” Alleluia. P. “Who makes his angels spirits,” Alleluia, “and his ministers a burning fire.” Alleluia. V. “Who founded the earth upon its stability, and it shall not be moved for ever and ever.” P. “Who makes.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “Who makes the angels.”

**Hymn.** “The Word of the Most High Father.” See fol. 94.

**Supplication.** “Let us pray the immense and ineffable One,” etc. See fol. 423.

**Capitulum.** Let us incline our hearts to God with tears, dearest brothers, and, confessing our sins to the most merciful Creator, let us cry out from the earth with continual supplication:

**The Lord’s Prayer.** “Delivered from evil.” fol. 2.

**Blessing.** May Almighty God bless you, who has deigned to fashion us from nothing. R. Amen. May he himself heal our infirmities, for he alone is our Lord and Redeemer. R. Amen. And may he always care for you, in whom is the fullness of our salvation. R. Amen.

**Through mercy, etc.**

**Praise.** “By the word of the Lord the heavens.”

[Col. 0699A] **Prayer.** “Almighty God the Father, who,” etc. See fol. 423.

# On the Second Sunday after Holy Pentecost

## At Vespers

**Praise.** “In the nights lift up your hands toward the holy place.” P. “And bless the Lord.” V. “You who stand in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God.” P. “And bless the Lord.”

**May the Lord be with you.** R. And with you.

**Tone.** “In you, O God, I have hoped; Lord, do not.” See fol. 112.

**Antiphon.** “The Lord gives wisdom.” P. “And from his mouth knowledge and prudence proceed.” V. “Great is the Lord and exceedingly worthy of praise, and there is no end to his greatness.” P. “And from his mouth.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “And from his mouth.”

**May the Lord be with you.** R. And with you.

**Antiphon.** “Love righteousness, you who judge the earth. Think of the Lord in goodness.” P. “And in simplicity of heart seek him.” V. “Hear this, all nations; listen, all who inhabit the world.” P. “And in.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “And in.”

**May the Lord be with you.** R. And with you.

**Antiphon.** “Counsel is mine, and equity; prudence is mine, and strength is mine.” P. “Through me princes and kings rule, and the powerful decree justice.” V. “Hear, my people, and I will testify to you; Israel, if you will listen to me.” P. “Through me.” V. “Glory.” P. “Through me.”

**May the Lord be with you.** R. And with you.

[Col. 0699C] **Praise.** “I have acquired your testimonies as an inheritance forever,” Alleluia. P. “For you are the rejoicing of my heart.” Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V. “Incline my heart to perform your justifications forever, because of the reward.” P. “For you are the rejoicing.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “For you are.”

**Hymn.** “O blessed light of the Trinity.” See fol. 113. **Supplication.** “Let us pray the Redeemer.” fol. 66.

**Capitulum.** When the course of the day has passed and the span of night is approaching, we offer you, Lord, the evening incense of light, humbly asking your magnificence: whatever in us is darkened by the gloom of sins, illumine by the kindling of your light; and our breast, which the enemy darkens, do you, Lord, enlighten with your customary compassion. And although we sleep in the night with bodily eyes, grant, Almighty God, that we may direct the gaze of our mind toward you; and when the limit of night has been completed, rising to prayer with the light restored, may we await the moments of the coming day in praise of your glory.

**The Lord’s Prayer.** “Delivered from evil.” fol. 2.

**Blessing.** May the Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God and eternal King, bless you and have mercy on you. R. Amen. May the Lord send you his holy angel Michael, the prince, to guard your hearts and bodies. R. Amen. May the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ remain with you, so that you may walk in the light of peace and be counted among the number of the saints. R. Amen.

**Through his mercy.**

[Col. 0700A] **Praise.** “It is good for me,” Alleluia. P. “The law of your mouth.” Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V. “You have dealt kindly with your servant, O Lord, according to your word.” P. “The law.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “The law.”

**Prayer.** Lord, before you is all our desire, and our groaning is not hidden from you. Grant, therefore, what we desire, and pardon what we have done; grant also fruit to our desires, and grant pardon for our sins. R. Amen.

**Through mercy.**

## At Matins

**Hymn.** “Eternal Maker of all things.” fol. 3.

**Prayer.** Almighty, eternal, merciful God, who appoint times to the seasons and give each season the grace by which it is governed: when you come, the length of darkness is dispelled; you console us when the cock crows, so that, while the herald of day sounds, meditation on the work of the day may revive. Therefore look upon us continually and stir us up, lest, persuaded by the error of deep night, we forget the everlasting day; but raise us when we slip in darkness, and correct us by seeing us, so that with Peter we may repent of our errors and mourn our committed crimes with equal tears. R. Amen.

**Through your mercy.**

**Antiphon.** “I beseech you, hear my voice from your holy mountain.” **Psalm III.**

**Antiphon.** “Against you alone have I sinned, O Lord; my soul has done evil before you.” **Psalm L.**

**Antiphon.** “O God, protect us under the shadow of your wings.” [Col. 0700C] **Psalm LVI.**

**Prayer.** Drive away from us, Only-begotten Son of the unbegotten Father, the sleep of the body; and, mercifully appeased, pardon our sins, so that in you the multitude of the redeemed may be gathered in pious vigils and be held worthy of your sacred sight. May what the ignoble frailty of the flesh now strives to implant in us rise, by the gift of your divinity, in glory. Therefore, Lord, bestow abundant light upon all who trust in you, and draw us to the heavenly homeland beneath the shadow of your wings. R. Amen.

**Through your mercy, O God, etc.**

**Antiphon 1.** “In you, Lord, is all our desire.” P. “And our groaning is not hidden from you. For our heart is troubled within us.” V. “Therefore we shall not fear when the earth is troubled and the mountains are moved into the heart of the sea.” P. “And our groaning.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “And our groaning.”

**Prayer.** “Lord, before you is all our desire.” See in the preceding Vespers.

**Antiphon 2.** “Our soul is humbled in the dust; our belly clings to the earth.” P. “Arise; why do you sleep, O Lord? Arise, and do not reject us forever.” V. “Why do you turn your face away? Why do you forget our poverty and our tribulation?” P. “Arise.” V. “Glory and honor to the Father.” P. “Arise; why do you sleep?”

**Prayer.** Arise, O Lord; help us against all the wickedness of those who persecute us, and for the sake of your name deliver us from the opposition of unclean spirits, so that you who humbled us in a place of affliction may raise us up again in the recompense of virtue. R. Amen.

**Through mercy.**

**Antiphon 3.** “Hear, my people, and I will speak; Israel, and I will testify to you, for I am God, your God. In tribulation you called upon me.” P. “And I delivered you and heard you in the hidden place of the storm.” V. “The Lord, God of gods, has spoken, and has called the earth from the rising of the sun to its setting; from Zion comes the appearance of his beauty.” P. “And I delivered you.” V. “Glory and honor to the Father.” P. “And I delivered.”

**Prayer.** Lord, who are believed to be manifest when you come in majesty for judgment, may your mercy rescue us from sins, lest justice drag us along with sinners. R. Amen.

[Col. 0701B] **Through.**

R. “We have acted wickedly and provoked you to anger, O Lord; therefore you are inexorable. Let us examine our hearts, seek, and return.” P. “To you, O Lord.” V. “Will you forget us forever? Will you abandon us for a long succession of days? Turn us, and we shall turn.” P. “To you, O Lord.” V. “Glory and honor to the Father.” The response R. “We have acted wickedly” is repeated.

**Another Responsory.** “Do not take your mercy away from us, O Lord.” P. “For behold, we have become despised and hostile, humbled upon the earth because of our sins.” V. “Remember, O Lord, what has happened to us; look and see our reproach.” P. “For behold.” V. “Glory and honor.” R. “Do not take away.”

[Col. 0701C] **Another Responsory.** “Be merciful, O Lord, to your people, for they have sinned against you.” P. “And remember none of their iniquities, but show them mercy and hear them, for whom I called upon you, O Lord.” V. “Turn, O Lord, for a little while, and take pleasure in your servants.” P. “And remember none.” V. “Glory and honor.” R. “Be merciful.”

## At Lauds

**At the Canticle. Antiphon.** “Lord our God, possess us; Lord, besides you we know no other; we have called upon your name.”

**Canticle.** “My spirit keeps vigil through the night.” fol. 64.

**Prayer.** “Keeping vigil through the night.” See fol. 124.

**At the Benedictus. Antiphon.** “There is a God in heaven whom we serve, and he is powerful to deliver us from our evils and rescue us from the hand of death.”

**Canticle.** “Blessed are you, O Lord.” fol. 6. **Prayer.** “Lord God of our fathers.” **Tone.** “My words.” See fol. 93.

**Reading from the Book of Ecclesiasticus (Chapter VII).**

R. Thanks be to God.

Son, do not be reluctant to visit the sick, for by such things you will be strengthened in love. In all your works remember your last things, and you will never sin. (Chapter VIII.) Do not quarrel with a powerful man, lest perhaps you fall into his hands. Do not contend with a wealthy man, lest perhaps you provoke a lawsuit against yourself; gold and silver have destroyed many and have reached even the hearts of kings and turned them. Do not quarrel with a talkative man, lest he speak evil of your family. Do not despise one who turns away from sin, nor reproach him; remember that we are all under correction. Do not disdain a man in his old age, for we too are growing old. Do not rejoice over the dead, knowing that we shall all die and wish to come into joy. Do not despise the account of wise elders; for associate with their words. From them you will learn the teaching of understanding and how to keep the commandments without complaint. R. Amen.

**Hymn.** “Radiance.” fol. 67. **Supplication.** “Let us pray the Redeemer,” as above.

**Capitulum.** We beseech you, holy Father, eternal God, author of everlasting light, who caused unfailing light to arise and enclosed temporal light within the setting of its end, so that night might exclude day in succession and day, once revealed, might drive away night with its brightness: we therefore beseech you, Lord, maker of all things, that earthly activity may likewise fail together with its author.

**The Lord’s Prayer.** “Delivered from evil.” fol. 2.

**Praise.** “Sing to the Lord.” **Prayer.** “To you, O Lord.” fol. 94.

At the conclusion of Vespers, let everything be said as at the conclusion of Vespers on the First Sunday after the Octave of Epiphany. See fol. 94. Except:

**Capitulum.** Beseeching the forgiveness of our sins in continual prayers, let us ask beforehand for the evening mercy of Almighty God the Father, and may Jesus Christ our Lord deign in every way to guard us, inflamed with the love of faith and joined together in the unity of charity.

**The Lord’s Prayer.** “Delivered from evil.” fol. 2.

**Blessing.** We beseech you, Almighty Father, to guard these servants of yours with favorable majesty. R. Amen. May they be girded with the virtues of peace and be enriched with precious gifts. R. Amen. May they remain steadfast in the struggle and emerge victorious in battle. R. Amen.

**Through mercy.**

**Prayer.** “Lord, before you,” etc. fol. 425.

# On the Third Sunday after Holy Pentecost

## At Vespers

**Praise.** “With you, O Lord, is the fountain of life,” etc. **Prayer.** “Lord, with whom is the fountain,” etc. See fol. 120. **Tone.** “Darkness does not.” See fol. 120.

**Antiphon.** “Your throne, O God, is incomparable and your glory incomprehensible; all the armies of angels stand before you with trembling.” P. “Your appearance dries up the abyss, and your indignation makes the mountains waste away.” V. “Lord God of hosts, who is like you? You are powerful, Lord, and your truth is all around you.” P. “Your appearance.” V. “Glory.” P. “Your appearance.”

**May the Lord be with you.** R. And with you.

**Antiphon.** “I will praise the Lord on my bed.” P. “By day and by night I will hold fast to him, and I will not let him go.” V. “I will exalt you, Lord my God and my king, and I will bless your name forever and ever.” P. “By day and by night.” V. “Glory.” P. “By day.”

[Col. 0703A] **May the Lord be with you.** R. And with you.

**Antiphon.** “Lord God of our father Abraham and God of Isaac, you who said that you would do good to us.” P. “Deliver us from the hand of our iniquity.” V. “Turn us, our God, and turn your anger away from us.” P. “Deliver us.” V. “Glory.” P. “Deliver us.”

**May the Lord be with you.** R. And with you.

**Praise.** “You are righteous, O Lord,” Alleluia. P. “And your judgment is right.” Alleluia. V. “Your word, O Lord, remains forever in heaven.” 428 Alleluia, alleluia. P. “And your judgment is right.” V. “Glory,” etc. P. “And your judgment is right.”

**Hymn.** “Inventor of the shining light.” fol. 91. **Supplication.** “Let us pray.” fol. 66.

**Capitulum.** Offering you, Lord our God, the evening sacrifice of praise on the day of this holy solemnity, we pray that you incline the ear of your mercy to the vows of your supplicating people. Let the prayer of your suppliants be before you as incense of sweetness; let the lifting of my hands be an evening sacrifice. May this, Lord, avail for the sure protection of your servants, so that at every hour and at every time you may protect us through the gift of your mercy in the activities of the day and guard us in the sleep of night.

**The Lord’s Prayer.** “Delivered from evil,” etc. See fol. 2.

**Blessing.** May the most loving Lord kindly pour upon you the rain of his blessings. R. Amen. May angelic protection guard you and drive the ancient enemy from your hearts. R. Amen. May the crafty enemy deter you, bound with the belt of chastity, by no trick of his deception. R. Amen.

[Col. 0703C] **Through.**

**Praise.** “The beginning of your words is truth.” Alleluia. P. “All the judgments of your justice endure forever.” Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V. “Your word is a lamp to my feet, O Lord, and a light to my paths.” P. “They endure forever.” V. “Glory.” P. “In.”

**Prayer.** Sweet and gentle God, and exceedingly merciful to those who call upon you, hear our prayer with your ears, and remove our errors from the multitude of your mercy. Do not allow us to crawl face-down upon the ground, but set us free to behold you. R. Amen.

**Through your mercy.**

## At Matins

**Hymn.** “Eternal Maker of all things.” See fol. 3.

[Col. 0703D] **Prayer.** God, who by your provident majesty administer the governance of every creature and oppose nightly rest to the cares of the day: coming, dispel the length of darkness, and console us when the cock crows, so that, while the herald of day sounds, meditation on the work of the day may revive. Look upon us continually with a merciful gaze, and stir us up, lest, persuaded by the error of deep night, we forget the everlasting day; but raise us when we slip in darkness, and correct us by seeing us, so that with Peter we may repent of our errors and mourn what we have done with equal tears. R. Amen.

**Through mercy.**

**Antiphon.** “You are the salvation of all, O God; let your blessing come upon your people.” **Psalm III.**

[Col. 0704A] **Antiphon.** “You love truth, O God; you have made uncertain and hidden things of wisdom known to me.” **Psalm L.**

**Antiphon.** “I will cry to the Most High God, the God who created all things and did good to me.” **Psalm LVI.**

**Prayer.** Many say to our soul, “There is no salvation for us in you, O Lord.” Crush them with your strength, O God, and by your power reduce the thousands of our enemies to nothing. Wash us from the filth of iniquity and cleanse us from the crime of our sins, so that our heart may be ready to sing a psalm of your resurrection and faithfully fulfill its vow at the office of Matins. R. Amen.

**Through mercy.**

**Antiphon 1.** “Hear, O Lord, the supplication of the people.” P. “And from heaven, O God, hear the prayers of all who pray in this place.” V. “For you, Lord, are sweet and gentle, and exceedingly merciful to those who call upon you.” P. “And the prayers of all.” V. “Glory.” P. “And the prayers of all.”

**Prayer.** “Sweet and gentle God.” See in the preceding Vespers.

**Antiphon 2.** “You are for us, O Lord, a refuge from the distress that surrounds us.” P. “For the scourges of our sins are many.” V. “For this every holy person shall pray to you at an appropriate time.” P. “For the scourges are many.” V. “Glory,” etc. P. “For the scourges are many.”

**Prayer.** Grant us, Lord, remission of sins, you who bestow blessedness upon the purified. Be a refuge from the distress of condemnation, you who grant freedom. And because we feel the many scourges of sins in us when the blow of punishment falls, grant that, by trusting in you, we may feel ourselves surrounded by your mercy. R. Amen.

**Through.**

**Antiphon 3.** “Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy.” P. “For we have been filled exceedingly with contempt.” V. “To you I have lifted my eyes, you who dwell in the heavens.” P. “For.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “For we have been filled exceedingly.”

**Prayer.** Have mercy on us, Lord; grant the help sought by our expectation, so that we who have been filled with the contempt of the proud may be fortified by the help of your defense. R. Amen.

**Through mercy.**

R. “Be for us, O Lord, protector and physician; by your customary compassion you grant medicine for the wounds of our sins; you are the way for those who have gone astray.” P. “And to those who seek you, merciful God, you grant a crown.” V. “May the orphan deserve to have you as father, and the poor and sinners as shepherd.” P. “And to those who seek you, merciful God.” V. “Glory.” R. “Be for us.”

## At Lauds

**At the Canticle. Antiphon.** “Lord our God, give us your peace; for you have given us everything.”

**Canticle.** “My spirit keeps vigil through the night.” fol. 64. **Prayer.** “Keeping vigil through the night.” fol. 124.

**At the Benedictus. Antiphon.** “Bless the Lord, servants of God, who rescued you from the underworld and delivered us from the hand of death.”

**Canticle.** “Blessed are you, Lord God.” fol. 6.

**Prayer.** “Lord God, who above.” **Tone.** “Send forth your light,” with the Praise and Psalm. See fols. 111 and 112.

[Col. 0705A] **Reading from the Book of Ecclesiasticus of Solomon (Chapter IX).**

R. Thanks be to God.

Son, do not abandon an old friend, for a new one will not be like him. New wine is a new friend; it will grow old, and you will drink it with pleasure. Do not envy the glory and wealth of a sinner, for you do not know what his downfall will bring. Do not delight in the injury of the unjust, knowing that the impious will not be pleasing even to the underworld. Keep far from a man who has the power to kill, and you will not suspect the fear of death; but if you approach him, commit nothing, lest perhaps he take your life. Know that you share in death, for you walk amid snares and tread upon the weapons of the sorrowful. According to your ability, guard yourself from your neighbor, and consult with the wise and prudent. Let just men be your companions at table, and let your glory be in the fear of the Lord. R. Amen.

**Hymn.** “Radiance.” fol. 67. **Supplication.** fol. 66.

**Capitulum.** Almighty God, who govern all things and recognize the past, present, and future with your eyes as though they were recent: grant pardon for our evils; grant remission for past deeds; give peace to the present, and grant complete confidence concerning the future, so that, with the stains of our sins cut away from us, we may deserve to be protected on this day by the vigils of the holy angels.

**The Lord’s Prayer, etc.** “Delivered from evil.” fol. 2.

**Praise.** “Sing to the Lord a new song.” **Prayer.** “To you, O Lord.” fol. 94.

At the conclusion of Vespers, let everything be said as at the conclusion of Vespers on the First Sunday after the Octave of the Lord’s Epiphany, fol. 94, except for the Capitulum and Blessing that follow:

**Capitulum.** Lord God, life of mortals, light of the faithful, strength of those who work, rest of the dead: grant us, Lord, a tranquil night, free from every disturbance, so that after the intervals of peaceful sleep, when the light comes, endowed through the activity of the Holy Spirit with the grace of your gift, we may deserve to return gifts of thanks to you unharmed.

**The Lord’s Prayer.**

**Blessing.** Bless, Lord, this people of yours, purchased by the blood of your Christ. R. Amen. Let those who have now been numbered among Christ’s flocks possess nothing of blindness. R. Amen. Preserve in them, Lord, a secure nuptial life, so that they may deserve to be guests of the patriarchs and of all the saints. R. Amen.

**Through mercy.**

**Note:** Although we have fourteen Sundays in the Missal, here we have only ten to be recited. If a feast is lacking and they wish to recite the Sunday office, let the Sundays that have already passed be said, namely, those after Holy Pentecost.

# On the Sunday before the November Kalends fast

## At Vespers

**Praise.** “In the nights lift up your hands toward the holy place.” P. “And bless the Lord.” V. “You who stand in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God.” P. “And bless.”

**Prayer.** In the nights we lift our hands to you, Lord, so that you may establish us firmly in your Church and, while we are pressed by worldly burdens, grant that you may be praised by our action. R. Amen.

**Through mercy.**

**Tone.** “Enter the gates.” See fol. 128.

**Antiphon.** “Alleluia. Lord God of our father Abraham and God of Isaac, you who said that you would do good to us.” P. “Deliver us from the hand of our iniquity.” V. “Turn us, our saving God, and turn your anger away from us.” P. “Deliver us.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “Deliver us.”

**May the Lord be with you.** R. And with you.

[Col. 0706B] **Praise.** “Do not remember, O God.” P. “Our ancient iniquities,” Alleluia. V. “May your mercy quickly come before us, for we have become exceedingly poor.” P. “Our iniquities.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “Our iniquities.”

**Hymn.** “Inventor of the shining light,” etc. fol. 91. **Supplication.** “Let us pray the Redeemer.” See fol. 66. **Capitulum.** “Our defense, O Lord.” **Blessing.** “May Almighty God bless you.” See fol. 121.

**Praise.** “Be angry, and do not sin,” Alleluia. “Speak in your hearts,” Alleluia. P. “And be pierced with remorse upon your beds.” Alleluia, alleluia. V. “Offer the sacrifice of justice and hope in the Lord.” P. “Speak.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “And upon your beds.”

**Prayer.** To you alone, Lord, our soul is subject, you whom every nature recognizes as its Creator. From you we receive the strength of patience, so that we may not be moved by scandal; we know that we owe you everything that we are. Therefore make us never rely upon the hope of iniquity, nor set our heart upon deceptive riches, so that we may grow accustomed to resting in you alone; and, that we may obtain the things sought, make our hearts contrite before you. R. Amen.

**Through.**

## At Matins

**Hymn.** “Eternal Maker of all things.” fol. 3.

**Prayer.** “God, whom the whole.” fol. 118.

**Antiphon.** “Your salvation, O Lord, is upon your people.” **Psalm III.**

**Antiphon.** “Blot out my iniquities.” **Psalm L.**

**Antiphon.** “I will cry to the Most High God, who has done good to me.” [Col. 0706D] **Psalm LVI.**

**Prayer.** “Lord God, to whom.” fol. 119.

**Antiphon.** “Rich and poor are the sons of men.” P. “Let us incline our hearts to God, and let us not fear on the evil day.” V. “Hear this, all nations; listen, all who inhabit the world.” P. “Let us incline.” V. “Glory.” P. “Let us incline.”

**Prayer.** May both rich and poor hear you together, Lord, the author of their salvation; may they bend their ears to your commandments, hear together, and come together, lest, separated by the error of schisms and heresies, your life-giving commands be for some an odor of life unto life and for others an odor of death unto death. Therefore, Lord, gather together those who are opposed, and do not allow those who are joined to be divided from the unity of the Church. There may the hearing of all be prepared to receive the faith, where the fullness of grace is promised to those who are to be saved. R. Amen.

**Through mercy, etc.**

**Antiphon 2.** “Hope in God, all the assembly of the peoples.” P. “Pour out your hearts before him, for he is your creator.” V. “Do not hope in iniquity, and do not desire robberies; if riches flow in, do not set your heart upon them.” P. “Pour out.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “Pour out.”

**Prayer.** “To you alone, Lord, our soul is subject,” etc. See in the preceding Vespers.

**Antiphon 3.** “Turn us, our saving God.”

**Prayer.** “Turn us, our God.” See fol. 116.

R. “In you all souls trust, saying: Soon God will have mercy on us, because the Lord has spoken, saying: ‘I will rejoice over one repentant sinner.’” P. “More than over ninety-nine righteous persons who do not need repentance.” V. “There will be joy in heaven before the angels of God over one sinner doing penance.” P. “More than.” V. “Glory.” R. “In you all souls trust.”

## At Lauds

**At the Canticle. Antiphon.** “You, Lord, on account of us.”

**Canticle.** “Lord, who dwell forever.” fol. 128.

**At the Benedictus. Antiphon.** “Sons of men.” As above. **Prayer.** “Lord God of the fathers.” fol. 93.

**Tone.** “May God have mercy on us,” P. “And bless us,” Alleluia. V. “May the Lord illumine his face upon us,” P. “And bless us.”

[Col. 0707C] **Praise.** “Praise the Lord from the heavens,” Alleluia; “praise him in the heights.” Alleluia. **Psalm CXLVIII.**

**Reading from the Book of Ecclesiasticus of Solomon (Chapter II).**

R. Thanks be to God.

You who fear the Lord, wait for his mercy, and do not turn away from him, lest you fall. You who fear the Lord, believe him, and your reward will not be lost. You who fear the Lord, hope in him, and mercy will come to you for your delight. You who fear the Lord, love him, and he will enlighten your hearts. Look, children, at the nations of men, and know who has hoped in the Lord and been put to shame; who has remained in his commandments and been abandoned; and who has called upon him and been despised? For God is gracious and merciful, and in the time of tribulation he forgives sins to all who seek him in truth. Woe to the double-hearted, to lips that are criminal, and to hands that do evil; and to the sinner who walks the earth by two paths. Woe to the fainthearted, who do not believe God; therefore they are not protected by him. Woe to those who have lost endurance, who have abandoned the right ways and turned aside into crooked paths. And what will you do when the Lord begins to look upon you? Those who fear the Lord will not be disobedient to his word, and those who love him will keep his way. Those who fear the Lord will seek what pleases him, and those who love him will be filled with his law. Those who fear the Lord will prepare their hearts and sanctify their souls in his sight. R. Amen.

[Col. 0708A] **Hymn.** “Radiance of the Father’s glory.” fol. 67. **Supplication.** “Let us pray.” fol. 66.

**Capitulum.** Now the east shines; now the day hastens on; now, with darkness driven away, dawn grows red; now the heavens gleam in the purest light; and the shining sun brings forth its rays upon the world. All things hasten; they desire to have you, Lord, favorable, whom they always recognize alike as their creator and defender.

**The Lord’s Prayer.**

**Praise.** “Be angry, and do not sin.” See in the preceding Vespers.

**Prayer.** “To you, Lord, in the assembly of the saints.” fol. 117.

# In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ

Here begins the office of the fast of the November Kalends, [Col. 0708B] which is observed for three days before the feast of Saint Cyprian, as follows.

## Over the Psalms

**Antiphon.** “But you, Lord, are my protector, my glory, and the one who lifts up my head.” **Psalm III.**

**Prayer.** “Although, Lord.” See fol. 68.

**Antiphon 1.** “Who understands his offenses?” **Psalm XVIII.**

**Prayer.** “From our hidden sins.”

**Antiphon 2.** “Hear us on the day.” **Psalm XIX.**

**Prayer.** “The tribulations of our heart.” fol. 68.

**Antiphon 3.** “We shall sing and praise your powers.” **Psalm XX.**

**Prayer.** Almighty strength, Lord, may our soul and body be subject to you, and may our life serve you with complete sincerity. Fulfill the desire of our soul, by which it may reach you, and receive the supplication of our lips, lest that many-formed enemy steal it away. Conquer the hidden enemy by your strength; go before us with blessing; and lead us through the way of life to everlasting joys. R. Amen.

**Through mercy.**
God have mercy on us, and forgive our sins. P. And turn his anger away from us. V. May he illumine his face upon us, and have mercy on us. P. And turn it away. V. Glory and honor. P. And turn it away.

## At Lauds

Antiphon. I acknowledge my iniquities, and my sin is always before me. Psalm 50.

[Col. 0708D] Prayer. As we acknowledge our iniquities and lay bare before you, Lord, the sins that are our own, weeping with tears and beating our breasts, we humbly pray that you turn your face away from our crimes and blot out all the sins we have committed. Create, therefore, O God, in our heart what you love; and in your accustomed favor forgive what you hate. And if our sinful vices repeatedly provoke you to anger against us, may your abundant indulgence render you reconciled to us. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

For the Canticle. Antiphon. Do not destroy the people. And the Canticle: “Lord, Lord, King of the gods,” fol. 103.

Matins Hymn. May the splendor of the Lord our God be upon us, and direct upon us the work of our hands. V. Look upon your servants and upon your works, and direct their children. P. And direct the work of our hands. V. Glory and honor. P. And direct the work.

[Col. 0709A] Lauda. Praise him in his holy places: alleluia, alleluia. Praise the Lord in the firmament of his power. Psalm 150.

Reading from the Book of Ecclesiasticus of Solomon (Chapter 4).

R. Thanks be to God.

My son, preserve the proper time and avoid evil. For the sake of your life, do not be ashamed to speak the truth. For there is a shame that brings sin, and there is a shame that brings glory and grace. Do not show partiality to the detriment of yourself, nor utter a lie against your own soul. Do not be overawed by your neighbor in his fall, and do not withhold a word at the time of salvation. Do not hide your wisdom in its beauty. Wisdom is recognized in his speech, as are understanding, knowledge, and instruction in words of truth, and firmness in works of justice. Do not oppose the truth in any way, and be ashamed of the error of your ignorance. Do not be ashamed to confess your sins, and do not submit yourself to every person because of sin. Do not resist the face of the powerful, and do not strive against the force of the river. Fight for justice for the sake of your soul, and contend for justice even unto death, and God will overthrow your enemies for you. R. Amen.

Hymn. God, fountain of kindness.

Supplication. Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world. Fol. 69.

Capitulum. What could human frailty, weighed down daily by such heavy burdens of crimes, worthily render to you, O most merciful Trinity, our God? We disclose our crimes by the confession of our own mouths; we declare our iniquities against ourselves; we display the weaknesses of our wounds, and we earnestly ask that you, the true physician, apply a remedy to our ulcers. Therefore, since you are the Lamb of God who take away the sin of the world, prostrate we ask the power of your divinity: whenever we offend you, may you deign to forgive us each time. For at your command, though unworthy, we cry from the earth:

Our Father.

Deliver us from evil. Fol. 10.

Lauda. Let your mercies come to me, and I shall live, alleluia. P. For your law is my meditation. Alleluia, alleluia. V. Let your mercy come, that it may comfort me, according to your word to your servant. P. For your law. V. Glory and honor. P. For your law.

[Col. 0709D] Blessing. May Christ, the Son of God, who with the Father and the Holy Spirit possesses the unity of the Godhead, mercifully accept this appointed three-day fast of abstinence, for the welfare of the Church and the salvation of the whole people. R. Amen. And may he alone, who endured the cross’s gallows for our salvation, cleanse your hearts. R. Amen. So that, purified from every defilement of sin, you may receive from him the reward of the promise obtained. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

## At Terce

Prophecy. My son, have confidence. Fol. 95.

Reading from the Book of Leviticus (Chapter 23).

R. Thanks be to God.

[Col. 0710A] In those days: The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: On the tenth day of this seventh month shall be the most solemn Day of Atonement, and it shall be called holy; and you shall afflict your souls on it and offer a burnt offering to the Lord. You shall do no servile work during this day, for it is a day of propitiation, so that the Lord your God may be propitious to you. Every person who is not afflicted on this day shall perish from among his people; and whoever performs any work, I shall destroy him from among his people. Therefore you shall do no work on it; it shall be an everlasting ordinance for you throughout all your generations and dwellings. And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the children of Israel: From the fifteenth day of this seventh month shall be the Feast of Booths for the Lord, for seven days. The first day shall be called most solemn and most holy; you shall do no servile work. But for seven days you shall offer burnt offerings to the Lord; and the eighth day shall also be most solemn for you, and you shall offer a burnt offering to the Lord, for it is an assembly and a gathering; you shall do no servile work on it. These are the feasts of the Lord, which you shall call most solemn and most holy, and on which you shall offer offerings to the Lord, burnt offerings and libations according to the rite of each day. Therefore, from the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when you have gathered all the fruits of your land, you shall celebrate the feast of the Lord for seven days. On the first day you shall take the fruit of a most beautiful tree, palm fronds, branches of trees with thick foliage, and willows of the torrent, and you shall rejoice before the Lord your God. [Col. 0710C] You shall celebrate his solemnity for seven days each year; it shall be an everlasting ordinance throughout your generations. In the seventh month you shall celebrate the feast in shelters for seven days. R. Amen.

Reading from the Book of the Prophet Ezekiel (Chapter 33).

R. Thanks be to God.

The word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, speak to the house of Israel: Thus you have spoken, saying: “Our iniquities and our sins are upon us, and in them we waste away; how, then, can we live?” Say to them: As I live, says the Lord God, I do not desire the death of the wicked, but that the wicked turn from his way and live. Turn back from your most evil ways; why will you die, O house of Israel? But you, son of man, say to the children of your people: The justice of the just man will not save him on whatever day he sins; and the wickedness of the wicked man will not harm him on whatever day he turns from his wickedness; nor will the just man be able to live by his justice on whatever day he sins. Even if I say to the just man, “You shall surely live,” and, trusting in his justice, he commits iniquity, all his justice shall be forgotten, and in the iniquity he has committed, in that he shall die. But if I say to the wicked man, “You shall surely die,” and he repents of his sin and practices judgment and justice; if that wicked man restores the pledge and returns what he has seized, walks in the commandments of life, and does nothing unjust, he shall surely live and shall not die. None of his sins that he has committed shall be held against him; he has practiced judgment and justice, and he shall surely live. And the children of your people have said: “The way of the Lord is not balanced,” while their own way is unjust. For when the just man turns away from his justice and commits iniquities, he shall die in them.
