And when the wicked man turns away from his wickedness and practices judgment and justice, he shall live and shall not die, says the Lord Almighty. R. Amen.

The continuation of the Epistle of the Apostle Paul to the Romans (Chapter 3).

R. Thanks be to God.

Brothers, God is truthful, while every human being is a liar, as it is written: “So that you may be justified in your words and prevail when you are judged.” But if our iniquity commends the justice of God, what shall we say? Is God unjust, who inflicts anger? (I speak according to human reasoning.) By no means. Otherwise, how will God judge this world? For if the truth of God has abounded through my lie to his glory, why am I still judged as a sinner? And why not—just as we are slanderously accused, and as some claim that we say—“Let us do evil so that good may come”? Their condemnation is just. What then? Are we superior to them? Not at all. For we have already charged that Jews and Greeks alike are all under sin, as it is written: “There is no one who is just; there is no one who understands; there is no one who seeks God. All have turned aside; together they have become useless. There is no one who does good, not even one. Their throat is an open tomb; with their tongues they have acted deceitfully. The poison of asps is under their lips. Their mouth is full of cursing and bitterness. Their feet are swift to shed blood; destruction and misery are in their ways, and they have not known the way of peace. There is no fear of God before their eyes.”

Now we know that whatever the law says, it speaks to those who are under the law, so that every mouth may be stopped and the whole world may become subject to God; for no flesh will be justified before him by works of the law. Through the law comes knowledge of sin. But now the justice of God has been manifested apart from the law, attested by the law and the Prophets. The justice of God through faith in Jesus Christ is for all and upon all who believe, for there is no distinction: all have sinned and lack the glory of God. They are justified freely by his grace, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus our Lord. R. Amen.

Antiphon 1. For the honor of your name, Lord, deliver us, and be favorable toward our sins, for the sake of your name. Psalm 78.

Prayer. Be favorable toward our sins. Fol. 413.

Antiphon 2. Save your people, Lord, and bless your inheritance. Psalm 27.

Prayer. Hear, Lord, the voice of our supplication, which we direct to you with humble entreaty; and, we ask, surround us with the protection of your mercies, so that we may not be joined to the evils of sinners, but that peace may be firmly fixed in our hearts; and may our flesh flourish in your love, and our life please you. Therefore we ask you to be the strongest protector of your people; save your people, and raise up your inheritance by governing and blessing it. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 3. O God, attend to our help; Lord, hasten to help me. Psalm 69.

R. Let us beseech the Lord, and he will be reconciled to us. P. And he will hear us and have mercy on us. V. Come, let us exult in the Lord; let us rejoice in God our salvation. P. And he will hear us. V. Glory and honor. P. Let us beseech the Lord.

Prayers. Let us all say: Have mercy, Lord, and hear us. P. For you are compassionate. V. Hear us, Lord, as we pray to you with all our heart and with all our mind. P. For. V. You who dwell in heaven and look upon the humble, grant forgiveness to penitents. P. For. V. Protect this city and all who dwell in it, O Christ, with the right hand of your power. P. For. V. Grant remission of sins and amendment of conduct, Lord. P. For you are compassionate.

Prayer. Attend to our help, Lord, and hasten to help us; for our efforts in good works achieve nothing unless you assist us, from whom human steps are directed. For you are the one through whom weakness is strengthened.

Our Father. Deliver us from evil. Fol. 10.

Let the blessing be said that is said at Terce throughout the year.

## At Sext

[Col. 0712C] Reading from the Book of the Prophet Isaiah (Chapter 33).

R. Thanks be to God.

Lord, have mercy on us; for we have waited for you. Be our arm in the morning and our salvation in time of tribulation. At the voice of the Angel the peoples fled, and at your exaltation the nations were scattered. Your spoils shall be gathered as the locust is gathered, as when ditches are filled with it. The Lord has been magnified, who dwells on high; he has filled Zion with judgment and justice. And there shall be faithfulness in its times: riches of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge of the fear of the Lord—he himself is its treasure. Behold, those who see shall cry out outside, and the Angels of peace shall weep bitterly. The roads have been abandoned; the passerby has ceased from the path; the covenant has been annulled; he has rejected the cities and regarded human beings as nothing. The earth mourned and languished; Lebanon was confounded and withered, and Sharon became like a desert; Bashan and Carmel were shaken. Now I shall arise, says the Lord; now I shall be exalted; now I shall be lifted up. R. Amen.

Antiphon 1. Our eyes are toward the Lord our God, until he has mercy on us. Psalm 122.

Prayer. To you, Lord, we lift our eyes. Fol. 73.

Antiphon 2. The snare has been broken, and we have been delivered. Psalm 123.

Prayer. Be with us, Lord. Fol. 78.

Antiphon 3. Do good, Lord, to those who are good and upright in heart. Psalm 124.

R. Have mercy, for you are God. P. Merciful one, have mercy, for we have sinned against you. V. To you we lift our eyes, who dwell in heaven. P. Merciful one. V. Glory and honor. R. Have mercy.

Prayers. Let us all say: Be favorable toward your people, O Christ. P. And have mercy. V. At last attend to our prayers; attend now in your favor. P. And have mercy. V. We have sinned; we have acted wickedly; we have acted impiously. P. And have mercy. V. Turn away your anger, and grant forgiveness with the grace of your countenance. P. And have mercy. V. Cleanse us, Lord, from our sins and offenses. P. And have mercy.

Prayer. Do good, Lord, to those who are good. Fol. 73.

## At None

[Col. 0713B] Prophecy. My son, keep my words. Fol. 96.

Reading from the Book of Deuteronomy (Chapters 23, 24, and 25).

R. Thanks be to God.

In those days: The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the children of Israel, and say to them: I am the Lord your God. You shall not offer the wages of a prostitute or the price of flesh in the house of the Lord your God. You shall not lend money, grain, or anything else to your brother at interest, but you may lend at interest to a foreigner. To your brother you shall lend without interest whatever he needs, so that the Lord your God may bless you in all the work of your hands in the land that you are entering to possess.

When you make a vow to your God, you shall not delay in fulfilling it, for the Lord your God will require it of you; and if you delay, it will be counted as sin against you. If you do not wish to promise, you will be without sin. But what has gone forth from your lips, observe and do just as you promised to the Lord your God; you spoke of your own will and with your own mouth.

When you demand from your neighbor the thing he owes you, you shall not enter his house to take the pledge. Instead, you shall stand outside, and he shall bring out to you whatever he has. But if he is poor, the pledge shall not remain with you overnight; you shall return it to him immediately before sunset, so that he may sleep in his garment and bless you, and you may have justice before the Lord your God.

You shall not deny the wages of your needy and poor brothers, or of the foreigners who dwell with you in the land and within your gates. On the same day you shall give him the price of his labor before sunset, because he is poor and sustains his life by it, lest he cry out against you to the Lord and it be counted as sin against you.

Fathers shall not be put to death for their sons, nor sons for their fathers; each person shall die for his own sin. You shall not pervert the judgment of the foreigner or the orphan, nor take the widow’s garment as a pledge. Remember that you were a servant in Egypt and that the Lord your God rescued you from there. Therefore I command you to do this.

When you reap your grain in your field and, forgetting, leave a sheaf behind, do not return to collect it; leave it for the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow, so that the Lord your God may bless you in all the work of your hands. If you gather the fruit of your olive trees, whatever remains on the trees, do not return to collect it; leave it for the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow. If you harvest your vineyard, do not gather the remaining clusters; they shall belong to the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow. Remember that you were a servant in Egypt; therefore I command you to do this.

You shall not have different weights in your bag, a larger and a smaller one; nor shall there be in your house a larger and a smaller measure. You shall have a just and true weight, and a measure that is equal and true, so that you may live for a long time upon the land that the Lord your God will give you. R. Amen.

Prophecy. Hear, you who are far away. Fol. 71.

The continuation of the Epistle of the Apostle Paul to the Romans (Chapter 12).

R. Thanks be to God.

Brothers, I beseech you by the mercy of God to present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God, your reasonable service. Do not be conformed to this age, but be transformed in the renewal of your mind, so that you may discern what the will of God is—what is good, pleasing, and perfect.

For by the grace given to me I say to everyone among you: Do not think more highly than you ought to think, but think with sober judgment, according to the measure of faith God has assigned to each one. For just as in one body we have many members, and all the members do not have the same function, so we, though many, are one body in Christ, and individually members of one another.

We have gifts differing according to the grace given to us: if prophecy, according to the measure of faith; if service, in serving; if one teaches, in teaching; if one exhorts, in exhortation; if one gives, in generosity; if one presides, with diligence; if one shows mercy, with cheerfulness.

Let love be without pretense. Hate what is evil; cling to what is good. Love one another with brotherly affection; outdo one another in showing honor. Do not be sluggish in diligence; be fervent in spirit; serve the Lord. Rejoice in hope; be patient in tribulation; persevere in prayer. Share in the needs of the saints; pursue hospitality.

Bless those who persecute you; bless, and do not curse. Rejoice with those who rejoice; weep with those who weep. Be of the same mind toward one another; do not set your mind on high things, but associate with the humble. Do not be wise in your own eyes. Repay no one evil for evil; provide what is good not only before God but also before human beings.

If possible, so far as it depends on you, live at peace with all people. Do not defend yourselves, beloved, but give place to anger, for it is written: “Vengeance is mine; I will repay,” says the Lord. But if your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him drink. By doing this you will heap burning coals upon his head. Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good. R. Amen.

Antiphon 1. Give thanks to the Lord with the harp; sing psalms to him on the ten-stringed psaltery. Psalm 32.

Prayer. Lord, who [art] of the righteous. Fol. 403.

Antiphon 2. Our soul patiently waits for the Lord, for he is our helper and protector. Psalm 32.

Defend the Church which you chose beforehand; willingly receive the vows of the priests; hear the prayer. P. And have mercy. V. Almighty, eternal ruler of the heavens, most high God, behold our groaning and weeping; give ear. P. And have mercy. V. The old, the young, and nursing infants are destroyed by cruel death in suffering: Redeemer, spare [them]. P. And have mercy. V. We have sinned; we have committed iniquities: you, Redeemer, wash away every offense; release [us from] guilt. P. And.

Prayer. Let your mercy be [upon us]. Fol. 401.

## ON THE SECOND DAY

## At Matins

[Col. 0715C] Antiphon. But you, O Lord. Psalm 3. Prayer. Although, Lord. Fol. 68.

Antiphon 1. Magnify the Lord with me, and let us exalt his name together. Psalm 33.

Prayer. At all times. Fol. 405.

Antiphon 2. Children of men hope in the protection of your wings, O Lord. Psalm 35.

Prayer. O Lord, do not at all uncover the children of men who hope in the protection of your wings; rather, cherish and nourish them as chicks, so that we may be prepared for heavenly flights. Do not allow us to be snatched away by the tearing of those who lie in wait, nor permit us to fly away from the nest of your Church; but, while you rule us by a kingly fatherly governance, may we come, aided by your help, to the abundance of your house. R. Amen.

Reading from the Book of Exodus (Chapter 22).

R. Thanks be to God.

In those days: The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Whoever sacrifices to gods shall be put to death, except [one who sacrifices] to the Lord alone. You shall not grieve or afflict a stranger, for you yourselves were strangers in the land of Egypt. You shall do no harm to widow and orphan. If you injure them, they will cry out to me, and I shall hear their cry; my anger will be kindled, and I shall strike you with the sword, and your wives shall be widows and your children orphans. If you lend money to my poor people who dwell with you, you shall not press him as an exactor, nor oppress him with usury. If you take your neighbor’s garment as a pledge, return it before sunset. For it alone is what covers him, the garment of his flesh, and he has no other in which to sleep; if he cries out to me, I shall hear him, because I am merciful. You shall not revile gods, and you shall not curse the ruler of your people. You shall not delay to offer your tithes and firstfruits. (Chapter 23.) You shall not accept a lying report, nor join your hand so as to bear false witness for the wicked. You shall not follow a crowd in doing evil, nor in judgment acquiesce in the opinion of the majority so as to depart from the truth. Nor shall you show favor to the poor in judgment. You shall not pervert the judgment of the poor. You shall flee falsehood. You shall not kill the innocent and the just, because I oppose the wicked. Nor shall you accept gifts, which blind even the prudent and overturn the words of the just. You shall not be troublesome to strangers, for you know the lives of strangers, because you yourselves were strangers in the land of Egypt. Bring the firstfruits of your land into the house of the Lord your God. R. Amen.

Reading from the Book of the Prophet Zechariah (Chapters 7 and 8).

R. Thanks be to God.

The word of the Lord of hosts came to me, saying: Speak to all the people of the land and to the priests, saying: When you fasted and mourned in the fifth and seventh [months] throughout these seventy years, did you fast a fast for me? And when you ate and drank, did you not eat for yourselves and drink for yourselves? Are these not the words which the Lord spoke through the hand of the former prophets, when Jerusalem was still inhabited and prosperous, it and the cities around it, and when the south and the plain were inhabited? And the word of the Lord came to Zechariah, saying: Judge true judgment, and show mercy and compassion, each one to his brother. Do not accuse the widow, the orphan, the stranger, or the poor, and let no man devise evil against his brother in his heart. But they refused to heed; they turned a withdrawing shoulder and made their ears heavy, lest they should hear. They made their heart like adamant, lest they should hear the law and the words which the Lord of hosts sent in the Holy Spirit through the hand of the former prophets; and there was great indignation from the Lord of hosts. And it came to pass, as the Lord spoke and they did not hear, so they shall cry out and I shall not hear, says the Lord of hosts. I scattered them among all kingdoms which they did not know, and the land was desolated after them because there was none passing through or returning; and they made the desirable land a wilderness. The word of the Lord of hosts came to me, saying: Thus says the Lord of hosts: I have been jealous for Zion with great zeal, and with great indignation have I been jealous for her. Thus says the Lord of hosts: I have returned to Zion, and I shall dwell in Jerusalem; and Jerusalem shall be called the city of truth, and the mountain of the Lord of hosts, the sanctified mountain. R. Amen.

The continuation of the Epistle of the Apostle Paul to the Romans (Chapters 13 and 14).

R. Thanks be to God.

Brothers, put on our Lord Jesus Christ, and do not make provision for the flesh in its desires. (Chapter 14.) Receive the weak in faith, not for disputes over opinions. One person believes that he may eat all things, but one who is weak may eat vegetables. Let not the one who does not eat despise the one who eats, and let not the one who does not eat judge the one who eats, for God has received him. Who are you to judge another’s servant? He stands or falls to his own lord; indeed, he shall stand, for God is able to make him stand. One person judges one day above another, while another judges every day alike: let each be fully convinced in his own mind. The one who observes the day observes it for the Lord. The one who eats eats for the Lord and gives thanks to God. The one who does not eat does not eat for the Lord and gives thanks to God. For none of us lives for himself, and none dies for himself. For whether we live, we live for the Lord, and whether we die, we die for the Lord. Therefore, whether we live or die, we are the Lord’s. For to this end Christ died and rose again, that he might rule over the living and the dead. R. Amen.

Thus says the Lord: Let your hands be strengthened, you who in these days have heard these words from the mouths of the prophets, on the day when the house of the Lord of hosts was founded, so that the temple might be built. For before those days there was no wage for human beings, nor any wage for animals; there was no peace for those entering or leaving because of the tribulation, and I set all human beings against one another.

But now I will not deal with the remnant of this people as in former days, says the Lord of hosts. Rather, there shall be a seed of peace: the vine shall give its fruit, the earth shall give its produce, and the heavens shall give their dew. Do not fear. Speak truth, each one with his neighbor; judge truth and the judgment of peace in your gates. R. Amen.

Reading from the Book of Deuteronomy (Chapter 7).

[Col. 0719B] R. Thanks be to God.

In those days: Moses spoke to all Israel, saying: Behold, the Lord your God has chosen you to be his special people from among all the peoples who are upon the earth. It was not because you surpassed all the nations in number that the Lord was bound to you and chose you, for you are fewer than all peoples. Rather, it was because the Lord loved you and kept the oath that he swore to your fathers. He brought you out with a mighty hand and redeemed you from the house of slavery, from the hand of Pharaoh, king of Egypt.

Know, therefore, that the Lord your God is himself the mighty and faithful God, keeping his covenant and mercy with those who love him and keep his commandments for a thousand generations, and repaying immediately those who hate him, destroying them, and not delaying; promptly repaying them what they deserve.

Therefore keep the commandments, statutes, and judgments that I command you today to perform. If, after you hear these judgments, you keep and do them, the Lord your God will keep for you the covenant and mercy that he swore to your fathers. He will love you and multiply you; God will bless the fruit of your womb, the fruit of your land, your grain, your wine, your oil, and the herds of your cattle and flocks of sheep, upon the land that he swore to your fathers to give you.

You shall be blessed above all peoples. Neither among human beings nor among your herds shall there be anyone sterile, male or female. God will remove every sickness from you, and he will not inflict upon you the terrible diseases of Egypt that you have known; rather, he will inflict them upon all your enemies. You shall devour all the peoples that the Lord your God is about to give you. Your eye shall not spare them, and you shall not serve their gods, lest they become a ruin to you.

If you say in your heart, “These nations are more numerous than we are; how can I destroy them?” do not fear, but remember what the Lord your God did to Pharaoh and to all the Egyptians: the great plagues that your eyes saw, the signs and the power, the mighty hand and the outstretched arm by which the Lord your God brought you out. So will the Lord your God do to all the peoples whom you fear.

Moreover, the Lord your God will send hornets among them until he destroys and scatters all those who have escaped from you and hidden themselves. You shall not fear them, because the Lord your God is in your midst. R. Amen.

## The continuation of the Epistle of the Apostle Paul to the Romans (Chapter XIV)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

Brothers, Christ died and rose again for this reason: that he might rule over the living and the dead. But you—why do you judge your brother? Or why do you despise your brother? For we shall all stand before the tribunal of Christ. For it is written: “As I live, says the Lord, every knee shall bend to me, and every tongue shall confess to God.” Therefore each of you shall give an account of himself to God.

Let us no longer judge one another, then; but judge this rather: that you should not place a stumbling-block or an occasion of scandal before your brother. I know, and am confident in the Lord Jesus, that nothing is unclean in itself; but to one who considers something unclean, to him it is unclean. For if your brother is offended because of food, you are no longer walking according to charity. Do not destroy, by your food, the one for whom Christ died. Therefore do not let what is good for you be blasphemed. For the kingdom of God is not food and drink, but righteousness and peace in the Holy Spirit.

**R.** Amen.

**Antiphon 1.** Let all the earth adore you and sing praise to you. **Psalm 65.**

**Prayer.** Let all the earth adore you. Folio 78.

**Antiphon 2.** Say to God: “How fearful are your works, in the abundance of your power!” **Psalm 65.**

**Prayer.** O God, whom the whole earth, proclaiming aloud, celebrates with joyful praise, whose glory the singing voice of the psalm cries out, and whose fearful power it acknowledges in your works: grant that our voices may offer you a joyful song pleasing to you, and that our prayers may utter the psalm perfectly; grant that we may proclaim you the creator of every virtue.

Since your eyes look upon the nations, and you search out inwardly, though imperceptibly, the hearts of all, we ask you: look upon us mercifully with your sight, and correct us compassionately, so that you neither pour out anger upon us when provoked by our crimes, nor withhold your mercy when you are entreated. Grant that the discipline by which we fear you for our offenses may itself be for our benefit, and that the reward of pardon may be the very thing by which we believe and confess your divinity.

Therefore, Lord, bring our souls to life, so that here we may lament what we have done and may regain the grace that we lost by sinning.

**R.** Amen. Through mercy.

## Reading from the Book of the Wisdom of Solomon (Chapter XI)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

Have mercy on all, O God, because you can do all things, and you overlook the sins of human beings for the sake of repentance. For you love all that exists, and you hate nothing that you have made; for you did not establish anything while hating it. How could anything endure unless you had willed it? Or how could anything be preserved that had not been called into being by you?

But you spare all, because they are yours, Lord, who love souls. For your spirit is good in all things. Therefore you correct those who go astray little by little, and you admonish and address them concerning the things by which they sin, so that, having abandoned wickedness, they may believe in you, Lord.

## Reading from the Book of Deuteronomy (Chapter XVI)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

In those days Moses spoke to the whole assembly of the children of Israel and said to them:

“You shall count seven weeks for yourself, beginning from the day when you first put the sickle to the standing grain. You shall celebrate the feast of weeks to the Lord your God, offering a voluntary gift from your hand, according to the blessing of the Lord your God. You shall feast before the Lord your God—you and your son and your daughter, your male servant and your female servant, the Levite who is within your gates, and the stranger, the orphan, and the widow who dwell among you.

“You shall remember that you were a servant in Egypt, and you shall observe these ordinances.

“You shall also celebrate the feast of booths for seven days, when you have gathered the produce from your threshing floor and winepress. You shall feast at your festival—you and your son and your daughter, your male servant and your female servant, the Levite as well as the stranger, the orphan and the widow who are within your gates.

“For seven days you shall keep the feast to the Lord your God, and the Lord your God will bless you in all your crops and in every work of your hands, and you shall be joyful.

“Three times a year every male among you shall appear before the Lord your God in the place that he chooses: at the feast of Unleavened Bread, at the feast of Weeks, and at the feast of Booths. You shall not appear before God empty-handed; each shall offer according to what he has, according to the blessing of the Lord his God that he has given him.

“You shall appoint judges and magistrates in all your gates that the Lord your God gives you, throughout your tribes, so that they may judge the people with a just judgment and not incline to either side. You shall not show partiality or accept gifts, for gifts blind the eyes of the wise and alter the hearts of the just. You shall pursue justice—justice—so that you may live and possess the land that the Lord your God gives you.”

**R.** Amen.

## Reading from the Book of the Prophet Jeremiah (Chapter V)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

This is what the Lord says:

“Listen, foolish people, who have no heart: you have eyes and do not see; you have ears and do not hear. Will you not fear me, then, says the Lord, and will you not tremble before my face?

“I have placed the sand as the boundary of the sea, an everlasting ordinance that it cannot pass. Its waves are shaken, but they cannot prevail; its billows surge, but they cannot cross it. Yet this people has an unbelieving and rebellious heart: they have turned away and departed.

“They have not said in their hearts: ‘Let us fear the Lord our God, who gives us the early and latter rain in its season and preserves for us the fullness of the annual harvest.’

“Our iniquities have turned these things aside, and our sins have kept good things from us. For wicked men have been found among my people, lying in wait, setting snares and traps to catch human beings. As a cage is full of birds, so their houses are full of deceit. Therefore they have become great and rich. They have grown fat and sleek, and they have passed beyond my words most wickedly.

“They have not judged the case of the widow, nor defended the case of the orphan, nor judged the judgment of the poor. Shall I not visit these things, says the Lord? Shall my soul not take vengeance on a nation such as this?

“Stunning and astonishing things have occurred in the land: the prophets prophesy lies, the priests applaud with their hands, and my people love such things. What, then, will happen to it at the end?”

(Chapter VI.) “Strengthen yourselves, children of Benjamin, in the midst of Jerusalem.”

**R.** Amen.

## The continuation of the Epistle of the Apostle Paul to the Ephesians (Chapter IV)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

Brothers, be renewed in the spirit of your mind, and put on the new person, who was created according to God in righteousness and holiness of truth.

Therefore, putting away all falsehood, speak truth, each of you with his neighbor, for we are members of one another. Be angry, but do not sin; do not let the sun go down upon your anger. Do not give place to the devil. Let the one who used to steal steal no longer; rather, let him labor, working with his hands at what is good, so that he may have something to give to one who suffers need.

Let no evil word proceed from your mouth, but only whatever is good for building up the faith, so that it may give grace to those who hear. And do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, in whom you were sealed for the day of redemption. Let all bitterness, anger, indignation, shouting, and blasphemy be taken away from you, together with all malice. Be kind and compassionate toward one another, forgiving one another, just as God in Christ forgave you.

**R.** Amen.

## Reading from the Book of Exodus (Chapter XXXIII)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

In those days the Lord spoke to Moses face to face, as a man is accustomed to speak with his friend. When he returned to the camp, his minister Joshua son of Nun, a young man, did not depart from the tabernacle.

Moses said to the Lord: “You command me to lead out this people, yet do not tell me whom you will send with me, especially since you have said: ‘I know you by name, and you have found favor before me.’ If, therefore, I have found favor in your sight, show me your face, that I may know you and find favor before your eyes. Look upon your people and this nation.”

The Lord said: “My face shall go before you, and I shall give you rest.” Moses said: “Unless you yourself go before us, do not lead us out from this place. For how shall it be known that I and your people have found favor in your sight, unless you walk with us, and we are glorified above all peoples who dwell upon the earth?”

The Lord said to Moses: “Behold, I shall do this thing also that you have spoken, for you have found favor before me, and I know you yourself by name.” He said: “Show me your glory.” The Lord answered: “I shall show you all good things, and I shall call upon the name of the Lord before you; I shall have mercy on whom I will, and I shall be gracious to whom it pleases me.”

Again he said: “You cannot see my face, for no human being shall see me and live.” And again he said: “Behold, there is a place beside me, and you shall stand upon the rock. When my glory passes by, I shall place you in a cleft of the rock and protect you with my right hand until I pass by. Then I shall take away my hand, and you shall see my back; but you cannot see my face.”

(Chapter XXXIV.) Rising by night, Moses went up Mount Sinai as the Lord had commanded him, carrying with him two tablets. When the Lord came down in a cloud, Moses stood with him, invoking the name of the Lord. As he passed before him, he said: “Lord God, ruler, merciful and gracious, patient and of great compassion, and true; you preserve mercy for thousands; you take away iniquity, wicked deeds, and sins, yet no one is innocent before you in himself; you repay the iniquity of fathers upon their children, to the third and fourth generation.”

Moses hastened, bowed prone to the earth, and worshipped, saying: “If I have found favor in your sight, Lord, I beg you to walk with us—for this is a stiff-necked people—so that you may take away our iniquities and sins and possess us.” The Lord answered: “Behold, I shall make a covenant: in the sight of all I shall perform signs never seen upon the earth or among any nations, so that the people in whose midst you are may see the fearful work of the Lord that I shall perform. Observe all that I command you today.”

**R.** Amen.

## Reading from the Book of the Prophet Jeremiah (Chapter V)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

This is what the Lord says: “Go through the streets of Jerusalem; look, consider, and seek in its squares whether you can find a man who does justice and seeks faithfulness, and I shall be gracious to it. Even when they say, ‘As the Lord lives,’ they swear falsely. Lord, your eyes look upon faithfulness: you struck them, and they did not grieve; you crushed them, and they refused to receive discipline. They hardened their faces beyond the earth and would not return.

“But I said: ‘Perhaps they are poor and foolish, ignorant of the way of the Lord and the judgment of their God. I shall go to the great and speak to them, for they know the way of the Lord and the judgment of their God.’ But behold, these all the more together broke the yoke and burst the bonds. Therefore the lion from the forest struck them, the wolf at evening laid them waste, and the leopard watches over their cities; everyone who goes out from them shall be taken, because their transgressions have multiplied and their turnings away have grown strong.

“For what reason can I be gracious to you? Your children have forsaken me and swear by those who are not gods. I fed them to the full, and they committed adultery and luxuriated in the house of a harlot. They became lustful horses and stallions for females; each one neighed after the wife of his neighbor. Shall I not visit these things, says the Lord? Shall my soul not take vengeance on such a nation? Go up upon her walls and destroy, but do not make a full end.”

**R.** Amen.

## Reading from the Book of Exodus (Chapter XXIV)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

In those days the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

“Go up to the Lord—you, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy elders of the elders of Israel—and you shall worship from a distance. Moses alone shall go up to the Lord; they shall not approach, and the people shall not go up with him.”

Moses came and recounted all the words of the Lord and all the judgments to the people. The whole people answered with one voice: “All the words that the Lord has spoken we shall do.”

Moses wrote down all the words of the Lord. Rising early the next morning, he built an altar at the foot of the mountain, with twelve pillars for the twelve tribes of Israel. They offered burnt offerings and sacrificed peace offerings to the Lord—young bulls.

Moses took half of the blood and put it in bowls; the other half he poured upon the altar. Then he took the book of the covenant and read it in the hearing of the people. They said: “All that the Lord has spoken we shall do, and we shall be obedient.”

Moses took the blood and sprinkled it upon the people, saying: “This is the blood of the covenant that the Lord has made with you concerning all these words.”

Then Moses and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel went up. They saw God, and beneath his feet there was something like a work of sapphire stone and like the sky when it is clear.

He did not lay his hand upon those who had withdrawn afar off among the children of Israel. They saw God, and they ate and drank.

The Lord said to Moses: “Go up to me on the mountain and remain there. I shall give you the stone tablets, the law and the commandments that I have written, so that you may teach them.”

Moses rose, with Joshua his servant, and Moses went up the mountain of God. He said to the elders: “Wait here until we return to you. You have Aaron and Hur with you; if any matter of dispute arises, bring it before them.”

When Moses had gone up, the cloud covered the mountain, and the glory of the Lord dwelt upon Sinai, covering it with the cloud for six days. On the seventh day he called to him from the midst of the darkness.

The appearance of the glory of the Lord was like a burning fire upon the summit of the mountain in the sight of the children of Israel. Moses entered into the midst of the cloud and went up the mountain. He remained there forty days and forty nights.

(Chapter XX of Leviticus.) And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: “Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: Keep my commandments and do them, and you shall know that I am the Lord who sanctifies you.”

**R.** Amen.

## The continuation of the Epistle of the Apostle Paul to the Hebrews (Chapter XIII)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

Brothers, Jesus, in order to sanctify the people through his own blood, suffered outside the gate. Let us therefore go out to him outside the camp, bearing his reproach. For we have no abiding city here, but we seek the one that is to come. Through him, therefore, let us continually offer a sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of lips confessing his name. Do not forget beneficence and fellowship, for with such sacrifices God is pleased. Obey your leaders and submit to them. For they keep watch, as those who must give an account of your souls, so that they may do this with joy and not with groaning; for that would not be profitable for you. Pray for us, for we are confident that we have a good conscience, wishing to conduct ourselves well in all things. But I appeal to you all the more to do this, so that I may be restored to you more quickly. Now may the God who brought back from the dead the great shepherd of the sheep, our Lord Jesus Christ, by the blood of the eternal covenant, equip you with every good thing, so that you may do his will, accomplishing in you what is pleasing in his sight through Jesus Christ; to him be honor and glory forever and ever. R. Amen.

## Reading from the Book of Ecclesiasticus of Solomon (Chapter 36)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

Have mercy on us, God of all, and look upon us, and show us the light of your mercies. Send your fear upon the nations that have not sought you, so that they may know that there is no God but you and may proclaim your mighty deeds. Lift up your hand over foreign nations, so that they may see your power. For just as you have been sanctified among us in their sight, so you will be magnified among them in our sight, so that they may know you, just as we also have known that there is no God besides you, O Lord. Pass over, renew, and change the wonders. In anger let the flame devour sinners, and let those who mistreat your people meet with destruction. Crush the heads of the leaders of the enemies who say, “There is no other besides us.” Gather all the tribes of Jacob, so that they may know that there is no God but you and may proclaim your mighty deeds; and take them as your inheritance, as from the beginning. Have mercy on your people, over whom your name has been invoked, and on Jacob, whom you made equal to your firstborn. Have mercy on the city of your sanctuary, Jerusalem, the city of your rest. Fill Zion with your unspeakable words, and your people with your glory. Give testimony that they are your creatures from the beginning, and raise up the proclamations that the former prophets spoke in your name. Give a reward to those who wait for you, and your prophets are found faithful; and hear the prayers of your servants. According to the blessing of your people, give to your people, and guide us in righteousness, so that all who dwell on the earth may know that you are God, the observer of the ages. R. Amen.

## Reading from the Book of Deuteronomy (Chapter 12)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

In those days Moses spoke to the whole assembly of the children of Israel and said to them: Observe and hear all that I command you, so that it may be well with you and with your children after you forever, when you do what is good and pleasing in the sight of the Lord your God. When the Lord your God has destroyed before your face the nations into whose land you are entering to possess it, and when you have taken possession of it and dwell in their land, beware lest you imitate them after they have been overthrown as you enter, and seek out their rites. Do not act similarly toward the Lord your God. Whatever I command you, that alone you shall do for the Lord; you shall neither add anything nor take anything away.

**Chapter 13.** Follow the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul, fear him, keep his commandments, and hear his voice. You shall serve him and cling to him, so that the Lord may turn away from the anger of his wrath and have mercy on you and multiply you, as he swore to your fathers. When you hear the voice of the Lord your God, keep all his commandments that I command you today, so that you may do what is pleasing in the sight of the Lord your God.

**Chapter 14.** Be faithful to the Lord your God. You shall not cut yourselves, nor make baldness for the dead, because you are a holy people to the Lord your God, and he chose you to be his special people from all the nations that are upon the earth. Give food to the sojourner who is within your gates, or sell it to him, because you are a holy people of the Lord your God. Learn to fear the Lord your God at all times, so that they may eat and be satisfied, and so that the Lord your God may bless you in all the works of your hands that you do.

**Chapter 15.** You shall not have the power to reclaim what belongs to your fellow citizen and kinsman. And there shall be no needy beggar among you, so that the Lord may bless you in the land that he is going to give you as a possession. Provided that you hear the voice of the Lord your God and keep all that is his, which I command you today, as you have promised, you will lend to many nations, but you yourself will borrow from none; you will rule over many nations, but no one will rule over you. Beware lest an ungodly thought perhaps steal upon you, lest you turn your eyes away from your poor brother and, unwilling to lend him what he requests, refuse him a loan; lest he cry out against you to the Lord and it become sin for you. Rather, you shall give to him, and you shall do nothing deceitfully in relieving his need, so that the Lord your God may bless you at all times, in everything to which you put your hand. The poor will not be lacking in the land of your dwelling; therefore I command you to open your hand to your needy and poor brother who lives with you in the land, so that the Lord your God may bless you in all your works. R. Amen.

## Reading from the Book of the Prophet Isaiah (Chapter 59)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

Behold, the hand of the Lord is not shortened so that it cannot save, nor is his ear burdened so that it cannot hear. But your iniquities had made a division between you and your God, and your sins had hidden his face from you, so that he would not hear. For your hands are defiled with blood, and your fingers with iniquity; your lips have spoken falsehood, and your tongue confesses iniquity. There is no one who calls for justice, nor anyone who judges truthfully; rather, they trust in nothingness and speak vanities. They have conceived labor and given birth to iniquity. They have broken the eggs of asps and woven spiders’ webs; whoever eats of their eggs will die, and what has been hatched from them will burst forth as a basilisk. Their webs will not become clothing, nor will they cover themselves with their garments. Their works are useless works; the work of iniquity is in their hands. Their feet run toward evil and hasten to shed innocent blood. Their thoughts are useless thoughts; devastation and destruction are in their ways. They have not known the way of peace, and there is no judgment in their footsteps. Their paths have been made crooked for them; everyone who treads upon them does not know peace.

Because of this, judgment is far from you, and justice does not reach you. We expected light, and behold, darkness; brightness, and we walked in darkness. We groped like the blind along a wall, and as though without eyes we felt our way. We stumbled at midday as though in darkness, and, gloomy as the dead, we roared like bears, all of us, and like doves we mournfully meditated. We expected judgment, and there was none; salvation, and it was far from us. For our iniquities have multiplied before you, and our sins have answered against us, because our crimes are with us, and we have known our iniquities: sinning and lying against the Lord, we have turned away so as not to follow behind our God; we have spoken slander and transgression. We conceived and spoke words of falsehood from the heart.

And judgment has turned backward, and justice has stood far away, because truth has fallen in the street, and equity could not enter. Truth has become forgotten, and whoever withdrew from evil was exposed to plunder. The Lord saw this, and it appeared evil in his eyes that there was no judgment. He saw that there was no man, and he was astonished because there was no one to intervene. Then his own holy arm saved him, and his justice itself strengthened him. R. Amen.

## Continuation of the Epistle of the Apostle Paul to the Galatians (Chapter 5)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

Brothers, the whole law is fulfilled in one saying: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.” But if you bite and devour one another, see that you are not consumed by one another. I say, then: Walk by the Spirit, and you will not fulfill the desires of the flesh. For the flesh desires against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh; for these oppose one another, so that you do not do whatever you wish. But if you are led by the Spirit, you are not under the law.

Now the works of the flesh are manifest: fornication, uncleanness, licentiousness, the service of idols, sorcery, enmities, quarrels, rivalries, anger, strife, dissensions, factions, envy, murders, drunkenness, revelries, and things like these. I warn you, as I warned you before, that those who do such things will not obtain the kingdom of God. But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, goodness, kindness, faith, and modesty. Against such things there is no law. Those who belong to Christ have crucified their flesh with its vices and desires. If we live by the Spirit, let us also walk by the Spirit. Let us not become desirous of empty glory, provoking and envying one another.

**Chapter 6.** Brothers, even if someone should be overtaken in some offense, you who are spiritual should restore such a person in a spirit of gentleness, considering yourself, lest you also be tempted. Bear one another’s burdens, and so you will fulfill the law of Christ. R. Amen.

**Antiphon 1.** Before you, O Lord, is all our desire, and our groaning is not hidden from you. For our heart has been troubled within us.  
**V.** Do not abandon me, O Lord my God; do not depart from me.  
**Psalm 37.**

[Col. 0737A]

**Prayer.** O Lord, all our desire is before you, and our groaning is not hidden from you. Therefore grant what we desire and forgive what we have done. At the same time grant fruit to our desires and pardon our sins. R. Amen.

Through.

**Antiphon 2.** Our soul has been humbled into the dust; our belly has clung to the earth. Arise—why do you sleep, O Lord? Arise, and do not reject us forever.  
**Psalm 43.**

**V.** We have heard with our ears, O God, and our fathers have declared it to us.

**Prayer.** O God, our King, who commands salvation for Jacob, overcome by the majesty of your name the assaults of the temptations that rise against us, and shatter by the strength of your arm the snares of the enemies who lie in wait. Since you know the secrets of the heart, wash away the stains of our conscience; make our faith firm in you; favorably regard our humility; and always rise up in our defense. R. Amen.

Through.

**Antiphon 3.** Hear, my people, and I will speak; Israel, and I will testify to you: I am God, your God. In tribulation you called upon me, and I delivered you; I heard you in the hidden place of the storm.  
**V.** The Lord, God of gods, has spoken and summoned the earth from the rising of the sun to its setting; from Zion, the perfection of his beauty.  
**Psalm 49.**

**R.** Guard our souls, O Lord, because you are holy. Save your people, O God, who hope in you. For you are gracious and gentle, and abundantly merciful—  
**P.** To those who call upon you.  
Hear our prayer with your ears.  
**V.** On the day of my tribulation I sought God; by night my hands were before him, and I was not deceived. My soul refused consolation.  
**V.** Protect this city, O Lord, and be a helper to your people, and deliver us from all the evils to which you have handed us.  
**V.** O Lord, you have become our refuge from generation to generation. Before the mountains were made, or the earth and the world were formed, from age to age and forever, you are.  
**V.** May God repay you in remembrance for the work of your hands; do not remember all our crimes against us. Act with us for the sake of your name.  
**V.** Glory and honor.

[Col. 0737D]

**Prayers.** Word of the Most High Father—  
**P.** Redeemer, have mercy on sinners.  
**V.** Blot out our crime, you who were handed over for us.  
**P.** Redeemer.  
**V.** Purify us from vices, you who were struck with blows.  
**P.** Redeemer.  
**V.** You who were given gall to drink for us, fill us with sweetness.  
**P.** Redeemer.  
**V.** Kindle us with the fire of your Cross, us whom you redeemed with blood.  
**P.** Redeemer.

**Prayer.** We call upon you, O Lord, in the day of tribulation, so that you may rescue us and make us grow through the nourishment of faith, so that what we advance in mind may serve you, and the practice of our action may be praise of your name forever.

**Our Father.** Deliver us from evil. Folio 10.

**Blessing.** Seek the one that is said in Terce throughout the year.

## At Sext

[Col. 0738A]

**Prophecy.** O Lord, have mercy on us. Folio 434.

**Antiphon 1.** Hear, O Lord, the supplication of your people and the prayers of all who pray in this place; O God, hear from heaven.  
**V.** For you, O Lord, are gracious and gentle, and abundantly merciful to those who call upon you.  
**Psalm 85.**

**Prayer.** Save us, your servants, O Lord our God, who hope in you, because you are gracious and gentle and abundantly merciful. Look upon us and have mercy on us, so that our heart may rejoice in the greatness of your name; may it fear you, so that it may rejoice. Lead us in your way, and as we walk in your truth, comfort us with your help, and help us by comforting us. R. Amen.

Through.

[Col. 0738B]

**Antiphon 2.** You are for us, O Lord, a refuge from the oppression that surrounds us, for the scourges of our sins are many.  
**V.** Blessed are those whose iniquities are forgiven and whose sins are covered.  
**Psalm 31.**

**Prayer.** Grant us forgiveness of sins, O Lord, you who grant blessedness to the purified. Be a refuge from the oppression of condemnation, you who grant freedom. And because many scourges of sins rage within us as the blow falls, let us feel, by trusting in you, that your mercy surrounds us. R. Amen.

Through.

**Antiphon 3.** Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy, for we are exceedingly filled with contempt.  
**V.** To you we raise our eyes, who dwell in the heavens.  
**Psalm 122.**

**R.** There is no God besides you, O Lord. Renew the signs and change the wonders. Have mercy on your people, over whom your name has been invoked. Have mercy on the city of your sanctuary. Fill Zion with your unspeakable words, and the people for your glory.  
**V.** You, O Lord our God, are gracious and gentle, patient and ordering all things with complete mercy. And if we have sinned against you, we are yours, awaiting your mercy.  
**V.** Both those born of the earth and the children of human beings, rich and poor together as one.  
**V.** Hear, O Lord; be appeased, O Lord; attend and act. Do not delay for your own sake, my God.  
**V.** We acknowledge our sins, O Lord, and the iniquities of our fathers. We have sinned before you; spare us, O Lord.  
**V.** Have mercy, God of all, because you can do all things and overlook human sins for the sake of repentance.  
**V.** You, O Lord of hosts, judge with tranquility and order all things with great reverence.  
**V.** I am God; walk before me and be perfect, so that you may possess the land of your inheritance.  
**V.** I am, and my covenant is with me, says the Lord. Turn back to me and mourn, and I will quickly console you.  
**V.** Glory and honor.

Let the response be repeated: There is no God.

**Prayers.** Those whom you redeemed with blood—  
**P.** Save by your power, merciful Christ.  
**V.** For whom you were scourged and led away,  
**P.** By your power.  
**V.** For whose crime, Most Merciful, you were fastened to the cross,  
**P.** By your power.  
**V.** For whom you were beaten and struck on the head,  
**P.** By your power.  
**V.** We who weeping disclose our evils to you,  
**P.** Save by your power.

**Prayer.** Have mercy on us, O Lord; grant the help sought by our expectation, so that we, who are filled with the contempt of the proud, may be fortified by the help of your defense.

[Col. 0739]

# PSALTERIUM (C)

## IN THE NAME OF THE LORD, HERE BEGINS THE FIRST BOOK OF THE PSALMS ACCORDING TO DAVID THE PROPHET

## HERE BEGINS THE FIRST PSALM

Prophecy concerning the Lord Jesus Christ, or concerning the fruit of the righteous and the destruction of the wicked.

[Col. 0739B]

### I

**Antiphon.** His delight was in the law of the Lord, by day and by night he will meditate on his law.

Blessed is the man who has not gone in the counsel of the ungodly, nor stood in the way of sinners; he has not sat in the seat of pestilence.

But his delight was in the law of the Lord, and on his law he will meditate by day and by night.

And he will be like a tree that has been planted beside the courses of waters.

It will give its fruit in its season, and its leaf will not fall; and everything that he does will prosper.

[Col. 0739C]

Not so the wicked, not so; but they are like dust that the wind casts away from the face of the earth.

Therefore the wicked do not rise in judgment, nor sinners in the assembly of the righteous.

For the Lord knows the way of the righteous, but the path of the wicked will perish.

### II. To the victor. A psalm of David.

**Antiphon.** Now understand, O kings; be instructed, all you who judge the earth. Serve the Lord in fear.

Why did the nations rage, and the peoples meditate on empty things?

The kings of the earth stood up, and the rulers gathered together against the Lord and against his Christ.

Let us break their bonds and cast their yoke away from us.

He who dwells in the heavens will mock them, and the Lord will deride them.

Then he will speak to them in his anger, and in his fury he will trouble them.

**Diapsalma.**

But I have been appointed king by him over Zion, his holy mountain, proclaiming the commandment of the Lord.

The Lord said to me: You are my Son; today I have begotten you.

[Col. 0740B]

Ask of me, and I will give you the nations as your inheritance, and the ends of the earth as your possession.

You will rule them with an iron rod, and like a potter’s vessel you will shatter them.

And now understand, O kings; be instructed, all you who judge the earth.

Serve the Lord in fear, and rejoice in him with trembling.

Embrace discipline, lest the Lord become angry at some time and you perish from the righteous way.

When his anger is kindled in a brief moment, blessed are all who trust in him.

### III. A psalm of David, when he fled from the face of Absalom his son.

O Lord, why have those who trouble me become so numerous? Many rise up against me.

Many say to my soul: There is no salvation for him in his God.

**Diapsalma.**

But you, O Lord, are my protector, my glory, and the one who lifts up my head.

With my voice I cried to the Lord, and he heard me from his holy mountain.

**Diapsalma.**

I slept, and rested, and rose again, because the Lord will raise me up.

I will not fear thousands of people surrounding me.

Arise, O Lord; save me, my God.

For you have struck all those who oppose me without cause; you have crushed the teeth of sinners.

Salvation belongs to the Lord, and your blessing is upon your people.

### IV. To the victor, with stringed instruments. A song of David.

**Antiphon.** When I called upon you, you heard me; God of my righteousness, you delivered me.

When I called upon you, you heard me, God of my righteousness; in tribulation you enlarged me.

Have mercy on me, O Lord, and hear my prayer.

Children of men, how long will you be heavy of heart? Why do you love vanity and seek falsehood?

[Col. 0741A]

**Diapsalma.**

Know that the Lord has made his holy one wonderful; the Lord will hear me when I cry to him.

Be angry, and do not sin; what you say in your hearts, and on your beds, be compunctionate.

**Diapsalma.**

Offer the sacrifice of righteousness and hope in the Lord. Many say: Who will show us good things?

The light of your face, O Lord, has been marked upon us; you have given gladness in my heart.

They have multiplied since the time of their grain, wine, and oil.

In peace, at the same time, I will sleep and rest, because you, O Lord, have established me uniquely in hope.

### V. To the victor, for inheritances. A song of David.

**Antiphon.** In the morning you will hear my voice, O Lord; in the morning I will stand before you and worship you.

Give ear to my words, O Lord; understand my cry; attend to the voice of my prayer,

my King and my God, for to you I will pray, O Lord.

In the morning you will hear my voice; in the morning I will stand before you, and I will see you.

For you are a God who does not will iniquity; the wicked will not dwell beside you, nor will the unjust remain before your eyes.

[Col. 0741C]

You hate, O Lord, all who work iniquity; you will destroy those who speak falsehood.

The Lord will abominate a man of blood and deceit. But I will hope in the abundance of your mercy. I will enter your house; I will worship toward your holy temple in your fear.

O Lord, lead me in your righteousness because of my enemies; direct my way before your sight.

For there is no truth in their mouth; their heart is vain.

Their throat is an open tomb; they dealt deceitfully with their tongues.

Judge them, O God; let them fall by their own counsels.

Drive them out according to the multitude of their ungodliness, for they have provoked you, O Lord.

[Col. 0741D]

Let all who hope in you rejoice; they will exult forever, and you will dwell in them. All who love your name will glory in you.

For you will bless the righteous, O Lord; O Lord, as with a shield of good will you have crowned us.

### VI. To the victor, with stringed instruments, concerning the eighth. A song of David.

**Antiphon.** Do not rebuke me, O Lord, in your anger.

O Lord, do not rebuke me in your anger, nor correct me in your fury.

Have mercy on me, O Lord, for I am weak; heal me, O Lord.

For my bones have been troubled, and my soul has been greatly troubled.

And you, O Lord, how long? Turn back and rescue my soul; save me for the sake of your mercy.

For in death there is no one who remembers you; and in the underworld, who will confess to you?

I labor in my groaning; every night I wash my bed; I water my couch with tears.

My eye is troubled because of anger; I have grown old among all my enemies.

Depart from me, all you who work iniquity, for the Lord has heard the voice of my weeping.

The Lord has heard my supplication; the Lord has received my prayer.

Let all my enemies be ashamed and confounded; let them turn backward and be very quickly confounded.

### VII. A psalm of David, which he sang to the Lord concerning the words of Cushi, the son of Jemini.

[Col. 0742B]

**Antiphon.** My just help is from the Lord, who saves the upright of heart.

O Lord my God, I have hoped in you; deliver me from all those who pursue me, and rescue me.

Lest at some time he seize my soul like a lion, while there is no one to redeem and no one to save.

[III] O Lord my God, if I have done this, if there is iniquity in my hands, if I have repaid those who requited me with evils, may I justly fall empty before my enemies.

May the enemy pursue my soul and seize it, and trample my life into the earth, and bring my glory down into the dust.

**Diapsalma.**

Arise, O Lord, in your anger; rise up at the boundaries of my enemies.

Arise, O Lord my God, according to the command that you gave; the assembly of peoples will surround you, and for its sake return on high, O Lord.

Judge the peoples; judge me, O Lord; save me according to my righteousness and according to the innocence of my hands upon me.

Let the wickedness of sinners be brought to an end, and direct the righteous, you who scrutinize hearts and reins, O God.

My just help is from the Lord, who saves the upright of heart.

God is a just, strong, and patient judge. Is he angry every day?

Unless you turn back, he will brandish his sword; he has bent his bow and prepared it.

And in it he has prepared the instruments of death; he has made his arrows burning.

Behold, iniquity is in labor; it has conceived pain and given birth to wickedness.

He opened a pit and dug it, and he fell into the pit that he himself made.

His pain will return upon his head, and his iniquity will descend upon his crown.

I will confess to the Lord according to his righteousness, and I will sing psalms to the name of the Most High Lord.

### VIII. To the victor, concerning the winepresses. A psalm of David.

**Antiphon.** How wonderful is your name, O Lord, throughout the whole earth.

[Col. 0743A]

O Lord, our Lord, how wonderful is your name throughout the whole earth.

For your magnificence has been exalted above the heavens; from the mouth of infants and nursing children you have perfected praise.

Because of your enemies, so that you may destroy the enemy and the defender.

For I will see the heavens, the works of your fingers; the moon and the stars that you established.

What is man, that you remember him, or the son of man, that you visit him?

You made him a little lower than the angels; you crowned him with glory and honor, and appointed him over the works of your hands.

You subjected all things beneath his feet: sheep and oxen,

[Col. 0743B]

and all the animals of the field besides,

the birds of the heavens and the fish of the sea, which travel along the paths of the sea.

O Lord, our Lord, how wonderful is your name throughout the whole earth.

### IX. To the victor, for the death of the son. A song of David.

**Antiphon.** I will rejoice and exult in you, and I will sing to your name, O Most High.

I will confess to you, O Lord, with all my heart; I will recount all your wonders.

I will rejoice and exult in you, and I will sing to your name, O Most High.

When my enemy turns backward, they will grow weak and perish before your face.

[Col. 0743C]

For you have made my judgment and my cause; you sit upon the throne, judging equity.

You rebuked the nations, and the wicked perished; you blotted out their name forever and ever.

The swords of the enemies have failed completely; you destroyed their cities.

Their memory has perished with a sound, but the Lord remains forever.

He will prepare his throne for judgment, and he himself will judge the world in equity.

He will judge the peoples with justice, and the Lord has become a refuge for the poor, a helper in times of opportunity and in tribulation.

And let all who know your name hope in you, for you do not abandon those who seek you, O Lord.

Sing psalms to the Lord who dwells in Zion; proclaim his wonders among the nations.

For, when seeking their blood, he remembered it, and he did not forget the prayer of the poor.

Have mercy on me, O Lord, and see my humiliation before my enemies, you who lift me up from the gates of death, so that I may proclaim all your praises at the gates of the daughter of Zion; I will exult in your salvation.

The nations are fixed in the destruction that they made; their foot has been caught in the snare that they hid.

The Lord is known by executing judgments; the sinner has been caught in the works of his hands.

Let sinners turn back—all the nations [IV] that forget the Lord—to the underworld.

For the poor will not be forgotten forever; the patience of the poor will not perish forever.

**Antiphon.** To you the poor man is abandoned; you will be the helper of the orphan.

Arise, O Lord; let man not prevail. Let the nations be judged in your sight.

Appoint, O Lord, a lawgiver over them, so that the nations may know that they are human.

**Diapsalma.**

Why, O Lord, have you withdrawn far away? Why do you despise us in times of opportunity, in tribulation?

[Col. 0744B]

In the pride of the wicked the poor is set on fire; they are caught in the thoughts that they devise.

For the sinner is praised in the desires of his soul, and the one who acts wickedly will be blessed.

The sinner has provoked the Lord; according to the multitude of his anger he will seek.

God is not before his eyes; his ways are defiled at all times.

Your judgments are removed from his sight; he will dominate all his enemies.

For he said in his heart: I shall not be moved, from generation to generation, without evil.

His mouth is full of cursing, bitterness, and deceit; beneath his tongue are labor and pain.

He sits in ambush with the rich in secret places, so that he may kill the innocent; his eyes look upon the poor.

He lies in wait in secret places, like a lion in his lair; he lies in wait to seize the poor, to snatch the poor.

Until he brings him down in his own scheme, and humbles him in his snare * he will bow down, and fall, when he has gained power over the poor.

For he said in his heart: “God has forgotten; he has turned away his face, so that he may not see unto the end.”

Arise, Lord my God, and let your hand be exalted * do not forget the poor forever.

Why has the wicked provoked God? * For he said in his heart: “God will not require an account.”

You see, for you consider labor and sorrow * to deliver him into your hands.

[Col. 0744D] The poor man is left to you * you will be the helper of the orphan.

Break the arms of the sinner and the wicked * his offense will be sought, and it will not be found.

The Lord will reign forever and ever * you will destroy the nations from his land.

The Lord will hear the desire of the poor * your ear will hear the prayers of their heart.

To judge the orphan and the humble, * so that man may no longer presume to exalt himself upon the earth.

## X. For the end. A psalm of David.

**Antiphon.** For the Lord is just, and has loved justice; his face has looked upon equity.

[Col. 0745A] In the Lord I trust * how can you say to my soul: “Flee to the mountain like a sparrow”?

For behold, sinners have bent the bow * they have prepared their arrows in the quiver, to shoot in darkness at the upright in heart.

For what you established, they have destroyed; * but what has the just man done?

The Lord is in his holy temple * the Lord’s throne is in heaven. His eyes look upon the poor.

His eyelids examine the children of men. The Lord examines the just and the wicked; * but whoever loves iniquity hates his own soul.

He will rain snares of fire upon sinners * sulfur and the spirit of storms are the portion of their cup.

For the Lord is just, and has loved justice * [Col. 0745B] his face has looked upon equity.

## XI. For the eighth. A psalm of David.

**Antiphon.** Because of the misery of the needy and the groaning of the poor, now I will arise, says the Lord.

Save me, Lord, for the holy one has failed * for truths have diminished among the children of men.

Each has spoken vanity to his neighbor * with deceitful lips; in heart and from heart they have spoken evils.

May the Lord destroy all deceitful lips * and the tongue that speaks great things.

They said: “With our tongue we will prevail; * our lips are our own: who is our lord?”

Because of the misery of the needy and the groaning of the poor * now I will arise, says the Lord.

“I will place him upon my salvation; * I will act confidently toward him.”

The sayings of the Lord are pure sayings * silver tested by fire, purified of earth sevenfold.

You, Lord, will preserve us and guard us from this generation * forever.

The wicked walk around * according to your exaltation you have multiplied the children of men.

## XII. For the end. A psalm of David.

[V] **Antiphon.** My heart will rejoice in your salvation; I will sing to the Lord, [Col. 0745D] who has dealt bountifully with me.

How long, Lord, will you forget me forever? * How long will you turn your face away from me?

How long shall I set counsel in my soul, * sorrow in my heart throughout the day?

How long will my enemy be exalted * over me?

Look upon me and hear me, Lord my God * enlighten my eyes, lest I ever sleep in death,

lest my enemy say: * “I have prevailed against him.”

Those who trouble me will rejoice if I am shaken * but I will hope in your mercy.

My heart will rejoice in your salvation * I will sing to the Lord, [Col. 0746A] who has dealt bountifully with me, and I will sing praises to the name of the Most High Lord.

## XIII. For the end. A psalm of David.

**Antiphon.** The fool said in his heart: “There is no God.” You are our God?

The fool said in his heart: * “There is no God.”

They have been corrupted and have become abominable in their pleasures * there is none who does good, not even one.

The Lord looked down from heaven upon the children of men * to see whether there was anyone with understanding, or seeking God.

All have turned aside; together they have become useless in their pleasures: * there is none who does good, not even one.

[Col. 0746B] Their throat is an open tomb * they acted deceitfully with their tongues.

The poison of asps is under their lips * their mouth is full of cursing and bitterness.

Their feet are swift to shed blood; destruction and misery are in their ways, and they have not known the way of peace * there is no fear of God before their eyes.

Will all who practice iniquity not know this,

those who devour my people as though eating bread? They have not called upon the Lord * there they trembled with fear where there was no fear.

For the Lord is with the righteous generation * you have confounded the counsel of the poor, because God is his hope.

[Col. 0746C] Who will grant salvation to Israel from Zion? * When the Lord turns back the captivity of his people, may Jacob rejoice and Israel exult.

## XIV. A psalm of David.

**Antiphon.** Lord, who will dwell in your tabernacle, or who will rest upon your holy mountain?

Lord, who will dwell in your tabernacle? * Or who will rest upon your holy mountain?

The one who walks without blemish and practices righteousness; who speaks truth in his heart and has not acted deceitfully with his tongue; who has done no evil to his neighbor and has not accepted reproach against his neighbor * in his sight the wicked is brought to nothing; but he glorifies those who fear the Lord.

[Col. 0746D] The one who swears to his neighbor and does not deceive him * who has not lent his money at interest and has not accepted gifts against the innocent.

The one who does these things * will not be shaken forever.

## XV. With the title of the inscription. A psalm of David.

**Antiphon.** I said to the Lord: “You are my God.”

Preserve me, Lord, for I have hoped in you. I said to the Lord: * “You are my God, for you have no need of my goods.”

To the saints who are in his land, he has made all his wills wonderful among them.

Their infirmities have been multiplied * afterward they hastened after you.

[Col. 0747A] I will not gather their assemblies from bloods * nor will I remember their names with my lips.

The Lord is the portion of my inheritance and my cup * you are the one who restored my inheritance to me.

The measuring lines have fallen for me in splendid places * indeed, my inheritance is splendid to me.

I will bless the Lord, who has given me understanding * moreover, even until night my kidneys have admonished me.

I foresaw the Lord always before me * because he is at my right hand, I shall never be shaken.

Therefore my heart rejoiced, and my tongue will exult * moreover, my flesh also will rest in hope.

For you will not abandon my soul to the underworld [Col. 0747B] * nor will you allow your holy one to see corruption.

You have made known to me the paths of life * you will fill me with joy in your presence; delights are at your right hand forever.

## XVI. For the end. A prayer of David himself.

[VI] **Antiphon.** Hear, God, my justice; attend to my prayer; listen with your ears, Lord, to my prayer.

Hear, God, my justice; attend to my prayer; * listen with your ears to my prayer, and not to deceitful lips.

Let my judgment proceed from your presence * let my eyes see equity.

[Col. 0747C] You have tested my heart and visited me * you examined me with fire by night, and no iniquity was found in me.

So that my mouth may not speak of the works of men * because of the words of your lips I have kept to difficult ways.

Perfect my steps in your paths * so that my footsteps may not be shaken.

I cried out, because you heard me, God * incline your ear to me and hear my words.

Make your mercies wondrous, you who save those who hope in you * from those who resist your right hand.

**Antiphon.** Guard me, Lord, as the apple of the eye; protect me beneath the shadow of your wings.

From the face of the wicked who have afflicted me: my enemies have surrounded my soul * they have shut me in with their fat; their mouth has spoken pride.

[Col. 0747D] Casting me down, they have now surrounded me * they have fixed their eyes on bending toward the earth.

They have seized me like a lion prepared for prey * and like a lion’s cub dwelling in hiding places.

Arise, Lord, go before them and overthrow them * rescue my soul from the wicked, your sword from the hand of my enemies.

Lord, separate them from the few upon the earth * and supplant them in their lifetime.

Their belly has been filled from your hidden treasures * they have been satisfied with desires, and they have left what remained to their little ones.

But I will appear in righteousness before your presence * I will be satisfied when your glory is revealed.

## XVII. For the victor, servant of the Lord, David, who spoke to the Lord the words of this song on the day when the Lord delivered him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul, and he said:

[Col. 0748A]

**Antiphon.** My strength: I will love you, Lord, my fortress.

I will love you, Lord * my strength.

The Lord is my fortress and my refuge * and my deliverer.

My God is my helper, and I will hope in him * my protector, the horn of my salvation, and my redeemer.

Praising, I will call upon the Lord * and I shall be saved from my enemies.

[Col. 0748B] The pangs of death surrounded me * and torrents of iniquity troubled me.

The sorrows of the underworld found me * the snares of death overtook me.

In my tribulation I called upon the Lord * and I cried out to my God.

He heard my voice from his holy temple * my cry came into his presence and entered his ears.

He looked, and the earth was shaken and trembled * the foundations of the mountains were troubled and shaken, because God was angry with it.

Smoke rose in his anger * and fire blazed from his face.

Coals were kindled by him; he inclined the heavens, [Col. 0748C] and descended * and darkness was beneath his feet.

He ascended upon the cherubim * and flew.

He flew upon the wings of the winds, and made darkness his hiding place * his tent was around him: dark water in the clouds of the air.

From the brightness before him the clouds passed by * hail and fiery coals.

The Lord thundered from heaven * and the Most High gave his voice.

He sent his arrows and scattered them * he multiplied lightning and troubled them.

And the springs of waters appeared * and the foundations of the world were revealed.

At your rebuke, Lord * and at the breath of the spirit of your wrath.

[Col. 0748D] He sent from on high, took me, and drew me out from the multitude of waters * he rescued me, because he desired me.

He delivered me from my strongest enemies * and from those who hated me, because they had grown too strong against me.

They overtook me on the day of my affliction * and the Lord became my protector.

He brought me out into a spacious place * he rescued me, because he desired me.

He delivered me from my powerful enemies * and rescued me from those rising up against me.

The Lord repaid me according to my righteousness * and according to the innocence of my hands he repaid me.

[Col. 0749A] [VII] For I have kept the ways of the Lord * and I have not acted wickedly against my God.

For all his judgments are always before my eyes * and I have not rejected his righteous statutes from me.

And I shall be blameless before him * and I shall guard myself from my iniquity.

The Lord repaid me according to my righteousness * and according to the innocence of my hands before his eyes.

With the holy you will be holy; with the innocent man you will be innocent * with the chosen you will be chosen, and with the perverse you will overthrow.

For you will save the humble people * but you will humble the eyes of the proud.

**Antiphon.** Who is God besides the Lord, or who is God besides our God? God who girded me with strength.

For you enlighten my lamp, Lord * my God, enlighten my darkness.

For by you I will be rescued from temptation * and in my God I will leap over a wall.

My God, his way is undefiled; the sayings of the Lord are tested by fire * he is the protector of all who hope in him.

For who is God besides the Lord * or who is God besides our God?

God who girded me with strength * and made my way blameless.

He makes my feet like those of a deer * and sets me upon high places.

He teaches my hands for battle * you have made my arms like a bronze bow.

You have given me the protection of your salvation * and your right hand, God, has received me; your discipline itself will teach me, and your instruction will guide me to the end.

You have widened my steps beneath me * and my footsteps have not been weakened.

I will pursue my enemies and overtake them; I will not turn back until they fail * I will afflict them, and they will not be able to stand; they will fall beneath my feet.

You girded me with strength for battle * you have cast down beneath me all who rise up against me.

You gave me the backs of my enemies * and you destroyed those who hated me.

[Col. 0749D] They cried out, but there was no one to save them, to the Lord * and he did not hear them.

I will crush them like dust before the face of the wind * like the mud of the streets I will wipe them away.

You will rescue me from the disputes of the people * you will establish me as head of the nations.

A people whom I did not know served me * at the hearing of the ear they obeyed me.

Foreign sons lied to me * foreign sons grew old and limped away from their paths.

The Lord lives, and blessed is my God * and exalted is the God of my salvation.

God, who gives me vengeance * and has subjected peoples beneath me.

My deliverer, the Lord, from angry nations, and [Col. 0750A] from those rising up against me—you will exalt me * you will rescue me from the unjust man.

Therefore I will confess to you among the peoples, Lord * I will sing a psalm to your name.
