Magnifying the salvation of his king and showing mercy to his anointed, David * and to his offspring forever.

## XVIII. For the victor. A song of David.

**Antiphon.** The commandment of the Lord is bright, enlightening the eyes.

The heavens declare the glory of God * and the firmament proclaims the work of his hands.

Day pours forth the word to day * and night declares knowledge to night.

[Col. 0750B] There are no speeches or words * whose voices are not heard.

Their sound has gone out into all the earth * and their words to the ends of the world.

He placed his tabernacle in the sun * and he himself, like a bridegroom coming forth from his chamber.

He will exult like a giant to run the way: his going forth is from the highest heaven * and his course reaches to its highest point; there is no one who can hide from his heat.

The law of the Lord is blameless, converting souls * the testimony of God is faithful, giving wisdom to the simple.

The Lord’s righteous statutes are right, gladdening hearts * the commandment of the Lord is bright, enlightening the eyes.

The fear of the Lord is holy, enduring forever and ever [Col. 0750C] * the judgments of God are true, justified in themselves.

More desirable than gold and many precious stones * and sweeter than honey and the honeycomb.

Indeed, your servant keeps them * in keeping them there is great reward.

Who understands offenses? * Cleanse me, Lord, from my hidden faults, and spare your servant from those of others.

If they do not dominate me, then I shall be blameless * and I shall be cleansed from the greatest offense.

[VIII] And the words of my mouth will be pleasing * and the meditation of my heart will always be in your presence.

Lord, my helper * and my redeemer.

## XIX. For the victor. A song of David.

**Antiphon.** May the name of the God of Jacob protect you; may he send you help from the sanctuary, and may he guard you from Zion.

May the Lord hear you on the day of tribulation * may the name of the God of Jacob protect you.

May he send you help from the sanctuary * and guard you from Zion.

May he remember all your sacrifice * and may your burnt offering be made fat.

Diapsalma.

May the Lord grant you according to your heart * and confirm all your counsel.

We will rejoice in your salvation * and in the name of the Lord our God we will magnify ourselves.

May the Lord fulfill all your petitions. Now I know that the Lord will save his anointed [Col. 0751A] and will hear him from his holy heaven * salvation is in the powers of his right hand.

Some trust in chariots and horses * but we will magnify ourselves in the name of the Lord our God.

They were bound and fell * but we have risen and stand upright.

Lord, save the king * and hear us on whatever day we call upon you.

## XX. For the end. A psalm of David.

**Antiphon.** Be exalted, Lord, in your strength; we will sing and praise your powers.

Lord, in your strength the king will rejoice * and he will exult greatly in your salvation.

You granted him the desire of his soul * and you did not deprive him of the prayer of his lips.

For you went before him with the blessing of sweetness * you placed a crown of precious stone upon his head.

He asked for life, and you gave it to him * length of days forever and ever.

Great is his glory in your salvation * you will place glory and great beauty upon him.

For you will make him a blessing forever and ever * you will gladden him with joy in your presence.

For the king will hope in the Lord * and through the mercy of the Most High he will not be shaken.

Let your hand be found by all your enemies * let your right hand find all who hate you.

[Col. 0751C] You will place them like a furnace of fire * at the time of your presence.

The Lord will trouble them in his anger * and fire will devour them.

You will destroy their fruit from the earth * and their offspring from the children of men.

For they turned evil things against you * they devised a plan that they could not establish.

For you will place them below * and in your remnants you will prepare their face.

Be exalted, Lord, in your strength * we will sing and praise your powers.

## XXI. For the end, at the morning reception. A psalm of David.

**Antiphon.** God, my God, look upon me, and do not abandon me.

[Col. 0751D] My God, my God, look upon me; why have you abandoned me? * The words of my offenses are far from my salvation.

My God, I will cry out by day, and you will not hear * and by night, yet it will not be foolishness for me.

But you dwell in the holy place, the praise of Israel * in you our fathers hoped; they hoped, and you delivered them.

They cried out to you and were saved * they hoped in you and were not confounded.

But I am a worm and not a man * the reproach of men and the outcast of the people.

All who saw me mocked me * they spoke with their lips and shook their heads.

He hoped in the Lord; let him rescue him * let him save him, because he desires him.

[Col. 0752A] For you are the one who brought me out of the womb * my hope from my mother’s breasts.

Upon you I was cast from the womb; from my mother’s belly you are my God * do not depart from me, for tribulation is near, and there is no one to help.

Many calves surrounded me * fat bulls besieged me.

They opened their mouths against me * like a lion rending and roaring.

I was poured out like water * and all my bones were scattered.

My heart became like melting wax * in the midst of my belly.

My strength dried up like a potsherd, and my tongue clung to my jaws * and they brought me down into the dust of death [Col. 0752B].

For many dogs surrounded me * the assembly of the wicked besieged me.

They pierced my hands and my feet * and they counted all my bones.

[IX] But they themselves considered and looked upon me * they divided my garments among themselves, and cast lots for my clothing.

But you, Lord, do not keep your help far from me * look to my defense.

Rescue my soul from the sword * and my only one from the hand of the dog.

Deliver me from the lion’s mouth * and my humility from the horns of the unicorns.

**Antiphon.** I will proclaim your name to my brothers; in the midst of the Church I will praise you, Lord.

You who fear the Lord, praise him * all the offspring of Jacob, glorify him.

Let all the offspring of Israel fear him * because he has neither despised nor disdained the prayers of the poor.

Nor has he turned his face away from me * and when I cried to him, he heard me.

With you is my praise in the great Church * I will fulfill my vows before those who fear him.

The poor will eat and be satisfied; and those who seek him will praise the Lord * their hearts live forever and ever.

All the ends of the earth will remember and turn to the Lord * and all the families of the nations will worship in his presence [Col. 0752D].

For the kingdom is the Lord’s * and he himself will rule the nations.

All the wealthy of the people will eat and worship in his presence * all who descend to the earth will proceed.

And my soul will live for him * and my offspring will serve him.

The coming generation will be announced to the Lord * and the heavens will proclaim his righteousness to the people who will be born, whom the Lord has made.

## XXII. For the end. A psalm of David.

**Antiphon.** Even if I walk in the midst of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for you are with me, God.

[Col. 0753A] The Lord governs me, and I shall lack nothing * and in a green place he will settle me there.

He will teach me beside the water of refreshment * there he restores my soul.

He led me upon the path of righteousness * for his name’s sake.

For even if I walk in the midst of the shadow of death * I will fear no evil, for you are with me.

Your rod and your staff * they themselves have comforted me.

You have prepared a table before me * against those who trouble me.

You have anointed my head with oil * and your cup, making drunk—how splendid it is.

And may your mercy follow me all the days of my life * so that I may dwell in the house of the Lord for length of days [Col. 0753B].

## XXIII. For the end. A psalm of David himself. First of the Sabbath.

**Antiphon.** He established it upon the seas and prepared it upon the rivers.

The earth is the Lord’s, and its fullness * the world and all who dwell in it.

He established it upon the seas * and prepared it upon the rivers.

Who ascends the mountain of the Lord, or who will stand in his holy place? * The innocent in hands and pure in heart.

The one who has not received his soul in vain * and has not sworn deceitfully to his neighbor.

This one will receive blessing from the Lord * and mercy [Col. 0753C] from God his savior.

This is the generation of those who seek the Lord * of those seeking the face of the God of Jacob.

Lift up your gates, O princes, and be lifted up, eternal gates * and the King of glory will enter.

Who is this King of glory? * The Lord, strong and mighty, the Lord mighty in battle.

Lift up your gates, O princes, and be lifted up, eternal gates * and the King of glory will enter.

Who is this King of glory? * He is the King of glory of hosts.

## XXIV. For the end. A psalm of David himself.

**Antiphon.** My God, in you I trust; I shall not be ashamed.

To you, Lord, I have lifted up my soul * my God, in you I trust; I shall not be ashamed.

Nor may my enemies mock me * for all who wait for you will not be confounded.

Let the unjust be confounded * those who act vainly.

Make your ways known to me, Lord * and teach me your paths.

Guide me in your truth and teach me * for you are God my savior, and I have waited for you all day.

Remember your mercies, Lord * and your mercies, which have been from eternity.

Do not remember the offenses of my youth and my ignorance * according to your great mercy remember me.

For the sake of your goodness, Lord, because the Lord is sweet and upright [Col. 0754A] * for this reason he established a law for sinners on the way.

[X] He will guide the meek in judgment * he will teach the humble his ways.

All the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth * for those who seek his covenant and his testimonies.

For your name’s sake, Lord, you will be merciful to my sin * for it is great.

Who is the man who fears the Lord? * He established a law for him on the way he chose.

His soul will dwell among good things * and his offspring will possess the land as an inheritance.

The Lord is a firmament for those who fear him * and his covenant, so that it may be revealed to him.

My eyes are always toward the Lord * because he will draw my feet out of the snare [Col. 0754B].

Look upon me and have mercy on me * for I am alone and poor.

The tribulations of my heart have been multiplied * rescue me from my necessities.

See my humility and my labor * and forgive all my sins.

Look upon my enemies, for they have been multiplied * and they hate me with unjust hatred.

Guard my soul and rescue me * Lord, I shall not be confounded, because I have called upon you.

The innocent and upright have adhered to me * because I have waited for you, Lord.

Redeem Israel, O God * from all his afflictions.

## XXV. A psalm of David himself.

[Col. 0754C]

**Antiphon.** Lord, I have loved the beauty of your house and the place of the glory of your majesty.

Judge me, Lord, for I have entered in my innocence * and, hoping in God, I shall not be weakened.

Test me, Lord, and try me * burn my kidneys and my heart.

For your mercy is before my eyes * and I have pleased you in truth.

I have not sat in the council of vanity * and I will not enter with those who act unjustly.

I have hated the assemblies of the wicked [Col. 0754D] * and I will not sit with the impious.

I will wash my hands among the innocent * and I will surround your altar, Lord.

So that I may hear the voice of your praise * and recount all your wonders.

Lord, I have loved the beauty of your house * and the place of the dwelling of your glory.

Do not destroy my soul with the impious * nor my life with men of blood.

In whose hands are iniquities * and whose right hand is filled with gifts.

But I have entered in my innocence * redeem me and have mercy on me.

For my foot has stood on the straight way * in the churches I will bless the Lord.

## XXVI. A psalm of David before he was anointed.

[Col. 0755A]

**Antiphon.** The Lord is my illumination and my salvation; whom shall I fear?

The Lord is my illumination and my salvation * whom shall I fear?

The Lord is the defender of my life * from whom shall I tremble?

When evildoers draw near against me * to eat my flesh.

Those who trouble me, my enemies * they themselves were weakened and fell.

Though armies encamp against me * my heart will not fear.

And though battle rise against me * in this I will hope.

[Col. 0755B] One thing I asked of the Lord; this I will seek * that I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life.

To see the will of the Lord * and to be protected by his holy temple.

For he hid me in his tabernacle * on the day of evils he protected me in the hiding place of his tabernacle; upon a rock he exalted me.

But now he has exalted my head * above my enemies.

I will go around and offer in his tabernacle a sacrifice of jubilation * I will sing and recite a psalm to the Lord.

**Antiphon.** Wait for the Lord, act courageously; let your heart be strengthened, and wait for the Lord.

Hear, Lord, my voice, with which I cried to you * have mercy on me and hear me.

[Col. 0755C] To you my heart said: * “I have sought your face; your face, Lord, I will seek.”

Do not turn your face away from me * nor turn away in anger from your servant.

You are my helper, Lord * do not abandon me or despise me, God my savior.

For my father and my mother abandoned me * but the Lord took me up.

Establish a law for me, Lord, in your way * and guide me in the right path because of my enemies.

Do not hand me over to the hands of those who pursue me * for unjust witnesses have risen against me, and iniquity has lied to itself.

[XI] I believe that I will see the good things of the Lord * in the land of the living. [Col. 0755D] Wait for the Lord; act courageously * let your heart be strengthened, and wait for the Lord.

## XXVII. For the end. A psalm of David.

**Antiphon.** The Lord is my helper and my redeemer; in him my heart has hoped, and I was helped.

To you, Lord, I cried * my God, do not be silent toward me, and I will become like those descending into the pit.

Hear the voice of my prayer when I pray to you * when I lift up my hands toward your holy temple.

Do not hand me over together with sinners * and do not destroy me with those who practice iniquity.

With those who speak peace with their neighbor * but evil is in their hearts.

Give them, Lord, according to their works and according to [Col. 0756A] the wickedness of their endeavors * according to the works of their hands repay them; repay them their recompense.

For they have not understood the works of the Lord, and they have not considered the works of his hands * destroy them, and do not build them up.

Blessed is the Lord * for he has heard the voice of my prayer.

The Lord is my helper and my redeemer * and in him my heart has hoped, and I was helped.

And my flesh has blossomed again * and from my will I will confess to him.

The Lord is the strength of his people * and the protector of the salvations of his anointed.

Save your people, Lord, and bless [Col. 0756B] your inheritance * and shepherd them, and exalt them forever.

## XXVIII. A psalm of David for the completion of the Tabernacle.

**Antiphon.** In the temple of the Lord all will say, “Glory,” and the Lord will sit as king forever.

Bring to the Lord, sons of God * bring to the Lord the sons of rams.

Bring to the Lord glory and honor; bring glory to the name of the Lord * worship the Lord in his holy court.

The voice of the Lord is over the waters; the God of majesty has thundered * the Lord is over many waters.

The voice of the Lord is in strength * the voice of the Lord is in magnificence.

[Col. 0756C] The voice of the Lord breaks cedars, and the Lord has broken the cedars of Lebanon * and he has crushed them like a calf of Lebanon, and the beloved like the son of unicorns.

The voice of the Lord cuts through the flame of fire * the voice of the Lord shakes the wilderness, and the Lord will shake the wilderness of Kadesh.

The voice of the Lord prepares the deer, and the Lord will reveal the thickets * and in his temple all will say, “Glory.”

The Lord will inhabit the flood * and the Lord will sit as king forever.

The Lord will give strength to his people * and the Lord will bless his people with peace.

## XXIX. For the end. A psalm of David for the dedication of the house of the Lord.

[Col. 0756D]

**Antiphon.** Lord my God, I cried out to you, and you healed me.

I will exalt you, Lord, because you received me * and you did not gladden my enemies over me.

Lord my God, I cried out to you * and you healed me.

Lord, you brought my soul up from the underworld * you saved me from those descending into the pit.

Sing praises to the Lord, his holy ones * and confess to the memory of his holiness.

For there is wrath in his anger * and life in his will.

[Col. 0757A] In the evening weeping will remain * and in the morning, joy.

But I said in my abundance: * “I shall not be shaken forever.”

Lord, in your will you provided strength for my beauty * you turned your face away from me, and I became troubled.

To you, Lord, I will cry out * and I will pray to my God.

What profit is there in my blood * when I descend into corruption?

Will dust confess to you * or proclaim your truth?

The Lord heard, and had mercy on me * the Lord became my helper.

[Col. 0757B] You turned my mourning into joy for me * you cut off my sackcloth and girded me with gladness.

So that my glory may sing to you and I may not be pierced * Lord my God, I will confess to you forever.

## XXX. For the end. A psalm of David.

**Antiphon.** In you, Lord, I have hoped; I shall not be confounded forever. In your righteousness deliver and rescue me.

[XII] Incline your ear to me * and hasten to rescue me.

Be for me a protecting God * and a fortified place, so that you may save me.

For you are my firmament and my refuge * and for your name’s sake you will be my guide; you will nourish me and lead me out of the snare that they set for me [Col. 0757C].

For you are my protector, Lord * into your hands I commend my spirit.

You have redeemed me, Lord God of truth * you have hated all who observe vanity in vain.

But I will hope in the Lord * I will exult and rejoice in your mercy.

For you have looked upon my humility; you have saved my soul from necessities * and you have not shut me into the hands of the enemy.

You have set my feet in a spacious place * have mercy on me, Lord, for I am afflicted.

My eye, my soul, and my belly have been troubled by anger.

For my life has failed in sorrow * and my years [Col. 0757D] in groaning.

My strength has been weakened in poverty * and my bones have been troubled.

More than all my enemies, I have become an excessive reproach to my neighbors * and a fear to those who know me.

All who saw me outside fled from me * I was cut off like one dead from the heart, and I became like a ruined vessel.

For I heard the reproach of many * of those dwelling around me.

While they were all gathering together against me to take my soul, they plotted * but I hoped in you, Lord.

I said: “You are my God; in your hands are my times [Col. 0758A] * deliver me and rescue me from the hands of my enemies and from those who pursue me.”

**Antiphon.** Lord, I shall not be confounded, because I have called upon you.

Make your face shine upon your servant * and save me in your mercy.

Lord, I shall not be confounded, because I have called upon you * let the impious be ashamed and be led down into the underworld.

Let wicked lips become mute * which speak iniquity against the just, in pride and contempt.

How great is the abundance of your sweetness, Lord, which you have hidden for those who fear you! * And you have perfected it for those who hope in you, in the sight of the children of men.

You will hide them in the secrecy of your face, from the disturbance of men * you will protect them in your tabernacle from [Col. 0758B] the contradiction of tongues.

Blessed is the Lord, for he has made his mercy wondrous * in a city under siege.

But I was cast away in my fear from the sight of your eyes * therefore you heard the voice of my prayer when I prayed to you.

Love the Lord, all his holy ones * for the Lord will seek out truth and repay those who act with abundant pride.

Act courageously, and let your heart be strengthened * all who hope in the Lord.

## XXXI. For the end. An understanding of David.

**Antiphon.** My exultation, O God; redeem me from those surrounding me [Col. 0758C].

Blessed are those whose iniquities have been forgiven * and whose sins have been covered.

Blessed is the man to whom the Lord has not imputed sin * nor is there deceit in his mouth.

For when I was silent, all my bones grew old * while I cried out all day.

For day and night your hand was heavy upon me * I turned in misery while the thorn was being broken.

I said: “I will confess my transgressions to the Lord”; * and you forgave the guilt of my heart.

[Col. 0758D] For this every holy person will pray to you * at an appropriate time.

Yet in the flood of many waters * they shall not come near him.

You are my refuge from the distress that surrounds me; * my exultation, deliver me from those who surround me.

I will give you understanding and instruct you * in the way you shall go; I will fix my eyes upon you.

Do not become like a horse or a mule, which have no understanding; * constrain their jaws with bit and bridle, for they do not draw near to you.

Many are the scourges of sinners; * but mercy will surround those who hope in the Lord.

Rejoice in the Lord and exult, you righteous; * and glory, all you upright of heart.

### XXXII. To the end. A Psalm of David.

[Col. 0759A]

**Antiphon.** Give thanks to the Lord on the lyre; * sing praise to him on the ten-stringed psaltery.

Rejoice in the Lord, you righteous; * praise is fitting for the upright.

[XIII] Give thanks to the Lord on the lyre; * sing praise to him on the ten-stringed psaltery.

Sing to him a new song; * sing well to him with jubilation.

For the word of the Lord is upright * and all his works are in faithfulness.

He loves mercy and judgment; * the earth is full of the mercy of the Lord.

By the word of the Lord the heavens were established; * and by the breath of his mouth all their host.

Gathering the waters of the sea as in a wineskin; * placing the deeps in storehouses.

Let all the earth fear the Lord; * and all things will be shaken by him, and all who inhabit the world.

For he spoke, and they came to be; * he commanded, and they were created.

The Lord scatters the counsels of the nations; * but he rejects the thoughts of the peoples, and he rejects the counsels of princes.

But the counsel of the Lord remains forever; * the thoughts of his heart from age to age.

**Antiphon.** Our soul waits patiently for the Lord, * for he is our helper and protector.

[Col. 0759C] Blessed is the nation whose God is the Lord, * the people whom the Lord chose as his inheritance.

From heaven the Lord looked down and saw all the children of men; * from his prepared dwelling he looked upon all who inhabit the world.

He formed their hearts individually; * he understands all their works.

A king will not be saved by the abundance of his strength; * nor will a giant be saved by the abundance of his power.

A horse is deceptive for salvation; * in the abundance of its strength there will be no deliverance.

Behold, the eyes of the Lord are upon those who fear him * and upon those who hope in his mercy,

[Col. 0759D] to deliver their souls from death * and to feed them in famine.

But our soul waits patiently for the Lord, for he is our helper and protector; * and in him our heart will rejoice, and in his holy name we have hoped.

Let your mercy, Lord, be upon us * as we have hoped in you.

### XXXIII. A Psalm of David, when he changed his countenance before Abimelech, who dismissed him; and he said:

**Antiphon.** Magnify the Lord with me * and let us exalt his name together.

I will bless the Lord at all times; * his praise will always be in my mouth.

[Col. 0760A] In the Lord my soul will be praised; * let the meek hear and rejoice.

Magnify the Lord with me * and let us exalt his name together.

I sought the Lord, and he answered me; * and he delivered me from all my distress.

Draw near to the Lord and be enlightened; * and your faces shall not be ashamed.

This poor man cried out, and the Lord heard him; * and he delivered him from all his tribulations.

The Lord sends an angel around those who fear him; * and he will rescue them.

Taste and see how sweet the Lord is; * blessed is the man who hopes in him.

Fear the Lord, all his saints; * for nothing is lacking to those who fear him.

[Col. 0760B] The rich have become needy and hungry; * but those who seek the Lord will not lack any good thing.

**Antiphon.** The Lord will redeem the souls of his servants, * and he will not abandon all who hope in him.

Come, children, hear me; * I will teach you the fear of the Lord.

Who is the man who desires life * and wishes to see good days?

Restrain your tongue from evil * and your lips from speaking deceit.

Turn away from evil and do good; * seek peace and pursue it.

The eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous; * and his ears are toward their prayers.

[Col. 0760C] But the face of the Lord is against those who do evil, * to destroy their memory from the earth.

The righteous cried out, and the Lord will hear them; * and he will deliver them from all their tribulations.

The Lord is near to those who are troubled in heart; * and he will save the humble in spirit.

Many are the tribulations of the righteous; * and from them all the Lord will deliver them.

The Lord guards all their bones; * not one of them will be broken.

The death of sinners is grievous; * and those who hate the righteous will go astray.

The Lord will redeem the souls of his servants; * and he will not abandon all who hope in him.

### XXXIV. A Psalm of David.

[Col. 0760D]

**Antiphon.** Say to my soul, Lord: * I am your salvation.

Judge, Lord, those who harm me; * and fight against those who fight against me.

[XIV] Take up arms and shield * and rise to my aid.

Draw the sword and close ranks against those who persecute me; * say to my soul: I am your salvation.

Let my enemies be put to shame and dishonored, * those who seek my soul.

Let those who devise evil against me be turned back and put to shame.

[Col. 0761A] Let them become like dust before the face of the wind; * and let the angel of the Lord afflict them.

Let their way become darkness and slippery ground; * and let the angel of the Lord pursue them.

For without cause they secretly hid a pitfall for me, their destruction; * without cause they reproached my soul.

Let the trap they do not know come upon them, * and let the snare they concealed seize them; and let them fall into the very trap.

But my soul will exult in the Lord; * it will delight in his salvation. All my bones will say: Lord, who is like you?

You who rescue the poor from the hand of one stronger than he, * and the needy and poor from those who plunder them.

Unjust witnesses arose; they questioned me about things I did not know; * they repaid me evil for good, and barrenness for my soul.

But when they troubled me, I put on sackcloth * and humbled my soul with fasting; and my prayer returned into my bosom.

As for a neighbor and as for our brother, so I pleased them; * as one mourning and sorrowful, so I humbled myself.

They rejoiced against me and gathered together; * scourges were gathered against me, and they did not know.

They were scattered, yet felt no remorse; they tested me and mocked me with mockery; * they gnashed their teeth against me.

Lord, when will you look upon this? Restore my soul from their evil deeds, * my only one from lions.

[Col. 0761C] **Antiphon.** I will confess to you, Lord, in the great assembly; * among a numerous people I will praise you.

Let those who oppose me unjustly not insult me, * those who hate me without cause and nod with their eyes.

For they spoke peaceably to me, * but deceitfully they plotted anger against me.

They opened their mouths wide against me; * they said: “Aha, aha! Our eyes have seen it.”

You have seen, Lord; do not be silent. * Lord, do not depart from me.

Rise and attend to my judgment, * my God and my Lord, to my cause.

Judge me according to your mercy, Lord my God; let them not rejoice over me, my enemies; * [Col. 0761D] let them not say in their heart: “Aha, our soul!” nor let them say: “We shall devour him.”

Let those who rejoice in my misfortunes be ashamed and confounded; * let those who speak arrogantly against me be clothed with shame and confusion.

Let those who desire my righteousness exult and rejoice; * and let them always say: “The Lord is magnified,” those who desire the peace of his servant.

And my tongue will meditate on your righteousness * and on your praise all day long.

### XXXV. To the end. The word of the Lord. A Psalm of David.

**Antiphon.** In your light, God, we shall see light.

The unjust man said within himself that he should sin: * “There is no fear of God before his eyes.”

[Col. 0762A] For he acted deceitfully in his presence * so that he might discover his own iniquity and hatred.

The words of his mouth are iniquity and deceit; he refused to understand so as to do good; * he meditated iniquity upon his bed.

He stood by every evil way; * but he did not hate wickedness.

Lord, your mercy is in heaven * and your truth reaches to the clouds.

Your righteousness is like the mountains of God; * your judgments are like the great abyss.

You will save human beings and beasts, Lord; * you have multiplied your mercy, O God.

But the children of men will hope in the protection of your wings; * they will be filled from the abundance of your house, and you will give them drink from the torrent of your delight.

For with you, Lord, is the fountain of life; * and in your light we shall see light.

Extend your mercy to those who know you * and your righteousness to those who are upright in heart.

Let not the foot of pride come upon me; * and let not the hand of sinners move me.

There all who work iniquity have fallen; * they have been driven out and could not stand.

### XXXVI. A Psalm of David.

**Antiphon.** Delight in the Lord, * and he will grant you the petitions of your heart.

[Col. 0762C] Do not be jealous of evildoers; * and do not envy those who practice iniquity.

For they will quickly wither like grass * and quickly fall like the green plants.

[XV] Hope in the Lord and do good; * dwell in the land, and you will be fed with its riches.

Delight in the Lord, * and he will grant you the petitions of your heart.

Reveal your way to the Lord and hope in him; * and he will act. He will bring forth your righteousness like the light, and your judgment like midday.

Be subject to the Lord and entreat him; * do not envy the one who prospers in his way, the man who practices iniquity.

[Col. 0762D] Cease from anger and abandon indignation; * do not envy, lest you do evil.

For those who act unjustly will be destroyed; * but those who wait for the Lord will possess the land as an inheritance.

A little while longer, and the sinner will not exist; * you will seek his place, and you will not find it.

But the meek will possess the land * and delight in an abundance of peace.

The sinner will watch the righteous and gnash his teeth at him; * but the Lord will laugh at him, because he sees that his day is coming.

Sinners have drawn their sword; * they have bent their bow to cast down the needy and poor, and to slaughter the upright in heart.

[Col. 0763A] Let their sword enter their own heart * and let their bows be broken.

Better is a little to the righteous man * than the great riches of sinners.

For the arms of sinners will be broken; * but the Lord confirms the righteous.

The Lord knows the ways of the blameless, * and their inheritance will be forever.

They will not be put to shame in evil times; * and in days of famine they will be satisfied.

For sinners will perish; but the enemies of the Lord, once they have been honored and exalted, * failing like smoke, will fail away.

The sinner borrows and does not repay; * but the righteous man has mercy and gives.

[Col. 0763B] For those who bless him will possess the land; * but those who curse him will perish.

The steps of a man are directed by the Lord; * and he greatly desires his way.

When the righteous man falls, he will not be troubled, * for the Lord strengthens his hand.

**Antiphon.** Wait for the Lord and keep his ways, * and he will exalt you.

I was young, and now I am old, * and I have not seen the righteous man abandoned, nor his offspring begging bread.

All day long he has mercy and lends; * and his offspring will be in blessing.

Turn away from evil and do good; * and dwell forever and ever.

For God loves judgment; * and he will not abandon his saints. They will be preserved forever.

The unjust are punished; * and the offspring of the impious will perish.

The righteous will possess the land as an inheritance * and dwell upon it forever and ever.

The mouth of the righteous will meditate wisdom * and his tongue will speak judgment.

The law of his God is in his heart; * and his steps will not be overthrown.

The sinner watches the righteous and seeks to destroy him; * but the Lord will not abandon him into his hands, nor condemn him when judgment is passed against him.

Wait for the Lord and keep his ways, and he will exalt you, so that you may inherit the land; * when sinners perish, you will see it.

[Col. 0763D] I saw the wicked man highly exalted * and lifted up like the cedars of Lebanon. I passed by, and behold, he was no more; I sought him, and his place was not found.

Keep innocence and observe equity, * for there are remnants for the peaceful man.

But the unjust will perish; * together the remnants of the impious will perish.

The salvation of the righteous is from the Lord, * and he is their protector in time of tribulation.

The Lord will help them and deliver them; he will rescue them from sinners * and save them, because they have hoped in him.

### XXXVII. A Psalm of David, for remembrance.

**Antiphon.** Before you is all my desire, O God; * and my groaning is not hidden from you.

Lord, do not rebuke me in your anger; * nor correct me in your fury.

For your arrows are fixed in me, * and you have strengthened your hand against me; there is no health in my flesh.

Because of the face of your anger there is no peace in my bones, * because of my sins.

For my iniquities have risen above my head; * like a heavy burden they have weighed heavily upon me.

My wounds have become foul and have grown worse * because of my folly.

I am afflicted with miseries and deeply troubled; [XVI] * all day long I went about mourning.

For my soul is filled with mockeries; * [Col. 0764B] and there is no health in my flesh.

But I have been bent down and humbled utterly; * I roared because of the groaning of my heart.

Before you is all my desire, O God; * and my groaning is not hidden from you.

My heart is troubled within me, and my strength has abandoned me; * and the light of my eyes is not with me.

My friends and neighbors stood against me and drew near; * and my neighbors stood far away.

Those who sought my soul used force; and those who sought evil for me spoke vanity; * and all day long they meditated deceit.

But I, like a deaf man, did not hear; * and like a mute man who does not open his mouth.

[Col. 0764C] And I became like a man who does not hear * and who has no reproofs in his mouth.

For in you, Lord, I have hoped; you will hear me, Lord my God; * for I said: Let my enemies never insult me; and when my feet were shaken, they spoke arrogantly against me.

For I am ready for scourges, * and my pain is always before me.

For I declare my iniquity * and I will think upon my sin.

But my enemies live and have grown strong against me; * those who hate me unjustly have multiplied.

Those who repaid me evil for good slandered me, * because I pursued righteousness.

Do not abandon me, Lord my God; * do not depart from me.

Attend to my help, * Lord, God of my salvation.

### XXXVIII. To the end. For Jeduthun. A song of David.

I said: “I will guard my ways, so that I do not sin with my tongue”; * I placed a guard over my mouth while the sinner stood against me.

I was mute and humbled myself, and was silent concerning good things; * and my pain was renewed.

My heart grew hot within me; and in my meditation the fire burned; * I spoke with my tongue.

Make known to me, Lord, my end * and the number of my days, what it is, so that I may know what I lack.

[Col. 0765A] Behold, you have made my days as handbreadths; * and my substance is as nothing before you.

Yet all is utter vanity; * every living human being.

**Interlude.**

Although a man walks in the image of God, * yet he will be troubled in vain.

He stores up treasure and does not know for whom he gathers it; * and now what is my expectation? Is it not the Lord? My substance is always as nothing before you.

Deliver me from all my iniquities; * you have made me a reproach to the fool.

I was mute and did not open my mouth, * because you are the one who made me.

Remove your scourges from me; * for I have failed under the strength of your hand, [Col. 0765B] under your reproofs.

Because of iniquity you have disciplined man * and made his soul waste away like a spider.

Yet all is utter vanity; * every living human being.

Hear my prayer and my supplication; * listen with your ears to my tears; do not be silent toward me.

For I am a sojourner with you on earth * and a pilgrim like all my fathers.

Forgive me, so that I may recover my breath before I depart * and no longer exist.

### XXXIX. To the end. A Psalm of David.

**Antiphon.** Waiting, I waited for the Lord; * and he looked upon me and brought me out of the pit of misery.

Waiting, I waited for the Lord, and he looked upon me and will hear my supplication; * and he brought me out of the pit of misery and from the mud of mire.

He set my feet upon a rock and directed my steps; * and he put a new song into my mouth, a hymn to our God.

Many will see and fear, * and they will hope in the Lord.

Blessed is the man whose hope is the name of the Lord; * and who did not turn toward vanity and false madness.

You have done many wonders, Lord my God, * and in your thoughts there is none like you.

I proclaimed and spoke; * they have multiplied beyond number.

You did not desire sacrifice and offering; * but you fashioned ears for me. You did not ask for burnt offerings even for sin.

[XVII] Then I said: “Behold, I come”; * in the heading of the book it is written concerning me.

I desired to do your will, my God; * and your law is in the midst of my heart.

I proclaimed your righteousness well, Lord, in the great assembly; * behold, I will not restrain my lips; Lord, you know.

I did not hide your righteousness in my heart; * I declared your truth and your salvation.

I did not conceal your mercy * and your truth from the great assembly.

But you, Lord, do not keep your mercies far from me; * your mercy and your truth have always upheld me.

For evils beyond number have surrounded me; * my iniquities have seized me, and I could not see.

They have multiplied beyond the hairs of my head, * and my heart has abandoned me.

It pleased the Lord to deliver me; * Lord, look upon my help.

Let all my enemies who seek my soul to take it be put to shame and dishonored.

Let those who devise evil against me be turned back and put to shame.

Let those who say to me, “Aha, aha,” bear their shame immediately.

[Col. 0766B] Let all who seek you, Lord, exult and rejoice in you; * and let those who love your salvation always say: “The Lord is magnified.”

But I am needy and poor; * the Lord takes care of me.

You are my helper and deliverer; * Lord, do not delay.

### XL. To the end. A Psalm of David.

**Antiphon.** I said: “Lord, have mercy on me; * heal my soul, for I have sinned against you.”

Blessed is the one who understands concerning the needy and poor; * on the evil day the Lord will deliver him.

May the Lord preserve him and give him life * and make him blessed.

[Col. 0766C] And may he cleanse his soul from the earth * and not deliver him into the hand of his enemy.

May the Lord bring him help upon his bed of pain; * you have turned his entire bed in his sickness.

I said: “Lord, have mercy on me; * heal my soul, for I have sinned against you.”

My enemies spoke evil against me: * “When will he die, and his name perish?”

And they came in to see; * their heart spoke falsely; they gathered iniquity for themselves.

And they went outside * and spoke together as one.

All my enemies whispered against me; * they plotted evil against me; they sent an iniquitous word against me.

“Surely one who sleeps will not rise again?” * [Col. 0766D]

Indeed, the man of my peace, in whom I hoped, * who ate my bread, has greatly increased his treachery against me.

But you, Lord, have mercy on me and raise me up, * and I will repay them.

By this I know that you have desired me, * because my enemy will not rejoice over me.

But because of my innocence you have received me * and established me in your presence forever.

Blessed is the Lord, the God of Israel, from age to age * and forever: amen, amen.

## HERE BEGINS THE SECOND BOOK

[Col. 0767]

### XLI. To the end. A Psalm of David, an understanding for the sons of Korah.

[Col. 0767A]

**Antiphon.** My soul thirsts for the living God; * when shall I come and appear before the face of God?

As a deer longs for the springs of waters, * so my soul longs for you, O God.

My soul thirsts for the living God; * when shall I come and appear before the face of God?

My tears have been my bread day and night, * while it is said to me every day: “Where is your God?”

These things I have remembered, * and my soul was poured out within me.

For I shall enter into the place of the tent of the wondrous house of God, * amid the voice of exultation and the sound of confession, as of one feasting.

Why are you sorrowful, my soul, and why do you trouble me? * Hope in the Lord, for I will confess to him, the salvation of my face and my God.

My soul is troubled within me; * therefore I will remember you, Lord, from the land of the Jordan and Hermon, from the little mountain.

[XVIII] Deep calls to deep * at the sound of your cataracts.

All your heights and your waves * have passed over me.

By day the Lord will command his mercy; * and by night he will declare it.

With me is my prayer to the God of my life; * I will say to God: “You are my protector; why have you forgotten me, and why have you rejected me? I walk sorrowfully while the enemy afflicts me.”

[Col. 0767C] While all my bones are being broken, those who trouble my soul reproach me; * while it is said to me each day: “Where is your God?”

Why are you sorrowful, my soul, and why do you trouble me? * Hope in the Lord, for I will confess to him, the salvation of my face and my God.

### XLII. To the end. A Psalm of David for the Jews.

**Antiphon.** Send forth your light and your truth, Lord.

Judge me, God, and distinguish my cause from an unholy nation; * deliver me from the unjust and deceitful man.

For you are my God and my strength; * why have you rejected me, and why do I walk sorrowfully while the enemy afflicts me?

While all my bones are being broken, * those who trouble my soul reproach me.

Send forth your light and your truth; * they themselves have led me and brought me to your holy mountain and to your tabernacle.

* And I will enter the altar of my God, * to God, who gladdens my youth.

I will confess to you on the lyre, God, my God; * why are you sorrowful, my soul, and why do you trouble me?

[Col. 0768A] Hope in the Lord, for I will confess to him, * the salvation of my face and my God.

### XLIII. To the end. An understanding of the sons of Korah. A Psalm of David.

**Antiphon.** You are yourself my King and my God, * who command salvation for Jacob.

We have heard with our ears, O God; * our fathers declared it to us:

The work that you did in their days, * in ancient days.

Your hand destroyed nations, and you planted them; * you afflicted peoples and drove them out.

For they did not possess the land by their own sword, * nor did their own arm save them.

But your right hand and your arm, and the illumination [Col. 0768B] of your face, * because you were pleased with them.

For you are yourself my King and my God, * who command salvation for Jacob.

In you we will scatter our enemies; * and in your name we will despise all who rise against us.

For I will not hope in my bow, * and my sword will not save me.

For you saved us from those who afflict us * and put to shame those who hate us.

In God we will praise all day long, * and in your name we will confess forever.

**Interlude.**

But now you have rejected and spurned us; * and you do not go forth, O God, with our armies.

[Col. 0768C] You have turned us back before our enemies, * and those who hate us plundered us for themselves.

You have given us like sheep for food, * and you have scattered us among the nations.

You sold your people for no price, * and there was no multitude in their exchange.

You have made us a reproach to our neighbors, * a mockery and derision to those around us.

You have made us a likeness among the nations, * a shaking of the head among the peoples.

All day long my shame is before me, * and the confusion of my face has covered me,

at the voice of one reproaching and reviling, * at the face of the enemy and persecutor.

All these things have come upon us, yet we have not forgotten you; * nor have we acted wickedly against your covenant. Our heart has not turned back, nor have you caused our paths to decline from your way.

For you have humbled us in a place of affliction, * and the shadow of death has covered us.

If we have forgotten the name of our God, * and if we have spread out our hands to a foreign god, would not God investigate this? For he knows the secrets of the heart.

For on your account we are put to death all day long; * we are reckoned as sheep for slaughter.

[Col. 0769A] Rise up: why do you sleep, Lord? * Rise up, and do not reject us forever.

Why do you turn your face away? * Why do you forget our poverty and our tribulation?

For our soul has been humbled in the dust, * and our belly has clung to the earth.

Rise up, Lord, help us * and deliver us for the sake of your name.

### XLIV. To the end. For those who will be changed. An understanding of the sons of Korah. A song for the beloved.

[XIX] **Antiphon.** My heart will pour forth a good word; * I speak of my works to the king.

My tongue is the pen of a scribe * writing swiftly.

Beautiful in form * beyond the sons of men.

[Col. 0769B] Grace has been poured upon your lips; therefore God has blessed you forever. * Gird your sword around your thigh, O most mighty.

Direct your splendor and your beauty; * go forth prosperously and reign.

Because of truth, meekness, and righteousness, * your right hand will lead you wondrously.

Your sharp arrows, O most mighty, * the peoples will fall beneath you, in the hearts of the enemies of the king.

**Antiphon.** Your throne, O God, is forever and ever; the scepter of equity is the scepter of your kingdom. * You have loved righteousness and hated iniquity.

Your throne, O God, is forever and ever; * an upright scepter is the scepter of your kingdom.

You have loved righteousness and hated iniquity; * therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness beyond your companions.

Myrrh, drops, and cassia from your garments; * from ivory steps they have delighted you, the daughters of kings in your honor.

The queen stood at your right hand, * clothed in gold, surrounded by variety.

Hear, daughter, and see; incline your ear, forget your people and your father’s house; * for the king will desire your beauty.

For he himself is the Lord your God, * and the daughters of Tyre will worship him with gifts.

All the wealthy among the people * will entreat your face.

All the glory of the king’s daughter is within; * she is clothed in varied garments with golden fringes.

[Col. 0769D] Virgins will be brought to the king after her; * her companions will be brought to you with joy and exultation; they will be brought into the king’s temple.

In place of your fathers, sons have been born to you; * you will appoint them princes over all the earth.

They will remember your name, Lord, * throughout every generation and generation.

Therefore the peoples will confess to you forever, * and from age to age.

### XLV. To the end. For the sons of Korah, for Jeduthun. A Psalm of David.

**Antiphon.** God is our refuge and strength, * a helper in the tribulations that have found us exceedingly.

[Col. 0770A] God is our refuge and strength, * a helper in the tribulations that have found us exceedingly.

Therefore we will not fear when the earth is shaken * and the mountains are moved into the heart of the sea.

Its waters roared and were troubled; * the mountains were shaken by its strength.

The river’s streams gladden the city of God; * the Most High will sanctify his tabernacle.

God is in its midst; it will not be moved; * God will help it by his look.

The nations were troubled and kingdoms were bowed down; * the Most High gave his voice, and the earth was moved.

The Lord of hosts is with us; * the God of Jacob is our protector.

**Interlude.**

[Col. 0770B] Come and see the works of the Lord, * the wonders he has placed upon the earth.

He removes wars to the ends of the earth; * he will break the bow and shatter the weapons, and burn the shields with fire.

Be still and see that I am the Lord; * I will be exalted among the nations, and I will be exalted on the earth.

The Lord of hosts is with us; * the God of Jacob is our protector.

### XLVI. For the victors, of the sons of Korah. For the second Sabbath. A song of David.

**Antiphon.** The great king, the Lord over all the earth, * chose us as his inheritance.

All nations, clap your hands; * shout joyfully to God with a voice of exultation.

For God is most high and terrible, * a great king over all the earth.

He subjected peoples to us * and nations beneath our feet.

He chose us as his inheritance, * the beauty of Jacob, whom he loved.

God ascended with jubilation; * the Lord with the sound of the trumpet.

Sing praises to our God, sing praises; * sing praises to our king, sing praises. For God is the king of all the earth; sing praises wisely.

The Lord will reign over all the nations; * God sits upon his holy throne.

The princes of the peoples gathered with the God of Abraham; * [Col. 0770D] for the strong gods of the earth have been exceedingly exalted.

### XLVII. To the end. A Psalm, a song for the sons of Korah. For the second Sabbath.

[XX] **Antiphon.** We have received your mercy, God, * in the midst of your temple.

Great is the Lord and exceedingly praiseworthy * in the city of our God, on his holy mountain.

Spreading exultation over all the earth, * Mount Zion, the northern sides, the city of the great King.

God will be recognized in its steps * when he receives it.

For behold, the kings of the earth gathered; * they came together as one.

[Col. 0771A] When they saw it, they were amazed, troubled, and shaken; * trembling seized them.

There were pains like those of a woman in labor; * in the fierce wind you will shatter the ships of Tarshish.

As we have heard, so we have seen, in the city of the Lord of hosts, * in the city of our God; God will establish it forever.

**Interlude.**

We have received your mercy, God, * in the midst of your temple.

According to your name, God, so is your praise to the ends of the earth; * your right hand is full of righteousness.

Let Mount Zion rejoice, and let the daughters of Judah exult, * because of your judgments, Lord.

Surround Zion and embrace her; * tell it in her towers.

[Col. 0771B] Set your hearts upon her strength * and mark her steps, so that you may recount them to the next generation.

For this is our God forever and ever; * and he himself will rule us forever.

### XLVIII. To the end. A Psalm of the sons of Korah.

**Antiphon.** Hear this, all nations; listen with your ears, * all you who inhabit the world.

All you earthborn, children of men, * rich and poor together as one.

My mouth will speak wisdom, * and the meditation of my heart understanding.

I will incline my ear to a likeness; * I will open my proposition on the psaltery.

[Col. 0771C] Why should I fear on the evil day, * when the iniquity of my heel surrounds me?

Those who trust in their strength * and glory in the abundance of their riches.

A brother will not redeem; can a man redeem? * He will not give God his propitiation, nor the price of the redemption of his soul.

He will labor forever and live to the end; * for he will not see destruction when he sees wise men dying.

The foolish and the senseless will perish together * and leave their riches to strangers.

Their graves are their houses forever; * their dwellings in every generation and generation.

They will call their names upon their lands.

[Col. 0771D] And man, though he was in honor, did not understand; * he was compared to senseless beasts and became like them.

This is their way, a stumbling block to themselves; * and afterward they will bless with their mouth.

**Interlude.**

Like sheep they are placed in the underworld; death feeds upon them; * and the righteous will rule over them in the morning. Their help will grow old in the underworld, away from their glory, and they have been expelled from their glory.

Yet God will deliver my soul from the hand of the underworld * when he receives it.

Do not fear when a man becomes rich * and when the glory of his house is multiplied,

[Col. 0772A] for when he dies he will not take everything with him, * nor will the glory of his house descend with him.

For his soul will be blessed during his life, * and he will praise you when you have done good to him.

They will enter among the generation of their fathers, * and forever they will not see light.

And man, though he was in honor, did not understand; * he was compared to senseless beasts and became like them.

### XLIX. To the end. A Psalm of David.

**Antiphon.** Call upon me in the day of distress; * and I will deliver you, and you will glorify me.

The God of gods, the Lord, has spoken * and summoned the earth.

[Col. 0772B] From the rising of the sun to its setting, * from Zion comes the beauty of his splendor.

God will come openly; * our God, and he will not be silent.

Fire will burn before him, * and around him there will be a mighty storm.

He will summon the heavens above * and the earth, to distinguish his people.

Gather his saints to him, * those who establish his covenant over sacrifices; and the heavens will declare his righteousness, for God is judge.

**Interlude.**

Hear, my people, and I will speak; * Israel, I will testify against you: I am God, your God.

I will not rebuke you because of your sacrifices; * your burnt offerings are always before me.

I will not take calves from your house, * nor goats from your flocks.

For all the beasts of the forests are mine, * the cattle on the mountains and the oxen.

I know all the birds of heaven, * and every beauty of the field is with me.

If I were hungry, I would not tell you; * for the world and its fullness are mine.

Will I eat the flesh of bulls, * or drink the blood of goats?

Sacrifice a sacrifice of praise to God * and repay your vows to the Most High.

Call upon me in the day of tribulation; * and I will deliver you, and you will glorify me.

[Col. 0772D] But to the sinner God said: * “Why do you recount my righteous acts and take up my covenant in your mouth?

Yet you hated discipline * and cast my words behind you.

If you saw a thief, you ran together with him; * and with adulterers you placed your portion.”

Your mouth overflows with wickedness * and your tongue fashions deceit.

You sit and slander your brother * and you place a stumbling-block against the son of your mother.

You have done these things, and I was silent * you thought wickedly that I would be like you?

I shall rebuke you and set it forth * before your face.

[Col. 0773A] Understand this, all you who forget the Lord * lest he seize you, and there be no one to deliver you.

He will honor me with a sacrifice of praise * there is the way on which I shall show him my salvation.

**L. To the end. A Psalm of David, when Nathan the prophet came to him, when he had gone in to Bathsheba, and said:**

Have mercy on me, O God, according to your great mercy * and according to the multitude of your compassions blot out my iniquities.

Wash me completely from my iniquity * and cleanse me from my sin.

For I acknowledge my iniquity * and my sin is always against me.

Against you alone I have sinned, and I have done what is evil before you * so that you may be justified in your words, and prevail when you are judged.

[Col. 0773B] For behold, I was conceived in iniquities * and my mother bore me in sins.

For behold, you have loved truth * you have made known to me the uncertain and hidden things of your wisdom.

You shall sprinkle me with hyssop, and I shall be cleansed * you shall wash me, and I shall be made whiter than snow.

You shall give joy and gladness to my hearing * and the humbled bones shall rejoice.

Turn your face away from my sins * and blot out all my iniquities.

Create a clean heart in me, O God * and renew a right spirit within my inward parts.

Do not cast me away from your presence * and do not take your Holy Spirit from me.

Restore to me the joy of your salvation * and strengthen me with a governing spirit.

I shall teach the wicked your ways * and the ungodly shall turn back to you.

Deliver me from bloodshed, O God, God of my salvation * my tongue shall praise your righteousness.

Lord, you shall open my lips * and my mouth shall proclaim your praise.

For if you had desired sacrifice, I would surely have given it * but you will not delight in burnt offerings.

The sacrifice acceptable to God is a troubled spirit * a contrite and humbled heart God will not despise.

Deal graciously, Lord, in your good will toward Zion * so that the walls of Jerusalem may be built.

[Col. 0773D] Then you will accept the sacrifice of righteousness, offerings, and burnt offerings * then they shall place calves upon your altar.

**LI. To the end. An Intellectus of David, when Doeg the Idumaean came and informed Saul, and said: “David has come to the house of Abimelech,” and said:**

**Antiphon.** I, like a fruitful olive tree in the house of the Lord, have hoped in your mercy, O God.

Why do you boast in wickedness * you who are powerful in iniquity?

All day long your tongue devised injustice * like a sharp razor you fashioned deceit.

You loved wickedness more than goodness * iniquity more than speaking equity.

[Col. 0774A] You loved every word of destruction * and a deceitful tongue.

Therefore may God destroy you forever, pluck you out, and remove you from your tent * and your root from the land of the living.

**Diapsalma.**

Then the righteous shall see and fear * and they shall laugh at him and say:

Behold the man who did not make God his help * but trusted in the abundance of his riches and prevailed in his vanity.

But I, like a fruitful olive tree in the house of the Lord * have hoped in your mercy, O God, forever and ever.

I shall confess to you forever, because you have done this; and I shall await your name, for it is good * before the presence of your holy ones.

**LII. To the end, for Amalek. An Intellectus of David.**

**Antiphon.** When the Lord restores the captivity of his people, let Jacob rejoice and Israel exult.

The fool said in his heart * “There is no God.”

They are corrupt and have become abominable in their pleasures * there is no one who does good, not even one.

The Lord looked down from heaven upon the sons of men * to see whether there was anyone understanding or seeking God.

All have turned aside; together they have become useless in their pleasures * there is no one who does good, not even one.

[Col. 0774C] Will they not all know * those who practice iniquity?

Those who devour my people as though eating bread * they did not call upon the Lord; there they trembled with fear where there was no fear.

For God will scatter the bones of those who please themselves * they were confounded, because God despised them.

Who will grant salvation to Israel from Zion? When the Lord turns back the captivity of his people * let Jacob rejoice and Israel exult.

**LIII. To the end, with songs. An Intellectus of David, when the Ziphites came and said to Saul: “Behold, David is hiding among us.”**

**Antiphon.** O God, save me by your name, and deliver me by your power * O God, hear my prayer.

Give ear * to the words of my mouth.

For strangers have risen up against me, and the strong have sought my life * and they have not set God before their eyes.

**Diapsalma.**

For behold, God helps me * and the Lord is the protector of my soul.

Turn the evils back upon my enemies * and in your truth destroy them.

I shall sacrifice to you willingly, and confess your name, O Lord * for it is good.

For you have delivered me from every tribulation * and my eye has looked upon my enemies.

**LIV. To the end, with songs. An Intellectus of David.**

[Col. 0775A]

**Antiphon.** Do not reject my supplication; attend to me and hear me, O Lord.

Hear, O God, my prayer, and do not reject my supplication * attend to me and hear me.

I was troubled in my exercise * and I was disturbed by the voice of the enemy and by the tribulation of the sinner.

For they brought iniquities against me * and in anger they harassed me.

My heart was troubled within me * and the fear of death fell upon me.

[Col. 0775B] Fear and trembling came upon me * and darkness covered me, and I said:

Who will give me wings like a dove’s * and I shall fly away, so that I may rest?

Behold, I fled far away and remained in solitude * I awaited the Lord, who would save me from faintheartedness and from the storm.

Destroy, Lord, and divide their tongues * for I have seen iniquity and contradiction in the city.

By day and by night he will surround it upon its walls * iniquity and labor are in its midst, and injustice; usury and deceit have not ceased from its streets.

For if my enemy had cursed me, I would surely have endured it * and if those who hated me had spoken great things against me, I would surely have hidden myself from him.

But you, a man of one mind with me, my leader and my acquaintance, who together with me took sweet food * we shall walk in agreement in the house of the Lord.

Let death come upon them * and let them descend alive into the underworld.

For wickedness is in their dwellings * in their midst.

I shall cry out to God, and the Lord will hear me * evening, morning, and midday.

I shall tell and proclaim, and he will hear my voice * he will deliver my soul in peace from those who draw near to me, for there were many with me.

[Col. 0775D] And God will hear and humble them, he who is before the ages * and he remains forever.

For there is no change in them * and they did not fear God.

He stretched out his hand in repaying them; they defiled his covenant * they were divided from the anger of his face, and his heart drew near.

They softened their words more than oil * but they themselves are arrows.

Cast your thought upon God, and he himself will nourish you * he will never permit the righteous to waver.

But you, O God, will lead them down into the pit of destruction * men of blood and deceit will not live out half their days; but I have hoped in you, O Lord.

**LV. To the Victor, for Cumulato [uncertain], because David, humble and simple, had gone far away, when the Philistines seized him in Gath.**

[Col. 0776A]

**Antiphon.** In me are vows to you, O God, which I shall repay as praise to you.

Have mercy on me, Lord, for man has trampled me * all day long, fighting, he has afflicted me.

My enemies have trampled me all day long * from the height of the days.

For many who fought against me shall fear * but I have hoped in you, O Lord.

In God I shall praise the word; in the Lord I shall praise the utterance; in God I shall hope * I shall not fear what man can do to me.

All day long they detested my words against me * [Col. 0776B] all their plans were for evil.

They will dwell in hiding; they themselves watched my heel, waiting for my life * for nothing you will save them; in anger you will break the peoples.

I shall proclaim my life to you, O God; you have placed my tears in your sight * as in your promise.

Then my enemies shall turn back * on whatever day I call upon you, behold, I know; for you are my God.

In God I shall praise the word; in the Lord I shall praise the utterance; in God I shall hope * I shall not fear what man can do to me.

In me are vows to you, O God, which I shall repay * as praise [Col. 0776C] to you.

For you have delivered my soul from death * my eyes from tears, my feet from falling,

so that I may be pleasing before the Lord * in the light of the living.

**LVI. To the end. A Psalm of David for the people who have gone far away, attributed to David in the inscription, when the Philistines seized him in Gath. The voice of the apostle Paul praying.**

Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me; for in you my soul trusts * and in the shadow of your wings I shall hope until iniquity passes away.

I shall cry out to God Most High * to the Lord who has done good to me.

**Diapsalma.**

He sent from heaven and saved me * he gave those who trampled me over to reproach.

[Col. 0776D] God sent his mercy and his truth * and he delivered my soul from the midst of lion cubs; I slept while disturbed.

The sons of men: their teeth are weapons and arrows * and their tongue is a sharp sword.

Be exalted above the heavens, O God * and let your glory be over all the earth.

They prepared snares for my feet * and they bent down my soul.

They dug a pit before my face * and they themselves fell into it.

My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready * I shall sing and make melody.

[Col. 0777A] Awake, my glory * awake, psaltery and lyre; I shall awake at dawn.

I shall confess you among the peoples, O Lord * I shall sing a psalm to you among the nations.

For your mercy is magnified to the heavens * and your truth to the clouds.

Be exalted above the heavens, O God * and let your glory be over all the earth.

**LVII. To the end. A Psalm of David.**

**Antiphon.** If indeed you speak righteousness, judge rightly, sons of men.

For in your heart you practice iniquities * on earth your hands fashion injustices.

Sinners have been estranged from the womb * from the belly they have gone astray; they have spoken falsehoods.

Their wrath is like that of a serpent, like a deaf asp, and they harden their ears [XXIV,] which do not hear the voices of enchanters * and of the sorcerer who is enchanted by the wise man.

God has crushed their teeth in their mouths * the Lord has broken the molars of lions, so that they may come to nothing like water flowing away.

He stretched out his bow until they became weak * like wax melted, they shall be taken away.

Fire fell upon them, and they did not see the sun * before your thorns produce the bramble. [The final clause is textually uncertain.]

As living creatures * so in anger he swallows them.

The righteous shall rejoice when he sees the vengeance of the ungodly * he shall wash his hands in the blood of sinners.

[Col. 0777C] And a man shall say * “If indeed there is fruit for the righteous, then indeed there is a God judging them on earth.”

**LVIII. To the end. A Psalm of David, when Saul sent and guarded his house in order to kill him, and he said:**

**Antiphon.** In the morning I shall exalt your mercy, for you have become my protector and my refuge on the day of my distress.

Deliver me from my enemies, my God * and free me from those who rise up against me.

Deliver me from those who practice iniquity * and free me from men of blood.

For behold, they have seized my soul; the mighty have rushed upon me * neither my iniquity nor my sin, Lord; without iniquity I ran and was directed.

Rise up to meet me, and see; and you, Lord God of hosts, God of Israel, attend to visit all the nations * do not have mercy on all who practice iniquity.

They shall return toward evening and suffer hunger like dogs * and they shall go around the city.

Behold, they will speak with their mouths, and a sword is on their lips * for who has heard?

But you, Lord, will laugh at them; you will regard all the nations as nothing * my strength, I shall be guarded by you, for you are God my protector; my God’s mercy will go before me.

My God, show me among my enemies * do not kill them, lest they forget your law.

[Col. 0778A] Scatter them by your power * and destroy them, my protector, Lord.

The sins of their mouths are the words of their lips * let them be caught in their pride, and let them be torn away because of the curse and the lie.

Consume them in the anger of consummation, and they shall be no more * and they shall know that God will rule Jacob and the ends of the earth.

**Diapsalma.**

They shall return toward evening and suffer hunger like dogs * and they shall go around the city.

Behold, they shall be scattered to eat * but if they are not satisfied, they shall murmur.

But I shall sing of your power, and in the morning I shall exalt your mercy * for you have become my protector [Col. 0778B] and my refuge on the day of my tribulation.

I shall make melody to you, my helper, for you are God my protector * my God, my mercy.

**LIX. To the end, for those who shall be changed, in the inscription. A Psalm of David for instruction, when he burned Mesopotamia and Syria of Zobah, and Joab returned and struck twelve thousand in the Valley of Salt.**

**Antiphon.** O God, you have rejected us and destroyed us; you were angry and then had mercy on us.

You shook the earth and troubled it * heal its fractures, for it has been shaken.

You showed your people hard things * you gave us wine of compunction.

[Col. 0778C] You gave a sign to those who fear you * so that they might flee from the face of the bow.

So that your beloved might be delivered * let your right hand save me, and hear me.

God spoke in his holy place: “I shall rejoice, and I shall divide Shechem * and I shall measure out the Valley of Booths.

“Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine * Ephraim is the strength of my head.

“Judah is my king; Moab is the pot of my hope * upon Idumaea I shall stretch out my sandal; the Philistines have been subjected to me.”

Who will lead me into the fortified city, or who will lead me as far as Idumaea * is it not you, O God, who rejected us, and you, O God, who will not go out with our forces?

[Col. 0778D] Give us help in tribulation * human salvation is vain.

In God we shall act valiantly * and he himself will bring those who trouble us to nothing.

**LX. To the end. A Psalm of David. A supplication with good favor.**

**Antiphon.** From the ends of the earth I shall cry out to you, Lord.

Hear, O God, my supplication * attend to the voice of my prayer.

[XXV] From the ends of the earth I shall cry out to you * when my heart was anxious, you exalted me upon a rock.

You led me, for you became my hope * a tower of strength in the face of the enemy.

[Col. 0779A] I shall dwell in your tabernacle forever * I shall be protected beneath the covering of your wings.

**Diapsalma.**

For you, O God, have heard my prayer * you have given an inheritance to those who fear your name.

You shall add days upon the days of the king; his years shall endure to the day of generation and generations * they shall remain forever in the sight of God.

Mercy and truth * who will seek them?

Thus I shall make melody to your name, O God, forever * so that I may repay my vows from day to day.

**LXI. To the Victor, for Jeduthun. A Psalm of David.**

A teaching of salvation.

**Antiphon.** Is not my soul subject to God, since my patience is from him? For he himself is my God and my savior, my helper; I shall not be moved any further.

How long will you rush upon men, killing them all * like a leaning wall and a driven fence?

Yet they planned to repel my honor * they ran in thirst.

With their mouths they blessed * and with their hearts they cursed.

**Diapsalma.**

Yet my soul is subject to God * for my endurance is from him.

For he himself is my God and my savior * my helper; I shall not be uprooted.

In God is my salvation and my glory * God is my help; my hope is in God.

[Col. 0779C] Hope in him, all the assembly of my people * pour out your hearts before him, for God is our helper.

Yet the sons of men are vain * the sons of men are liars in the balances, so that they may deceive; together they are vanity.

Do not hope in iniquities, and do not desire plunder * if riches flow, do not set your heart upon them.

God spoke once; I heard these two things * that power belongs to God, and to you, Lord, mercy; for you repay each according to his works.

**LXII. A Psalm of David, when he was in the desert of Judaea.**

The good favor of the one who is perfect according to God.

**Antiphon.** In the desert, and in a pathless and waterless land, O God, my God, I keep watch for you at first light.

O God, my God * I keep watch for you at first light.

My soul thirsts for you * how greatly—and my flesh—in a desert and pathless and waterless land.

Thus I appeared to you in the holy place, that I might see your power and your glory * for your mercy is better than life.

My lips shall praise you; thus I shall bless you in my life * and in your name I shall lift up my hands.

As with fat and richness my soul shall be filled * and lips of exultation shall praise your name.

Thus I remembered you upon my bed * in the morning I shall meditate on you, for you became my helper, and in the covering of your wings I shall hope.

[Col. 0780A] My soul clung after you * your right hand shall receive me.

But they sought my soul in vain * they shall enter the lower parts of the earth; they shall be handed over to the hands of the sword; they shall become the portion of foxes.

But the king shall rejoice in the Lord; everyone who swears by him shall be praised * for the mouth of those speaking iniquity has been stopped.

**LXIII. To the Victor. A Psalm of David.**

A teaching for the athlete who worships God.

**Antiphon.** Hear, O God, my prayer when I am troubled * deliver my soul from the fear of the enemy.

You protected me from the assembly of the malicious * and from the multitude of those who practice iniquity.

[Col. 0780B] For they sharpened their tongues like a sword * they bent the bitter word like a bow, to shoot the blameless in secret.

Suddenly they will shoot at him, and they will not fear * they strengthened an evil word for themselves, they discussed snares, and said: “Who will see them?”

They searched out iniquity * they failed while searching with scrutiny.

A man approaches a deep heart * and the Lord shall be exalted.

The arrows of children became their wounds * and they regarded them as nothing, and their tongues were weakened against them.

[XXVI] All who saw them were disturbed * and every man feared.

[Col. 0780C] And they proclaimed the works of God * and they understood his deeds.

The righteous shall rejoice in the Lord and hope in him * and all who are upright in heart shall be praised.

**LXIV. A Psalm of David, a Song of Jeremiah and Ezekiel concerning the word of pilgrimage, when he began to set out.**

The calling of the nations.

**Antiphon.** You will delight the goings forth of morning and evening, O God.

Praise befits you, Lord, in Zion, and a vow shall be paid to you in Jerusalem * hear my prayer; all flesh shall come to you.

The words of the iniquitous have prevailed over us * and you will be propitious toward our impieties.

Blessed is the one whom you have chosen and taken up * he shall dwell in your tabernacles.

We shall be filled with the good things of your house * your temple is holy, wondrous in righteousness.

Hear us, O God our savior * hope of all the ends of the earth and of the distant sea.

You prepare the mountains by your power, girded with strength; you trouble the depths of the sea * but who can endure the sound of its waves?

The nations shall be troubled * and all who inhabit the ends of the earth shall fear because of your signs.

The goings forth of morning and evening * you will delight.

You visited the earth and intoxicated it * you multiplied its riches.

[Col. 0781A] The river of God is filled with water * you prepared their food, for such is your preparation.

Water its furrows; multiply its generations * in its showers it shall rejoice when it rises.

Blessing the crown of the year of your goodness * and let your fields be filled with abundance.

The desert boundaries shall grow fat * and the hills shall be girded with exultation.

The rams are clothed with sheep, and the valleys shall abound in grain * indeed they shall cry out and sing a hymn.

**LXV. To the end. A Song, a Psalm of David, of the resurrection.**

The calling of the nations and the testimony of the apostles.

**Antiphon.** Sing a psalm to his name, give glory to his praise, say to God: “How fearsome are your works!”

[Col. 0781B] Shout joyfully to God, all the earth; sing a psalm to his name * give glory to his praise.

Say to God: “How terrible are your works!” * because of the greatness of your power your enemies will lie to you.

Let all the earth worship you and sing to you * let it sing a psalm to your name, O Most High.

Come and see the works of the Lord * terrible in his purposes concerning the sons of men.

He turned the sea into dry land, and he will cross the river on foot * there we shall rejoice in the same one.

He rules by his power forever * his eyes look upon the nations.

Those who provoke him in anger * let them not exalt themselves.

Bless our God, O nations * and hear the voice of his praise.

[Col. 0781C] He placed my soul in life * and did not allow my feet to be moved.

For you tested us, O God * you examined us by fire, as silver is examined.

You brought us into a snare; you placed tribulations upon our back * you set men upon our heads.

We passed through fire and water * and you led us into refreshment.

I shall enter your house with burnt offerings * I shall repay you my vows, which my lips distinguished, and my mouth spoke in my tribulation.

I shall offer you fat burnt offerings with incense, and rams * I shall offer you cattle with goats.

Come and hear, and I shall tell you, all you who fear [Col. 0781D] the Lord, * how much he has done for my soul.

To him I cried out with my mouth * and exaltation was under my tongue.

If I had seen iniquity in my heart * God would not hear.

Therefore God will hear me * and attend to the voice of my supplication.
