Blessed is the Lord, who has not removed my supplication * or his mercy from me.

**LXVI. To the end. A Psalm, a Song of David.**

The calling of the nations and the preaching of the apostles.

**Antiphon.** May the Lord enlighten his face upon us.

May God have mercy on us * and bless us.

[Col. 0782A] May the Lord enlighten his face upon us * and have mercy on us.

[XXVII] So that we may know your way on earth * your salvation among all the nations.

Let the peoples confess you, O God * let all the peoples confess you.

Let the nations rejoice and exult * for you judge the peoples in equity and guide the nations on earth.

Let the peoples confess you, O God * let all the peoples confess you.

The earth has given its fruit: may God bless us; may God, our God, bless us * and may all the ends of the earth fear him.

**LXVII. To the end. A Psalm of David.**

[Col. 0782B] The incarnation of Christ and the calling of the Gentiles.

**Antiphon.** Let God arise, and let his enemies be scattered * and let those who hate him flee from his face.

As smoke fails, let them fail * as wax flows from the face of fire, so let sinners perish from the face of God; and let the righteous feast.

Let them exult in the sight of God * and delight in gladness.

Sing to God, sing a psalm to his name * make a way for him who ascends from the setting place; the Lord is his name.

Rejoice in his sight * fathers of orphans and judges of widows shall be troubled before him.

God is in his holy place * God who makes those of one mind dwell in a house.

[Col. 0782C] He brings out captives in strength * likewise those who provoke him in anger, who dwell in tombs.

O God, when you went out before your people * when you crossed through the desert.

**Diapsalma.**

The earth was shaken, for the heavens dripped from the face of God * Mount Sinai from the face of God, the God of Israel.

You separated a willing rain, O God, for your inheritance * for indeed it was weakened.

But you perfected it * your animals shall dwell in it.

In your sweetness you prepared for the poor, O God * the Lord will give the word to those evangelizing with great power.

The kings of the armies are beloved * and the beauty of the house divides the spoils.

If you sleep among the middle ranks, the wings of a silvered dove * and the rear parts of its back in the appearance of gold.

**Diapsalma.**

When the heavenly one distinguishes kings upon the earth * they shall be whitened with snow on Zalmon.

A mountain of God is a rich mountain * a mountain of curdled cheese, a rich mountain.

Why do you suspect the rich mountain * the mountain in which it pleased God to dwell?

**Diapsalma.**

For the Lord will dwell there to the end * forever.

[Col. 0783A] **Antiphon.** Blessed is God, blessed is the Lord from day to day.

The chariots of God are ten thousand times a thousand rejoicing * the Lord is among them, on Sinai, in the holy place.

He ascended on high, he took captivity captive, he gave gifts to men * indeed, that even those who do not believe may dwell with the Lord God.

Blessed is God * blessed is the Lord from day to day.

May God our savior make our journey prosperous * our God is the God who saves, and the Lord’s are death and the Lord’s are the ways out.

Yet God will crush the heads of his enemies * the crown of the hair of those who walk in their sins.

[Col. 0783B] The Lord said: “I shall return from Bashan * I shall return into the depths of the sea, so that your foot may be dipped in blood, and the tongue of your dogs in the blood of your enemies, from him.”

Your steps have been seen, O God * the steps of my God, of the king who is in his holy place.

The joined leaders went before the singers * in the midst of young women playing tambourines.

Bless the Lord God in the churches * from the springs of Israel.

There was Benjamin, the youngest, in astonishment; the leaders of Judah were their guides * the leaders of Zebulun, the leaders of Naphtali.

Command, O God, your strength * strengthen this, O God, which you have worked in us.

[Col. 0783C] From your temple in Jerusalem * kings shall offer gifts to you.

Rebuke the beast of the forest, the assembly of bulls among the calves of the peoples * so that those tested by silver may not be excluded.

Scatter the nations that desire wars; ambassadors shall come from Egypt * Ethiopia shall hasten to stretch out its hands to God.

Kingdoms of the earth, sing to God; sing praises to the Lord, sing praises to God * who ascends above the heavens of heavens toward the east.

Behold, he will give his voice, the voice of his strength * give honor to God.

His magnificence is over Israel, and his strength * in the clouds.

[Col. 0783D] [XXVIII] Wondrous is God in his holy places * the God of Israel himself will give strength and power to his people; blessed is the Lord.

**LXVIII. To the end, for those who shall be changed. A Psalm of David.**

The sufferings and rejections of the Jews, as follows:

**Antiphon.** Save me, O God, Lord, for the waters have entered as far as my soul.

I am stuck in the mire of the deep * and there is no firm ground.

I have come into the depth of the sea * and the storm has overwhelmed me.

I have labored, crying out; my throat has become hoarse * my eyes have failed while I hope in my God.

[Col. 0784A] Those who hate me unjustly have multiplied beyond the hairs of my head * those who persecuted me unjustly have grown strong against me; what I did not seize, then I repaid.

O God, you know my foolishness * and my offenses are not hidden from you.

Let those who await you, Lord God of hosts, not be put to shame because of me * let those who seek you, Lord God of Israel, not be disgraced because of me.

For on your account I endured reproach * disgrace covered my face.

I became a stranger to my brothers * and a foreigner to the sons of my mother.

For zeal for your house consumed me * and the reproaches of those reproaching you fell upon me.

I humbled my soul with fasting * and it became a reproach to me.

I made sackcloth my garment * and I became a byword to them.

Those sitting at the gate exercised themselves against me * and those drinking wine sang against me.

But I, my prayer is to you, Lord * at the time of favor.

O God, according to the abundance of your mercy * hear me in the truth of your salvation.

Deliver me from the mire, so that I may not stick fast; free me from those who hate me and from the depth of the waters * let not the storm of the water drown me, nor let the deep swallow me, nor let the pit close its mouth over me.

[Col. 0784C] Hear me, Lord, for your mercy is kind * according to the multitude of your compassions look upon me.

Do not turn your face away from your servant * for I am troubled; hear me quickly.

Attend to my soul and deliver it * because of my enemies, rescue me.

For you know my reproach, my confusion, and my shame * all those who trouble me are before you.

My heart awaited reproach and misery; I looked for one who would grieve together with me, and there was none * and for one who would console me, and I did not find one.

And they gave me gall for food * and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.

[Col. 0784D] Let their table before them become a snare * and a trap and a stumbling-block.

Let their eyes be darkened, so that they may not see * and always bend their backs.

Pour out your anger upon them * and let the indignation of your anger seize them.

Let their dwelling become desolate * and let there be no one dwelling in their tents.

For the one whom you struck, they themselves persecuted * and they added to the pain of my wounds.

Add iniquity upon their impiety * and let them not enter into your righteousness.

Let them be erased from the book of the living * and let them not be written with the righteous.

[Col. 0785A] I am poor and sorrowful * but the salvation of your face, O God, has received me.

I shall praise the name of my God with a song * I shall magnify him with praise.

And it will please God more than a young calf * producing horns and hooves.

Let the poor see and rejoice * seek the Lord, and your soul shall live.

For the Lord has heard the poor * and he has not despised his captives.

Let the heavens and earth praise him * the sea and everything that creeps in it.

For God will save Zion, and they shall build the cities of Judah, and dwell there, and inherit it * and the offspring of his servants shall possess it; and [Col. 0785B] those who love his name shall dwell in it.

**LXIX. To the end. A Psalm of David, for remembrance of God, when the Lord saved him.**

The supplication of the righteous and of Christ himself.

**Antiphon.** O God, attend to my help; Lord, hasten to help me.

[XXIX] Let my enemies be confounded and ashamed * those who seek my soul.

Let them turn back and be confounded, those who think evil against me.

Let them turn back immediately, blushing * those who say to me: “Good, good!”

Let all who seek you, Lord, exult and rejoice in you * and let those who love your salvation always say: “The Lord be magnified,” [Col. 0785C]

But I am needy and poor * the Lord takes care of me.

You are my helper and my deliverer * Lord, do not delay.

**LXX. To the end. A Psalm of David, of the sons of Amminadab, who were taken into captivity.**

The passion and resurrection of Christ.

**Antiphon.** In you I have hoped, Lord; let me not be confounded forever * in your righteousness deliver me and rescue me.

Incline your ear to me * and deliver me.

Be for me a protecting God * and a fortified place, so that you may save me.

[Col. 0785D] For you are my strength and my refuge * my God, rescue me from the hand of the sinner, and from the hand of the transgressor and the unjust.

For you are my patience, Lord * my hope from my youth.

Upon you I have been established from the womb; from my mother’s belly you are my God * in you is my song always.

I have become like a portent to many * but you are a strong helper.

Let my mouth be filled with your praise, so that I may sing your glory * your magnificence all day long.

Do not cast me away in the time of old age * and when my strength fails, do not abandon me.

[Col. 0786A] For my enemies have spoken evil against me, and those who guarded my soul took counsel together, saying: “God has abandoned him; pursue and seize him, for there is no one to rescue him.”

O God, do not be far from me * my God, look to my help.

Let those who slander my soul be confounded and fail * let shame and confusion cover those who seek evil for me.

But I shall always hope in you * and I shall add to all your praise.

My mouth shall proclaim your righteousness * your praise all day long.

For I have not known the business of trade; I shall enter into the powers [Col. 0786B] of the Lord * I shall remember your righteousness alone.

**Antiphon.** My lips shall rejoice when I sing to you, and my soul, which you have redeemed, O Lord.

You have taught me, O God, from my youth * and until now I shall proclaim your wonders, and until old age and senility, O God, do not abandon me.

Until I proclaim your arm * to every generation that is to come;

Your power and your righteousness, O God, are to eternity * you who have done great things, O God, who is like you?

For you have shown me many and evil tribulations * and, turning back, you have given me life; and from the depths of the earth you have brought me back again. You have multiplied your righteousness * and, turning back, you have consoled me.

[Col. 0786C] And I shall confess you with instruments of psalms * I shall sing your truth to you on the lyre, O Holy One of Israel.

My lips shall rejoice when I sing to you * and my soul, which you have redeemed.

And my tongue also shall meditate on your righteousness * your praise all day long.

When all who seek evil for me are confounded * and put to shame.

**LXXI. In Solomon. A Psalm of David.**

Prophecy of Christ’s kingdom and the calling of the nations.

**Antiphon.** Let the mountains receive peace for your people, and the hills your righteousness.

[Col. 0786D] O God, give your judgment to the king * and your righteousness to the king’s son.

To judge your people in your righteousness * and your poor in judgment.

Let the mountains receive peace for your people * and the hills your righteousness.

In his righteousness he shall judge the poor of this people * and he shall save the sons of the poor.

And he shall humble the accuser * and he shall remain with the sun, and before the moon, forever and ever.

And he shall descend like rain upon fleece, * and like drops falling upon the earth.

In his days righteousness shall arise, and an abundance of peace * until the moon is exalted.

[Col. 0787A] And he shall rule from sea to sea * and from the rivers to the ends of the earth.

Before him the Ethiopians shall come forth * and his enemies shall lick the dust.

[XXX] The kings of Tarshish and the islands shall offer gifts * the kings of Arabia and Sheba shall bring presents.

And all the kings of the earth shall worship him * all nations shall serve him.

For he shall deliver the poor from the powerful * and the needy who had no helper.

He shall spare the poor and the needy * and shall save the souls of the poor.

From usury and iniquity he shall deliver their souls * and his name shall be glorious before them.

And he shall live, and gold from Arabia shall be given to him * and they shall pray for him always; all day they shall bless him.

And he shall be a firmament upon the earth, on the summits of the mountains; his fruit shall rise above Lebanon * and he shall flourish from the city like the grass of the earth; and his name shall be blessed forever.

Before the sun his name endures * and before the moon his throne.

And all the tribes of the earth shall be blessed in him * all nations shall magnify him.

Blessed is the Lord, the God of Israel, who alone does great wonders * and blessed is the name of his majesty forever and unto ages of ages.

And the whole earth shall be filled with his majesty * let it be, let it be.

# THE THIRD BOOK BEGINS

[Col. 0787]

## LXXII. The hymns of David, son of Jesse, have ended: a Psalm of Asaph

[Col. 0787B]

### A confession of human weakness concerning the wicked

**Antiphon.** How good is the God of Israel * to those who are upright in heart.

But my feet were almost moved * my steps were nearly spilled.

For I was jealous of sinners * seeing the peace of sinners.

For there is no restraint of death for them, nor firmness in their affliction.

They are not in the labors of men * and they shall not be scourged with mankind.

[Col. 0787C] Therefore pride took hold of them * they are covered with iniquity and their impiety.

Their iniquity came forth as though from fatness * they went according to the disposition of their heart.

They thought and spoke wickedness * they spoke iniquity on high.

They set their mouth against heaven * and their tongue passed over the earth.

Therefore my people shall return here, and days of abundance shall be found in them.

And they said, “How does God know? * Is there knowledge in the Most High?”

Behold, these are sinners, and they abound in the age * they have obtained riches.

And I said, “Have I justified my heart in vain, and washed my hands among the innocent? * I have been scourged all day, and my correction came each morning.”

If I said, “I shall speak in this way,” * behold, I would betray the generation of your children.

I considered how I might understand this; it is labor before me * until I enter the sanctuary of God and understand at the end.

Nevertheless, because of their deceitfulness you set evils before them * you cast them down when they were being exalted.

How suddenly they became desolate, failed, [Col. 0788B] and perished because of their iniquity * like those awakening from a dream.

Lord, in your city * you shall reduce their image to nothing.

For my heart grew dry, and my kidneys were dissolved * and I was reduced to nothing and knew nothing.

I became like a beast before you * yet I am always with you.

You held my right hand * and by your will you led me, and afterward you received me with glory.

For what remains for me in heaven * and, apart from you, what have I desired upon earth?

My heart and my flesh failed; you are the strength of my heart, and my portion, O God, forever.

For behold, those who distance themselves from you shall perish * you have destroyed all who commit fornication away from you.

But for me, it is good to cling to God * to place my hope in God, so that I may recount all your promises at the gates of the daughter of Zion.

## LXXIII. The understanding of Asaph

The voice of Christ concerning the future. A final proclamation concerning the Jews and the devastation that occurred under Vespasian and Titus.

**Antiphon.** Remember your congregation, Lord, which you established from the beginning.

[XXXI] Why have you rejected us forever, O God? * Your fury has become angry against the sheep of your pasture.

Remember your congregation * which you established from the beginning.

You redeemed the rod of your inheritance * Mount Zion, where you dwell.

Raise your hand against their pride * to the end.

How greatly the enemy has acted wickedly in your holy places * and all who hate you have gloried.

In the midst of your court they set up their signs, signs * and they did not understand, as though on a road above the summit.

Like one cutting wood in a forest with axes, they cut it down * at once.

With a double axe and an axe they cast them down; they burned your sanctuary with fire [Col. 0789A] * they defiled on earth the dwelling of your name.

They said in their heart * “Let all their kindred be alike”:

“Come, let us suppress all the feast-days of the Lord * from the earth.”

We no longer see our signs * there is no longer a prophet, and he will not know us any more.

How long will the enemy reproach, O God? * Will the adversary irritate your name forever?

Why do you turn your face away, and your right hand * from the midst of your bosom, forever?

But God is our king from ages past * he has worked salvation in the midst of the earth.

You established the sea by your strength * you crushed the heads of dragons upon the waters.

You broke the head of the great dragon * and gave him as food to the Ethiopian people.

You split open springs and torrents * you dried up the rivers of Ethan.

The day is yours, and the night is yours; you made the sun and the moon; you made all the boundaries of the earth * summer and spring, you made them.

Remember this creature of yours * for the enemy has reproached the Lord, and a foolish people has provoked your name.

Do not hand over to beasts the souls of those who confess you * do not forget forever the souls of your poor.

Look upon your covenant, for they have been filled * for the dark places of the earth have been filled with the houses of those who commit iniquity.

[Col. 0789C] Let the humble one who has been made ashamed not turn away * the poor and needy shall praise your name.

Arise, Lord; judge your cause * remember the reproach of your servants and of those who are foolish all day long.

Do not forget the voice of those who seek you * let the pride of those who hate you ascend forever.

## LXXIV. For the end: “Do not destroy.” Of David. A Psalm of Asaph. A song

Christ’s declaration of divinity and remembrance of God.

**Antiphon.** We shall confess you, O God, we shall confess you; and we shall call upon your holy name.

I shall recount all your wonders * when I have received the appointed time, I shall judge righteous judgments.

[Col. 0789D] The earth melted, and all its inhabitants * but I established its pillars.

I said to the wicked, “Do not act wickedly” * and to sinners, “Do not exalt your horn.”

Do not raise your horn on high * and do not speak iniquity against God.

For neither from the east nor from the west, nor from the desert mountains * for God is judge.

He humbles one and exalts another * for there is a cup in the Lord’s hand, full of unmixed wine mingled with mixture, and he pours from it into one and then another.

Nevertheless, its dregs have not been emptied * all the sinners of the earth shall drink from it.

But I shall rejoice forever, and sing to the God of Jacob [Col. 0790A] * and I shall break all the horns of sinners, while the horns of the righteous shall be exalted.

## LXXV. For the end, with hymns. A Psalm of Asaph. A song for the Assyrians

Vengeance against the ungodly according to God’s judgment.

**Antiphon.** You are illuminating; you are wondrous from the everlasting mountains.

God is known in Judea * his name is great in Israel.

And his place has become in peace * and his dwelling in Zion.

There he broke the horn, the bow, * the shield, the sword, and the battle.

You are illuminating; you are wondrous * from the everlasting mountains.

All the foolish in heart were troubled * they slept their sleep, and all the men of riches found nothing in their hands.

At your rebuke, O God of Jacob * those who mounted horses fell asleep.

You are terrible, and who shall resist you? * From that time onward, [XXXII] from your anger, judgment was shot from heaven.

The earth trembled and became still, when God arose for judgment * to save all the quiet of the earth.

For the thought of man shall confess you * and the remaining thoughts shall keep festival for you.

Vow and repay to the Lord your God * all you who offer gifts around him.

He is terrible, and terrible to the one who takes away the spirit of princes * terrible above the kings of the earth.

## LXXVI. For the victor, concerning Iditun. A Psalm of David

[Col. 0790C]

Concerning God’s patience and his wondrous works

**Antiphon.** In the day of my tribulation I sought God; with my hands at night before him, and I was not deceived.

With my voice I cried to the Lord * and my voice was directed to God, and he regarded me.

In the day of my tribulation I sought God * with my hands at night before him, and I was not deceived.

I refused to console my soul * I remembered God and rejoiced.

I was alienated, and my spirit failed for a little while * all my enemies anticipated the watches; I was troubled and did not speak.

[Col. 0790D] I remembered the ancient days * I kept the everlasting years in mind.

I meditated at night with my heart * I thought and examined my spirit.

And I said, “Will God reject forever? Or will he no longer continue to do good? * Will he cut off his mercy forever, from age and generation?”

Will God forget to show mercy * or will he restrain his mercy in anger?

And I said, “Now I have begun” * this is the change of the right hand of the Most High.

I remembered the works of God * for I shall remember your wonders from the beginning.

And I meditated on all your works * and I shall exercise myself in your inventions.

[Col. 0791A] O God, your way is in the holy place; what god is great like our God? * You are the God who alone does great wonders.

You made your power known among the peoples * with your arm you redeemed your people, the children of Jacob and Joseph.

The waters saw you, O God; the waters saw you and were afraid * the abysses were troubled.

At the multitude of the sound of the waters * the clouds gave their voice.

Indeed, your arrows passed through * the voice of your thunder was in the wheel.

Your lightnings illuminated the world * the earth was moved and trembled.

Your ways were in the sea, and your paths in many waters * and your footprints shall not be known.

[Col. 0791B] You led your people like sheep * by the hand of Moses and Aaron.

## LXXVII. Instruction of Asaph

The voice of Christ concerning the Jews. Christ’s address to the Church concerning the iniquity of the former people.

**Antiphon.** Incline your ear to the words of my mouth; my people, attend to my law.

Attend, my people, to my law * incline your ear to the words of my mouth.

I shall open my mouth in parables * I shall speak propositions from the beginning of the age.

What things we have heard and known * and our fathers announced to us.

They were not hidden from their children * in another generation. [Col. 0791C]

Tell the praises of the Lord and his powers * and his wonders, which he did.

And he raised up a testimony in Jacob * and established a law in Israel,

Which he commanded our fathers * that they might make these things known to their children,

So that the next generation might know them * the sons who would be born would arise and tell them to their sons,

So that they might place their hope in God * and not forget the works of their God, but seek his commandments.

Let them not become like their fathers * a crooked and bitter generation,

A generation that did not direct its heart * and whose spirit did not believe God.

[Col. 0791D] The sons of Ephraim, who bent the bow and shot their arrows * turned back on the day of battle.

They did not keep the covenant of their God * and they refused to walk in his law.

And they forgot his benefits * and his wonders, which he showed them.

Before their fathers he did great things in the land of Egypt * in the field of Tanis.

[XXXIII] He divided the sea and led them through * and he set the waters as though in a wineskin.

And he led them in a cloud by day * and by night in the illumination of light.

He divided the rock in the wilderness * and gave them water as from many abysses.

[Col. 0792A] And he brought water from the rock * and brought out waters like rivers.

Yet they continued to sin against him * in anger they provoked the Most High in the dry land.

And they tested God in their hearts * by asking for food for their souls.

And they spoke evil concerning God, and said * “Can God prepare a table in the wilderness?”

For he struck the rock, and waters flowed * and torrents overflowed.

“Can he also give bread * or prepare a table for his people?”

Therefore the Lord heard, and delayed, and increased his anger, and fire was kindled against Jacob * and God’s anger rose against Israel.

[Col. 0792B] For they did not believe in their God * nor hope in his salvation.

And he commanded the clouds above * and opened the doors of heaven.

And he rained manna upon them to eat; he gave them the bread of heaven * man ate the bread of angels; he sent them food in abundance.

**Antiphon.** They did not remember his hand on the day when he delivered them from the hand of tribulation.

And he raised up the south wind from heaven * and brought in the southwest by his power.

And he rained flesh upon them like dust * and winged birds like the sand of the sea.

And they fell in the midst of their camp * around their tents.

[Col. 0792C] And they ate and were filled exceedingly * and he gave them what they desired.

They were not deprived of their desire * while their food was still in their mouths.

God’s anger rose against them and killed many of them * and struck down the chosen of Israel.

In all these things they sinned still * and did not believe in his wonders.

And their days failed in vanity * and their years in haste.

When he killed them, then they sought him * and they turned back at dawn and came to him.

And they remembered that God was their helper * and that God Most High was their redeemer.

[Col. 0792D] And they loved him with their mouth * and with their tongue they lied to him.

But their heart was not right with him * nor were they faithful to his covenant.

Yet he is merciful and became propitious toward their sins * and he did not destroy them.

And he abounded in turning away his anger from them * and did not kindle all his wrath.

And they remembered that they were flesh * a spirit that goes away and does not return.

How often they provoked him in the wilderness * in anger they aroused him in the waterless land.

And they turned back and tested God * and provoked the Holy One of Israel.

[Col. 0793A] They did not remember his hand * on the day when he delivered them from the hand of tribulation.

He set his signs in Egypt * and his wonders in the field of Tanis.

He changed their rivers into blood * and their pools, so that they could not drink.

He sent against them the dog-fly, and it devoured them * and the frog destroyed them.

And he gave their fruits to the beetle * and their labors to the locust.

He killed their vineyards with hail * and their mulberry trees with frost, and their possessions with fire.

And he gave their cattle over to hail * and their possessions to fire.

He sent against them the anger of his indignation * indignation, [Col. 0793B] anger, and tribulation, the sending of evil angels.

He made a path for his way of anger, and did not spare their souls from death * and he shut up their cattle in death.

And he struck every firstborn in the land of Egypt * the first fruits of all their labor in the tents of Ham.

And he took away his people like sheep * and led them like a flock in the wilderness.

**Antiphon.** He brought them to the mountain of his holiness.

And he led them in hope, and they did not fear * and the sea covered their enemies.

He brought them to the mountain of his holiness * this mountain which his right hand acquired.

And he cast out nations before them * he divided the land among them by lot with the measuring cord of distribution.

[Col. 0793C] And he dwelt in their tents * the tribes of Israel.

Yet they tested and provoked God Most High * and did not keep his testimonies.

They turned away and did not observe, like their fathers * [XXXIV] and they turned into a crooked bow.

In anger they provoked him on their hills * and with their carved images they rivaled him.

The Lord heard and despised them * and reduced Israel to utter nothingness.

And he rejected the tabernacle of Shiloh, his tabernacle * in which he had dwelt among human beings.

And he delivered their strength into captivity * and their beauty into the hand of the enemy.

[Col. 0793D] And he shut up his people under the sword * and despised his inheritance.

Fire consumed their young men * and their maidens were not lamented.

Their priests fell by the sword * and their widows did not weep.

And the Lord awoke as one sleeping * and like a mighty man reeling from wine.

And he struck his enemies in their hind parts * he gave them everlasting disgrace.

And he rejected the tabernacle of Joseph and did not choose the tribe of Ephraim * but chose the tribe of Judah, Mount Zion, which he loved.

And he built his sanctuary like that of unicorns [Col. 0794A] * he founded it upon the earth forever.

And he chose David his servant and took him from the flocks of sheep * from following the nursing ewes he took him,

To shepherd Jacob his servant * and Israel his inheritance.

And he shall feed them without deceit of heart * and by the understanding of his hands he led them.

## LXXVIII. A Psalm of Asaph

The voice of the Apostles after Christ’s Passion. A prophecy which, under Antiochus, befell the Jews, according to the history in the Maccabees.

**Antiphon.** Let your mercy, Lord, quickly come before us.

O God, the nations have entered your inheritance; they have defiled your holy temple * they have made Jerusalem like a place for guarding fruit.

[Col. 0794B] They gave the bodies of your servants as food to the birds of heaven * the flesh of your saints to the beasts of the earth.

They poured out their blood like water around Jerusalem * and there was no one to bury them.

We have become a reproach to our neighbors * an object of mockery and derision to those around us.

How long, O God, will you be angry forever? * Will your jealousy burn like fire forever?

Pour out your anger upon the nations that did not know you * and upon the kingdoms that did not call upon your name.

For they devoured Jacob * and desolated his place.

Do not remember our ancient iniquities; let your mercy, Lord, quickly anticipate us * for we have become exceedingly poor.

**Diapsalma.**

Help us, O God our savior, and for the honor of your name deliver us, and be propitious toward our sins for the sake of your name * lest the nations ever say, “Where is their God?”

Let the defense of the blood of your servants that was poured out become known among the nations before our eyes.

Let the groaning of the imprisoned enter into your sight * according to the greatness of your arm, possess the children of those condemned to death.

Repay our neighbors sevenfold in their bosom * the reproach with which they reproached you, Lord.

But we, your people and the sheep of your pasture, shall confess you [Col. 0794D] forever * and unto ages of ages we shall recount your praise.

## LXXIX. For those who shall be changed, a testimony of Asaph. A Psalm for the Assyrians

A prophecy concerning those surrounded by adversaries, and a supplication concerning Christ’s advent.

**Antiphon.** You who shepherd Israel, attend; you who lead Joseph like a sheep.

You who sit above the cherubim, reveal yourself before Ephraim * and Benjamin and Manasseh.

Stir up your power * and come, so that you may save us.

O God of hosts, restore us * and show your face, and we shall be saved.

[Col. 0795A] Lord God of hosts * how long will you be angry at the prayer of your servant?

You fed us the bread of tears * and gave us drink in tears by measure.

You placed us in contradiction to our neighbors * and our enemies mocked us.

[XXXV] O God of hosts, restore us * and show your face, and we shall be saved.

**Diapsalma.**

You transferred a vine from Egypt * you cast out the nations and planted it.

You made a way before it * and planted its roots, and it filled the earth.

Its shadow covered the mountains * its branches the cedars of God.

[Col. 0795B] You extended its shoots to the sea * and its branches to the rivers.

Why have you destroyed its wall * so that all who pass along the way may gather its grapes?

The boar from the forest will ravage it * and the solitary wild beast will consume it.

Lord God of hosts, restore us * look now from heaven, see, visit this vine, and direct it, which your right hand planted, and the son of man whom you strengthened for yourself.

Burned with fire and dug out by hand, they shall perish at the rebuke of your face, Lord * let your hand be upon the man of your right hand, and upon the son of man whom you strengthened for yourself.

And we shall not depart from you; you will revive us * and we shall call upon your name.

[Col. 0795C] Lord God of hosts, restore us * and show your face, and we shall be saved.

## LXXX. For the end, concerning the winepresses. A Psalm of Asaph himself, for the fifth day of the week

The calling of the nations and the instruction of those who have come upon the former people.

**Antiphon.** Rejoice in God our helper; shout joyfully to the God of Jacob.

Take up a psalm and give the timbrel * the pleasing psaltery with the harp.

Sound the trumpet at the beginning of the month, on the day of your notable solemnity * for it is a commandment for Israel and a judgment for the God of Jacob.

[Col. 0795D] He established a testimony in Joseph when he went out from the land of Egypt * he heard a language that he did not know.

He turned his back away from burdens * his hands served with the basket.

You called upon me in tribulation, and I delivered you; I answered you in the hidden place of the storm * I tested you at the waters of contradiction.

**Diapsalma.**

Hear, my people, and I shall speak * Israel, and I shall testify to you.

Israel, if you hear me, there shall be no new god among you, nor shall you worship foreign gods.

For I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt * open your mouth wide, and I shall fill it.

[Col. 0796A] But my people did not hear my voice * and Israel did not attend to me.

And I let them go according to the desires of their heart * and they walked in their pleasures.

If my people had heard me, if Israel had walked in my ways, I would have humbled their enemies to nothing * and I would have laid my hand upon those who afflicted them.

The enemies of the Lord lied to him * and their time shall be forever.

He shall feed them with the fat of wheat * and satisfy them with honey from the rock.

## LXXXI. A Psalm of Asaph himself

The voice of Christ to the Jews. An accusation of the Jewish rulers.

[Col. 0796B]

**Antiphon.** Judge for the orphan and the needy; justify the humble and the poor.

God stood in the assembly of gods * and in the midst he distinguishes among the gods.

How long will you judge unjustly * and show partiality to sinners?

**Diapsalma.**

Judge for the orphan and the needy * justify the humble and the poor.

Rescue the poor and needy * deliver him from the hand of the sinner.

They did not know, nor did they understand; they walked in darkness * all the foundations of the earth shall be moved.

I said, “You are gods * and all of you are sons of the Most High.”

But you shall die like human beings * and like one of the princes you shall fall.

Arise, Lord; judge the earth * for you shall inherit all the nations.

## LXXXII. A song of the Psalm of Asaph

The voice of Christ concerning the Jews.

A supplication concerning those on behalf of him who suffered the sorrows of the people; and a prophecy concerning the end of God’s enemies.

**Antiphon.** Let the nations know that the name given to you is Lord; you alone are Most High over all the earth.

O God, who is like you? * Do not be silent, and do not restrain yourself, O God.

For behold, your enemies have sounded forth * and those who hate you have raised their head.

[Col. 0796D] [XXXVI] Against your people they have plotted * they have devised a plan against your holy ones.

They said, “Come, let us destroy them as a nation * and let the name of Israel no longer be remembered.”

For they devised a plan together; against you they established a covenant * the tents of the Edomites and the Ishmaelites, Moab and the Hagrites.

Gebal, Ammon, and Amalek * foreigners together with the inhabitants of Tyre.

Indeed, Assyria also came with them * they became a support for the sons of Lot.

**Diapsalma.**

Do to them, O God, as to Midian, Sisera, and Jabin at the torrent of Kishon * they perished at Endor; they became like dung upon the earth.

[Col. 0797A] Make their princes like Oreb and Zeeb, Zebah and Zalmunna * all their princes who said, “Let us possess for ourselves the sanctuary of God.”

My God, make them like a wheel * and like straw before the face of the wind.

Like fire that burns the forest * and like a flame that burns the mountains,

So pursue them in your storm * and trouble them in your anger.

Fill their faces with shame * and let them seek your name, Lord.

Let them be confounded and troubled forever and ever * let them fear and perish forever and unto ages of ages.

And let them know that the name given to you is Lord * you alone are Most High [Col. 0797B] over all the earth.

## LXXXIII. For the victor, concerning the winepresses, for the sons of Core. A Psalm

A prophecy concerning Christ and his churches.

## LXXXIV. A Psalm of David, for the victors, the sons of Core

A prophecy concerning Christ and those who were delivered through him.

**Antiphon.** You will turn and revive us, O God; and your people shall rejoice in you.

[Col. 0794A] You blessed your land, Lord * you turned back the captivity of Jacob.

**Diapsalma.**

[Col. 0798B] I shall hear what the Lord God speaks within me * for he will speak peace to his people, to his holy ones, and to those who turn their hearts toward him.

Mercy and truth have met one another * righteousness and peace have embraced.

Truth has arisen from the earth * and righteousness has looked down from heaven.

[XXXVII] For the Lord will give goodness * and our land will give its fruit.

## LXXXV. A Psalm of David: David’s supplication

The voice of Christ, or of the people.

[Col. 0798C]

**Antiphon.** For you, Lord, are gentle and mild, and exceedingly merciful to all who call upon you.

Incline your ear, Lord, and hear me * for I am needy and poor.

Guard my soul, for you are holy * save your servant, Lord my God, who hopes in you.

Have mercy on me, Lord, for I have cried to you all day * gladden the soul of your servant, for to you, Lord, I have lifted up my soul.

[Col. 0798D] Give ear to my prayer * and attend to the voice of my supplication.

In the day of my tribulation I shall cry to you * and you answered me.

All the nations that you made shall come and worship before you, Lord * and they shall honor your name, for you are great and do wonders; you alone are God.

Lead me, Lord, in your way, and I shall enter into your truth * let my heart rejoice and fear your name.

I shall confess you, Lord my God, with my whole heart, and I shall honor your name, because your mercy toward me is great [Col. 0799A] * and you have rescued my soul from the depths of hell.

O God, the unjust have risen against me, and the assembly of the powerful has sought my soul * and they have not set God before their eyes.

But you, Lord God, are compassionate and merciful * patient, exceedingly merciful, and truthful.

Look upon me and have mercy on me * give strength to your servant, and save the son of your handmaid.

## LXXXVI. Of the sons of Core: A song-Psalm

[Col. 0799B]

Christ’s incarnation.

**Antiphon.** The Lord loves the gates of Zion above the tents of Jacob.

**Diapsalma.**

**Diapsalma.**

## LXXXVII. A song of the sons of Core. For the end, concerning Amalek, for a response. The understanding of Heman the Ezrahite

He prophesies Christ’s death.

**Antiphon.** And I shall cry to you, Lord; and in the morning my prayer shall come before you.

Lord God of my salvation * by day I cried out, and by night before you.

For my soul is filled with evils * and my life has drawn near to hell.

[Col. 0799D] I have been counted among those descending into the pit * I have become like a man without help, among the dead who are free.

And like the wounded who sleep, cast into tombs, whose memory is no more * and indeed they have been driven from your hand.

They placed me in the lowest place * in darkness and the shadow of death.

Your anger has been established against me * and you have brought all your choices upon me.

**Diapsalma.**

You have distanced my acquaintances from me * you have made me an abomination to them; I was handed over and could not go out.

[XXXVIII] Do you work wonders for the dead * or will physicians raise them up, and will they confess you?

**Diapsalma.**

Will anyone declare your mercy in the grave * or your truth in destruction?

Will your wonders be known in darkness * or your righteousness in the forgotten land?

And I shall cry to you, Lord * and in the morning my prayer shall come before you.

Why, Lord, have you rejected my prayer and turned your face away from me? * I am poor, and in labors from my youth.

I was exalted, but then humbled * and confounded.

[Col. 0800B] Your angers passed over me * and your terrors troubled me.

They surrounded me like water all day * they surrounded me together.

You distanced friend and acquaintance from me * because of misery.

## LXXXVIII. Understanding: of Ethan the Israelite

Christ’s kingdom from the seed of David.

**Antiphon.** Your truth shall be prepared in the heavens, Lord.

I shall sing your mercies, Lord * forever.

From generation to generation * I shall proclaim your truth with my mouth.

For you said, “Mercy shall be built forever” [Col. 0800C] * your truth shall be prepared in the heavens.

I established a covenant with my chosen ones * I swore to David my servant.

I shall prepare your seed forever * and I shall build your throne from generation to generation.

**Diapsalma.**

The heavens shall confess your wonders, Lord * and your truth in the assemblies of the holy ones.

For who among the clouds shall be equal to the Lord * or who shall be like God among the sons of God?

God, who is glorified in the council of the holy ones * great and fearful above all who surround him.

Lord God of hosts, who is like you? * You are powerful, Lord, and your truth surrounds you.

[Col. 0800D] You rule the power of the sea * and you calm the movement of its waves.

You humbled the proud one as though wounded * and by the strength of your arm you scattered your enemies.

The heavens are yours, and the earth is yours * you founded the world and its fullness.

You created the north and the sea * Tabor and Hermon shall rejoice in your name.

Your arm is with power. Let your hand be strengthened, and let your right hand be exalted * righteousness and judgment are the preparation of your throne.

Mercy and truth shall go before your face * blessed is the people who know the joyful shout.

Lord, they shall walk in the light of your face, and in your name they shall rejoice all day [Col. 0801A] * and in your righteousness they shall be exalted.

For you are the glory of their strength * and by your favor our horn shall be exalted.

For exaltation is from the Lord * and from the Holy One of Israel, our king.

Then you spoke in a vision to your sons, and said, “I have placed help upon a mighty one * I have exalted a chosen one from my people.”

I found David my servant * with my holy oil I anointed him.

My hand will help him * and my arm will strengthen him.

The enemy will gain no advantage over him * and the son of iniquity will not harm him.

And I will cut down his enemies before his face * and put those who hate [Col. 0801B] him to flight.

And my faithfulness and my mercy will be with him * and in my name his horn will be exalted.

And I will set his hand upon the sea * and his right hand upon the rivers.

He himself will call upon me: “You are my Father * my God, and the protector of my salvation.”

And I will make him my firstborn * highest among the kings of the earth.

I will keep my mercy for him forever * and my covenant will remain faithful to him.

And I will establish his seat for ever and ever * and his throne like the days of heaven.

If his sons forsake my law and do not walk in my judgments, if they profane my ordinances [Col. 0801C] * and do not keep my commandments, I will visit their iniquities with a rod, and their sins with scourges.

But I will not remove my mercy from them, nor harm them in my faithfulness; I will not profane my covenant * nor make void the things that proceed from my lips.

[Col. 0802A] Once I have sworn by my holiness: if I lie to David, his seed will remain forever * and his throne like the sun before me.

**[XXXIX]** Like the full moon, it will remain forever * and like a faithful witness in heaven.

Yet you have rejected and spurned him * you have delayed your anointed one.

You have turned away the covenant of your servant * you have profaned his sanctuary on the earth.

You have destroyed all his walls * you have reduced his fortifications to terror.

All who pass along the road have plundered him * he has become a reproach to his neighbors.

You have exalted the right hand of his enemies * you have gladdened all his foes.

[Col. 0802B] You have turned away the help of his sword * and have not assisted him in battle.

You have dissolved him from purification * and crushed his seed upon the earth.

You have shortened the days of his throne * you have covered him with shame.

**Diapsalma.**

How long, God, will you be angry to the end * or will your wrath blaze like fire forever?

Remember what my substance is * for you did not establish the sons of men in vain.

Who is the man who will live and not see death * or who will rescue his soul from the hand of the underworld?

**Diapsalma.**

[Col. 0802C] Where are your ancient mercies, Lord * as you swore to David in your faithfulness?

Remember the reproach of your servants, which I have carried in my bosom from many nations * the reproach with which your enemies reproached, Lord, with which they reproached in exchange for your anointed one.

Blessed be the Lord forever * let it be, let it be.

## LXXXIX. The prayer of Moses, the man of God

[Col. 0801D]

**The objections of the Jews.**

**Antiphon.** May the splendor of the Lord our God be upon us.

Lord, you have become our refuge * from generation to generation.

Before the mountains were made, or the earth and the world were formed * from age to age, you are.

Do not turn man away in his lowliness * though you said: “Return, sons of men.”

For a thousand years in your sight are like one day * and like yesterday, which has passed, and like a watch in the night, which is counted as nothing: so will their years be.

In the morning, may he pass away like grass; in the morning may it bloom and pass away * in the evening may it fall, harden, and wither.

[Col. 0802D] For we have failed because of your anger * and in your fury we have been troubled.

You have set our iniquities before you * our age in the illumination of your face.

For all our days have failed * and we have failed in your anger.

Our years will be meditated upon like a spider * the days of our years are themselves seventy years.

But if they are in strength, eighty years * and most of them are labor and sorrow.

For gentleness has come upon us * and we shall be corrected.

Who knows the power of your anger * or, because of fear, can reckon your wrath?

Make your right hand known to us, Lord * and instruct the wise in heart.

[Col. 0803A] Turn, Lord, for a little while * and be reconciled to your servants.

We have been satisfied in the morning with your mercy * and we will exult and rejoice throughout all our days.

We have rejoiced for the days in which you humbled us * for the years in which we saw evil.

Look upon your servants and your works, Lord * and direct their children.

May the splendor of the Lord our God be upon us; direct the work of our hands among us * and establish the work of our hands.

## XC. A song of praise of David

The victory of Christ over everyone who persecutes [Col. 0803B] according to God.

**Antiphon.** He who dwells under the protection of the God of heaven will abide; he says to God: “You are my protector.”

He who dwells in the help of the Most High * will abide under the protection of the God of heaven.

For he will deliver me from the snare of the hunters * and from the harsh word.

His faithfulness will surround you like a shield * you will not fear the terror of the night.

**[XL]** From the arrow flying by day, from the affair that moves about [Col. 0803C] in darkness * from ruin and the noonday demon.

For you are my hope, Lord * you have made the Most High your refuge.

Evil will not approach you * and the scourge will not come near your dwelling.

For he will command his angels concerning you * to guard you in all your ways.

They will carry you in their hands * lest you ever strike your foot against a stone.

He will call upon me, and I will hear him * I am with him in tribulation; I will rescue him and glorify him.

## XCI. A song of praise of David on the Sabbath day, when he rests according to God

**Antiphon.** It is good to confess to the Lord and to sing psalms to your name, Most High.

[Col. 0804A] With a ten-stringed psaltery * with song and lyre.

For you have gladdened me, Lord, by your creation * and I will exult in the works of your hands.

How greatly your works have been magnified, Lord * your thoughts have become exceedingly deep.

The foolish man does not know * and the fool does not understand them.

When sinners are burned up like grass, and all who practice iniquity are searched out, so that they may perish forever and ever * you, Most High, are forever, Lord.

For behold, your enemies, Lord, will perish * and all who practice iniquity will be scattered.

And my horn will be exalted like that of the unicorn * and my old age will flourish in abundant mercy.

[Col. 0804B] And your eye has looked upon my enemies * and your ear has heard those who rise against me and act wickedly.

## XCII. A song of praise of David on the Sabbath day, when the earth was founded

A hymn of the reign of Christ at his first coming.

[Col. 0804C] **Antiphon.** The uprisings of the sea are wondrous; the Lord is wondrous on high.

[Col. 0804D] Holiness befits your house, Lord * for length of days.

## XCIII. A psalm of David, on the fourth day of the Sabbath

The Jews persecuting the Church of God.

**Antiphon.** The Lord will not reject his people, and he will not abandon his inheritance.

God of vengeance, Lord * God of vengeance has acted freely.

Rise up, you who judge the earth * repay the proud.

How long will sinners, Lord * how long will sinners boast?

[Col. 0805A] They will speak and utter iniquity * all who practice injustice will speak.

**[XLI]** He who planted the ear, will he not hear * he who formed the eye, will he not see?

[Col. 0805B] Blessed is the man whom you instruct, Lord * and whom you teach from your law.

Until justice is turned into judgment * and all who are upright in heart hold to it.

**Diapsalma.**

Who will resist me against those who act wickedly * or who will stand with me against those who practice iniquity?

Unless the Lord had helped me * my soul would almost have dwelt in the underworld.

If I said: “My foot has slipped” * your mercy, Lord, would help me.

According to the multitude of the sorrows in my heart * your consolations have gladdened my soul.

Will the throne of iniquity cling to you * you who fashion pain into a command?

And the Lord became my refuge * and my God my help and hope.

And he will repay them their iniquities * and in their wickedness the Lord our God will destroy them.

## XCIV. A hymn, a song of David

The calling of the Jews and their kinship.

**Antiphon.** Let us go before the face of God in confession, and let us exult to him in psalms.

To them I swore in my anger * “They shall not enter into my rest.”

A hymn of the reign of Christ at his second coming.

[Col. 0807B]

The calling of the nations and the coming of Christ.

## XCIX. A psalm of confession

## C. A psalm of David

A hymn of the one who is perfect according to God.

**[XLIII] Antiphon.** In the mornings, Lord, destroy all our sins.

## CI. The prayer of a poor man when he is anxious before the Lord and pours out his prayer

The tribulation of the former people, the prophecy of the new people, and the calling of the nations.

**Antiphon.** On whatever day I call upon you, hear me quickly, Lord my God.

**Antiphon.** The nations will fear your name, Lord, and all the kings of the earth your glory.

For he has looked down from his holy height * the Lord has looked from heaven upon the earth.

When peoples gather together as one * and kingdoms, to serve the Lord.

He answered him on the way of his strength * “Declare to me the small number of my days.”

And do not take me away in the midst of my days * your years endure from age to age.

But you are the same * and your years will not fail.

## CII. A psalm of David

[Col. 0810A]

The teaching of glorification.

To him who divided the Red Sea into divisions * for his mercy is forever.

[LX] And led Israel through its midst * for his mercy is forever.

To him who shook off Pharaoh and his army into the Red Sea * for his mercy is forever.

To him who led his people through the wilderness * for his mercy is forever.

To him who brought water out of the rock of stone * for his mercy is forever.

To him who struck many nations * for his mercy is forever.

And killed mighty kings * for his mercy is forever.

[Col. 0836D] Sihon, king of the Amorites * for his mercy is forever.

And Og, king of Bashan * for his mercy is forever.

And killed all the kingdoms of Canaan * for his mercy is forever.

And gave their land as an inheritance * for his mercy is forever.

As an inheritance to Israel his servant * for his mercy is forever.

For in our lowliness the Lord remembered us * for his mercy is forever.

And redeemed us from the hand of our enemies * for his mercy is forever.

[Col. 0837A] He gives food to all flesh * for his mercy is forever.

Give thanks to the God of heaven * for his mercy is forever.

Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good * for his mercy is forever.

## CXXXVI. Psalm of David and Jeremiah. The Voices of the Holy Ones Who Are in Captivity.

Upon the rivers of Babylon, there we sat and wept * when we remembered you, Zion.

Upon the willows in its midst * there we hung up our instruments.

For there those who led us captive asked us for the words of songs * and those who carried us away said to us, [Col. 0837B] “Sing us a hymn from the songs of Zion.”

How shall we sing the song of the Lord * in a foreign land?

If I forget you, Jerusalem * may my right hand forget me.

May my tongue cling to my jaws * if I do not remember you.

If I do not set Jerusalem first * at the beginning of my joy.

Remember, Lord, the sons of Edom on the day of Jerusalem * who said, “Empty it, empty it, down to its foundation.”

Daughter of miserable Babylon * blessed is the one who repays you with the repayment that you repaid us.

[Col. 0837C] Blessed is the one who seizes * and dashes your little ones against the rock.

## CXXXVII. Psalm of David. Good Grace. The Prophecy of David.

Antiphon. In the sight of your angels I shall sing to you, Lord.

I shall give thanks to you, Lord, with all my heart, because you heard all the words of my mouth * and in the sight of your angels I shall sing to you.

I shall worship toward your holy temple * and I shall give thanks to your name.

For your mercy and your truth * because you have magnified your holy name above all things.

[Col. 0837D] On whatever day I call upon you, hear me swiftly, Lord * you have multiplied my soul in your truth.

Let all the kings of the earth give thanks to you, Lord * because they have heard all the words of your mouth.

And let them sing to the Lord in songs, because the glory of the Lord is great * because the Lord is exalted, and he regards the lowly, while he recognizes the proud from afar.

If I walk in the midst of tribulation, you will revive me * and against the anger of my enemies you have stretched out your hand, and your right hand has saved me.

Lord, repay on my behalf * Lord, your mercy is forever; do not despise the works of your hands.

## CXXXVIII. A Song of David for Victory. The Declaration of the Righteous with God’s Pronouncement.

[Col. 0838A]

Antiphon. You formed me and placed your hand upon me, Lord.

Lord, you have tested me and known me * you have known my sitting and my rising; you understood my thoughts from afar.

You investigated my path and my limit * and foresaw all my ways, for there is no deceit upon my tongue.

Behold, you, Lord, have known all things * the newest and the ancient.

[LXI] You formed me and placed your hand upon me * your knowledge has become wonderful beyond me; it has been strengthened, and I cannot attain it.

Where shall I go from your spirit * and where shall I flee from your face?

If I ascend into heaven, you are there * and if I descend into hell, you are present.

If I take up my wings before daylight * and dwell at the farthest parts of the sea,

even there your hand will lead me * and your right hand will hold me.

And I said, “Perhaps darkness will trample me” * and the night will be illumination in my delights.

For darkness will not be darkened by you * and the night will be illuminated like the day.

As is its darkness, so also is its light * for you possess my reins, Lord.

You took possession of me from my mother’s womb * I shall give thanks to you, [Col. 0838C] Lord, because you have been wondrously made terrible.

Your works are wonderful, God * and my soul knows this exceedingly.

My bone was not hidden from you, which you made in secret * nor my substance in the lower parts of the earth.

My imperfect state your eyes saw * and in your book they will all be written:

The days will be established * and no one among them.

But your friends, God, have been honored exceedingly by me * their dominion has been greatly strengthened.

I shall number them, and they will be multiplied beyond the sand of the sea * and I arose, and I am still with you.

If you kill sinners, God, men of blood, depart from me; for they say in their thoughts * “May their cities receive vanity.”

Do I not hate those who hate you, God * and waste away over your enemies?

With perfect hatred I hated them * and they became enemies to me.

Test me, Lord, and know my heart * question me, and know my paths.

And see whether there is a way of iniquity in me * and lead me in the eternal way.

## CXXXIX. A Song of David for Victory. Voices That Struggle Against God.

Antiphon. Lord God, strength of my salvation, overshadow my head on the day of battle.

Deliver me, Lord, from the evil man * free me from the iniquitous man.

[Col. 0839A] Those who devised evils in their heart * all day long they prepared battles.

They sharpened their tongues like serpents * the venom of asps is under their lips.

Guard me, Lord, from the hand of the sinner * free me from iniquitous men.

Those who devised the overthrow of my footsteps * they hid proud snares for me.

And they stretched out ropes with my feet bound together * beside the path they placed stumbling-blocks for me.

I said to the Lord, “You are my God” * hear the voice of my supplication.

Lord God, strength of my salvation * overshadow my head on the day of battle.

Do not hand me over, Lord, to the sinner’s desire * they have devised against me; do not abandon me, lest they ever be exalted.

The head of their encirclement * the labor of their lips will cover them.

Burning coals will fall upon them; and you will cast them into fire * they will not stand amid miseries.

A slanderous man will not be established upon the earth * evil will seize the unjust man for destruction.

I have known that the Lord will execute judgment for the needy * and vengeance for the poor.

Yet the righteous will give thanks to your name * and the upright will dwell in your presence.

## CXL. Song of David. The Prayer of Those Who Are Perfect According to God.

[Col. 0839C] Lord, I cried to you; hear me * attend to the voice of my prayer when I cry to you.

Let my prayer be directed like incense in your sight * the lifting of my hands like an evening sacrifice.

Place, Lord, a guard over my mouth, and a door of restraint over my lips * so that my heart may not turn aside to an evil word,

to make excuses for excuses in sins with people who work iniquity * and so that I may not join in their chosen company.

The righteous will chastise me in mercy and rebuke me * but the oil of the sinner will not make my head fat.

For my prayer is still among their pleasures; their judges have been swallowed up beside the rock * [Col. 0839D] they heard my words, because they prevailed.

As the thickness of the earth erupts upon the earth * our bones have been scattered beside hell.

For to you, Lord, Lord, are my eyes * in you I have hoped; do not take away my soul.

[LXII] Guard me from the snare that they set for me * and from the stumbling-blocks of those who work iniquity.

Sinners will fall into his nets * I am alone until I pass through.

## CXLI. The Instruction of David, When He Was in the Cave. The Voice of Those Who Are Perfect for God.

Antiphon. I shall pour out my prayer in the sight of God; I shall declare my tribulation before him.

[Col. 0840A] With my voice I cried to the Lord * with my voice I entreated God.

I shall pour out my prayer in the sight of God * I shall declare my tribulation before him.

When my spirit failed within me * you knew my paths.

On this way on which I walked * the proud hid snares for me.

I looked to the right and saw * and there was no one who knew me.

My escape perished * and there is no one who seeks my soul.

I cried to you, Lord; I said, “You are my hope * my portion in the land of the living.”

Attend to the voice of my prayer, for I have been humbled exceedingly * [Col. 0840B] deliver me from those who persecute me, for they have grown strong against me.

Bring my soul out of prison, that I may give thanks to your name * the righteous await me until you repay me.

## CXLII. Song of David. The Prayer of Confession.

Antiphon. Make me hear your mercy in the morning.

Lord, hear my prayer * listen with your ears to my supplication in your truth.

Hear me in your righteousness, and do not enter into judgment with your servant * for no living person will be justified in your sight.

For the enemy pursued my soul * [Col. 0840C] he humbled my life to the earth.

He placed me in dark places like the dead of ages, and my spirit was troubled within me * my heart was disturbed within me.

I remembered the days of old, and I meditated upon all your works * and I shall meditate upon the works of your hands.

I stretched out my hands to you * my soul is like land without water; hear me swiftly.

Lord, my spirit has failed; do not turn your face from me * otherwise I shall become like those who descend into the pit.

Make me hear your mercy in the morning * for I have hoped in you, Lord.

Show me the way in which I should walk * for to you, Lord, I have lifted my soul.

[Col. 0840D] Deliver me from my enemies, my God, for I have fled to you * teach me to do your will, for you are my God; your good spirit will lead me into the right way.

For the sake of your name, Lord, you will revive me in your righteousness * and you will lead my soul out of tribulation.

And in your mercy you will scatter my enemies and destroy all who trouble my soul * for I am your servant.

## CXLIII. Psalm of David.

Antiphon. My mercy, my refuge, my protector, and my deliverer.

[Col. 0841A] Blessed is the Lord my God, who teaches my hands for battle * and my fingers for war.

My mercy and my refuge * my protector and my deliverer.

My protector, and in him I have hoped * subduing peoples beneath me.

Lord, what is a human being, that you have made yourself known to him * or the son of man, that you regard him?

A human being has become like vanity * his days have passed like a shadow.

Lord, bend the heavens and descend * touch the mountains, and they will smoke.

Flash flashes of lightning, and you will scatter them * send your arrows, and you will trouble them.

Send your hand from on high, rescue and deliver me [Col. 0841B] from many waters * and from the hand of foreign sons.

Those whose mouth has spoken vanity * and whose right hand is a right hand of iniquity.

God, I shall sing a new song to you * upon a ten-stringed psaltery I shall sing psalms to you.

To him who gives salvation to kings and delivers David his servant from the evil sword * rescue and deliver me from many waters, and from the hand of foreign sons.

Those whose mouth has spoken vanity * and whose right hand is a right hand of iniquity.

Their sons are like young plants * established from their youth.

Their daughters are adorned * decorated like the likeness of a temple.

[Col. 0841C] Their storehouses are full * overflowing from one place to another.

Their ewes are fertile, abundant in their paths * their oxen are fat.

There is no breach in the wall * no passage, nor cry in their streets.

They called the people blessed to whom these things belong * blessed is the people whose Lord is their God.

## CXLIV. Hymn of David. Aleph. A Hymn with God’s Pronouncement.

Antiphon. The Lord is gracious to all, and his mercies are over all his works.

I will exalt you, Lord my king and my God * and I will bless your name forever and throughout all ages.

Every day we bless you * and praise your name forever and throughout all ages.

Great is the Lord and exceedingly worthy of praise * and there is no end to his greatness.

Generation and generation will praise your name * and they will declare your power.

They will speak of the magnificence of your majesty and your holiness * and they will recount your wonders.

They will speak of the power of your fearful deeds * and they will tell of your magnificence.

They will pour forth the memory of the abundance of your sweetness * and they will exult in your righteousness.

Merciful and compassionate is the Lord * patient and greatly merciful, and holy in all his works.

The Lord is gracious to all * and his mercies are over all his works.

Let all your works give thanks to you, Lord * and your holy ones shall bless you.

They will speak of the glory of your kingdom * and they will speak of your power.

So that they may make your power known to the sons of men * and the glory of the magnificence of your kingdom.

Your kingdom is a kingdom of all ages, Lord * and your dominion is in every generation and generation.

The Lord is faithful in his words * and holy in all his works.

[Col. 0842B] The Lord raises up all who fall * and restores all who have been cast down.

The eyes of all look to you in hope, Lord * and you give them food at the proper time.

You open your hand * and fill every living soul with blessing.

The Lord is righteous in all his ways * and holy in all his works.

The Lord is near to all * who call upon him in truth.

He will do the will of those who fear him * and he will hear their prayers, and he will save them.

The Lord guards all who love him * but he will destroy all sinners.

My mouth shall speak the praise of the Lord * and all flesh shall bless his holy name forever and throughout all ages.

## CXLV. Alleluia. A Hymn with God’s Pronouncement.

Antiphon. The Lord raises up those who have been cast down; the Lord frees those bound in chains; the Lord gives light to the blind.

Praise the Lord, my soul * I will praise the Lord in my life; I will sing psalms to my God as long as I am.

Do not trust in princes * nor in the sons of men, in whom there is no salvation.

Their spirit will go out, and they will return to their earth * on that day all their thoughts will perish.

Blessed is he whose God is the God of Jacob, his helper * whose hope is in the Lord his God, who made heaven and earth, the sea and all that is in them.

He keeps truth forever * he executes judgment for those suffering wrong, and gives food to the hungry.

The Lord raises up those who have been cast down; the Lord frees those bound in chains; the Lord gives light to the blind * the Lord directs the righteous.

The Lord guards the resident alien; he will receive the orphan and the widow * but he will destroy the ways of sinners.

The Lord will reign forever * your God, Zion, from age to age.

## CXLVI. Alleluia. A Hymn with God’s Pronouncement.

Antiphon. He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds; great is our Lord, and great is his power.

[Col. 0843A] Praise the Lord, for the psalm is good * let praise be sweet to our God.

The Lord builds Jerusalem * and gathers the scattered of Israel.

He heals the brokenhearted * and binds up their wounds.

He numbers the multitude of the stars * and calls all of them by name.

[LXIV] Great is our Lord, and great is his power * and there is no measure of his wisdom.

The Lord receives the meek * but he humbles sinners to the earth.

Begin with the Lord in thanksgiving * sing psalms to our God on the lyre.

He covers the heavens with clouds * and prepares rain for the earth.

[Col. 0843B] He brings forth grass on the mountains * and plants for the service of men.

He gives their food to the beasts * and to the young ravens that call upon him.

He will not take pleasure in the strength of a horse * nor are the tents of a man pleasing to him.

The Lord takes pleasure in those who fear him * and in those who hope in his mercy.

## CXLVII. Alleluia. A Hymn with God’s Pronouncement.

Antiphon. Jerusalem, praise the Lord; Zion, praise your God.

[Col. 0843C] Praise the Lord, Jerusalem * praise your God, Zion.

For he strengthened the bars of your gates * he blessed your children within you.

He established your borders in peace * satisfying you with the fat of wheat.

He sends forth his utterance to the earth * his word runs swiftly.

He gives snow like wool * he scatters mist like ashes.

He sends his crystal like pieces of bread * who can stand before his frost?

He sends his word, and he will melt them * his spirit blows, and the waters flow.

He declares his word to Jacob * his righteousness and judgments [Col. 0843D] to Israel.

He has not done such a thing for every nation * and he has not manifested his judgments to them.

## CXLVIII. Alleluia. A Hymn with God’s Pronouncement.

Praise the Lord from the heavens * praise him in the heights.

Praise him, all his angels * praise him, all his powers.

Praise him, sun and moon * praise him, all stars and light.

Praise him, heavens of heavens * and let the waters that are above the heavens praise the name of the Lord.

[Col. 0844A] For he spoke, and they were made * he commanded, and they were created.

He established them forever and throughout all ages * he set down a command, and it will not pass away.

Praise the Lord from the earth * dragons and all the depths.

Fire, hail, snow, ice, and the spirit of the storm * you who do his word.

Mountains and all hills * fruitful trees and all cedars.

Beasts and all cattle * creeping things and winged birds.

Kings of the earth and all peoples * princes and all judges of the earth.

Young men and virgins, elders with the younger * [Col. 0844B] let them praise the name of the Lord.

For his name alone has been exalted * his praise is above heaven and earth.

And he will exalt the horn of his people * a hymn for all his holy ones, for the sons of the people who draw near to him.

## CXLIX. Alleluia.

Sing a new song to the Lord * his praise is in the churches of the holy ones.

Let Israel rejoice in him who made it * and let the sons of Zion exult over their king.

Let them praise his name in the choir * let them sing psalms to him with tambourine and psaltery.

For the Lord takes pleasure in his people * and he will exalt the meek in salvation.

The holy ones will exult in glory * and they will rejoice in their beds.

The exaltations of God are in their throats * and two-edged swords are in their hands.

To execute vengeance among the nations * rebukes among the peoples.

To bind their kings in fetters * and their nobles in iron chains.

To execute upon them the judgment that has been written * this glory belongs to all his holy ones.

## CL. Alleluia.

Praise the Lord in his holy places * praise him in the firmament of his power.

Praise him in his mighty deeds * praise him according to the multitude of his greatness.

Praise him with the sound of the trumpet * praise him with psaltery and lyre.

Praise him with tambourine and chorus * praise him with strings and organ.

Praise him with well-sounding cymbals; praise [LXV] him with cymbals of jubilation * let every spirit praise the Lord.

## CLI.

This Psalm is properly written as being David’s, outside the number, when he was fighting against Goliath alone.

I was small among my brothers * and younger in my father’s house.

[Col. 0845A] I was tending my father’s sheep * my hands made an organ, and my fingers tuned a psaltery.

And who will announce it to my lord? * The Lord himself will hear me.

He is the hearer of all * he himself sent his angel and took me away from my father’s sheep, and anointed me with the mercy of his anointing.

[Col. 0846A] But my brothers were good and great * and the Lord took no pleasure in them.

I went out to meet the foreigner * and he reviled me with his idols.

But I, having drawn his sword from him, cut off his head with that very sword * and removed the reproach from the sons of Israel.

[Col. 0845]

# THE SONGS BEGIN. (C)

## THE SONG OF DEUTERONOMY. Chapter 33.

[Col. 0845A]

Antiphon. The Lord appeared from Mount Paran, and with him were thousands of holy ones.

The Lord will come from Sinai * and from Seir he rose for us. [Col. 0845B]

The Lord appeared from Mount Paran * and with him were thousands of holy ones.

In his right hand was a fiery law * he loved the peoples.

All the holy ones are in his hand * and those who draw near to his feet will receive instruction from him.

His hands will fight for him * and his helper will be against his adversaries.

The cub of the lion will flow abundantly from Bashan * he will enjoy abundance, and he will be full of the Lord’s blessing; in the morning and at noon he will possess it.

As the firstborn of the bull is his beauty; the horns of the rhinoceros are his horns * with them he will drive the nations to the ends of the earth.

## II. THE SONG OF THE PROPHET ISAIAH. Chapters 8 and 9.

[Col. 0845C]

Antiphon. The mighty God will sit upon the throne of David, to establish it forever.

Bind up the testimony and seal the law among my disciples * I shall wait for the Lord, who hides his face from the house of Jacob, and I shall await him.

Behold, I and the children whom the Lord has given me, as a sign and portent for Israel * from the Lord of hosts, who dwells on Mount Zion.

And when they say to you, “Seek answers from the python-spirits” * and from diviners who hiss in their incantations,

surely a people does not seek from its God concerning the living and the dead * and should they turn instead to the law and the testimony?

[Col. 0845D] But if they do not speak according to this word * there will be no morning light for them.

And he will pass through it, and he will fall and hunger * and when he hungers he will become angry and curse his king and his God.

And he will look upward [the printed reading is suscipiet; perhaps suspiciet, “look upward”] * and gaze upon the earth.

And behold, tribulation and darkness, dissolution and distress, and pursuing gloom * and he will not be able to escape from his distress.

At the first time the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali were made light; but in the latter time the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations, was made heavy.

[Col. 0846A] The people of the nations who sat in darkness saw a great light; for those dwelling in the region and shadow of death, light has dawned.

You have multiplied the nation, but you have not magnified its joy. They will rejoice before you as those rejoice at harvest, as victors exult when they divide the spoils.

For you have broken the yoke of its burden, the rod upon its shoulders, and the staff of its oppressor, as on the day of Midian.

For every violent plundering amid tumult, and every garment mixed with blood, will be for burning and fuel for the fire.

For a child is born to us, a son is given to us; and sovereignty has been placed upon his shoulders.

And his name will be called: Wonderful Counselor,

Mighty God, Father of the age to come, Prince of Peace.

[LXVI] His dominion will be multiplied, and there will be no end to his peace. [Col. 0846C]

He will sit upon David’s throne and over his kingdom, to establish it and strengthen it with judgment and justice, from now and forever.

The zeal of the Lord of hosts will do this.

## III. CANTICLE OF THE PROPHET ISAIAH. Chapters 10 and 11

**Antiphon.** The root of Jesse, who stands as a sign for the peoples: the nations themselves will appeal to him.

Behold, the Lord, the Ruler of hosts, will shatter the thicket in terror; the tall trees will be cut down, and the lofty will be humbled.

The dense growth of the forest will be overturned by iron, and Lebanon with its lofty trees will fall.

[Col. 0846D] And a shoot will come forth from the root of Jesse, and a flower will rise from his root.

And the Spirit of the Lord will rest upon him: the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and strength, the spirit of knowledge and piety.

And he will be filled with the spirit of the fear of the Lord.
