He will not judge according to the sight of his eyes, nor reprove according to the hearing of his ears; but he will judge the poor with justice and reprove the meek of the earth with equity.

And he will strike the earth with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips he will slay the wicked.

And justice will be the belt of his loins, and faith the girdle of his reins.

[Col. 0847A] The wolf will dwell with the lamb, and the leopard will lie down with the kid.

The calf, the lion, and the sheep will dwell together, and a little child will lead them.

The calf and the bear will pasture, and their young will rest together.

And the lion will eat straw like an ox, and the infant will delight at the breast.

Over the hole of the asp and in the den of the basilisk, the weaned child will place his hand.

They will neither harm nor kill throughout all my holy mountain, for the earth is filled with the knowledge of the Lord, as waters cover the sea, on that day.

The root of Jesse, who stands as a sign for the peoples: the nations themselves will appeal to him, and his tomb will be glorious. [Col. 0847B]

## IV. CANTICLE OF THE PROPHET ISAIAH. Chapter 30

God of judgment, the Lord: blessed are all who await him.

For the people of Zion will dwell in Jerusalem, weeping; you will certainly weep no longer, for he will surely have mercy on you.

At the sound of your cry, as soon as he hears it, he will answer you.

And the Lord will give you scant bread and little water; he will no longer cause your teacher to flee from you.

And your eyes will see your instructor, and your ears will hear the word of one admonishing behind you.

[Col. 0847C] This is the way; walk in it, neither turning to the right nor to the left. And you will defile the plates of your silver idols and the garment of your molten gold, and you will scatter them like the impurity of a menstruating woman. “Go out,” you will say to it.

And rain will be given to your seed wherever you sow it in the land; and the bread of the produce of the land will be most abundant and rich.

On that day, your lambs will feed in a spacious pasture, and your bulls and the young of your donkeys that work the ground will eat mixed fodder, winnowed as on a threshing floor.

And upon every high mountain and every elevated hill there will be streams of flowing waters, [Col. 0847D] on the day of the slaughter of many, when the tower falls.

And the light of the moon will be like the light of the sun, and the light of the sun will be sevenfold, like the light of seven days, on the day when the Lord binds up the wound of his people and heals the blow of its injury.

Behold, the name of the Lord comes from afar, his anger burning and grievous to bear.

His lips are filled with indignation, and his tongue is like a devouring fire.

His breath is like an overflowing torrent reaching to the middle of the eternal hills, to destroy the nations utterly; and it is a bridle of error in the jaws of the peoples.

Your song will be like the night of a sanctified festival, [Col. 0848A] and the gladness of the heart like that of one proceeding with a flute to enter the mountain of the Lord, to the Mighty One of Israel.

And the Lord will make the glory of his voice heard, and he will display the terror of his arm in the threat of fury and the flame of devouring fire.

He will strike in a whirlwind and with a stone of hail.

[LXVII] For at the voice of the Lord Assyria will tremble, struck by the rod; and the passage of the rod will be firmly established, which the Lord will cause to rest upon him.

With tambourines and lyres, and with decisive battles, he will fight against him.

For the breath of the Lord, like a torrent of sulfur, will burn him.

## V. CANTICLE OF THE PROPHET ISAIAH. Chapter 35

[Col. 0848B]

**Antiphon.** Behold, our God will come and save us.

Strengthen the slack hands, and make firm the weak knees.

Say to the fainthearted: “Take courage and do not fear.”

Behold, your God brings vengeance and recompense; God himself will come and save you.

Then the eyes of the blind will be opened, and the ears of the deaf will be unstopped.

Then the lame man will leap like a stag, and the tongue of the mute will be opened.

For waters have burst forth in the desert, and torrents in the wilderness; what was dry has become pools, and the thirsty land, springs of water.

[Col. 0848C] In the dens where dragons formerly dwelt, greenery of reed and rush will spring up; and there will be a path and a way, and it will be called the holy way.

The unclean will not pass through it; rather, it will be a direct way for us, so that fools will not wander on it.

There will be no lion there, and no evil beast will ascend it, nor will it be found there.

And those who have been liberated and redeemed by the Lord will walk there; they will return and come to Zion with praise, and everlasting joy will be upon their heads.

They will obtain joy and gladness, and sorrow and groaning will flee.

## VI. CANTICLE OF THE PROPHET ISAIAH. Chapter 40

[Col. 0848D]

**Antiphon.** Prepare the way of the Lord; make straight the paths of our God.

“Be comforted, be comforted, my people,” says the Lord your God.

Speak to the heart of Jerusalem and call to her, for her wickedness is completed, her iniquities are forgiven; she has received from the Lord’s hand double for all her sins.

A voice crying in the wilderness: “Prepare the way of the Lord; make straight in the desert the paths of our God.”

Every valley will be exalted, and every mountain and hill will be humbled.

[Col. 0849A] And the uneven places will become level, and the rough places, smooth roads.

And the glory of the Lord will be revealed, and all flesh together will see that the mouth of the Lord has spoken.

A voice saying: “Cry out.” And I said: “What shall I cry?”

All flesh is grass, and all its glory like the flower of the field.

The grass has withered and the flower has fallen, because the spirit of the Lord will blow upon it.

Truly, the people are grass. The grass has withered and the flower has fallen; but the word of our God will stand forever.

Climb upon a high mountain, you who evangelize Zion; raise your voice with strength, you who evangelize Jerusalem; raise it and do not fear. Say to the cities of Judah: “Behold, your God.”

[Col. 0849B]

## VII. CANTICLE OF THE PROPHET ISAIAH

**Antiphon.** Behold, the Lord will come in strength, and his arm with dominion.

Behold, the Lord God will come in strength, and his arm will rule.

Behold, his reward is with him, and his work is before him.

As a shepherd feeds his flock, so he will gather the lambs in his arm and lift them in his bosom; he himself will carry the nursing ewes.

Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, and weighed the heavens with a span?

[Col. 0849C] Who has weighed the mass of the earth with three fingers, and measured the mountains by weight and the hills on a balance?

Who has assisted the spirit of the Lord, or who was his counselor and instructed him?

With whom did he take counsel—the text reads inid; perhaps iniit, “entered into”—and who instructed him? Who taught him the path of justice, instructed him in knowledge, and showed him the way of understanding?

Behold, the nations are like a drop from a bucket, and are counted as a moment on the balance.

Behold, the islands are like fine dust, and Lebanon would not suffice for burning, nor would its animals suffice for a burnt offering.

All the nations are as though they did not exist before him; [LXVIII] they are counted as nothing and emptiness.

## VIII. CANTICLE OF THE PROPHET ISAIAH. Chapter 42

[Col. 0849D]

Sing to the Lord a new song, his praise from the ends of the earth.

You who go down to the sea and its fullness, the islands and their inhabitants.

Let the wilderness and its cities be exalted; in the houses Cedar will dwell.

Praise him, inhabitants of the rock; cry out from the top of the mountains.

They will give glory to the Lord and proclaim his praise in the islands.

[Col. 0850A] The Lord will go forth like a mighty man; like a warrior he will stir up zeal.

He will cry out and shout; he will prevail against his enemies.

I have always been silent; I have kept still and been patient. Like a woman in labor, I will speak.

I will destroy and swallow up; I will make the mountains and hills desolate, and dry up all their vegetation.

I will make rivers into islands and dry up the pools.

And I will lead the blind along a way they do not know, and make them walk along paths they do not know.

I will make darkness before them into light, and crooked things into straight.

## IX. CANTICLE OF THE PROPHET ISAIAH. Chapter 49

[Col. 0850B]

**Antiphon.** The Lord has comforted his people, and he will have mercy on his poor.

Thus says the Lord, the Redeemer of Israel, its Holy One, to the contemptible soul and the abhorred nation, to the servant of rulers:

Kings will see and rise, and princes will worship, because of the Lord, for he is faithful—the Holy One of Israel who chose you.

Thus says the Lord: “At an acceptable time I answered you, and on the day of salvation I helped you.

And I preserved you and gave you as a covenant to the people, to raise up the land and possess the scattered inheritances,

so that you might say to those who are bound: ‘Come out,’ and to those who are in darkness: ‘Reveal yourselves.’”

[Col. 0850C] They will feed along the roads, and their pastures will be on every open height.

They will neither hunger nor thirst, and heat and sun will not strike them, because their merciful one will guide them and lead them to springs of water.

And I will place all my mountains on a road, and my paths will be exalted.

Behold, these will come from far away; and behold, those from the north and from the sea; and these from the southern land.

Praise, heavens, and exult, earth; mountains, break forth in praise, because the Lord has comforted his people and will have mercy on his poor.

## X. CANTICLE OF THE PROPHET ISAIAH. Chapter 51

[Col. 0850D]

**Antiphon.** “My salvation will be forever,” says the Lord, “and my justice from generation to generation.”

Attend to me, my people; and my tribe, listen to me.

For a law will go forth from me, and my judgment will rest as a light for the peoples.

My righteous one is near, and my savior has gone forth; my arms will judge the peoples.

For the islands will await me, and they will await my arm.

Lift your eyes to heaven, and look down upon the earth.

For the heavens will melt like smoke, and the earth will wear out like a garment; and its inhabitants will perish in the same way.

[Col. 0851A] But my salvation will be forever, and my justice will not fail.

Listen to me, you who know justice, the people who have my law in their hearts.

Do not fear the reproach of human beings, and do not dread their blasphemies.

For as a garment, so the worm will consume them; and as wool, so the moth will devour them.

But my salvation will be forever, and my justice from generation to generation.

Rise, rise; put on strength, O arm of the Lord. Rise as in ancient days, in the generations of ages.

[Col. 0851B] Are you not the one who struck the proud one and wounded the dragon?

Are you not the one who dried up the sea, the waters of the mighty abyss,

who made the depths of the sea a road for the redeemed to cross?

And now those redeemed by the Lord will return and come to Zion, praising, with everlasting joy upon their heads.

They will obtain joy and gladness, and sorrow and groaning will flee.

[LXIX] “I, I myself will comfort you,” says the Lord.

## XI. CANTICLE OF THE PROPHET ISAIAH. Chapter 52

[Col. 0851C]

**Antiphon.** How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the one announcing peace, proclaiming salvation, saying: “Your God will reign.”

Rise, rise; put on your strength, O Zion. Put on (indere [induere], “put on”) your garments of glory, O Jerusalem, holy city.

For the uncircumcised and unclean will no longer pass through you. Shake yourself free from the dust; rise, sit, O Jerusalem. Loosen the bonds of your neck, captive daughter of Zion.

For thus says the Lord: “You were sold for nothing, and without silver you will be redeemed.”

For thus says the Lord God: “In the beginning my people went down into Egypt to dwell there as a settler, and Assyria oppressed him without cause.

[Col. 0851D] And now, what is mine?” says the Lord, “for my people has been taken away for nothing.

Its rulers act wickedly,” says the Lord, “and my name is continually blasphemed all day long.

Therefore my people will know my name on that day, for I am he—indeed, I am he who was speaking; behold, I am here.”

How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the evangelizer and the one proclaiming peace, announcing good things and proclaiming salvation, saying to Zion: “Your God will reign.”

The voice of your watchmen: they will raise their voice; together they will praise, for eye to eye they will see when the Lord restores Zion.

## XII. CANTICLE OF THE PROPHET ISAIAH. Chapter 56

[Col. 0852A]

**Antiphon.** “My salvation is near, that it may come, and my justice, that it may be revealed,” says the Lord.

Thus says the Lord: “Keep judgment and practice justice, because my salvation is near, that it may come, and my justice, that it may be revealed.

Blessed is the man who does this, and the son of man who grasps it,

keeping the sabbath so as not to profane it, keeping his hands from doing any evil.

And let not the son of the sojourner who adheres to the Lord say: ‘The Lord will surely separate me from his people.’

[Col. 0852B] And let not the eunuch say: ‘Behold, I am a dry tree.’ For thus says the Lord to the eunuchs:

‘Those who keep my sabbaths, choose what I desire, and hold fast to my covenant: I will give them in my house and within my walls a place and a name better than sons and daughters; I will give them an everlasting name that will not perish.

And the son of the sojourner who adheres to the Lord, to worship him, and who loves his name, to be his servants,

everyone who keeps the sabbath so as not to profane it and holds fast to my covenant—I will bring them to my holy mountain and make them rejoice in my house of prayer.

Their burnt offerings and sacrifices will please me upon my altar, for my house will be called a house of prayer for all peoples,’ says the Lord God, who gathers the dispersed of Israel.” [Col. 0852C]

## XIII. CANTICLE OF THE PROPHET ISAIAH. Chapter 62

**Antiphon.** Say to the daughter of Zion: “Behold, your savior comes.”

The Lord has sworn by his right hand and by the arm of his strength:

“If I give your grain any longer as food to your enemies, and if foreigners drink your wine for which you have labored,

then those who gather it will eat it and praise the Lord, and those who collect it will drink it in my holy courts.”

Pass through, pass through the gates; prepare the way for my people. Make the road level and choose the stones.

[Col. 0852D] Raise a sign for the peoples. Behold, the Lord has caused it to be heard to the ends of the earth.

Say to the daughter of Zion: “Behold, your Savior comes; behold, his reward is with him and his work is before him.”

And they will call them “Holy People,” “The Redeemed of the Lord”; but you will be called “A Sought-After City, Not Forsaken.”

## XIV. CANTICLE FROM THE GOSPEL ACCORDING TO LUKE. Chapter 1

**Antiphon.** He who is mighty has done great things for me, and holy is his name, and his mercy is from generation to generation.

My soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit will rejoice in God my Savior,

[Col. 0853A] [LXX] because he has looked upon the lowliness of his servant. For behold, from now on all generations will call me blessed.

For he who is mighty has done great things for me, and holy is his name; and his mercy is from generation to generation for those who fear him.

He has performed mighty deeds with his arm; he has scattered the proud in the thought and understanding of their heart.

He has brought down the powerful from their thrones and will exalt the humble.

He will fill the hungry with good things and has sent the rich away empty.

He has received Israel, his servant, remembering his mercy, as he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and to his offspring forever.

## XV. CANTICLE OF THE PROPHET ISAIAH. Chapter 45

[Col. 0853B]

**Antiphon.** Let the earth open and bring forth the Savior, and let justice arise together.

Drop dew, heavens, from above, and let the clouds rain down the righteous one.

Let the earth open and bring forth the Savior, and let justice arise together. I, the Lord, will create him.

Woe to the one who contradicts his maker, a potsherd among the potsherds of the earth.

Does clay say to its potter, “What are you doing?” and, “Your work is without hands”?

Woe to the one who says to his father, “What are you begetting?” and to the woman, “What are you giving birth to?”

Thus says the Lord, the Holy One of Israel, its maker: “Question me about things to come concerning my sons, and command me concerning the work of my hands.

[Col. 0853C] I made the earth, and I created the human being upon it. [Note: In the manuscript, this pronoun “I” occurs at the beginning of the following verse.] My hands stretched out the heavens, and I commanded all their host.

I will raise him up for justice, and I will direct all his ways.

He himself will build my city, and he will release my captives,

not for a price nor for gifts,” says the Lord of hosts.

Thus says the Lord: “The labor of Egypt, and the commerce of Ethiopia and the Sabaeans.

Tall men will pass over to you and will be yours; they will walk behind you, proceeding in fetters, and they will worship you [Col. 0853D] and entreat you.

Surely God is in you, and there is no other God besides you. Truly, you are a hidden God, God of Israel, Savior.

They have all been confused and put to shame together; the makers of errors have gone away in confusion. Israel is saved in the Lord with eternal salvation.

You will not be put to shame, and you will not be disgraced, forever and ever.

For thus says the Lord, creating the heavens—he is God, forming the earth and making it; he is its maker.

He did not create it in vain, but formed it to be inhabited.

[Col. 0854A] I am the Lord, and there is no other. I have not spoken in secret, in a dark place of the earth.

I have not said to the offspring of Jacob, ‘You seek me in vain.’ I am the Lord, speaking justice and announcing what is right.

Gather yourselves and come; draw near together, you who are saved from among the nations.

They know nothing, those who carry the wood of their carved image and pray to a god who cannot save.

Announce it and come, and take counsel together: who made this known from the beginning, who foretold it from that time?

Is it not I, the Lord, and is there no other God besides me? There is no God besides me, a just God and a savior; there is none except me.

Turn to me and be saved, all the ends of the earth, for I am the Lord, and there is no other.

[Col. 0854B] By myself I have sworn; a word of justice has gone forth from my mouth and will not return: “To me every knee will bow, and every tongue will swear.”

Therefore, in the Lord, they will say, “Righteousness and dominion are mine.” To him they will come, and all who oppose him will be put to shame.

In the Lord, all the offspring of Israel will be justified and will be praised.

## XVI. CANTICLE FROM THE GOSPEL ACCORDING TO LUKE. Chapter 2

**Antiphon.** I will glory in the Lord; I will rejoice in my God Jesus.

Now you dismiss your servant, Lord, according to your word, in peace, because my eyes have seen your salvation, [Col. 0854C]

which you have prepared before the face of all peoples:

a light for revelation to the nations, and the glory of your people Israel.

## XVII. [LXXI] CANTICLE OF THE PROPHET ISAIAH. Chapter 60

**Antiphon.** Shine, Jerusalem, for your light is present.

Rise, shine, Jerusalem, for your light has come, and the glory of the Lord has risen upon you.

For behold, darkness will cover the earth, and gloom the peoples.

But the Lord will rise upon you, and his glory will be seen in you.

[Col. 0854D] And the nations will walk in your light, and kings in the splendor of your rising.

Lift your eyes around and see: all these have gathered and come to you.

Your sons will come from far away, and your daughters will rise at your side.

Then you will see and overflow with abundance; your heart will wonder and expand.

When the multitude of the sea has been turned toward you, and the strength of the nations has come to you,

an inundation of camels will cover you, the dromedaries of Midian and Ephah.

[Col. 0855A] All those from Sheba will come, bringing gold and frankincense and announcing praise to the Lord.

All the flocks of Kedar will be gathered to you; the rams of Nebaioth will minister to you.

They will be offered upon my acceptable altar, and I will glorify the house of my majesty.

Who are these who fly like clouds and like doves to their windows?

For the islands will await me, and the ships of the sea at the beginning,

to bring your sons from far away, their silver and gold with them, in the name of the Lord your God, and of the Holy One of Israel, because he will glorify you.

And the sons of foreigners will build your walls, and their kings will minister to you.

[Col. 0855B] For in my indignation I struck you, but in my reconciliation I had mercy on you.

And your gates will continually be open, day and night; they will not be closed,

so that the strength of the nations may be brought to you, and their kings led in.

For the nation and kingdom that will not serve you will perish, and the nations will be laid waste in desolation.

The glory of Lebanon will come to you, the fir tree, the box tree, and the pine together, to adorn the place of my sanctuary; and I will glorify the place of my feet.

And the bowed sons of those who humbled you will come to you, and all who reviled you will worship the traces of your feet.

[Col. 0855C] And they will call you “City of the Lord, Zion of the Holy One of Israel,” because you were not forsaken or hated, and there was no one passing through you.

I will make you an everlasting pride, a joy from generation to generation.

And you will suck the milk of the nations and be nourished at the breasts of kings.

And you will know that I am the Lord, your Savior, and your mighty Redeemer, the God of Jacob.

For bronze I will bring gold, for iron I will bring silver, for wood bronze, and for stones iron.

And I will appoint your visitation as peace, and your overseers as justice.

Iniquity will no longer be heard in your land, nor devastation and destruction within your borders.

[Col. 0855D] And salvation will occupy your walls, and praise your gates.

The sun will no longer be your light by day, nor will the brightness of the moon illuminate you; rather, the Lord will be your everlasting light, and your God your glory.

Your sun will no longer set, and your moon will not diminish, because the Lord will be your everlasting light, and the days of your mourning will be completed.

But all your people will be righteous; they will inherit the land forever, a shoot of my planting, the work of my hands, for glorification.

The least will become a thousand, and the smallest a very strong nation.

[Col. 0856A] I am the Lord; in its time I will accomplish it suddenly.

## XVIII. CANTICLE OF THE PROPHET JEREMIAH. Chapter 31

Thus says the Lord: A voice was heard on the heights, lamentation, weeping, and wailing: Rachel weeping for her sons, and she refused to be comforted concerning them, because they are not.

Thus says the Lord: Let your voice cease from weeping and your eyes from tears, for there is a reward for your work, says the Lord.

And they will return from the land of the enemy, and there is hope for your future, says the Lord; and the sons will return to their borders.

I have surely heard Ephraim, who is migrating: “You chastised [Col. 0856B] me, and I was instructed, like an untrained young bull.”

[LXXII] “Convert me, and I will return, for you are my God.

For after you converted me, I did penance; and after you showed me understanding, I struck my thigh.

I was confused and ashamed, because I bore the reproach of my youth.

Is Ephraim an honorable son to me, a delightful child? For ever since I spoke of him, I will still remember him.

Therefore my inward parts are troubled over him; surely I will have mercy on him,” says the Lord.

Set up a watchtower for yourself; place bitter signs for yourself. Direct your heart onto the straight way by which you walked.

Return, virgin Israel; return to your cities. [Col. 0856C] How long will you dissolve in pleasures, wandering daughter? For the Lord will create a new thing upon the earth: A WOMAN WILL ENCIRCLE A MAN.

# THE CANTICLES TO BE RECITED DURING LENT BEGIN

## XIX. CANTICLE OF THE PROPHET ISAIAH. Chapter 58

Cry out without ceasing, says the Lord; raise your voice like a trumpet.

And announce to my people their crimes, and to the house of Jacob their sins.

For they seek me day after day and desire to know my ways.

[Col. 0856D] Like a nation that has practiced justice and has not abandoned the judgment of its God.

They ask me for judgments of justice; they desire to draw near to God.

“Why have we fasted and you have not looked upon us? We have humbled our souls and you did not know?”

Behold, on the day of your fasting your own will is found, and you exact all your debts.

Behold, you fast for quarrels and disputes, and you strike wickedly with your fist.

Do not fast as you have done until this day, so that your cry may be heard on high.

Is this the fast that I have chosen: for a day to afflict a person’s soul?

[Col. 0857A] Is it to bow his head like a reed and spread out sackcloth and ashes?

Will you call this a fast and a day acceptable to the Lord?

Is not this rather the fast that I have chosen:

to dissolve the bonds of wickedness, to loosen the bundles that oppress,

to set free those who are crushed, and to break every burden?

Break your bread for the hungry, and bring the poor and homeless into your house.

When you see the naked, cover him, and do not hide yourself from your own flesh.

Then your light will break forth like the morning, and your healing will quickly arise.

[Col. 0857B] And justice will go before your face, and the glory of the Lord will gather you.

Then you will call, and the Lord will answer; you will cry out, and he will say: “Behold, I am here.”

## XX. CANTICLE OF THE PROPHET JEREMIAH. Lamentations, Chapter 5

Remember, Lord, what has happened to us; look and see our reproach.

Our inheritance has been turned over to foreigners, our houses to strangers.

We have become orphans without a father; our mothers are like widows.

We drank our water for money, and we purchased our wood at a price.

[Col. 0857C] We bore the yoke upon our necks; no rest was given to the weary.

We gave our hand to Egypt, and to the Assyrians we gave our necks, so that we might be satisfied with bread.

Our fathers sinned and are no more, but we bear their iniquities.

Slaves have ruled over us, and there was no one to redeem us from their hands.

At the cost of our lives we brought bread to ourselves, in the face of the sword in the wilderness.

Our skin has been scorched like an oven, because of the storms of famine.

Women were humbled in Zion, and virgins in the cities of Judah.

Princes were hanged by the hand, and the faces of the elders [Col. 0857D] were not respected.

They abused young men shamefully, and boys fell beneath the wood.

The elders have ceased from the gates, and the young men from the chorus of singers.

The joy of our heart has ceased; our chorus has been turned into mourning. Our crown has fallen from our head. Woe to us, because we have sinned.

Therefore our heart has become mournful in sorrow; for this reason our eyes have been darkened, because of Mount Zion, which has been destroyed. Foxes have walked upon it.

[LXXIII] But you, Lord, remain forever, and your throne from generation to generation.

[Col. 0858A] Why then will you forget us forever? Why will you forsake us for the length of our days?

Convert us, Lord, to you, and we will be converted; renew our days as at the beginning.

But by rejecting, you have rejected us; you have been exceedingly angry with us.

## XXI. PRAYER OF JEREMIAH [NEHEMIAH] FROM THE SECOND BOOK OF EZRA. Chapter 1

**Antiphon.** Have mercy, O great and terrible God, who keeps the covenant and mercy with those who love you and keep your commandments.

I beseech you, Lord God of heaven, strong, great, and terrible, who keeps the covenant and mercy with those who love you and keep your commandments.

[Col. 0858B] Let your ear be attentive and your eyes open, so that you may hear the prayer of your servant, which I pray before you today, night and day, for the sons of Israel, your servants.

And I confess the sins of the sons of Israel, in which they have sinned against you; both I and my father’s house.

We have sinned; we have been led astray by vanity, and we have not kept the commandment, the ceremonies, and the judgments that you commanded Moses, your servant.

Remember the word that you commanded Moses, your servant, saying: “When you transgress, I will scatter you among the peoples.

And if you return to me and keep my commandments and do them, even if you have been driven to the end of heaven, from there I will gather you and bring you to the place that I chose, so that my name might dwell there.”

[Col. 0858C] And they are your servants and your people, whom you redeemed by your great strength and by your mighty hand.

I beseech you, Lord: let your ear be attentive to the prayer of your servant and to the prayers of your servants who desire to fear your name.

And direct your servant today, and grant him mercy before this man.

## XXII. PRAYER OF KING MANASSEH FROM THE BOOK OF CHRONICLES

**Antiphon.** I have sinned, Lord, I have sinned, and I myself acknowledge my iniquity.

Most High God, long-suffering, merciful, and rich in mercy, patient toward human evils:

Therefore, Lord, according to the abundance of your goodness, you promised indulgence and forgiveness to those who sin against you, [Col. 0858D] and in the abundance of your mercy you established repentance for sinners unto salvation.

Therefore, Lord God of the righteous, you did not appoint repentance for your righteous ones, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, who did not sin against you; but you appointed repentance for me, a sinner, because my iniquities have multiplied beyond the number of the sand of the sea, and there is no turning away from the multitude of my offenses.

And now I am justly confined and deservedly restrained, bound with many iron chains, unable to raise my head.

For I am not worthy to look upon and see the height of heaven, because of my injustices.

For I provoked your anger and did evil before [Col. 0859A] you, establishing abominations and multiplying hateful things.

And now I bend the knees of my heart, asking you for goodness.

I have sinned, Lord, I have sinned, and I myself acknowledge my iniquity.

Do not destroy me with my iniquities, nor restrain me in anger forever because of my evils; do not condemn me with those who are in the regions below (inferibus; [inferioribus], “lower”) of the earth.

For you are the God of those who repent, so that you may show your goodness in me.

You will save me, though unworthy, according to the abundance of your mercy, and I will glorify your name all my life.

For every power of the heavens praises you, and yours is the glory forever and ever.

## XXIII. CANTICLE OF TOBIT. Chapter 13

Great are you, Lord, forever, and your kingdom throughout all ages.

For you scourge and save; you lead down to the underworld and bring back, and there is no one who can escape your hand.

Confess to the Lord, sons of Israel, and praise him in the sight of the nations.

For this reason he scattered you among nations that do not know him, so that you might proclaim his wonders and make them know that there is no other almighty God besides him.

He himself will chastise us because of our iniquities, [LXXIV] and he himself will save us because of his mercy. [Col. 0859C]

Consider, therefore, what he has done with you. Confess to him with fear and trembling, and praise the King of the ages; praise and exult in him through your works.

But I, in the land of my captivity, will confess to him, because he has shown his majesty over a sinful nation.

Therefore, sinners, turn back and practice justice before God, believing that he will show you his mercy.

But I and my soul will rejoice in God.

Bless the Lord, all his elect; celebrate a day of joy and confess to him.

## XXIV. PRAYER FROM THE BOOK OF JESUS. Chapter 36

[Col. 0859D]

Have mercy on us, God of all, and look upon us; show us the light of your mercy.

Send your fear upon the nations that have not sought you, so that they may know that there is no God but you, and may proclaim your mighty deeds.

Raise your hand over foreign nations, so that they may see your power.

For just as you were sanctified among them through us, so you will be magnified among them in our sight, so that they may know you as we also have known you: that there is no God besides you, Lord.

Renew signs and change wonders.

Glorify your hand and your right arm.

[Col. 0860A] Stir up fury and pour out wrath.

Raise up the adversary and afflict the enemy.

Hasten the time and remember the end, so that they may proclaim your mighty deeds.

May sinners be consumed in the flame of anger, and may those who mistreat your people find destruction.

Crush the head of the wicked rulers who say, “There is no one besides us.”

Gather all the tribes of Jacob, and let them know that there is no God but you, so that they may proclaim your mighty deeds; and you will inherit them as from the beginning.

Have mercy on your people, upon whom your name has been invoked, and on Israel, whom you equated with your firstborn.

Have mercy on your holy city, Jerusalem, [Col. 0860B] the city of your rest.

Fill Zion with your ineffable mighty works, and your people with your glory.

Bear witness that they are yours from the beginning of creation, and raise up the prayers that the former prophets spoke in your name.

Give a reward to those who endure for you, so that prophetui [prophetae tui, “your prophets”] may be found faithful; and hear the prayers of your servants.

According to the blessing of Aaron, give to your people, and direct us in the way of justice.

So that all who inhabit the earth may know that you are God throughout the ages.

## XXV. CANTICLE OF ZECHARIAH [AZARIAH] FROM THE BOOK OF DANIEL. Chapter 3

[Col. 0860C]

**Antiphon.** Whatever you have done to us, Lord, you have done in true judgment, and all these things are because of our sins.

**Another.** You are just, Lord, in everything that you have done to us, and all your works are truth, and your ways are right.

Blessed are you, Lord, God of our fathers, and worthy of praise; and glorious is your name forever.

For you are just in all that you have done for us, and all your works and your ways are right; and all your judgments are true.

For you have executed true judgments in everything that you have brought upon us, and upon the holy city of our fathers, Jerusalem.

For in truth and in judgment you have brought all these things upon us [Col. 0860D] because of our sins.

For we have sinned and acted wickedly by turning away from you; we have offended in everything, and have neither listened to nor observed your commandments, nor done as you commanded us, so that it might be well with us.

Therefore, everything that you have brought upon us, and all that you have done to us, you have done by true judgment.

And you have delivered us into the hands of unjust, exceedingly wicked, and transgressing enemies, and into the hand of an unjust and exceedingly wicked king, beyond all the earth.

And now we cannot open our mouth; we have become a disgrace and reproach to your servants and to those who worship you.

Do not, we beseech you, hand us over forever for the sake of your name; do not destroy your covenant, and do not take your mercy away from us.

[Col. 0861A] For the sake of Abraham, your beloved, and Isaac, your servant, and Israel, your holy one, to whom you spoke, promising that you would multiply their offspring [LXXV] like the stars of heaven and like the sand on the seashore.

For, Lord, we have been diminished more than all the nations, and today we are humbled throughout the whole earth because of our sins.

And at this time there is neither prince nor prophet nor leader, neither burnt offering nor sacrifice nor offering nor incense, nor a place where we can offer the firstfruits before you, so that we might find your mercy.

But may we be received with a contrite soul and a humble spirit, as with the burnt offerings of rams and bulls, and as with thousands of fat lambs; so may our sacrifice [Col. 0861B] be in your presence today and be pleasing to you.

And bring to completion those who follow you, for there is no shame for those who trust in you.

And now we follow you with our whole heart and fear you, and we seek your face; do not put us to shame.

But deal with us according to your gentleness and according to the abundance of your mercy; deliver us by your wonders and give glory to your name, Lord.

Let all who inflict evils upon your servants be put to shame; let them be put to shame in all their power, and let their strength be crushed.

And let them know that you alone are the Lord, and glorious throughout the whole world.

## XXVI. The Canticles of the Betrayal of the Lord Begin. The Canticle from the Second Book of Maccabees. Chapter 1

[Col. 0861C]

Antiphon. Lord, Lord, God of all, creator, terrible and strong, just and merciful: gather our dispersed people and deliver those who serve the nations.

Another. Lord, Lord, look upon the despised and abhorred; afflict those who oppress and insult in their arrogance, so that the nations may know that you are our God.

Lord, Lord, God of all, creator, terrible, strong, and merciful.

You alone are the good king, alone excellent, alone just, almighty and eternal.

You who deliver Israel from every evil, who chose our fathers and sanctified them.

[Col. 0861D] Receive a sacrifice for all your people Israel, and guard your portion and sanctify our dispersion.

Deliver those who serve the nations; look upon the despised and abhorred, so that the nations may know that you are the Lord our God.

Afflict those who oppress and insult in arrogance.

Establish your people in your holy place, as Moses said.

## XXVII. The Canticle of the Prophet Jeremiah. Chapter 11

Antiphon. Like a gentle lamb led to the slaughter, I was led.

[Col. 0862A] But you, Lord, showed me, and I knew.

Now you have shown me their designs, and you have saved my life from my persecutors.

And I was like a gentle lamb being carried to the slaughter; now I knew that they had devised schemes against me.

“Let us put wood in his bread, and let us wipe him from the land of the living, so that his name may no longer be remembered.”

But you, Lord of hosts, who judge justly and test the kidneys and the heart, let me see your vengeance upon them, for to you I have revealed my cause.

You are indeed just, Lord, if I dispute with you; nevertheless, I shall speak justly to you.

Why does the way of the wicked prosper? Why is it well with all [Col. 0862B] who transgress and act wickedly?

You planted them, and they took root; they advance and bear fruit.

You are near to their lips, but far from their kidneys.

And you, Lord, know me and have seen me, and you have tested my heart before you.

Gather them like a flock for slaughter, and sanctify them for the day of slaughter.

## XXVIII. The Canticle of the Prophet Jeremiah. Chapter 15

You know, Lord; remember me, visit me, and protect me from those who persecute [Col. 0862C] me.

Do not receive me in your patience; know that I have endured reproach for your sake. Your words were found, and I consumed them.

And your word became for me joy and gladness of heart, because your name was invoked over me, Lord God of hosts.

[LXXVI] I did not sit in the assembly of those who mocked, and I gloried.

Because of the threat of your hand I sat alone, for you filled me with indignation.

Why has my pain become perpetual, and my wound incurable, refusing to be healed?

It became for me like a deceptive stream, like unreliable waters.

[Col. 0862D] Therefore the Lord says this: “If you return, I will restore you, and you shall stand before my face.

And if you separate what is precious from what is worthless, you shall be as my mouth.

They shall turn to you, but you shall not turn to them.

And I will make you for this people a strong bronze wall; they will fight against you, but they will not prevail, because I am with you to save you and deliver you,” says the Lord.

“And I will deliver you from the hand of the wicked, and redeem you from the hand of the powerful.”

## XXIX. The Canticle of the Prophet Jeremiah. Chapter 18

[Col. 0863A]

Attend to me, Lord, and hear the voice of my adversaries.

Should evil be repaid for good? For they have dug a pit for my soul.

Remember that I stood before you to speak good on their behalf and to turn your indignation away from them.

Therefore give their children over to famine, and deliver them into the hand of the sword.

Let their wives be childless and widows, and let their husbands be killed by death.

Let their young men be pierced by the sword in battle; let a cry be heard [Col. 0863B] from their houses.

For you will bring a marauder suddenly upon them, because they dug a pit to capture me and hid snares for my feet.

But you, Lord, know all their counsel against me, directed toward death.

Do not forgive their iniquity, and do not erase their sin from before your face.

Let them fall before you; in the time of your anger, deal with them.

## XXX. The Canticle of the Prophet Jeremiah. Chapter 20

Antiphon. Lord, let those who persecute me fall and become weak. [Col. 0863C]

You enticed me, Lord, and I was enticed; you were stronger than I and prevailed.

I have become a laughingstock; all day long everyone mocks me.

For whenever I speak, I cry out; I proclaim violence and devastation.

And the word of the Lord has become for me reproach and mockery all day long. I said, “I will not remember him, nor speak any longer in his name.”

And it became in my heart like a burning fire, shut up in my bones; I grew weary and could not endure it.

For I heard the insults of many, and terror on every side.

“Pursue him, and let us pursue him,” from all the men who had been at peace with me and watching my flank.

“Perhaps he will be deceived, and we shall prevail against him and take our revenge on him.”

But the Lord is with me like a mighty warrior; therefore those who persecute me will fall and become weak.

They will be utterly put to shame, because they have not understood an everlasting disgrace that will never be erased.

And you, Lord of hosts, tester of the just, who test the kidneys and the heart, let me see your vengeance upon them, for to you I have revealed my cause.

## XXX. The Canticle of the Prophet Jeremiah. Chapter 23

[Col. 0864A]

My heart is broken within me; all my bones trembled.

I have become like a drunken man, like a man overcome by wine,

because of the Lord and because of the words of his holiness.

For the land is filled with adulterers; because of the curse the land mourns, and the pastures of the wilderness have dried up.

Their course has become evil, and their strength unlike what it was.

For both prophet and priest are polluted; in my house I found their evil, says the Lord.

[Col. 0864B] Therefore their way shall be like a slippery path in darkness; they shall be driven forward and fall upon it.

For I will bring evils upon them in the year of their visitation, says the Lord.

## XXXII. The Canticle of the Prophet Jeremiah [Micah]. Chapter 7

Antiphon. Do not believe a friend, and do not trust a leader, for a man’s enemies are the members of his own household.

[LXXVII] Do not believe a friend, and do not trust a leader; guard the doors of your mouth from her who lies in your bosom.

For a son dishonors his father, a daughter rises against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law; a man’s enemies are the members of his own household.

[Col. 0864C] But I will look to the Lord; I will wait for God my savior. My God will hear me.

Do not rejoice over me, my enemy; though I have fallen, I shall rise.

Though I sit in darkness, the Lord is my light. I will bear the Lord’s anger, because I have sinned against him,

until he judges my cause and executes my judgment; he will bring me out into the light, and I shall see his justice.

My enemy will look and be covered with shame, she who says to me, “Where is the Lord your God?”

## XXXIII. The Canticle of the Prophet Ezekiel. Chapter 36

Antiphon. I will pour clean water over you, says the Lord, [Col. 0864D] and you shall be cleansed from all your defilements.

I will take you from the nations and gather you from all the lands, and I will bring you into your land.

I will pour clean water over you, and you shall be cleansed from all your defilements; and I will cleanse you from all your idols.

And I will give you a new heart, and I will put my spirit within you.

I will take the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh; and I will put my spirit within you.

And I will make you walk in my commandments, and you shall keep my judgments and observe them.

And you shall dwell in the land that I gave to your fathers; [Col. 0865A] you shall be my people, and I shall be your God.

## XXXIV. The Canticles of the Resurrection of the Lord Begin. The Canticle from the Book of Genesis. Chapter 49

Antiphon. You have gone up for prey, Lord; you have lain down to rest like a lion, and by your strength you have risen.

Your brothers shall praise you, Judah; your hand shall be upon the necks of your enemies.

The sons of your father shall worship you; Judah is a lion’s cub.

For prey you have gone up, my son; resting, you have lain down like a lion, and like a lioness—who will rouse him?

The scepter shall not be taken from Judah, nor the ruler from his loins, until he comes who is to be sent; and he [Col. 0865B] shall be the expectation of the nations.

Tying his colt to the vine, and his donkey, my son, to the vine.

He will wash his robe in wine and his cloak in the blood of grapes.

His eyes are more beautiful than wine, and his teeth whiter than milk.

He sat firm with his bow; the bonds of his arms and his hands were loosened by the hand of God Almighty. From there Jacob, the shepherd, went forth—the stone of Israel.

The God of your father shall be your helper, and the Almighty shall bless you

with blessings from heaven above, with blessings of the abyss lying below,

with blessings of breasts and womb. The blessings [Col. 0865C] of your father are strengthened

by the blessings of his fathers, until the desire of the everlasting hills should come.

May they come upon the head of Joseph and upon the crown of the Nazirite among his brothers.

## XXXV. The Canticle of the Prophet Isaiah. Chapter 43

Antiphon. Do not consider the former things; I will do new things, says the Lord.

Before me no god was formed, and after me there shall be none.

I am, I am the Lord, and there is no savior besides me.

[Col. 0865D] I announced and saved; I made it known, and there was no foreign god among you.

You are my witnesses, says the Lord, and I am God from the beginning.

I myself am he, and there is no one who can deliver from my hand; I shall act, and who can turn it back?

Thus says the Lord, your redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: for your sake I sent to Babylon and brought down all the bars, and the Chaldeans rejoicing in their ships.

I am the Lord, your Holy One, creator of Israel, your king.

Thus says the Lord, who made a way in the sea and a path in the rushing waters,

who brought out chariot and horse, army and strong force together; they slept, and they would not rise again.

[LXXVIII] They were crushed like flax and extinguished; do not remember former things, and do not consider ancient things.

[Col. 0866A] Behold, I am doing new things, and now they shall arise; surely you will know them.

I will make a way in the wilderness and rivers in the desert; the beasts of the field, the dragons and ostriches, will glorify me.

For I gave water in the wilderness and rivers in the desert, to give drink to my people, my chosen people. I formed this people for myself; it shall proclaim my praise.

## XXXVI. The Canticle of the Prophet Isaiah. Chapter 63

Antiphon. My arm saved me, and my justice itself came to my aid.

Who is this who comes from Edom, with garments stained from [Col. 0866B] Bozrah?

This one is glorious in his robe, advancing in the greatness of his strength.

I am the one who speaks justice, and I am a champion for saving.

Why, then, is your garment red, and your clothing like that of one who treads the winepress?

I have trodden the winepress alone, and from the nations no man was with me.

I trod them in my fury and trampled them in my anger; their blood was sprinkled upon my garments, and I stained all my clothing.

For the day of vengeance is in my heart, and the year of my recompense has come.

I looked around, and there was no helper; I sought, and [Col. 0866C] there was no one to assist.

My arm saved me, and my justice itself came to my aid.

I trampled peoples in my fury and made them drunk in my indignation; I brought down their strength to the earth.

## XXXVII. The Canticle of the Prophet Isaiah [Jeremiah]. Chapter 31

Antiphon. I have been awakened as if from sleep, and I saw; and my sleep was sweet to me.

Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: “This word will still be spoken in the land of Judah and in its cities when I restore their captivity.”

[Col. 0866D] “May the Lord bless you, beauty of justice, holy mountain; and Judah and all its cities shall dwell in it, together with farmers and those who lead flocks.”

For I will refresh the weary soul and satisfy every hungry soul.

Therefore I was awakened as if from sleep, and I saw; and my sleep was sweet to me.

Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, when I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of humans and the seed of animals.

And just as I watched over them to uproot, demolish, destroy, scatter, and afflict, so I will watch over them to build and plant, says the Lord.

## XXXVIII. The Canticle of the Prophet Isaiah [Hosea]. Chapter 6

[Col. 0867A]

Antiphon. The Lord will revive us after two days; on the third day he will raise us up, and we shall live.

Come, let us return to the Lord, for he has seized us, and he will heal us; he will strike us and heal us.

He will revive us after two days; on the third day he will raise us up, and we shall live in his presence. We shall know, and we shall follow on to know the Lord.

His going forth is prepared like the dawn; he will come to us like the early and latter rain upon the earth.

What shall I do for you, Ephraim? What shall I do for you, Judah? Your mercy is like the morning cloud and like the dew that passes away [Col. 0867B] in the morning.

Therefore I have hewn them by the prophets and slain them by the word of my mouth; and my judgments shall go forth like the light.

For I desired mercy and not sacrifice, and knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.

## XXXIX. The Canticle of the Prophet Zephaniah. Chapter 3

Antiphon. Wait for me on the day of my resurrection, says the Lord, when I gather the nations and assemble the kingdoms.

Wait for me, says the Lord, on the day of my resurrection in the future, for my judgment is to gather the nations and assemble the kingdoms.

To pour out upon them all my indignation and all the anger of my fury.

[Col. 0867C] For in the fire of my zeal the whole earth shall be consumed; for then I will give the peoples a chosen lip [LXXIX], so that all may call upon the name of the Lord and serve him with one shoulder.

From beyond the rivers of Ethiopia, my suppliants, the children of my dispersed ones, shall bring me an offering.

On that day you shall not be put to shame because of all your inventions by which you transgressed against me.

For then I will remove from your midst those who exult in your arrogance, and you shall no longer continue to exalt yourself on my holy mountain.

And I will leave in your midst a poor and needy people, and the remnant of Israel shall hope in the name of the Lord.

They shall commit no iniquity and speak no falsehood; [Col. 0867D] no deceitful tongue shall be found in their mouths.

For they themselves shall feed and lie down, and there shall be no one to terrify them.

# The Canticles of the Saints Begin

## XL. The Canticle of Jesus Son of Sirach. Chapter 26

The gift of God remains with the righteous, and its benefit will have lasting success.

Blessed is the husband of a good wife; the number of their years is doubled.

A strong woman delights her husband and fills his years with peace.

[Col. 0868A] A good portion is a good wife; she is given as a good portion to those who fear God, and to a man for his good deeds.

## XLI. The Canticle from the Book of Judges. Chapter 5

Antiphon. May those who love you, Lord, shine like the sun at its rising.

You who willingly offered your lives from Israel to danger, bless the Lord.

Hear, kings; listen, rulers: I am, I am the one who will sing to the Lord; I will chant to the Lord, the God of Israel.

Lord, when you went out from Seir and passed through the regions of Edom, the earth shook and the heavens and clouds dripped with water.

[Col. 0868B] The mountains melted before the Lord, and Sinai before God, the God of Israel.

The Lord chose new battles and himself overturned the gates of the enemies.

When shield and spear appeared among the forty thousand of Israel, my heart loved the leaders of Israel.

You who willingly offered yourselves to danger, bless the Lord.

You who willingly offered yourselves to danger, bless the Lord.

You who ride upon shining donkeys and sit in judgment and walk on the road, speak where the chariots were shattered and the army of the enemy was suffocated.

There let the Lord’s justice and his mercy toward the strong in Israel be recounted.

Then the people of the Lord went down to the gates and gained supremacy.

[Col. 0868C] The remnant of the people was saved; the Lord fought among the strong.

Kings came and fought; the kings of Canaan fought at Taanach beside the waters of Megiddo, yet they took no plunder. Heaven fought against them.

So may all your enemies perish, Lord; but may those who love you shine like the sun at its rising.

## XLII. The Canticle of the Prophet Isaiah. Chapter 61

Antiphon. Everlasting joy shall belong to my chosen ones when I give them their works in truth.

You shall be called the holy ones of the Lord; you shall be called ministers of our God.

[Col. 0868D] You shall consume the strength of the nations and boast in their glory.

For your double shame and disgrace, they shall praise their portion; therefore they shall possess double in their land.

Everlasting joy shall be theirs, for I am the Lord, who love judgment and hate robbery for a burnt offering.

And I will give their work in truth, and I will make an everlasting covenant with them.

Their offspring shall be known among the nations, and their descendants in the midst of the peoples.

All who see them shall recognize them, for they are the offspring whom the Lord has blessed.

# The Canticles of One Just Man Begin

## XLIII. The Canticle of the Prophet Jeremiah. Chapter 17

[Col. 0869A]

Blessed is the man who trusts in the Lord, and the Lord shall be his confidence.

He shall be like a tree planted beside streams of water, sending its roots toward moisture; he shall not fear when the heat comes.

Its leaf shall be green, and in the time of [LXXX] drought it shall not be anxious, nor shall it ever cease to bear fruit.

Heal me, Lord, and I shall be healed; save me, and I shall be saved, for you are my praise and my strength.

Behold, they say to me, “Where is the word of the Lord? Let it come.” But I was not troubled, following you as shepherd, and I did not desire the day of man; you know.

What went forth from my lips was right in your sight.

Let there be no fear for me; you are my hope on the day of my affliction.

Let all who persecute me be put to shame, but let me not be put to shame; let them be terrified, but let me not be terrified.

Bring upon them the day of affliction, and crush them with double destruction.

## XLIV. The Canticle of Jesus Son of Sirach. Chapter 51

Antiphon. To the one who gives me wisdom I will give glory; I resolved to practice it, and I was zealous for what is good, so that I might not be put to shame.

Before I went astray, I sought wisdom; openly, in my prayer.

Before the appointed time I asked for it, and until the end I will seek it.

It blossomed like an early grape; my heart rejoiced in it.

My foot walked on a straight path; from my youth I sought it.

I inclined my ear a little and received it; I found much wisdom for myself and made great progress in it.

To the one who gives me wisdom I will give glory; I resolved to practice it, and I was zealous for what is good, so that I might not be put to shame.

My soul struggled [possibly “wrestled”] with it, and in practicing it I was strengthened.

I stretched out my hand on high and lamented its ignorance.

I directed my soul toward it, and in knowledge I found it.

From the beginning I possessed a heart with them; therefore I shall not be abandoned.

My belly was troubled in seeking it; therefore I shall possess a good possession.

For the Lord gave me a tongue as my reward, and with it I shall praise him.

Draw near to me, you who are unlearned, and gather yourselves into the house of instruction.

[Col. 0870A] Why do you still delay, or what do you say? Your souls thirst intensely.

I opened my mouth and spoke: acquire wisdom for yourselves without silver, and submit your necks to its yoke.

Your soul shall receive instruction, for finding it is near.

See with your eyes that I have labored little, and I have found much rest for myself.

Acquire instruction at great cost of silver, and possess abundant gold through it.

Let your soul rejoice in its mercy, and you shall not be put to shame in its praise.

Perform your work before the appointed time, and it will give you your reward at its proper time.

## XLV. The Canticle of the Prophet Isaiah. Chapter 42

[Col. 0870B]

Behold, my servant; I will receive him, my chosen one, says the Lord; my soul has been pleased with him.

I have put my spirit upon him; he will bring judgment to the nations.

He will not cry out, nor show partiality, nor will his voice be heard outside.

He will not break a bruised reed, nor extinguish a smoldering wick.

He will bring forth judgment in truth; he will not be sad or turbulent until he establishes judgment on the earth, and the islands shall await his law.

## XLVI. The Canticle of the Prophet Zechariah. Luke, Chapter 1

[Col. 0870C]

Antiphon. And you, child, shall be called the prophet of the Most High, for you will go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways, to give knowledge of salvation to his people.

Blessed is the Lord God of Israel, for he has visited and accomplished redemption for his people.

And he has raised up for us a horn of salvation in the house of David, his servant.

As he spoke through the mouth of his holy prophets, who have been from of old.

Salvation from our enemies and from the hand of all who hate us.

To show mercy to our fathers and to remember his holy covenant, [Col. 0870D] the oath that he swore to Abraham our father, that he would grant us, delivered from the hand of our enemies without fear, to serve him in holiness and righteousness before him all our days.

And you, child, shall be called the prophet of the Most High, [LXXXI] for you will go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways,

to give knowledge of salvation to his people in the forgiveness of sins,

through the merciful compassion of our God, by which the dawn from on high will visit us,

to enlighten those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, and to guide our feet into the way of peace.

# The Canticles of Virgins Begin

## XLVII. The Canticle of Jesus Son of Sirach. Chapter 39

[Col. 0871A]

Antiphon. In the songs of your lips, say to the Lord: all your works are exceedingly good.

Hear me, divine offspring, and flourish like a rose planted beside streams of water.

Be like Lebanon; possess the fragrance of sweetness.

Bloom like flowers, like a lily; give fragrance, put forth leaves in grace, and sing a hymn of praise; bless the Lord in his works.

Give magnificence to his name, and confess him with the voice of your lips, with songs of the lips and with lyres; and thus you shall say in confession: all the works of the Lord [Col. 0871B] are exceedingly good.

## XLVIII. The Canticle of the Prophet Isaiah. Chapters 61 and 62

I will rejoice greatly in the Lord, and my soul shall exult in my God.

For he has clothed me with the garment of salvation and wrapped me in the robe of righteousness,

like a bridegroom adorned with a crown and like a bride adorned with her jewels.

For just as the earth produces its shoot and as a garden makes its seed germinate, so the Lord God will make righteousness and praise germinate before all the nations.

For Zion’s sake I will not be silent, and for Jerusalem’s sake [Col. 0871C] I will not rest until her righteousness goes forth like splendor and her savior is kindled like a lamp.

And the nations shall see your righteousness, and all the kings of the earth your renowned one.

And you shall be called by a new name, which the mouth of the Lord shall name.

And you shall be a crown of glory in the hand of the Lord and a diadem of the kingdom in the hand of your God.

You shall no longer be called “Forsaken,” and your land shall no longer be called “Desolate.”

But you shall be called “My Delight Is in Her,” and your land shall be inhabited.

For the Lord has taken delight in you, and your land shall be inhabited.

[Col. 0871D] For a young man shall dwell with a virgin, and your sons shall dwell in you.

And as a bridegroom rejoices over a bride, so your God shall rejoice over you.

Upon your walls, Jerusalem, I have appointed watchmen; all day and all night they shall never be silent.

You who remember the Lord, do not be silent, and do not give him silence until he establishes and until he makes Jerusalem a praise on the earth.

## XLIX. The Canticle of the Prophet Zephaniah. Chapter 3

Sing praise, daughter of Zion; shout, Israel; rejoice and exult with all your heart, daughter of Jerusalem.

[Col. 0872A] The Lord has removed your judgment; he has turned away your enemies. The king of Israel, the Lord, is in your midst; you shall no longer fear evil.

On that day it shall be said to Jerusalem: “Do not fear”; and to Zion: “Let not your hands grow slack.”

The Lord your God, the mighty one, is in your midst; he himself will save you.

He will rejoice over you with gladness; he will be silent in his love, and he will exult over you with praise.

I will gather the idlers who have departed from the law, who were from you, so that you may no longer bear reproach concerning them.

Behold, at that time I will kill all who afflicted you; I will save the lame and gather her [them] who had been cast out.

[Col. 0872B] And I will make them a praise and a name throughout the whole land of their shame.

At that time when I bring you in, and at the time when I gather you,

I will make you a name and a praise among all the peoples of the earth, when I restore your captivity before your eyes, says the Lord God.

## L. The Canticle of the Prophet Zechariah. Chapter 2

Sing praise and rejoice, daughter of Zion, for behold, I am coming and will dwell in your midst, says the Lord.

[LXXXII] And many nations shall join themselves to the Lord on that day, and they shall become my people, and I will dwell in your midst; and you shall know that the Lord of hosts has sent [Col. 0872C] me to you.

And the Lord shall possess Judah as his portion in the sanctified land, and he shall again choose Jerusalem.

Let all flesh be silent before the Lord, for he has risen from his holy dwelling.

## LI. The Canticle of Solomon at the Dedication of the Basilica. 2 Chronicles, Chapter 6

Antiphon. Lord, let your eyes be open over this house.

Lord God of Israel, there is no god like you in heaven and on earth, who keep covenant and mercy with your servants who walk before you with [Col. 0872D] their whole heart.

You have kept for your servant David, my father, whatever you spoke to him; what you promised long ago, you fulfilled by your work, as the present time also proves.

Now therefore, Lord God of Israel, fulfill for your servant David, my father, whatever you spoke to him, saying:

“No man from you shall fail before me who will sit upon the throne of Israel,

provided that your sons guard my ways and walk in my law, just as you have walked before me.”

And now, Lord God of Israel, let your word be confirmed which you spoke to your servant David.

Is it therefore not [or, perhaps: is it] credible that God should dwell with human beings upon the earth?

[Col. 0873A] If heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain you, how much less this house that I have built!

But it was made for this purpose only: that you may look upon the prayer and supplication of your servant.

My Lord God, hear the prayers that your servant pours out before you, so that you may open your eyes over this house, by day and by night, over the place where you promised that your name would be invoked; and hear the prayer that your servant prays in it.

Hear the prayers of your servant and of your people Israel, whoever prays in this place.

Hear from your holy dwelling, that is, from the heavens, and be gracious, for you are my God.

Let your eyes, I beseech you, be opened, and let your ears be attentive to the prayer that is made in this place.

[Col. 0873B] Now therefore arise, Lord God, to your rest, you and the ark of your holiness.

Let your priests, Lord God, be clothed with righteousness, and let your holy ones rejoice in good things.

Lord God, do not turn away the face of your anointed; remember the mercies shown to your servant David.

## LII. The Canticle of the Restoration of the Basilica. Tobit, Chapter 13

You shall shine with bright light throughout all the ends of the earth.

Many nations shall come to you from afar, and inhabitants from the remotest parts of the earth, to the name of the Lord God.

And carrying their gifts in their hands, they shall offer them to the King of heaven [Col. 0873C] with joy; and the name of the Lord shall be great throughout all ages.

Cursed are all who despise you, and all who blaspheme you.

Cursed are all who hate you, and all who have spoken a harsh word against you.

Cursed are all who cast you down, and all who destroy your walls, and all who overturn your towers, and all who burn your dwellings; but blessed shall be all who love you forever.

Then rejoice and be glad with the children of the righteous, for all shall be gathered together and shall bless the Lord forever.

Happy are those who love you; happy are those who rejoice in your peace; and happy are all people who grieve over your scourges, for they shall rejoice over all your joy forever.

My soul shall bless the great King, the Lord, for he will deliver Jerusalem; and his house shall be rebuilt. Throughout all ages it shall give thanks to the King of heaven.

The gates of Jerusalem shall be built of emerald (izmaragdus) and sapphire, and all your walls of precious stones.

The towers of Jerusalem shall be built with jewels, and its battlements with pure gold.

The streets of Jerusalem shall sing a song of joy, and “Alleluia” shall be sung throughout all its lanes.

Blessed is the Lord who exalts you, and blessed [Col. 0874A] throughout all ages, for in you every holy person shall be blessed forever.

## LIII. The Canticle of Balaam from the Book of Numbers. Chapter 23

Taking up his parable, Balaam said: “Balak, king of Moab, brought me from Aram, from the mountains of the east.

‘Come,’ he said, ‘and curse Jacob; hurry and denounce Israel.’

How can I curse one whom the Lord has not cursed? Or how can I denounce one whom God has not denounced?

From the tops of the crags I shall see him, and from the hills I shall behold him.

[Col. 0874B] For this people shall dwell alone and shall not be reckoned among the nations.

Who can count the dust of Jacob or know the number of the descendants of Israel?

May my soul die the death of the righteous, and may my end be like theirs.

God is not like a human being, that he should lie, nor like a son of man, that he should change.”

## LIV. The Canticle from an Apostle. First Epistle to Timothy, Chapters 4 and 6

Take hold of eternal life, to which you have been called, and you have confessed the good confession before many witnesses.

Be an example to the faithful in word, in conduct, [Col. 0874C] in charity, in faith, and in chastity.

Until I come, attend to reading, exhortation, and teaching.

Do not neglect the grace that is in you, which was given to you through prophecy with the laying on of hands.

Meditate on these things; be occupied with them, so that your progress may be manifest to all.

Attend to yourself and to teaching; persist in them.

For by doing this you will save both yourself and those who hear you.

## LV. The Daily Canticles Begin. The Canticle of Moses from the Book of Exodus. Chapter 15

Let us sing to the Lord, for he has been gloriously honored.

Horse and rider he has thrown into the sea.

[Col. 0874D] The Lord is my helper and protector, and he has become my salvation.

This is my God, and I will honor him; the God of my father, and I will exalt him.

The Lord is the one who crushes wars; the Lord is his name. Pharaoh’s chariots and his army he threw into the sea.

His chosen mounted warriors, three by three, he plunged into the Red Sea; the deep covered them, and they sank into the depths like a stone.

Your right hand, Lord, has been glorified in strength; your right hand has shattered the enemies, and by the greatness of your majesty you have crushed your adversaries.

You sent forth your anger, and it consumed them like stubble; by the breath of your wrath the water was divided.

[Col. 0875A] They stood like a wall of water; the waves froze in the midst of the sea.

The enemy said, pursuing: “I will overtake them, I will divide the spoils, I will fill my soul; I will kill with my sword, and my hand shall rule.”

You sent forth your spirit, and the sea covered them; they sank like lead in mighty waters.

Who is like you among the gods, O Lord? Who is like you, glorious, among the holy, wondrous in majesty, performing marvels?

You stretched out your right hand, and the earth swallowed them. You guided this people of yours in your righteousness, the people whom you redeemed.

You led them by your strength to your holy dwelling-place.

The nations heard and were enraged; pains seized the inhabitants of Philistia. [Col. 0875B]

Then the chiefs of Edom hastened, and the leaders of Moab were seized by fear; all the inhabitants of Canaan melted away.

Let fear and trembling fall upon them because of the greatness of your arm; let them become like stone until your people, O Lord, pass over—until this people of yours passes over, whom you redeemed.

Bring them in and plant them on the mountain of your inheritance, in the dwelling-place you prepared for yourself, the sanctuary, O Lord, which your hands prepared. O Lord, you reign forever and ever, and beyond.

[Col. 0875C] For Pharaoh’s cavalry will enter with chariots and horsemen into the sea, and the Lord brought the waters of the sea over them; but the children of Israel walked on dry ground through the midst of the sea.

## LVI. The Song of the Prophet Isaiah. Chapter 5.

I will sing now for my beloved the song of my beloved’s vineyard: my beloved had a vineyard in a fertile place.

I enclosed it with a hedge and surrounded it with a wall; I dug it over and planted it with the choicest vine.

I built a tower in its midst and dug a winepress in it.

I waited for it to produce grapes, but it produced thorns.

And now, man of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem, judge between me and my vineyard. What more should I have done for my vineyard that I did not do for it?

For I waited for it to produce grapes, but it produced thorns.

Now, then, I shall announce to you what I am about to do to my vineyard.

I shall remove its hedge, and it will become a spoil; I shall tear down its walls, and it will be trampled.

I shall abandon my vineyard, and it shall neither be pruned nor dug.

Thorns will grow up in it as in uncultivated ground, and I shall command the clouds not to rain upon it.

For the vineyard of the Lord of hosts is the house of Israel, and the house of Judah is his beloved planting.

[Col. 0876A] For I waited for it to produce justice, but it produced wickedness—and not righteousness, but a cry.

## LVII. The Song of the Prophet Isaiah. Chapter 26.

**Antiphon.** My soul longs for you in the night; at dawn, O Lord, I shall keep watch for you.

The city of our strength is the Savior.

A wall and an outer defense will be set within it.

Open the gates, that the righteous nation which keeps faith may enter. The ancient error has passed away.

You will preserve peace—peace, because we have hoped in you. Hope in the Lord forever, in the Lord God, the strong one, forever.

For he will humble the inhabitants of the heights; he will bring down the lofty city. [Col. 0876B]

He will humble it to the ground; he will bring it down to the dust.

The foot will trample it: the feet of the poor, the steps of the needy.

The path of the righteous has been made straight; the way of the righteous is straight for walking.

On the path of your judgments, O Lord, we have waited for you. Your name and your memorial are the desire of the soul.

My soul longs for you in the night; indeed, my spirit within me will keep watch for you at dawn.

When you execute your judgments on the earth, the inhabitants of the world will learn righteousness.

[Col. 0876C] Though mercy be shown to the wicked, he will not learn righteousness in the land of the saints. He has acted wickedly and will not see the glory of the Lord.

O Lord, let your hand be exalted, and let them not see. Let them see and be confounded—those who are jealous for the people—and let the fire devour your enemies.

## LVIII. The Song of the Prophet Isaiah. The same chapter.

**XVIII. The appointed text.**

**Antiphon.** Your dead shall live; my slain shall rise again.

O Lord, you will grant us peace, for you have accomplished all our works for us.

O Lord our God, other masters besides you have possessed us; only in you shall we remember your name.

[Col. 0876D] The dead shall not live; the giants shall not rise again. Therefore you visited them, crushed them, and destroyed all their memory.

You have spared the nation, O Lord; you have spared the nation—have you indeed been glorified? You have extended all the boundaries of the earth.

O Lord, in distress they sought you; in the tribulation of murmuring, your instruction was within them.

As a woman who has conceived, when she draws near to childbirth, cries out in pain, so have we become before your face, O Lord.

We conceived and were, as it were, in labor, and gave birth to wind. We have not brought salvation to the land; therefore the inhabitants of the earth have not fallen.

Your dead shall live, and my slain shall rise again.

Awake and praise the Lord, you who dwell in the dust, for your dew is a dew of light, and you will cast the land of the giants down into ruin. [Col. 0877A]

Go, my people; enter your chambers, shut your doors behind you, and hide yourself for a little while, for a moment, until the indignation has passed.

## LIX. The Song of the Prophet Isaiah. Chapter 33.

**Antiphon.** Hear, you who are far away, what I have done, says the Lord, and know my strength.

The sinners in Zion are terrified; fear has seized the hypocrites.

[LXXXV] Who among you can dwell with devouring fire? Or who among you can dwell amid everlasting burnings?

[Col. 0877B] He who walks in righteousness and speaks truth;

who rejects greed and slander, and shakes his hands free from every bribe;

who closes his ears so as not to hear of bloodshed, and shuts his eyes so as not to see evil.

This man will dwell on the heights; the fortifications of rocks will be his refuge. His bread will be given to him; his waters will be sure.

His eyes will see the king in his beauty; they will behold a land far away. Your heart will meditate on fear.

Where is the learned man? Where is the one who knows the law? Where is the one who weighs words? Where is the teacher of little ones?

You will not see the insolent people, the people of deep speech, so that you cannot understand the eloquence of their language, in which there is no wisdom.

[Col. 0877C] Look upon Zion, the city of our solemn assembly [solemnity]. Your eyes will see Jerusalem, a wealthy dwelling-place.

The tent that can never be moved, whose pegs will never be removed, and whose cords will never be broken.

For only there our magnificent Lord is present, a place of rivers, broad and wide streams.

No ship of oars will pass through it, nor will a large trireme cross it.

For the Lord is our Judge, the Lord is our lawgiver, the Lord is our King; he himself will save us.

## LX. The Song of the Prophet Jonah. Chapter 2.

[Col. 0877D]

**XXXV. In your [tone].**

**Antiphon.** What vows shall I pay to the Lord, my Savior?

**Another.** Your waves, O Lord, passed over me, and I said: “I am driven away from your eyes; shall I ever again see your holy temple?”

I cried to the Lord from my distress, and he answered me.

From the belly of the underworld I cried, and he heard my voice.

You cast me into the depths, into the heart of the sea, and the current surrounded me.

All your torrents and your waves passed over me, and I said: “I am cast away from the sight of your eyes.” Yet I shall again see your holy temple. [Col. 0878A]

The waters closed over me, reaching my soul; the abyss surrounded me; the sea covered my head. I descended to the foundations of the mountains; the bars of the earth closed over me forever.

But you will raise my life from corruption, O Lord my God.

When my soul was fainting within me, I remembered my Lord, and my prayer came to your holy temple.

Those who keep worthless things have abandoned their own mercy in vain.

But I, with a voice of praise, shall sacrifice to you; whatever vows I have made, I shall pay to the Lord for salvation.

## LXI. The Song from the Fourth Book of Ezra. Chapter 8.

[Col. 0878B]

**XLII. Send forth.**

**Antiphon.** Your throne, O God, is beyond estimation, and your glory incomprehensible. The whole army of angels stands before you with trembling; your appearance dries up the abysses, and your indignation makes the mountains waste away.
