**Another.** Have mercy, O Lord, on those who do not possess the substance of good works.

O Lord, who dwell forever, whose eyes are raised on high and above the air;

whose throne is beyond estimation and whose glory is incomprehensible;

[Col. 0878C] before whom the whole army of angels stands with trembling, whose watch is changed into wind and fire;

whose word is firm and whose utterances endure;

whose ordering is strong and whose command is dreadful;

whose appearance dries up the abysses, whose indignation makes the mountains waste away, and whose truth bears witness.

Hear, O Lord, the prayer of your servant; receive with your ears the supplication of your creature; attend to my words.

For while I live I shall speak, and while I have understanding I shall answer.

Do not look upon the offenses of your people, but upon those who have served you in truth.

Do not heed the endeavors of those who act wickedly [perhaps: “of the wicked”—the reading is uncertain], but those who have kept your covenants with sorrow.

[Col. 0878D] Do not consider destroying those who have behaved falsely in your sight, but remember those who have known your fear by their own will.

Do not wish to destroy those who have had the ways of beasts [LXXXVI], but look upon those who have taught your law splendidly.

Do not be angry with those who have been judged worse than beasts, but love those who have always trusted in your glory.

For we and our fathers have lived by such ways; but you have been called merciful because of us sinners.

For if you decide to have mercy on us, then you will be called merciful.

[Col. 0879A] For we have no works of righteousness; but the righteous, for whom many works are stored up with you, O Lord, will receive their reward from their own works.

For what is a human being, that you should be angry with him? Or what is a corruptible race, that you should be so embittered against it?

In truth, there is no one born who has not acted wickedly, nor among those who trust is there one who has not sinned.

But in this your righteousness and goodness will be proclaimed, O Lord, when you have had mercy on those who do not possess the substance of good works.

## LXII. The Song of Moses from Deuteronomy. Chapter 32.

**LVIII. I will exalt.**

[Col. 0879B] Give ear, O heaven, and I shall speak; let the earth hear the words from my mouth.

Let my speech be awaited like rain, and let my words descend like dew.

Like mist upon the grass and like snow upon the hay; for I shall invoke the name of the Lord. Give greatness to the Lord our God: God’s works are true, and all his ways are judgments.

God is faithful, and there is no iniquity in him; the Lord is just and holy.

They sinned: are they not his unblemished children, a depraved and perverse generation? Do you repay this to the Lord, foolish and senseless people?

Is he not himself your father, who possessed you, made you, and created you?

[Col. 0879C] Remember the days of old; understand the years of generation after generation.

Ask your father, and he will tell you; ask your elders, and they will say to you.

When the Most High divided the nations, when he scattered the children of Adam, he established the boundaries of the nations according to the number of the angels of God.

The Lord’s portion became his people Jacob; Israel was the cord of his inheritance.

He gave him abundance in a desert land, in the thirsty heat where there was no water.

He led him around and instructed him, and guarded him like the pupil of his eye.

As an eagle protects its nest and hovers over its young, he spread out his wings, took them up, [Col. 0879D] and carried them upon his shoulders.

The Lord alone led them, and there was no foreign god with them.

## LXIII. The Song of Hannah from the First Book of Samuel. Chapter 2.

**LXII. In the desert.**

My heart has been confirmed in the Lord, and my horn has been exalted in my saving God.

My mouth has been opened wide against my enemies.

I rejoice in your holiness, for there is no other God like you; there is none holy besides you, and there is none righteous besides our God.

Do not boast, and do not speak lofty things in arrogance; [Col. 0880A] do not let grandiloquence come from your mouth, for the Lord is a God of knowledge.

The God who prepares his designs: the bows of the mighty have been weakened, and the weak have girded themselves with strength.

Those who were full of bread have become poor, and the hungry have crossed the land.

The barren woman has borne seven, and she who had many children has grown weak.

The Lord puts to death and gives life; he leads down to the underworld and brings back.

The Lord makes poor and makes rich; he humbles and exalts.

He raises the needy from the earth and lifts the poor from the dungheap.

He makes him sit with the mighty of the people, and [Col. 0880B] gives him the throne of glory as an inheritance.

He gives a vow to the one who vows [reading uncertain], and he will bless the years of the righteous.

For a man is not mighty through strength; the Lord makes his adversary weak, the holy Lord.

Let the wise man not boast in his wisdom; let the rich man not boast in his riches; let the strong man not boast in his strength. Rather, let the one who boasts boast in knowing and understanding the Lord, and in practicing judgment and righteousness upon the earth.

The Lord has ascended into the heavens and thunders; he himself will judge the ends of the earth.

He is powerful and gives strength to our kings, and he will exalt the horn of his Christ.

## LXIV. The Song from the First Book of Chronicles. Chapter 29.

[Col. 0880C]

**LXIV. The going forth.**

**Antiphon.** In your hand, O Lord, are strength and power; in your hand are greatness and rule over all.

Blessed is the Lord, the God of Israel our father, from eternity and forever.

Yours, O Lord, are magnificence and power, glory and victory, and praise is yours.

For everything in heaven and on earth is yours.

Yours, O Lord, is the kingdom, and you are above all rulers.

Yours are riches, and yours is glory; you rule over all.

In your hand, O Lord, are strength and power; in your hand [Col. 0880D] are greatness and rule over all.

Now, therefore, O Lord our God, we give thanks to you and praise your renowned name.

Who am I, and who are my people, that we should be able to promise you all these things?

For everything is yours, and what we have received from your hand we have given to you.

For we are strangers before you and sojourners, as were all our fathers.

Our days on earth are like a shadow, and there is no delay.

O Lord God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, our fathers, preserve forever this intention of our heart, and may this mind always remain in your worship.

## LXV. The Song of the Prophet Isaiah. Chapter 12.

[Col. 0881A]

**LXVI. Illuminate.**

**Antiphon.** Your anger has turned away, and you have comforted me.

I shall give thanks to you, O Lord, because you were angry with me; your anger has turned away, and you have comforted me.

Behold, God is my Savior; I shall act confidently and shall not fear.

For the Lord is my strength and my praise, and he has become my salvation.

You shall draw water with joy from the springs of the Savior, and you shall say on that day:

Give thanks to the Lord and invoke his name; make his designs known among the peoples. Remember [Col. 0881B] that his name is exalted.

Sing to the Lord, for he has acted magnificently; announce this throughout the whole earth.

Rejoice and praise, O dwelling-place of Zion, for great in your midst is the Holy One of Israel.

## LXVI. The Song of the Prophet Isaiah. Chapter 33.

**LXXV. Illuminating.**

O Lord, have mercy on us; for we have waited for you.

Be our arm in the morning, and our salvation in the time of tribulation.

At the voice of the angel the peoples fled; at your expectation the nations were scattered.

Your spoil will be gathered as the locust is gathered, and as when ditches are filled with it. [Col. 0881C]

The Lord has been magnified, for he will dwell on high.

He will fill Zion with judgment and righteousness, and faithfulness will be established in its times.

The riches of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge: the fear of the Lord itself is his treasure.

Behold, those who see will cry out outside; the angels of peace will weep bitterly.

The roads have been deserted; the traveler has ceased from the path; the covenant has been annulled. He has rejected the cities and has not counted their inhabitants.

The land mourned and languished; Lebanon was confounded and withered. Sharon became like a desert, and Bashan and Carmel were shaken.

[Col. 0881D] Now I shall rise, says the Lord; now I shall be exalted, and now I shall be lifted up.

## LXVII. The Prayer of Mordecai from the Book of Esther. Chapter 13.

**Antiphon.** Have mercy, O Lord, on your people, and do not despise your inheritance, which you redeemed.

O Lord, Lord, almighty King, everything is placed under your dominion, and there is no one who can resist your will.

If you have decreed to save Israel, you made heaven and earth and everything contained within the circuit of heaven.

For you are Lord of all, and there is no one who can resist your majesty.

And now, O Lord, King and God of Abraham, have mercy on your people, because our enemies intend to destroy us and erase your inheritance. [Col. 0882A]

Do not despise your portion, which you redeemed for yourself from Egypt.

Hear my supplication, and be favorable to your lot and your allotted inheritance.

[LXXXVIII] Turn our mourning into joy, so that, living, we may praise your name, O Lord, and do not close the mouths of those who sing to you.

## LXVIII. The Song of the Prophet Jeremiah. Chapter 14.

**LXXXVII. And I.**

Do not give us over to reproach for the sake of your name, O Lord. [Col. 0882B]

Let my eyes pour out tears day and night, and let them not be silent.

For the virgin daughter of my people has been crushed with a great crushing, with a grievous wound exceedingly.

If I go out into the fields, behold, those slain by the sword; and if I enter the city, behold, those weakened by famine.

For prophet and priest have gone into a land they did not know.

Have you utterly rejected Judah? Or has your soul loathed Zion?

Why, then, have you struck us so that there is no healing?

We hoped for peace, but there is none; for a time of healing and goodness, but behold, turmoil.

[Col. 0882C] We acknowledge our wickedness, O Lord, and the iniquities of our fathers, because we have sinned against you.

Do not give us over to reproach for the sake of your name, nor make us a disgrace.

Remember the throne of your glory; do not annul your covenant with us.

Are there among the nations’ idols those who bring rain? Or can the heavens give showers?

Are you not the Lord our God, whom we shall await? For you made all these things.

## LXIX. The Song from Deuteronomy. Chapter 9.

**LXXXVIIII. Let there be splendor.**

[Col. 0882D] O Lord God, do not destroy your people and your inheritance, which you redeemed in your greatness, whom you brought out of Egypt with a strong hand.

Remember your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

Do not look upon the hardness of this people, its wickedness and sin.

Lest the inhabitants of the land from which you brought us should say: “The Lord was unable to bring them into the land that he promised them, and he hated them; therefore he brought them out to kill them in the wilderness.”

For they are your people and your inheritance, whom you brought out by your great strength and your outstretched arm.

## LXX. The Song of Jehoshaphat from the Second Book of Chronicles. Chapter 20.

[Col. 0883A]

**XCI. It is good.**

O Lord God of our fathers, you are God in heaven, and you rule over all the kingdoms of the nations.

In your hand are strength and power, and no one can resist you.

Was it not you, O Lord our God, who destroyed all the inhabitants of this land before your people Israel, and gave it to the offspring of Abraham, your friend, forever?

They dwelt in it and built in it a sanctuary for your name, saying:

If evils come upon us—sword, judgment, pestilence, [Col. 0883B] and famine—we shall stand before you in this house, in your presence, where your name has been invoked. We shall cry out to you in our tribulations, and you will hear us and save us.

Now, therefore, our God, will you not judge our enemies?

We do not possess enough strength to resist this multitude that has come against us.

But since we do not know what we ought to do, this alone remains to us: to direct our eyes toward you.

## LXXI. The Song of the Prophet Isaiah. Chapter 25.

**C. At the morning offices.**

[Col. 0883C] You are my God; I shall exalt you and give thanks to your name.

For you have done marvelous things; your ancient purposes are faithful. Amen.

For you have made a city into a mound, a fortified city into a ruin, a house of strangers, so that it is no longer a city and will never be rebuilt.

For this a strong people will praise you; the city of powerful nations will fear you.

For you have become a stronghold for the poor, a stronghold for the needy in tribulation, a hope against the storm, a shelter from the heat.

For the spirit of the mighty is like a storm driving against a wall.

[LXXXIX] As heat in thirst, you will humble the mound of strangers; and as heat beneath a burning cloud, [Col. 0883D] you will make the branch of the mighty wither.

And the Lord of hosts will make for all peoples on this mountain a banquet of rich foods, a banquet of wine, of rich foods full of marrow and wine well refined.

And on this mountain he will destroy the covering bound over all peoples, and the web woven over all nations. He will destroy death forever.

And the Lord God will remove the tear from every face, and he will take away the reproach of his people from the whole earth, for the Lord has spoken; and it will be said on that day:

Behold, this is our Lord God; we have waited for him, and he will save us.

[Col. 0884A] This is the Lord; we have waited for him. We shall exult and rejoice in his salvation, because the hand of the Lord will rest on this mountain.

## LXXII. The Song of the Prophet Isaiah. Chapter 37.

**CVII. I shall rise.**

O Lord of hosts, God of Israel, who sit upon the Cherubim, you alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth.

You made heaven and earth. Incline your ear, O Lord, and hear; open your eyes and see, and hear all the words of Sennacherib, which he sent to blaspheme the living God.

For truly, O Lord, the kings of Assyria have laid waste the lands and their territories, and have given their gods to the fire. [Col. 0884B]

For they were not gods, but the works of human hands, wood and stone; and they destroyed them.

And now, O Lord our God, save us from his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you alone are the Lord.

## LXXIII. The Song of the Prophet Isaiah. Chapter 38.

**CXVII. God is the Lord.**

**Antiphon.** You will chastise me, O Lord, and you will give me life.

I said: “In the middle of my days I shall go to the gates of the underworld; I sought the remainder of my years.” I said: “I shall not see the Lord God in the land of the living.”

[Col. 0884C] I shall not look upon human beings or any inhabitant again. My generation has ceased; it has been taken away and rolled up from me like shepherds’ tents.

My life has been cut off like a weaver’s cloth; while I was still weaving, he cut me off. From morning until evening he was bringing me to an end.

I hoped until morning; like a lion, so he crushed all my bones.

Like a swallow, so I cried out; I mourned like a dove. My eyes grew weak as I looked upward. O Lord, I am oppressed; answer for me.

What shall I say, and what will he answer me, when he himself has done it? I shall review all my years in the bitterness of my soul.

[Col. 0884D] O Lord, if this is how one lives, and if such things constitute the life of my spirit, you will chastise me and give me life.

Behold, my bitterness is most bitter in peace; but you have rescued my soul so that it would not perish.

You have cast all my sins behind your back.

For the underworld will not give thanks to you, nor will death praise you.

Those who descend into the pit will not await your truth.

The living, the living, will give thanks to you, as I do today; a father will make your truth known to his children.

O Lord, save us, and we shall sing our psalms all the days of our life in the house of the Lord.

## LXXIV. The Song of the Prophet Jeremiah. Chapter 51.

[Col. 0885A]

**CXVIII. They came before.**

**Antiphon.** He who made all things is God himself, and Israel is his inheritance; the Lord of hosts is his name.

The Lord of hosts swore by his own life: “I shall fill you with human beings like locusts, and a battle-song shall be sung over you.”

He who made the earth by his strength prepared the world by his wisdom, and by his understanding stretched out the heavens.

When he gives his voice, the waters in heaven multiply.

He raises clouds from the end of the earth; he makes lightning into rain. [Col. 0885B]

He brings forth winds from his treasuries. Every human being has become foolish through his knowledge.

Every metalworker is confounded by the carved image, for his cast image is false, and there is no spirit in them.

For their works are empty and worthy of ridicule; at the time of their visitation they will perish.

Not like this is the portion of Jacob, for he who made all things is God himself; and Israel is the scepter [XC] of his inheritance; the Lord of hosts is his name.

## LXXV. The Song from Ecclesiasticus. Chapters 11 and 12.

**CXXVIIII. At the vigil.**

Rejoice, young man, in your youth, and let your heart be in good spirits in the days of your youth.

Walk in the ways of your heart and in the sight of your eyes, but know that for all these things God will bring you into judgment.

Remove anger from your heart and put away evil from your flesh, for youth and pleasure are vain.

Remember your Creator in the days of your youth,

before the time of affliction comes and the years draw near of which you will say: “They do not please me.”

Before the sun, the light, the moon, and the stars grow dark, and the cloud returns after the rain.

When the guardians of the house tremble, and the strongest men are bent, and the millers cease because they have become few,

[Col. 0885D] when those who look through the windows grow dark, and the doors in the street are closed, at the weakening of the millstone’s sound;

when they rise at the sound of the bird, and all the daughters of song grow deaf;

when the heights are feared, and there are terrors on the road;

[Col. 0886A] when the almond blossoms, the locust becomes fat, and the caperberry is scattered;

because a man is going to his eternal home, and mourners go about in the street;

before the silver cord is broken, the golden ribbon returns, the jar is shattered at the spring, and the wheel is broken over the cistern;

and the dust returns to the earth from which it came, and the spirit returns to God who gave it.

## LXXVI. The Song from the Book of Job. Chapter 19.

**CXLII. Heard.**

For I know that my Redeemer lives, and at the end [Col. 0886B] he will rise from the earth.

And again I shall be clothed with my skin, and in my flesh I shall see God, whom I myself shall see.

I myself, and my eyes, shall behold him, and no other.

This hope has been laid up in my bosom, and my inheritance is in my God.

## LXXVII. The Song of the Angels. Of the Nativity of Christ.

Glory to God in the highest.

And on earth peace to people of good will.

We praise you.

We bless you.

[Col. 0886C] We adore you.

We glorify you.

We offer you a hymn.

We give you thanks because of your great glory.

Lord God, heavenly King,

God the almighty Father,

Lord, the only-begotten Son,

Jesus Christ, Most High,

Lord God,

Lamb of God,

Son of the Father,

you who take away the sins of the world, have mercy on us.

You who take away the sins of the world, receive our supplication.

[Col. 0886D] You who sit at the right hand, have mercy on us.

For you alone are holy.

You alone are Lord.

You alone are Most High,

Jesus Christ,

with the Holy Spirit, in the glory of God the Father. Amen.

[Col. 0885]

# Here Begin the Hymns for the Whole Cycle of the Year. (C, S)

## [XCI] Prologue of the Hymns

[Col. 0885D]

The first wonders of hymns, in clear melody,

the angelic mouths proclaimed when the Lord was born,

namely, the gifts poured down from heaven, few in number,

which the earthly gaze of the shepherds saw and took up again.

Already in ancient times, indeed, the order of hymns had shone forth [perhaps: “had shone forth”].

When the three mouths of the young men, after conquering the furnace’s fire,

[Col. 0887A] took up a hymn of praise to the ancient Father, to the Son already then, and to the one joined with them,

a hymn of all life, in the circuit of heaven

and in the circle of the earthly world,

for the blessed company and for every created element,

all sacred things and all lands were hymned in the art of the Muses.

Now the Church, spread throughout the whole world,

established in the divine sacrament, celebrates this through all things;

and when the Redeemer fulfilled the sacred time of the Supper,

he offered to the eternal Father a hymn joined to the apostolic choir,

turning his blessed footsteps for the sake of prayer,

he went out onto the neighboring mountain to entreat the Father.

Paul also, the ruler of faith and teacher to all ages,

admonishes us to speak in psalms and hymns.

From this the sacred doctrine of hymns arose,

through Hilary, Pope Ambrose, and the others, according to their custom,

[Col. 0887B] to compose such melodies of hymns for divine praise,

now to recount the praises of the Lord, now the triumphs of the martyrs,

to pour forth every celibate song in voices,

and to make sweet melody for the Maker of all.

The highest glory of God consists in praise and joy.

In these the Trinity is praised, and the Church gives off fragrance.

When we recite a hymn, we give honor and glory;

when we sing a hymn, we show the Church’s vows;

and finally we ask for an end to all offenses.

## [XCII] Hymn of the Advent of the Lord and of the Festival of the Saints, sung three times, to be said at Matins when the Advent of the Lord begins

Rejoice, flowers of the martyrs;

[Col. 0887C] hail, peoples of the nations;

send forth what has been seen through the stars;

hope for the sign of glory.

The voices of the prophets resound,

announcing that Jesus will come,

the forerunner of redemption,

by which grace he redeemed us.

He shines forth as our dawn,

and joyful hearts burn within us,

when the faithful voice sounds,

announcing glory beforehand.

The joy of so great a salvation,

by which the world has been redeemed,

the illustrious favor [reading uncertain],

from now on let us sing.

[Col. 0887D] This first Advent was

when he came, not to punish,

to wipe away the world’s sore,

saving what had perished.

Now the second foretells

that Christ is at the doors,

to restore crowns to the saints

and open the kingdoms of heaven.

Eternal light is promised,

and the saving star is proclaimed.

Now may the most radiant splendor

call us to the rights of the heavenly ones.

Christ, we seek you alone,

to see you as God,

[Col. 0888A] so that this joyful vision

may snatch us from every hell,

when you, the Redeemer, come,

with the white-robed band of martyrs;

then join us to the blessed company.

To God the Father be glory,

and to his only Son,

with the Spirit, the Paraclete,

now and forever.

Amen.

**V.** The saints shall exult in glory.

[Col. 0889A]

From the rising hinge of the sun [*cardine*]. To be used on the feast of the Annunciation of the Blessed Virgin Mary, on the 18th.

It is not said on another festival.

Christ’s gate becomes passable,

the Bridegroom, Redeemer, and Creator

through the dark cups of death,

will resolve our sins.

the Shepherd, Creator of all,

### Hymn for the feast of Saint Sebastian

[Col. 0890B]

The solemn feast of the martyr Sebastian.

Blessed people, faithful congregation, sing

with kindly mind a new song to God,

who grants the saints triumph and victory

and commands them to possess the heavenly homeland.

This man was truthful, modest, sober,

gentle, joyful, exceedingly dear,

renowned in speech, most eloquent in tongue;

for this purpose he concealed himself beneath the cloak of the world,

so that he might proclaim the kingdom of heaven to all.

From the mouth of the holy man a multitude of peoples,

hearing Christ’s commands, say:

“It is shameful for us, who have lived until now

in obedience to wicked parents;

let us follow Christ, the Redeemer of all.”

[Col. 0890C] Holy Sebastian, our little servant,

teach, cherish, guide, and protect us,  
how our minds ought most readily and diligently  
to come to suffering,  
and bravely conquer the cruel enemy.

The blessed man did as he had commanded him:  
he immediately ordered all earthly things abandoned.  
With all their heart they despised  
and rejected perishable things as dung,  
that they might seek the future joys of life.

When this had promptly been announced to their parents,  
that they were coming with great surging waves,  
“What has happened to you, dearest sons,” they asked,  
“that you abandon the pleasant and excellent things of the world  
and voluntarily hasten toward the worst death?”

[Col. 0890D] The saints began to bend their hearts toward grief  
and to soften them at their parents’ words;  
but soon, when they had become the aforesaid martyrs,  
they were strengthened with immense steadfastness  
to endure atrocious torments.

“God now opens the gate of heaven for you,  
so that you may come to that holy homeland  
in which there is no death, but everlasting joy  
and great delight.

Taste and see how sweet the Lord is.  
If you seek the beauty of houses,  
the eternal city has beautiful dwellings  
and many mansions in the heavens.

There, without syllables, [the angels]  
[Col. 0891A] thrice proclaim ‘Holy’; the multitude rejoices;  
organs resound there in praise of the King;  
the fields breathe various fragrances;  
radiance shines forth without any shadows;  
there is serenity without cloud;  
and God is there, everlasting light.

How great is the abundance of your sweetness, O God,  
which you conceal for those who fear you,  
and which you have perfected for those who love you greatly!  
You grant the gift of your grace  
and merciful forgiveness to those who ask.”

Blessed Zoe, remaining mute,  
saw twice three [i.e. six] angels of God  
holding a book, from which she uttered Sebastian’s words before her own eyes.

[Col. 0891B] With a loud cry she invokes the Creator:  
“Blessed is the one who believes your words,  
great and wondrous Sebastian!”

She said: “Now I believe in God’s Son,  
whom my mouth quickly proclaims,  
so that I may praise him in the heavenly homeland.”

What voice, O God, can speak your praises?  
What mind can conceive your power?  
Filled at once with divine flame,  
the martyrs hasten fearlessly to their passion,  
so that they may enjoy you, supreme and good God.

With you assisting, they became martyrs  
through your pious and most holy servant,  
Sebastian, the most valiant soldier.  
Through them we tearfully ask you: hear  
[Col. 0891C] our prayers, and cut away all our sins.

The day arrives, adorned with the highest joys,  
which is beautified by the victories of the martyrs.

[XCV] The holy and devout Church celebrates it;  
therefore let us fittingly bring forth  
a hymn in harmonious songs to the Most High.

This illustrious man, renowned for merits and words,  
turns peoples away, by divine utterances, from the wicked *ultibus* of idols  
[*cultibus*, “cults,” is suggested];
he makes their worshipers adherents of the Catholic faith  
and ardent lovers of martyrdom.

He strengthens the wavering mind of his dear brothers  
by health-giving exhortation;  
the offspring of parents and spouses alike,  
[Col. 0891D] and the faithless minds of their loved ones,  
he subjects to the worship of holy faith.

Then, with Cromatius leading the peoples,  
he made Nicostratus, Claudius, Castulus,  
and also Zoe and Castorius  
athletes of Christ God’s Son,  
who endured martyrdom without hesitation.

Washed in the salutary bath,  
they shine with signs and excel in virtues.  
For when a certain man had fallen, his limbs already shattered,  
Tiburtius immediately restored him by praying—  
and afterward he offered his parents as a gift to Christ.

That illustrious man, Cromatius,  
despising the profane worship of idolatry  
and cleaving chastely to the discipline of faith,  
[Col. 0892A] freely released the bonds of servants,  
giving to Christ those whom he had lawfully possessed.

Soon showing himself devoted to the Most High,  
he abandoned all the transitory things of the world;  
with devoted mind he attended to divine service,  
striving to fulfill the revealed commands.  
He despised the forum and sought solitude.

A crowd of believers gathered around him,  
unable to bear the burden of martyrdom.  
With them, on the Campanian shore,  
he lived a monastic life worthily;  
together they offered themselves to God as a sacrifice.

The sacrilegious rulers of Rome,  
angered by this, raged still more fiercely  
and burned with greedy fury  
in persecuting Christ’s witnesses of faith,  
because they refused to offer libations to the gods.

[Col. 0892B] Then the Bishop of the City, having summoned  
the company of Catholics who remained with him,  
consecrated some of them as priests,  
honored others with Levitical dignity,  
and made all the rest subdeacons.

Through the zeal of Sebastian the author,  
the armed confession of all these  
springs fearlessly toward passion.  
For Zoe, victorious, first conquered in combat;  
then Tranquillinus triumphed more gloriously.

Afterward Claudius and Nicostratus,  
Castor and Victor together with Simpronius,  
while seeking the sacred bodies along the shores,  
were suddenly captured by ambushers,  
cast into the sea, and killed for Christ.

After them, the blessed combatants, more splendidly,  
the holy Castulus and also Tiburtius,  
overcame fires and the torturers’ blows;  
struck down by the sword, they migrated to heaven,  
admitted to the kingdom with the angelic host.

[Col. 0892C] Then two most noble brothers,  
twins and bearing one name,  
were fastened to wood with iron spikes;  
the soles of their feet were goaded with nails.  
Confessing Christ, they were pierced through with a lance  
and crowned with all their blood.

A radiant star and shining lamp  
could in no way remain hidden for long:  
[Col. 0892D] the illustrious presence of Sebastian,  
who was an energetic exhorter to all,  
was revealed.

This man, through the plots of cunning men,  
is brought before the king, yet stands undaunted;  
he is asked why he despises the gods.  
He confessed, praising Christ without hesitation,  
that he is eternally God with the Father.

At his words the furious, impious judge  
orders him to be pierced with arrows in the field,  
thinking that this kind of punishment would bring him death  
and serve his own vengeance.  
In his madness he leaves him as though dead.

The blessed man is crushed by no pain,  
since he was armed with divine virtues;  
[Col. 0893A] rather, recovering and now endowed with strength,  
he approaches the persecutor with restraint,  
setting forth the way of Christian teaching.

That monstrous man, raging again,  
orders the frail saint of God to be cut down  
without ceasing, until he should fail.  
But as soon as he had endured the sentence itself,  
he breathed out his spirit into the heavenly homeland.

Stand by us, glorious martyrs of God;  
stand by us, most valiant soldiers of Christ.  
Bring favor to those who obey you;  
protect those who love you;  
and assist the Christian assembly.

Behold, all the clergy and priesthood;  
behold every age, sex, and condition:  
today they rejoice with you in your victories.  
Grant suitable remedies to all  
and whatever is already fitting to your merits,

[Col. 0893B] so that, bestowing what peoples ask  
and providing protection for those who serve Christ,  
you may be everlasting consolation to all,  
opening the entrance of paradise.

[XCVI] We who venerate the joyful celebration of this feast,  
grant, we pray, undivided Trinity,  
to those who confess you what they desire,  
you alone who possess the name of Godhead—  
Father with the Son and Holy Spirit—  
you who reign in Trinity forever.

Amen.

V. “The saints shall exult in glory.”

[Col. 0893D]

[Christ is life.]

“O illustrious crown of priests.” As in his feast, on the 25th.

Hymn for the feast of Saint Thyrsus. Five days before the Kalends of February.

“Exult greatly, crowd of the faithful.” As in his feast, on the 28th.

Hymn for the feast of Saint Agatha.

[Christ, heavenly one.]

“An illustrious and radiant feast has appeared.” As in her feast, on 5 February.

V. “Beauty and splendor.”

Hymn for the feast of Saint Dorothy. Seven days before the Ides of February. An illustrious feast.

[Col. 0894A]

A hymn is due to you in Zion, Almighty,  
while each person fulfills his vow in Jerusalem.  
Taking steadfastness from faith in the vow,  
he drives himself away from every enticement,  
so that he may follow you, bearing his cross.

By this example the earlier Apostles  
acted, proven in the deed of faith.  
By preaching this they founded the Church,  
and, remaining the true and unharmed mother,  
the gracious bride brought forth her worthy offspring.

Into the most powerful ranks of the faithful,  
and into the nectar-bearing fruits among the martyrs,  
she bears to the confessors an abundant gift,  
while she rejoices in the heavenly kingdoms,  
expecting to receive unspeakable riches.

[Col. 0894B] Hence today, through four witnesses,  
the victorious Church sends forth royal gifts,  
suitable and pleasing to you, King of heaven—  
truly blessed and most excellent offerings—  
which she won together through your blood.

For Dorothy she appoints ambrosial privet,  
and lilies and roses;  
for Calliste and Christeta, violets  
filled with the sweetest fragrance;  
and a precious dish for Theophilus.

Of these, Dorothy, the first combatant,  
shines splendidly, adorned with a double crown:  
namely, having gained the reward  
of both virginity and martyrdom,  
in fellowship with her two sisters and Theophilus.

[Col. 0894C] Cappadocia’s city of Caesarea—  
these citizens, born under the highest protection,  
offer the city an exemplary model:  
preeminent in faith, resplendent in conduct,  
and accomplishing a martyr’s triumph.

When the infamous governor Sabricius  
learned of the reputation of this holy virgin,  
he ordered her brought before him for examination.  
He tried to deceive her with flattering persuasion  
and terrified her with the harshest threats.

But when the governor saw her undaunted,  
in fury he raised her onto the rack to be slaughtered.  
Yet, innocent and readily enduring the punishment,  
she proclaimed Christ’s name in a loud voice,  
saying that he is one with the Father and the Paraclete.

[Col. 0894D] The cunning man, seeking to weaken her faith,  
summoned Christeta together with Calliste,  
so that they might make themselves equal to her.  
But soon, corrected through her, they believed  
that she had already become a more exalted martyr.

[XCVII] Who, O Christ, could recount  
your remarkable works of miracles,  
which you yourself perform while glorifying the saints?

For when the winged bishop stood guard,  
you mercifully corrected those who were falling.  
When your holy virgin was inflamed by the Spirit,  
she brought salvation to the sisters who had escaped,  
[Col. 0895A] restoring their minds with exhortations of faith  
and rekindling in them the fervor of martyrdom,  
so that they might hasten joyfully to the palm.

Sapricius, grieving that he had been mocked,  
thought to burn the limbs of both women in a cauldron.  
But while he sought vengeance through their death,  
he made the victorious women ascend to heaven  
to obtain the royal diadem.

Rejoicing, the martyr, while she still lived,  
was raised on a stake to suffer punishments.  
She was torn by scourges and claws;  
she willingly endured torches on her sides,  
and hastened her face toward their palms.

Having surpassed the governor’s cruelty,  
she was handed over to the executioner to be killed,  
already betrothed to the martyr’s Bridegroom.  
At her request, Theophilus the scholar  
was crowned with blood by the gift sent to him.

[Col. 0895B] Theophilus, receiving from paradise the gifts sent,  
stared at them in astonishment:  
three apples and the sweetness of roses,  
whose fragrance was renewed with living freshness.  
Believing, he praised Christ, the Son of God.

Once he had been a mocker of Christ’s cross;  
suddenly he became a most eminent confessor.  
With open mouth he preached the Crucified  
and announced before the governor  
that the imposture of the idols would be cast into flames.

Then the furious judge placed him on the rack  
to be afflicted with deadly punishments.  
When he saw him undaunted in countenance  
and persisting stubbornly in the faith,  
he immediately killed him with the sword,  
and made him a martyr.

[Col. 0895C] Therefore, O Redeemer, we suppliants ask  
that all of us who rejoice in their merits  
and devoutly honor their feast day  
may, defended by them, remain free from vices  
and be cleansed from all offenses.

May these too, by showing compassion for our misery  
and sharing in our needs,  
stand continually as patrons for all,  
so that, now delivered from adversities,  
they may lead us with themselves to the reward.

Grant, we ask, supreme Unity and Power,  
you who rule the ages of ages,  
that we may enjoy you through endless time,  
Light of the angels and everlasting Day;  
may you yourself, the Sun, shine perpetually for us.

[Col. 0895D] V. “The souls of the righteous.”

Hymn for the feast of Saint Eulalia of Barcelona.

“The honor of the martyr Eulalia’s tomb shines forth.” As in her feast, on 12 February.

“O Peter, rock of the Church.” As in this feast, on the 22nd.

V. “Glory and riches.”

Hymn for the feast of Saints Emeterius and Celedonius. Five days before the Nones of March.

“The writing of the two has been inscribed in heaven.” As in their feast, on 3 March.

Hymn to be sung on Sundays after the Lord’s Epiphany at Vespers until the Sunday before the taking away of meat.

[Col. 0896A]

“Lord, begetter of the Lamb.” As in the Breviary, fol. 65.

Hymn for the taking away of meat.

“Alleluia, produced by devout praises.” Fol. 137.

V. “How sweet.”

Hymn for Lent.

“O Nazarene, light of Bethlehem, Word of the Father.” Fol. 144, 145, 146, 147.

Another for mid-Lent.

Favoring the vows of the redeemed concerning abstinence,  
[Col. 0896B] come to the weary, true Guide Emmanuel.  
From you the holier form of fasting  
is understood as a pattern for future glory,  
a heavenly work and the gate of the kingdom.

If a bright, gleaming star,  
a fiery lamp, and generosity are joined to this as companions,  
who, tasting both with uplifted right hand,  
and duly equipped as though with wings,  
swiftly enters the innermost heavens in flight?

[XCVIII] Moses, whose illustrious mystery  
the friend of God set forth by an oracle;  
Elijah, snatched away in a fiery chariot of heaven;  
Nineveh, upheld together with its citizens—  
all bear witness to the clarity of the word of truth.

Then, everywhere, you, teacher of celibates,  
[Col. 0896C] after a course of forty days,  
triumph victoriously in the desert of paradise,  
washing away the bite of sin by fasting  
and altogether resisting the cunning tempter.

Following you, we too, as is customary,  
now offer at least the tithe of these days as a sacrifice.  
You also, gentle and constant indulgence,  
make these holocausts most rich,  
by which we may atone for the sins of our hearts.

Be a cup of life for the thirsty,  
a fountain of living water, the kingdom’s allotted denarius.  
We who fell through deceit when we tasted in Adam,  
rising in you and fasting from food,  
may we be refreshed with the citizens above.

You who, through the practice of sacrifice by the penitent,  
[Col. 0896D] were present to the thief on the cross,  
be present to us from heaven, Lord;  
remember us, look upon us from your throne,  
whom you redeemed with your sacred blood.

When you yourself come as the fearsome Judge,  
preceded by the cross upon the shoulders of angels,  
and shake the world with terror and the trumpet,  
may we, adorned with the saints’ glory,  
holding the right hand, escape Tartarus.

Grant, supreme Trinity and Power,  
you who rule all the ages of ages,  
that, enjoying you in glory without end,  
Light of the angels and everlasting Day,  
you yourself, the Sun, may shine perpetually for us.

Amen.

Hymn to be sung on the Saturdays of Lent at Matins.

[Col. 0897A]

Dawn now scatters the sky;  
day slips upon the earth.  
Let the dart of light resound;  
let every slippery thing depart.  
Let the phantom of night fall away;  
let it overthrow the guilt of the mind.  
Whatever dreadful night  
has brought in the darkness of sin, let it fall.

So may that most excellent morning  
which we await with bowed heads  
pour forth its light upon us,  
while this song rings out melodiously:

Glory to the unbegotten Father,  
[Col. 0897B] glory to the Only-Begotten,  
together with the Holy Spirit,  
through everlasting ages.

Amen.

Hymn for the Saturdays of Lent at Vespers.

“Word of the Most High Father.” Fol. 94.

Hymn to be sung on the Sundays of Lent at Matins.

May the Author of light resound  
through the songs of this assembly,  
which you have filled with grace  
by the power of the Resurrection.

This day signifies for us  
the setting forth of the final day,  
[Col. 0897C] when the dead will rise  
and be restored to life.

The first octave is restored,  
when abundant death is taken away,  
when we are circumcised in mind,  
and at last are born anew.

When we see our morning  
return with our enemies defeated,  
we despise the world’s luxury  
and receive the bread of salvation.

With the dry sacrifices of fasts  
we offer our bodies as a sacrifice;  
through holy acts of moderation  
we partake of sacred offerings.

May this gracious solemnity be holy;  
may this festival be bright;  
may this day, restored from the underworld,  
be a holiday of joys.

[Col. 0897D] Glory to the unbegotten Father,  
glory to the Only-Begotten,  
together with the Holy Spirit,  
through everlasting ages.

Amen.

Hymn at midday on a feast day, or on Lazarus, both at Vespers and at Matins.

“The Word of the Father, which came forth and was made flesh.” Fol. 252.

V. “Deliver me, Lord.”

Hymn for Palm Sunday.

“You are called to life, sacred race of God.” Fol. 334.

V. “Come, children, hear me.”

Hymn for Vespers on the Lord’s Supper.

[Col. 0898A]

“Now the shadow of the Law is closed.” Fol. 354.

[XCIX] Hymn for the Lord’s Resurrection.

“Let the height of heaven sing psalms.” Fol. 385.

Monday.

Behold him whom ancient prophets  
sang through the ages,  
whom the faithful pages of the prophets  
had promised:  
he shines forth, once promised;  
let all things praise him together.

Water poured at Cana  
becomes noble Falernian wine;  
the steward announces that the wine  
is ready from the water-jug;  
the king himself marvels  
at the cups touched with flavor.

[Col. 0898B] To limbs ulcerated by disease  
and to the putrefaction of the entrails  
he says, “I command you to be washed.”  
What he commanded comes to pass:  
the swollen skin, resisting,  
is cleansed of its wounds.

You apply healing clay  
and the nectar of sacred fragrance  
to eyes long buried in darkness;  
once opened, light is restored  
to the very pupils.

Rebuking the raging wind,  
[Col. 0898C] which in grievous storms  
turns the sea from top to bottom  
and tosses the wandering boat,  
he commands it; and the obedient, gentle wave  
is laid flat.

Tuesday.

A woman secretly touched  
the edge of the sacred garment;  
salvation immediately followed;  
the pallor departed from her body.  
The stream of blood was stopped  
that had flowed without cease.

The sweet youth saw a boy carried off by death—  
a boy (*abevum*; perhaps *ephebum*) whom his bereaved mother  
was burying with her final tears.  
“Rise,” he said; he rises  
and is restored alive to his mother.

[Col. 0898D] Lazarus, already deprived of the sun  
for four days and hidden in a tomb,  
he orders to live again,  
his breath being restored.  
The returning breath reenters  
the stinking liver.

He walks across the waters of the sea  
and treads upon the tops of the waves;  
the moving fluid of the deep  
provides a path for him who hangs above it.  
[Col. 0899A] Nor does the wave grow tired  
when pressed beneath holy footsteps.

Wednesday.

Accustomed to gnashing in a burial cave  
under chains,  
with mind powerless amid savage  
and frenzied passions,  
he springs forth and rushes supplicantly  
when he senses that Christ is present.

The plague of slippery demons,  
in a thousand forms,  
seizes the herd of swine,  
dirty with filth,  
and plunges itself into black waters  
with the frantic herd.

[Col. 0899B] Once five loaves  
and two fish had been consumed,  
thousands of those reclining at table  
were abundantly refreshed;  
twelve baskets  
carried away the fragments.

You are our food and bread,  
you are everlasting sweetness.  
Whoever receives your meal  
does not know hunger forever;  
nor does he merely fill the hollow of the belly,  
but he nourishes the vital powers.

Thursday.

The passage of the ears, closed  
and ignorant of sounds,  
is cleansed at Christ’s command  
of every thick obstruction;  
it becomes capable of enjoying voices  
and ready for whispers.

Every illness gives way;  
all weakness is driven off.  
The tongue that age-old silence  
had bound now speaks,  
and the joyful sick man carries  
his own bed through the world.

[Col. 0899C] Indeed, so that the inhabitants below  
might not be deprived of salvation,  
the merciful one enters Tartarus.  
The broken [Perhaps: shattered] door gives way;  
the bolt falls when torn away;  
[Col. 0899D] the hinge is undone.

That door, ready for those rushing in  
and tenacious against those returning,  
its barrier having been forced out, stands open  
and gives the dead back.

[C] According to your law, the dark threshold  
is now open to be trampled again.

But while God illuminates  
the chambers of death with shining light,  
while he offers a bright day  
to the astonished darkness,  
the stars grew pale  
in the mournful, barren sky.

The sun, soiled with mournful rust,  
[Col. 0900A] abandoned its fiery axis  
and, grieving, hid itself,  
and the world is said to have collapsed  
into the chaos of eternal night.

Friday.

Loose your voice, sonorous mind;  
loose your moving tongue.  
Tell of the trophy of the Passion;  
tell of the triumphant cross.  
Sing the marked banner  
that shines upon foreheads.

O new and wondrous deed,  
miracle [source: “miracles”] of the wound!  
From one side flowed a stream of blood,  
from the other, water;  
water indeed gives the bath,  
and then the crown is made from blood.

[Col. 0900B] The serpent saw the sacrificed  
sacred bodily victim;  
it also saw the gall that had been burned,  
and the voice lost its poison.  
Wounded by great pain,  
its neck broken, it hisses in pain.

What did it profit you, profane serpent,  
to strike the first creation  
with your newly devised,  
crafty counsel?

The mortal form, having received God,  
washed away the guilt.

[Col. 0900C] Saturday.

For a brief use of death  
the Leader of salvation gave himself,  
so that the dead, once buried,  
might grow accustomed to return,  
their former bonds of sin  
having been dissolved.

Then the fathers and many saints,  
following the advancing Creator  
as he was already returning,  
at last, on the third day,  
put on the garments of the flesh.

And from the tombs you might see  
their bodies, once dry and shapeless,  
emerging;  
the cold dust, with its veins restored,  
growing warm;

[Col. 0900D] bones, nerves, and marrow  
being clothed with skin by adhesion.

Hymn after [Perhaps: before] the Lord’s Ascension.

After he had undone life’s sunset  
and restored humanity,  
the victorious one ascended  
to the lofty tribunal of the Father,  
bringing back to heaven  
the illustrious glory of the Passion.

Hail, Judge of the dead;  
hail, King of the living;  
you who are at the right hand  
in the Father’s citadel,  
[Col. 0901A] from there you will come,  
the just avenger of all crimes.

The old and the young,  
the children’s chorus,  
the crowd of mothers and virgins,  
the simple young girls—  
all, harmonious in chaste voices,  
will resound with songs.

The courses of rivers and waves,  
the ridges of shores,  
rain, heat, snow, frost,  
forest and breeze, night and day—  
let all celebrate you  
through the ages of ages.

[Col. 0901B] Let us sound forth the glory  
of the Father with melodious voices;  
let us sing glory to Christ,  
glory to the Paraclete—  
the triune and one God  
who reigns before the ages.

Amen.

Hymn for the Lord’s Resurrection during the week at Terce. [“Holding firmly.”]

Jesus, Redeemer of all,  
who, crushing death by death,  
on the third day rise  
from the depths of hell,

we beseech you, wretched as we are,  
for whom you poured out your blood:  
[Col. 0901C] cleanse us from our crimes  
and lead us back to the heavenly seats,  
where we may be joined to those above  
who sing this hymn  
and offer songs of praise to you;  
there may we enjoy you more fully.

Grant:::::

[CI] Hymn for the Lord’s Resurrection on Sundays, from the octave of Easter until the Ascension.

“Angels of a hundred thousand legions.” Fol. 382.

Hymn for the feast of Saint Engratia and the eighteen martyrs.

Twice nine of our people  
keep the ashes of the martyrs  
in one tomb.  
We call the city Zaragoza,  
[Col. 0901D] a thing so great is its glory.

A house full of great angels  
does not fear the ruin of the fragile world,  
bearing in its bosom together  
the offerings to be presented to Christ.

He will come, shaking the flashing right hand of God,  
supported by a cloud and reddened,  
to place before the nations  
a just balance with an equal weight.

Raising its head from the great earth,  
the city will hasten to go out to meet Christ;  
the precious city too, carrying  
gifts in baskets.

You, Zaragoza, devoted to Christ,  
will lead forth the eighteen saints,  
your crown bound with yellow olives  
in honor of peace.

You alone have prepared for the Lord  
a more numerous crowd of martyrs  
to meet him;  
you alone, rich in great piety,  
will enjoy abundant light.

Hardly does the populous mother  
of the world, Rome herself seated on her throne,  
deserve in this gift  
to surpass you, our glory.

[Col. 0902A] Here too, Engratia, your bones rest—the tokens of your valor—  
by which, forceful virgin, you dishonored  
the spirit of the savage world  
[the printed *Spiritu* is syntactically damaged].

[Col. 0902B] No martyr returning to life  
has been granted to dwell in our lands;  
you alone, surviving your own death,  
live throughout the world.

You live, and almost unfold the whole sequence  
of your mutilation;  
you preserve the flesh’s cut-off remains,  
telling what wounds the earth’s furrows contain.

The barbarous torturer tore your entire side;  
blood was poured out; your limbs were lacerated;  
your breast, its nipple cut off, was exposed,  
with the heart beneath it.

Not yet has the price of death been fully paid:  
he who destroyed the venomous pains  
gave your agitated limbs rest  
at the final end.

[Col. 0902C] A raw scar held you for a long time;  
for a long while burning pain remained in your veins,  
while a wasting fluid thinned  
your rotting marrow.

Although the persecutor’s sword, envious of your final death,  
denied you death itself,  
nevertheless, martyr, as one wholly slain,  
your punishment crowns you.

We saw part of your liver torn away;  
it would have lain far off, pressed down by claws.  
Death, driving something from your limbs,  
has you too alive.

Christ himself gave Zaragoza  
this new title to enjoy:  
[Col. 0902D] that it should be a perpetual house  
dedicated to a living martyr.

Therefore, with three times six sacred candidates,  
rich together with Optatus and Lupercus,  
go on, set forth in psalms  
the senate enrolled for you.

Bring forth Successus; sing Martial;  
let Mors and Urbanus be sung for you;  
let the song of Julius resound,  
together with Quintilianus.

Let the chorus sing Publius,  
and unfold what trophy Fronton possessed;  
what the good Felix endured,  
and what the fierce Caecilianus endured.

How much blood of Euvotus  
dyed your battles; how much of Primitive;  
while praise of Apodemus  
recalls your living triumphs.

[Col. 0903A] After these, the name of four men remains  
to be extolled, although the meter resists it;  
ancient times remember them  
as having been called Saturnini.

This throng, placed beneath the eternal altar,  
prays pardon for our faults,  
while the creator of the purple-robed nobles preserves it  
[the subject of *servat* is implicit; *mater* is not in the supplied text].

Let us wash with pious tears  
the furrows of the marble  
under which hope is buried,  
so that it may release  
the bonds of my restraints.

[Col. 0903B] Cast yourself down, noble-robed city, with me  
upon the holy tombs;  
then you will wholly follow  
the souls and bodies of those who soon rise again.

Let the glory resound:::::

V. “The saints shall exult.”

Hymn for the feast of Saints Cyriacus and Paula. Thirteen days before the Kalends of June. [“Praise of blessed Eulalia.”]

[Col. 0903D]

The sacred season is marked in the reckoning;  
the circle of the year revolves.  
Let praise resound in the choir  
from the mouths of people and clergy.

Let them praise Christ God,  
who gave Cyriacus the martyr  
and Paula his companion  
the strength of steadfastness.

For the governor of Carthage  
at that time was a terrible man,  
Anolinus by name,  
bearing a monstrous reputation.

He is intent on searching out the saints;  
when the name of Christ has been marked,  
Silvanus soon led Cyriacus and Paula  
into the hall.

[Col. 0904A] Then, questioned, the martyrs  
confess the God who is in heaven.  
They declared with gracious words  
that they would not sacrifice to idols.

Thereupon the saints’ soothing words anointed their hearts;  
yet they scorned the empty shrines  
and believed in Christ in heaven.

The judge, filled with fury,  
struck their sacred bodies;  
he changed the kinds of punishments,  
but did not change their believing hearts.

The martyrs were cut down  
beside beautiful palm trees.  
[Col. 0904B] With a broad stroke, their souls  
migrated to the halls of heaven.

Then Silvanus cast the bodies  
into the fire;  
but a great rain from heaven  
extinguished the fire’s force.

Therefore, Lord, we pray:  
on the feast of these martyrs,  
receive the vows of all  
and grant what they ask.

So, while we complete our lives,  
free us from vices,  
and, our conduct amended,  
make us abound in virtues.

To God the Father.

[Col. 0904C] V. “The souls of the righteous.”

Hymn for the feast of Saint Matthew. [“Feast of Clemens.”]

Christ, creator and craftsman of things,  
you rule Olympus and sustain the dry earth;  
you adorn the heavens with starlit light,  
and [Col. 0905C] fill the world with the offspring of humankind.  
Command that the sea not overflow its boundary.

You gave to the first-formed man and his offspring  
the meaning of the law implanted in nature,  
so that he might impose it upon the brother  
whom he wishes for himself.  
At last Moses received from you, on two tablets,  
ten life-giving commandments.

[Col. 0905D] After this came the prophets, twice eight in number;  
they instructed the hearts of the people toward salvation,  
destroyed the vain error of idols,  
proclaimed that you are the heavenly God,  
and announced that the Incarnate One was to be awaited.

When the world had five thousand two hundred years  
in sequence from its origin,  
then the true Lamb, born of the Virgin,  
in the thirtieth year of your time  
was baptized by John.

Thereafter you chose the foreknown Apostles:  
Peter, Andrew, John, and James,  
Bartholomew, Judas, and Simon,  
Thomas, Philip, and James of Alphaeus,  
and Matthew, calling him from the tax office [source: telonium].

After your ascension, O Christ, into heaven,  
he quickly journeyed to the Ethiopians.  
Soon he was received by Candace’s eunuch;  
he freed the magician from the magi [or: the magician from the magicians],  
and in sleep transformed the most savage dragons.

He exhorted the people to despise false gods  
and to believe in the true God, Jesus Christ,  
[Col. 0906A] so that they might enjoy the delights of paradise.

Soon he was summoned by King Eglippus  
and raised his son from the dead.

[CIV] The king saw, believed, and the people built a temple,  
in which the king and his wife,  
having been baptized,  
with Eufranon, the people, and Eugenia led a holy life  
until Irtacus took up the rule.

For the unlearned king summoned the Apostle  
and promised him half the kingdom,  
so that Eugenia, a virgin, might be given to him;  
she had two hundred holy virgins  
in monasteries, wearing sacred veils.

At this Matthew exhorted Irtacus:  
“It is not lawful for a servant  
to take the King’s bride,  
nor is it lawful for Christ’s bride  
to be joined to your marriage.”

[Col. 0906B] Because of this Irtacus immediately ordered  
the Apostle to be struck with a sword.  
Praying, he migrated to heaven, pierced through.

Soon the virgin Eugenia offered gold,  
and they built a basilica worthy of Christ,  
in which Matthew rests in a sarcophagus.  
Virtues flourish there through everlasting ages.

The king ordered the virgins to be burned,  
but a wind driving the flame  
burned the king’s halls.  
Soon he was struck throughout by elephantiasis,  
seized by the fury of a demon;  
but the father, struck by the sword, breathed out his soul.

Then Eugenia’s brother succeeded to the kingdom,  
whose baptismal name was Beor,  
[Col. 0906C] whom the holy martyr had anointed  
and marked with chrism.  
The provinces and basilicas alike  
sing to God with sweet melody.

O Christ, make the king’s and people’s vows effective.  
Give help to the sick, raise up the crushed,  
grant comfort of mind, give rest to the dead;  
ward off plague, war, and litigation,  
and strengthen peace in the fraternal heart.

We, your little servants, suppliantly ask, O Christ:  
may this Apostle stand as our advocate;  
may he obtain pardon for our sins,  
with all vices utterly torn away,  
so that, while life remains, it may flourish in virtues.

[Col. 0906D] Let glory resound to the unbegotten Father;  
glory always to Christ the Only-Begotten;  
glory to the Holy Spirit, the Paraclete,  
whose praise and power are eternal  
through infinite ages of ages.

V. “In everlasting memory.”

Hymn for the Beheading of Saint John the Baptist.

“This John was wondrously born.” As in this feast.

V. “In everlasting memory.”

Hymn for the feast of Saint Jerome, priest. [“An illustrious feast.”]

“Christ is the Father’s power and wisdom” [source: wisdom]. As in his feast.

Hymn for the feast of Saints Maximus and Julia, most valiant.

This day, joyful for us,  
the blood of the martyrs has consecrated:  
the faith of the most valiant Maximus  
and of his sister Julia.

The Trinity rejoices in these,  
in their unequal yet joyful number;  
the heavens are filled with joy  
at the fellowship of the martyrs.

[Col. 0907A] They are dragged to punishment,  
born of noble stock.  
They believe themselves noble  
if they can die for the Lord.

The impious judge, roaring,  
orders punishments to be prepared;  
he tries to disturb the saints,  
whom he sees standing unmoved.

[Col. 0907B] They are suspended on the rack,  
armed with the banner of the cross,  
faithful souls offering their lives  
for the King unto death.

They are plunged into the vast sea,  
stones pressing upon their necks.  
The swift soldiers of Christ  
reach the shore sooner than rowers  
[the compressed *ora … quam remiges* is uncertain].

The Basque Charybdis gave them back;  
Olisipo deserved them;  
the farthest boundaries of the earth  
are made glorious by the martyrs’ blood.

Therefore we offer thanks  
to you, almighty God,  
the one God in Trinity,  
who give help to the saints.

[Col. 0907C] Therefore we pray, Lord:  
on the feast of these martyrs,  
receive the vows of all  
and grant what they ask.

Grant . . . .

Hymn for the feast of Saints Faustus, Januarius, and Martial. [“Christ, King and Creator of the world.”]

Let the mystical melody be offered  
and let the people dedicated to God the Father  
raise their praises.  
With due honor  
let them sweetly sing a hymn

[CV] to Christ and the Paraclete.

For the triumphs of the blessed

At 0898A, *quam* [*quem*], “whom”; at 0899A, *percitis* [*percitus*], “frenzied,” and *greges subilli* [*gregis suilli*], “herd of swine”; at 0899B, *vatur* [*fatur*], “speaks”; at 0899D, *Facta* [perhaps *Fracta*], “made” [perhaps “broken”], and *refulsis* [*revulsis*], “shining” [read “torn away”]; at 0900A, *Polluerunt* [*Palluerunt*], “defiled” [read “grew pale”], and *miracula* [*miraculum*], “miracles” [read “miracle”]; at 0900B, *immolatum* [*immolatam*], “sacrificed”; at 0900C, *diem* [*die*], “day”; and at 0900D, *medulla* [*medullas*], “marrow,” and *post* [perhaps *ante*], “after” [perhaps “before”].

At 0905D, *toloneo* [*telonio*], “tax office”; at 0906A, *a magos* [*a magis*], “from magicians”; at 0906C, *ratam* [*rata*], “effective”; and at 0906D, *sapientiam* [*sapientia*], “wisdom.” The source’s bracketed hymn incipits are retained at their corresponding feast headings above.

[Col. 0907D] Faustus, Januarius,

And third, Martialis;

In the contest they conquered,

By confessing the Trinity,

Having undergone martyrdom.

With a faithful voice proclaiming

The titles of the blessed,

How they conquered the enemy

Amid their sufferings,

By confessing the Trinity,

They attained joy.

With bloodstained hands the cruel enemy,

With a savage claw,

Ordered the consecrated bodies

Of the blessed to be torn apart;

[Col. 0908A] Stretched out alike and cut to pieces,

The burning flame torments them.

Then, with their eyes torn out,

And the heads of the skins/bodies [cutenorum; reading uncertain]—

The structure of their sinews destroyed—

Cruelty nevertheless preserves them;

It crushes the bones of the righteous

And penetrates their marrow.

Protected by the right hand of Christ,

They do not fear the fires;

By angelic medicine

Their eyes are restored,

Their broken limbs are strengthened,

And their wounds are healed.

The tyrant is utterly amazed

[Col. 0908B] At such great miracles,

When he sees alive

Those whom he had ordered to perish;

How they had overcome every kind

Of torture.

They patiently endure

What the enraged men inflict,

Knowing that those who have endured

Such things for Christ

Acquire heavenly rewards

In which they rejoice forever.

Some saw the heavenly gifts

Coming down,

A great host of angels

Waiting above,

[Col. 0908C] To crown

The glorious heads of the saints.

Come to us, saints of God,

To the people who beseech you,

And grant those who ask

The remedy they seek,

So that they may share

In your fellowship of the kingdom.

Grant [this] . . . .

℣. Of the righteous.

Hymn for the feast of Saints Cosmas and Damian.

The people dedicated to God, resplendent. As in their feast.

℣. Precious.

Hymn for the feast of Saints Servandus and Germanus. [“Christ, King of the world.”]

[Col. 0908D] Christ, true King of the saints. As in their feast.

℣. “They shall exult.”

Hymn for the feast of Saints Vincent, Sabina, and Christeta.

“Here the devout people lovingly summon you.” As in their feast.

℣. As above.

Hymn for the feast of Saint Martin, bishop.

“Martin, confessor of God.” As in his feast.

Also hymns for the saints.

Let us, companions, sing the glorious joys

Of the merits of the saints and their mighty deeds,

For the spirit burns to proclaim in song

The excellent race of the victorious.

These are they before whom the world, holding them back, trembled,

[Col. 0909A] For they utterly scorned it, with its barren flower,

Along the arduous way, and followed you,

Good heavenly King Christ.

For you they trampled underfoot furies and savagery,

The fierce scourges of men;

You endured the claws tearing you violently

[The reading is uncertain: “Cessit iis . . . ungula”—“the claw yielded to them . . .”]

And did not cut into the inner parts.

Swords are struck down, as those who see [them],

Yet no murmur resounds, no complaint;

But with a silent heart and a conscience rightly aware,

Patience preserves [them].

What voice, what tongue could unfold

What gifts you prepare for the martyrs?

For, with flowing red blood, they are enriched

With shining crowns.

[Col. 0909B] [CVI] We beseech you, Triune and One God,

To wash away guilty offenses and remove evils,

To grant peace to your servants, and also glory to us,

Throughout all ages.

Another.

Ruler, Redeemer, and Creator,

Who once granted your little servants

In this age

The grace to despise its pleasures,

Pour down upon us from heaven

Your equal glory with the Father,

So that our now lukewarm hearts

May blaze with their own fire.

There, leaving earthly things behind,

Moved by your inspiration,

They followed the slaughter of their bodies

[Col. 0909C] And attained the kingdom of heaven.

Therefore, we beseech you, prostrate,

That on account of the triumphs of the martyrs

To whom we offer a hymn to God

At their appointed recurring times,

Through their intercessions

You may lead all cleansed from filth

Upward from the depths,

Restoring them to the sacred dwelling.

Grant [this] . . . .

Another.

Glorious King of the martyrs,

Crown of those who confess,

[Col. 0909D] You lead those who despise earthly things

To heavenly realms.

Immediately lend a kindly ear

To our voices.

We sing of the sacred trophy;

Forgive what we have done wrong.

You conquer in the martyrs

By sparing those who confess;

You conquer our sins

By granting pardon.

Another.

The eternal gifts of Christ

And the victories of the martyrs,

Let us sing praises and hymns,

Let us sing with joyful hearts.

[Col. 0910A] The leaders of the churches,

The triumphant commanders,

The soldiers of the heavenly court,

And the true lights of the world,

Having conquered the terrors of the age [the source also prints singular *Terrore*]

And scorned bodily punishments,

By the shortcut of sacred death

They possess blessed light.

The martyrs are handed over to fire

And to the teeth of beasts;

The mad hand of the torturer rages,

Armed with chains.

Their exposed entrails hang down;

Sacred blood is poured out,

And their devoted faith remains unmoved.

[Col. 0910B] Their hope in the grace of everlasting life

Is unconquered,

Their love of Christ is perfect.

The leaders of the world triumph;

In them is the glory of the Father,

In them the will of the Spirit,

In them the Son rejoices;

Heaven is filled with joy.

Now we beseech you, Redeemer,

To join your servants who pray

To the fellowship of the martyrs

Forever and ever.

Another.



[Col. 0910C] Let us sing with pure hearts

The praises of the holy martyrs,

Whom sacred suffering made

Conformed to the glory of Christ,

The soldiers of heaven,

Secure in future rewards.

Neither the vanity of the world



Nor impious terror broke them.

Neither the dark prisons,

Nor the burdens of iron on their necks,

Nor handcuffs or fetters

Could alter their minds from joy.

Even the water of the eternal fountain,

Once they had been refreshed by its draught,

[Col. 0910D] Cooled the thirst of their present bodies.

Denied bread,

The holiness within them felt no hunger;

Those whom he habitually feeds by his word

Lived richly by faith,

With the proven strength of their hearts.

Overcoming so many afflictions,

They undertook the public contest.

Seeking life, the martyrs,

Whom neither prison,

Nor hunger, nor chains had broken,

Joyfully endured punishments

And conquered the prince of the world,

Following Christ,

Their Lord and Creator.

[Col. 0911A] After cruel fires and swords

They flourish in eternal rewards.

[CVII] Hymns for one righteous man.

God, lot, crown, and reward

Of your soldiers,

As we sing the praises of the martyr,

Release us from the bond of sin.

He rightly regarded

The joys of the world

And its harmful allurements

As fleeting,

And reached the heavenly realms.

He bravely ran through punishments

And manfully endured them;

Pouring out his blood for you,

He possesses eternal gifts.

[Col. 0911B] Therefore, suppliantly praying,

We beseech you, most merciful one:

At this triumph of the martyr,

Forgive the guilt of your servants.

Another.

God, immense Trinity,

Ever-glorious Unity,

Father, Christ, Paraclete,

Unconquered Lord of all things,

By the abundance of your gift

You granted your martyr

To endure with steadfast mind

This most devoted feast

Which we celebrate today,

And these most savage torments,

These varied sufferings,

[Col. 0911C] Which he bore

With your victorious right hand.

We beseech you more abundantly,

As we bow before you,

Lord, that through him

You may grant heavenly fellowship,

The lofty gifts of the heights.

You are recognized as the prince

Of princes and the mystical King.

By generous mercy

Erase our acknowledged sins,

So that, when your radiant coming,

Christ, has appeared,

Under the guidance of your martyr

We may joyfully go to meet you.

Another.

[Col. 0911D] Martyr of God, who, following

The only Son of the Father,

Triumphs victoriously over enemies,

And, victorious, enjoys heavenly things,

By the gift of your prayer

Wash away our guilt,

Keep the contagion of evil away,

And remove the weariness of life.

The bonds of your consecrated body

Have now been broken;

Release us from the bonds of the world

Through love of the Son of God.

May your devotion draw near,

You who are coequal with the Father,

[Col. 0912A] And with the Holy Spirit,

Living throughout every age.

Amen.

Hymn for one Confessor.

Most high holy Confessor and priest,

The turning wheel of time drives on the years;

The time has come for us, consecrated to you,

To celebrate the feast.

Distinguished bishop, renowned for your merits,

The sacred throng of clergy and people,

Prostrate in heart with great devotion,

Calls you “Father.”

In the court of the eternal King,

may you present the vows of all

and cherish both orders,

Whose devout shepherd

You were in the city.

[Col. 0912B] All the mourners recount their complaints;

They reveal by deeds and tears

The crimes of their minds and souls,

Their wickedness and dark guilt.

When the harsh wrath of heaven burns the wretched,

it calls their deeds back to their lips,

compelling them to pay the deserved penalty

for deeds that disturb the world.

Keep us far from the thunderer’s fall;

Drive away sins and restrain his fury.

We ask that pestilence and disease

withdraw. [The following transmitted phrase, “Sospite cibe,” is corrupt.]

Govern life with cultivated morals;

grant a clear and peaceful mind,

So that hearts may meditate upon

The weapons of virtue,

The gifts of Christ.

[Col. 0912C] Holy one, whenever you are asked,

Provide abundant fruits

And plentiful rains.

We believe that, with the Lord’s favor,

You are able to grant all things.

We believe that Christ has given

a just reward for labors;

released from those labors even in your body,

you are blessed in death.

Let us sing glory to Christ,

with a mouth serving him excellently [the source also prints the variant *prestanti*];

To him who, simple in his great divinity,

Is Three and One.

Another.

[Col. 0912D] God, immense Trinity,

Crown of those who confess,

[CVIII] Great praise of the martyrs,

Receive the prayers of the faithful.

Grant us the consolations

Of the merits of this holy bishop

And confessor,

And cleanse all evils,

So that you may raise up those who confess

And redeem sinners,

Granting pardon

And bestowing grace.

And just as this man confessed

Your name before mortals,

[Col. 0913A] So may we, with devoted minds,

Confess you before all.

Hymn for Virgins.

Jesus, crown of virgins,

Whom that mother conceived,

Whom the virgin alone gave birth to,

Mercifully accept these vows.

You feed among lilies,

Surrounded by choirs of virgins;

You adorn your brides with glory,

And return rewards to your brides.

Wherever you go, virgins

Follow you,

Rushing behind you while singing praises

And sounding sweet hymns.

[Col. 0913B] We beseech you most earnestly:

Increase in our minds

[So that we may] know absolutely none

Of the wounds of corruption.

Hymn for one Virgin.

Offspring of a Virgin and Maker of your mother,

you whom a Virgin carried and a Virgin bore,

We sing the triumph of the virgin’s feast;

Receive our vow.

This blessed virgin of yours,

While she bore a fragile lot,

Conquered it;

She subdued the bloody sex of the flesh

and the world through her body.

Therefore, fearing neither death

Nor death’s beloved,

Savage kinds of punishment,

[Col. 0913C] By the shedding of blood

She deserved to ascend

To the consecrated heaven.

For her sake, gracious God,

Now spare our sins,

Remitting our vices,

So that with pure hearts

We may resound for you

A holy hymn.

Glory to the Father and to the Son begotten,

And to you, ever equal to both,

Gracious Holy Spirit, one God,

Throughout all times and ages.

Amen.

Hymn at the consecration of a basilica.

Behold, Christ, this throng of suppliants

Always holds you dear;

With humble devotion it seeks

You, the almighty Redeemer, as Father.

[Col. 0913D] May this sacred, everlasting seat of yours

stand and remain perpetually for us,

with forgiveness granted for sins

committed in body and heart.

May heaven’s gate stand open here [*sedentis* is uncertain],

closed to the condemned

and opened to the just.

May Truth, Life, Way, Light, and Fire

Flow here gently.

Here, true man, God, and teacher,

Rock and shepherd, sheep and priest,

Bread and vine, sower and creator,

Look upon your people.

Here, [perhaps “flows” rather than “remains”] blessed water from the rock,

[Col. 0914A] Washing away offenses,

Destroying vices;

Renewing minds,

Removing stains,

From an everlasting spring.

Here, the head may revisit

Its own members;

Let open teaching feed the peoples,

So that the Bridegroom may give

Holy kisses to friendly souls.

Here let virtue blaze forth,

A beautiful appearance;

Here may doctrine reach its height and teach hearts;

Let supreme Life water

hearts laid open by doubt [the transmitted syntax is uncertain].

Whoever has fallen, is sad, and mourns,

Whoever is weary and languishing,

Whoever, wandering and humble,

Prays for anything—

He grants everything.

[Col. 0914B] Let him sing glory. ::::

Hymn for the anniversary of the consecration of a basilica.

Christ, gracious ruler of all,

Begotten from the mouth of the eternal Father,

Kindly behold the vows and hymn

Of those who beseech you.

Behold how your people, suppliant,

Resound in pure honor to God

Within this hall,

Whose annual feast returns

To be celebrated.

This house is rightly dedicated to you [the source prints *He*; the editor supplies *Haec*];

In it, the consecrated people

Are known to receive the sacred body

And drink the blessed

Blood.

These most holy streams

Wash away sins and destroy offenses,

So that, through true chrism,

A race of worshipers of Christ

May be created.

[Col. 0914C] Here salvation is brought to the sick,

Medicine to the weary,

[CIX] Light to the blind,

And forgiveness to our offenses;

All fear and grief

Are driven away.

Here savage plunder perishes

At the hands of demons;

The obstinate monster is afraid

And, abandoning the bodies it has seized,

Flees swiftly,

Far from them, into the shadows.

This place is rightly called

the hall of the immense King

and the snow-white gate of heaven and of life;

it receives all who seek the homeland.

[Col. 0914D] No storm shakes it,

Nor do wandering winds

Overturn and pierce it with clouds;

The grim, black, horrifying Tartarus

Does not harm it.

Therefore we beseech you, God,

As you govern your servants

With a serene face,

Who celebrate the joys of your temple

With supreme love:

Let no trouble of life torment us [the editor supplies singular *molestia*];

Let our days be joyful

And our nights peaceful;

When the world perishes,

Let none of us feel the fires.

May this day, on which you see

The altar consecrated to you,

grant us everlasting joy,

and may it flourish for us through long use [the transmitted ending is uncertain].

[Col. 0915A] Let glory resound to the Most High Father;

Glory likewise to Christ

And to the Holy Spirit.

Let us sing a sweetly composed hymn

Throughout every age.

Hymn for the restoration of a basilica.

O blessed Jerusalem,

City worthy of praise,

Joyful in your triumphs

Among the heavenly citizens,

Renewed by the great mark

Of the King’s radiance,

Bearing glorious honor,

A mother full of children,

[Col. 0915B] Rejoicing within the glorious bounds

of gracious peace,

Rightly restored

By the radiant lamp

Of holiness:

Here the more sacred memory

Of your temple shines,

On the luminous foundation

Of restoration.

When it shines with beauty,

With the star of dignity,

We beseech you, most holy Creator,

To be present here,

And here, ready to consecrate

The seats, to enter.

[Col. 0915C] And as the consecrator himself,

Be present here continually.

Now make us, your little servants,

A temple of your honor.

Let neither our flesh nor our hearts

Serve in peril,

But, dedicated to your sacred name,

Let us serve.

Visit, heavenly King,

This altar of yours,

Now rightly prepared again

In the glory of beauty.

Here let your power overflow;

Here let honor shine.

May this altar of the Most High King

[Col. 0915D] Be sparkling with light;

Let it be devoted to honor,

Filled with gifts;

Let it be blessed and serene,

Pleasing to God the King.

Here consecrate for you,

From above, O gracious judge,

The altars of our hearts,

Renewing us by grace,

Granting gifts from heaven

As you enter these dwelling-places.

So may the most holy Trinity,

Throughout every age,

Have honor, immeasurable power,

And everlasting glory,

[Col. 0916A] You who remain God in Trinity

Forever and ever.

Amen.

Hymn at the ordination of a bishop.

True Redeemer, Christ, light of light,

Image of the Father, invisible splendor,

Born from the Father before the ages,

Proceeding truly from a mother in time,

Fulfilling the covenant of the promise,

You are priest; you create priests.

You granted Aaron the primacy of this splendid office,

O glorious consecrator,

By the pouring of sacred, holy oil,

And, proclaiming his face with holy vesture,

The sublime one whose head receives

[Col. 0916B] Shining olive oil beneath a golden-foiled mitre,
