The stole of beauty and the vestment of the robe

Surround the same man,

Declaring him consecrated.

The dignity of colors impressed upon the garment,

Whose hyacinth, twisted byssus, and purple,

Whose devoted splendor they display,

The border of the sacred vestment,

[CX] radiant with bells hanging properly,

So that the pontiff might be heard as he entered the temple.

A beauty distinguished by gems

Was affixed beneath excellent figures:

Emerald, sardius, topaz,

Onyx, carbuncle, ligure,

Sapphire, jasper, and shining chrysolite,

Then beryl or gleaming agate,

[Col. 0916C] Together with amethyst, placed there

In its proper position within the order

And according to the law of distinction.

They gave a sign of future grace,

For these figures proclaimed that you are God,

Whose sacrament of grace,

Passing through the shadows of the age,

Reached you, excellent Liberator,

So that the truth might be revealed,

Completed in you,

Which the figures had mystically foretold [the source prints *que* and supplies *quem*].

Hence the very end of the law,

Approaching to cleanse the world’s guilt

For righteousness,

You yourself, the offering and consecrator,

Placed the victim upon the altar

Set before the Father;

By this sacrament raising up the Church,

[Col. 0916D] Of which you were made the Head

And the guiding Leader,

Placing bishops and rulers within it,

By whose laws it might be governed

And instructed,

So that, taught by the grace of pontiffs,

It might avoid the savage harms of death.

Therefore the crown of the brethren seeks you, Christ;

May the glorious grace of this succession

Descend upon these whom you choose for the future,

Leaders preferred by the one Dove [the phrase is textually uncertain],

Granting them the glory of the apostleship.

At Matins.

The consecration of the day is present, Christ,

To raise up for it the bishop of honor,

Renewed by the recurrence of our time,

With which all those appointed leaders

[Col. 0917A] Of the churches must resound.

May they be consecrated with sacred oil;

May they shine with the lamp of holiness;

May they be drenched with the gift of contrition;

May they be renewed by the song of confession,

With every contagion of sins driven away.

May they be pure in flesh

And radiant in speech;

May they be hospitable

And loving toward one another.

May they shine with signs,

Possessing healings;

May they drive away demonic spirits by their virtue,

And grow strong through the grace of truth.

May the twisted byssus of radiant chastity

And the purple concord of unity

Unceasingly fill their hearts.

When these things have openly taken their place

In their minds,

[Col. 0917B] May they be able to stand free

Before Christ’s altar.

May they have power both to bind and to loose

by episcopal privilege [the printed *probra* is corrupt];

To cure diseases of bodies and minds;

To bear witness to compassion;

To bear the turmoil and scandal

of disputes that have arisen.

Thus, after completing the courses of holiness,

May they attain the crown of life

Which you have prepared for all

Who love you, Christ, with a true heart,

Here, after the triumphs of the world,

To be consecrated forever

In the everlasting kingdom.

To the Trinity be everlasting glory,

highest honor, and illustrious power [the printed *sumus* is probably *summus*],

To the Trinity—the Father and the Son of the Father—

With the Spirit, one God in substance,

[Col. 0917C] Who reigns throughout all ages of ages.

Hymn at the ordination of a king.

Illustrious great King of kings,

Consecrator of rulers,

Truth, sign of the Father,

Christ, with true chrism,

By whose favor kingdoms endure

And rule over kings,

Advance the kingdom

Of the faithful prince

To glory.

May he shine with sacred oil;

May he flourish in holiness;

May the crown of life shine forth;

May mercy abound.

[Col. 0917D] May the whole people rejoice with him,

And all the people with their prince.

May this birthday

Be made a holiday in joy.

May it be full of every good vow,

A complete rejoicing,

So that, governing the kingdom piously,

With blessed customs,

He may rule modestly

Among those over whom he now presides,

So that together with them

He may enjoy the everlasting gift.

At the king’s birthday.

When the circle of the year has been completed,

This more solemn day is present,

The birthday of our prince,

The new return of time,

When, brought forth from his mother’s womb,

He sought the light of the world,

And entered the rising of this light,

Unknowing.

You, excellent Creator,



[Col. 0918A] have carried him through the cradles of infancy

and through the courses of time;

[CXI] you have brought him, mature in age, to manhood,

have trained him in learning,

and, as he advanced in understanding with the maturity of time,

have enriched him with royal honour.



Therefore, God, we beseech you

[Col. 0918B] To be present to his petitions,

Hearing the prayer of the one who asks

And granting the requested gift.

Hymn for the departure of an army, to be sung until its return during the days of the litanies.

O true governance of faithful people, Christ,

Who are life, way, and pious truth,

Illuminating believers

With conspicuous light

And also darkening the faithless:

You are the gracious only-begotten Redeemer,

The true begetter,

And we are your little dependents.

We beat our breasts with such tears;

Kindly attend to us who beseech you.

We humbly ask you:

Lead the rulers of the homeland

And all the peoples entrusted to them



[Col. 0918C] Along a straight road,

Giving the good of peace to all.

You who, answering the prayer of your servant Moses,

Divided the purple waters of the sea,

Lead the Israelite ranks across

The dried bed of the sea.

And you who reduced to nothing the enterprise

of that ruler Pharaoh,

returning by a most mighty path

and trampling the impious one,

you immediately drowned him

in overflowing water;

[Col. 0918D] And when you kindly answered his petitions,

Amalek, raging with great force

and becoming still more savage,

was struck by divine blows,

All his people being destroyed:

Be a peaceful leader to these your servants.

May angelic virtue remain with them;

May your glory keep watch over them,

You who are supreme goodness.

May your people proceed like calves,

From the flock of faith, with free courage,

And scatter the barbarian nations

With their horns,

And trample the impious beneath their feet.

The hostile ranks and weapons of war

Which the crowd of attendants vainly threatens [the editor suggests *frustra minitat*]

To direct more fiercely toward the slaughter of the people—

Overturn them, God, utterly.

With whose protection the renowned warrior,

David the shepherd,

[Col. 0919A] Subdued the tyrannical Goliath

By the impact of a stone,

And returned joyfully with the gift.

After him, in a later age,

you made generous Judas victorious in battle,

mercifully and swiftly driving distress

from the life-giving camp of the faithful.

Look upon the groans of our rulers,

Beholding the funeral murmurs of the people;

Cut down our rivals [the transmitted phrase *ex iusto iugulo* is corrupt].

You are the Father of all kings.

Let no dagger harm our borders,

But strengthen the spirit of the illustrious prince.

May he be strong in the power of grace in all things,

Having gained mastery everywhere.

Defend the people with your avenging right hand,

[Col. 0919B] The people purchased at the sacred price of blood,

And wash them in this flood of the font.

Grant, Christ, all your sacred soldiers [the source prints *militer*, with *milites* supplied as the correction]

A victorious palm over their enemies;

Grant it from heaven to Christ-loving rulers,

Who love you with all their strength.

May they now complete what they have begun

With prosperous steps;

May they return in peace to their own homes

and sing again the hymn pledged to you

with these ethereal voices.

To the Triune and One Lord

Be glory;

To him be everlasting kingdom

And ever-increasing perpetuity,

Who are always a jeweled crown

For your servants,

Reigning through all ages.

Amen.

Hymn for various disaster.

[Col. 0919C]

Eternal King, God, fountain of mercy,

Tranquil hope, true salvation, healing,

Rest for the weary, pasture of life,

Unfailing light, overflowing pardon:

To you we all draw near,

Offering murmurs of grief,

Your servants bowed down.

You do not wish to punish the wretched with death,

But rather that the converted should live.

You are that shady refuge

To which, while wavering,

The mind conscious of guilt

At last hastens

And perceives it as forgiveness

And salvation for the frail.

Therefore we, exceedingly terrified by this event,

[Col. 0919D] Whom a devastating blow of disaster punishes,

Flee to you, gracious Redeemer,

So that mercy may soon follow guilt.

The death that the prophet once foretold

In threatening words,

As Jeremiah prophesied,

We see approaching our own homes

And swiftly entering our houses and windows.

And David, in a more grievous time,

When impious disaster ravaged the city,

Suffered;

Now, too, the avenging sword

Cuts down those who dwell within our borders

On account of our merits.

[CXII] Behold, the plague of disease,

ranging more widely [the printed *crasans* is corrupt],

draws dangerously near us.

Now close at hand because of our sins,

it cuts down the ranks of the people [the transmitted syntax is uncertain].

[Col. 0920A] Some it kills more harshly,

sending the fiery heat of fever through their limbs.

Their members, reduced to putrefying flow,

Give off no breath,

Nor does the lung breathe.

No strength remains in human flesh;

It lies helpless,

Exhausted by pain.

At this spectacle of ruin [the printed *laudis* is corrupt],

everything wastes away,

As wax is accustomed to flee

Before fire.

Infants, young men,

Both sexes,

Old age itself,

Already like a swan,

And even nursing children at their mothers’ breasts—

All alike are struck down

By the dreadful wound.

Cities once filled beyond measure with citizens,

Castles with peoples, and every village with inhabitants,

Have been made empty;

They have become a solitude.

[Col. 0920B] The dry earth remains without cultivator.

Our sins deserve this plague;

Our crime gives birth to this ulcer.

This deadly fate of the livestock, too,

exacts the penalties that our offenses have earned.

Therefore, all of us bow down

And beseech you, merciful Christ,

To behold your holy face.

You who are always good and kind,

Raise up those contrite in heart [the printed *piatos* is uncertain].

At Sext. [“Eternal King.”]

O Creator, now suspend

The anger by which we are deservedly laid low,

According to your fatherly justice,

And mercifully drive away from our people

The greatly raging sword of the plague.

Erase now the stains committed in the mind;

Cleanse whatever unjust wound is present;

Release the knots of faithlessness;

[Col. 0920C] Restrain this savage blow from heaven everywhere [the line is corrupt].

May your mercy plead with you for us;

And, glorious one, inspire your saints

To raise such a voice for the wretched

That it may enter your ears.

Now see our groans;

Behold the lamentations,

And hear, mercifully,

The roar of the people,

The cries and tears and mournful complaints

Of the bishops and sacred rulers.

Lend us, undeserving as we are,

Your favorable ear,

So that, although burdened by the weight of guilt,

You may not destroy us

By the easy decay of the ulcer.

You redeemed us with your own sacred blood.

You changed the weeping of the sinners of Nineveh

For the better,

And suddenly from heaven

Made harmless the death

Which the fearful had already dreaded.

[Col. 0920D] Let all these, so many murmurs of ours,

Ascend to the fiery summit of your height,

So that saving relief

May rightly come swiftly to all.

Great one, restrain the plague of the groin in all it has seized [the syntax is uncertain];

powerfully check the varied assaults of death

and every harmful thing inflicted.

With your holy right hand,

Mercifully keep them away.

Heavenly physician, awe-inspiring Christ,

[Col. 0921A] Gather up the various attacks of death;

Restore them powerfully,

And reveal strength to the suffering people.

At None. [“Eternal King.”]

Drive away this bitter punishment of plague,

O Creator, once the crime has been removed,

So that, as the dreadful old disease flees [the editor suggests *morbi fugiens* for the corrupt wording],

increased health may succeed among the peoples.

O giver, with the holy oil of your own reward,

cherish the weakened limbs;

Join together the sinews now loosened,

And, granting life,

Wash away the bonds.

Even if a heavier guilt presses upon us,

May your greater grace prevail,

[Col. 0921B] So that, releasing the bonds

Of our burden,

You may grant forgiveness

And remit the debts due [to us].

Grant, Unbegotten One,

Supreme glory,

Who, with the Begotten One,

Fill all things;

Equal to the Spirit,

One Trinity,

True God,

Governing the ages.

Hymn for drought.

The fields of the soil lie rough with much dust;

The dry air grows pale;

The earth cracks.

There is no burden of dew,

No beauty,

When no strength or grace of flowers exists.

The parched earth thirsts;

it knows no *aroris* [perhaps ploughing or ploughman; the reading is corrupt].

The fountain no longer knows waters,

Nor the rivers their courses.

The soil does not know grass;

It does not know the plow.

Broken, it lies open,

Ugly with great fissures.

[Col. 0921C] The fiery earth boils with heat;

The burning ardor rages.

The heat burns the leafy branches themselves;

the dusty sands deny shelter

to the weary;

the traveller spits with a dry mouth.

The beast carries its mouth toward the winds,

And men, seeking the breath of the wind,

Open their mouths toward the winds;

Birds likewise open their beaks to the winds,

Wishing by this deception

To soothe their thirst.

The doe refuses her young,

Her cherished offspring,

Exhausted by thirst;

The sad doe abandons her young

because she cannot find the grass she seeks. [The preceding doe-and-offspring lines are badly transmitted.]

Young men come with cups [the printed *noti* is uncertain],

seeking a well, but the water flees.

[Col. 0921D] [CXIII] They return to their homes

with empty vessels,

their own mouths trembling with weeping [the line is uncertain].

The ox leaves its empty manger,

And, wishing to crop the grass of the meadows,

Turns over the bare earth;

Thus every animal,

Cheated of grass,

Falls dying.

The rustic people search the roots

Of the woods with miserable labor,

Seeking to relieve hunger with bark;

But the dry earth provides no tender juices.

Our sins deserve this hunger.

But, Christ, be appeased by the fitting recompense [the transmitted wording is uncertain],

So that, where guilt is greater,

Grace may be greater,

And may loosen the bonds

Of just punishment.

Now open the heavens,

And loosen the fields;

We ask for a second, gentle rain.

[Col. 0922A] By the merits of Elijah

You gave rain to the impious age;

Grant it to us also,

Eternal Father.

Glory to Christ;

May glory always be to you,

With the Begotten One,

And to the equal Spirit,

Who are one God,

Powerful throughout everlasting ages,

Illustrious forever.

Amen.

℣. “God, watering the mountains.”

Hymn for abundance of rain.

The clouds of heaven have covered the sky

And conceal the day,

With the sun driven away [the source also prints *sole*];

We endure continuous nights,

Bare of stars,

And once bereft of the moon.

The dreadful ether flashes

With flickering fire,

And the world trembles

At the shaken hinge of the heavens.

[Col. 0922B] The waters of the sea swell with the rains,

And now the waters know no proper boundaries;

The wave fluctuates over the earth,

Wearied by the land,

And a wandering keel cuts through the fields.

The sailor seeks his ports,

The sailor seeks his shores,

The sailor seeks his retreats.

The sailor, himself a guest, sails over vines and crops

that have become hostile to him [the transmitted couplet is corrupt].

The farmers leave their cultivated fields,

Weeping,

And watch the sad shipwreck of their labor.

The joyful harvest floats,

The seed of wealth;

The offspring seek their homes,

And migrate from the fields.

You may see the high roofs of houses

Being carried away,

[Col. 0922C] And lights set in altered places;

You may see fish

Playing amid the sad dwellings [the printed *abes* is probably *aedes*],

Playing in trembling roofs.

You may see nests torn from the trees,

Carried across the waters

With their tender young,

And the mother, banished,

No longer able to care for them,

compelled by greater fear to seek the waters [the transmitted syntax is uncertain].

A crowd of men watches from the windows;

A crowd of female modesty watches;

A crowd of those praying laments their lot [the printed *famam* is uncertain].

May the sailor provide food

From the ships.

Jesus, spare those whom your death redeemed.

The earlier age endured the flood,

So that water might cleanse the sins of the earth;

But the earth has been cleansed

By your blood.

[Col. 0922D] The dove, sent forth,

Carrying an olive branch,

The gift of peace,

Signifies by its joyful flight

That the lands have been freed

From the liquid flood.

Hymn for the newly married.

With a clarion trumpet, summon back

The people of Christ;

Celebrate these vowed joys in the church,

instructed by surpassing faith,

and confess your offenses.

Rightly proclaim the divine wonders;

Sound forth to heaven’s open gates

The gates which the dreadful envy of the serpent [the editor supplies *Quas*]

Had shut:

Christ now opens them all again.

[The transmitted fragment *Sit fera framea serpentis lancea* is incomplete or corrupt.]

[Col. 0923A] Womanly Eve defiled Adam, the first-created,

The original inhabitant,

Through the lips of womanly Eve,

And expelled him from his homeland.

They seized the forbidden fruits of the tree;

Their deceived eyes saw

Their bodies made squalid,

Burned by the serpent-bearing flame;

In sorrow they begot children.

Let the marriage songs be restored;

Let them receive grace again

With a paradisal voice.

“Be fruitful,” he cries;

“Fill the barren earth;

Adorn the marriage chambers.”

With nard-scented pistis [πίστις, “faith”; the transmitted line is corrupt] and ambrosial herb,

When the virgin mother [bore] the heavenly Christ,

Redeeming the wretched and inviting them to life,

It proclaims: “Rejoice.”

[Col. 0923B] Exult with choirs and drums;

Return everlasting vows to the Lord,

Who by the glory of the cross rescued [the source also prints nominative *gloria*]

The souls whom the serpent had bitten.

Little marriage band,

Take up the flute,

The lyre and the pipe;

Offer a song,

With an instrumental voice,

A melodious hymn;

Sing Davidic deeds [divitica; probably Davitica].

Make these present marriages fruitful,

O Lord,

With most worthy offspring

Who may serve you,

Give thanks to your name,

And remain blessed.

Let the lyre rejoice;

Let the cymbals resound;

Let the cithara sound;

Let the nabla dance

To the exalted Lord

Who rules all things

[Col. 0923C] Throughout all ages.

Amen.

[CXIV] General hymn for the sick.

“Christ, heavenly medicine of the Father.” Fol. 105.

General hymn for the dead.

“Christ, King, creator of the world.” As in the Office of the Dead.

Hymn to be sung at the funeral of the dead.

“God, fiery fountain of souls.” As in the Office of the Dead.

Hymn for one dead person.

Now is the day of his death (*functionis*),

For the believer in you, God the King.

Lead the faithful spirit of the deceased

To the choirs of heaven.

[Col. 0923D] Dispel his darkness;

Scatter his sins.

Let him be placed among heavenly beings,

Joined to the citizens of heaven.

May a serene day shine upon him;

May an everlasting star shine.

Let no weariness hold him;

May he be carried to the highest joys.

As he passes through

The prisons of the underworld

And every terrifying enclosure,

May he enjoy the homeland of heaven

In the ether.

Then, having received his body,

May he rise to glory,

[Col. 0924A] Praising for ever, as a heavenly inhabitant,

Your merciful grace [the transmitted reading is corrupt].

Grant [this] ::::

Daily Sunday hymns.

“Good inventor, leader of radiant light.” Fol. 91.

Another.

“O blessed light of the Trinity.” Fol. 113.

Another.

Attend to our prayers;

Now kindly attend,

O glory of Christ and of the world,

And pour out festive light.

May evening prayer sing you;

May morning prayer sing you;

May an unwearied hymn

Resound to you

[Col. 0924B] With sweet song.

At evening, fitting praise;

In the morning, the voice shall sing you.

Let every time resound to you

A hymn of everlasting glory.

Another.

True light, splendor of light,

Remaining inheritance of light,

Praise is brought forth in darkness;

Let splendor be given to those who pray.

May you, the time of every time,

And whatever has strength within us,

Praise together

Throughout the everlasting ages.

Another.

[Col. 0924C]

God, creator of all,

And ruler of heaven,

Who clothe the day

With beautiful lights,

And the night

With the grace of sleep:

So that rest may render the relaxed limbs fit again for labor,

And refresh exhausted minds,

And loosen anxious griefs.

With day now completed,

and at the rising of night, we offer prayers:

help us who are bound by our vow

as we sing a hymn.



[The transmitted text is corrupt: “Exultare nostru lubrico, / Te cordi alta somniet.”]

Lest the enemy’s envious deceit

[Col. 0924D] Awaken us from peaceful rest.

Let us ask Christ and the Father,

And the Spirit of Christ and the Father;

One Trinity,

Powerful over all things,

Favor those who pray.

Another.

“Christ, light, salvation, and power of the world.” Fol. 110.

Also daily evening hymns. Monday at Vespers.

Excellent Creator of light,

Bringing forth the light of day,

At the beginnings of light

Preparing the origin of the world;

[Col. 0925A] You who command

That the joining of morning and evening

Be called “day,”

while gloomy chaos comes on,

[CXV] Hear our prayers with tears,

Lest the mind, weighed down by sin,

Be exiled from the gift of life,

While it thinks of nothing eternal

And binds itself with sins.

May it strike the innermost heavens;

May it take up the reward of life.

Let us avoid every harmful thing;

Let us cleanse every evil.

Grant [this] . . . .

Monday at Vespers.

Immense Creator of heaven,

[Col. 0925B] Who, dividing the flowing waters,

Prevented the mingled waters

From being confused,

And gave the sky as a boundary,

Firmly establishing a place

For heavenly things,

And likewise for earthly streams,

So that water might temper the flames

And not scatter the soil:

Pour forth now, Most Merciful One,

The gift of everlasting grace,

Lest ancient error crush us

Through the new snares of deceit.

May faith discover the light;

May it bear the ray of light,

So that it may terrify all vain things

And no false thing may oppress it.

[Col. 0925C] Grant [this] . . . .

Tuesday.

Mighty Creator of the earth,

Who, clearing away the troubles of water,

Established the earth unmoving,

So that, bearing suitable shoots,

It might display a rich covering

Of golden flowers,

Produce fruit in abundance,

And provide agreeable food:

Cleanse the scorched wounds of the mind

With the greenness of grace,

So that it may wash away deeds with tears

And crush wicked impulses.

May it obey your commands;

May it draw near to no evils;

May it rejoice to be filled with good things,

And know nothing of the act of death.

[Col. 0925D] Grant [this] . . . .

Wednesday.

Most holy God of heaven,

Who paint the shining center of the sky

With fiery brightness,

Increasing its beautiful lights;

On the fourth day,

Establishing the flaming wheel

Of the sun,

And assigning the moon its order,

The wandering courses of the stars,

So that during the nights

They might mark the limit

[Col. 0926A] Of the light’s withdrawal,

And in the beginnings of months

Give a most familiar sign:

Enlighten the hearts of men;

Wipe away the filth of minds;

Remove the bond of guilt;

Overturn the burdens of sins.

Thursday.

Great God of power,

Who, from the waters,

Created living creatures,

Some returning to the deep,

Some rising into the air;

Assigning those submerged to the waters,

and those raised up to the heavens,

So that, produced from one stock,

[Col. 0926B] They might occupy different places:

Grant to all your servants,

Whom the water of blood cleanses,

That they may know no fall into sin

And bear no weariness of death.

May guilt oppress no one;

May boasting exalt no one;

May the humbled mind not collapse,

Nor the exalted mind fall.

Friday.

God, creator of man,

Who alone ordered all things,

Commanding the earth

To produce the race of creeping things.

[Col. 0926C] You who, by the word of your command,

Made the great bodies of things alive,

And, subjecting them in their appointed order,

Gave them to man:

Drive away from your servants …

Whatever through impurity

Either insinuates itself through conduct,

Or inserts itself through actions.

Grant the rewards of joys,

Grant the gifts of grace,

Loosen the bonds of strife,

Fasten the ties of peace.

### Saturday

God, source of all things,

Who, when all things had been made,

Filled the whole circuit of the world

With the abundance of your gifts,

Remaining unwearied by deeds,

Unwounded by labors,

You grant rest to all the sick,

Lest they collapse beneath troubled cares.

Grant now to mortals

That, after the sacrifices of their evils,

They may already press on toward virtues

And be rewarded with prosperity.

So that, when the supreme terror

Of the Judge’s dread has seized us,

We may all rejoice together,

Filled with the gift of peace.

### Hymn for the twelfth hour

[Col. 0927A]

Before the end of daylight,

We ask you, Creator of all things,

That in your accustomed mercy

You may be our guardian and protector.

Let dreams depart far away,

And the phantoms of the night;

Restrain our enemy as well,

Lest our bodies be polluted.

### Hymn before Compline

Having taken suitable food,

With the uses of the meal completed,

We come to you, illustrious Redeemer,

To utter praises.

Come quickly to us,

Remove the heaviness of food,

And prepare the body for prayer,

Granting faith in confession.

So that whatever we proclaim with our mouth

In your sacred praises,

You may confer a crown upon us,

While we give glory to God alone.

Grant . . . .

### Hymns for Compline

Sun of the angels, whom chastity of mind,

With intent gaze, desires to behold

As you remain above, look upon us.

By whom all things are endowed with strength from heaven,

Through prosperous course and return,

By whom the life of all things is sustained,

Attend to the prayers of your suppliants.

Grant your servants protection,

So that their advantages may be controlled,

Their adversities rendered harmless,

And their hearts not corrupted.

You are the source, salvation, and refreshment

Of the senses’ moderation;

Drink and food, joy,

Light and strength of hearts:

Drive from our limbs what is slippery,

Lest wantonness pollute them,

Lest foul passion afflict them,

And the mind’s action be blamed.

[Col. 0927D]

Bring the abundance of virtue,

By which you may grant mercy,

So that, forgetting our sins,

You may give us times of rest.

With abundant vows we ask:

May heavenly peace descend,

So that you may keep all things safe forever,

With scandals subdued.

Glory . . . .

### Another

Worshiper of God, remember

That you have undergone

The sacred dew of the font and washing,

And that you have been anointed with chrism.

When, at the call of sleep,

You seek a chaste bed,

Let your forehead and the place of your heart

Be marked with the sign of the cross.

The cross drives away every crime;

Darknesses flee the cross.

A mind dedicated to such a sign

Knows no wavering.

Far away, far away, be

The wandering monsters of dreams;

Far away be the obstinate

Heat of the sorcerer.

O twisted serpent,

Who, through a thousand winding paths

And deceitful turns,

Stirs peaceful hearts—

[Col. 0928B]

Depart; Christ is here;

Here Christ is—melt away.

The sign that you yourself know

Condemns your host.

Although the wasting body

Lies down and rests for a little while,

Nevertheless, beneath that very sleep

We will meditate on Christ.

Glory to God the Father,

And to Christ, the living King,

And to the holy Paraclete,

Now and forever. Amen.

### Hymns for the first vigil

We all prepare songs

Against the assaults that confront us,

Against the ruler of darkness,

Against the grim attendant.

Let hope and faith fully arm our hands;

Let the mighty cross cover our loins;

Let us gird ourselves with the sword of the Spirit

Because of the terrors of the night.

Jesus, by your most powerful hand,

Save the faithful through faith;

Overthrow the adversaries by the cross;

Protect all things in peace.

[CXVII] ### Another

The first darknesses are present,

The course of the gloomy night,

And now let us all dedicate ourselves

To songs and hymns.

For this is that time

Of which Jeremiah says

That we must rise

At the beginning of the night.

Arm us completely in spirit,

Unconquered Root of David;

Break the chains of night,

And give the radiance of salvation.

May the rest of sleep be welcome;

May the ever-watchful mind rise again.

Let us not be defiled in deed,

Nor burdened in spirit,

But, in body and mind,

With a fervent spirit,

[Col. 0929A]

With an unwearied step,

May we follow you, Christ.

### Another

We have passed through

The beginnings of the gloomy night in praises.

Now we ask you, Trinity,

To hear us as we sing beforehand.

You give grace to all;

You also lift up the weary.

Blot out our errors and sins;

Exclude continual scandal.

May the true light illuminate us;

May it drive away the darknesses of the mind,

So that peace may abound for all

Who believe that you are the Creator.

### Another

The time for rest is at hand,

That innocent rest may possess

The weary limbs,

And the mind may keep vigil for Christ.

God, we ask you,

Drive every gloomy thing from us:

The malicious serpent-fish

And deadly poison.

So that, protected beneath

The safest shadow of your wings,

We may remain;

And rise to your praises.

May glory and honor be

To God the Father and the Son,

And to the equal Paraclete,

Throughout the ages of ages.

Amen.

### Also, Sunday hymns

Christ, who are both light and day,

Uncover the darkness of night.

You yourself are light, bringing light,

Proclaiming blessed life.

We ask you, holy Lord:

Defend us during this night.

May our rest be in you;

Grant us a quiet night.

May oppressive sleep not fall upon us;

May the enemy not steal upon us;

May the flesh not consent to him,

And make us guilty.

May the eyes receive sleep,

But may the heart always keep vigil for you.

May your right hand protect

The servants who love you.

Look upon us, our defender;

Restrain the one lying in ambush.

Guide your servants,

Whom you purchased with blood.

Remember us, Lord,

In this heavy body;

You who are the defender of the soul,

Be with us, Lord.

Free us from the ambushes

And terror of this gloomy night;

Illuminate the whole clergy

With the greatness of your light.

Glory to the unbegotten Father,

Glory to the Only-Begotten,

Together with the Holy Spirit,

Throughout everlasting ages.

Amen.

### Another

Merciful Author of light, immeasurable light,

Light in whom the holy, eternal Christ shines,

With whom you reign as one,

And with the Holy Spirit, one power.

Drive away the darkness of this gloomy night;

We ask you, put the serpent’s deceit to flight.

Save us, armed with the sign of the cross;

Enrich us with your sacred and holy name.

Those whom the burden of sin pressed down,

Whom its thousand-shaped deceit deceived,

Let it, though rejoicing that it was victorious, recognize

That the power of the Almighty has nevertheless conquered it.

Immortal Father, shepherd of all,

Break the envious enemy who darkens.

Give us everlasting light from the holy one,

So that we may not fear the darksome path.

Eternal Redeemer, King of the whole earth,

Attend mercifully to the groaning of our sins.

Break the enemy who lies in ambush, Savior;

Make us blessed in eternal life.

[Col. 0930C]

Grant us this night in quiet;

Drive the hostile enemy from us.

May the sign of the cross conquer every enemy.

Christ, we ask you: remain with us.

Glory, honor, power, and strength

To the unbegotten God and to Christ the Begotten,

And likewise to the Holy Paraclete,

By whose word all the ages shine.

### Hymn for rest

The time suitable for sleep is here;

May rest be granted in due measure.

Let us water the bed with tears;

Let us moisten the couch with weeping.

Let prayer follow the sign,

And then let us arm ourselves,

Kissing one another,

By the cross itself.

Thus let us give our weary limbs to the little bed,

Beneath that Judge

Who keeps watch while we rest,

So that he may protect us as we sleep.

Let the throng of demons depart;

Let the craft of their attendants melt away

Through the name of this holy cross,

Which may scatter you and your followers.

But you, Creator of all,

Drive weariness far away;

Scatter all adversities,

And grant all things tranquil.

### Hymns for midnight

[Col. 0931A]

When, with our limbs folded together,

We lie sluggish, weighed down by sleep,

Remove from our dreams

The shameful flow of semen.

Most merciful Father,

We earnestly ask with poured-out tears

That now the foul phantoms

Of lust may depart.

Wash what the enemy has polluted;

Renew what he has made filthy.

May we all, filthy in flesh,

Be cleansed in spirit.

Grant . . . .

### Another

Rising to you, Lord,

In the black silence of night,

Following the order of the fathers

In vigil services,

Which they left to us

By hereditary right,

We minister in watchfulness

To you, holy Paraclete.

You are glorious with the Father,

Most subtle with Christ,

The manifold Spirit.

[The remainder is missing.]

Your flock, devoted to you,

Is held by no crime,

The flock whom you, Christ,

Wished to redeem with your blood.

Look upon the wandering sheep,

Most good and merciful Shepherd;

Carry them on your shoulders

Back to the court of your majesty.

The wounded one has been weakened;

Let the prince of demons depart.

Let insatiable rage

Lose its prey from its jaws.

Let Christ the Lord rejoice;

Let the angelic choir sing psalms;

Let praises resound in the organ;

Let “Holy, Holy, Holy” be said three times to the Lord.

### Another

Jesus, defender of all,

Protector and wondrous one,

The accustomed night has arrived,

And we, given over to sleep,

In your name, Christ,

Who are guardian and defender,

May we keep vigil in spirit,

So that we may deserve the lamps.

Your singers, Lord,

Whom you command to rise at night

To invoke your name,

Which is praiseworthy for us,

Whom the whole earth fears

Because of such greatness—

May we follow in your praise,

[Col. 0932A]

As we devoutly ask, Holy One.

May the harmonious sound of hymns

Resound from the hearts of those singing you.

May we follow the promise

Of such great joy of the Holy Spirit.

A cry has been made in the night:

Jesus has entered through the doors

And urges those keeping vigil

To enter the holy halls.

The bridegroom of virgins rejoices,

Having entered the chamber,

Where the crowns of martyrs

Shine brilliantly before the Lord.

[CXIX] You are about to give

The reward of such glory to believers;

May we deserve to attain

What our spirit thirsts for.

At midnight

The prophetic voice admonishes us:

Let us sing praises to the Lord,

To the Father always and to the Son,

And also to the Holy Spirit;

For the perfect Trinity,

Of one substance,

Must always be praised by us.

At midnight,

The destroying angel proceeded,

Bringing death upon Egypt,

And destroyed the firstborn.

This hour is salvation for the righteous,

In which the conquered angel

Did not dare to punish

Those marked with the sign of blood.

Egypt mourned bitterly

The dreadful deaths of so many;

Israel alone rejoiced,

Protected by the blood of the Lamb.

But we are Israel;

Let us rejoice in you, Lord,

Overthrowing the evil enemy,

Defended by Christ’s blood.

At midnight,

According to the evangelical word,

The bridegroom who is to come

Is believed to be the Creator of the heavenly kingdom.

The holy virgins will meet

That coming when it arrives,

Carrying shining lamps,

Rejoicing with great joy.

The foolish remain outside,

Those whose lamps have gone out,

Knocking in vain at the door,

The gate of the kingdom already closed.

Therefore let us watch soberly,

Standing radiant in mind,

So that when Jesus comes

We may be worthy to meet him.

At midnight,

Paul and Silas also,

Bound in prison for Christ,

Were released while praising him.

This world is a prison for us;

Christ, release our bonds;

Forgive our sins,

As we believe in you, holy one.

Make us worthy, holy King,

Of the glory of the coming kingdom,

So that we may deserve

To sing your praises eternally.

Grant . . . .

### Hymns for the nocturns

On the first of all days,

When the world was brought into being,

Or when the Creator rose again

And freed us by conquering death,

Let all of us rise quickly,

With our sluggishness driven far away,

And seek the merciful one at night,

As we know the Prophet did,

So that he may hear our prayers

And extend his right hand,

And here, cleansed of defilements,

Restore us to the dwellings of heaven.

So that, whenever during the sacred hours

Of this day

We sing psalms during times of rest,

He may enrich us with blessed gifts.

Now, Fatherly Radiance,

We earnestly ask you:

Let lust that defiles

And every harmful deed be absent.

Let the structure of our body

Be neither foul nor slippery,

Lest through it we ourselves

Be burned more harshly in the fires of hell.

For this, Redeemer, we ask you:

Wash away our disgrace,

And kindly bestow upon us

The blessings of everlasting life.

So that, exiled from the deeds of the flesh,

Having become celibate ourselves,

We may, bowed down as we await,

Sing the melody of glory.

[Col. 0933D]

Grant . . . .

### Thursday

You, unity of the Trinity,

Who powerfully rule the world,

Attend to the songs of praise

That we sing while keeping watch.

For we rise from our little bed

At the quiet time of night,

That we may ask from you

Healing for all wounds.

So that what we have done wrong,

Persuaded by the deceits of the attendants,

Your glorious power may wipe away

From heaven.

Let the body not be filthy;

Let sluggishness not oppress the heart;

And let the contagion of sin

Not cool the ardor of the spirit.

For this, Redeemer, we ask you:

Fill us with your gift,

Through which, in the circuits of our days,

We may fall into no evil deeds.

### Friday

Supreme God of mercy,

Maker of the world’s structure,

One in power,

Three in person,

Kindly receive our tears

Together with our songs,

So that, with hearts cleansed of filth,

We may enjoy you more fully.

Burn the loins and diseased liver

With a fitting fire,

So that they may be girded forever,

With the worst indulgence removed.

So that all of us who now break

The hours of night by singing together

May be richly endowed

With the gifts of the blessed homeland.

### Saturday

You, King and Redeemer of all,

Who dispose and order

All things that have been created

By fixed laws forever,

We rise during the hours of night,

We disclose our sinful deeds,

And the instrument of our mouth

Praises you with sweet hymns.

So that whatever the whole throng of demons

Has corrupted by its own cunning,

You may heal everything by sparing us

And grant the gifts of life.

Lest that most wicked people,

And all the authors of crime,

Draw us with themselves

To everlasting fire, there to be burned.

Now, groaning, we ask

For your power, God,

So that you may quickly free us

From every expiatory punishment.

### Monday

With our limbs refreshed by sleep,

We rise, having rejected the bed,

And ask you, Father,

To be present as we sing.

May the tongue first sing of you;

May the ardor of the mind surround you,

So that you, Holy One,

May be the beginning of the deeds that follow.

Let darkness yield to light,

And night to the daylight star,

So that the sin which night brought in

May fade through the gift of light.

We ask the same thing as suppliants:

Cut away all offenses,

And may you be praised forever

By the mouths of those singing you.

### Tuesday

Partner of the Father’s light,

Light and day itself of light,

We break the night by singing;

Stand by those who ask.

Remove the darknesses of our minds;

Drive away the hosts of demons;

Expel drowsiness,

Lest it overwhelm us as we grow sluggish.

Thus may you forgive all of us,

Christ, who believe,

So that you may aid those who pray,

As we sing what we chant beforehand.

### Wednesday

Best Creator of all things,

And our ruler, look upon us.

Free us, sunk in harmful rest,

From sleep.

We ask you, holy Christ:

Forgive our sins.

We rise to confess,

And break the delays of night.

We lift up minds and hands.

Thus the Prophet commands us

To conduct ourselves in the nights,

And Paul confirmed it by his deeds.

You see the evil we have done;

We disclose our hidden things;

We pour out groaning prayers.

Forgive what we shall have sinned.

### Also, others at cockcrow

The time of night has now passed. Fol. 257.

### Another

We come at the crowing of the cock. Same folio.

### Another

At this hour of the night, you who know beforehand. Same folio.

[CXXI] ### Another

We rise at the morning offices. Fol. 103.

### Sunday hymn at cockcrow

Eternal Creator of all things. Fol. 3.

### Sunday hymn at Matins

[Col. 0935D]

We praise you, God: we confess you as Lord. Fol. CXXVI.

### The daily Matins hymns begin

Splendor of the Father’s glory,

Bringing forth light from light,

Guide of light and source of brightness,

Day illuminating day,

And true Sun, descend upon us,

Shining with everlasting radiance,

And pour into our senses

The brilliance of the Holy Spirit.

Let us call upon you in our vows,

Father of everlasting glory,

Father of mighty grace.

Drive away slippery guilt;

Shape energetic deeds;

Dull the tooth of the envious one;

Make rough falls prosper.

[Lacuna]

Here in the codex at least two, or perhaps more, pages are missing.

With the circuit completed by the mouth,

To bring forth to God

A hymn of everlasting glory.

Rise, Jesus; lift up

The weariness of the guilty heart,

So that the tongue may clearly sing

The greatness of your praise.

Pour in the Spirit’s light;

Give love to our hearts,

So that in all things

We may always praise you as God,

Throughout the ages.

Amen.

### Hymn for Terce

Holding to the appointed order,

Let us ask with devoted heart,

At the third hour of the day,

For the power of the Trinity’s name.

So that we may be a dwelling

For the Holy Spirit,

Who was once distributed

Among the Apostles at this hour.

By which, as he proceeded according to the order,

He splendidly adorned all things,

The Creator of the heavenly kingdom,

With the rewards of eternal life.

### Another

Lord of majesty,

Powerful in the threefold name,

We, your servants, ask you:

Willingly hear us.

Wash away our errors;

Receive the voice of our cry.

Grant the rewards of the heavenly kingdom

To those confessing you.

### Another

Now, Holy Spirit,

One with the Father and the Son,

Deign readily to enter,

Poured into our breast.

Let tongue, mind, and the strength of our senses

Resound with confession.

Let love blaze with fire;

Let ardor kindle those near us.

### Hymn for the Fourth Hour

You who now water

The four corners of the world

With the fourfold stream

Of the Evangelists,

Hear us, suppliants, we ask.

Forgive our crime;

Remove the lukewarmness of our minds;

Make us all worthy

Of the gift of compunction.

Let lust not wear down the body;

Let anger not creep into the sad;

Let truth shape our conduct;

Let chastity preserve modesty.

### Hymn for the Fifth Hour

You who, through the whole book of Moses,

Instruct the passing age,

And rule us, King and Redeemer,

Through the senses of the body,

Make us remain forever

In your laws,

So that in spirit and body

We may sing together faithfully.

Drive away what we fear;

Grant what we ask of you;

So that we may praise you,

Pious and most gentle,

Forever.

### Hymn for Sext

Powerful and truthful God, our ruler,

Who regulate the changes of things,

You furnish morning with splendor,

And midday with fires.

Extinguish the flames of quarrels;

Remove harmful heat;

Grant health to bodies

And true peace to hearts.

### Another

Now the course of the day

Has turned six times in its circuit;

It admonishes us in all things

To offer worthy praises.

Now Peter, praying,

Foresees the future faith of the nations;

Now the living Christ urges the woman

To offer the flowing waters.

At this mystical time,

The patriarch alone receives three messengers,

Bodily figures of the Trinity’s divinity.

This first part

Of the perfect highest number is established;

Drawn through itself,

It completes itself

And holds together the structure of the world.

Indeed, your power preserves

This creation of Christ;

Whose glorious power

Reigns throughout all ages.

### Hymn for Sept

Author of everlasting glory,

Who give the Spirit of sevenfold grace

To believers,

Stand kindly by all.

Drive away diseases of the body;

Remove scandal from the mind;

Cut away the poison of sins;

Drive away the sorrows of hearts.

So that, when you have mercifully received

The prayers of your peoples,

We may all return glory

To the triune God throughout the ages.

### Hymn for Octave

The eighth circuit

Now inclines toward its end

And instructs us

To mourn with sighs

The day of the future judgment.

Through the courses of seven days

All time is now led;

That eighth and final day

Will be the day of judgment.

On it, Redeemer of the age,

Do not accuse us in anger,

But free us from the left,

And place us at the right.

### Hymn for None

It is time to pour out prayers;

The course of the day admonishes us

To sing a song of praise

To you, Redeemer of all.

Make the mind serene;

Complete an honorable work;

Receive the prayer of those praying;

Grant everlasting life.

### Another

The vaulted orbit of the sun,

Rolled through nine circles,

Having completed its course,

Completes it three times threefold.

At this time of the Passion,

The Author of all things completed this;

Now he sent the called servants

To the labor of the vineyard.

At this mystical hour,

Peter loosens the chains of the lame man;

Now the creator of visions

Brings them to an end through a threefold return.

At this hour let us sing glory

With pure minds and voice

To God, who creates prosperity,

When the ages appointed for the just are completed.

### Hymn for the Tenth Hour

Now the tenfold commandment

Of the sacred Law forewarns us,

So that amid the darknesses of the age

We may not serve as soldiers of sin.

For this, God, we ask you:

Correct us when appeased;

Wash away our offenses;

And also keep adversities away.

Be our joy,

You who are the future reward.

May our glory be in you

Throughout all ages forever.

### Hymn for the Eleventh Hour

When eleven hours have been completed,

The day rushes toward evening.

Let us all render

A kindly, due song of the mind.

The daytime labor has passed,

By which you, Christ, had led us.

Now give the promised gift of grace

To the workers of the vineyard.

You also summon to their reward

Those whom you endow for the life to come.

Help us in our labor,

And refresh us after labor.

### Hymn for the Twelfth Hour

Whatever hours, most merciful God,

Mark out the day,

May this flock pay you

Due praises and honors.

Now the day lies toward evening;

The heavenly light passes away.

Rise, renew our minds

With spiritual grace.

Let the shadow of sins depart;

Let the anger of demons be driven away.

Visit our bed,

God, with your protection.

### At Vespers

God, enduring strength of all things,

Remaining unmoved in yourself,

You determine the daylight hours

By their successive changes.

Grant a bright evening,

So that life may never fall away,

But the reward of sacred death

May remain as everlasting glory.

[Col. 0939]

## THE CANONICAL HOURS BEGIN. (C)

[CXXIV] ## THE AURORA BEGINS, RECITED BEFORE PRIME ON FERIAL DAYS THROUGHOUT THE YEAR

[Col. 0939B]

Antiphon. God, attend to my help; Lord, hasten to help me.

Psalm 69. God, attend to my help. Folio XXVIII. CXVIII. A Psalm of David. Blessed are the undefiled in the way. In what way does a young man correct his path? Reward your servant; I shall live. Fol. LII.

Let the Antiphon be repeated: God, attend to my help; Lord, hasten to help me.

Let the Priest say: The Lord be always with you. R\. And with you.

Praise. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. I rose before dawn and cried out, because I hoped exceedingly in your word. P. Alleluia. V\. My eyes went before the dawn to you, O God, so that I might meditate on your words. P. Alleluia.

### Hymn

The limit of night has now passed;

The rest of sleep has now gone by;

The radiant dawn rises;

New light scatters across the sky.

But since we all now behold

The mirror of the day,

It is necessary to pour out prayers

To you, heavenly Light.

You, Holy Spirit of light,

Make us renewed

By works of charity,

After the likeness of that glory.

Grant this, most merciful Father,

And Only-Begotten equal to the Father,

Reigning with the Paraclete Spirit

Throughout every age.

Amen.

V\. Rise, Lord, help us; and free us for the sake of your name.

[Col. 0940B]

Or another Verse. From the morning watch until night, holy God, guard us.

Another Verse. You are our helper and liberator, Lord; do not delay in saving us.

Lord, have mercy. Christ, have mercy. Lord, have mercy.

Our Father, who are in heaven: R\. Amen. Hallowed be your name: R\. Amen. Your kingdom come: R\. Amen. Your will be done, as in heaven and on earth. R\. Amen. Give us our daily bread today: R\. Because you are God. And forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors. R\. Amen. And do not lead us into temptation: R\. But deliver us from evil.

Deliver us from evil, and strengthen us, our God the Trinity, in your fear and in good works; and may we serve you, God and our Lord, with everlasting service: You who live and rule all things, now and throughout eternal ages of ages. R\. Amen.

Prayers. God, have mercy; God, have mercy: God, have mercy on the weak, the oppressed, the scattered, the captives, travelers, sailors, the afflicted, and penitents; and quickly come to the aid of the faithful departed, heavenly Father.

Other Prayers. God, have mercy; God, have mercy; God, have mercy. Have mercy on us, wretched ones, Lord. Have mercy on your servants. Have mercy on the sick; have mercy on the oppressed; have mercy on captives; have mercy on pilgrims; have mercy on sailors; have mercy on travelers; have mercy on penitents; have mercy on mourners; have mercy on sinners. Christ, spare all living Christians, because we are worn down by various evils on account of our merits; and because before you we confess our own misery, may we feel within us the help of your mercy; and command that the healing of their deeds and rest be granted to all faithful departed. Amen.

## THE ORDER OF PRIME BEGINS, WHICH IS TO BE SAID THROUGHOUT THE YEAR

Antiphon. My eyes went before the dawn to you, O God, so that I might meditate on your words. 2. My eyes went before. Glory and honor. 3. My eyes went before.

[Col. 0941A]

Psalm 66. Psalm 144. Psalm 144. Your kingdom, Lord, is a kingdom, etc. Psalm 112. [CXXV] CXVIII. A Psalm of David. My soul clung to the pavement. Teach me your law, Lord. Let your mercy come upon us, Lord. Fol. LII and LIII.

Antiphon. My eyes went before the dawn to you, O God, so that I might meditate on your words.

Responsory on ferial days. You are our helper and liberator, Lord. V\. Save me, God, by your name; and judge me by your strength. P. You are, Lord. V\. Glory and honor to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and always, throughout the ages of ages. Amen. P. Let the Responsory be repeated: You are our helper and liberator.

Another ferial Responsory. Help us, God our Savior. V\. And for the honor of your name, Lord, free us. P. Our Savior. V\. Glory and honor. P. Help us, etc.

Responsory for a Confessor. In the sight of the angels I will sing to you, Lord, alleluia. V\. I will adore toward your holy temple, and I will confess to you, Lord. P. I will sing. V\. Glory and honor.

Responsory for one righteous person or martyr. Instruction proceeds from the mouth of the righteous. Alleluia, alleluia. Honeycomb drips from his lips. V\. The mouth of the righteous will meditate wisdom, and his tongue will speak judgment. P. Honeycomb. V\. Glory and honor. Let the Responsory be repeated.

Responsory for Saints or Martyrs. The bonds of the Saints have now been loosed, and their wounds have now been healed; like travelers, they were carried from the world into heaven. V\. Who are these who fly like clouds, and like doves to their windows? P. They were carried. V\. Glory and honor.

Responsory on ferial days in Lent. Seek first the kingdom of God, and all these things will be added to you. V\. Seek the Lord and be strengthened; seek his face always. P. And all these things. V\. Glory. P. Seek.

Responsory on Sundays in Lent. Servants of God, bless the Lord and praise together the King of the ages, because we must always pray and never grow faint. V\. You who stand in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God. P. Because we must. V\. Glory.

Responsory for the Advent of the Lord. Mountains of the daughter of Zion, extend your branches, put forth shoots, and bring the fruit of joy to the people of God, Israel, because the day of the Lord will come. V\. Praise the heavens, and rejoice, earth; mountains, shout for joy in praise. V\. And bring the fruit of joy. P. Glory.

Responsory for the Nativity of the Lord. Today heaven and earth shine, because the Savior has been born for us to redeem our sins. He is the Lord our God. V\. For a little one has been born for us, and a son has been given to us. P. He is the Lord. V\. Glory and honor. Let the Responsory be repeated.

Responsory on feast days throughout the year. May your light, Lord, shine upon us, and may your majesty illuminate us, alleluia, so that, filled with your Spirit, we may not fear the enemy’s ambushes. Alleluia, alleluia. V\. Illuminate your face, Lord, upon us, and have mercy on us. P. So that, filled with your Spirit. V\. Glory and honor. P. Your light, Lord, etc. Or this Responsory may be said during the Octave of the Nativity.

### Reading from the Book of the Prophet Zechariah (Chapter 8)

Thus says the Lord: I have returned to Zion, and I will dwell in Jerusalem; and Jerusalem will be called the City of Truth, and the mountain of the Lord of hosts, a sanctified mountain. R\. Amen.

### Letter of the Apostle Paul to the Romans (Chapter 13)

Brothers, the night has passed, but the day has drawn near. Therefore let us cast away from us the works of darkness, and let us put on the arms of light. Let us walk honorably as in the day: not in feasting and drunkenness, not in bedrooms and indecencies, not in contention and rivalry; but put on our Lord Jesus Christ. R\. Amen.

Praise. Alleluia. I will sing to the Lord during my life. P. Alleluia. V\. I will sing psalms to my God as long as I am. P. Alleluia.

Praise. Alleluia. The right hand of the Lord has shown strength. P. Alleluia. V\. The right hand of the Lord has exalted us. P. Alleluia, alleluia.

And note that during Lent “Alleluia” is not said in this Praise.

### Hymn

Now that the star of daylight has risen,

Let us humbly pray to God,

That in the deeds of the day

He may guard us from harmful things.

May he restrain and temper the tongue,

Lest the error of quarrels resound;

May he watch over the eyes,

Lest they drink in vanities.

May the innermost parts of the heart be pure,

And may foolishness stand aside.

May moderation in food and drink

Wear down the pride of the flesh,

So that, when the day has departed

And chance has brought back the night,

Through abstinence from the world

We may sing glory to him.

Now the completed circuit

Of the second hour admonishes us

To bring forth to God

A hymn of everlasting glory.

[Col. 0942D]

Rise, Jesus; lift up

The weariness of the guilty heart,

So that the tongue may clearly sing

The greatness of your praise.

Pour in the Spirit’s light;

Give clarity to our hearts,

So that in all things

We may always praise you as God

Throughout the ages.

Amen.

V\. It is good to confess to the Lord. P. And to sing psalms to your name, O Most High.

Responsory for the Resurrection. Tell it among the nations, alleluia: the Lord has reigned from the wood, alleluia, alleluia. V\. For he set the world right, and it will not be moved. P. The Lord has reigned. V\. Glory and honor. Let “Tell it” be repeated.

### Hymn

The dawn of light shines red;

Heaven resounds with praises;

The rejoicing world shouts for joy;

Groaning hell howls.

When that most powerful King,

Having broken the strength of death,

Trampling Tartarus beneath his foot,

Freed the wretched from punishment—

He who, shut inside a stone,

Was guarded beneath the soldiers,

Rising as victor from the tomb,

Triumphs in noble procession.

Now the groans and pains

Of hell have been loosed,

Because the Lord has risen;

The shining angel proclaims it.

The Apostles were sad

At the death of their Lord,

Whom impious servants

Had condemned to cruel death.

The angel, with gentle words,

Announced to the women:

“The Lord in Galilee

Will be seen very soon.”

As they hurried along

To tell this to the Apostles,

Seeing him alive,

They kissed the Lord’s feet.

When the disciples recognized this,

They hastened to Galilee

To see the desired face

Of the Lord.

In clear Paschal joy,

The sun shines upon the world with its rays,

When the Apostles behold Christ

Already with bodily sight.

Seeing the wounds displayed,

Shining in Christ’s flesh,

They publicly confess

That the Lord has risen.

Most merciful King Christ,

Possess our hearts,

So that at all times

We may return you due praises.

Glory to you, Lord,

Who rose from the dead,

With the Father and the Holy Spirit,

Throughout everlasting ages.

Amen.

V\. It is good to confess to the Lord. P. And to sing psalms to your name, O Most High.

And what follows, namely the Canticle “Blessed are you, Lord, God,” and Psalm 50, must always be said throughout the year on ferial days, except during the season of the Resurrection.

[Col. 0944A]

Canticle. Blessed are you, Lord, God of our fathers. Fol. 6. Psalm 50.

And note that on Sundays and feast days the Canticle “We praise you, God,” the Canticle “Glory in the highest,” and the Creed “We believe in one God” must always be said.

### Canticle

We praise you, God; we confess you as Lord.

You, eternal Father, are venerated by the whole earth.

To you all the angels, to you the heavens and all powers;

To you the Cherubim and Seraphim proclaim with unceasing voice:

Holy, Holy, Holy, Lord God of hosts.

[Col. 0944B]

The heavens and earth are full of the glory of your majesty.

You are praised by the glorious choir of the Apostles;

By the laudable number of the prophets;

By the white-robed army of martyrs.

The holy Church throughout the world confesses you,

The Father of immeasurable majesty,

And venerates your true Only-Begotten Son,

And also the Holy Spirit, the Paraclete.

[CXXVII] You are the King of glory, Christ.

You are the eternal Son of the Father.

When you undertook to free humanity,

You did not shrink from the Virgin’s womb.

Having conquered the sting of death,

You opened the kingdoms of heaven to believers.

You sit at the right hand of God

In the glory of the Father.

You are believed to be the Judge who will come.

Therefore we ask you: help your servants,

Whom you redeemed with your precious blood.

Make them be numbered with your saints

In eternal glory.

Save your people, Lord,

And bless your inheritance.

And rule them;

And exalt them forever and throughout the ages of ages. Amen.

Each day we bless you,

And we praise your name forever

And throughout the age of the age.

Deign, Lord, on this day

To guard us without tribulation and sin.

Have mercy on us, Lord;

Have mercy on us.

Let your mercy, Lord, be upon us,

As we have hoped in you.

In you, Lord, I have hoped;

I shall not be confounded forever.

Spare, Lord, spare your people,

And do not give your inheritance over to reproach.

### Canticle of the Angels

Glory to God in the highest,

And on earth peace to people of good will.

We praise you;

We bless you;

We adore you;

We glorify you;

We offer a hymn to you.

We give you thanks because of your great glory,

Lord God, heavenly King,

God the Father almighty,

Lord, Only-Begotten Son, Jesus Christ, Most High.

Lord God, Lamb of God, Son of the Father,

You who take away the sins of the world,

Have mercy on us.

You who take away the sins of the world,

Receive our supplication.

You who sit at the right hand of the Father,

Have mercy on us.

For you alone are holy;

You alone are Lord;

You alone are Most High,

Jesus Christ,

With the Holy Spirit

In the glory of God the Father.

Amen.

### Apostles’ Creed
We believe in one God, the almighty Father, Maker of heaven and earth, creator of things visible and invisible. And in one Lord Jesus Christ, the only-begotten Son of God, born from the Father before all ages, God from God, Light from Light, true God from true God, begotten, not made, consubstantial (*Homousion*) with the Father—that is, of the same substance as the Father—through whom all things were made, both those in heaven and those on [Col. 0945B] earth. Who, for us human beings and for our salvation, descended from heaven; *and was incarnate from the Holy Spirit, born of the Virgin Mary, and became man.* He suffered under Pontius Pilate; was buried; on the third day he rose again; he ascended into heaven; he sits at the right hand of the Father; he will come again in glory to judge the living and the dead, and his kingdom will have no end.

We believe in the Holy Spirit, the Lord and giver of life, who proceeds from the Father and the Son, who with the Father and the Son is to be worshiped and glorified, who spoke through the Prophets; in one holy, catholic, and Apostolic Church. We confess one baptism for the forgiveness of sins. We await the resurrection of the dead and the life of the age to come. Amen.

V. We have been satisfied in the morning with your mercy, and we have rejoiced [Col. 0945C] and been glad throughout all our days.

**Supplication.** Let us pray to our merciful and readily heard Lord Jesus Christ; let us beseech him with every supplication, that in his favor he may deign to lead the course of our struggle to the end of good works and to heavenly blessedness.

R. Grant this, eternal almighty God.

Lord, have mercy.

R. Christ, have mercy. Lord, have mercy.

**Three Capitula for feast days.** Hasten, O God, to help us; lest either the enemy prevail while you delay assistance, or despair arise while you defer help. Set both your aids against these dangers, and extend your gracious protection to us and to all Christians, so that we who place our trust in your [Col. 0945D] power may always be fortified by your Divinity.

**Our Father.**

Deliver us from evil. Fol. 10.

**Blessing.** May the eternal Ruler, the Lord, bless us.

R. Amen.

May he protect us, fortify us, and defend us from every evil.

R. Amen.

May he establish in heaven as heirs those who have been rescued from evils.

R. Amen.

Through his mercy.

**Ferial Capitula.** O God, attend to our help; and, O Lord, hastening to assist us, come to our aid. Grant us strength to accomplish what we know, and count as perfected what we desire.

**Our Father.**

Deliver us from evil. Fol. 10.

[Col. 0946A] **[CXXVIII] Blessing.** May truth and divine mercy be with us, so that we may prevail against the enemy through good deeds.

R. Amen.

May our heart rejoice in his benevolence, so that all the wounds of sins may fall away from us.

R. Amen.

May his right hand instill the triumph of the merciful one, by which, with Christ guiding us, we may crush the sting of the ancient enemy.

R. Amen.

**Sunday Capitula.** To you, O Lord, we pour out the desire of our heart. With tears we pray that you hear the voice of our cry and grant effect to our petitions. Be for us, O Lord, in all good things our most ready helper and, in dangers, our constant deliverer. Drive deceit from us; destroy vice. Grant an increase of mutual sweetness. Let the correction of our conduct be the forgiveness of our crimes, so that you may receive our [Col. 0946B] prayer; forgive our sins; fill us with faith; cherish us with pardon; protect us with mercy; destroy adversities; grant prosperity. May we possess in this age the example of good action, the gift of chastity, devotion to charity, and affection for holy love; and in the future may we attain the kingdom with the holy Angels. Through your great mercy, grant everlasting rest to all the departed faithful Christians.

**Our Father.**

Deliver us from evil. Fol. 10.

**Blessing.** May the almighty Lord bless us with heavenly blessings and fill us with spiritual gifts.

R. Amen.

May he grant us charity, joy, patience, gentleness, hope, faith, and self-restraint.

R. Amen.

So that, filled with all his benefits, we may be able to reach the blessedness of eternal life.

R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

## HERE BEGINS THE ORDER TO BE SUNG OR RECITED AT TERCE

**Antiphon.** Let us go before his face with confession, and let us exult for him in psalms. Psalm 94.

Psalm 118. A Psalm of David. Remember your word to your servant. “The Lord is my portion.” You have dealt graciously with your servant. Fol. LIII.

**Antiphon.** Let us go before his face with confession, and let us exult for him in psalms.

**Responsory on feast days.** Righteous Defender, defend us and deliver us from the hand of our enemies.

V. Save us, O God, by your name, and by your power.

P. Deliver us from the hand of—

V. Glory and honor.

Let the Responsory be repeated.

**Ferial Responsory.** Grant us help, O God, in tribulation, for the salvation of man is vain.

P. For it is vain.

V. Glory and honor.

**Responsory on weekdays in Lent.** Let us beseech the Lord, and he will be gracious to us. He will hear us and have mercy on us.

V. Come, let us rejoice in the Lord; let us exult in God our salvation.

P. He will hear us.

V. Glory and honor.

**Responsory on carnal Sundays.** I will sing mercy and judgment to you, O Lord. Alleluia, alleluia.

V. I walked in the innocence of my heart, in the midst of your house.

P. I will sing to you, O Lord. Alleluia, alleluia.

V. Glory and honor.

Let the Responsory be repeated.

**Reading from the Book of Leviticus (Chapter 26).**

R. Thanks be to God.

Thus says the Lord: “I will place my dwelling in your midst, and my soul will not reject you. I will dwell among you, and I will be your God, and you will be my people, and I, the Lord, will be your God.”

R. Amen.

**Epistle of the Apostle Paul to the Ephesians (Chapter 5).**

R. Thanks be to God.

**Lauda.** Alleluia, alleluia. Great is our Lord, and great is his power.

P. Alleluia.

V. And of his wisdom there is no number.

P. Alleluia.

**Lauda.** Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. O God, hear our prayer.

P. Alleluia, alleluia.

V. And may our cry reach you.

P. Alleluia, alleluia.

**Hymn.**

Holding firmly to the appointed order,  
let us ask with devout heart  
at the Third Hour of the day  
for the power of the Triune God,

that we may be a dwelling place  
for the Holy Spirit,  
who once was distributed  
among the Apostles at this hour;

walking in this order,  
the Creator of the heavenly kingdom  
adorned all things splendidly  
with the rewards of eternal life.

Grant this, most loving Father,  
and only-begotten One equal to the Father,  
with the Spirit, the Paraclete,  
reigning throughout every age.

Amen.

[Col. 0947D] **Clamores.** 1. Do not deal with us according to our sins, O God, nor repay us according to our iniquities. 2. “Not according to—” 3. “Not according to our sins—”

V. But according to the multitude of your mercies, have mercy on us, O Lord.

**Supplication.** Let us pray to our merciful and readily heard Lord Jesus Christ; let us beseech him with every supplication, that in his favor he may deign to grant us the grace of his mercy and forgiveness of sins.

R. Grant this, eternal one.

Lord, have mercy.

R. Christ, have mercy. Lord, have mercy.

**Capitula.** Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God the Father, who at the Third Hour of the day, suspended on the gibbet of the Cross, washed away the sin of the whole world by your suffering, and at that same hour gave the gift of the Holy Spirit as fire upon the heads of your Apostles: we beseech and implore you to illumine our hearts with that gift and bless our souls.

**Our Father.**

**Blessing.** May the Triune Majesty and the one Divinity bless us.

R. Amen.

The Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit.

R. Amen.

May the days of our testing find us such as the fountain of regeneration sent forth.

R. Amen.

**Responsory for Advent.** The Lord will come and appear in the midst of the children of his people. He will deliver them from the hand of the wicked and redeem them from death.

V. The almighty Lord will raise up the righteous one for us, and he himself will save his people from their sins.

P. And he will deliver them from the hand of the wicked.

V. Glory and honor.

[Col. 0948B] **Another.** Behold, the Lord will come, our Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel, wearing the crown of the kingdom upon his head.

P. Wearing the crown of the kingdom upon his head.

V. I was looking in the clouds of heaven, and one like a Son of Man was coming.

P. Wearing the crown of the kingdom.

V. Glory and honor.

V. Glory and honor.

**Reading from the Book of the Prophet Isaiah (Chapter 35).**

R. Thanks be to God.

R. Amen.

**Epistle of the Apostle Paul to the Philippians (Chapter 4).**

R. Thanks be to God.

Brothers, rejoice in the Lord always; again I say, rejoice. Let your moderation be known to all people. The Lord is near. Be anxious about nothing, but in every prayer and supplication, with thanksgiving, let your petitions be made known before God. And the peace of Christ, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts, your bodies, and your understanding, [Col. 0948D] through the faith that is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

R. Amen.

**Lauda.** Alleluia, alleluia. Come, Lord, and appear to your people.

P. Alleluia.

V. And release their crimes.

P. Alleluia.

**Hymn.**

You, Lord of majesty,  
whom we, your servants, worship  
in the Triune Name,  
we pray that you willingly hear us.

Wash away our errors;  
receive the voice of our cry;  
grant to those who confess you

[Col. 0949A] Grant this, most loving Father,  
and only-begotten One equal to the Father,  
with the Spirit, the Paraclete,  
reigning throughout every age.

Amen.

**In the season of the Holy Spirit.** Glory to you, Trinity. Fol. 422.

[CXXX] **Supplication.** Let us pray to our merciful and readily heard Lord Jesus Christ; let us beseech him with every supplication, that in his favor, through the grace of his coming, he may renew in us day by day a new heart and a right spirit.

R. Grant this, eternal almighty God.

**Capitula.** Already the Third Hour of the day is rising, O Lord, at which you deigned to pour the Holy Spirit into the hearts of the Apostles, and you resounded in their mouths so that they might speak in various tongues. Grant therefore, eternal almighty God, that just as at that time you opened their mouths in your praises, so also we may in the future be worthy to attain your mercy.

**Our Father.**

**Blessing.** May the Lord guard us, go before us everywhere, and make us observers of his commandments.

R. Amen.

And may we who gather at this Third Hour of the day with devout mind to entreat him always be worthy to have the approach and assistance of the ineffable Trinity.

R. Amen.

So that, saved by his protection, we may be worthy to rejoice with that same Lord throughout eternal ages.

R. Amen.

**Responsory in Lent.** Behold, the great days of the Lord are coming: days of almsgiving and fasting. Be ready to do good to the oppressed, widows, and orphans, so that you may receive your reward in the last times, says the Lord. P. So that you may receive—

V. Glory and honor.

Let the Responsory be repeated.

**Reading from the Book of the Prophet Isaiah (Chapter 55).**

R. Thanks be to God.

In those days Isaiah spoke, saying: Seek the Lord while he may be found; call upon him while he is near. Let the wicked abandon his ways, and the unrighteous man his thoughts; let him return to the Lord, and he will have mercy on him, and to our Lord God, for he is abundant in forgiveness.

R. Amen.

[Col. 0949D] **Epistle of the Apostle Paul to the Ephesians (Chapter 4).**

R. Thanks be to God.

Brothers, let no evil word proceed from our mouth, but only whatever is good for edification when needed, so that it may give grace to those who hear. And do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, in whom you were sealed for the day of redemption.

R. Amen.

**Lauda.** Praise to you, praise to you, O Lord, King of eternal glory. O God, hear our prayer.

P. King of eternal glory.

V. And may our cry reach you.

P. King of eternal glory.

**Hymn.**

God, fountain of kindness,  
who have no end of goodness,  
over the wickedness of the evil  
ever gracious, ever good,

we beat our sorrowful heart enough,  
and strike our grieving breast;  
we pour out the waters of our eyes;  
we bring sadness upon our cheeks.

We greatly regret having done  
what was horrid, foul, or wicked,  
most shameful and filthy;  
we confess every harmful deed.

Our raised voice calls upon you:  
“You, Creator, spare us.”  
It cries out, pleading, “Now spare us;  
forgive what we have committed.”

May anger not consume the sorrowful;  
may punishment not crush the weary.  
Quickly console the brokenhearted,  
and grant us joy.

[Col. 0950B] Grant this, most loving Father,  
and only-begotten One equal to the Father,  
with the Spirit, the Paraclete,  
reigning throughout every age.

Amen.

**Clamores.** 1. Do not deal with us according to our sins, O God, nor repay us according to our iniquities. 2. “Not according to—” 3. “Not according to—”

V. But according to the multitude of your mercies.

**Supplication.** Let us pray to our merciful and readily heard Lord, as above.

**Capitula.** Hear our prayer, O Lord, and perceive our groans with your ears. For we acknowledge our iniquities [Col. 0950C] and disclose our sins before you. We have sinned against you, O God, and, confessing to you, we ask forgiveness. And because we have departed from your commandments and have not obeyed your law at all, turn, O Lord, toward your servants whom you redeemed with your blood. We beseech you, pardon us and grant forgiveness for our sins; deign to bestow upon us the mercy of your goodness.

**Our Father.**

**Blessing.** May God, who is the fountain of pardon, accept the offering of our abstinence.

[CXXXI] R. Amen.

And may he who is Almighty and the substance of Divinity grant the ability to obey his commands.

R. Amen.

And what we cannot accomplish because of bodily weakness, may we be worthy to fulfill with the help of his Divinity.

R. Amen.

[Col. 0950D] **Responsory for the Lord’s Betrayal.** Have mercy, for you are God; merciful one, have mercy, for we have sinned against you.

V. To you we raise our eyes, who dwell in the heavens.

P. Merciful one, have mercy.

**Another Responsory.** How many are the days of your servant, O Lord? When will you execute judgment upon those who persecute me?

V. Sinners have set traps for me, yet I have not strayed from your commandments.

P. Lord, when will you execute judgment?

**Reading from the Book of the Prophet Jeremiah (Chapter 9).**

R. Thanks be to God.

Thus says the Lord: Behold, I will smelt and test my enemies; for what else should I do before the son of my people? Their tongues are arrows that wound; they have spoken deceit with their mouth. With his friend he speaks peace, but secretly he lays ambushes for him. Shall I not visit these things, says the Lord? If there is any wise man who understands this, to whom the word of the Lord may come, let him announce it, says the almighty Lord.

R. Amen.

**First Epistle of the Apostle John to the Gentiles (Chapter 2).**

R. Thanks be to God.

Beloved, do not love the world, nor the things that are in the world. If anyone loves this world, the love of the Father is not in him, because everything that is in the world is the desire of the flesh, the desire of the eyes, and the pride of life. But whoever is of this world—and the world passes away, and its desire. Whoever does the will of God remains forever, just as God remains forever.

R. [Col. 0951B] Amen.

**Lauda and Hymn.** “Fountain of kindness,” as above.

V. Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man; free me from the unjust and deceitful man.

**Supplication.** Let us pray to our merciful and readily heard Lord Jesus Christ; let us beseech him with every supplication, that in his favor he may deign to justify us through the marks of his Passion.

R. Grant this, eternal almighty God.

**Capitula.** Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us; hear those who trust in you. Crush the weapons of our adversaries and destroy the traps prepared for us, so that, surrounded by heavenly brightness, we may not fall into the pit of death, but with a ready heart may exalt your merciful truth among the peoples—you who bore the disgrace of the Cross for us.

[Col. 0951C] **Our Father.**

**Blessing.** May the death of Christ, an admirable sacrament, drive away from us every defilement of sin.

R. Amen.

May his blood, an ineffable price, extinguish in you every deformity of vice.

R. Amen.

May the distinguished banner of his Cross make you companions of the Angels.

R. Amen.

**Responsory for the Resurrection of the Lord.** This is now the third time that Jesus manifested himself to his disciples after he had risen from the dead. Alleluia, alleluia.

P. After he had risen.

V. Glory and honor.

R. Thanks be to God.

I, John, servant of Jesus Christ, was in the Spirit, and I heard a voice from heaven saying to me: “I am the first, and I am the last, and the living one; I was dead, and behold, I am alive throughout the ages of ages.”

**Epistle of the Apostle Paul to the Colossians (Chapter 3).**

R. Thanks be to God.

Brothers, if you have risen with Christ, seek the things that are above, where Christ is seated at the right hand of God. Set your minds on the things that are above, not on those that are upon the earth. For you have died, and your life is hidden with Christ in God.

R. Amen.

**Lauda.** Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.

V. The Lord Jesus Christ has risen.

P. Alleluia, alleluia.

V. Glory be to him throughout the ages of ages. Amen.
