Now the Third Hour rises,  
and we hasten, intent upon it;  
we complete the work of psalmody:  
let us praise Christ the Lord.

At the Third Hour also  
Christ was suspended upon the Cross;  
he fulfilled the Father’s will,  
removed the sin of the world,

and sits at the Father’s right hand;  
the thrones praise the Lord,  
whom the wicked had denied.

[Col. 0952B] We worship Christ as God  
and await him as Judge;

Glory to you, O Lord,  
who rose from the dead,

**Supplication.** Let us pray to our merciful and readily heard Lord Jesus Christ; let us beseech him with every supplication, that just as at this Third Hour of the day the Holy Spirit illumined and taught the hearts of the Apostles, so he may graciously illumine us, though unworthy, with the true light.

R. Grant this, eternal almighty God.

Lord, have mercy.

R. Christ, have mercy.

**Capitula.** Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God the Father, who at the Third Hour of the day desired to be handed over for the redemption of your people and by the power of your glory reduced the necks of your enemies to nothing: grant to us and to your household forgiveness of the guilt of conscience and life from death, so that we may rightly find you to be the Redeemer whom we now and throughout all ages believe to be Judge and most merciful Savior.

**Our Father.**

R. Amen.

R. Amen.

Through mercy.

[Col. 0953B] R. Thanks be to God.

I, John, servant of Jesus Christ, was in the Spirit and saw: and behold, the throne of God had been set in heaven, and one was seated above the throne. The one who was seated was called the faithful and immortal Witness throughout the ages of ages.

R. Amen.

**Epistle of the Apostle Paul to the Ephesians (Chapter 4).**

R. Thanks be to God.

**Lauda.** Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. God has ascended amid jubilation.

Now, Holy Spirit,

with the Spirit, the Paraclete,

## HERE BEGINS THE ORDER TO BE SAID OR RECITED AT SEXT

**Antiphon.** Save me, O God, by your name, and by your power deliver me. Psalm 53.

Psalm 118. A Psalm of David. I have practiced judgment and justice. Your testimonies are wonderful. You are righteous, O Lord. Fol. LV.

[Col. 0954A] **Antiphon.** Save me, O God, by your name, and by your power deliver me.

**Responsory on feast days.** In every place are his dominions. Bless the Lord, O my soul. Alleluia, alleluia.

V. He heals all your diseases; he redeems your life from destruction.

P. Bless the Lord, O my soul.

V. Glory and honor.

**Ferial Responsory.** Have mercy, O merciful one; have mercy on us.

V. To you we raise our eyes, who dwell in the heavens.

P. Have mercy on us.

V. Glory and honor.

**Responsory on Sundays.** Grant us, O Lord, joy of heart, and grant peace in our days. Alleluia, alleluia.

V. Save us, O God, by your name, and by your power deliver us.

P. And grant—

V. Glory and honor.

**Responsory for Advent.** Rejoice, Jerusalem, at the Advent of the Lord, for he himself will come to you. And he will take from you the garment of mourning and anxieties, and at his coming he will clothe you with the beauty of righteousness.

V. And I will establish your visitation as peace, and your leaders as righteousness.

P. And he will take from you the garment of mourning.

V. Glory and honor.

**Reading from the Book of the Prophet Micah (Chapter 6).**

R. Thanks be to God.

In those days Micah spoke, saying: I will show you, O man, what is good and what the Lord requires of you: surely, to do judgment and justice, to love mercy, and to walk carefully with the Lord your God.

R. Amen.

**Epistle of the Apostle Paul to the Romans (Chapter 7).**

R. Thanks be to God.

Brothers, wretched man that I am! Who will free me from this body of death? The grace of God, through Jesus Christ our Lord.

R. Amen.

**Lauda.** Alleluia, alleluia. Save us, O Lord our God, and gather us from the nations. Alleluia.

V. So that we may confess your holy name and glory in your praise.

P. Alleluia, alleluia.

**Responsory for the Resurrection of the Lord.** Behold the mighty works of God, which the Lord has done; take courage and do not fear.

P. For God fights on our behalf. Alleluia, alleluia.

V. Praise the Lord, all nations; praise him together, all peoples.

P. For God on our behalf—

[Col. 0954D] V. Glory and honor to the Father.

**Hymn.**

Powerful Ruler, truthful God,  
who regulate the changes of things,  
who furnish morning with splendor  
and midday with fires,

extinguish the flames of strife,  
take away harmful heat,  
grant health to bodies  
and true peace to hearts.

Grant this, most loving Father,  
and only-begotten One equal to the Father,  
with the Spirit, the Paraclete,  
reigning throughout every age.

Amen.

**Hymn in Lent.**

[Col. 0955A]

Let us sing praises to the Lord  
with a very fervent spirit;  
the hour, having revolved six times,  
calls us to prayer.

For at this hour, for the faithful,  
the true grace of salvation,  
the sacrifice of the blessed Lamb,  
is restored through the power of the Cross.

By whose brightest light  
midday is darkened;  
with our whole heart  
let us receive such great splendor of grace.

[CXXXIV] Amen.

**Another.**

[Col. 0955B] Now the course of the Sixth Hour  
turns in the time of day  
and admonishes us in all things  
to render due praises.

Now Peter, praying,  
foresees the future faith of the Gentiles;  
now Christ urges the living waters  
to be given to the woman.

At this time of day, mystically,  
the Patriarch hosts three  
messengers in bodily form,  
under the sign of the Trinity.

This hour consists  
of the parts of the perfect, highest reckoning;  
drawn out, it perfects itself  
and holds together the fabric of the world.

[Col. 0955C] These things, O Christ, once created,  
remain through your power;  
whose power of glory  
reigns throughout all ages.

Amen.

**Clamores.** 1. Do not cast us away from your presence, O God, and do not take your Holy Spirit from us. 2. “Do not cast away—” 3. “Do not cast us away.”

V. From ruin and the noonday demon, protect us, holy God.

**Supplication.** Let us pray to our Redeemer, the Lord Jesus Christ; let us beseech him with every supplication, that in his favor he may deign to grant us help from heaven and his abundant mercy.

[Col. 0955D] R. Grant this, eternal almighty God.

**Capitula.** O God, who consecrate the times of the hours, at the course of the Sixth Hour you triumphed for the salvation of the world upon the gibbet of the Cross. Under the sanctification of this time, your Church offers you the service of her mind and brings forth the prayers of her confession. Therefore we ask that, while we live, we may render you the service of this celebration in such a way that after our passing we may be worthy to come to you to receive our crown.

**Our Father.**

**Blessing.** Deign to grant your salvation, O Lord, to your servants.

R. Amen.

Receive our prayers; fulfill our petitions; forgive our sins.

R. Amen.

Heal us from illnesses and cleanse the hearts of the faithful from the stains of sins.

R. Amen.

[Col. 0956A] **Responsory at Sext in Lent.** Turn your anger away from us, O Lord.

P. Do not be angry with us forever.

V. Mitigate all your anger, O Lord, and turn away from the anger of your indignation.

P. Do not be angry with us forever.

V. Glory and honor.

**Reading from the Book of the Prophet Joel (Chapter 2).**

R. Thanks be to God.

Thus says the Lord: Turn to me with all your heart, in fasting, weeping, and mourning. Tear your hearts and not your garments, and turn to the Lord your God, for he is gracious and merciful.

R. Amen.

**First Epistle of the Apostle John to the Gentiles (Chapter 2).**

R. Thanks be to God.

Beloved: I am writing a new commandment to you, which is true in him and in you, because the darkness has passed away and the true light is already shining. Whoever says that he is in the light but hates his brother is still in darkness. Whoever loves his brother remains in the light, and there is no stumbling block in him. But whoever hates his brother is in darkness and walks in darkness, and does not know where he is going, because the darkness has blinded his eyes. I am writing to you, little children, because your sins are forgiven you for his name’s sake, to whom belong honor and glory throughout the ages of ages.

R. Amen.

**Lauda.** Praise to you, O Lord, King of eternal glory. Save us, O Lord.

V. So that we may confess your holy name.

**Hymn.** “Let us sing praises to the Lord.” Folio CXXXII.

[Col. 0956C] **Capitula.** Receive, O Lord, the sacrifice of our confessions from the hand of our tongue, which you formed and raised up so that it might confess your holy name. Heal the wounds of our soul, and let them say: “Lord, who is like you?” For in your goodness he teaches us how he may have mercy on the one who confesses to him. Therefore release us from the wretched, shrieking chain of vices, and rescue us from the yoke of crimes into which we have been plunged; and from the intense darkness of confusion, graciously illumine us with the love of your serenity.

**Our Father.**

Deliver us from evil. Fol. 10.

**Blessing.** May the almighty Lord, who has made us devout through abstinence, make us most pure in chastity.

R. Amen.

And may he who inspired in us the vow of fasting grant us to find with him the reward of blessedness.

R. Amen.

So that we may bear fruit in spirit, while through fasting we desire to extinguish carnal pleasures.

[CXXXV] R. Amen.

[Col. 0956D] **Responsory for the Lord’s Betrayal.** Deliver me from my enemies, O Lord, for you are my God.

V. Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man, and free me from the unjust man.

P. For you are—

Let it be repeated.

**Another Responsory.** Be gracious, O Lord, and show yourself to us in the time of our tribulation and distress.

V. Save us, O God, by your name, and by your power deliver us.

P. In the time of tribulation.

Let the Responsory be repeated.

**Reading from the Book of Lamentations (Chapter 1).**

R. Thanks be to God.

[Col. 0957A] In those days Jeremiah said: The enemy sent fire into my bones and instructed me; he spread a net for my feet and turned me backward. The Lord is righteous, because it provoked his mouth to anger. Hear, I beseech you, all peoples: “The Lord is my portion,” my soul said; therefore I will wait for him.

R. Amen.

**First Epistle of the Apostle John to the Gentiles (Chapter 5).**

R. Thanks be to God.

Beloved: This is the message that you heard from the beginning: that we should love one another, not like Cain, who was from the evil one and killed his brother. And why did he kill him? Because his works were evil, while his brother’s were righteous. Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer. And we know that no murderer has eternal life abiding in him. By this we have known love: that he laid down his life for us; and we ought to lay down our lives for our brothers.

R. Amen.

**Lauda.** Praise to you, O Lord, King of eternal glory. Save us.

V. So that we may confess.

**Hymn.** “Now the course of the hour.”

**Clamores.** “Do not cast away—,” fol. CXXXIII, CXXXIV.

**Supplication.** Let us pray to our merciful and readily heard Lord Jesus Christ; let us beseech him with every supplication, that in his favor he may deign to justify us through the marks of his Passion.

R. Grant this, eternal almighty God.

**Capitula.** Say to our soul, O Lord: “I am your salvation.” And do not allow it, though you see it disturbed by the sight of its weakness, to remain “in eternal utterance” [printed: in aeterno eloquio; the sense is uncertain]; nor abandon our inmost being when iniquity has revealed itself in its poisonous form. Judge us, though guilty, and by your power conquer those who attack us.

**Our Father.**

**Blessing.** May Christ the Lord, who, innocent, hung upon the wood with outstretched hands, save us through the sacrament of his Cross.

R. Amen.

May he also raise us upward by his hanging, who deigned to be exalted on the Cross for us.

R. Amen.

So that we may truly be the gain of his blood, we who direct the confidence of our heart toward him.

R. Amen.

## HERE BEGINS THE ORDER TO BE SAID AT NONE

## Hymn throughout the year

It is time to pour forth prayers;

the course of the day urges us

to sing a hymn of praise

to you, Redeemer of all.

Make the mind serene;

complete the honorable work;

receive the prayers of those who pray;

grant everlasting life.

Grant this, most merciful Father,

and Only-Begotten One, equal to the Father,

reigning with the Spirit, the Paraclete,

through every age.

Amen.

## Hymn in Lent

[Col. 0959A]

The sun’s vaulted orbit,

having rolled through nine circles,

at the completion of the course of the hours,

completes three times three.

In this season of the Passion

the Author of all things completed it;

now he sent the summoned servants

to the labor of the vineyard.

At this mystical hour Peter

loosed the bonds of the lame man;

now, the knower of visions,

he brings them to an end at the third return.

At this hour let us sing glory

with voice and pure minds

[Col. 0959B] to God, who creates favorable ages,

completed for the righteous.

Amen.

1. Be favorable to our iniquities, and heal, O Lord, our illnesses.  
2. Be favorable.  
3. Be favorable.

Let us pray to our gracious and merciful Lord Jesus Christ; with every supplication let us ask that he may mercifully grant us the desire to repent, the fruit of repentance, and the remedy of eternal life. R. Grant this, eternal almighty God.

## Chapter

O God, who, for the salvation of the world, at the course of the ninth hour triumphed [Col. 0959C] in the glorious sign of the Cross through a miracle, and, having destroyed death, rescued the souls of the saints from the infernal prison, opening the way for us by returning to the heights: we ask that you may be pleased with our service in such a way that, after our passing, we may hasten with very swift steps to that place where you, our true redemption, went before us.

Our Father.

Save your people, O Lord, whom you yourself created. R. Amen. Bless your inheritance, which you redeemed with precious blood. R. Amen. Rule it and exalt it forever and ever. R. Amen.

Defiled in mouth, in heart, in deed, and by all vices, we ask forgiveness, because we acknowledge our guilt; and that you may forgive this offense of sin, we prostrate ourselves and, committing ourselves to the faith, ask.

Our Father.

## Hymn

Look upon the Sun of the angels,

whom purity of mind desires

to behold with intent gaze,

remaining above.

By whom all things flourish in heaven

with prosperous course and return;

by whom the life of all is established,

[Col. 0962A] heed the thanks of your suppliants.

Grant your servants protection,

by which their blessings may be moderated;

let adversities be harmless;

let hearts not be corrupted.

You are the moderation and creator

of the senses, salvation and restoration;

drink and food, joy,

light, and strength of hearts.

Drive slippery wantonness from our limbs,

lest foul passion torment them,

and the mind’s action incur blame.

Bring an abundance of virtue,

through which you may bestow mercy;

[Col. 0962B] so that, forgetting our sins,

let heavenly peace descend,

by which you may preserve all things safely forever,

Glory to the unbegotten Father,

glory to the Only-Begotten,

together with the Holy Spirit,

through everlasting ages.

## Hymn

Remember, worshiper of God,

that you have undergone the sacred dew

of the font and the washing,

and that you have been renewed by chrism.

When sleep calls,

seeking a chaste bed,

let the sign of the Cross mark

your forehead and the place of your heart.

The Cross drives away every sin;

let darkness flee before the Cross;

[Col. 0963A] when the mind is dedicated

to such a sign, it knows no wavering.

Far away, far away be

[Col. 0963B] may recline for a little while,

Glory to God the Father,

[CXL] ## Hymn

Let us prepare songs

against opposing assaults,

against the leader of darkness,

against the grim henchman.

Let hope and faith fully arm our hands;

[Col. 0965A] let the mighty Cross cover our loins;

let us gird ourselves with the sword of the Spirit

because of the terrors of night.

By your strongest hand, Jesus,

save the faithful through faith;

overturn the adversaries by the Cross;

protect all things in peace.

## Hymn

The first darkness is present;

let us now all dedicate

the advance of the dreadful night

with songs and hymns.

For this is the time

of which Jeremiah says

that we must rise

[Col. 0965B] at the beginning of night.

With the weapons of the spirit,

O unconquered root of David,

break the chains of night,

and give the radiance of salvation.

May the rest of sleep be pleasant;

may the ever-watchful mind rise again;

let us not be defiled in deed,

nor weighed down in spirit;

but in body and mind,

with a fervent spirit,

with an unflagging step,

may we follow you, O Christ.

[Col. 0965C]

## Hymn

We have passed through

the beginnings of dreadful night in praises;

now we beg you, Trinity,

to hear us as we sing beforehand.

Give grace to all;

raise up even the weary;

erase the errors of sins;

exclude continual scandal.

May the true light enlighten us;

may it drive away the darkness of the mind,

so that peace may abound for all

who believe in you, Creator.

The time for rest is here,

which innocent rest

[Col. 0965D] may grant to weary limbs,

the malignity of the ancient serpent,

and its deadly poison.

beneath the safest shadow

of your wings,

we may remain and rise to your praises.

Let there be glory and power

to God the Father and the Son,

and to the co-equal Paraclete,

through ages of ages.

Amen.

Merciful author of light, immeasurable light,

[Col. 0966B] with whom the Holy Spirit reigns as one,

to the unbegotten God and the begotten Christ,

Then the Litanies of Mercy are to be said on each weekday, in the order that follows, on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, and Saturday. And because the Chapters precede the Litanies of Mercy, they are arranged in this way, as they should be said on each weekday.

## Monday — Chapter

Enlighten our night, eternal almighty God; cause us, your servants, to fall asleep in quietness and to be awakened by the virtues of the saints, so that, with your help, we may deserve to reach the bright day free from every disturbance of darkness.

Our Father.

## Blessing

May the Cross of our Lord Jesus Christ defend us from the fear of the enemy. R. Amen. May the light of truth drive every darkness of blindness from us. R. Amen. [Col. 0967C] So that, saved by its illumination, we may deserve to receive eternal blessing. R. Amen.

## Tuesday — Chapter

O God, eternal light, splendor of the stars, brightness of the nights, incomprehensible illumination of darkness, grant us this night safe, tranquil, and peaceful; and if we have contracted any sins today, merciful and compassionate one, graciously forgive them. Hear also willingly the prayers of your servants, and grant their requests.

Our Father.

## Blessing

May the hand of God the almighty Father assist us. R. Amen. May his holy arm strengthen us. R. Amen. May no enemy prevail over us. R. Amen. But may our Lord Jesus Christ incline [Col. 0967D] his ear to us in all things. R. Amen.

## Wednesday — Chapter

If we have contracted any sins during the day, in deed, word, or thought, O Lord, forgive them; and graciously grant us this night tranquil, peaceful, and without sin.

Our Father, who are.

## Blessing

May the Lord Jesus Christ, who redeemed us, guard us this night. R. Amen. May he sanctify our hearts and bodies. R. Amen. And may he complete our desires in good works. R. Amen.

## Thursday — Chapter

Guard our souls, O Lord, and rescue them from the hand of the tempter. Keep the nighttime thief far from us, and drive away from us the snares of his falsehood, because the many-shaped one is [Col. 0968A] present during the nighttime hours, seeking to deceive the sleeper whom he cannot overcome while awake. But you, O Lord, as a good shepherd and most merciful guide, do not abandon your flock. You laid down your soul for the sheep; save us, whom you redeemed with your precious blood.

Our Father, who are.

## Blessing

Look graciously upon your flock, good Shepherd, and fill these servants of yours with your blessings. R. Amen. Grant soundness of mind and body, and bestow perpetual salvation. R. Amen. Give us quiet and peaceful times, so that we may serve you with devoted mind. R. Amen.

## Friday — Chapter

Guard us as we rest during this night, and graciously hear quickly the prayers we pour out before you; and so that we may not [CXLII] fear the enemy tempter in the darkness, [Col. 0968B] surround us with the strength of the Cross.

Our Father.

## Blessing

May the Lord pour over us a rain of his blessings, and may the inseparable Trinity never depart from us. R. Amen. May he protect us with angelic visitation and drive the nighttime thief from our beds. R. Amen. So that, bound by the belt of chastity, the enemy may not frighten us with any art of his deception. R. Amen.

## Friday — Chapter

Guard us, O Lord, just as you graciously heard and guarded holy Daniel praying in the lions’ den, and the beasts did not touch him, because your strongest right hand protected him. Fierce animals became harmless before him and fled when they scented him. [Col. 0968C] May your Christ shine in us, O Lord, and may the treacherous enemy flee from our hearts and from our beds.

Our Father.

## Blessing

Almighty God, who are eternal light, enter, we ask, into the understanding of your servants. R. Amen. Guard your flock and repel the lurking wolf. R. Amen. Preserve all hearts and breasts, and drive the nighttime thief and his angels far away from them. R. Amen.

## Saturday — Chapter

Remove from us, O Lord, the stumbling-block of night, so that we may not fear walking in the midst of the shadow of death. May your rod and your staff seize us; the rod of Jesse through Blessed Mary. May he himself [Col. 0968D] lead us to the morning vigil, who taught us to pray and to say:

Our Father, who are.

## Blessing

May the Lord hear us and bless us. R. Amen. May he protect us from the cunning enemy and defend us from every evil. R. Amen. And beneath the shadow of his wings may he guard us this night and at all times. R. Amen.

When these things have been completed, every day throughout the year, after Compline has ended in this manner and before the sprinkling of holy water, the following Verse and the Prayer attached to it are to be said.

V. Guard us, O Lord, as the apple of the eye; protect us beneath the shadow of your wings.

## Prayer follows

You saved us, Lord Jesus Christ [Col. 0969A] while we watched during the day; guard us as we rest during this night. And if we should fall asleep, may your Holy Spirit watch over us, and guard us during this night and at all times, and remain always with us. R. Amen.

Through your mercy, etc.

May the Lord always be with you. R. And with your spirit.

In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, let us sleep and rest this night in peace. R. Thanks be to God.

And when holy water is sprinkled over the altar, let the Priest say: May the Father bless you, may the Son teach you, and may the Holy Spirit enlighten you. R. Amen.

And when holy water is sprinkled upon the Christian faithful, the Priest should say: May the grace of the Holy Spirit cleanse you from every sin. Or thus: May God the Son of the almighty Father cleanse you from every defilement.

[Col. 0969B]

## Monday — Litanies of Mercy

Have mercy on us, God; have mercy on us. R. Have mercy on us, and be reconciled. V. Hear, merciful eternal King, the prayers of those who plead, and turn away your anger. Forgive every crime and grant rest to the faithful people. R. Have mercy on us, God. V. All together we beseech you, good God Jesus: heed us, moved by compassion for us and entreated by our prayers, and grant what your faithful people ask. R. Have mercy on us, God. V. Grant peace, give rest and tranquility to the times. We ask: send the angel of salvation, and favor those who pray from your heights. R. Have mercy on us, God. V. [Col. 0969C] Be continually our merciful defender and protector, O gracious God; take up arms, rise up, help us, and mercifully be present. R. Have mercy on us, God.

## Tuesday — Litanies of Mercy

Have mercy, O Merciful One, and be reconciled; show yourself merciful and forgive sins; born as a human from Mary, God in nature. R. Forgive the iniquities by which we have sinned against you. V. Through whom we always believe that you reign in heaven; with your help, may we thus be free from evils. R. Forgive the iniquities. V. We ask you, we beseech you, holy and gracious God, that you look mercifully upon us wretched ones, O Christ. R. Forgive. V. Your flock confesses to you the evils it has committed; you, holy Father—from the enemy’s devouring [fragmentary as printed]. V. We are weighed down; we weep over our sins; do not allow what you acquired to be destroyed by angels. V. The whole assembly of the Catholic Church, [Col. 0969D] crying out to you, grant a place of mercy. V. [CXLIII] Restore a homeland to travelers or the needy; restore former health to the sick, and rest to the dead.

## Wednesday — Litanies of Mercy

Have mercy, O Lord, have mercy on us; we have sinned against you alone. R. Forgive us, we ask. V. We have fallen grievously into great sins; we ask forgiveness. Christ, spare our offenses. V. We weep over the crime committed; do not repay us as we deserve. Merciful Father, erase our guilt and release us from our sins. V. Restore a contrite heart to repentant converts, and now help those who have been crushed, heavenly King. V. Now help the poor, the needy, travelers, shipwrecked people, the fallen, widows, and orphans, heavenly King. V. Now help travelers, the oppressed, [Col. 0970A] the dispersed, captives, prisoners, the sick, and the dead, heavenly King. V. If we have sinned against you, we are yours, O God, awaiting your mercy, O Lord. V. What is a human being, O Lord, that you should be angry with him, or a corruptible race, that you should be so fiercely angry with it? V. There is no one among those born who has not acted impiously, nor among those who confess who has not sinned against you. V. In this your goodness will be proclaimed, O God, when you have had mercy on our iniquities.

## Thursday — Litanies of Mercy

Have mercy, have mercy, R. Lord; we have sinned, you forgive, R. Lord. V. We have gone astray, you correct us, R. Lord. V. For the sick we pray to you, R. Lord. V. For the dead we ask you, R. Lord. V. For captives we ask you, R. Lord. V. For travelers we beseech you, R. [Col. 0970B] Lord. V. For those sailing we pray to you, R. Lord. V. For penitents we entreat you, R. Lord. V. We ask forgiveness, R. Lord.

## Friday — Litanies of Mercy

Lord, have mercy on us; Lord, have mercy on us. R. And turn your anger away from us. V. Lord, hear those who weep; Lord, hear those who seek forgiveness. R. And turn it away. V. Lord, merciful and compassionate, help the prayers of orphans. R. And turn it away. V. Lord, for your own sake receive the prayers of each person. R. And turn it away. V. Lord, do not despise the people who seek your mercy. R. Turn away the anger.

## Saturday — Litanies of Mercy

Have mercy, have mercy, have mercy, good Jesus. R. Put an end to our sins. V. Hear mercifully, heed us, and console those who groan, [Col. 0970C] merciful Father, eternal King. V. Be the author and Redeemer of your people’s protection, and the forgiver of sins. V. We all prostrate ourselves and ask; we beseech you to acknowledge us; we entreat you to forgive. V. You who wished to take the form of a servant for us, now hear the penitents. V. You who placed the confessing thief in paradise and condemned the other. V. You who endured the suffering of the Cross for us, now remember your servants. V. Protect now by your Cross those whom you redeemed through it; guard them now by your right hand. V. You who raised Lazarus, already putrefying, from the tomb, guard your sheep. V. Eternal King, good Jesus, absolve us from stain and strengthen us in good things. V. Grant rest to the dead; grant paradise; place the bound among the host of the saints.

[Col. 0970D] ## Litanies of Mercy at the Time of the Lord’s Betrayal

God, have mercy; God, have mercy; have mercy, God, have mercy. R. Christ, have mercy. V. You are light to the blind, hearing to the deaf, speech to the mute, walking to the lame, and strength to the weak. V. You are shepherd and sheep on the way of salvation; you suffered for us; you are the eternal victor. Christ, spare us. V. Hear widows; rule orphans; grant consolation to orphans, prisoners, and all the faithful. V. Heed and hear those who pray; help us; remove fury; provide protection, eternal Redeemer.

## Prayer

Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us; and in your compassion graciously deign to erase the abundance of our iniquities, so that whatever, at the enemy’s prompting, we have done wrong during the course of this day in thought, word, or deed, you [Col. 0971A] who are gracious and merciful, may mercifully forgive. Thus, escaping the nighttime snare, may we rise at the appointed order of the services and safely offer you a jubilant song of praise. R. Amen.

## Prayer

Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us; and mercifully grant consolation to orphans, the needy, the crushed, travelers, the sorrowful, and the fallen. Raise up the oppressed, gather the dispersed, recall captives, visit the sick, erase the crimes of penitents and guilty persons, and grant fitting assistance to all Christians. Increase the health of souls and bodies for travelers, prisoners, and all the faithful. Erase our countless crimes, and because of your great mercy grant eternal rest to all the dead. R. Amen.

[Col. 0971B] These two Prayers are to be said during Lent after the Litanies of Mercy, one of them on one day and the other on another day. [CXLIV] When these have ended, the Priest should sprinkle holy water, as stated above.

## The Blessing of the Table follows

V. The eyes of all hope in you, O Lord, and you give them food at the proper time. V. Glory and honor. V. You open your hand and fill every living thing with blessing. V. Glory and honor. V. The poor will eat and be satisfied, and those who seek him will praise the Lord, and their hearts will live forever and ever. Here “Glory” is not said.

And thus the Minister who brought the loaves for the table approaches and inserts this verse:

He gives food to all flesh, for his mercy endures forever. Glory and honor to the Father, and to the Son, and to [Col. 0971C] the Holy Spirit; as it was in the beginning, and is now, etc.

[Col. 0972A] ## Blessing

Sanctify, O Lord, this food and drink that we are about to receive, so that, sanctified through the hands of your holy angel, we may deserve to consume both. R. Amen.

Through your mercy, O our God, who live and rule all things through all ages of ages. Amen.

In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, sanctified and blessed, let us be refreshed in peace. R. Thanks be to God.

And while lunch or dinner is taking place, everyone must keep silence; and among the regular members, the book of the Rule should be read, so that popular tales may not be interspersed. When lunch or dinner has ended, this Praise is inserted:

A voice of joy and salvation, Alleluia. R. In the tents of the righteous. Alleluia, alleluia. Behold how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to dwell together as one. R. In the tents of the righteous. V. Glory and honor to the Father. [Col. 0972B] R. In the tents.

This verse is inserted:

You have refreshed us, O Lord, in your creation; and in the works of your hands we will rejoice. V. Glory and honor to the Father.

## Prayer

We give you thanks and bless you, Lord Jesus Christ, who have graciously satisfied us with bodily food and drink. Refresh us with a spiritual gift, and free us from every bond of sin, so that we may always serve you unharmed. R. Amen.

Through your mercy, O our God, who live and rule all things forever and ever. R. Amen.

In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ: may the Lord cause his servants to abound in every blessing and peace. Amen. V. May joy always be in this house with these [Col. 0972C] brothers. Amen.

[Col. 0971]

# THE COMMON OFFICE BEGINS. (C)

# THE OFFICE OF ONE SICK PERSON OR OF SEVERAL SICK PERSONS BEGINS

[Col. 0971C]

This office is said on Friday, when there is no feast to be recited, or at another time when it pleases one to recite it.

[CXLV] ## At Vespers

[Col. 0971D] In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, light with peace. R. Thanks be to God.

May the Lord be with you. R. And with.

## Praise

The Lord is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear?

May the Lord be with you. R. And with.

## Sound

Heal, O Lord, all our illnesses. Alleluia. V. Redeem our life from destruction. Alleluia, alleluia.

## Antiphon

Christ the Lord, who are the saving physician. R. Grant the sick the help of heavenly medicine. V. O Lord, save us; O Lord, prosper us. R. Grant. V. Glory and honor. R. Grant.

May the Lord be with you. R. And with.

## Praise

May your right hand save us. Alleluia. R. [Col. 0972C] Hear us, O Lord our God. Alleluia, alleluia. V. So that we may confess your holy name and rejoice in your praise. R. Hear us. V. Glory and honor. R. Hear us.

May the Lord be with you. R. And with.

Lauda. Save us, Lord our God: Alleluia. P. And gather us from the nations: Alleluia, alleluia. V. That we may give thanks to your holy name and [Col. 0972D] glory in your praise. P. And gather us. V. Glory. P. Alleluia, alleluia.

**Hymn**

Christ, heavenly medicine of the Father,

True physician of human salvation,

Powerfully unfold your favor

To the prayers of your provident people.

Behold, we beseech you for the sick,

Whom destructive pestilence and disease afflict;

That, merciful, you may relieve the illness

By which the prostrate are shaken.

You, manifest in power,

Soon saved Peter’s mother-in-law lying in fever,

The ruler’s son, and the boy

Of the centurion.

[Col. 0973A] Give strength to the languishing people;

Pour forth abundant salvation upon the peoples;

Restore the sick to their former strength,

As is your wont.

Heal the diseases of their bodies and souls;

Apply your remedy to the causes of their wounds,

Lest, without fruit, suffering burn

Our bodies.

Let every destructive assault withdraw;

Let every tormenting attack melt away;

Let the strength of the desired salvation

Foster the suffering limbs.

Now, God, have mercy on our tears;

Thus heal those for whom we now ask you,

So that every sick person lying here

[Col. 0973B] May feel your healing:

That, while they are worn down by the evils inflicted,

They may enter, adorned among the number of the learned,

And, sharing in the reward,

Possess the realms of heaven.

Let the choir sing glory and resound;

Let it speak, sing, and repeat glory;

Let the stars cry out to the triune name,

To the one Godhead alone.

**Supplication.** Let us pray; with every supplication let us beseech our Redeemer, our Lord Jesus Christ, that he may graciously deem it worthy to heal the wounds of his servants, all the faithful who are sick. R. Grant this, eternal almighty God.

[Col. 0973C] Kyrie eleison. R. Christe eleison. Kyrie eleison.

**Capitula.** We beseech you, Lord, not to rebuke us in your anger, nor permit your fury to rage against us; but, as a gentle reprover, remove the practice of sinning, lest by rebuking us too harshly you drive us to destruction. Therefore have mercy [CXLVI] on our infirmity and bestow your healing upon your servants, all the faithful who are sick; and those whom you see troubled by their own sin, count among the peaceful through merciful forgiveness.

**Our Father.** Deliver us from evil. fol. 10.

**Blessing.** May the almighty Lord, who chastises his most faithful servants, all the faithful who are sick, with bodily affliction, himself cleanse them and us from the illnesses of body and mind. R. Amen. And may he who took our infirmity upon himself grant to us and to them [Col. 0973D] the reward of unfailing endurance. R. Amen. Thus may his mercy cherish us all together, so that neither our corrupted health may rage against us, nor the infirmity of despair brought upon us overwhelm us. R. Amen.

Lauda. Save us, Lord our God: Alleluia. P. That we may give thanks to your holy name, alleluia, and glory in your praise. Alleluia, alleluia. V. Remember us, Lord, in your favor; visit us with your salvation, O God. P. That we may give thanks. V. Glory and honor. P. That we may give thanks.

**Prayer.** Almighty eternal God, incline… As below.

Through mercy.

May the Lord be with you. R. And with you.

[Col. 0974A] In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, salvation of the sick, with peace. R. Thanks be to God.

**At Matins**

Do not cast us away, Lord, from your presence. P. And do not take your Holy Spirit from us. Psalm 50. P. And do not take your Holy Spirit. Do not cast us away.

**Prayer.** Do not cast us away, Lord, from your presence, nor take your mercy from us; so that those whom the guilt of their crime holds liable may, through the clemency of your compassion, be made absolved. R. Amen.

Through.

**Antiphon.** Our Savior, save us in your love. P. And by your forgiveness set us free. V. To you we lift our eyes, who dwell in heaven. P. And by your forgiveness. V. Glory. P. And by your forgiveness.

[Col. 0974B] **Prayer.** Almighty eternal God, incline your ear to our supplications, and grant your heavenly grace as medicine to your servants, all the faithful who are suffering from adverse bodily health.

Through. R. Amen.

**Antiphon.** Show us, Lord, your mercy. P. And grant us your salvation. V. That we may give thanks to your holy name and glory in your praise. P. And grant us your salvation. V. Glory and honor. P. And grant us your salvation.

**Prayer.** O God, who purify the hearts of those who confess to you and absolve the accusing conscience from every bond of iniquity, grant forgiveness to your servants and bestow upon [Col. 0974C] their bodies the pure medicine of heavenly grace. R. Amen.

Through.

**Antiphon.** Turn, Lord, and rescue our souls. P. And save us for the sake of your mercy, for no one in death remembers you. V. Lord, do not rebuke us in your fury, nor chastise us in your anger. P. And save us. V. Glory and honor. P. And save us.

**Prayer.** Be present, we beseech you, Lord, to your suppliants; and to those upon whom you impose the severity of just correction graciously bring the help of your most merciful consolation. R. Amen.

Through.

R. Be our strength, Lord, and the support of the sick. [Col. 0974D] P. Be a refuge and deliverer for the oppressed. V. Be our arm in the morning and our salvation in time of tribulation. P. Be a refuge. V. Glory and honor. Let the Responsory be repeated.

**Antiphon.** I kill and I make alive; I strike, and I myself heal.

**Canticle of Deuteronomy (chapter 32)**

For I saw them exhausted,  
and weakened in obscurity, and undone.

And I said: Where are your gods, O Israel,  
in whom you trusted?

You ate the fat of their sacrifices  
and drank the wine of their libations.

Let them rise now and help you,  
and become your protectors.

[Col. 0975A] See, see, that I am the Lord,  
and there is no other besides me.

I am he who kills and makes alive;  
I strike, and I myself heal.

**Matutinarium.** Shine, Lord, your face upon us and have mercy on us. P. That we may know your way on earth. V. May God have mercy on us and bless us. P. That we may know.

Lauda. Praise the Lord, all nations, alleluia, alleluia, and praise him together, all peoples. P. [CXLVII] For his mercy has been confirmed upon us, and the truth of the Lord remains forever. V. Glory and honor.

**Reading from the Book of the Prophet Jeremiah (chapter 29)**

R. Thanks be to God.

[Col. 0975B] Thus says the Lord: Behold, I will visit you and raise up over you my good word, and I will bring you back to this place. For I know the thoughts that I think concerning you, says the Lord—thoughts of peace and not of affliction—to give you faith, salvation, and patience. And you will call upon me and fear; you will pray to me, and I will hear you. You will seek me and find me, when you seek me with all your heart; I will be found by you, says the almighty Lord. R. Amen.

**Hymn.** “Christ, heavenly…” As above at Vespers.

**Capitula.** Look upon your servants, Lord, all the faithful who are sick and who rejoice in the invocation of your name; grant them heavenly medicine, pour into them protection of mind, and graciously [Col. 0975C] deign to free them from every illness and sickness.

**Our Father.** Deliver us from evil. Fol. 10.

Lauda. “Save us.” As above at Vespers.

**At Terce**

**Reading from the Book of Proverbs of Solomon (chapter 7)**

R. Thanks be to God.

My son, keep my words and store up my commandments within you. Keep my precepts, and you will live. R. Amen.

**Antiphon.** The Lord of hosts is himself the King of glory. Psalm 23.

**Prayer.** Powerful and mighty Lord, Lord of hosts, you are yourself the King of glory. Cleanse our heart from every sin, keep our hands innocent, and separate our souls from vanity, so that we may [Col. 0975D] stand in your holy place and deserve to receive a blessing from you, Lord our God. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Psalm 124.

**Antiphon.** To you, Lord, I have lifted up my soul; my God, in you I trust; let me not be put to shame, nor let my enemies mock me. Let the Antiphon be repeated: “To you, Lord…”

**Prayer.** To you, Lord, we pray, raising the form of our soul with the support of hope; so imbue it with spiritual desires that it may cease to live according to the flesh, lest enemies mock the soul that spiritual grace draws toward heavenly things by promising earthly ones. Therefore, almighty God, grant that it may prefer to cling to truth [Col. 0976A] rather than falsehood; let it be pleased to persist in humility, so that by this it may avoid the disease of pride and become accustomed to share with the saints in the rewards of your goodness. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

**Antiphon.** See my humility, Lord; see my labor, and forgive my sins.

**Psalm 24**

See my humility and my labor,  
and forgive me all my sins.

Look upon my enemies, for they have multiplied,  
and they hate me with wicked hatred.

Guard my soul and rescue me.  
Let me not be put to shame, for I have called upon you.

The innocent and upright have clung to me,  
because I have waited for [Col. 0976B] you, Lord.

Redeem me, God of Israel,  
from all my tribulations.

Glory and honor. Let the Antiphon be repeated: “See my humility.”

R. Hasten to help us, Lord; to deliver us, P. Do not delay. V. Save us, O God, by your name, and deliver us by your strength. P. Do not delay. V. Glory and honor. Let the Responsory be repeated.

Lauda. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. Praise to you, praise to you, praise to you, praise to you, Jesus Christ. V. Glory and honor. P. Alleluia, alleluia.

**Prayers.** There is no other, P. Except you, O God. V. Who can be prayed to. P. Except you. V. Who can show mercy. P. Except you. [Col. 0976C] V. Who can heal the contrite. P. Except you. V. Who can visit the sick. P. Except you. V. Who can free captives. P. Except you. Let “There is no other” be repeated.

**Supplication.** Let us pray; with every supplication let us beseech our Redeemer, our Lord Jesus Christ, that he may graciously deem it worthy to heal the wounds of his servants, all the faithful who are sick. R. Grant this, eternal almighty God.

Kyrie eleison. R. Christe eleison. Kyrie eleison.

[CXLVIII] **Capitula.** Raising our souls to you, Lord, we beseech you to lift them up by spiritual desire, since they are so often submerged by carnal inclination. Grant humility, which you yourself may behold, and bring fruitful labor to completion, so that you may forgive sins. Let simplicity and justice cling to our souls; let deceit and injustice withdraw [Col. 0976D] far from us.

**Our Father.** But deliver us.

Deliver us from evil, and confirm us in your fear and in good works, O God our Trinity, who are blessed, live, and rule all things forever and ever. R. Amen.

Let the blessing be said as at Terce, which is said on weekdays throughout the year. At Sext and None let everything be said as at another time.

# THE OFFICE OF THE DEAD BEGINS

**At Vespers**

**Antiphon.** Deliver our souls from death, Lord, so that we may please you in the light of the living.

**Psalm**

[Col. 0977A]

Deliver my soul from the wicked man,  
and your sword from the enemies of your hand.

Deliver me from the hand of our enemies  
and from those who pursue me.

Shine your face upon your servant; save me in your mercy.  
Lord, let me not be put to shame, for I have called upon you.

Deliver me from my enemies, my God,  
and free me from those who rise up against me.

Deliver me from those who work iniquity,  
and save me from men of blood.

Deliver me from the mire, lest I become stuck;  
free me from those who hate me and from the depths of the waters.

Deliver me, for you know my reproach,  
and [Col. 0977B] my shame and my dishonor.

Deliver me from my enemies, Lord; to you I have fled.  
Teach me to do your will, for you are my God.

Deliver me and free me from many waters  
and from the hand of foreign sons, whose mouth has spoken vanity  
and whose right hand is a right hand of iniquity.

Deliver me, Lord, from the evil man;  
from the iniquitous man deliver me.

You will deliver me from the contentions of the people;  
you will set me at the head of the nations.

You deliver the needy from the hand of one stronger than he,  
the poor and needy from those who plunder him.

He delivered me from my strongest enemies and from those who hated me,  
for they were strengthened [Col. 0977C] against me.

Glory and honor.

**Antiphon.** Your dead shall live, Lord, and my slain shall rise. Alleluia, alleluia. V. Awake, you who sleep in the dust, and praise the Lord your God. Alleluia, alleluia.

**Psalm of David**

How long will my enemy be exalted over me?  
Look upon me and hear me, Lord my God.

How long, Lord, will you forget me forever?  
How long will you turn your face from me?

How long will the enemy reproach me?  
Will the adversary provoke your name forever?

How long, Lord, will you be angry forever?  
Will your jealousy be kindled [Col. 0977D] like fire?

How long, Lord, will you turn away forever?  
Will your anger blaze like fire?

How long, Lord, will sinners—  
how long will sinners glory?

How long shall you be heavy-hearted? Why do you love vanity  
and seek falsehood?

How long will you judge iniquity  
and take on the faces of sinners?

Glory and honor.

**Antiphon.** Redeem the souls of your servants, Lord. P. Alleluia. V. Guard all their bones, and do not forsake the souls of your servants. P. Alleluia. V. Glory and honor to the Father.

**Psalm of David**

[Col. 0978A]

Redeem me and have mercy on me; my foot has stood on the straight way;  
in the churches I will bless you, Lord.

The Lord will redeem the souls of his servants,  
and will not forsake all who hope in him.

You redeemed your people with your arm,  
the sons of Jacob and Joseph.

The Lord sent redemption to his people;  
he commanded his covenant forever.

Glory and honor.

**Antiphon.** Do not enter into judgment P. with your servants, Lord. V. For no living person will be justified in your sight. P. With your servants. V. Glory and honor. P. With your servants.

**Psalm**

[Col. 0978B] Will God cast us off forever,  
or will he not continue to be favorable?

Will you be angry with us forever?  
[CXLIX] Or will you extend your anger from generation to generation?

Will he be angry every day?

Will the dust give thanks to you,  
or proclaim your truth?

Will you work wonders for the dead,  
or will physicians raise them up and give you thanks?

Will anyone in the grave tell of your mercy,  
or of your truth in destruction?

Will your wonders be known in darkness,  
and your justice in the land of forgetfulness?

Will the seat of iniquity cling to you,  
you who fashion labor into a commandment?

[Col. 0978C] Are you angry, Lord, in the rivers,  
or is your fury in the rivers? Or your indignation in the sea?

Is he not your father, God,  
who possessed you, made you, and created you?

Will Zion say: “A man, and a man, was born in her,”  
and the Most High himself founded her?

Will God forget to show mercy,  
or restrain his mercies in anger? Glory and honor.

**Antiphon.** We believe that our Redeemer will resurrect us. P. And in our flesh we shall see the Lord God. V. The Lord is faithful in all his words and holy in all his works. P. And in our flesh. V. Glory and honor. P. And in our flesh [Col. 0978D] we shall see the Lord God.

Lauda. Alleluia. Do with your servants, O God, P. according to your mercy. Alleluia, alleluia. V. Remember your congregation, Lord, which you founded from the beginning. P. According to your mercy. V. Glory and honor. P. According to your mercy.

Lauda. Alleluia. Lead them out, Lord, from darkness and the shadow of death. P. And break their bonds. Alleluia, alleluia. V. Remember your congregation, Lord, which you founded from the beginning. P. And break their bonds. V. Glory and honor. P. And break their bonds.

**Hymn**

Fiery God, fountain of souls,

You who join the two elements,

You fashioned the living and the dying

[Col. 0979A] Human being together, Father.

Both are yours, both are yours, Ruler;

Their union is joined to you;

While they remain enlivened together,

Spirit and flesh alike serve you.

But when these are separated,

They dissolve and destroy the human being;

Dry earth receives the body,

The soul takes up the airy element.

Since everything created must necessarily

At last become weakened by age,

And things compacted must be separated,

And discordantly woven things be unwoven,

For this reason the greatest care

Is devoted to tombs; for this reason

[Col. 0979B] The final honor receives the limbs dissolved,

And the funeral procession adorns them.

This is what the provident devotion

Of Christ’s worshipers strives for,

Since it believes that all things will immediately become living

That cold sleep now oppresses.

He who, in compassion, covers

Scattered corpses with a mound of earth

Performs a kindly work,

Pious toward almighty Christ.

For the same law moves everyone

To utter a groan under a single lot:

To grieve over kindred funerals,

Though the death is another’s.

We follow your words, Redeemer,

[Col. 0979C] By which, triumphing over black death,

You command, in your footsteps,

The companion of the cross—the thief—to go.

Behold, a broad luminous way

Of paradise is now open to the faithful;

It is permitted for human beings also to enter

That grove which the serpent had taken away.

There, I pray, best Leader,

Command that the mind devoted to you

Be consecrated in its native dwelling,

Which it had left in exile and wandering.

For the souls—for this reason, not forgetful—

Of whom we ourselves are mindful,

We beg, God, that they be cleansed of filth

And made strangers [Col. 0979D] to the fires of Erebus.

Honor be to you, fountain of mercy;

Praise, glory, supreme power

To the Father, the Begotten, or the Lord,

King of the world, who is one God.

Amen.

**Supplication.** Let us pray; with every supplication let us beseech our Redeemer, our Lord Jesus Christ, that he may graciously deem it worthy to place the spirits and souls of his servants, all the faithful departed, among the ranks of the blessed. R. Grant this, eternal almighty God.

Kyrie eleison. R. Christe eleison, Kyrie eleison.

**Capitula.** God, with whom the spirits of the dead live, and in whom the souls of the elect, [CL] [Col. 0980A] once the burden of the flesh has been set aside, rejoice in complete happiness, grant us who beseech you that the souls of your servants, all the faithful departed, who while in the body were deprived of the use of the vision of this temporal light, may enjoy the consolation of that eternal light. May no torment of death touch them; may no pain of a dreadful vision afflict them; may no penal fear torture them; may no nearby chain of the guilty bind them. Rather, with forgiveness of their sins granted to them, may they deserve to attain the promised joys of their desired rest.

**Our Father:** And lead us not.

Deliver us from evil, and confirm us in your fear and in good works, O God our Trinity, who are blessed, live, and rule all things forever and ever. R. Amen.

[Col. 0980B] Humble yourselves for the blessing.

R. May the Lord be with you. R. And with you.

**Blessing.** May Christ the Lord, who by his death came to the aid of the dead, hear us as we pray for the faithful departed. R. Amen. May we through our prayers obtain both the salvation we desire for ourselves and rest for them. R. Amen. May the faith by which we believe together with them in the Lord both justify us from sins and free them from punishments. R. Amen.

Lauda. The souls of the departed P. Do not abandon in hell, Lord. Alleluia, alleluia. V. For you, Lord, are gracious and gentle, and rich in mercy toward all who call upon you. P. Do not abandon. V. Glory and honor. P. Do not abandon.

May the Lord be with you. R. And with your spirit.

[Col. 0980C] **Prayer.** We commend to you, Lord, the soul of your servant N., and the souls of your servants and handmaids N. N.; and we beseech you, Christ Jesus, Savior of the world, that you would not refuse to receive into the bosom of your patriarchs the soul for whose sake you mercifully descended to earth. Acknowledge, Lord, your creature, created not from foreign gods but by you alone, the living and true God; for there is no other God besides you, and there is none according to your works. Gladden, Lord, his soul in your presence, and do not remember his former iniquities and drunkenness, which anger or the heat of evil desire aroused. For although he sinned, nevertheless he did not deny the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, but believed; and he possessed [Col. 0980D] zeal for God within himself, and worshiped the God who made all things.

Through mercy. R. Amen.

May the Lord be with you. R. And with you.

In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, may all the souls of the faithful departed, through the mercy of God, rest forever in peace. R. Amen.

# IN THE RITE FOR THE DEAD

**Antiphon.** Eternal rest. Psalm 1. Entire, with Gloria.

**Antiphon.** May the Lord grant you eternal rest, and may perpetual light shine upon you forever.

**Responsory.** I will arise and go to my father, and I will say to him: P. Father, I have sinned against you; forgive me. V. While he was still far away, his father saw him and, [Col. 0981A] moved with compassion, fell upon his neck, and the son said to him: P. Father.

**Abecedarian chant (Abicidaria).** God, have mercy; God, have mercy: alas for me! Let “God, have mercy” be repeated. P. Wretched, unhappy me: I did not understand the evil I had done. Alas for me! V. To you, Lord, I raise my soul. Alas for me! Now, guilty, I reveal the secrets of my heart. Alas for me! P. Wretched, unhappy me. V. O life, altogether very bitter! Alas for me! In which I committed very many evils. Alas for me! P. Wretched, unhappy me. V. My eyes, pour forth waters! Alas for me! Perhaps God wipes away sins. Alas for me! P. Wretched, unhappy me.

**Antiphon.** Now understand, you kings. Psalm 2. Entire, with Gloria.

**Antiphon.** Now understand, you kings; be instructed, all you who judge the earth. Serve the Lord in fear.

[Col. 0981B] **Responsory.** I know, Lord, that nothing occurs on earth without cause. P. For a human being is born for labor, and a bird for flying. V. But I will entreat the Lord, and I will address my words to him. P. For a human being is born.

**Abecedarian chant (Abicidaria).** God, have mercy, God, have mercy on his sins. Let “God, have mercy” be repeated. V. Behold, now the dreadful day of death and the final hour of life has arrived, so that, placed with those fathers, he may now rest together with them. P. God, have mercy. V. You, my friends, sisters, and mothers, grieving over me, pour forth worthy prayers for me to the Lord in pious supplication. P. God, have mercy.

**Antiphon.** Establish your mercy upon us. Psalm 116. Entire, with Gloria.

**Antiphon.** Establish your mercy [Col. 0981C] upon us, O God.

[CLI] **Responsory.** As I sin daily and do not repent, Lord, fear of death troubles me; and because in hell there is no confession, P. Have mercy on me, God; have mercy on me. V. I have sinned, Lord, I have sinned, and I myself acknowledge my iniquities; I ask and beseech you: P. Have mercy on me, God.

**Abicidaria.** Have mercy, have mercy, have mercy on him, God. P. Merciful one, have mercy; grant him forgiveness. V. Lamb of God, who were sacrificed for us like a sheep, and who, as a human being, are treated with indignity, yet as true God are worshiped. P. Merciful one. V. Sweet Jesus, gracious Jesus, Son of the Virgin Mary, who for us ascended the cross: Father, spare this man. P. Merciful one. V. Wipe away the evils he committed; erase the guilt that he incurred; and grant him a place of everlasting light [Col. 0981D] and pleasantness. P. Merciful one.

**Supplication.** Let us pray; with every supplication let us beseech our gracious Lord Jesus Christ, who hears prayer, that he may graciously deem it worthy to place the spirit and soul of his servant in the place of light among the ranks of the blessed. R. Grant this, eternal almighty God.

Kyrie eleison. R. Christe eleison. Kyrie eleison.

**Prayer.** To you, Lord, we commend the soul of your servant, so that, dead to the world, he may live to you; and whatever sins he committed through the frailty of worldly conduct, wipe away through the forgiveness of your most merciful compassion. Through Christ our Lord. R. Amen.

May the Lord always be with you. R. And with you.

Let the priest say: In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, [Col. 0982A] may all the souls of the faithful departed, through the mercy of God, rest forever in peace. R. Amen.

**At Matins**

Lauda. A contrite and humbled heart, O God, you will not despise. Psalm 50. Entire, with Gloria.

**Prayer.** May the secrets of our hearts, which are daily soiled by carnal cares, be cleansed by the sprinkling of the hyssop of your word, almighty God; so that the crafty sower may depart from us, and Christ the Lord remain in us as perpetual comforter. R. Amen.

**Antiphon.** Remember, Lord, that we are earth: a human being—his days are like grass; like the flower of grass, so his spirit passed away from him.

**Psalm of David**

[Col. 0982B]

To you we lift our eyes,  
who dwell in heaven.

To you, Lord, I will cry; and I will entreat my God.  
What profit is there in my blood when I descend into corruption?

Will the dust give thanks to you,  
or proclaim your truth?

To you, Lord, I will cry; my God, do not be silent toward me,  
lest you become silent toward me and I become like those descending into the pit.

To you our fathers cried, and they were saved;  
in you they hoped, and they were not put to shame.

To you I cried; when my heart was troubled, you lifted me up upon a rock.  
And you led me, for you became [Col. 0982C] my hope, a tower of strength against the enemy.

To you I will pray, Lord, in the morning; you will hear my voice.  
In the morning I will stand before you and see, for you are not a God who wills iniquity.

To you, Lord, I have lifted up my soul; my God, in you I trust; let me not be put to shame, nor let my enemies mock me;  
for all who await you will not be put to shame.

To you I have fled.  
Teach me to do your will, for you are my God.

To you, Lord, I have lifted up my soul.  
Deliver me from my enemies.

May the Lord grant you eternal rest;  
and may perpetual light shine upon you forever.

**Prayer.** We ask your mercy, Lord, that you may drench [Col. 0982D] the souls of your servants, all the faithful departed, with the dew of your compassion; free them from the hands of terrible ministers; lead them out from the place of burning; command them to reach the regions of paradise, so that, placed in Abraham’s bosom, they may be raised with all your saints in the first resurrection. R. Amen.

**Antiphon.** Remember, Lord, that our life is a wind; our years have passed in swift course. Now have mercy on us, for we are dust.

**Psalm of David**

Have mercy on me and hear my prayer.  
Have mercy on me, Lord; see my humility because of my enemies.

Have mercy on me, Lord, for I am weak;  
[Col. 0983A] heal me, Lord, for my bones are troubled. And my soul is greatly troubled.

Have mercy on me, Lord, for I am alone and poor.  
The troubles of my heart have multiplied; deliver me from my necessities.

Have mercy on me; my foot has stood on the straight way.  
In the churches I will bless you, Lord.

Have mercy on me and hear me. To you my heart said,  
“My face has sought you”; your face, Lord, I will seek. Do not turn your face from me.

Have mercy on me, Lord, for I am afflicted; my eye, my soul, and my belly are troubled in anger;  
for my life has failed in sorrow, and my years in groaning.

Have mercy on me, God, according to your great [Col. 0983B] mercy;  
and according to the multitude of your compassions, blot out my iniquity.

Have mercy on me, God; have mercy on me, for my soul trusts in you.  
And in the shadow of your wings I will hope until iniquity passes away.

Have mercy on me; a human being has trampled me; all day long, attacking, he has afflicted me.  
My enemies have trampled me all day long, for many are fighting against me.

Have mercy on me, Lord, for I have cried to you all day long.  
Gladden the soul of your servant, for to you, Lord, I have lifted up my soul.

Have mercy on me, and give authority to your servant;  
save the son of your handmaid. Give me a sign for good.

Have mercy on us, Lord; have mercy on us,  
for we are [Col. 0983C] filled exceedingly with contempt.

Eternal rest, etc.

**Prayer.** God, who are the lover of human souls, deliver the souls of your servants, all the faithful departed, whom true faith held while they remained in their bodies, free from every torment of hell; so that, separated from the prisons of hell, they may deserve the aid of the fellowship of the saints. R. Amen.

**Antiphon.** Remember, Lord, your congregation, which you founded from the beginning.

**Psalm of David**

Deliver me, lest he seize my soul like a lion,  
while there is no one to redeem and no one to save.

Deliver me from bloodshed, God, God of my salvation,  
and [Col. 0983D] my tongue will exult in your justice.

Deliver me from those who hate me,  
and from the depths of the waters.

Deliver me, for I am needy and poor,  
and my heart is troubled within me.

Deliver me from those who pursue me,  
for they have been strengthened against me.

Deliver me from many waters and from the hand of foreign sons,  
whose mouth has spoken vanity and whose right hand is a right hand of iniquity.

Deliver me from those who work iniquity,  
and save me from men of blood.

Deliver my soul, Lord, from lying lips  
and from a deceitful tongue.

[Col. 0984A] Deliver my soul.  
Merciful and just is the Lord, and our God has mercy.

Deliver the afflicted of Israel, God,  
from all their tribulations.

You have delivered the rod of your inheritance:  
Mount Zion, in which you dwelt.

Eternal rest, etc.

**Prayer.** Grant, we beseech you, Lord, this mercy to your servants, that those who held the truth of your faith in their vows may not receive the recompense of their deeds in punishments; so that, just as true faith joined them here to the ranks of the faithful, so there your mercy may unite them to the angelic choirs. R. Amen.

**Abecedarian chant (Abicidaria).** Have mercy, have mercy, have mercy on him, God. P. Christ the Redeemer, grant him forgiveness. V. [Col. 0984B] Ruler and Redeemer of the world, Jesus Christ, maker of all things. P. Christ the Redeemer. V. You who hear those entreating and look upon those groaning. P. Christ the Redeemer. V. You who await penitents and those lamenting their sins. P. Christ. V. Hear the prayers of priests, who implore your ears. P. Christ the Redeemer. V. The grave is my dark and sorrowful house. P. Christ.

**Prayer.** Do not remember, Lord, the sins of his youth and his ignorance, we beseech you; but according to your great mercy, remember him in the glory of your brightness. May the heavens be opened to him; may the angels rejoice with him; receive your servant into your kingdom, Lord. May Saint Michael the Archangel of God receive him, who deserved the leadership of the heavenly host. May the holy angels come to meet him and lead him into the heavenly [Col. 0984C] city of Jerusalem. May Blessed Peter the Apostle receive him, to whom the keys of the heavenly kingdom were handed by God. May Saint Paul assist him, who was worthy to be the vessel of election. May Saint John, the chosen apostle of God, intercede for him, to whom the heavenly secrets were revealed. May all the holy apostles pray for him, to whom the Lord gave the power of binding and loosing. May all the saints of God intercede for him, who endured torments in this world for the name of Christ, so that, freed from the bonds of the flesh, he may deserve to reach the glory of the heavenly kingdom, through our Lord Jesus Christ, who with the Father…

**In the Second Nocturn**

**Antiphon.** Those sitting in darkness and the shadow of death, release those bound in chains, Lord.

**Psalm of David**

[Col. 0984D]

For you, Lord, are gracious and gentle,  
and greatly merciful to those who call upon you.

You, Lord God, are compassionate and merciful,  
patient, rich in mercy, and truthful.

You, Lord, have helped me  
and comforted me.

You, Lord, are my protector,  
my glory and the one who lifts up my head.

You, Lord, will preserve and guard us  
from this generation forever.

You, Lord, do not keep your help far from me;  
look to my defense.

You, Lord, have blessed the just.

You, Lord, do not put your mercies [Col. 0985A] far from me;  
your mercy and truth have always upheld me.

You, Lord, have delivered my soul so that it might not perish;  
you have cast all my sins behind your back.

You, Lord, will mock the wicked  
and bring all nations to nothing.

Eternal rest, etc.

**Prayer.** Most merciful God, receive into the bosom of Abraham the patriarch the souls of your servants, all the faithful departed, and join them with the saints and elect. Let the guilt of the flesh not be to them for punishment; but let your merciful compassion profit them for forgiveness. R. Amen.

**Antiphon.** Do not forget the souls of your poor, Lord, forever.

**Psalm of David**

[Col. 0985B] The heavens are yours, and the earth is yours,  
the sea and all that are in them.

You made all the boundaries of the earth; summer and spring—you fashioned them.  
You delivered my soul so that it might not perish; you cast all my sins behind your back.

You founded the world;  
you created the north and the sea.

You illumine my lamp, Lord;  
my God, illumine my darkness.

You knew all things, final and ancient;  
you formed me and placed your hand upon me.

You will save the humble people,  
and you will humble the eyes of the proud.

[Col. 0985C] You are terrible, and who can resist you?  
And from that time, your anger.

Eternal rest, etc.

**Prayer.** We ask your mercy, Lord, that the souls of your servants, all the faithful departed, having exchanged the lot of sorrowful dwellings, may enjoy the blessed fellowship of the just. R. Amen.

**Antiphon.** Spare us, Lord, for you love souls.

**Psalm of David**

To you we lift our eyes,  
who dwell in heaven.

Behold, as the eyes of servants  
are toward the hands of their masters,

as the eyes of a handmaid are toward the hands of her mistress,  
so are [Col. 0985D] our eyes toward the Lord our God, until he has mercy on us.

I cried to my Lord, and from his holy temple he heard my voice;  
and my cry entered his ears.

When I was afflicted, I cried to the Lord, and he heard me.  
Lord, deliver my soul from lying lips and from a deceitful tongue.

I was directed toward all your commandments;  
I hated every wicked way.

Eternal rest, etc.

**Prayer.** We beseech you, almighty God, that the souls of the departed who believe in you and hope in your goodness and mercy may be [Col. 0986A] absolved from all sins, so that they may not be held liable in eternal shame. V. Amen.

### Alphabetical Chant (Abicidaria)

Have mercy, have mercy, O God, have mercy: grant him pardon and blot out his sins.

**V.** We now knock at the ear of your compassion: grant rest to your servant.

**P.** Have mercy.

**V.** O Jesus, good, holy, eternal Redeemer, grant pardon to this man for whom we beseech you.

**P.** Have mercy.

**V.** Forgive him all his sins; do not call his deeds to mind on that day.

**P.** Have mercy.

**V.** Pray, priests, to God for me, that I may not now be found guilty before him.

**P.** Have mercy.

**V.** And together, all you Levites, utter a groan—you who minister before Christ’s altar.

**P.** Have mercy.

### [CLIV] Prayer

O God, for whom all things live, and for whom our bodies do not perish by dying but are changed for the better: we beseech you, suppliants, to cause the soul of your servant to be received and led by the hands of your holy angels into the bosom of your friend Abraham the patriarch, and to be raised on the last day of the great judgment. Whatever vices it contracted through the devil’s deception, do you, merciful and compassionate, wash away by granting forgiveness.

**R.** Amen.

## At the Third Nocturn

**Antiphon.** Do not abandon us, O Lord; do not hand our souls over to the power of our enemies.

**Psalm of David.**

O Lord, I have loved the beauty of your house, * and the place where your glory dwells.

O Lord, you will preserve us and guard us * from this generation forever.

O Lord, divide them from the few during their lifetime; * their belly has been filled from your hidden treasures.

O Lord, O Lord, strength of my salvation, * you have overshadowed my head on the day of battle.

O Lord, have you withdrawn far away? Do you despise us in times of trouble? When the wicked man is arrogant, the poor man is set on fire; they are caught in the schemes they devise.

O Lord God, I cried to you, * and you healed me.

O Lord, you brought my soul up from the underworld; * you saved me from those descending into the pit.

O Lord, in your will you gave strength to my beauty; * you turned your face from me, and I became troubled.

O Lord, when will you look upon me? * Restore my soul from their wickedness, my only soul from the lions.

O Lord, O Lord, King of gods and of the heavens, * do not destroy your people and your inheritance, which you delivered from the power of their enemies.

Eternal rest.

### Prayer

Receive, O Lord, the soul of your servant N., whom today you have deigned to call from the prison of this age; and free it from the places of punishment. May it enjoy the blessedness of rest and eternal light, and may it deserve to be raised among your saints and elect in the glory of the resurrection.

**R.** Amen.

**Antiphon.** Your dead shall rise, O God; those who are in the tombs shall rise, and they shall rejoice before you.

### [Col. 0987A] Psalm of David

Look upon me and have mercy on me, * for I am alone and poor.

Look upon me and have mercy on me; * give your dominion to your boy, and save the son of your maidservant.

Look upon my enemies, for they have multiplied, * and they hate me with unjust hatred.

Look upon your servants and your works; * direct their children.

Look upon your covenant, * for the dark places of the earth are filled with houses of iniquity.

Look upon me and hear me, O Lord my God. Enlighten my eyes, lest I ever sleep in death, * lest my enemy ever say, “I have prevailed against him.”

Eternal rest.

### [Col. 0987B] Prayer

Do not enter into judgment with your servant, O Lord, for no human being will be justified in your sight unless, through you, forgiveness of sins is granted to him. Therefore, we beseech you, let not your judicial sentence oppress him whom a true entreaty of Christian faith commends to you; but, with your grace coming to his aid, may he deserve to escape the judgment of vengeance—he who, while he lived, was marked with the seal of the holy Trinity.

**R.** Amen.

**Antiphon.** Your dead shall live, O God; my slain shall rise again.

**Psalm of David.**

The just man will rejoice when he sees vengeance; * he will wash his hands in the sinner’s blood.

The just man will rejoice in the Lord, and hope in him, and * all the upright in heart will be praised. I will rejoice and exult in you; I will sing praise to your name, O Most High.

We shall rejoice in your salvation; * and in the name of our God we shall magnify him.

Rejoice in the Lord and exult, you just; * and glory, all you upright in heart.

Rejoice, you just, in the Lord, and confess the memory of his sanctification.

Let all who hope in you rejoice; * they shall exult forever, and you shall dwell in them.

Let the heart of those who seek the Lord rejoice. * Seek the Lord, and be strengthened.

Rest.

### [Col. 0987D] Prayer

Most merciful Lord, hear the prayers of your servants, and cause the soul of your servant N. to be placed among the ranks of the victorious hosts. May he stand at the right hand of your Son, our Lord, destined to find mercy; and, numbered among the company of your saints, may he possess the heavenly kingdom without end.

**R.** Amen.

### Alphabetical Chant (Abicidaria)

Have mercy, have mercy, have mercy on him, O God; put an end to his evils—put an end to them, and comfort those who mourn.

**P.** Now, Lord, have mercy.

**V.** Hear me, all you brothers, or mothers of the dead; the order of brothers and sisters lamenting with devout voice:

**P.** Now, Lord, have mercy.

**V.** Deliver me from hell, you Son of God the Father; for your own sake, O Christ, put an end to my evils.

**P.** Now, Lord.

**V.** A good shade sheltered us when this tree stood here; inside and outside it adorned us, * and it governed us all.

**P.** Now, Lord.

### [Col. 0988A] Prayer

Lord Jesus Christ, who by dying conquered death and restored life to the dead, we beseech your power: may your servant, whose commemoration we make today, stripped of the contagion of the left-hand side, hold the right; so that, brought to the homeland without fear, without corruption, and without mortality—the homeland he desired for so long—he may be there where the whole assembly of the just remains in equality with the angels.

**R.** Amen.

## At Lauds

**For the Canticle. Antiphon.** Light has risen in the darkness for the upright in heart: the Lord is merciful, compassionate, and just.

### [Col. 0988B] Canticle from Matthew (Chapter XXII)

The Sadducees, who say that there is no resurrection, came to Jesus * and questioned him, saying:

“Teacher, Moses said, ‘If someone dies without having a son, * his brother shall marry his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.’

“Now there were seven brothers among us. The first, after marrying, died; * and, having no offspring, he left his wife to his brother.

“Likewise the second and the third, down to the seventh. * Last of all, the woman also died.

“In the resurrection, therefore, whose wife will she be of the seven? * For they all had her.”

But Jesus answered them: * “You are mistaken, because you do not know the Scriptures or the power of God.

“For in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, * but are like the angels of God in heaven.

“Concerning the resurrection of the dead, * have you not read what was spoken by the Lord, who said to us:

“‘I am the God of Abraham, * and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’?

“He is not the God of the dead, * but of the living.”

Eternal rest.

Repeat the Antiphon: “Light has risen.”

**For the Benedictus. Antiphon.** Hear, O Lord, my voice with which I cried to you; have mercy on him and hear me.

**Canticle.** “Blessed are you, O Lord.” Fol. 6.

Repeat the Antiphon: “Hear, O Lord.”

### [Col. 0988D] Sonus

Your dead shall live, O God.

**P.** My slain shall rise again.

**V.** And all who are upon the earth shall rejoice.

**P.** My slain.

### Lauda

Let every spirit praise the Lord. Alleluia. And let it praise him together. Alleluia, alleluia.

**Psalm 150.**

Repeat the Lauda: “Let every spirit.”

May the Lord be always with you.

**R.** And with you.

### Reading from the Book of the Prophet Isaiah (Chapter LVIII)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

Thus says the Lord: “Light shall rise for you in the darkness, and your darkness shall be like midday. The Lord will always give you rest, and will fill your souls with splendor, and will free your bones; and you shall be like a watered garden and like a spring of waters whose waters do not fail,” says the Almighty Lord.

**R.** Amen.

## Hymn

Christ, King, Creator of the world,

And glorious Redeemer,

Kindly receive

The vows of the supplicant people.

With humble voice we beseech you:

Come when summoned.

Once, powerfully conquering death

As its prince,

You entered savage Tartarus,

Destroying its dreadful barriers,

Loosening its iron bonds,

And freeing those shut within.

Confessing you in this triumph,

With humbled mind we ask:

Grant that you give rest from death,

And joy together with rest,

At the trophy of the Father’s right hand,

With all the blessed.

Let no flame consume them;

Let no chain bind them;

Let no one suffer the punishment

Of that dreadful worm;

But, blessed by your gift,

Let them rejoice without end.

May the Unity ever grant this,

And the supreme Trinity,

Whose name is everlasting,

Whose glory is eternal;

And may the triune and one God

Reign before all ages.

Amen.

### Supplication

Let us pray. Let us beseech our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer of the world, with every supplication: may he graciously deign to place the spirits and souls of his servants, all the faithful departed, among the ranks of the blessed.

**R.** Grant this, eternal almighty God.

Kyrie eleison.

**R.** Christ, have mercy. Lord, have mercy.

### Capitula

We beseech your holy clemency, almighty Father God, for the souls of your servants, all the faithful departed, whom you wished to withdraw from the brokenness of this life and the pollution of the earthly body; associate them with the heavenly assembly, and raise them from the dwellings of hell to bind them to heavenly habitations. Thus may their flesh, which now lies lifeless, awaken in glory. Let them not be subject to punishments, but joined to the spirit of grace. In your loving kindness forgive all their deeds, words, and thoughts, so that through the grace of your Only-Begotten they may receive a share in glory and may be able to obtain the fullness of the resurrection in the future with all the saints.

Our Father. Deliver us from evil. Fol. 10.

**Blessing.** Christ the Lord, who by death…

**Lauda.** The souls of the dead.

**Prayer.** We commend to you, O Lord.

And all the rest as above. Fol. 149.
