## Hymn

Let us praise with mouth and heart

The distinguished Martyr of Christ,

Whom the radiant glory of death

Made a dweller in heaven.

For this witness of faith,

Proclaiming Christ the Author,

Fearlessly rejected

Sacrifice to the sacred rites of the nations.

Neither the punishment of prison,

Nor the savage severity of the sword,

Nor iron nor fires

Distressed him as he contended in faith.

His body, returned to the tomb

By the purifying wound of death,

His spirit flashing into heaven

Flies after Christ.

God encircles him with a crown;

He shines with radiant light.

The joyful victor he joins

To the angelic choirs.

This death is precious

With the saints; and blessed is the people

By whom heaven is opened to the just,

By whom the kingdom of light is bestowed.

To God the Father be glory,

And to his only Son,

With the Spirit, the Paraclete,

Forever and ever.

Amen.

### Supplication

Let us pray. Let us beseech our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer of the world, with every supplication: may he graciously deign, through his grace, through the intercession of holy Mary the Virgin and his Mother, and through the intercession of his holy Martyr N., to grant us forgiveness of sins and peace.

Kyrie eleison.

### Capitula

Honoring with due reverence the birthday of your most blessed Martyr N., O Lord, we seek the help of your right hand. Though weighed down by the burden of our sins, we do not fear to ask for divine power; yet we cannot grasp how greatly our frailty is struck by the obstacle of vices. By turning away from you and walking through so many precipitous paths of crimes, we incurred the sin of blindness and, by despising you, who are the true light of justice, lost you. Therefore, we beseech you, unchangeable Trinity, God, hear the prayers of your household and receive them favorably. In this evening hour, graciously release the sins of all; and, with every stain of wrongdoing cleansed away, deign to grant all the promised rewards of the heavenly homeland.

Our Father. Delivered from evil. Fol. 2.

May he now make our minds cling to what is good, and in the future join us to the joys of his own.

### Reading from the Book of the Wisdom of Solomon (Chapter 18)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

Death’s trial touched the just man, and a disturbance of the multitude occurred in the wilderness; but your anger did not last long. For a blameless man hastened to contend, bearing the shield of his ministry, prayer, and offering supplication with incense. He resisted your anger and put an end to the necessity, showing that he was your servant.

He overcame the crowds, not by bodily strength or the armor of power, but by the word of God he cast down the destroyer, recalling the oaths made to the ancestors. For when the dead had already fallen in heaps upon one another, he stood between them, cut off the advance, and divided the path that led to the living.

For the whole world was depicted on the robe reaching to his feet which he wore, and the glorious deeds of the ancestors were carved in four rows of stones, while your magnificence was inscribed upon the diadem of his head.

**R.** Amen.

## Hymn

Let us, companions, sing the illustrious joys

Of the merits of the saints and their valiant deeds;

For the spirit eagerly desires to proclaim in song

The noblest race of victors.

These are those at whom the world, while holding them, shuddered;

For they utterly despised the world itself,

With its barren flowering amid the dry waste,

And followed you.

Good King Christ from heaven.

These men for your sake trampled underfoot the furies and savagery  
of men, and the cruel scourges;  
the rending claw yielded bravely to them  
and did not penetrate their innermost parts.

They are cut down by swords like two-year-old sheep;  
no murmur resounds, no complaint;  
but, with a silent heart and conscience clear,  
the mind preserves patience.

What voice, what tongue could recount  
what gifts you prepare for the Martyrs?  
For, enriched by flowing red blood,  
they are richly endowed with bright-shining laurels.

We ask you, supreme Divinity, and you alone,  
to wash away our faults and remove what is harmful;  
give peace to your servants, and to us glory  
through all ages, to you.

Amen.

**Supplication.** Let us pray. With every supplication, let us beseech our Redeemer, the Lord Jesus Christ, that through his grace, through the intercession of holy Mary, his Virgin Mother, and through the intercession of his holy Martyrs, N. N., he may graciously deign to grant us forgiveness of sins and peace.

**R.** Grant this, eternal almighty God.

**Kyrie, eleison.** **R.** Christ, have mercy; Lord, have mercy.

**Capitula.** Christ, who are the unfailing light of God the Father, at this setting close of the day and at the beginning of the day that is coming, in commemoration of your holy Martyrs, N. N., we pour out before you our votive prayers, faithfully beseeching you: that, with these same saints interceding, you may mercifully and graciously deign to accept the concordant and peaceful prayers of your servants, offered with hymns and songs at the voice of the evening sacrifice.

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. Fol. 2.

**Benediction.** Through the merits of his saints, N. N., may the divine mercy bestow blessing upon us.

**R.** Amen.

May he graciously hear our prayers.

**R.** Amen.

May his anger meet us with forgiveness, and may he transform our death into life.

**R.** Amen.

**Lauda.** Everlasting joy is upon the head of the saints; **P.** praise and gladness shall seize them. Alleluia, alleluia.

**V.** Blessed are those who keep judgment and practice justice at all times. **P.** Praise and gladness shall seize them.

**V.** Glory and honor. **P.** Praise and gladness shall seize them.

**Prayer.** Remember us, Lord; and just as you grant worthy rewards to your most blessed saints, N. N., so spare and have mercy on our sins, that, released from what is past, we may deserve protection in what is to come.

Through.

In the name of the Lord.

## MATINS OF SAINTS FOLLOW, WHETHER FOR PRINCIPAL OR SOLEMN FEASTS OF MANY MARTYRS

**Antiphon.** Give us the joy of your salvation; with a princely spirit strengthen us, Lord. Psalm 50.

**Prayer.** Restore to us, Lord, the joy of your salvation, which we lost by acting wickedly and neglected through indifference. Call us back to it and restore it to us, so that, once sin has been driven out, justice may take its place; and, once sorrow has been banished, joy may be present. Grant us, we ask, this gladness, that we may deserve to attain eternal salvation.

**R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**Antiphon.** Let the just feast and exult in the presence of the Lord; **P.** and let them delight in gladness.

**V.** But the salvation of the just is from the Lord God, in the time of opportunity and in the time of tribulation. **P.** And let them delight in gladness.

**V.** Glory and honor. **P.** And let them delight.

**Prayer.** Remember us, Lord. As above here.

**Antiphon.** Those who were persecuting the just you plunged into the depths, Lord; **P.** and you were their guide in a pillar of cloud.

**V.** For you, Lord, are gracious and gentle, and rich in mercy toward all who call upon you. **P.** And you were their guide in a pillar.

**V.** Glory and honor. **P.** And you were their guide in a pillar of cloud.

**Prayer.** Our joy and our salvation, our strength and our righteousness, almighty Lord God, make us, we ask, rejoice with you in the peaceful lot of the saints; and there, as rulers, let us perpetually sing your praises.

**R.** Amen.

**Antiphon.** Salvation is near those who fear God, and upon his saints, **P.** and upon those who turn to him.

**V.** The Lord is faithful in all his words and holy in all his works. **P.** And upon those who turn to him.

**V.** Glory and honor. **P.** And upon those who turn to him.

**Prayer.** Strengthened by the protection of the most blessed Martyrs, N. N., let our faithful prayer proceed to our Lord, so that, although we celebrate their glorious triumph in this world, we may be helped forever by their prayers.

**R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**R.** The saints who endured the contest for the faith: the enemy shall have no power over them, because they cried out with one voice, saying:

**P.** Holy God, holy and mighty, exalted, holy and immortal, have mercy on us.

**V.** I saw in heaven a great multitude that no one could count, and they cried out with a loud voice, saying:

**V.** Holy God, holy and mighty.

**V.** Glory and honor. Repeat the Responsory, “The saints.”

## At Lauds

**For the Canticle. Antiphon.** Those who love you, Lord, shine like the sun at its rising; thus they gleam.

### Canticle of Judges (chapter 5)

You who freely offered your lives from Israel to danger,  
* bless the Lord.

Hear, kings; give ear, princes:  
* I am, I am she who will sing to the Lord, and I will sing praise to the Lord God of Israel.

Lord, when you went out from Seir  
* and passed through the regions of Edom,

the earth was shaken, and the heavens and the clouds dripped water.

The mountains flowed before the Lord,  
* and Sinai before the Lord God of Israel.

In the days of Shamgar son of Anath, in the days of Jael, the paths were at rest;  
* those who entered them walked along trackless ways.

The strong ceased in Israel and rested,  
* until Deborah arose, until a mother arose in Israel.

The Lord chose new battles,  
* and he himself overthrew the gates of the enemy.

Shield and spear, if they appeared, among forty thousand in Israel.  
* My heart loves the leaders of Israel,

you who offered yourselves willingly to danger;  
* bless the Lord.

You who ride upon shining asses and sit in judgment, and walk along the road,  
* speak! Where the chariots of the enemy were smashed and the army was suffocated,

there let the righteous deeds of the Lord  
* and his mercy toward the strong in Israel be recounted.

Then the people of the Lord went down to the gates  
* and seized command.

Rise, rise, Deborah; rise, rise, speak a song;  
* rise, Barak, and seize your captives, son of Abinoam.

The remnants of the people were saved;  
* the Lord fought among the strong.

From Ephraim I shall destroy them in Amalek,  
* and after him Benjamin.

Among your peoples, O Amalek: from Machir leaders descended,  
* and from Zebulun those who would lead the army to battle.

The commanders of Issachar were with Deborah, and Barak followed in their footsteps,  
* he who cast himself into danger as into a precipice and abyss.

Ruben, divided against himself,  
* was found to have a dispute among the great-hearted.

Why do you dwell between two boundaries,  
* to hear the whistling of flocks?

Gad beyond the Jordan rested,  
* and Dan was occupied with ships.

Asher shall dwell on the shore of the sea  
* and remain in its harbors.

But Zebulun and Naphtali offered their lives to death  
* in the region of Canaan.

Kings came and fought; the kings of Canaan fought at Taanach beside the waters of Megiddo,  
* yet they took no spoil.

From heaven battle was waged against them: the stars, remaining in their order and course,  
* fought against Sisera.

The torrent Kishon dragged away their corpses,  
* the ancient torrent, the torrent Kishon.

Tread down the life of the mighty:  
* the hooves of the horses fell, rushing upon the fugitives, while the strongest of the enemy roared headlong.

Curse the land of Meroz, says the angel of the Lord;  
* curse its inhabitants, because they did not come to the help of the Lord, to the aid of his strongest ones.

Blessed among women is Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite;  
* blessed be she in her tent.

To him who asked for water she gave milk,  
* and in a bowl fit for princes she offered butter.

She put her left hand to the peg and her right to the workmen’s hammers;  
* she struck Sisera, seeking the place of the wound in his head, and forcefully pierced his temple.

Between her feet he collapsed; he weakened and died;  
* before her feet he rolled and lay lifeless and miserable.

Looking out through the window, his mother wailed;  
* from the upper room she spoke, saying:

Why are his chariots delayed in returning?  
* Why have the feet of his chariots been slow?

One of his wives, wiser than the others,  
* answered these words to her mother-in-law:

Perhaps he is now dividing the spoils,  
* and the most beautiful of women is being chosen for him.

Garments of various colors will also be handed over as spoil to Sisera,  
* and varied furnishings are gathered to adorn the necks.

Thus may all your enemies perish, Lord;  
* but may those who love you shine like the sun at its rising.

Glory and honor to the Father.

**P.** Those who love you, Lord, shine like the sun at its rising; thus they gleam.

**For the Benedictus. Antiphon.** Saints and humble of heart, spirits and souls of the just, bless the Lord.

**Canticle.** Blessed are you, Lord. Fol. 6.

Repeat the antiphon, “Saints.”

**Sonus.** The salvation of the just is from the Lord, and he will save them. Alleluia, alleluia.

**V.** Because they hoped in the living God. **P.** And he will save them. Alleluia, alleluia.

**Lauda.** Praise the Lord from the heavens. Alleluia. Praise him in the heights. Alleluia. Psalm 148.

### Reading from the Book of the Wisdom of Solomon (chapter 5)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

The just shall live forever, and their reward is with the Lord, and their thought is with the Most High. Therefore they received the kingdom of beauty and the crown of splendor from the hand of the Lord, because with his right hand he will cover them and with his arm he will defend them. Then the just will stand with great firmness against those who afflicted them and took away their labors. Seeing this, they will be shaken by terrible fear and amazed at the suddenness of an unexpected salvation, saying among themselves in repentance and groaning from anguish of spirit:

“These are the ones whom we once held in derision and made an object of reproach. We fools considered their life madness and their end without honor. How have they been counted among the children of God, and how has their lot been found among the saints?”

**R.** Amen.

[CLXV] **Hymn.**

Let us sing with pure hearts  
the praises of the holy Martyrs,  
whom sacred suffering made  
conformed to Christ’s glory.

As soldiers of heaven, secure  
in the rewards to come,  
neither the vanity of the world moved them  
nor impious terror broke them.

Neither dark prisons,  
nor the iron burden upon the neck,  
nor handcuffs or fetters  
changed the joys of their minds.

Once refreshed by a draught  
from the eternal fountain,  
the Spirit cooled  
their thirst for the present age.

Though bread was denied,  
holiness felt no hunger;  
nourished by the accustomed word,  
they drank deeply in faith.

With the tested strength of their hearts,  
while enduring so many troubles,  
the public contest received  
the Martyrs seeking life.

Thus the saints, whom prison,  
hunger, and chains did not break,  
joyfully undergoing punishments,  
conquered the prince of the world.

The Martyrs followed Christ,  
their Lord and Maker;  
after fires, crosses, and swords,  
they flourish in eternal rewards.

Glory be to God the Father  
and to his only Son,  
with the Spirit, the Paraclete,  
through everlasting ages.

Amen.

**Supplication.** Let us pray. Fol. CLXII.

**Capitula.** God, wonderful in the protection of all your saints, who consecrated this day to your principal Martyrs, N. N.: we ask your power; grant your Catholic Church to rejoice in such great leaders, that we may deserve to follow with devout devotion the teaching of those who fed with your bread the flocks dear to you; and, aided by the prayers of those who pleased you through your own gift, may we deserve to be delivered from present distresses.

**Our Father.** Delivered. Fol. 2.

**Lauda.** He looked upon them when they were afflicted. Alleluia. **P.** When he heard their prayers. Alleluia, alleluia.

**V.** The just cried to the Lord when they were afflicted, and he delivered them from their necessities. **P.** When he heard them.

**V.** Glory. **P.** When he heard them.

**Benediction.** Through the merits of the saints. Fol. CLXII.

In the name of the Lord.

Let a commemoration be made. **Lauda.** To proclaim. **Prayer.** Remain, Lord. Fol. CLIX.

N., and having passed this day prosperously through your mercy, we may also pass this night peacefully before you, in purity of soul and body.

## At Lauds

**For the Canticle. Antiphon.** All the saints are in the hand of God, and those who draw near to his feet shall receive his teaching.

### Canticle of Deuteronomy (chapter 33)

The Lord came from Sinai  
* and rose for us from Seir.

He appeared from Mount Paran,  
* and with him were thousands of saints.

In his right hand was a fiery law.  
* He loved the peoples.

All the saints are in his hand,  
* and those who draw near to his feet shall receive his teaching.

Moses gave us the law  
* as the inheritance of the multitude of Jacob.

He shall be king among the upright,  
* when the princes of the people are gathered with the tribes of Israel.

Let Ruben live and not die,  
* and let him be small in number.

Hear, Lord, the voice of Judah  
* and bring him to his people.

His hands fought for him,  
* and his helper will be against his adversaries.

Your perfection and your teaching  
* belong to Levi, your holy man,

whom you tested in temptation  
* and judged at the waters of contradiction.

He said to his father and mother, “I do not know you”;  
* and to his brothers, “I do not recognize them”; and they did not know their own sons.

They kept your word and observed your commandment:  
* your judgments, O Jacob, and your law, O Israel.

They shall place incense in your anger  
* and a burnt offering upon your altar.

Bless, Lord, his strength,  
* and accept the works of his hands.

Strike the backs of his enemies,  
* and let those who hate him not rise again.

Benjamin, most beloved of the Lord, shall dwell securely in him;  
* like one in a bridal chamber he shall remain all day, and he shall rest between his shoulders.

May the Lord bless the land of Joseph  
* with the fruits of heaven, dew, and the abyss beneath; with the fruits produced by the sun and moon;

with the summit of the ancient mountains, with the fruits of the everlasting hills,  
* and with the fruits of the earth and its fullness.

May the blessing of him who appeared in the bush come upon Joseph’s head,  
* and upon the crown of the Nazirite among his brothers.

His beauty is like that of a firstborn bull; his horns are the horns of a rhinoceros.  
* With them he shall drive the nations to the ends of the earth.

These are the multitudes of Ephraim  
* and these the thousands of Manasseh.

Rejoice, Zebulun, in your departure,  
* and Issachar in your tents.

They shall call the peoples to the mountain;  
* there they shall sacrifice sacrifices of righteousness.

They shall suck the abundance of the sea like milk  
* and the hidden treasures of the sands.

Blessed is he who enlarges Gad;  
* like a lion he rested and seized the arm and crown of the head.

And he saw his principality, that it had been placed among the teachers.

He was with the princes of the people,  
* and he performed the righteousness of the Lord and his judgment with Israel.

Dan is a lion’s cub;  
* he shall flow abundantly from Bashan.

Naphtali shall enjoy abundance  
* and shall be full of the Lord’s blessing; he shall possess the sea and the south.

Blessed among sons is Asher;  
* let him be pleasing among his brothers.

Let him dip his foot in oil;  
* iron and bronze shall be his footwear.

As the days of your youth,  
* so shall be your old age.

There is none like the most powerful God,  
* who rides through the heavens to help you.

His magnificence traverses the clouds; his dwelling is above,  
* and beneath are everlasting arms. He shall drive out the enemy from before you and say: “Destroy!”

Israel shall dwell securely and alone;  
* Jacob’s eyes shall be upon a land of grain and wine, and the heavens shall drip with dew.

Blessed are you, Israel;  
* who is like you, a people saved by the Lord?

He is the shield of your help  
* and the sword of your glory.

Your enemies shall deny you,  
* and you shall trample their necks.

**P.** And those who draw near to his feet shall receive his teaching. Glory and honor.

**P.** And those who draw near.

**Prayer.** Hearing that you, Lord, came with thousands of saints and will come according to the prophecies of the prophets, we ask that we who already believe you came for the redemption of the world may also await with purified hearts your coming for judgment. Since the multitude of the saints rests in your hand, may the return of sinners be increased by your merciful remedy, so that, drawing near to your feet, we may always be filled with the inner teaching of vision.

**R.** Amen.

Through.

**For the Benedictus. Antiphon.** Saints and humble of heart, spirits and souls of the just, bless the Lord.

### Reading from the Book of the Wisdom of Solomon (chapter 3)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

The souls of the just are in the hand of God, and no torment of death shall touch them. In the eyes of the foolish they seemed to die, and their departure was considered an evil; they went away from the just path into destruction, and what was a way of destruction to us, they are in peace. And though in the sight of men they suffered torments, their hope is full of immortality. After being chastised a little, they shall be greatly rewarded, because God tested them and found them worthy of himself. As gold in a furnace he tested them, and as a burnt offering he accepted them, and in due time there will be a visitation of them. The just shall shine, and like sparks they shall run through stubble. They shall judge nations and rule over peoples, and their Lord shall reign forever.

**R.** Amen.

Glorious King of the Martyrs,  
crown of those who confess,  
you who lead to heavenly things  
those who reject earthly things,

quickly incline  
a kindly ear to our voices.

forgive us what we do wrong.

You conquer in the Martyrs  
by sparing those who confess.  
Conquer our crimes  
by granting forgiveness.

Glory be to God the Father  
and to his only Son,  
with the Spirit, the Paraclete,  
through everlasting ages.

Amen.

# THE HISTORY OF ONE PRINCIPAL CONFESSOR AND BISHOP BEGINS

## At Vespers

**Lauda.** You have clothed yourself with confession and beauty. **P.** You are robed in light as in a garment.

**V.** Confession and hope are before him; holiness and magnificence are in his sanctuary. **P.** You are robed in light.

**Dominus sit.** **R.** And with your spirit.

**Sonus.** I will confess to you, Lord, with all my heart; I will recount your wonders. Alleluia.

**V.** I will rejoice and exult in you, Lord; I will sing praise to your name, O Most High. Alleluia.

**Dominus sit.** **R.** And with your spirit.

**Antiphon.** I will confess to you, Lord, with all my heart; **P.** in the council of the just and in the assembly.

**V.** I will worship toward your holy temple and confess your name. **P.** In the council.

**V.** Glory and honor. **P.** In the council.

**Dominus sit.** **R.** And with your spirit.

**Lauda.** I will confess to you, Lord the King. Alleluia. **P.** And I will praise God my Savior. Alleluia, alleluia.

**V.** In the sight of the angels I will sing praise to you; I will worship toward your holy temple and confess your name. **P.** And I will praise.

**V.** Glory and honor. **P.** And I will praise.

**Hymn.**

Supreme Confessor, holy and priest,  
the wheel of the year turns through  
the boundaries of the seasons;  
the time has come for us  
to consecrate a feast to you.

Distinguished bishop, illustrious in merits,  
the sacred throng of clergy and people,  
prostrate in heart and filled with devotion,  
calls you its gentle father.

You review the vows of all  
in the hall of the eternal King;  
foster both orders,  
whose devoted shepherd  
you were in the city.

All the mourners recount  
their laments to you;  
through deeds of guilt and tears  
they reveal the dreadful crimes  
of a wicked mind and darkened soul.

A deserved punishment recalls them  
to our lips, when dreadful heavenly wrath,  
changed by their deeds, drives the wretched  
to pay the penalty in this world.

Keep the thunderbolt’s disasters far away;  
drive out sins and lessen your fury.  
We ask that plague and sickness  
depart, while the citizen is safe.

Govern life by cultivated morals;  
grant a clear and peaceful mind.  
May hearts meditate upon  
the nourishing gifts of Christ.

Holy one, whenever you are asked,  
provide abundant fruits  
and plentiful rains.  
We believe that, with the Lord’s favor,  
you are able to give all things.

We believe that Christ gave  
the price of labors and a just reward  
for efforts; through these  
you rejoice even after your limbs  
have been released by death.

Let us sing glory to Christ  
with open voice, generous to one who serves him,  
who in such great divinity, simple,  
is Three and One.

Amen.

**Supplication.** Let us pray. With every supplication, let us beseech our Redeemer, the Lord Jesus Christ, that through his grace, through the intercession of holy Mary, his Virgin Mother, and of holy N., bishop and confessor, he may graciously deign to grant us salvation of soul and body, forgiveness of sins, and peace.

**R.** Grant this, eternal almighty God.

**Kyrie, eleison.** **R.** Christ, have mercy. Lord, have mercy.

**Capitula.** You, consort of the Father’s Divinity and joined to the Only-Begotten, Holy Spirit, we ask you to place your mercy upon these evening sacrifices, so that the people who honor your Confessor may dutifully feel you as the giver of benefits, and each person may rejoice that his vows have been obtained, while he celebrates, at the returning festivals, the nativity of his Confessor and Bishop, N.

**Our Father.** Delivered. Fol. 2.

**Benediction.** Through the intervention of his most blessed Bishop and Confessor, N., may the Lord’s most abundant blessing come upon you.

**R.** Amen.

May he incline his ear to your prayers and graciously hear the prayer of your petitions.

**R.** Amen.

With him interceding, may we go before along the way of salvation in this life, so that we may all reach the summit of the heavenly kingdom unharmed.

**R.** Amen.

Through.

**Lauda.** Your bones shall germinate like willows. Alleluia.

**P.** Beside flowing waters. Alleluia, alleluia.

**V.** And he shall be like a tree that has been transplanted. **P.** Like willows.

**V.** Glory and honor. **P.** Beside.

**Prayer.** Lord God, who granted your most blessed Confessor and Bishop, N., that his flesh might rest and that, for confessing your name, he might obtain the crown of righteousness: grant us wretched ones, who do not possess the merit of confession, that through his prayers and merits we may escape the punishment deserved for our crimes. And just as his flesh was not abandoned in the underworld, but, freed from the corruption of sins, will afterward be joined to the spirit with the saints in glory, so command us sinners, Redeemer of crimes, to come to you.

**R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

In the name. Let a commemoration be made.

**Antiphon.** In the evening, morning, and midday we praise you, Lord.

**Prayer.** Almighty Lord God, who commanded that evening, morning, and midday be called one day, and ordained that the sun should recognize its setting: open, we ask, the darkness of our hearts, so that, as you shine upon us, we may know you as the true God and eternal light.

**R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

In the name of the Lord.

Matins of one principal confessor and bishop follows.

**Antiphon.** Lord, open my lips, and my mouth shall proclaim your praise. Psalm 50.

Repeat: “Lord, open my lips.”

**Prayer.** May our tongue praise you, Lord, by proclaiming your righteousness, and may our lips exult in the proclamation of truth, so that they may not be dissolved in the empty talk of falsehood. May we who rejoice in you, confessing you and having our sins forgiven, become heirs of the blessed life, singing praise in the assembly of the just and in the sacred host.

**R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**Antiphon 1.** My flesh shall rest in hope.

**P.** For you will not abandon my soul in the underworld, nor will you allow your holy one to see corruption.

**V.** You have made known to me the paths of life, and you will fill me with joy in your presence; delights are at your right hand forever.

**P.** For you will not abandon my soul.

**V.** Glory and honor.

**P.** Nor will you allow your holy one to see corruption.

**Prayer.** Lord God, who granted your most blessed Confessor and Pontiff N. that his flesh might rest and that he might obtain the crown of righteousness in confession of your name: grant us wretched sinners, who do not possess the merit of confession, that through his prayers and merits we may escape the punishment deserved for our crimes; and just as his flesh was not abandoned in hell, but, freed from the corruption of sins, will thereafter be joined to the spirit in glory with the Saints, so command that we sinners may come to you, Redeemer of sins. **R\. Amen.**

**Through [your mercy].**

**Antiphon 2.** You have kept my body from every pollution. **P.** Your fragrance, O Lord, has awakened in me eternal desires. **V\.** For you illumine my lamp, O Lord; and I said: “Illumine my darkness.” **P.** Your fragrance, O Lord. **V\.** Glory and honor. **P.** Your fragrance.

**Prayer.** Christ Jesus, Son of God, who kept the body of your most blessed Confessor and Pontiff N. from every pollution, and in whom the fragrance of your gift awakened eternal desires: awaken in us such love of your charity that we may overcome carnal pleasures; and let us live in such a way that we do not come into future punishments; so that we, who deserve the punishment we have earned, may through the holy intercessions attain the kingdom of blessedness. **R\. Amen.**

**Through [your mercy].**

**Antiphon 3.** Your face will be illumined like pure water. **P.** Your countenance, however, will rise like the morning star from the southern region; it will cause life to spring forth for you. **V\.** May he not allow your foot to be shaken, nor may he sleep who guards you. **P.** Your countenance. **V\.** Glory. **P.** Your countenance.

**Prayer.** Eternal almighty God, who made your holy Pontiff and Confessor N., whose present feast we now celebrate with joy, resist the world’s deceits so bravely for your name that he preferred nothing in this present age to your great love: grant also to us, your sinful servants, through his prayers, that, hindered by no adversity of the enemy, we may hasten undefeated toward you, the Lord. **R\. Amen.**

Through your mercy, etc.

**[CLXXI] Responsory.** Behold, O Lord, your Confessor N. confesses and believes in you alone with his whole heart; while, confessing, he proclaims the love of your faith conceived within him, and announces your wonders with his whole heart, so that we who believe may have life in him. **P.** In him he merited to find his reward through confession. **V\.** Therefore rejoice, and make us rejoice in you continually and openly, so that after our trials we may have rest in you. **P.** In him he merited. **V\.** Glory and honor. Repeat the Responsory “Behold.”

**Prayer.** O Lord of hosts, wondrous in your Saints, hear your suppliants and grant us sinners the patronage of your most blessed Confessor and Pontiff N., and bestow an abundance of perpetual charity. He merited the crown of virtue; may we, through his intercessions and by your gift, merit to obtain forgiveness of our crimes and the peace of perpetual charity. **R\. Amen.**

Through mercy.

## At Lauds

**For the Canticle. Antiphon.** I will confess to you, O Lord, because you have delivered me from those roaring and prepared for the slaughter, and from the hand of those seeking my life.

**Canticle of Ecclesiasticus (chapter LI).**

I will confess to you, Lord and King,  
*and praise you, God my Savior.*

I will confess your great name,  
*because you became my helper and protector,*

And you delivered my soul from destruction,  
*from the snare of an unjust tongue, and from the lips of those who work deceit,*

And against those who stood by, you became my helper.  
*And you delivered me according to the abundance of the mercy of your name*

From those roaring and prepared for the slaughter,  
*and from the hand of those seeking my life, and from the gates of tribulation that surrounded me;*

From the pressure of the flame that surrounded me,  
*and in the midst of the fire I did not grow hot;*

From the depth of the belly of hell, and from an unjust tongue and a word of falsehood,  
*from an unjust king and an unjust tongue;*

My soul will praise the Lord until death,  
*and my life, as it drew near to hell, was approaching the lower regions.*

They surrounded me on every side, and there was no one to help.  
*I looked toward my help, and there was none.*

**[CLXXII]** I remembered your mercy, O Lord,  
*and your work, which has existed from the beginning;*

For you rescue those who endure for your sake,  
*and free them from the hands of the nations.*

You exalted my dwelling on earth,  
*and for the dead man, mourning, I prayed.*

I called upon the Lord, the Father of my Lord, that he might not abandon me in the day of tribulation,  
*and in the time of the proud, when there was no help.*

I will praise your name continually,  
*and praise it in confession;*

My prayer was heard.  
*You delivered my soul*

From destruction,  
*and rescued me from the time of iniquity.*

Therefore I will confess and give you praise,  
*and bless the name of the Lord.*

While I was still young, before I went astray,  
*I openly sought wisdom in my prayer.*

Before the appointed time I asked for it,  
*and to the very end I will seek it. And I flowed out like an early grape cluster.*

My heart rejoiced in it.  
*My foot walked on a straight path.*

From my youth I sought it.  
*I inclined my ear a little, and received it.*

I found much wisdom for myself,  
*and made great progress in it.*

To him who gives me wisdom, I will give glory.  
*For I resolved to practice it; I was zealous not to be put to shame.*

My soul struggled with it,  
*and in practicing it I was strengthened.*

**[Col. 1015A]** I stretched out my hands on high,  
*and I mourned over its ignorance.*

I directed my way toward it,  
*and found it in greatness.*

From the beginning I possessed a heart along with it;  
*therefore I shall not be abandoned.*

My belly was troubled in seeking it;  
*therefore I shall possess a good possession.*

For the Lord gave me a tongue as my reward,  
*and with it I will praise him.*

Draw near to me, you who are unlearned,  
*and gather yourselves into the house of discipline.*

Why do you still delay, and what do you say?  
*Your souls thirst exceedingly.*

I opened my mouth and spoke: acquire it for yourselves  
*without silver,*

And submit your necks to its yoke, and let your souls receive discipline;  
*for it is near at hand to find it.*

See with your eyes that I have labored little,  
*and have found much rest.*

Acquire discipline at great cost in silver,  
*and possess abundant gold through it.*

Let your soul rejoice in its mercy,  
*and you will not be put to shame in its praise.*

Perform your work before the appointed time,  
*and it will give you your reward in its time.*

**Antiphon.** I will confess to you, O Lord, because you have delivered me, as above.

**For the Benedictus. Antiphon.** The Lord’s blessing hastens as the reward of the righteous.

**Canticle.** Blessed are you, O Lord. fol. 6.

**Sonus.** In the presence of the Angels I will sing to you, O Lord, Alleluia. **V\.** I will worship toward your holy temple and confess to you, O Lord. Alleluia.

**May the Lord be with you. R\.** And with you.

**Lauda.** Alleluia. His confession is above heaven and earth, Alleluia. He has exalted the horn of his people. Alleluia. A hymn belongs to all his Saints. Alleluia, alleluia. Psalm 148. Repeat the Antiphon. Alleluia. His confession is above heaven and earth. **V\.** Glory and honor. **P.** He has exalted the horn of his people. Alleluia. As above.

**Reading from the Book of the Prophet Isaiah (chapter XLII).**

**[Col. 1015D] R\.** Thanks be to God.

Thus says the Lord: “Behold my servant; I will receive him. My chosen one, in whom my soul is well pleased. I have given my spirit; he will bring forth judgment to the nations. He will not cry out, nor accept a person’s status, nor will his voice be heard outside. He will not break a bruised reed, nor extinguish smoking flax; in truth he will bring forth judgment. He will not be sad or disturbed until he establishes judgment on the earth, and the islands will await his law.” **R\. Amen.**

**Hymn.**

God, immense Trinity,

Crown of those who confess,

And great praise of Martyrs,

Receive the prayers of the faithful.

By the merit of this holy Pontiff

And Confessor,

Grant us consolations,

And cleanse every harmful thing:

That you may raise up those who confess,

And redeem sinners,

By granting forgiveness

And conferring grace.

And just as this man confessed

Your name before mortals,

**[CLXXIII]** so may we, with devoted minds,

Confess you before all.

Glory be to God the Father,

And to his only Son,

With the Spirit, the Paraclete,

**[Col. 1016B]** throughout everlasting ages.

Amen.

**Supplication.** Let us pray to the Redeemer. fol. CLXX.

**Capitulum.** Christ God, who said through your Apostle that confession of the mouth is beneficial for salvation: by the prayers of your Confessor and Pontiff N., look after our salvation, so that what we believe in our heart and profess with our mouth may be more swiftly heard by you; and, at your command, let us say:

**Our Father.** Deliver us from evil. fol. 10.

**Let the Priest say:** Humble yourselves for the blessing.

**May the Lord be with you. R\.** And with you.

**Lauda.** Your bones will flourish.

**Blessing.** Through the intercession of the most blessed... fol. CLXX.

In the name of the Lord. Let a commemoration be made.

**[Col. 1016C] Lauda.** To announce your mercy in the morning. **Prayer.** In the morning, O Lord, our prayer. fol. CLIX.

# THE OFFICE OF ONE DISTINGUISHED CONFESSOR WHO IS NOT A PONTIFF BEGINS

## At Vespers

**Lauda.** Confession and beauty. fol. CLXIX.

**May the Lord be with you. R\.** And with you.

**Sonus.** In the presence of the Angels I will sing to you, O Lord, Alleluia. I will worship toward your holy temple and confess to you, O Lord. Alleluia.

**May the Lord be with you. R\.** And with you.

**Antiphon.** I will confess to you, O Lord, because you have heard me. **P.** And you have become my salvation. **V\.** O God, I will sing a new song to you; on the ten-stringed psaltery I will sing to you. **P.** And you have become. **V\.** Glory and honor. **P.** And you have become.

**May the Lord be with you. R\.** And with you.

**Lauda.** I will confess to the Lord, Alleluia. **P.** According to his righteousness. Alleluia. And I will sing. Alleluia. **V\.** I will rejoice and exult in you, O Lord, and sing to your name, O Most High. **P.** According to his righteousness. **V\.** Glory and honor to the Father. **P.** And I will sing. Alleluia.

**Hymn.**

This consecrated Confessor of the Lord,

Whose feast the people celebrate throughout the world,

Today, rejoicing, merited

To ascend the hidden places of heaven.

He was devout, prudent, humble, chaste,

Sober, pure, and peaceful;

While the present life gave vigor to his limbs,

His body flourished.

At whose sacred tomb, the limbs of the sick,

However burdened by any disease,

Are now often restored to health.

Therefore now our choir, in his honor,

Gladly sings this hymn,

That we may be helped by his holy merits

Throughout all ages.

Let there be salvation, honor, and power

For him who, seated above heaven’s summit,

Governs the structure of the entire world,

Three and one.

Amen.

**[Col. 1017B] Supplication.** Let us beseech our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer of the world, with every supplication: that through his grace and through the intercession of holy Mary, his Virgin and Mother, and of his holy Confessor N., he may graciously deign to grant us salvation of soul and body, forgiveness of sins, and peace. **R\.** Grant this, eternal almighty God.

**Kyrie eleison. R\.** Christe eleison. Kyrie eleison.

**Capitulum.** Eternal almighty God, from whom every good thing arises and advances along a better course, who strengthens the faith of Confessors: grant endurance to the good while the harshness of persecutors rages. We ask your omnipotence, O Lord, that you graciously attend to and mercifully receive our prayers, which we offer in honor of your most blessed and pleasing Confessor N.; so that, through his intercession and with your mercy cooperating, those who ask in faith may obtain without doubt what they seek, and, absolved from all offenses, may possess the heavenly kingdom.

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

**Blessing.** May Christ the Lord, who caused his most blessed Confessor N. to confess him worthily before human beings on earth, confess us before his Father who is in heaven. **R\. Amen.** And may he who placed in his mouth songs of confession pleasing to himself receive our confession to reward it. **R\. Amen.** So that, by confessing and praising the name of Jesus Christ forever after the example of his most blessed Confessor N., we may merit to be participants in heaven with him whom we have confessed. **R\. Amen.**

Through.

**[Col. 1017D] Lauda.** Your bones will flourish. fol. CLXX.

**Prayer.** We humbly beseech your clemency, most merciful Father, that today’s solemnity, which we have undertaken for the veneration of your most blessed Confessor N., may itself commend us to you; and just as you granted him the crown of holy perfection, so through his intercession grant us forgiveness and pardon for all our offenses. **R\. Amen.**

Through mercy.

In the name of the Lord. Let a commemoration be made. fol. 170.

## At Matins

My lips, O Lord. Psalm 50. **P.** And my mouth. **Prayer.** May our tongue praise you, O Lord. fol. CLXX.

**Antiphon 1.** I will confess to you, O Lord, with psaltery vessels; I will sing your truth to you, my God. **V\.** My lips will rejoice when I sing to you, and my soul, which you have redeemed. **P.** Your truth. **V\.** Glory and honor. **P.** Your truth.

**Prayer.** Let us pour forth prayers with all humility, dearest brothers, to the eternal King and Father God, instructed by the examples and merits of his most holy Confessor N.; so that, just as he made that man undergo examples of various struggles for our instruction, so he may grant him the fullest power to intercede for us before the clemency of his goodness. **R\. Amen.**

**Antiphon 2.** You will have confidence in the hope laid up for you, and, once placed in the earth, you will sleep securely; you will rest, and there will be no one to frighten you. **V\.** May he not allow your foot to be shaken, nor may he sleep who guards you. **P.** You will sleep securely. **V\.** Glory and honor. **P.** You will rest.

**Prayer.** With attention, dearest brothers, let us ask the Lord in prayer that he may graciously grant us and our posterity a celebrated triumph in affairs and actions on this day, which the confession of his Saint N. illumines; so that, as we merit to be his venerator in this age, we may through his merits merit to obtain forgiveness for our offenses. **R\. Amen.**

Through mercy.

**Antiphon 3.** I will sleep and rest in peace, because you, O Lord, have established me uniquely in hope. **V\.** I will confess to you, O Lord, with my whole heart, in the council of the righteous and in the assembly. **P.** Because you, O Lord. **V\.** Glory and honor. **P.** Because you.

**[Col. 1018C] Prayer.** We humbly beseech your clemency, most merciful Father, that today’s solemnity, which we have undertaken for the veneration of your most blessed Confessor N., may itself commend us to you; and just as you granted him the crown of holy perfection, so through his intercession grant us forgiveness and pardon for all our offenses. **R\. Amen.**

Through mercy.

**R\.** Behold how the righteous man dies, and no one considers it; righteous men are taken away, and no one perceives it in his heart. The righteous man has been taken away from the face of iniquity; there will be peace at his burial. **V\.** If the righteous man is overtaken by death, his soul is in refreshment; there will be peace. **V\.** Glory and honor. **P.** Behold how.

**Prayer.** As we solemnly recall the annual return of the memory of your most blessed Confessor N., O Lord, enrich us with the sprinkling of heavenly grace, so that those who now pursue his feast with devoted zeal may also always be guided and protected by his merciful regard. **R\. Amen.**

Through mercy.

## At Lauds

**For the Canticle. Antiphon.** I will confess to you, O Lord. fol. CLXXI. **Canticle.** I will confess to you, O Lord. **P.** Because you have delivered me. **V\.** Glory and honor. **P.** And from the hand.

**For the Benedictus. Antiphon.** The blessing of the Lord. **Canticle.** Benedictus. fol. 6. **P.** As the reward of the righteous. **V\.** Glory and honor. **P.** As the reward of the righteous. **V\.** Let us bless the Father. **P.** As the reward of the righteous. **Sonus.** In the presence of the Angels. fol. CLXXII.

**[Col. 1019A] Lauda.** Alleluia. His confession is above heaven and earth, Alleluia. **P.** He has exalted the horn of his people. Alleluia. **V\.** A hymn belongs to all his Saints. Alleluia, alleluia. Psalm 148.

Before “Glory and honor to the Father” is said: **[CLXXV] P.** He has exalted the horn. **V\.** Glory and honor. **P.** Alleluia. His confession. Entirely.

**Prophecy.** Thus says the Lord. **Hymn.** God, immense Trinity. fol. CLXXII. **Supplication.** Let us pray to the Redeemer. **Capitulum.** Eternal almighty God. fol. CLXXI. **Lauda.** Your bones will flourish. fol. 170. **Blessing.** Christ the Lord, who is the most blessed... fol. CXXIII.

In the name of the Lord.

Let a commemoration be made. fol. CLIX.

# THE OFFICE OF ONE SIMPLE CONFESSOR, WITH TWO COPES OR NINE LESSONS, BEGINS

**[Col. 1019B]**

## At Vespers

**Lauda.** Confession and beauty. **Sonus.** I will confess to you, O Lord. fol. CLXIX.

**Antiphon.** I will confess to you, O Lord, with my whole heart. **P.** Because you have heard the words of my mouth. In the presence of the Angels I will sing to you. **V\.** You are my God; I will confess to you. You are my God, and I will exalt you. **P.** Because you have heard. **V\.** Glory and honor. **P.** In the presence.

**May the Lord be with you. R\.** And with you.

**[Col. 1019C] Lauda.** I will confess to the Lord. **Hymn.** This Confessor. **Supplication.** Let us pray to the Redeemer. fol. CLXXIII.

**Capitulum.** Glorious and merciful Lord, who granted your blessed Confessor N. to confess you exceedingly with his mouth, and willed that you be praised in the midst of the righteous through his confession: you recognize that your Confessor has been brought forth at this evening hour. But you, O Lord, who bestowed the crown for confession of your name, grant also to us sinners mercy and the effectiveness to obtain what we ask while confessing our offenses.

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. See fol. 2.

**Blessing.** May the Lord Jesus Christ, who is the reward of Confessors, magnify us by the gift of holy confession through the suffrage of his Confessor N. **R\. Amen.** So that, truly imitating the example of so great a Confessor, we may merit to reach the heavenly promise. **R\. Amen.** And may he grant us the will to confess, who bestowed on that man the reward of confession. **R\. Amen.**

Through.

**Lauda.** Your bones will flourish. fol. CLXX.

**Prayer.** Son of God, whom your Confessor N. confessed with his whole heart and, honoring your name, was led to the crown: put confession in our mouth that may cleanse us from crime, so that whatever we utter in honor of your praise we may perceive to benefit us as gain of an eternal gift. **R\. Amen.**

Through mercy.

In the name of the Lord.

**[Col. 1020A] Let a commemoration be made.**

**Antiphon.** In the evening and in the morning.

**Prayer.** Lord God. fol. CLXX.

## At Matins

**Antiphon.** My lips, O Lord. Psalm 50.

**Prayer.** May our tongue praise you, O Lord. fol. CLXX.

**Antiphon.** I will confess to you among the peoples, O Lord; I will sing a psalm to your name among the nations. **V\.** O Lord, I am your servant; I am your servant and the son of your handmaid. **P.** I will sing a psalm. **V\.** Glory and honor. **P.** I will sing a psalm.

**Prayer.** Son of God. As above.

**Antiphon.** I will confess greatly to the Lord with my mouth. **P.** And in the midst of many I will praise him. **V\.** For he stood at the right hand of the poor, to save my soul from those who persecuted me. **P.** And in the midst. **V\.** Glory and honor to the Father. **P.** And in the midst.

**Prayer.** You made N. your Confessor blessed indeed, O Lord; he confessed you with his whole heart and is shown to be conspicuous in the council of the righteous and in the assembly. Grant us, therefore, through his merits, that by simpler confession we may be cleansed from crime and merit to take part in the assembly and gatherings of the Saints. **R\. Amen.**

Through mercy.

**Antiphon.** I will sleep and rest in peace. **P.** Because you, O Lord, have established me uniquely in hope. **V\.** I will confess to you, O Lord, with my whole heart; I will recount all your wonders. **P.** Because you, O Lord. **[Col. 1020C] V\.** Glory and honor. **P.** Because you, O Lord.

**Prayer.** God, who, accepting the confession of your most blessed N., heard all the words of his mouth so fully that you made him a participant in your kingdom, where he might sing to you in the presence of the Angels: now receive through him the vow of our confession, you who led him to his reward; and you who willed him to be blessed through confession, draw us, after our fall in this world, at last into the eternal homeland, to be crowned. **R\. Amen.**

Through mercy.

**R\.** This man was not unfaithful in his profession, and in the time of his oppression he was found faithful; therefore he became beloved by the Lord his God. **[Col. 1020D] V\.** This man kept the law of the Most High God in distress and temptation. **P.** He was found faithful. **V\.** Glory and honor. **R\.** This man.

**Antiphon for the Canticle.** I will confess, O Lord. **Canticle.** I will confess to you, O Lord. **For the Benedictus. Antiphon.** The blessing of the Lord. **Canticle.** Blessed are you, O Lord. **With the Sonus.** In the presence. **And the Lauda.** Alleluia. His confession. Psalm 148. **Prophecy.** Thus says the Lord: Behold my servant. **Hymn.** God, immense Trinity. fol. CLXXII. **Supplication.** Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world. **Capitulum.** Glorious and merciful. See the preceding folios above. **Lauda.** Your bones will flourish. fol. **Reading from the Book of the Wisdom of Solomon (chapter XLIV).**

**R\.** Thanks be to God.

The Lord has wrought much glory by his magnificence from of old: rulers in their dominions, men great in strength and endowed with wisdom; proclaiming things with the dignity of prophets; governing in the present [Col. 1025C] age; and, by the power of wisdom, declaring most holy words to the peoples. In their youth they sought musical modes and recited the songs of the Scriptures. All were rich in virtue, devoted to the pursuit of beauty, and making peace in their households. All these attained glory among the generations of their people, and in their days they were held in praise. Those born from them left behind a name, recounting their praises; and there are others whose memory has vanished. They perished as though they had never existed; they were born as though they had not been born, and their children with them. But those men were merciful, whose devotion did not fail; and their goodness continues with their offspring. The inheritance of their descendants remains, and their seed stood firm in covenants; and their children are on their account. Forever [Col. 1025D] their seed will remain, and their glory will not be abandoned. Their bodies were buried in peace, and their name will remain from generation to generation. The peoples recount their wisdom, and the Church proclaims their praise. R. Amen.

Hymn: *Glorious King of Martyrs*. Folio CLXVII. Supplication: *Let us pray to the Redeemer*. Folio CLXII. Capitula: *Almighty God, who diversities...* Lauda: *You are the holy vessels of the Lord*. Blessing: *Christ the Lord, who is the justifier of the justified*. Fol. CLXXVIII.

## THE OFFICE OF A PARTICULAR VIRGIN BEGINS

### At Vespers

Lauda: “My soul has hoped in the Lord, from the morning watch [Col. 1026A] until nightfall.” V. “My soul has waited for your word, O Lord. Let your ears be attentive to the prayer of your handmaid.” P. “Until nightfall.”

Sonus: “Alleluia. I will sing praise to your name, O God, forever.” P. “That I may repay my vows day after day.” Alleluia. V. “You have led me, O Lord, because you became my hope; a tower of strength against the enemy. I shall dwell in your sanctuary, O God, forever.” P. “That I may repay my vows.”

Antiphon: “Show me your face, O Zion, and let your voice be in my ears; for your voice is sweet, and your face is beautiful.” V. “Hear, daughter, and see, and incline your ear; forget your father’s house.” P. “For your voice is sweet.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “For your voice is sweet.”

Antiphon: “Most prudent virgin, where are you going, shining like a brilliant dawn? Daughter of Zion, you are altogether beautiful [Col. 1026B] and pleasing, beautiful as the moon and chosen as the sun.” V. “By day the sun shall not burn you, nor the moon by night.” P. “You are altogether beautiful.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “Beautiful as the moon.”

Lauda: “You have become beautiful and pleasing in your delights. Alleluia. Your beauty is like an unfading palm in the fullness of splendor. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.” V. “Praise the Lord, Jerusalem, and praise your God, O Zion.” P. “Your beauty.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “Your beauty.”

Lauda: “In your appearance and beauty, turn your attention; go forth prosperously, and reign. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.” V. “Because of truth and meekness and justice, your right hand will lead you wondrously.” P. “Turn your attention; go forth prosperously.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.”

### Hymn

[Col. 1026C]

Offspring of a virgin, and maker of your mother,  
whom a virgin bore, though herself remaining a virgin;  
we sing the triumph of the Virgin’s feast:  
accept our vow.

This your blessed Virgin, by a twofold  
lot, while she sought to subdue  
the fragile sex of the body,  
subdued the bloodstained world in her body.

Therefore, fearing neither death nor  
the savage kinds of punishments, companions of death,  
she deserved, after her blood had been poured out,  
to ascend to the consecrated heaven.

By her intercession, gracious God,  
now spare our sins, remitting our faults;  
so that we may resound for you  
the sacred hymn of a pure heart.

Glory to the Father, and to the begotten Son,  
and to you, equal to both,  
holy Spirit, one God,  
through every age of the world.

Amen.

Supplication: “Let us pray. With every supplication let us entreat the Redeemer of the world, our Lord Jesus Christ, that through his grace, and through the intercession of his immaculate and glorious, most blessed Virgin Mary, his mother, and of holy N., virgin and martyr, he may graciously deign to grant us salvation of soul and body, remission [Col. 1027A] of sins, and peace.” R. “Grant it, eternal almighty God.”

Lord, have mercy. R. Christ, have mercy. Lord, have mercy.

Capitula: “Lord Jesus Christ, who promise a hundredfold fruit to those who preserve bodily virginity, through the intercession of your virgin release the bonds of our sins, so that we who are cast down by bodily frailty may be raised up by her patronage.”

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” Fol. 2.

Blessing: “May the Lord Jesus Christ, who preserved his virgin N. in chaste modesty, enrich us with the gift of chastity.” R. Amen. “And may he who betrothed her to himself with the ring of faith join us to his own indissoluble love.” R. Amen. “May he receive as an advocate for us with himself her whom he took as his bride in incorruptible love.” R. Amen.

Through.

Lauda: “I have been exalted like a palm in Kadesh, Alleluia, and like a beautiful olive tree in the fields. Alleluia. Like a vine I have produced the sweetness of fragrance, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.” V. “But I, like a fruitful olive tree in the house of the Lord, will hope in the mercy of my God forever and ever.” P. “Like a vine.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.”

Prayer: “Lord Jesus Christ, who love chastity and embrace virginity, through the intercession of your holy virgin N., forgive our offenses; and grant us the gift of chastity in the present life so that in the future we may rejoice with the holy angels.” R. [Col. 1027C] Amen.

Through mercy.

In the name of the Lord.

Let a commemoration be made.

Let our tongue speak the judgment of truth, so that with the readiest devotion it may praise your Christ, the true judge; and let your commandments continually turn over in our heart, so that our steps may not be tripped by the treacherous snares [Col. 1027D] of deception.” R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Through mercy.

Amen.

Having put to death in us the burning impulse of lust, gird our loins with the safeguard of chastity.” R. Amen.
