## THE SANCTORALE BEGINS (C)

[CLXXXV] JANUARY 9. ON THE SOLEMNITY OF THE SAINTS JULIAN AND BASILISSA, OR OF THEIR COMPANIONS

[Col. 1031D]

### At Vespers

“In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, light with peace.” R. Deo gratias.

[Col. 1032D] “May the Lord be.” R. “And with...”

Lauda: “Light has risen in the darkness.” Sonus: “The souls of the just.” See in the common office, fol. CLXII.

Antiphon: “These are the saints full of innocence, whom virginity also adorned.” P. “And made them sharers in the palm of martyrdom in the kingdom of God.” V. “Rejoice in the Lord, you just; praise is fitting for the upright.” P. “And made them sharers in martyrdom.” V. “Glory.” P. “And made them sharers.”

“May the Lord be.” R. “And with...”

Lauda: “These are the saints who were not defiled in this world; for they are virgins.” P. “Therefore they washed their robes and made them white. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.” V. “Blessed are those whose iniquities have been forgiven and whose sins are covered.” P. “Therefore...” V. “Glory.” P. “Therefore...”

### Hymn

The distinguished feast of the martyr Julian,  
in which, embracing the beloved companionship of a Virgin,  
he attained heaven and became a heavenly inhabitant:  
let the multitude of the consecrated people resound,  
and let the full faith of each one proclaim it.

[Col. 1033B] Here Julian, of illustrious stock by his lot,  
a citizen of the toga-clad city of Antioch,  
imbued with every discipline of the arts,  
an only and illustrious pledge to his parents,  
was leading a life consecrated by his conduct.

When he had completed eighteen annual cycles,  
and was showing in himself hope of sowing offspring,  
his parents came. They rightly proposed marriage,  
so that the chaste procreation of children  
might consecrate their ancestors with an everlasting name.

But behold, the servant of Christ fled to God,  
watchful for seven days and nights;  
he now sought to learn what he himself should say and desire.  
God came near and taught his faithful servant;  
commanding him, he sought the marriage of salvation.

Strengthened by the oracles of grace,  
he rose and agreed more gladly with his parent.  
According to custom, a virgin girl was then sought;  
soon Basilissa was betrothed to him by lot,  
and a beauty equal to his beauty was joined to him.

The day of the wedding itself now arrived.  
The summoned multitude of the city gathered;  
the peoples of neighboring cities flowed together.  
The townspeople sang joyful songs,  
and cymbals resounded with the love of the flesh.

With musical assemblies scattered throughout,  
melody resounded across the whole city;  
the organs thundered with ringing song,  
the lyres tinkled with clattering strings,  
and the keys of the street resounded with zithers.

[Col. 1033D] But the blessed man, eager to despise these things,  
prepared his mind for the victory to come.  
Then, victorious, after the Virgin had been entrusted to him,  
he entered the consecrated chamber of the bridal bed;  
there, reclining, they soon beheld God.

But the Virgin first perceived the gifts of grace;  
then, suffused with the blessed nectar of fragrance,  
she was consecrated and recoiled from the bridal bed.  
Thus the foundations of the bed trembled,  
and they were renewed as celibates in bright light.

Then, with the radiance of lamps going before,  
Christ the King was shown to them in clear light.  
Choirs of angels and of sacred virgins  
beheld the vision of salvation with bowed gaze;  
[Col. 1034A] then they were cherished and taught still more.

Provoked by this most holy gift,  
the two were joined in a union of spirit;  
knowing nothing of the slippery act of the flesh,  
they held a blessed celibate marriage,  
through which they might bring forth spiritual offspring for God.

After their parents had soon died,  
they survived as children of illustrious name,  
[CLXXXVI] and divided estates, houses, and properties,  
and consecrated them to Christ as shining monasteries  
for men and women to dedicate themselves there.

But the flowering palm of the martyr Julian  
is extended over ten thousand men,  
whom he governed within paternal authority.

Hence Basilissa also flourishes,  
surrounded by choirs of virgins  
and by the grace of spiritual gifts.

This was peculiar to the future Martyr,  
together with his most holy wife Basilissa:  
whomever the fire of his mouth touched,  
that person immediately obtained heavenly grace;  
leaving earthly things behind, he grasped heavenly ones.

Thus teaching the crowds of the people,  
thus consecrating many thousands to Christ,  
the two lamps placed upon a lampstand  
shine with the serene light of splendor  
and gleam with the everlasting lamp of graces.

Then, when Basilissa admonished the virgins,  
a lofty pillar of light appeared,  
displaying a blessed writing with its stylus,  
which proclaimed the assembled company of virgins  
radiant and pleasing to God.

The Virgin obtained the desires of her prayers  
and sent ahead all the virgins  
who were to be placed among the blessed stars  
of the heavenly court. After he himself followed them  
at the glorious end of death,  
he dies while devoted to prayer.

To the Trinity be everlasting glory,  
highest honor, and illustrious power:  
the Trinity who—Father, Son of the Father,  
and Spirit—is one God in substance  
and reigns through all ages of ages.

Amen.

### Hymn

Now the glory of the passion about to begin  
calls forth the faith of blessed Julian.  
When Marcianus could not endure the news,  
he ordered all the faithful, the sacred choirs of martyrs,  
to be burned by flames through his agent.

But Julian, whom he regarded as a rebel,  
he ordered to be beaten with astonishing clubs.  
One of the men who struck him, in a criminal assault,  
beating his consecrated limbs with savage blows,  
was immediately deprived of the sight of one eye.

Julian, illuminating him in flesh and heart,  
was preparing him to become a future martyr for Christ.  
But Julian himself was dragged through the streets,  
to be tortured with every weight of cruelty  
and harshly wounded with severe punishments.

Now the turbulent order of the governor  
had bound the saint with bloody sufferings.  
And behold, the Martyr, dragged to the place, arrives  
where the governor’s sweet pledge was being brought up,  
called by the high-sounding name Celsius.

When he, through the glorious light of a vision,  
soon saw Christ’s faithful one face to face,  
and fixed his gaze upon the Martyr,  
he was astonished to see the white legions of heaven  
consoling the blessed man with gentle words.

Again he sees the same thing, with glory increased:  
above the Martyr’s head was a little crown,  
golden and glittering with gems,  
while three men, with radiant faces,  
sang heavenly melody more sweetly.

At such a vision he himself, marveling  
at the songs that the sweeter harmony joined,  
removed his garments and quickly ran  
to the Martyr of God, confessing himself Christian  
in heart and mouth.

Then, being drawn near, sacred with the warmth of Christ,  
he kissed the Martyr’s footprints,  
licked his wounds and touched his holy injuries with his tongue,  
confessing himself a follower of Julian  
and renouncing the name and honor of his parents.

Soon the mother and father waste away  
with the anguish of the news.  
Unable to endure the funeral fate of their son,  
they shower the earth with lamenting cries;  
they mourn and groan and cannot be consoled.

But behold, again the fury of the governor rages  
and orders the child to be separated from the Martyr.  
The execution of the order is frustrated; indeed,  
seeing that each person wished to advance,  
he contracts his face, wails, and beats his arms.

Then he shuts them both in a deadly prison,  
where everything was dark, blind, and foul.  
But there a star of nourishing light shone,  
and added luminous nectar to the prison;  
the dreadful place became brighter for the blessed ones.

The soldiers tremble at what has rightly occurred,  
and, seeing the light of this grace,  
offer hearts converted to Christ through vows.  
They prostrate themselves at the nourishing footprints of the Martyr;  
they honor Christ and proclaim his name.

When these guards had been summoned to the faith,  
twenty of them set their breasts aflame;  
seven faithful men of illustrious stock were produced,  
whom sacred kinship had bound to Christ.  
They had the illustrious teacher Antony as their master.

With such a guide and the angel going before them,  
they joyfully approached the dread prison’s doors,  
where the blessed Martyrs were seated.  
Immediately Celsius and the soldiers  
received Christ’s radiant baptism.

Thus made one company in the Christian faith,  
with Julian and Antony as their teachers,  
they were bound in a single servitude,  
and, held in the custody of one prison,  
they eagerly longed to end their lives in triumph.

[Col. 1036A] The proven faith of the martyr Julian,  
to be proved again by signs and virtues,  
raises up a body destined for burial.  
While the people are astonished and the signs make them tremble,  
he conquers earthly things and soon conquers hell as well.

But behold, rising, he cries out in a thunderous voice  
that the Martyr’s vows have been accepted by Christ;  
at his prayer, by a glorious gift,  
all hell trembled and grew pale,  
returning alive the one whom it had held dead.

He had seen the savage ministers of hell,  
under whose guidance he had been led  
more deeply through the realms below  
and had become fixed in the abyss.  
Then, freed by the lot of death, he emerged  
and confessed Christ, joining himself to Julian.

[Col. 1036B] Having received the grace of baptism,  
he likewise became a strong athlete of Christ.  
Renewed in faith and fervent in charity,  
he was named Anastasius from the sacrament.

He shares with the blessed the stronghold of the contest.

The shining dawn had already restored the day.  
The punishments prepared were announced to the governor:  
threatening vats, already filled with sulfur,  
pitch, tow, and an abundance of bitumen.  
Yet these substances did not burn the limbs of the Martyrs.

For the Martyrs were placed there to be burned,  
and, with the common people and the crowd of the populace standing by,  
they were tested by fire. Then, like shining gold,  
each one, all resounding with a single cry,  
sang a melody from the fire, a song of David.

[Col. 1036C] When the fire had been consumed, it displayed  
the glorious Martyrs, with their dignity’s glory increased.  
And, confirming the miracle of so great a matter,  
the governor—just as Marcianus had previously promised—  
handed the mother over to blessed Celsius.

She, remaining there more readily with her son,  
received the pleasing fruits of fragrance through her nostrils.  
Then, restored by the nectar of sweetness,  
she soon endured forgetfulness of her sorrows,  
confessing Christ with joyful heart and body.

Having been immersed in the stream of the most holy font,  
and, with her offspring, reborn through the Father and the Son,  
burning with the warmth of the Christian name,  
she struck her persecutors with blindness  
and refused the marriage bed in chastity.

Then Marcianus, struck by this funeral  
of his own people, standing nearby received a new wound:  
at the clear voice and imprecation of the Martyrs,  
the beauty of the submerged temple perished,  
and the temple itself was swallowed by a cleft in the earth.

From then on the savage and threatening fury of the governor,  
after the saints had been burned and the rest killed,  
soon tore the skin from the glorious heads  
of Julian and blessed Celsius;  
and he then subjected them to the bites of beasts.

Then the Martyrs, brought into the theater  
among a deadly crowd of the condemned,  
were killed by the stroke of the sword.  
Yet by their bright blood they were approved,  
a red mass of the bodies of the faithful.

For each one appeared above the case of his body  
to the Christian assembly,  
marked with a virginal sign;  
their blood, scattered far and wide, proves  
that this very earth could not conceal them.

Their blessed bodies, now buried,  
pour forth an everlasting stream from their tombs.  
From its waters, a sacred fountain of grace  
is filled with broad-flowing currents,  
through which astounding miracles arise.

There, at the sacred time of the liturgical observance  
of their anniversary, those to be baptized gather.  
Soon ten lepers receive healing.  
Then a terrible voice thunders from above:

[Col. 1037B] “Faith deserves all these things from Julian.”

Now, blessed Martyr, hear those who beseech you;  
now, Julian, cherish your servants;  
as advocate together with the company of Martyrs,  
favor the redeemed; help those who are sick,  
driving away adversity and granting prosperity.

As your proven followers, let us all learn  
to despise the world in our conduct,  
to master anger, and to reject the fleeting things of the flesh.  
Using no enticement of clinging bodily pleasure,  
may we enjoy the joys of heaven.

Burdened by no contagion of sins,  
may we always burn with heavenly fires;  
always fervent in heavenly love,  
may we be renewed by the gift of remorse;  
following Christ, may we await the Judge.

When that day comes with terror,  
and the world is oppressed by the dread of the Judge,  
with you, our sacred and native patron, as sponsor,  
may we hold the right hand and escape hell;  
having gained the kingdom, may we be clothed in glory.

To the Trinity be everlasting glory,  
highest honor, and illustrious power:  
the Trinity who—Father, Son of the Father,  
and Spirit—is one God in substance  
and reigns through all ages of ages.

Amen.

Supplication: “Let us pray. With every supplication let us entreat the Redeemer of the world, our Lord Jesus Christ, that through the intercession of [CLXXXVIII] [Col. 1037D] the holy martyrs Julian and Basilissa and their companions, he may deign to grant us remission of sins and peace.” R. “Grant it, eternal almighty God.”

Lord, have mercy. R. Christ, have mercy. Lord, have mercy.

Capitula: “Lord Jesus Christ, who granted to the most blessed spouses Julian and Basilissa, joined to you by faithful love, the companionship of a heavenly marriage, giving them both not to know the contagion of corruption and to fulfill the vows of holiness; while through Julian a multitude of men is gathered to you in both sexes, and through Basilissa a multitude of holy virgins is acquired; while she is received through confession and he is glorified through passion; while she flourishes among virgins and he rejoices among sufferings; granting that both be summoned to you by a glorious passing; while she is summoned to you after the assault of sins, and he, after the cutting off of the skin of his head, is brought to completion by the glorious end of martyrdom: through their prayers and intercessions join us to yourself in an unbroken bond of love, so that you, who then consecrated to yourself through them the most spotless vessels, may lead us, sanctified in body and spirit by you, to the heavenly kingdom.”

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” Fol. 2.

Blessing: “May Christ the Lord, who commanded a spiritual marriage to exist between Julian and Basilissa, make you flourish in the spiritual gift of virtues.” R. Amen. “And may he who did not allow blessed Celsius to be separated from the Martyr’s side not permit you to be separated in any way from his body.” R. Amen. “And through them may you receive the defenses of eternal life, through whom Christ consecrated many spotless vessels to himself.” R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Lauda: “Everlasting joy.” See fol. CLXII.

Prayer: “Your saints, O Lord—Julian and his companions—flourish like a palm in your sight; planted and rooted, they stand in your holy courts. Established in the contest of martyrdom, they gained from punishment the palm of victory, and from death in your house everlasting glory. Therefore we pray, illustrious God, that through their renowned merits you may deign to forgive us the guilt of our sins.” R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

In the name of our Lord.

### At Matins

[Col. 1038C] Antiphon: “Give us joy.” Psalm L. Prayer: “Restore to us, O Lord, joy.” Fol. CLXIII.

Antiphon 1: “The saints sprout like roses by day.” P. “And like an olive shoot throughout the whole night.” V. “Blessed is the nation whose God is the Lord, the people whom the Lord chose as his inheritance.” P. “And like an olive shoot.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “And like an olive shoot.”

### Prayer

Thus, O Lord, your saints Julian and Basilissa have blossomed in you, who are the true day, like a rose; and, like an olive shoot, during the night they deserved in the contest to attain the reward of eternal salvation. Their labor was in suffering, but their reward remains in glory. Grant that we, who are unequal to the merits of your saints, may, through their intercession and with your help, deserve to be companions with them in your kingdom. **Response:** Amen.

Through mercy.

### Antiphon 2

Palms were in the hands of the saints, and they said with a great cry: **P.** Salvation belongs to our God, who sits upon the throne, and to the Lamb. **V.** The Lord will help them, and he will free them; he will save them, because they have hoped in him. **P.** Salvation belongs to our God. **V.** Glory and honor. **P.** Salvation.

### Prayer

Thus, O Lord, your saints Julian—see above in the preceding Vespers.

### Antiphon 3

These are holy men who draw near to the Lord: **P.** These are just men, full of justice, with palms in their hands. **V.** This is the generation of those who seek the Lord, who seek the face of the God of Jacob. **P.** These are. **V.** Glory and honor. **P.** These are.

### Prayer

Your hand, O Lord, is recognized in your saints, when it raises the holy Julian and his companions to the contest of illustrious battle, making them sprout like grass amid deceits and worldly threats, as they overcame the most wicked enemies by their strongest struggle. Merciful and most gracious God, heed the prayers of the saints, so that, by the example of your martyrs Julian and Basilissa, you may cause us, cleaving to your footsteps, to be crowned in the heavenly kingdom. **Response:** Amen.

Through mercy.

**R.** I heard a voice from heaven saying: “Julian, my beloved, **P.** who despised the world for me, let him be numbered among the saints.” Basilissa, worthy of her name, prayed: “This pleases me to fulfill.” **V.** For the sake of my beloved Julian, let the soul be restored. **P.** Who for me. **V.** Glory and honor. **P.** Who for me.

### Prayer

Behold, O Lord, we proclaim the distinguished miracles of your beloved Julian and his companions. For those aforesaid martyrs, believing in you and following you, were plunged into blazing cauldrons and emerged unharmed; afterward they shone with the radiant brightness of fire. From among them a voice thundered from above: “The faith of my beloved Julian deserved all these things, and deserves even greater ones.” For he restored an eye to a certain man so that he might believe in your name, raised body and soul, and reduced the utterly vain images of idols to dust.

We beseech you, most merciful Lord, through the intercession of this martyr, that the darkness of our heart may be enlightened; that we may rise from the tombs of our vices; and that we may preserve the temple of our body unharmed, so that we may live forever with you and with your saints without end. **Response:** Amen.

Through.

### Antiphon 1

The souls of the just are in the hand of God, **P.** and the torment of death will not touch them. **V.** But the just will possess the earth as an inheritance, and they will dwell upon it forever and ever. **P.** And it will not touch them. **V.** Glory. **P.** And it will not.

### Prayer

Lord Jesus Christ, giver of heavenly grace, you granted such grace to your saints Julian and Basilissa that, having renounced all that belongs to this world, you made them companions among the saints and in the assembly of the elect. Therefore we beseech you, illustrious God, by the services of the saints, to infuse spiritual light into our minds; so that, after every worldly desire has been wiped away from us, you may, through their illustrious merits, deign to forgive us the offenses of our sins. **Response:** Amen.

Through.

### Antiphon 2

The Son of God rejoiced over the just, **P.** and he will establish them in the paradise of delights. **V.** For the Lord loves judgment and will not abandon his saints; they will be preserved forever. **P.** And he will establish them in the paradise.

**V.** Glory. **P.** And he will establish them in the paradise.

### Prayer

Christ, Son of God, who are glorious in the saints and admirable in majesty, by whose powerful virtue you granted such a gift of praise to your athlete Julian and his companions, who contended for your name, that they received a precious crown adorned with gold and gems, and were able confidently to do for you all that they wished: through their intercession, join us also, your servants, to the faithful promise of your fellow soldiers, so that, even if our sins, through evil living, do not make us worthy of a crown, you may at least draw us upward through the reward of mercy; and, through their holy merits, may you deign to prepare and grant us gifts of grace. **Response:** Amen.

Through mercy.

### Antiphon 3

Flourish, O saints, like roses planted beside the waters, **P.** and, like lilies, give forth the fragrance of sweetness. **V.** Planted in the house of the Lord, they will flourish in the courts of the house of our God. **P.** And, like lilies. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father. **P.** And, like—

### Prayer

Glorious King of all, Christ, who love justice and in whom flowering holiness shines, you granted such a gift of holiness to your servant Basilissa that, while she admonished the virgins, a column of light appeared to her to illuminate them, and an exceedingly sweet fragrance strengthened her, so that she answered:

“I insult you, devil, because of the flock entrusted to me, not one of them will perish with you. You alone rejoice in your punishment.”

Through their intercession we ask you, most loving God, to grant the healing of your mercy for the sins of all of us who do not merit the glory of merits, so that forgiveness may come to us as a gift of mercy. **Response:** Amen.

Through mercy.

**[Col. 1040C] R.** Thus says the Lord: “I will visit my saints in the midst of fire, and from the midst of the flame I will free them; and I will give them a kingdom.” **P.** Forever and unto ages of ages. **V.** The saints will exult in glory; they will rejoice upon their beds. **P.** Forever. **V.** Glory and honor. **P.** Forever.

### Prayer

Almighty and eternal God, Christ Jesus, with whose help your athlete Julian placed the sign of the Cross upon an eye that had been torn out and immediately deserved to restore its sight, having invoked the name of the Trinity: receive, according to your accustomed mercy, the vows of those who pray, and enlighten the darkness of our blindness. Grant us also, through the intercession of the holy martyrs, a generous outpouring of your blessing, so that the darkness of the gloom in our heart may be enlightened and the bonds of our sins may be loosed. **Response:** Amen.

Through mercy.

### Antiphon 1

Near to those who fear God is his salvation, **P.** and it is upon the saints and upon those who turn to him. **V.** The Lord is faithful in his words and holy in all his works. **P.** And it is upon the saints. **V.** Glory. **P.** And it is upon.

### Prayer

Strengthened by the protection of the most blessed martyrs Julian and Basilissa and their companions, may our faithful prayer proceed to the Lord, so that, just as we celebrate their glorious triumph in this age, we may be helped forever by their prayers. **Response:** Amen.

Through.

### Antiphon 2

Let the just feast and exult in the presence of the Lord, **P.** and let them delight in joy. **V.** The salvation of the just is from the Lord, and he is their protector in time of tribulation. **P.** And let them delight. **V.** Glory. **P.** And let them delight.

### Prayer

Remember us, O Lord; and just as you render worthy rewards of martyrdom to your saints Julian and Basilissa and their companions, so spare and have mercy on our sins, so that, absolved from what is past, we may deserve protection in what is to come. **Response:** Amen.

Through mercy.

### Antiphon 3

The just accepted death so that they would not be confounded, but they were strengthened so as not to violate the holy covenant. **P.** And all spoke on account of the kingdom of the Lord and on account of the covenant of our fathers. **V.** They will still increase in a fruitful old age, and they will endure patiently. **P.** And they spoke. **V.** Glory and honor. **P.** And they spoke.

### Prayer

Behold, O Lord, a clear voice invites us to the banquet, or to the joy of the saints, where all your friends feast. Grant us, your servants, we beg, the affection of your love, which may draw us to heavenly things; and by the intervention of your martyrs Julian and his companions, whom you have acquired by a heavenly gift, may we be introduced through them into the eternal dwellings of the saints; may we be worthy. **Response:** Amen.

Through mercy.

**R.** Holy men, paradise is opened for you; the tree of life is planted; abundance is prepared; the city is built; rest is found. **P.** Love is perfected; weakness has been extinguished from you. Sorrows have passed away. **V.** Behold how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to dwell together in unity. **P.** Love is perfected. **V.** Glory and honor. **P.** Love is perfected.

### Prayer

True and undivided Trinity, supreme God, one and three, who promise that through a brief tribulation we shall go to eternal rest: grant us, through the intercession of your holy martyrs Julian and his companions, that we may walk by the spirit and not fulfill the desires of the flesh; and that we may renounce our parents in such a way that we do not depart from you. Thus, while your love, given through the Holy Spirit, is poured into our hearts, may we, cleaving to your footsteps, be crowned. **Response:** Amen.

Through mercy.

## At Lauds

### At the Canticle

**Antiphon:** Those who love you, O Lord, shine like the sun in its rising; so they gleam.

**Canticle:** You who offered yourselves willingly. See folio CLXIII.

### At the Benedictus

**Antiphon:** Holy and humble in heart, spirits and souls of the just, bless the Lord.

**Canticle:** Blessed are you, Lord. Folio 6.

**Chant:** The way of the just has been made.

**Praise:** Praise the Lord from the heavens. Alleluia.

**Psalm:** CXLVIII.

**Prophecy:** The souls of the just are in the hand of God. See folio CLXVII.

## Hymn

Julian, the life of the martyr,  
Noble through the love of Christ,  
Rejecting the world’s lofty things,  
Desires to hold the citadel of heaven.

He is ordered by his parents  
To accept marriage;  
Yet he was not disobedient to his father,  
Nor faithless in his mind toward God.

Having consulted the Author of light,  
He suggests that the commands be fulfilled.  
The joyful father is led in,  
And Basilissa is sought.

They are joined as equals in faith;  
They celebrate a heavenly wedding.  
But, with the organ of the heart,  
They ask that their loins be set aflame. **[The Latin is obscure.]**

As they entered the bedchamber,  
The fragrance of roses was poured forth.  
The virgin consented  
To preserve an undefiled union.

He was captured at Antioch  
Under the governor Marcianus.  
He is tortured in all his limbs  
And restores an extinguished eye.

When he prayed, the faithless idols  
Were overturned.  
Anastasius rises again,  
And Celsius too is converted.

They fill the cauldrons with fire,  
With tow, pitch, and bitumen;  
Unharmed, they emerge from them  
And destroy the overthrown temples.

The Child acquires a Mother;  
The Son becomes the Father of the Mother;  
The Son of the second Birth  
Regenerates the Mother.

Sent into the amphitheater  
Among beasts, the leopard and lion caress him;  
Then, struck by a wound,  
He is snatched from the citadel into glory.

To God the Father be glory,  
And to his only Son,  
Together with the holy Paraclete,  
Throughout everlasting ages.

Amen.

**Supplication:** Let us pray. Folio CLXXXVII.

### Chapters

Lord Jesus Christ, you fortified Julian and Basilissa with the riches of your grace so that they might be bound together by the bond of a spiritual marriage, without in any way mingling through the union of the flesh. Make us, after their example, exalted in chastity and equal to them in the fervor of loving you through the Holy Spirit. And just as you made them vessels most pure for yourself, so, after carnal pleasure has been overcome in us, kindle many through their example toward the heavenly kingdoms.

**Our Father. Deliver us from evil.** Folio 2.

**Praise:** Everlasting joy. See folio CLXII.

**Blessing:** Christ the Lord, who among Julian—see folio CLXXXVIII.

In the name of our Lord, etc.

# 13 January — Feast of the Holy Forty Martyrs

**[Col. 1043A]**

Everything is to be said as for the feast of Many Martyrs, folio CLXVIII, except for the Office of Vespers and the Chapters, and the Blessings and Chapters at Matins, which are as follows.

## At Vespers

**Praise:** Light has risen for the just, **P.** and joy for the upright in heart. **V.** He has made straight the way of the just and prepared the path of the saints. **P.** The merciful, etc.

May the Lord be always with you. **R.** And with you.

**Chant:** Rejoice in the Lord, you just; praise is fitting for the upright. Alleluia. **V.** Give thanks to the Lord upon the harp; sing praise to God upon the ten-stringed psaltery. Alleluia.

May the Lord be always with you. **R.** And with you.

**Antiphon:** They raised their hands to the Lord, **P.** and said: “Lord, we are forty; may forty be crowned.” **V.** Praise the Lord, Jerusalem; praise your God, Zion. **P.** And they said. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father. **P.** And they said.

May the Lord be always with you. **R.** And with you.

**Praise:** “I will require the blood of the saints,” says the Lord; **P.** “and I will dwell with them in my kingdom.” Alleluia, alleluia. **V.** The Lord is faithful in his words and holy in all his works. **P.** And I will dwell with them. **V.** Glory and honor. **P.** And I will dwell.

**Hymn:** The merits of the saints.

**Supplication:** Let us pray. Folio CLXII.

### Chapters

Take, O God, the sword from the hand of the pursuing devil, so that your peace may abound among the saints. Let the tempter no longer be permitted to wound those for whom the Savior wished to provide such remedies, so that in the house of peace, among the children of peace, we may cry out from the earth:

**Our Father. Deliver us from evil.**

### Blessing

May the Lord fortify you by the patronage of his Forty Holy Martyrs and cleanse you from sin. **R.** Amen.

By their intercession may he make you happy, you who now serve in their solemn celebrations. **R.** Amen.

May you likewise deserve heaven with them, whose triumph you now celebrate on earth. **R.** Amen.

Through.

May the Lord be with you. **R.** And with you.

**Praise:** Everlasting joy. Folio CLXII.

# 19 January — Feast of Saint Sebastian and His Companions

## At Vespers

**[Col. 1043D]**

**Praise:** Light has arisen in the darkness for the upright in heart: **P.** the Lord is merciful, compassionate, and just. **V.** He has made the way of the just straight and prepared the path of the saints. **P.** The merciful, etc.

May the Lord be always with you. **R.** And with you.

**[CXCII] Chant:** The souls of the just are in the hand of God, and the torment of death will not touch them. Alleluia. **V.** In the eyes of the foolish they seemed to die, and their departure was considered an affliction; but they are in peace. Alleluia.

May the Lord be always with you. **R.** And with you.

**Antiphon:** Let the just feast and exult in the presence of the Lord, **P.** and let them delight in joy. **V.** The salvation of the just is from the Lord, and he is their protector in time of tribulation. **P.** And let them delight. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father. **P.** And let them delight.

May the Lord be always with you. **R.** And with you.

**Praise:** The just cried out, and the Lord heard them. Alleluia. **P.** And he freed them from all their afflictions. Alleluia, alleluia. **V.** Many are the tribulations of the just, and from all of them the Lord delivered them. **P.** And from all. **V.** Glory and honor. **P.** And from all.

## Hymn

Let the kindly crowd pour forth the solemn feast  
Of the most holy martyr Sebastian,  
By which, leaving the world, he possesses the kingdoms of heaven.  
All, with ringing rejoicing, sing together,  
And offer vows to Christ with pure heart.

Here was one learned in letters, and a worshiper of Christ,  
A native of Milan by birth;  
He was dear to the Tyrant, for he served the rulers  
Under a worldly guise,  
So that he might sweeten worthy words of faith.

Two twin and faithful soldiers,  
The brother Marcelianus and devout Marcus,  
While they worshiped the name of Christ with obedient minds,  
Were punished with a dreadful prison bond,  
Soon to be heard by the excellent governor.

At this, their parents and modest wives,  
With mournful cries and requests for imprisonment,  
Together with the harmful enticements of their friends,  
Displayed their sons and demanded them with lamentation—  
Not that they should desire to die, but to live.

Amid the tears of parents and wives,  
The soldiers of Christ began to soften  
And to bend their minds toward the pain of punishment.  
But then before their assembly was  
Sebastian, a most courageous warrior.

Soon, placing himself among them,  
Instructing all with deliberate speech,  
He declared that the world’s gains were false;  
Proclaiming the insignia of the heavenly kingdom,  
He urged them to end their lives for Christ.

While the blessed man was explaining these things more aptly,  
A chorus, with light shining from heaven,  
Immediately made Sebastian radiant,  
And a young man appeared clothed in light,  
By which, it is said, he was filled completely.

These events took place in the house of Nicostratus,  
Whose wife Zoe first believed.  
For twenty-six years she had lived without speech,  
But by the martyr’s command she was made eloquent  
And entirely followed his words in due order.

For she reported that she saw an angel  
Holding a sacred book before him,  
From which she drew everything that was arranged.  
At once all cried out that they believed this,  
And urgently requested baptism.

But Sebastian, always cautious and worthy of foresight,  
Ordered Nicostratus that those held in bonds  
And delivered into prison  
Should be compelled to remain there, since already then  
All the believers would receive baptism appropriately.

This having been properly done, Claudius also believed,  
With his dear children and beloved wife,  
Polycarpus, a presbyter and advocate, who had been hiding through fear of the persecutors, ordered those to be baptized to give their names.

Then everyone gave their own names,  
And sixty-eight persons of both sexes  
Were baptized by him in the holy waters.  
Now reborn under divine grace,  
They sang joyful hymns for ten days.

But the prefect of the city of Rome, Cromatius,  
Summoned Tranquillinus for questioning.  
He was to speak concerning the judgment of his sons;  
And, fully declaring the faith of Christ to him,  
He showed that he himself had been born through belief.

The governor, learning of his healing,  
Immediately ordered the saints to come secretly.  
Thinking that the grace of Christ could be bought,  
He promised immeasurable weights of gold  
And asked that his limbs be healed.

“You cannot obtain this by bargaining  
Unless you first believe in Christ,” said the saints.  
“Otherwise there will be no healing for your body.”  
He is present; immediately the governor vows to believe,  
With all fear removed from his heart.

But soon, happier, he sees him successfully  
Breaking the previously fashioned monsters of the gods,  
Driving away all harmful worship,  
And immediately renouncing every offense.  
He eagerly desires that this be done.

Then the martyrs began to destroy  
The vain shrines of mechanical workmanship.  
A handsome young man stands beside Cromatius; he attends to everything and immediately loosens the gout-ridden knots by a heavenly remedy.

By the prudent counsel of Sebastian,  
Cromatius then pretends to be ill.  
The other prefect of public affairs says this,  
So that, having cast away the losses of this world,  
They may receive the first beginnings of the life to come.

The sweet Tiburtius believes with his father,  
And his entire household believes as well:  
Four thousand persons of both sexes  
Are washed in the sacred bath  
And receive the grace of spiritual gifts.

The chief priest, the great and most powerful Galustus,  
Who gathers the holy people by protecting Cromatius,  
Leads them by sacred instructions in his own house.  
He nurtures and moves them all in such a way  
That no worldly pageantry occupies anyone.

But because the fury of tyranny presses on,  
This can in no way remain concealed.  
By sacred writing Cromatius is ordered  
To go farther from his city  
With his companions, under the pretext of healing.

The intention then warns both saints,  
Sebastian and holy Polycarpus,  
That one of them should go with those departing.  
But both seek the prize of suffering  
And desire to remain in the city.

But Pope Polycarpus advises that he should not abandon the people he has acquired, where he may water the newly planted flock with the dew of Christ.  
At once the holy elder falls silent at this,  
And assents to the gentle command of the prophet.

Then, with the Pope, the martyrs remain:  
Marcelianus, Marcus, Tranquillinus,  
Tiburtius, Castulus, and Nicostratus;  
But with his brother Claudius and his son,  
Sebastian and the most holy Zoe.

He duly consecrates all these  
As ministers of Christ in the holy Church,  
And, vigorous, they fulfill the sacred mysteries.  
Each is powerful in different offices  
And in the grace of healing bestowed upon them.

To the Trinity be everlasting glory,  
Highest honor, and illustrious power—  
To the Trinity, the Father and the Father’s Son,  
With the Spirit, one God in substance,  
Who reigns through all ages of ages.

Amen.

**Supplication:** Let us pray, with the names changed. Folio CLXVII.

### Chapters

The solemn feast of your foster-child, the noble soldier Sebastian, is here, O Christ. He gives us the support of recovered hope and nourishes us with the food of heavenly life. While he reforms the wayward and enlightens the unlearned in doctrine, may he draw us by prayer to the sublime court of heaven, where he rejoices perpetually with you. And as, in their struggle, he carried away from the enemy a triumph bearing palms, may he shelter us with tireless protection beside you, and may we pray to him and say:

**Our Father. Deliver us from evil.** Folio 2.

### Blessing

May the Lord preserve us through the intercession of the martyr Sebastian, whom he raised with his companions to the seat of heaven. **R.** Amen.

And as, when he prayed, he once opened Zoe’s obstructed mouth, so may he open your mouth in confessions of his praise. **R.** Amen.

So that, burning with faith and supported by good works, you may deserve to obtain the heavenly kingdoms with rejoicing. **R.** Amen.

Through.

**Praise:** Everlasting joy. Folio CLXXVI.

**Prayer:** Behold, he rejoices in you, O Lord.

**Antiphon:** Give us the joy of your salvation.

**Psalm:** L. See below, at Matins for this feast.

**Prayer:** Restore to us, O Lord, our joy. See folio CLXIII.

### Antiphon 1

The saints will exult in glory, **P.** and they will rejoice upon their beds. **V.** Blessed is the nation whose God is the Lord, the people whom the Lord chose as his inheritance. **P.** And they will rejoice. **V.** Glory and honor. **P.** And they will rejoice.

### Prayer

That the saints would exult in glory and rejoice upon their beds was foretold by the divine Spirit and by prophetic speech. Therefore, clinging to the patronage of Saint Sebastian, let us offer vows in the morning prayer in praise of this most blessed martyr. The words of the Godhead testify that those crowned by a divine gift have been cleansed of dark death and made children of light. **Response:** Amen.

Through.

### Antiphon 2

Rejoice in the Lord and exult, you just, **P.** and glory, all you upright in heart. **V.** Rejoice in the Lord, you just; praise is fitting for the upright. **P.** And glory. **V.** Glory. **P.** And glory.

### Prayer

Behold, your martyr Sebastian rejoices in you, O Lord, and glories in you, because he is crowned by you. Therefore we beseech you, Lord God, with all the prayers we can offer: since today we celebrate the solemn feast of this man, may we deserve to obtain forgiveness for our sins. **Response:** Amen.

Through mercy.

### Antiphon 3

The exaltations of God are in the throats of the saints. **[Col. 1047B] P.** This glory belongs to all his saints. Alleluia, alleluia. **V.** The voice of joy and salvation is in the tents of the just. **P.** This glory belongs. **V.** Glory and honor. **P.** This glory belongs.

### Prayer

Your exaltations, O Lord, are in the throat of your servant, the martyr Sebastian, while he glories in you and rejoices in you, so that he who was a wondrous victor for the Lord may be a magnificent intercessor for his servants. **Response:** Amen.

Through mercy.

**R.** The saints will exult with confidence, **P.** and rejoicing, they will hasten to see the face of God, whom they served and from whom they begin to receive their glorious reward. **V.** The saints will exult in glory and rejoice upon their beds. **P.** And rejoicing. **V.** Glory and honor. **P.** And rejoicing.

### Prayer

Illustrious love, certain hope, unshaken faith, Lord our God: grant that, while we sing a new song to you, we may be cleansed from the leaven of our former wickedness; and that, while we glory in your praise, we may not be weighed down by the burden of our sins. Through the help of your holy martyrs Sebastian and his companions, may we sing your power with devout affection, so that we may deserve to obtain the constant protection of your mercy. **Response:** Amen.

Through mercy.

## At Lauds

### At the Canticle

**Antiphon:** Those who love you, O Lord.

**Canticle:** You who offered yourselves willingly.

### At the Benedictus

**Antiphon:** Holy and humble in heart.

**Canticle:** Blessed are you, Lord, God of our fathers. Folio 6.

**Chant:** The way of the just. Folio CLXVII.

**Praise:** Praise the Lord from the heavens. Alleluia. Psalm CXLVIII.

**Prophecy:** The souls of the just are in the hand of God. See folio CLXVII.

## Hymn

Now it is fitting to hasten to him,  
Because the time of immense suffering will testify—  
For on the birthday of the apostles,  
While blessed Zoe prayed, she more readily  
Yielded her spirit to Christ in her sleep.

Eight days having passed, Tranquillinus,  
While praying at Paul’s house,  
Was nevertheless then cruelly stoned,  
And his great body was submerged in the river;  
But his spirit breathed forth into the lofty heavens.

Immediately seeking their bodies,  
Nicostratus and Claudius with his offspring,  
Held for ten days, together with Castorius,  
Sank amid the waves in the sea’s currents,  
And completed the worthy reward of suffering.

Torquatus is deceitfully joined to the saints;  
Through his contrivance Tiburtius is captured,  
With savage feeling and a dreadful executioner.  
He ordered him to be struck with the sword,  
And consecrated him a martyr strong in Christ.

Castulus Zetarius, the host of the saints,  
Was captured and soon became Christ’s martyr.  
Afterward, when the holy Marcelianus  
And the upright Marcus had been beaten with spears,  
Thus crowned, they poured out their spirits to heaven.

After acquiring a white robe for God,  
Sebastian, the beautiful and excellent shepherd,  
As a shepherd, with the flock entrusted to Christ,  
He is ambushed and overcome by cruel men  
And led by servants before the rulers.

Then the impious Tyrant orders him  
To be led into the field and pierced with arrows.  
But afterward, healed by Christ’s grace,  
He finally ends his life amid scourges  
And flies into the ether, into the consecrated citadel.

Come now, blessed Sebastian, to those who pray;  
Now guard your little servants  
Together with that holy company of his.  
Forgive guilt and grant pardon,  
So that we may all enjoy heavenly joy.

May fraternal love bind the clergy together;  
May no quarrel separate anyone from the company.  
Let deceit, rust, luxury, and greed depart;  
Let every impious alliance depart,  
So that they may always seek Christ with pure mind.

By your gracious help drive away  
The yoke with which an impious people now oppresses us.  
May neither hostile disease nor scarcity be present;  
May all adversities quickly flee;  
May there be perpetual peace and welcome rest for the dead.

May the Judge not rebuke us in anger  
When his terror shines forth in glory.  
May devouring fire not claim us for punishment,  
But, following you as our guide,  
May we especially share in the fellowship of the saints.

Grant, we pray, undivided Trinity,  
The things desired to those who confess you:  
You alone possess the name of God,  
Father with the Word and the Holy Spirit,  
Reigning forever in the Trinity.

Amen.

**Supplication:** Let us pray, with the names changed. Folio CLXII.

### Chapters

Glorious is the palm of victory of your holy martyrs Sebastian and his companions, O Lord, for as great as their virtue is in merit, so great is their patience proven in deeds. The flesh fell; the world was put to shame; the persecutor trembled; and for those to whom life was punishment, victory was made in death. Therefore we ask you, almighty God, that through their intervention forgiveness of all our sins may not be denied us.

**Our Father. Deliver us from evil.** Folio 2.

**Praise:** Everlasting joy. Folio CLXII.

Humble yourselves for the blessing.

May the Lord always be with you. **R.** And with your spirit.

### Blessing

May almighty God bless you, who rejoice in the passion of the holy martyrs Sebastian and his companions. **R.** Amen.

May he grant you the fullness of every blessing, to whom he has deigned to establish the law. **R.** Amen.

May you offer a sacrifice of praise to almighty God and continually show one another the service of charity. **R.** Amen.

Through his mercy, etc.

# Feast of Saint Lucian, Priest and Martyr

Everything is to be said as for One Martyr with nine lessons, folio CLX, except for the Chapters and Blessings at Vespers, and the Chapters at Matins, which are as follows.

### Chapters

Let us celebrate, dearly beloved brothers, with solemn vows the contest of his most blessed martyr, Lucian the Priest, perfected by divine power, so that he who, with Christ’s aid, deserved to obtain the triumphant palm through the defenses of faith may deign to grant us the help of his intercession with him, whose presence he now rejoices in; and may he himself grant us forgiveness of sins, who bestowed upon him the crown of immortality.

**Our Father. Deliver us from evil.** Folio 2.

### Blessing

May Christ the Lord, who gave his martyr Lucian the Priest the desire to suffer, grant you patience against all the enticements of vice. **R.** Amen.

And may he who, after his passion was completed, gave him a crown grant you, when the struggle of the world is completed, the promised joys. **R.** Amen.

May you who on this day celebrate with rejoicing the solemn feast of so great a martyr rejoice to be placed with him in the heavenly dwellings after your departure. **R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

### At Matins — Chapters

Since, O Lord, we know from your law that the just man is in everlasting memory, we offer this holocaust to you not for his commendation but for ours, asking that you who made his soul victorious in suffering may make our vow victorious in confession, so that, with him interceding, you may receive the cry of our voice:

**Our Father. Deliver us from evil.** Folio 2.

# 20 January — Feast of the Holy Virgins Agnes and Emerentiana

## At Vespers

**Praise:** All your angels have praised you, O Lord.

**Chant:** Alleluia. Your right hand is full of justice.

**Antiphon:** Behold these devout women.

**Praise:** Your daughters, Jerusalem, will rise at your side. See folio CLXXXII.

## Hymn

Agnes’s tomb is in the city of Romulus,  
That of the strong girl, the illustrious martyr.  
Buried in the very sight of the towers,  
The Virgin preserves the salvation of the Quirites.

A double crown was granted to the martyr,  
A virgin untouched by every sin:  
Then, free in the glory of death,  
She offered herself willingly and did not refuse to die.

When Agnes saw the savage man standing  
With drawn sword, she said more joyfully:  
“Now call the soul that follows you, Christ,  
Along with the virginal sacrifice to the Father.”

Having spoken thus, she worships Christ  
With bowed head and supplication,  
So that her neck might more readily undergo  
The impending wound;  
But he completes such great hope by his hand.

Noble inhabitant of the heavenly citadel,  
Turn your attention to our defilements  
With a face bearing a twin diadem,  
You to whom the universal Father alone gave power.

To the unique Trinity be glory,  
Virtue, power, and supreme might,  
Holding the kingdom—for he is the one God—  
Throughout all ages of ages.

Amen.

**Supplication:** Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world. Folio CLXXXII. With the names changed.

**[CXCVI] Chapters**

Be present, O Lord, to those supplicating you, and meet those invoking your holy name with favor. Through the intervention of the holy virgins and martyrs Agnes and Emerentiana, grant that the raised-up and redeemed may rejoice forever. As we confess that we have been redeemed by the pouring out of the mixed chalice, lead us through its transformation from this lowliness to eternal glory.

**Our Father. Deliver us from evil.** Folio 2.

### Blessing

May Christ the Lord, who espoused his virgins Agnes and Emerentiana to himself in chaste love, join you inseparably to his charity. **R.** Amen.

May he who bestowed upon them the gift of virginity bestow upon you the fullness of his grace. **R.** Amen.

May you who do not shine with the beauty of virginity obtain joys through the merits of the virgins. **R.** Amen.

Through the mercy of our God, etc.

**Praise:** The daughters of Jerusalem have been exalted. **P.** And they proceeded in glory. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. **V.** Let Mount Zion rejoice, and let the daughters of Judah exult because of your judgments, O Lord. **P.** And they proceeded. **V.** Glory and honor. **P.** And they proceeded.

### Prayer

O God, who declare that the fruits of these your virgins Agnes and Emerentiana are not earthly but divine, grant through their intercession that we may not savor earthly things but, with cleansed heart, await heavenly things. May we who devoutly celebrate the feast of these virgins be cleansed from the filth of our offenses. **Response:** Amen.

Through your mercy, our God, etc.

In the name of our Lord.

## At Matins

**[Col. 1051A]**

**Antiphon:** Give us joy.

**Psalm:** L.

**Prayer:** Restore to us, O Lord, our joy. Folio CLXIII.

### Antiphon 1

The Lord, who said, “Let light shine from darkness,” has shone in our hearts, **P.** to shine for the illumination of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ. **V.** Let us go before his face in confession, and let us sing joyfully to him in psalms. **P.** To shine. **V.** Glory and honor. **P.** To shine.

### Prayer

O God, shining in the hearts of these your virgins and martyrs Agnes and Emerentiana, you caused light to shine from darkness, so that those who had been corrupted by nature might be illuminated by grace: shine in our hearts for the benefit of eternal salvation, so that, after the darkness of our vices has been wiped away, only the everlasting brightness of your light may possess us. **Response:** Amen.

Through mercy.

### Antiphon 2

With unveiled face, we all behold the glory of the Lord, and we are transformed into the same image, from glory to glory, as by the Spirit of the Lord. We do not walk **P.** in cunning, nor do we adulterate the word of God, but in the manifestation of truth. **V.** Sing to the Lord a new song; sing well to him with jubilation. **P.** In cunning. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father. **P.** In cunning.

### Prayer

Beholding your glory with unveiled face, Christ the Lord, we ask and beseech you to grant that we may be transformed more perfectly from the glory of hope into the glory of that perfected reality. Just as your virgins Agnes and Emerentiana, advancing from the virtue of suffering to the virtue of eternity, were transferred from glory to glory, so may we live blessedly in this hope in which we stand; and when we pass from this life to that one, may we reign with you without end. **Response:** Amen.

Through your mercy.

### Antiphon 3

Hear me, divine fruits, and bless the Lord, **P.** and confess him with the voice of our lips, and say: Alleluia, alleluia. **V.** Sing and praise him; recount all his wonders. **P.** And confess him. **V.** Glory and honor to the Father. **P.** And confess him.

### Prayer

O God, who [of these your virgins Agnes, etc.]. See above in the Vespers for this feast.

[Col. 1051D] **R.** “The kingdom of heaven is like ten virgins who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.”  
**P.** “And those who were ready entered with him into the marriage feast, and the door was shut.”  
**V.** “At midnight a cry was raised: Behold, the bridegroom is coming; go out to meet him.”  
**P.** “And those who were ready.”  
**V.** “Glory and honor to the Father.”  
**P.** “And those who were ready.”

**Prayer.** Make us, Lord Jesus Christ, preserve the oil of joy in the vessels of our conscience with pure integrity of mind, so that, when the cry is raised, we may go out to meet you, the Bridegroom, when you come to judgment, and may be counted among the wise Virgins to be crowned, not among the foolish. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy, our God, and so forth.

## Hymn

He also protects even strangers  
Who supplicate with a pure and faithful heart;  
A double crown has been granted to the Martyr:  
Virginal integrity untouched by every crime,  
And then the glory of a freely chosen death.

[Col. 1052B] They say that the little girl was scarcely fit  
For the marriage bed in her earliest years,  
Yet she burned fiercely for Christ  
And resisted the commands of the impious,  
So that she would not abandon the holy faith  
And become devoted to idols.

For she had first been tested by two methods:  
Now by the flattering speech of a deceptive judge,  
Now by the threats of a raging executioner.  
She stood firm with fierce strength  
And willingly offered her body  
To harsh tortures, refusing not to die.

Then the savage tyrant said: “If it is easy,  
Endure punishment under the torment of pain,  
Since a worthless life is despised. But her modesty,  
Her consecrated virginity, must be attacked.

[Col. 1052C] It is decided: she shall be handed over  
To a public brothel, unless she bows her head  
At the altar and now begs Minerva for pardon—  
Minerva whom the virgin persists in despising,  
Though she too is called a virgin.  
All the young men will rush upon her  
And seek this new object of mockery.”

“Christ,” said Agnes, “is not so forgetful  
Of his own that he should destroy our golden modesty  
Or abandon us.  
He is present to the chaste and does not permit  
The gifts of sacred purity to be defiled.

With the sword, impious offspring, you may do your work;  
You shall not pollute my limbs with lust.”

After she had spoken thus publicly, he ordered  
The virgin to be placed naked in the streets.  
The sorrowful crowd stood back, turning away its faces,  
Lest anyone should gaze too shamelessly  
Upon the place that ought to be revered.

One man, perhaps insolently, fixed his gaze  
Upon the girl and did not fear to behold  
Her sacred beauty with lustful eyes.  
The fire of Gehenna, blazing like a flame,  
Flashed forth and struck his eyes.  
Blinded by the flashing light, he fell  
And writhed in the dust of the street.

Her companions lifted him, half-dead, from the ground  
And mourned him with funeral words.  
The virgin went forth in triumph, singing  
To God the Father and to Christ in sacred song,  
Because, beneath the stain of profane danger,  
Her victorious virginity had remained chaste  
In a brothel that could not violate it.

[Col. 1053A] Some have reported that, when asked,  
She poured out prayers to Christ, asking him  
To restore light to the condemned man lying there.  
Then he found breath and received life anew,  
Restored to unimpaired use of his faculties.  
But Agnes gained this distinction:  
Soon another place in the heavenly court was granted her.

The enemy, inflamed with anger—for fury drives him—  
Groaned: “I am conquered. Draw your sword, soldier,  
And carry out the royal commands  
Of the supreme Prince.”

When Agnes saw the savage man standing there  
With naked sword, she spoke more joyfully:

[Col. 1053B] “I rejoice that such a man has come to me:  
A mad, savage, turbulent armed man,  
Rather than a weak and tender youth,  
A soft ephebe perfumed with spices,  
Who would destroy me through the death of my modesty.

This is the lover—now I confess it—who pleases me.  
I shall go to meet him with rushing steps;  
I shall not delay my burning desire.  
I shall receive the whole sword into my breasts;  
My breast shall take the sword’s force; I shall draw the sword.

Thus, wedded to Christ, I shall leap beyond the heavens,  
Higher than all darkness, higher than the ether.

Eternal Ruler, open the gates of heaven,  
Previously barred to those born on earth,  
And call to yourself the soul that follows you, Christ,  
Together with the Father’s virginal victim.”

Having spoken thus, she reverently adores Christ  
With bowed head, so that her neck may more readily  
Submit to the approaching wound.

But he completes so great a hope with his hand.  
At a single blow he cuts off her head;  
Swift death forestalls the sensation of pain.  
Her spirit, released, leaps forth,  
And, free, springs into the air; angels  
Surround her as she goes along a shining path.

She marvels at the world placed beneath her feet;  
From on high she gazes upon the subdued darkness;  
She laughs at what the sun’s wheel encompasses,  
At what the whole world turns and entangles,  
At the life lived amid the dark whirlwind of things,  
At what the empty instability of the age carries away—

[CXCVIII] Kings, tyrants, governments, and ranks,  
The pomp of foolishly swelling honors,  
The raging thirst for silver and gold,  
Sought by all through varied wickedness,  
Habitations built with abundant splendor,  
The empty illusions of painted clothing,  
Anger, death, vows, and dangers,  
Now prolonged sorrow, now brief joy,  
The smoky torches of black envy,  
From which the hope and glory of humankind grow dark—

And, worst of all evils,  
The filthy clouds of paganism.

Agnes tramples these and crushes them underfoot,  
Standing and pressing the dragon’s head with her heel:  
The dragon of the world, savage, who scatters everything  
With poisons and plunges it into the depths below.

Now subdued by a virgin’s foot alone,  
He lowers Cerberus’ fiery crests  
And, conquered, dares not lift his head.  
Meanwhile God encircles the forehead  
Of the unmarried Martyr with two crowns:  
One, produced thirtyfold six times,  
Completes its reward in everlasting light;  
The other yields a hundredfold fruit.

O blessed virgin, O new glory,  
Make even the brothel itself chaste.  
Cleanse our hearts with your propitiating radiance;  
If you fill our inward parts,  
Nothing is unchaste where your holy inward parts are present.

Deign even with your gracious foot to touch  
The vows that your devout people dedicate to you;  
And cleanse from sins the little servants  
Whom you see singing your joys.

Flying swiftly upward on rapid wings,  
Send joys down to the peoples  
Who, by your gift, sing as your citizens;  
Grant us all to live through the ages.

To the one Trinity be unique glory,  
Strength, power, and supreme might;  
To him who, being the one God, retains the kingdom  
Throughout all ages of ages.

Amen.

**Supplication.** “Let us pray to the Redeemer.” With the names changed. [Col. 1054C] Folio CLXXXII.

**Chapters.** Almighty God, who in ineffable goodness redeems all things: through the intercession of the holy virgins Agnes and Emerentiana, incline the ear of your mercy to our prayer; and against the bitterest darts of the invisible enemy extend to us victorious protection and faithful weapons, so that we who direct the height of our heart toward the loftiness of your throne may, in this lowly earthly condition, be saved from the assembly of the wicked through the protection of true faith, most mercifully.

**Our Father.** “Delivered from evil.” Folio 2.

**Lauda.** “The daughters of Jerusalem have been exalted.”  
**P.** “And they went forth in glory. Alleluia, alleluia.”  
**V.** “Let Mount Zion rejoice; let the daughters of Judah exult because of your judgments, Lord.”  
**P.** “And they went forth.”  
**V.** “Glory and honor.” [Col. 1054D]  
**P.** “And they went forth.”

**Blessing.** May the Lord Jesus Christ, who preserved his virgins Agnes and Emerentiana for himself in chaste purity, enrich us with the gift of chastity. **R.** Amen. And may he who betrothed them to himself with the ring of faith bind us indissolubly to his love. **R.** Amen. May he admit as intercessors for us those whom he took as brides for himself in incorruptible love. **R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

## Hymn

O triple honor, O threefold summit,  
By which the head of our city is raised,  
Towering above all Iberian cities,  
Under whose protection we are all nurtured.

The choir standing around, of both sexes,  
Sing your Fructuosus rightly;  
Let the hymn resound in praise of Augurius,  
Making Eulogius equal in blended melodies.

These men enter amid the swift, crackling fires,  
Advancing step by step, and themselves threaten  
The crackling furnaces of the flames—  
Whom the eternal fire will one day flee.

Happy souls, to whom it has been granted  
To climb through fire to the heights of the Thunderer!  
Pray to Christ for all peoples,  
That he may shield us from the Tartarean fire.

[Col. 1055D] Glory to the eternal Father, to Christ  
Ever begotten, and to you, equal Spirit;  
You who are one God, illustrious,  
Prevail through everlasting ages.

Amen.

**Supplication.** “Let us pray to the Redeemer.” With the names changed. See folio CLXII.

**Chapters.** Your three Saints’ life and feast, Lord, have been sufficiently tested, like bright gold shining as metal. While you assay their faith in the proving furnace, you assign it to yourself as pleasing through your praiseworthy judgment. Thus, in these three sheaves of priests whom our mother the Church sent to you, you possess offices of the priesthood distinguished in rank but venerable in service. In Fructuosus the pontifical grace shines; in Augurius and Eulogius the ministry of Levitical dignity gleams. Therefore let them present our vows for sanctification before your gaze: let the former adorn what is to be consecrated for you according to the custom of the priesthood; through the ministry of the latter may we receive the saving chalice unto life; sanctified by the invocation of the former, may we be brought to glory.

[Col. 1056A] **Our Father.** “Delivered from evil.” Folio 2.

**Blessing.** May Christ, the Son of God, who deigned to show himself as the fourth man to the three boys placed in the furnace, enlighten you with the grace of seeing him. **R.** Amen. And may he who did not allow Fructuosus, the priest, together with his deacons, to be extinguished amid the crackling fires by the heat of his love, not permit you to be burned by any fire of temptation. **R.** Amen. May you also receive, in the land of the living, the refreshment which they deserved to receive after the fires of this age. **R.** Amen.

Through his mercy.

**Lauda.** “The righteous cried out, and the Lord heard them. Alleluia.”  
**P.** “And he delivered them from all their afflictions. Alleluia, alleluia.”  
**V.** “Many are the tribulations of the righteous, and the Lord delivered them from them all.”  
**P.** “And he delivered them.”  
**V.** “Glory and honor.”  
**P.** “And he delivered them.”

**Prayer.** The steadfastness of your three priests, Lord, is truly marvelous: Fructuosus the Bishop, and Augurius and Eulogius the Levites. Their devotion was united and not divided. While they were prepared to be burned by the kindling of the furnace, they steadfastly endured the burning with manly courage, burning more intensely with love for you than they were overcome by the alien fire. Although their bodies yielded to the flames, their victorious souls were snatched into the ether. Grant, therefore, that by their merits we may not be touched by the fire of temptations, may be rescued from eternal flames, and, after the course of this age, may be joined to you with hearts aflame with desire. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy, and so forth.

In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.

Since they burned more intensely through your power, the fire brought against them could not harm them. Rescue us, therefore, from the fires of vice, and kindle us with the warmth of virtues, so that, made exceedingly hot by the fire of your charity, we may deserve to carry off victory from the world. **R.** Amen.

**Prayer.** Lord Jesus Christ, who deigned to visit your Saints in the midst of the fire, when you took from the midst of the flame those whom you knew to have completed martyrdom while fighting manfully for you, in order to crown them: rescue our life from the furnace of wicked deeds, and visit us with the consolations of your graces, so that with these three Martyrs we may deserve to have a share in the heavenly places, with whom we are recognized as companions not in suffering but in faith. **R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**Antiphon 1.** “Ananias, Azarias, Misael, bless God.”  
**P.** “Who delivered you from the furnace of blazing fire.” [Col. 1057D]  
**V.** “Exult in God our helper; shout for joy to the God of Jacob.”  
**P.** “Who delivered you.”  
**V.** “Glory and honor to the Father.”  
**P.** “Who delivered you.”

**Prayer.** Ananias, Azarias, and Misael, those three boys tested by Babylonian fire, gave a great example to the holy martyrs, Lord, whose revered victory became their example. In the former, the fire withdrew so that they would not die; in the latter, it was admitted so that they might be crowned. In the former, while the time of their passion had not yet fully arrived, the punitive fire could not touch their consecrated bodies; in the latter, when the appointed time had come, when the way to paradise already stood open through Christ’s death, the fire consumed their bodies precisely when the gate of paradise had already been opened to the blessed.

Therefore we bless you, God, who both rescued the former from the flames and crowned the latter after the flames; who scattered fires for the deliverance of the former and admitted fires for the taking up of the latter. Grant us, through the examples and intercessions of both groups, to be so delivered from the fire of bodily vices that, burned by the sweetness of your fiery words, we may deserve to reach you in peace. **R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**Antiphon 2.** “Ananias, Azarias, and Misael, servants of the Most High God.”  
**P.** “Great is the Lord, who delivered us from the fire.”

**Prayer.** O most blessed Martyrs of Christ, servants of the Most High God: great is the Lord, who did not wish to rescue you from the fire so that the life of this age might remain in you. Since, therefore, amid the heat of the fires you deserved eternal life, shelter us continually by your prayer amid the vapors of this age. **R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**Antiphon 3.** “Ananias, Azarias, and Misael, fearing the Lord, who rescued them from the midst of the burning flame.”

**Prayer.** Behold, like those three boys, these martyrs of yours also, placed in the fires of this age and standing in the furnace for your name, praise you, Lord, with a similar manner of devotion. They, fearing you as Lord, sing to you a song of glory because you rescued them from the midst of the burning flame. These, however, do not offer a prayer of praise in order not to be touched by fire; rather, so that they may be crowned by you through the torments of fire, they bring you a hymn with freedom of conscience. Grant us, therefore, as we lead the course of our life in peace, to be free from the fires of lust and to deserve deliverance from future punishments. **R.** Amen.

**Antiphon 1.** “We make it known to you, O king, that we do not worship your gods, nor do we adore the images that you have set up.”

Through mercy.

**Antiphon 2.** “The fire that you, O king, threaten us with, our God in heaven is able to rescue us from.”

**P.** “But if he does not wish to.”

**Prayer.** The fire that was not only threatened but also prepared by persecutors to burn your Saints, Lord, brought them a marvelous shortcut to victory: the very hastening of punishment swiftly directed them toward the completion of victory. Since they were quickly burned by the flames, they thereby deserved to climb all the more quickly to the step of the crown. We ask, therefore, that by the merits of your Martyrs that future fire prepared for the torments of the impious dare in no way touch us; but, delivered by the power of the banner of your divinity, may we deserve to receive the scepter of the heavenly kingdom. **R.** Amen.

Grant us, therefore, through the intercession of your Martyrs, that, journeying through the darkness of this age under the guidance of your light, we may reach the heavenly dwellings in happiness. **R.** Amen.

**Prayer.** God, who wished to test your Saints on earth through the customary trial of your kindness, and do not permit them to be tested beyond what you foresee can be endured in them by the gift of your grace: rescue us from every temptation that could overwhelm our mind, so that, serving you faithfully in a way pleasing to you, you may permit us to be tested in such a manner that the temptation itself may bind us firmly not to the confusion of error but to the embrace of truth. **R.** Amen.

Through.
