**Prayer.** God, who wished to subject your Saints to many human torments so that they might gain profit from patience and a trophy from suffering: rescue us from the punishments of hell, so that devotion pleasing to you may unite us to you here, and in the future the faith by which we believe in you may bring us into eternal dwellings. **R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**Antiphon 2.** “How greatly the enemy has acted wickedly against your Saints; and those who hate you have gloried in the midst of your court.”  
**P.** “Raise your hand, Lord, against their pride to the end.”  
**V.** “They set your sanctuary on fire; on earth they defiled the dwelling of your name.”  
**P.** “They raised up.”  
**V.** “Glory.”  
**P.** “They raised up.”

**Prayer.** Lord Jesus Christ, by whose power your holy Martyrs extinguished the rotating force of fire and practiced righteousness: grant your favor and mercy to us sinners, so that through the faith by which the Saints conquered kingdoms, we sinners may deserve to obtain heavenly fellowship. **R.** Amen.

Through.

[CCIII] **Antiphon 3.** “Your Saints, Lord, exulted like sheep.”  
**P.** “Glorifying you, because you delivered them.”  
**V.** “Lord, they shall walk in the light of your face, and in your name they shall exult all day; and in your righteousness they shall rejoice.” [Col. 1061C]  
**P.** “Glorifying.”  
**V.** “Glory and honor to the Father.”  
**P.** “Glorifying.”

**Prayer.** God, who filled the devout hearts of your Martyrs with ineffable splendor, so that they earned crowns shining by your gift, as though here they had purchased the grace of hope through suffering and there deserved to receive them from you as a reward: make us shine and gleam through a sweetness toward our neighbors that is pleasing to you and through the excellence of perfected works, so that, even if we do not deserve to receive crowns through the shedding of blood, we may deserve to obtain from you a perpetual inheritance through the fruit of true love. **R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**R.** “Blessed are the eyes that see what you see, and the ears that hear what you hear, because you have remained with me through many tribulations, says the Lord.”  
[Col. 1061D] **P.** “Amen, I say to you: it has been given to you to know the mystery of the kingdom of heaven, and your names are written in heaven. Alleluia.”  
**V.** “Come, blessed of my Father; possess the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.”  
**P.** “Amen, I say to you.”  
**V.** “Glory.”  
**P.** “Amen.”

**Prayer.** Be present to us, Almighty God, as we celebrate the triumphant day of your Saints Fructuosus, Augurius, and Eulogius; grant us the joy of spiritual gladness; and through their intercession grant rest to the buried and safety to the bodies of those who offer [them] to you. Their faith burned so fiercely in their limbs as those limbs were consumed by fire that they felt the weakness of corruptible nature but did not know how to alter the purpose of their heavenly spirit. **R.** Amen.

Through.

## At Lauds

[Col. 1062A]

**At the Canticle. Antiphon.** “Those who love you, Lord, shine like the sun, resplendent at its rising; so they gleam.”

**Canticle.** “You who offered yourselves willingly.” Folio CLXIII.

**At the Benedictus. Antiphon.** “The three boys were thrown into the furnace at the king’s command; without fearing the flame of the fire, they said: Blessed are you.”  
**V.** “These three, as though with one voice, sang to the great King and said: Blessed are you.”

**Canticle.** “Blessed are you, Lord.” Folio 6.

**Sono.** “When the furnace was being heated.” See above, in the preceding Vespers.

**Lauda.** “Praise the Lord from the heavens. Alleluia, alleluia; praise him in the heights. Alleluia.” Psalm CXLVIII.

[Col. 1062B] **Prophecy. Reading from the Book of the Wisdom of Solomon, chapter XVI.**

**R.** Thanks be to God.

The righteous suffered worthy torments and were destroyed by a multitude of wild beasts. For these torments you provided well for your people, granting them the desire for their delight and preparing for them a new-tasting food, quail. Thus, while they desired the food because of what had been shown and sent to them, they were also turned away from necessary desire. But these, having quickly become destitute, tasted a new food. For destruction had to come upon those who exercised tyranny without excuse, while for the others it was necessary only to show how their enemies were destroyed.

For while the savage anger of beasts came upon them, they were destroyed by the bites of crooked serpents. Your anger did not continue forever, but they were troubled for a short time as correction, possessing a sign of salvation as a reminder of the commandment of your law. For the one who turned toward it was not healed by what he saw, but by you, the Savior of all. **R.** Amen.

## Hymn

Happy Tarragona, you are clothed in Fructuosus;  
The choir raises its head toward the fires,  
Shining afar with the two Levites beside him.  
Through these holy men God looks upon us kindly.

For when the powerful Trinity crowns  
The Iberian citadel with a threefold Martyr,  
Burning Augurius rises to the ether;  
And Eulogius too, shining, reaches together  
The heavenly seat of Christ.

Their leader, guide, and teacher,  
Fructuosus, illustrious in his episcopal name,  
Went before them to such great glory.

Because he had been summoned suddenly  
By the governor’s command, the priest  
Had come to the forum with two Levites beside him.  
From there the executioner, sated with blood,  
Dragged the men toward the prison in chains.  
Fructuosus rejoiced to run forward of his own accord.

And, lest fear strike his companions,  
The ardent teacher strengthened them as they went  
And kindled their faith with the warmth of Christ.

[Col. 1063A] “Stand with me, men: the bloody serpent  
Calls the ministers of God to punishment.  
Let death not terrify you; behold, the palm is ready.

Prison is a step toward the crown for Christ’s people;  
Prison leads upward to the heights of heaven;  
Prison reconciles the blessed to God.”

After these words they approached the den of the condemned.  
There they performed a mystical washing,  
A cleansing in water; the darkness was amazed.

For six continuous days they lay hidden there;  
At last they stood before the tribunal of the savage enemy.  
The racks tremble before the three brothers.

Judge Aemilianus confronted them,  
Savage, turbulent, insolent, profane;  
He ordered the demonic altars to be worshiped.

[Col. 1063B] “You who are a teacher,” he said, “are sowing  
A new kind of invention, so that foolish girls  
May abandon the groves and leave Jupiter.  
If you are wise, condemn the doctrine of Augustus.  
It has been ordered by the voice of Caesar Gallienus:  
What the prince worships, let us all worship.”

While he was speaking thus, the calm priest replied:

“I worship the eternal Prince,  
The maker of days and lord of Gallienus,  
And Christ, begotten from the everlasting Father,  
Whose servant I am and shepherd of his flock.”

Smiling, the other said: “You once were.”

His fury neither delayed nor restrained its anger.  
He assigned them to be burned in savage fires;  
They exulted and forbade the crowd to weep.

[Col. 1063C] The priest saw certain people from the crowd  
Offering him a cup to drink.

“We are fasting,” he said; “I refuse the drink.  
The ninth hour has not yet released the day.  
I shall never violate the appointed law,  
Nor will death itself dissolve my sacred observance.  
Thus Christ, thirsting at the hour of the Cross,  
Refused the cup offered to him  
And, unwilling to drink, completed his thirst.”

Meanwhile they entered a place enclosed  
By a rounded cage, wet with the abundant blood  
Of beasts, which frenzy continually renewed  
While the bloody spectacles resounded.

A lowly gladiator, struck by a hard sword,  
Falls, and pleasure roars.

[Col. 1063D] Here, beside the blazing pyre, a black servant,  
Ordered to prepare the burning punishment,  
Built the pyre with bundles for the final fire.  
When he released the bodies to be burned,  
He would free the souls, burning with love of light,  
From the shattered cavern of the prison.

The devout companions competed in service.  
With sandals loosened by the straps,  
One bent down, eager to remove them.

But holy Fructuosus forbade it and said:  
“Do not press down with bowed faces; go away,  
Lest your service burden our death.

Rather, let me loosen my own feet,  
Lest my steps, hindered by slow bonds,  
Fall into the fire with delayed movement.

Why do your tears wet your drenched cheeks?  
Why do you ask me to remember you?  
I shall pray to Christ for all peoples.”

He had scarcely spoken these words when he himself  
Loosened the coverings of his feet, just as Moses  
Had once done when he approached the bush:  
No one was permitted to tread upon the sacred burning  
Or stand before God until pure feet had been planted there.

He stood with bare feet. Behold, his spirit  
Rang out toward heaven and uttered words  
That made all who heard them tremble:

“Believe me, the punishment you see  
Is no punishment; it passes swiftly in a brief moment.  
It does not seize life but renews it.

[Col. 1064B] Happy souls, to whom it has been granted  
To climb through fire to the heights of the Thunderer—  
Whom the eternal fire will one day flee.”

Amid these swiftly crackling fires  
They enter with measured steps  
And themselves threaten the crackling furnaces of flame.

At last the bonds that had repeatedly fastened  
Their hands behind their backs  
Fall away, their skin untouched, burned through.

The punishment did not dare restrain their hands  
From being raised to the Father in the manner of the Cross;  
It released the arms that prayed to God.

You might have thought them an example  
Of the three men of old whom the trembling tyrant  
Once saw singing amid Babylonian fire.

But the holy flame then spared those men,  
Since the time suitable for their passion had not yet come  
And Christ had not yet begun the glory of death.

These men, when the vaporous heat withdrew,  
Prayed that the swift fire would hasten upon them  
And bring an end to their anxious dangers.

Having been entreated, at last it began to go to meet its own … [the sentence is incomplete in the source].

Majesty commands the servants, sent away from their perishable bodies, to be restored to himself.

From the governor’s house the officer saw heaven opened wide for the martyrs, and distinguished men carried through the stars.

Moreover, warning the little daughter of her master, he displayed the mark of her father’s crime: those whom the savage man had slain were living in heaven.

Then that virginity was granted openly to see the faithless, blind father, so that the household might fear the Lord’s crime.

Then the ashes of the sacred bodies and the bones washed with wine are gathered, while each person eagerly claimed a portion for himself.

So great was the brothers’ love of bringing home the dedicated gifts of the saints’ ashes, or of carrying a faithful pledge in their bosom.

But they also decreed that the remains, destined to be raised again and soon to be with the Lord, should be divided among separate tombs by location:

bowed down, clothed in white robes, they ordered them to be restored and the corpses to be enclosed, to be consecrated with dust mixed with marble.

O triple honor, O threefold summit, by which the head of our city is raised, surpassing all the cities of Iberia!

It is fitting to exult in the three Patrons, under whose protection all the peoples of the Pyrenean lands are sheltered.

Let a choir of both sexes stand around: hero, virgin, boy, old man, little maid.

Sing your Fructuosus duly; let the hymn resound in praise of Agurius; let us make Eulogius equal in blended strains; let us return equal Muses to equals.

From here let the gilded roofs in the citadel resound.

From there let the shore utter its gentle murmur, and let the seas at rest compose their song.

There will come a time when the world collapses, when Fructuosus will free you, Tarragona, from fierce punishment, shielding you from the fire.

Perhaps he will deign to grant healing even to my torments, with Christ prospering, as I roll forth sweet hendecasyllables,

and the chorus, dancing and mingling with heaven, lives through the ages in the ether.

Glory to the eternal Father; to Christ, eternally begotten, be glory always; and to you, coequal Spirit, who, one God, reign gloriously through everlasting ages.

[Col. 1065C] Amen.

Supplication. Let us pray, with the names changed, fol. CLXII.

Capitulum. Christ, Son of God, who wondrously stood by as deliverer when the three boys were placed in the furnace, and who shone forth in these three martyrs, Fructuosus, Agurius, and Eulogius, proven by fire: granting that the former might escape the death prepared for them in the furnace, and the latter find crowns when the flames extinguished their bodies; displaying in both groups distinct offices of grace, since the fire neither touched the former nor, touching the latter, crowned them all the more readily; suspending death from the former and consuming in the latter their laudable passion; the fire itself serving the wishes of both with obedient ministry, since it withdrew from the former so that they would not die, and came upon the latter so that the eagerly desired crown might arrive: grant us that, rejoicing in the holiness of both groups, we may celebrate the victories of the martyrs in such a way that we may rejoice with them in unending joy.

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.”

Lauda. “The column of fire.” Fol. CXCIX.

Benediction. May Christ the Lord, who led Bishop Fructuosus and his deacons, tested by fire, into the kingdom, make you, delivered from the furnace of lust, heirs of the kingdom of heaven. R. Amen. And may he who willed that the ashes of their bodies, taken up by the brothers, be gathered together for burial in one place, not divide you from the unity of holy mother Church. R. Amen. May he grant that you deserve to find him as deliverer amid the flames of desire, in whom they, after hunger, deserved to find refreshment. R. Amen.

[Col. 1066A] Through mercy.

In the name of the Lord.

## 22 January. On the feast of Saint Vincent, Levite and Martyr

### At Vespers

Lauda. “My soul has hoped.” Fol. CLVI.

Sono. “You are my hope, my portion in the land of the living.” P. “Attend, O God, to my prayer.” Alleluia. V. “In the sight of the Lord I shall pour out my prayer; before him I shall declare my tribulation. When my spirit failed within me, you knew it, Lord.” P. “Attend.” V. “On the path by which I walked they hid a snare for me. I looked to the right and saw, but there was no one who recognized me.” P. “Attend, O God.” V. “My escape has vanished from me, and there is no one who seeks my soul. Lord, I cried to you.” P. “Attend, O God.”

May the Lord be always with you. R. And with you.

Antiphon 1. “Deliver me, Lord, from the mire, so that I may not stick fast; let me be rescued from those who hate me.” P. “And from the depth of the waters. May the storm of water not overwhelm me, nor the deep swallow me.” V. “Save me, O God, for the waters have entered even to my soul.” P. “And from the depth.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “And from the depth.”

Prayer. O God, who wondrously crowned Vincent, conquering through many kinds of suffering, freeing him from every destructive torment, so that his footsteps, which had not adhered to the mire of vices, might wondrously trample every punishment of cruelty: lest he be swallowed by the depth of waters, who, trampling the world underfoot in mind, was already a near heir of heaven—grant us, through the prayers of so great a martyr, neither to be touched by the mire of vices nor overwhelmed by the deep chasm of despair; but may we be presented to you, adorned with the bright freedom of conscience, on the day of judgment. R. Amen.

May the Lord be with you. R. And with you.

Antiphon. “I was in many labors and in prison. Three times I was beaten with rods; night and day I was in the depth of the sea.” P. “And from all these things God delivered me; blessed is he through the ages.” V. “Those who hate me without cause have multiplied beyond the hairs of my head.” P. “And from all these things.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “And from all these things.”

May the Lord be with you. R. And with you.

[Col. 1066D] Lauda. “The waters surrounded me even to my soul.” Alleluia. P. “The sea enclosed me on every side; in the midst of the sea you finally delivered me, Lord.” Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V. “From the depths I cried to you, Lord; Lord, hear my voice.” P. “The sea enclosed me on every side.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “The sea.”

### Hymn

Here is the wondrous passion  
of the holy martyr Vincent, the Levite,  
to whom a bright crown, blazing  
with virtue, is given.

Blessed is that spirit  
which, after the triumph of battle,  
after the terrible chains of prison,  
the heavenly court receives.

All marvel forever at the martyr,  
after the bloodshed was accomplished,  
whom fragments of pottery  
wound with a sharp blade.

No pain breaks him,  
no punishment conquers him;  
bearing flames through the torturing claws,  
his steadfast faith remained.

After this they lay  
Christ’s faithful soldier  
upon soft things;  
leaving behind the burden of flesh,  
the spirit migrates to the stars.

The mad emperor orders  
the corpse to be thrown to wild beasts;  
but, with the raven as its guardian,  
wolfish hunger is driven from the body.

The tyrant is roused by a heavy fury  
and orders the martyr, sewn into  
a small bag, to be sunk  
into the deep sea.

Then the highest honor is rendered  
to the shore at Christ’s command;  
the waters having been calmed,  
he comes before all the rowers.

You alone, O doubly glorious one,  
alone have borne the palm  
of a double prize;  
you prepared two laurels at once.

Be present now and receive  
the suppliant voices of those who pray,  
an effective advocate for our guilt  
before the Father’s throne.

Through you, through that prison,  
an increase of your honor;  
through chains, flames, and torturing claws;  
through the prison stake;  
through that fragment of pottery  
by which your glory, once won, increased;  
through which, trembling descendants,  
we kiss your little bed.

Have mercy on our prayers,  
that Christ, appeased toward his own,  
may incline his favorable ear  
and not reckon all our offenses against us.

If we duly venerate  
the solemn day with mouth and heart,  
if in the joy of your footsteps  
we prostrate ourselves:

enter here for a little while,  
bringing Christ’s favor,  
so that those weighed down in mind  
may feel the relief of indulgence.

Thus no delay remains  
when the spirit resumes  
the noble flesh that has been raised,  
having fulfilled an equal virtue.

So that the flesh, which shared  
in the labors and bore the common danger,  
may also be a fellow-heir of glory  
through all ages forever.

Grant this, most merciful Father,  
and Only-Begotten One, equal to the Father,  
with the Spirit, the Paraclete,  
reigning through every age.

Amen.

[CCVII] Supplication. Let us pray, with the name changed. Fol. CLXVII.

Capitulum.

Here is present, Lord, your witness’s solemn and most famous feast, displayed annually before mortal eyes. In it, Vincent, your martyr, wondrously conquering, tested both on land and at sea, is conquered neither by earthly punishments nor bound by marine whirlpools; he conquers darkness and chains alike.

As a preacher of light, he is overcome neither by the punishments of bonds nor by the dark constraints of a remote prison; rather, because he had truly confessed the name of Truth, he saw the services of heavenly light ministering to him in truth.

Therefore, as we receive the solemn feast of so great a martyr with annual devotion, we ask that we may be rewarded by you for this reception, so that through the intervention of the aforesaid martyr you may remove from our borders plague and every harmful adversity; so that the earth may bring forth peaceful crops, and our souls may be warmed by the divine fountain of virtues; so that, when the works of darkness have been expelled, we may overcome every adversity in your light, Christ, and that here and in the future the joys desired in common may come to us—

you who grant us to pray and say:

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” Fol. 2.

Benediction. May Christ the Lord, who infused light and grace into Vincent, triumphing manfully and dwelling in a dark prison, visit us with his light in such a way that he may enrich us with the gift of eternal grace. R. Amen. May he who shone upon him amid the darkness of prison shine in your hearts, so that you may escape the punishments of future retribution. R. Amen. May he who was proved victorious in the very word of his name make us, through the prayers of his passion, companions in the heavenly kingdoms. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Lauda. “Your love remains like a fountain of life.” P. “And your wisdom like a golden ornament.” Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V. “He will not let your foot be moved, nor will he sleep who guards you.” P. “And your wisdom.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “And your wisdom.”

Prayer. O God, who wondrously promised to give conquering Vincent hidden manna, so that the one who had overcome every kind of torture inflicted on mortals might be enriched with the gift of immortality: grant us, through the merits of him who followed you in faith, name, and passion, that the new name bestowed upon us in the title of Christianity may both increase for us in this life the possession of good works and prepare for us in the future an eternal kingdom and joy without end. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

In the name of the Lord.

### At Matins

[Col. 1069A]

Antiphon. “Lord, open my lips, and my mouth shall proclaim your praise.” Psalm 50.

Prayer. “Let them rejoice, Lord.” Fol. CLXXX.

Antiphon 1. “You tested me, Lord, like gold; you placed tribulations upon my back.” P. “I passed through fire and water, and you led me into refreshment.” V. “I shall enter your house with burnt offerings; I shall fulfill my vows to you, which my lips declared, and my mouth spoke in my tribulation.” P. “I passed through.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “I passed through.”

Prayer. We bless you, almighty God, who freed your most blessed martyr Vincent, as once you freed the three boys, from the burning of fire. For although flame was applied to his limbs, it existed to burn but not to conquer. Pour, therefore, through his prayers, the dew of your mercy into our inward parts, so that, when the fire of carnal burning has been moistened, the flame of sin may grow lukewarm within us. Though that flame does not naturally cease from us, we ask that, materially kindled, it may not consume our frailty; rather, may grace so assist nature that by your gift we may extinguish what we lack by origin. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 2. “I am your protector; do not fear, says the Lord. If you pass through fire, it will not burn you.” P. “The rivers will not overwhelm you, because I shall hold your hand.” V. “By day the sun will not burn you, nor the moon by night.” P. “The rivers.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “The rivers.”

[Col. 1069C] Prayer. Christ, Son of God, protector of the most blessed and glorious martyr Vincent, who wondrously sustained his hand as an act of help and did not allow him to be burned by flames or overcome by waters: grant that the fires of lust may not defile us in any way, nor the blasts of hatred disturb us in any way; but may we also be helped by the right hand of your protection, by which your witness was assisted to overcome the dangers of the sea, so that we may not come into future punishment. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 3. “The Lord chose me as one of the princes and appointed me as a strong man for battle.” P. “The Lord gave me a white robe and adorned me with a crown.” V. “Blessed be the Lord my God, who trains my hands for war and my fingers for battle.” P. “The Lord gave me.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “The Lord gave me.”

Prayer. Almighty God, who honored your martyr with an eternal name and chose him from among princes in his passion, so that the one who had endured the envy of those blaspheming because of your name might, in your name, receive the service of those who praise you, and so that you might adorn him with a crown: grant, therefore, to your rejoicing servants the unfailing help of the triumphant one, so that, through his persistent intercession, he may restore the badly torn garments of baptism. You clothed him in a robe of honor spattered with the blood of martyrdom when he fought for you. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

“You tested me, Lord, as silver is tested. You placed tribulations upon my back; I passed through fire and water, and you led me into refreshment. I shall enter the house of the Lord.” P. “Who heard my prayer.” V. “Come and hear, all you who fear God, and I shall tell you how much he has done for my soul.” P. “Who heard.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “Who.”

Prayer. O God, who willed that your saint be tested on earth by the customary test of your goodness, and do not permit him to be tested beyond what you foresee has been granted to him as a gift of endurance by your bounty: rescue us from every temptation that could overwhelm our mind, so that, serving you faithfully with service pleasing to you, you may permit us to be tested in such a way that the temptation itself may bind us firmly, not in the confusion of sorrow, but in the embrace of truth. R. Amen.

[Col. 1070B] Through mercy.

Antiphon 1. “I called you by your name, says the Lord. If you cross the waters, the rivers will not overwhelm you.” P. “And if you begin to pass through fire, the flame will not burn you.” V. “You shall eat the labors of your fruits; you are blessed, and it shall be well with you.” P. “And if you begin to pass through fire.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “And if you begin to pass through fire.”

Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ, who declare by the very name that the martyr Vincent belongs to you, since he conquered for you while serving under your name, both in crossing waters and in the burning of fires; since you deign to be present with him and, by your help, make him unconquerable in those very sufferings: we ask your mercy to protect us through our supplications, so that you who in him conquered the weight of water may also extinguish from us the flames of eternal fires. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 2. “Perfection and instruction belong to your holy man, whom you tested, Lord, in temptation. They shall place incense before you.” P. “And he shall burn incense upon your altar.” V. “You granted him the desire of his soul, and you did not deprive him of the request of his lips.” P. “And he shall burn.” V. “Glory and honor to the Father.” P. “And he shall burn.”

Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ, who are the head of your Church, grant that your most blessed martyr Vincent, established in the body of the Church, who then gave his limbs for the Head, may now never cease to approach the Head on behalf of the members; and, being close to the Head, may he guide and protect the whole body, expending more abundantly what he rejoices to have obtained more happily. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 3. “Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.” P. “To Vincent I shall give to eat from the tree of life, which is in the paradise of my God.” V. “For my hand shall assist him, and my arm shall strengthen him.” P. “To Vincent.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “To Vincent.”

Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ, who deigned to give your most blessed martyr Vincent an ear of obedience, by which, with the healthy understanding of his heart, he might recognize what the Spirit was saying to him: grant us, through his merits, to eat from the tree of life and receive the fruit of everlasting inheritance, so that we may deserve to become citizens of your Paradise, as we now celebrate with the deepest devotion the passion of your martyr. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

R. “I called you by your name; you are mine. If you cross the waters, I am with you, and the rivers will not overwhelm you.” P. “If you begin to pass through fire, the flame will not defile you.” V. “And I gave men in your place, and peoples for your soul. Do not fear, my most upright servant, whom I chose.” P. “If you begin to pass through fire.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “If you begin to pass through fire.”

Prayer. Almighty Lord, who permitted your most blessed martyr Vincent to be tested, like heaps of threatening waves, by the goads of suffering, but not to be overwhelmed; although, while he fought, punishment did not overcome him, nor did the wave suppress him when immersed: because you were present with him there also, lest he be conquered by tortures, and here you granted that he be carried against nature upon the waves—grant faith to all through such great miracles, so that the prayers of those who celebrate may be most devoutly fulfilled. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 1. “Whoever conquers and keeps my works to the end,” P. “I shall give him authority over the nations, and he shall rule them with an iron rod.” V. “And I shall place his hand upon the sea, and his right hand upon the rivers.” P. “I shall give him.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “I shall give him.”

Prayer. Lord God, graciously grant that your most blessed martyr Vincent may, by his merits, conquer our sins; he who was able to overcome the punishments of raging men not by his own but by divine powers. May he who once conquered the cruelty of impiety in them overcome in us the will of evil desire. R. Amen.

Through your mercy, etc.

Antiphon 2. “Draw near to me, peoples, and gather yourselves into the house of the discipline of our God. See the glory of Vincent, for because of what he labored he found abundant rest; in doing it he was strengthened.” P. “Let our soul rejoice in the mercy of God.” V. “Magnify the Lord with me, and let us exalt his name together.” P. “Let our soul rejoice.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “Let our soul rejoice.”

Prayer. Only-Begotten Son of God the Father, who made your most blessed martyr Vincent, laboring in your name, rejoice in your mercy: we ask the power of your divinity that, in imitation of him, our vows for your name may be acceptable, and the effectiveness of our works may remain pleasing to you in all things; so that, conquering the dangers of the world, we may deserve to become the structure of an everlasting building. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 3. “Vincent shall be given the crown of life, and he shall not be harmed by death.” P. “But the morning star shall be given to him.” V. “And I shall make him my firstborn and exalted among the kings of the earth.” P. “But the morning star shall be given.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “But the morning star shall be given.”

Prayer. O God, who have always shown your power gloriously in the victor Vincent, in all his works and sufferings; since, for all these things, you enrich him with the crown of life and strengthen him, so that he may not be harmed by death, with the promise of the morning star—which, signifying the light of the resurrection, is called “morning” because it drives away night and announces light; since, when the world’s night has been driven away, the star of everlasting reward is promised—make us, therefore, Lord Jesus Christ, sharers in this morning star, so that, rejoicing in the consolation of your promise, we may reach unharmed the fruit of your righteousness. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

R. “To Vincent I shall give a crown, and I shall make him a pillar in the temple of God.” P. “I shall inscribe upon him the name of the city, Jerusalem, and my new name.” V. “Everyone who conquers I shall make sit upon the throne of my Father.” P. “I shall inscribe upon him.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “I shall inscribe upon him.”

Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ, who wondrously grant this martyr Vincent both a crown from victory and a place as a pillar in your temple, assigning him to be, as it were, an ornament of the building; since you both suggest to him the zeal for conquering that he may be crowned and lavish upon him an unconquered will of perseverance in his sufferings: grant us, following his example, an equal desire to love you and a will to conquer, so that the name of that new city, Jerusalem, may be inscribed upon our hearts in such a way that, while we continually fix our mind’s gaze upon its vision, we may rejoice forever in its peace. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

In the name of the Lord.

### At Lauds

For the Canticle. Antiphon. “The waters surrounded me even to my soul; the abyss enclosed me, the sea covered my head. I cried to you, Lord; hear me.”

Canticle. “I cried to the Lord.” Fol. 315.

For the Benedictus. Antiphon. “The blessing of the Lord hastens as the reward of the righteous.”

[CCX] Canticle. “Blessed are you.” Fol. 6.

Sono. “They cast me into the midst of the sea, and great calm came to me.” P. “For you delivered me, Lord, from the abyss and had mercy on me.” Alleluia, alleluia. V. “Those who go down to the sea in ships, doing their work upon many waters—they saw your wonders.” P. “For you delivered me.” V. “I became abhorrent in the midst of the water, and I dwelt in the heart of the sea, and I called upon you, Lord.” P. “For you delivered me.” V. “You commanded the storm, and it stood still in the breeze; the waves of the sea were tossed, and I rejoiced exceedingly.” P. “For you delivered me.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “For you delivered me.”

Lauda. “Praise the Lord from the heavens, alleluia; praise him in the heights.” Alleluia. Psalm 148.

Reading from the book of the prophet Isaiah (chapters XLIII–XLIV).

R. Thanks be to God.

Thus says the Lord, who created you, Jacob, and formed you, Israel: Do not fear, for I have redeemed you and called you by your name; you are mine. When you pass through the water, I shall be with you, and the rivers will not cover you; when you walk through fire, you will not be burned, and the flame will not burn you. For I am the Lord your God, the Holy One of Israel, your Savior. Since you have become honorable in my eyes and glorious, I have loved you; I shall give men in your place and peoples for your soul. Do not fear, for I am with you. Thus says the Lord, who makes and forms you, your helper from the womb: Do not fear, my most upright servant Jacob, whom I chose. For I shall pour water upon the thirsty and streams upon the dry ground; I shall pour my spirit upon your offspring and my blessing upon your descendants. And they shall sprout among the grasses like willows beside flowing waters. R. Amen.

### Hymn

Blessed Martyr, make prosperous  
the triumphant day  
on which the reward of blood,  
a crown, is given to you, Vincent.

This day raised you from the darkness  
of the world to heaven,  
with the torturer and judge defeated,  
and restored you rejoicing to Christ.

Now a companion of the angels,  
now marked by the distinguished robe of light,  
which, as an unconquered witness,  
you had washed in streams of blood.

When the officer of the Idol,  
girded with dark commands,  
ferociously compelled you with chains  
to sacrifice to the gods of the nations,

he poured out the gentle words  
of the rulers, softly persuading,  
lest a free life, torn away,  
fall into the torture chambers.

“The greatest king of the world,”  
he said, “who holds the Romulean scepters,  
has decreed that all must serve  
the ancient worship of the gods.

“You Nazarenes, stand forth,  
and reject your faith and rite.  
Appease with smoke and sacrifice  
these stones which the ruler worships.”

Then Vincent cries out,  
the Levite of the holy tribe,  
minister of the altar:  
“We worship the true God.

“Let those divinities rule over you;  
you worship stones, you worship wood;  
you, dead, become the dead  
pontiff of the gods.

“But we confess the Father,  
author of light,  
and his Son Christ,  
whom alone we confess as the true God,  
Datianus.”

Then the other man, already more enraged, said:

“Dare you, wretched man,  
to violate with harsh words  
the commands of the gods and rulers?

“The law is sacred and public,  
to which the human race yields.  
Does not even a child,  
when you ardently command it, fear danger?

“Take this decree:  
either from now on you must pray  
at the altar, with incense and turf,  
or you must pay the price of death in blood.”

The other replied:

“Come, then. Whatever strength,  
whatever power you possess,  
exercise it openly;  
I resist.

“Receive what our voice declares:  
Christ and the Father are God,  
and we are servants and witnesses of this one.  
If you can, extort our faith.

“Tortures, prison, claws,  
fire hissing amid flames,  
and death itself, the final punishment—  
for Christians these are sport.”

“In your madness you order your vanity  
and the shield of your Caesar—  
deities suited to your own understanding—  
to be worshiped.”

“Cut out by a craftsman’s hand,  
baked in hollow kilns and bellows,  
things without voice or movement,  
motionless, blind pieces of wood.

“For these sumptuous shrines  
rise in shining marble;  
for these the necks of bellowing bulls,  
struck down, fall.

“There are spirits there as well:  
teachers of crimes,  
and hunters of your salvation,  
wandering, powerless, filthy.

“Secretly they stir you  
and drive you into every wickedness,  
to destroy the righteous by slaughter  
and prey upon the people of the devout.

“They themselves know and feel  
that Christ prevails and lives,  
and that his terrifying kingdom  
is already at hand for the faithless.

“Finally, driven from the hiding places  
of bodies by the power and name of Christ,  
those same demons cry out openly.”

The impious judge could not endure  
the martyr thundering these words.  
He shouts: “Close his mouth,  
lest the criminal say more.

“Silence the voice of the speaker;  
seize him and hand him over to the lictors.  
Take him aside for the dogs to feed upon,  
and exercise your hands upon him.

“Let the reviler, fixed in the praetorium,  
feel this; lest anyone go unpunished  
who has ordered laws to be built  
for his gods.

“Must the Tarpeian rites  
be trampled by you alone in defiance?  
Must you alone crush Rome,  
the Senate, and the Caesars?”

With his arms twisted behind him,  
stretch him upward and downward  
until the joint of his bones,  
torn apart, creaks limb by limb.

After this, with diverse blows,  
the hidden parts of his exposed ribs  
are laid bare, so that through the gaps  
of his wounds his liver may palpitate, exposed.

The soldier of God laughed at this,  
rebuking the bloody hands  
because the claw did not enter  
more deeply into his limbs.

Now all the strength of his limbs  
had given way through evisceration,  
and the effort had loosened his sinews,  
the bulk of his exhausted arms.

But he was all the happier,  
seeing you, Christ, present,  
with his brow serene in light,  
free from every cloud.

“What is that face?”  
cried Datianus in furious shame.  
“He rejoices, bound,  
and provokes the torturer,  
though tortured more fiercely.

“All that force, exercised  
through the deaths of so many guilty men,  
accomplishes nothing in this contest;  
the art of the idols is conquered.

“But you, brood of the prison,” he says,  
“spare the unconquered man;  
hold back your right hands for a while,  
so that his weary strength may breathe.”

Again, through the dry wounds,  
while the scar gathered itself,  
the hand tears them open,  
furrowing the cooled blood.

The Levite replies to this:

“You see the strength of your dogs,  
your own men, growing weak.  
Come, you greater executioner yourself.

“Show how they can cut  
into the recesses,  
and put your own hands in;  
drink the flowing streams.

“You are mistaken, bloody man,  
if you think you are inflicting my punishment,  
when you kill limbs subject to death,  
torn apart.

“There is another man within,  
whom no one can violate:  
free, tranquil, whole,  
without the sad share of suffering.

“This vessel, which you strive  
with such furious strength to destroy,  
is loosened and earthen,  
to be broken in any manner.

“Indeed, now exert yourself  
to cut and punish it,  
while the one within remains—  
the one who tramples your madness, tyrant.

“Attack him, torture him,  
the unconquered, the unsurpassable,  
subject to no storms,  
subject only to God.”

He speaks, and again he is torn  
by the hissing hooks.  
The governor, with deceitful mouth,  
envenoms his words and hisses:

“If such a stubbornness  
of a cunning heart remains hardened,  
so that you abhor touching  
our empty cushion,

“at least destroy the hidden pages,  
the covered books,  
by which you sow your evil sect.  
Let these be burned in the fires.”

When the martyr heard this, he said:

“The fire with which you maliciously  
threaten the mystical writings—  
you yourself shall burn in it  
all the more justly.

“Will not the heavenly avenging will  
burn with lightning  
the tongue that interprets  
such great poison?”

“You see the ashes, witnesses  
of the crimes of the people of Gomorrah;  
the ash of the Sodomites’ destruction,  
witnesses of everlasting death.

“This is always your example:  
soon smoke of sulfur,  
bitumen, and pitch mixed together  
will entangle you in deepest Tartarus.”

Wounded by these words,  
the persecutor grows pale and falters;  
immediately, twisting his mad eyes  
and gnashing his teeth, he pours out foam.

Then, after long hesitation,  
he decrees the most extreme of all:  
let the ordeal of fire  
and of oppressive light be applied.

He rushed toward these tasks  
with quickened pace  
and, swift with joy,  
outstripped the ministers of punishment themselves.

They came to the arena of glory;  
hope and cruelty contend.  
An uncertain struggle is joined:  
the martyr here, the executioner there.

They roughen a saw-shaped bed  
with a frequent tooth,  
while a great heap of coals  
steams out living breath.

The holy man voluntarily  
climbs upon this pyre,  
with fearless face, conscious  
of heaven and the crown,  
to ascend the high tribunal.

Beneath the crackling spray,  
the course of salt sparkles;  
with sharp, searing points  
it is scattered and fixed into his limbs.

Then the fat pressed upon  
the fiery grating licks it;  
scarcely does the smoky liquid  
slowly melt outward into his limbs.

Meanwhile he remains unmoved,  
as though unaware of pains,  
and raises his eyes upward;  
for chains had pressed his hands.

From there, made stronger,  
he is thrust into a gloomy cavern,  
lest the free origin of light  
animate his lofty spirit.

Deep within the prison  
there is a place blacker than darkness;  
narrow rocks, sunk beneath  
the vaulted roof, constrict and choke it.

Eternal night lies hidden there,  
deprived of the star of day.  
This dreadful prison is said  
to have its own underworld.

Into this abyss the savage enemy  
cast the martyr and fixed his feet  
in a piece of wood,  
with his legs spread apart.

Moreover, he adds a new punishment,  
an ingenious trial of the cross,  
unknown to any tyrant  
and never before heard of.

He orders fragments of pottery,  
rough, pointed, shapeless,  
with unworked claws,  
to be spread beneath the back of the one lying there.

They arm the entire bed  
with spikes and stones for pain,  
so that the sleepless side beneath  
may be struck by the opposing blade.

In this shadow he turns over,  
meditating on the devices Beelzebub had devised;  
but Christ destroyed  
the clever contrivances of Beelzebub.

For the prison’s blindness  
flashes with the brilliance of light,  
and the double bite of the stake  
bursts apart through the shattered cavern.

Here Vincent recognizes  
that what he had hoped for is present:  
the reward of such great labor,  
Christ, the giver of light.

Then he sees the fragments  
of the pottery already clothing themselves  
with soft flowers,  
while the prison smells of nectar.

Indeed, angels frequently stand there  
and speak face to face.  
One of them, more august in speech,  
addresses the man with these words:

“Arise, renowned martyr;  
arise, secure in your own destiny;  
arise and join our company  
as a companion in blessed assemblies.”

Grant this, most merciful Father,  
and Only-Begotten One, equal to the Father,  
with the Spirit, the Paraclete,  
reigning through every age. Amen.

Supplication. Let us pray to the Redeemer. Fol. CLXXXVII.

Capitulum. Most merciful Lord God, grant that your strongest martyr Vincent, who fought manfully for you and conquered by your gift, may continually be present to us in your name, so that, victorious over the rack, he may prove victorious over sin; may he wash away daily faults, who overcame so many and such great punishments; so that he who became a wondrous triumphant victor for the Lord may become a magnificent intercessor for his servants.

Our Father. “Delivered.” Fol. 2.

Lauda. “Alleluia. Your love remains like a fountain.” Fol. CCV.

Benediction. May the Lord Jesus Christ, who powerfully gave his victorious martyr Vincent the morning star as a gift, enrich you with the joys of the first resurrection and of the future. R. Amen. And may he who gave that same Vincent hidden manna, through his glorious intercession clothe you with the garment of immortality. R. Amen. May, following the example of the aforesaid martyr, you conquer prisons and flames and, brought out of the prison of the world, escape the flames of eternal punishment. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

In the name of the Lord.

### At the close of Vespers

[Col. 1078C] Lauda. “My soul hoped in the Lord.”

Sono. “You are my hope, my portion.” Fol. CCV.

Antiphon. “Saint Vincent shines like a ray of the sun and blossoms like the lilies of the field.” P. “Bearing the fragrance of sweetness in the sight of the Lord.” V. “The king shall rejoice in your strength, Lord, and shall exult greatly in your salvation.” P. “Bearing.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “Bearing.”

May the Lord be with you. R. And with you.

Lauda. “An everlasting, splendid crown.” Alleluia. P. “To Vincent I shall give.” Alleluia, alleluia. V. “For my hand shall assist him, and my arm shall strengthen him.” P. “To Vincent.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “To Vincent.”

Hymn. “Here is the wondrous passion.”

[Col. 1078D] Supplication. Let us pray to the Redeemer. Fol. CLXXXVII.

Capitulum. O God, who adorned your Levite Vincent with so great a gift of virtues that, relying upon the office of sacred ministry and intending to follow your Son, our Lord, in his passion, he first ministered the cup of that same Christ to believers for salvation: make us deal worthily before you with the offices of ministry we have undertaken and whose service we have assumed to bear.

Thus may your martyr Vincent, strengthened by the divine Spirit, attack the persecuting Datianus with hard arguments, when Datianus complained that he had spoken lightly against his bishop Valerius. By his merits, may he grant all people a happier course in this life and an unending kingdom of blessedness in the future. Just as you received him amid punishments while he confessed you, so now command that he be heard praying for us, when we cry out to you from the earth.

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” Fol. 2.

Source preparation: Supplied feast headings, liturgical forms, folio references, internal section numbers, and column transitions retained.

Benediction. May God, eternal light, whose new light shone forth when his martyr Vincent was placed in prison, shine in your hearts for eternal reward. R\. Amen. And may he who brought back his body from the depths of the sea to the shore restore your life from destruction and from harmful deeds. R\. Amen. May he also, through the service of the raven, who spread abroad the glory of the aforesaid Martyr, receive your devotion with his customary favor. R\. Amen.

Through.

## JANUARY 25. FEAST OF SAINT BABYLAS, BISHOP, AND THE THREE BOYS

[Col. 1079B]

### At Vespers

Lauda. “Light has dawned in the darkness.” Sono. “The souls of the righteous.” fol. CLXII.

Antiphon. “Let the righteous feast and rejoice in the sight of the Lord,” P. “and delight in gladness.” V\. “The salvation of the righteous is from the Lord, and he is their protector in the time of tribulation.” P. “And delight in gladness.” V\. “Glory and honor.” P. “And delight in gladness.”

[CCXIV] Lauda. “Let the righteous rejoice,” Alleluia, P. “and be glad,” Alleluia, alleluia. V\. “The voice of gladness and salvation is in the tents of the righteous.” P. “And be glad.” V\. “Glory and honor.” P. “And be glad,” Alleluia, alleluia.

Hymn.

[Col. 1079C] O illustrious crown of priests,

and radiant order of Levites,

with the clergy gathered, let us sing a hymn



with a gracious mind.

Bishop Babylas, fighting for us,

impressed upon us the pattern of example to be observed:

that we should not open the doors of God’s temple

to the crafty enemy.

This man, fortified by the strength of faith,

while governing the Antiochene citadel,

despised the impious Numerianus

in the sacred courts.

Immediately he is seized and brought before the tyrant,

a true victim to be sacrificed to Christ:

[Col. 1079D] he rejects the deceitful assertions,

using what is true.

For, considering the perverse doctrines,

he confesses the Author of all things,

the coeternal offspring of the exalted Father,

to have created the world.

He is urged to sacrifice on the altars of demons;

refusing, he is bound in chains;

his neck is weighed down by the weight of balls,

his foot fastened in a shackle.

He becomes a great example to the flock;

he is displayed to the city as an object of contempt:

thereupon, triumphant, he offers vows of praise to Christ,

a renowned victor.

By reasoning he conquered the clay image;

[Col. 1080A] he thoroughly exposes the empty liberal arts;

rather, he proclaims the eloquent understanding

of the three boys.

The offspring follow their parent, who sends them



to struggle with the holy Bishop:



they say that he suffers such things



as their Father and Master himself suffered.

For he is a true parent, like Abraham,

who offered himself with the three boys

as a sacred victim upon the altar of the wood

to the King of heaven.

Among the innocent, with washed arms, he embraces

the sacred altar, raised upon the wood;

while he undergoes dreadful chains and tortures,

he teaches by accompanying them.

[Col. 1080B] Together they confess the name of the Trinity;

together they endure the blows that tear them apart;

but by divine gift they snatched a trophy

from the enemy.

Afterward brought forth to be killed,

they go forward joyfully, singing beforehand

a psalm of dancing, the avenging fortieth psalm,

in ringing voice.

Then the Bishop addresses the people who bear witness;

although weighed down with chains,

he is buried in order to confound

the impious judge.

Babylas assigns the little boys also to be sacrificed

to the Father, to be struck down by the sword;

[Col. 1080C] their contest he brings to a more glorious end

with the shedding of blood.

Laid in a sepulchral urn,

they live on in everlasting remembrance of what they suffered,

having attained the promised seat in the citadel,

with the diadem.

Through them, by their twofold gift,

you obtain the envoys you sought, O city:

rejoice exceedingly, glorying in Christ

with great jubilation.

Here the city possesses their bodies, to be venerated and restored to life;

above are the victorious souls,

clothed in shining white robes,

carry palms.

From there, Redeemer, behold from heaven

[Col. 1080D] the vessel of the redeemed flock,



riding upon the sea of the age,

driven by the whirlwinds of temptations.

Give the assistance of your right hand,

and defend it from every evil:

carry it to live with you above

through everlasting ages.

Highest glory, Christ, be always to you,

together with the Father and the Holy Spirit:

now and always, to you alone, God,

be glory, threefold and one.

Amen.

Supplication. “Let us pray to the Redeemer,” with the names changed, fol. CLXXXVII.

Capitula. Dearly beloved brothers, consider the steadfast hope of the priest [Col. 1081A] Babylas and the stronger faith of spirit of the three boys, stronger than bodily strength. The aforesaid outstanding teacher, about to be struck continuously by the sword, embraces them in turn with his sacred arms, giving tearful thanks to the Creator because he has offered to him those whom he had received from his hand to be crowned. Therefore, imitating the example of their constancy, let us correct our conduct for the better, let us preserve charity toward one another, let us fulfill the ministry entrusted to us through love, and let us kindle the others to the service of God. Let us rejoice in doing justice, let us flee [CCXV] harmful things, let us pray in the spirit, and let us say:

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” fol. 2.

Benediction. May your sins be loosed through the prayers of Babylas, [Col. 1081B] by whose power the thresholds of God’s house were closed against Numerianus. R\. Amen. May you rejoice that, through his intercession, you have obtained the gain of your souls, by whose example the company of the three boys deserved to undergo martyrdom. R\. Amen. Just as those same little children, with their teacher following, were beheaded for Christ by a comparable sentence, so may you, bound together in united fellowship, always perform divine service. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

Lauda. “Everlasting joy.” fol. CLXII.

Prayer. Grant, Lord, that as we receive the venerable temples of Saints Babylas and the three boys, we may deserve to become ourselves a temple of pure heart and undefiled body for you; and, [Col. 1081C] remaining in the dwellings of your house, may we deserve to share in the company of your elect. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

In the name of the Lord.

### At Matins

Antiphon. “Give us gladness.” Psalm L.

Prayer. “Restore to us, Lord, gladness.” fol. CLXIII.

Antiphon 1. “You made a way in the sea, Lord, and, showing a most secure path among the waves”: P. “because you are powerful to save those crossing the sea.” V\. “The Lord is near to those who are troubled in heart, and he will save the humble in spirit.” P. “Because you are powerful.” V\. “Glory and honor.” P. “Because you are powerful.”

Prayer. Do not burden us, Lord, with the weights of our own sins; [Col. 1081D] and we earnestly beseech you, who were made known in the regions of Judea, to dwell in our hearts. May the name of Jerusalem, which is great, through the intercession of the holy martyrs Babylas and the three boys, be especially present in our way of life. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 2. “They crossed the Red Sea as though through dry land. Thus says the Lord: Cross over, cross over”: P. “for I will lead you out of my land.” V\. “Rejoice in the Lord, you righteous; praise is fitting for the upright.” P. “Because.” V\. “Glory and honor.” P. “Because.”

Prayer. Almighty God, who direct your eyes upon the righteous, graciously attend to our prayers through their merits, [Col. 1082A] so that we may be cleansed from our sins by the visitation of your countenance and, by the gift of your mercy, be joined to the number of your own.

Antiphon 3. “O God, who are glorified in the assembly of the saints,” P. “you are great and greatly to be feared.” Alleluia. V\. “Praise the Lord, Jerusalem; praise your God, Zion.” P. “You are great.” V\. “Glory and honor.” P. “You are great.”

Prayer. “Grant, Lord, that while we …”

Seek this in the preceding Vespers.

R\. “The saints rest in the paradise of God; their unfailing fruit endures there, where there is fullness and healing.” P. “Their faces will shine above the stars.” V\. “The righteous will shine, and like sparks they will run through the reeds.” P. “Above the stars.” V\. “Glory and honor.” P. “Above.”

### At Lauds

[Col. 1082B]

At the Canticle. Antiphon. “Those who love you, Lord, like the sun in …”

Canticle. “You who freely offered yourselves.” At the Benedictus. Antiphon. “Holy and humble.” fol. CLIV. Canticle. “Blessed are you, Lord.” fol. 6. Sono. “The salvation of the righteous is from the Lord.” Lauda. “Praise the Lord from the heavens.” Psalm CXLVIII. fol. CLXIV. Prophecy. “The souls of the righteous.” fol. CLXVII. Capitula. God, glory of the saints and abundant in mercy, hear the people who plead with you and appeal to you through the intercession of the saints. Govern us through the alternating changes of the seasons, and guard us with equal protection through the differing succession of days and nights, so that, aided by the prayers of your holy martyrs Babylas [Col. 1082C] and the three boys, we may have brought this day to a prosperous close through your mercy and may also pass this night with purity of soul and body pleasing to you.

[CCXVI.] Benediction. May the Lord guard you through the intercession of his most blessed martyrs Babylas and the three boys. R\. Amen. May he, appeased, look upon the needs of those who hope in him. R\. Amen. And may he, in his mercy, pardon the sins of those who entreat him. R\. Amen.

[Col. 1082D] Through mercy.

In the name of the Lord.

## JANUARY 28. FEAST OF SAINT TYRSUS, MARTYR

### At Vespers

Lauda. “Light has risen for the righteous.” P. “And joy for the upright in heart.” V\. “The righteous will rejoice with all the saints.” P. “And joy for the upright in heart.”

May the Lord be present. R\. And with you.

Sono. “Rejoice in the Lord, you righteous; praise is fitting for the upright.” P. “Alleluia.” V\. “Give thanks to the Lord with the lyre; sing to God with the ten-stringed psaltery.” P. “Alleluia.”

May the Lord be present. R\. And with you.

[Col. 1083A] Antiphon. “The saints despised the life of the world and attained the reward of the kingdom,” P. “and washed their robes in the blood of the Lamb.” V\. “For God loves judgment and will not forsake his saints; they will be preserved forever.” P. “And washed.” V\. “Glory and honor.” P. “And washed.”

May the Lord be present. R\. And with you.

Lauda. “Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.” P. “Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.” V\. “Blessed are those who keep judgment and do justice at all times.” P. “Alleluia.” V\. “Glory and honor.” P. “Alleluia.”

Hymn.

Rejoice exceedingly, faithful throng;

today is the solemn feast

of the illustrious Martyr:

sing boldly songs

[Col. 1083B] in praise of the Lord and his power.

Thinking upon the joys

of the heavenly homeland,

Tyrsus, a holy man,

drove away all worldly things;

when he did not at all believe in God,



he was suddenly filled with the breath of the Holy Spirit.

Seeing the savage judge, he rebukes him:

“Why,” he says, “do you torture the saints of the Lord

with exceedingly cruel punishments?

Unhappy man! You will be burned

in the fire of hell.”

At once the enemy Cumbricius,

raging in his fury,

had pressed hard upon them;

many of those who worshiped the Lord on earth

were slain,

thousands of shining martyrs.

The holy Leucius strives

to surrender his chosen soul for the Lord;

rather, innocent, he endured

[Col. 1083C] various kinds of punishment,

desiring heavenly rewards.

The athlete Tyrsus, swift-footed as he walked,

when he came upon the impious king,

seized and held him,

admonishing and teaching him

that he should now cease to worship false idols.

Then, pretending a cheerful expression, he spoke:

“Tyrsus, I desire you to assent

to my proposal and sacrifice to the gods,

so that you may receive great abundance

of gifts.”

“It is clear, impious man,”

said the saint,

“that the most wicked,

crooked and envious serpent

now dwells wholly within you.

Perish horribly with such a ruler.”

[Col. 1083D] He orders a vessel to be brought swiftly,

full of water, and suffocates

the Martyr’s head;

the pestilent man orders the body that remains

to be struck more fiercely with knotted clubs.

But the servant of the Lord

rebukes the wretched judge

with a most holy voice:

“Acknowledge the Lord, slippery and envious man,

when you see his great and illustrious works.”

A tower is built, rising high above,

with swords fixed in a circle

in ordered rows,

so that, when the holy man is placed upon the summit

and falls, his faithful limbs

may be received by the sword.

“Great are you, Lord, above all gods!

You are greatly wondrous to those who believe in you!

Be a snare for the wicked!”

[Col. 1084A] The saint glorifies in heaven

the omnipotence of Christ.

The insatiable, savage and terrible man,

having been defeated, could not prevail;

he devises new tortures,

thirsting to conquer the Martyr.

But the holy Lord struck terror into evil.

“Do not fear, Tyrsus,” says the Angel;

“I have been sent by the Lord God.

I will take away all punishments from you,

and you will be able to conquer

the worst of enemies.”

Hear, Lord. The impious man plans

to inflict weights, chains and everything else:

boiling oil, lead and claws,

to overcome and kill the holy martyr.

Seeing that he accomplished nothing by his own strength,

he orders the saint to be [Col. 1084B] thrown headlong

into the sea,

far from the shore,

so that human eyes might not see him,

thirty stadia away.

How marvelous are your works, Lord!

The Angels bring the Martyr back

in their hands,

and sound a song in sweet melody:

the judge was not worthy to see the Angels.

[CCXVII] We must recount in full the deeds

through which he repaid good to the holy merits—

the three judges, slipping into guilt,

were repeatedly cast out by the earth as dead.

The peoples entreat the Martyr; they say:

“We pray, Lord, command at once

that the earth receive the bodies of the judges,

which, rotting and putrefying,

are pouring forth worms.”

Graciously, he receives their tears and takes a hoe (*sarculum*),

[Col. 1084C] marking the place where

the bodies ought to be buried.

“Grant forgiveness, holy Martyr, we ask;

we humble people believe in God.”

May the hearts of all who desire

to seek the joys of the heavenly homeland rejoice;

and may the wicked do no harmful thing,

and fly like chaff

before the wind.

We, your little servants, beseech you with tears, Martyr:

through you may the almighty Creator

quickly remove this hard yoke

under which we are oppressed,

and make the ages joyful forever.

Now, Most High Lord, look upon the people

wounded by sins; erase the bond;

and mercifully behold our groaning,

granting us help at the fitting time.

[Col. 1084D] Grant rest to all the dead, O best of Lords;

give prosperous times;

food to the poor and assistance to widows;

may all receive what they devoutly ask.

May our praise sing joyfully to you forever,

who alone are the triune and one Lord,

holding the ages under eternal rule,

ruling all things and commanding everything.

To the Triune Lord be unfailing glory,

everlasting kingdom and power;

by his customary might he governs all things,

mercifully sustaining what he has created

through the ages.

Amen.

[Col. 1085A] Supplication. “Let us pray to the Redeemer,” with the names changed. fol. CLXXXVIII.

Capitula. Author of light, fountain of light, and splendor of immense radiance, Christ, the only-begotten offspring of the unbegotten Father, who sent from heaven to your athlete Tyrsus, thirsting at the bath of the perennial fountain, a messenger bearing light, so that he might outwardly illumine the one whom you had kindled within, and so that he might become a lamp for his feet and a constant enlightener of his mind: we ask you, most merciful Lord, burn in our minds with the kindly fervor of your fire, which you promised with your own mouth to send from on high, so that, burning within to consume vices, it may illumine us outwardly to receive everlasting rewards.

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” fol. 2.

Benediction. May Christ, the Son of God, [Col. 1085B] from whom the most blessed martyr Tyrsus received the foretaste of his passion before baptism, himself enrich us with the gift of eternity and reward us with the everlasting prize of blessing. R\. Amen. And may he who, when Tyrsus had been cast into the sea, brought him back to the shore carried by Angels, join you with himself, rejoicing in the dwellings of heaven. R\. Amen. May you always invoke as God and Father the one whom that same martyr Tyrsus invoked with a free voice even beneath the waters. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

Lauda. “He looked upon them when they were in tribulation.” fol. CLXVIII.

Prayer. O Christ, Son of God, grant that we may come to you as those blessed by your Father, to receive from you the kingdom which you foretold had been prepared for them from the foundation of the world. Therefore make us, though unworthy, attain to them, so that we who celebrate [Col. 1085C] the feast of your most blessed martyr Tyrsus and his companions may rejoice forever with those same saints. And just as you did not permit your Martyr to be cut apart by the saw’s teeth, so through his intercession do not allow us, for any reason, to be separated from the bosom of Mother Church; but with the blessed may we receive the kingdom that you promised to your saints throughout the eternal ages of ages. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

In the name of the Lord.

### At Matins

Antiphon. “Give us gladness.” Psalm L. Prayer. “Restore to us.” fol. CLXIII.

Antiphon 1. “Come to me, my saints, says the Lord; harvest the fruit of your labors, [Col. 1085D] the shoot of righteousness”: P. “whose fragrance is great, like the fragrance of lilies and roses in their season.” V\. “Planted in the house of the Lord, they will flower in the courts of the house of our God.” P. “Whose fragrance.” V\. “Glory and honor.” P. “Whose.”

Prayer. As your saints, Lord, come to you at your invitation to harvest the fruits of their labors, grant that through your mercy we may attain to them in the land of the living. You consecrated your most blessed athlete Tyrsus to martyrdom before baptism, in faith before regeneration, and even in suffering before baptism. Forgive all our sins and grant us the kingdom of an everlasting inheritance, so that through good works and conduct we may arrive in the paradise of delights; [CCXVIII] and, [Col. 1086A] rejoicing in the fruit of our labors, may harvest our fruits in eternal joy. R\. Amen.

Antiphon 2. “Come to me, all my saints, says the Lord,” P. “you who labor and are burdened, and I will refresh you.” V\. “Come, children, hear me; I will teach you the fear of the Lord.” P. “You who labor.” V\. “Glory and honor.” P. “You who.”

Prayer. Coming to you, holy God, are all who have labored and endured much for you, so that you may cause them to rest, as you promised them, saying, “I will refresh you.” Therefore grant that we, praying in your Church, may attain to them with the whole attention of our minds, so that we may obtain your mercy and not be condemned to punishment according to our deserts, since by our own merit we do not deserve forgiveness. You went before the most blessed Tyrsus [Col. 1086B] with the blessing of grace, showing him light in darkness and the perfection of grace after labor. We therefore ask, although unworthy, that through the intercession of the aforesaid Martyr, burdened by our labor, we may be refreshed with your saints by the honey-sweet teaching of your word in the land of the living. R\. Amen.

Antiphon 3. “Come, you blessed of my Father, says the Lord,” P. “receive the kingdom that has been prepared from the foundation of the world.” V\. “Approach me and be enlightened, and your faces will not blush.” P. “Receive the kingdom.” V\. “Glory and honor.” P. “Receive the kingdom.”

Prayer. “Coming to you, you blessed of my Father …” Seek it earlier in the preceding Vespers.

R\. “The name of the Lord Jesus Christ has been glorified in the saints through endurance and faith in all the persecutions [Col. 1086C] which they endured,” P. “so that they might be deemed worthy of the kingdom of God, for which they also suffered.” V\. “He led them by a straight path, so that they might go to the city of their dwelling.” P. “So that they might be deemed worthy.” V\. “Glory and honor.” P. “So that they might be deemed worthy.”

### At Lauds

At the Canticle. Antiphon. “Those who love you, Lord, like the sun.” Canticle. “You who freely offered yourselves.” fol. CLXIII. At the Benedictus. Antiphon. “Holy and humble in heart.” Canticle. “Blessed are you, Lord.” fol. VI. Sono. “The way of the righteous.” Lauda. “Praise the Lord from the heavens, Alleluia.” Psalm CXLVIII. fol. CLXIX. Prophecy. “The righteous will live forever, and with …” fol. CLXIV. Hymn. “Rejoice exceedingly, faithful throng.” Seek it earlier in the preceding Vespers. And Supplication. “Let us pray to the [Col. 1086D] Redeemer.”

Capitula. Lord God almighty, knower before the foundation of the world of your chosen ones, graciously blot out every sin as those who receive with joyful devotion the yearly return of the solemn feast of your martyr Tyrsus and his companions. And may he who endured so many and such great punishments for your name, through his intercession, blot out our sins, so that, freed from every bond of sin through his prayers, we may deserve after our passing to come to you, clothed in the robe of honor, most merciful Lord.

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” fol. 2.

Lauda. “The praise of the Lord is in the Church of the saints.” Alleluia. P. “Let Israel rejoice in him who made him.” Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V\. [Col. 1087A] “Sing to the Lord a new song, for he has done marvelous things.” P. “Let Israel rejoice.” V\. “Glory and honor.” P. “Let Israel rejoice.”

Benediction. May the blessing of God, descended from heaven through the intervention of the saints Tyrsus and his companions, protect you and defend you from every evil. R\. Amen. May you be guarded from every misfortune through the prayers of those whose feasts you lovingly receive. R\. Amen. May you share eternal blessedness with those whose solemn feasts you celebrate with the deepest devotion. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

In the name of the Lord.

## FEBRUARY 2. FEAST OF THE PURIFICATION OF SAINT MARY

### At Vespers

Lauda. [Col. 1087B] “All your Angels, Lord, praised you and sang a hymn when you completed the structure of heaven. The day is yours and the night is yours”: P. “You made the sun and the moon.” V\. “You established the sea by your strength; you shattered the heads of dragons upon the waters.” P. “You made the sun and the moon.”

Prayer. They praise you, Lord, all your Angels, recognizing that they were created by you and not doubting that every heavenly and earthly creature subsists and is ordered by you, its maker. [CCXIX] Therefore grant our minds to give you glory in all your works, and let the light of the sun of righteousness shine upon us perpetually with its radiance, so that we may always be able to avoid the darkness of night through your illumination. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

Sono. “Alleluia. Your right hand is full of righteousness. Let [Col. 1087C] Mount Zion rejoice and the daughters of Judah exult,” P. “because of your judgments.” Alleluia, alleluia. V\. “Alleluia. Great is the Lord and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, on his holy mountain, making the rejoicing of the whole earth abundant.” P. “Because of your judgments.”

May the Lord always be present. R\. And with you.

Antiphon. “All the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God.” P. “Sing joyfully to God, all the earth; sing, exult and play the psaltery.” V\. “Sing to the Lord a new song, for he has done marvelous things.” P. “Sing joyfully to God.” V\. “Glory and honor.” P. “Sing joyfully to God.”

Prayer. Lord, whom human beings saw born as a man and whom the ends of the earth, as foretold, saw; you who had been foretold long before by the voices of the Prophets and [Col. 1087D] were seen and glorified in due time in the songs of the peoples, mercifully grant that we may remain your purest vessels, so that you, author of light, may continually illumine us and dwell in us without end. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon. “My eyes have seen your salvation, Lord, which you prepared in the sight of the peoples.” P. “A light for revelation to the Gentiles and the glory of your people Israel.” V\. “Lord, our Lord, how wonderful is your name in all the earth!” P. “A light for revelation.” V\. “Glory and honor.” P. “A light for revelation.”

May the Lord always be present. R\. And with you.

Lauda. “The Lord has made his salvation known,” P. “before the sight of the nations he has revealed his righteousness.” Alleluia, alleluia. V\. “He remembered [Col. 1088A] his covenant forever, the word that he commanded for a thousand generations.” P. “Before the sight of the nations.” V\. “Glory and honor.” P. “Before the sight of the nations.”

Hymn.

This holy day of Purification shines brightly,

on which Christ, according to the flesh,

is presented in the temple to Simeon,

coeternal with the Father,

not by adoption but by nature.

The womb of the incorrupt Virgin

is filled by the Spirit.

She who gives birth remains unmarried,

a virgin, whom [Col. 1088B] the offspring chose

as an undefiled mother,

a chaste parent.

Thereupon the aged Simeon,

rejoicing, receives him in his arms,

and, embracing him,

seemed to behold

the salvation of the Lord:

“Now release these fragile limbs

in peace.”

Nor was Anna, no less devoted,

who walked in continence,

whom a husband had widowed

in the flower of youth,

silent: she confesses

that the child who cries

will be the Ruler of the world.

Then, according to the venerable law,

gifts are offered—

[Col. 1088C] a pair of turtledoves

and two young pigeons in sacrifice—

to teach the purity

of body and soul.

Let glory resound

to powerful God in the highest;

let us sing glory to Christ

and to the Holy Spirit,

to whom be praise and power

through eternal ages.

Amen.

Supplication. Let us beseech our pious and prayer-hearing Lord Jesus Christ with every supplication, that he may graciously deign to grant us, through the grace of his Presentation and of the Purification of [Col. 1088D] his mother Mary, salvation of soul and body, forgiveness and peace. R\. Grant it, eternal almighty God.

Kyrie eleison. R\. Christe eleison, Kyrie eleison.

Capitula. Jesus Lord, whose wondrous name the Angel foretold, the Mother bestowed, Simeon recognized and Anna praised: save your people throughout the whole world, whose magnificent name exists in heaven, so that you, who alone are glorious in power, may also be mercifully kind through indulgence toward the lost.

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” fol. 2.

Benediction. And may he who was received in the hands of the righteous Simeon join you to himself, rejoicing in everlasting blessing. R\. Amen. [Col. 1089A] May the same one who, by the commandment of his law, received the sign of circumcised flesh cleanse all our uncleanness through [CCXX] the bond of his love. R\. Amen. And may he who promised to bless you as children of Abraham in himself, who is Abraham’s seed, enrich you by the bestowal of blessed inheritance. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

Lauda. “Let the name of the Lord be announced in Zion,” P. “and his praise in Jerusalem.” Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V\. “And the nations will fear your name, Lord, and all the kings of the earth your glory.” P. “And his praise.” V\. “Glory and honor.” P. “And his praise.”

Prayer. Almighty God, Father and Lord, grant peace to your believing people, so that in your temple we may see your Salvation, [Col. 1089B] whom the righteous Simeon received in his arms; so that he who was a light for revelation to the Gentiles may himself be perceived by believers as the pardoner of sins. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

In the name of the Lord.

### At Matins

Antiphon. “Salvation belongs to the Lord, and your blessing is upon your people.” Psalm III.

Prayer. You are, Lord, salvation, and salvation belongs to you. We rejoice that you have bestowed it upon us, and we ask that you continue to bestow it upon us even to the end. Pour out, we ask, your blessing upon your people, so that the curse of punishment may be removed and the fruit of righteousness may abound in us. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 1. “When the parents brought [Col. 1089C] the child Jesus into the temple, to do for him according to the law of Moses”: P. “Simeon took him in his hands and blessed God.” V\. “Great is the Lord and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, on his holy mountain.” P. “Simeon took him.” V\. “Glory and honor.” P. “Simeon took him.”

Prayer. “Almighty God, Father …” Seek it earlier in the preceding Vespers.

Antiphon 2. “Simeon raised his voice in the temple, saying: ‘Now release your servant in peace,’” P. “because my eyes have seen the salvation of your people.” V\. “The Lord has made his salvation known; before the sight of the nations he has revealed his righteousness.” P. “Because my eyes have seen.” V\. “Glory and honor.” P. “Because my eyes have seen.”

Prayer. Make the blessed voice of your righteous Simeon resound in us with equal devotion, Lord, so that, [Col. 1089D] because we have seen and believed in your Salvation, we may be released in peace when you command—not so that, dismissed by you, we may receive the limits of life, but so that, absolved by you from our debt, we may possess everlasting peace at the end. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 3. “We have seen the glory of the Lord, glory as of the Only-begotten.” P. “Full of grace and truth from the Father.” V\. “As we have heard, so have we seen in the city of the Lord of hosts, in the city of our God: God founded it forever.” P. “From the Father.” V\. “Glory and honor.” P. “From the Father.”

Prayer. We have seen your glory, Lord, glory as of the Only-begotten from the Father: the Only-begotten in divinity, the [Col. 1090A] Firstborn in gift; there, the Father’s only one, here, the chief among brothers; there, subsisting as one with the Father, here, first among brothers; there, existing equally and remaining in the Father’s bosom, here, not abandoning his companions. Grant, therefore, that those toward whom you have shown mercy in the world may become participants in your kingdom: for those whom you first came to redeem, become their rewarder in the future. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

R\. “He who was born is our redemption, and he is Lord and God.” P. “He will console us from our wound and from our labor in the land of our captivity.” V\. “A child is born for us, a son is given to us, and his principate has been made upon his shoulder.” P. “He will console us.” V\. “Glory and honor.” P. “He will console us.”



[Col. 1090B] Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ, who are our redemption and our salvation, heal the wound of our contrition; you who assumed the flesh of human weakness, and who, coming, deigned to lift our burdens: we ask that you empty our labors of evil works and mercifully confirm our endeavors in what is good. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 1. “My eyes have seen your salvation, Lord,” P. “which you prepared for the revelation of the Gentiles.” V\. “It is good to confess to the Lord and sing psalms to your name, Most High.” P. “Which you prepared.” V\. “Glory and honor.” P. “Which you prepared.”
