Prayer. Make us, Lord, experience your Salvation, whom we have seen with the eyes of faith, as merciful in judgment, so that he who was prepared for revelation to the Gentiles [Col. 1090C] may present himself as judge of the redeemed not for punishment but for salvation. R\. Amen.

Antiphon 2. “They brought Jesus to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord, as it is written [CCXXI] in the law of the Lord.” P. “Because every male opening the womb shall be called holy to the Lord.” V\. “Sing to the Lord and bless his name; announce his salvation from day to day.” P. “Because every male.” V\. “Glory and honor.” P. “Because every male.”

Prayer. Lord God, who testify that every male opening the womb is holy, make us serve you in holiness and righteousness, so that you who sanctify the womb of the mother by incorruption may raise believing people up to the reward of eternal sanctification; [Col. 1090D] so that those who announce your glorious name among the Gentiles may recognize you as their rewarder in the future. R\. Amen.

Through.

Antiphon 3. Alleluia. “They offered a sacrifice for Jesus according to what is written in the law of the Lord.” P. “A pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.” Alleluia. V\. “Praise the name of the Lord; praise the Lord, servants.” P. “A pair of turtledoves.” V\. “Glory and honor.” P. “A pair of turtledoves.”

Prayer. O God, who command that, for the purification of women after childbirth, a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons be offered to you, prepare us as a living sacrifice, you who yourself became a sacrifice for us, so that you who [Col. 1091A] came to fulfill the law, not to abolish it, may deign to spread the grace of the Gospel more abundantly in us. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

R\. “Now, Lord, you will give peace to your people, because my eyes have seen your salvation.” P. “A light for revelation to the Gentiles.” V\. “You have made gladness with your servant, Lord, according to your word.” P. “A light.” V\. “Glory and honor.” P. “A light.”

Prayer. Almighty God, Father and Lord, grant peace to your believing people, so that we who have seen your Salvation may be endowed with the vision of your grace; so that he who has been a light for revelation to the Gentiles may himself be perceived by believers as the pardoner of sins. R\. Amen.

Through.

### At Lauds

[Col. 1091B]

At the Canticle. Antiphon. “All will rejoice.” Canticle. “He keeps watch by night.” Prayer. “O God, who have made known …” fol. 64.

Another Antiphon from the Canticle. “I will glory in the Lord; I will rejoice in God my Jesus.”

Canticle (Luke I).

“Now release your servant, Lord, * according to your word in peace:

because my eyes have seen your salvation, * which you prepared before the face of all peoples;

a light for revelation to the Gentiles, * and the glory of your people Israel.”

At the Benedictus. Antiphon. “To you alone, God, be honor, glory, strength and power throughout the ages of ages.”

[Col. 1091C] Canticle. “Benedictus.” fol. 6. Sono. “Your right hand is full of righteousness.” fol. CLXXXII.

Lauda. “Praise the Lord from the heavens, alleluia; praise him in the heights, alleluia. Praise him, all his Angels; praise him, all his powers.” Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. Psalm CXLVIII.

Prophecy. “Hear me, Jacob, and Israel, whom …” fol. 65. Hymn. “This holy day of Purification.” Seek it in the preceding Vespers. And Supplication. “Let us pray to the Redeemer.” Capitula. “The salvation of the Lord has been made known.” fol. 65. Lauda. “Let the name of the Lord be announced in Zion, and his praise.” Benediction. “And may he who was received in the hands of the righteous Simeon …” Seek it in the preceding Vespers, fol. CCXIX.

## FEBRUARY 5. FEAST OF SAINT AGATHA, VIRGIN AND MARTYR

[Col. 1091D]

### At Vespers

Lauda. “My soul has hoped in the Lord.” fol. CLXXIX.

Sono. “The Lord God of heaven bless you; the honor of the kingdom will be given into your hand.” P. “And the sons of many nations will worship before you.” Alleluia. V\. “Hear, daughter of Zion, because you have been exalted, and your face shines in the temple of God; the sun of righteousness will rise in your course.” Alleluia. P. “And they will worship.”

Antiphon. “Most prudent virgin, where are you going?” Lauda. “In your beauty and loveliness.” fol. CLXXX.

Hymn.

Be present, most faithful people,

[Col. 1092A] for the lovely feast:

[CCXXII] bring forth songs of praise

and the greatest vows to Christ.

Blessed virgin Agatha,

bright through faith and noble birth,

rejecting the harmful things of the world,

attained heavenly things.

Loving Christ with deep devotion,

and proclaiming him alone,

stretched out at the command of the governor,

she is confined in the depths of prison.

The girl of Christ is terrified

by the savage judge’s fury;

but the holy virgin refuses

to offer sacrifice on the impious altars.

[Col. 1092B] Now, O Martyr, you are afflicted

more fiercely by blows;

the breast’s nipple is torn away,

and the chaste body is beaten.

But the great elder of Christ

breaks open the prison’s barriers;

he restores the breast whole

and heals all the wounds.

Thus, thus the holier girl,

having obtained so great a reward,

bends her knee in prayer

and pours out her spirit to heaven.

For soon a radiant young man,

carrying a written tablet,

sacredly pronouncing

[Col. 1092C] the defense of the homeland,

appears.

For when the fire of Mount Etna,

with its swiftest rush,

turns downward toward the city,

the girl’s merit shines forth.

Then from the Martyr’s tomb

the people carry forth the sacred veil;

its holy presence

immediately extinguishes the fires.

Now, the most holy Virgin

[The supplied source ends here.]

To the faithful people grant

The forgiveness of sins.

Restoring the blessings of peace:

You who once rescued your fellow citizens

[Col. 1092D] From the great fire,

Now restore us, set free,

With the most evil yoke removed.

Let there be for all, let there be for the faithful,

A peaceful place of tranquil rest;

Grant protection to orphans,

And assistance to widows.

Grant this, most merciful Father,

And Only-Begotten, equal to the Father,

Reigning with the Spirit, the Paraclete,

Throughout every age.

Amen.

**Supplication.** Let us pray, with the name changed. fol. CLXXXVIII.

**Capitulum.** O God, author of justice and giver of chastity, from whom your servant Agatha, recognizing that she had been visited, receives healing in her wounded limbs, and, bound in prison in the middle of the night, is deemed worthy to be enlightened by heavenly light: illumine our minds with that light of the Holy Spirit, and make us strong in body for seeing you and purer in spirit; so that, while spiritual devotion has poured itself into the inner heart, they may praise you together by proclaiming you with faithful lips.

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

**Blessing.** May Christ the Lord wipe away the wounds of your souls—he who did not cease to heal the breast severed from the most blessed Agatha for his name’s sake. **R.** Amen. And just as by her merits he removed and drove away fires from the borders, so now, through her assistance, may he turn away from you the flame of evil desire. **R.** Amen. [Col. 1093B] May she who, by a heavenly inscription, was invoked as the liberator of her homeland preserve us all together through her tireless patronage. **R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**Laud.** “I have been exalted like a palm tree.” fol. CLXXX.

**Prayer.** O God, who clothed holy Agatha in the robe of faith through baptism and adorned her with the garments of your glory, crowning her with a laurel after the palm of martyrdom: grant us, through her prayers, that, clothed in the beauty of a true confession and robed in justice and holiness, we may be presented to you in the coming rest. **R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.

## At Matins

**Antiphon.** “O Lord, you will open my lips, and my mouth shall proclaim your praise.” [Col. 1093C] **Psalm L.**

**Prayer.** “Let my lips rejoice, O Lord.” fol. CLXXX.

**Antiphon 1.** “The wise virgin shall be blessed; she herself praises the fear of the Lord.” “Give her of the fruit of her hands.” **P.** “Let her works be praised in the gates.” **V.** “You shall eat the labors of your fruits; blessed are you, and it shall be well with you.” **P.** “Let her works be praised.” **V.** “Glory and honor.” **P.** “Let her works be praised.”

**Prayer.** Virgin of Christ, Agatha, who are rightly blessed as wise and crowned by God in his courts, while you earn forgiveness from the Lord through the fruit of your hands: grant us, we ask, through your merit, to possess the praise of wisdom and, with your help, to remain in the fear of Christ, so that we may deserve to be blessed by him forever. **R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**Antiphon 2.** “Most prudent virgin, where are you going, shining brightly like the dawn? Daughter of Zion.” **P.** “You are wholly beautiful and gracious, fair as the moon, chosen as the sun.” **V.** “In your beauty and loveliness, pay attention; go forth prosperously and reign, because of truth, gentleness, and justice; and your right hand shall lead you wondrously.” **P.** “You are wholly beautiful.” **V.** “Glory and honor.” **P.** “You are wholly beautiful.”

**Prayer.** Your virgin, Christ, Agatha, became gloriously wise; compared with the rising dawn, she is shown to be beautiful and chosen like the sun, and like the moon, as she shines with brighter light and gleams in her blood like the full moon; and, like the blazing sun, knowing no diminution of herself, she persists in the work of holiness. Grant therefore that, through the intercession of the aforesaid martyr, we may deserve to obtain forgiveness from you, while we now pour out tears or offer sighs for our offenses. **R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**Antiphon 3.** “Virgin of Israel, I have spread my mantle over you, says the Lord.” **P.** “And I have clothed you in a robe of splendor. Alleluia, alleluia.” **V.** “The Lord builds Jerusalem and gathers the dispersed of Israel.” **P.** “And I have clothed you.” **V.** “Glory and honor.” **P.** “And I have clothed you.”

**Prayer.** “O God, who [of Saint Agatha].” See above in the preceding Vespers.

**R.** “Go forth among the lilies, O beautiful daughter of Jerusalem, for you are perfect and lovely, and there is no reproach in you; ascend like a bride to Lebanon.” **P.** “And receive the blessing of faith from the Lord your God.” **V.** “Rise, hasten, my beautiful beloved, and come.” **P.** “And receive.” **V.** “Glory and honor.” **P.** “And receive.”

**Prayer.** Lord Jesus Christ, who so inflamed holy Agatha the martyr in your spirit that she overcame the flame of wantonness and the exterior fire did not burn her: through her intercession pour upon us the dew of your mercy, so that we may extinguish the natural fire while obtaining the remedy of salvation. **R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

## At Lauds

**For the Canticle. Antiphon.** “Blessed is the Lord, who clothed me.” **Canticle.** “Rejoicing, I shall rejoice in the Lord.” **At the Benedictus. Antiphon.** “Daughter of Zion, bless.” **Canticle.** “Blessed are you, O Lord.” **Sono.** “The Lord God of heaven bless you.” **Laud.** “Praise the Lord from the heavens.” **Psalm CXLVIII. Prophecy.** “The Lord has appeared from afar.” fol. CLXXXI.

### Hymn

A distinguished feast shines forth resplendent;

Let the voices of all resound in the court;

Let the whole devoted people, consecrated to God,

Declare their vows.

This holy virgin, illustrious in her lineage,

Rejected all the fleeting things of the age;

Following Christ, she subjected her limbs

To harsher punishment.

The unjust judge Quintianus himself,

When he saw the holy virgin Agatha,

Ordered her to be handed over

To ten wicked and obscene women.

When they saw her, they enticed her with words:

“Listen to the command of the judge who admonishes you:

Worship the gods, gain your life,

And many rewards.”

But the noble girl, full of faith,

Cursed all the words of vanity;

She held her hope fixed in Christ,

Always unconquered.

When Quintianus ordered her to be brought before him,

He compelled her to worship worthless idols;

The brave girl kept perfect faith

In Christ.

The enraged judge cruelly hisses;

The savage man rouses his torturers

And orders the delicate, sacred body

Of the girl to be tortured.

She bears the punishments inflicted with courage;

She preserves her body undefiled for the Lord;

By the faith in which she believes, she bravely conquers

Every torment.

A cruel and savage punishment is added:

The breast of the holy virgin is tortured;

After torturing it for a long time, he ordered

Her sacred breasts to be cut off.

Then the holy virgin, thrust into prison,

Became a champion, strong in Christ;

An angelic ministry from heaven

Heals her breast.

[Col. 1095B] Holy splendor illumines the darkness;

Throughout the night, light flashes from heaven;

The guards, terrified by great fear,

All flee.

The voluntary torturer, filled with fury,

Orders sharp potsherds and burning coals

To be rolled over her sacred body

On her bare side.

Behold, a tremendous earthquake occurs,

And grief terrifies all the torturers;

One named Silvanus is crushed

By part of the wall.

The whole assembly of that city,

Seeing the tremor, all hasten together,

Wanting the savage judge to be killed;

He himself flees.

Afterward the joyful virgin, shut up in the prison,

Stretched out her hands and implored the Lord;

She breathed forth her sacred soul into heaven,

Clothed with the saints.

An angel of God descended from heaven,

And buried the holy body; golden tablets,

Marked with sacred letters,

Were set as a sign of honor.

The unjust judge, never ashamed,

Turns over and investigates her possessions;

He is destroyed by a most evil death,

Torn apart by the bites of horses.

Many wondrous signs appeared,

Confirming what the turning year had brought to pass:

Mount Etna itself vomited forth

Blazing fire.

When everyone saw the approaching blaze,

They spread out the veil of the tomb;

The fire stopped, honoring

The blessed body.

O God, who granted such great gifts—

The heavenly kingdom—to your virgin,

For her honor wash away

The sins of us unworthy ones.

May the clergy, singing her praise,

Make their prayers acceptable to you,

And render the sustenance of your people

Sacred through honor.

May the priest be regarded as illustrious in life;

May he be adorned for you with good conduct,

So that he may worthily offer

Your blessed body.

May we fulfill with annual recurrence

The vow of praise and honor for her feast;

Through her intercession may we rejoice with your saints

In heaven.

He spoke these words and songs in her honor,

And recounted the merits of the holy virgin;

By your gift may he be heir in heaven

With the choir of the saints.

Glory to you, glorious Father,

And to Jesus Christ our Redeemer,

Who reigns with you and the Holy Spirit

Forever through the ages.

Amen.

**Supplication.** Let us pray, with the name changed, fol. CLXXXVIII.

**Capitulum.** Lord Jesus Christ, to whom the virgin and martyr Agatha is joined by purity and united by blood, since she vowed chastity to you and shed her blood for you: grant your servants who entreat you that, cleansed from sins, we may cling to you so firmly that we may never again depart from you.

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

**Laud.** “Like a palm tree.” fol. CLXXX. **Blessing.** “Christ of your souls.” See above in the preceding Vespers.

## 7 February. On the feast of Saint Dorothea, virgin and martyr

### At Vespers

**Laud.** “The light has risen.” **Sono.** “The souls of the righteous.” fol. CLXII. **Antiphon.** “The saints germinate like roses.” fol. CLXV. **Laud.** “I shall require the blood of the saints.” fol. CLXII.

### Hymn

Christ, true light of light, God of angels,

Life of the saints, salvation of the innocent,

Your devout people wish to celebrate the feast:

Receive their vow.

Behold, your holy virgin Dorothea,

Following you, always loves you with a pure heart,

And desires to offer her chaste body to you

With a pure mind.

She bears a crown with double merit,

Since she remains a virgin and willingly shed

Her own blessed blood, desiring

To conquer death.

At the command of the bloodthirsty judge she is seized,

And thus tortured with dreadful scourges;

But she remains steadfast, mocking

The mute black idols.

Then your mercy won back to you by fire two women

Who had fallen grievously—one sister called Crystetes,

Or Callistes.

Afterward the martyr is stretched on the rack,

Enduring punishments for a long time while beaten;

Thus, with her blood poured out,

She gave her soul worthy of God.

She sends Theophilus a snow-white boy

With three roses and an equal number of apples;

He saw and was utterly astonished at the gift,

So discerning and fitting.

Full of faith, he invokes Christ

And makes the message known: the tyrant could believe

That, with his head cut off, he had merited

The bright court of heaven.

Now favor the prayers of your people, Virgin;

Grant your servants pardon for their evils;

Make your own associates and patrons for us

For a long age.

May we be pleasing through your love,

Who celebrate the feast with worthy honor;

May we, joined together, enjoy

The worthy gift of peace.

May pestilence depart and sickness flee;

Drive away the yoke that weighs upon peoples;

May there be rest for the dead, medicine for the sick,

And fitting life.

So may we, holy Dorothea, with you

Possess the spacious court of heaven,

And may our melodious mouths

Resound for Christ.

May the choir sing glory and echo it;

May it speak, sing, and repeat glory;

May the stars proclaim to the triune Name,

To the Godhead alone.

Amen.

**Supplication.** Let us pray, with the name changed, fol. CLXXXVII.

**Capitulum.** Make us, Lord Jesus Christ, turn to you and remain in your fear. You caused your martyr Theophilus to turn to you at the sight of the delightful fruit; and just as, by inscribing in his mind through three apples and an equal number of roses the mystery of the Trinity, you brought him to the summit of perfect suffering, glorifying him by the punishment of the cross, so refresh us with the fragrance of your love, and make us pleasing to you in action and stronger in body. Thus, strong in both virtues, may we run after you in the fragrance of your ointments, and may we always find you favorably disposed toward us in fatherly affection when we call upon you:

[Col. 1097D] **Our Father.** Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

**Blessing.** May your Redeemer and Lord strengthen you through the intercession of the virgin Dorothea, who through her accepted the lamentations of Crystetes and Callistes in repentance. **R.** Amen. And just as they returned to the way of salvation after their fall, so may you, abandoning the superstitions of the world, follow Christ. **R.** Amen. May you, following her footsteps after the example of Theophilus, be filled with the fragrance and grace of Christ. **R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**Laud.** “Everlasting joy.” fol. CLXII.

**Prayer.** In memory of your holy and venerable virgin and martyr Dorothea, whose martyrdom bloomed like a rose in blood: Lord God, who strengthen the chosen amid punishments and justify sinners without delay, who granted Dorothea’s petitions—three apples and an equal number of roses—and made Theophilus a co-heir of your kingdom: by their prayers may we be cleansed from every contagion of sins and receive peace with them in the land of the living. **R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

In the name of the Lord.

## At Matins

**Antiphon.** “Give us gladness.” **Psalm L.** **Prayer.** “Restore to us, O Lord.” fol. CLXIII.

**Antiphon 1.** “The bones of the saints shall sprout from their place.” **P.** “And their names shall blossom like pure lilies.” **V.** “Many are the tribulations of the righteous, and the Lord delivered them from them all.” **P.** “And their names.” **V.** “Glory and honor to the Father.” **P.** “And their names.”

**Prayer.** O God, salvation of the despairing, way of the wandering, and medicine for sinners, you recalled the most blessed virgins Crystetes and Callistes—whom the ancient enemy had drawn away from the purpose of your Christ through his snares—to the worship of the Christian faith through the teachings and prayers of your servant Dorothea. May your mercy likewise drive from us the fall into sin; and grant that we may sprout from our place on the day of your coming, and that, like pure lilies, we may blossom in your sight, secure and free from every offense. **R.** Amen.

**Antiphon 2.** “The saints shall sprout like a lily.” **P.** “And they shall blossom like roses, their memory.” **V.** “The righteous shall flourish like a palm tree, and like the cedar that is in Lebanon he shall multiply.” **P.** “And they shall blossom.” **V.** “Glory and honor.” **P.** “And they shall blossom.”

**Prayer.** “Of holy and venerable remembrance.” See above in the preceding Vespers.

**Antiphon 3.** “Blossom, O saints, like a rose planted beside the waters.” **P.** “And like a lily, give forth the fragrance of sweetness.” **V.** “Planted in the house of the Lord, they shall blossom in the courts of the house of our God.” **P.** “And like a lily.” **V.** “Glory and honor.” **P.** “And like a lily.”

**Prayer.** Lord Jesus Christ, for whom your holy virgin Dorothea blossomed like a planted rose when she shed her blood for you in martyrdom, and gave forth the sweetest fragrance like a lily—you approving, adorned by your regard, assisted by faith, and consecrated in passion through her work—graciously heed the prayers of your petitioners. Make us pleasing to you through repentance and joined to you through honorable conduct. **R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**R.** “The righteous shall live forever.” **P.** “And with God is their reward.” **V.** “The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and the torment of death shall not touch them.” **P.** “And with God.” **V.** “Glory and honor.” **P.** “And with.”

## At Lauds

**For the Canticle. Antiphon.** “Those who love you, O Lord.” **Canticle.** “You who offered yourselves willingly.” fol. CLXIII. **At the Benedictus. Antiphon.** “Holy and humble.” **Canticle.** “Blessed are you, O Lord.” fol. 6. **Sono.** “Salvation belongs to the righteous from the Lord.” **Laud.** “Praise the Lord from the heavens.” **Psalm CXLVIII. Prophecy.** “The Lord has appeared from afar.” fol. CLXVII. **Hymn.** “To you it is fitting.” fol. XCVI. **Capitulum.** “Make us, Lord.” **Laud.** “Everlasting joy.” **Blessing.** “Your Redeemer.” See above in the preceding Vespers.

## 12 February. On the feast of Saint Eulalia, virgin of Barcelona

### At Vespers

**Laud.** “My soul has hoped in the Lord.” **Sono.** “Alleluia. I shall sing to your name, O God.” **Antiphon.** “Most prudent virgin.” **Laud.** “In your beauty and loveliness.” fol. CLXXIX.

### Hymn

Here shines the honor of the tomb

Of the martyr Eulalia,

Which the same person marked

With the sacred stigma of sufferings;

She calls everyone to be present here:

All should come together.

The offspring of this lineage,

Or the gathered multitude,

Ever august Barcelona,

Increased by illustrious stock,

A flourishing crown of citizens,

A renowned faithful people.

Behold your virgin,

How she is a sign of glory:

Tested by faith, she terrifies

The raging judge,

Proclaiming the honor of the Cross

And the Judge of salvation.

For she, struck with scourges,

Is placed upon the rack;

She is beaten, raked,

And burned in flames,

Knowing no end to her praise

Amid these things.

Seeking the patron of the Cross,

She is suspended upon the Cross;

There, for the honor of her body,

The snow of the heavens protects her.

Thus, filled with holy warmth,

She endured the passion;

From her mouth a dove,

With her limbs already released,

Leaps wondrously through the air,

As if in swift flight,

Proclaiming that the virgin has conquered

In the heavenly dwellings.

Yet the maiden of God,

Eager to precede it,

When the law of death had been fulfilled,

Is lifted up into joys;

And thus, with embodied laughter,

She soothes the hearts of those who weep.

Happy Barcelona, radiant throughout the world,

You are lifted up,

Holding in your bosom a pledge

So salutary and holy—

Namely, because you possess

The fellowship of so great a body.

O blessed bride of Christ,

Most merciful virgin,

Receive now the vows

And sighs of each person;

Ask Christ in prayer

To hear those who groan.

May we not serve wicked factions

With our minds;

May rebellious flesh not refuse

Christ’s gentle yoke;

But may all shine with the holiness

Of sacred fervor.

Release what is wearisome, what presses upon us

Toward the destruction of death;

May pestilential disease depart;

May the enemy’s sword be overthrown;

May life be tranquil for all;

May the times be peaceful.

Come to the citizens, O Citizen,

And extend salvation;

Be thus our patroness

In the distribution of grace,

Just as you are near the heavens

For the favor of glory.

Amid these things let Quiricus himself,

Who consecrated the place of your tomb

According to monastic rules

For the honor

Of the eternal Godhead,

Join in his plea:

After the prison of my flesh,

Remember me in heaven;

And complete with strength

What I accomplished here, though insufficient.

Consecrating these vows

That have been brought to you with song.

Glory always to the Father

And to the Son and the Paraclete;

Praise, power, and might,

An abundance of thanksgiving:

May all things confess him as God

Through ages of ages.

Amen.

**Supplication.** Let us pray, with the name changed, fol. CLXXXII.

**Capitulum.** The feast of the blessed virgin Eulalia is present, Lord, and we receive it for annual celebration. In it, the same martyr, a citizen and inhabitant of Barcelona, preferred her native soil by the titles of her merits and also glorified it by the honor of her tomb, while what she builds by the word of her living voice she teaches by the example of her shed blood. For, joyfully rushing toward suffering, she enters the forum fearlessly and, intending to rebuke the profane judge with thunderous words, offered herself to a passion she had not sought. We therefore ask you, most merciful God, to make us vigorous through a similar kindling of your love and fit through perfection of holiness, so that, just as on this day we venerate the passion and tomb of your aforesaid martyr, we may likewise, freed from our passions and from the tombs of our sins, be led to heaven.

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

**Blessing.** May Christ the Son of God, who clothed the lifeless body of the blessed Virgin in snowy whiteness, cause you to be clothed in robes of justice and works of holiness. **R.** Amen. And may he who made her victorious beyond her years, through her intercession, bring your sins to an end; and may we through her merits deserve to find rest in the future. **R.** Amen. May he who, after the flames, granted her heaven grant us, after our fall, fellowship with the angels. **R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**Laud.** “Exalted like a palm tree.” fol. CLXXX.

**Prayer.** Lord Jesus Christ, who so inflamed holy Eulalia the martyr in your Spirit that she overcame the flame of wantonness and the exterior fire did not burn her: through her intercession pour upon us the dew of your mercy, so that we may extinguish the natural fire while obtaining the remedy of salvation. **R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

In the name of the Lord.

## At Matins

**Antiphon.** “O Lord, you will open my lips.” **Psalm L.**

**Prayer.** “Let our lips rejoice, O Lord.” fol. CLXXX.

**Antiphon 1.** “Blessed are you, therefore, by the Most High God above all women.” **P.** “For this reason your praise shall not depart from the mouth of men forever.” **V.** “May he not allow your foot to be moved, nor may he who guards you slumber.” **P.** “For this reason.” **V.** “Glory and honor.” **P.** “For this reason.”

**Prayer.** Blessed, therefore, is the virgin Eulalia by you, O Most High God and eternal King, since you made her victorious through glorious martyrdom. Therefore we ask and beseech your holy mercy that your praise may never at any time depart from our mouths, but that, through the merit of the aforesaid virgin, our hearts may prevail in your law. **R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**Antiphon 2.** “Great is her beauty, exalted above the stars, and her arm is in the clouds of heaven.” **P.** “And her name remains forever.” **V.** “O God, when you went forth before your people, when you passed through the desert.” **P.** “And her name.” **V.** “Glory to the Father.” **P.** “And her name.”

**Prayer.** Great, therefore, is the beauty of the blessed virgin Eulalia, Lord God, whom you exalted above the stars when you crowned her with the glory of martyrdom. Grant us through her prayers to be free from our sins and to rejoice with you forever without end. **R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**Antiphon 3.** “You are clothed in garments of glory and adorned with holy ornaments.” **P.** “And you have become beautiful, invoked by the Lord. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.” **V.** “He has established peace within your borders and satisfies you with the fat of grain.” **P.** “And you have become.” **V.** “Glory and honor.” **P.** “And you have become.”

**Prayer.** Clothe us, Lord Jesus Christ, in garments of glory by which we may reach the banquet of your table, so that, just as you crowned the most blessed virgin Eulalia with a wreath of beauty through the shedding of blood, we too may appear beautiful before you on the day of judgment when you come. **R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**R.** “Go forth among the shadowy lilies, daughter of Jerusalem, for you are perfect and lovely, and there is no reproach in you; ascend like a bride to Lebanon.” **P.** “And receive the blessing of faith from the Lord your God.” **V.** “Rise, hasten, my beautiful beloved, and come.” **P.** “And receive the blessing.” **V.** “Glory and honor.” **P.** “And receive.”

**Prayer.** Lord Jesus Christ, who so [in the Spirit]. See above in these preceding Vespers.

## At Lauds

**For the Canticle. Antiphon.** “Blessed is the Lord, who clothed me.” **Canticle.** “Rejoicing, I shall rejoice.” fol. LXXXI.

**At the Benedictus. Antiphon.** “Daughter of Zion, bless.”

**Canticle.** “Blessed are you, Lord God.”

**Sono.** “The Lord God of heaven.”

**Laud.** “Praise the Lord.” **Psalm CXLVIII.**

**Prophecy.** “The Lord has appeared from afar.” See fol. CLXXXI. **Hymn.** “Here shines the honor of the tomb.” See above in the preceding Vespers.

**Capitulum.** O God, who mercifully taught blessed Eulalia, before the grace of her passion, what she should pray for when she ascended, since you do not allow anything to perish that she had learned from you and firmly believed: grant us that we may rejoice that what we know and believe about you has advanced us toward eternal gladness, so that what her blood merited through you by its outpouring, we, your servants, may likewise deserve to obtain through the words of our Lord.

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

**Laud.** “Exalted like a palm tree.” See fol. CLXXX.

**Blessing.** May Christ the Lord, who made the virgin Eulalia victorious amid the flames, cause you through her prayers to overcome the incentives of your flesh and, having perfectly conquered the world, to carry away victory in the heavens. **R.** Amen. And may he who clothed the virgin’s body in snowy embers in the tomb for glory himself clothe your hearts and bodies for the perfection of holiness. **R.** Amen. May you, together with her, deserve the palm of perfection, whose solemnity you now celebrate in obedience. **R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

In the name of our Lord.

## 22 February. On the Chair of Saint Peter the Apostle

### At Vespers

**Laud.** “My soul has hoped.” **Sono.** “God has girded.” See fol. CLVI.

**Antiphon.** “You are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my Church.” **P.** “And I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven.” **V.** “I have placed help upon the mighty and exalted the chosen one from my people.” **P.** “And I will give you.” **V.** “Glory and honor.” **P.** “And I will give you.”

**Laud.** “The Lord has established him.” fol. CLVII.

### Hymn

O Peter, rock of the Church,

Blessed by this name,

By which Peter is from Christ the Rock,

Not Christ the Rock from Peter.

You are Peter, who were the first

Confessor of the Son of God,

Remaining first among his members;

For this reason you were called Cephas.

This is the day on which

You were consecrated in the Roman city;

On which, ascending the throne

Of the noble Chair, you are raised up.

Therefore, with glory bestowed,

With power overflowing in you,

May you loose bound offenses

And shut the gates of hell.

Therefore, as a most merciful shepherd,

Govern the sheep entrusted to you;

Watchful within and without,

Protect us lest we be overthrown.

And with that heavenly key,

Loosening the chains of sins,

Bring the guilty in there,

Where you shine as the illustrious gatekeeper.

So that, when you have commanded

The severed members to the Prince of the heavens,

There may always be glory to the Trinity

Throughout all ages.

Amen.

**Supplication.** Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world, with the name changed, fol. CLXXXVII.

**Capitulum.** Christ, Son of God, who, intending to build your Church upon the rock, gave the keys of the kingdom of heaven to the most blessed Peter, prince of all the apostles, so that the Church might first rise built upon him who before the others merited not only to love you but also to confess you: grant us that on the day when he, destined to govern the Church, received the summit of pontifical grace, we too may receive the holiness of complete perfection, so that through him to whom you granted in the Church the power of binding and loosing, through him you may command our sins to be forgiven and us to enter the kingdom of eternal life.

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

**Blessing.** May Christ the Son of God, who founded his first Church in the most blessed Peter the Apostle, possess you, founded in himself, without stain or wrinkle. **R.** Amen. And may he who chose him as the first keeper of the keys of the kingdom make you guardians of his commandment. **R.** Amen. May you, by the command of him through whom the gate of heaven is opened, escape through him the gates of hell as sinners. **R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**Laud.** “I shall love him with all my heart, says the Lord.” **P.** “And he shall be like dew: Israel shall sprout like a lily and shall blossom. Alleluia, alleluia.” **V.** “And I shall make him firstborn, high among the kings of the earth.” **P.** “And he shall be.” **V.** “Glory and honor.” **P.** “And he shall be like.”

**Prayer.** Christ, Son of God, who entrusted your sheep to Peter, prince of all the apostles, under the testimony of your love, so that, when you questioned him and he answered, he might be proved worthy to be the shepherd of the Church: make us always to be true lovers of you, so that through him to whom the keys of the kingdom were given, through him we may deserve to enter the gate of Paradise. **R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

In the name of the Lord.

## At Matins

**Antiphon.** “O Lord, you will open my lips.” **Psalm L.**

**Prayer.** “Let our lips rejoice, O Lord.”

See fol. CLXXX.

**Antiphon 1.** “Blessed are you, Simon Bar-Jona.” **P.** “For flesh and blood has not revealed this to you, but my Father who is in heaven; he himself chose you.” **V.** “The Lord, God of gods, has spoken and summoned the earth from the rising of the sun to its setting; from Zion comes the beauty of his splendor.” **P.** “For flesh and blood.” **V.** “Glory.” **P.** “For flesh and blood.”

**Prayer.** Jesus, our Savior and Lord, who graciously conferred the primacy of apostolic dignity upon your most blessed apostle Peter, whose first calling by the name Bar-Jona signifies the beloved generation of the Law, while the name Peter resounds as the firmness of the Church in Christ: grant us, with his assistance, that, rendering the obedience of those who are called according to his teachings, we may deserve to be fellow heirs of eternal inheritance. May flesh and blood, which do not know your revelation, have no dominion in us; but may your Spirit, by whom, when filled with it, he confessed you to be the Son of God, fill us so that we may obtain the reward of the coming judgment. **R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**Antiphon 2.** “If you love me, Simon Peter, feed my sheep; you know, Lord, that I love you.” **P.** “And I shall lay down my life for you.” **V.** “To you my heart has spoken; I have sought your face; your countenance, O Lord, I shall seek.” **P.** “And I shall.” **V.** “Glory and honor.” **P.** “And I shall.”

**Prayer.** Christ, Son of God, who [the sheep]. See above in these preceding Vespers.

**Antiphon 3.** “The Lord chose me as one of the princes and appointed me as a strong man for battle.” **P.** “The Lord gave me a white robe and adorned me with a crown.” **V.** “Blessed is the Lord my God, who teaches my hands for war and my fingers for battle.” **P.** “The Lord gave me.” **V.** “Glory and honor.” **P.** “The Lord gave me.”

**Prayer.** O God, Son of God, who exalted Peter in yourself as the most solid rock, and through Peter the Church, becoming his confidence in tribulation so that he might overcome every present adversity: extend to us the help of your right hand, so that through him who, after his denial, was restored to salvation and deserved to be made firm in you, through him you may deign to rescue us from the temptations of vices. May our faith, appearing in no way wavering before you, draw both our souls and bodies to the things above. **R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**R.** “We give thanks to God, who chose you as bishop from among your brethren and gave you the honor of priesthood.” **P.** “That you may offer an immaculate offering to your God.” **V.** “Behold, the Lord has appointed you prince and given you authority over the nations.” **P.** “That you may offer an immaculate offering.” **V.** “Glory and honor.” **P.** “That you may offer an immaculate offering.”

**Prayer.** Christ, Son of the living God, whom Peter, made firm upon the rock, truly confessed, since indeed Peter was called from the rock, not the rock from Peter, and upon it the Church was founded: we humbly beseech you that the same man who received the keys of the kingdom of heaven may open to sinners the entrance of the heavenly way, so that through him from whom we received examples of sublime teaching, through him we may perceive that we have received the blessings of eternal life. **R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

## At Lauds

**For the Canticle. Antiphon.** “Inheriting the throne of glory, he gives what is vowed to the one who asks and shall bless the years of the righteous.”

**Canticle.** “It has been confirmed.” fol. LXXXVI.

**At the Benedictus. Antiphon.** “The Lord’s blessing as a reward.”

**Canticle.** “Blessed are you, Lord God.” fol. 6. **Sono.** “God has girded.” fol. CLVI.

**Laud.** “Praise the Lord from the heavens. Alleluia, alleluia; praise him in the heights. Alleluia, alleluia.” **Psalm CXLVIII.**

**Prophecy.** Reading from the Book of the Prophet Isaiah (chapter XXXII).

**R.** Thanks be to God.

[Col. 1105C] Thus says the Lord: “Behold, a king shall reign in justice, and his princes shall rule in judgment. The eyes of those who see shall not be dim, and the ears of those who hear shall listen attentively. The heart of fools shall understand knowledge, and the tongue of stammerers shall speak swiftly and plainly.

“The fool shall no longer be called a prince, nor shall the deceitful be called noble. For the fool shall speak foolishness, and his heart shall practice iniquity, to carry out hypocrisy, to speak deceitfully to him, and to empty the soul of the hungry. The instruments of the deceitful are evil, for he has devised plots to destroy the meek with lying speech when he speaks judgment against the poor.

“But the prince shall devise what is worthy of a prince, and he himself shall stand above rulers.

“Rise, wealthy women, and hear my voice; daughters, confidently receive my words with your ears, until the spirit is poured out upon you from on high. Then the desert shall become Carmel, and Carmel shall be reckoned as a forest. Judgment shall dwell in the wilderness, and justice shall sit in Carmel. The work of justice shall be peace, and the service of justice shall be quiet and security forever.

“And the people shall dwell in the beauty of peace, in tents of confidence and in abundant rest,” says the Lord Almighty.

**R.** Amen.

**Hymn.** “O Peter, rock of the Church.” **Supplication.** “Let us pray to the Redeemer.” See above in these preceding Vespers.

**Capitulum.** Most blessed apostle of God, Peter, rock of the Church, shepherd of the heavenly court, who because you were the first to confess Christ to be the Son of God deserved to receive the keys of the kingdom of heaven: by the privilege of this power you received, dissolve all our bonds, and as a glorious gatekeeper stand beside us, so that you may happily bring us sinners in.

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

**Laud.** “With psaltery and lyre.” fol. CLVIII. **Blessing.** “Christ the Son of God.” See above in these Vespers.

## 24 February. On the feast of Saint Matthias the Apostle

Let everything be said as for one principal martyr, fol. CLVI, and after the Prophecy let this Epistle be read.

**Reading from the Acts of the Apostles (chapter I).**

**R.** Thanks be to God.

[Col. 1106B] In those days Peter, rising in the midst of the brothers, said:

“Men, brothers, the Scripture had to be fulfilled which the Holy Spirit foretold through the mouth of David concerning Judas, who became the guide of those who arrested Jesus. He was numbered among us and received a share in this ministry.

“Now this man acquired a field from the reward of his iniquity, and, hanging himself, burst open in the middle, and all his entrails were poured out. This became known to all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so that that field was called in their language *Acheldemach*, that is, ‘Field of Blood.’ For it is written in the Book of Psalms:

‘Let his dwelling become desolate,
and let there be no one dwelling in it;
and let another take his episcopate.’

“Therefore, from these men who have gathered with us throughout all the time during which the Lord Jesus entered and went out among us, beginning from the baptism of John until the day on which he was taken up from us, one of these must become with us a witness to his resurrection.”

And they appointed two men: Joseph, who is called Barsabas and was surnamed Justus, and Matthias. And praying, they said:

“You, Lord, who know the hearts of all, show which one of these two you have chosen to receive the place of this ministry and Apostleship, from which Judas transgressed, so that he might go to his own place.”

And they cast lots for them, and the lot fell upon Matthias, and he was numbered with the eleven Apostles.

R\. Amen.

## FESTIVALS OF MARCH. DAY III. THE FEAST OF THE HOLY MARTYRS HEMETERIUS AND CELEDONIUS

[Col. 1106D]

Everything is to be said from *Of Several Martyrs*, four capes, fol. CLXV, except for the Hymn at Vespers, the Capitulum, the Blessing, and the Hymn at Matins.

### At Vespers

#### Hymn

The names of two martyrs

Are written in heaven,

Which Christ there inscribed

In letters of gold;

He delivered the same names,

Written in marks of blood,

To the earth.

[Col. 1107A] This blessed land of Iberia

Glories throughout the world

In this distinction:

This place seemed worthy to God

To hold their bones,

That it might be

The chaste host of blessed bodies.

Here he drew up the boiling waters;

He strikes with a double blow:

The inhabitants now throng

The sands stained with holy blood,

Entreating with voice,

With vows, and with offerings.

A stranger, and likewise

A citizen of the city,

Comes here as a settler;

For fame, the herald,

Has run ahead throughout all lands,

[Col. 1107B] Announcing that these are

The patrons of the world,

Whom those who pray surround.

No one here has gathered

Pure prayers in vain by petitioning:

The suppliant returns from here rejoicing,

His tears wiped away,

Perceiving that everything just

For which he asked has been obtained.

So great is the care

Of those who intercede for our dangers:

They do not allow anyone

To pour out an empty murmur in speech;

They hear it, and immediately carry it

To the ear of the eternal King.

[Col. 1107C] From there, through the abundant fountain of the abyss,

Gifts flow down upon the earth,

Which water the causes of suppliants

With the remedies they seek.

Christ has never denied anything

To his own witnesses:

These are the men whom neither

Harsh chains nor death terrified—

To confess the one God

At the cost of their blood.

Yet the loss of blood of such a kind

Is repaid by a longer light:

This kind of death is honorable;

It is worthy of virtuous men

To give limbs, woven with feeble veins,

To be cut away by diseases,

To give themselves to the hostile sword,

And by death to conquer the enemy.

A beautiful thing! Beneath the persecutor’s sword

He suffers the blow;

Through the great wound

A noble entrance is opened for the righteous;

The mind, washed clean in the forehead,

Leaps forth in crimson splendor.

They had not previously led

An untrained life of harsh labor—

Those soldiers whom Christ calls

To an everlasting service:

[CCXXXII] Their valor, accustomed to war by the sword,

Serves under consecrated arms.

[Col. 1108A] They abandon Caesar’s standards;

They choose the sign of the Cross.

In place of the wind-filled dragons

Which they carried upon their cloaks,

They bear before them the emblem of the wood

Which subdued the dragon.

They consider it worthless

To carry a spear in their unencumbered right hands,

To strike a wall with engines,

To surround a camp by force,

Or to stain their impious hands

With bloody slaughter.

At that time, perhaps, the savage author

Of the universal palace

Had ordered the descendants

Of the second Israel

To go to the altar:

To sacrifice to black idols,

To become renegades from Christ.

The sword-girded pestilence

Was pressing upon the free faith;

That faith, fearless through love of Christ,

Was willingly awaiting

Rods and axes

And double-clawed hooks.

The prison, bound with harsh

Fetters, attacks their necks;

Throughout the whole forum

The executioner exercises barbarous hands;

Truth is considered a crime,

And the faithful voice is punished.

[Col. 1108C] Then valor, struck down by the sword,

Beat the sorrowful ground,

And, thrust upon mournful pyres,

Drank in the flames with its mouth.

Then it was sweet for the righteous to be burned;

Sweet to endure the iron.

Sing more joyfully, with votive rejoicing,

The glory of the eternal King

Throughout every age,

Exulting in song—

He who turns the revolving sphere,

Who sustains the world everywhere.

Amen.

#### Supplication

Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world, changing the names, fol. CLXXXVII.

[Col. 1108D] #### Capitulum

Behold, as we celebrate the sacred solemnities of the holy brothers, we beseech you, God of mercy, with devoted intention: since by the burial of their bodies you have consecrated the land of Iberia, may you, through their prayers, guard in peace the whole Church redeemed by your blood. Thus, with these same saints interceding, may we deserve to be heard by you, from whom we receive the command to pray.

Our Father. Delivered from evil. Fol. 2.

#### Blessing

May almighty God, to whom the most blessed martyrs Hemeterius and Celedonius, as the sign of their confession and faith, sent a *orarium* and a ring to be carried up to heaven, preserve you by both gifts of grace.

R\. Amen.

May you, strengthened by them in the power both of faith and confession, be counted citizens of the eternal heavenly homeland, whose twofold feast you celebrate today with rejoicing.

R\. Amen.

And just as the fostered people rejoice at the reception of their two bodies, so may the whole Church rejoice that it is guarded and defended by their patronage.

R\. Amen.

### Hymn at Matins

Here the hearts of two dear brothers

Grow warm;

A faithful companionship

Had joined them throughout all time.

They stand ready to endure

Whatever final fate might bring:

Whether the neck must be offered

To the public double-edged axe,

After the violence of cracking whips,

[Col. 1109B] After fiery racks;

Or whether the breast must be offered

To leopards or lions.

Shall we, begotten for Christ,

Be dedicated to Mammon?

And, bearing the form of God,

Shall we serve the world?

Far be it that heavenly fire

Should mingle with darkness.

Let it be enough that the life

First captured under contract

Paid every debt,

Having discharged the affairs of Caesar.

It is time to repay to God

Whatever belongs to God.

Go, commanders of standards,

And you, tribunes, stand forth;

Offer golden collars,

The rewards of the wounded.

Here the clear voice of angels

Calls the soldiers to their pay;

There Christ presides over

The cohorts in white garments,

And, reigning from his throne above,

Condemns the infamous gods—

The monsters which you fashion

As gods, for us to mock.

[CCXXXIII] As they speak these words,

The martyrs are overwhelmed

By a thousand punishments:

A harshness twisted around

Both hands binds them in fetters,

And rubbed steel

Encloses their necks harshly

With rings.

O obsolete forgetfulness

Of a silent antiquity!

These things are begrudged us,

And fame itself is extinguished;

For once a blasphemous attendant

Removed the written tablets,

So that learned ages,

Through enduring books,

Would not spread through the ears

Of posterity, in sweet speech,

The order, time, and manner

Of the recorded Passion.

[Col. 1110A] Yet these ancient silences

Withhold only this:

How, dragged for a long time

By unbroken chains to the hair,

The torturer afflicted the men,

Or with what display he adorned them.

That hidden glory is not concealed,

Nor does it grow old with time:

The gifts sent upward

Through the air have flown away,

Showing by their reward

That the way to heaven was open.

The ring, symbolizing his faith,

Is borne upon a cloud;

[Col. 1110B] The *orarium*, as they say,

Gives the pledge of his mouth.

Carried away by the heavenly breath,

The gifts enter the innermost light.

Through the axis of the melting sky

The gleam of gold is hidden;

And the whiteness of the woven cloth

Escapes the pursuing gaze.

They are carried up to the stars

And are seen no more.

The assembled crowd saw this;

The executioner himself saw it,

And, astonished, restrained his hand

And grew pale with wonder.

Yet he completed the blow,

[Col. 1110C] So that the glory might not perish.

Do you not now believe, brutish

Pagan people of the Basques,

That the cruel man sacrificed

The sacred blood of heroes?

Do you believe that the spirit

Of the victims was carried to God?

See how openly the fierce demons

Are subdued here,

They who, having seized men

In wolf-like fashion,

Disfigure their inmost hearts;

They strangle even the minds

And mingle themselves with the senses.

Then, already filled with his enemy,

The raging man is brought forward,

Foaming and breathing out saliva,

Twisting his raw eyes;

He must be cleansed by examination,

Though not of his own crimes.

Hearing this, the torturer approaches,

With a mournful wail.

The body is torn by lashes,

Yet no lash is seen;

And the man himself, suspended,

Grows in the hidden bonds.

By these methods the power of the martyrs

Shakes the filthy robber;

It restrains him, tortures him, burns him;

It fastens chains upon him.

[Col. 1111A] The afflicted thief leaps forth,

Driven from his very marrow.

He leaves his prey unharmed,

Flees with dry jaws,

And restores it wholly safe,

From the lowest nail to the hair,

Confessing that he is burning,

Though he is not an inhabitant of Gehenna.

Why should I speak of bodies,

White and cleansed from long diseases?

When a chilly horror

Shakes the discolored limbs,

The swelling leaves the face from one side,

And from the other the true color returns.

This good the Savior himself

Has granted us to enjoy:

He consecrated the bodies of the martyrs

To our city,

And now they protect the settlers

Whom the Iberus waters.

Stand now, unconquered mothers,

Rejoicing over your children restored;

Let the voices of wives resound,

Joyful at the safety of their husbands.

Let this day be festive for us;

Let it be consecrated to joys.

Glory to the Father and to the Son,

And always to the Paraclete;

Praise, power, and strength,

And abundance of graces.

All things confess God

Throughout the ages of ages.

Amen.

[CCXXXIV] ## FESTIVALS OF APRIL. DAY XVI. THE FEAST OF SAINT ENGRATIA, OR OF THE EIGHTEEN MARTYRS

Everything is to be said from *Of Several Martyrs*, fol. CLXII, except the Hymn, which is *Bis novem noster*, fol. CL.

## FESTIVALS OF MAY. DAY I. THE FEAST OF SAINT TORQUATUS AND HIS COMPANIONS, THE BISHOPS

[Col. 1111D]

### At Vespers

Lauda. *Exortum est*. Fol. CLXII.

Sono. Alleluia. “Their sound has gone out into all the earth.”

P\. “And their words to the ends of the world. Alleluia.”

V\. Alleluia. “There are no speech or language in which their voices are not heard.”

P\. “And their words to the ends of the world.”

The Lord be with you.

R\. And with you.

Antiphon. Alleluia. “These are the men renowned for their virtue.”

P\. “Teachers of the people, administering judgment in their doctrine.”

V\. “The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament announces the works of his hands.”

P\. “Teachers of the people.”

V\. “Glory and honor.”

P\. “Teachers of the people.”

The Lord be with you.

R\. And with you.

Lauda. “The Lord filled them with discipline and wisdom. Alleluia.”

P\. “He created in them the grace of his Holy Spirit; he filled their hearts with understanding. Alleluia, alleluia.”

V\. “They cried to the Lord when they were afflicted, and he delivered them from their distresses.”

P\. “He created in them.”

V\. “Glory and honor.”

P\. “He created in them.”

#### Hymn

Now the white toga of Romulus’ city

Shines forth, destined for seven pontiffs,

Whom ancient tradition assigns

As sent from the Apostles to Hesperia’s faith.

These are the heralds of brilliant light:

Torquatus, Tesiphons, and Hesychius;

Then Indaletius, or Secundus,

Joined with Euphrasius and Caecilius.

Endowed with the evangelical lamp,

[Col. 1112B] They illuminate the arid lands

Of the western region,

So that they may burn with Catholic fires

And the harmful furnaces

May yield to the torches.

Acci comes close at hand to the men,

Only twelve stadia away,

Where they had settled from afar.

They send their followers to seek food,

That their weary bodies might be restored

With nourishment.

There the disciples see

The idols of the nations honored

With empty rites.

While they linger there, grieving with tears,

They are instead terrified

By the impious deeds.

Soon the insane, roaring crowd of attendants,

When it recognized in them

The marks of faith,

Drives them in swift assault

Over rough ground as far as the river bridge.

[Col. 1112C] But the bridge, stronger than mighty masonry,

Suddenly collapses and falls apart,

Rescuing the righteous from the hands of the enemies,

And plunging the enemies beneath

The river’s whirlpool.

This is the first path of faith

Among the peoples.

Among them the holy woman Luparia

Meets the saints as they approach

And entreats them,

Storing the saints’ instructions

Within her heart.

Then the woman who served Christ,

Obedient to their request,

Decided to build a structure for the saints,

So that the water of the baptistery

Might be opened,

And grace might cleanse everyone’s sins.

There the holy woman of God is baptized,

And, washed in the bath of life,

Is reborn.

[Col. 1112D] Here the people immediately hasten to the faith,

And become numerous in Catholic doctrine.

After this the beloved fellowship of the pontiffs

Hurries away and divides among seven cities,

So that, distributed among the places,

They might establish their teaching

And set the peoples ablaze

With scattered fires.

Through these men the grace of faith,

Introduced into the lands of Hesperia,

Shone forth with early brilliance.

By varied signs and by the power

Of miracles they urge people to believe.

From then on, renowned for the fruits of justice,

They bring their lives to an end

With manifold increase,

Surrounded by tombs in their own cities.

Thus, though their ashes are scattered,

There is one crown.

From here, powerful crowd,

With a single voice sevenfold,

We ask you for the hidden things of our hearts:

That through your prayers,

As companions of the citizens of heaven,

We may be carried to the starry heavens.

Let glory be to the triune and one Lord,

To the Father with the Begotten

And the Paraclete,

Who alone is the triune and one Lord,

Mightily sustaining the ages of ages.

Amen.

#### Supplication

Let us pray, changing the names, fol. CLXII.

#### Capitulum

Behold, Lord, as we commemorate the memory of our bishops, through whose teachings Christian faith first flowed into our regions—namely Torquatus, Secundus, Indaletius, Tesiphons, Euphrasius, Caecilius, [CCXXXV] and Hesychius—we offer you this evening light, beseeching you to cleanse us through their prayers from the filth of sins and renew us by the grace of spiritual gifts, since you have deigned to visit the western region through their presence.

Our Father. Delivered from evil. Fol. 2.

#### Blessing

May God, who gloriously became the guide of Torquatus and his companions on their journey, himself be the forgiver of your sins.

R\. Amen.

And may he who, by the wondrous breaking of the bridge, delivered their disciples from the impious, rescue you from all incitements to carnal vices.

R\. Amen.

May you be able, with that same ardor of spirit by which we believe they preached the name of Christ in your regions, both to reject earthly things and always to retain heavenly things in your hearts.

R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

Lauda. “You are holy vessels for the Lord, shining with gold. Alleluia.”

[Col. 1113C] P\. “Because you willingly offered your souls to the Lord God. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.”

V\. “Blessed are you by the Lord, who made heaven and earth.”

P\. “Because you willingly offered.”

V\. “Glory and honor.”

P\. “Because you willingly offered.”

#### Prayer

Truly blessed, Lord, and worthy of extraordinary honor are those whose portion you have deigned to be. Therefore, through the intercession of your saints Torquatus and his companions, may heavenly love, burning within us, utterly destroy whatever in us does not serve you. And afterward may your mercy join us in the heavenly kingdom with these saints, whose souls are in your hand.

R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

[Col. 1113D] In the name of the Lord.

### At Matins

Antiphon. “Give to us.” Psalm L. Prayer. “Restore to us, Lord.” Fol. CLXIII.

Antiphon 1. “These are those who were sent throughout the world and prostrated themselves before the Lamb.”

P\. “Holding golden bowls full of incense, which are the memorials of the saints, singing a new song.”

V\. “Their sound has gone out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world.”

P\. “Holding golden bowls.”

V\. “Glory and honor.”

P\. “Holding golden bowls.”

#### Prayer

These are, Lord, the seven torches sent from heaven into the regions of Hesperia to drive away the infidelity of its foul night. Therefore, because of this gift of grace conferred upon us by you, may the fragrance of evangelical teaching and of commandments rightly fragrant as incense restore us; and, more fully filled with this doctrine, may our hearts and mind bring forth that very thing which our worthy petition earnestly asks to be rewarded by you at the time of judgment.

R\. Amen.

Through your mercy, etc.

Antiphon 2. “Blessed and worthy of great honor are those whose portion is God.”

P\. “For the kingdom was prepared for them from the beginning, and their souls are in the hand of God.”

V\. “The righteous cried out, and the Lord heard them; and he delivered them from all their tribulations.”

P\. “For the kingdom was prepared for them from the beginning.”

V\. “Glory and honor.”

P\. “For the kingdom was prepared for them from the beginning.”

Prayer. “Truly blessed, Lord, and worthy of extraordinary honor.” Seek it above in the preceding Vespers.

[Col. 1114B] Antiphon 3. “They taught your law brilliantly; their works are many.”

P\. “Stored up with you, Lord.”

V\. “Those who trust in the Lord are like Mount Zion, which shall not be moved forever, which dwells in Jerusalem.”

P\. “Stored up.”

V\. “Glory and honor.”

P\. “Stored up.”

#### Prayer

God, Son of God, light of the stars, radiance of the constellations, bright and morning star, everlasting brightness, and abundant instruction of the saints: we ask you, through the continual intercession of your saints Torquatus and his companions, to instruct us with the rod of your justice. Thus, by our deeds, may we exist in heart as what they preached when brilliantly illumined; so that, after death, we may approach unharmed and freed from the bond of sins that which is stored up with you—“that which eye has not seen nor ear heard.”

R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

R\. “The saints who instructed many in righteousness will shine like the brightness of the firmament.”

P\. “And like the stars of heaven throughout perpetual eternity.”

V\. “These are the holy men whom the Lord chose in sincere love; and from their teaching the Church shines like the sun and moon.”

P\. “And like the stars.”

V\. “Glory and honor.”

P\. “And like the stars.”

#### Prayer

Christ, Son of God, who, foreknowing your saints, chose them before the foundation of the world and established them here as our example: make us so obedient to the teaching of the saints that after our death we may deserve, by adoption as sons, to become partakers.

[Col. 1114D] R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

### At Lauds

At the Canticle. Antiphon. “You who willingly offered yourselves to danger, bless the Lord, declaring his righteousness and mercy toward the strong men of Israel.”

Canticle. “You who willingly offered yourselves.” Fol. CLXIII.

At the Benedictus. Antiphon. “Holy and humble in heart, spirits and souls of the righteous, bless the Lord.”

V\. “Righteous and holy priests, humble in heart, bless the Lord.”

Canticle. “Blessed are you, Lord.” Fol. 6.

Sono. Alleluia. “Their sound has gone out into all the earth.” Seek it above in the preceding Vespers.

Lauda. “Praise the Lord from the heavens, alleluia, alleluia; praise him in the heights, alleluia, alleluia.” Psalm CXLVIII.

#### Reading from the Book of Wisdom (Chapter XLIV)

R\. Thanks be to God.

The Lord displayed great glory through his magnificence from of old. They ruled in their powers: men great in strength and endowed with wisdom, proclaiming in the dignity of prophets, ruling in the present age, and by the power of wisdom teaching the peoples most holy words.

In their youth they sought musical modes and recited the songs of the Scriptures. All of them were rich in strength and devoted to beauty; they brought peace to their households.

All these obtained glory among the generations of their nation, and in their days they were held in praise. Those born from them seek their name, recounting their praises. Yet there are others whose memory does not exist: they perished as though they had never been; they were born as though they had not been born, and their children with them.

But those men were merciful, whose compassion did not fail; and good inheritance remains with their descendants and their offspring. Their seed stood firm in their covenants, and their children because of them.

Their seed will remain forever, and their glory will not be abandoned. Their bodies were buried in peace, and their name will live from generation to generation. The peoples recount their wisdom, and the Church proclaims their praise.

R\. Amen.

Hymn. “The city of Romulus.” Supplication. “Let us pray to the Redeemer.” Seek it above in the preceding Vespers.

[Col. 1115C] #### Capitulum

The annual celebration of those seven illustrious and shining pontiffs, returning with the passage of time, is present, Lord—an auspicious solemnity! Through them you once deigned to plant the rule of the new faith in the western region with the hoe of preaching; through them you deigned to drive away the doctrine of wicked superstition with the flashing ray of light.

Therefore, through their intercession, let the furnaces of our desires burn in the sight of your glory. Let the truthful holocausts of prayers be brought forward; let the pure libations of vows be accepted. While these saints pray, grant to all who serve at your sacred altar the purity of snowy brightness in chastity; grant to virgins the integrity of mind and body, of nourishing modesty and worthy of reward; and grant to the continent and to all the faithful together the fruits of holy works, to be rightly blessed by you at the future judgment.

May Torquatus obtain for us ornaments of virtues as necklaces. May Tesiphons, from you who are the fountain of life, satisfy us with the cup of the most abundant stream of teaching. May Hesychius cleanse away the expiations of our sin. May Indaletius, herald of good works, provide spiritual nourishment. May Secundus join us to the participation of the elect in the joy of your future coming. May Euphrasius, through the fourfold stream of the Gospels, strengthen the doctrines of the Catholic faith. May Caecilius associate us with the assemblies of angels.

Thus also may the people, fostered by your saints, rightly celebrate the feast in songs of their lips and a jubilation of praise, and may they overflow sevenfold with the gift of graces, so that, the burden of sins removed, they may be led by the guidance of those mentioned to the kingdom, to contemplate it in heavenly dwellings, and brought to that which eye has not seen nor ear heard, which you have prepared for those who love you.

[Col. 1116A] Our Father. Delivered from evil. Fol. 2.

Lauda. “You are holy vessels for the Lord.”

Blessing. “The God who guided Torquatus and his companions.” Seek it above in the preceding Vespers.

#### Hymn

Sing, tongue, the glorious

Battle of the conflict,

And proclaim upon the trophy

Of the Cross the noble triumph:

How the Redeemer of the world,

Sacrificed, conquered.

The Maker, grieving over

The deception of the first parent,

When by the bite of the deadly fruit

He fell into death,

Then himself marked the wood,

So that he might undo

The losses caused by the wood.

This was the order demanded

For our salvation:

That the art of the many-formed betrayer

Might be defeated by art,

And that healing might be brought from the place

From which the enemy had wounded us.

When therefore the fullness

[Col. 1120B] Of sacred time came,

The Maker of the world,

Sent from the Father’s citadel,

Was born,

And came forth made flesh

From a virgin’s womb.

The infant wails, enclosed

Within the narrow manger;

The virgin mother binds

His limbs in swaddling clothes,

And a band tightly encircles

His hands, feet, and legs.

When six periods of years

Had now been completed,

Fulfilling the time of his bodily life,

He, born for this by his own will,

Gave himself to suffering;

The Lamb was lifted upon the Cross,

To be sacrificed upon the wood.

Here vinegar, gall, reed,

Spittle, nails, and spear

Pierce the gentle body;

Blood flows forth in a stream.

Earth, sea, stars, and world—

By this stream are they washed!

Faithful Cross, among all others

The one noble tree:

No forest produces another like you

In leaf, flower, and bud.

Sweet wood, sweet nails,

You bear the sweet burden.

[Col. 1120D] Bend your branches, lofty tree;

Relax your stretched fibers;

And let that stiffness grow gentle,
Whom birth gave,

so that you might stretch out your gentle trunk

for the limbs of the heavenly King.

You alone were worthy

to bear the price of the world;

and to prepare a harbor

for the world’s shipwrecked Sailor,

whom the sacred blood anointed

when the Lamb’s blood was poured out.

Glory and honor to God,

the Most High, everywhere,

one to the Father and the Son,

[Col. 1121A] and the renowned Paraclete,

to whom belong praise and power

through everlasting ages.

Amen.

**Supplication.** Let us beseech our Redeemer, the Lord Jesus Christ, with every supplication, that he may graciously deign to make us righteous by the standard of his Cross. **R.** Grant this, eternal almighty God.

**Capitula.** Our Lord Jesus Christ, our Creator and Redeemer, who know that we have fallen wounded in our sins, raise us up through the strength and victory of the holy Cross. Grant us as the reward of salvation that which for our sake was a painful punishment to you, so that by what you took upon yourself—death for the victory over death—we may obtain forgiveness of sins and eternal life.

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

**Benediction.** May Christ, the Son of God, who reconciled all things through the blood of his Cross, mortify us by a true crucifixion. **R.** Amen. May we, always raised up into the victory of the Cross and with the devil ever defeated, triumph. **R.** Amen. May we, celebrating this venerable feast of the Cross with the readiest devotion, be found worthy to be happy both here and forever. **R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

Through mercy.

**P.** And the woman who keeps the paths of righteousness, guarding the ways of the saints. Alleluia, alleluia.

**V.** But the salvation of the righteous is from the Lord, and he is their protector in time of tribulation.

**V.** Glory and honor.

**P.** And a gracious woman.

**Hymn.**

Glorious Jerusalem,

one mother of martyrs,

blessed lot after labors,

holy right after storms,

you who, rejoicing in the course of your children,

are raised up with greater readiness;

wipe away mourning, take up applause,

open the harbor to your citizens.

Receive those whom you sustained,

now more joyful after their triumphs,

among whom you resound victorious;

grant the honor of victory.

[CCXLII] Adrian, together with his blessed

wife Natalia,

[Col. 1124A] a twofold banquet of love,

a union of gifts of grace,

a fiery offering, a cherished pledge,

a celibate marriage:

on this day, dedicating vows of conscience

to you, they hasten back to you in their courses;

hence, rejoicing together,

they give gifts to God in turn,

the grace of marriage.

He shines with the supreme

mark of suffering;

she, with the appointed gift

of devoted compassion.

Their course is different,

[Col. 1124B] their lot and glory one.

This man is joined among men

bound for the hope above;

he longs immediately

to be enrolled with the blessed.

Then he is bound to oxen,

and is again handed over to her.

His wife, rising to see him,

through hurried encounters,

enters the distant prisons,

sees the camps of the martyrs;

she kisses the blessed chains

and gives her husband strength.

As though urging him toward the contest,

she persuades him of the power

of the sacred arena;

[Col. 1124C] she urges the promises of heaven,

and urges him still more continually,

by voice, vow, and accomplished intercession,

with the urgency of her gift.

Freed at her summons

from bodily bonds,

he is struck,

his entrails are torn out,

his limbs are stretched by their attachments;

and with the structure of his feet severed,

his body is dissolved.

His beloved wife, moved by her final kisses,

said to him: “Rise, extend the right hand,

which has been cut off from your spouse;

give it to me as a pledge of love,

[Col. 1124D] give me a gift of sweetness.”

Willingly he extended his hand,

which the executioner cut off.

Without delay, amid those wounds,

he was killed

and, with a second dowry

of blood, endowed his wife.

She, prolonging the practice

of sacred labor among those who were contending,

makes bearable whatever is painful,

softened, worn down, and weakened.

She warns, commands, and cherishes,

a challenger to glory.

You might see manly strength

[Col. 1125A] in fervent efforts,

tending the exhausted limbs,

binding up wounds

with applied remedies,

serving with a healing hand

or with her voice

the peril of the martyrs.

She brings them counsels of peace,

brings food for consolation;

serving all by her deeds,

she is punished in each one.

Yet her husband’s crown,

returned through triumphs,

while she smears her own body

with the blood of the devout,

suffers nothing less from those

in whom she has conquered.

[Col. 1125B] O truly sacred and honorable

bond of marriage!

O new course of labors

for a unique union!

Both run, both conquer;

there is glory for each.

This diversity of gifts,

O heavenly Guardian,

draws and marks them out for that

fatherland where the blessed,

after their contests,

raise praises to you.

[Col. 1125C] That illustrious Michael,

the Archangel,

shines here,

as one outstanding in accomplishing

God-like mighty works.

His name gives a place

to the power that comes

from the favor of his gift.

Therefore, at his intercession,

or through that of your martyrs,

bring us this healing,

by which you may wash away guilt;

loosen the knots of sins

and grant the soothing remedy of grace.

When the dread day

of the Judge dawns,

may we be joined to the joys

of the feasts we proclaim;

[Col. 1125D] and for those who have no crown,

may faith be unto glory.

[CCXLIII] Praise to you throughout all time,

undivided Trinity,

highest praise, honor, and power,

singular glory,

which resounds that you are the Lord

through ages of ages.

Amen.

**Supplication.** Let us beseech the Redeemer, changing the names, fol. CLXXXVII.

**Capitula.** Christ, who by the manifold diversity of virtues and the abundant contest of sufferings advanced the blessed martyrs Adrian and Natalia to the kingdom—while you endow him with strength to endure and her beforehand with the grace of service; while through him you lay low the enemies of faith and through her refresh the martyrs bound for you—grant us, by both virtues, to attain what we desire and escape what we fear. Having become victors over carnal vices, may we be made worthy before you through the display of good services. And since we do not deserve a crown through the shedding of bodily blood, may we be brought to forgiveness through the offering of our vows.

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

May the flesh have power to do nothing that displeases you; may the mouth proclaim nothing that disagrees with your command. God’s gift remains with the righteous, and its progress shall have success forever. Blessed is the husband of a good woman; the number of her years is beyond reckoning. A strong woman delights her husband, and she will complete the years of his life in peace. A good portion, a good woman, in the portion of those who fear God she shall be given to a man for good deeds. The grace of a diligent woman [Col. 1128A] delights her husband, and she will make his bones fat. Her discipline is God’s gift. For a sensible and quiet woman, there is no alteration of a well-instructed soul. Grace upon grace: a holy and modest woman. No weighing is worthy of a continent soul. As the sun rising upon the world of the Most High God, so is the beauty of a good woman in the adornment of a house; a shining lamp upon a holy lampstand, the beauty of her face upon a steadfast age. Golden columns upon silver bases, and firm feet upon the feet of a steadfast woman. Eternal foundations upon solid rock, and the commandments of God in the heart of a holy woman. **R.** Amen.

May we have as companions in virtue those whom we hold blameless in covenant; summoned by them to glory, since we stand equal to them in nature, may we, set aflame by the example of each, receive forgiveness after our passage through their alternating merits, since by the singular effectiveness of good works we do not deserve to earn a crown.

## June 19

# The Feast of Saints Gervasius and Protasius, Martyrs

[Col. 1129B] Let everything be said from “Of Many Martyrs,” with nine lessons, except the hymn, which is this:

I sing new thanks to you, Jesus,

for a new gift discovered:

for Protasius and Gervasius,

the martyrs who were found.

Pious victims lay hidden,

but they were not hidden;

for sacred blood cannot remain concealed,

the blood that cries out to God the Father.

Grace, shining from heaven,

revealed their sacred limbs.

We could not be martyrs,

but we discovered martyrs.

For one who seeks

the voices of witnesses,

there faith is established.

The man feeble in mind is healed;

by their help he confesses the martyrs.

The blind man, having received light,

proves the merit of the sacred death.

Severus is the man’s name;

he was a servant of the public authorities.

When he touched the martyr’s garment

and wiped his clouded face,

light immediately shone forth,

and blindness, driven away, fled.

The crowd, released from its bonds,

freed from the coils of the dragon,

set free throughout all the cities,

returns home with joy.

We have seen ancient ages

and demons cast down,

and through the touch and even the shadow

of bodies, health restored to the sick.

To God the Father be glory,

and to his only Son,

together with the Holy Paraclete,

through everlasting ages.

Amen.
