Source/review notes: The supplied chunk opens mid-hymn and closes at the end of a liturgical cross-reference; these are ordinary supplied chunk boundaries, not claimed manuscript lacunae. In the Saint Zoilus hymn, the printed form *infolata* is retained beside its contextual gloss, “crowned with the *infula*.”

And thus, on the day of the age,

the Word of God becomes something to be proclaimed;

this barren woman becomes a mother,

foreseeing the Virgin’s fruit,

a Son greater than his mother,

the holy minister of Baptism:

thus, after his birth, he shed light upon the Lord who was before him.

Let us pray with poured-out prayers

to God the Father with the Son,

together with the Holy Spirit,

one mighty in name.

Amen.

[Col. 1134D] Supplication. Let us pray to the Redeemer, with the name changed; fol. CLXXXVII.

Capitulum. “Here are present, Lord, the beginnings of Christian joy: long ago, the sanctified Voice preceded the Word who was to be born in the flesh, and the herald who proclaimed the Light’s rising announced it illustriously. From this arose both the sacraments of the Christian faith and the signs of the saving bath. His conception is proved a miracle; his birth, a joy. We therefore ask that, as we now receive with rejoicing the birthday of your Forerunner, we may also approach the feast of your own birth with purified hearts: that the voice which proclaimed you in the wilderness may cleanse us in this world; and that he who, preparing the way for the coming Lord, washed living bodies with his baptism may now cleanse our hearts from vices and error by his prayers. Thus, following in the footsteps of the Voice, may we deserve to reach the promises of the Word, since at your command we pray:

Our Father. Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

Benediction. Almighty God the Father, who willed John to be the forerunner of his Only-Begotten Son who was to be born in the flesh, may he deign to rescue you, protected by angelic guardianship, from every evil. R. Amen. And may he who granted many people joy at John’s birth also lavish upon the prayers of the peoples who supplicate through him the fulfillment of their petitions. R. Amen. May he make you, through him whom he willed to be the lamp of the Light, blameless disciples of the truth. R. Amen.

Through his mercy.

[Col. 1135B] Lauda. “From my mother’s womb he called me; he appointed me prophet among the nations,” P. “And beneath the shelter of his hand he protected me.” Alleluia, alleluia. V. “And the Lord repaid me according to my righteousness, and according to the innocence of my hands before his eyes.” P. “And beneath the shelter.” V. Glory and honor to the Father. P. “And beneath the shelter.”

Prayer. Voice of the Word, friend of the Bridegroom, you who proclaim that Christ will come in the wilderness, preparing his way in the hearts of unbelievers: be for us likewise the preparer and purifier of our hearts and minds, so that what you once accomplished for them by the preaching of your voice, you may now obtain for us by your daily intercessions. Thus, just as the way was prepared through you for the Lord in Israel, so may a joyful dwelling in the heavens be prepared for us through you after our passage from this life. R. Amen.

Through.

At Matins.

Antiphon. “O Lord, open my lips, and my mouth shall proclaim your praise.” Psalm L.

Prayer. May our lips rejoice in you, Lord, through the proclamation of truth; may they not be dissolved into the babbling of falsehood. May they always speak glory to you and not resound indecorously with the quarrels of disputes. May our soul also, which you redeemed, by praising the triumph of your martyr John the Baptist and Forerunner, deserve to have you favorable through his patronage. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Antiphon 1. “An angel appeared to Zechariah at the right side of the altar, saying to him: Do not fear, because your prayer has been heard.” P. “Behold, a son will be born to you, for he will be great before the Lord.” V. “I will hear what the Lord God speaks within me, for he will speak peace to his people, to his saints, and to those who turn their hearts toward him.” P. “Behold, a son will be born.” V. Glory and honor to the Father. P. “Behold, a son will be born.”

Prayer. Your benefits, Lord, are full and overflowing, by which you deigned, when an angel appeared at the right side of the altar, to visit the old age of the priest Zechariah. He deserved both to hear, “Do not fear, because your prayer has been heard,” and to be sustained equally by sight and by speech, so that, enriched by this gift, he might recognize either what he had understood in the symbolic figures of the past or what was appearing in the grace of the novelty shown to him. Instructed, therefore, by these examples, we ask you, most holy God, that our trusting hearts may always receive your mysteries and place their fixed faith in your messengers. Thus, through the intercession of your Forerunner, may a way be prepared for you in our hearts, so that, while you remain eternally within us, we may escape punishment. R. Amen.

Through.

Antiphon 2. “When Elizabeth saw Mary, the infant leaped in her womb.” P. “And she was filled with the Holy Spirit, cried out, and said: Why is this granted to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?” V. “Truth has arisen from the earth, and righteousness has looked forth from heaven.” P. “And she was filled.” V. Glory and honor to the Father. P. “And she was filled.”

[CCL] Prayer. God, who granted John, the Son of promise, to barren Elizabeth, unfruitful in old age, and who, while he was still carried enclosed in her womb, prophesied by his greeting the God dwelling as a guest in the Virgin: we ask and entreat you that, since by his preaching you opened to believers the gate of the heavenly kingdom, through his intercession you may lead us to glory in your kingdom. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Antiphon 3. “From my mother’s womb he called my name, to preach peace, to give joy to the peoples.” P. “To prepare a way in the desert for those who mourn in Zion.” V. “God, who girded me with strength and made my way blameless.” P. “To prepare a way for those who mourn.” V. Glory and honor to the Father. P. “To prepare a way for those who mourn.”

Prayer. Christ, Son of God, who call your Forerunner by his name both before his birth and glorify him by that same name after his birth—since an angel foretells in his name that he will be born, and the peoples marvel at him when born under that name—we ask you, through him whom you willed to proclaim peace to the peoples, to wipe away the filth of our guilt. May he who came to prepare for you a perfect people restore the peoples of believers to be illumined by your splendor. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

R. This is the Forerunner who was sent forth, the shining lamp before God; for he is John, P. who prepared the way for the Lord in the wilderness and, to point out the Lamb of God, illumined human minds by the sweet proclamation of his voice. V. “Among those born of women there has not arisen anyone greater than John the Baptist.” P. “Who prepared the way for the Lord.” V. Glory and honor to the Father. P. “Who prepared the way.”

Prayer. God, who established your Forerunner John as a burning and shining lamp in your temple, so that by the ardor of faith with which he burned he might also illumine others with the flame of his works: grant us, by his merits, both to possess the ardor of your sweetness and to reach the light of your eternity. Grant our frailty that our souls may be your lamps, so that, while you pour into them the oil of sweetness, you may console them with future joys. R. Amen.

Through.

At Lauds.

For the Canticle. Antiphon. “And you, child, will be called prophet of the Most High, for you will go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways, to give knowledge of salvation to his people.”

Canticle of Zechariah (Luke I).

Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, * for he has visited and accomplished the redemption of his people;

And he raised up for us a horn of salvation in the house of David his servant. * As he spoke through the mouth of his holy prophets, who have been from of old:

And he delivered you from your enemies and from the hand of all who hate us: * to show mercy to our fathers;

And to remember his holy covenant. * The oath that he swore to Abraham our father, that he would grant us:

That, delivered without fear from the hand of our enemies, * we might serve him in holiness and righteousness before him all our days.

And you, child, will be called prophet of the Most High: * for you will go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways:

To give knowledge of salvation to his people, * for the forgiveness of their sins:

Through the merciful compassion of our God, * by which the rising from on high has visited us:

To illumine those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death: * to direct our feet into the way of peace.

Antiphon. “And you, child.”

Prayer. Christ, Son of God, who choose John, your sanctified Forerunner, as your prophet, preparing your way at the beginning of your ways, and through him send that child before you as a messenger of good news: grant us always to have our hearts above, so that the Word whom the Voice, still confined in the womb, proclaimed may enrich sinners with the gift of pardoning mercy. R. Amen.

Through.

For the Benedictus. Antiphon. “The Lord’s blessing hastens as the reward of the righteous.”

Canticle. “Blessed are you, Lord.” fol. 6.

Sono. “Thus says the Lord: Before I formed you in the womb, I knew you; and before you came forth from the womb,” P. “I sanctified you.” Alleluia. V. “I also gave you as a prophet to the nations, and everything that I command you, you shall speak. Do not fear: behold, I have given my words into your mouth, and I have set you over the nations and over kingdoms.” P. “I sanctified you.”

[CCLI] Lauda. “Praise the Lord from the heavens, alleluia; praise him in the heights, alleluia.” Psalm CXLVIII.

Reading from the Book of the Prophet Isaiah (Chapter LXI).

R. Thanks be to God.

“The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me; he has sent me to announce good news to the meek, to heal the brokenhearted, to proclaim release to captives and opening to the imprisoned; to proclaim an acceptable year of the Lord and a day of vengeance for our God; to comfort all who mourn; to place joy in Zion upon those who mourn, and to give them a crown instead of ashes, the oil of joy instead of mourning, a cloak of praise instead of a spirit of sorrow. And they shall be called strong in righteousness, the Lord’s planting, for his glorification. And I shall give their work in truth, and I shall make an everlasting covenant with them. Their seed shall be known among the nations, and their offspring in the midst of the peoples. All who see them shall recognize them, because they are the seed whom the Lord has blessed.” R. Amen.

Hymn.

Sound the lyre, Zechariah,

chief of the priests,

whose wife, joined to him,

was descended from Aaron’s daughters

and clung to the marriage chamber,

accustomed to prophetic announcements.

Holier in their works,

they surpassed the others;

and with sincere obedience

they walked in the Lord’s commands,

and, with no child granted,

they advanced into old age.

Soon the hour shone forth

at the time of the incense.

The prophet was carrying

the customary fire in the censers,

bearing the nectarous fragrance

into the sacred courts.

He hears a message from heaven,

a resounding messenger;

when he foresaw its brightness,

trembling seized the prophet,

whom the strong one made more steadfast

with gentle words.

“Behold, your wife, joined to you in the marriage bed,

bears offspring;

you shall immediately give him

the name JOHN.

His birth is proclaimed

throughout the whole world.”

“This man will be great before the Lord,

filled with the Holy Spirit

while still within his mother’s womb,

and he will go before the Lord;

in strength and spirit

he will go before as Elijah.”

“Such things, priest—” and in reply

he spoke thus to the angel:

“Behold, already under the burden of years

our inward parts have withered,

and to our old senses

offspring is denied.”

“I have been sent from the stars,

a companion of the angels;

but you appear unbelieving

toward the divine commands.

Therefore, deprived of speech,

you will be silent in your lips.”

When the appointed times were completed,

the infant is seen to be born.

His father entered his name beforehand

in a book;

when the bond of his tongue was loosened,

he praised the Lord.

Glory and honor to God,

the Most High everywhere,

to the Father and the Son,

with the glorious Paraclete;

to him be praise and power

through eternal ages.

Amen.

Supplication. Let us pray to the Redeemer, the Lord of the world.

Capitulum. Almighty God, we humbly ask and entreat you that, in this festival of the Nativity of your Forerunner and Baptist John, you grant your people instruction in spiritual joys and direct the minds of all the faithful into the way of salvation and peace. May the presence of the one whom the announcement of the messenger revealed fulfill what was announced.

Our Father. Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

Lauda. “From my mother’s womb he called me.”

Benediction. “Almighty God the Father, who willed for his Only-Begotten Son…” See in the preceding Vespers.

At the end of Vespers.

Lauda. “A lamp for my feet.” fol. CLX. Sono. “Before I formed you.” See in the First Vespers.

Antiphon. “This child will be called a Nazirite; he will not drink wine or strong drink,” P. “and he will eat nothing unclean from his mother’s womb.” V. “His glory is great in your salvation; you will place glory and great splendor upon him.” P. “And he will eat nothing.”

[Col. 1139C] The Lord be always with you. R. And with you.

Lauda. “The child will be strengthened, alleluia, and will be great before God, alleluia.” P. “And he will turn many hearts toward the Lord. Alleluia, alleluia.” V. “He will receive blessing from the Lord and mercy from God his savior.” P. “And he will turn many.” V. Glory and honor. P. “And he will turn many.”

Hymn.

This child sounds forth as John,

the nursling of the begotten God,

the powerful friend of the Lord,

the glowing lamp of the world,

after the radiant Sun has completed its course,

wisdom in speech,

a fitting herald of the Godhead,

poured into an old woman’s womb,

born from an aged womb,

glorious in his ancestral honor.

Favor us with your prayers, we ask;

let holy piety overflow.

Stand by us in our misery;

let salvation fill those who are failing;

forgive every crime.

Let the modest man rule his homeland;

let the battle-line withdraw;

let the sword that kills fall,

let fire blunt the sword,

let the enemy bend his neck.

Let there be honor to God and to the Only-Begotten

from the Father’s mouth.

Let enduring power,

like and steadfast,

and the summit of high honor

belong to the Paraclete.

Amen.

Supplication. Let us pray to the Redeemer, as above.

Capitulum. God, in whose praise and glory everything offered through the worship and services of your saints is rendered: receive our devotion and illumine the festival which today the Lord’s Baptist consecrated, which the lamp of light kindled, which the Voice of the Word introduced, and at which he appeared as a witness of the truth. His spirit, foreknowing, leaped in the womb; his outpouring spread joy through the world; his birth announced the sacraments of faith; his conception closed the offices of an unbelieving mouth. Grant, Lord, we ask, that at least the final line of faith may remain in us, by which, clinging to them, we may deserve to reach them and follow step by step in their footsteps, lest we fall back. Just as we now discharge public vows in common joys, so may we fulfill personal vows that please you through daily progress.

Our Father. Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

Benediction. Christ, the Son of God, who kindled John as the lamp preceding his coming, by which he might be seen, may he deign to burn you with the fires of holy illumination. R. Amen. And may he who caused him to leap in his mother’s womb enrich you with an increase of spiritual joys. R. Amen. May he whom John preceded in spirit and in the power of Elijah when he was to be born himself bring you into the joys of eternal life. R. Amen.

[Col. 1140C] Through mercy.

Lauda. “Let my mouth be filled, God, with your praise, alleluia.” P. “That I may sing your glory. Alleluia, alleluia.” V. “For the Lord is great and exceedingly worthy of praise; he is terrible above all gods.” P. “That I may sing.” V. Glory and honor. P. “That I may sing.”

Prayer. “Voice of the Word, friend of the Bridegroom.” See in the First Vespers.

## DAY 27. THE FEAST OF SAINT ZOILUS, MARTYR

Everything is to be said as for one martyr, with nine readings, fol. CLX, except for the hymn, which is this:

Hymn.

Bearing the martyr’s crown, Zoilus

will hasten to meet Christ;

the precious city too, bearing

the victor’s gifts.

The citizens honor him, as though the earth itself

enclosed his limbs

and, embracing them, guarded in the tomb

the blessed martyr’s bones,

both its own and its father’s.

Our boy, and ours in the arena,

having learned through the art of virtue,

by the coin of faith,

to subdue with all his strength

the fearsome enemy.

To no martyr, with life returning,

has it been granted to dwell

upon our lands:

you alone, surviving your own death,

live throughout the world.

You preserve the martyrs;

you crown the homeland

devoted to sacred things.

From there arises a choir;

it stretches toward heaven,

white in the robe of noble rank.

You alone, coming before the Lord,

prepared larger throngs of martyrs;

you alone, rich in piety,

enjoy abundant light.

Behold, Zoilus, the palm of your victory.

So great a clergy produced this triumph;

let this house of priests, crowned with the *infula* [printed *infolata*],

celebrate its vow.

Let the choir sing glory and resound;

let it speak, sing, and repeat glory

to the Triune Name,

to the Godhead alone.

Let the stars cry out.

[Col. 1141B] Amen.

## DAY 28. THE VIGIL OF THE APOSTLES PETER AND PAUL

At Matins.

Antiphon. “Give us joy.” Psalm L. Prayer. “Restore joy to us, Lord.” See fol. CLXIII.

Antiphon 1. “I gave them my commandments, says the Lord,” P. “and I showed them my judgments for my name’s sake, so that he may be praised in Zion.” V. “Blessed are those who keep judgment and practice righteousness at all times.” P. “And my judgments.” V. Glory and honor. P. “And my judgments.”

Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ, who, at the voice of Peter asking, promise that in the regeneration you will grant those who follow you to sit upon twelve thrones and receive authority to judge the twelve tribes: by this gift of your promise you delight Peter after his denial and reward Paul after his course of unbelief. For Peter was not harmed after repentance by what he had denied, and for Paul, after his conversion, what he had done became forgivable. Grant us, by the merits of both, to avoid sin, to weep abundantly over what we have committed, to wipe away our errors with tears, and to punish our deeds of wrongdoing with almsgiving, so that, abandoning the world in spirit, we may deserve consolation in the promise of eternity. R. Amen.

Through.

Antiphon 2. “I chose you so that you may bear abundant fruit,” P. “and your fruit may remain forever.” V. “Draw near to God and be illumined, and your faces shall not be ashamed.” P. “And your fruit.” V. Glory and honor. P. “And your fruit.”

Prayer. Christ, Son of God, who by the gratuitous gift of calling chose both Peter as the first and Paul as the last Apostle, so that, one preceding and the other following, endowed with the grace of one calling and one Apostolate, they might, while scattering the field of the world with their teaching, bring you abundant fruit: grant us, with their intercession, to labor in this world in such a way that the fruit of our labors, approved by you, may remain forever. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Antiphon 3. “But your friends, O God, have been greatly honored by me,” P. “their principality has been greatly strengthened.” V. “Behold, Lord, you have known all things, the latest and the ancient; you formed me and placed your hand upon me.” P. “Their principality has been greatly strengthened.” V. Glory and honor to the Father and the Son. P. “Their principality has been greatly strengthened.”

Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ, who consecrated your chief Apostles Peter and Paul, one by the cross and the other by the sword: grant that Peter, taking up his cross and following you, may draw us after him, and that Paul, fighting for you and cutting away bodily things through spiritual devotion, may unite us to you. Let the one teach us to remain upon the cross, and the other to triumph by the sword, so that through Peter the cross may offer us to you for union, and through Paul the sword may join us to you for crowning. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

R. The saints who instructed many in righteousness will shine like the splendor of the firmament, P. and like the stars of heaven through everlasting eternity. V. These are the holy men whom the Lord chose in sincere love, and from their teaching the Church shines like the sun and moon. P. “And like the stars.” V. Glory and honor. P. “And like the stars.”

At Lauds.

For the Canticle. Antiphon. “Those who love you, Lord.” Canticle. “You who offered yourselves willingly.” See fol. CLXIII.

For the Benedictus. Antiphon. “Holy and humble in heart, spirits and souls of the righteous, bless the Lord. Righteous and priests, holy and humble in heart, bless the Lord.”

[CCLIV] Canticle. “Blessed are you, Lord.” fol. 6.

Sono. “The salvation of the righteous is from the Lord.” P. “And he saved them. Alleluia, alleluia.” V. “For they hoped in the living God.” P. “And he saved them.”

Lauda. “Praise the Lord from the heavens, alleluia; praise him in the heights, alleluia, alleluia.” Psalm CXLVIII. Prophecy. “The righteous [are] forever.” Fol. CLXIV. Hymn. “Praises of the Saints.” Fol. CLXV. Supplication. “Let us pray to the Redeemer,” with the names changed; fol. CLXXXVII.

Capitulum. In these two servants and Apostles of yours, Christ God, wondrous gifts of grace were distributed, by your granting: Peter is magnificent in the display of signs, while Paul is perfected in knowledge of the law; the one excels in miracles, the other shines in letters; the one heals the sick by his shadow, the other raises the dead by his word. We therefore ask that these two candelabra, always shining in your sight, may stand before you to intercede for us all, so that whatever we have received from their teaching we may fulfill by the effect of our works.

Our Father. Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

Lauda. “He looked upon them.” Benediction. “By the merits of the Saints.” See fol. CLXV.

## DAY 29. THE FESTIVAL OF THE SAINTS PETER AND PAUL, APOSTLES

At Vespers.

Lauda. “Light has risen in the darkness.” fol. CLXII.

Sono. “Alleluia. Their sound has gone out into all the earth,” P. “and their words to the ends of the world. Alleluia, alleluia.” V. “There are no languages or speeches in which their voices are not heard.” P. “And their words to the ends.”

The Lord be with you. R. And with you.

Antiphon. “Alleluia. These are the ones who were sent throughout the world and prostrated themselves before the Lamb,” P. “holding golden bowls full of incense, which are the memorials of the saints, singing a new song.” V. “Their sound has gone out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world.” P. “Holding.” V. Glory and honor to the Father. P. “Holding.”

The Lord be with you. R. And with you.

Antiphon 2. “These are men renowned for strength,” P. “teachers of the people, rendering judgment in their teaching.” V. “The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament proclaims the works of his hands.” P. “Teachers.” V. Glory and honor. P. “Teachers.”

Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ, who by the singular gift of your choosing willed to show these disciples of yours joined in the love of charity, by which perfection would shine forth: so that the Church, founded on their teaching, might be adorned by the power of love rather than of signs; so that all its structure might be shown wonderful through love rather than through signs; so that, in the very administration of your gift, signs might follow teaching, not the ranks of signs precede teaching; and so that the preaching of truth might be strengthened by the aid of signs: we ask and entreat you to establish our hearts so that they may remain in the charity pleasing to you, removing from us the place of a deceitful heart and cleansing the mark of a wickedly accustomed discord. Through those whose teaching makes the Church shine, may we deserve to obtain radiance in the land of the living. R. Amen.

Through.

Antiphon 3. “These are holy men whom the Lord chose in sincere love,” P. “and he gave them everlasting glory; through their teaching the Church shines like the sun and moon.” V. “Blessed is the nation whose God is the Lord, the people whom the Lord chose as his inheritance.” P. “And he gave them.” V. Glory and honor. P. “And he gave them.”

Prayer. Christ, we believe that the honeycomb of your ineffable sweetness, which you granted in the mouths of your Apostles, is very rich. For the sweetness of the word that was in their hearts formed in their mouths streams of knowledge burning with flame; it preserved the hearing of the peoples so that they might believe, and nourished their hearts so that they might love what they had heard. Within them was what overflowed outward to others. Hence they also deserved to draw near to you, because what they taught with their voices they carried out in their works. Grant us, therefore, that, since the Church arose through their preaching, it may stand strengthened by their prayer, so that the Church, filled with the honeycombs of their teaching, may by their prayers pass through the shipwrecks of this life to Christ, there to be crowned. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Antiphon 4. “Everlasting joy shall be for my elect.” P. “When I give their works in the tree of life.” V. “Blessed are those who keep judgment and practice righteousness at all times.” P. “When I give.” V. Glory and honor. P. “When I give.”

The Lord be with you. R. And with you.

Lauda. “The Lord filled them with discipline and wisdom. Alleluia.” P. “He created in them the grace of his Spirit and filled their hearts with understanding. Alleluia, alleluia.” V. “And they cried to the Lord when they were afflicted, and he delivered them from their necessities.” P. “He created in them.” V. Glory and honor. P. “He created in them.”

The Lord be always with you. R. And with you.

Lauda 2. “Everlasting joy shall be yours, says the Lord.” P. “For in your land you shall possess a double portion. Alleluia, alleluia.” V. “Blessed are you by the Lord, who made heaven and earth.” P. “For in your land.” V. Glory and honor. P. “For.”

Hymn.

The martyrdom of the Apostles

has consecrated the day of the age,

bringing forth Peter’s noble triumph

and Paul’s crown.

The blood of triumphant death

joined equal men;

the faith that followed God

crowned Christ’s ruler.

Peter was the first Apostle,

and Paul was not unequal in grace.

The vessel of sacred election

matched Peter’s faith.

With the position of the cross reversed,

Simon, giving honor to God,

ascended while hanging, mindful

of the oracle that had been given.

Girded, as it was said,

the old man was lifted up by another;

he would go where he did not wish,

but willingly he subdued harsh death.

Here, exalted at Rome’s summit,

he raised up devotion;

founded on such blood,

and on so great a prophet,

the noble Church flourished.

Throughout the circuit of the great city,

the throngs move in procession;

along three ways the feast

of the sacred martyrs is celebrated.

One might think the world had come forth,

the people chosen by God had gathered,

the head of the nations,

the faith that teaches the nations.

To God the Father be glory,

and to his Only-Begotten Son,

with the Spirit, the Paraclete,

through everlasting ages.

Amen.

Supplication. Let us pray to the Redeemer, with the names changed; fol. CLXXXVII.

Capitulum. Lord Jesus Christ, who placed your first and last Apostles, Peter and Paul, at the highest summit of perfection, so that the election to Apostolic dignity might be recognized as beginning in the one and completed in the other: grant these men as rulers to your Church, whom you chose as its princes; grant them as governors of righteousness, whom you appointed as leaders and outstanding men, so that they may cherish it with tireless protections, the Church which they founded through excellent commandments and examples.

Our Father. Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

Benediction. Christ the Lord, whom both Peter’s power and Paul’s teaching declared in the world to be the Only-Begotten Son of God the Father, may he deign to cleanse you from every pollution of worldly conduct. R. Amen. May the same one, for whom Peter was killed by the cross and Paul by the sword, make you possessors of the kingdom of heaven. R. Amen. May the kingdom of heaven, whose keys they themselves received through the grace of the Apostolate, never be shut against you on account of your merits, when those same men open it. R. Amen.

Through.

Lauda. “You are holy vessels for the Lord, shining with gold, alleluia.” P. “For you willingly offered your souls to the Lord God. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.” V. “Hear, my people, and I will testify to you: Israel, if you will hear me.” P. “For you willingly offered.” V. Glory and honor to the Father. P. “For you willingly offered.”

Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ, who, at the voice of Peter asking, promise that in the regeneration you will grant those who follow you to sit upon twelve thrones and receive authority to judge the twelve tribes: by this gift of your promise you delight Peter after his denial and reward Paul after his course of unbelief, since what Peter denied did not harm him after repentance, and what Paul had done became forgivable after his conversion. Grant us, by the merits of both, to erase our sin, to weep abundantly over what we have committed, to wipe away our errors with tears, and to punish our deeds with almsgiving, so that, abandoning the world in spirit, we may deserve consolation in the promise of eternity. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

In the name of our Lord.

At Matins.

Antiphon. “Give us.” Psalm L.

Prayer. “Restore to us.” See fol. CLXIII.

Antiphon 1. “Your friends, God, have been honored; their principality has been greatly strengthened.” P. “I shall number them, and they shall be multiplied beyond the sand.” V. “Behold, Lord, you have known all things, the latest and the ancient; you formed me and placed your hand upon me.” P. “I shall number them.” V. Glory and honor. P. “I shall number them.”

Prayer. Your friends, Christ, have been honored, while their sound went out into all the earth—not because they exercised worldly citizenship in earthly matters, but because they filled the world by the power of preaching and held preeminence in the performance of miracles. In Peter, power was displayed; in Paul, knowledge shone brightly; and they humbled the swollen power of the world beneath your gentle yoke. Hear our prayers, so that the benefits by which they ruled the world may never be absent from the Christian people. Rather, in that unending affection of sweetness by which, while placed in this life, they loved one another, may they deign to be present both to the vows and to the prayers of those who supplicate. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Antiphon 2. “These are your friends, Lord, who handed over their bodies to death,” P. “so that they might not serve idols or worship foreign gods.” V. “They shall walk, Lord, in the light of your face, and in your name they shall rejoice all day; and in your righteousness they shall be exalted.” P. “So that they might not serve.” V. Glory and honor to the Father. P. “So that they might not serve.”

Prayer. These are your friends, Lord Christ, Peter and Paul, who, handing over their bodies to death, became leaders of grace and founders of the Church. The unity of their preaching and the blessedness of their dying allowed neither division nor destruction to overcome them. We therefore ask that, since through their teaching you made peoples into believers in you, through their prayer you may make us coheirs of the heavenly kingdom. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Antiphon 3. “They fought manfully and passed from death to life.” P. “These are your friends, Lord.” V. “Those who trust in the Lord are like Mount Zion; he shall not be moved forever, who dwells in Jerusalem.” P. “These are.” V. Glory and honor. P. “These are.”

Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ, who deigned to consecrate Peter and Paul, fighting manfully, one by the cross and the other by the sword, so that, for love of your name, in faithful devotion the one might receive the destruction of the cross and the other the blow of the sword: grant us, following you with a similar love, to enter through Peter into the mystery of the cross and through Paul always to be defended by the spiritual sword of the word. Thus, through the cross of Christ, may we escape the torments of hell, and through the sword of the Spirit penetrate the hidden places of heaven. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

R. They showed the people the sacred rites and the observance; they demonstrated to human beings how to worship God, for they were predestined from all peoples as those who fear God, P. because they fulfilled his commandments among humankind. V. These are the men who attained glory among the generations of their nation and are held in praise in their days. P. Because. V. Glory and honor. P. Because.

Prayer. These are your Apostles, Lord, Peter and Paul. They showed the peoples the sacred rites of the law and the observance of worshiping you. While with open speech and unconquered constancy they scattered the seed of your word through the hearts of unbelievers, they were slain in a desirable passion. Paul, longing to be released, died by the sword, and Peter asked to be crucified with his footsteps reversed. Therefore we ask your mercy: since you crowned them with glorious martyrdom, free us from future torment, so that we may preserve in the receptacle of our hearts your word, which they scattered through the world by their glorious voices. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

At Lauds.

[Col. 1147A]

For the Canticle. Antiphon. “You who offered yourselves willingly to danger, bless the Lord, recounting his righteousness and mercy toward the mighty of Israel.”

Canticle. “You who offered yourselves willingly.” fol. CLXIII.

Prayer. Christ, Son of God, who introduce the sons of the new grace after the preceding Prophets, making the Apostles succeed the Prophets as sons succeed fathers—those who offer their souls willingly, whose lot was certainly found among the saints, because the preaching of the Apostles was strengthened by the prophecy of the preceding Prophets: we ask and entreat you, who by a wondrous arrangement ordered the rays of both Testaments, so that in the revelation of truth you might make the new succeed the old worthily and most beautifully, to make us always heirs of these your Apostles. Since through them we received faith, may we also with them always possess you as our inheritance. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

For the Benedictus. Antiphon. “Holy and humble in heart, spirits and souls of the righteous, bless the Lord. Righteous and priests, holy and humble in heart, bless the Lord.”

Canticle. “Blessed are you, Lord.” fol. 6. Sono. “Alleluia. Their sound has gone out into all the earth.” See in the preceding Vespers.

Lauda. “Praise the Lord from the heavens, alleluia; praise him in the heights, alleluia.” Psalm CXLVIII.

[Col. 1147C] Prophecy. “The Lord has accomplished great glory.” fol. CLXXIX. Hymn. “The martyrdom of the Apostles.” Supplication. “Let us pray.” See in the preceding Vespers.

Capitulum. Lord Jesus Christ, who destroy and overthrow hostile powers through your chief Apostles Peter and Paul, so that neither the wickedness of evil men nor the trickery of magicians may oppose the preaching of truth drawn forth from the Apostolic mouth: Peter cast down Simon Magus, and Paul struck Elymas with blindness. Be present to us, so that all who disturb may fall in your Church, and those who try to impede people coming to the faith may be thrown into confusion. May Peter’s power admit those who press on toward the heavenly kingdoms, to where the piety of Paul the teacher has led them.

Our Father. Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

[Col. 1147D] Lauda. “You are vessels.” Benediction. “Christ the Lord.” See in the preceding Vespers.

At the end of Vespers.

Lauda. “Light has risen.” Sono. “Alleluia. Their sound has gone out into all the earth.” See in the First Vespers.

Antiphon. They taught your law splendidly;  
P. Their works are many, stored up with you, O Lord.  
V. Those who trust in the Lord are like Mount Zion: he who dwells in Jerusalem shall not be moved forever.  
P. Whose are—.  
V. Glory and honor.  
P. Whose are—.

May the Lord be—.  
R. And with—.

Praise. He clothed them, alleluia.  
P. With a robe of glory: he gave them life in you and instruction, alleluia, alleluia.  
V. Wonderful is your knowledge, beyond me; it has grown strong [Col. 1148A], and I cannot attain it.  
P. A robe—.  
V. Glory and honor.  
P. A robe—.

Hymn. The passion of the Apostles.

Supplication. Let us pray. See in the First Vespers.

Capitula. Honoring at each annual recurrence the precious death of your saints, the Apostles Peter and Paul, we give glory to your praise, because these precious lamps, kindled by you from the true and unfailing light, illuminate not only when they are read about but also when they are venerated. For these are the two olive trees and the two golden lampstands in your sight, and throughout the whole earth the word of their mouth has gone forth. When, appeased by their intercession, you receive the service of devotion, grant, we ask, the fulfillment of our prayers when we cry out to you from the earth.

[Col. 1148B] Our Father. Delivered from evil. Folio 2.

Blessing. May almighty God, who grants every remedy of compassion to the wretched, grant that you may be cleansed by Peter’s tears from every contagion of guilt.  
R. Amen.  
May the teaching of Paul grant you the wisdom of the word.  
R. Amen.  
May the one through repentance and the other through teaching bring you to eternal life.  
R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Praise. The law of truth dwelt in their mouth, alleluia.  
P. For no iniquity was found upon their lips; he had perfected the fruit of life in peace. Alleluia, alleluia.  
V. The Lord will give the word to those who proclaim the Gospel with great power.  
P. For iniquity—.  
V. Glory and honor.  
P. For iniquity—.

[Col. 1148C] Prayer. Christ, Son of God, who [in the preceding prayer]. See back in the preceding Lauds.

# JULY FEASTS. JULY 12. FEAST OF SAINT MARTIANA, VIRGIN AND MARTYR

## CCLIII. At Vespers

Praise. My soul has hoped in the Lord.

Tone. Alleluia: I will sing psalms to your name, O God.

Antiphon. Show me your face, O Zion.

Praise. Exalted like a palm tree. Folio CLXXIX.

### Hymn

Let the Church’s voice celebrate  
the triumph of the holy martyr:

[Col. 1148D] Let one Muse be shared by all  
in praise of the virgin Martiana.

As she strives to attain  
the reward of suffering,  
she dares, ready and willing,  
to enter the arena of glory.

For when she saw the demon  
standing before her, she struck down his image;  
beneath it a broad stream  
was continually flowing at her feet.

Soon, beaten with scourges, she is dragged  
to the lofty halls of the Praetor.  
He entices her with spectacles  
and throws the Virgin’s limbs to the ground.

Whom the plunderer [printed pudicitur, unintelligible]—  
[Col. 1149A] while he follows amid the shadows—  
[printed Oble tata, unclear], at once from heaven,  
is shut off by a wall.

[The printed sequence Quam praedo pudicitur / Dum inter umbras sequitur / Oble tata extemplo coelitus / Secluditur maceria is damaged; its surviving words are rendered above, but the syntax and subject of the final clause remain uncertain.]

Then, bound to a stake,  
she is enclosed because of her vain speech;  
but blasphemy brings punishments,  
ruins, and fires.

When she is sent out to the beasts,  
a lion rushes ahead in fury;  
he comes to worship,  
not to consume, the Virgin.

Then a bull springs forth,  
with form and terrifying bellow;  
with a blow he furrows  
her tender breasts, wounding them.

But the swift wild beast,  
in body and spotted hide,  
at last tears the Maiden’s limbs  
with its deadly tooth.

After these triumphs, her soul, escaped  
from the bonds of the body,  
clapping its hands, seeks  
the free heights of the highest heaven.

To God the Father be glory,  
and to his only Son,  
together with the Holy Paraclete,  
through everlasting ages.

Amen.

Supplication. Let us pray, with the name changed; folio CLXXXII.

[Col. 1149C] Capitula. Lord Jesus Christ, by whose command the most savage lion not only refrained from killing the most blessed virgin and martyr Martiana, but also, laying aside its fierceness, worshiped her immaculate body and, when present, did not dare to touch it with hostile violence: grant that, surrounded by the radiance of your Holy Spirit, we may not fear the savagery of the dreadful lion, but that, repelled by the power of your majesty, it may always remain distant from harming us.

Our Father. Delivered from evil. Folio 2.

Blessing. May almighty Lord, who adorned the most blessed Martiana with the beauty of virginity and chastity, cleanse your minds from every contagion of worldly corruption.  
R. Amen.  
May he who granted her not to bow her neck to idols keep the temptation of evil spirits away from you.  
R. Amen.  
And just as she rejoices with Christ after her victory, so, with her patronage, may you rejoice in being brought back to paradise.  
R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Praise. You have become beautiful and pleasant in your delights, alleluia.  
P. Your beauty is like a palm tree; its brightness is continually in fullness. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.  
V. Praise the Lord, O Jerusalem; praise your God, O Zion.  
P. Beauty—.

Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ, who, while loving your most blessed virgin and martyr Martiana, make her beautiful and fair in your appearance and beauty and espouse her to yourself with immense love: by your heavenly gift, be present to us through the tireless patronage [Col. 1150A] of your most blessed martyr Martiana, so that, since such great compassion has raised her in triumph to praise, it may lead suppliants to salvation.  
R. Amen.

Through mercy.

## CCLIX. At Matins

Antiphon. Lord, you will open my lips, and my mouth shall proclaim your praise. Psalm 50.

Prayer. May they rejoice, Lord.

Antiphon 1. With eternal love. See folio CLXXX.

Prayer. Blessed Martiana, virgin of God, who remained gloriously in the contemplation of Zion, whom God himself testifies that he loved, since he promises that mercy will not depart from her thereafter: grant us, by your merits, that, aflame with divine love, we may be found unharmed at the future Judgment.  
R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 2. You are one who is near. Folio CLXXX.

Prayer. One and good is your near virgin Martiana, O Lord, who, as she is made near to you, is shown through her own passion to be your beautiful servant, made beautiful by her blood. Therefore, through the intervention of her sufferings, wipe away our stains, so that, made beautiful both in vows and in works, we may deserve, blessed, to enter the gates of eternal Jerusalem.  
R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 3. Come, bride, from Lebanon; come from the mountains of pasture; let us run  
P. At the fragrance of your perfumes.  
V. Hear, O daughter, and see, and incline your ear; forget your people and your father’s house.  
P. Hear.

Prayer. Beautiful, Christ, Son of God: the virgin Martiana, coming from Lebanon into the eyes of the faithful, is in a manner seen again at each annual recurrence, when her honor is presented to human sight and opened for honorable service. The good fragrance of her garments is therefore more fragrant than all spices, because the discernments of her virtues bear fruit in overflowing brightness. Grant us, then, that the fragrance of her virtues may rouse our drowsing heart and sense to repentance, so that we who now receive joy from that fragrance may afterward receive from repentance unfailing glory.  
R. Amen.

Through mercy.

R. Rejoice, daughter of Zion. Folio CLXXXI.

[Col. 1150D] Prayer. Jesus, Son of God, who, entering the garden of the Elect, feed among dark lilies when you are adorned in your body, which is the Church, by companies of holy virgins: there, having wonderfully introduced the most blessed Martiana, you chose so marvelously to support her with flowers that the fragrance of her virginity, like a little flower of her perfumes, rose all the way to us. We humbly and earnestly beg you that, once the figures of the Old Testament have been removed—figures that went before like shadows in symbolic observances—that day, namely the Gospel tradition, may advance in us through its inspiration, so that we may follow the light of the Gospel with complete devotion according to the example of blessed virgin Martiana, and know nothing of the shadows of past error and crime.  
R. Amen.

Through mercy.

[Col. 1151A] For the Canticle. Antiphon. Blessed is the Lord.

Canticle. Rejoicing, I will rejoice. Folio CLXXXI.

For the Benedictus. Antiphon. Daughter of Zion.

Canticle. Blessed are you, O Lord. Folio 6.

Tone. The Lord gives me a tongue of learning, alleluia, so that I may know when it is fitting for me to speak, alleluia.  
P. You placed me at the morning watch and inclined an ear for me to hear, alleluia, alleluia.  
V. I asked my God for wisdom, and he said to me: “Behold, I have done according to your word, and I have given you a wise and understanding heart, so that you may know and understand how it is fitting for you to say alleluia, alleluia.”  
V. I spread out my branches like a terebinth. I caused the morning star to rise in heaven, alleluia. I love all who love me, for my ends are the ends of life. Pass over to me, all who desire me, and be filled from my generations; for my hope is alleluia, and alleluia is sweeter than honey.  
P. You placed me.

Praise. Praise the Lord from the heavens, alleluia, alleluia; praise him in the highest, alleluia, alleluia. Psalm 148.

Reading from the Book of the Prophet Isaiah, chapter 54.

R. Thanks be to God.

Thus says the Lord:

“Praise, barren woman who do not give birth; sing praise, you who did not give birth, for the daughters of the desolate woman are many, more than of her who has a husband,” says the Lord.

“Enlarge the place of your tent and stretch out the skins of your tabernacles; do not spare. [Col. 1151C] Make your cords long and strengthen your stakes. For you shall break forth to the right and to the left; your offspring shall possess [CCLX] nations and shall inherit deserted cities.

“Do not fear, for you shall not be confounded, nor be ashamed, for you shall not be put to shame; for you shall forget the confusions of your youth and shall remember the reproach of your widowhood no more. For he who made you shall rule over you; the Lord of hosts is his name. Your redeemer is the Holy One of Israel; God shall summon all to you.

“For the Lord has called you as a woman forsaken and grieving in spirit, and as a wife cast off in youth, says the Lord your God. For a brief moment I abandoned you, and with great mercies I will gather you. In a moment of my indignation I hid my face from you for a little while, and with everlasting mercy I have had compassion on you,” says your redeemer, the Holy One of Israel, the almighty Lord.

R. Amen.

Hymn. The triumph of the holy martyr.

Supplication. Let us pray. See in the preceding Vespers.

Capitula. Hear, Lord, the voice of our cry, and grant earnestness to our petitions [printed affectum]. Drive deceit away from us; banish quarrels far away; destroy vice, and grant growth in mutual sweetness. For we acknowledge our own merit, but we follow your saving command. Therefore, we ask, let us be confounded in nothing, but deign to hear us from heaven when we cry out to you from the earth.

Our Father. Delivered from evil. Folio 2.

[Col. 1152A] Praise. You have become beautiful.

Blessing. Almighty Lord. In the preceding Vespers.

## At the conclusion of Vespers

Praise. My soul has hoped.

Tone. Alleluia. I will sing psalms to the name. Folio CLXXIX.

Antiphon. You exalted me upon a rock. You led me, because you became my hope: a tower  
P. Of strength against the face of the enemy.  
V. I shall dwell in your tabernacle forever; I shall be protected beneath the shelter of your wings.  
P. Of strength.  
V. Glory and honor.  
P. Of strength.

May the Lord be—.  
R. And with—.

Praise. How sweet are your sayings to my throat, alleluia; sweeter than honey and the honeycomb, alleluia.  
V. How I have loved your law, O Lord; it is my meditation all day long.

Hymn. The triumph of the holy martyr.

Supplication. Let us pray. See in the preceding Vespers.

Capitula. God our Savior, who preserves eternal integrity, supports the corruption of our flesh with indulgence, and spares the body’s constitution, and who preserves the integrity bestowed by you upon virgins so that you might bring it to its appointed merit: we ask you, through her intercession, so cleanse us from the impulses of lust that, resisting every adversity, we may confidently cry out to you from the earth.

Our Father. Delivered from evil. Folio 2.

Blessing. The Lord Jesus Christ, who espoused his virgin Martiana to himself in chaste love, enrich you with the gift of chastity.  
R. Amen.  
And may he who betrothed her to himself with the ring of faith bind you indissolubly to his love.  
R. Amen.  
May he admit as your advocate before himself her whom he took as his bride in incorrupt love.  
R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Praise. You have become beautiful. See in the First Vespers.

Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ, as above.

# JULY 16. FEAST OF SAINT JUSTA, VIRGIN

## At Vespers

Praise. My soul has hoped in the Lord.

From the morning watch  
P. Until night.  
V. My soul has waited for your word, O Lord. Let your ears be attentive to the prayer of your handmaid.  
P. Until night.

May the Lord be—.  
R. And with—.

Tone. Grace has been poured upon your lips, alleluia.  
P. Therefore God has blessed you forever. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.  
V. My heart has uttered a good word; I speak my works to the king. Alleluia.  
V. Sons have been born to you; you shall appoint them princes over all the earth. They shall remember your name, O Lord, from generation to generation.  
P. Therefore.

May the Lord be—.  
R. And with—.

Antiphon. Alleluia. The memory of Justa, [CCLXI] which is known before God and human beings, is attended with praises; and, crowned forever, she triumphs.  
V. Her offspring shall be powerful on earth; the generation of the upright shall be blessed.  
P. Is known.  
V. Glory and honor.  
P. Is known.

May the Lord be—.  
R. And with—.

[Col. 1153A] Antiphon. Blessed are you by the Most High God, above all women.  
P. For this reason your praise shall not depart from human lips forever.  
V. May he not let your foot be moved, nor may he slumber who guards you.  
P. For—.  
V. Glory and honor.  
P. For—.

May the Lord be—.  
R. And with—.

Antiphon. Jerusalem, holy city, adorned with Justa’s beauty,  
P. Whose streets resound with praises from day to day.  
V. Glorious things have been spoken of you, O city of God.  
P. Whose.  
V. Glory and honor.  
P. Whose.

May the Lord be—.  
R. And with—.

Praise. Alleluia. Rejoice, daughter of Zion; be glad and exult with all your heart, daughter of Jerusalem.  
P. For the King of Israel, the Lord, has taken away your enemies. Alleluia, alleluia.  
V. Praise the Lord, O Jerusalem; praise your God, O Zion.  
P. For he has taken away—.  
V. Glory and honor.  
P. For—.

### Hymn

Let the fostered people celebrate  
with equal song the triumph  
of the holy virgin Justa,  
prepared by heavenly grace,  
and let it resound in pious strains,  
opening forth nurturing songs.

The congregation devoted to you, Christ,  
adds vows in dedication  
to the martyr, so that through the martyr’s prayer  
it may be able to remain free  
from its own dreadful offenses,  
fortified by her intercessions.

She often conquered the world  
and the impious enemy together.  
Following you in love of heart,  
she tramples the foul Zabulon.  
With a double wreath and crown  
she forever reigns in heaven.

By her dwelling this western region  
shines more brightly;  
always echoing her triumph,  
may it excel other places,  
claiming the sacred blood from its soil  
as a pledge for heaven.

Often serving God without fear,  
she shattered the tenacious life of the world  
and its profane image.  
Immediately she suffered  
the dreadful sentence of the King.

Afflicted by varied punishments,  
burning with the fires of her spirit,  
pierced by the enemy’s sword,  
she returned her spirit to heaven.  
Hence her body is transferred to another place,  
living perpetually for God.

Called to the heavenly fellowship  
of the virgins,  
she despises the enemy through her blood  
and conquers Zabulon in mind;  
[Col. 1154A] therefore she shines forth  
crowned with twofold glory.

Rejoicing before the heavenly King alone,  
thus mingled with the everlasting  
choirs of angels,  
she composes a new song.  
Having gained the kingdom  
of everlasting glory, she triumphs.

Therefore we bow and pray,  
O serene King, your little servants,  
and at the same time, confessing  
the deeds of our sins:  
now cherish us with remedies, Father,  
whom you see trembling.

At her holy entreaty,  
wipe away our crimes,  
loosen the knots of our wickedness;  
grant the remedies of grace.  
And, destined to live forever with you,  
may we glory with you, Holy One.

Drive anger away; keep plague  
from our borders.  
Blunt the enemy’s sword  
through this martyr’s prayer,  
and grant heavenly peace  
to your servants, O Christ.

Let us sing glory to the Father  
and perpetually to Christ,  
together also with the Holy Spirit  
of both,  
the one eternal God  
who reigns before the ages.

Amen.

Supplication. Let us pray, with the name changed; folio CLXXX.

Capitula. Lord Jesus Christ, who promise to repay a hundredfold fruit to those who preserve the virginity of the flesh: through the intercession of your virgin [CCLXII] Justa, loosen the bonds of our sins, so that we who are cast down by the frailty of the flesh may be raised up by her patronage.

Our Father. Delivered from evil. Folio 2.

Blessing. The Lord Jesus Christ, who preserved his virgin Justa in chaste modesty, enrich you with the gift of chastity.  
R. Amen.  
And may he who betrothed her to himself with the ring of faith bind you indissolubly to his love.  
R. Amen.  
May he admit as your advocate before himself her whom he took as his bride in incorrupt love.  
R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Praise. I kept the Lord always before me, for he is at my right hand, so that I may not be moved.  
P. Therefore my heart was glad and my tongue rejoiced. Alleluia.  
V. Hear, O daughter, and see, and incline your ear; forget your people and your father’s house.  
P. Therefore.  
V. Glory and honor.  
P. Therefore.

Prayer. God, who glorified your blessed virgins and martyrs Justa and Rufina with the distinction of virginal chastity and the banner of passion: grant that we may be so adorned with the flowers of sacred chastity that, with the fruit of good works, we may attain fellowship [Col. 1155A] in heavenly blessedness.  
R. Amen.

Through.

## At Matins

Antiphon. You will open my lips, and my mouth shall proclaim your praise.

Prayer. May our lips rejoice in you, Lord, with the proclamation of truth, and not be dissolved into the empty speech of falsehood; may they always speak glory to you, and not resound indecently with quarrelsome disputes. May our soul also, which you redeemed, by praising the triumph of your martyr Justa, deserve through her patronage to have you favorable to it.  
R. Amen.

Through.

Antiphon 1. Her memory is in the blessing of honor; in every mouth her name will grow sweet like honey;  
P. For she directed her heart to God, and the Lord heard her voice.  
V. All day long she is merciful and lends, and her offspring is in blessing.  
P. For she directed.  
V. Glory and honor.  
P. For she directed.

Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ, who willed Justa to be called so both in name and in merits, so that, by following you, who are just, she might become a participant in your justice and might not fail in seeking, “lest she obtain the reward of martyrdom” [printed ne potiretur; the negative makes the construction uncertain]: grant us through her intercession that, just as she fought and conquered for your name, so we, made followers of justice, may deserve to be justified through regard for your compassion.  
R. Amen.

Through.

Antiphon 2. I have not rejected the justices of the Lord.  
P. And I shall be blameless before him.  
V. And the Lord repaid me according to my justice, and according to the innocence of my hands he repaid me.  
P. And.  
V. Glory and honor.  
P. And I shall be.

Prayer. God, giver of heavenly riches and wondrous performer of eternal gifts, who chose blessed Justa as poor in this world but exalted her with eternal riches because she fought for you: grant that we may always follow poverty of spirit, by which we ask to please your majesty in all things.  
R. Amen.

Through.

Antiphon 3. Justa knew justice, saw the wonders of God, and entreated the Most High,  
P. And she entered the number of the saints.  
V. You granted her the desire of her soul and did not deprive her of the will of her lips.  
P. And she entered.  
V. Glory and honor.  
P. And she entered.

Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ, in whose power blessed Justa trusted and cast down a dreadful monster, which the power of your majesty also crushed and destroyed because of the strength of her martyrdom: grant us, with her patronage, to avoid the dangers of every enticement, so that, while we crush the instigator of wickedness, we may share with your Justa the laurel crowns of victory.  
R. Amen.

Through.

R. Justa rejoices with the Lord, because she confessed God before human beings; therefore the Lord will hear her praying for the people.  
P. So that the Lord’s anger may be taken away from us.  
V. Justa knew justice, [Col. 1156A] and saw the wonders of God, and entreated the Most High.  
P. So that it may be taken away.  
V. Glory and honor. Repeat the Responsory, “Justa.”

Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ, from whom pious souls are protected and crowned—those who burn with love for you in [CCLXIII] this world and, when martyrdom approaches, eagerly desire to reach you by denying themselves—appoint also the soul of the most holy Justa, whom you placed in your bosom, as an intercessor for us, so that we may not be deprived of her aid, whose memorial song of praise we offer.  
R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 4. Like gentle doves they clap their wings and shall glory on their journey;  
P. But let the people rejoice with great joy in their gladness.  
V. Let Mount Zion rejoice, and let the daughters of Judah exult because of your judgments, O Lord.  
P. The people—.  
V. Glory and honor.  
P. The people—.

Prayer. Lord God, who granted your virgins, burning with glorious love, both to seek and to burn with desire in their choosing: grant that we may seek you with an ever more fervent vow, so that we may deserve to carry back the reward of fruitful labor.  
R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Antiphon 5. Virgins shall be brought to the king after her; her companions.  
P. They shall be brought to us with joy and exultation.  
V. They shall remember your name, O God, in every generation and generation.  
P. They shall be brought.  
V. Glory and honor.  
P. They shall be brought.

Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ, whom the daughters of Tyre were foretold to worship with gifts—namely, the daughters of the nations—when the Church, joined to you from all nations, is recognized: you did not seek her with gifts acquired for profit or money, but in acts of holiness, by which every devout soul is joined to you, and from whom gifts are granted to believers. Grant us to seek the face of your queen in works of holiness, so that, practicing justice and mercy, we may fulfill them not from a desire to please human beings, but so that it may be known to God alone, both in our vows and in our works.  
R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 6. All the glory of the king’s daughter is within; virgins follow him; they shall be led in joy and exultation.  
P. They shall be led into the temple of the king.  
V. Instead of your fathers, sons have been born to you; you shall appoint them princes over all the earth.  
P. They shall be led.  
V. Glory and honor.  
P. They shall be led.

Prayer. God, shining in the hearts of these Virgins, caused light to shine from darkness, so that those who had been corrupted by nature might be enlightened by grace: shine in our hearts for the benefit of eternal salvation, so that, when the darkness of our vices has been wiped away, the everlasting brightness of your light alone may possess us.  
R. Amen.

Through mercy.

R. The kingdom of heaven is like ten virgins who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.  
P. Those who were ready entered with him to the wedding, and the door was closed.  
V. At midnight [Col. 1157A] a cry was made: “Behold, the bridegroom is coming; go out to meet him.”  
P. Those who were.  
V. Glory and honor. Repeat the Responsory.

Prayer. Make us, Lord Jesus Christ, preserve the oil of prudence in the vessels of our conscience with pure integrity of mind, so that, when the cry is made and we go out to meet you, the Bridegroom, coming to judgment, we may be counted among the prudent Virgins to be crowned, not among the foolish.  
R. Amen.

Through mercy.

## At Lauds

For the Canticle. Antiphon. Hear, O kings; listen with your ears, O princes: I am she who will sing to the Lord; I will sing psalms to the God of Israel.

Canticle. You who offered yourselves willingly. Folio CLXIII.

[Col. 1157B] Prayer. God, who desire all the glory of Virgins, namely the daughters of the King, to be inward, so that those whom virtue makes rejoice eternally do not seek the testimony of another’s praise: grant our request through the prayers of those Virgins, that we may both flee human praises and carry within us the testimony of a good work, so that we may persevere as virgins in faith and thereby receive an incorrupt inheritance.  
R. Amen.

Through mercy.

For the Benedictus. Antiphon. Daughter of Zion, bless the Lord God Most High in every blessing and praise.

Canticle. Blessed are you, O Lord God.

Tone. The Lord gives me a tongue. See folio 378.

Praise. Alleluia. Praise the Lord from the heavens, [Col. 1157C] [CCLXIV] alleluia, alleluia; praise him in the highest, alleluia, alleluia. Psalm 148.

Reading from the Book of Jesus, chapter 39.

R. Thanks be to God.

Hear me, divine fruits, and bear fruit like a rose planted beside streams of water. Have the fragrance of sweetness like Lebanon. Bloom as flowers, like a lily; give off fragrance, put forth leaves in grace, praise the song, and bless the Lord in his works. Give magnificence to his name and confess him with the voice of your lips, in songs of the lips and on harps; and thus you shall say in confession: “All the works of the Lord are exceedingly good.” Amen.

### Hymn

With equal song let us sing of Justa,  
[Col. 1157D] the virgin who pleased God by her modesty,  
chaste from her earliest, untutored years,  
she remained unmarried after conquering desire.

By the earnings of her labor in earthen vessels,  
she supplies sustenance to the poor and to herself;  
despising the world and following Christ,  
she thus lives forever in heaven.

At last, powerful through eternal oracles,  
she destroys the pierced monster, brandishing  
the heavenly darts of the King; she blunts  
the scepter and the faithlessness of the savage enemy.

Immediately undergoing harsh torments,  
through lofty punishments she finds  
the heavenly life, which, mighty upon earth,  
[Col. 1158A] the diligent victorious servant sought.

Now, Christ, always admit her as an intercessor  
for our sins,  
so that she may bravely protect the citizens,  
fortifying them with her blood and guarding them with prayer.

To the eternal Offspring, to the unbegotten Father,  
with the Holy Spirit everlasting,  
let honor be given to you; let glory  
be ever powerful and enduring.

Amen.

Supplication. Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world, our Lord, as above in the Vespers.

Capitula. God, who so fortified the steps of the most holy Justa in the preparation of the Gospel of peace that neither the weariness of the laborious journey softened the tenderness of her body, nor the variety of punishments weakened the strength of her mind: grant us, your humble servants, to turn aside from and despise the journeys of worldly love, and mercifully place our steps on the way of peace by which we may reach you.

Our Father. And lead us not. But deliver us. Delivered from evil. See folio 2.

Humble yourselves. The Lord.  
R. And.

Praise. I kept the Lord before me, as above in the Vespers.

Blessing. May almighty Lord, appeased by the prayers of his saints Justa and Rufina, guard you.  
R. Amen.  
May he be favorable to you everywhere, who is always glorious in his saints.  
R. Amen.  
And, by his own compassion, may you, rescued from every evil, be filled with the chrism of the Holy Spirit.  
R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

In the name of our Lord.

# JULY 16. FEAST OF SAINT RUFINA, VIRGIN AND MARTYR

## At Vespers

Praise. My soul has hoped in the Lord.

From the morning watch.  
P. Until night.  
V. My soul has waited for your word, O Lord. Let your ears be attentive to the prayer of your handmaid.  
P. Until night.  
V. Glory and honor.  
P. Until night.

May the Lord be always—.  
R. And with—.

Tone. Hear, O daughter, and see, and incline your ear.  
P. For the king has desired your beauty. Alleluia.  
V. He himself is the Lord your God, and daughters shall worship him; all the rich of the earth shall entreat your face with gifts. All her glory.  
P. For he has desired—.

May the Lord be always—.  
R. And with—.

Antiphon. My soul shall praise the Lord until death, who rescued me from an unjust king;  
P. And from the pressure of the flame that surrounded me, and in the midst of the fire I was not scorched.  
V. I will bless the Lord at all times; his praise is always in my mouth.  
P. And from the pressure.  
V. Glory and honor to the Father.  
P. And from the pressure.

May the Lord be always—.  
R. And with—.

Praise. You tested me with fire, O Lord,  
P. And [CCLXV] [Col. 1159A] iniquity was not found in me. Alleluia, alleluia.  
V. Hear my justice, O God; attend to my supplication. Give ear to my prayer, and not to deceitful lips.  
P. And there was not—.  
V. Glory and honor to the Father.  
P. And there was not—.

### Hymn

Here are the little crimson flowers of virgins,  
green with the gentle dew of heaven,  
whose vessels of heaven have been tested  
by the mark of the stars in the world’s fiery flame.

First smeared with showers of oil,  
she kindles like a torch of the heart toward heaven,  
conquering the treachery of night  
and the enemy’s assault with the excellent light of faith.

Behold, Justa and Rufina together,  
shining in merits and illustrious character:  
distinct indeed in name as virgins,  
but one in the service of their devotion as martyrs.

Carrying the Lord’s treasure, renowned in the Law,  
in earthen vessels of a single body,  
they sell the little vessels for a price,  
so that by the proceeds they may satisfy the poor.

But by these means the cunning craftsman,  
in envy, breaks the earthen vessels,  
lest human clay should climb to heaven  
and dust become heavenly glory.

Hence robust faith, rising from the broken earthen vessel,  
receives the martyrdom of the body,  
offering rewards to the female sex,  
by which they may glide into the lofty star.

For this reason, O King Christ,  
life, salvation, and way and truth,  
we beseech you with highest prayers:  
consecrate us to yourself through their intercession,  
for you were pleased by the voice of their faith.

Make us virgins in mind, as with a lamp;  
make us free from bodily flow,  
so that, bearing hearts warmed by strict vows,  
we may possess everlasting kingdoms.

May our glory rejoice in you forever,  
who alone are the Triune and One Lord,  
holding the ages under unchanging rule  
and ruling all things, commanding everyone.

Amen.

Supplication. Let us pray. With the name changed, as above.

[Col. 1159D] Capitula. Lord Jesus Christ, by whose command the most savage lion not only refrained from killing the most blessed virgin and martyr Rufina, but also, laying aside its fierceness, having smelled her immaculate body, does not presume to molest it directly: grant that, surrounded by the radiance of your Holy Spirit, we may not fear the savagery of the dreadful lion, but that, repelled by the power of your majesty, it may always remain distant from harming us.

Our Father. Delivered from evil. Folio 2.

Blessing. Almighty God, who adorned the most blessed Rufina with the beauty of virginity and chastity, cleanse our minds from every contagion of worldly corruption.  
R. Amen.  
May he who granted her not to bow her neck to idols keep [Col. 1160A] the temptation of evil spirits away from you.  
R. Amen.  
And just as she rejoices with Christ after her victory, so, with her patronage, may you rejoice in being brought back to paradise.  
R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Praise. My branches are branches of honor and grace. Alleluia.  
P. I flourished like a vine with the sweetness of fragrance. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.  
V. But I, like a fruitful olive tree in the house of the Lord, shall hope in the mercy of my God forever and for ages of ages.  
P. I, like—.  
V. Glory and honor.  
P. I, like—.

Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ, who, while loving your most blessed virgin and martyr Rufina, make her beautiful and fair in your appearance and beauty and espouse her to yourself with immense love: be present to us through the tireless patronage of your most blessed martyr, so that such great compassion, which has raised her in triumph to praise, may lead suppliants to salvation [printed quam makes the construction irregular].  
R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

## At Matins

Antiphon. My tongue shall praise. Psalm 50.

Prayer. May our tongue praise you, Lord. Folio CLXXI.

Antiphon 1. The Lord strengthened her arms for good work;  
P. And he tested her, because it is good to work: her lamp shall not be extinguished throughout the night.  
V. Praise and magnificence are his work, and his justice remains forever and ever.  
P. And he tested—.  
V. Glory and honor.  
P. And he tested—.

[Col. 1160C] Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ, who promise to repay a hundredfold fruit to those who preserve the virginity of the flesh: through the intercession of your virgin and martyr Rufina, loosen the bonds of our sins, so that we who are [CCLXVI] cast down by the frailty of the flesh may be raised up by her patronage.  
R. Amen.

Through.

Antiphon 2. In the assembly of the saints, like a cedar,  
P. I was exalted in Lebanon and raised like a cypress on the mountains of Hermon.  
V. But I, like a fruitful olive tree in the house of the Lord, shall hope in the mercy of my God forever and for ages of ages.  
P. I was exalted.  
V. Glory.  
P. I was exalted.

Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ, to whom the virgin and martyr Rufina is joined both in integrity and in blood, since she vowed chastity to you and shed her blood for you: grant to your suppliant servants that, cleansed from sins, we may obey you in such a way that we do not depart from you again.  
R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 3. The Lord clothed her in a robe of glory. He stored up gladness and exultation over her and gave her an eternal name as inheritance.  
V. Her offspring shall be powerful on earth; the generation of the upright shall be blessed.  
P. And by a name—.  
V. Glory.  
P. And by a name—.

Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ, who consecrated your most blessed Rufina to yourself both as witness and as virgin, as she followed you incorruptly and was gloriously sacrificed for you: grant our prayer through her, so that, with her intercession, we, though unworthy, may deserve to obtain both the gift of chastity [Col. 1161A] and the triumph of confession.  
R. Amen.

Through.

R. Daughter of Zion, let your voice cease from weeping and your eyes from tears, for there is a reward for your work and hope for your future.  
P. Return, for I will have compassion on you in pity, and I will direct your heart on the straight path by which you walked.  
V. I remembered you, having compassion on your youth and the love of your betrothal.  
P. Return.  
V. Glory and honor. Repeat the Responsory, “Daughter of Zion.”

## Prayer

O Lord, by whose double gift the martyr Rufina rejoices in a double reward, since she is both an adornment to chastity and an example to all for martyrdom, grant that those things may flourish in the Church with flowers which are worthy of eternal fruits; and may we pursue the great martyr’s footsteps alike in intention and in deed, so that lust may not overthrow us, but chastity may hold us fast; that confession may prove our own children free, and perfection may seek those who are to be rewarded. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

## At the Canticle

**Antiphon.** I will glory in the Lord; I will rejoice in God my Jesus.

**Canticle.** “Lord, I have heard your report.” See fol. 22.

**Antiphon.** I will glory in the Lord.

# DAY XXI. THE FEAST OF SAINT SPERATUS AND HIS COMPANIONS

## At Vespers

**Lauda.** “Light has risen in the darkness.”

**Sono.** “The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God.” See fol. CLXVII.

**Antiphon.** The righteous shall live forever. Therefore they shall receive the kingdom of splendor and the diadem of beauty from the hand of the Lord.  
V. He will help them and deliver them; he will rescue them from sinners and save them, because they have hoped in him.  
P. Therefore they shall receive.  
V. Glory and honor.  
P. Therefore they shall receive.

The Lord be with you.  
R. And with you.

**Lauda.** “Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.”

## Hymn

Let us sing with alternating choirs  
in mystical hymns  
the renowned palm of virtue  
of the holy martyr Speratus.

The mighty city of Africa,  
Carthage, preserves this martyr;  
and the Western people,  
dedicated to Christ,  
embrace him.

His tomb flourishes  
with extraordinary virtues,  
so that the glory of his passion  
may be magnified by miracles.

Here, with his companions,  
when he was compelled to sacrifice,  
he bravely refused  
to say that incense should be offered  
to idols.

For he immediately exclaimed:

“I am a minister of Christ;  
and those companions whom you see—  
believe that they are present  
as such.”

At these words the impious governor,  
stirred by mad anger,  
ordered the necks  
of the devout martyrs  
to be struck with the sword.

Through this trophy of faith  
their souls flew forth;  
seeking the Father’s throne,  
they receive equal crowns.

And thus, bearing the marks  
of Christ in their own flesh,  
they became conformed to Christ  
in the heavenly kingdom  
and in reward.

Glory be to God the Father,  
and to his only Son,  
with the Spirit, the Paraclete,  
who reigns throughout every age.

Amen.

**Supplication.** “Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world,” with the name changed. See fol. CLXXXVII.

**Capitula.** You are marvelous, Lord, and beyond estimation in your Saints, you who are the glorious author of all wonders and the merciful rewarder of glorious combat in future blessedness. Therefore we ask you, ineffable and merciful God, and with bowed mind we earnestly entreat you: through the prayer of your martyr Speratus, favor the petitions of those who hope in you; receive the fragrance of the evening sacrifice; mercifully wipe away the record of our sins; remove from your people the intolerable yoke of worldly pressures; grant abundance of crops; restrain excess; and bestow upon all the illnesses of the faithful the healing of salutary medicine. Thus, tested by the fire of tribulation, may we, clothed in white robes and admitted to the assemblies of the Saints Speratus and his Companions, continually proclaim and say to you, wherever you go:

**Our Father.** “Delivered from evil.” Fol. 2.

**Benediction.** May the heavenly blessing of his holy Saints Speratus and his Companions cling to your minds and enrich you with everlasting gifts.  
R. Amen.

And may you, rejoicing as you receive their feasts, defended by their patronage, reach Christ unharmed after your passing.  
R. Amen.

May all of you who have gathered on this day, with the joyful faith of devotion and bowed prayer, attain eternal rewards in the future.  
R. Amen.

Through mercy.

**Lauda.** “They called upon the Lord,”  
P. and he himself heard them; he spoke to them in the pillar of cloud. Alleluia, alleluia.  
V. And they cried to the Lord when they were afflicted, and he delivered them from their necessities.  
P. And he himself.  
V. Glory and honor.  
P. And he himself.

**Prayer.** God, the joy and palm of your holy martyrs Speratus and his Companions, hear us, your suppliants, and grant that, since we venerate the relics of those whose merits are in your love and recall their benefits, we may through their merits deserve to be freed and preserved from every evil.  
R. Amen.

Through mercy.

## At Matins

**Antiphon.** “Give to us.” Psalm L.

**Prayer.** “Restore to us.” See fol. CLXIII.

**Antiphon 1.** Palms were in the hands of the Saints, and with a great cry they were saying:  
P. Salvation belongs to our God, who sits upon the throne, and to the Lamb.  
V. The Lord will help them and deliver them; he will rescue them from sinners and save them, because they have hoped in him.  
P. Salvation.  
V. Glory and honor.  
P. Salvation.

**Prayer.** God, exaltation and palm, as above at Vespers.

**Antiphon 2.** The Son of God rejoiced over the righteous:  
P. And he will establish them in the paradise of delights.  
V. The righteous cried out, and the Lord heard them; he delivered them from all their tribulations.  
P. And in the paradise.  
V. Glory and honor.  
P. And in the paradise.

**Prayer.** Remember us, Lord, and just as you render worthy rewards to your Saints Speratus and his Companions, so spare and have mercy on our sins, that, absolved from the past, we may deserve protection for the future.  
R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon 3.** The salvation of the righteous is from the Lord; he is their protector in the day of trouble. The Lord will help them,  
P. and he will deliver them from sinners,  
V. and he will save them, because they have hoped in him.  
P. And he will deliver.  
V. Glory and honor.
