P. And he will deliver.

**Prayer.** Our joy and our salvation, our strength and righteousness, Lord God almighty, grant, we ask, that we may rejoice in the lot of your holy martyrs Speratus and his Companions, pleasing to you; and there may we continually sing your praises by the office of the Righteous.  
R. Amen.

Through mercy.

R. The righteous shall live forever.  
P. With God is their reward.  
V. The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and the torment of death shall not touch them.  
P. With God.  
V. Glory and honor to the Father. Let R. “The righteous” be repeated.

## At Lauds

**At the Canticle.** **Antiphon.** “Those who love you, Lord.”

**Canticle.** “You who offered yourselves willingly.” Fol. CLXIII.

**At the Benedictus.** **Antiphon.** “Saints and humble of heart.”

**Canticle.** “Blessed are you.”

**Sono.** “The salvation of the righteous.”

**Lauda.** “Praise the Lord from the heavens.”

**Prophecy.** “The righteous shall live forever.” See fol. CLXIV.

**Hymn.** “Of the holy martyr Speratus.”

**Supplication.** “Let us pray,” as above at the preceding Vespers.

**Capitula.** Only-begotten Son of the unbegotten Father, God, coeternal and consubstantial with the Holy Spirit, who, descending from the height of your heavenly throne to the lowest places of this world in order to adopt humanity, did not shrink from taking on the garment of flesh, and for the liberation of the faithful did not disdain to save us in the form of a servant, to be weighed upon the scale of the Cross, and to endure the destruction of death: through the intervention of your Saints Speratus and his Companions, be gentle toward us who celebrate today’s solemnity, so that we may proclaim from earth to the Father, with the service of our hearts, the prayer you taught your disciples to keep:

**Our Father.** “Delivered from evil.” Fol. 2.

**Lauda.** “The praise of the Lord is in the assembly of the Saints.” Alleluia.  
P. Let Israel rejoice in him who made him. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.  
V. Sing to the Lord a new song, for he has done marvelous things.  
P. Let Israel rejoice.  
V. Glory.  
P. Let Israel rejoice.

**Benediction.** “Through the merits of the Saints.” See above at the preceding Vespers.

# DAY XXIV. THE FEAST OF SAINT CHRISTINA, VIRGIN AND MARTYR

[Col. 1165B]

Everything is to be said as for one Virgin, fol. CLXXIX, except:

## Hymn

Let us pursue with praises  
the triumph of the sacred Virgin,  
who, fighting manfully,  
conquered the wicked enemy  
and, preserving chastity,  
deserved renown.

For while this virgin  
was still a little child,  
she desired to adore  
Christ the King, the Lord,  
and, rejecting the idols,  
to offer pure incense.

She laughed at her father’s  
whips and punishments;  
she paid no attention  
to his wicked words,  
nor set her heart upon them,  
but with tranquil face  
she bravely endured  
the penalties.

Blessed in the very name  
by which she is called Christina,  
she is named a devout virgin;  
but it is evident that her name  
is derived from the name of Christ.

Proved by faith,  
she despised her father’s anger;  
delighted by heavenly joy,  
she rejoiced in God.  
She cast it away and rested  
upon heavenly rewards.

No torture broke her,  
no death terrified her;  
but, enduring every trial  
with joyful heart,  
she mocked the torments  
in their senseless madness.

She was beaten while suspended  
and pierced with rods;  
then she was thrown into  
a bronze vessel filled  
with resin, oil, and pitch,  
and with a raging fire.

There the gracious virgin  
was cast.

Pressed beneath the waves of the sea,  
she was rescued by Christ;  
she drove away  
every kind of serpent’s fury,  
regarding both death  
and torments as nothing.

Thus, having conquered  
three pagan judges,  
she triumphs happily  
by confessing the Trinity;  
called away from the world,  
she departs to heavenly things.

In your honor,  
holy Virgin, we sing;  
help all who make supplication;  
protect your servants;  
pour out prayers for our sins  
to Christ the King and Lord.

And you, immeasurable Christ the King,  
hear the prayers of those who entreat you;  
receive the voice of all;  
wipe away the guilt of sins;  
be a help to us who pray here  
on this feast.

Glory and honor to God,  
the Most High forever,  
to the one Father and Son  
with the glorious Paraclete;  
to him be praise and power  
through eternal ages.

Amen.

# DAY XXV. THE FEAST OF SAINT CHRISTOPHER AND HIS COMPANIONS

**Lauda.** “Light has risen.”  
**Sono.** “The souls of the righteous.” Fol. CLXVII. [CCLXX]  
**Antiphon.** “I will give to my Saints.”  
**Lauda.** “The blood of the Saints.” Fol. CLXII.

## Hymn

O blessed Author of the world,  
and Creator of all things,  
who are not a respecter of persons  
or of gifts,  
but, whenever anyone seeks you,  
are most mercifully present:

You drew the blessed citizen of heaven,  
the martyr Christopher,  
from the filthy mud  
of an evil birth,  
and, foreseeing him by your glorious will,  
mercifully attracted him.

The devoted man rejected  
the disgrace of his lineage,  
so that he might more eagerly  
follow the footsteps of truth  
and thereby, O Christ,  
obtain your grace.

The Emperor Decius,  
having captured him through his Companions,  
endeavored to have this Blessed One  
bound by his soldiers,  
whose valor he had thoroughly  
proved in war.

Of elegant stature,  
and more elegant in mind,  
shining in appearance,  
bright-hearted,  
and radiant in his hair,  
Christopher proclaimed Christ  
with his mouth and in his heart.

This man, not knowing  
the language of our people,  
implored that a Father  
be given him through the power of Christ;  
immediately, with God’s favor,  
he spoke everything.

Then, clinging to Christ’s court  
in order to pray,  
he obtained what he asked:  
that his staff should put forth leaves.  
Strengthened by power,  
he advanced in the struggle.

Full of faith in the truth,  
following its footsteps,  
he multiplied the fragments  
of the soldiers pursuing him,  
so that all, once filled,  
carried full sacks.

Therefore the soldiers,  
called to the faith of Christ,  
rejoiced with blessed Christopher,  
washed in the gracious fountain  
of the bath,  
at the beginning of grace.

Then these soldiers  
bind this prophet  
and, with one will,  
present him before Decius;  
the latter immediately attacks  
the Saints with savage speech.

Nor did the cruel king delay:  
fiercely raging,  
he orders Saint Christopher  
to be flayed with claws,  
so that, with his ribs laid bare,  
his flesh might be torn away.

Then he violently drives  
the martyrs Aquilina  
and holy Gallena  
through punishments,  
and consecrates the aforementioned soldiers  
with the dagger.

After this he consigns  
the Blessed One to terrible fires.  
The mighty pyre’s flame  
never touched him;  
rather, it approached him like gleaming, glowing gold.

Then, after sending ten soldiers  
with his companions to the stars,  
the tyrant’s sword cut them to pieces  
for Christ;  
struck by the same sword,  
he is carried into heaven.

Therefore we all beseech you,  
most faithful Surety,  
not to deny the covenant  
of your promise,  
which you sweetly made  
with Saint Christopher;  
but through him may we deserve  
to attain heavenly things,  
with every sin utterly  
cut away from us;  
and may the eternal God shine  
through everlasting ages.

Amen.

**Supplication.** “Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world,” as above.

**Capitula.** Christ God, King of the Saints, creator and enlightener of all ages, who reward with marvelous gifts the gracious Christopher, your witness, though drawn from a foreign people, and who, most mercifully, taught by your great example that he should become a most powerful warrior and shine as a conqueror in adversity—while, captive among enemies, he appeared gloriously great though from a humble origin, and became from a soldier a leader of faithful peoples—we ask you, we beg you, we entreat you with bowed hearts, and with groans we invoke your omnipotence: deign to guard us in your courts through the tireless patronage of your martyr Christopher and his Companions; mercifully and favorably hear the groans of each person. Weeping, we pray and ask that you graciously and kindly hear the prayer of those who lament and the vows of the faithful; and may those who mourn what they have lost enjoy what they ask.

Before your sight, Lord, may this prayer of the peoples, through continual supplication, be acceptable to the majesty of your mercy. Lord, at this solemnity may the assembly of the faithful of your witness Christopher be heard, and may it be strengthened by the power of your Spirit. Look, most mercifully, upon acceptable devotion; make our will most pure for you, O Christ; grant righteous action; and, merciful and kind in all things, graciously bestow what you may worthily receive, and unceasingly have mercy on us, making us worthy to be reconciled.

**Our Father.** “Delivered from evil.” Fol. 2.

**Benediction.** May the God of sanctification and ruler of heavenly powers deign to hear the prayers of his peoples who honor him through the annual devotion of his witness Christopher and his Companions.  
R. Amen.

May the unfailing rewarder, at the solemnity of the holy martyr Christopher, cause those whom he sees now serving him in his temple to be present as devotees.  
R. Amen.

May he willingly receive the vows of his assembled people through the intervention of Christopher, his glorious martyr; and may the Almighty himself, appeased and kindly as a father, pardon the sins of each person.  
R. Amen.

For he is kind and merciful through all ages of ages.  
R. Amen.

Through mercy.

**Lauda.** Everlasting joy is upon the heads of the Saints.  
P. Praise and gladness have seized them. Alleluia, alleluia.  
V. Many are the tribulations of the righteous, and from them all the Lord delivered them.  
P. Praise and gladness.  
V. Glory and honor.  
P. Praise and gladness.

**Prayer.** God, the joy and palm of your holy martyrs Christopher and his Companions, hear us, your suppliants, and grant that, since we venerate the relics of those whose merits are in your love and recall their benefits, we may through their merits deserve to be freed and preserved from every evil.  
R. Amen.

Through mercy.

## At Matins

**Antiphon.** Give us the joy of your salvation; strengthen us, Lord, with a princely spirit. Psalm L.

**Prayer.** Restore to us, Lord, the joy of your salvation, which we have lost by acting wickedly and neglected through carelessness. Call us back to it and restore it to us, so that, sin being driven out, righteousness may take its place, and, sadness being banished, joy may be present. Grant, we ask, this gladness, so that we may deserve to reach eternal salvation.  
R. Amen.

Through mercy.

**Antiphon 1.** Palms were in the hands of the Saints, and with a great cry they were saying:  
P. Salvation belongs to our God, who sits upon the throne, and to the Lamb.  
V. The Lord will help them and deliver them; he will rescue them from sinners and save them, because they have hoped in him.  
P. Salvation.  
V. Glory and honor to the Father.  
P. Salvation.

**Prayer.** God, joy and palm, as above.

**Antiphon 2.** The Son of God was directed toward the righteous:  
P. And he will establish them in the paradise of delights.  
V. And they cried out to the Lord when they were afflicted, and he delivered them from their necessities.  
P. And in the paradise.  
V. Glory and honor to the Father.  
P. And in the paradise.

**Prayer.** Remember us, Lord, and just as you render worthy rewards to your Saints Christopher and his Companions, so spare and have mercy on our sins, that, absolved from the past, we may deserve protection for the future.  
R. Amen.

Through mercy.

**Antiphon 3.** The salvation of the righteous is from the Lord; he is their protector in the day of trouble. The Lord will help them.  
P. And he will deliver them from sinners.  
V. And he will save them, because they have hoped in him.  
P. And he will deliver.  
V. Glory and honor.  
P. And he will deliver.

[CCLXXII] **Prayer.** Our joy and our salvation, our strength and righteousness, Lord God almighty, grant, we ask, that we may rejoice in the lot of your holy martyrs Christopher and his Companions, pleasing to you; and there may we continually sing your praises by the office of the Righteous.  
R. Amen.

Through mercy.

R. The Saints, who through faith conquered kingdoms, practiced righteousness, obtained promises, quenched the force of fire, and escaped the edge of the sword,  
P. became strong in war.  
V. They closed the mouths of lions and recovered from weakness.  
P. Became strong.  
V. Glory and honor.  
P. Became strong.

## At Lauds

**At the Canticle.** **Antiphon.** “All the Saints are in the hand.”

**Canticle.** “The Lord will come from Sinai.”

**At the Benedictus.** **Antiphon.** “Saints and humble of heart.”

**Canticle.** “Blessed are you, Lord.”

**Sono.** “The way of the righteous.”

**Lauda.** “Praise the Lord.” Psalm CXLVIII.

**Prophecy.** “The souls of the righteous.” Fol. CLXVII.

**Hymn.** “O blessed Author of the world.”

**Supplication.** “Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world.”

**Capitula.** “Christ God, King…” See at the preceding Vespers.

**Lauda.** “The praise of the Lord.” Fol. CCLXIX.

**Benediction.** “God of sanctifications.” See at the preceding Vespers.

# DAY XXX. ON THE DAY OF SAINT CUCUFAS

Everything is to be said as for one Martyr, nine lessons, fol. CLXII.

## Hymn

Barcelona, flourishing with joyful Cucufas,  
honoring the tomb of the holy body  
and venerating the place of the sacred sepulcher,  
scatter privet flowers.

The Scillitan city sent you this  
splendid gift and gave you the blessed Felix,  
when the people of Gerunda  
were allotted him for veneration.

These men, leaving aside  
the honor of the tomb,  
return to guard their own seats:  
here he is celebrated at Barcelona,  
there at Gerunda.

From this point the blood  
of gracious Cucufas  
became the heir of our region;  
and here, placing his limbs among us,  
he grants us life.

Here, full of faith,  
loving Christ in return,  
he endures the tyrant hostile to the light;  
and soon, tortured by twelve soldiers,  
he is terrified though destined for blessedness.

Struck by the furious man’s  
terrible blows,  
he poured out his entrails  
as though they were about to perish;  
restored, he receives them again  
into his belly,  
whole for the moment.

Sent into the flames,  
he destroys by his prayers  
the threatening power  
of the fire brought against him;  
the flame cannot burn  
the blessed body too fiercely.

Ordered to be burned  
upon a fiery grate,  
the fuel of the heat grows;  
but none of the torments  
does harm to Christ’s servant.

After this, that devout man endures  
the blow of iron thorns  
striking him;  
and so his spirit breathes forth  
into heaven when his head is cut off.

Now favor the prayers  
of your dependents, O Martyr;  
instruct the citizen; protect the people;  
and soothe the hearts of the priests  
with the love of peace.

When guilt has been removed,  
may the soul grow strong;  
may we all be nourished  
with heavenly bread;  
may the Spirit adorn  
the corrupted limbs  
of the flesh that has fallen away.

May we not perish  
through a ruinous deed;  
may the body, weighed down  
by foods and vices, not be destroyed;  
may the soul not burn  
in hidden fires of evil.

Thus, blessed Cucufas,  
may we possess with you  
the kingdoms of heaven  
through our merits,  
so that our resounding tongue  
may offer to God  
a pleasing song.

May we celebrate the Father  
with honor;  
may we sing eternal glory  
to the Son,  
with whom the one Holy Spirit  
is joined.

Amen.

# AUGUST FEASTS. AUGUST 1. THE FEAST OF SAINT FELIX THE MARTYR

## At Vespers

**Lauda.** “My soul has hoped in the Lord.” Fol. CLVI.

**Sono.** Alleluia. Blessed is the man who fears the Lord. Alleluia.  
P. He will greatly delight in his commandments. Alleluia, alleluia.  
V. Glory and riches are in his house, and his righteousness endures forever and ever.  
P. Alleluia, alleluia.

**Antiphon.** If the righteous man is taken beforehand by death,  
P. his soul will be in refreshment.  
V. Blessed is the man who fears the Lord; he greatly delights in his commandments.  
P. His soul will be.  
V. Glory.  
P. His soul will be.

**Prayer.** Gird us, Lord, with the strength by which you strengthened your holy Felix through the bestowal of holiness, so that, just as he is victorious through punishment, he may find us unconquered in the face of enticement. Thus weaken in us the forces of growing desires, just as your martyr, having conquered suffering, now remains in eternal glory.  
R. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God, etc.

**Lauda.** “The righteous shall flourish like the palm.” See fol. CLIX.

## Hymn

God, fountain of everlasting life,  
light, source of light,  
look upon the people singing  
the feast of the great Martyr;  
receive the vows of those who pray;  
accept the songs of praise.

Behold, we set forth  
the honors of your gracious Felix:  
loosen the bonds of our tongue,  
granting resonant songs,  
so that we may duly proclaim  
your mighty deeds.

For while this man  
was studying the disciplines  
of the world in the city  
of Caesarea in Mauritania,  
he abandoned the smoky craft  
of the arts, following you.

Hearing that the faithful  
were being punished,  
he soon reached Gerunda.  
Detained by order of the governor,  
he was thrust into prison,  
laden with iron chains;  
the Angels spoke with him.

He is brought before the altar  
so that he might sacrifice  
to bloodstained idols;  
he rejected the infamous deed,  
professing Christ with his voice.

The crowd roars with forked claws,  
stripping his bones;  
then, tied to mules,  
he is torn limb from limb.

Pressed beneath the waters of the sea,  
he is submerged under the swelling wave;  
an Angel, joining him,  
opens his lips in gracious songs.

With brave heart  
he endured every torment;  
then, leaving behind  
punishments, chains, claws,  
and blows,  
he departs to heavenly things,  
leaving the prison of flesh.

O Gerunda, exceedingly fortunate!  
O blessed city!  
You fear no evils,  
relying upon so great a Martyr.  
Whatever is requested  
is obtained by whoever gathers here.

Here demons, oppressed  
by the power of God,  
are lacerated;  
they are scourged, bound,  
and fiercely burned;  
and, becoming smoke and ash,  
they possess no strength.

Here desired salvation  
flows down from the heavens  
for the weary;  
sight opens to the blind;  
speech comes to the mute;  
the deaf recover their ears here,  
and the lame leap up.

Therefore we all beseech you,  
one supreme Trinity:  
at the Martyr’s request,  
remove our sins,  
drive away every harmful thing,  
and grant favorable things.

May the clergy shine here  
with life,  
and may the priest flourish;  
may the faithful people  
feel that they have obtained  
what they seek;  
may every age and sex  
rejoice in this patron.

Glory to the Father and to the Son,  
and always to the Paraclete;  
praise, power, and strength,  
an abundance of thanksgiving,  
to him whom all things confess as God  
through ages of ages.

Amen.

**Supplication.** “Let us pray to the Lord, the Redeemer of the world,” as above, with the name changed.

**Capitula.** Your martyr Felix, Lord, flourishes greatly in your commandments and is enlarged by the fruit of righteousness in rewards, because he obeyed all your precepts, so that, for one whose happiness was in his name, eternity might arise from his deed; and what he was called, he might be recognized as being, since he is free from misery through suffering and obtains happiness through triumph. Through the intercession of so great a martyr, may eternal kindness advance our cause; and, while he rejoices in perpetual happiness, may he by your accustomed mercy release us from the yoke of unhappiness.

**Our Father.** “Delivered from evil.” Fol. 2.

**Benediction.** The supreme God, who calls him happy whom he sees rejoicing in affection for that blessed Jerusalem, may through the prayer of his Felix cause you happily to remain in love of that same city.  
R. Amen.

May he also happily wipe away the unhappinesses of your deeds, and, appeased, grant the gifts of perpetual happiness to your more fortunate prayers.  
R. Amen.

May, through the intervention of this martyr Felix, you happily flee the unhappiness of this age and deserve to be freed from the punishment of perpetual unhappiness.  
R. Amen.

Through mercy.

**Lauda.** “The righteous shall flourish like the palm.” See fol. CLIX.

**Prayer.** Your martyr Felix, Lord, whom you chose and received—since both his election proves him a witness and his reception proves him happy—may his intercession cause us to dwell in your tabernacles, where you, the perpetual rewarder, both receive those who strive and crown those who triumph forever.

Through your mercy.

## At Matins

**Antiphon.** “My lips, Lord.” Psalm L.

**Prayer.** “May our lips rejoice, Lord.” See fol. 60.

**Antiphon 1.** The righteous man will be like a flower of the field, and his fragrant odor will be pleasing.  
P. And everyone who hopes in God will praise him.  
V. Blessed is the man who fears the Lord; he will greatly delight in his commandments.  
P. And everyone.  
V. Glory and honor to the Father.  
P. And everyone.

**Prayer.** Your martyr Felix, Lord, whom you chose. See at the preceding Vespers.

**Antiphon 2.** This man was made strong in the struggle;  
P. and he was delivered from his persecutors, because he persevered in his innocence.  
V. His glory is exceedingly great in your salvation; you place glory and great beauty upon him.  
P. And he was delivered.  
V. Glory.  
P. And he was delivered.

**Prayer.** Happy is this martyr of yours, Lord, Felix, who, justified by you and through you, appeared glorious in every struggle. Grant us, therefore, that in the future we may share in that happiness whose fortunate martyrdom now fills us with joy.  
R. Amen.

Through.

**Antiphon 3.** “In the paradise of delights.” Fol. CLVII.

**Prayer.** The happy martyr, who bore witness to human beings, was received by you in hope; Felix, who remains in you without end and deserved to be killed for you; Felix, so that through your gift he may cause us to become participants and, by serving you, make us happy.  
R. Amen.

Through.

R. While Saint Felix was being beaten by his enemies,  
P. the Angel of the Lord came and said to him: “Take courage, Felix; do not fear. For I have been sent by the Lord God to free you from the hand of those who persecute you.”  
V. While Saint Felix prayed to the Lord with intent heart and hands extended toward heaven,  
P. the Angel came.  
V. Glory and honor to the Father.  
P. The Angel came.

**Prayer.** God, whose honor is holiness, whose love is salvation, and whose affection is perfection, enter our hearts. Grant that throughout your Church the footsteps of your Felix may shine through his merits, so that, under your guidance, the steps of all may be led along the road to life—the road by which your Martyr was raised to the crown.  
R. Amen.

Through your mercy, etc.

## At Lauds

**At the Canticle.** **Antiphon.** I rejoice in your holiness, for there is no other God like our God.

**Canticle.** “My heart has been confirmed.” Fol. 55.

**Prayer.** Grant us, Almighty One, the constant patronage of your most blessed Felix, so that we may also deserve to attain his splendid example; feeling most abundantly the help of his intercession, may we follow most bravely the one who fights.  
R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

**At the Benedictus.** **Antiphon.** The Lord’s blessing hastens as the reward of the righteous.

**Canticle.** “Blessed are you, Lord.”

**Sono.** “Seven times a day I praise you.”

**Lauda.** “Praise the Lord.” Psalm CXLVIII.

**Prophecy.** “Blessed is the man who has not fallen.” See fol. CCXXXVIII.

**Hymn.** “God, fountain of life.”

[CCLXXV] **Supplication.** “Let us pray to the Redeemer.” At the preceding Vespers.

**Capitula.** God, who crowned your martyr Felix in mercy and compassion, while he believed in you and was willing to suffer for you, so that by enduring temporal punishment he might seize an everlasting crown: through his intercession grant us, your servants, that, if we do not attain the greatness of suffering, we may at least be free from disgrace; and that, since the titles of virtues do not assign us glory, the dishonor of vices may be erased, lest we come into punishment.

**Our Father.** “Delivered from evil.” Fol. 2.

**Lauda.** “With the psaltery.” Fol. CLVIII.

**Benediction.** “The supreme God.” At the preceding Vespers.

At the conclusion of Vespers, everything is to be said as at the first Vespers, except the Capitula, Benediction, and Lauda.

**Capitula.** Be present, Lord, at the solemn celebrations of your Church; and may the mysteries that she offers in praise of your martyr Felix be pleasing in your sight. May we not become defiled in nocturnal deeds, we who frequent your glorious martyr in the offices of evening; and may our life not be discordant with sacred devotion, so that, while we honorably commemorate the martyr, we may hold fast the dignity of his most holy life.

**Our Father.** “Delivered from evil.” Fol. 2.

**Benediction.** May heavenly grace hear your petitions and, through the intercession of its martyr Felix, bestow heavenly gifts upon you.  
R. Amen.

May it enrich you by bestowing, multiply you by enriching, preserve you by multiplying, and gladden you by preserving.  
R. Amen.

May you who honor the martyr’s feast with faithful vows receive, through his merit, everything that is fitting.  
R. Amen.

Through his mercy.

**Lauda.** “The righteous, like the palm.” Fol. CLIX.

**Prayer.** As above at the first Vespers.

# AUGUST 6. THE FEAST OF THE HOLY MARTYRS JUSTUS AND PASTOR

## At Vespers

[Col. 1175B]

**Lauda.** “Light has risen in the darkness.” Fol. CLXII.

**Sono.** “The righteous shall live forever.” Fol. CLXVIII.

**Antiphon.** “Righteous men, sprout forth like…” Fol. CLXII.

**Lauda.** “He looked upon them when they were afflicted.” Fol. CLXV.

## Hymn

O everlasting Word of God,  
brought forth from the Father’s mouth,  
who employ the weak instrument  
of infants,  
giving them breath  
so that they may utter the sound of their voice:

Be graciously present to us;  
heal the fibers of our throats;  
equip our mouths with speech;  
fill our hearts with tears,  
so that we may celebrate in song  
the feasts of the Saints  
with worthy songs.

Behold Justus, behold Pastor,  
both joined by blood,  
whom loving brotherhood  
had bound together  
in a devout kinship;  
the unity of an equal  
sacred passion joined them.

While these two were still held  
in the schools and being instructed  
in letters,  
they heard that the tyrant  
was entering the city  
persecuting people.

Immediately they left the school  
and rejected their tablets;  
then they hastened  
to the presence of the governor,  
and, following the Cross of Christ,  
armed their feeble bodies,  
so that they might bravely  
complete the triumphs of passion.

Announcing this suddenly  
to Dacianus, they said:

“Behold, the little ones  
come confessing Christ,  
willingly to endure  
the sufferings of death  
and the slaughter.”

Then the governor, enraged,  
hastening his sentence,  
shouted to his cruel ministers  
that they should seize them,  
ordering their tender bodies  
to be cut apart with clubs.

Then, with sacred speech,  
they addressed one another,  
so that they might properly  
despise the temporal pains  
of the body,  
by which they would possess  
future joy with the Angels.

Soon Dacianus heard  
the steadfastness of the martyrs;  
roused to fury,  
he dictated this sentence:  
that both brothers,  
having been killed,  
should perish by a dreadful death.

Immediately the frenzied attendants  
dragged them  
to an open field,  
which they call Laudabile.  
There they are struck by the sword  
and crowned with blood.

O truly blessed place,  
where the holy blood  
of the little ones  
is hidden for the salvation  
of the peoples,  
and from which many signs  
of healing flow forth for the sick!

Indeed, here divine power  
conquers the rages of demons;  
it cures ulcers, heals limbs,  
and eases pains.

They receive the vows of all,

and raise up those who fall.

Now, relying on the passion of your servants,

the city rejoices—

the city of Complutum, rightly so—

in the life-giving blood by which you were washed;

and soon restore to the Twin Martyrs

the songs owed to them by their vow.

Therefore, God, we ask you

to hear us as we pray:

drive away diseases, loosen bonds,

and remit sins;

[Col. 1176D] and grant that, unharmed,

we may seek our future homeland.

Give your servants

the love of your name;

let us love nothing temporal,

but love one another.

Let us follow you, sing to you,

and enjoy you forever.

Glory to you through all time,

undivided Trinity;

highest praise, honor, and power,

single glory—

you who resound you as God of the ages

through ages without end.

Amen.

[Col. 1177A] Supplication. Let us pray, changing the name; fol. CLXXXVII.

Chapters. The clear and radiant solemnity of the Innocents is present before the eyes of mortals today. In it, a double pledge and a doubled offering of sweetness deserves to enter heaven: for in their bright fellowship brotherhood is recognized as most just in Justus and devout in Pastor; and the beloved faces of the infants exhort one another to the glory of martyrdom. Grant us, therefore, through the prayers of your Justus, to preserve justice while we live, and through the protection of Pastor to escape what we fear; so that Justus may make the justice which he bears in his name more radiant in the merits of those who supplicate, and Pastor may receive us under the guidance of his goodness and protect us; so that through Justus, the just, and through Pastor, the shepherd’s guidance, we may deserve to enter the blessed dwelling of the outstanding Shepherd.

Our Father. And lead us not. Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

Benediction. May God, who is the just crowner of the just and the devout shepherd of souls, free you from injustice through Justus and sanctify you through Pastor by the protection of Christ the Shepherd. R\. Amen. Through Justus may he make you lovers of justice, and through Pastor may he nourish you with the food of infinite glory. R\. Amen. So that, when the justice of Justus has made you commendable to God, you may deserve to be heirs in heaven under the guidance of Pastor. R\. Amen. Through the mercy of that same God of ours, etc.

Lauda. “Like pure lilies the saints have blossomed”: Alleluia. P. “And the fragrance of God appears upon them.” Alleluia, alleluia. V\. “Planted in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God they will flourish.” P. “And the fragrance of God.” V\. Glory [Col. 1177C] and honor to the Father and the Son. P. “And the fragrance of God.”

Prayer. Clothe us, Lord, in the brightness of justice. For the little ones slain for you, you granted Justus and Pastor the everlasting glory of their reward. As you made them, through martyrdom, whiter and more beautiful than snow, purify us from sins through confession. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

At Matins.

Antiphon. “Give us the joy of your salvation.” Psalm L. Prayer. “Restore to us.” See fol. CLXIII. Antiphon 1. “Palms were in the hands of the Saints.” Fol. CLXVIII.

Prayer. All the saints earnestly implore you, Lord, with a great cry [Col. 1177D], while they await the vengeance of their persecutors—not with bodily voices [CCLXXVII], but with their desires. And therefore we ask that you, who hear their voices or desires and grant their request, may not allow the souls of those who confess you to be dragged into eternal torment. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

Antiphon 2. “These are they who have laid aside mortal tunics,” P. “And have taken up immortal life; now they are crowned and receive palms.” V\. “They will still multiply in abundant old age, and they will be patient in doing good.” P. “And have taken up immortal life.” V\. Glory and honor to the Father. P. “And have taken up immortal life.”

Prayer. Clothe us, Lord, as above in Vespers.

Antiphon 3. “The Son of God rejoiced over the just”; [Col. 1178A] P. “And he will establish them in the paradise of delights.” V\. “The just cried out, and the Lord heard them, and delivered them from all their tribulations.” P. “In the paradise.” V\. Glory and honor to the Father. P. “In the paradise.”

Prayer. Look and listen, Lord, to the voice of the groaning Church, which mourns the death of her infants. Be therefore her consoler concerning her children, you who are acknowledged as the father of her children; so that in you she may rejoice both in the number of the slain and in the return of her adversaries. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

R\. “Holy men.” See fol. CLXXVII.

Prayer. Make us, Lord, always stand before you innocent and upright, so that, joined to your uprightness by an indissoluble bond [Col. 1178B], we may deserve to share in the little ones slain for you. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

R\. “For those who love God all things work together for good, for those who are called saints according to God’s purpose.” P. “Those whom he foreknew, he predestined to be conformed to the image of the Son of God.” V\. “Those whom he called, he also justified; and those whom he justified, he also glorified.” P. “Those whom he foreknew.”

Prayer. May the innocent and righteous blood of innocent souls, with an unwearied cry of the voice, plead with you for us, Only-Begotten Son of God the Father, so that the multitude of the faithful may reach that place where they are to be crowned, where their innocence endures crowned. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

In Lauds.

[Col. 1178C]

For the Canticle. Antiphon. “We beseech you, Saints.” Canticle. “The Lord from Sinai.” For the Benedictus. Antiphon. “Saints and humble ones.” Canticle. “Blessed are you, Lord God.” Sonus. “The way of the just is straight.” Lauda. “Praise the Lord from the heavens”: Alleluia, alleluia. Psalm CXLVIII. See fol. CLXVII. Prophecy. “The souls of the just are in the hand of God.” See fol. CLXVII. Hymn. “O everlasting God.” Supplication. “Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world, our Lord.” See in the preceding Vespers.

Chapters. O most blessed blood of the children of God, which will be avenged at the time of judgment: before judgment, come to the aid of Christian peoples; for since vengeance will be returned by the Lord upon the enemies for you, through you may remission of sins be granted to all Christians.

Our Father. Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

Lauda. “Like pure lilies they have blossomed.” Benediction. “God, who is the crowner of the just.” See in the preceding Vespers.

TENTH DAY. ON THE FEAST OF SAINT LAWRENCE, ARCHDEACON AND MARTYR.

At Vespers.

Lauda. “You crowned him with glory and honor,” P. “Lord.” V\. “You placed glory and great splendor upon him.” P. “Lord.”

May the Lord be always present. R\. And with your spirit.

Sonus. “He scattered and gave to the poor”: Alleluia; “his justice [Col. 1179A] endures forever.” Alleluia. V\. “His horn will be exalted in glory.” Alleluia.

May the Lord be always present. R\. And with your spirit.

Antiphon. “The man who is inclined to mercy will be blessed”: P. “He gave of his bread to the poor.” V\. “Blessed is he who understands concerning the needy and the poor; on the evil day the Lord will deliver him”: Alleluia. P. “He gave of his bread.” [CCLXXVIII] V\. Glory and honor to the Father. P. “He gave of his bread.”

May the Lord be always present. R\. And with your spirit.

Antiphon. “He who possesses wisdom will be saved. He who gives to the poor will never be in need.” P. “But the just man will be in joy and gladness.” V\. “Blessed is the man who fears the Lord; he greatly delights in his commandments.” P. “But the just man.” V\. Glory and honor to the Father. P. “But the just [Col. 1179B] man.”

May the Lord be always present. R\. And with your spirit.

Lauda. “He has consoled the poor man; he himself will be consoled concerning him.” P. “He distributed from his own bread to the needy; he received victory and honor”: Alleluia. V\. “The gracious man who shows mercy and lends will order his words in judgment, for he will never be shaken.” P. “From his own bread.” V\. Glory and honor. P. “From his own.”

Hymn.

Behold, the faith of the martyr Lawrence

fought armed,

after prolonged heat

had cooked his burned side.

Before this, the priest had said it,

when he saw Xystus,

fastened to the cross,

and Lawrence weeping

beneath the very crossbeam:

“Cease to pour out

your sorrowful tears over my departure.

I go before you, brother;

you too will follow

after three days.”

The bishop’s final voice,

foretelling glory,

deceived no one;

for the foretold day

granted the palm.

Therefore, holy Lawrence,

we seek your passion:

whatever each suppliant asks,

extend it to all

by your favor.

[Col. 1179D] To God the Father be glory,

and to his only Son,

with the Paraclete Spirit,

who reigns through every age.

Amen.

Supplication. Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world, changing the name. See fol. CLXXXVII.

Chapters. Lord Jesus Christ, who made the most blessed Lawrence, burning with the fire of your love, overcome the fires of desires and passions—while he both trampled gold and flame, proving generous in distributing to the poor and devoted in the burning of his own body—grant us, through the intercession of that servant, that, kindled by the vapor of the Holy Spirit, we may overcome the flames of lust and be consumed by the fire of complete holiness [Col. 1180A]; so that after our passage our lot may be found among those saints for whom we now render service to you.

Our Father. And lead us not. But deliver us. Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

Benediction. May the Lord Jesus Christ, for whom blessed Lawrence offered the holocaust of his cooked body, burn your minds with the kindling of heavenly virtues. R\. Amen. And may he whom, roasted on the gridiron, Lawrence did not cease to confess deem you worthy to be comforted by the rewards of holy confession. R\. Amen. And, established amid the flames of the world, may you alone blaze for him through the practice of holiness, to whom this martyr clung after the fires of his passion. R\. Amen.

Through his mercy.

[Col. 1180B] Lauda. “The Lord established.” fol. CLXVII.

Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ, who showed your most blessed martyr Lawrence, rejecting the worthless world, as the purest gold which fire would not consume but approve—and the more it burned, the more brightly it shone—grant that the fires of desire may not consume those whom such shining examples of your martyr illumine. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

At Matins.

Antiphon. “My lips.” Psalm L. Prayer. “Let them rejoice, Lord.” See fol. CLXXX.

Antiphon 1. “His gifts are manifest in his God.” P. “And the Church of the saints will recount his almsgiving.” [Col. 1180C] V\. “A little possessed by the just is better than the many riches of sinners.” P. “And his almsgiving.” V\. Glory and honor to the Father and the Son. P. “And the Church will recount his almsgiving.”

Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ, who granted that your most blessed martyr Lawrence should shine more brightly through merits than he suffered through flames, so that the strongest martyr burned more through love than through heat: grant that we may be so inflamed by the spark of his faith that we are not consumed by the fire of the world. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy, etc.

Antiphon 2. “The merciful man finds grace in the eyes of all flesh.” P. “Beloved by God and by human beings, whose memory is in blessing.” V\. “A man’s steps will be directed by the Lord, and he will greatly desire his way.” P. “Beloved by God.” V\. Glory [Col. 1180D] and honor to the Father. P. “Beloved by God.”

Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ, who received your most blessed martyr Lawrence in your name in the manner of a cooked holocaust, so that whole and entire in body and soul he might be offered to you: grant, in answer to his merits, that you mercifully accept in us the sacrifice of a contrite heart, since you recognize us as suppliant worshipers of your martyr. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy, etc.

Antiphon 3. “The Lord chose me as one of the leaders and appointed me as a strong man for battle.” P. “The Lord gave me a white robe and adorned me with a crown.” V\. “Blessed is the Lord my God, who trains my hands for war, my fingers [Col. 1181A] for battle.” P. “The Lord gave me.” V\. Glory and honor to the Father. P. “The Lord gave me.”

Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ. See above, in Vespers.

R\. “He opened his hand to the needy and stretched out his palms to the poor.” P. “Give him from the fruit of his hands, and let his works praise him in the gates.” V\. “He opened his mouth to wisdom, and the law of mercy is on his tongue.” P. “Give him.” V\. Glory and honor. P. “Give him.”

Prayer. Christ our God, who willed that the hands and palms of your most blessed martyr Lawrence should be extended to the poor by right of generosity: grant us to carry away some useful fruit from the labors of his hands, so that the labor of his hands may benefit not only him but also us—while you grant him glory for the perfection of his works and, through his imitation and prayer, lead us to the crown; and so, while the perfection of completed work shows the just man praiseworthy in the gates of Zion, may sinners obtain the merit of holiness through his example. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 4. “You tested me, Lord, like gold. You placed tribulations on my back.” P. “I passed through fire and water, and you brought me into a place of refreshment.” V\. “I will enter your house with holocausts; I will pay you my vows, which my lips have uttered, and my mouth spoke in my tribulation.” P. “I passed through.” V\. Glory and honor to the Father. P. “I passed through.”

Prayer. His justice endures forever, Lord, whose mercy has poured itself out in the consolation of the poor. Make us imitators of your archdeacon Lawrence, so that, first becoming merciful toward our own selves, extending worthy alms, we may be spared our evil deeds and may bestow upon our neighbors the good things we seek. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 5. “I am your protector; do not fear, says the Lord. If you pass through fire, it will not burn you.” P. “Rivers will not overwhelm you, for I will hold your hand.” V\. “By day the sun will not burn you, nor the moon by night.” P. “Rivers.” V\. Glory and honor. P. “Rivers.”

Prayer. Jesus, our God and Lord, who made the illustrious archdeacon Lawrence so distinguished in merit that he guarded wisdom and stood in the glory and joy of his spirit: grant us, Lord, understanding of wisdom and zeal for holy action, so that, giving our substance to the poor, we may escape the vengeance for our crimes. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 6. “The just man shows mercy and lends, and his offspring will be in blessing.” P. “And his inheritance will endure forever.” V\. “His offspring will be mighty upon the earth; the generation of the upright will be blessed.” P. “And his inheritance.” V\. Glory and honor. P. “And his inheritance.”

Prayer. All day long, Lord, your just servant shows mercy and lends; throughout the entire course of this mortal life he gives temporal things in order to receive eternal ones. May his offspring therefore bear fruit in blessing upon us, so that, sharing in his merit [Col. 1182A], we may also deserve to share in his rewards. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

R\. “You tested me, Lord, as silver is tested. You placed tribulations on my back; I passed through fire and water, and you brought me into a place of refreshment. I will enter the house of the Lord.” P. “For he heard my prayer.” V\. “Come and hear, and I will tell all you who fear God how many things he has done for my soul.” P. “For he heard.” V\. Glory. P. “For he heard.”

Prayer. God, who willed that your holy martyr Lawrence should be tested on earth by the customary test of piety, and do not allow him to be tempted beyond what you foresee has been granted to him as the gift of endurance [Col. 1182B]: deliver us from every temptation that could overwhelm our minds, so that, faithfully serving you with service pleasing to you, you may permit us to be tested in such a way that the temptation itself may bind us firmly—not in the confusion of error, but in the embrace of truth. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

In Lauds.

For the Canticle. Antiphon. “The throne of glory.” Canticle. “It has been confirmed.” fol. 55. For the Benedictus. Antiphon. “The blessing of the Lord hastens as the reward of the just.”

Canticle. “Blessed are you, Lord God of our fathers.” Sonus. “He scattered and gave.” See in the preceding Vespers. Lauda. “Praise the Lord.” Psalm CXLVIII.

[Col. 1182C] Reading from the Book of Ecclesiasticus of Solomon (Chapter XXXI).

R\. Thanks be to God.

“My son, he who loves gold will not be justified, and he who pursues completion will be filled with it. Many have been given over to the downfall of gold, and their destruction has appeared in its face. Gold is a stumbling block to those who sacrifice; woe to those who pursue it, and every imprudent person will perish in it. Blessed is the rich man who has been found without blemish, who has not gone after gold, nor hoped in money and treasures. Who is he, and we will praise him? For he has done wonders in his life. Who has been tested in it and perfected, and it will be for him in eternal glory? He could have transgressed, but did not transgress; he could have done evil, but did not. Therefore his goods have been established [Col. 1182D] in God, and the Church of the saints will recount his almsgiving.” R\. Amen.

Hymn. “Behold, the faith of the martyr Lawrence.” Supplication. “Let us pray to the Redeemer.” See in the preceding Vespers.

Chapters. Lord Jesus Christ, who make the body of your most blessed archdeacon Lawrence, cooked by the burning of fire, a purest holocaust to you, while that same martyr, mindful of his mystery, became both priest and minister, pleasing you in offering himself: may he stand before you, we ask, for the salvation of the faithful—he who, while his limbs melted amid the flames, rejoiced in spirit while confessing you—so that he who overcame the fires through human devotion may by his fitting prayer drive punishments away from us.

[Col. 1183A] Our Father. Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

Lauda. “He consoled the poor man.”

Benediction. “The Lord Jesus Christ.” See in the preceding Vespers.

At the end of Vespers.

Lauda. “You crowned him with glory and honor.” Sonus. “He scattered and gave to the poor.” See in the preceding Vespers.

Antiphon. “I entered the praetorium of Caesar.” P. “Questioned, I confessed Christ; accused, I did not deny him; dragged away, I held fast to my God, and I will hold fast.” V\. “I passed through fire and water, and you brought me into a place of refreshment.” P. “Questioned.” V\. Glory and honor. P. “Questioned.”

May the Lord be present. R\. And with your spirit.

Lauda. “You tested me with fire, Lord,” P. “And no iniquity was found in me”: Alleluia, alleluia. V\. “Hear, O God, my justice; attend to my prayer. Give ear to my prayer, and not to lips of deceit.” P. “And no iniquity was.” V\. Glory and honor. P. “And no iniquity was.”

Hymn. “Behold, the faith of the martyr Lawrence.” See in the preceding Vespers. And Supplication. “Let us pray.”

Chapters. God, who received the Levite Lawrence, tested by fire, as the victim of a true holocaust, so that, cooked in the manner of a holocaust, he might come to you whole and intercede for the wretched: by his intercession, we ask, kindle in all of us the torches of heavenly fire, so that, with conscience purified, we may deserve to proclaim and say to you:

Our Father. Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

[Col. 1183C] Benediction. May Christ the Lord look upon our vows, for whom Xystus was tortured and Lawrence consumed by flame. R\. Amen. And, with his favor, may the Catholic flock be so protected through Xystus that through Lawrence it may be saved by drinking the saving chalice. R\. Amen. And, while that one protects us and this one intercedes, may we be so kindled by the example of the former that we may be relieved by the intercession of the latter. R\. Amen. Through him who grants and helps, who with the Father and the Holy Spirit lives and reigns as one God through ages of ages. R\. Amen.

[CCLXXXI] Lauda. “The Lord established.” Fol. CLVII. Prayer. “Lord Jesus Christ, who made the most blessed one,” as above.

THIRTEENTH DAY. ON THE FEAST OF SAINT HIPPOLYTUS THE MARTYR.

[Col. 1183D]

At Vespers.

Lauda. “He hoped.” fol. CLVI. Sonus. “Bless, O my soul.” fol. CLX.

Antiphon. “Your holy one clothed himself in justice, and in your name he won the victory.” P. “You are merciful, Lord, who give a crown without a reward.” V\. “He asked for life, and you gave him length of days forever and ever.” P. “You are merciful.” V\. Glory and honor. P. “You are merciful.”

May the Lord be present. R\. And with your spirit.

Lauda. “The Lord has done good.” fol. CLXI.

Hymn.

The celebrated feasts are here, O peoples,

which the happy orbit of time brings back,

returning upon its revolving axis:

return praise to the starry Prince.

For here Hippolytus, once despised

in the earthly age,

climbs to the snowy heavens,

when, releasing his soul from the body,

he deserved to receive

the living heavenly laurel.

While here he was commander

of a warlike band,

he received the Martyr

to be kept in prison

by Caesar’s commands;

and the Martyr, with the cross going before him,

restored to the blind eyes

the light they had lost.

When Hippolytus saw

the favorable signs,

he soon believed in Christ the Lord;

and, rejecting the idols

of the impious demonic doctrine,

he rebuked them with voices

joined to those of Christ’s followers.

Then Caesar, burning with furious violence,

[Col. 1184B] ordered the holy mouth

to be split by a stone.

The fragments of his teeth flew far apart;

but the voice proclaimed

the only-begotten One.

The torturer, blazing with iron claws,

armed himself with the darts

of the thorn-bearing thistle.

The Martyr’s utterly torn entrails

were drenched with streams

of rosy blood.

Then they bound him

to the backs of fierce hoofed beasts;

dragged over rough ground,

he suddenly surrendered

his life-giving breath,

by which he was able

to conquer the dread world.

For this reason we humbly ask

the divine King of all,

as suppliants, that the renowned Martyr

stand as a helper for the wretched

and obtain pardon

for sins confessed from the heart.

[Col. 1184C] May life be rich and abundant in crops;

may fitting prosperity in worldly affairs prevail;

may war perish, may good peace flow forth;

may virtues flourish, may crimes pass away.

To the unbegotten Father

be the greatest glory;

equal glory to the Begotten

and to the Paraclete—

to the One who eternally holds the scepters,

living through everlasting ages.

Amen.

Supplication. Let us pray, as above.

Chapters. Christ the Lord, light of angels and splendor of human beings, brightness of days and times, of souls and bodies, sprinkling with the light-bearing descent of the Holy Spirit the gift of flame-haired radiance offered in reverence for your witness Hippolytus, make it pleasing to your will and render it beneficial to us; so that by visible brightness it may restrain the dark blackness of night’s wandering monsters, and by invisible gift consume the rough errors of sins [the reading “maledulcium” is uncertain].

Our Father. Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

Benediction. May Christ grant you immense joys through the martyr Hippolytus. R\. Amen. May he grant prosperity and drive away the hardships of life. R\. Amen. May he grant pardon for sins and rewards for vows. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

Lauda. “The Lord established.” fol. CLVII.

Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ, who bestowed such strength of spirit upon your witness Hippolytus that, cut by iron spikes, he proclaimed you to be God in the heavens [Col. 1185A]: blunt in us the spike of deceptive pleasure, and permit us continually to confess your holy name, so that, overcoming the temptations of carnal corruption, we may deserve to rejoice in the company of the saints. R\. Amen.

Through.

At Matins.

Antiphon. “My lips.” Psalm L. Prayer. “Let them rejoice.” fol. CLXXX.

Antiphon 1. “I cried out because you heard me, O God.” P. “Incline your ear to me and hear my words.” V\. “Guard me as the apple of your eye; shelter me under the shadow of your wings.” V\. “Hear, O God, my justice; attend to my prayer. Give ear to my prayer, and not to lips of deceit.” [CLXXXII] P. “Guard me.” V\. Glory and honor. P. “Hear.”

[Col. 1185B] Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ, as above in Vespers.

Antiphon 2. “This holy man cried out, and the Lord heard him.” P. “And delivered him from all his tribulations.” V\. “His offspring will be mighty upon the earth; the generation of the upright will be blessed.” P. “And delivered him.” V\. Glory and honor. P. “And.”

Prayer. Arm our mouth, Lord, for the duty of proclaiming the truth. You made the mouth of your Hippolytus, though struck, invincible; as his confession deserved glory, so may our supplication deserve to be heard for pardon. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 3. “Behold, my discerning servant will be exalted and lifted up.” P. “And I will receive him.” V\. [Col. 1185C] “For my hand will help him, and my arm will strengthen him.” P. “And I will.” V\. Glory and honor. P. “And.”

Prayer. Christ the almighty Lord, who, while your holy martyr Hippolytus was dragged by the ferocity of horses over the points of thorns, placed him in the starry realms, carried by angelic hands: restore to the heavenly homeland, by the transport of your assisting grace, the substance of our nature, which wanton lust, in the manner of unbridled and most savage hoofed beasts, tears apart by dragging it over its spurs. Since we are weighed down by the burden of sins and cannot rise upward, let us be raised by the favors of your mercy. R\. Amen.

Through.

R\. “I invoked the Most High, the Powerful One, and he overcame my ministers; for he made me steadfast against enemies and shattered the mutterings of their malice.” P. “The mighty Lord remained with me forever.” V\. “The Lord established my feet upon a rock and directed my steps.” P. “The Lord.” V\. Glory and honor. P. “The Lord.”

Prayer. Holy martyr Hippolytus, renowned for the titles of your virtues and glorious through the abundance of your praises, stand beside us as we pray and offer our prayers to the divine hearing, so that your passion may provide us the remedy we seek, since it offered a marvelous example of striving. R\. Amen.

Through.

In Lauds.

For the Canticle. Antiphon. “The throne of glory.” Canticle. “Confirmed.” For the Benedictus. Antiphon. “The blessing of the Lord.” Canticle. “Blessed are you.” Sonus. “Seven times a day.” Lauda. “Praise.” Psalm CXLVIII. Prophecy. “If the just man.” fol. 53. Hymn. “The celebrated feasts are here, O peoples.” See in the preceding Vespers. And Supplication. “Let us pray.”

Chapters. After the pitch-black chaos of dark night, the dawn that precedes Phoebus now rises with pure light, clothed in a milk-white robe; it borders the limits of monstrous sleep and displays the beginnings of returning light. Therefore, immense Power of lofty light, our frailty asks you in every way: mindful of holy Hippolytus, once slaughtered for you, stand graciously and kindly beside us today; and just as you granted him endurance to undergo danger, so grant us strength to overcome the filthy stain of sin.

[Col. 1186B] Our Father. Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

Lauda. “On the psaltery and lyre I will sing”: P. “On the ten-stringed instrument there is sweet sound”: Alleluia. V\. “Sing to the Lord a new song, for he has done marvelous things.” P. “On the ten-stringed.” V\. Glory and honor. P. “On the ten-stringed.”

Benediction. “Of the martyr Hippolytus.” In the preceding Vespers.

FIFTEENTH DAY. ON THE FEAST OF THE ASSUMPTION OF BLESSED MARY.

At Vespers.

Lauda. “Virgin of Israel, adorn yourself with your drums,” P. “And go forth in the choir of those who sing psalms.” V\. “Blessed are you, O Queen, who look forth like light.” P. “And go forth.”

May the Lord be present. R\. And with your spirit.

Sonus. “May the Lord God of heaven bless you; the honor of David’s kingdom is in your hand.” P. “And the sons of many nations will worship before you.” Alleluia. V\. “Hear, daughter of Zion, for you have been exalted, and your face shines in the temple of God; the Sun of justice will rise at your entrance.” P. “And they will worship.”

May the Lord be present. R\. And with your spirit.

[CCLXXXIII] Antiphon. “Blessed are you by the Most High God above all women.” P. “Therefore your praise will not depart from the mouths of human beings forever.” V\. “He will not let your foot be moved, nor will he who guards you sleep.” P. “Therefore.” V\. Glory and honor. P. “Therefore.”

May the Lord be present. R\. And with your spirit.

Lauda. Alleluia. “Rejoice, daughter of Zion; be glad and exult with all your heart, daughter of Jerusalem.” P. “For the King of Israel, the Lord, has taken away your enemies.” Alleluia, alleluia. V\. “Praise the Lord, Jerusalem; praise your God, Zion.” P. “For.” V\. Glory and honor. P. “For.”

Hymn.

O sacred glory of virgins,

whom the Virgin bears as her only one,

and whom holy virgins,

the nourishing ladies, follow.

You made this virginal dwelling

a chariot,

in which, with troops of virgins,

the preeminent head shines.

This earthly temple

the heavenly God fashioned,

from whom the redeemed world stands,

and all Tartarus.

You made Mother and Disciple

like one another at their departure,

as a prodigy,

for the sake of virginal glory.

When the tomb received

their bodies according to its own law,

from there they were divinely raised

to where they behold the Son.

Nor can it in any way be believed

that, with such a Son,

the sacred flesh of the Mother

could perish and dissolve in decay.

[Col. 1187B] And even if sleep came upon her,

and she lay hidden in the earth’s hollow,

how was she taken up from there,

and afterward given to heaven?

He who thus received the Virgin,

Queen of heaven and earth,

made her share in the company of angels

in the lofty citadel.

The day on which she is taken away,

Mother of all nations,

on which she seeks the innermost heaven,

[lacuna]

There, most holy Virgin,

carry our prayers,

where you have crossed over in the glory

of renowned Assumption.

Through your Only-Begotten,

whom you bore as Lord,

may we seek heaven’s bosom

for all ages without end.

Amen.

Supplication. Let us pray with every supplication to the Redeemer of the world, our Lord Jesus Christ, that he may mercifully deem us justified by his grace and through the intercession of the Assumption of Holy Mary, his Virgin Mother. R\. Grant this, eternal almighty God.

Kyrie eleison. R\. Christe eleison. Kyrie eleison.

Chapters. O undefiled gift, O truly virginal glory! O work dedicated to sacred offspring, and sacred Virgin Mary, fittingly filled with the sevenfold gift, and reward of every chastity! Your conception is a mystery, your manifestation a privilege, and your giving birth produces salvation and joy. Neither any marital union, nor any lascivious touch, nor any stubborn sin ever defiled you. Carry now the prayers of true believers there, where, taken up, you remain amid the garlands of the saints and virgins. There, we ask, be our refuge, where you deserved to be raised divinely from earthly things to the height of heaven. And just as through this whole of yours you were worthy to obtain the undivided whole, so may we, through our half-alive double, deserve to be revived in both respects through Christ our Lord, by whose teaching we have learned:

[Col. 1188A] Our Father. Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

Benediction. May Christ the Lord, who once mercifully took up his Mother from below, wherever he wished, deem us, whom he mercifully created, always transported to himself in mind. R\. Amen. And just as the Son born from her powerfully offered light to the world, so, enlightened in heart through her, may we deserve to ascend to the heavenly seat above. R\. Amen. And just as she rejoices in presenting herself through her Assumption among the hosts of the heavenly army, so may we, cleansed from the sorrow of all our sins, eventually deserve to be raised more blessedly into the heavenly kingdoms. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

[CCLXXXIV] Lauda. “My branches are branches of honor and grace”: Alleluia. P. “I bore fruit like a vine, with the sweetness of fragrance.” Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V\. “But I, like a fruitful olive tree in the house of the Lord, will hope in the mercy of my God forever and ever.” P. “I bore fruit like.” V\. Glory and honor. P. “I bore fruit like.”

Prayer. This is that glorious virgin Mary, Lord God, who today is recognized as taken up above from the valley of tears and the desert of the world, resting upon your beloved Only-Begotten and her Son in an indescribable place. A kind of seal and precious necklace of this is revealed when we confess that the Lord’s body, of one nature—that of this undefiled Mother—has been assumed by the Divinity. Therefore we ask you, ineffable and supreme God, that our intention may be extended there, where today this worthy and most blessed Virgin, our intercessor, has gone before us through her strong love. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

At Matins.

Antiphon. “My lips.” fol. CLXXX. Psalm L.

Prayer. May our lips rejoice in you, Lord, with the proclamation of truth, praising the true Assumption of undefiled Mary the Mother; and, since she deserved by your power to be taken up from the earth and raised divinely to the heavenly seats, may we through her favor deserve to be rescued here from all sins and mercifully led there into the shining choirs of the blessed. R\. Amen.

Through.

Antiphon 1. “In love.” fol. CLXXX. Prayer. “This is she.” In the preceding Vespers.

Antiphon 2. “Most prudent Virgin.” fol. CLXXX.

[Col. 1188D] Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ, who today took Mary, the glorious Queen of heaven, from the worldly desert and sorrowful Egypt, and willed her to be with you in the heavenly seat, beautiful as the moon and chosen as the sun: grant that we may nowhere be insolently burned by the sun’s heat during the day, nor indecently scorched by the moon’s fires at night, so that, renewed from the sorrow of both soul and body, we may through the Assumption of your Mother be led more blessedly to the place where she has gone before us. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 3. “In the congregation of the saints is my inheritance. I have been exalted like a cedar in Lebanon.” P. “And like a cypress in the mountains of Hermon, I have been raised.” V\. [Col. 1189A] “But I, like a fruitful olive tree in the house of the Lord, will hope in the mercy of my God forever and ever.” P. “And like.” V\. Glory and honor. P. “And like.”

Prayer. Behold, Lord: just as the cedar exalted today in heaven, the glorious Virgin Mary remains there, so, like a beautiful olive tree, she bestows the oil of wisdom upon foolish minds, and, like a fruit-bearing vine, sends the sweetness of a good life forth upon the earth. Therefore we ask that, enriched on earth through her intercession by the fragrance of virtues, we may entirely reject the stench of wanton flesh, so that we may glory before you without end in the merits of good works. R\. Amen.

Through.

R\. A voice came from heaven to her, saying: “Come, receive the crown which I promised you from the beginning; my angels will receive you.” P. “And they will lead you into that holy city, Jerusalem.” V\. “For he has commanded his angels concerning you, to guard you in all your ways; they will carry you in their hands.” P. “And they will lead you.” V\. Glory and honor. P. “And they will lead you.”

## Prayer

Virgin of Christ, Mary, whose sacred procession today remained wondrous in the heavenly seat among the shadowy lilies—that is, above the ranks of virgins: we ask that, through your holy favor, future rest may be granted to us unworthy ones, whereby you were able to be assumed in the glory of so great a miracle; so that we may deserve to hear with the ear of the heart that word of the Lord which, as he assumed you into the heights, said: “Ascend.” There, indeed, may we receive eternal rest with all the saints, where we believe that you obtained from the Lord the blessing of the most sincere faith. R. Amen.

### At Lauds

For the Canticle. Antiphon. “Blessed be the Lord.” Canticle. “Rejoicing.” At the Benedictus. Antiphon. “Daughter of Zion.” Canticle. “Blessed.” Sonus. “The Lord from heaven.” Seek it in the preceding Vespers. Lauda. “Praise the Lord from the heavens.”

[CCLXXXV] Reading from the book of the Song of Songs (Chapter I).

R. Thanks be to God.

O beautiful virgin of God among women, go forth and follow after the footsteps of your flocks. I have likened you, my beloved. How beautiful are your cheeks, like a tower. Behold, you are beautiful, my beloved; behold, you are beautiful; your eyes are like those of doves.

(Chapter II.) Arise, hasten, my beloved, and come. For winter has already passed and departed. The flowers have appeared on the earth. Arise, show me your face, and let your voice sound in my ears; for your voice is sweet and your face lovely.

(Chapter III.) Who is this who comes up over the wilderness like little branches of smoke from the aromatics of myrrh and incense and every kind of fragrant powder?

(Chapter IV.) How beautiful you are! Your eyes are like those of doves, apart from what lies hidden within, like the tower of David. For you are altogether beautiful, and there is no blemish in you. Come from Lebanon, my bride; come from Lebanon, and you will be crowned. An enclosed garden is my sister, my bride; an enclosed garden, a sealed fountain. Your shoots are a paradise full of pomegranates, with the fruits of apple trees.

(Chapter VI.) One is my dove, my perfect one; she alone is her mother’s queen, chosen by her who bore her. The daughters of Jerusalem saw her and called her most blessed; queens and concubines praised her. Who is this who comes forth like the rising dawn, beautiful as the moon, chosen as the sun, terrible as an army set in ordered ranks?

(Chapter VIII.) Who is this who comes up from the wilderness, abounding in delights, having given birth upon her beloved? Set me as a seal upon your heart and as a necklace upon your arm; as a seal upon your arm. And the true love of God remains. R. Amen.

## Hymn

Let us sing the hymn of the Virgin Mary  
with the angels,  
whom Christ, the Son of God,  
sanctified in the womb.

Let us celebrate her Assumption  
with the angels,  
with rest granted to us,  
our wicked enemies removed.

The mother who refused a man,  
the mother who was worthy of Christ;  
a virgin before childbirth;  
a virgin who shone forth after childbirth.

Now Christ, begotten of God,  
not seizing anything from God,  
assuming the form of a servant,  
joins himself to a servant’s body.

Nor did he, departing, break the weary Virgin’s temple-courts;  
rather, he left closed the enclosure  
that he had found closed.

O truly sacred vessel,  
whose glory is military glory,  
whom neither heaven nor earth can contain—  
yet the womb of the Virgin can contain him!

But we hasten to you  
and beseech you, gracious Mother:  
rescue us from the nations  
by your blessed prayers.

Through your Only-Begotten,  
whom you gave birth to as Lord,  
may we seek heaven’s embrace  
through all the ages of eternity.

Amen.

Supplication. Let us pray, as above.

## Chapters

With our morning prayers we earnestly beseech you, most merciful Lord: just as the illustrious and most glorious Virgin Mary today attained the heavenly seat through the honor of virginity, so may we, through the merit of that most acceptable favor, deserve to rejoice with you in the heavenly kingdoms.

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” fol. 2.

Lauda. “My branches.” Blessing. “Christ the Lord.” Seek them in the preceding Vespers.

At the end of Vespers, everything is to be said as in the first Vespers, except for the Chapters and the Blessing.

[Col. 1191A] Chapters. Lord Jesus Christ, who so honored the Virgin Mother that, through the grace of the Assumption, you made her before you an incomparable intercessor for us: we unworthy ones ask for the mercy of your divinity, so that, through the intercession of that most blessed Mother, whom today you made celibate in the heavenly kingdoms, cleansed from every contamination, we may dare to cry out and say:

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” fol. 2.

Blessing. At the prayer of the sacred Virgin Mary, may your merits stand firmly before Christ, and may your sins be utterly abolished. R. Amen. And just as she rejoices today in the heavenly seat with the holy angels, so may you rejoice in having obtained the paradise of eternal blessedness. R. Amen. May you therefore depart from here whole and sound in soul and body and happily and worthily reach that seat, from which, by his mercy, you may in no way be separated. R. Amen.

Through.

# THE TWENTY-FOURTH DAY. ON THE FEAST OF SAINT BARTHOLOMEW THE APOSTLE

## At Vespers

Lauda. “My soul has hoped.” Sonus. “Make with me, O God, a sign for good.”

Antiphon. “The eye of God looked upon the just.” fol. CLIX.

Lauda. “The just man shall be in everlasting remembrance. Alleluia.” P. “He shall not fear evil report. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.” V. “Blessed is the man who fears the Lord; he greatly delights in his commandments.” P. “He shall not fear evil report.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “He shall not fear evil report.”

## Hymn

Offspring of the eternal Father, and glorious equal  
of him whom you are known to be,  
kindly Spirit, holding certain power  
over all things throughout the ages:

Behold Bartholomew, your disciple,  
holy and youthful from within,  
one of the Apostles, wondrous by his lot;  
now behold, he shines exalted in heaven.

His consecrated feasts now appear;  
now, by their everlasting gift,  
may it certainly refresh the peoples  
and also imbue them  
with strength to despise the fleeting world.

By his prayer, O exalted Pontiff,  
we, your weak little servants, beseech you:  
forgive offenses and grant gifts;  
may your grace be with your wretched servants.

Bartholomew, martyr and Apostle,  
deign to be our patron  
through all ages, and favor us as we bow;  
make us, your little servants, blessed.

May grace, by your prayer, favor those  
whom you see abundantly  
to have given themselves to you as suppliants  
each year, as the seasons of the passing world flow on.

To you, Christ, be praise through all things;  
to the eternal Father be power;  
to the one who rules all ages,  
may glory likewise be given forever.

Amen.

Supplication. Let us pray, with the name changed, fol. CLXXXVII.

[Col. 1192A] Chapters. Christ, Son of God, power of God and wisdom of God, who deigned to be born through the womb of the Virgin as true invisible God and appeared in the flesh as true visible man: through the intercession of your holy Apostle and Martyr Bartholomew, may we be washed from the guilt of sins and deserve to enter the promised land, namely, that blessed perfection; so that through you—who strengthened that same martyr of yours, the Apostle Bartholomew, whose solemnity today we devoutly celebrate for the praise of your name and the manifestation of your divinity, with many protections and aids of the holy angels, and whose inmost being you suffused with the warmth of the Holy Spirit—you may cause us to escape unharmed from the snares of the enemy.

Just as he received from you the power to place his feet upon serpents and scorpions and upon all the strength of the enemy, so may we also receive invincible help from your holy power, so that we may trample down and extinguish the little king (*regulus*) and basilisk, which sometimes, through our negligence, reign over us in the kingdom of sin. Thus, with pure heart and cleansed lips, may we deserve to serve you most worthily on earth.

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” fol. 2.

[Col. 1192C] Blessing. May Christ the Lord, who through his martyr, the Apostle Bartholomew, performed a notable miracle by converting both a king and a people to faith in his name, grant you attainment of the kingdom of heaven. R. Amen. And may he who through him revealed the cunning of the Devil to the assembled peoples, through his intervention assist you in the congregation of his saints. R. Amen. And through this same Apostle Bartholomew, who rejected gold and jewels as ornaments as though they were mud, may Christ the Lord cause you to ascend above, where his unending dominion reigns over every creature. R. Amen.

Lauda. “I shall love him.” fol. CLVI.

Oration. Immense and glorious God, whom we worship in the sufferings of the martyrs, venerate in the solemnities of the blessed, and praise together with those who conquer in the struggles: attend to the prayers of those who supplicate through the intercession of your martyr, the Apostle Bartholomew. We fear you as terrible on account of our offenses; may you, entreated by his prayers, find us pleasing in your mercy. R. Amen. Through mercy.

## At Matins

[Col. 1192D]

Antiphon. “Open my lips.” Psalm L. Oration. “May they rejoice, O Lord.” fol. CLXXX.

Antiphon 1. “I shall place a crown of glory upon his head,” says the Lord, “and I shall clothe him in a white robe.” P. “For he kept my commandments, and for my name his blood was poured out upon the earth.” V. “For my truth and my mercy are with him, and in my name his horn shall be exalted.” P. “For he kept.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “For he kept.”

[Col. 1193A] Oration. Grant us, Lord, wisdom, by which both the sluggishness of our foolishness may be taken away and the glory of blessedness bestowed; so that, while you clothe your martyr, the Apostle Bartholomew, in the robe of honor, you may mercifully wash away in us, through his intercession, the garment of Baptism which we have stained by sinning; and when that holy martyr of yours is crowned among the vessels of virtue, may we be cleansed from the pollution of sins. R. Amen.

Antiphon 2. “The Lord crowned him, blessed him, and loved him.” P. “And he will set him over many gifts.” V. “He who walks without blemish and practices righteousness, who speaks truth in his heart.” P. “And he will set him over.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “And he will set him over.”

Oration. Almighty God, we pray that you may make us, through the merits of your martyr, the Apostle Bartholomew, and of all the saints, companions in faith, equal in devotion, strong in suffering, like them, and equal to the blessed in the resurrection. R. Amen.

[Col. 1193B] Antiphon 3. “I have fought the good fight; I have finished the course.” P. “From now on the crown of righteousness is laid up for me.” V. “For I kept the ways of the Lord and did not act wickedly against my God.” P. “From now on.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “From now on.”

Oration. Immense and glorious God. Seek it above in the preceding Vespers.

Responsory. “I am the light.” fol. CLVIII.

### At Lauds

For the Canticle. Antiphon. “You alone are Lord, for there is no other; nor is there any just one besides you, our God.”

Canticle. “My heart has been confirmed.”

At the Benedictus. Antiphon. “The blessing of the Lord.” Canticle. “Blessed are you.”

Sonus. “Seven times a day.” Lauda. “Praise the Lord.” Psalm CXLVIII. Prophecy. “If the just man.” fol. 53. Hymn. “Offspring of the eternal Father.” Seek it in the preceding Vespers. Supplication. “Let us pray to the Redeemer.”

[Col. 1193C] Chapters.

Behold, Lord, the annual feast of your Apostle and martyr Bartholomew is received for celebration; it summons the entire body of the Catholic people to rejoicing, while through his miracles it has now spread throughout the whole world. Therefore we ask your abundant power, almighty God: since you gave him through the Holy Spirit power to command demons, do not take away from us the grace of your mercy as we run to you with humble devotion in his honor. May we, who are burdened by sins and now celebrate his venerable feast, through his merits come blessed to the heavenly kingdom; and if we do not deserve to be justified by our own merits, may we through his patronage deserve to be joined forever to your saints.

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” fol. 2.

[Col. 1193D] Lauda. “I shall love him with my whole being.” Seek it in the preceding Vespers. Blessing. “Christ the Lord, who through the martyr,” as above.

# THE TWENTY-FIFTH DAY. ON THE FEAST OF SAINT GENESIUS

## At Vespers

Lauda. “My soul has hoped.” fol. CLVI. Sonus. “Bless the Lord, O my soul.” fol. CLX. Antiphon. “Your holy one.” Seek it under Saint Hippolytus. Lauda. “The Lord dealt well with him.” fol. CLXI.

## Hymn

[Col. 1194A]

O Lord, creator of all things,  
continually apply the plectrum  
to the strings of my throat,  
granting me to unfold with zeal  
the struggle of your glorious athlete.

[CCLXXXVIII] For the innermost heart greatly desires  
to bring forth the conspicuous deeds  
and mighty accomplishments  
of the warrior soldier,  
as well as your excellent gifts.

That young man Genesius, therefore,  
an outstanding citizen of the town of Arles,  
passing through the first little flower  
of youthful age,  
obeyed the order imposed upon him.

While he was an imperial secretary  
and was shining forth,  
writing the public commands on tablets,  
he was suddenly inspired by a heavenly gift  
through which he crowned his devout vows.

[Col. 1194B] At once he rejected the impious office  
and refused to imprint his hand upon the wax,  
desiring to become a citizen  
of the heavenly life  
in vows and conduct.

After the Gospel message thundered forth,  
seeking various hiding places far and wide,  
he secretly withdrew into secluded places,  
overcome by great terror.

When a powerful crowd of soldiers sought him  
and nowhere found him as it wished,  
the judge then, roaring with wide-open jaws,  
shouted: “Take up the sword! Hurry,  
strike with swift steps;  
when the fugitive is found, strike him down—  
the man who dared to despise our commands  
and does not worship the sacred gods.”

[Col. 1194C] When report of this reached the martyr’s ears,  
he sought the Rhône in fervent spirit,  
that, washed in its waters, he might no longer recognize himself [that is, his former self], and that his defilement might be washed away.

Returning from there brighter than gold,  
he was found and struck down violently  
at the throat;  
at once he was joined to the ranks of heaven,  
his head adorned with laurel.

[Col. 1194D] Therefore, almighty One, we earnestly ask: receive kindly the vows of the faithful who pray, you yourself being the witness; and forgive their offense.

May the heap of guilt be utterly overthrown;  
may fitting grace continually increase;  
so that, made pure through the merits of the saints,  
vengeance may depart far away.

May there be constant glory  
to the triune Lord,  
everlasting kingdom and power,
