who by his accustomed might rules all things,  
mercifully sustaining what he has created.

Amen.

Supplication. Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world, as above.

[Col. 1195A] Chapters. Only-begotten Son of God, who crowned your most blessed athlete Genesius, as he passed through the first flower of youth, with the title of a double victory: when, by avoiding the persecutor’s rage, you adorned him with the sacred washing of baptism as he entered the waters of the Rhône, and when, after abandoning the office of secretary that he held, you consecrated him as a true follower of yours—grant that, supported by his intercession, we may walk unharmed along the way of this world and become worthy imitators of your footsteps. May we, not darkened by any stench of vices, complete the course of life in peace, like this soldier of yours, and, with him as our patron, deserve to reach your glorious brightness.

Our Father. “And do not.” “Delivered from evil.” fol. 2.

[Col. 1195B] Blessing. May Christ the Lord, who did not allow the most blessed Genesius, crossing the bed of the Rhône, to be impeded by any [uncertain: *aeribus*] of algae, himself loosen your feet from the bonds of crimes and direct them along the paths of his commandments. R. Amen. And may he who caused him, while still in the earliest years of life, to turn away from the allurements of the executioners and made him share the lot of the citizens of heaven, cleanse you from every incentive of fleshly titillation. R. Amen. Thus, at the time of judgment, purified from every bond of sins and made pure, may you deserve with him to receive a place of eternal peace. R. Amen.

Through his mercy.

Lauda. “Blessed is the man who fears the Lord. Alleluia.” P. “He greatly delights in his commandments. Alleluia, alleluia.” V. “His offspring shall be mighty upon the earth; the generation of the upright shall be blessed.” P. “He greatly delights in his commandments.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “He greatly delights in his commandments.”

[Col. 1195C] Oration. Grant us, God, the continual patronage of your most blessed martyr Genesius, so that we may also deserve to attain his splendid example; and, experiencing him as our most devoted helper, may we follow him most courageously in battle. R. Amen.

Through.

## At Matins

Antiphon. “Open my lips.” Psalm 50. Oration. “May they rejoice, O Lord.” fol. CLXXX.

Antiphon 1. “I cried out, for you heard me, O God; incline your ear to me and hear my words.” P. “Guard me as the apple of the eye; protect me under the shadow of your wings.” V. “Hear, O God, my justice; attend to my supplication. Give ear to my prayer, and not to deceitful lips.” P. “Guard me.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “Guard me.”

[Col. 1195D] [CCLXXXIX] Oration. “Grant us,” in the preceding Vespers.

Antiphon. “This holy man cried out, and the Lord heard him.” P. “And he delivered him from all his tribulations.” V. “Thus shall the man who fears the Lord be blessed.” P. “From all.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “From all.”

Oration. With your martyr Genesius preceding and praying for us, your servants, may there be in us a ready will to love you, Lord, so that weakness of the flesh may hinder us in nothing. Thus, taught by him, may the desire of the world be trampled down by us, so that, through his intercession, we may attain the victory of charity. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

[Col. 1196A] Antiphon 2. “Behold, my servant shall understand; he shall be exalted and lifted up.” P. “And I shall receive him.” V. “For my hand shall help him, and my arm shall strengthen him.” P. “And I shall receive him.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “And I shall.”

Oration. Make us, Lord, followers of your most blessed martyr Genesius, so that, armed with his intercession, we may reject the deceits of demons; instructed by his patronage, may we see the good things in the land of the living. R. Amen.

Through.

R. I called upon the Most High, the Powerful One, and he defeated my enemies, because he made me steadfast against my foes and broke the murmurs of their malice. The strong Lord remained with me. P. Forever. V. The Lord set my feet upon a rock and directed my steps. P. Forever. V. Glory and honor to the Father. P. Forever.

[Col. 1196B] Oration. Almighty Lord, who permitted your most blessed martyr Genesius to be tested, not overwhelmed, by the goads of suffering and the waves of threatening floods—when neither punishment overcame him as he struggled, nor the engulfing water suppressed him: because you were present with him there so that he would not be conquered by torments, and here you granted that he be carried by the waves contrary to nature—grant faith to all through such great miracles, so that petitions may be granted to all who most devoutly celebrate the vows. R. Amen.

Through.

Antiphon. “Wisdom delivered the just man from the impious who were perishing and clothed him with righteousness as a breastplate and with the helmet of salvation upon his head.” V. “Blessed is the man who fears the Lord; he greatly delights in his commandments.” P. “And clothed him.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “And clothed him.”

[Col. 1196C] Oration. Almighty God, we pray that you may make us, through the merits of your martyr Genesius and of all the saints, companions in their merits, equal in faith, vigorous in devotion, alike in suffering, and equal to the blessed in the resurrection. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon. “This man in the struggle.” fol. CLXI.

Oration. Immense and glorious God, whom we worship in the sufferings of the martyrs, venerate in the solemnities of the blessed, and praise together with those who conquer in the struggles: attend to the prayers of those who supplicate through the intercession of your glorious martyr Genesius. We fear you as terrible on account of our offenses; may you, entreated by his prayers, find us pleasing in your mercy. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

[Col. 1196D] Antiphon. “I shall place a crown of glory upon his head,” says the Lord, “and I shall clothe him in a white robe.” P. “For he kept my commandments, and for my name his blood was poured out upon the earth.” V. “And I shall place his hand upon the sea and his right hand upon the rivers.” P. “And for my name.” V. “Glory and honor to the Father.” P. “And for my name.”

Oration. God, whose honor is holiness, whom to love is salvation and to cherish is perfection: enter into our hearts. Grant that the footsteps of your glorious martyr Genesius may shine throughout your whole Church, so that the path along which you lead all our steps may bring us to life, the path that raised your martyr to the crown. R. Amen.

Through.

[Col. 1197A] Responsory. “I am the light.” fol. CLVIII.

Oration. Lord Jesus Christ, who wondrously grant both a crown of victory to this martyr of yours, Genesius, and assign him as a pillar in your temple, like a future ornament of the building, while you inspire him with the zeal to conquer for the crowning and lavish upon him an unconquered will of perseverance in suffering: grant us, after his example, an equal desire to love you and a will to conquer, so that the name of that new city, Jerusalem, may be inscribed upon our hearts. Thus, while we fix our mind’s gaze continually upon its vision, may we rejoice forever in its peace. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

[CCXC] At Lauds.

For the Canticle. Antiphon. “You alone are Lord, for there is no other; nor is there any just one besides you, nor any holy one besides our God.”

Canticle. “My heart has been confirmed.”

At the Benedictus. Antiphon. “Blessing.” Canticle. “Blessed are you, Lord.” fol. 6.

Sonus. “Bless the Lord, O my soul.” fol. CLX. Lauda. “Praise.” Psalm CXLVIII. Prophecy. “Wisdom led the just man.” fol. 56. Hymn. “O Lord, creator of all things.” Supplication. “Let us pray.” Seek it in the preceding Vespers.

[Col. 1197C] Chapters. The feast of your most renowned athlete, your martyr Genesius, is present, Lord; while fighting manfully for your name, he was violently decapitated by the sword’s edge. Therefore, with devout supplications we earnestly beseech your generous power, almighty God: through his patronage, deign so to cut away every vice from our hearts and bodies that, cleansed from the stains of sins, we may rejoice in hymns of praise to have entered the courts of heaven, which he approached through the triumph of martyrdom.

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” fol. 2.

Blessing. “Christ the Lord, who [did this] through his martyr,” in the preceding Vespers.

[Col. 1197D] At the end of Vespers, everything is to be said as in the first Vespers, except for the Chapters and the Blessing that follow.

Chapters. God, who go before those willing in faith and, by following believers, make them not to have believed in you in vain; who first went before the most blessed Genesius with the grace of sweetness before the regeneration of baptism: we humbly beseech you to let us now be preceded by your mercies, so that we may confidently cry out to you from the earth:

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” fol. 2.

[Col. 1198A] Blessing. May the grace of Christ, which went before the most blessed martyr Genesius in faith, follow you with its gift. R. Amen. And may he who by the waters of the Rhône freed him from the bond of original sin quicken you through the sacrament of this chalice. R. Amen. And may he who consecrated him from the river’s whirlpool not overthrow you in the tempest of the world. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

# THE TWENTY-SIXTH DAY. ON THE FEAST OF SAINT GERONTIUS, BISHOP

## At Vespers

Lauda. “Confession and beauty.” Sonus. “I shall confess to you, Lord.” fol. CLXIX. Antiphon. “I shall confess to you, Lord.” fol. CLXIX. Lauda. “I shall confess to you, Lord and King.” fol. CLXIX.

## Hymn

Let us sing with worthy praises  
and celebrate with our voices  
the sacred bishop of Christ,  
Gerontius the Confessor.

[Col. 1198B] He is said to have shone  
as a prophet in apostolic times  
and to have preached  
the supreme Father of the mighty Son [that is, the Father of the Son who is mighty].

While he was journeying, renowned,  
through the western region,  
at last the anger of the Gentiles  
dragged him to his passion.

But soon, at the command of the presiding authority,  
he was burdened with iron bonds  
and handed over to the executioner  
in the dreadful shadows of the prison.

[Col. 1198C] They say that, bound in chains,  
amid the pallid darkness,  
he gave his soul to heaven,  
snatched from his sacred body.

Thus now placed among  
the apostolic company,  
he rejoices in heavenly glory  
and in the glorious grace of Christ.

For, clothed in a double honor,  
he shines and gleams:  
in the title of priesthood  
and in the merit of confession.

Let glory resound to the Father,  
to Christ the Only-Begotten,  
and to the Spirit, the Paraclete,  
through ages of ages.

Amen.

Supplication. Let us pray, with the name changed, fol. CLXXXVII.

[Col. 1198D] [CCXCI] Chapters. O glorious and merciful Lord, who granted that your most blessed confessor Gerontius, Bishop, confess you greatly with his mouth, and desired to be praised by the confession of his righteous ones, so that, confessing you on earth and glorifying him in the council of the saints, you might make him rejoice: we ask for the gift of your grace, that through his prayers you may grant us to be cleansed from the pollution of sin, rescued from everlasting fires, and brought to attain the blessedness of your glory.

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” fol. 2.

[Col. 1199A] Blessing. May Christ the Lord, who caused his most blessed confessor Gerontius, Bishop, worthily to confess him before men on earth, confess you before his Father who is in heaven. R. Amen. And may he who placed upon his lips songs of confession acceptable to himself receive your confession to be rewarded. R. Amen. Thus, by confessing and praising the name of Jesus Christ forever, after the example of the most blessed confessor Gerontius, Bishop, may you deserve to be participants in heaven of the one whom you have confessed. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Lauda. “Your bones shall flourish like willows. Alleluia.” P. “Beside flowing waters. Alleluia, alleluia.” V. “He shall be like a tree planted beside the streams of waters, which shall yield its fruit in its season.” P. “Beside.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “Beside.”

[Col. 1199B] Oration. God, Son of God, whom the most blessed Bishop Gerontius confessed with his whole heart, and by honoring your name was brought to the crown: place confession in our mouths, so that it may cleanse us from guilt; so that whatever we utter in honor of your praise, we may perceive to profit us as gain of an eternal gift. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

## At Matins

Antiphon. “Open my lips.” Psalm L. Oration. “May they rejoice, O Lord.” fol. CLXXX.

Antiphon 1. “My flesh shall rest in hope.” Seek it, fol. CLXX.

[Col. 1199C] Oration. God, who made your confessor Gerontius rejoice and exult through ages of ages, so that, continually singing praise to you alone, he might offer a hymn, through whose confession he deserved to obtain fellowship with you: with devoted hearts we ask you to let our life flourish through his merits and shine, amended from evil deeds; so that we, who already deserved punishment for our crimes, may through confession and the worship of Christian faith deserve to attain future glory. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 2. “Your face.” fol. CLXXI.

Oration. You made your confessor Gerontius, Bishop, exceedingly blessed, Lord; for he confessed you with his whole heart and is shown to be conspicuous in the assembly of the righteous and the congregation. Grant us, therefore, through his merits, to be cleansed from guilt by a simple confession of the mouth and to deserve to be present in the heavenly congregation of the saints.

[Col. 1199D] R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 3. “You guarded my body.” fol. CLXXI. Oration. “God, Son of God.” Seek above in the preceding Vespers. Responsory. “Behold, Lord, with his whole heart.” fol. CLXXI.

Oration. Behold, Lord, your confessor Gerontius, Bishop, confesses and believes you alone with his whole heart, while he declares the perfect love of your faith and proclaims your wonders with devoted mouth. Therefore make us rejoice and exult in you continually and visibly, so that after our trials we may have rest in you, in whom he deserved to find his reward after his confession. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

## At Lauds

[Col. 1200A]

For the Canticle. Antiphon. “I shall confess to you, Lord.” Canticle. “I shall confess to you, Lord and King.” At the Benedictus. Antiphon. “The blessing of the Lord.” Canticle. “Blessed are you, Lord.” Sonus. “In the sight of the angels.” Lauda. “Alleluia. His confession.” Prophecy. “Behold my servant.” Seek it, fol. CLXXII. Hymn. “The sacred bishop of Christ.” Supplication. “Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world, the Lord.” Seek it in the preceding Vespers.

[Col. 1200B] Chapters. God, whom the tongue of the faithful praises together in confession and whom the devotion of confessors abundantly exalts: grant us, through the intercession of your confessor Gerontius, Bishop, to obtain what we ask and escape what we fear. For you are our God, and we shall confess to you; may we also devoutly exalt you as God in our hearts. Therefore make us cling to you unceasingly in deed and in word alike, you who made us know the truth of the Christian faith.

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” fol. 2.

Lauda. “Your bones shall flourish like willows.” Blessing. “Christ the Lord, who…” Seek it in the preceding Vespers.

[Col. 1200C] At the end of Vespers, everything is to be said as in the first Vespers, except for the Chapters and the Blessing that follow.

Chapters. You made your confessor Gerontius, Bishop, exceedingly blessed, Lord; for he confessed you with his whole heart and is shown to be conspicuous in the assembly of the righteous and the congregation. Grant us, therefore, through his merits, to be cleansed from guilt by a simple confession of the mouth and to deserve to be present in the heavenly congregation of the saints.

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” fol. 2.

Blessing. May the Lord Jesus Christ, who is the reward of confessors, enrich you through the intercession of his confessor Gerontius with the gift of his holy confession. R. Amen. May he grant you the desire to confess him, who bestowed upon that same man the reward of confession. R. Amen. Thus, by truly imitating the example of so great a Confessor, may you deserve to reach the heavenly promise. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

# THE TWENTY-EIGHTH DAY. ON THE FEAST OF SAINT AUGUSTINE, BISHOP AND DOCTOR

[Col. 1200D]

Everything is to be said for one Confessor and Bishop, fol. CLXIX, except the

## Hymn

Light, God Christ, overflowing mercy,  
who, loving Augustine your prophet,  
restored from heresy,  
make him rightly  
your suitable disciple.

Through his favor remove deceit from here,  
preserve the homeland, govern the peoples;  
may every quarrel be absent,  
and may the grace of peace abound  
among the redeemed.

May charity restore the bond  
of those who have been cut off;  
may anger be far away,  
may ruin depart;  
may disasters, famine, sickness,  
and every harmful thing withdraw.

[Col. 1201A] May the clergy shine  
with gleaming doctrine;  
may the bishop retain  
the lofty summit,  
and, cleansed of stain, may he be pleasing thereafter through good works.

May everlasting praise  
resound for you with jubilation,  
simple Trinity and one Divinity,  
you who, creating all things,  
are believed to be the maker  
in heaven.

Amen.

# FEASTS OF SEPTEMBER

A fast is observed for three days before the feast of Saint Cyprian. If you wish to recite it, seek fol. [Col. 1201B] 431.

# THE FOURTEENTH DAY. ON THE FEAST OF SAINT CYPRIAN, BISHOP

## At Vespers

Lauda. “Glory and honor.”

Sonus. “Make with me.” Seek fol. CLIX.

Antiphon. “You placed upon his head, Lord, a crown of precious stone.” P. “You will place glory and great beauty upon him.” V. “He asked for life, and you gave him length of days forever and through ages of ages.” P. “You will place glory and great beauty.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “You will place glory.”

The Lord be always present. R. And with you.

Lauda. “Alleluia. Everyone who conquers I shall make sit upon the throne of my Father. Alleluia.” P. “Just as I also conquered and sit upon it. Alleluia, alleluia.” V. “Blessed is he who understands concerning the needy and the poor; on the evil day the Lord will deliver him.” P. “Just as.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “Just as.”

## Hymn

You, Cyprian, Bishop,  
teacher of the city of Tascia,  
luminous and effective torch,  
teaching by word and by blood.

You are a martyr and devout teacher,  
renowned in both doctrines:  
you pour words into the foolish  
and strengthen the learned by examples.

That heavenly Spirit  
who presided in the prophets  
watered you from heaven,  
filled you, guided you, and drenched you.

[Col. 1201D] [CCXCIII] Hence, from the clear fountain of lights,  
you nourish the minds of the faithful;  
you traverse trackless regions,  
refreshing the palate with nourishment.

You distribute the glory of suffering at the price offered,  
purchasing death with its reward,  
when the executioner struck you.

Thus, teaching what is true,  
you pour out blessed blood;  
you enrich Africa with your blood  
and teach Hesperia by your word.

[Col. 1202A] You are a devout Teacher on earth,  
a Martyr in the heavens.  
Through prayer, make us hold fast  
to what you preached as doctrine.

To God the Father be glory,  
and to his only Son,  
with the Spirit, the Paraclete,  
who reigns through every age.

Amen.

Supplication. Let us pray, with the name changed, as above.

[Col. 1202B] Chapters. O glory of the world, O unique teacher, catholic master of truth, guide of the Catholic Church, most holy martyr Cyprian! You are shown to be eminent in proclaiming Christ both by voice and by blood, gracious in speech and illustrious in suffering: while you practice what you teach and leave to posterity, by teaching, what you practice; admirable and renowned in both respects; recognized both as a wondrous Teacher and as a glorious martyr; shining in the world through doctrine and rejoicing in heaven over the blood poured out.

We ask and entreat you: rule us, cherish us, and instruct us always through both your intercessions and your teachings. Instruct the ignorant by your mouth; protect the weak by your prayers; teach by your words what we should do; obtain by your merits the means by which we may enter. From there, water our ignorance with words; here, continually cherish our weakness with your intercessions. Thus, through the one God in perfect Trinity, whom you proclaimed both by doctrine and by blood, may we here drink more gladly the fruit of your words and, after our passage, be filled with the joys of your merits through him who taught us to pray and say:

[Col. 1202C] Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” fol. 2.

Blessing. May Christ the Lord, who made the most blessed Cyprian a ruler of his Church, renowned for his teaching office and illustrious as a Martyr, fill you both with the grace of holy teaching and with the sweetness of the abundance of his love. R. Amen. May you receive from the Martyr’s words a complete correction of life, and in his examples attain what will make you heirs in the heavenly kingdoms. R. Amen. Thus, through his teaching may the rust of sins flee from you, and through his intercession may eternal life be granted to you. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

[Col. 1202D] Lauda. “Blessed is the man who fears the Lord. Alleluia.” P. “He greatly delights in his commandments. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.” V. “His offspring shall be mighty upon the earth; the generation of the upright shall be blessed.” P. “He greatly delights in his commandments.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “He greatly delights in his commandments.”

Prayer. We render to you, eternal Lord, the thanks that are owed, and to Jesus Christ our Lord, in whose likeness the most blessed Cyprian, while offering the victim, was himself the victim; while choosing the priesthood, he devotedly fulfilled martyrdom. Therefore, O Most High God, may he who deserved to undergo martyrdom after the priesthood obtain from you forgiveness for the wretched after their sin. R\. Amen.

Through.

## At Matins

[Col. 1203A]

Antiphon. “My lips—” Psalm 50. Prayer. “Let them rejoice, O Lord.” fol. CLXXX

### Antiphon 1

“Man of God, the Lord has shown you the mystery: for he saw your great perseverance.”

P. “Because you were deeply saddened on account of his people, and you prayed for Israel.”

V\. “May he not allow your foot to be moved; nor will he who guards you sleep.”

P. “Because.”

V\. “Glory and honor.”

P. “Because.”

Prayer. “We render to you, O eternal Lord.” Seek it in the preceding Vespers.

### Antiphon 2

“This man accomplished everything that God had commanded him, and he said to him: ‘Enter into my rest.’”

P. “Because I chose you as righteous before me from among all the nations.”

V\. “Blessed is the man who fears the Lord; [Col. 1203B] he greatly desires his commandments.”

P. “Because you—”

V\. “Glory and honor to the Father.”

P. “Because you—”

Prayer. We beseech you, almighty God, by the eternal name of your power, that you make us companions, equal in faith, vigorous in devotion, like in suffering, and equal in the resurrection of the blessed, through the merits of your martyr Cyprian the Bishop and of all the Saints. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

### Antiphon 3

“This man was greatly honored, and God shattered his enemies’ hearts, [CCXCIV] and he hastened into the house of the Lord his God with a perfect heart.”

P. “And all saw what God made manifest through him.”

V\. “Great is his glory in your salvation; you will place glory and great splendor upon [Col. 1203C] him.”

P. “And they saw.”

V\. “Glory and honor.”

P. “And they saw.”

Prayer. O immensely glorious God, whom we worship in the sufferings of the martyrs, venerate in the solemnities of the blessed, and praise together in the contests of the victorious: attend to the prayers of those who entreat you through the intercession of your martyr Cyprian the Bishop, so that although we fear you as terrible because of our offenses, once entreated by his prayers we may find you favorable in mercy. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

R\. “The lips of the priest guard knowledge, and they seek the law from his mouth, because he is the angel of the Lord.”

P. “The law of truth is in his mouth, and wickedness was not [Col. 1203D] found upon his lips; he walked directing his way in peace, and turned many away from iniquity.”

V\. “The priest who utters justice from his mouth and announces truth to those who seek him: for he is the angel of almighty God.”

P. “The law.”

V\. “Glory and honor.”

P. “The law.”

Prayer. O God, you so filled the mouth of the most blessed martyr Cyprian the Bishop with an abundance of wisdom that, appearing surrounded by a diversity of virtues and radiant with joy and beauty, you showed him glorious with heavenly splendor; so that, while guarding knowledge with his lips, you might seek the law from his mouth. Extend to our mouth the light of knowledge and the perfection of true wisdom, so that, just as he turned many from iniquity to you, you may command us also to turn perpetually and rejoice. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

## At Lauds

[Col. 1204A]

For the Canticle. Antiphon. “Throne of glory.” Canticle. “It has been confirmed—” fol. 55. For the Benedictus. Antiphon. “The blessing of the Lord hastens as the reward of the righteous.” Canticle. “Blessed are you.” fol. 6.

Sono. Alleluia. “I will sing your power, O Lord.” Alleluia. V\. Alleluia. “My Savior, to you I will sing psalms, because you are my God, my protector and refuge in the day of my distress.” Alleluia.

Lauda. “Praise the Lord from the heavens, alleluia; praise him in the heights, alleluia.” Psalm 148.

Reading from the Book of Ecclesiasticus of Solomon (chapter 50).

R\. Thanks be to God.

This man kept the law of the Most High God, and in trial he was found faithful. And the Lord established with him [Col. 1204B] an eternal covenant, and gave him the priesthood of the nation; and he blessed him with glory, and girded him with a belt of glory, and clothed him in the vessels of virtues.

He cared for his people and delivered them from destruction. He prevailed in building the city; he attained glory in the conduct of the nation; and the entrance of the house and court was enlarged.

Like the morning star amid the clouds, and like the full moon in its days, he shines. And like the sun shining forth, so did he shine in the temple of God. And like a rose blossom in the days of spring, like lilies beside running water, and like fragrant incense in the days of summer. Like a fire blazing forth and incense burning in the fire. Like a solid vessel of gold adorned with every precious stone. Like an olive putting forth shoots and a cypress rising to the heights, when receiving [Col. 1204C] the robe of glory itself and being clothed in the perfection of virtue.

In ascending the holy altar he gave glory, putting on the vesture of holiness; and, when receiving portions from the hand of the priest, he himself stood beside the altar. And around him was a crown of brothers: like a planting of cedars on Mount Lebanon, so they stood around him.

Like branches on a palm tree, he extended his hand in the libation; he poured out the blood of the grape and shed it upon the foundation of the altar as a fragrance to the divine and exalted ruler. Then the sons of Aaron cried out; they sounded on long trumpets and made their voice heard as a memorial before God. R\. Amen.

Hymn. “Master of the city.” Supplication. “Let us pray to the Redeemer.” Capitulum. “O glory of the world.” Lauda. “Blessed is the man.” [Col. 1204D] Benediction. “Christ the Lord,” as above in the preceding Vespers.

## Day XVI. On the Feast of Saint Euphemia, Virgin and Martyr

Let everything be said as for one Virgin, fol. CLXXIX, except for the hymn.

Behold, the renowned feast of the Virgin has appeared,

the finest martyr Euphemia shining forth;

[CCXCV] now let all peoples sing in measured strains,

eagerly rendering their vows.

May the Lord, coming to meet us, cleanse our inmost parts;

may the merciful one grant the gifts of grace,

he who now may bring himself forth in the songs of soldiers,

in the praises of the Saints [the printed construction, Qui se ... carmina promere ... queat, is uncertain].

[Col. 1205A] For she, serving the Lord in majesty,

while dedicating herself to the heavenly Prince,

is immediately pierced by the envy of demons,

lest she proclaim Christ with her voice.

Happy Euphemia, yet remaining devout;

when faithless murmuring came to her with a roar [printed agreement irregular],

by the sudden gift of the Spirit

she was restored with a clear mind.

Chaste in conduct, renowned in birth,

mingled with the people of Chalcedon,

she resolves in mind to serve Christ,

and also to remain a virgin.

But the enemy himself is recognized, who, envious,

stirs up the fury of an envious judge,

so that he might impiously compel the holy woman

[Col. 1205B] to offer incense as a libation to idols.

But the virgin, joined to her most devoted companions,

whom he appointed seven times seven in number,

dedicated to the efforts of martyrdom,

joyfully undertakes the contest.

She enters the flames, is surrounded by fires,

and thunders that she is giving herself back to Christ;

paying her vows in praises,

so that she may bend heavenly grace to those who pray.

Emerging unharmed, she is handed over to prison.

The soldiers marvel at having seen such things

at close range; but the judge himself, undaunted,

the savage man gives another command.

He orders the virgin dedicated to the Lord

to be suddenly submerged in the sand of the sea,

[Col. 1205C] the madman wishing to lead the innocent woman to ruin;

and the martyr fulfills her vows.

But the martyr of the Lord, enduring such things,

now thinks that her spirit ought to be received,

so that the assembled heavenly hosts of martyrs

might be able to attain their vows.

Therefore now, Virgin, we eager peoples

devoutly pray to you, children of the washing:

sending heavenly gifts and showing mercy,

hear the prayers of the devout.

Now, Christ, be merciful to the wretched,

and, through the Saint’s merits, remit our sins,

granting us everlasting joys,

Lord God, for all.

Let unceasing glory be given to the triune Lord,

[Col. 1205D] an eternal kingdom and power,

who by his accustomed might rules all things

and lovingly sustains what he has created.

Amen.

## Day XXI. On the Feast of Saint Matthew, Apostle and Evangelist

### At Vespers

Lauda. “With glory and honor.” Sono. “Do with me.” Antiphon. “The eye of God.” fol. CLIX.

Lauda. “The righteous man will be in everlasting remembrance, alleluia.”

P. “He will not fear evil tidings, alleluia, alleluia.”

V\. “Blessed is the man who fears the Lord; [Col. 1206A] he greatly desires his commandments.”

P. “From hearing—”

V\. “Glory and honor.”

P. “From hearing—”

### Hymn

It is fitting that the people (pay heed!) should sing

in a chorus of praise

the illustrious soldier of Christ,

noble in the gifts of virtues.

For this is that Matthew

whom the Lord, summoning him with a clear voice

to himself from passing things [printed: Sese defluxa arcessens; construction uncertain],

snatched from the tax office.

And to him he granted the lofty summit

of the apostleship;

then he bestowed upon him

the illustrious glory of the Gospel.

[Col. 1206B] He alone approached the burning region,

and with a still more ardent spirit

set fierce peoples aflame

with heavenly fire.

He drove away wicked magicians,

expelled the venom of serpents,

and armed peoples dedicated to Christ

with sacred admonitions.

Taught by chaste rules,

he won over the difficult people,

and in royal courts

poured forth the oracles of life.

After many miracles

and the rewards of a holy life,

having spoken this sacred proclamation,

he was struck down

[Col. 1206C] and died.

May he, the best patron,

willingly attend our prayers,

and, merciful in his devout heart,

entreat the exalted Prince.

May he obtain for us joys

in the present age and beyond,

ward off every adversity,

and grant whatever things are beneficial.

To God the Father be glory,

[CCXCVI] and to his only Son,

with the Spirit, the Paraclete,

who reigns throughout every age.

Amen.

[Col. 1206D] Supplication. “Let us pray,” with the name changed, fol. CLXXXVII.

Capitulum. Lord Jesus Christ, you chose from your people Matthew, who took the surname Levi, as Apostle and Evangelist; and so you established him at the head of the Church, chosen by you, Christ, from a tax collector. First you caused him to evangelize in Judea, and afterward, as he proclaimed you in Macedonia, he rests in the mountains of the shepherds. Grant our prayers, so that through his intervention you may free us from future torment; so that we may preserve as sanctified in the receptacle of our heart your word, which he gloriously spread throughout the world with his voice. You who taught us to pray and say:

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” fol. 2.

Benediction. May the Lord Jesus Christ, who in his immense [Col. 1207A] devotion made his Apostle Matthew the Evangelist wondrous from a tax collector, always grant us to deserve victory over adversities. R\. Amen. And may he who exalted him through a most prompt calling deign to rescue us from every contagion of worldly conduct. R\. Amen. And may he who enriched him in the world with the voice of preaching and the grace of the apostleship furnish us with an increase of spiritual joys. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

Lauda. “I will love him with all my heart,” says the Lord.

P. “And he will be like the dew of Israel; he will sprout like a son [printed filium; apparently for lilium, ‘lily’] and blossom.” Alleluia, alleluia.

V\. “And he will be like a tree planted beside running waters, which will yield its fruit in its season.”

P. “And he will be like—”

V\. “Glory and honor.”

P. “And he will be—”

[Col. 1207B] Prayer. Grant us, O Lord, wisdom, by which both the sluggishness of our foolishness may be taken away and the glory of blessedness bestowed; so that, while you clothe your martyr Matthew the Apostle and Evangelist with the robe of honor, you may mercifully wash away through his intercession the garment of Baptism that we have polluted by sinning; and, when that holy martyr of yours is crowned amid the vessels of virtues, may we be cleansed from the contagion of sins. R\. Amen.

Through.

## At Matins

Antiphon. “Lips—” Psalm 50. Prayer. “Let them rejoice.” fol. CLXXX.

### Antiphon 1

“I will place a crown of glory upon his head,” says the Lord, “and I will clothe him in a white robe.”

[Col. 1207C] P. “Because he kept my commandments, and his blood was poured out upon the earth for my name.”

V\. “And my truth and my mercy are with him; and in my name his horn will be exalted.”

P. “And for the sake of—”

V\. “Glory and honor.”

P. “And for the sake of—”

Prayer. Grant us this, as above.

### Antiphon 2

“The Lord crowned him, blessed him, and loved him.”

P. “And he will appoint him over many gifts.”

V\. “He who enters without blemish and practices justice, who speaks truth in his heart.”

P. “And over—”

V\. “Glory and honor to the Father.”

P. “And over—”

Prayer. We beseech you, almighty God, by the eternal name of your power, that you make us companions, [Col. 1207D] equal in faith, vigorous in devotion, like in suffering, and equal in the resurrection of the blessed, through the merits of your martyr Matthew the Apostle and Evangelist and of all the Saints. R\. Amen.

### Antiphon 3

“I have fought the good fight; I have finished the course.”

P. “From now on a crown of justice has been laid up for me.”

V\. “Because I have kept the ways of the Lord and have not acted wickedly against my God.”

P. “From now on.”

V\. “Glory and honor.”

P. “From now on.”

Prayer. O immensely and gloriously powerful God, whom we worship in the sufferings of the martyrs, venerate in the solemnities of the blessed, and praise together in the contests of the victorious: attend to the prayers of those who entreat you through the intercession of your martyr Matthew the Apostle and Evangelist, so that although we fear you as terrible because of our offenses, [Col. 1208A] once entreated by his prayers we may find you favorable in mercy. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

Responsory. “I am the light.” fol. CLVIII.

Prayer. O God, whose honor is holiness, to love whom is salvation and to cherish whom is perfection: enter into our hearts. Grant that throughout your Church the footprints of your martyr Matthew the Apostle and Evangelist may shine, so that, with you guiding the steps of all, that path may lead us to life which raised your martyr to the crown. R\. Amen.

[CCXCVII]

## At Lauds

For the Canticle. Antiphon. “You alone are Lord, because there is no other; nor is there any righteous one besides you, nor any holy one besides our God.”

[Col. 1208B] Canticle. “The heart has been confirmed—”

For the Benedictus. Antiphon. “The blessing of the Lord.” Canticle. “Blessed are you.” fol. 6.

Sono. “Seven times a day.” Lauda. “Praise the Lord.” fol. CLX. Psalm 148. Prophecy. “The righteous man, if death should overtake him.” fol. 53.

### Hymn

The solemn and venerable feast

now shines forth. Peoples, open your hearts:

offer gifts to the heavenly Lord,

and devoutly render thanks.

For Matthew, the chosen disciple

of the Lord, called and highly renowned,

has appeared worthy of veneration

to all peoples.

[Col. 1208C] This man, made Christ’s companion

and Apostle,

gives sacred gifts to peoples

through his writings;

and, illustrious in his work,

he flourished in heaven,

showing good things through his merits.

This godly man, renowned in his offices,

is seen as God ruling

with royal commands,

set exalted among human beings in the world,

so that he might give life to all.

While here he restores youthful limbs,

he is said to govern all that the heavens bear [printed polifera].

The King immediately commands him

to be given gifts,

marveling at what pleased him.

But the Saint refuses to be God from that point onward,

and loudly proclaims himself entirely a little servant,

[Col. 1208D] the least Apostle of the people of the Creator,

who nevertheless possesses the world.

But looking toward heaven, he despises earthly things,

and, proclaiming what is lofty, rejects what is low;

despising what is deadly, he seeks magnificent things,

and presents what is approved to Christ.

Desiring chastity, he proclaims the best things,

and thus devoutly dedicates to Christ the Lord

those women whom he had previously known as servants,

and heaps up devout vows.

While he performs the priesthood well,

he is suddenly struck by the sword’s blade,

is joined to the holy peoples in heaven,

and is piously placed in heaven.

Such a man, we beseech you, illustrious Creator,

[Col. 1209A] may he stand beside the wretched,

and join us to you without crime

in the heavenly seat,

you who illustriously rule all things.

Make us equal to him in merits;

and also, in answer to those who pray,

make us chaste;

make us equal in heaven to the exalted peoples,

and grant us a share in the Saints.

May all created things celebrate you, Christ:

those placed upon the earth, the seas, and hidden places,

and all things resounding in measured song

to you throughout every age.

Amen.

Supplication. “Let us pray.” Capitulum. “Lord Jesus Christ, you.” Lauda. “I will love him.” Benediction. “The Lord Jesus Christ,” as above in the preceding Vespers.

## Day XXIV. On the Feast of the Beheading of Saint John the Baptist

[Col. 1209B]

### At Vespers

Lauda. “My soul has hoped.” fol. CLVI. Sono. “Bless the Lord, O my soul.” Antiphon. “I have announced well.” fol. CLX. Lauda. “The Lord has set my feet upon a rock.” Seek it on fol. CLVII.

### Hymn

This John, wondrously born

from an aged womb,

prophesying before the Judge,

before the herald was brought forth [printed: Ante judicem prophetans, / Quam sit index editus; the construction is uncertain],

preceded Christ in his birth,

and also preceded him in death.

[Col. 1209C] The man filled with the wine of the marriage-bed

orders this man’s blood to flow;

for bold adultery yields to marital crime [printed: Quare stuprum cedit audax / Conjugalis criminis; the sense is uncertain];

but he receives the sacred crown,

crowned with glory.

This man preceded God’s only Son,

born of a mother,

at the time when the truthful herald

goes before the one who follows;

and the Forerunner of death himself

was the first to fall by death.

He announces that Christ

is Redemption for the ages;

[Col. 1209D] he announces that Christ

is the gift of life for the dead;

therefore he said that Christ

could take away the world’s disgraces.

[CCXCVIII] Let us, the sorrowful hearts of hidden breasts,

entreat him,

so that he may drive away our crime,

and, moved, grant forgiveness

and the gifts of life

with everlasting joy.

May he ward off the anger

of the heavenly Judge, which we fear;

may he summon the gracious favor

of the Father, which we thirst for;

and grant all people

[Col. 1210A] possession of the blessed homeland.

Praise to you throughout all time,

undivided Trinity;

praise, honor, and highest power,

singular glory,

which proclaims you, God of the ages,

throughout the ages.

Amen.

Supplication. “Let us pray to the Redeemer,” as above.

Capitulum. Lord Jesus Christ, you deigned to make your most blessed John the Baptist your martyr, the forerunner both of your birth and of your death: so that, like a torch burning with the light of truth and forbidding adultery by words concerning marital crime, he might go before you in death when killed by the sword, having appeared to have preceded you by his birth [Col. 1210B] in the flesh; so that he whom he had announced by his voice he might proclaim also by his blood, while he was beheaded in prison for the sake of him whom he proclaimed as herald in the desert. Through his intercession, place in our mouth the oracle of your favor; grant also fruits of justice in our work, so that, made more illustrious by both gifts, just as he endured both prison and the sword for the truth, so we may escape eternal prisons and Tartarus through truth:

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” fol. 2.

And just as he became by dying the forerunner of the Lord’s death, so may you, by living blessedly, be followers of the only Redeemer. R\. Amen.

### Hymn

The devout offspring of a noble prophet,

illustrious in his parent, nobler than his father,

whom his mother’s womb knew not how to contain,

born, he came forth with an aged herald [printed: Ortus senili prodiit indice; sense uncertain].

Whom the royal glory of a virgin,

in the name of the supreme Thunderer’s offspring,

[Col. 1212B] was to carry within the innermost

chamber of the noble, fruitful palace,

with chastity intact— [the printed construction is uncertain].

A voice sent forth roused the mother who had given birth [printed puerporam],

and nourished the joys of the little prophet;

the mothers, for so great a gift of offspring— [the printed clause is incomplete],

and the mute man spoke the name of his son.

He must be written down, so that he may hear

the song of our voice,

and with his broad prophetic mouth

may dissolve dire bonds,

having the letter of his name in his words.

For he is the voice of the Word, the voice of Wisdom,

greater than the Prophets but less than the Angels,

who prepared the hearts of the faithful

and laid out the straight ways of justice.

The defender who, neither through royal power

[Col. 1212C] nor through harsh death, had abandoned

the path of truth and right conduct:

“You may not,” he said, “have your brother’s adulterous wife.”

Hence the king’s anger and cruel deaths,

sold as the price of a dance;

he filled the tyrant’s tables and the girl’s

drunken excesses with sober blood.

Here the stepfather gives gifts more insane

than if he were offering cups of poison:

it is better to refuse than to give,

for a stepfather it is better to hate; this love does greater harm.

Glory to the eternal Father and Lord,

glory to Christ, the everlasting King,

who rules with the Holy Spirit,

[Col. 1212D] and whose kingdom endures throughout every age.

Amen.

Capitulum. O God, who crowned the most blessed John with flowers of many palms: for you granted him to be a Saint before his birth, a Prophet after his birth, a Baptist in the Jordan, an Evangelist in the wilderness, and a Martyr in death. Grant us, your suppliant servants, that just as he followed the footsteps of your only-begotten Son, the Lord and Savior, so we may follow the ways of the Lord’s forerunner; and just as you deigned [CCC] to grant him to die for the truth, so grant us to live in truth.

Bring our souls out of prison, O Lord, you who consecrated the most blessed John by the Herodian sword: through him may the choice of repentance be granted to us, for he was the preacher of repentance; may he preserve the peoples in faith, he who rebuked the proud for unbelief; may he carry to you the confession of the humble, he who became the rebuker of the contemptuous. And he who was the messenger of the Word may now obtain for us the grace of what was announced, when we proclaim to you from the earth.

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” fol. 2.

May the most blessed John the Baptist, whose [Col. 1213B] head, cut off today, was brought to the bloodthirsty king amid the cups upon a platter, be an intercessor for you all before God. R\. Amen. And just as that same man became the forerunner of the Lord’s death, so may he be a forerunner and intercessor for your offenses. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

### Hymn

O gracious Prince of heaven,

most powerful Michael,

the supreme and radiant bearer

of the supreme King Christ,

called holy Michael:

“Who is like the Lord?”

[Col. 1214A] You are the foundation of the heavenly court;

you are a citizen of the thrones.

You, excelling in the fortress

of the Dominions and Virtues,

shine as the flashing light

of the Principalities and Powers.

Then you, renowned among the Cherubim

in the sacred choir of fire,

then you, powerful among the Seraphim,

supported by the august company,

properly the first elder,

bearing the fortress of the Legions.

You flourish in your course

in the fourfold order of elders;

you are a stream in the fourth company

[Col. 1214B] of twice-two senators [the printed numerical construction is uncertain].

Placed upon the Creator’s throne,

properly sent forth, you stand present;

You, in the thrice-three sacred order

of the Angels’ countenance [printed vultus; construction uncertain],

a thousand, a hundred times, in the civic

structure of legions [printed Mille centies urbana / Legionum compage; the arrangement of the words and numbers is uncertain],

resounding the perpetual song

of the Trinity, three times “Holy.”

You cover the face

[CCCI] and feet of the eternal, supreme God;

with those three, by turns,

you signal with your gaze,

a companion to Uriel,

Gabriel, and Raphael.

[Col. 1214C] And hence, breathing forth golden ones with flames

in twice-three flights [printed Hincque flantes flavos flammis / Bis ternis volatibus; syntax and referents uncertain],

namely, covering the highest things

before the world’s beginnings:

a tremendous thing! When the end is accomplished,

the last things are for each [printed Immane! peracto fine, / Cuique sunt novissima; sense uncertain].

Created yourself, obedient

to the office of the Creator,

though exalted, you do not leave the lowly world

because of your high position [printed Humilem praelatus axem / Non linquis fastigio; construction uncertain];

while that one, punished as a deserter,

is cast, insolent, into Tartarus.

Therefore supreme virtue

and glorious strength shine in you:

to rule over the [Col. 1214D] dark

demonic throngs,

to judge the devil

with his angels.

You are the salvation of the people of Judea,

a bearer sent from heaven,

bringing a ray to the gracious prophet

Daniel in an oracle:

he says that you fight mightily

for the faithful people.

Therefore, we ask you, gracious

and renowned victorious soldier:

now grant to all those reborn

through Baptism

what you once devoutly bestowed

[Col. 1215A] upon the ancient mystery.

Remove the weapons cast down,

the guilty wrath of demons;

drive away the ulcer, ward off disease,

take away every scandal;

may peace, salvation, and fervent faith

cover every soul.

Behold, all gathered together

as the year of time

has revolved, alleluia,

we fulfill what was dedicated

to your court;

may it be acceptable to Christ the King,

while you favor us as we live.

Grant that we, blind in mind,

may be pure in body;

[Col. 1215B] lest we fall into soft filth,

wounded by lust;

mercifully lift us up,

so that we may rise to salvation.

Favor peaceful times,

increase the bonds of peace;

may the sword of the enemy

not cut through the boundaries of our city;

may no pestilence or plague

slaughter anyone, with you as guide.

May every sex and every age

learn to leave the world’s empty things;

may we learn to climb together

the true path of Christ,

so that after our passing [Col. 1215C]

we may seek the gate of heaven.

On the final day, when he

shines forth in rising again,

may we, bound by the lot of the guilty,

not be handed over to Tartarus;

but may we be assigned

to the free place of urban light.

Then there will be a twofold honor,

when a worthy reward is given to the Saints;

may the evils we have done

not bind us, though we deserve them [printed non indignis, ‘not undeserving’];

but may we, though wavering, be transferred

by faith to the stars [printed nutandi; syntax uncertain].

So that, through your prayer, gracious

[Col. 1215D] and most powerful Michael,

they may strive in song toward glorious Jerusalem [the subject and construction of Sint enixi are uncertain],

so that we may duly enjoy

the immense light.

Let us who have attained

the right hand of the Spirit,

the Father, and the Lamb,

sing manifold praise

to the only triune Godhead;

may we rejoice and exult abundantly

through the ages.

Amen.

Supplication. “Let us pray to the Redeemer,” with the name changed, fol. CLXXXVII.

Lord God, almighty Father, creator [Col. 1216A] of all things and founder of the elements, you who deigned to place your Michael before the armies of messengers, whose service offers obedience to your command and who are never wearied by such a title of offices: this resounds from the mystery, and virtue shines forth from merit; for although they are always spirits, when they are sent by you they are nevertheless called Angels embodied in air, so that they may visibly appear to all eyes; their substance remains incorporeal, and although they are circumscribed locally, they nevertheless ceaselessly enjoy the sight of the Creator.

Grant us, we ask, through the intercession of this Archangel and of all the Angels, to obtain forgiveness of sins, so that we who utter praise to you, our God, in their honor [CCCII] may also obtain the everlasting pardon of eternal blessedness [printed veniam, ‘pardon’].

### Reading from the Book of the Prophet Daniel (Chapter X)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

In those days, in the third year of Cyrus, king of the Persians, a word was revealed to Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar; and the word was true, and there was great strength. He understood the word, for understanding is needed in a vision.

In those days I, Daniel, mourned for three weeks of days. I ate no desirable bread, and neither meat nor wine entered my mouth; nor was I anointed with ointment, until the three weeks of days were completed.

On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, I was beside the great river, which is the Tigris. I lifted up my eyes and saw, and behold, a man clothed in linen, whose loins were girded with refined gold. His waist was girded with the color of ophaz; his body was like chrysolite; his face was like the appearance of lightning; his eyes were like a burning lamp; his arms and everything below them down to his feet were like the appearance of glowing bronze; and the sound of his words was like the sound of a multitude.

I, Daniel, alone saw the vision. The men who were with me did not see it, but an exceedingly great terror fell upon them, and they fled into hiding. I was left alone and saw this great vision; no strength remained in me. My appearance was changed within me, I languished, and I had no strength at all.

I heard the sound of his words; and as I heard, I lay terrified upon my face, with my countenance clinging to the ground. And behold, a hand touched me and raised me upon my knees and the joints of my hands. He said to me: “Daniel, man of desires, understand the words that I speak to you, and stand in your place; for now I have been sent to you.” When he had spoken this word to me, I stood trembling.

He said to me: “Do not fear, Daniel, for from the first day on which you set your heart to understand and to afflict yourself before the Lord your God, your words have been heard, and I have come because of your words. But the prince of the kingdom of the Persians resisted me for twenty-one days; and behold, Michael, one of the chief princes, came to my aid, and I remained there beside the king of the Persians. I have come to teach you what will happen to your people in the latter days, for the vision still awaits its appointed time.”

While he spoke these words to me, I cast my face toward the ground and was silent. And behold, something resembling a human form touched my lips; it opened my mouth, and I spoke. I said to the one standing opposite me: “My lord, in your vision my joints have come undone, and no strength remains in me. How can the servant of my lord speak with my lord? No strength remains in me, and my breath is failing.”

Again, something resembling the appearance of a man touched me and strengthened me. He said: “Do not fear, man of desires; peace be with you. Take courage and be strong.” While he spoke with me, I recovered and said: “Speak, my lord, for you have strengthened me.”

He said: “Do you know why I have come to you? Now I shall return to fight against the prince of the Persians. When I was going out, the prince of the Greeks appeared, coming. Nevertheless, I shall announce to you what has been set down in the writing of truth; and no one is my helper in all these matters except Michael, your prince” (Chapter XI).

“I, from the first year of Darius the Mede, was standing so that he might be strengthened and made strong. And now I announce the truth to you” (Chapter XII).

“At that time Michael, the great prince who stands for the sons of your people, will arise. There will be a time such as has never been since nations began to exist until that time. At that time your people will be saved, everyone who is found written in the book.

“Many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth will awake: some to everlasting life, others to reproach, so that they may see forever. Those who have been instructed will shine like the splendor of the firmament, and those who teach many to righteousness will shine like the stars for everlasting ages.

“But you, Daniel, close up the word and seal the book until the appointed time. Many will pass through, and knowledge will be multiplied.”

I, Daniel, saw, and behold, two white figures stood, one here on the bank of the river and the other there on the opposite bank. I said to the man clothed in linen, who stood above the waters of the river: “How long until the end of these wonders?”

I heard the man clothed in linen, who stood above the waters of the river. He raised his right hand and his left hand toward heaven and swore by him who lives forever that it would be for a time, times, and half a time. “When the scattering of the hand of the people has been completed, all these things will be fulfilled.”

I heard, but I did not understand. I said: “My lord, what will happen after these things?” He said: “Go, Daniel, until the appointed time. Many will be chosen, purified, and tested as by fire; the wicked will act wickedly, and none of the wicked will understand, but the instructed will understand.

“From the time when the continual sacrifice is taken away and the abomination of desolation is set up, there will be 1,290 days. Blessed is the one who waits and reaches 1,335 days.

“But you, go on to the appointed end. You will rest, and you will stand in your allotted place at the end of the days.”  
**R.** Amen.

## Hymn

All together, let the whole Catholic people,  
the foster-child of glory,  
present their vows  
and disclose their sins,  
so that the merciful Author of all  
may grant to all what has been granted.

For that Michael,  
exalted in name,  
conspicuous in the court of heaven  
for the love of the supreme God,  
was made prince of the angels  
and high in title.

His name, from his power,  
and his work, from his commission,  
he received from the hand  
of the Almighty to preserve,  
so that he might glory in God  
with his fellow companions.

He is the Lord’s highest,  
now made a great messenger,  
who, by conquering that gloomy,  
dreadful, rebellious angel,  
hurled him headlong  
down into the abyss.

He is always protector  
and defender of all,  
so that he may present  
the petitions of everyone  
to God the King  
and grant the people  
the favor appointed by him.

Great indeed is this  
festival of God,  
of this gracious Archangel,  
the messenger Michael.  
We ought to celebrate it  
and undertake it devoutly,  
so that through his entreaty  
we may be worthy to obtain  
from God the forgiveness  
of our sins,

and, after our departure,  
to enjoy the kingdom  
of blessed life.

Praise to you throughout all time,  
undivided Trinity:  
one praise to the Father,  
the Son,  
and the glorious Paraclete,  
whose praise and power endure  
through eternal ages.

Amen.

**Supplication.** Let us pray to the Redeemer, as above.

### Capitulum

O light of light, inexpressible splendor, Christ God, wisdom, power, and glory of the Father, who appeared in this world to the sight of all in the flesh as the star of salvation, and, having defeated the prince of darkness, returned to the heights as the Word made flesh: grant to us, your suppliants, in the darkness of this age, the most abundant brightness of your splendor. Establish for us the supreme angel Michael as patron and defender, that he may guard our entrance and our departure, and admit us, to be crowned, to your right hand.

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. Fol. 2.

**Lauda.** The Lord is in heaven.

**Blessing.** Christ, Son of God. See in the preceding Vespers.

# THE THIRTIETH DAY: FEAST OF SAINT JEROME THE PRIEST

Everything is said as for one Confessor who is not a Pontiff, CLXXIII, except the following:

## Hymn

Christ is the strength and wisdom of the Father  
for all whom spiritual grace fills,  
so that they may rightly direct  
the rule of conduct  
and illumine the darkness of their neighbors,  
so that they may worthily enjoy heavenly things.

By his gift, the eminent breath of inspiration  
once filled this prophet, Jerome by name,  
known to all through the sources of learning,  
watering everyone with nourishing doctrines,  
as the sun shines resplendent at its fiery rising.

He trampled far beneath his feet  
all the affairs of the world,  
as though they were utterly filthy;  
he rejected the world’s dishonor,  
nourishing the entrails of the poor and needy  
and acquiring eternal wages for himself.

Thus he also sought the monastic life  
and bound himself tightly by its rule.  
Leaving parents, homes, and homeland,  
he found the most blessed fields of Bethlehem,  
where he completed his perfected works.

While he was fervent and burning in intellect,  
and, with the greatest zeal,  
was hiding in his mind a little work  
for the elegant charm of pagan prose,  
he deserved to be corrected by such a divine utterance.

For behold, illness invaded his little body,  
and now, reclining in pain upon his bed,  
as is customary in ordinary funerals,  
he seemed merely to be returning his spirit  
to heaven, while his limbs  
were suddenly being laid in the tomb.

But swiftly, penetrating the heights,  
he was led in spirit  
and brought before the ethereal Prince.  
Far away stood a legion  
of countless attendants serving him.  
Then, thundering words, he complained  
by striking him; and as soon as he discovered  
that he was Christ’s servant,  
he declared—not, as he testifies,  
with words of moderation—  
but, judging the treasury of his heart,  
he brought forth the truth about Cicero.

He ordered blows to be inflicted  
throughout his limbs  
and dense scourges to be applied  
to his body.  
His tongue quickly began  
to testify with a howling cry:  
“If ever I dare to read this man again,  
I have denied you, Lord.”

Then the thousands of angels standing by  
bent their knees  
and prayed with humble supplication  
that forgiveness might be granted him.  
And thus, having returned with his body cut up,  
he displayed it to everyone,  
so that these true events might be proved,  
not false, sleep-filled tales  
by which we are often shamefully deceived.

Thus corrected by divine glory,  
he sought the lofty things of heavenly divinity  
and no longer desired worldly concerns.

From then on he shines with such a light of learning;  
with such radiant brilliance he possesses power,  
and, adorned by his flourishing instruction,  
he shines splendidly,  
so that the people of Christ, redeemed by blood,  
may be restored by his gift, O Holy One.

You are our splendor;  
you also appoint us through yourself.  
Through you the Church shines everywhere.  
You are a warrior in the Catholic faith,  
a great ram, strong in doctrine,  
destroying the wall of heretics.

The activity of the envious pursues you;  
the faction of foolish accusers pursues you;  
false commentary yields to you;  
their slippery purpose has no strength,  
being frivolous, because it returns to nothing.

Anyone who resists you  
is proved a heretic  
and is soon judged ignorant.  
Whoever here gives assent to you  
is immediately known to be Catholic  
in conduct, capable, upright,  
and rich in doctrine.

Protect this people  
with holy intercessions;  
illumine their hearts with heavenly gifts,  
and, made firm in the doctrines of peace,  
let them flourish in the word.  
May they, fruitful in good works,  
stand with all in the heavenly seats.

Grant this, most merciful Father God,  
one with the Son  
and with the Holy Spirit,  
who continually govern all things  
by your command,  
always, throughout the span of the age,  
through endless ages of ages.

Amen.

# OCTOBER FEASTS: THE FIRST DAY, OF SAINTS VERISSIMUS, MAXIMA, AND JULIA

Everything is said as in the Common of Several Martyrs, except the hymn, which is *Jucundum nobis nunc diem*, fol. CIV.

# THE EIGHTEENTH DAY: FEAST OF SAINT LUKE THE EVANGELIST

## At Vespers

**Lauda.** Confession and beauty.

**Sono.** I will confess to you.

**Lauda.** I will confess. See fol. CLXIX.

## Hymn

Behold, Lord, the feast  
of Luke the Evangelist is here,  
whom you exalted from the age,  
for Paul the Apostle  
presents him as a physician  
heavenly in spirit and in body.

This day is worthy to be sung  
with pleasing musical songs.  
We ought to celebrate it  
with the deepest strength,  
so that we may be rescued by Christ  
from the worst dangers.

This man proved to be a virgin;  
joined to the celibate,  
he served the Lord without sin  
in all things.  
Thus he received from God  
a happier diadem.

Urged on by the Holy Spirit,  
in the regions of Achaea  
he wrote the Gospel  
for faithful peoples,  
which he learned from Paul  
or sent into the best hands.

Afterward, when he had written  
the Acts of the Apostles,  
in the city of Rome,  
to teach the peoples,  
through him he also completed  
the gracious and peaceful Catholics.

This citizen of Antioch,  
Luke, a physician by profession,  
was again a foster-child and teacher  
of the flock;  
by his words he gave health  
to darkened limbs and spirits.

He lived seventy years,  
and twice two in the arid region [the wording is uncertain],  
and, full of the Holy Spirit,  
died in Bithynia.  
After fulfilling Christ’s commands,  
he possesses heavenly things.

Therefore we beseech you, Christ,  
most faithful Author,  
that through his entreaty  
we may be free from sin  
and through him enjoy you  
in firm blessedness.

Through his intercession  
may there be true faith  
for unbelievers,  
and may the firm truth of faith  
grow strong in believers,  
as they judge nothing evil  
to be in their hearts.

May there be peace in his land,  
moderation in conduct;  
may the harvests of the fields  
be multiplied a hundredfold  
and even seven times over.  
May there be everlasting glory  
for the Catholic dead.

Amen.

**Supplication.** Let us pray, changing the name. Fol. CLXXXVII.

### Capitulum

You made your Confessor Luke the Evangelist, Lord, truly blessed: he confessed you with his whole heart and is shown to be conspicuous in the assembly of the righteous and in the congregation. Grant us, therefore, through his merits, that, cleansed from sin by the simple confession of our mouths, we may deserve to take our place in the assembly of the saints and in the heavenly congregation.

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. Fol. 2.

### Blessing

May the Lord Jesus Christ, who is the reward of confessors, enrich you with the gift of holy confession through the intercession of his confessor Luke the Evangelist.  
**R.** Amen.

May he grant you the desire to confess, who bestowed the reward of confession upon that same man.  
**R.** Amen.

So that, truly imitating the example of so great a confessor, Luke the Evangelist, we may deserve to reach the heavenly promise.  
**R.** Amen.

Through.

**Lauda.** They will flourish. Fol. CLXX.

### Prayer

O God, who have caused your confessor Luke the Evangelist to rejoice and exult throughout the ages of ages, so that, singing praise to you alone without end, he might offer a hymn to the one whose confession earned him a place among the company of the elect: we ask you with devoted hearts that through his merits our life may flourish again and, corrected from evil deeds, shine forth; so that those who now deserve punishment for their sins may, through confession and the worship of the Christian faith, deserve in the future to reach glory.  
**R.** Amen.

Through.

## At Matins

**Antiphon.** My lips. Psalm L.

**Prayer.** May he praise you, Lord. Fol. CLXX.

**Antiphon.** My flesh. Fol. CLXX.

**Prayer.** O God, who made the confessor—here above.

**Antiphon 2.** Your face will be illumined like pure water.  
**P.** But your countenance will rise like the morning star from the southern region; life will spring forth for you.  
**V.** By day the sun will not burn you, nor the moon by night.  
**P.** Your countenance.  
**V.** Glory and honor.  
**P.** Your countenance.

### Prayer

O God, Son of God, whom Luke the Evangelist, the bishop, confessed with his whole heart, and, by honoring your name, reached the crown: place confession in our mouths that may cleanse us from sin, so that whatever we utter in honor of your praise, we may perceive to be profitable as gain for an eternal gift.  
**R.** Amen.

Through.

**Antiphon 3.** You have guarded my body from every pollution.  
**P.** Your fragrance, Lord, has awakened eternal desires in me.  
**V.** You have made known to me the paths of life; you will fill me with joy by your countenance. Delights are at your right hand forever.  
**P.** Your fragrance.  
**V.** Glory and honor.  
**P.** Your fragrance.

### Prayer

O God, who accepted the confession of the most blessed Luke the Evangelist and heard all the words of his mouth so fully that you made him a sharer in your kingdom, where he might sing to you in the sight of the angels: now receive through him the vow of our confession, you who led him to his reward. And you who wished him to be a blessed confessor, draw us, after the falls by which we have fallen in this world, to the eternal homeland, there to be crowned.  
**R.** Amen.

Through.

**Responsory.** This man. Fol. CLXXVI.

### Prayer

O Lord, wondrous in your saints, God of powers, hear your suppliants; grant to us sinners the patronage of your most blessed confessor Luke the Evangelist, and bestow the abundance of perpetual charity. As he deserved the crown of virtue, so may we, through his intercessions and by your gift, deserve to obtain forgiveness for our sins and the peace of perpetual charity.  
**R.** Amen.

Through.

## At Lauds

### For the Canticle

**Antiphon.** I will confess to you.

**Canticle.** I will confess.

### For the *Benedictus*

**Antiphon.** Blessing.

**Canticle.** Blessed are you, Lord.

**Sono.** Before the angels.

**Lauda.** Praise.

Psalm CXLVIII.

**Prophecy.** Thus says the Lord. Fol. CLXXII.

**Hymn.** Behold, the feast of the Evangelist is here.

**Supplication.** Let us pray, as in the preceding Vespers.

### Capitulum

O God, whom the tongues of the faithful praise together by confessing you, and whom the devotion of confessors abundantly exalts: grant that, through the entreaty of your confessor Luke the Evangelist, we may obtain what we ask and escape what we fear. For you are our God, and we will confess you; we will also devoutly exalt you as God in our hearts. Make us therefore cling to you unceasingly both in deed and in word, you who have made us know the truth of the Christian faith.

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. Fol. 2.

**Lauda.** They will flourish.

**Blessing.** The Lord Jesus Christ. As in the preceding Vespers.

# THE NINETEENTH DAY: FEAST OF THE SAINTS FAUSTUS, JANUARIUS, AND MARTIALIS, MARTYRS

## At Vespers

**Lauda.** It has risen. Fol. CLXII.

**Sono.** When the furnace was heated, Ananias, Azarias, and Misael were prepared to be burned; and when they entered the fire, they were so refreshed by the heat of the flame—for the angel of God stood in the midst, with a wind of dew blowing—that you may understand and judge.  
**V.** Then the rejoicing youths sang:  
**P.** The almighty God is terrible and to be feared forever. Amen. Alleluia.  
**V.** The three youths were thrown into the furnace at the king’s command; not fearing the flames of the fire, they sang as though with one mouth:  
**P.** The almighty God.

May the Lord be present.  
**R.** And with.

**Antiphon.** The saints were tested like gold in the fire.  
**P.** And like a holocaust offering they were accepted in the sight of their God.  
**V.** But the righteous will possess the land as an inheritance and dwell upon it forever and ever.  
**P.** And like.  
**V.** Glory and honor.  
**P.** And like.

May the Lord be present.  
**R.** And with.

**Lauda.** They had a column of fire as guide on their journey, alleluia.  
**P.** Through it God showed them the light, alleluia, alleluia.  
**V.** He sent his word and healed them and delivered them from their destruction.  
**P.** Through it.  
**V.** Glory and honor.  
**P.** Through it.

## Hymn

The noble company rejoices,  
filled with God’s grace;  
the glorious solemnity  
of the three holy Martyrs is here.

The blessed Trinity  
established for itself  
an everlasting temple,  
from which a new  
and sweetest song is brought forth.

These three men  
come together to their passion;  
in the name of the Trinity  
they conquered the worst enemy.

First is kind Faustus,  
who says: “The suffering  
of this present time, brothers,  
is not worthy of the future glory.”

Blessed Januarius says:  
“An open door  
has now been set before us;  
let us rejoice  
in the finest heaven.”

Behold, Martialis advances,  
ascending with all the gracious saints of God  
to glory;  
he rejoices happily in their company.

Then Martialis began:  
“For the sake of eternal glory  
we must despise idols  
and the cruelty of the Judge.”

At once the Governor began to rage.  
He ordered the teeth,  
nostrils, ears, lips,  
and even the eyebrows  
of the saints to be cut off.

The gracious Martyrs said:  
“Unjust and wicked judge,  
why do you afflict God’s servants?  
Why do you accept false gods?”

Then the Tyrant, inflamed with fury, said:  
“Throw these men into the fire,  
since they dare to despise  
our commands.”

“Unjust and wicked judge,  
why do you afflict God’s servants?  
Why do you profanely worship vain things  
and accept false gods?”

The blessed Martyrs enter the furnace joyfully;  
they sing a hymn to God  
and a new song  
with devout harmonies.

Having cast away the burden of the flesh,  
they send their spirits to the stars.  
They see Christ, whom they love,  
the saints of God with the angels.

Pray to God, O saints,  
so that he may quickly repel evil,  
grant us good things,  
and give us fitting peace.

We beseech you, gracious Martyrs,  
by the one and triune God,  
to remove swiftly  
the dreadful yoke  
which we endure.

May the merciful and favorable God  
grant comfort to the living  
and give pleasant places  
to the faithful dead.

Grant this, most holy Father,  
and Only-Begotten equal to the Father,  
who reign with the Spirit, the Paraclete,  
through every age.

Amen.

**Supplication.** Let us pray, changing the names. Fol. CLXXXVII.

### Capitulum

Christ, Son of God, glory of the saints, true blessedness of the Martyrs, and everlasting reward: receive the vows of your faithful, who eagerly gather to the memory of your Martyrs; relieve them from oppression; and mercifully suspend the scourges of all the hardships and troubles of life by which your people are afflicted.

You who once, standing as mediator for the three placed in the furnace, extinguished the visible flame so that they would not be burned, now, through the intervention of your saints, extinguish the fires that consume us.

May Faustus, by his prayers, favor the wretched and oppressed. May Januarius, an excellent guide, open for us the gate of the heavenly way. May Martialis, by his merits, obtain whatever the foster-child people devoutly desire in their hearts to be done for their sins. Thus, saved through the intercession of both, may we be free from present distress and afterward, having become celibate, be led to the eternal homeland.

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. Fol. 2.

### Blessing

May the ineffable mystery of the gracious Trinity keep from you the loss of disaster inflicted upon you.  
**R.** Amen.

May Faustus present your ardent vows in the sight of the Lord and be the best intercessor for your desires.  
**R.** Amen.

May Januarius receive the libations of your holocaust and, by his prayers, cleanse you from every stain of sin.  
**R.** Amen.

May Martialis also commend your sighs to the Spirit and obtain as quickly as possible the healing which you ask from him.  
**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Lauda.** Everlasting joy. Fol. CLXVIII.

### Prayer

Make your people joyful, Lord, in this celebration of the most blessed Faustus, Januarius, and Martialis, so that we who are saddened by our sins may be consoled by their prayers.  
**R.** Amen.

Through.

## At Matins

**Antiphon.** Give us. Psalm L.

**Prayer.** Restore to us. See fol. CLXIII.

**Antiphon 1.** To your saints, Lord. Fol. CLXVI.

### Prayer

Great is the light among your saints, Lord, when in the night of this age they deserve to have you as a burning column of fire, by which they are both illumined regarding what they should do and helped to accomplish what they understand.

Grant us, therefore, through the entreaty of your Martyrs, that, traveling the dark road of the age under the guidance of your light, we may reach the heavenly dwellings in happiness.  
**R.** Amen.

Through.

**Antiphon 2.** How much he has acted wickedly. Fol. CLXVI.

**Prayer.** Make joyful, Lord, as above at Vespers.

**Antiphon 3.** Your saints. Fol. CLXVI.

### Prayer

Lord Jesus Christ, by whose power your holy Martyrs extinguished the whirling force of the fire and practiced righteousness, bestow upon us sinners the favor of your mercy, so that through the faith by which the saints conquered kingdoms, we sinners may deserve to obtain the heavenly crown.  
**R.** Amen.

Through.

**Responsory.** You have tested us, God. Fol. CLXXXIX.

### Prayer

Lord Jesus Christ, who receive your saints in the midst of the flame of fire to be crowned, since you know that they completed their martyrdom by fighting manfully for you: rescue our life from the furnace of crimes and visit us with gifts of grace, so that with these three Martyrs we may deserve to have a share in heavenly things, with whom we are recognized as companions not by passion but by faith.  
**R.** Amen.

Through.

**Antiphon.** Ananias, Azarias, and Misael, servants of the Most High God.  
**P.** Great is the Lord, who delivered you from the fire.  
**V.** Confess to the Lord and invoke his name; declare his works among the nations.  
**P.** Great.  
**V.** Glory and honor.  
**P.** Great.

### Prayer

Ananias, Azarias, and Misael, those three youths tested by the Babylonian fire, offered great hope to these Martyrs, whose revered victory provided them an example.

For those three, the fire withdrew so that they would not die; for these, it was admitted so that they might be crowned. In the former, because the fitting time of their passion had not yet come, the penal fire could not touch their consecrated bodies; in the latter, at the appointed time, when through Christ’s death the way of paradise stood open, the fire consumed bodies given over to it, since the gate of paradise was now open to the blessed.

Therefore we bless you, God, who both delivered those men from the flames, who scatter fires for their deliverance, and admit fires for the reception of these men. Grant us, through the examples and intercessions of both groups, to be so freed from the fire of carnal vices that, burned by the sweetness of your utterances as by fire, we may deserve to come to you in peace.  
**R.** Amen.

Through.

**Antiphon.** The three youths. Fol. CC.

### Prayer

Behold, in the likeness of those three youths, these Martyrs of yours, also placed in the fire of the age and set in the furnace for your name, praise you, Lord, with a similar devotion.

Those youths, fearing you as Lord, sang a hymn of glory to you because you had rescued them from the midst of the burning flame. These men, however, do not offer prayers of praise so that they may not be touched by the fire; rather, so that they may be crowned for you through the punishments of fire, they offer you a hymn with the freedom of conscience.

Grant us, therefore, while leading the course of our life in peace, to be free from the fires of lust and to deserve to be freed from future punishments.  
**R.** Amen.

Through.

**Antiphon.** The fire. Fol. CCI.

### Prayer

The fire which your persecutors not only threatened but also prepared to burn your saints brought them a wondrous means of victory. The very hastening of the punishment quickly directed them to the completion of victory; and because they were soon consumed by the flames, they deserved all the sooner to climb the step toward the crown.
