We therefore ask that the future fire prepared for the impious as a punishment may in no way dare to touch us, but that, freed from it by the power of your divinity, we may deserve to receive the scepter of the heavenly kingdom.  
**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Responsory.** You have tested us, God. Fol. CCII.

### Prayer

O God, who wished your saints Faustus, Januarius, and Martialis to be tested on earth by the customary test of your mercy, and did not permit them to be tempted beyond what you saw had been granted them as a gift of endurance by your grace: rescue us from every temptation, lest it be able to overwhelm our minds.

May we serve faithfully in a service pleasing to you, and may you permit us to be tempted in such a way that the temptation itself draws us not into the confusion of error but strongly into the embrace of truth.  
**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

## At Lauds

### For the Canticle

**Antiphon.** Those who love you, Lord.

**Canticle.** You who offered yourselves willingly. Fol. CLXIII.

### For the *Benedictus*

**Antiphon.** The three youths were sent at the king’s command. Fol. CCIII.

**Canticle.** Blessed are you, Lord God.

**Sono.** When the furnace was heated. See in the preceding Vespers.

**Lauda.** Praise the Lord. Psalm CXLVIII.

**Prophecy.** They suffered. Fol. CCIII.

**Hymn.** Let the mystical melody be completed. Fol. CIV.

**Supplication.** Let us pray, as above.

### Capitulum

O God, eternal light, unquenchable lamp, and light of truth, who graciously caused your most blessed Martyrs Faustus, Januarius, and Martialis to shine so brightly that they in no way feared the threats of raging impious men, but hastened instead toward you, the one true God, who graciously predestined them before the ages: grant to us, your unworthy and sinful servants, that we may deserve to obtain the company of those whose feasts we honor with eagerness and rejoicing.

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. Fol. 2.

**Lauda.** The column of fire. Fol. CXCIX.

**Blessing.** As above at Vespers.

At the concluding Vespers, everything is said as at the first Vespers, except the Capitulum, Blessing, and Lauda.

### Capitulum

O God, who graciously sent your only Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, at the evening of this age, as the fulfillment of the Law and the Prophets, so that he might show the path of eternal light to those walking in darkness and the shadow of death, and open the darkness of perpetual death: grant that, in this feast of your saints Faustus, Januarius, and Martialis, our steps may remain so firm through their intercession that they do not depart from your paths.

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. Fol. 2.

### Blessing

Through the entreaty of his Martyrs Faustus, Januarius, and Martialis, may the blessing of the Lord accompany you on earth, the blessing that raises them to heaven.  
**R.** Amen.

May the holy Trinity, which was with them unto the end, remain with you forever.  
**R.** Amen.

And just as they fought for righteousness unto death, so may you, following in their footsteps, hasten freely toward the heavenly kingdoms.  
**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Lauda.** Everlasting joy. Fol. CLXVIII.

**Prayer.** Make joyful, Lord, as at the first Vespers.

# THE TWENTY-FIRST DAY: FEAST OF THE HOLY MARTYRS COSMAS AND DAMIAN

## At Vespers

**Lauda.** It has risen.

**Sono.** The souls of the righteous. Fol. CLXII.

**Antiphon.** I will give my saints a kingdom in Jerusalem; for the tree of life is an aroma of ointment.  
**P.** And they will not labor, nor will they grow weary.  
**V.** Those who trust in the Lord are like Mount Zion; those who dwell in Jerusalem will not be moved forever.  
**P.** And they will not.  
**V.** Glory and honor.  
**P.** And they will not.

**Lauda.** He looked upon them. Fol. CLXV.

## Hymn

People dedicated to God, powerful,  
and the many-sided company,  
every gathering and assembly  
of the world encompassed by blood,  
whom the cleansing wave  
of the singular Victim purifies:

Open the clear passages of your ears,  
the depths of your breast,  
the innermost parts of your heart,  
and the heights of your mind.  
A holy matter is being told:  
come here swiftly, all of you.

Behold, in a new procession  
a miracle leaps forth,  
while a rank of remedies  
stands full of every gift.  
For Cosmas and his companion Damian,  
the renowned men, live:

By mouth, by touch, by command,  
with the grace of healing,  
with the fire of iron  
and the fire of the word,  
they dry up all diseased things.  
By the art of books  
and the art of heaven,  
they heal every languishing thing.

Whatever is present in them  
for salvation proves effective.  
One power itself forms it,  
whatever things are life-giving,  
while all that they determine  
with mouth and hand remains active.

Bones, nerves, and marrow,  
blood, limbs, and inward parts,  
the spirit and every breast  
troubled by weariness:  
all these ask to receive  
such a full healing from the saints,

so that the demon may fall,  
and terror, sickness, and ulcer  
may collapse;  
so that grace may follow guilt  
and mercy, crime;  
so that there may be an end  
to all evils  
and eternity for the good.

Praise to you throughout all time,  
undivided Trinity,  
praise, honor, and supreme power,  
unique glory,  
which remains God  
through the ages of the ages.

Amen.

**Supplication.** Let us pray, changing the name. Fol. CLXXXVII.

### Capitulum

O God, medicine of the sick, health of the infirm, healer of bodies, provident physician of souls, who made the most blessed men Cosmas and Damian skillful through a twofold art of healing, so that by word and deed they might assist human sicknesses; who made them healers of souls and bodies through the same twofold kind of medicine, since they cure both by signs and are wondrous in the work of their hands; since they heal bodies by worldly art and souls by heavenly medicine:

We ask you, we beseech you, that through the patronage of these men you may bestow upon our wounds the provident care of healing and remove inward and outward sufferings, so that, with hearts and bodies healed, while we render you service pleasing to you in this pilgrimage, we may deserve to reach the rest of perfected salvation.

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. Fol. 2.

### Blessing

May Christ the Lord, who made his saints Cosmas and Damian conspicuous through their glorious art of healing, make you free from every sickness.  
**R.** Amen.

And may he, who wished them to provide cures for infirmities, through their prayers grant an abundance of healings.  
**R.** Amen.

So may the hidden and manifest sickness of sins flee from you through their healing and intercession; to them God has plainly granted the power to heal.  
**R.** Amen.

Through.

**Lauda.** Everlasting joy. Fol. CLXVIII.

### Prayer

O God, who bestowed on your saints Cosmas and Damian twin crowns before death, granting them both devotion in the art of healing and victory through suffering: we ask and beseech you to grant health to our soul and body through their intercession; may our life be free from the disease of incentives to sin, and may the desire for spiritual instruction grow within us. R\. Amen.

Through [your] mercy.

### At Matins

Antiphon. Give us joy. Psalm 50.

Prayer. Restore to us. Fol. CLXIII. Antiphon 1. They were palms. Fol. CLXVIII.

Prayer. We earnestly beseech you, O Lord God of hosts, wonderful in your saints Cosmas and Damian, that you grant us strength to drive away adversities—you who bestowed on your saints dignity for attaining heavenly things. We also ask that you grant strength to your people through the intercession of those whom, in your immense goodness, you deign to associate with your friendship. R\. Amen.

Through [your] mercy.

Antiphon 2. The just, whose many works [CCCXII] are stored up. P. With you, O Lord, they receive their reward from their own works. V\. But the just shall possess the earth as an inheritance, and shall dwell upon it for ever and ever. P. With you. V\. Glory and honor. P. With you.

Prayer. O God, our healer and everlasting physician, who made Cosmas and Damian unshaken in faith and unconquerable in virtue, so that through the wounds they received they might heal human wounds—those who, before their passion, were workers of salvation among the peoples through earthly medicine—appoint them, we ask, as both guardians and physicians for our infirmities. Through them may the sick be healed; through them may medicine for the soul be obtained. R\. Amen.

Antiphon 3. The bones of the saints shall spring up from their place, and their names, like pure lilies, have blossomed. V\. O Lord, save us; O Lord, prosper us. P. And their names. V\. Glory and honor. P. And their names.

Prayer. O God, who [did so], as above at Vespers.

R\. The saints who through faith conquered kingdoms, practiced righteousness, obtained the promises, quenched the violence of fire, and put armies to flight: P. They were made strong in battle. V\. They closed the mouths of lions and recovered their strength from sickness. P. They were made strong. V\. Glory and honor. P. They were made strong.

Prayer. O God, in whose sight the commemoration of your martyrs Cosmas and Damian has been celebrated: they were beaten with cords for your sake, cast into the waves of the sea, thrown into flames, placed upon the rack, fastened to the cross, and, undefeated in their passion, became triumphant conquerors through death. We implore you with suppliant prayers: on this day of their passion, grant your faithful people spiritual joy and bestow eternal gladness. R\. Amen.

### At Lauds

For the Canticle. Antiphon. All the saints. Canticle. The Lord from Sinai. Fol. CLXVI. For the Benedictus. Antiphon. Holy and humble. Canticle. Blessed are you, O Lord. Tone. The way of the just. Lauda. Praise the Lord. [Col. 1232B] Fol. CLXVII. Psalm 148.

Reading from the book of Isaiah the Prophet (Chapter LXI).

R\. Thanks be to God.

Thus says the Lord: You shall all be called the saints of God, and you shall be called ministers of our God. You shall consume the strength of the nations and shall glory in their honor. In place of your double shame and disgrace, they shall praise their portion; therefore they shall possess double things in their land, and everlasting joy shall be theirs. For I am the Lord, loving judgment and hating robbery for a burnt offering; and I shall give them their work in truth, and I shall make an everlasting covenant with them. Their offspring shall be known among the nations, and their descendants in the midst of the peoples; all who see them shall recognize them, because they are the offspring whom the Lord has blessed. R\. Amen.

Hymn. The people of God. Supplication. Let us pray to the Redeemer. Capitula. God our medicine. Lauda. Joy. Benediction. Christ the Lord, who …

### On the First Vespers

## The Twenty-Third: Feast of Saints Servandus and Germanus

### At Vespers

Lauda. It has arisen. Fol. CLXII. Tone. Rejoice, you just. Fol. CLXV.

Antiphon. The saints have given forth a great fragrance; flowers have appeared in our land. P. Jerusalem rejoiced, and the cities of Judah exulted. V\. They shall walk, O Lord, in the light of your countenance, and they shall exult all day in your name, and in your righteousness they shall be exalted. [Col. 1232D] P. Jerusalem rejoiced. V\. Glory and honor to the Father. P. Jerusalem rejoiced.

May the Lord be always with you. R\. And with you.

Antiphon. Blessed and worthy of great honor are those whose portion is God. P. For the kingdom was prepared for them from the beginning. P. And the souls of these are in the hand of God. V\. The just cried out, and the Lord heard them, and delivered them from all their tribulations. P. And the souls of these. V\. Glory and honor. P. And the souls of these.

May the Lord be always with you. R\. And with you.

Lauda. The kingdom prepared for the saints by the Most High: he himself feeds them. P. And he gave them a mountain sprouting roses and lilies. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V\. Those who trust in the Lord are like Mount Zion: he shall not be shaken for ever, who dwells in Jerusalem. P. And he gave them. V\. Glory and honor. P. And he gave them.

### Hymn

Christ, true King of the saints,  
And consecrator of martyrs,  
You are the truth and the way,  
And the life of believers.  

To those who ask, you grant their desire,  
And to the blessed their prize;  
The whole choir of the faithful  
Pours forth vows of praise to you.  

You granted Servandus and Germanus  
Exceeding strength at once,  
So that in combat they might conquer  
The Devil.  

For the worldly governor  
Commands them to go to the altar:  
“To sacrifice to empty idols,  
You strong soldiers of Christ,  
And to offer up the harmful victims  
In sacrificial blood.”  

They awaited punishments,  
Undaunted by love of Christ:  
It was sweet for them then to be burned,  
Sweet to endure the sword,  
And to offer their bodies  
To mighty punishments.  

We, confessing Christ,  
Abominate idols;  
And worshiping heavenly things,  
We despise earthly things.  
Far be it that, in profane ritual,  
We should bow our bodies.  

As they said these things,  
The martyrs were overwhelmed by a thousand punishments:  
A harsh restraint bent and bound  
Both their hands;  
And rubbed bronze encircled  
Their necks with cruel rings.  

Through the broad wound  
The noble gate is opened to the just;  
Christ gathers them, now made white,  
Into his companies;  
He mingles them with the choirs of angels  
And crowns them with rewards.  

Stand now, all hymn-singers,  
With voice, vows, and gift;  
Let the voice of all resound  
In praise of the saints.  
May this day and feast for us  
Be consecrated joy.  

May glory to God the Father  
Resound in the highest;  
Let us sing glory to Christ  
And to the Holy Spirit,  
To whom belong praise and power  
Through everlasting ages.  

Amen.

[Col. 1234A] Supplication. Let us pray, as above.

Capitula. On this day of the passion of your martyrs Servandus and Germanus, O Christ God, we rejoice and earnestly ask you to grant forgiveness for our offenses. We beseech you: just as you did not terrify their steadfastness by the punishment of the sword, so, through their intercession, wash away our crimes and receive our petitions.

Our Father. Delivered from evil. Fol. 2.

Benediction. Through the prayer of Servandus, may Christ the Lord preserve you in fear of his name; and through the intercession of Germanus may he cause you to germinate with the multiplied seed of righteousness. R\. Amen. May you also flourish together through the instrument and aid of these saints, who, though divided in body, enjoy the undivided presence of truth. R\. Amen. May you, in imitation of them, lovingly receive the divine yoke upon your necks, just as they were deemed worthy to receive the sword for the Lord. R\. Amen.

Through [your] mercy.

Lauda. Receive the joy of your glory, alleluia. P. Giving thanks to God, who called you to the heavenly kingdoms. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V\. Come, children, hear me; I shall teach you the fear of the Lord. P. Giving thanks. V\. Glory and honor. P. Giving thanks.

Prayer. O God, who gave your saints Servandus and Germanus such great grace in their passion that they notably overcame the enemy openly through faith—those who had first conquered, spiritually within themselves, the battles of their own bodies—grant us the firmest help from your goodness. Armed and girded by it, may we restrain the flesh that rebels against the spirit, and prepare ourselves fearlessly for spiritual battles. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

### At Matins

Antiphon. Give us. Psalm 50. Prayer. Restore to us. Fol. CLXIII.

Antiphon. Your saints, O Lord, have accomplished a wondrous journey, serving your commands, so that they might be found unharmed in mighty water. [CCCXIV] P. The earth appeared dry, and in the Red Sea there was a way without impediment. V\. Let them confess to the Lord his mercies, and his wonders to the children of men. P. The earth. V\. Glory and honor. P. The earth.

Prayer. O God, who [did so] for your saints Servandus, as above.

Antiphon. The Lord gave them the power of a kingdom against those who persecuted them. P. And he was a covering for them by day, and in the light of the stars throughout the night. V\. He sent his word and healed them, and delivered them from their destruction. P. And he was. V\. Glory and honor to the Father. P. And he was.

Prayer. Christ, Son of God, who are pleased more by contrition of heart than by the offering of gifts: look, O God, upon the prayers of your servants, so that on this day, when the aforesaid martyrs were cut down for you by the sharp edge of a flashing sword, the aforesaid martyrs may bestow upon us, as we seek them from you in both respects, suitable remedies. R\. Amen.

Antiphon. Come to me, all my saints, says the Lord; harvest the fruit of your labors, the growth of righteousness. P. Its fragrance is great, like the fragrance of lilies and roses in their season. V\. Come, children, hear me; I shall teach you the fear of the Lord. P. Its fragrance. V\. Glory and honor. P. Its fragrance.

Prayer. O God, in whose sight the commemoration has been celebrated: you place in separate regions the bodies of your martyrs, burning with the reward of one undivided glory; you give Servandus to the land of Gades and entrust Germanus to the citizens of Emerita. Grant that, enlightened by the light of your grace, though separated bodily, we may retain unity in sweetness and, gathered into one, overflow with the gift of charity. R\. Amen.

Through [your] mercy.

R\. The saints traveled through deserts where no one dwelt; in hidden places they fixed their camps; they took vengeance on their enemies. P. They thirsted and called upon you, and water was given them from the highest rock. V\. He gave them the bread of heaven; they ate the bread of angels. P. They thirsted. V\. Glory and honor. P. They thirsted.

### At Lauds

For the Canticle. Antiphon. Those who by their own will … Canticle. You who willingly offered yourselves. Fol. CLXIII.

For the Benedictus. Antiphon. Just men and priests, holy and humble of heart, bless the Lord.

Canticle. Blessed are you.

Tone. The way of the just. Lauda. Praise the Lord. Psalm 148.

Reading from the Book of the Wisdom of Solomon (Chapter XI).

R\. Thanks be to God.

The saints traveled through deserts where no one dwells, [Col. 1235C] and in hidden places they fixed their camps. They stood against their enemies and took vengeance on their foes. They thirsted and called upon you, and water was given them from the highest rock, and relief from thirst from a hard stone. He repaid the just for their labors, led them by a wondrous way, and was their covering by day and the light of the stars throughout the night. He brought them across the Red Sea and carried them through abundant water. He drowned their enemies in the sea and brought them up from the depths of the underworld. Therefore the just carried off the spoils of the ungodly, and sang, O Lord, your holy name, and together praised your victorious hand. R\. Amen.

Hymn. Christ, true King of the saints. Supplication. Let us pray to the Redeemer. [Col. 1235D] Capitula. On this day of your own. Lauda. Receive. Benediction. Through the prayer of Servandus. At the preceding Vespers.

## The Twenty-Seventh: Feast of Saints Vincent, Sabina, and Chrysteta, Martyrs

Everything is to be said as for several martyrs, “sex capparum” [reading uncertain], Fol. CLXII, except the following hymn.

### Hymn

Here the Lord of virtues  
Kindly summons you, devout people,  
To the halls of his witnesses.  
Bring fervent vows with offerings  
To the innermost places of heaven.  

Joined to the martyrs,  
Join your joys;  
Let a devout voice hold  
The gifts of Vincent.  
Let the heavenly writing celebrate Sabina;  
[May] Chrysteta [attain]  
The blessed heavens.  

They despise the miserable gains  
Of this world and the treacheries  
Of suffering men, through difficult victories.  
They strike their crimsoned necks  
Everywhere, crowned with laurel  
For you, Christ the King.  

Simple and Trinity,  
God and Unity,  
We ask you to hear  
What we ourselves seek through their prayers.  
Prolong, O immeasurably good one,  
Our fervent hearts.  

May there be glory to you,  
Triune Divinity,  
Who, while remaining one,  
Judge and hold all things,  
Continuing generously  
Through endless ages.  
And may you prosper us still further.  

Amen.

## The Twenty-Eighth: Feast of the Apostles Simon and Jude

### At Vespers

Lauda. It has arisen in darkness. Tone. Alleluia. Into all the earth. See Fol. CLXXVII.

### Hymn

Go forth, peoples; sing swiftly:  
Jude and his companion Simon, unmarried,  
Let them go into renowned assemblies  
For the feast, now granting joys  
To all their servants.  

Behold, the voice of the young prince resounds.  
At once, servants, render  
The vows that you promise to the Lord,  
So that your illustrious Apostles  
May receive your offering.  

Now let us bring forth a worthy song  
In prayers,  
And worthily embrace the Prince of heaven.  
May he now mercifully give grace  
To his peoples,  
And grant them afterward  
To attain the heavenly homeland.  

And, with the bond of sins already handed over,  
May they be able to stand before  
The heavenly Prince;  
And, with guilt removed and the path made passable,  
May they remain rightly inspired  
By the Paraclete.  

Thus may the people be instructed by Jude,  
And may Simon run beneath gentle Christ  
Along the way,  
Keeping the commandments prescribed by the laws,  
So that they may attain the highest rewards.  

May glory be to the triune and only Lord,  
To the Father with the Son  
And the Paraclete,  
Who alone is the Triune and One Lord,  
Strongly encompassing the ages of ages.  

Amen.

Supplication. Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world, as in the other offices.

Capitula. O God, glory of the saints and abundant in mercy, hear your suppliant people, who beseech you through the intercession of the saints. Govern us through the alternating cycles of the seasons, and guard us with equal protection through the differing succession of days and nights, so that, aided by the prayers of your saints, the Apostles Simon and Jude, through whose mercy we have passed this day prosperously, we may also pass this night pleasing to you in purity of soul and body.

Our Father. And lead us not. Delivered from evil. Fol. 2.

Benediction. May the Lord fortify you with the patronage of his saints, the Apostles Simon and Jude, and cleanse you from sin. R\. Amen. May he make you happy through their intercession, you who are now serving their solemnities. R\. Amen. May you deserve to enter heaven together with them, whose triumph you now celebrate on earth. R\. Amen.

Through [your] mercy.

Lauda. You are holy vessels for the Lord, shining with gold, alleluia. P. Because you willingly offered your souls to the Lord God. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V\. Hear, O my people, and I will testify to you: Israel, if you will hear me. P. Because you willingly. V\. Glory and honor. P. Because.

Prayer. O God, who granted your holy Apostles Simon and Jude both the desire and the ability to climb the difficult step of martyrdom—(you give the beginning of the will, you bestow the accomplishment of the deed)—hear us, your servants, and give us the beginning of fervent devotion and grant the effect of a good completion. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

### At Matins

Antiphon. Give us. Psalm 50. Prayer. Restore to us. See Fol. CLXIII.

Antiphon. Your friends, O God, have been honored; their authority has been greatly strengthened. P. I shall number them, and they shall be multiplied beyond the sand. V\. Behold, O Lord, you have known all things, the latest and the ancient; you formed me and placed your hand upon me. P. I shall number them. V\. Glory and honor to the Father. P. I shall number them.

[Col. 1237C] Prayer. O God, beneath whose altar the souls of the holy Apostles Simon and Jude rest peacefully and receive the robe of charity, do you, the faithful Promiser, also join us, your servants, to the number of their fellow soldiers, so that at least our life may attain mercy, if death does not bring us to the crown. R\. Amen.

Through [your] mercy.

Antiphon. These are your friends, O Lord, who handed over their bodies to death. P. So that they might not serve idols or worship foreign gods. V\. They shall walk, O Lord, in the light of your countenance, and they shall exult all day in your name; and in your righteousness they shall be exalted. P. So that they might not serve. V\. Glory and honor. P. So that they might not serve.

Prayer. O God, who [did so] for the saints, as above. Antiphon 3. They fought manfully. Fol. CCLVI.

Prayer. O God, honor and glory of all the saints, to whom you granted a reward when they fought and supplied strength so that they might conquer: we ask your holy clemency to make us, your humble servants, delivered from every evil, companions of their footsteps. R\. Amen.

Through [your] mercy.

Responsory. They displayed the sacred rites. Fol. CCLVI.

### At Lauds

For the Canticle. Antiphon. Those who by their own will … Canticle. You who willingly offered yourselves. Fol. CLXIII. For the Benedictus. Antiphon. Just men and priests. Canticle. Blessed are you, O Lord. Tone. Alleluia. Into all the earth. Fol. CLXXVIII. Lauda. Praise the Lord. Psalm 148. Prophecy. Great glory. Fol. CCXXVI. Hymn. Go forth, peoples. Supplication. Let us pray to the Redeemer. See at the preceding Vespers.

Capitula. These are, O Lord, the truthful patrons who, receiving their sentence with confidence, run rejoicing toward the palm and hasten gladly toward the crown. Through their intercession, O Lord God almighty, just as you made your martyrs and Apostles Simon and Jude free from the Devil’s deception, so make us, your unworthy servants, attain their mercy.

Our Father. Delivered from evil. Fol. 2.

[Col. 1238B] Lauda. You are. Fol. CLXXVIII. Benediction. Of his saints, as above at the preceding Vespers.

At the concluding Vespers, everything is to be said as at the first Vespers, except the Capitula and Benediction.

Capitula. Lord Jesus Christ, who deign to be mercifully present when we assemble in honor of your holy Apostles and martyrs Simon and Jude, make us followers of their teaching; make us lovable and teachable, so that we may be found unharmed by those whom we know to have been outstanding leaders of the faith. May our hope of glory have its reward with them, who, after shining with the teaching of masters, deserved to obtain it through martyrdom. May the Church shine with the teaching of those whose glorious preaching is held within her. Let those who were wondrous teachers of the Church be present as helpers to us in our miseries. May those who became outstanding through teaching raise the fallen to repentance. May those who founded the Church by their teachings obtain forgiveness of crimes for sinners, so that we, who have been stirred by their victories and celebrate their solemnities, may, freed from crimes by their merits, come to you after our passage from this life.

Our Father. Delivered from evil. Fol. 2.

Benediction. May Christ, the only-begotten Son of God the Father, who gave his holy Apostles Simon and Jude power to command demons, deign to protect you by grace and fortify you by the Holy Spirit. R\. Amen. And may he who gave them the power, after despising riches, to seek temporal poverty, command that you be led happily from this present and temporal life to the blessed life. R\. Amen. May you, who recall the memory of his saints for love of him, rejoice afterward before him with those same saints in the heavenly places. R\. Amen. With the same Lord Jesus Christ, who with the Father and the Holy Spirit rules all things for ever and ever. R\. Amen.

Through [your] mercy.

## The Thirtieth: Feast of Saint Marcellus, Martyr

Everything is to be said as for one martyr, except the following hymn.

### Hymn

The feast of the blessed martyr  
Marcellus shines forth. Come, peoples;  
Let us make the hymn of God resound  
With a single voice.  

He teaches citizens and following peoples  
To put on Christ, to flee what passes away,  
And throughout all time  
To subdue the shameful things of the spirit  
By devotion.  

He rejected pomp and shunned honors;  
And while he was regarded as a fierce soldier,  
He withdrew at close hand  
From the royal commands imposed upon him.  

He seized the sword of his mind,  
Strong in a consecrated gift;  
With swift flight he traversed earthly things,  
Conquering all for the Lord of thunder.  

Rightly contrite, he arms his soul;  
Taught by the Spirit, he overcomes  
The profane judge. Gentle in speech,  
He eagerly desires to pour out his blood.  

From that time the upright servant  
Of the Lord of thunder stands firm  
With the strength of his mind in prayer.  
The Lord knows his vows  
And answers them with powerful purpose.  

He despises lofty honors  
And fleeting wealth, shining  
With the brightness of his spirit;  
And celebrating his vows to Christ,  
He holds thanksgiving in his breast.  

Preferring to become a citizen  
With a heavenly mind and religious devotion,  
Let him dedicate himself entirely  
To the Lord of heaven,  
Who remains throughout every age.  

Behold, he who was ordered  
To defend his homeland threw down his weapons;  
He rejoices to be the servant  
Of the eternal Lord,  
Resounding with consecrated songs  
To Christ.  

Then the raging tyrant cries out:  
“Is this Marcellus, who despises  
My commands and thinks weapons  
Must be renounced?  
Is he not to be handed over to death?”  

From then the joyful voice  
Of the blessed servant Marcellus  
Began to resound with Christ;  
And he asks that it may come well  
To the savage governor himself.  

For praise is not [enough],  
And it is sought in words;  
The martyr resounds through the merit  
Of his blood.  
Speech has no power;  
Let the soul repay the gifts of praise.  

Although this understanding remains keen  
And all the strength of the mind is present,  
What a gift is nevertheless given  
To the saints in the future age!  

No human being clothed  
In fragile flesh can ever speak of it;  
Blessed is he who, leaving the confines  
Of the flesh, rises again  
With Christ as judge.  

Therefore, with gentle voices,  
We all ask you, O God,  
And with humble mind:  
In your mercy grant rest to the dead  
And joys to the living.  

Grant that, without guilt,  
We may celebrate the feast  
Of the blessed servant Marcellus,  
And together praise you  
For ever with sweet hymns.  

Thus extend forgiveness  
To your singing people,  
That you may pardon our crimes,  
And, through the prayer of the witness  
Marcellus, open  
The hidden things of heaven.  

May there always be one honor  
To you, loving Father,  
And to you, Christ;  
And to you, one God who encompasses  
All things,  
Through ages of ages.  

Amen.

On the Sunday of the Kalends of November. See in the Sunday Office, Fol. 429.

The office of fasting on the Kalends of November is observed three days before the Feast of Saint Martin. See at the end of the Sunday Office, Fol. 441.

# November Feasts

## The Eleventh: Feast of Saint Martin, Bishop

### At Vespers

Lauda. Confession and beauty. Tone. I will confess to you. Antiphon. I will confess to you, O Lord, with my whole … Fol. CLXIX. Lauda. I will confess to the Lord. Fol. CLXXIII.

### Hymn

Martin, confessor of God,  
Strong in the vigor of the spirit,  
Fading in the limbs of the flesh,  
Aware of approaching death;  

You who abound in the peace of Christ,  
In the unity of the Spirit,  
Restore the divided members  
Of the Church to a single peace.  

Life makes you worthy of praise;  
Bloody death does not weary you,  
When at the hour of death  
You overcome the crafty one’s deceit.  

This people, most ready in faith,  
Honors the joys of your day  
With faithful vows;  
Be gentle and present to all.  

Through you may there be rest for the seasons;  
May comfort be given to life;  
May the benefit of peace overflow;  
May every scandal be brought to rest.  

That we may thus abound  
In the Spirit’s charity toward one another,  
So that with our hearts and deepest sighs  
We may follow Christ.  

To God the Father be glory,  
And to his only Son,  
With the Spirit, the Paraclete,  
Who reigns through every age.  

Amen.

Supplication. Let us pray to the Redeemer, with the name changed. Fol. CLXXXVII.

Capitula. Blessed is that wondrous confessor of yours, O Lord, your Martin, who, by thinking of the poor man, deserved to attain the final reward; and therefore he was saved on the evil day, because you, O Lord, helped him. Grant us, then, through his intercession, that when we see our nakedness we may fly to the shelter of your protection; and thus may we be clothed with the gift of virtues, that we may deserve to become participants in him whose feast we now celebrate.

Our Father. Delivered from evil. Fol. 2.

Benediction. May Christ the Lord, who adorned the most blessed Martin with the honor of confession, grant you that confession which extinguishes sins. R\. Amen. And may he who through Martin satisfied the need of the poor himself receive, through him, the vows of peoples that deserve reward. R\. Amen. May the vows of the faithful be rewarded through the intercession of him by whose generosity the weakness of the needy was restored. R\. Amen.

Through [your] mercy.

Lauda. Your bones shall spring up. Fol. CLXX.

[Col. 1241B] Prayer. All day long, O Lord, your just man shows mercy and lends; throughout the whole course of this mortal life he gives temporal things so that he may receive eternal things. May his seed bear fruit among us in blessing, so that, possessing a share in his merits, we may also deserve to participate in his rewards. R\. Amen.

Through [your] mercy.

### At Matins

Antiphon. O Lord, my lips. Psalm 50. Prayer. May our tongue praise you, O Lord. Fol. CLXI. Antiphon. My flesh shall rest. Fol. CLXX.

Prayer. The man who, inspired by you, O Christ, shows mercy and lends is exceedingly pleasing, O Lord; and we believe that your confessor Martin wonderfully fulfilled this, since, devoted to a twofold almsgiving, he both nourished bodies with gifts and hearts with speech. Therefore, weeping, we ask and beseech you that, strengthened by both gifts in this life, we may one day reach you at our passage from this life to be crowned. R\. Amen.

Through [your] mercy.

Antiphon. Your face is like … Fol. CLXVI.

Prayer. His righteousness remains for ever and ever, whose mercy has poured itself out in the consolation of the poor. Therefore make us imitators of your confessor Martin, so that, first becoming merciful ourselves, granting fitting alms to us, we may both refrain from evil deeds and bestow upon our neighbors the good that we can. R\. Amen.

Through [your] mercy.

[Col. 1241D] Antiphon. You have guarded my body. Fol. CLXXI.

Prayer. Jesus, our God and Lord, who made the confessor and bishop Martin illustrious in merits and so guarded his wisdom that he deserved to remain in glory and joy: grant us understanding of true wisdom and zeal for holy action, so that, distributing our substance to the poor, we may escape the vengeance for our crimes. R\. Amen.

Through [your] mercy.

Responsory. Behold, O Lord, with his whole … Fol. CLXXI.

Prayer. Behold, O Lord, your confessor Martin confesses and believes that you alone are in his whole heart, as he tells of the love of your faith conceived within him through confession and declares your wonders with devoted mouth. Make us therefore rejoice and exult in you continually and openly, so that after our trials we may have rest in you, in whom he deserved to find his reward after his confession. R\. Amen.

Through [your] mercy.

### At Lauds

For the Canticle. Antiphon. I will confess to you, O Lord. Canticle. I will confess to you, Lord King. Fol. CLXXI.

Prayer. Make us, O Lord, pass day and night with attentive hearts in meditation on your law, so that, meditating on your words with devoted attention of heart, we may return fruit to you at the fitting time. Then, aided by the intercession of your most blessed confessor Martin, may you make us enter the heaven which he acquired by his merits, through the gifts of your grace. R\. Amen.

Through [your] mercy.

[Col. 1242B] For the Benedictus. Antiphon. Blessing, O Lord. Canticle. Blessed are you, O Lord.

Tone. I shall sing in the sight of the angels. Lauda. Alleluia. His confession is above … Psalm 148. Prophecy. Thus says the Lord. Canticle. Behold my servant. Fol. CLXI. Hymn. Martin, confessor of God. Supplication. Let us pray to the Redeemer. See at the preceding Vespers.

Capitula. Behold, O Lord, that day approaches, clothed in the manifold beauty of joys, which the passing of your most blessed confessor Martin, the bishop, makes illustrious. Since, foreknowing his future death, he wished to enter heaven joyfully, he was seen to terrify the Devil opposing him by the wondrous power of his words. Therefore we humbly ask your goodness: through his intercession, may that same adversary always flee from us, so that while we live he may not overthrow us in any way, nor defile us in any manner when we die.

Our Father. Delivered from evil. Fol. 2.

Lauda. Your bones shall spring up. Fol. CLXX.

Benediction. Christ the Lord, as above at the preceding Vespers.

## The Twelfth: Feast of Saint Emilian, Abbot and Confessor

Everything is to be said as for one confessor, Fol. CLXXIII, except what follows.

### Hymn

O great Christ, renowned Ruler of all things,  
Whom the stars of Olympus continually obey,  
Grant us vows favorable to the yearly feasts,  
Pure and sober,  
Which may appease your mercy.  

Behold, the whole people fulfills  
Its duty as the days return,  
Prone in heart and body,  
Trusting in mind and imploring aid,  
So that indulgence in its goodness  
May lift up hearts weighed down by individual pleas.  

It returns joyful song  
With the harmonies of hymns;  
It composes a song with sonorous mouth and throat,  
Supplicating that your right hand,  
Powerfully removing shameful deeds,  
May correct our actions  
And be the helper within  
Of those who weep over their evils.  

We can always obtain, as we ask,  
The healing of our sickness,  
With our conduct cleansed,  
If you look upon us with kindness and mercy,  
You who have bestowed so much upon such little servants,  
So that this patron may lack nothing of grace.  

We, most wretched, openly confess our guilt;  
We do not believe that we shall lose our service,  
Since abundant power is nourished  
By the King,  
And the excellent Intercessor stands near,  
Who could bend harmful anger.  

May the enemy not feel  
That new misfortunes arise  
For the blessed companies through warfare;  
May the frail vessel not bring forth hatreds,  
Or be stirred by the devices  
Of fraud or deceit,  
Or cause flame to consume  
The modest lilies.  

While we turn these things over  
With fixed and clear mind,  
We delight to proclaim the dedicated servant,  
Your minister, Christ Jesus, your little servant;  
And as we compose the feast  
With mingled joys,  
May praise of you follow  
Throughout the whole day.  

You, Father, have sacred temples,  
You have heavenly places consecrated;  
You, God, possess the kingdom  
Through the ages,  
And are seen wondrous in the Holy of Holies,  
Ruling alone and displaying  
Wondrous deeds.  

Therefore we beseech you,  
By your gift, to cleanse us  
And restore us wholly, as you direct;  
Receive into heaven  
And place in the royal court  
Those already lost.  
You who grant that dead bodies rise again,  
Grant also that hearts may recover  
Through grace.  

We confess and reveal our guilt;  
May judgment destroy the restrained blows  
That gnaw at the dark conscience.  
You grant us to ask,  
When a favorable will reveals  
Your open mouth and door.  

No moments pass into time  
That are not stained by shameful sin.  
We ask that pollution may be anticipated,  
That a purification worthy of our worst deeds  
May follow,  
One that renders the punishment  
Due to our acts.  

We see the blind restored to light,  
And the lame leaping on swollen feet;  
Members consumed by wasting sickness  
Recover their strength;  
Those pressed down by the sleep of death  
Finally rise  
And then joyfully come together in safety.  

The twisted are driven away,  
And demons are put to flight,  
Howling under the torments  
And punishments of Tartarus.  
The deceitful angel approaches heaven  
And is secretly pierced by his own wound,  
And, wounded by his own weapons,  
Is crushed.  

Just as these are the open miracles  
Of the Creator,  
So may those limping through sickness of mind  
Be healed.  
May the most wicked serpent, driven away, depart;  
And may black hearts, clouded by the darkness  
Of sloth, shine most brightly  
In his radiance.  

This, surely, is the safest power: Christ,  
Who carried Emilian through the difficult  
Trophies of life,  
Who crowns him with a reward,  
So that he might be imitated  
In our age  
And become a strong advocate  
For the lowly.  

Sing hymns with me in harmonious song;  
Tell all things, proclaim them, and sing psalms  
To the eternal King, whose are all these things.  
Let the songs of our cry resound,  
And let the temples of heaven  
Echo with harmonies.  

Offer glory to the Most High and Sublime;  
Offer the greatest honor to the Trinity;  
Offer thanks to the Prince of the ages;  
Offer a psalm with voices or deeds;  
Offer praise through everlasting ages.  

Amen.

## The Seventeenth: Feast of Saint Acisclus and His Companions

### At Vespers

Lauda. It has arisen in darkness. Tone. Alleluia. The just shall live for ever. Fol. CLXII.

Antiphon. Behold the fragrance of my saints. P. Like the fragrance of a full field, which the Lord has blessed. V\. The Lord, God of gods, has spoken and called the earth, from the rising of the sun to its setting; from Zion comes the beauty of his splendor. P. Like the fragrance. V\. Glory and honor. P. Like the fragrance.

May the Lord be always with you. R\. And with you.

Lauda. Like pure lilies. Fol. CCLXXVI.

### Hymn

Rejoice, flowers of the martyrs;  
Hail, peoples of the nations.  
Send your vision through the stars;  
Hope for the sign of glory.  

The voices of the prophets sound;  
They announce that Jesus will come,  
The grace that goes before redemption,  
By which he redeemed us.  

Here our morning shines forth,  
And joyful hearts burn with fervor,  
When the faithful voice resounds,  
Foretelling glory.  

Let us now sing the joy  
Of so great a salvation,  
By which the world was redeemed,  
The renowned hymn of deliverance.  

His first coming was such  
That he would not come to punish the world,  
But to wipe away its wound,  
Saving what had perished.  

But now the second warns us  
That Christ is at the doors:  
To restore crowns to the saints  
And open the kingdoms of heaven.  

Eternal light is promised,  
And the saving star is revealed.  
May its radiance now help us  
And call us to the right  
Of the heavenly ones.  

We seek you alone, O Christ,  
To see you as you are, God,  
So that this joyful vision  
May snatch us from every Tartarus.  

When you, the Redeemer, come,  
With the white-robed company  
Of martyrs,  
May you then unite us, blessed,  
To their celibate assembly.  

To God the Father be glory,  
And to his only Son,  
With the Spirit, the Paraclete,  
Now and for ever.  

Amen.

Supplication. Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world, with the name changed. Fol. CLXXXVII.

## Chapters

Lord God Almighty, who by the glorious gift of your ordering dispose all things before the ages, which you will proceed in ordered course throughout the ages; since from yourself, before all times, you will bring forth the only Son coeternal, coequal, almighty, and consubstantial with you; whom at the end of the ages you show visibly as man to human eyes, so that by his humility you might restore to heaven the human race which the devil’s deceit had driven from paradise; whom you appointed to unite the Church to himself as a bridegroom proceeding from the bridal chamber; from whose womb you gather together the assembled companies of the saints like roses, or lilies of martyrs, confessors, and virgins; who, pleasing you through you and fulfilling your commands, regarding the whole world as nothing, were slain in body for your sake: grant that through the merits of the holy souls of Acisclus and Victoria, whose annual feast we receive in succession, we may obtain everlasting rewards.

And because the fragrance of your majesty, wonderfully sweet-smelling, now invites us to receive that desirable feast of your advent, we ask in prayer and earnestly entreat with repeated supplication that we may celebrate the joys begun by your advent on the appointed days with hymns, songs, psalms, and the modulation of our voices, so that we may approach the holy day of the Nativity of your Son with the stains of our sins cleansed and with the fruit of good works.

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” Folio 2.

Blessing. May God the Father Almighty, who is the fountain and source of all divinity, reward you with the prize of eternal salvation. R. Amen. May Jesus Christ, the Son of God, who is coequal with the Father and the Holy Spirit, command that you be cleansed from every sin. R. Amen. May the Holy Spirit also, who is the holiness of the Father and the Son, fill you with the grace of his name. R. Amen.

Through his mercy.

Lauda. “Everlasting joy.” Folio CLXII.

Prayer. O God, who promise to the holy and glorious martyrs Acisclus and Victoria that holy Jerusalem, the vision of peace, where they may possess everlasting blessedness with the greatest consolation, so that they may rejoice in seeing it and that those joys themselves may remain infinite in them: grant us, through their intercession, both to enjoy the blessedness of that holy vision and to be refreshed by spiritual joy in eternal rest; so that, just as their bones—which are the virtues of their souls—spring green again like plants when others, stirred by their examples, obtain the merits of holiness through holy desires, so we too, following their footsteps, may reach everlasting joys. R. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

## At Matins

[Col. 1246A]

Antiphon. Grant us the joy of your salvation, and strengthen us, Lord, with a princely spirit. Psalm L.

Prayer. Restore to us the joy of your salvation. See folio CLXIII.

Antiphon. The Lord will come from Sinai, and with him thousands of saints. In his right hand is the fiery law. All the saints are in his hand. P. And those who draw near to his feet will receive his teaching. V. God will come openly: our God, and he will not be silent. P. And those who draw near. V. Glory and honor to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. P. And those who draw near.

Prayer. Make us flourish, Lord, like pure lilies in the courts of your house, and present the fragrance of good works to the faithful as an example of devout conduct; so that, relying on the protection of your saints Acisclus and Victoria, we may escape the snares of the enemy and deserve to obtain eternal blessedness with all the saints and elect. R. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

Antiphon. There will be great joy for all people, says the Lord. P. For behold, I am coming, that I may be glorified in the midst of my saints. V. Behold, the eyes of the Lord are upon those who fear him, and upon those who hope in his mercy. P. For behold, I am coming. V. Glory and honor to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. P. For behold.

Prayer. With great exultation, Lord, we await seeing the glory of your majesty, in which the saints have been received, so that, although unworthy, we may enjoy the blessedness of your kingdom with them; and since we truly know that they are blessed because they fulfilled the commandment of your law, make us free from our sins through their merits. Just as their souls, gathered in your holy storehouses, rest there with great joy, so may we also, through their intercessions, deserve to be consoled by the reward of everlasting blessedness. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Antiphon. I will await your holy name, Lord. P. For it is good in the sight of all your saints. V. For who among the clouds can be compared with the Lord, or who is like God among the sons of God? P. For it is good. V. Glory and honor. P. For it is good.

Prayer. O God, who [didst grant] to the holy and glorious martyrs. See in the preceding Vespers.

Antiphon. The Lord will come from Sinai; he will descend upon Mount Paran and will appear alone from the East. Before him goes the army of angels, and with him thousands of saints. P. Carrying the law in his right hand, so that all may receive his teaching. He will proceed from his bridal chamber like a bridegroom, by whose blessing the whole earth bears fruit. V. He rejoiced like a giant to run his course from the summit of heaven. P. The law in his right hand. V. Glory and honor to the Father. P. The law.

Prayer. Hearing from the prophetic oracles that you, Lord, will come from Sinai with thousands of saints, we entreat you: since we already believe that you came for the redemption of the world, grant that we may also await with purified hearts your coming for judgment; so that, since a great recompense for the saints rests in your hand, the return of sinners to you may be increased through the remedy of your mercy, and thus, drawing near to your feet, we may always be filled with the teaching of inward vision. R. Amen.

Through [your mercy].

Antiphon. They will see with exultation the great glory of God, who received the righteous, because while living they kept the law. P. Now their souls, gathered in his storehouses, rest in profound silence. V. The righteous cried out, and the Lord heard them, and delivered them from all their tribulations. P. Now. V. Glory and honor. P. Now.

Prayer. O God, Son of God, whom all the saints, awaiting him with great exultation, will see in that glory in which you are like the Father in nature: as we devoutly celebrate the solemn feast of your saints Acisclus and his companions, erase the records of our sins; so that, having begun on this day the joys of your advent, we may deserve after our passing to rejoice with them in that future blessedness in our homeland. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Antiphon. The saints will possess joy and gladness; sorrow and sighing will flee from them. P. I, the Lord, will console them. Alleluia. V. Blessed are the undefiled in the way, who walk in the law of the Lord. P. I, the Lord. V. Glory and honor to the Father. P. I, the Lord.

Prayer. O Christ, Son of God, what great joy of everlasting gladness you grant your saints after bitter grief, allowing them to behold your sweetness, where sorrow and sighing have no place: finally grant us, though unworthy, the remedy of consolation; so that we who have been separated from you through guilt may deserve to be gathered among the assemblies of the saints and obtain infinite gladness with them. R. Amen.

Through [your mercy].

Antiphon. Hear, all peoples, for the Lord will go forth from his place. P. And he will descend, trampling the ends of the earth. V. Hear this, all nations; perceive it with your ears, you who inhabit the world. P. And. V. Glory and honor. P. And.

Prayer. We have heard, Christ, we confess and believe that, proceeding from the Father’s bosom, you came to be clothed in our flesh, in order to free—through the mystery of the Incarnation you assumed—that which had perished through the contagion of corrupted nature. Therefore make us receive the proclaimed joys of your advent with the most ready devotion of welcome; and since, proceeding secretly from your fatherland, you hastened into public view to save human beings, grant that we, coming forth from the place of sin, may look upon the swift arrival of your divinity in greater purity; so that, while you do not involve the ends of our life in the trampling of any danger, you may arouse us by the terror of justice and justify us by your accustomed mercy. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Antiphon. Blessed are those servants whom, when the Lord comes, he finds watching. P. Amen, I say to you, he will gird himself and serve them. Alleluia. V. And if he comes in the second or third watch and finds them watching. P. Amen, I say. V. Glory and honor. P. Amen, I say.

Prayer. Truly blessed, Lord, and worthy of great honor are those servants whom the advent of your Son finds watching as they meditate upon the law. Therefore we ask you, almighty Father, that, awakened from sleep, we may await seeing his face as it truly is, everywhere without fear; and although, as our merits demand, we are not worthy to obtain his grace, nevertheless, through the intervention of your saints whose solemn feast we celebrate today, may we rise here to life in good works and there escape the avenging wrath of that eternal Judge himself. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

## At Lauds

[Col. 1248B]

For the Canticle. Antiphon. The Lord appeared from Mount Paran, and with him thousands of saints.

Canticle. The Lord came from Sinai.

Prayer. “That you have come, Lord.” Folio CLXVI.

For the Benedictus. Antiphon. Holy and humble.

Canticle. “Blessed are you.” Folio 6.

Prayer. We look, Lord, and now, with the eye of faith purified, we see that indescribable joy which shone forth from you, Lord, in the bestowal of your gift upon the city of Jerusalem, your city looking toward the East; and therefore we ask that you, who placed it first through the joys of your Incarnation, preserve us unharmed in its bosom from the contagion of every offense, so that there both the dignity of our works may save us and the expectation of your advent may justify us without end. R. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

Sono. “The way of the righteous.” Lauda. “Alleluia. Praise the Lord.” Psalm CXLVIII. Prophecy. “The souls of the righteous.” Folio CLXVII. Hymn. “Rejoice, flowers of the martyrs.” Supplication. “Let us pray.” Back in the Vespers.

Chapters. Christ, your precious fragrance burns among the nations: by it you seek earthly things and do not abandon heavenly ones; by it you make those banished far away in foreign regions run after you at the news of good things, after the fragrance of your ointments. Grant, therefore, that what we perceive by faith in this fragrance we may receive as an eternal gift, so that because we sing of you with the affections of our voices, we may rejoice most fully in the reward of the righteous.

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” Folio 2.

[Col. 1248D]

Lauda. “Everlasting joy.” Blessing. “God the Father Almighty.” In the preceding Vespers.

# The Eighteenth Day: Feast of Saint Romanus the Martyr

## At Vespers

Lauda. “It has risen.” Sono. “The souls of the righteous.” Folio CLXII.

Antiphon. Rejoice, because your names are written in heaven. P. Blessed are the eyes that see what you see, and the ears that hear what you hear. V. Blessed are those who keep judgment and practice righteousness at all times. P. Blessed. V. Glory and honor. P. Blessed.

Lauda. “I will require the blood of the saints.” Folio CLXII.

### Hymn

Romanus, strong champion of Christ our God,  
O patron, move the instrument of my speechless mouth;  
grant an adorned and most auspicious song,  
and make me sing the wonders of your praises.

You yourself know how even the mute can speak:  
the cruel torturer tore away  
the plectrum of your palate and your throat;  
yet he did not impose silence  
on the mouth by which you confessed God.

The voice of truth cannot be extinguished;  
even if it pulses through severed passages,  
the tongue never failed to speak of Christ  
when Christ himself, the giver of words, is proclaimed.

Now, holy martyr, the feeble people ask you:  
cleanse away our stains, drive out dreadful sins;  
with worthy dew suppress the fires of hell,  
and draw us, blessed, toward the heights.

Honor and glory be to the eternal God,  
to the one Father and to his only Son,  
with the Spirit; may this Trinity  
live in power throughout the ages of ages.

Amen.

Supplication. “Let us pray,” as above.

Chapters. Celebrating the victories of your most beloved servant, the blessed Romanus, Christ our God—through which he did not allow the enemy of the Christian faith to enter the lights of your temple—we ask and entreat you: through him open Paradise to us, through whom you shut the entrance of your Church to unbelievers; so that through him by whom the unbelief of the faithless was repelled, our faith may reach the crown, most merciful Lord.

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” Folio 2.

Blessing. May Christ the Lord, who wonderfully made his tongue-less martyr Romanus eloquent, always make your mouth fruitful for himself. R. Amen. And may he who, after the cutting off of his tongue, formed in him words aflame, grant you gifts of virtues after your confession with your mouth. R. Amen. May you, always possessing the office of a disciplined mouth, deserve in the same tongue with which you confess your sins to God also to obtain the forgiveness of all sins. R. Amen.

Through his mercy.

Lauda. “Everlasting joy.” Folio CLXII.

Prayer. May almighty God, who through the blessed Romanus closed the doors of the Church to unbelievers, open the barriers of his kingdom to us who believe; and may he who revealed through the office of his tongue-less mouth his praise receive his intercession for the cleansing of your sins, so that in him, through whom the faith of the little Theodulus completed its martyrdom, you too may have an everlasting reward. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

## At Matins

Antiphon. “Grant us the joy.” Psalm L. Prayer. “Restore to us.” Folio CLXIII.

Antiphon. “I will establish an everlasting covenant with my saints,” says the Lord, “and their offspring will be known among the nations.” P. For these are the seed whom the Lord has blessed. V. Blessed are those whose iniquities are forgiven and whose sins are covered. P. For these. V. Glory and honor to the Father. P. For these are.

Prayer. Holy Lord, in whose love we rejoice in the devout confession of your martyr Romanus, we pray and ask you: since for the sake of your servant David you do not turn away the face of your Christ, for our sake, your servants, do not delay the intercession of your saints. R. Amen.

Through [your mercy].

Antiphon. I will give the saints glory and make them renowned throughout the whole earth, says the Lord. P. And they will not be confounded at that time, when I have done good to them. V. They will speak of the glory of your kingdom and declare your power. P. And they will not. V. Glory and honor to the Father. P. And they will not.

[Col. 1250B]

Prayer. Lord, we faithfully and humbly invoke you in love for your saints Romanus and his companions: may your mercy be present for those who fear you, bringing salvation which is poured out in power upon those who love you; may he who perfected the course of vocation in the least complete it, who fulfilled the fruit of love in the saints. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Antiphon. I will give my saints a kingdom in Jerusalem, for the tree of life will be theirs as an ointment’s fragrance. P. And they will not labor or grow weary. Alleluia. V. Blessed are the undefiled in the way, who walk in the law of the Lord. P. And they will not. V. Glory and honor. P. And they will not.

Prayer. O almighty God, life of the saints and vivifier of all the faithful, enliven our souls; and since you help those who serve you by your gifts and crown those who conquer, through the intercession of the holy martyrs Romanus and his companions, we ask that you always sanctify us by your will and strengthen us by the abundance of your mercy. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

R. Behold, the Lord will come, and all his saints with him; and on that day there will be great light, and pure water will go forth from Jerusalem. P. And the Lord will reign forever over the whole earth. V. The Lord will come in the clouds, and every eye will see him. P. And he will reign. V. Glory and honor. P. And he will reign.

Prayer. Almighty God, who… In the preceding Vespers.

## At Lauds

For the Canticle. Antiphon. “All the saints.” Canticle. “The Lord came from Sinai.” Prayer. “That you have come, Lord.” For the Benedictus. Antiphon. “Holy and humble.” Sono. “The way of the righteous.” Lauda. “Praise the Lord.” Psalm CXLVIII. Prophecy. “The souls of the righteous.” See folio CLXVII. Hymn. “Romanus, strong champion,” as above. Supplication. “Let us pray to the Redeemer.” Folio 2.

Chapters. O God, who specially granted this gift of grace to your most blessed martyr Romanus, that after the cutting off of his bodily tongue he might proclaim you, the giver of words, more effectively and more abundantly: we humbly ask you to make the instrument of our tongue always serve your laws, so that, devoted only to holy duties, it may always serve you with a devotion pleasing to you.

[Col. 1251A]

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” Folio 2.

Lauda. “Everlasting joy.” Folio CLXII. Blessing. “Christ the Lord, who made the tongue-less man…” In the preceding Vespers.

# The Nineteenth Day: Feast of Saint Crispinus, Bishop and Confessor

Everything is to be said as for one confessor and bishop, folio CLXIX, except the hymn.

### Hymn

Let us praise the distinguished martyr of Christ, Crispinus,  
who washed his body in sacred blood;  
following the one God in the name of the Trinity,  
leaving the world and all its riches behind,  
he became a companion of the angels in God’s kingdom.

Not looking upon the flatteries of this age,  
but beholding the Lord, ruler of the world,  
he followed him with great joy  
and hastened happily to Paradise,  
swiftly repelling the unspeakable enemy.

He placed the sign of Christ upon his forehead,  
as the mercy of God himself taught him.  
Whenever the serpent wished to attack,  
he, with strong and courageous spirit,  
renounced the envious devil.

The true grace of almighty God  
granted Crispinus such steadfastness  
that prison, punishments, scourges, or fires,  
neither thirst nor hunger could disfigure his body,  
nor could they violate his faith.

And when the joyful soldier looked toward heaven,  
his neck prepared to receive the sword,  
and his blood was poured out as a consecration,  
his body was buried and laid in a tomb,  
and was restored to the city of Astigi.

To his sacred body the sick come;  
the lame, deaf, blind, and lunatic,  
confessing Christ, receive salvation;  
and they receive the true oracles  
and healing remedy of the holy martyr.

O gracious martyr, leading intercessor,  
intercede more often for our evils,  
that all our sins may be washed away;  
may he free our souls and our whole body  
from the snares of the pursuing enemy.

Most merciful Father, forgive us  
through the intercession of your holy martyr;  
erase hidden sins and release every offense,  
so that each year, in your praises,  
we may sing this feast with joyful hearts.

Let us, your servants, proclaim glory to the Father;  
let us likewise sing glory to Christ,  
who redeemed us with precious blood,  
sending the Paraclete Spirit among us  
and making us heirs of heavenly joy.

Amen.

# The Twenty-Second Day: Feast of Saint Cecilia, Virgin and Martyr, and Her Companions

## At Vespers

Lauda. “The light has risen in the darkness.” Folio CLXII. Sono. “Rejoice, righteous ones, in the Lord.” Folio CLXV.

Antiphon. There will be great joy for all people, says the Lord. P. For behold, I am coming, that I may be glorified in the midst of my saints. V. All nations, clap your hands; shout aloud with exultant voice. P. For. V. Glory and honor. P. For.

May the Lord be [with you]. R. And with [you].

Lauda. “The Lord God will come, and all the saints with him. Alleluia.” P. “And on that day which is known to the Lord it will be so. Alleluia, alleluia.” V. “Come and see the works of the Lord, who has placed wonders upon the earth.” P. “And on that day…” V. Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son. P. And on that day.

### Hymn

Let us sing with ready heart and glorious voice  
the feast of the noble chastity  
of the virgin Cecilia,  
by which, the law of death dissolved,  
she is lifted into the heavens:

This illustrious Virgin,  
more illustrious in holiness,  
holding Christ within her heart  
and proclaiming him alone,  
conquered the age in spirit  
and the enemy in blood.

She fortifies the recesses  
of her sacred heart with the Gospel;  
she scourges her blessed body  
with a rough hair shirt,  
and fills the hours of night and day  
with the song of her mind.

For she had received a bridegroom  
of radiant lineage  
and declares that she has  
an angel of God as her defender;  
she reminds him, reverencing this angel,  
to honor her chastity.

This bridegroom, in blind fury,  
threatens the Virgin;  
but the blessed Virgin,  
fully proving her words by deeds,  
soon made the angel and the gift of heaven  
appear before him.

The promised man appeared,  
clothed in shining garments,  
displaying crowns adorned  
with brilliantly gleaming flowers,  
teaching blood by the roses  
and chastity by the lilies.

Moved by this gift,  
the bridegroom, converted to faith in Christ,  
immediately obtained his brother’s salvation by entreaty;  
and thereafter both were consecrated  
by the blood of their passion.

Then Cecilia, the virgin of Christ,  
following them,  
earned the glory  
of triumphal honor;  
shut up in fiery baths,  
she became unaware of the heat.

Thus, burning more intensely  
with the fire of Christ,  
she conquered the fire of the world;  
she courageously endured three times  
the stroke of the flashing sword,  
then laid her limbs upon the earth  
and sought the heavens in spirit.

Therefore, holy Virgin,  
send us heavenly gifts;  
grant us from above  
the gift of lilies or roses,  
from where you drew  
the joys of heavenly truth.

May chastity, gleaming with lilies,  
shine brightly upon us;  
may the will for passion burn  
with crimson roses;  
overcome by the burden of sin,  
may we be renewed by grace.

Behold, we await  
the advent of the coming Judge;  
we endure and await  
those blessed joys of light.  
May we then not be punished as guilty,  
nor burned in fires;  
but, gathered among the sacred assemblies  
of the martyrs,  
may we escape what we fear,  
beholding the glory  
and summoned to the right hand  
of the gracious King for the crown.

So that, seeing your presence, Christ,  
we, your little servants,  
may rejoice and be glad,  
may proclaim your glory,  
and be cherished forever  
in the citadel of the heavenly court.

Amen.

Supplication. “Let us pray to the Redeemer,” as above.

Chapters. Attend, most beloved brothers, to what the prayer of the saints is worth and what the intercessions of the righteous, offered for the ungodly, obtain: when Urban prays, the vows of the virgin Cecilia are fulfilled, and the faith of Valerian and Tiburtius is increased and adorned with the glory of martyrdom. Therefore, with palms extended toward heaven, let us ask aid from above, invoking him in piety and fearing the terrible Father who will come as judge; for certainly through him eternal life will be ours, through whom the virgin Cecilia was not burned amid the flames. For he who heard them when they were placed in the struggle of martyrdom will hear us when we pour out to him the cry of our groaning, proclaiming and saying:

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” Folio 2.

Blessing. May almighty God, who established a spiritual marriage between Valerian and Cecilia, grant you an increase of heavenly concord. R. Amen. And may he who brought Tiburtius to the faith through his brother’s prayer kindle through you many people to love the dwelling-place of eternal glory. R. Amen. May you always be cherished by the protection of those whose triumphs you now celebrate with open exultation. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Lauda. “The faithful will endure in love of God.” P. “For there is kingdom and peace for his elect. Alleluia, alleluia.” V. “They cried out, and the Lord heard them and delivered them from all their tribulations.” P. “For there is kingdom.” V. Glory and honor to the Father. P. For there is kingdom.

Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ, who alone possess knowledge of your name and hold the power of magnificent virtue—whom no one has known except the Father and his revelation—through the intercession of your martyrs Cecilia and her companions, reveal to us the majesty of so great a mystery; and as we believe you to be one with the Father and the Holy Spirit, let us know you as inseparable, so that by the merit of faith we may always find you favorable and gentle when we confess. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

## At Matins

Antiphon. “Grant us the joy.” Psalm L. Prayer. “Restore to us.” Folio CLXIII.

Antiphon. “The vision will be fulfilled,” says the Lord, “so that the Holy of Holies may come, and sin will reach its end.” V. Yet in the flood of many waters they will not draw near to him. P. So that he may come. V. Glory and honor. P. So that he may come.

Prayer. O God, who foretold by prophetic oracle that you would be anointed as the Holy of Holies in the place of sanctification: preserve inviolate the mysteries of your anointing bestowed upon us, so that, with iniquity erased, our sin may reach its end, and we may rightly attain everlasting righteousness. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Antiphon. “The prince will not fail from the people of Judah, nor the leader from his loins, until the Holy of Holies comes.” P. “And he himself will be the expectation of the nations.” V. “The Lord has sworn and will not repent: you are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.” P. And he himself. V. Glory and honor. P. And he himself.

Prayer. O God, who reveal to Jacob our patriarch, your prophet and servant, the sacrament of your mercy, while through him you announce to us, saying: “The prince will not fail from Judah, nor the leader from his loins, until our one-begotten Lord Jesus Christ, your Son”: open to us the mysteries of your mercy, so that whatever antiquity kept obscure in us may be disclosed by the truth of your words; and so that Jesus Christ your Son, who is our expectation, may enlighten us with his light and set us aflame, and we may deserve to be cleansed from every stain of sin. R. Amen.

Through [your mercy].

Antiphon. The bodies of the saints were not distressed by the flame. P. And while they walked through it, they were not burned. V. They called upon the Lord, and he heard them; he spoke to them from the pillar of cloud. P. And while they walked. V. Glory and honor. P. And while they walked.

Prayer. Only-begotten Son of God, who test the bodies of your saints by fire like gold in a furnace: we ask you to inspect the strength of our hearts, and, according to our capacity, if it pleases you, permit us to be tested by the fire of tribulations in such a way that through the good of patience we may deserve to obtain an inheritance in the heavens. R. Amen.

[Col. 1255B]

Through your mercy.

R. This one who has come: no one knows his name except he himself. He will be called Lord by the word; he has a splendid garment, and the whole choir of saints follows him with hymns. P. They follow him with hymns. V. The Lord will come from Sinai, and from Seir he has risen for us; he appeared from Mount Paran, and with him thousands of saints. P. They follow him. V. Glory and honor. P. They follow him.

Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ, [as] in the preceding Vespers.

## At Lauds

For the Canticle. Antiphon. “All the saints.” Canticle. “The Lord will come from Sinai.” Prayer. “That you have come, Lord.” For the Benedictus. Antiphon. “Holy and humble.” Canticle. “Blessed are you, Lord.” Sono. “The way of the righteous.” Lauda. “Praise the Lord.” Psalm CXLVIII.

Reading from the book of the prophet Zechariah, chapter XIV.

R. Thanks be to God.

The Lord will go forth and fight against those nations, as he fought on the day of battle. And his feet will stand on that day upon the Mount of Olives, which is opposite Jerusalem on the east; and the Mount of Olives will split in the middle, from east to west, a very great chasm; half of the mountain will separate toward the north and half toward the south. And the Lord God will come, and all the saints with him. And on that day living waters will go forth from Jerusalem: half of them toward the eastern sea and half toward the western sea; they will flow in summer and winter. And the Lord will be king over all the earth; on that day the Lord will be one, and his name will be one. And the whole land will return as far as the wilderness, from the hill of Rimmon south of Jerusalem; it will be raised up and dwell in its holy place. R. Amen.

Hymn. “Let us sing the feast of the noble chastity of the virgin Cecilia.” See in the preceding Vespers.

Supplication. “Let us pray to the Redeemer,” as above.

Chapters. Christ, true light of the saints, who by the illumination of your advent destroy the raging enemy against your elect, come to us and enlighten our hearts with that light by which you were pleased to illumine the hearts of your saints Cecilia and her companions, the martyrs; so that, lifted from the burden of our sins, we may await the day of your advent unharmed.

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” Folio 2. Lauda. “Faithful in love,” as above.

Blessing. May Christ the Son of God, with whom thousands of saints will come to judgment, join us to the assemblies of the holy martyrs Cecilia and her companions, so that we may be crowned. R. Amen. And may he who will grant the elect a place in the judgment not repay sinners with punishment according to their deserts. R. Amen. May he reward the righteous with such joy at his advent that the faith by which he is believed may rescue the wretched from punishments. R. Amen.

Through [your mercy].

# The Twenty-Third Day: Feast of Saint Clement, Pope and Martyr

## At Vespers

[Col. 1256B]

Lauda. “With glory and honor.” Folio CLIX. Sono. “Bless the Lord, my soul.” Folio CLX.

Antiphon. You made a way in the sea, Lord, and, showing a most secure path amid the waves, P. because you are powerful to save those crossing the sea. V. Wonderful are your works, and my soul knows them exceedingly well. P. Because. V. Glory and honor. P. Because.

May the Lord be [with you]. R. And with [you].

Lauda. “I am stuck in the mire of the deep, where there is no firm ground. I have come into the depths of the sea, and the storm has overwhelmed me.” P. “I have grown weary crying out; hear me. Alleluia, alleluia.” V. “Save me, God, for the waters have entered even to my soul.” P. “I have grown weary.” V. Glory and honor. P. I have grown weary.

### Hymn

The feast of Clement is celebrated today:  
come, peoples, and marvel at the follower  
of Peter, the Lord’s apostle,  
the third bishop of the Roman see,  
whom Christ consecrated as his martyr.

Dwelling in the city of Romulus,  
proclaiming Christ the Lord,  
he enlightened Theodore and Sisinnius,  
when he perceived Peter appearing in a vision;  
thus baptized by Clement, they believed.

Preaching the Gospel of Christ  
and gathering crowds of the faithful,  
he was led into exile by Trajan’s command,  
across the Pontic Sea, into a very rugged wilderness.

There he performed a remarkable miracle:  
he drew springs of water from the abyss  
and satisfied the thirsty inhabitants,  
who were cutting marble from the mines  
and were burning with wasting illness and intense thirst,  
bearing sufferings for Christ’s name.

When the blessed Father saw them,  
bringing him a cup by a two-mile journey,  
he urged them all to preach the Lord,  
so that he might open for his people  
a fountain of waters, wonderfully healing  
for the holy confessors.

While the holy bishop, more distinguished  
by his merits, offered and sacrificed for them,  
he saw the Lord standing before him as a lamb,  
marking the place; when he struck that place,  
he brought forth abundant water into a river.

When this report filled all the provinces round about,  
it stirred the peoples to believe.  
They came together, received baptism,  
and embraced the rule of the Catholic faith;  
they also built seventy-five churches.

Because jealous envy increased,  
he was sunk into the deep sea with an anchor;  
there he was buried in a sepulchral chamber,  
in which a church now stands,  
where the faithful gather throughout the ages.

Covered by mighty waters during the year,  
his tomb lies hidden beneath the waves in the deep sea.  
When its annual feast returns,  
the sea recedes nearly three miles  
and for seven days provides shining paths.

His tomb gleams like gold,  
and the anchor on his neck shines like silver.  
Miracles are performed at the petitions of the faithful,  
who give God manifold thanks,  
for he grants such wonders to the saints.

Therefore, gracious martyr Clement,  
as we celebrate the joys of your struggle,  
we humbly ask you today with tears  
to be present for the guilty and help those who fall;  
through you may we be free from the burden of sin.

Turned from worse things by your example,  
may we continually attend to better things,  
seeking what is best and, more worthily,  
observing the commandments of life,  
so that afterward we may be joined  
to the assemblies of the saints.

Let us ask the only-begotten Word of the Father  
and beseech the gracious Spirit,  
that he may remove far from us the arrogance of the world  
and grant us abundance of virtues,  
through whom we may possess eternal glory.

Grant, we ask: O immense and eternal glory, one in united power,  
who alone fill the entire fabric of the world  
and establish it by your strength, be present;  
your praise, mercy, and unceasing honor  
abound throughout the ages.

Amen.

Supplication. “Let us pray to the Redeemer,” as above.

Chapters. Almighty God, who permitted the blessed Clement, bishop and martyr, to be tested—but not overwhelmed—by the goads of sufferings, like heaps of threatening waves; when neither punishment overcame him in combat nor the wave submerged him: because you were present with him there, lest he be conquered by tortures, and here granted that he should be carried contrary to nature by the waves. Through such great miracles grant faith to all, so that what is most devoutly believed by those who celebrate may be bestowed most abundantly upon those who believe.

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” Folio 2.

Blessing. May Christ the Lord, who did not allow the blessed Clement, bishop, to remain fixed in the mire of the deep or to be held by the law of the sea’s waves, himself rescue you from the filth of your muddy pleasures. R. Amen. And may he who did not allow the martyr’s body to be held by the rocks in the depths of the sea free you from every temptation and rescue you from the deep of sins. R. Amen. May he, with that same saint as your patron, bring you to infinite joys. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Lauda. “The waters enclosed me in the midst of the sea, and the storm overwhelmed me. Alleluia.” P. “I cried to you, Lord, and you healed me. Alleluia, alleluia.” V. “But I, Lord, make my prayer to you; it is the time of your favor, O God.” P. I cried. V. Glory and honor. P. I cried.

Prayer.
