O God, who recalled to the heights the consecrated body of the martyr Clement, fixed in the mire of the deep, so that, since his mind had clung to you with devotion pleasing to you, the services of the sea might serve his body: we ask and entreat you that, through the merits of this martyr, no water of temptation may cover us and no storm of sins plunge us into the deep of wrongdoing; but, supported by the gentle oar of your hand, may we deserve to reach the shore of righteousness free. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

## At Matins
Antiphon. “My lips.” Psalm 50. Prayer. “Let them exult, O Lord.” Folio CLXXX. Antiphon. “I am sunk,” as above in the preceding Vespers. Prayer. “O God, who consecrated to you,” as above.

Antiphon. “Send forth, O Lord, your hand from on high; rescue me.” P. “And deliver me from many waters and from the hand of foreign sons.” V. “Blessed be the Lord, my God, who trains my hands for battle and my fingers for war.” P. “And deliver me.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “And.”

Prayer. O Lord, who freed your most blessed martyr Clement by rescuing him from the counsel of the wicked and from many waters, and made him victorious in every suffering: free us from the hand of foreign sons, so that our life may not be exposed to harm by enemies lying in wait, nor may their savage arrogance rejoice at the calamities of our ruin; but, girded with the sword of your word, may we here overcome adversity without fear and afterward deserve to come to you unharmed and blessed. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon. “Blessed is the man who places his hope in God: the Lord will be his confidence.” P. “His bones will flourish like a tree planted beside the waters.” V. “It will yield its fruit in its season; its leaf will not fall, and all that it does will prosper.” P. “His bones will flourish.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “His bones will flourish.”

Prayer. Lord God, who adorned the most blessed Clement with the crown of martyrdom, so that, sanctified among his companions and crowned among the citizens of heaven, he might shine forth: with your assent, let him now be a special Patron for your people, who was great among the chosen; so that, because he did not hope in man but placed you as his help, the hope of believers, strengthened through his intercession, may be increased. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

R. “I am sunk in the mire of the deep, and there is no foothold. I have come into the depths of the sea, and the storm has overwhelmed me. I have labored, crying out.” P. “And hear me, O Lord, for your mercy is gracious.” V. “Let not the storm of water overwhelm me, nor let the deep swallow me.” P. “And hear me.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “And hear me.”

Prayer. O God, who did not allow the body of your most blessed Martyr Clement to be held fast by any law of the sea’s waves in the mire of the deep, so that the depth of the sea could in no way engulf him—he who had conquered the hostile bands rising against him for your name’s sake: through the intervention of your Martyr, free us from every temptation; and, snatched from the depth of our crimes, raise us up in the light of a manner of life pleasing to you, so that, with your help, we may be free from vices and abound in virtues. [CCCXXX] R. Amen.

Through mercy.

In Lauds.

For the Canticle. Antiphon. “Your waves, O Lord, have passed over me. And I said, ‘I am driven away from your sight,’ thinking, ‘I shall see your holy temple.’”

Canticle. “I cried to the Lord.” Folio 315.

At the Benedictus. Antiphon. “The blessing of the Lord hastens as the reward of the just.”

Canticle. “Blessed are you.” Folio 6.

Sono. “From the depths I have cried to you, O Lord; Lord, hear my voice. Let your ears be attentive.” P. “To the prayer of your servant. Alleluia.” V. “If you observe iniquities, O Lord, Lord, who will endure? For with you there is forgiveness and abundant redemption.” P. “To the prayer.”

Lauda. “Praise the Lord.” Psalm 148.

Reading from the Book of the Wisdom of Solomon (chapter 6).

R. Thanks be to God.

“My son, those who guard righteousness will be justified, and those who have learned these things will find what they should answer. Therefore desire my words, love them, and you will possess discipline. Wisdom is radiant and never fades, and she is easily seen by those who love her and found by those who seek her. She anticipates those who desire her and shows herself to them first. Whoever rises early for her will not labor; he will find her sitting at his doors. For thinking about her is perfect understanding, and whoever keeps watch for her will soon be secure. For she herself goes about seeking those worthy of her, and she shows herself to them graciously in her ways, and she will meet them in every act of prudence. Her true beginning is the desire for discipline. Therefore the love of discipline is secure; and love is the keeping of her laws, while the keeping of her laws is the perfection of incorruption. But whoever does not keep the law defiles incorruption. Incorruption, moreover, brings one near to God. Thus the desire for wisdom leads to an everlasting kingdom.” R. Amen.

Hymn. “The feast of Clement is celebrated.”

Supplication. “Let us pray to the Redeemer,” as above in the preceding Vespers.

[Col. 1260A] Capitulum. Christ the Lord, who are the head of your Church, grant that your most blessed martyr Clement, established in the body of the Church—who then gave his limbs for the Head—may now not cease to approach the Head on behalf of the limbs; but, being near the Head, may govern and protect the whole body, freely rendering that service which he rejoices to have obtained more happily.

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” Folio 2.

Lauda. “The waters have closed over me.”

Blessing. “Christ the Lord, who [blessed] the most blessed Clement.” Seek it in the preceding Vespers.

## The Twenty-Ninth: Feast of Saint Saturninus, Bishop and Martyr

### At Vespers

[Col. 1260B] Lauda. “With glory and honor.” Sono. “Deal with me, O God.” Folio CLIX. Antiphon. “You have placed, O Lord, upon the head.” Folio CCXCII.

Antiphon. “The nations will see your righteous one, O Zion, and all kings your illustrious one; and you will be called by a new name, which the Lord has named.” P. “And you will be a crown of glory in the hand of the Lord and a royal diadem in the hand of your God.” V. “And the nations will fear your name, O Lord, and all the kings of the earth your glory.” P. “And you will be.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “And you will be.”

May the Lord be always with you. R. And with you.

Lauda. “Alleluia. Whoever conquers, I will make him sit on the throne of my Father. Alleluia.” P. “Just as I also conquered and sit upon it. Alleluia, alleluia.” V. “And I will set him as firstborn, high among the kings of the earth.” P. “Just as I also.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “Just as.”

Hymn.

The novelty of the voice that was heard shone forth,  
proclaiming again the coming of the heavenly King:  
let the earth bring forth its flowers  
as is right for its cultivators.

Let snowbound Toulouse, enclosed by snowy expanses,  
burn, kindled by the warmth of faith;  
it was by Saturninus, with Christ resounding,  
that she began, through the Martyr.

At whose teaching the idols fall;  
at whose coming the crafty mouths  
of the ruler of the demons  
learn to be silent, their voice stilled.

Here he proclaimed that the Son begotten  
of God the Father must be worshiped,  
and, by both voice and blood, he is conquered,  
to be offered as a victim to Christ beneath the bull’s feet.

His ashes, unharmed, deserve  
to be transferred according to sacred rite  
to a consecrated tomb,  
so that faith might remain increased  
by the honor of the twofold sanctification.

Therefore, coming to you, Christ, we ask:  
appear in your coming gentle to the just,  
and join us, associates of the victorious,  
to your shining crowns.

Let the choir sing glory and resound;  
let it speak, sing, and repeat glory:  
let the stars cry out to the Triune Name,  
to the Godhead alone.

Amen.

Supplication. “Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world,” as above.

Capitulum. Great, O Lord, is the sacrament of piety: he was manifested in the flesh, justified in the Spirit, appeared to angels, was preached among the nations, believed on in the world, and taken up in glory. Through him the righteous lives by faith, and through him the impious turns back to you. We therefore ask that you, who by the illumination of your coming deigned to illumine the heart of the present martyr Saturninus, Bishop—so that he might lose the life extorted from him by punishments, in order to receive you as his reward—may also deign to soften our heart by the gift of your grace, so that we may disclose our sins to you with devoted faith and obtain from you the remedy we ask; so that we, too, may deserve through him to welcome as our liberator you whom he already believed had once come with us for the salvation of the world.

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” Folio 2.

Blessing. Christ, the Son of God, whose faith justifies the impious, through the prayers of this righteous man, may release you from the bonds of your sins. R. Amen. And may he who is awaited for judgment grant you fellowship with him whose feast you celebrate. R. Amen. May the glory of Christ’s coming join you to this Martyr in future joys and enrich you with the reward of eternity. R. Amen.

Through his mercy, etc.

Lauda. “Blessed is the man who fears.” Folio CCXCIII.

[Col. 1261C] Prayer. O God, who so filled the mouth of your most blessed martyr Saturninus, Bishop, with an abundance of wisdom that, appearing surrounded by a diversity of virtues, you showed him glorious in heavenly joy and beauty; and so that, because he guarded his lips, you might seek knowledge and the law from his mouth: extend to our mouth the light of knowledge and the perfection of true wisdom, so that, in that by which he converted many from iniquity to you, you may command us also to be converted and to rejoice forever. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

### At Matins

Antiphon. “My lips.” Psalm 50. Prayer. “Let the Lord rejoice in you.” Folio CLXXX. First antiphon. “The man of God showed.” Prayer. “The due things to you, O Lord.” Second antiphon. “This man accomplished everything.” Folio CCXCIII.

Prayer. Christ God, giver of all graces, who established your servant Saturninus the Priest as the first and chief shepherd of the city of Toulouse: may we come without confusion to you, who are the most just rewarder. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Third antiphon. “This man was honored.” Folio CCXCIII.

Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ, who are ineffable goodness and unconquered power, for whose name’s sake the most blessed Saturninus, Bishop and martyr, while refusing to be offered upon demonic altars, was dragged by crowds to the Capitol and consecrated through the punishment of the raging bull: receive our prayers through his merits and, in your compassion, justify all the faithful together. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Responsory. “The lips of the priest guard.” Folio CCXCIV.

Prayer. “O God, who [filled] the mouth of the most blessed martyr.” Seek it in the preceding Vespers.

### In Lauds

For the Canticle. Antiphon. “The throne of glory.” Canticle. “My heart is confirmed.”

At the Benedictus. Antiphon. “The blessing of the Lord.” Canticle. “Blessed are you, O Lord.” Folio 6.

Sono. “Alleluia. I shall sing of strength.” Lauda. “Praise the Lord.” Psalm 148. Prophecy. “This man preserved.” Folio CCXCIV. [CCCXXXII] Hymn. “The novelty of the voice that was heard.” Supplication. “Let us pray to the Redeemer.” [Col. 1262B] In the preceding Vespers.

Capitulum. Christ, Son of God, who are awaited as judge by the righteous for judgment, grant that through the prayers of this righteous man we may be cleansed from our injustices; so that, as the celebration of your coming is mingled with the celebration to be held in his honor, through his reception we may obtain the gifts of an everlasting reward.

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” Folio 2.

Lauda. “Blessed is the man.” Blessing. “Christ, the Son of God.” Seek it in the preceding Vespers.

## The Thirtieth: Feast of Saint Andrew the Apostle

### At Vespers

Lauda. “With glory and honor.” Folio CLIX.

Sono. “O good Cross.” Folio CCXXXIX.

Antiphon. “Alleluia. For through the law I died to the law.” P. “So that I might live for God; I have been crucified with Christ. Yet I live, no longer I, but Christ lives in me.” V. “The Lord is the portion of my inheritance and my cup; you are the one who will restore my inheritance to me.” P. “So that I might live for God.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “So that I might live for God.”

May the Lord be with you. R. And with your spirit.

Lauda. “I spoke of your testimonies before kings, and I was not ashamed.” P. “And I meditated on your commandments, which I loved. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.” V. “And let your mercy come upon me, O Lord, and your salvation, and your word.” P. “And I meditated.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “And I meditated.”

Hymn.

Adornment of the sacred Name,  
Name expressing life,  
this name proclaims you beautiful,  
the glory of the blessed Cross.

Andrew, Apostle of Christ,  
by this very name already beautiful;  
likewise, mystically,  
you are marked by this name.

The Cross raises him to the heights;  
the blessed Cross loves him;  
the beloved Cross prepares for him  
the future joys of light.

In you the mystery of the Cross  
shines forth with a twofold mark:  
while you conquer reproaches through the Cross,  
you reveal the blood of the Cross.

Now cherish us in our weakness  
and take care of us,  
so that through the victory of the Cross  
we may seek the homeland of heaven.

Grant this, almighty Father,  
through Jesus Christ the Lord,  
who with you forever  
reigns with the Holy Spirit.

Amen.

Supplication. “Let us pray,” as above.

Capitulum. Christ our Lord, who adorned the most blessed Andrew with both the grace of apostleship and the crown of martyrdom, granting him this special gift: that by preaching the mystery of the Cross he might deserve to come to the Cross’s gallows—grant us, made true lovers of your holy Cross, to deny ourselves, take up our cross, and follow you; so that, sharing in your sufferings in this life, we may happily deserve to reach eternal life.

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” Folio 2.

Blessing. Almighty Lord, who received the soul of the Apostle Andrew upon the Cross, may free you from every torment of eternal condemnation. R. Amen. And through him, by whose preaching he acquired peoples who would believe in him, may he, through his prayer, make believers glorious. R. Amen. May you, made lovers of Christ’s Cross through the example of his Apostle, here overcome the fires of vices and afterward deserve to reach the promises of eternity. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

[Col. 1263C] Lauda. “The Lord established.” As above. Folio CLVII.

Prayer. Holy Andrew, man of God, that Apostle of yours, Christ, who declares that he saw you in the final vision of peace, when he confesses that he recognized the mysteries of the holy Cross: may he be a constant intercessor for us with you, so that he who preached you by voice, body, and blood may assist us with you by both teaching and prayer. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

### At Matins

Antiphon. “My lips, O Lord.” Psalm 50.

Prayer. “Let the Lord rejoice.” Folio CLXXX.

Antiphon. “Let it be far from me to glory except in the Cross of our Lord Jesus Christ.” P. “Through whom the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.” V. “I waited, yes, I waited for the Lord, and he turned toward me; he heard my supplication.” P. “Through whom.” V. “Glory and honor to the Father.” P. “Through whom.”

Prayer. Make us, God the Father, glory fully in the Cross of Jesus Christ your Son, our Lord, so that the confession of our mouth may agree with the effectiveness of our works; and, by truly crucifying ourselves to the world, may we deserve to be filled with the reward of eternity. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon. “Hail, Cross, which, long wearied, now rest while awaiting me with certainty. I know that you rejoice, receiving the disciple of him who hung upon you.” V. “The Lord has heard and had mercy on me; the Lord became my helper.” P. “I know.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “I know.”

Prayer. Holy Apostle of God, who cry out with devout affection that the Cross, long wearied, at last rested when you came to it in expectation: grant us full joy in your passion, so that through your intercession you may prepare the future kingdom for us, for whom you left not merely by word but also by blood an example and a lesson in virtues. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon. “Good Cross, receive me and restore me to my Lord.” P. “For through you he redeemed me, he who hung upon you.” V. “In you I have hoped, O Lord; let me never be put to shame. In your righteousness free me and rescue me.” P. “For through you he redeemed me.” V. “Glory and honor to the Father.” P. “For through you.”

Prayer. Your Apostle and martyr Andrew, O Lord, wonderfully aflame with love for your Cross, longs to be restored through it to you, his Lord, through which he does not doubt that he was redeemed. Therefore we ask that, through the favor of him who hung upon that Cross, you may graciously and powerfully free us from all future torments of punishment. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

R. “The holy man of God, while he looked upon heaven, said with a loud voice: ‘You are my God and my Lord, whom I have seen, in whom I have believed, whom I have loved.’” P. “Do not allow me to be taken down by the wicked judge, for I have now recognized the mysteries of the holy Cross.” V. “This man prayed in the sight of the Lord, saying: ‘God the Father and Ruler of my life.’” P. “Do not allow me.” V. “Glory and honor to the Father.” P. “Do not allow me.”

Prayer. “The holy man of God, Andrew.” Seek it in the preceding Vespers.

### In Lauds

For the Canticle. Antiphon. “I shall glory in the Lord; I shall rejoice in God, my Jesus.”

Canticle. “Lord, I have heard your report.” Folio 22.

At the Benedictus. Antiphon. “The blessing of the Lord hastens as the reward of the just.”

Canticle. “Blessed are you, O Lord.” Folio 6.

Sono. “O good Cross.” Seek it in the preceding Vespers.

Lauda. “Praise the Lord from the heavens, alleluia; praise him in the heights, alleluia, alleluia.” Psalm 148.

Prophecy. “If the righteous is overtaken by death.” Folio 53.

Hymn.

Prostrate, we all, as suppliants,  
let us give thanks to almighty God  
for the contest of Saint Andrew.

Praying to the Redeemer,  
he acknowledged him as the true one,  
was hostile to the demons,  
and resisted the deceivers.

Strengthened by Christ the Lord,  
he preached in Achaea:  
the whole people was converted  
and surrendered itself to the Cross.

Behold Jesus almighty,  
upon whose Cross he was suspended;  
he was summoned from the heavens  
and crowned through faith.

He did not fear torments;  
rather, he asked to be placed upon the Cross,  
so that from there he might depart  
to the seat of the true Lord.

Then, amid the people’s cries,  
as they raised their voices in their ears:  
“Wicked, faithless Aegeas,  
defend the Apostle!”

Now placed upon the Cross,  
preaching the truth,  
adorned with good morals,  
pious, holy, most chaste,

Aegeas, most frightful,  
is seized by demons,  
received by hell,  
and joined to darkness.

But his brother,  
holding the Apostle’s body,  
buried him without fear  
with a great multitude.

To God the Father be glory,  
and to his only Son,  
with the Spirit, the Paraclete,  
reigning through every age.

Amen.

[Col. 1265C] Supplication. “Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world, our Lord Jesus Christ,” as above.

Capitulum. In your body, Christ, we venerate the mystery of your Cross, which both received you, the Lord bringing redemption to the world, and restored to you the dying disciple, destined to live more fully. We ask and beseech you to join us to him in the reward whose passion we inhabit here while venerating it.

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” Folio 2.

Lauda. “With psaltery and lyre.” See folio CLX.

Blessing. “Almighty Lord.” Seek it in the preceding Vespers.

### At the end of Vespers

Lauda. “A lamp to my feet.” Folio CLX.

Sono. “O good Cross, which.” In the preceding Vespers.

Antiphon. “Whoever serves me, let him follow me.” P. “And where I am, there also will my servant be.” V. “What shall I repay the Lord for all that he has given me? I will receive the cup of salvation and call upon the name of the Lord.” P. “And where I am.” Glory and honor to the Father. P. “And where.”

May the Lord be always with you. R. And with you.

Lauda. “Well done, good and faithful servant; you were faithful over a little, I will set you over much.” P. “Enter into the joy of your Lord. Alleluia, alleluia.” V. “You shall eat the labors of your fruits; blessed are you, and it shall be well with you.” P. “Enter.” V. “Glory and honor to the Father.” P. “Enter.”

Hymn. “God of the sacred Name.” Seek it in the preceding Vespers.

Supplication. “Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world, the Lord,” as above.

Capitulum. God, from whom your only Son was sent into this world and, suspended upon the Cross for us, gave his blood as the price of our redemption, so that, reconciled through his death, we might deserve adoption as sons before you: through the favor of this same mediator of ours, grant to us, though undeserving, that we may confidently call you Father and, in the prayer which we learned from the Lord himself as our teacher, proclaim to you from the earth not only with words but also with merits:

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” Folio 2.

Blessing. May Saint Andrew the Apostle, who was suspended upon the Cross for the crucified Lord and our Redeemer, always prove a provident Patron for you before that same Lord of grace. R. Amen. And because your assembly is joyful today in celebrating his solemnity, may he be a constant intercessor for your sins before God. R. Amen. And just as this Saint, relying upon the strength of the crucified Lord, overcame the devil through the victory of the Cross, so may you trample every vice through the mortification of the Cross. R. Amen.

Through.

Lauda. “The Lord established.” Folio CLVII.

[Col. 1266C] Prayer. “The holy man of God.” In the preceding Vespers.

## December Feasts: The Fourth Day, Feast of Saint Barbara, Virgin and Martyr

Everything is to be said from the Office of One Virgin, folio CLXXIX, except the hymns at Vespers and Matins:

Hymn.

O Martyr of Christ and illustrious  
virgin, consecrated Barbara,  
whose struggle subjected  
the flesh, the world, and Tartarus!

You are light arising from darkness,  
pouring light throughout the age;  
withdrawn from enticements,  
you break the rival of salvation.

You wonderfully adorn your father’s palace  
with a threefold window,  
showing by simple faith  
the mystery of the Trinity.

By cursing the rustic,  
you give him a marble nature—  
he who, bearing a stony mind,  
betrays you by a public gesture.

The father, more savage than a wild beast,  
cuts the throat of his daughter,  
but through a heavenly spear  
death strikes him more fiercely.

To the Father, the Son, and the Paraclete  
be honor, glory, and praise.  
By the merits of this holy woman,  
may eternal joys be ours.

In the heavenly assembly  
a new companion is honored;  
in the rose-garden of the saints  
a fresh flower is brought forth.

Barbara, flowering with grace,  
made beautiful among the humble,  
joyfully possesses glory,  
a companion of the exalted in her lot.

From the scattered seed  
she gathers a sheaf of the full harvest,  
deceiving beneath the covering  
the rival of our salvation.

She gives the pride of the flesh  
subject to the spirit;  
she conquered the world and its vices,  
and, conquered herself, became illustrious in victory.

From the darkness of misery,  
with the stars that lead the way,  
let us seek the Father of grace,  
that at last we may share in glory.

Amen.

### At Matins: Hymn

Rejoice, mother Church,  
clapping with maternal applause,  
and, for your blessed daughter,  
frequent in the praises of God.

Let us praise together  
Barbara, the handmaid of Christ,  
and happily imitate  
the bearer of Christ’s Cross.

By confessing Christ,  
she establishes the faith more clearly;  
arguing against the governor,  
she conquers torments more strongly.

She tramples her father’s rage,  
striving in Christ’s name;  
she breaks the hostile line  
in glorious combat.

The father’s hand cuts down  
the young girl, and immediately  
he perishes: the demon  
spurs the parricide with thunder.

In the field of combat,  
zealous for the glory of the holy woman,  
let us, led by divine light,  
press on toward victory.

May the Holy Trinity grant this  
through the merits of holy Barbara,  
and, O highest Sweetness,  
lead us by upright paths to you.

Amen.

## The Sixth Day: Feast of Saint Nicholas, Bishop

Everything is to be said from the Office of One Confessor and Pontiff, folio CLXIX, except the hymns at Vespers and Matins.

Hymn.

This most holy day is present,  
bright with sacred virtue,  
on which Nicholas is placed  
in the heavenly dwellings.

Thus, small in bodily stature  
but great in faith toward God,  
on Wednesday and Friday  
he suckled at the breast only once.

Shining with noble virtue,  
through fasts and vigils  
the young man subdued his body,  
so that it might not be defiled by vices.

Thus the noble Bishop of Christ,  
because of the merit of his holiness,  
is adorned by the glory  
of the heavenly kingdom.

Be present, illustrious Bishop,  
and receive our prayers;  
offer to the highest Bishop  
the people’s devoted prayers.

To the Trinity be glory,  
eternal and illustrious praise:  
to God the Father and the Son,  
and to the Spirit with the Flame.

Amen.

### At Matins: Hymn

Let the heavenly palace rejoice,  
let the structure of the world be glad,  
while the orbit of the sun  
recalls Nicholas.

He wonderfully adorned  
the cries of infancy,  
giving the beginnings of virtues  
among the toys of childhood.

On Wednesday and Friday  
he suckled at the breast only once;  
already in tender age  
he practiced this abstinence.

His tomb carries oil,  
such as mothers do not know from the olive;  
what nature did not produce,  
the marble gives birth to by sweating.

O venerable Pontiff,  
kind and not slow to work,  
for all who seek you  
with believing hearts in danger:

Take away the losses of the mind,  
grant the resources of life,  
so that after the exile of the flesh  
we may be with you in glory.

Grant this, unbegotten Father,  
Jesus, with the sacred Breath,  
so that through Nicholas’s prayers  
we may be joined to heaven’s citizens.

Amen.

## The Ninth Day: Feast of Saint Leocadia, Virgin

### At Vespers

Lauda. “You have clothed yourself with confession and beauty.” Sono. “I shall confess to you, O Lord, with all my heart.” Folio CLXIX.

Antiphon. “I shall confess to you, O Lord, with all my heart, because you have heard the words of my mouth.” P. “In the sight of the angels I shall sing to you.” V. “You are my God, and I shall confess to you; my God, I shall exalt you.” P. “In the sight of the angels I shall sing to you.” V. “Glory and honor to the Father.” P. “In the sight.”

May the Lord be always with you. R. And with your spirit.

Antiphon. “Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion; shout for joy, Israel.” P. “Behold, your King comes to you, righteous and saving.” V. “Confession and magnificence are his work, and his righteousness remains forever and ever.” P. “Behold, your King.” V. “Glory and honor to the Father.” P. “Behold, your King.”

May the Lord be always with you. R. And with you.

Lauda. “I shall confess to you, Lord and King. Alleluia.” Folio CLXIX.

Lauda. “I shall confess to the Lord, alleluia, according to his righteousness. Alleluia.” P. “And I shall sing.” Alleluia. V. “I shall rejoice and exult in you, and sing to your name, O Most High.” P. “And I shall sing.” V. “Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son.” P. “And I shall sing.”

Hymn.

The solemn feast  
of most holy Leocadia has appeared,  
on which, spurning the vanities of earth,  
she passed to the kingdoms of heaven.

Come, all of you, as suppliants;  
lay open the guilt of your heart;  
rejoicing, fulfill your vows,  
and give thanks to God.

For this noble Virgin,  
sprung from illustrious stock,  
confessed Christ bravely  
and willingly endured punishments.

Seized by order of the governor,  
she is bound with iron fetters,  
so that by the weight of her bonds  
the girl’s faith might yield.

There, desiring through abstinence  
to please Christ,  
she offers the return of praise  
and presents the sacrifices of prayers.

But soon she learns of the sacred death  
of blessed Eulalia;  
in the bonds of prison  
she poured forth her spirit to heaven.

Now, holy Virgin, we ask  
and plead with tears  
that you wash away our reproaches  
and present our vows to Christ.

You are our illustrious fellow-citizen,  
you are the humble Patroness;  
from the boundary of this city  
drive far away weariness.

Let no enemy prevail here,  
nor sickness or want;  
let every harmful thing depart,  
and let prosperity be bestowed.

Thus may life abound in goods,  
yet may hearts not be soiled by luxury;  
and may indulgence be granted  
to all on account of their sins.

Everlasting glory and abundance of thanks  
be to God, who orders all times  
and reigns before the ages.

Amen.

Supplication. “Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world, our Lord,” with the name changed, folio CLXXXVII.

Capitulum. Lord Jesus Christ, who are the bridegroom of virgins and the heavenly rewarder of confessors, who grant holy Leocadia both to remain a virgin and to be glorified as a confessor: we humbly ask you that, through her intercession, just as by confessing she earned the heavenly kingdom, so we may escape everlasting punishment.

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” Folio 2.

Blessing. Christ the Lord, who caused the most blessed Leocadia worthily to confess him before men on earth, may confess you before his Father who is in heaven. R. Amen. And may he who placed upon her lips songs of confession acceptable to himself receive your devotion to reward it. R. Amen. May you, following the example of the blessed virgin Leocadia, by confessing and praising the name of Jesus Christ in this world, deserve to be participants in heaven with him whom you have confessed. R. Amen. He who remains God in the Trinity forever and ever. Amen.

Lauda. “Your bones will sprout like willows. Alleluia.” P. “Beside flowing waters. Alleluia, alleluia.” V. “And he will be like a tree planted beside streams of water, which will yield its fruit in its season.” P. “Beside.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “Beside.”

Prayer. Lord, who are great and glorious, grant us, your servants, that while we admire the greatness of your works, we may praise your magnificence with due confession; and through the intercession of your glorious virgin and confessor Leocadia, grant us to practice the perfect beauty of understanding through obedience to fear, and carefully to love your faithful commandments with all our heart’s vigilance. R. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God, etc.

### At Matins

Antiphon. “My tongue will praise your righteousnesses, my God.” Psalm 50.

Prayer. “Let our tongue praise you, O Lord.” Folio CLXX.

Antiphon. “Daughter of Zion, I have loved you, says the Lord.” P. “And my mercy will not depart from you.” V. “Hear, daughter, and see, and incline your ear; forget your people and your father’s house.” P. “And my mercy.” V. “Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son.” P. “And my mercy.”

[Col. 1271A] Prayer. Blessed virgin of God, who stand gloriously in Zion’s watchtower, whom God himself testifies that he has loved, since he promises you that his mercy will no longer depart from you: grant us, O Lord, through her merits, that, aflame with divine love, we may be found unharmed in the future judgment. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Antiphon. “Rejoice, daughter of Zion, because your God will rejoice over you; he will be silent in his love for you.” P. “And he has exulted over you in praise.” V. “Praise the Lord, Jerusalem; praise your God, O Zion.” P. “And he has exulted.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “And he has exulted.”

Prayer. Rejoice, daughter of Zion, because the Only-Begotten Son of God rejoices over you, and exult in praise, since he grants you both to be an incorrupt Virgin and glorifies you with the honor of confession. We therefore ask that, through you, who shine with this twofold gift, our life, which lacks the gift of virginity, may at least bear fruit through the virtue of confession. R. Amen.

Through your mercy, etc.

Antiphon. “Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion; shout for joy, Israel.” P. “Behold, your King comes to you, righteous and saving.” V. “He will not let your foot be moved, nor will he who guards you sleep.” P. “Behold, your King.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “Behold, your King.”

Prayer. Hasten to meet your God, Virgin daughter of Zion, for he will come to you, gentle, strengthening and restoring you in his confession. Therefore we ask that our life may be increased through your intercession in your merits, so that he who came to you in this world as your most welcome crowned rewarder may be, in the future judgment, for us a most merciful liberator. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

R. “Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion; praise and rejoice, daughter of Jerusalem, for behold, your King will come to you, gentle and saving; he himself, poor, riding upon a colt, the foal of a beast of burden. And the bow of war will be destroyed, and he will speak peace to the nations.” P. “For his power is from sea to sea and from the rivers to the ends of the earth. For what is his goodness, or what is his beauty, except the grain of the chosen and the wine that makes virgins flourish? Ask rain from him in the late season, and he will give you showers and grass in the fields.” V. “The Lord will visit his people, the house of Judah, and will establish him like a beautiful horse in battle.” P. “For his power.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “For his power.”

Prayer. Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion, because behold, your King will come to you, gentle; by his gift the grain of confessors shines with virtues and the integrity of virgins gleams in praises. Grant us, therefore, that, justified, we may one day deserve to be admitted among the grain of the chosen, though we now remain covered by the crimes of our works; so that you, who have deserved a crown from God for your confession, may obtain for us who confess the indulgence of all our sins before him. R. Amen. For the Lord is kind and is recognized as merciful through all ages of ages. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

[Col. 1272A] Antiphon. “Blessed are you by God Most High above all women.” P. “Therefore let your praise not depart from the mouth of men forever.” V. “Glorious things are spoken of you, city of God.” P. “Therefore.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “Therefore.”

Prayer. Your virgin has become glorious, Christ, your Leocadia, who, compared with the rising dawn, is proved beautiful as the moon and chosen as the sun. Shining with a brighter light, like the full moon she gleams in confession, and like the blazing sun, knowing no diminution of herself, she persists in the work of holiness. Grant us, therefore, through her, to deserve to obtain from you indulgence according to our petitions, though for our offenses we now pour out tears or offer groans. R. Amen.

Through.

[Col. 1272B] Antiphon. “Come forth, rising like the dawn.” P. “Beautiful as the moon, chosen as the sun, and adorned.” V. “Hear, daughter, and see, and incline your ear; forget your people and your father’s house.” P. “Beautiful.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “Beautiful.”

Prayer. O God, who, as the best of sailors, steer the ship of your Church as it is tossed by the dangers of this world, and, as its most vigilant guardian, watch over it lest it be overwhelmed by the storm of unbelief: grant to all reborn through its washing, through the intercession of your glorious confessor and virgin Leocadia, to conquer the storms of persecution in confessing your name and to offer ourselves to you as a sacrifice pleasing to you; and may those who wonderfully look into the deep be led to heaven by the rowing of your right hand. R. Amen.

Through your mercy, O God.

Antiphon. “You have become beautiful. Alleluia.” Folio CLXXIX. Prayer. “Lord, who are great,” as above, folio CCCXXXVII. Responsory. “Beautiful and comely.”

### Prayer

Lord Jesus Christ, who are exalted above all nations and dwell gloriously in the heavens, look down graciously from on high upon our humility; and just as your Church, once hindered by the defect of barrenness, is now, believing in you, full of the merits of virtues and numerous in children, so may our mind, barren and unproductive in works, through your gift and by the intercession of your glorious confessor and virgin, Leocadia, receive the seed of the word and overflow with abundant fruits. May it encompass your name, renowned from the rising of the sun to its setting, with the united love of its heart, and praise it with the assent of faith.  
**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy, our God, etc.

## At Lauds

### At the Canticle

**Antiphon.** I will confess to you, Lord, because …

**Canticle.** I will confess.

### At the Benedictus

**Antiphon.** Daughter of Zion, bless the Lord God Most High with every blessing and praise.

**Canticle.** Benedictus.

**Sono.** In the presence of … Psalm 148. Folio 173.

**Prophecy.** The Lord is far away. Folio 181.

**Hymn.** Of the most holy Leocadia.

**Supplication.** Let us pray. At the preceding Vespers.

### Capitula

Glorious and merciful Lord, who granted blessed Leocadia to confess you greatly with her mouth and desired her to praise you by her confession in the midst of the righteous, so that, confessing you on earth and glorifying you in the assembly of the saints, you might make her rejoice: we ask for the gift of your grace, that through her prayers you may grant us to be cleansed from the contagion of sin, rescued from everlasting fires, and attain the blessedness of your glory.

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. Folio 2.

**Lauda.** Your bones shall flourish. Folio 170.

### Blessing

May God, who caused Leocadia, renowned for her confession, to attain the beauty of confessors, justify you from every contagion of guilt.  
**R.** Amen.

And may he who made her conspicuous through the abundance of her confession make you glorious through the evident signs of true repentance.  
**R.** Amen.

And just as the confession of Christ was sweet in the mouth of this Virgin, so may the love of the everlasting kingdom become sweet in your hearts.  
**R.** Amen.

Through.

At the conclusion of Vespers, let everything be said as at First Vespers, except for the Capitula and Blessing that follow.

### Capitula

Receive, O God, the confession of our lips, and loosen every bond of our crimes, so that by the prayer of this virgin of yours, Leocadia, we may be free from vices and enriched with gifts when we cry to you from the earth:

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. Folio 2.

### Blessing

May Christ, God the Son, who received Leocadia’s spirit in the confession of his name, receive your faithful devotion and reward it.  
**R.** Amen.

And may you who exalt this feast of the Confessor in songs of confession be rewarded eternally by God.  
**R.** Amen.

May your devotion come to the place where the confession of the most blessed Leocadia has been brought to receive its reward.  
**R.** Amen.

By the grace of that divinity who is blessed for ever and ever.  
**R.** Amen.

Through his mercy, etc.

**Lauda.** Your bones shall flourish.

### Prayer

Lord, who are great, as above at the preceding Vespers.

# Day Ten: The Feast of Saint Eulalia, Virgin and Martyr

## At Vespers

**Lauda.** My soul has hoped in the Lord. See folio 179.

**Sono.** The Lord, God of heaven. Folio 181.

**Antiphon.** Alleluia. Rejoice and be glad, daughter of Zion, for behold, I come and shall dwell in your midst, says the Lord.  
**P.** And many nations shall be joined to the Lord on that day.  
**V.** My heart has uttered a good word; I speak my works to the king. My tongue is the pen of a swift-writing scribe.  
**P.** And many nations shall be joined.  
**V.** Glory and honor to the Father, etc.  
**P.** And many nations shall be joined.

### Prayer

Rejoice and be glad, daughter of Zion, because the Lord promises that he will dwell in your midst, since he has made you victorious in your passion and innocent from every contagion of heresy. We ask, therefore, that by your merits we may be saved from every temptation—we who dwell here venerating your day—and that, believing Christ to have conquered in you, we may rejoice that through him we have conquered the assaults of carnal passions.  
**R.** Amen.

For now he possesses one name with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever and ever.  
**R.** Amen.

May the Lord be always with you.  
**R.** And with you.

**Antiphon.** A beautiful column, perfected with gold and girded with gems.  
**P.** Its head is full of dew, and its locks with drops.  
**V.** Hear, O daughter, and see, and incline your ear; forget your people and your father’s house.  
**P.** Its head is full of dew.  
**V.** Glory and honor to the Father.  
**P.** Its head is full of dew.

May the Lord be always with you.  
**R.** And with you.

**Lauda.** Daughter of Zion, the Ruler of Israel shall come to you.  
**P.** And the first power, the kingdom of the daughter of Jerusalem, shall come; his going forth is from the days of eternity. Alleluia.  
**V.** Praise the Lord, Jerusalem; praise your God, Zion.  
**P.** And the first power shall come.  
**V.** Glory and honor to the Father.  
**P.** And the first power shall come.

### Hymn

Noble by birth, Eulalia,  
Yet nobler in the character of her death,  
The holy virgin adorns Emerita,  
From whose breast she was born,  
And cherishes it with love.

Near the setting sun lies the place  
That bore this eminent glory,  
A powerful city, rich in peoples,  
But richer still in the blood of martyrdom,  
And powerful in the title of its virgin.

She had reached twelve years of age,  
When, amid the crackling pyre,  
She terrified the trembling executioners  
And willingly underwent the sweet punishment.

She had already given a sign  
That she was stretching toward the Father’s throne;  
She had rejected childish ornaments,  
Though her limbs were dedicated to the bridal chamber,  
A little girl unknowing of play.

She scorned amber, flowers, and roses;  
She rejected golden necklaces.  
Severe in expression, modest in step,  
And exceedingly tender in conduct,  
She contemplated the white hair of old age.

But when the maddened plague  
Rouses itself against the servants of the Lord  
And bloodily commands Christians  
To burn incense and kindle the entrails of sheep  
For deadly gods,

Eulalia’s sacred spirit roared,  
Fierce in courage, and prepared  
To break the turbulent battles.  
The woman, breathing God, with her untrained breast,  
Challenges the weapons of men.

But the pious care of her parent strove  
To hide the spirited virgin at home,  
Concealed in the countryside and far from the city,  
Lest the girl, driven by love of death,  
Rush savagely to purchase blood with her own.

Hating the aid of quiet  
And unable to endure a disgraceful delay,  
By night she moves the doors without a witness,  
Opens the barred gates as a fugitive,  
And then takes a path through trackless places.

With wounded feet she enters  
Through places rough with decay and thorns,  
Accompanied by an angelic choir.  
Although the dreadful night is silent,  
She nevertheless has a guide of light.

Thus the noble multitude of the Fathers  
Had a ray-bearing column:  
It was powerful to cleave a path  
Through the dark night with a shining torch,  
While Chaos perished.

In the same way the holy Virgin,  
Following a road by night, merited the day  
And was not covered by darkness  
When she fled the Canopic realms  
And prepared a path above the stars.

With swift, wakeful steps  
She first travels many thousands,  
Before the eastern region opens the sky.  
In the morning she approaches the proud tribunal  
And stands amid the fasces.

Crying out thus:

“What madness is this—  
To destroy souls headlong  
And wickedly cast prodigal hearts  
Upon sharp rocks,  
And to deny the Father of all?

Do you seek, O pitiable band,  
The race of Christians? Behold, I am one,  
An enemy of demonic rites.  
I trample idols beneath my feet;  
With heart and mouth I confess God.

Isis, Apollo, and Venus are nothing,  
And Maximianus himself is nothing.  
She is nothing because she was made by human hands;  
He is nothing because he worships what hands have made.  
Both are frivolous, and both are nothing.

Maximianus is lord of riches,  
And yet he himself is a client of stones.  
Let him prostitute and dedicate his own head  
To his divinities;  
Why does he strike generous hearts?

A good leader, an excellent judge,  
He feeds upon innocent blood.  
Gaping for pious bodies,  
He tears apart sober entrails  
And rejoices to torture faith.”

Then the executioner, burn and cut,  
Divide limbs joined to clay.  
It is easy to dissolve a fragile thing;  
The inner mind will not be pierced  
By pain that agitates it.”

Stirred to madness by such words,  
The governor said:

“Seize her and carry her away, lictor,  
And bury her beneath punishments.  
Let her learn that the ancestral gods exist,  
So that she may not despise the emperor’s command.  
Yet how I wish, before death,  
If you are able, to recall  
Your wickedness, fierce little girl!

Consider how many joys you are abandoning,  
Which your marriageable honor brings you.  
Your household, weakened by tears, follows you,  
And the anxious nobility of your family  
Urges upon you the thought  
That you are dying in the flower of tender youth,  
Close to dowry and bridal chamber.

Does the golden pomp of the marriage bed not move you?  
Does not the venerable devotion to the old men move you,  
Whom your rash weakness is making frail?

Behold, punishments are prepared,  
Death-dealing and agonizing.  
Either your head will be struck by the sword;  
Or your limbs will be torn by beasts;  
Or, committed to smoking torches,  
You will flow, amid lamentation and wailing for your own,  
Dissolved into ashes.

Tell me, what labor is it to escape these things?  
If you, kind Virgin, would touch  
A little salt with your fingertips  
And a small amount of incense,  
You would, alas, escape the grievous punishment.”

To this the martyr said nothing;  
Rather, she roared and spat  
Into the eyes of the tyrant.  
Then she shattered the images  
And kicked apart the millstone  
Placed upon the incense burners.

Without delay, two executioners  
Tear open her breast with a lance;  
The claw strikes either side  
Of the Virgin’s flank and cuts to the bones,  
While Eulalia counts the marks.

“Behold, Lord, I am written for you.  
How gladly I read these letters  
That mark your trophies, O Christ.  
The sacred name itself speaks  
Through the purple of the blood drawn forth.”

Without tears or groaning  
She sang these things, joyful and fearless.  
The terrible pain is absent from her soul;  
Her limbs, stained with fresh blood,  
Wash the skin in a spring that grows warm.

Then comes the final execution:  
Not tearing by a wound-bearing rack,  
Nor skin furrowed by cuts,  
But flame, raging everywhere  
With torches against her sides and stomach.

Her hair and fragrance had flowed  
Down toward her shoulders and throat,  
Where modest chastity  
And virgin honor might be hidden  
By the covering placed over her head.

The crackling flame flies into her face  
And, fed through her hair,  
Seizes her head and surpasses its crown.  
The Virgin, desiring a swift death,  
Approaches and drinks the pyre with her mouth.

Then a Dove flashes forth,  
Whiter than snow, filling the martyr’s mouth;  
It is seen to depart and follow the stars.  
This was Eulalia’s spirit,  
Milky-white, swift, and innocent.

Her neck slackens as her soul departs,  
And the fiery pyre dies out.  
Peace is granted to her lifeless limbs;  
The breath flies exultantly into the heavens  
And seeks the lofty temples like a bird.

The attendant himself saw the Bird  
Clearly issue from the woman’s mouth.  
Astonished and stunned,  
He leaps away and flees from his own deeds;  
The executioner too flees in fear.

Behold, icy winter pours down snow  
And covers the entire forum.  
It covers Eulalia’s limbs as well;  
Her bones lie beneath the cold,  
In place of a small linen cloak.

Let the love of weeping humans give way,  
Those who customarily celebrate the final rites;  
Let the mournful service also give way.  
The elements themselves, at God’s command,  
Carry out your funeral rites, Virgin.

Now the place of your tomb is Emerita,  
The famous colony of Vettonia,  
Which the memorable river Ana passes by,  
And whose beautiful walls it drenches  
With its rushing, green current.

Here, where luminous marble  
Makes the gracious halls shine  
For traveler, foreigner, and native,  
The venerable earth keeps  
Your relics and sacred ashes in its bosom.

Above, gleaming roofs shine  
From golden ceilings,  
And cut stones vary the pavement,  
So that you might think dew-covered meadows  
Were reddening with many kinds of flowers.

Gather purple violets  
And harvest blood-red crocuses.  
Winter is not without these twin flowers;  
The warming ice loosens and contracts,  
So that it may heap up baskets with flowers.

Give these gifts, Virgin and boy,  
From the leafy, flower-bearing foliage.  
But I shall carry a garland woven  
For the choir and in its midst,  
In dactylic measure—  
Poor and withered, yet festive.

Thus I delight to honor your bones,  
And the altar placed upon your bones.  
She, seated beneath God’s feet,  
Looks upon this place and her peoples,  
And may she cherish them with such a song of her own.

Let the stars, the earth, the sea—whatever exists—  
Extol you in outstanding praises,  
Father, and your Begotten Son.  
Let them resound in everlasting measures  
Your Son and the simple Spirit as well.

In the praises of this feast,  
Let the gracious choir resound  
With voices to the Lord,  
The Three-in-One Lord, who made Eulalia victorious  
And joins her forever to the heavenly citizens.

Amen.

**Supplication.** Let us pray to the Redeemer, changing the name, folio 187.

### Capitula

Jesus, Son of God, who, entering the garden of the Elect, feed among the lilies, when in your body, which is the Church, you are adorned by the assemblies of holy virgins, and when you wonderfully introduced the most blessed Eulalia, choosing to support her with such marvelous flowers that the fragrance of her virtues, like little aromatic blossoms, descended even to us: we earnestly beseech you that, once the figures of the Old Testament have been removed—figures which went before like shadows in typical observances—the day, that is, the evangelical tradition, may advance in us through its inspiration, so that we may follow the light of the Gospel with complete devotion, after the example of the virgin Eulalia, and know nothing of the shadows of past error and crime.

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. Folio 2.

### Blessing

May the God of virtues, through whom holy Eulalia, going to her passion, arrived at glory, grant you neither to be bound by the passions of vices nor to be freed from the vices of passions.  
**R.** Amen.

May she who subjected her limbs not to vices but to sufferings for God obtain for you never to be overcome in the contests of temptations.  
**R.** Amen.

And just as she obtained a crown after her passion, so may you come through repentance to forgiveness.  
**R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**Lauda.** I have been exalted like a palm tree in joy. Alleluia. And like a beautiful olive tree in the fields. Alleluia.  
**P.** I have borne fruit like a vine, the sweetness of fragrance. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.  
**V.** But I, like a fruitful olive tree in the house of the Lord, shall hope in the mercy of my God for ever and ever.  
**P.** I have borne fruit like a vine.  
**V.** Glory and honor.  
**P.** I have borne fruit like a vine.

### Prayer

Lord Jesus Christ, who did not permit blessed Eulalia the virgin to be overcome, in the tender age of youth, either by the allurements of the world or by the torments of persecutors; in her, through your gift, neither sex nor affection is defeated; whose constancy was frightened neither by savagery nor subdued by punishment, diminished by the claw, or restrained by flame: may her intercession for us prevail with you, so that it may remove present and future evils from us.  
**R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

## At Matins

**Antiphon.** You shall open my lips.

**Psalm 50.**

### Prayer

Let them rejoice, Lord. Folio 180.

**Antiphon.** Arise, hasten, my bride, and come. For winter has already passed and gone away; flowers have appeared in our land.  
**P.** How beautiful you are, my beloved, and how lovely! Your eyes are more beautiful than doves’, apart from what is hidden within.  
**V.** In your beauty and loveliness, look forth; prosper, advance, and reign, because of truth, meekness, and justice, and your right hand shall lead you wonderfully.  
**P.** How beautiful.  
**V.** Glory and honor to the Father.  
**P.** How beautiful.

### Prayer

Virgin of Christ, Eulalia, who at the voice of the Bridegroom calling rose to faith, hastened to rest, betrothed through blood and made beautiful through Baptism: behold, winter has already passed and the rain has gone away, because every temporal tribulation has departed, conquered by you. Therefore, at your prayer, let the assault upon virtues depart from our minds, so that we who stand full of the gift of belief may shine with the fullest aid of holiness.  
**R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**Antiphon.** Who is this who comes forth like the rising dawn?  
**P.** Beautiful as the moon, chosen as the sun, terrible as an army arranged for battle?  
**V.** Glorious things are spoken of you, city of God.  
**P.** Beautiful as the moon.  
**V.** Glory and honor to the Father.  
**P.** Beautiful as the moon.

### Prayer

Christ, Son of God, toward whom blessed Eulalia advances with desirous longing like the dawn, hear the people praying to you through her. Grant us both to preserve what we have been powerfully created by you to be and to love more abundantly what we have been redeemed by your compassion to be, so that, compared with the moon of the Church, we may shine in her bosom, and, chosen like the sun, may gleam as an example of brightness.  
**R.** Amen.

Through.

**Antiphon.** Your coming blossoms for me like a vine, and like chosen myrrh you have given the sweetness of fragrance.  
**P.** And like unmixed balsam is your fragrance, and like a fragrant rose are your dwellings.  
**V.** May he not allow your foot to be moved, nor let him who guards you sleep.  
**P.** And like …  
**V.** Glory and honor to the Father.  
**P.** And like …

### Prayer

It is a very wondrous thing, Lord, that at your coming your martyr Eulalia, fruit-bearing like a true vine and offering the fragrance of grace to the faithful in this world like chosen myrrh, should merit eternal consolation in her reward. We ask and beseech you that, by her intercessions, through the fragrance of virtues we may flee the odors of crimes, so that, restored by that heavenly inspiration, we may be found exiles from the foulness of every vice and self-controlled.  
**R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**R.** Proceed among the shadowy lilies, daughter of Jerusalem, for you are perfect and beautiful, and there is no reproach in you. Ascend like a bride from Lebanon and receive the blessing of faith.  
**P.** From the Lord your God.  
**V.** Come, bride, from Lebanon; come, you shall be crowned.  
**P.** From the Lord.  
**V.** Glory and honor.  
**P.** From the Lord.

### Prayer

Lord Jesus Christ, who made blessed Eulalia a Virgin … See at the preceding Vespers.

**Antiphon.** The voice of the turtledove has been heard in our land; flowering vines have given their fragrance.  
**P.** Your voice is sweet and your face beautiful. My beloved is mine, and I am his.  
**V.** Virgins shall be brought to the King after her; her companions shall be brought to you.  
**P.** Your voice.  
**V.** Glory and honor.  
**P.** Your voice.

### Prayer

The bride of Christ, the Son of God, the virgin Eulalia, is provided in the eyes of the faithful, in a manner like a turtledove, through recurring annual observances: while the honor of her tomb is presented to human eyes and opened for honorable veneration; while her sweet voice and her face, more beautiful through overflowing brightness, produce fruit. Grant us, therefore, that the fragrance of her virtues may awaken our dormant heart and move it to repentance, so that we who now receive joy from her fragrance may afterward receive tireless glory from repentance.  
**R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**Antiphon.** Go forth like a bride arising.  
**P.** Beautiful as the moon, chosen as the sun, and adorned.  
**V.** The sun shall not burn you by day, nor the moon by night.  
**P.** Beautiful as the moon.  
**V.** Glory and honor.  
**P.** Beautiful as the moon.

### Prayer

Your virgin, Eulalia, has become glorious, O Christ; compared with the rising dawn, she is shown to be beautiful as the moon and chosen as the sun. Shining with a brighter light, she gleams like the full moon in her passion, and like the blazing sun, without knowing any diminution, she persists in the work of holiness. Grant us, therefore, through her, to merit obtaining from you the pardon we seek, we who now pour out tears or offer sighs for our offenses.  
**R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**Antiphon.** Rejoice, virgin daughter of Zion; be glad and rejoice, daughter of Jerusalem.  
**P.** For behold, your King comes to you, meek.  
**V.** Praise the Lord, Jerusalem; praise your God, Zion.  
**P.** For behold.  
**V.** Glory and honor.  
**P.** For behold.

### Prayer

Lord God, who by prophetic prediction declare that the daughter of Jerusalem should rejoice and be glad, make us exult in the sacraments that flow forth and rise to the dignity of the works of your Son, our Lord. While we join faith to these things, may we, through the intercession of the virgin Eulalia, enjoy the joys of heaven; through the ineffable power of your riches, O supreme and wondrous God, our God, who are blessed for ever and ever.  
**R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**R.** Come, my bride: how beautiful and exceedingly lovely you have become! Arise, take the oil of wisdom, hasten.  
**P.** To the coming of the Lord your God.  
**V.** In your beauty and loveliness, look forth; prosper, advance, and reign.  
**P.** To the coming.  
**V.** Glory and honor to the Father.  
**P.** To the coming.

### Prayer

The bride of Christ, the virgin Eulalia, who has become beautiful and lovely, receiving the oil of wisdom and bearing the whiteness of Baptism, while receiving faith from the font, through which you are wondrously crowned among the daughters of Jerusalem: through you, we ask that we may deserve to attain the whiteness of chastity, since through virginity you merited pleasing Christ; through you may we obtain advancement in virtue, by which the cruelty of the persecutor was conquered; and may his name be blessed for ever and ever.  
**R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**Antiphon.** Rejoice and be glad with all your heart, daughter of Zion.  
**P.** Behold, the Lord, mighty in your midst, will rejoice over you with praise.  
**V.** Delight in the Lord, and he will grant you the requests of your heart.  
**P.** Behold, the Lord.  
**V.** Glory and honor to the Father.  
**P.** Behold, the Lord.

### Prayer

Rejoice and be glad, daughter of Zion, because the Lord has removed your enemies, since he has made you victorious in your passion and innocent from every contagion of heresy. We ask, therefore, that by your merits we may be saved from every temptation—we who dwell here venerating your day—and that, believing Christ to have conquered in you, we may rejoice that through him we have conquered the assaults of carnal passions.  
**R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**Antiphon.** Come, bride, into the prepared kingdom of heaven; enter into joy.  
**P.** And receive blessing from the Lord.  
**V.** May he not allow your foot to be moved, nor let him who guards you sleep.  
**P.** And receive.  
**V.** Glory and honor to the Father.  
**P.** And receive.

### Prayer

Lord Jesus Christ, who clothed the little body of your most blessed martyr Eulalia, hanging upon the Cross, with a heavenly sprinkling, so that the virgin might put on brightness and the martyr refreshment: be graciously present to us, and continually show such great benefits in the martyr, while through her you bestow heavenly gifts, make known the martyr’s vigils through miracles, and graciously illumine the feasts of the Church by visiting them.  
**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon.** Virgin of Israel, you shall be adorned with your tambourines.  
**P.** And you shall go forth in the choir of those who sing psalms.  
**V.** Hear, O daughter, and see, and incline your ear; forget your people and your father’s house.  
**P.** And you shall go forth.  
**V.** Glory and honor.  
**P.** And you shall go forth.

### Prayer

Lord Jesus Christ, who examine the soul of your servant, the most blessed martyr Eulalia, triumphing happily for you, through flame, receive it through a dove, and join it to yourself in everlasting glory: be present to us, so that the martyr’s Spirit may not be absent from those who plead for her intercession—the Spirit who also shone upon her persecutors through a remarkable miracle. May she never withdraw her benefits from the Church, since she rests with you in the heavenly court.  
**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**R.** Thus says the Lord: “With everlasting love I have loved you.”  
**P.** Therefore I have drawn you to mercy. I shall again build you, and you shall be built, virgin of Israel; take up your tambourine and proceed in the choir of those who sing psalms, for the day of consolation shall come to you.  
**R.** I remembered you, taking pity on your youth and the love of your betrothal.  
**P.** Therefore I have drawn you.  
**V.** Glory and honor to the Father.  
**P.** Therefore I have drawn you.

### Prayer

Hear and receive the vows of those who pray, beloved virgin of God, Eulalia, who are shown to be the bride of Christ through faith and his sister through blood. May flowers of virtues flow forth in us, and may the shadows of temptations flee. May we advance toward what is better by your example, lest, remaining in what is worse, we lose the gifts of life. When the time of pruning arrives, may the faith by which we believe in Christ free us from punishments, and may the affection by which we strive to draw near to him enrich us with everlasting gifts.  
**R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

## At Lauds

### At the Canticle

**Antiphon.** You know, Lord, that I have not eaten at the table of execration, nor drunk libations of wine; for your handmaid has never rejoiced except in you, Lord.

### Canticle of Esther (Chapter 14)

My Lord, almighty King, help me who am anxious, for I have no other helper besides you. *My danger is in my hand.*

For I have heard from my father that you, Lord, took Israel from among all the nations, *and our fathers from all their ancestors of old,

that you might possess an everlasting inheritance,* and you acted toward them as you had spoken.

We sinned in your sight, and therefore you delivered us into the hand of our enemies.

You are just, Lord; *and now it is not enough for them that they oppress us with the harshest slavery,

but, attributing the strength of their hands to the power of idols, *they seek to change your promises and destroy your inheritance,

to close the mouths of those who praise you,* and extinguish the glory of your temple and altar,

so that they may open the mouths of the nations and praise the power of idols,* and proclaim a fleshly king for ever.

Do not hand over your scepter, Lord, to those who do not exist,* lest they laugh at our ruin.

But turn their plan against them,* and destroy the one who began to rage against us.

Remember, Lord, and show yourself to us in the time of our tribulation,* and give me confidence, King of the gods and Lord of every power.

Grant a well-ordered speech to my mouth in the presence of the lion, and turn his heart into hatred of our enemy,* so that he himself may perish, together with the others who agree with him.

Help us with your unfettered hand; we have no other helper,* except you, Lord, who have knowledge of all things. You know that I hate the glory of the wicked,

and abhor the bed of the uncircumcised,* and that of every foreigner.

You know my need: that I hate the sign of my pride and glory,* which is upon my head in the days of my display,

and that I abhor it like a menstrual cloth,* and do not wear it in the days of my silence.

I have not eaten at Haman’s table,* nor has the king’s banquet pleased me, nor have I drunk libations of wine.

Your handmaid has never rejoiced since I was brought here until this present day,* except in you, Lord God of Abraham.

Strong God above all, hear the voice of those who have no other hope,* and free us from the hand of the wicked, and rescue me from my fear.

### Prayer

We entrust our weakness to your help, Lord, to be defended and protected, so that it may be yours to enable us to escape the snares of the ungodly, just as it was yours that venerable Eulalia should not yield to the terrors of her persecutors. And just as the savagery of the raging enemy did not frighten her, so may the traps of the barking adversary be unable to ensnare us; so that the one who was conquered through Eulalia, whose passion prevailed, may himself alone be conquered through us, together with all his insults and errors.  
**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

### At the Benedictus

**Antiphon.** Daughter of Zion, bless the Lord God Most High with every blessing and praise.

**Canticle.** Blessed are you, Lord. Folio 6.

### Prayer

Blessed Virgin of God, who stand gloriously in the watchtower of Zion, whom God himself testifies to have loved, since he promises you that his mercy will never again depart from you: grant us, Lord, through her merits, that, burning with divine love, we may be found unharmed at the future judgment. Amen.

And aided by the grace of that divinity who is pious and merciful throughout all ages of ages.  
**R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**Sono.** Alleluia. Go forth after the footsteps of your flocks, virgin daughter of Zion, and feed your lambs. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.  
**V.** Alleluia. Enter my garden, my bride, daughter of Jerusalem. Behold, your flowers shall sprout upon the earth. Feed now among the lilies until the day breathes and the shadows are removed.

**Lauda.** Praise the Lord from the heavens. Alleluia, alleluia; praise him in the heights. Alleluia, alleluia. Psalm 148.

### Reading from the Book of Ecclesiasticus of Solomon (Chapter 24)

**R.** Thanks be to God.

Wisdom shall praise herself, and shall be honored in the Lord. In the midst of her people she shall glory; in the assemblies of the Most High she shall open her mouth, and in the sight of his power she shall be honored. In the midst of the people she shall be exalted, and in the fullness of holiness she shall be admired. Among the multitude of the elect she shall have praise, and among the blessed she shall be blessed, saying:

“I have been exalted like a cedar in Lebanon, and like a cypress on Mount Zion; I have been exalted like a palm tree in Cades, and like a rose plantation in Jericho; like a beautiful olive tree in the fields, and like a plane tree I have spread out beside the water in the streets.

Like cinnamon and fragrant aspalathus, I have given forth perfume; like chosen myrrh I have given sweetness of odor; like storax, galbanum, onycha, and stacte, and like unburned incense, I have perfumed my dwelling; and like unmixed balsam is my fragrance.

I have spread my branches like a terebinth, and my branches are branches of honor and grace. I have borne fruit like a vine, the fragrance of sweetness; and my flowers are flowers of honor and dignity.

I am the mother of beautiful love, of fear, of knowledge, and of holy hope. In me is every grace of life and truth; in me is every hope of life and virtue.

Come over to me, all who desire me, and be filled with my fruits; for my spirit is sweeter than honey, and my inheritance is sweeter than honey and the honeycomb. My memory is through the generations of ages.

Those who eat me will hunger still, and those who drink me will thirst still. Those who hear me will not be confounded, and those who work in me will not sin. Those who make me known will possess eternal life.”  
**R.** Amen.

### Hymn

Let us sing the praise  
Of blessed Eulalia  
With a pure heart:  
Christ consecrated her  
Among the martyrs  
With chaste blood.

Confined behind hard doors  
And between strong hinges,  
Knowing neither sleep nor food,  
She sang to Christ  
Through the wakeful night.

The guardian of dreadful light  
Was amazed at the brightness in the chains;  
In the narrowness of the prison  
Were the joys  
Of the blessed mind.

The judge, turbulent with fury,  
Rises with bloody jaws  
And rebukes the delay of night,  
About to offer  
A holy victim.

With a slow first blow  
The girl of Christ is struck,  
But she utterly refuses  
To consecrate  
An impious libation upon the altars.

Then, with her arms drawn upward  
Upon a cut-off tree,  
The girl’s side is struck,  
And naked she is burned  
By the flames.

The victorious spirit departs,  
Leaving the body pale;  
May God restore to life  
That which has perished  
By the law of death.

Now sing psalms to Rest,  
Give praise to the Father,  
And let us praise the merciful Christ,  
Together with the Holy Spirit.

This Trinity has redeemed us;  
Its everlasting glory  
Knows no death through the ages,  
Living throughout every age.

Amen.

**Supplication.** Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world, changing the name, folio 187.

### Capitula

Lord Jesus Christ, to whom blessed Eulalia was pleasing as a virgin and adhered as a martyr: while she remains chaste as a virgin for you and is stretched out upon the rack for you; while she preserves her body whole for you and rejoices to have it scored by claws for you: favoring her chastity and victory, deign to be gracious to us, so that our uncleanness may be washed away through her prayer, and our torments may be undone through her courage.

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. Folio 2.

**Lauda.** I have been exalted like a palm tree.

**Blessing.** God of virtues. Seek it at the preceding Vespers.

May the Lord be with you.  
**R.** And with you.

**Lauda.** In beauty and loveliness. Folio 179.

**Hymn.** Let us praise blessed Eulalia.

**Supplication.** Let us pray to the Redeemer. See above at Lauds.

### Capitula

Lord Jesus Christ, possessing the mysteries of your holy Eulalia, you granted her both the modesty of virginity and the redness of passion, while she remains modest in secret and unconquered in the public place; while there she remains in order to merit you, and here she conquers in order to be crowned by you. Grant her prayers, that modesty may possess our conscience in such a way that courage does not abandon it; that it may remain tranquil there, lest it be defiled; and that here it may strive to conquer, so that it may be proved, O most merciful one.

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. Folio 2.

### Blessing

May the Lord Jesus Christ, who strengthened holy Eulalia with steadfastness, make you strong in temptation.  
**R.** Amen.

May he who glorified her through passion wipe away from you the disgrace of sufferings.  
**R.** Amen.

May he who made her victorious over her torturers amid torments rescue you from every perilous outcome amid the whirlwinds of the world.  
**R.** Amen.

**Lauda.** I have been exalted like a palm tree.

### Prayer

Lord Jesus Christ, who blessed Eulalia … See at the preceding Vespers.

# Day Twelve: The Feast of Saint Eugenia, Virgin, and Her Companions, Martyrs

## At Vespers

**Lauda.** It has risen. Folio 162.

**Sono.** Rejoice, righteous ones. Folio 165.

**Antiphon.** Righteous men. Folio 162.

**Lauda.** They called upon the Lord. Folio 168.

### Hymn

In honor of Saint Eugenia  
Let us sing with chaste praises;  
With faithful rejoicing in Christ,  
Let us sing with a sweet measure.

He who long ago consecrated  
The holy Virgin with a pure heart,  
Possessing the mysteries of her mind,  
Illumines her with sacred radiance.

The faithful servant of Christ  
Tramples the world’s pride;  
Taking up the narrow path,  
She follows the heavenly life.

While she lived a chaste life  
And dwelt in a monastery,  
Having become a father to the monks,  
She concealed her womanhood beneath her disguise.

The devouring disease of lust  
Torments Melantia’s heart.  
When she had seen the beautiful face,  
She is seized by blind love.

The Virgin of Christ, perceiving this,  
Drives it away with her words,  
Rejecting with a sure song  
The savage venom of serpents.

Armed with a demon’s fury,  
She approaches the judge’s tribunal  
With wicked words,  
Assailing the chaste soul.

But the obscenity is burned away,  
And chastity is proved holy.  
The prefect, when he received Eugenia  
As his own child,

Immediately they despise the idols;  
The Church is opened;  
The father, in the priesthood,  
Is dedicated as a martyr to Christ.

Soon Claudia returns  
From Alexandria to Rome  
With her children; but Eugenia  
Follows the courts of Christ.

Then Eugenia, unmarried,  
Offers Prothus and Hyacinthus, her companions,  
Filled with the virtue of Christ,  
As servants to Basilla,  
Soon through divine oracles…

They search the Virgin’s heart;

therefore Pompeius spurned,

and believed Christ to be God,

for whom he is struck with the sword

and joined to Christ as his bridegroom.

[Col. 1286C] [CCCXLVII] Prothus and Hyacinthus once more

are punished with the sword at their necks.

After these things Eugenia,

struck by twenty blows,

knowing neither drink nor food,

is struck by the sword-point [*mucrone plectitur civis*; syntax uncertain].

Her spirit is placed in heaven

with the ranks of the saints;

we, at the yearly recurrence,

pay a hymn to God.

By the merits of these saints, O God,

now snatched away from vices,

raise us upward from defilement,

restoring us to the sacred dwellings.

Grant this, illustrious Father,

who rules all things with the Son,

together with the Paraclete Spirit,

through every age.

Amen.

**Supplication.** Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world, with the name changed, fol. ClXXXVII.

**Capitula.** Behold, behold, beloved brothers, the wondrous works of God: how Eugenia the virgin endured martyrdom for the name of Jesus, so that she was neither cast into the waters nor burned by the flames. This faith was certainly increased, for which our Lord foretold that nothing would be difficult for those who ask him in faith: therefore, with this faith, which works through love, let us entreat the mercy of the loving Father, that he receive our tears, [Col. 1287A] wash away our sins, bestow grace, and ward off whatever things seem adverse to us. For if we ask him confidently, we have hope that he will hear the voice of our cry, when we proclaim from the earth to him those things which we have learned by the instruction of the Lord Jesus Christ:

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

**Blessing.** May the Most High and eternal God, terrible, in whose service Eugenia offered herself to serve in manly attire and with her hair shorn, cause you, with the cares of the world cut off and severed, to grasp an undefiled life. R\. Amen. May he who made manifest to the assembled peoples her virginity, which deceived Melantia, show forth in you the riches of his mercies. R\. Amen. And after her passing, may you deserve to have a share with her who deserved to win the crown for Christ her Lord. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

**Praise-song.** Everlasting joy. fol. ClXII.

**Prayer.** O God, who gave your saints Eugenia the virgin and her companion martyrs such great grace in their passion that they signally overcame the openly revealed enemy of faith, once they had spiritually conquered within themselves the battles of their bodies: grant us the firmest aid of your devotion, so that, fortified and girded by it, we may restrain the flesh rebelling against the spirit, and may strive fearlessly to prepare ourselves for spiritual battles. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

## At Matins

[Col. 1287C] **Antiphon.** Give us. Psalm L. **Prayer.** Restore to us. Fol. ClXIII.

**Antiphon.** Your saints, O Lord. **Prayer.** O Lord, your saints—the virgin Eugenia and her fellow martyrs—supported by the strength of your right hand, [are] invincible. See fol. ClXVI.

**Antiphon.** Your saints, O Lord, have attained a wondrous journey, serving your commandments, so that they were found unharmed in the mighty water.

**P.** The earth appeared dry, and in the Red Sea a way without impediment.

**V\.** Let them confess to the Lord his mercies, and his wonders to the children of men.

**P.** The earth appeared.

**V\.** Glory and honor.

**P.** The earth.

**Prayer.** O God, who [did this] for the saints, as above.

**Antiphon.** The salvation of the righteous. fol. CClXVIII.

[Col. 1287D] **Prayer.** O God, who lavish both strength upon the saints and the ornaments of holiness, adorn with the marks of sanctity this Church, which observes this feast in honour of the martyrs, the virgin Eugenia and her companions, so that the martyrs who glory in standing victorious in triumph may be embraced by the eternal happiness of your saints. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

**Responsory.** Blessed are those who have. fol. CCXVI.

## At Lauds

**For the Canticle. Antiphon.** Those who love you. **Canticle.** He who willingly. **At the Benedictus. Antiphon.** Holy and humble. **Canticle.** Blessed are you. **Sounding.** The salvation of the righteous. **Praise-song.** Praise the Lord. Fol. ClXIV.

**Prophecy.** The souls of the righteous. Fol. ClXVII.

**Hymn.** With honor [Col. 1288A] to Saint Eugenia.

**Supplication.** Let us pray.

**Capitula.** Behold, behold.

## At the preceding Vespers

[CCCXLVIII] **Praise-song.** The Lord’s praise in the church of the saints. Alleluia.

**P.** Let Israel rejoice in him who made it. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.

**V\.** Sing to the Lord a new song, because he has done wonders.

**P.** Let Israel rejoice.

**V\.** Glory and honor.

**P.** Let Israel rejoice.

**Blessing.** The Most High and eternal God. At the preceding Vespers.

# DAY XIV. THE FEAST OF SAINTS JUSTUS AND ABUNDUS

## At Vespers

**Praise-song.** It has arisen. **Sounding.** Rejoice, you righteous. Fol. ClXV.

**Antiphon.** Great joy.

**Praise-song.** The Lord will come. fol. CCCXXV.

## Hymn

[Col. 1288B]

Behold, the living voice of the prophets resounds,

announcing and proclaiming that Christ will come and be born;

now the devout people celebrate his feast,

which, bearing bright water, puts forth its light.
