The one whom Gabriel’s clear voice announces,

whom the Virgin bears, who alone shines brightly,

the fruitful Virgin suckles,

and the Virgin nurse devotes herself to him.

His dedicated passion urges

that every faithful person grow red with blood,

and become powerful through the gift of passion,

and rejoice to be slain in both ways.

The holy resolve of Justus and Abundus hastens to follow him,

and also proclaims that he must be followed—

he who lies hidden in faith

and jubilantly declares that he will be strong.

Numerianus judges that those who follow him

must be slain, and commands Olybrius

to subject Christians to the sword

and openly oppress Christ’s servants.

Olybrius, when he hears of Justus,

seized by fury, neither asks nor inquires

whether Justus himself is a Christian, but investigates it;

the servant of Christ immediately cries out:

he is faithful, and does not hesitate to die.

The governor, terrified at this,

provokes the faithful man’s limbs,

nor does he cry out,

so that the cruel device of the wheels may crush him.

[Col. 1288D] But the mind, enriched, is not at all afraid;

with clear voice it jubilantly sings songs.

Christ so glorifies him for himself

that, surpassing his vows, he now offers him free.

The savage tyrant thunders out commands:

that the terrible furnace should blaze with fires,

that it should receive the limbs of the holy witness,

and that, as the martyr walks to offer incense,

he should either perish in the fire stirred up by anger

or submit himself to harsh death

and swiftly cling to the flames of the pyres,

so that he may be unable to oppose the governor.

But the one whom his enriched mind raises up well,

and whom the grace of his merits consecrates,

is conquered neither by flame nor overcome by punishment;

[Col. 1289A] thrust into the fire, he walks unharmed.

While Abundus still watches devoutly,

he quickly joins himself to the martyr,

suddenly tastes Christ in his mind,

and assails Olybrius himself with his words.

When the fame of this resounds to the governor,

he rages in anger and begins to terrify him:

Saint Abundus must yield to the idols,

and, yielding to them, freely offer incense.

But because the saint could not be conquered,

he commands that his companion Justus

be burned by torches,

so that his life may perish

and he may now quickly yield to danger.

But he who walks upon the sea with his feet,

and by his power passes through closed bodies,

causes these men to flee the punishments of fire

and likewise makes them stand secure.

He himself joins them to the saints in heaven,

and that flaming fire flies away,

and those whom the flame had received for burning,

once the fire was extinguished, it consecrates with cooling dew.

Thus neither does a hair of their heads burn,

nor does the garment itself cling to the fires;

but, moistened with dew, it remains safe.

The Spirit who governs all things brings this about,

so that now, following their example, every faithful person may dare,

and may offer the gift of his prayer,

and serve with his mind

the one who, taking pity, judges all things.

May he himself receive the vows of those who pray,

[Col. 1289C] and open the gate of paradise—

he who, thundering in heaven, lovingly helps us

and alone wills to fight all things.

Honor be to him who alone thunders

from the seat of heaven and judges all things;

to him may every tongue submit itself

and sing songs throughout every age.

Amen.

**Supplication.** Let us pray, as in the others.

**Capitula.** O God, eternal light, unquenchable lamp, and light of truth, gladden your people on this celebration of your most blessed martyrs Justus and Abundus, so that [CCCXLIX] those who are saddened by their own merits may be consoled by their prayers.

[Col. 1289D] **Our Father.** Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

**Blessing.** Through the intercession of his martyrs Justus and Abundus, may the blessing of the Lord accompany you on earth—he who advanced them to heaven. R\. Amen. May he make you happy through the intercession of those whose solemnities you are now celebrating. R\. Amen. So that, just as they contended for justice unto death, so may you, following in their footsteps, hasten free to the heavenly kingdoms. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

**Praise-song.** Faithful in love. And let all the other things through the Capitulum be said successively, as at the feast of Cecilia the virgin, fol. CCCXXVI.

**Capitula.** Give us, O Lord, the joys of eternal happiness, so that we may always be able to rejoice in you, lest we be overwhelmed by contemptible [Col. 1290A] sadness, and lest we be anxious about temporal things in any respect; so that we who already believe you to be near may feel you most gentle when you come.

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

**Praise-song.** Faithful in love.

**Blessing.** Through the intercession of the martyrs. See at the preceding Vespers.

# DAY XVIII. THE FEAST OF THE ANNUNCIATION OF THE HOLY VIRGIN MARY

## At Vespers

**Praise-song.** Virgin of Israel, adorn yourself with your timbrels.

**P.** And go forth in the choir of those who sing psalms.

**V\.** Blessed are you, queen, who look forth like the light.

**P.** And go forth.

**V\.** The queen stood in a golden garment.

**P.** And go forth.

**V\.** Go forth, shining exceedingly like the moon.

**P.** And go forth.

[Col. 1290B] **V\.** Go forth, like a bride rising up, beautiful as the moon.

**P.** And go forth.

**Prayer.** Virgin of Israel, who are understood to be the mother of the One who sees, adorn yourself with your timbrels—that is, with the members of the Church—so that we may have you as our patroness in this age, whom we believe will remain a blessed queen in the future; so that, looking upon you as without doubt the light of our faith, through your intercession we may deserve most firmly to obtain the favor of blessedness. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

**Sounding.** The angel appeared to Mary, saying: Behold, you will conceive and bear a son.

**P.** And you shall call his name Emmanuel. Alleluia.

**V\.** The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you; therefore the Holy One who will be born from you will be called the Son of God.

**P.** And he will be called.

**V\.** Glory and honor.

**P.** And he will be called.

**May the Lord be with you.**

**R\.** And with you.

**Antiphon.** Alleluia: I saw a gate in the house of the Lord, closed; and the angel said to me: This gate which you see shall not be opened, and no one shall pass through it.

**P.** Because the Lord God of Israel will enter through it, and it shall remain closed.

**V\.** Lift up your gates, princes, and be lifted up, eternal gates, and the King of glory shall enter.

**P.** Because.

**V\.** Glory and honor.

**P.** Because.

**Prayer.** Word of power and Wisdom of the Father, who neither violate the gate of the mother’s womb when entering nor corrupt the Virgin by conception, and who are not recognized as depriving the mother of virginity in childbirth: grant us that, through the intercession of her who bore you as Son, she may obtain for us what is asked; and that she who deserved to bear you without intercourse may cause us to bring forth through your conception, so that, enlarging our mouth in the gates of Zion, we may conceive the spirit of salvation; and thus may we proclaim the miracle of your new people, so that uncorrupted faith may always possess our heart. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

**Antiphon.** The Lord will give you a sign on the earth: a virgin shall conceive in the womb and bear a son, and you shall call his name Emmanuel.

**P.** Know, nations, that God is with us.

**V\.** Hear, my people, and I will testify to you: Israel, if you will hear me.

**P.** Know, nations.

**V\.** Glory and honor.

**P.** Know, nations.

**May the Lord be with you.**

**R\.** And with you.

[Col. 1291A] **Praise-song.** Shine forth, Jerusalem.

**P.** Behold, your king comes, and the majesty of the Lord has overshadowed you. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.

Praise the Lord, Jerusalem; praise your God, Zion.

**P.** Behold, your king.

**V\.** Glory and honor.

**P.** Behold, your king.

## Hymn

From the rising of the sun’s course

to the farthest limit of the earth,

let us sing of Christ the Prince,

born of the Virgin Mary.

[CCCL] The blessed Author of the age

put on a servant’s body,

so that, by freeing flesh through flesh,

he might not lose those whom he created.

The closed womb of the Mother

is entered by heavenly grace;

the maiden’s womb carries

secrets it had not known.

The house of the chaste heart

suddenly becomes God’s temple.

Untouched, knowing no man,

she created a Son by the Word.

The mother gave birth:

to him whom Gabriel had foretold;

whom John, enclosed within his mother’s womb,

perceived.

The gate of Christ becomes passable,

restored and full of grace;

the king passes through and remains,

closed as it was throughout the ages.

[Col. 1291C] The offspring of the heavenly Godhead

proceeded from the Virgin’s palace—

the Bridegroom, Redeemer, Creator,

the giant of his Church.

The Mother’s honor and joy,

the immense hope of believers,

through the bitter cups of death

resolved the sins of the world.

Glory be to God the Father

and to his only Son,

with the Paraclete Spirit,

reigning throughout every age.

Amen.

**Supplication.** Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world, our Lord [Col. 1291D] Jesus Christ, with every supplication, so that through the intercession and merit of the glorious holy Virgin Mary, his mother, he may graciously deign to grant us forgiveness of sins and peace. R\. Grant this, eternal almighty God.

**Kyrie eleison.** R\. Christ, have mercy. Lord, have mercy.

**Capitula.** Virgin, mother of Christ and restorer of the human race, present the prayers of those who implore you to the divine ears, so that, rejoicing in your gift and made worthy through your intercession, we may obtain from God forgiveness of sins, whose sex, without corruption of modesty, bore the Savior of all.

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

**Blessing.** May the Lord Jesus Christ, who once deigned to be born of a Virgin, sanctify you through the intercession of his Mother. R\. Amen. May he who preserved his mother from the contagion of corruption cleanse the bosom of your heart from sin. R\. Amen. And may he who caused her to remain a virgin after childbirth grant you possession of heaven after your passing. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

**Praise-song.** Behold the time, says the Lord, in which she who is in labor will give birth. Alleluia.

**P.** And this will be peace forever. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.

**V\.** Hear this, all nations; listen with your ears, you who inhabit the world.

**P.** And this will be.

**V\.** Glory and honor.

**P.** And this will be.

**Prayer.** We believe that you, O Virgin Mary, glorious mother of Christ and restorer of the human race, possess the fullness of grace, for by giving birth you bestowed such great joys upon us that the fruit of your womb, which is Christ [Col. 1292B] the Son of God, rescued us from the dominion of the enemy raging against us and made us his companions in the eternal kingdom. Therefore we ask and entreat you to be our patroness, so that by your merit your Son may make us exiles from sin and afterward bring us into his kingdom, where we shall dwell forever. Grant us that he who, desiring you, called you to himself as mother may bestow upon us the abundant sweetness of his desire. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

In the name of the Lord.

## At Matins

**Antiphon.** The Lord God sprinkled me with hyssop and cleansed me; he washed me and made me whiter than snow. Psalm L.

[Col. 1292C] **Prayer.** O God, who always love what is true and reveal the things hidden in your wisdom, who deigned to enter a virgin womb for the salvation of the world: sprinkle us with the hyssop of your word and cleanse us from our iniquities, so that although we have sinned against you alone and done evil before you, you may not, in anger at our sins, inflict punishment, but, in your mercy, pour into our inward parts a right spirit that may invoke you. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

**Antiphon 1.** Hail, Mary, full of grace; the Lord is with you. Blessed are you among women.

**P.** And blessed is the fruit of your womb.

**V\.** Grace has been poured upon your lips; therefore God has blessed you forever.

**P.** And blessed is the fruit.

[Col. 1292D] [CCCLI] **V\.** Glory and honor.

**P.** And blessed is the fruit.

**Prayer.** We believe that you possess the fullness of grace. See above, at the preceding Vespers.

**Antiphon 2.** We saw a great miracle in the Virgin’s conception: she neither lost her virginity nor experienced the burdens of motherhood.

**P.** She alone deserved to bear God after the heavens; she alone, a virgin, deserved to come forth after childbirth.

**V\.** The earth is the Lord’s and its fullness, the world and all who dwell in it.

**P.** She alone deserved.

**V\.** Glory and honor.

**P.** She alone deserved.

**Prayer.** We saw a very great miracle in the Virgin’s conception: she neither lacked the beauty of modesty nor endured the burdens of motherhood. For it was not fitting that she should have sighs who gave birth to the joys of all, or that the source of joy should know the force of pain. Thus the virgin alone deserved to come forth after childbirth, because in her the Word was made flesh. Therefore we entreat you, good Jesus, that just as you bestowed this reward upon your Mother, so you may be present to us wretched people by granting us a remedy. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

**Antiphon 3.** The Spirit of the Lord will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you.

**P.** Therefore the Holy One who will be born from you will be called the Son of God.

**V\.** You have loved righteousness and hated iniquity; therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your companions.

**P.** Therefore.

**V\.** Glory and honor.

**P.** Therefore.

**Prayer.** Holy Spirit, who are the sanctification of the Father [Col. 1293B] and the Son, descend into our hearts, so that from you we may understand what is true and confess what is true. For you are a good spirit in all things, because you rightly will everything that you will. You filled our Virgin and illumined her with the nourishing grace of your sanctification. From her you suddenly brought forth for us a new offering upon the earth, so that, walking in her light, we may happily deserve to attain the salvation of our souls. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

**R\.** The angel Gabriel was sent by God to Mary the Virgin, saying: Hail, Mary, full of grace; the Lord is with you; blessed are you among women.

**P.** Therefore also the Holy One who will be born from you will be called the Son of God.

**V\.** The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you.

**P.** Therefore also the one who will be born.

**V\.** Glory and honor.

**P.** Therefore also the one who will be born.

**Prayer.** O most holy Gabriel, O strength of the Most High Father, O messenger of truth, O appointed bearer of the divine mystery, most true discoverer: you come to the Virgin, you greet her as a messenger, you overshadow her as a servant. “Hail,” you say, “Mary”; you proclaim, “My Lord is with you”; you declare that she is blessed among women; you proclaim that the Word will come forth from her; and you profess with wondrous testimony that he should be called the Son of God. Therefore we ask that you, who came wondrously to the Virgin as a messenger of truth, present our petition to the divine ears, and that through you we may know the hidden mysteries in such a way that we never fall into the prison of the enemy; so that through the Word of the Most High God the Father himself, whom you announce that you come beforehand to the Virgin, we may have both the restoration of pardon and a most certain habitation in the eternal homeland. R\. Amen.

**Antiphon 1.** In me is every hope of life and virtue. I am the mother of beautiful love.

**P.** And my branches are of honor and grace.

**V\.** My heart has poured forth a good word; I speak of my works to the king. My tongue is the pen of a swift-writing scribe.

**P.** And my branches.

**V\.** Glory and honor.

**P.** And my branches.

**Prayer.** Truly wondrous, O Lord, is the root of your Church, which advances and grows toward the perfect day, whose branches are the martyrs and whose supports have become the confessors; among them is the most blessed Virgin Mary, your mother, fruit-bearing like a true vine. While she offers the faithful the fragrance of grace in this age, she deserves to be consoled eternally [Col. 1294A] by her reward. Therefore we ask that, through her intercession and the fragrance of her virtues, we may flee the odors of our sins; that, refreshed by that heavenly breath, we may be found exiled from the stench of all vices and sober. R\. Amen.

**Antiphon 2.** You are clothed in garments of glory and adorned with holy ornaments.

**P.** And you have been made beautiful when invoked by the Lord.

**V\.** The Lord guards you from every evil; the Lord guards your soul.

**P.** And you have been made.

**V\.** Glory and honor.

**P.** And you have been made.

**Prayer.** Virgin Mary of Christ, now clothed in garments of glory and adorned with holy ornaments, you who have indeed been made beautiful when, invoked by the Lord, you became the mother of the Lord and the chosen handmaid of the Son, when you conceived the Word through your ear and gave birth to the Lord both for us and for yourself: receive the vows of the little people gathering toward you, [CCCLII] and present to your Son, our Lord, the service of our servitude, so that we who, driven by vices, fall toward what is low may through your merits be raised to heavenly things; and so that we who cannot be adorned with the ornaments of merits, cleansed from sins through your intercession, may celebrate at its yearly recurrence the most sacred feast of your conception. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

**Antiphon.** The Lord gave her wisdom, made her blessed, and girded her with a belt of glory.

**P.** He clothed her in a robe of beauty and crowned her with vessels of virtue.

**V\.** Her seed will be powerful on earth; the generation of the upright will be blessed.

**P.** He clothed her.

**V\.** Glory and honor.

**P.** He clothed her.

[Col. 1294C] **Prayer.** Lord God the Father, who bestowed wisdom upon the blessed Mother of your Son, our Lord, making her blessed, girding her with a belt of glory, and clothing her in a robe of beauty—that is, so that a virgin might conceive, and a virgin give birth, and the glory of her childbirth, spread throughout the whole world, might bear fruit: give us such wisdom of the spirit that it may make us blessed before you in our works, render us splendid in dignity, and clothe us in a robe of beauty; so that, just as the Virgin Mary, conceiving the Wisdom of God, bore the Lord for every creature, so we may be filled with wisdom by which we may become pleasing to you in vessels of virtue. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

**R\.** Daughter of Zion, you shall consecrate multitudes of peoples to the Lord; and you, Bethlehem, house of acceptance, very least among the thousands of Judah: from you will go forth the beginning of the kingdom of Israel.

**P.** Whose procession is from the beginning of the age. Therefore the time of the woman in labor has come, and you will swiftly bear the Redeemer of all the children of Israel.

**V\.** Bethlehem, city of the Most High God, from you the Ruler of Israel went forth.

**P.** Whose procession.

**V\.** Glory and honor.

**P.** Whose procession.

**Prayer.** Jesus, God of all virtues, who through the mystery of your blessed Mother consecrate multitudes of peoples to yourself, enriching the Virgin by a wondrous conception through a new miracle, yet not depriving the mother of the honor of virginity, so that the mystery of your Incarnation might remain both a singular pattern beyond comparison and an admirable reality without any rational explication: [Col. 1295A] grant us to know fully the secrets of this mystery in complete faith and to love them with fuller ardor of charity, so that through what we believe to be true about you we may come more ardently to what you grant to those who love you. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

**Antiphon 1.** You are the cloud-covered tower of the king, daughter of Zion; the Savior will come to you.

**P.** And the first power will come, the kingdom of the daughter of Jerusalem.

**V\.** Pray for the things that are for the peace of Jerusalem, and abundance for those who love you.

**P.** And he will come.

**V\.** Glory and honor.

**P.** And he will come.

**Prayer.** Lord Jesus, who by divine birth precede all things and are born at the end of the ages to redeem all things, giving a beginning to wretched realities in your omnipotence and restoring justification to human beings in humility, when you enter the dwelling of the cloud-covered tower and come to it as the first power to reign: grant us to confess you with that spirit by which you willed, through the Virgin’s womb, to be joined to human mortality. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

**Antiphon 2.** Bethlehem, house of Ephrathah, you are not least among the princes of Judah; from you will go forth a king who will rule my people Israel.

**P.** And his going forth is from the days of eternity.

**V\.** The mother Zion will say: A man and a man was born in her; and the Most High himself founded her.

**P.** And his going forth.

**V\.** Glory and honor.

**P.** And his going forth.

**Prayer.** Great is Bethlehem, O Lord, that city which nourished your Incarnation, illumined by the proclamations of the prophets, since you were announced as going forth from it and were gloriously revealed in it; for there you adorned your most blessed mother and virgin, Mary, with appearance and beauty. She rightly bore you incorrupt, just as she conceived you incorrupt. Therefore be present to us wretched people through her continual prayers, so that, just as your birth advanced her to praise, so her merits may advance us to salvation. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

**Antiphon 3.** Virgin of Israel, return to your cities. How long will you turn away in sorrow?

**P.** You will bear the Lord the Savior, a new offering on earth; people will walk in salvation.

**V\.** Glorious things are spoken of you, city of God.

**P.** You will bear the Lord.

**V\.** Glory and honor.

**P.** You will bear the Lord.

**Prayer.** Lord Jesus, who, being born of the Virgin, trampled underfoot both the head of the ancient Serpent and all the contagions of pleasure, when the Virgin Mother bore you on earth as a new offering, which the serpent desired to drive into exile from its dwelling: grant us to hate the mystical touch of this serpent [CCCLIII] and of all sins in such a way that our soul may love you alone, whom it may receive as its reward and possess in the delight of eternity. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

**R\.** Hear a sign from the Lord, people of God: a virgin has been found with a child in the womb by the Holy Spirit, and the Virgin’s name is Mary. For the Holy Spirit came upon her, and the power of the Most High overshadowed her, so that what was spoken by the prophet from the Lord might be fulfilled: Behold, a virgin shall have a son.

**P.** And his name shall be called Emmanuel.

**V\.** The angel of the Lord came to Mary the Virgin, saying: Behold, you will conceive and bear a son.

**P.** And his name.

**V\.** Glory and honor.

**P.** And his name.

**Prayer.** Ineffable, only-begotten Word of the unbegotten Father, at whose birth the modesty of the Virgin Mother shone forth and the splendor of a new generation illuminated the world: for through you all things were made which we believe were accomplished in the mystery of your Incarnation—namely, that the angel appeared to Joseph, the husband of your Mother, and foretold that you had been born in her from the Holy Spirit. Therefore grant us, we ask, through the merits of your holy Mother and Virgin, that, made fruitful by the conception of the Holy Spirit, we may conceive you in our heart in such a way that we may always bring forth in our works nothing other than you. R\. Amen.

**Antiphon 1.** My soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit has rejoiced in God my Savior.

**P.** Because he has regarded the humility of his handmaid.

**V\.** What shall I repay the Lord for all that he has repaid me?

**P.** Because he has regarded.

**V\.** Glory and honor to the Father.

**P.** Because he has regarded.

**Prayer.** How much and how greatly divine kindness distributed to you, most holy Virgin and mother of God, so that, although you were an earthly virgin, you became the mother and little handmaid of the Most High; so that he whose holy name you proclaimed in every generation and lineage may come to the aid of us who are weak, once the evil suggestion of rancor has been wiped away. And may he who was present to you as the best inhabitant deign to rule within us as the gentlest rewarder, so that through the one God perfect in Trinity both the merits of faith may flourish and the joys of his distribution may grow together. And because, though unworthy, we ask this, may we through you, queen and mother of the Creator of all ages, enjoy the flowering fields of paradise—you who have remained an intact, God-bearing virgin. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

**Antiphon 2.** I am betrothed to him alone whom the angels serve, whose beauty the sun and moon admire.

**P.** To him alone I keep faith; to him alone I commend myself with complete devotion.

**V\.** To him I cried out with my mouth, and under my tongue I rejoiced.

**P.** To him alone.

**V\.** Glory and honor to the Father.

**P.** To him alone.

**Prayer.** Jesus, Son of God, who so approve the most blessed Mary as a virgin that you show her to be a mother, and so honor her as a mother that you make her a virgin through an admirable conception, when your Godhead sends an angel to her, by whom she hears herself called blessed among women: grant your suppliant household that, in her likeness, our heart may bear fruit in chastity and not refuse to obey your commands, so that with her we may deserve to stand at your right hand at the final judgment, whom we now truly believe she bore as a virgin. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

**Antiphon 3.** Alone I have traveled around the circle of heaven and walked upon the waves of the sea. Over every land and among every people I held primacy. By my own power I trampled the necks of the proud and the humble.

**V\.** Until I enter the sanctuary of God and understand at the last.

**P.** And among every people.

**V\.** Glory and honor.

**P.** And among every people.

**Prayer.** Christ, Wisdom of God and Word of the Most High Father, who build for yourself a most beautiful house, the womb of the Virgin Mary, in which you yourself look forth as heavenly justice and from which you bring forth the fruit of your kindness—entering it as God even without bodily clothing, and proceeding from it clothed in flesh: grant us, your suppliants, that you may make us a sanctified house for yourself, from which, proceeding as a bridegroom, you may appear surrounded by the dignity of our works. R\. Amen.

**R\.** Chastity and immaculate virginity pleased God.

**P.** Therefore holy devotion entered her womb; from the Word she showed that she had borne an admirable child, Virgin, God and human being.

**V\.** The heavens proclaimed his righteousness, and all peoples saw his glory.

**P.** Therefore.

**V\.** Glory and honor.

**P.** Therefore.

**Prayer.** May every creature sing a new song to you, O Lord, who displayed in the Virgin Mary the miracle of a new childbirth, so that a woman might surround a man and a virgin, without intercourse with a man, might bear a male child. [CCCLIV] Grant us, therefore, through her intercession, protection in this age—her who bore you through incorrupt childbirth—so that our mind, enlivened by the radiance of the Holy Spirit, may conceive the love of your devotion in such a way that it may always bring forth an increase of good works. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

[Col. 1297C] **Antiphon.** The angel Gabriel was sent to Mary the Virgin, betrothed to Joseph, announcing the Word; and the Virgin was terrified by the light. Do not fear, Mary; you have found grace with the Lord.

**P.** Behold, you will conceive and bear a son, and he will be called the Son of the Most High.

**V\.** For the word of the Lord is upright, and all his works are in faith.

**P.** Behold, you will conceive.

**V\.** Glory and honor.

**P.** Behold, you will conceive.

**Prayer.** Holy Mother of God, who, greeted by the angel, conceive the Word through your ear, mature obedience through faith, and bear the Son in the flesh, trembling at the light and trusting in the grace that comes beforehand: effectively receive the vows of suppliant peoples and richly reward the prayers of each one, so that, receiving into your maternal lap, to be comforted, all whom you see in this pilgrimage running to you and bowed down, you may present them unharmed to Jesus Christ, your Son, our Lord. R\. Amen.

Through.

## At Lauds

**For the Canticle. Antiphon.** He who is mighty has done great things for me, and holy is his name. And his mercy is from generation to generation.

**Canticle (Luke I).**

My soul magnifies the Lord, * and my spirit has rejoiced in God my Savior.

For he has regarded the humility of his handmaid:

Behold, from this moment all generations will call me blessed. * For he who is mighty has done great things for me,

And holy is his name. And his mercy is from generation to generation [Col. 1298A] * upon those who fear him.

He has shown strength with his arm: * he has scattered the proud in the understanding of their heart.

He has brought down the mighty from their throne, * and has exalted the humble.

He has filled the hungry with good things, * and has sent the rich away empty.

He has received Israel his servant, * remembering his mercy,

Which he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham * and to his seed forever.

Glory and honor.

**Prayer.** Behold, the whole assembly of the Church magnifies you, O Lord our Redeemer, with the voice of the blessed Mother, because you regarded the humility of your handmaid [Col. 1298B] when the holy Virgin conceived you; and the Church recognized it through believing when you came forth from her and redeemed this Church; when all nations call her blessed, may the nations of all peoples be blessed in this Church. Therefore receive, O Lord, your people Israel, remembering your mercy, which you spoke to our fathers, so that the singular redemption of the whole world may be the fulfillment of the divine promise. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

**At the Benedictus. Antiphon.** Blessing, honor, glory, and power be to our God, because the marriage of the Lamb has come; let us rejoice and be glad in him.

**Canticle.** Benedictus. fol. 6.

**Sounding.** The angel appeared to Mary. See above at the preceding Vespers.

[Col. 1298C] **Praise-song.** Praise the Lord from the heavens. Alleluia; praise him in the heights. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. Psalm CXLVIII.

**Reading from the Book of the Prophet Ezekiel (chapter XLIII).**

**R\.** Thanks be to God.

The hand of the Lord came upon me, and the spirit lifted me up and led me to the gate that looked toward the eastern road. And behold, the glory of the God of Israel was entering; and its sound was like the sound of many waters, and the earth shone with his majesty. And I fell upon my face. And the majesty of the Lord entered the house of the Lord. And I heard one speaking to me from the house, and the man who stood beside me said to me: Son of man, the place of my throne and the place of the soles of my feet, where I dwell forever. Chapter 44. After this I turned toward the way of the gate of the sanctuary, which looked toward the east; and it was closed. And the Lord said to me: This gate which you see closed shall not be opened, and no man shall pass through it, because the Lord God of Israel will enter through it, and it shall remain closed for the prince. And the prince himself shall sit in it to eat bread before the Lord. And again I saw: and behold, the glory of the Lord filled the house of God, and I heard the voice of one saying: [CCCLV] Blessed is the glory of the Lord from his holy place. R\. Amen.

## Hymn

From the rising of the sun’s course

and to the farthest limit of the earth,

let us sing of Christ the Prince,

born of the Virgin Mary.

[Col. 1299A] Rejoice, whatever peoples there are—

Judea, Rome, and Greece,

Egyptian, Thracian, Persian, Scythian—

one king possesses them all.

Praise your Prince,

all you blessed and lost;

where are the weak and the dead?

After this no one is dead.

The gate of Christ becomes passable,

Filled, full of grace;

And the King passes through, yet it remains

Closed, as it was throughout the ages.

The offspring of the heavenly Godhead

Came forth from the Virgin’s chamber,

The Bridegroom, Redeemer, Creator,

The giant of his Church.

The honor and joy of the Mother,

The boundless hope of believers,

By the dark draughts of Death

Loosed our sins.

The stone coming from the mountain,

And filling the world with grace,

Which, not cut by human hands,

The ancient prophets announce.

He who is the Word, made flesh

By the angelic proclamation,

Was born from the virginal enclosure,

A virgin born of a Virgin.

The heavens gave dew,

And the clouds poured forth the Just One;

The open earth received the Lord,

Bringing forth salvation.

A wondrous conception

Brought forth Christ as offspring,

So that the Virgin might give birth,

And after giving birth remain a virgin.

Let every soul rejoice—

Now that the Lord of the nations,

The Lord of the world, has come

To redeem those whom he created.

The Creator of the whole race,

Whom the entire world cannot contain,

In your holy womb,

O Mother, enclosed himself:

He whom, before the ages,

The Father, God, begot as God,

The gracious virginity of the Mother

Brought forth in time,

Taking away all offenses

And granting holy gifts,

Bringing an increase of light

And inflicting loss upon the darkness.

To God the Father be glory,

And to his only Son,

With the Spirit, the Paraclete,

Throughout everlasting ages.

Amen.

[Col. 1300A] **Supplication.** Let us pray to the Redeemer. Seek it in the preceding Vespers.

**Capitulum.** O most sacred handmaid and mother of the Word, whom childbirth shows to be a Virgin, and virginity proves to be a Mother! Receive, in the open bosom of your compassion, the people running together to you. With the outpouring entrails of your compassion, feed the flock that the Son proceeding from you purchased with his own blood. You who became the nurse of the Creator, offer breasts to those being brought forth. By the service of your servitude glorify those whom you see being given to you for service. May we be fortified by your intercession and protection, who rejoice to enjoy the sweet yoke of your service in your gentle service, so that all who, in honor of your Conception, sing your praises in this place may live perpetually in your service, coming to him whose Mother we celebrate with votive offices, after the stain of sins has been cast off: so that here you may protect us forever with manifold affection, and he who was born from you may possess in eternity those who will reign; he who taught us to pray and say:

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

**Lauda.** “Behold, the time,” says the Lord.  
**Blessing.** May the Lord Jesus Christ, who once came forth from a Virgin—seek it earlier in the preceding Vespers.

### At the conclusion of Vespers

**Lauda.** “Virgin of Israel, adorn yourself with your timbrels.”  
**Tone.** “An angel appeared to Mary, saying: Behold.” Seek it earlier in the First Vespers.

**Antiphon.** O what a great and unheard-of miracle! The Power looked forth from heaven and overshadowed the Virgin’s womb.  
**P.** The Majesty can be enclosed within the chamber of the heart, while the doors remain shut.  
**V.** Truth has sprung from the earth, and justice has looked forth from heaven.  
**P.** The Majesty can.  
**V.** Glory and honor.  
**P.** The Majesty can.

**May the Lord be [with you].**  
**R.** And with [your spirit].

**Lauda.** “Blessed am I, who believed.”  
**P.** “For all the things that were said to me by the Lord will be fulfilled.” Alleluia, alleluia.  
**V.** “O God, I shall sing a new song to you; on the ten-stringed psaltery I shall sing praise to you.”  
**P.** “For all the things that were said to me will be fulfilled.”  
**V.** Glory and honor.  
**P.** “For all the things.”

**Hymn.** “From the rising of the sun.”  
**Supplication.** Let us pray. Seek it in the First Vespers.

**Capitulum.** Blessed is she, O Christ, your glorious Virgin Mary, ruler of the world, who believed from the Angel that what had been said to her by the Lord would be accomplished. Grant us, therefore, we ask, that we who have completed the celebration of the Virgin’s Conception may come to the feast of your Nativity with purified hearts.

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

**Blessing.** May the Word, who made a mother so that she might remain a virgin, grant us the aid of virginity.  
**R.** Amen.  
And may he who preserved the inviolate womb of her belly deign to be continually present as your guardian.  
**R.** Amen.  
So that you who celebrate the Conception of the Mother with rejoicing may be lights in the world, with God justifying you.  
**R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**Lauda.** “Behold the time,” says the Lord, in which—  
[Col. 1301A] **Prayer.** “To possess fullness of grace.” Seek it earlier in the First Vespers.

## The twenty-first day: the feast of Saint Thomas the Apostle

### At Vespers

**Lauda.** “With glory and honor.” fol. CLIX.  
**Tone.** “God girded me.” fol. CLVI.

**Antiphon.** The Lord crowned him, blessed him, and loved him.  
**P.** And he appointed him over many gifts.  
**V.** The mouth of the just shall meditate wisdom, and his tongue shall speak judgment.  
**P.** And he appointed him over many.  
**V.** Glory and honor to the Father.  
**P.** And he appointed him over many.

**May the Lord be always [with you].**  
**R.** And with [your spirit].

**Lauda.** The Lord crowned him with a crown of graces.  
**P.** And with a crown of delights he protected him. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.  
**V.** Blessed is the man who fears the Lord; he greatly desires his commandments.  
**P.** And with a crown.  
**V.** Glory and honor.  
**P.** And with a crown.

**Hymn.**

The saving feast of Christ the King

Has shone throughout the world,

On which the whole company of the faithful

Confesses you

And offers glory and a hymn

For the triumphs of the martyrs.

Behold, your glorious

Thomas, the Disciple,

By handling the scars,

Was convinced that you were the Lord;

Glorious among the brethren,

He became an Apostle.

A messenger came from India

To seek a craftsman,

To construct a royal palace.

He was walking through the marketplace

Among all the things for sale.

“I have a faithful servant,”

Said the Lord,

“whom you are seeking, one suited

To be this craftsman.”

Abbanes, seeing and rejoicing,

Received the Apostle.

The holy Apostle of God

Was handed over to the king’s ministers.

He entered Eliophorus

And received a banquet;

A fitting vengeance

Was rendered to his killer.

When the king saw and heard

The remarkable miracle,

He humbly begged

That he might bless the young men.

Thus he consecrates

Those seeking baptism with the veil.

King Gundaphorus of the Indians,

Wicked and treacherous,

Wanted a palace for himself

In the Roman manner.

He ordered the Apostle

To construct this work.

But the blessed and holy

Apostle Didymus,

By distributing the king’s gold,

Built a palace,

Radiant and glittering with gems,

In the heavenly places.

Soon afterward King Abbanes

Thrust him into prison with the Apostle.

Gath, the king’s sick brother,

Departed from this world.

Led into heaven, he saw

The palace worthy of his brother.

The angels appeal to Christ

That the dead man may rise,

That he may return the gold to Gundaphorus,

Buy the building,

And release the Lord’s Disciple

From his chains.

Rising immediately, he explains

The sacred order to the king.

Then he goes to the prison

And brings out the Apostle.

The brothers everywhere beg

For forgiveness of their sins.

Now Thomas calls the Indian peoples

Into the open country.

He climbs a high stone

And soothes the hearts of the nations;

Through baptism he promises

Forgiveness of sins.

Visiting Upper India,

He proceeds onward,

Preaching the teaching of Christ;

He founded a Church

And consecrated countless thousands

Through baptism.

Performing wondrous and astonishing

Miracles,

He restored Sintica’s bodily sight,

And pours a stream of water over her and Mindonia.

Now the Christian wife

Of the king, Treptia,

Desiring the kingdom of Christ,

Rejected earthly things.

The ulcerous leper

Asks to be healed.

At Thomas’s prayers, from Christ

An angel is sent.

He removes the entire ulcerous covering in part [the precise sense is uncertain].

And clothes him with the covering

Of new bodily skin.

The Temple of the Sun, shattered,

Collapsed with its idol,

And the precious metal

Was dissolved into dust.

The king of that city

Fled with Carisius.

Then the priest of the idols,

Furious, stood forth

And pierced through with a sword

The holy martyr of Christ,

Crowned with the glorious

Blood of his passion.

O blessed among all,

City of Edessa,

Which received the gracious pledge

Of the Lord’s Disciple,

Where his body rests,

Buried with honor.

From there we all beseech you,

Son of the Most High Father:

Send us from heaven

Unconquered aid,

So that, believing, we may escape

Eternal punishment;

So that the entire company

Of the faithful, joined together

Under one [head],

May follow you, sing to you,

And enjoy you forever.

With humble confession

May we proclaim your glory.

Glory to the Father, etc.

**Supplication.** Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world, with the name changed, fol. CLXXXVII.

[Col. 1303C] **Capitulum.** Lord God, almighty Father, who reign forever and unto ages of ages, who dwell in light, incomprehensible God, who established heaven and earth, who made the two great lights; God, who created the human race so that not only heavenly but also earthly beings might magnify you, their Creator, with fitting praise; you who deigned to send our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, to us from the seat of your glory, so that he might free us from original sin and restore us to you, God, as a loving Lord; so that the man whom the envious robber had plunged into hell by his deception might, by Christ’s unconquered power, be lifted into heaven to the seat from which he had never departed; we ask you, Lord, that at this hour of the incense of this evening sacrifice, in honor of your holy Apostle and martyr Thomas, you may be merciful to your people and wipe away from them every stain of sin; so that he who conquered the cunning enemy in your name may not refuse to bear aid for us, your servants; so that we may be freed from the snare of the devil our ambusher, and, with all sins wiped away, may rejoice together with your Saints in your kingdom, O most merciful one:

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

**Blessing.** May almighty God, through the intercession of his most blessed Apostle Thomas, grant you forgiveness of sins and, in his mercy, pardon your faults.  
**R.** Amen.  
May he remove your sins from you and, by releasing you from your offenses, forgive them.  
**R.** Amen.  
May he wash away the stains of your crimes and, through the intercession of his most blessed Apostle, mercifully grant you indulgence.  
**R.** Amen.

Through his mercy, etc.

**Lauda.** “The Lord established him.” fol. CLVII.

**Prayer.** Almighty God, who crowned your martyr, the Apostle Thomas, in compassion and mercy, when you granted him both to believe in you and to suffer through you, so that, enduring temporal punishment, he might seize an everlasting crown: through his intercession grant us, your servants, that, if we do not attain the eminence of his passion, we may at least be free from ignorance of passion; so that, although titles of virtues are not assigned to us for glory, the disgrace of vices may be erased, lest we come into punishment.  
**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

### At Matins

**Antiphon.** “You will open my lips.”  
**Psalm I.**  
**Prayer.** “Let them rejoice, O Lord.” fol. CLXXX.

**Antiphon.** You placed upon his head, O Lord, a crown of precious stone.  
**P.** Placing glory and great beauty upon him.  
**V.** Blessed is the man who has not walked in the counsel of the ungodly, nor stood in the way of sinners, nor sat in the seat of pestilence.  
**P.** Placing glory and great.  
**V.** Glory and honor to the Father.  
**P.** Placing glory.

**Prayer.** Lord Jesus Christ, who placed upon the head of your martyr, the Apostle Thomas, a crown of precious stone, founded upon a foundation, so that he would not be confounded because he believed in you and would be crowned because he laid down his life for you: through his intercessions let there be in us, your servants, true faith by which we believe in you, and steadfast confession by which we confess you with the readiest devotion even before persecutors, so that, through the intervention of so great a Martyr, we may not be confounded before you and your Angels.  
**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**Antiphon.** Perfection and doctrine belong to your holy man, whom you tested, O Lord; he offered incense in your sight.  
**P.** And he burned incense upon your altar.  
**V.** The mouth of the just shall meditate wisdom, and his tongue shall speak judgment.  
**P.** And he burned incense.  
**V.** Glory and honor to the Father.  
**P.** And he burned incense.

**Prayer.** Almighty God, who [made] your martyr, as above in Vespers.

**Antiphon.** You protected him, O Lord, from the assembly of the wicked. Alleluia.  
**P.** And from the multitude of those who work iniquity. Alleluia.  
**V.** You have made gladness with your servant, O Lord, according to your word.  
**P.** And from the multitude.  
**V.** Glory and honor.  
**P.** And from the multitude.

**Prayer.** God, who raised up the life of your holy Apostle Thomas the martyr in such a manner that he might be crowned for his merits and we might be called forth by his examples: grant that, since today we venerate with due honor the day of his birth [into glory], we may be joined to that defender before the sight of your majesty.  
**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy.

**R.** I found one just person who pleased me, and I gave my sign between myself and him, so that when he began to sacrifice to me, I would smell the fragrance of sweetness.  
**P.** And I shall remember my holy covenant, so that henceforth I may not destroy all flesh.  
**V.** Because he hoped in me, I shall deliver him; I shall protect him, because he knew my name.  
**P.** And I shall remember.  
**V.** Glory and honor to the Father.  
**P.** And I shall remember.

**Another Responsory.** Alleluia. Grace shall cling to the lips of the just; his mouth shall be sought in the Church, and his words—  
**P.** Shall contemplate what is right. Alleluia, alleluia.  
**V.** Honey flows from the mouth of the just; the sweetness of honey is his tongue; his lips drip with a honeycomb.  
**P.** Shall contemplate.  
**V.** Glory and honor.  
**P.** Shall contemplate.

**Prayer.** Grant us, almighty God, the constant patronage of your most blessed witness, the Apostle Thomas, so that we may also deserve to attain his illustrious example and, experiencing his most devoted assistance, may follow him most courageously in battle.  
**R.** Amen.

Through the mercy of you, God, etc.

### At Lauds

[Col. 1305B] **For the Canticle. Antiphon.** “I rejoice in holiness.”  
**Canticle.** “My heart is steadfast.”  
**For the Benedictus. Antiphon.** “The blessing of the Lord hastens as the reward of the just.”  
**Canticle.** “Blessed are you, Lord God.” fol. 6.  
**Tone.** “God girded me with strength.” fol. CLVI.  
**Lauda.** “Praise the Lord.”  
**Psalm CXLVIII.**

**Reading from the book of Ecclesiasticus of Solomon (Chapter XXXI).**

**R.** Thanks be to God.

Blessed is the man who has been found without blemish, who did not pursue gold, nor hope in money and treasures. Who is he, and we shall praise him? For he performed wonders in his life. He was tested in that matter and was found perfect, and eternal glory shall be his: he could have transgressed but did not transgress, and could have done evil but did not. Therefore his good things have been established in God, and the Church of the saints shall recount his almsgiving.  
**R.** Amen.

**Hymn.**

The whole world openly triumphs;

Jesus, coming from the heavens, shines forth,

At whose coming the entire world

Is renewed forever.

O people, declare blessed ways

On account of Thomas:

Let this highest day be called gracious,

Because, singing Christ’s faith in India,

He counts them among his own.

Holy and mindful of the heavenly homeland,

He wins a people through the piety of Christ;

He rightly joined to himself a hymn,

And powerfully

That people.

He displays a dwelling of immense size

In the field, to be enjoyed

By their king according to his merit;

Rather, once opened there,

He brought that dwelling in.

From there this Martyr is cut by saws;

The holy one, summoned, lays down

His limbs smeared with blood,

So that the earth may come to his aid

On the following day.

His companion, taught by remarkable signs, is killed;

His brother prepares a palace,

And, rendering abundance to the Redeemer,

Immediately obeys our Creator.

Christ, when you come with the Saints on the day,

Draw the peoples to yourself, O Prince;

May we flee the dreadful fire

And sing of him from heaven.

Let the choir sing glory and resound;

Let it speak, sing, and repeat glory;

Let the stars cry out to the Triune Name,

To the Godhead alone.

Amen.

**Supplication.** Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world, as above.

**Capitulum.** Hear, O Lord, the voices of this family of yours, which we humbly pour forth in prayers; and, appeased, grant what we suppliantly ask: that we who celebrate this most renowned day in honor of your most blessed martyr, the Apostle Thomas, may all be found as worthy in this very service of our devotion as he was able to obtain through his intercession, so that, at your command, we may say:

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

**Lauda.** “With psaltery and harp.” fol. CLX.

**Blessing.** May the Lord guard you through the intercession of the most blessed martyr, the Apostle Thomas.  
**R.** Amen.  
May he mercifully regard the needs of those who hope in him.  
**R.** Amen.  
And, being propitious, may he forgive the sins of those who entreat him.  
**R.** Amen.

Through the mercy of our God, who is blessed and lives, etc.

**May the Lord be always with you.**  
**R.** And with your spirit.

## The thirtieth day: the feast of Saint James the Apostle, brother of Saint John the Apostle and Evangelist

### At Vespers

[Col. 1306C]

**Lauda.** “It has arisen.”  
**Tone.** “The souls of the just.” fol. CLXII.

**Antiphon.** I shall give my saints a kingdom in Jerusalem, for the tree of life is fragrant with ointment.  
**P.** And they shall not labor, nor shall they grow weary.  
**V.** Those who trust in the Lord are like Mount Zion; he who dwells in Jerusalem shall not be moved forever.  
**P.** And they shall not.  
**V.** Glory and honor.  
**P.** And they shall not.

**May the Lord be [with you].**  
**R.** And with [your spirit].

**Lauda.** “The blood of the saints.” fol. CLXII.

**Hymn.**

O Word of God, brought forth from the Father’s mouth,

Creator of things and true beginning,

Everlasting Author, light and source of light,

Born from the womb of the glorious Virgin,

Christ, truly our Emmanuel,

King and priest, for whom the sacred stones are:

Behold, four times three—onyx, agate,

Shining beryl, sapphire, carbuncle,

Or amethyst, sardius, topaz,

Emerald, jasper, ligure, chrysolite—

And rightly, with twelve gems,

The sun, shining through twelve hours of the day,

With the finest pearls,

Shone upon the world once the darkness had been driven away,

And with a candelabrum set above you,

Gleaming with twelve Apostolic lamps.

Peter went to Rome, his brother to Achaea,

Thomas to India, Levi to Macedonia,

James to Jebus, and Zelotes to Egypt,

Bartholomew possessed Lycaonia,

Matthias Pontus, and Philip Gaul.

Then the great sons of thunder,

Having received the insignia of the summit of life

Through the prayer of the illustrious Mother,

Both shine forth:

John alone ruled the right-hand region of Asia,

And his brother obtained Spain.

Famous with the Master, admitted unharmed

To his right hand, one was drawn

Into the covenants of peace;

The other to the left, into judgment.

Both hasten to Mitridepolis,

Their twice-chosen pledges, to the kingdoms of glory.

Brought forward, I say, glorious in reward,

Chosen there, he departs through martyrdom:

He is called James of Zebedee, Christ’s Apostle,

Fulfilling what is owed by right of the apostolate,

And as victor he seizes the marks of passion.

Indeed, covered with divine assistance,

He restrains the guilty rage of the Magi

And the venom of demons,

Punishing their rivalry.

And at last, alive in his robes,

In prophetic utterances,

Let a penitent believing heart

Be given as a sign.

Once perplexed, having obtained his wish,

He grants help to the sick man who seeks an opening;

To the one who asks, he opens the gifts of faith,

The standards of peace for the abundance of salvation,

And, having wielded the sword,

He fortifies himself with glory.

O truly worthy and most holy Apostle,

The golden, shining head of Spain!

Be our guardian and native patron;

By avoiding pestilence, be salvation from heaven.

Drive away every disease, ulcer, and crime.

Be present favorably to the flock, merciful creditor,

And gentle shepherd to flock, clergy, and people;

That by heavenly help we may enjoy joy,

And, having obtained the kingdom, may be clothed in glory

Eternal; through you may we escape Tartarus.

Grant this, we ask, O Unique Power,

Who alone fills the entire universe with glory,

Mighty, everlasting Virtue, be present as eternal glory;

Your praise and mercy endure,

And your honor continually throughout the ages.

Amen.

**Supplication.** Let us pray to the Redeemer, with the name changed, fol. CLXXXVII.

**Capitulum.** Bend our necks beneath your yoke, O most merciful God, so that we may bear your burden—which is light for those who love it—with such desirable devotion as your Apostle James, dragged to his passion with a rope fastened around his neck, endured joyfully. Through this miracle he so pierced the heart of the one mocking him that, instructed in the sacraments of faith, he made him attain the glory of martyrdom. Thus afterward, having confessed your Son, he was killed by decapitation and fell asleep, reaching him in peace, for whose sake he endured this passion. For he is your only-begotten Son, who gave his life as a redemption for many; through him, O God the Father, command that our sins be spared.

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

**Blessing.** May Christ God, Son of God the Father, whom James, having left his father in the boat, followed with the whole intention of his heart, make you cling continually to his footsteps.  
**R.** Amen.  
And may he who through this Apostle converted worshipers of demons to the faith grant us, by rejecting the vanities of the world, to love him in truth.  
**R.** Amen.  
So may you be rewarded by the protection of him whose triumph of passion you celebrate today.  
**R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**Lauda.** “Everlasting joy.” fol. CLXII.

**Prayer.** Christ, whose virtue and power shone forth so greatly in your Apostle James that, in your name, he deserved to command powerfully the hosts of demons he had expelled: defend your Church from the assault of its adversaries, so that, overcoming adversity by the power of the Spirit, it may complete in works the teaching of him whose example of holy passion it honors today.  
**R.** Amen.

Through.

### At Matins

**Antiphon.** “Give us joy.”  
**Psalm L.**  
**Prayer.** “Restore joy to us.” fol. CLXIII.

**First Antiphon.** The Lord gave them the power of a kingdom against those who persecuted them.  
**P.** And it was for them a covering by day, and the light of the stars throughout the night.  
**V.** He sent his word and healed them, and rescued them from their destruction.  
**P.** And it was.  
**V.** Glory and honor.  
**P.** And it was.

**Prayer.** Christ, whose virtue—seek it above in the preceding Vespers.

**Second Antiphon.** Come to me, all my saints, says the Lord; reap the fruit of your labors, the shoot of righteousness.  
**P.** Its fragrance is great, like the scent of lilies and roses in their season.  
**V.** Come, children, hear me; I shall teach you the fear of the Lord.  
**P.** Its fragrance.  
**V.** Glory and honor.  
**P.** Its fragrance.

**Prayer.** Holy and merciful God, who are glorified in the assembly of the Saints and are great and greatly to be feared, existing in power over all nations: James followed you after leaving his father Zebedee in such a way that, loving you fervently, he became chosen in life, pure in conscience, and approved in teaching; finally, he so commended knowledge through his deeds that he died with his head cut off for you, knowing that you had laid down your life for him or for all. O Lord, be favorably appeased by our prayers through his intercession, so that we may deserve to obtain from you forgiveness of our sins.  
**R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**Third Antiphon.** The bones of the saints shall sprout from their place.  
**P.** And their names shall flower like pure lilies.  
**V.** O Lord, save us. O Lord, prosper us.  
**P.** And their names.  
**V.** Glory and honor to the Father.  
**P.** And their names.

**Prayer.** Precious in your sight, O Lord, is the death of your Saints. You called your Apostle James to yourself, having chosen him as he was setting out nets in a boat, so that he might teach the peoples with spiritual doctrines and rejoice in heaven through the pouring out of his blood. We ask your omnipotence that, while we endure present evils with the greatest patience, we may live with you now and forever in peace and charity without end.  
**R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**R.** The Saints who contended for the faith: the enemy shall have no power over them, because they cried out with one voice, saying:  
**P.** Holy God, Holy Strong One, hear us; Holy Immortal One, have mercy on us.  
**V.** I saw in heaven a great crowd that no one could count, and they cried out with a loud voice, saying:  
**P.** Holy God.  
**V.** Glory and honor.  
**P.** Holy God.

### At Lauds

**For the Canticle. Antiphon.** You who voluntarily offered yourselves to danger, bless the Lord, declaring his righteousness and mercy toward the strong ones of Israel.

**Canticle.** “You who voluntarily offered yourselves.”

**For the Benedictus. Antiphon.** “Holy and humble.”  
**Canticle.** “Blessed are you, Lord.” fol. 6.

**Tone.** “The way of the just.”  
**Lauda.** “Praise the Lord.”  
**Psalm CXLVIII.**  
**Prophecy.** “The souls of the just.” fol. CLXVII.

**Hymn.**

Let the whole devout, nourished people rejoice;

Let it resound at once with voice and blood;

Let it always ask Christ

For the interest of peace,

In the honor of praise.

Truth, life, and ever-calm hope

In your gracious servant and holy James—

We are now tortured,

Burned by fires,

And with great chains.

The great Lord and our Lord says:

“Release the dreadful fiery chain,

Which harms no one;

Now bring me

The wicked Magus.”

At whose command they immediately came;

They place him, already bound,

Before his feet,

So that they might contend, be avenged, and be tortured.

“Recognize henceforth Christ, whom you denied,

as the true Creator of the human race;

though wicked, acknowledge that you have him as Father.”

“I acknowledge the true Savior,” he says,

“And I beseech you, holy intercessor:

I believe that, with the Lord’s favor,

You can grant forgiveness.”

Afterward he removed the wound

Of the one who had struck him;

But he is dragged by the neck with a rope

And bound.

Thus by Herod he is punished by decapitation;

Thus he is ordained.

They lead the bound man through the village.

A lame man asks him for food;

By his power he is made to walk upright,

And he goes on, sound,

For a time.

Then the torturer sees the lame man

Given the power to walk,

And addresses him thus:

“Christ is praised,

By whose power salvation is given

To the sick

Through his Saints.”

Let the choir sing glory and resound;

Let it speak, sing, and repeat glory;

Let the stars cry out to the Triune Name,

To the Godhead alone.

Amen.

**Supplication.** Let us pray to the Redeemer.  
**Capitulum.** “Bend our necks, O most merciful God.”  
**Lauda.** “Everlasting joy.”  
**Blessing.** “Christ God, Son of God the Father,” as above in the preceding Vespers.

## The thirty-first day: the feast of Saint Columba, Virgin

### At Vespers

[Col. 1310B]

**Lauda.** “My soul has hoped.” fol. CLXXIX.  
**Tone.** “The Lord, God of heaven.”  
**Antiphon.** “Most prudent Virgin.” fol. CLXXIX.  
**Lauda.** “Like a palm.” fol. CLXXX.

**Hymn.**

The nard of Columba has blossomed;

The privets of the garden are fragrant.

Support the joyful Virgin with flowers;

Surround her with apples.

Fit for the embraces

And kisses of the King, she consecrates

To Christ the faith she had promised

As the pledge of her blood.

She laid low, subdued, and drove away

The twin fires of the world—

The wanton flame of the Barbarian

And the fires brought against her.

When she was placed in a brothel

And restrained the lurid lust

Of those entering to her,

She burned herself in the flames.

Thus freed from the fires,

And brought back from the theatrical places,

She is punished with a drawn sword,

And taken up to heaven to be married.

To her a voice resounding from the stars

Calls out:

“Come, Columba,”

It rings forth.

You, favoring our voices,

Make us possessors of the heavens.

Grant this, most merciful Father,

And Only-Begotten, equal to the Father,

Reigning with the Spirit, the Paraclete,

Throughout every age.

Amen.

**Supplication.** Let us pray with every supplication to the Redeemer of the world, our Lord Jesus Christ, that through the grace of his Nativity and through the intercession of his holy virgin and martyr Columba he may deign to grant us remission and peace.  
**R.** Grant it, eternal almighty God.

**Capitulum.** God, who made the most blessed Columba wondrous in the simplicity of doves, so that in the innocence of Christian faith she might follow you both as Virgin and as Martyr, while she preserved her inviolate body for you and, already victorious as a Martyr, clung to you; while, by a voice given and formed by you from heaven, she was called, and through you was wondrously crowned in heaven: grant the joys desired by our minds, so that, made victorious over our sins through her merits, we may deserve to be placed in the heavenly dwelling places.

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. fol. 2.

**Blessing.** God, who willed the most blessed virgin Columba to be victorious over the flame, extinguish in you every burning of carnal arousal.  
**R.** Amen.  
And through him by whose heavenly voice she deserved to be called to her reward, may you through her deserve to obtain the resolve of holiness.  
**R.** Amen.  
So that, following her example, just as she submitted her neck to the material sword for him, you may likewise always subject your souls to divine rule.  
**R.** Amen.

[Col. 1311B] Through his mercy, etc.

**Lauda.** “You have been made beautiful.” fol. CLXXIX.

**Prayer.** Almighty, eternal God, who on this day made blessed Columba, your virgin and martyr, ascend to glory through the palm of martyrdom: grant us, aided by her merits, forgiveness of all sins, so that we may deserve to reach her fellowship.  
**R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

### At Matins

**Antiphon.** “You will open my lips.”  
**Psalm L.**

**Prayer.** “Let them rejoice, O Lord.” fol. CLXXX.

**Antiphon.** Columba, beautiful and perfect, girded with gold and gems.  
**P.** Her head is full of dew, and her hair with drops.  
**V.** Hear, O daughter, and see, and incline your ear; forget your people and your father’s house.  
**P.** Her head is full.  
**V.** Glory and honor to the Father, etc.  
**P.** Her head is full.

**Prayer.** One and perfect virgin of Christ, Columba, who are shown to be illustrious through the unity of faith and conspicuous through the perfection of works: therefore, through your prayers, make us live within the bosom of Mother Church so blamelessly that we may deserve to reach the heavenly promises, to be crowned.  
**R.** Amen.

Through your mercy, etc.

**Antiphon.** You are my one nearest one; you are my one Columba.  
**P.** And there is no blemish in you.  
**V.** By day the sun shall not burn you, nor the moon by night.  
**P.** And there is no blemish.  
**V.** Glory and honor.  
**P.** And there is no blemish.

[Col. 1311D] **Prayer.** Your Church, O Christ, is one and undivided, your nearest one; behold, one Columba, who has neither wrinkle in faith nor blemish in works. We ask that she intercede with you for our sins, so that, abiding in her body in perpetual happiness, we may deserve to share in the eternal citizens.  
**R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**Antiphon.** Come, Columba, bride from Lebanon; come from the mountains of pasture.  
**P.** Let us run after the fragrance of your ointments.  
**V.** May he not give your foot over to agitation, nor may he who guards you sleep.  
**P.** Let us run.  
**V.** Glory and honor.  
**P.** Let us run.

**Prayer.** Good is your nearest one, Lord, the virgin Columba, who, while she became your nearest one, is shown through her own passion to be your beautiful sister by blood. Through her intercession, therefore, wipe away the stains of our passions, so that, made beautiful by you in vows and works, we may deserve, blessed, to enter the gates of eternal Jerusalem.  
**R.** Amen.

Through mercy.

**R.** Rejoice, daughter of Zion, says the Lord: may my Spirit, which is in you, and my words, which I have placed in your heart, not depart from your mouth or from the mouth of your offspring.  
**P.** Forever and ever.  
**V.** Praise the Lord, Jerusalem; praise your God, Zion.  
**P.** Forever.  
**V.** Glory and honor, etc.  
**P.** Forever.

**Prayer.** Almighty, eternal God, who—seek it in the preceding Vespers.

### At Lauds

**For the Canticle. Antiphon.** “Daughter of Zion.”  
**Canticle.** “Rejoicing, I shall rejoice.”  
**For the Benedictus. Antiphon.** “Blessed is the Lord.”  
**Canticle.** “Blessed are you, Lord God.”  
**Tone.** “The Lord, God of heaven.”  
**Lauda.** “Praise the Lord.”  
**Psalm CXLVIII.**  
**Prophecy.** “The Lord appeared to me from afar.” Seek it at fol. CLXXXI.  
**Hymn.** “The nard of Columba.”  
**Supplication.** Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world, our Lord; above in Vespers.

**Capitulum.** Lord Jesus Christ, who by the words of the most blessed virgin and martyr Columba overturned the understanding of a wanton young man, so that he who had entered for the prostitution of the Virgin intending to blaspheme your name was shown, upon departing, to be your preacher: grant us, through the merits of your Virgin, to change our life from evil deeds for the better, so that, freed from the incitements of lusts, we may deserve to receive the rewards of eternal joys.

**Our Father.** Delivered from evil. fol. 2.  
**Lauda.** “You have been made beautiful and pleasant,” above in Vespers.

**Blessing.** God, who rejoices in the unity and perfection of the virgin Columba, reward you with the innocence of doves.  
**R.** Amen.  
And may he who, thundering from heaven with voices, announces that the heavens have been opened through her merits place you among those to be numbered in the heavenly dwelling places.  
**R.** Amen.  
So may our mind, which rejoices in her after the glory of her passion, always be directed there to receive its reward.  
**R.** Amen.

Through the mercy of our God.

### At Terce for the Dead

This is to begin at the end of Lauds for the Dead, fol. CLVI, where it says: “The Office begins.”

**Antiphon.** Redeem me, O Lord, and have mercy on me, so that in the Churches I may bless you, O Lord.

**Psalm XXV**

Judge me, O Lord, for I have entered in my innocence;  
* and, hoping in the Lord, I shall not be weakened.

Test me, O Lord, and try me;  
* burn my kidneys and my heart.

For your mercy is before my eyes,  
* and I have pleased in your truth.

I have not sat in the council of vanity,  
* and with those who act wickedly I shall not enter.

I have hated the assemblies of the wicked,  
* and with the impious I shall not sit.

I shall wash my hands among the innocent,  
* and I shall surround your altar, O Lord,

[Col. 1313A] So that I may hear the voice of your praise  
* and recount all your wonders.

Lord, I have loved the beauty of your house  
* and the place where the glory of your dwelling is.

Do not destroy my soul with the impious,  
* nor my life with men of blood,

In whose hands are iniquities,  
* and their right hand is filled with gifts.

But I have entered in my innocence;  
* redeem me and have mercy on me.

For my foot has stood on the straight path;  
* in the Churches I shall bless you, O Lord.

Glory and honor.

**Prayer.** Redeem us, O Lord, and have mercy on us, so that our voice may sing psalms to you in the Churches and our life may bless you among the peoples. Burn our kidneys and our heart in the testing of your charity, and henceforth cut away from us all pleasures, so that neither lust may loosen the structure of our kidneys and the flow of evil thought may depart from the seat of our heart.  
**R.** Amen.

Through.

**First Antiphon.** Hear, O Lord, my voice with which I cried to you; have mercy on me and hear me.

**Psalm XXVI**

The Lord is my light and my salvation;  
* whom shall I fear?

The Lord is the defender of my life;  
* from whom shall I tremble?

When evildoers draw near against me  
* to eat my flesh,

My enemies who trouble me—  
* they themselves have been weakened and have fallen.

If armies encamp against me, my heart shall not fear.  
* If battle rises against me, in this I shall hope.

I asked one thing of the Lord; this I shall seek: * that I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life;

That I may behold the Lord’s will, * and be protected in his holy temple.

For he hid me in his tabernacle on the day of troubles; * he protected me in the hiding-place of his tabernacle.

On a rock he exalted me; * and now, behold, he has lifted up my head above my enemies.

[Col. 1313D] I shall go about and sacrifice in his tabernacle a sacrifice of jubilation; * I shall sing and recite a psalm to the Lord.

Hear, O Lord, my voice with which I cried to you; * have mercy on me and hear me.

My heart said to you, “I have sought your face”; * your face, O Lord, I shall seek.

[Col. 1314A] Do not turn your face from me; * and do not turn away in anger from your servant.

You are my helper, O Lord; * do not abandon me, nor despise me, O God my Savior.

For my father and my mother abandoned me; * but the Lord took me up.

Set me a law, O Lord, in your way; * and guide me on a straight path because of my enemies.

Do not hand me over to the souls of those who pursue me; * for unjust witnesses have risen against me, and iniquity has lied against itself.

I believe that I shall see the good things of the Lord * in the land of the living.

Wait for the Lord; act bravely; * and let your heart be strengthened, and wait for the Lord.

[Col. 1314B] Glory and honor.

Prayer. Hear, O Lord, our voice with which we cry to you; and let our heart seek your face, so that we who now behold you through a riddle may deserve, present in your house face to face, to attain blessedness. R\. Amen.

Through.

Antiphon 2. The Lord is my helper; and in him my heart has hoped, and I have been helped. Psalm 27 of David.

R\. Righteous Defender, defend us and deliver us. P. From the hand of our enemies. V\. O God, save us in your name, and in your strength deliver us. P. From the hand. V\. Glory. Let the Responsory be repeated.

[Col. 1314C] Lauda. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. O God, hear our prayer. P. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V\. And may our cry come to you. P. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.

Prayers. Have mercy, O Lord. P. You who are powerful in mercy. V\. Hear the prayers of those who entreat. P. You who are powerful. V\. Look upon us with a kindly face. P. You who are powerful. V\. Wash away our crimes. P. You who are powerful. V\. Grant forgiveness for sins. P. You who are powerful. V\. Grant rest to the departed. P. You who are powerful. Let “Have mercy” be repeated.

Capitulum. Our Helper and Redeemer and Lord, help us; and may our flesh blossom again either with the verdure of chastity or with the newness of holiness. And because you are the strength [Col. 1314D] of your people, save your people and exalt your inheritance with an abundance of blessing.

Our Father. Deliver us from evil. Fol. 10.

In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, may all the souls of the faithful departed, through the mercy of God, rest forever in peace. R\. Thanks be to God.

[Col. 1315]

APPENDIX. FEASTS ADDED TO THE GOTHIC-HISPANIC BREVIARY IN THE EDITION OF CARDINAL XIMENES, IN THE YEAR 1502; NOW PLACED HERE, SO THAT THE MEMORY OF SUCH A MATTER MAY NOT PERISH. (C)

[Col. 1315A] 1 On folio CCLI, column 3, of the aforesaid edition, the following feast is found on the first Sunday after holy Pentecost.

Whoever wishes to know and announce to the people how many days of indulgence are granted by the Supreme Pontiffs to all the faithful in Christ who truly repent and hear the divine Offices on this most holy feast should know it in the following manner:

Pope Urban, the institutor of this solemnity, granted one hundred for First Vespers; one hundred for Matins; one hundred for the Mass; one hundred for Second Vespers; and forty for each of the other lesser Hours; for each day of the Octave, one hundred for all the Hours together.

Pope Martin granted all these indulgences in their proper order doubled.

[Col. 1315B] Pope Eugene, however, granted as many as Martin. Thus there are two hundred for First Vespers; two hundred for Matins; two hundred for the Mass; two hundred for Second Vespers; two hundred for each of the other Hours; and for each day of the Octave, two hundred for all the Hours together; two hundred for one who fasts on the vigil, or gives some alms in place of fasting. If the feast of Corpus Christi and the Nativity of Saint John the Baptist occur on the same day, the Office is to be celebrated in full for Corpus Christi.

On Friday, however, the Office is to be celebrated in full for Saint John, with a commemoration of Corpus Christi. Throughout the Octave, the Office is to be celebrated in full for Corpus Christi, with a commemoration of Saint John.

## ON THE FEAST OF CORPUS CHRISTI

### At Vespers

[Col. 1315C] Lauda. With you, O Lord. P. The fountain of life; and in your light we shall see light. V\. The sons of men will hope in the protection of your wings; and they will be intoxicated by the abundance of your house, and you will give them drink from the torrent of your delight. P. The fountain of life.

Prayer. O Lord, with whom is the fountain of life. See fol. 423.

Sono. Jesus took bread, blessed it, gave it to his disciples, and said: “Take and eat; this is my body.” Alleluia.

May the Lord be always with you. R\. And with you.

Antiphon. The Lord prepared his table. He sent his servants, summoning them with much proclamation to the bowl, saying: “If anyone is foolish, let him turn aside to me.” And he said to those lacking understanding: P. “Come and eat of my breads.” [Col. 1316A] V\. Man ate the bread of angels, containing in itself every delight. P. Come and eat. V\. Glory and honor to the Father. P. Come.

May the Lord be always with you. R\. And with you.

Lauda. Drink the wine that I have mixed for you. Alleluia. P. Abandon foolishness and live. Alleluia, alleluia. V\. You bring forth bread from the earth, and wine gladdens the heart of man. P. Abandon. V\. Glory and honor. P. Abandon.

Hymn.

Sing, O tongue, the mystery  
of the glorious Body  
and precious Blood,  
[Col. 1316B] which the King of the nations,  
the fruit of a noble womb,  
poured out as the world’s ransom.

Given for us, born for us  
from an untouched Virgin,  
and living in the world,  
having scattered the seed of the Word,  
he wondrously closed  
the course of his dwelling here.

On the night of the final supper,  
reclining with his brothers,  
having fully observed the law  
in the lawful foods,  
he gave himself with his own hands  
as food to the twelvefold company.

[Col. 1316C] The Word made flesh makes  
true bread flesh by the Word;  
and the blood of Christ becomes wine,  
and even if the senses fail:  
2 for confirming a sincere heart,  
faith alone is sufficient.

Therefore let us venerate, bowing low,  
so great a Sacrament;  
and let the ancient document  
yield to the new rite;  
let faith provide supplementation  
for the deficiency of the senses.

To the Begetter and the Begotten  
be praise and jubilation,  
[Col. 1317A] salvation, honor, and power also,  
and blessing;  
to the One proceeding from both  
let equal praise be given.

Amen.

[Col. 1317A] Supplication. Let us pray; let us ask our pious and hearable Lord Jesus Christ with every supplication that, through the grace of his Body and Blood, he may deign to grant us forgiveness of sins and peace. R\. Grant this, eternal almighty God.

Lord, have mercy. R\. Lord, have mercy. Christ, have mercy.

Capitula. Almighty, immeasurable, and merciful Lord, whom sinners do not provoke so often by sinning, set mercy against your wrath; and as often as [Col. 1317B] we provoke you to strike, so often may your compassion intervene so that you may forgive. Therefore satisfy us with the bread of angels, so that, strengthened by receiving it, we may overcome the malicious cunning of the Evil One and, once heaven’s gates have been opened, may enter, with your help, into the same food.

Our Father. Delivered from evil. Fol. 2.

Blessing. May the grace of almighty God protect you and refresh your hunger with spiritual food. R\. Amen. May he also water your thirst with rivers of righteousness and pour into your souls the new flavor of his sweetness. R\. Amen. May you, crushed in body and sanctified in spirit, deserve to be blessed by him with a heavenly gift. R\. Amen.

Through his mercy.

Lauda. Likewise. Alleluia and the chalice, and Alleluia. [Col. 1317C] P. After he had supped, saying, Alleluia. V\. I shall take the cup of salvation and call upon the name of the Lord. P. After he had supped. V\. Glory and honor. P. After he had supped.
