Prayer. O God, who under a wondrous Sacrament left us the memorial of your passion: grant, we ask, that we may so venerate the sacred mysteries of your Body and Blood that we may continually feel within us the fruit of your redemption. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.

### At Matins

Antiphon. I slept and rose again, because the Lord received me. Psalm 3.

[Col. 1317D] Prayer. Lord Jesus Christ, who for us accepted the sleep of death so that we might no longer sleep in death, grant that we who are reborn through your dying may also, through your giving life, rise from the bed of sins; and may we no longer be overwhelmed by the punishment of sin, since we rejoice that we have been redeemed by the price of your sacred Blood. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy, etc.

Antiphon 1. Wisdom built herself a house and set up seven columns. She slaughtered her sacrifices. P. She mixed her wine in the bowl and prepared her table. V\. They ate and were exceedingly satisfied, and he brought them what they desired; they were not deprived of their desire. P. She mixed. V\. Glory and honor to the Father. P. She mixed the wine.

[Col. 1318A] Prayer. O God, who give the bread of heaven to the children of men and satisfy the earthly creature with the fatness of angels, grant us an abundant harvest of your word; and refresh us with that spiritual food with which you fed our fathers in the wilderness. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God, etc.

Antiphon 2. Drink the wine that I have mixed for you. P. Abandon foolishness and you will live; and seek prudence, so that you may reign forever. V\. Man ate the bread of angels, containing in itself every delight. P. Abandon. V\. Glory and honor. P. Abandon.

Prayer. The portion of our inheritance, O Lord, consists in your eternity. Therefore we beseech you, O Lord, by your customary compassion, preserve your inheritance; and grant it forever, as a remedy, the cup of the Lord’s supper which you drank for it, so that, just as the gifts of redemption are splendid, so the Redeemer’s acquisition may be abundant; and may we who have been redeemed by your cross be forever your inheritance; so that you do not leave our soul in hell, but with you forever raise up victory incorruptible. R\. Amen.

Through your mercy.

3 Antiphon 3. We, many, are one bread and one body. P. All who share in one bread and one Cup. V\. You prepared in your sweetness, O God, for the poor; O God, who make them dwell of one mind in a house. P. All who. V\. Glory and honor. P. All who.

Prayer. May your creature repay you, O Lord, for however many benefits of your redemption you have bestowed upon it: for, having received the Cup of salvation, it recognizes that it escapes the peril of death only if it offers faithful vows to your redemption and, with darkness put to death, presents the service of its obedience in the courts of the house of God. Grant health, our God, so that, with the bonds of sins broken, we may perform the work by which you are pleased, and in the midst of Jerusalem offer you a sacrifice pleasing to you in your praise. May the truth of catholic belief admit to behold you securely those whom the excesses of the mind now present as liars. R\. Amen.

Through.

R\. This is the bread descending from heaven: if anyone eats of it, he will not die, but will have eternal life; and I shall raise him up on the last day. P. If anyone thirsts, let him come to me and drink. Whoever believes in me, rivers of living water will flow from his belly. V\. My flesh is truly food, and my Blood is truly drink. P. If anyone.

Prayer. Lord of hosts, receive the prayers of your servants, not in anger but in favor; and deign to show us what we ought to pray for. Strengthen with the food of eternity those whom the bread of tears troubles; and let the streams of tears flow from our eyes with such measured weeping that, our crimes having been destroyed, they may bend toward the abundance of your mercies. And may we who tremble and fear the coming of our Redeemer contemplate, by your gift, his glorious presence in profound peace. R\. Amen.

[Col. 1319A] Through mercy.

### At Lauds

For the Canticle. Antiphon. The sacrifice of the righteous is accepted, and the Lord will not forget his memory.

Canticle from Ecclesiasticus of Solomon (Chapter 35).

The salutary sacrifice is to attend to the commandments and depart from all iniquity; * to offer a sacrifice of propitiation.

Whoever shows mercy * offers a sacrifice.

It is pleasing to the Lord to withdraw from all iniquity; * and prayer is to withdraw from injustice.

You shall not appear empty before the presence of your God; * for all these things flow from the Lord’s commandments.

The offering of the righteous fattens the altar, * and it is an odor of sweetness [Col. 1319B] in the presence of the Most High.

The sacrifice of the righteous is accepted, * and the Lord will not forget his memory.

For the Benedictus. Antiphon. Holy priests offer incense and breads to God.

Canticle. Blessed are you, Lord God. Folio 6.

Sono. I am the living bread that came down from heaven; if anyone eats of this bread, he will live forever. Alleluia.

Lauda. Praise the Lord from the heavens. Alleluia; praise him, all his angels. Alleluia. Psalm 148.

Reading from the Book of the Wisdom of Solomon (Chapter 8).

R\. Thanks be to God.

Blessed is the man who hears and watches daily at my doors [Col. 1319C] and keeps watch at the posts of my doorway. Whoever finds me will find life and will draw salvation from the Lord. But whoever sins against me harms his own soul; and all who hate me love death (Chapter 9). Wisdom built herself a house; she cut out seven columns. She sacrificed her victims, mixed wine, and set her table. She sent her servants to call from the citadel and the walls of the city, saying: “If anyone is little, let him come to me.” And she spoke to the foolish: “Come, eat my bread and drink the wine that I have mixed for you. Leave childishness, and see, and walk in the ways of prudence.” R\. Amen.

Hymn.

Let joys be joined to the sacred solemnities,  
[Col. 1319D] And let praises resound from our inmost hearts.  
Let old things depart; let everything be new:  
hearts, voices, and works.

The final supper of the night is recalled,  
at which Christ is believed to have given  
the lamb and unleavened bread to his brothers,  
according to the ordinances granted to the ancient fathers.

After the figurative lamb, when the meal was completed,  
the Lord’s Body was given to the disciples.  
4 Thus we confess that the whole was given to all,  
and the whole to each, by his hands.

He gave a dish from the fruits of the body;  
he gave a cup of blood from the vines,  
saying, “Take the vessel that I hand over;  
all of you drink from it.”

[Col. 1320A] Thus he instituted this sacrifice,  
whose ministry he wished to be entrusted  
to priests alone, to whom it is fitting  
that they receive and give to the others.

The bread of angels becomes the bread of men;  
heavenly bread brings figures to an end.  
O wondrous thing! The poor, the servant,  
and the humble eat the Lord.

We ask you, Triune and One God,  
to visit us as we worship you.  
Lead us by your paths where we are going,  
to the light in which you dwell.

R\. Amen.

Supplication. Let us pray. Above, folio 2.

Capitulum. Placing our hope in you, O Lord, [Col. 1320B] we do not forget your works, since through justice and clemency you show yourself wondrous among the saints and terrible to the wicked; you who repay timely remedies to the righteous and due punishments to the unjust. Therefore we beseech you, most merciful one: glorify those whom you rescue from earthly enemies with the light of your commandments; removing the waves of temptations, open the saving way; refresh us in the desert of this age with the Body of your Christ as heavenly bread.

Our Father. Delivered from evil. Fol. 2.

Lauda. Likewise, Alleluia and the chalice. Above, folio 2.

Prayer. O God, who willed to redeem the human race with the precious blood of your only-begotten Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, mercifully grant that we who have come to adore the life-giving Body of Christ may be freed from the bonds of our sins. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

### At Terce

R\. My flesh is truly food, and my Blood is truly drink. P. Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my Blood remains in me, and I in him. Alleluia. V\. My food is to do the will of him who sent me, so that I may complete his work. P. Whoever eats. V\. Glory and honor to the Father. P. Whoever eats.

Prophecy. Blessed is the man who hears me. See above, in the preceding Matins.

Lauda. Alleluia. He gave them bread from heaven. Alleluia. [Col. 1320D] V\. Man ate the bread of angels. P. Alleluia.

Hymn.

The heavenly Word going forth,  
yet not leaving the Father’s right hand,  
going forth to his work,  
came to the evening of life.

In death, to be handed over  
by a disciple to his enemies,  
first in the meal of life  
he handed himself over to his disciples.

To the one and triune Lord  
be everlasting glory:  
may he grant us life without end  
[Col. 1321A] in our homeland.

Amen.

V\. He fed them with the fatness of wheat. R\. And he satisfied them with honey from the rock.

Supplication. Let us pray. Above, folio 2.

Capitulum. Most high Lord, be our helper; and, hastening to the liberation of your own, come quickly to meet us, so that we may be filled with the help of the strength of your abundance and enriched with gifts from the bounty of overflowing grace. May our mouth profess love without our tongue growing sluggish through falsehood; rather, may the profession of our mouth display purity of mind, and may your praise always resound on our lips through the instrument of our breast.

Our Father. Delivered from evil. Fol. 2.

Blessing. May the almighty Lord bless you, who is the Creator of all and the everlasting Maker. [Col. 1321B] R\. Amen. May he preserve your bodies undefiled and mercifully protect your souls. R\. Amen. And may he render you innocent of every crime of sin, so that the Holy Spirit may remain in you. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

For the other Hours, namely Sext and None, let everything be said as on feast days, which are said throughout the year.

During the Octave of Corpus Christi, let everything be said as on the day itself.

## FOR SAINT GABRIEL THE ARCHANGEL

### At Vespers

Lauda. All your angels praised you, O Lord, and sang a hymn when you completed the structure of heaven. [Col. 1323D] The day is yours, and the night is yours. P. You made the sun and the moon. V\. You established the sea by your power; you shattered the heads of dragons upon the waters. P. You made.

May the Lord be with you. R\. And with you.

Sono. Alleluia. Judgment has been given to the saints. P. At the hour of the evening sacrifice. Alleluia, alleluia. V\. Behold, Gabriel, one of the foremost princes, will come, so that many may be sanctified. P. At the hour of the sacrifice.

May the Lord be with you. R\. And with you.

Antiphon. Your throne, O immeasurable God, and your glory, incomprehensible, before which the entire army of angels stands in trembling. P. His appearance dries up the abysses, and his indignation makes the mountains waste away. V\. Lord God of hosts, who is like you? You are powerful, O Lord, [Col. 1324A] and your truth is all around you. P. His appearance. V\. Glory and honor. P. His appearance.

May the Lord be with you. R\. And with you.

Lauda. Alleluia. Your good Spirit, O God. P. Let him lead us on the straight way. Alleluia, alleluia. P. Worship the Lord, all his angels. He heard, and Zion rejoiced, and the daughters of Judah exulted because of your judgments, O Lord. P. Let him lead us. V\. Glory and honor to the Father. P. Let him lead us.

Hymn.

All you people of the Catholic faith,  
nurtured for glory,  
present your vows together  
and disclose your crimes,  
so that the merciful author of all  
[Col. 1324B] may grant everything requested.

For that Gabriel,  
exalted in name,  
conspicuous in the court of heaven,  
messenger of the Most High God,  
made prince of the angels  
and lofty in title,

whose name derives from power  
and whose work from office,  
snatched from the Almighty,  
holds what has been preserved,  
so that we may glory in God  
with our companion and associate.

[Col. 1324C] He is the Lord’s supreme  
and great messenger,  
who, by overthrowing that foul,  
dreadful, and rebellious angel  
for glory,  
cast him into the abyss.

He remains as protector,  
defender of all,  
to offer the petitions of all  
to God the King  
and grant the people  
the grace appointed by him.

Great indeed is  
the festivity of this day,  
whose name is that of the Archangel,  
Gabriel the messenger,  
[Col. 1324D] whom it is fitting to celebrate  
and receive with worthy devotion,

so that through his intercession  
we may deserve to obtain from God  
forgiveness of all sins  
and enjoy the kingdom  
of blessed life  
after our passing.

Let there be glory and honor  
to the Father and also to the Son,  
and likewise to the coequal  
Spirit, the Paraclete,  
who, one in the Trinity,  
reigns before the ages.

Amen.

[Col. 1325A] 7 Supplication. Let us pray; let us ask with every supplication our Redeemer, the Lord Jesus Christ, that through the intercession of Saint Gabriel the Archangel he may deign to grant us forgiveness of sins and peace. R\. Grant this, eternal almighty God.

Lord, have mercy. R\. Christ, have mercy; Lord, have mercy.

Capitulum. Lord God, almighty Father, Creator of all and Maker of the elements, who deigned to place your Gabriel before the ranks of messengers, whose service obeys your command and who are never wearied by such duties: his name sounds forth from mystery, and his power prevails by merit. Although they are always spirits, when they are sent by you and embodied from the air they are called angels, so that they may appear visibly to the sight of all; [Col. 1325B] their substance nevertheless remains incorporeal, and although they are circumscribed locally, they still enjoy without weariness the presence of the Creator. Grant us, we ask, through the intercession of this Archangel Gabriel and of all the angels, to obtain forgiveness of sins, so that we who utter praise and vows to you, our God, in their honor may attain the forgiveness and everlasting gift of eternal blessedness.

Our Father. Delivered from evil. Fol. 2.

Blessing. May Christ, the Son of God, the unique Word of the one Father, whom the angelic armies serve, make you glory in the perfection of good works. R\. Amen. And may he who exalted the Archangel Gabriel with sublime honor make you burn with love for him. R\. Amen. And may he who appointed him defender of the faithful people always make him more ready to answer your prayers. [Col. 1325C] R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

Lauda. The Lord prepared his throne in heaven. Alleluia. P. And his kingdom will rule over all. Alleluia. Bless the Lord, all his angels. Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V\. In the sight of the angels I shall sing to you, O Lord; I shall worship toward your holy temple and confess your name. P. And his kingdom. V\. Glory and honor. P. Bless the Lord, all.

Prayer. O Gabriel, prince of the army of angels, come, we ask, to free the souls of faithful peoples, so that the righteous, obtaining righteousness, may always bear fruit in good things, and the unjust, converted to repentance, may not [Col. 1325D] despair of receiving forgiveness. Let us thus urge one another toward what is better, so that we may deserve to attain the eternal reward. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

In the name of the Lord.

### At Matins

Antiphon. Give us joy. Psalm 50. Prayer. Restore to us, O Lord. Fol. CLXIII.

Antiphon 1. The angel Gabriel was sent by God to Mary, a virgin betrothed to Joseph, announcing the word, and the virgin was terrified by the light. Do not fear, Mary; you have found favor with the Lord. P. Behold, you will conceive and bear a son, and he will be called the Son of the Most High. V\. For the word of the Lord is upright, and all [Col. 1326A] his works are in faith. P. Behold, you will conceive. V\. Glory and honor. P. Behold, you will conceive.

Prayer. Most merciful Father, we humbly implore your mercy: commend to yourself the solemnities of this day which we have undertaken for the veneration of your most blessed Archangel Gabriel; and just as you granted him the crown of holy perfection, so by his intercession grant us the forgiveness and remission of all sins. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 2. I saw an angel flying through mid-heaven, having an eternal gospel and saying: P. Fear the Lord our God, and give him glory and honor. V\. You who stand in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God. P. Fear. V\. Glory and [Col. 1326B] honor. P. Fear.

Prayer. O Gabriel, prince. See above, in the preceding Vespers.

Antiphon 3. I, Jesus, send my angel to testify to human beings: Behold, I am coming quickly. P. And my reward is with me, to heal the sicknesses of my people. V\. Hear this, all nations; perceive it with your ears, you who inhabit the world. P. And my reward. V\. Glory and honor. P. And my reward.

Prayer. Send us, merciful God, Gabriel, prince of the heavenly army, so that he may free us from the hand of our enemies and present us unharmed to you, the Lord our God; 8 and may we always have him as our helper, whom we recognize as exalted in your gift; [Col. 1326C] so that by his support, resisting vices, we may flourish in virtues, and so that, once the inscription of our guilt has been removed, the book of eternal life may contain us forever. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

R\. The angel Gabriel was sent by God to the Virgin Mary, saying: “Hail, Mary, full of grace; the Lord is with you; blessed are you among women.” P. Therefore also the Holy One who will be born from you will be called the Son of God. P. The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. P. Therefore also the Holy One who will be born. V\. Glory and honor. P. Therefore.

Prayer. [Col. 1326D] O most holy Gabriel! O strength of the Most High Father! O messenger of truth! O appointed herald of the divine mystery! You come to the Virgin as the truest discoverer; you greet her as a messenger, you overshadow her as a servant. “Hail,” you say, “Mary”; you declare, “My Lord is with you”; you address her as blessed among women; you proclaim that the Word will proceed from her; and by wondrous testimony you affirm that he is to be called the Son of God. Therefore we ask that you who came to the Virgin as the messenger of truth may wondrously offer our petition in the divine ears; and that through you we may come to know hidden mysteries in such a way that we never fall into the enemy’s prison, but through the Word of the Most High Father himself, whose forerunner you declare yourself to be in coming to the Virgin, may we have both a return to forgiveness and a true dwelling in the eternal homeland. R\. Amen.

Through mercy.

### At Lauds

[Col. 1327A]

For the Canticle. Antiphon. The Lord appeared from Mount Paran, and with him were thousands of saints.

Canticle. The Lord from Sinai. Fol. CLXVI.

For the Benedictus. Antiphon. We bless you, O Lord, who sit above the cherubim, King of Israel.

Canticle. Blessed are you, Lord. Fol. 6.

Sono. In the sight of the angels I shall sing to you, O Lord. Alleluia. V\. I shall worship toward your holy temple and confess you, O Lord. P. Alleluia.

Lauda. Praise the Lord from the heavens. Alleluia; praise him in the heights. Alleluia. Psalm 148.

Reading from the Book of the Prophet Ezekiel (Chapters 9, 10, 11).

R\. Thanks be to God.

The hand of the Lord came upon me, and the spirit of the Lord lifted me up, [Col. 1327B] and I saw. And behold, a man clothed in linen, who had an ink-well on his back, answered with a word, saying: “I have done as you commanded me.” And I saw, and behold, in the firmament that was above the head of the cherubim there appeared above it something like sapphire stone and something resembling the appearance of the sun. And he said to the man clothed in linen: “Take fire from the midst of the wheels that are between the cherubim.” And I entered and saw, and behold, four wheels beside the cherubim: one wheel beside one cherub and another wheel beside another cherub; the appearance of the wheels was like the appearance of chrysolite stone. When they stood, they stood; and when they were lifted up, they were lifted up, for the spirit of life was in them. And the glory of the Lord went out from the threshold of the temple and stood [Col. 1327C] above the cherubim. And the Spirit lifted me up and brought me to the eastern gate of the house of the Lord, which faces the rising of the sun. And the glory of the Lord ascended from the midst of the city and stood upon the mountain that is east of the city, and the glory of the God of Israel was above it. R\. Amen.

Hymn. “All you people of the Catholic faith.” Supplication. “Let us pray to the Redeemer.” See above, in the preceding Vespers.

Capitulum. O light, splendor of light, ineffable Christ God! Wisdom, power, and glory of the Father, who appeared in this world to the sight of all in flesh as the star of salvation, and, having conquered the prince of darkness, returned to the heights as the Word made flesh: grant to us, your suppliants, in the darkness of this age, the most abundant brightness of your splendor. [Col. 1327D] Establish for us as patron and supreme defender your angel Gabriel, so that he may guard our entrance and our departure and you may admit us, crowned, to your right hand.

Our Father. Delivered from evil. Fol. 2.

Lauda. “The Lord prepared his throne in heaven.” Blessing. “Christ, the Son of God.” See above, in the preceding Vespers.

## ON THE FEAST OF SAINT MARY MAGDALENE

### At Vespers

[Col. 1332B] Lauda: “You have put on confession and beauty.” P. “Clothed with light as with a garment.” V. “Confession and splendor are before him; holiness and magnificence are in his sanctuary.” P. “Clothed with light.” V. “And I will give thanks to the Lord with psalters.” P. “Clothed with light.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “Clothed with light.”

May the Lord be always. R. And with you.

Sono: “I will give thanks to you, Lord, with my whole heart; I will tell of all your wonders.” Alleluia. P. “I will rejoice and exult in you, Lord; I will sing praise to your name, O Most High.” Alleluia.

May the Lord be always. R. And with you.

Antiphon: “I will give thanks to you, Lord, with my whole heart, because you have heard the words of my mouth.” P. “In the presence of the angels I will sing praise to you.” V. “You are my God, and I will give thanks to you; my God, and I will exalt you.” P. “In the presence.” V. “Glory.” P. “In the presence.”

May the Lord be. R. And with you.

Lauda: “I will give thanks to you, Lord the King, alleluia.” P. “And I will praise God my Savior. Alleluia, alleluia.” V. “I will worship toward your holy temple, and I will give thanks to you, Lord.” P. “And.” V. “Glory.” P. “And.”

### Hymn

In place of a special linen cloth,  
A head-covering served [Latin: *capitilio*];  
Amid sacred banquets  
Envy was not absent.

It was envy that drove  
The first-formed man from  
The glory of paradise;  
His long exile  
The cross’s gibbet serves.

For certain men, swollen in heart,  
Were reproaching the Lord:  
“If he knew the inward mysteries  
Of divinity,  
He would not allow  
A sinful woman to touch him.”

But he, answering wisely,  
The examiner of conscience,  
Whose eye does not fail to see  
The hiding place of any creature,  
Setting forth an unchanging  
Pattern of forgiveness,  
Said to Simon, privately  
(Speaking allegorically):

“There were two men,  
Bound by debts of different amounts:  
One by five hundred coins,  
The other by fifty.  
When their debt was called in,  
They had no means of repayment;  
The creditor, moved with compassion,  
Granted the favor.

Tell me, then: Which of them  
Loved more? The reward  
That you promised to all  
Who truly love you,  
With the Father and the Holy Spirit,  
For everlasting ages.

[Col. 1333A] Amen.

Supplication: “Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world,” with the name changed, fol. CLXXXVII.

Capitula: God, who made the repentance of blessed Mary Magdalene so pleasing and acceptable to you that you not only forgave her sins, but also, through the singular grace of your love, fully illumined the inmost recesses of her heart: grant us an abundance of your favor, that we may rejoice in the solemnity of her by whose prayers before you we are cleansed from the stains of our sins.

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” Fol. 2.

Benediction: May Christ the Lord, who made himself worthily confessed before human beings by most blessed Mary Magdalene, confess you before his Father who is in heaven. R. Amen. And may he who placed upon his lips songs of confession acceptable to himself receive your confession to reward it. R. Amen. So that, by the example of Mary Magdalene, confessing and praising the name of Jesus Christ forever, you may deserve to be in heaven as participants in him whom you have confessed. R. Amen.

Through his mercy, etc.

Lauda: “Your bones shall flourish like willows, alleluia.” P. “Beside flowing waters.” Alleluia, alleluia. V. “And he shall be like a tree planted beside channels of water, which will yield its fruit in its season.” P. “Beside flowing waters.” V. “Glory and honor to the Father and to the Son.” P. “Beside flowing waters.”

Prayer: God, who, accepting the confession of blessed Mary Magdalene, heard all the words of her mouth so fully that you made her a participant in your kingdom, so that she might sing psalms to you in the presence of the angels: receive now through her the vow of our confession, you who brought her to her reward; and since by confession you willed her to be blessed, grant that after our fall we may make confession in this world, so that it may lead us to the homeland where we shall be crowned eternally. R. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God, etc.

### At Matins

Antiphon: “You will open my lips, and my mouth will proclaim your praise.” Psalm L.

Prayer: “May our tongue praise you, Lord.” Seek at fol. CLXI.

Antiphon 1: “I will give thanks to you among the peoples, Lord.” P. “I will sing a psalm to your name among the nations.” V. “O Lord, I am your handmaid and the daughter of your handmaid.” P. “I will sing a psalm.” V. “Glory and honor to the Father,” etc. P. “I will sing a psalm.”

Prayer: God, Son of God, whom blessed Mary Magdalene confessed with her whole heart, honoring your name, and was led to the crown: grant that confession in our mouth which may cleanse us from guilt, so that whatever we utter in honor of your praise we may perceive to profit us as the gain of an eternal gift. R. Amen.

Through your mercy, our God.

Antiphon 2: “I will give great thanks to the Lord with my mouth.” P. “And in the midst of many I will praise him.” V. “For he stood at the right hand of the poor, to save my soul from those who pursued me.” P. “And in the midst.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “And in.”

[Col. 1334B] Prayer: You made Mary Magdalene, Lord, exceedingly blessed—she who confessed you with her whole heart and was shown to be conspicuous in the assembly of the righteous and in the congregation. Grant us, therefore, through her merits, that, cleansed from guilt by the simple confession of our mouth, we may deserve to take part in the assembly and congregation and gatherings of the saints. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Antiphon 3: “In peace I shall sleep and rest.” P. “For you, Lord, have established me uniquely in hope.” V. “I will give thanks to you, Lord, with my whole heart, in the assembly of the righteous and in the congregation.” P. “For you.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “For you.”

Prayer: God, who [concerning] blessed Mary—seek at the preceding Vespers.

[Col. 1334C] R. Mary Magdalene was standing outside at the tomb, weeping. While she was weeping, she looked to see where the body of Jesus had been placed, and she saw two angels seated in white. P. And turning backward, she saw Jesus standing, and she came announcing to the disciples: “I have seen the Lord, and he said these things to me.” V. Jesus said to Mary: “Woman, why are you weeping? Whom are you seeking?” P. “And turning.” V. “Glory,” etc. Let the Responsory be repeated.

Prayer: Your removal, Lord, from the tomb is lamented by the fruitful search of that Mary Magdalene, with an outpouring of tears; for she was indeed being consumed by the fire of her desire for you. We ask, therefore, that you likewise kindle in us the desire for your love, so that in seeking you we may be stronger and, when we find you, may deserve to be happy without end. R. Amen.

Through.

### At Lauds

For the Canticle. Antiphon: “Behold, in peace my bitterness is most bitter; but you have rescued my soul so that I would not perish, and you have cast all my sins behind your back.”

Canticle: “I said in the middle of my days.” Seek at fol. 122.

Let the antiphon be repeated: “Behold, in peace my bitterness.”

Prayer: Rescue our souls, Lord, so that we may not perish in destruction; cast behind your back all the deeds of all our sins, so that we, lost, may not be cast down into hell; but may confess you, the giver of life, here, and, awaiting your truth, may continually sing our psalms in your house. R. Amen.

Through.

For the Canticle. Antiphon: “I will give thanks to you.” Canticle: “I will give thanks to you, Lord the King,” folio CLXXI.

Prayer: Author and Lord of ineffable goodness, who filled the tongue of blessed Mary Magdalene with confession and rewarded the love of her heart: grant us, through her merits, that, confessing your name on earth, we may have peace in our days. R. Amen.

Through.

For the Benedictus. Antiphon: “Daughter of Zion, bless the Lord God Most High with every blessing and praise.”

Canticle: “Blessed are you, Lord.” Fol. 6.

Sono: “In the presence of the angels I will sing praise to you, Lord,” alleluia. V. “I will worship toward your holy temple, and I will give thanks to you, Lord.” Alleluia.

Lauda: “Alleluia. Her confession is over heaven and earth, alleluia; he has exalted the horn of his people. Alleluia. A hymn belongs to all his saints.” Psalm CXLVIII.

Reading from the Book of Proverbs of Solomon (chapter XXXI).

R. Thanks be to God.

Who will find a strong woman? Her price is from afar and from the farthest ends. The heart of her husband trusts in her, and he will have no need of spoils. She will repay him with good, not evil, all the days of her life. She sought wool and flax, and worked with the counsel of her hands. She became like a merchant’s ship, bringing her bread from afar. Rising at night, she gave food to her household and provisions to her maidservants. She considered a field and bought it; from the fruit of her hands she planted a vineyard. She girded her loins with strength and strengthened her arm. She tasted that her trade was good; her lamp will not be extinguished at night. She put out her hand to strong things, and her fingers grasped the spindle. She opened her hand to the needy and extended her palms to the poor. She will not fear for her house because of the cold of snow, for all her household are clothed with double garments. She made herself a covering; fine linen and purple are her clothing. Her husband is noble at the gate when he sits with the elders of the land. She made linen garments and sold them, and gave a girdle to the Canaanite. Strength and beauty are her adornment, and she will laugh on the last day. She opened her mouth to wisdom, and the law of kindness is on her tongue. She watched over the paths of her house, and she did not eat the bread of idleness. Her sons rose up and proclaimed her most blessed; her husband, and he praised her. Many daughters have gathered riches; but you have surpassed them all. False is charm, and vain is beauty; the woman who fears God is the one who shall be praised. Give her from the fruit of her hands, and let her works praise her at the gates. Amen.

Hymn: “For a special linen cloth.”

Supplication: “Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world.”

Capitula: “God, who [accepted the confession] of blessed Mary Magdalene.”

Lauda: “Your bones shall flourish.”

14 Benediction: “Christ the Lord, who …” Seek at the preceding Vespers.

For the feast of Apollinaris, Bishop and Martyr.

[Col. 1336A]

Let all things be said from the office of one Pontifical Martyr, fol. CLVI.

## ON THE FEAST OF SAINT ANNE, MOTHER OF THE VIRGIN MARY

### At Vespers

Lauda: “You have put on confession and beauty.”

Sono: “I will give thanks to you, Lord,” fol. CLXIX.

May the Lord be. R. And with you.

Antiphon: “I will give thanks to you, Lord, with my whole heart, because you have heard the words of my mouth.” P. “In the presence of the angels I will sing praise to you.” V. “You are my God, and I will give thanks to you; my God, and I will exalt you.” P. “In the presence.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “In the presence.”

May the Lord be. R. And with you.

Lauda: “I will give thanks to you, Lord the King, alleluia.” P. “And I will praise God my Savior. Alleluia, alleluia.” V. “I will worship toward your holy temple, and I will give thanks to the Lord.” P. “And I will praise together with you.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “And I will praise together with you.”

### Hymn

Let the honorable people  
Celebrate this feast  
Of the present light for the Lord,  
And let them throng the heavens  
With worthy hymns.

The mother of the Mother of Christ,  
Departing from this sorrowful world  
In faithful belief,  
Gives the gifts of life.

Thus the root of Jesse  
Brought forth Anna,  
So that she might be the Mother  
Of the Mother of the Son  
Of God the Father.

From this plant of flesh  
The holy Virgin arises;  
From this spring flows  
The stone cut from the mountain.

Now raised into heaven,  
May the blessed woman  
Cleanse us from guilt  
By her prayer.

Let praise be given  
To the triune and one God,  
With whom Anna lives  
Together with Mary.

[Col. 1336D]

Let the Church modulate  
The bright joys of the day,  
Celebrating in Anna,  
God’s handmaid,  
The wonders of heaven.

Anna, offspring of kings  
And succession of priests,  
Adorned her illustrious stock  
Among her fathers  
By her deeds.

Wedded to the Judge of heaven  
In faithful marriage,  
She conceived a heavenly fruit  
According to the angelic word.

For a time barren  
And with a body almost withered,  
By the decree of the Father of lights  
She gave birth to the Queen of virgins.

Through the appeal of the Mother’s daughter,  
Mary, full of grace,  
Grant us to have  
The Author of all things  
Favorable to us.

Let there be praise to the Father’s light,  
To the Son, and to the Spirit,  
Who through Anna’s merit  
May lead us to heaven’s entrance.

Amen.

Supplication: “Let us pray to the Redeemer,” with the name changed, fol. CLXXXVII.

Capitula: Eternal, almighty Lord Jesus Christ, from whom every good thing arises and advances along a better course, who strengthen the faith of confessors: grant the gift of endurance while the harshness of persecutors rages. We ask your omnipotence, Lord, that you graciously attend to and mercifully receive our prayers, which we pour out in honor of blessed Anne, mother of Mary the Virgin, your mother, so that, with your mercy cooperating, they may obtain without doubt what they ask in faith, and, freed from all offenses, may possess the heavenly kingdom without end.

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” Fol. 2.

Benediction: May Christ the Lord, who made himself worthily confessed before human beings by most blessed Anne, mother of Mary the Virgin, his mother, confess you before his Father. R. Amen. And may he who placed upon his lips songs of confession acceptable to himself receive your confession to reward it. R. Amen. So that, following the example of blessed Anne, mother of Mary the Virgin, his mother, confessing and praising the name of Jesus Christ forever, you may deserve to be in heaven as participants in him whom you have confessed. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Lauda: “Your bones shall flourish, like …” Folio CLXX.

Prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, who are great and glorious: grant us, your servants, that, while we admire the greatness of your works, we may praise your magnificence with due confession; and through the intercession of glorious blessed Anne, mother of Mary the Virgin, your mother, grant us the perfect beauty of understanding, obedience in fear, and the diligent fulfillment of your faithful commandments with complete custody of the heart. R. Amen.

[Col. 1337D] Through mercy.

### At Matins

Antiphon: “You will open my lips.” Fol. CLXXXI. Psalm L.

Prayer: “May they rejoice in you, Lord.” Fol. CLXXXI.

Antiphon 1: “I will rejoice forever, alleluia.” P. “I will confess, alleluia, and sing praise to God, alleluia, alleluia.” V. “Return, my soul, to your rest, for the Lord has dealt favorably with you.” P. “I will confess.” V. “Glory and honor to the Father.” P. “I will confess.”

Prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, who made blessed Anne, mother of Mary the Virgin, your mother, rejoice and exult forever and ever, so that, singing praise to you alone without end, she might offer a hymn of praise—she whose confession merited obtaining fellowship with you: we ask you with devoted hearts that through her merits our life may blossom again and, corrected from evil deeds, may shine; so that we, who now deserve punishment for our crimes, may through confession and the worship of Christian faith deserve to reach future glory. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon 2: “You have become beautiful, alleluia.” P. “And the fragrance of your garments is above all spices. Alleluia, alleluia.” V. “Praise the Lord, Jerusalem; praise your God, Zion.” P. “And the fragrance.” V. “Glory and honor to the Father.” P. “And the fragrance.”

Prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, who are great and glorious. Here above.

Antiphon 3: “I will give thanks to you, Lord, because I have been made fearfully wonderful; your works, O God, are wonderful.” P. “And my soul knows this exceedingly.” V. “I will give thanks to you, Lord, with my whole heart, in the assembly of the righteous and in the congregation.” P. “And my soul.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “And my soul.”

Prayer: Merciful and gracious Lord Jesus Christ, who glorify the righteous through the power of the heart and justify sinners without works; who bless those who confess you in the world and glorify those who confess you in heaven: grant us, through the intervention of blessed Anne, mother of Mary the Virgin, your mother, whose solemnity is celebrated, to confess you, the Lord, with devoted affection of heart; so that, revealing our own offenses, we may deserve to find forgiveness for which we grieve. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

[Col. 1338C] R. Blessed Anne, mother of Mary the Virgin, his mother, has become beautiful and fair, says the Lord. P. “And your fragrance is like unmixed balsam; your face, however, is like the shining sun at its rising.” Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia. V. “For your voice is sweet, and your face is beautiful.” P. “And your fragrance.” V. “Glory and honor to the Father.” P. “And your fragrance.”

Prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, who are exalted above all nations and dwell gloriously in the heavenly places: look down favorably from on high upon our humility; and just as your Church, which had been obstructed by the vices of barrenness, is now, believing in you, full of the merits of virtues and abundant in children, so, by your gift and through the intervention of glorious blessed Anne, mother of Mary the Virgin, your mother, may our mind, barren and unfruitful in works, receive the seed of the word and overflow with abundant fruits; and may it strive everywhere to love your renowned name with unanimity of heart and praise it with the assent of faith. R. Amen.

### At Lauds

For the Canticle. Antiphon: “I will give thanks to you, Lord.”

Canticle: “I will give thanks to you, Lord the King,” folio CLXXI.

Prayer: Most praiseworthy and great Lord Jesus Christ, imploring you, we seek you; seeking you, we entreat you through the intervention of glorious blessed Anne, mother of Mary the Virgin, your mother. Show mercy to us for your name’s sake; and in those things from which, by sinning, we have departed from you, let us remain in humble confession; and by that compassion with which you redeemed captives and helped the oppressed, now wipe away what we have done, and set those whom you have redeemed at your right hand. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

For the Benedictus. Antiphon: “Daughter of Zion, bless the Lord God Most High with every blessing and praise.”

Canticle: “Blessed are you, Lord.” Fol. 6.

Sono: “In the presence of the angels.”

### Hymn

Let the rejoicing world celebrate this feast,  
Following Anne, mother of Christ’s Mother,  
Who by sacred deeds receives  
The joys of life.

The offspring of Abraham, the line of priests,  
A king’s daughter, hope, a Hebrew stock—  
It sings her as noble  
In the merits and life of the saints.

Previously barren in an unfruitful womb,  
By the divine will she gave birth to Mary,  
The Lady of kings and the true flower  
Of virginity.

And through her, Jesus Christ,  
Wiping away our guilty offenses,  
Daughter, come to the aid of your mother . . . [lacuna]

May this piety, together with the gentle  
Holy Spirit, grant us this;  
May we be helped by the prayers  
Of Mother Anne in every . . . [lacuna]  
Time of the age.

Amen.

[Col. 1339C] Supplication: “Let us pray to the Redeemer of the world,” with the name changed. Fol. CLXXXVII.

Capitula: Glorious and merciful Lord, who granted blessed Anne, mother of Mary the Virgin, your mother, to confess you greatly with her mouth, and willed to be praised through her confession in the midst of the righteous, so that, confessing you on earth and glorifying her in the assembly of the saints, you might make her rejoice: we ask the gift of your grace, that through her prayers you may grant us to be cleansed from the contagion of sin, rescued from everlasting fires, and attain the blessedness of your glory.

Our Father. “Delivered from evil.” Fol. 2.

Lauda: “Your bones shall flourish.”

Benediction: “Christ the Lord, who blessed Anne …” Seek at the preceding Vespers. [Col. 1339D]

## FEASTS OF NOVEMBER

## FEAST OF ALL SAINTS

### At Vespers

Lauda: “It has arisen,” fol. CLXII. Sono: “Rejoice, you righteous,” fol. CLXV. Antiphon: “Righteous men,” fol. CLXII. Lauda: “They called upon the Lord,” fol. CLXVIII.

#### Hymn

Christ, Redeemer of all,

Preserve your servants;

Appeased by the holy prayers

Of the ever-blessed Virgin.

And may the blessed ranks

Of the heavenly spirits—

Those of the past and present—

Drive away future evils.

Prophets of the eternal Judge,

And Apostles of the Lord:

We humbly ask

That we may be saved by your prayers.

Illustrious Martyrs of God,

And radiant Confessors,

By your prayers

Carry us into the heavenly realms.

Make us companions of Christ

Together with the choir

Of holy Virgins

And all the Monks.

Drive the faithless people

From the lands of believers,

So that we may joyfully offer

To Christ the praises owed to him.

Glory to the unbegotten Father,

And to his only-begotten Son,

Together with the Holy Spirit,

For everlasting ages.

Amen.

Supplication: “Let us pray to the Redeemer,” with the names changed, fol. CLXXXVII.

Capitulum: O God, who are wondrous in the protection of all your Saints, and who have consecrated this day as a solemn feast of all your Saints, we ask your power: grant that your Catholic Church may rejoice in such great princes, so that we may deserve to follow their devout teaching, [Col. 1344B] ¹⁹ who fed the flocks dear to you with your bread; and that, having pleased you by your gift, and aided by their prayers, we may deserve to be freed from present troubles.

Our Father. “Delivered from evil,” fol. 2.

Benediction: May almighty God bless you as you rejoice in the grace of all the Saints. R. Amen. May he grant you firmness of faith, expectation of hope, and the sweetness of charity. R. Amen. Thus fortified by such supports of his grace, may you deserve to become participants in heaven also with those whose feasts you celebrate. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Lauda: “Everlasting joy,” fol. CLXIII.

Prayer: O God, exultation and crown of the Saints, hear us, your suppliants, and grant that we may deserve, by the merits of those whose relics we venerate in your love and whose memorials we recall, to be freed from every evil and preserved. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

### At Matins

Antiphon: “Give us.” Psalm L. Prayer: “Restore to us,” fol. CLXIII.

Antiphon: “On the day of our distinguished solemnity, bless God; the crown of the year of your goodness.” P. “And may your fields be filled with abundance.” V. “To you, O God, praise is due in Zion, and to you the vow shall be paid in Jerusalem.” P. “And your fields.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “And your fields.”

Prayer: Bless, O Lord, the crown of the year of your goodness on the day of our distinguished solemnity, so that minds may shine with an abundance of teaching and the fields may grow rich with the abundance of your gifts; thus grant us sustenance together with your grace, so that the flesh, fed with fruits, and the soul, nourished with divine things, may rejoice in virtues. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon: “Christ Jesus.” Prayer: “Christ Jesus, who [of mortality],” fol. CCXL.

Antiphon: “Thrones were set, and the Ancient of Days sat; his garment was exalted, and his throne was a flame of fire.” P. “Thousands of thousands served him, and ten thousand times a hundred thousand stood before him.” V. “All nations, clap your hands; shout to God with a voice of exultation.” P. “Thousands of thousands.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “Thousands of thousands.”

Prayer: Immense King of kings, to whom the God of heaven gave a strong, powerful, and honored kingdom, subjecting all things to your power, whom thousands upon thousands of Angels serve: grant rest to your people from all the burdens under which we stand weighed down; so that you, who ascended gloriously into heaven, may show yourself gentle when your grace is revealed. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

R. The King, Creator, and Lord of all taught wisdom. P. The Holy Spirit, one, simple, manifold, subtle, undefiled, sweet, and beloved. V. Great is our Lord, and great is his power; and of his wisdom there is no number. P. The Holy Spirit. V. Glory and honor. P. The Holy Spirit.

Prayer: The Creator and Lord of all taught wisdom, in which is the Holy Spirit, one, simple, manifold, and subtle; and there is one Father, one Son, and one Holy Spirit—not displayed in a plurality of deity, but joined in unity of power—so that they lack unity of person and remain in unity of nature; nor is anything there different where in each one the One resounds. Therefore, believing you, Holy Trinity, with this knowledge of faith, we ask and entreat that, through the manifestation of your Spirit, you may so illumine our heart that we may avoid the works of the flesh and pursue the perfection of holiness in every way. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon: “The Spirit of the Lord has filled the world.” P. “And he who contains all things has understanding of knowledge. For he created all things to exist.” V. “The Lord is exalted above all nations, and his glory is above the heavens.” P. “And he who contains all things.” V. “Glory and honor.” P. “And he who contains all things.”

Prayer: Place your Spirit, O Lord, in our midst; may he, washing us with the pure waters of repentance, always prepare us for you as a living sacrifice, so that neither desire may defile the temple of our heart nor the flame of eternal fire grievously afflict the earth of our body in any respect. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

R. The hand of the Lord came upon me. And I saw, and behold, a shining spirit was coming from the east, and great clouds were in it. P. And there was fire in its midst. V. Wherever the spirit went, the wheels were likewise raised, following it; for the spirit was in the wheels. P. And fire. ²⁰ V. Glory and honor. P. And fire.

[Col. 1345D] Prayer: Almighty God the Father, who in the beginning—that is, in your Son Jesus Christ our Lord—made heaven and earth, grant us that your Spirit, who moves over the waters—that is, over our dark and fluid heart—may produce in us fruits pleasing to you, so that, bearing fruit in our heart through an abundant outpouring of virtues, he may kindle us with the unceasing fire of your love. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon: “With eternal love,” fol. CLXXX.

Prayer: This is that glorious Virgin Mary, O Lord God, who today is known to have been taken up from the valley of tears and the desert of the world, resting upon your beloved only-begotten Son, who is also her Son, in an ineffable place; and her precious seal and necklace, as it were, is revealed when we confess that the body of the Lord, of one nature with this undefiled Mother who bore him, was assumed by the Divinity. Therefore we ask you, ineffable and supreme God, that our attention may be extended to the place where today, through strong love, the worthy advocate for us, the most blessed Virgin, has gone before us. R. Amen.

Through mercy.

Antiphon: “I, Jesus, send an Angel.” Prayer: “Send us, merciful God, Michael,” fol. CCCII. Antiphon: “From the womb of his mother.” Prayer: “Christ, Son of God, who [the Forerunner],” fol. CCL. Responsory: “This is the Forerunner.” Prayer: “O God, who [John the Forerunner].” Antiphon: “They have been honored.” Prayer: “They have been honored,” fol. CCLVI. Antiphon: “Blessed, and greatly honored,” fol. CLXXVIII.

[Col. 1346B] Prayer: Truly blessed, O Lord, and worthy of great honor are those whose portion you have deigned to be; therefore, through the intervention of your holy Bishops and Confessors, may whatever in us does not serve you be utterly destroyed by the love of the heavenly homeland burning within us; and afterward may your kindness join us in the heavenly kingdom with these Saints, whose souls are in your hand. R. Amen.

Through your mercy.

Antiphon: “All the glory of the king’s daughter.” Prayer: “O God, whose throne.” Responsory: “The kingdom of heaven is like ten.” Prayer: “Be present, O Lord, to those who beseech you.” Antiphon: “These are they who,” fol. CLXVIII. Prayer: “O God, exultation.” Antiphon: “Come to me.” Prayer: “Be propitious, O Lord.” Antiphon: “Come, blessed ones.” [Col. 1346C] Prayer: “Of the most blessed,” fol. CLXIII. Responsory: “The Saints who fought the contest,” fol. CLXIII.

### At Lauds

For the Canticle. Antiphon: “O Lord, those who love you shine like the sun shining at its rising.”

Canticle: “You who offered yourselves willingly,” fol. CLXIII.

For the Benedictus. Antiphon: “Holy and humble.” Canticle: “Blessed are you, Lord.” fol. 6.

Sono: “The way of the righteous,” fol. CLXVII. Lauda: “Praise the Lord.” Psalm CXLVIII. Prophecy: “The righteous shall live forever,” fol. CLIV.

#### Hymn

Jesus, Savior of the world,

Come to the redeemed with your aid;

And may the devout Mother of God

Ask salvation for the wretched.

May all the angelic companies,

The ranks of the patriarchs,

And the merits of the prophets

Intercede for us for pardon.

The Baptist, Christ’s Forerunner,

And the heavenly key-bearer,

Together with the other Apostles,

Release us from the bond of sin.

May the sacred choir of Martyrs,

The confession of Priests,

And virginal purity

Wash us from sins.

May the intercession of the Monks,

And all the heavenly citizens,

Approve the prayers of suppliants

And ask the reward of life.

Praise, honor, power, and glory

To God the Father and the Son,

And likewise to the Holy Paraclete,

For everlasting ages.

Amen.

Supplication: “Let us pray,” as above.

²¹ Capitulum: These are, O Lord, the truthful Patrons who, confidently receiving their sentence, run rejoicing toward the palm and hasten gladly toward the crown. Through their intercession, Lord almighty God, just as you have granted all your Saints freedom from the devil’s deceit, so make us, your unworthy servants, attain their mercy.

Our Father. “And lead us not into temptation.” “Delivered from evil,” fol. 2.

Lauda: “Praise of the Lord,” fol. CCXV.

Benediction: “May the Almighty bless us.” Seek it in the preceding Vespers.

## AT THE FEAST OF SAINT ELIZABETH OF HUNGARY

### At Vespers

Lauda: “Confession and beauty.” Sono: “I will confess to you,” fol. CLXIX. Antiphon: “I will confess to you, O Lord, with all my heart,” fol. CLXIX. Lauda: “I will confess to you, Lord King,” fol. CLXIX.

#### Hymn

A new star has shone forth;

The old error has fallen silent;

With new splendor it gleams.

The people jubilantly sing new praises.

Now let the Church

Open its tongue in praise of her,

And proclaim the glory

Of the new herald, hoping for pardon.

A solemn day is celebrated;

A day of salvation is honored;

A day on which hope is promised,

And, with this witness, fulfilled.

Therefore, you servant of God,

Elizabeth, reigning with Christ

Throughout the ages,

Ask pardon and grace for us.

To God the Father be glory,

And to his only Son,

With the Spirit, the Paraclete,

Now and forever.

Amen.

Supplication: “Let us pray to the Redeemer,” with the name changed, fol. CLXXXVII.

Capitulum: Lord Jesus Christ, eternal and almighty, from whom every good thing arises and advances along a better course, who strengthen the faith of Confessors, grant the gift of endurance while the harshness of persecutors rages. We ask your almighty power, Lord, that you graciously attend to and mercifully receive our prayers, which we pour out in honor of blessed Elizabeth, so that, with your mercy cooperating, those who ask in faith may obtain what they seek without doubt; and, freed from all sins, may possess the heavenly kingdom without end.

Our Father. “Delivered from evil,” fol. 2.

Benediction: May Christ the Lord, who caused the most blessed Elizabeth to confess him worthily before men on earth, confess you before his Father who is in heaven. R. Amen. And may he himself, who placed upon her lips songs of confession acceptable to him, receive your confession to reward it. R. Amen. Following the example of blessed Elizabeth, may you confess and praise the name of Jesus Christ forever and deserve to be participants in heaven with him whom you have confessed. ²² R. Amen.

Through the mercy of that same God of ours.

Lauda: “Your bones shall flourish like willows. Alleluia,” [Col. 1348D] fol. CLXX.

Prayer: “O God, who [the confession of the most blessed Elizabeth],” fol. CLXXV.

### At Matins

Antiphon: “You will open my lips, and my mouth will proclaim your praise.” Psalm L. Prayer: “May my tongue praise you, O Lord,” fol. CLXI. Antiphon: “I will confess to you among the peoples.” Prayer: “God the Son of God.” Antiphon: “I will confess greatly to the Lord.” Prayer: “Truly blessed, O Lord, is Elizabeth.” Antiphon: “I will sleep in peace,” fol. CLXXV. Prayer: “O God, who [the confession of the most blessed Elizabeth].” Seek it in the preceding Vespers.

R. I will confess greatly to the Lord with my mouth, and in the midst of many I will praise him; for he stood at my right hand. P. To save my soul from those who pursued it. V. For he hid me in his tabernacle; on the day of evils he protected me. P. To save. V. Glory and honor. P. To save.

Prayer: Rise up, our glory, O God, and rescue captives from the enemy; look with favor upon those for whom you have been magnified even to the heavens, who trust in you; and grant help in tribulation, you who are the completion of our salvation. Therefore, protect us by the aid of your blessed Confessor Elizabeth, lest, because of what our merit demands, we be handed over to hell; and thus reward us with recompense that, confessing you, you may lead us into heaven. R. Amen.

Through.

### At Lauds

For the Canticle. Antiphon: “I will confess to you, O Lord.” [Col. 1349B] Canticle: “I will confess to you, Lord King,” fol. CLXXI.

Prayer: Author of ineffable goodness and Lord, who filled the tongue of the most blessed Elizabeth with confession and rewarded the charity of her heart, grant us through her merits that, confessing your name on earth, we may have peace in our days. R. Amen.

For the Benedictus. Antiphon: “Daughter of Zion, bless the Lord God Most High with every blessing and praise.”

Canticle: “Blessed are you, Lord.”

Sono: “In the sight of the Angels,” fol. CLXXIII. Psalm CXLVIII. Prophecy: “Who will find a strong woman?” Here, fol. 13.

#### Hymn

Now let the joyful voice of all

Sing throughout the Church;

For rejoicing Zion, the mother,

The daughter, shares in joy

As she ascends from the deep

Valley of misery.

Born from royal stock

In the years of infancy,

A man took her as his bride,

A man of outstanding character;

Yet she was inspired above all

By a vow of continence.

By faith, offspring, and sacrament,

She teaches by true testimony

That this marriage was valid,

For she attained the company

Of the heavenly fathers

Through the growth of holy life.

The law of the flesh did not extinguish

The strong spirit within her; ²³

Rather, she fulfilled it through faith and vow,

And did not leave void

The purpose which her mind,

Completed by God,

Had undertaken.

She was distinguished; she was blessed,

The solace of the poor;

Not lifted up by worldly pride,

Nor by noble ancestors;

Having slain the flesh within herself,

She crucified vice.

The teacher of innocence

Preserved her innocent;

For a long time she pierced herself

With the nails of repentance:

She completed her passion

On the cross of patience.

Bearing poverty in her mind,

She redeemed pleasures;

From the treasury of devotion

She poured out abundance of gold,

And supplied the needs

Of many in want.

She performed work, seeking sustenance

By labour poured out for herself;

And, becoming contemptible in her own eyes,

She despised disgrace,

Knowing that to you alone, O Christ,

It is right to give glory.

Glory be to you, good

²⁴ Christ, now and forever:

You faithfully help those

Who struggle in the contest,

And give the crown’s reward

To the one who conquers manfully.

Amen.

Supplication: “Let us pray to the Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer of the world.” Seek it in the preceding Vespers.

Capitulum: Glorious and merciful Lord, who granted blessed Elizabeth to confess you greatly with her mouth and wished to be praised by her confession in the midst of the righteous, so that, confessing you on earth and glorifying her in the assembly of the Saints, you might make her rejoice: we ask for the gift of your grace, that through her prayers you may grant us to be cleansed from the contagion of sin, rescued from everlasting fires, and attain the blessedness of your glory.

Our Father. “And lead us not into temptation.” “Delivered from evil,” fol. 2.

Lauda: “Your bones shall flourish,” fol. CLXX. Benediction: “Christ the Lord, who ...” Seek it in the preceding Vespers.

At the feast of Saint Felicity, martyr.

Let everything be said as for one Virgin, fol. CLXXIX.

At the feast of Saint Chrysogonus, martyr.

Let everything be said as for one Martyr, fol. CLX.

## AT THE FEAST OF SAINT CATHERINE, VIRGIN AND MARTYR

[Col. 1350D]

Let everything be said as for one Virgin, fol. CLXXIX, except for the hymn at Vespers and Matins, which follows.

#### Hymn

Catherine, wondrous

And pleasing to God,

Praiseworthy in all things,

Come to the aid of us wretched ones.

Be present for us exiles,

Who honor your feast;

And, lacking virtues,

Raise us up to the stars.

From your sacred bones

A liquid flows for the sick,

Healing them of their sufferings

Through your prayers.

After the triumph of martyrdom,

The Angels carried you

To the holy mountain of Sinai:

Thus the Lord’s voice had commanded.

While you were in the world,

You lived in your heart for the Lord,

Blooming with virginal flower,

Shining upon the King’s throne.

Therefore, most holy Virgin,

Save us from everlasting death

By your constant prayer,

Throughout the ages of ages.

May almighty God grant this,

And the almighty Son,

With the Spirit, the Paraclete,

Who reigns forever.

Amen.

### At Matins, Hymn

Rejoicing with the Angels

And with the choirs of virgins,

Let us celebrate with songs

The feast of the virgin Catherine:

Whom the Lord, while she was in prison,

Miraculously fed

Through a dove

With the sweetness of his grace.

The Spirit taught her

So wisely that she taught

What prevailed among the learned;

Nor could she be overcome.

From her sacred wound

Milk flowed instead of blood:

It did not come from a breast,

But from a divine gift.

May the King of grace

Refresh us with the stream

Of this sacred flow,

So that at the soul’s departure

We may enjoy the gifts of glory.

For the feast of holy Catherine,

Virgin and martyr,

May the peoples of God rejoice

Throughout all ages.

For this Virgin, worthy of God,

Pious, sweet, and kind,

Completed twice six days of fasting

In prison,

To whom Michael was sent,

The Archangel and standard-bearer,

So that, secure from battle,

She might have God’s assistance.

He rebukes those who fight,

Those with whom she was in dispute,

Saying: Whoever hopes in God

Always wins and prevails.

At last Christ appeared,

Whom the holy Virgin deserved

To see; she rejected

²⁴ the world, for which she did not grieve.

Virgin born of King Costus,

Have mercy on us always:

May the day of judgment

Not be punishment and torment for us.

Fulfill what you asked;

And you, O King, who promised

That at the soul’s departure

There would be salvation of pardon for us.

Praise, honor, and dominion

Be to the Creator of all,

With the Nazarene Son

And the Spirit, the Paraclete.

Grant this, unbegotten Father,

And you, Most High Son,

With the Spirit, the Paraclete,

Who reigns forever.

Amen.

For Saint Peter, Bishop and martyr.

Let everything be said as for one Martyr Pontiff, fol. CLVI.

For Saints Facundus, Primitivus, Agricola, and Vitalis, martyrs.

Let everything be said as for several Martyrs with nine lessons, fol. CLXVIII, except for the hymn “Rejoice, flowers of the Martyrs,” fol. CCCXX.

For Saints Chrysanthus, Maurus, and Daria, martyrs.

Let everything be said as for several Martyrs, fol. CLXVIII.
